reviews.comment: He's very clear and specific about what he's looking for in the three major essays. It might seem like a lot at first, but as long as you follow the guidelines and participate in class, it's very manageable to get a good grade. I would definitely recommend Aaron for ENG125.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You have to attend class and participate. He can go on tangents a lot in class but is easy to meet for help on essays and is pretty helpful. He's pretty funny and overall very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron is a great instructor, chill/funny guy. He interacts well with students. This class really emphasizes the writing process, not just the essays themselves. Your grade is based off attendance/participation, essays, and some short writing assignments/annotated readings, pretty light workload. Definitely take this class with him if you can.

Would highly recommend this professor and class to anyone! Aaron Burch is very chill and engaging and you can tell he truly loves what he does and likes to get students excited about their writing. Took this class just because I needed ULWR and I feel like I learned a lot more than I thought I would. Not super tough, but you need to put in effort.

I've had Aaron Burch before for another class, too, and he was great in both of them He's big on group discussion, peer editing, and sharing work, so be ready for that!  If you like to not turn in tiny assignments, you may get in a bit of trouble because the small writing exercises for credit can add up. He's very comfortable and willing to chat!

I liked Aaron's class a lot because he was a really approachable and laid back instructor. I wasn't crazy about all the readings, some were boring, but instructions for essays were clear and it was not stressful or too hard. I went for extra help to his office hours and he really helped, I would definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron is a great lecturer at UM, I took his English 125 class my freshman year and had a blast. He's very sarcastic so be prepared for that, but he is genuinely a good guy. Class was mostly based on 3 essays, his grading style was clear and is willing to go over essays in office hours. Would take him again!
He seemed really into the material but got annoyed when the class did not participate. He talked a lot in class but tried to make it interesting.

Overall, the class was alright. My writing improved, and it was nice to have an opportunity to expand my portfolio. However, I do not recommend taking it with this professor. He would disrespect students (especially those who were female), refused to give content warnings despite how graphic the readings often were, and was largely inaccessible.

Great opportunity to improve your writing in this class, and often gives decent feedback, but is inaccessible outside of class. Doesn't reply to emails. Can be patronizing, especially to female students -- multiple instances where he sympathized with abusive men in stories, refuses to give content warnings, interrupts female students, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cool dude who I found really relatable. Wants class to participate. My section had a lot of people who slacked off so it made it awkward sometimes. There were a few moments where he literally just asked us why so few of us participated. Really passionate about writing and just wants students who care about it as much as he does was what I felt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really cool guy. Can be a tough grader. You have to be able to identify what he's looking for in essays or you'll do poorly, but it wasn't too hard to catch on. Overall, a great professor; I'd take a class of his again. And it's a REALLY good idea to go to office hours if you're struggling with a paper (saved me)!!

I took my first year writing English 125 with Burch and he was awesome. Hes super chill and nice and the essays arent bad, they can be pretty fun and you have a lot of freedom with them. Youll work for your grade, but its worth it. Super cool and laid back guy.

Aaron is great.  I was skeptical to take his English 325 class without there being a rating on rate my professor for him. He understands what it's like to be a student and accommodates his lessons to be interesting and applicable, along with his assignments. Essays aren't bad at all, they were fun. Read his books, he's great.

Lectures were very good, but grading seemed too harsh. More work than you would expect for a class like this, and very little leniency. Extra effort needed to get an A on every assignment, with points being docked regularly on discussion posts. More difficult tests than expected, takes the subject very seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had at Michigan. His lectures are structured very well, assigned readings complement lectures, and he can be quite funny. Some topics covered are obscure and fascinating. No devices are allowed in lecture or discussion sections to prioritize handwritten note-taking, which is not for everyone but helped me learn and study.

Dr. Mora is an incredibly engaging professor with well organized, easy to follow presentations. The readings he assigns never have a dull page, his lectures never a dull moment. He breaks down otherwise complicated moments in history well, helping students by presenting stories in memorable and fun ways. He's humorous and approachable above all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a great professor! Even with the odd subjects of the class, he encouraged great discussions. The readings and short essays each week were long but acceptable for an upper level writing requirement. He gives a lot of feedback on writing assignments that's important to consider if you want good grades. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Only material for the class are lectures and LENGTHY readings. You can only take notes on paper, no technology, otherwise your graded attendance for the day will be marked as a zero. Two exams and final project are the only things graded. Exams are hard to study for with dozens of pages of material to try to memorize, but an interesting

Professor Mora is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. Of course, it helps that he was talking about the history of superheroes, but every lecture was fun and engaging. No electronics in class and tests can be a little tough, but take detailed notes and you will be fine. HW is mainly discussion posts and reading comics to discuss in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take Professor Mora's Class. Always. He is a super engaging lecturer who is knowledgeable about everything he teaches. Fairly interesting readings. Loved his class and loved him as an instructor.

Professor Mora teaches the elements of US history that you missed in high school. Rather than focusing on major events such as world wars, he focuses on more obscure events like the Zoot Suit Riots and other things often forgotten to American History. The readings are interesting help you become a more critical thinker.

Hist. of the US West has been my favorite class I've taken in college so far. I'm a history major, and it's had a transformational effect on my view of US history. One of the few classes I've had where I've left and wanted to immediately tell people the crazy stuff I've learned. I did not find the exams difficult, but I also liked the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer who knows his stuff, extremely detailed lectures, take deep notes as you will need them to study! Some questions on his exams are extremely tough, so pay extra attention. fun end of term projects and cares about students. Hilarious dry humor, makes sure everyone is on the same page with class. Engaging and loves asking questions.

I took HIST261 and AMCULT373 with Professor Mora. The lectures are captivating! He obviously cares a lot about what he teaches. His tests are no joke, if you are not paying attention during lecture the test format is not forgiving, however, I would say the information asked is fair. TAKE DETAILED NOTES, they will be your study guide!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mora is old school. No devices allowed and doesn't post lectures. That being said, if you're engaged with course material and care about the subject, you will get more out of a class with Mora than most professors and receiving an A is definitely attainable.

Through my 3 years of college, I have never experienced a professor like this. Mora expects you to memorize centuries of in-depth, nitpicky details of history. His teaching style is the reason I hated history in high school and thought I got away from it by coming to UM. Thinks he is funny when he is not. Worst professor ever. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've had Mora for History 261 and History 373. He really knows his stuff and is a great teacher and guy. I took 373 because, while I'm not interested in the class, he was teaching it. He's definitely one of the teachers that makes the class. There's lots of reading, and while it might seem like you don't have to do it, it WILL be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dense, dry material, but somewhat interesting. Very fact and memorization heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Mora is extremely interesting in his lectures, and he is a great person to talk to. He cares a great deal about getting to know his students, and invites them to office hours just for that purpose. I was disappointed, however, that he skimmed over some very important topics to make time for some cultural histories.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Super nice and funny professor. Not much guidance. Lectures are not mandatory, but you wont pass without them. Discussions are useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Mora's class because his lectures are very narrative and entertaining. If you don't have much experience picking important information out of a lecture you might struggle to take notes. Don't expect exam prep help. I left the class with a greater grasp of the history of the U.S. and I strongly recommend the course and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are rambling stories that aren't in order most of the time. 100 pages of reading/ week. Exam is ridiculous. No study guide but ALL terms and lectures from the entire semester (3hours of detailed lecturing/week) or from any of the 7 200 pages books assigned. Now take all that x2 for the cumulative final. Do not take.

Anthony is a great lecturer and manages to make an already interesting topic even more exciting. You will learn a great deal from his class, but you'll have to work. There are many long readings but they are all well chosen and extremely informative. He is very invested in the success of his students and encourages everyone to come to office hours.

I liked Prof. Mora. He was very thorough in his lectures and posted an outline of every topic that would be discussed that day. Lectures fly by. There is A LOT of information so be sure to try write down everything he says, even the smallest details are fair game on the exams. Also the GSI's can be very nitpicky so follow syllabus closely.

Professor Mora is a good lecturer but you will have to pay attention. The reading load can be a bit high and the weekly one-page reading responses can be annoying but overall, I'd say this was a good class. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Lectures contained a ton of really interesting info. Even though the power points weren't elaborate, note taking wasn't bad at all. As long as you can listen/take notes at the same time, you'll do great. The point worth of assignments was a little questionable but the quizzes were super easy.There's A TON of reading.

We had the Understanding Race and Ethnicity semester and that took away from the actual history learned in this class. I doubt he teaches any more U.S. History classes like this because he's not as knowledgable about the history itself as he is about the race and ethnicity themes. He didn't seem interested. Don't take 261 with him, only got to 1975

most boring class I have ever taken. His power points are black and white and have 2 slides per lecture. Very monotonous and doesn't seem to care about what he's teaching. He is so boring, avoid at all costs.

Sex and Sexuality was an extremely interesting class. Learned a ton of new stuff in a subject I thought I already knew a lot about. Theres a lot of reading, and a 1-2 pg paper over it every week which can be very time consuming. There is also a midterm and final paper but they weren't graded too difficult. Recommend if you like the subject matter!!

The class is very easy, 10 2 page papers, 2 stupidly easy MC tests, and a leniently graded group project. Reading is pretty average. But he is an awful lecturer. He was bitter and cynical, and seemed to believe that any history that didn't revolve around minorities wasn't worth teaching. He also got pretty basic facts wrong more than once. Avoid!

The course was dull. Readings for this class were heavier than two of my other classes combined, and weekly summary papers are due on them (and are useless). Readings are rarely discussed in class, though. However, there are no exams, and the papers are relatively straightforward. Class is certainly mandatory. Film lab is amusing.

This class is terribly boring. Mora sounds like hes repeating facts he worked hard to memorize the night before. Some of the guest lecturers were great, while others were a complete waste of time. He takes attendence and thinks hes funny, when hes not.

I took Sex and Sexuality with him and I loved it. His lectures are straightforward, the class is well run and he follows the syllabus to a tee. The topics are interesting and the movies are basically good. Mora is nice and approachable. There is a lot of reading but most of it is skim-able.

Do not take this class or this professor. EVER. I wish someone would have told me this before I took it. Class is based on SEVERAL guest lecturers who come in and talk about whatever they want. No continuity. No review before tests. It's not a 'culture' class, it's a history class. A bad one.

Not only is the most unentertaining man of all time, he thinks that he is funny when he is not. He knowledgeable about history, many of the facts prove to be irrelevant. If you like history, he might be ok.

Lecture was three hours and painfully dull. He only spoke on his point of view and was condescending most of the time. Worst was the reading - useless, boring, and tons of it. Not a HORRIBLE class, but could have been a lot better.

The freshman seminar I took with him was cool. His subjects are really interesting, and his office hours were incredibly useful. It was mostly lecture though, and the readings were VERY important. (history compilations :( ) It was a little bit hard to keep up with but that might have been my course load.  All in all: cool guy interesting class.

He is a great teacher. I wish I could take his class a million times; he is the best teacher I have ever had. Funny and helpful. He can put you on the spot at first, but once you get used to it, it is fun to participate, and nobody cares if you make mistakes. makes the learning environment very fun and is the most hilarious person I have ever met.

Easy class, workload is manageable. He reviews for exams in class. Most of class is speaking exercises, so you get a lot of practice with the language. He is a very fair grader, and tends to be very gracious when grading written and oral exams. Took him for two semester.
He's only nice if he likes you.
Loved him so funny and I have learned so much italian. Best teacher I have had at Umich by far

Hilarious and made learning a new language, which is so difficult, a lot of fun. He grades very fairly especially considering how common it was for students to make mistakes when reading/writing/speaking in a brand new language. If you have the choice to take Italian with any prof, it should be him, hands down the best prof I've had at all of UMich

Loved Gu - he genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material. He will take extra time to help you if you put in the effort. He is also so funny and makes class go by quickly! Great Italian prof, and you will learn so much.

Gugu is such a great guy. Absolutely hilarious, he makes learning fun. I wouldn't say he is the best at teaching Italian, his English is pretty broken. If you are just looking to complete your language requirement and aren't super adamant about learning Italian, Gugu is the guy for you.

Do the homework, pay attention, answer questions and you'll be fine. It'll be clear if you don't, but the class is easy so dw. Gugu will get peeved if you don't do the hw. Still he is absolutely hilarious and most of my classmates are trying to get him for 102 next semester because we can't imagine italian without this man. Gugu is the goat.
gives a lot of free absences, Just do the easy work and you'll get a good grade. fun chill class enviornemnt, doesnt really care if your late. not great english but managable. would recomend

Gugu is amazing. I was intimidated by taking a language course but he made it enjoyable and fun. Lectures can be disorganized, but do the homework, read the book, and use YouTube (it's your BFF). Once you know his class structure and what he expects, it's an easy class and makes Italian fun. Buy a grammar book from Amazon though for extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you struggle with language in general do not take with him. He is a funny guy and if he likes you will definitely help out a lot. He doesn't really explain things and has difficulty understanding English. If you have questions, Id ask other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Take it P/F, I'm gonna get a B of some form, but, by taking this class P/F I never had a problem. P/F makes this class honestly pretty chill, never have been scared for my grade. Gugu himself, he's just a fun guy. If you like a sarcastic, funny guy, you'll like him and he'll like you. Can't take a joke, don't take this class with him. Seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gugu is my favorite professor I had a Michigan. Makes italian enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Gugu is hilarious, he will pretend to get offended if you get something wrong or if you don't know an answer, but he means well. He does have a thick accent and is kind of hard to understand, but you'll catch on. I had a lot of fun in the class and always got good grades. Just do the homework and learn how to pronounce things correctly.

If you've never taken a language before, you will struggle with gugu. He doesn't explain grammar and expects you to be an expert on the sections we are studying. His english is also really bad so he can't explain anything. Coming from a background in Spanish the class was really easy and I think as long as you do the homework, you'll be fine.

definitely take Gugu if you want to learn Italian but most importantly want to have fun! Class is mostly just talking in Italian with prompts, and I find this extremely more useful than language teachers that just reiterate the textbook almost like a math class. Gu is absolutely hilarious and does not pick favorites like some of these reviews say

Gugu is an amazing teacher! I had him for both Italian 231 and 232. Italian is a difficult language, but he does an amazing job teaching. He also has lots of office hours and enjoys chatting with students outside of class. His lectures are also hilarious, and he makes participating easy. I'm so glad I had him as a teacher! -Marielle

He is the best. Great best friend, always has suggestions to jump out the window. Tough, T-O-U-G-H grader. That il supposed to be la? 3 points off. Misspelled the word? kiss that A goodbye. Overall GUGU is hilarious and you will laugh and have fun in class but you must work hard to get a B . Also he will attack you with italian outside of class.

All the italian professors are generally easy-going, and Gugu fits right in. It was a fun class to be in. I can see how he would be a poor professor for someone who has to put in a lot of effort to learn, but I found no problems with him personally.

Very funny professor. The class is fairly easy as long as you take/study notes.  He highly encourages vocal practice which is great.  The only problem I had was that half the time, I couldn't even understand what he was saying.  His accent is just thick enough to where you have to really pay attention to what he means, or else you will get lost.
Gugu is a boss!

He is a great teacher. Gugu taught the material in a way that was easy to follow. If there is anything you want to improve on, he'll give you suggestions of what to practice. Office hours were helpful. Homework & tests were reasonable. If you put the effort in & stay on top of the material, you can do really well in this class.

Yes, gugu is hilarious. Is he a good teacher? no. He is not. He will get mad at you when you dont know the answer to a concept he taught just one second beforehand. He grades the compositions on a bell curve also. It absolutely sucks to be in this class. there arent enough words to explain how much i wish i took another prof.

He is super funny. He sometimes does not understand you completely in english and he will respond to something completely different but its not too bad. Homework is assigned daily but is not collected (We go over it in class). If you don't turn in something on time he will not get mad and will let you turn it in a few days late.
Super FUNNY!

Gugu is great.  He's funny, he keeps a lighthearted mood flowing throughout class, and he doesn't get mad if you're late or if you didn't finish your homework. No, he doesn't speak fluent english, but his use of Italian forces you to learn! I love him, and I look forward to his class! Highly recommended.
class with Prof gugu was great... he was very funny and laid back but taught us a lot at the same time.  i highly recommend taking language with him

Gugu makes extremely inappropriate jokes and frequently insults women, but you just have to laugh it off and roll with it. If you can do that, you'll like him. Homework is easy. You never really know what he's correcting you on, he barely speaks english, and he can't understand your questions, but he does do the best he can to teach you

Gugu is very entertaining.  As long as you participate and joke around with him, you will be on his good side.  He is very lenient with homework, but make sure you have some of the answers filled in.  I've had him for two semesters, and if you have a good attitude, you'll have fun in class with him.

Gugu is hilariously sweet, he wears awesome pants, but he's definitely not the MOST amazing teacher. He will either make you love or hate the class depending on if you're on his good side. Homework is graded pretty easily, you don't even have to do all of it. Overall not a bad class though

I absolutely love Gugu. He is a great professor and very entertaining. If you get on his good side he'll give you good grades. For having the class 4 times a week, it was never a huge burden to go. He's the best. I took him for 101 and 102 because he is awesome.

Poor and old fashioned teaching methodology, rather repetitive, sometimes his comments can be sarcastic and even (involuntarily, I think)offensive. He maybe funny and hilarious, but there are much better Italian teachers around.

Gugu is insane. I'm nearly positive he was randomly picked up in Italy somewhere and flown to U of M to teach. He's very chill, and a pretty awesome teacher. Sometimes he would grade random things really harshly, but overall he's a good guy. If you happen to smoke then he'll love you even more.
Gugu is really really guido. He's a chill guy, good teacher, and very knowledgeable on Italian culture.
gugu is hilarious. he makes class a lot of fun with his crazy antics.
highly intriguing teacher yet educational value was sub par.
Hard to understand him because his english isn't that great. Was a bit harsh when it came to grading temas. Okay teacher, but there are def professors better than him.

Really nice, but his accent makes it hard to understand when you are saying things right or wrong.  He skipped over a few things that were necessary for 102.  Overall he is such a crazy character and so funny that it's worth it. Do participate bc he makes it seem like it won't matter but then it does.
Gugu 's so sexy...! When he speaks I don't understand him because I'm in paradise. Gugu I LOVE YOUUUU! Kisssss
Gugu is really funny and makes class fun, but he's not the best teacher in the world.... but I love him anyway.
when Gugu speaks students melt! We all love the accent

Gugu is pretty funny, he does hilarious impressions of his american students, but I don't think he knows english that well which makes communicating really difficult. And he sometimes just talks way to fast.
Gugi is hard to understand, sometimes funny but not too great at teaching overall.
No Comments
Gugu is a great (and hilarious) teacher.  Sometimes, he'll help you on the quizzes and tests.
Off-beat, pretty funny, needs to take more showers.  But good class!
No Comments
No Comments
AA has the best lectures.

Prof Achilleas has PHENOMENAL lectures, and you can grasp most of the curriculum from just attending lecture. However, his exams are a little on the harder side, but the class curve is ultra generous!

He had very clear lectures and explained the background behind everything very well. I felt able to follow along, and the homework assignments were a bit tedious but really prepared us for the exams. As for the exams themselves, I didn't love the all or nothing multiple choice(the questions were very tricky). Honestly learned a lot though.

Not really a big fan of his lectures, hard to read his Microsoft OneNote writing. His IA notes did clutch up for studying though. I'd give a higher rating if the exams aren't half MCQs with no partial credit, but at least he curves the grading scale generously.
Very smart and intelligent professor, I found his lectures very interesting and compelling

He can be a bit curt at times, but he is really good at explaining the WHY behind everything. He is very good at explaining things in a way that students can actually understand. I actually had a different professor, but I would just watch Achilles's lecture recordings because he was that much better.
Achilleas is amazing! His lectures are very clear and as long as you pay attention you won't be surprised by anything on the exams. His personality makes it easy to stay engaged.
I would totally and absolutely avoid him for research. He is gaming the system and I don't want to be a victim and enabler of such a system...
Ummmm ummmm. Lectures weren't too bad for me but he gives me super nars vibes
LOVED his lectures !!!!

Seems to have a very bad rep from PhDs he advises, but as an undergrad professor, he was awesome. 

The lectures are comprehensive and funny, but the notes are a bit lacking. Watch/go to lecture and you will be fine. Exams are fair, all the problems are similar to homework/class, no tricks.

Class has a textbook but you can easily ignore it.

I agree. He is a great instructor who really makes sure his students learn and his lectures are so amazing. I think previous bad reviews could be about him as a research guide and are definitely not true for him as an instructor.

So far he is the best lecturer in the EECS departement. I don't know about his bad reputations in the previous reviews, but for me I felt he really wants students learn. Rather than just giving out the answers in the office hours, he directs students to the right answer. His manner might first seem humiliative, but you just need to get used to it.
A passionate professor that cares about about your learning

Professor Anastasopoulos is my favorite college professor I've ever had. He is the type of professor who wants to help you truly understand the material. If you ask him a question he will always try his best to understand it and answer it thoroughly instead of just saying "you don't have to worry about that; it won't be on the test".
Fraud guy
Don't write useless papers for him that have no meaning
Don't know about his research stuff, but he is really good as an instructor. HWs and exams are hard though.
Excellent lecturer. Opa!!

Prof Achilleas is an amazing instructor. It is very clear he understands the material and ask questions during the lectures to make sure students are following. HWs are long and heavy but closely follow the lectures. One of the best courses I have taken so far.
Due to his poor guidance, his students don't go anywhere. Avoid if you want to make something of your own life and want a better future

It's not an easy class, but listening to his lectures you get the feeling he deeply understands and cares about everything he's teaching. Though they're fast-paced, they're also highly engaging. I disagree with the people saying he makes you feel dumb for asking questions. I asked plenty of questions and he always gave good answers.

Its not that he is not competitive and doesnt know it or is trying his best to be there. He very well knows it, knows the system and doesnt care as he has an endless supply of top students coming over all the time. It doesnt matter to him to be competitive. He doesnt have to put in effort. Its given free to him. It is made possible by the students
In today's competitive world there is absolutely no future with him. Don't waste your time with him.

I think people are getting in not knowing what's out there how to maneuver their lives to the right place or what is even the right place for them and literally everyone is wasting their 20s thinking about and doing stupid stuff realizing later that it wasn't worth it.
But definitely stay away from him. I never had any personal experience with him but I have heard he is too over bearing and like the reviews below say he is just gaming the system.

I think you chose the wrong advisor and had a bad experience (and I don't blame you, most people's experience is like that) but trust me my friend there are some good professors out there. The whole world is not that bad. The key is to find an advisor whom you can trust, who has integrity and who is genuinely doing good work because they love it.
Super Exploitative!

Life is rare in this universe. Value your life and your time and only work with people who are worth investing your time and your life in, who add meaning and value to you and take your life forward. Stay away from people who want to fool you and use you to advance their agendas.
He is the kind of guy who will milk you for his gain as much as he can while fully knowing that it is not in your self interest to work for him, and then let you go while he finds the next victims

So many comments have already said it multiple times that he is a non serious guy in research who isn't doing anything fabulous by any means and is mainly enjoying his life. idk what's the point of anybody sticking with him and doing research. He is a good instructor (imo) and people should enjoy his courses
work for him only if you want to be exploited and scarred for the rest of your life
Don't waste a single day of your life around him. Value your life and stay away
I agree that he really seems to have some issues and if you work with him you might inherit those issues. Better to stay away

tbh i think the whole academia is pretty fake: everybody is hiring students to write papers that nobody reads, on topics that aren't necessarily aligned with the student's interests, just to get grants and put it on the website. seems like a pretty fake business to me

Hey guys, for the love of your own life, pleaaaase do not trust this guy. Just go and work with any other prof, there are sooo many good ones around. He has some serious issues and he is just faking things to exist in academia at students' cost and you will just end up psychologically hurting urself and ur career/life.

I feel it is such a nice thing to review profs here for their research/phd guidance (in the same way they ask for our reccos). If everyone starts doing this, it will be so much good for the students and science in general, and will also provide incentive for these profs to not cheat.

Any PhD student who realizes that he/she is writing bad papers should stop right then and there, get a job, sort things out and work with a better person who is indeed doing good work. its quite well known that profs write bad papers as it doesn't affect them but the only loser in this process is the student. Why unnecessarily suffer in your life?

While I think he is a good instructor (even though he does come off as condescending) my sincere advice is to avoid him, he is absolutely not worth your time, forget 5 crucial years of your life. There are many good profs in other universities who are doing good work and with whom you can learn a lot, and who provide healthy environment to learn

I think it is very imp for potential PhD students to do their HW properly before deciding on an advisor. There are so many bad fish in academia including him that specifically thrive on the inexperience and stupidity of students.

Achilleas really knows the course content well, but in order to do well, office hours are mandatory. 50+% of learning comes from office hours as class time is mainly to give info for office hours to cover. Questions are encouraged, but he can come across as derogatory while answering if it is about something he thinks he covered clearly.
Avoid. Doesn't really answer questions. Try his best to make you feel stupid.

He has a permanent position so he hardly cares about the problems he is working on. But his students spend 5 crucial years of their lives thinking about useless stuff and in the process hurting their careers and chances of going anywhere else. This level of exploitation of naivety of students is very sad.

He knows he is working on bad problems, he knows his students never go to any good places, he knows it is useless to work with him. But this is his way to survive in the world by faking and exploiting people as by the time you will know, it will be too late and he has endless supply of people to exploit.

My problem with him is that he knows the model perfectly. He knows there are many very talented people from Iran, India, China etc who want to come to US, who don't know much how academia works. If you naively join him, he will make you work on stupid problems and you will graduate with useless thesis. He is very conscious of this fact (1/2)
He is pretty fake. He knows he is exploiting students. But that is the only way he can survive in the system. Don't join him. You will only be a victim.

It makes no sense to work with him. 
In general, if you are a smart person, only work with people whose students have gone to good places in academia. Nobody's students in this department has. No point in wasting time.

It seems to me they are playing games with us. They know we don't know what are good problems, how research is done and how academia works so they wont put much effort & will basically make us write useless papers and get us a phony degree while pretending to the world we are doing research. Sounds like a fraud system to me. why r people doing phd?

I wonder why a reputed University like UM has profs like this? Why play with students' lives and careers? I am considering doing PhD but this whole business sounds super scary to me. It's super tricky to figure out which Prof is good and treats their students fairly and their students have a future.
I think he just comes off as this super over bearing person. Would be hard to have him as your boss

He is working on bad problems and he doesn't care. He is gaming the system and wants to enjoy life. I think it's just plain stupid and waste of time to work with him. You won't get anything and just waste 5 years.

He is a chill guy. Doesn't bother you too much but also doesn't teach you much. He is enjoying his life. If you want to get green card in US using PhD or get a sub mediocre PhD and go to industry he is an apt guy.

Choose a research guide someone whom you can trust someone who has your back someone who is actually going to guide you and has your best interest in mind. He is not that person. He is just a selfish guy who only cares about himself. He won't help you at all. As many people have said below try to stay away from him

If you want to spend 5 years thinking about something that doesn't matter but only because he can enjoy his tenured life and put out those publications to get more grants to repeat the process with other people, you should join him.

I think he has tenure so he doesn't care what problems he works on or pretty much anything else. But as a student you won't learn anything or do any meaningful research. It makes zero sense to work with him.

His research is dry af. Sooooo many equations without any meaning or intuition. He spends insane amount of time coding or thinking about trivial details. Outside world is so competitive and people are going at speed of light and he is moving at turtles pace on stupid problems. No wonder his students don't get anywhere. Dont waste you life with him.

Very passionate and knowledgeable about his field, but can be condescending or occasionally forget that his students aren't up to his level of knowledge. Very hard homeworks, the exams are a breeze compared to them. You will definitely learn a lot from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He clearly understands the material and makes it somewhat clear in class, but the homeworks are so much more difficult than what is presented, going to office hours is a must. He will also slam dunk you if you ask a question he deems easily answered. Achilleas does eventually answer it, but not before he makes you look dumb.

He was very unhelpful in answering questions. Often roasts students with extremely blunt / rude comments about their general course knowledge if they cant answer the questions that he asks you when you are trying to get help. He is passionate about his material and does a decent job lecturing.

I took a research course with him and he turned out to be a bad research guide. He doesn't know much stuff and uses and exploits students to do the work for him, while he teaches you nothing. In research world, he is not considered of much significance and is mostly writing trivial papers for the sake of it. I think it is waste of time.

Achilleas teaches in a way where you'll have your mind blown in class with theory and walk out not understanding the hieroglyphics in your notes. HW and exams are insane with labs being the only relatively easy thing (tho even prelabs are ass). TBF, EECS 216 is very difficult and he teaches as best he can. He can be condescending with questions tho
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stay away!!!!!!!
Very selfish Guy. He uses students for his own gain. I would recommend to stay away at all costs.
Very difficult to ask basic questions and very difficult to get help with things. He asks for questions and then slam dunks on people if the questions aren't profound.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He comes off as this cool dude, but he is bad researcher. He hardly spends much time thinking about research, what are good problems, and most of his work is kinda shallow. He treats students as his minions, as if they are there do the dirty work, not as somebody whom he would like to teach. He doesn't have many new ideas and is just gaming system.
He just copy notes in the class. The class contents have not been reasonable assigned.

His lectures help you gain an intuitive understanding of the material - just be prepared to read the notes before you attend lecture as he can go fast sometimes. He really emphasizes important concepts and drills them into your head with mantras ('complex exponential in, complex exponential out...'). Exciting lectures and great office hours.

He uses Winicks HW and labs for this class. So expect to spend a lifetime doing HW (labs are pretty easy...). Tests are his own (not bad). He's a great professor though. You get copies of his lecture notes and he is always willing to help. I feel like he is, at times, unapproachable, but that's only when I feel like asking a dumb question.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is good for people who like theory heavy lectures but who can actually learn the application of the concepts/solving problems on their own. Homework overly difficult to downright confusing and doesn't help you understand the material, extensive office hours required. If you do not learn this way, too bad, so sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This guy is about as approachable as a starving crocodile. Comes across as incredibly cold and condescending. Probably the most stressful class i've taken at umich. Whatever you do, do NOT take a class with this professor

Very good at explain complicated concept, and has creative ideas. He wants students not only know what he taught in class, but the intuition behind, which mean you are highly likely to see something haven't been taught in exams. It's good, but a little bit difficult for us.

He is good at explaining the material, especially out of class. Will take the time to make sure you understand the concepts. Be ready to write quickly in class and then process the info later. His exams are pretty fair.

What a great professor! His lectures are intense but they keep you interested like no other teacher I've had at this university. You can tell he cares about the subject and understands it completely. He is also the best at responding to questions, you can tell he makes sure he understands them fully before responding. Would take any of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He writes and talks so fast and it's already difficult to merely copy what's on the board, no time to actually digest the material during the lecture. Be careful of what you ask if you have a weak heart because he always try to make you feel stupid.

Professor Anastasopoulos knows his stuff, and you can tell by the way he teaches. He teaches VERY theoretically, which it good for understanding the foundations of the material, but not so great for actually working through examples. Going to discussion sections was imperative for my success as we went through examples there.  Heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer and posts the notes online after class. He writes really quickly which can be difficult but is necessary since there is so much to cover. He is extremely helpful in office hours because he helps you think your way to the correct answer.

Achilleas (or AA if you prefer) was an amazing professor for 216. Puts a ton of energy into his lectures, enthusiastic about the class, very knowledgeable. Homework is tough, but fair. You really learn the material. 10/10 would take another class with him.

Liked to move at a fast pace during lectures. Board handwriting is terrible. Did not separate important material from long proofs that had little importance in the long run. Good intentions, but had mentality that it was always the student at fault for not understanding rather than him not explaining it well. Makes sporadically hilarious comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He verbally clear.  But his writing on the board is horrid.  Sometimes it's difficult his writing is so poor; it's time consuming to understand.  His midterms are frustrating.  You can study all the material as much as you want, but he'll found some other material that he "mentions" in class.  He doesn't accept any formulas derived outside of class

Anastasopoulos was a great professor for 216. Workload was very fair for the class (historically it can be extremely heavy). If you devote roughly 10 hours a week to this class outside of lecture, you should be fine. Labs are fun, although some prelabs may be tough. Exams may be a bit tricky at times but are very fair.
Really a great guy and a great teacher, I would take any other class offered by him.

He's truly kind and willing to help. But the homework assigned doesn't have much to do with what he taught in class, which needs us learn much more in spare time. And the tests are also of a totally different style with homework.

Prof. Anastasopoulos is one of the best professors I have had at Michigan.  The material can be difficult, but he explains everything in the clearest, most intuitive way possible. Just go to class, do all of the HWs, and DO EXTRA PRACTICE PROBLEMS FROM THE BOOK.  The class really is not that hard if you practice a lot.

I liked Prof. Anastasopoulos. EECS 401 is definitely a hard class and one of the many roadblocks in the BSEE degree. However, he explained complex topics in fluid ways, understanding that the concepts are hard to understand for students. He also held almost daily office hours, and even more near exams.

A great prof, very very understanding and always willing to help and start from scratch when explaining. Is equally patient in office hours as well. as for his greek accent, its not hard to understand at all, and is actually really cool! Cool prof, I would recommend 401 with him. The class can be hard though, so be prepared..
He is the most dynamic professor I've ever seen. Always explains things well, never hesitates to repeat, or start from scratch...very helpful, motivating and energetic.
Never think to take a class with him.
Really good professor....very clear in his ideas and extremely helpful. Has a practical outlook towards all problems. Also I love his Greek accent :)
he is good enough to the extent that you can't understand any thing.
He is goof, but some times he is so mean to students. he thinks himself very smart and every body else is not smart like him.some times, I don't understand what he is saying with his greek accent.
great professror! extremely helpful! knows his stuff inside out.
Bad Bad Badddddddddd
he is a great teacher. he was really very helpful and friendly. The class wasn't that easy but he always tries to clarify his ideas.
Great teacher.  The material was difficult, but he really tries hard to help out when necessary.  Also...he's awesome.
his lectures are interesting and he gives clear explanations during office hours too.
No Comments
very cool and friendly and always there to help.
No Comments

This course felt like primary school busywork. Assignments took more time than my other 15 credits combined but left me confused and irritated. The professor just says "read the slide," and labs are unfathomably disorganized for a top university—rubrics often reference non-existent content. A waste of tuition. Save yourself: take EECS 215.

This is the most poorly managed class ever. Assignments often have errors that require fixes. Ganago is a bad lecturer, often asking you the student to read the slides to yourself. That said, there's so much extra credit, you are almost guaranteed a good grade. As a CS FlexTech or for ME, I recommend the course, just expect busy work for days.

Overall, he seemed like a nice guy. However, the class is incredibly poorly organized. Almost every hw and post lab had errors in it which usually resulted in an email the morning the assignment is due to redo the calculations with a different set of lab values. Not sure how a class which has been around for a few decades  can have so many errors

Overall, the man is knowledgeable and should be respected. Its disappointing that there are people below hating on his character. The class has an incredible amount of homework and very disorganized, but because there is so much work, you learn the material easily. Do not take 215 tho, def much worse.

Literally not that bad. He is a very knowledgable man that has experience in industry. People here criticizing his character are just weird. The class itself is not that fun, but so is every single class at Umich.

I can't believe this man is real and is still employed. I think he's possessed by a circuit demon. Can barely teach and refuses to answer questions in lecture. I would still recommend taking 314 over 215 because it's a guaranteed A. Just be prepared to sacrifice your sanity for a good GPA boost
And on the 8th day God created Alexander Ganago, and it was not good.

People complain too much. It's a free A for a degree requirement class. Yes the lectures suck and the work can be a lot at times, but its not like the guy is a terrible person, he's just really old. What he teaches is definitely enough to get you by and it is DEFINITELY better than 215.

reviews.comment: Ganago is like if you take the worst possibly qualitiy a teacher can have in any aspect and combine it all into one person. The only downside is you are pretty much guaranteed an A. Honestly, I don't know how this guy is still teaching. The fact that the teaching department is ok with him still teaching makes me question the U of M faculty. 81% of students get an A. His lectures are boring and pointless and they way he organizes the class is all over the place, but I guess he accounts for that by making it extremely difficult not to get an A.

literally gives an ungodly amount of busy work and his lab manuals are all 30+ pages and half of it doesnnt make any sense. Probably one of the worst professors i have had in my life if not the worst

Chances are that you'll have minimum interaction with Ganago - lecture times were just his office hours and as someone said before, no one showed up to lecture after the first one. The class is quite easy but this prof was awful.

LOTS of HW and classtime, meh as a lecturer, but gives a LOT OF EXTRA CRED, easy HW and fair exams (exams aren't worth that much of final grade), thus an A+ is very DOABLE! gotta give the guy some leeway because his grading scheme is rather fair

reviews.comment: This man's lectures are absolutely useless because his slides and actual dialogue are so incoherent. It's made worse by the fact that he takes iClicker participation, so you'll have to waste your time bothering to show up. The class is all busy work.

Professor Ganago gets through content about as fast as Dragon Ball Z advances the plot. His lectures are sleeping inducing and teach you about no more than you could have learned from 5 minutes of reading from a good textbook, but the course uses Dr Ganagos textbook (which is aweful), so self teaching by reading the textbook isnt easy either.

The material covered in genuinely interesting, important, but not that difficult. The class however, is about 75% busy work. The material simply is not that hard to necessitate all that work to understand it. There is lecture i-clicker, online module homework, written homework, pre-lab, in-lab, and post-lab. Pros: Online Lecture Rec, and extra cr
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: EECS 314 is incredibly homework heavy. Class is easy though.

There are good professors, bad professors, and then there is Ganago. His lectures are weak and incoherent.  EECS 314 is a horrible waste of your time, money, credits, and energy. Do yourself a favor and try to register for 215. It lay be a little tougher, bu tat least you can walk away saying you learned something, unlike me.

He is a nice professor but this class is ridiculous. There is a bunch of busy work due every week but most of the material is stuff you don't cover in class so it is typically very frustrating. The class is easy to maintain an A in due to all the extra credit available but you don't get much more besides that out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ganago is literally the worst professor I've ever had. The only reason I went to lectures were for I clicker questions which were participation based. He likes to use stories  extensively however some of them contained very sexist language. Easy A if you do the homework though. If you don't understand him in lecture you won't understand his book

Not as bad as some people say. He's a nice guy, but his lectures can be long. Always has some story/analogy to tell which can be interesting at times and he really seems to care about his students. Tries to give real world examples/applications of class concepts. Textbook/lab manual can be too detailed, but he offers summary handouts for material.

Absolute worst professor I have ever had. Ganago is a raving lunatic. However, there is so much extra credit that if you don't get an A or A+ you are doing something wrong. I actually did work during the year so that I could have gotten a zero on the final and still gotten an A. There is iClicker during lecture which is the only reason anyone came.

Big work load but the material isn't difficult. A lot of extra credit opportunities so it is easy to get the grade you want. Lectures aren't really useful apart for the fact that he uses iClickers that count towards your grade. He tends to ramble a lot.

you won't learn much, but will get an A. So much extra credit is offered that if you don't get an A you really tried not to. Ganago genuinely cares that you learn, but does a bad job of showing it. He is a great guy and wants everyone to get an A, can't really talk bad about him. If you actually want to learn about circuits/more work, take 215.

Ganago's a nice guy, and he's a decent teacher.  The real issue is that he usually talks about stuff that's completely unrelated to what he was lecturing on five minutes prior. The homework takes like 3-4 hours a week, but it's usually on topics not covered in class.  That said, there's a lot of extra credit-the average grade was a 92 (an A).

I'm currently sitting in lecture wondering why I am here? They are completely useless. He doesn't respond to emails and he thinks he answers questions because he cuts off students mid sentence and then answers nothing related to the question. Nice guy, but useless. Everything is uploaded late. labs, hwk, prelabs, self assessments,etc so get excited

Take this class! It will definitely take some time out your week, but you'll get an A+ out of it! Take it with a friend because you do not want to be working on those assignments alone. Also, you need to be in class to use the i-clicker to show participation for the lecture. And expect to learn everything from the coursepack.

Ganago is a genuinely nice guy - he wants you to learn! But he does not teach well. The course pack is pretty much how you teach yourself this class. Be prepared for 10+ hoursweek doing reading, the homework, multiple test centers, a pre lab, a post lab, etc. Overall a horrible way to learn circuits, but it is pretty easy to do well.
All I can think about during lecture is "how is it possible that he still teaches at this institution?"  Lectures are horrid, assignments are never put up on time.
Awful

Pretty much the same feedback as everyone else in this class - Ganago is helpful, nice and he genuinely cares about his students, but he's long-winded, unclear, and boring. It's a struggle to sit through the 90-minute lecture, which is why most people don't. That said, this class is an easy A.

Ganago is that grandpa that wants to teach you but can't fully articulate a complete sentence anymore. He will email you 3-4 emails a day talking about his emails he sent you the day before. Lectures are useless unless you need to catch up on sleep. It's an easy A if you put in the work outside of class. He is a horrible professor, good luck

Everything you need is in the readings he posts. If you don't get an A or A+ in this class, someone should hit you on the head with a tack hammer. The homework and labs are extremely tedious and a waste of time, but are extremely easy.
Nice Class.Labs and homeworks were easy but tedious. Exams are  very similar to practice exams.
Office hours help a lot, if you can go to them. Very little help available outside of class. Utilize surveys and demand that he teach you the homework

Nice old man who cares a lot about his students but is completely out of touch with them.  Don't go to class, just read the handouts online and turn the homework early for extra credit and you'll do fine.  Labs are a little long but not hard, and exam questions are multiple choice versions of past hw.  Easy A if you play by his rules.

Fantastic professor, probably one of the best I've had at Michigan. His homework is time consuming, but he makes every effort to make sure you know how to do it, from posting lectures online to separately recording loads of supplementary material. Incredibly thorough (if a bit slow at times) and really takes survey comments to heart.

Didn't make great use of class time -- often wasted time on tangents and silly survey questions. Lectures were difficult to follow and there was no textbook to fall back on. Homework was time consuming, but the exams were easy. The class material was interesting.

I don't understand how Ganago still has a job.  He spends class time doing things like writing out powers of 2 all the way up to 2^20, while his exam "reviews" are usually around 2-5 minutes long.  The homework is insanely tedious; be prepared to spend 10+ hours a week doing it until enough people in your class complain to the department.

Completely useless.He took the time to read the box of an anti static mat down to the color options.The class feels like high school with worse teaching.Everything is a hand out.Download his book on rapidshare, he doesn't deserve the money.His lab book is awful too.Inconsistent page numbers and repeated pages.Without prior knowledge I'd fail.
A terrible, terrible professor/class. As an ME student, glad I got it out of the way early
he is the WORST professor i have had during my time at U of M. terrible professor: reads his own useless textbook during lecture and is not helpful during office hrs. avoid if possible

What a terrible professor.  All of the notes were extremely unorganized, I could never find an answer when I needed it. He was very unhelpful in office hours and pretty much spent the time ridiculing students for not understanding the material that he taught so poorly. Attendance dropped to about 1/3 towards the end of the semester.

Worst teacher I ever had. Knows his stuff, but cannot explain it for the life of him. Going to lecture is worthless. I learned everything in that class from my GSI and the textbook I bought on my own (do not buy his book). If you're an Aero or ME major and you have to take this class, then just make good friends with your GSI.

This prof sucks balls. His exam format sucks. His lectures are a waste of time. He is one of the most annoying people in class and outside. HIs Hw's are very annoying. May god be with you if you are in his class.

This is really a learn-it-yourself kind of class.  Ganago posts lecture notes on ctools that have all the equations you need to do the homework, so there is very little thinking involved.  A few of the homeworks took some thinking, but nothing compared to other eng. courses.  Don't buy the book...he posts everything in his book on ctools for free!!

He is pretty good actually as opposed to the comments out here. I just took his lab so I have no clue about his teaching. But he is very understanding as a lab instructor. I lost my lab data and he had no problem with that. He also remembered all the people's names in the class and is very friendly. He is picky at some little things though.

THE ABSOLUTE WORST:  verbally abusive & ****. Extremely arrogant:  he is not a professor, he is a LAB INSTRUCTOR. Grade improved when I started skipping class and hired a tutor, who in one hour/week, did a better job than GANAGO, who had 4hrs/wk. to teach.  Don't bother going to office hours, he'll treat you like an idiot and not even answer you!

To begin with, don't bother with buying the text-book, you won't use it.  The auxilliary text by the prof. is $82 and more useful.  Don't expect anything useful in lecture.  Spends 65/80 min. talking of useless things or general theory, and not useful examples or explanations.  Hard to follow in class.  He is also very rude outside of class.
ABUSIVE.  Currently trying to get my Sp05 grade removed from transcript due to his incompetence.  Not recommended as a candidate for continued employment at this University.
In Soviet Russia, courses fail you.

He has an annoying tendency to waste copious amounts of class time and then assign homework problems on all that stuff he was supposed to have covered.He's not helpful at all to talk to. His lack of clarity and complete unoproductivity in class makes this class very hard to do well in (the exams are 20 q's mult choice-bad format, no partial credit)

He spent 25 minutes talking about Ben Franklin during an exam review, later calling it "extensive" after doing 2 problems.  He canceled a homework problem, then 2 hours later re-assigned it.  His homeworks and labs never use consistent formatting, giving headaches when trying to read them.  He only tries to express things through complexity.

I don't know why people don't like Ganago.  He's made the material accessable in my class and puts forth incredible effort on behalf of the students.  Lecture notes uploaded to the web everyday.  He is responsive to my questions.  My class isn't for EECS majors, so maybe that makes a difference, but overall I definitely recommend him.
Taking now in Sp05. Terrible. Teaches nothing. To sum up: AVOID AT ALL COST!

Absolutely wretched professor. Always goes over the time limit, and usually what he says after I have to leave to catch my lab is the most important, if he says anything important at all.  Very rude to talk to.  Has no regard for your time- wastes it in lecture.  Labs are absolutely worthless. Enjoy

Ha Ha Ha, if you have him...good luck...he does not teach at all but will expect you to know everything. He give you HW on stuff he does not cover in lecture, actually he dosen't teach anthing in lecture. I learned everything by-mself. I'd take it with another prof. Good Luck

Professor Romero is not as bad as people make her out to be. She goes through her slides, and although her explanations are not the most detailed, she provides in-class examples to help students understand.

Take Keane because Romero is the textbook definition of average. Her lectures are hard to follow, and unless you have the motivation and time to teach yourself the material afterward, it's very easy to fall behind (especially if stats is not your strong suit). Do active approach and you'll get an A- at the very least.

Romero isn't a bad professor, though sometimes hard to follow, especially if you already struggle. However she is very open to questions, and there are lots of resources available if you fall behind. I recommend the active approach and using both extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Romero is an average lecturer, the material is not very difficult to understand. The main issue is that there's no consistent grading standards or expectations. Labs and case studies are often graded poorly and no actual feedback is given. Office hours and lab section are hit or miss. You'll survive this class, but it's structured poorly.

She is very nice, but is not clear at all. I did well in the class because I taught myself everything and went to office hours. Office hours are only GSI's btw and can get very busy. I personally did not like this class. Try to get Keane if you can.
She isn't clear. And you have to do a lot outside of class to get an A

She's very sweet but not very clear when lecturing. I probably wouldn't have survived the class without office hours and there, basically everyone I met was her student, not Keane's, which should tell you enough.

If you're taking this class with Romero, I recommend doing the Active Approach for Lab and if you're not a good test taker then Active for lecture, otherwise Traditional is good. She's very nice and is willing to help you with whatever you need!

I personally think it's pretty easy to follow along in class with the lecture notes provided in Canvas. The homework workload is decent, but the questions aren't hard and GSIs are always there to help during office hours. GO TO OFFICE HOURS

I really think Dr. Romero is a great professor, I don't understand why people say she's hard to follow. Just go to lecture, and I strongly recommend active approach for both lab and lecture. Traditional may seem appealing, but getting practice in class with the group work is totally worth it.
She's super sweet and a great professor. Don't understand why a lot of people don't like her.

I came into this class thinking that it wouldn't be too bad since I took AP Stats in high school. I was terribly wrong. Romero is nice, but isn't a great lecturer. If you have the chance, take Keane. If you take Romero, good luck.

This was my first time taking a Stats class in my entire life, and honestly, the content itself was easy to grasp, but she assumes everyone in the room has prior knowledge. After a few weeks, she toned it down and slowed to a much more manageable pace. She is very approachable, though, and going to office hours is SUPER helpful!

Lectures are very fast-paced, and some information is skipped over. She is very sweet, but her explanations are sometimes missing full thoughts. The active approach is definitely more helpful for those who are not good test takers, but it is more work.

While lectures were sometimes unclear and exams could be tricky, if you do the active approach for lecture and lab and do the extra credit opportunities you should be okay. I would still recommend taking Keane if you have the option though. If I was confused about a topic I would watch his lecture and I felt he explained topics more clearly.

She was extremely nice, however, her teaching style was very unorganized and would often skip slides and pages in the notes. The exams were very difficult imo and I studied quite a bit. The case studies were very tedious and graded very harsh, same with the written portions on the exams. Had to take this as a prerec and it was a struggle.

OVERHATED!!! She's a decent professor. If fast teaching is not your style, take Keane, but you also have access to both lectures. I recommend meeting with Romero 1-on-1 during her office hours because it's so helpful!! If you're not a good test taker, pleasee do active. Also, make sure to attend GSI office hours for HW help or anything :)

Romero is lowkey overhated. She did make a few conceptual mistakes when teaching lectures, but expressed most things clearly. You can decide if you want attendance, pre-lecture, and post-lecture work to count toward your grade. There are not a lot of study materials provided for the exams (you get 1 practice exam and a concept problem set).

never really got the chance to speak 1-on-1 with her since the class was so big, but the structure of her class was easy to follow. the homework assignments were really helpful, and if you chose the active approach you got a chance to do a mini-assignment at the end of each lecture, which I personally found very helpful

I heard horror stories about this class before taking it, but I thought Dr. Romero was great and she explained most concepts very well. If you lock in on the hw and case studies, clarify hard concepts with GSIs at office hrs, you will be fine. The exams were difficult at times but they reflected the concepts from the assignments.
Kind of bad at explaining certain concepts

idk why ppl hate, i had keane and i would watch her lectures since I thought she made it easier to digest, whoever u have for stats youll be fine. stats is an semi easy but boring subject, do active approach, and check hw and case study with others and youll get an A easily dw

I don't understand the Romero hate. She is a great lecturer, even though the content can be dull. She is very nice and engaging and always willing to help and answer questions. Office hours are completely done with GSIs, though, but they are still very helpful and knowledgeable! I would definitely not skip out on Romero for stats.

She is a decent professor, I think Keane is better at explaining but his lectures are posted on Canvas. She is very nice and funny, even changing one of the lectures to have all the answers and questions have "67" in it when she found out about the joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: romero is really sweet; not the greatest lecturer, but it doesn't matter as long as u clarify any questions with ur gsi. make sure to practice, UNDERSTAND the concepts behind everything, and memorize the format of any writing that u have to do. its a pretty easy course once you do those things.

While she is very kind, Romero simply doesn't explain any content. It feels like she is telling you information, rather than teaching. The curve is nice, but everything feels super confusing. Take the other professor if you can.

After failing two of the exams I learned that Romero is the worst STATS professor bc she is horrible at explaining- started watching the other professor's lecture recordings and I'm doing so much better now
Also I'm supposed to get extended deadlines for accommodations and she outright said she won't offer them (which i found out was not okay)

Honestly, my rating is more about Stats 250 than Romero because I don't know the other stats professors. The class is just confusing and difficult for no reason. Homework is long, tests are difficult, and grades aren't curved. My best advice is go to office hours (!!!!!!!!!!), do the work, and pray to whoever/whatever you believe in.

Prof. Romero is an okay teacher. Her lectures are a little confusing, and she doesn't really explain things she just talks at you. Take Keane if you can. The class feels more like I'm being told a lot of things and not taught anything. Pretty good curve in the class.
Romero is clearly a nice person and likes the subject, but her lectures are just not good. You'll have a way easier time watching Keane's lectures.

Romero is super kind and has a lot of enthusiasm to bring to lectures. I think the material can feel a little rushed and sometimes her way of explaining things weren't the easiest to understand. Watching the online lectures from the other professor helps supplement. I would recommend the active approach, and either way the course curve is generous.

This course is pretty complicated. The answers that they are looking for are very specific, and the tests aren't relevant to the lectures. If you do the active approach, the tests are worth less and you have more assignments which helps. Overall, she doesn't explain stuff well but the class is manageable.

Romero came to every lecture with enthusiasm, but she sucks. She is very sweet but her lectures are extremely confusing and fast paced. You have the option to print/edit notes online. If you dont have a ipad, you must get a spiral notebook!! If you are a freshman, please dont take it now, wait until you get a better professor please. TRUST ME

Romero is better for students who already have a grasp on the material. She moves quickly, which can be overwhelming to students who are newer to stats. I took the active approach for lecture and lab, and I highly recommend it if you are not a good test taker. Romero does move quickly, but is always kind and respectful to students.

I was so nervous to take this class after seeing these reviews, but prof. Romero is great! Stats 250 can be hard; you have to go to class, pay attention, and put time in studying to be successful, but Romero is way over-hated. She always explains concepts in multiple ways, she's accessible outside of class, and her expectations are very clear.
ANGELIC DEVIL

I took the active learning version of this class, lectures were ok but GSIs were often better at answering questions clearly. Attending office hours regularly to get questions from homework and labs answered is a must!
The devil.

Overall she gives decent lectures, but I had to go to office hours at least once a week to really understand the material. The GSIs were super helpful and always eager to answer questions! I recommend doing the active learning style, it really gives your grade a boost and holds you accountable for learning the material.

Romero is very overhated for some reason. Her lectures are really captivating, and she's very accessible for help during and after the lectures. The class itself is well-organized, and it's very clear how the projects/exams are graded and what you need to study to do well. I loved this class and would take it again.
Sweet but unclear in lecture

for 1/2 of the semester i watched keane and for the second half i attended romeros lectures, theres literally no difference between the 2 so i dont get the low rating. there was a only handful of times where i felt like romero didnt explain a concept well--coming from someone who has never really excelled in math. gsi hw grading can be annoying tho

I honestly don't understand why she has such a low rating. The biggest issue with this class is not the professor but the graders. Some graders can be harsh, while some are very lenient, making it unfair. I even watched all of John's lectures, and Romero explains topics differently from John, but it's not that bad. She's not bad, the course is.
She is very nice, but she does not explain the content clearly. Also, everything in this class is graded by GSI's. Some GSI's mark answers wrong that another GSI would mark correct.

Dr. Romero is super sweet but this class's grading scheme is super messed up. Atlas will tell you the median is an A but DO NOT LISTEN to Atlas. The canvas final grade says the average is a Low B to high B-, and that's just the average. Try to avoid this class and attend GSI hours regularly.

The grading system for this class is terrible. You cannot afford to do bad on the exams or case studies or else it will ruin your entire expected grade for the semester. Extra credit opportunities barely boost grades and exam review material does not mirror actual exam questions. No leniency with grades. Would not recommend.

Sweet person, not a great teacher. Doesn't really explain things well but she's not horrible, if you're really confused would recommend watching keanes lecture. Overall not great but not horrible, if you get her you'll be fine. Homework is not too bad, GSIs in office hours help A LOT. saved my grade.
She's really not good at teaching. If you're in her section, I recommend watching Jack's recorded lectures or attending his lectures instead.

Dr.Romero is a very sweet person, but her lectures are not very good. Exams are a little tough but the GSIs grading can be even tougher. Stats honestly is not that hard especially as an intro course, but her explanations/lectures made it harder than it had to be.

I honestly don't have any complaints about Dr. Romero! I learned a lot about statistics and she always taught us with passion and a smile on her face. There is lots of homework, but if you do the work you will succeed! Give her a shot!
She skips a lot of the course pack and doesn't explain thoroughly, if an option take with Keane.

Romero is very nice, but moves really fast and doesn't cover basic concepts. I had never taken a stats class before taking 250, and I was always confused about the simple base parts of more complicated problems. I suggest watching Keane's lectures on Canvas if you're in the same position.
Class material was not hard to understand but Romero was very unhelpful and unhelpful with any issues with grading
Professor Romero is sweet, but her lectures move too fast and her grading can be harsh. I found unstuck AI helpful for study prep, alongside the textbook.

She moves through the content really quickly, but as long as you review outside of class you should do fine. You could take the traditional or active approach, but the only difference is that active requires lecture attendance and traditional doesn't.

Contrary to what I've heard from others, I had very little issue with Romero as a professor. My only complaint is that she told us we needed to use the course pack for lecture and sometimes wouldn't follow it. Some watch the other professors lectures, but I never found that necessary. Do the active approach + go to office hours and you will do fine

Romero's teaching style overcomplicated concepts. I would end up watching Keane's lectures as he made the content much more digestable. If you end up being placed in Romero's class and have no stats experience, consider doing active learning for lectures as that will cushion your grade. If you have the option, just go with Keane.

Dont take her, take it with John Keane, would just watch his lectures online, he actually explained info, 10x better dont make the same mistake I did... Also her lectures suck, she just yaps and yaps and doesnt explain anything

Her teaching style makes content really hard to grasp, even if you've taken stats before. Keane explains things a lot better, so if you have a choice take his lecture. For the class, case studies are graded so harshly and weigh so much for no reason. The exams can also be pretty bad if you don't understand the content, but hw & group work is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Romero was kind and there to help when I was confused. However, this course was incredibly difficult for me. The material was mainly to blame, but Romero's teaching style didn't benefit me either. Lectures move fast since there is so much material. Have your phone out for photos, and go to office hours early in the week because it gets so busy.
