reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There's a clear discrepancy between Alicia Romero and John Keane's classes. Keane's students tend to grasp the material better, while Romero's teaching felt scattered and ineffective, leaving me feeling I gained little despite taking an active approach. She is very nice and approachable, but her teaching style itself was not very effective.

Definitely not my favorite class, the lectures felt very rushed and it was honestly really hard to follow what she was saying. I opted for an active approach to the class, meaning I had to show up every day and do homework before every lecture, but I think it helped overall. Honestly wouldn't recommend, but it is definitely doable if you have to.
I don't recommend this professor if you don't already know statistics, the lectures are very messy and rarely follow the textbook. Don't buy the textbook use the slides.

She's actually the worst. Her lectures make no sense and don't even bother trying to go to office hours because there are a million people there at all times and only a maximum of 3 gsi's. Romero's lectures were always super hard to follow, I was always confused on what she was talking about, and they didn't help me learn the material for the exams
Do not take Alicia Romero. 100% take the other professor John Keane, there is a reason that only his lectures are recorded...

Romero explained things moderately-well but would often not finish several of the note-taking sections, making interpreting certain statistic values later on difficult. I would have to watch the other section's lectures to have concepts explained.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Romero was very kind & clearly passionate about Statistics. Even early in the morning, she was still super cheerful & did her best to engage students. I don't love the subject, but her as the lecturer was nice. There are some notes she makes during lecture that are SUPER helpful for understanding the content--she knows her stuff!

The labs, case studies, and homework are not that bad. The only problem was that the lectures were somewhat vague, and did not explain concepts thoroughly. I would often times watch Professor Keane's recorded lectures. Overall, not too bad but just more explanation. But there are a lot of extra credit opportunities
she doesn't explain things very clearly, as someone who watched a lecture from the other professor (keane?), he explains concepts a lot better. homework every week and the exams are very tricky

Do not take her, please for your own sanity. She doesn't explain anything yet every 20 seconds she asks us to "try it out." Take the class with John and build your schedule around it. I'm sure she's a nice lady but respectfully she's a horrible lecturer

Romero isn't bad, but she doesn't give much time in class for us to try things on our own. She instead will introduce material and expect us to know how to apply it. Also VERY GSI heavy class. As my gSI was a much tougher grader than many of my other friends, so it helps a lot if you get a lenient one.

I realized later in the semester that just watching Dr. Keane's recordings is better than going to Dr. Romero's lectures because she doesn't explain things very well and moves very fast. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities, and it's pretty easy to get an A from the number of assignments and drop policies.
she goes way too fast. office hours are always packed, and they are VERY harsh graders.

The class is not bad. The lecture work, hw, and labs are simple and can be easily completed. However, Prof Romero is definitely not my favorite lecturer. I wish she'd just stop asking us to try out problems every other minute without ever thoroughly teaching us how to do them. I am sure she is a kind person but pls make ur class make sense...
Very kind and responsive inside and out of lecture. She is a rambler, her lectures do not make any sense, ended up having to go to a different lecturer.

I took this course for credit that was needed, but for a 4 credit course, I felt like the work was too much to begin with. Alicia seems like such a nice lady, however, her lecture style does not match mine. She seems to go by so fast, and doesn't explain very well about the concepts of the topic we're on. The GSIs are such a harsh grader too.

She was an extremely fast lecturer and would fly through the slides, constantly jumping back and forth to give different examples that had no relation. The class itself is very easy. If you come in with some stats knowledge you will be fine, but if you come in having never taken a stats class I would suggest the other professor.

I feel super conflicted about giving her this low rating because she seems like a super nice lady. However, as a professor, she is super hard to understand. The grading by the GSIs is super harsh. Overall, I kinda wish I had taken this course with a different prof even though she seemed so sweet

She doesn't speak clearly about the material and always rushed through the slides. I gained zero understanding at the end of the term and I'm about to fail the final tomorrow. The instructional team can't take criticism; they defend their position expecting students to have "empathy" to hear their side instead of actually taking feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought lectures were clear, and Professor Romero was always willing to take questions and help. If you're in CSP, I recommend taking her lab because it is very beneficial! Other than that, just ask questions if something is confusing.

Romero goes very fast in lectures, and makes things sound a lot more complicated than they need to be! Halfway through the semester I found myself watching the Keene's lectures, because he made things easier to understand. I wouldn't say that this class is hard, but I feel like Romero makes it harder than it should be.

Hands down one of the worst professors I have ever had. I had to submit an assignment late due to medical reasons and she never responded to my emails, the GSI's had no clue what they were doing. Genuinely the worst decision I ever made to take this class. Absolutely nothing is clear and her lectures were useless. Just simply don't take Stats 250.
I'm not a fan

not the best lecturer so I watch the other prof. However biggest problem w the class is how it's run. Grading is nit-picky piazza often ignored GSIs for office hours are bad. Practice exam supposed to be up 7+ days b4 exam, but wasn't uploaded until 4 days b4. after the Mon evening exam, MWrite was due Thurs. they act like this class is ur only one

Alicia Romero is very amicable and joyful as a person but horrible as a lecturer. She doesn't respond to emails, she doesn't give clear explanations of any of the content that is necessary for anything in the class. A lot of the time she goes along the lines of saying "This is this because it just is". 3/10, I highly recommend John Keane instead.

If you're taking her, select the active participation chocie of the lecture when they ask you between the choices of standard lecture format and this one. This is the only way to survive her lectures; she goes way too fast and I can't comprehend any of it. Doing the active learning helped me bc that's the only way I can comprehend her lectures.

Overall, Professor Romero was good, however, one think I didn't like was how she kept her slide annotations from her 8am class while lecturing. This made it harder to write notes, as she'll just pass it quickly. Also, it was pretty hard to get in touch through email. Overall, the course isn't bad at all, but make sure you take it with some friends.

This class is not hard if you have half a work ethic. Lectures aren't that clear but I wouldn't say the work is terribly hard. I never went to lab and got 100% on every lab assignment. Easy enough but pretty boring and dull.

Homeworks are long and confusing I found the wording choices to be quite poor and the grading for them is unfairly harsh. The professor nitpicked my vocabulary when I asked for help, which was frustrating, and the larger assignments had little explanation of success.

she is a nice and understanding lady. she can be very unclear in lecture, isn't super helpful at explaining concepts. Mwrites were annoying and grading guidelines were extremely unclear. Pretty easy class overall with extra credit opportunities.
Did not describe things clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I ended up just watching the lecture recordings of the other professor because he explained everything much more clearly. She was nice but just didn't explain things well in my opinion.

Do not take her, her lecturing is so confusing and despite me trying my best to understand her explanations, I couldn't. She teaches as if you already know what she is talking about, despite this being an INTRO stats course. The other lecturer, John Keane, was much clearer and understandable in the lecture recordings I watched, take him instead.

This class had way more work than I would expect, and it was always due on 7 pm on Thursdays. I went to every lecture and took notes, but I never understood the content just from lecture- I had to put time in outside of class, because lecture was never super clear.
do not take this class with Romero. I had to watch professor Keane's lectures for the last 2 months because she is such a terrible lecturer.

I liked the way the class was set up (except for hw due at 7PM on Thursdays, WHY??) but I didn't like the way Prof. Romero taught. I can't really explain it but her explanations were so unclear and she moved way too fast. She just was not my favorite. Class was easy tho w/ lots of extra credit opportunities
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was a good professor but after watching the recorded lectures I think I would have wanted to take the course with the other instructor who teaches it. She does not explain things as well as him. There is a bunch of homework every week and everything is due at 7pm on Thursday which was weird. The grading is also left to GSI's and not consistent.

Prof Romero was fine. I could never pay attention in lecture because I find stats to be extremely dry, but that could just be me. The class itself has a ridiculous amount of homework, but at long as you try, do the extra credit, and study for the 2 exams, you should have no trouble getting an A.

Professor Romero is in her own world during her lectures. She goes so fast and basically repeats whatever is on the slides without explaining the reasoning or theory behind it. She also keeps repeating the same formulas and concepts within one lecture. She's also not clear when answering questions. Regardless, STATS250 is an overall easy class.

Plain and simple, she just doesn't explain anything. The only way people do well in this class and call it is easy is because a majority of students took a stats course in high school. If you haven't taken statistics, be prepared to be confused within a couple weeks and resort to teaching the material to yourself, because she certainly won't.

This class is very hard. The course doesn't really teach u stats but STATS 250 as in the structure it has &all the busy work that is given if that makes sense. This professor doesn't explain the material at all making going to lecture pointless. It's basically self taught. Be ready to be graded extremely harsh &having endless amount of assignments

TERRIBLE. All of my friends took stats in high school and can confirm she makes class more confusing.  I have to go home and watch the other guy's lectures because she is so bad at explaining material.  She rushes through content and doesn't explain anything.  Take anyone else. No idea how she has a 5/5 - that does not reflect how terrible she is.
Overall, I feel like Dr. Romero was a perfectly good prof for an intro-level stats course. She tries to engage students and gives the students different options for participation and grading.

Romero was a great lecturer but this class was just so annoying. 1.5 hour lectures twice a week (and also a pointless 1.5 hour lab) with AT LEAST 2 hours of hw (hw is graded so you actually have to try). If you don't have to take this class, just don't. 2 online exams that are open everything but still hard so you actually have to try.

She is great! STATS 250 is not a super difficult course, but her explanations made everything even easier to understand. I also love the fact that she is super patient with questions and very accessible outside classes. Take STATS250 with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Romero runs a great class. She is very clear during her lectures and on the lecture slides.  Lectures are not required but I encourage you to attend lecture because it helps with not falling behind.  She is very helpful outside of class--attend her office hours if you can.

Professor Romero is amazing, she makes the class easy.  There is a problem set that is completed in every lecture but there's tons of help to work through the problem set.  If you do the lecture work, the homework assignments and exams are pretty similar.  By far my favorite class this term!

Professor Romero is very informative in lectures and explains things really well. I would go to Office Hours all the time for help on the homework and she was always ready to help and easy to follow. Overall, a great professor and a great class to take.

lectures were a little boring, and moved fast especially in the last month of class, but overall a decent professor. Lab GSIs are pretty helpful at answering questions. I would recommend attending lecture even if it's not required to stay on top of concepts

It was hard to go back to the notes and study, they were hard to follow. The exams and homework aren't like the practice problems during lecture which is frustrating. Grading was inconsistent from one person to the next, my friends and I would work on homework together and get different scores. Exams were online though, open book and open note.

Professor Romero explained stats well and slow, so it was easy to catch on.  She was always accessible outside of class.  Lots of extra credit, and the paper assignments were not too difficult.  Grading scale is also designed differently, so I finished the class with a 91% and that is an A not an A-.  90% in the class is easily achievable
Pretty simple class if you don't get behind. Make sure to attend your lab sections because they pretty much give you all the answers to the lab, and you won't have to do it on your own time

I love this professor! Her lectures were not mandatory but I attended almost every single one of them in person. She is passionate about her course and actually loves her job. Dr. Romero often included many little jokes so it was even better! I heard office hours were super helpful though I did not attend any.. 100% would recommend Dr. Romero!

Prof. Romero was a very good teacher for the STATS 250 curriculum and did a great job of covering all the material. However, I found her lectures to be slower-paced than I would have liked -- it felt like only 50% of the lecture time was spent providing new material. There were many opportunities for extra credit, which I appreciated.

Professor Romero is wonderful. She seems to actually enjoy teaching and cares about the well-being of her students. Her lectures are thorough, and the exams are similar to the review guides. If you put in the work there should be no surprises with the exams.  Please save yourself headaches and attend the lectures even though they are not required.

A great teacher for Stats. Always open for questions after lectures and explains concepts in a manner that is relatively easy to understand. There was a fair bit of homework which was expected out of this class. She is a great option for Stats 250

Her class was not the easiest for me and this was highly due to the reason she would not give us the same note files she would project. She also flips through slides with lots of work (which you usually need time to write down). GSI were very helpful. I feel she could explain things a bit more clear but she was a cool teacher!

Dr. Romero is an awesome lecturer. You can tell she genuinely cares about teaching the material and works through the lectures at a manageable pace. Her course compared to Dr. Miller's is a little more writing dependent, but it offsets the weight of the exams a lot, and it is very much doable. Would recommend!

Her lectures don't help too much with the homework. You need to go to office hours to understand how to answer actual questions. She was confusing a lot of times in lectures and during office hours mostly complicating things. Just find a good GSI that will explain better.

Would not have taken this course with anyone else, Dr. Romero was an astounding Intro Stats professor, lectures can go fast at times but she is constantly re-emphasizing key concepts in her lectures.  It's amazing how much I've learned about this subject despite coming in with no experience!

Dr. Romero cares a lot about her students and really tries to make the course engaging.  She is by far one of the best professors I've had here at UM.  I highly recommend her class.  She explains concepts very clearly and offers many examples. Take her class, plus MWrite is actually an enjoyable assignment.

Dr. Romero really cares about her students, and understands that most of their students are only taking STATS 250 because their major requires it. I honestly really enjoyed the MWrite assignments. GSI quality can vary a lot, but labs are pretty simple.  I would highly recommend Dr. Romero, take her class!

Easily one of the best teachers or professors I've ever had. Dr. Romero is the kind of prof that not only genuinely wants their students to succeed but also wants everyone to fully understand the material-be sure to attend lectures because material builds on itself.   Dr. Romero made stats an absolute breeze.
OMG Dr. Romero is an amazing lecturer for Stats 250. if u wanted to take Stats 250 definitely take it with her and you will get an easy A.

Dr. Romero is an amazing lecturer for Stats 250. She provides ample preparation and practice for exams and is always accessible outside of class. The overall average grade for the class and one of the exams was an A, which is a testament to how well she prepares you.

I really loved Romero I'm not sure why she is rated lower than Miller. She is super sweet and the class is straightforward and well structured as long as you don't skip lectures. She goes a bit fast at times but will stop lecturing at any point to answer questions. Homeworks would take a bit but if you go to office hours you'll do well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Romero was a good professor, and it is obvious she cares about her students. I think the amount of work in the course is somewhat heavier than others, as there is a lab and homework weekly. If I really tried on the homework, it took me ~2 hours to complete. Other than the heavy workload, she was a pretty decent professor.

Essential to attend lecture & mandatory labs. Romero is amazing and I think the course load was appropriate. She actually made me love statistics after I really hated it in high school. The R coding/labs were easy, while homework slightly more difficult. She goes slightly fast in lecture, but her Canvas page is robust & contains any info you need.

The material is very straightforward. Professor was bothered when iClicker question had low correctness at times, but she teaches material fairly. Low commitment in studying, but HW can be a bit much for an easy class.  Around 75% of class got an A- or above on first exam. Final average is B+ from HWs, MWrite, etc. 

Overall good teacher for intro
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely recommend taking this class with Romero. She and the GSIs make the material easy to understand and help you prepare for the tests, quizzes, and M-Writes. Office hours are so helpful! As long as you pay attention in lectures, show up to labs, and get help when you need it (which you always can) you'll be fine in this class.

This class was harder than it shouldve been. Prof Romeros lectures can get frustrating. She goes fast and the coursepack notes dont include everything from her powerpoint. A flipped classroom would be MUCH better here. My saving grace in this class was office hours, the GSIs are legendary! And Ive heard better things about the other stats prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love her! Super kind and intelligent. She wants you to succeed. The workload is not super heavy, two exams, one quiz, and one weekly hw assignment and lab. The exams are usually just like the coursepack and hw, so practice with those.

Professor Romero is an angel. She is so intelligent and is a great lecturer. She can go quickly at times but is easy to communicate with and makes it easy to ask questions. She gives a ton of extra credit and really wants her students to do well.

class is available in person, async, or sync, but skipping is highly detrimental. lecture moves at a fast pace and topics build quickly. the stats dept is very adept and helpful if you ask for it. r coding is used but it isn't difficult by any means (mostly copy and paste). slightly overwhelming amounts of hw but manageable with good habits
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is very chill. Lectures are recorded, nice lady, exams are online and open note, labs seem scary but aren't if ur GSI gives u answers (most do). Sometimes she leads you astray in lectures but I am good at teaching myself. Material isn't bad, office hours help a lot. ALSO 20pt of extra credit is clutch with 2-3% grade increase at end of semester
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Romero is genuinely a kind soul and cares about her students. She can be a little disorganized sometimes, which was the hardest thing to work around for me, but overall the class was what was to be expected. Its a manageable class and I loved my GSI. There are ample resources for help, practice, and extra credit.

Romero was a great teacher and you could tell that she wanted her students to do well in this class. Yes, at times her lectures got confusing but this is a math class so that should be expected at some points. She gave many opportunities for extra credit and all the GSIs had so many office hours so it was very easy and accessible to get help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Romero is so sweet, and while her lectures can be a bit one-note, she always takes time to answer questions and clearly cares about teaching (unlike many professors at umich). I highly recommend taking Stats 250 with her :)

She's definitely a great professor to have during a pandemic! You can tell that she really cares about her students being successful. She gives lots of extra credit and she's always available throughout the week if you need help (OH's, AMA's, etc)! There weren't really any surprises on exams and she gives you tons of resources to help you.

Dr. Romero is a great professor. She's very organized and her guided notes and straightforward lectures make learning course content very easy and digestible. There is almost always someone available for office hours. Homework, chapter quizzes, and other resources are very beneficial in practicing the new content. I always felt prepared for exams.
This class was very well organized. Being online, made it really easy to understand guidelines and expectations. You do have to put aside a good chunk of hours in a week to complete work/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Romero was pretty good, but her lectures were honestly quite confusing. Fortunately, I took stats in high school, so this class was more of a review, but if I didn't have any background, I imagine my grade would be worse. If you're willing to put in work outside of lectures to understand topics though, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I didn't have much contact with Professor Romero but the setup of the class was the most organized I've seen at any UMich class. Modules and expectations are clearly defined. There is a lot of homework that is somewhat harshly graded but other assignments make up for this. Labs are really fun! Help is readily available if you need it!

Stats 250 is not generally a very difficult course, just very work-heavy. Romero's lectures were very slow and could be somewhat monotone, but she does explain things clearly and helpfully. Generally a good professor.

This class was great. Lectures were well-paced and covered everything you needed to know. Labs were kinda tricky but still easy to do well in. Exams were very fair and usually included many of the same types of questions as in the lecture so there were minimal surprises. I went to office hours and she was very helpful and kind.

I don't know if it was because I took this course when it was in online format, but I couldn't stand Romero's voice at 1x speed. She spoke very slowly and in a monotoned voice. The class itself was easy especially of how understanding they were during these rough times. This class was an easy A but without covid this class is really hard apparently

Dr. Romero is one of the best professors I've had at U of M. Despite remote learning, the STATS 250 team made it very accessible and easy to get into contact with them. Dr. Romero was more than understanding with the grading for this course and was always willing to help when confused on any material. Take the class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why everyone is hating on Romero because I took her class online and I thought she was great. She was super considerate and gave us lots of grade boosts and ec due to the pandemic and even though there is a lot of homework, if you do it all the exams are an easy A

Prof. Romero's lectures are full of information, so they can be dense at times. Grading is very fair--just make sure to start the weekly hw early because the points add up! Exams aren't too difficult but they can be nitpicky. Labs and MWrite were useless. As long as you stay on top of the work, stats 250 is a pretty straightforward class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Do not take STATS 250 as an online class, not worth it. Romero did surprisingly give us a lot of breaks considering we are in a pandemic, if you can avoid taking this online please do so, you won't learn anything and will only be getting by to receive a grade/credit for the course. Use the pass/fail option to your advantage if you must take it.

She is simply not a good teacher. She speaks in a monotone and unconfident tone, seems like she's reading straight from a textbook, and doesn't cover the concepts with any clarity or depth. Material itself is easy and you can easily get a good grade, but she definitely doesn't contribute to that. I took her online, so maybe she's better in person.
Dr. Romero is a great Instructor. She explains things clearly and always brings extra examples that she ties to the "harder" HW problems. Her iclickers are very helpful! I would recommend her 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Romero was a gem-if you can't get Gunderson, definitely take Romero! Her lectures were helpful and she was available for help outside of class. The tests and homework are VERY nitpicky so memorize the exact wording in the course pack. There are a good amount of EC opportunities and easy points as long as you stay on top of it and utilize office hrs

Professor Romero is a good lecturer. She is clear and goes through material at a nice and easy-to-understand pace. I don't understand why her lectures are not as popular as Professor Gunderson :) I was learning quite well with Professor Romero's teaching.

Dr. Romero covered the content clearly and at an even pace. She always seemed genuinely excited to be teaching even though this was just an introductory course, and she reminds us of available resources and wants us to do well. I found Stats 250 to be fairly easy as long as you pay attention in lecture, lab, and do the homework carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was ridiculous. The material wasn't even difficult, but the concepts on the homework didn't even closely mirror the exams. If you make a minor mistake expect to be marked down significantly. Aside from that, Romero is an extremely confusing lecturer and often makes mistakes even when it's obvious she's copying from an answer book.

Alicia was a great lecturer (before I compared her to any other professor). If gunderson is not an option for you, definitely go with alicia. She clearly cares about her students and is willing to sit down and clarify things outside of class!
Shes fabulous!!!!

STATS 250 is the hardest class I think I've taken in my lifetime and Professor Romero's lectures did very little to help. Although the concepts were explained somewhat in lectures, no amount of knowledge acquired from her lectures is sufficient enough to do well on exams, which contain much more difficult questions than the ones in class and on HW.
Take Gunderson, much better lecturer. You have to be very dilligent to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She teaches in an incredibly confusing manner. It is really hard to follow her, especially when she almost purposely misspeaks things that are the exact opposite of what is the right answer. I don't recommend taking the course with her, take it with the other professors.

Alicia Romero goes very fast and is not the most enthusiastic. She always seemed more disappointed that students weren't understanding something like it was our fault, even when 60%+ didn't understand it. It is very possible to get an A, but definitely not easy. A lot of hard work and absolutely no curve.

Romero is decent despite what all the other reviews said. She can move a little fast a times though. With that said, try to get Gunderson, she is way better. But, if you have Romero, like I did, it is not the end of the world. Success in stats comes from practice practice practice. Practicing is probably more effective than going to lecture, tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the worst in the department, she will put up an clicker question, show everybody the answers submitted, which almost all end up being wrong. When only 16% of a class is able to get a review question right at the beginning of class you know the problem cannot be the students.

The HW is tricky, Mwrite is really annoying but not hard, the professor isnt too bad, kind of boring but still nice. There's no curve in this class, and the exams were hard in my opinion. Practice is probably your friend in this class. You can easily lose points on something really small, so dont take the class as a joke. Lots of small extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I would always zone out in her lectures because of how bored I was. It doesnt really matter if you have her or not for Stats considering the lecture recordings for Gunderson are on canvas. I only went to class for iclicker points and she sometimes brought candy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She's a great lecturer and especially helpful in OA and after class. Though STATS250 is an easy class by no means it is an 'easy A' imo. There's homework, MWrite, Labs, xyz... Just keep up with what's going on, try to get full marks on each homework and use office hours, you'll be fine. Lectures are recorded and you can go to any lecturer, dw.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Romero is awesome! Imo the best 250 professor. The course has definitely changed though and is no longer a blowoff. The HW's can be tricky, MWrite is dumb, and our E1 avg grade was a 53/75 compared to 69/75 last year (NO curve). This class was still very very easy (just not a joke) if you put in just a little bit of time.

This class was awful for me. That being said Romero was never really much help in my troubles without my active forcing of the conversation and with several clarifying questions. If you are considering the CSP lab with her you'll be much better of in a general lab section. Regretted signing up for her lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: don't blow of the class and you'll get an a. if you don't show up to class, don't try on the hw, and don't really study, you'll get a d
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer. Isn't very lear about the material, and can be very confusing to listen to.

Clear criteria.  Never went to class.  Just watched Gunderson online.  So don't stress if you can't get Gunderson when registering.  Lab is mandatory tho and you just need to show up to get those points.  You do have to put in work for hW and exams but there's plenty of office hours and resources for all the students.  Pretty easy A

Overall Alicia was a good lecturer. She wasn't bad, but she wasn't particularly good. I found the class pretty hard because homework is assigned weekly and it's a pretty big part of your grade. It covers a lot of material that isn't addressed in lecture. Exams and homework are graded VERY harshly and points are taken away on super small details.

Dr. Akey is pretty bad. Going to his lectures is almost pointless as he raises his hand every 20 seconds and wastes a ton of time. However, re-watching his lectures is super helpful as it makes more sense.

I feel like people are a little too harsh on Dr. Akey. He's a super nice guy and if you rewatch his lectures, he's not hard to understand. He's clearly extremely passionate about teaching the course's content, and makes jokes that no one laughs at but are pretty funny :( He's always available to explain content again if needed or for any questions

Cannot explain concepts well and seems like he loses track of what he is saying multiple times throughout lecture. His lecturing style is inefficient and he isn't very helpful when reached out to. MCDB 310 isn't a difficult class content wise, but it seems that way when the lecturer is confused himself.

He seems like a nice guy but his teaching style is so hard to follow. If you handwrite notes you'll struggle to follow along in lecture as he clicks away from the slides often and rambles about various things instead of what is on the slides. It's a dense course and feels even more dense with Akey as he doesn't know how to break down hard concepts.

Absolutely terrible!!! He made people "raise their hands" to answer EVERY SINGLE QUESTION in class even when no one clearly wanted to. He did not know what was going and was poor at explaining difficult concepts. I should not have to show up to class twice a week to listen to him repeat back to me what is written on the slides. Please avoid!!

Taking the class in the spring is the way to go. An A ends up being an 86%, although there isn't a dropped exam. He wasn't the best at explaining but he clearly cared and was very kind and available. The cheat sheets for the exams are very helpful, making that along with good review should score you the grade you want in the class.

I absolutely loved mcdb 310 with dr. akey. he's clearly extremely passionate about teaching the course's content, and tries to make the sometimes dense lecture content as fun as possible. if you pay attention in class, and use discussion section as a chance to review, the course won't be overwhelming. clearly a professor who cares ab his students.

Lectures are not the place to learn. His pace is way too fast, rambles to the point where you do not know what is important for the exam. Office hours are better with him- he offers more clarification and personalized teaching style. Had to self teach everything. Memorize structures. Exams 3-4 are hardest. Have a goated Cheat Sheet. GL soldier.

He's a great person and clearly accomplished, but I often had to rewind parts of the lecture 3–4 times to understand. Sometimes, YouTube videos explained the material more clearly. It might've felt this way because Dr. N was especially good at breaking things down.
Does not prepare you for exams well. Slides are often confusing and not in order. Prepare to learn the content by yourself. Also please memorize all structures mentioned

Dr. Akey never gave us the chance to succeed. I always try to see the best in profs, but he completely misrepresented the contents of exam 4 beforehand. If I'd known what was expected of me, I could have studied accordingly. What he insisted wasn't a cumulative was entirely that. Students were balling as they left the exam room. He broke our trust.
Exams are atrocious- dropped after 2

Dr. Akey is a good professor. This class is difficult, and the exams are tough. There is going to be A LOT of content and a big time commitment. I believe that although the class is tough, its very fair. Seriously, do all the practice problems each Chapter and attend all the discussions. Problem roulette is a great resource and helps a lot on exams

This course was very difficult. The final exam (only exam we couldn't drop) was a whole other level of bad. However, I felt Dr. Akey did a decent job of being straightforward - lectures were less convoluted in his half of the course. Problem roulette saved my grade, and take advantage of SLC/outside resources.

Doesn't explain lectures in detail enough and then tests us on the most random stuff we didn't think was that important. Genuinely 4th exam was the most HORRENDOUS thing I've ever seen. This class is worse than orgo I and II. He's super sweet and cute as a person, but exams and his teaching style are terrible.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. 
I strongly suggest avoiding this professor. The teaching is painfully unclear, and the class structure is a complete mess. You'll likely spend more time trying to figure out what's going on than actually learning. It's not worth the frustration.

Dr. Akey is the worst lecturer I have ever had. He glosses over the most important information that is asked on the exam. He made our final exam (exam 4, the one you can't drop) genuinely impossible. I saw multiple people sobbing during and after the exam. The exam questions are just on another level and he doesn't even come close to preparing you.

Loved getting lectures from Dr. Akey. He always brings fun things into lectures and can be silly. He clearly explained concepts in lecture and lectures have a good "flow". He truly loves biochem and teaching, which was inspiring to me. You will probably need to rewatch the lectures because the content is challenging and the class moves fast.

EVERYONE TAKE THIS CLASS IT IS THE BEST!!!!!!!!!!!! you can redo everything up to 90%, and the majority of your grade is a take-home exam and project. You are also done with all assignments halfway through the semester. Most importantly, he brought donuts for the last class. love him so much.

Writing this at 4 am because of how much his bad teaching has me in the trenches. He explains things HORRIBLY and quickly glances (or doesn't even mention) the most important parts of the slides. Sometimes I literally laugh when watching from how bad his lecturing is. Literally had to use chat gpt to explain all the lectures and it takes FOREVER.

Dr. Akey teaches two of the four units of MCDB 310. He highlights important content from the lecture slides in blue so that you know what you need to study for the exam. he goes VERY fast and it can be difficult to keep up with the content, so prepare to rewatch the lecture recordings more often than not. His office hours are helpful.

Dr. Akey clearly cares about his students, and for that alone I really appreciated him as a professor. However, his lectures can be, often, hard to follow, which makes for a panicky/frustrating start to the course. Stick with it, and you will adapt. Stick to your study strategies, and of course, study like a maniac. You'll succeed if you do.
He just made the funniest joke in class OMG. Back-to-back jokes and I am still laughing. Great guy. He is making learning the Citric Acid Cycle so freaking fun.

What a guy. He wears keens every day and bikes to class (bless him). He cares about your learning and is always available to help. I recommend going to office hours as a lot of content is covered. Exam questions aren't too tricky, and today he told us that a chapter wouldn't be covered on the exam, knowing students were overwhelmed already!!!!!!!!!

He made the final too much to memorize. After doing the practice exam, the exam 1-3, and the problem roulette, I didn't expect there were so many details for the final. If you didn't make a good notes for the exam you won't pass the final.

Professor Akey's lectures are incredibly dense and very difficult to learn anything in class. He assumes lots of knowledge and expects that you remember things from past exams instead of explaining concepts. Be prepared to do a lot of work on your own to understand the content.

Really nice professor, but explains things as if the students are well versed in the material. I had to rewatch lectures and search up youtube videos to explain concepts that should be explained already. If you know the material coming into the lectures and go to office hours, then you will do well.
Another one of UMs bad biology department professors. Boring monotonous lectures with little help/resources to truly prepare for exams with low averages. Weeder class for sure

411 wasn't difficult and grades were fair, but instructions were poorly worded and led to wasted time. Lectures were filled with contradictory info (plus we never knew if attendance was part of the grade). Akey also plays favorites, so be prepared to be ignored as a "normal" student. Frustrating experience and wished for a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There's a lot of bad reviews but he's actually good. lectures must be rewatched a 2nd time cuz in person it's hard to get anything out of them. but has great office hours! seriously go to office hours he draws things out and explains at a depth that's not possible in a 400 person lecture. If you put in the time he will too. Also a really nice guy!

Akey's a kind professor, but his lectures are some of the worst I've experienced. There wasn't a single lecture that I walked out of feeling ok with the material. I had to rewatch them at 1.5 speed just to make sense of what was going on. His exams were fair, but biochem is a really hard class and a lot of it depends on how good your note sheet is.

Dr. Akey seemed nice and wrote fair exams, but his lecture style was simply ineffective. His slides were dense, and the order the material was presented often felt illogical, which led to a high amount of time needing to be spent outside of class only to make sense of the lecture. His explanations were far better during office hours, though.

Overall Akey's lectures are a bit on the dryer side and speaks really fast, but exams are straightforward. Pay attention in lecture and review the slides after class. Definitely not a 3/5 -- his class is overall manageable contrary to what people say. Biochem is hard be prepared!

Dr. Akey was one of the best professors I've ever had. He is so kind very engaging in the lecture. All of the assignments we did in MCDB 411 genuinely contributed to my understanding of structural biology.

I see a lot of reviews talking about how bad Dr. Akey's lectures are, but in my experience I saw tons of people doing other things while he was lecturing. He speaks quickly and is pretty dry, so stay really focused on the lecture! His tests are very straight forward, so the notecard is very helpful in that regard. Fill out your Cell Map!!!

Avoid at all costs. I'm a senior and this was the most difficult class I've ever taken (spring 22). Dr. Akey is knowledgable but his lectures lack clarity. From the start, he speaks as if he's lecturing to other professors or students with a good background in biochem. Definitely take another prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David Akey cares about the material but doesn't know how to explain it well. Grading criteria is confusing and constantly in flux, making it difficult to prepare for assignments and group projects. Same for syllabus, which only covered half the semester. Dry lecture style so hard to pay attention. Overall would not recommend Akey for 411 or 310.

MCDB310 is TOUGH, but Akey is a passionate professor who truly cares about his students. While I didn't do as well as I'd hoped, class expectations were always clear. He cares about his students and goes out of his way virtually and in-person to try to help students succeed. Best advice: go to office hours, don't fall behind, and get to know him!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult. Though I did not do as well as I hoped, the class was outlined well and expectations were clear. Dr. Akey was a great professor; excited about the material, offering significant office hours both in-person and virtually and very willing to meet 1-on-1 with me as I struggled with the material.

Not a very clear lecturer, and hard to follow.
He's incredibly knowledgeable but doesn't
know how to simplify things. He made the
fourth exam VERY difficult. Don't skip details
memorize and stay on top of lecture. Do
many practice problems as you can including
the books P. Roulette. nice guy but not the
best teacher Doable though

Good luck. I went into exam 4 with an A- and came out with a B. Akey's final exam was by far the worst experience of this course (avg. 57.5% before the curve). It also cannot be dropped. He's not an interesting or effective lecturer at all, which is evident by how poorly the class did on his exam (which was probably intentional on his part).

Dr. Akey is a good professor and a nice guy but a horrible HORRIBLE lecturer. His lectures made no sense whatsoever. I would not recommend taking a class with him. I still remember the feeling of despair and hopelessness after his lecture, from which I learned absolutely nothing.
He wasn’t the best but definitely not the worst lol. Funny guy!
projects are a little confusing and difficult but office hours were really helpful
hard class but go to office hours for specific help from akey
Highly recommend taking MCDB 411 with Akey
Very hard course!!! Extremely difficult exams, but Dr. Akey is super helpful during office hours. Come prepared with questions!!
For those who are going to take MCDB 310 with him, don't believe him when he says you don't need to memorize. Just memorize and know everything.
Would not recommend taking 310, but he is amazing at teaching 411
Great professor!!!!

I had Dr. Akey for both MCDB 310 and MCDB 411. I thought he was a really hard prof when I took 310, but now in 411, I realize that 310 was out of his control. He is so understanding and really focuses on his students and their needs. His office hours are really helpful as well and he has done nothing but be supportive during the pandemic.
He repeatedly says incorrect things in lectures and assumes that students know the basics perfectly. Some people can teach content, but he can't.

Dr. Akey moves through the material fast and includes a lot of details. Although this might make it harder to learn at first, rewatching the lectures and taking the time outside of class to put it all together really deepened my understanding of the material and helped me in the end.

the only things are his lectures are so so dry i could fall asleep, and he focuses on literally everything as if it's all gonna be on the exam. But I never had any super negative things to say about him, and he's obviously really knowledgable in the topics he teaches

Quite literally one of the worst professors I've ever had at this university. His lectures are completely unorganized, illogical and difficult to follow. They are also incredibly dry and cause students to tune out while he is talking. He teaches as if this isn't brand new information and expects us to know things way beyond our level.

Honestly, one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. He's so hard to follow and teaches as if you already know all of the material. Doesn't emphasize what you need to know from the slides at all and so disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is taught with alternating lecturers, so you only get him for half of the year. He is really hard to follow in lecture, its hard to watch his lectures as it isn't clear the points he is trying to emphasize, and he doesn't explain what is on the slides very well. It also doesn't help that he blazes through topics to quickly

He's a great lecturer, frankly most of the other reviewers are whining. He is very lenient when it comes to giving points back on quizzes; his exams are almost directly taken from his quizzes, so he is a pretty laid back teacher. Also, he is very accessible. Much better professor than these other reviews let on if you actually study the material.

His tests are some of the hardest I have taken at UM. His lectures can get kinda messy and he veers off topic sometimes. He also does not do a great job of emphasizing what you should know for test. However, he definitely cares about his students and will meet with you if you ask.
Exams are too long for the time given and cover material that is far more in depth than what was taught in class.

This class was horrible. The exams were closed note, but the class was graded on a curve. There was also no way to monitor cheating. This means that this class rewarded cheaters while punishing those that took the tests honestly. Whoever thought that was a good idea obviously isn't smart enough to have a teaching degree. Horrible all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Akey taught me in the spring term and he was great. I learned a lot from him and enjoyed having him as a professor. The class covers a ton of material but he teaches it well and was very understanding. I recommend taking MCDB 310 with him! His GSIs were cool too.
great professor with engaging lectures

This guy the goat frfr. He super chill and the class is an easy A. He's clearly passionate about the topic but doesn't try to make the class harder than it needs to. He lowkey highkirkenuinely pretty smexy too. 1000000/10 would recommend and take again. One of my favorite professors that I've ever had and unironically one of the best on campus.

Very easy class. Lectures are mandatory but they're pretty engaging and you don't have to pay attention if you don't want to since you're not tested on content. The only work you have to do is a weekly writing assignment and readings.

Dr. Ahn was awesome. Funny dude, great lecturer, and really just wanted students to grapple with some new material and do a bit of critical thinking. Such a chiller. I'm taking another one of his classes this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but the class is a grind. Lectures are dry, and the workload is heavy on busy work. You have to do long Perusall readings with 5 mandatory annotations each, plus weekly 400-word responses. The quizzes are easy if you follow the slides, but he is surprisingly strict about small details.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Ahn! Really caring guy, and also super accessible outside of class. The class was super easy as well and I thought Dr. Ahn was a really charismatic lecturer. Would highly recommend!
He's really sweet. Overall the class was heavier in workload than I expected, but it was really easy to complete/get a good overall grade. Attendance mandatory and I hated the MLB oml.

Incredible guy, super knowledgeable about a wide range of topics from Korea/Asia, religion, world history, etc.

Absolutely personable, and it shows in lecture and his interactions with students. 

Genuinely inspirational professor, I almost have to say wise.

Professor Ahn is incredibly nice and it's clear that he is passionate about teaching! I highly recommend you take this class if you are looking for easy HU credit. Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but he does do in-class exercises sometimes. Discussion attendance was mandatory, but I had a strict GSI you could have a different experience.
Easy, fun, and can learn something
Professor Ahn is kind, caring, and funny. His lecture is well-prepared and interesting. It is easy to receive an A in this course. Workload is light.

Professor Ahn is absolutely amazing. Very sweet and kind professor that genuinely cares about students and wants you to succeed. Lectures can be a bit long but he is very good at teaching content in an interesting and engaging manner. Highly recommend if you're looking to fulfill humanities credit with an easy A.
I loved his lectures and how the class was set up. He was very engaging and all the topics I learned about was very interesting to learn about.
Professor Ahn's lectures are always interesting and thought-provoking. This is an easy class and worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: great prof, easy a. super understanding and reasonable guy. knows his stuff but also doesn't talk down to students asking questions. would definitely recommend for anyone looking to fulfill a distribution requirement
As an ULWR there is obviously a lot of work, but it is easily the best ULWR at Michigan in my opinion. Two papers + 50ish annotations. Professor is a great guy and makes the class painless.

Asian 325 is an extremely easy A. He literally gives you the answers to the quiz right before in class. He also reduced the final paper to basically 3-4 paragraphs. He knows it's an easy A so you can either sit back and enjoy his funny lectures or stay home and sleep. You'll get an A either way.
Great professor that genuinely cares about his students. Not a difficult class but still teaches you a lot about interesting topics

Extremely easy class if you want a light class to fit into your schedule. 2 quizzes and 2 papers with weekly discussion for an hour. His lectures can feel long but he does make it interesting and funny at times. He's super laid-back and knows everyone's taking this class for an easy A so he just wants you to listen and chill.
Professor Ahn's class has been one of my favorite classes I've taken at this University. He's a great teacher and very knowledgeable.
Professor Ahn is great
This guy is absolutely a easy grader; but his lecture style is unnecessarily long and serious. I would recommend to say away from this guy.

He is a great professor to have. However, he does not go in chronological order, which may throw you off if that is how you better learn history like I do, but he is very good at clarifying and offering assistance. He is very approachable and has a good sense of humor. I would definitely recommend taking any of his classes.

Not a doable A like someone else says. I took other classes that were much much easier to get an A than this one. He says that he'll basically teach everything you need to know before the exams but for some reason it didn't help and if you do miss just a few questions on that multiple choice questions it adds up to a huge chunk of your grade.

I have to disagree with the posters before who said how interesting this class is. I found it to be completely boring and asinine, despite having a strong interest coming in to the class. While it is really easy and not stressful at all, I would suggest a different easy A class without mandatory attendance or so much writing.

Professor Ahn is fantastic!  He's super nice and funny, and he has great style.  He understands college students, so his classes aren't too difficult.  If you have any questions, he's a great resource.  I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Really nice, really helpful, most of the class just showed up to the review sessions where he re-taught everything and said exactly what we had to know. Didn't expect people to show up and made it clear he didn't care if you did. Two papers, two MC quizzes, a final, reading journal, and a participation blog. Doable A, great prof.

explains concepts and theories of buddhism simply and keeps the class easy. Very nice man and helpful if you ask him questions. he tells you exactly what will be on the exams. Does give your 4 essays with vague prompts but just wants you to show that you understand and gsi grades them easily. Very interesting class

Great professor, he's very knowledgeable and cares about the future to come with advancement in understanding microbiology. I have no complaints beside the fact that he's a Canadian and pronounces the word "bag" like "baeg" I just have problems with every Canadian pronouncing the word bag.

I was disappointed that he read right off of the slides during lecture. Sometimes exam questions asked niche questions that were a sentence on one slide (“what type of engineering is this similar to”). I appreciated that he tried to crack jokes and showed us videos pertaining to what we were learning to try and connect all of the dots.
This is the best professor.
I honestly really enjoyed Dr.V he tries to explain things in simpler ways and tries to crack jokes. I really enjoyed him because he is very inspirational.

Lectures can get boring at times, but overall is engaging and clear. Exams and his "two of the above" questions are... not fun. Pay attention to every detail and you will do fine. He also provides extra credit for attending lecture.

Dr. V is by far the best + most helpful professor I've had at UMICH! He genuinely cares about his students and is always happy to help, no matter the circumstance. His lectures are clear, and everything you need is on the slides. The exams are super fair and straightforward. Plus, he's just an overall kind and amazing professor. Highly recommend!

I loved Dr. V! Exams can be a little tricky, but if you know the slides, you will do well. If you go to his office hours, he will tell you some of the content on the exam at the end so be sure to go! Great class though and I found it to be an easy A.

Great professor all around! Probably one of the best teachers I have had at UMich so far. Definitely attend his Q&A sessions, as they are very helpful for the exams! He is a professor who wants you to succeed!

Great professor! His lectures were super engaging and you could tell he knew the content well. His exams were pretty difficult but he made sure to curve them if the class average was lower. Overall, enjoyed his class a lot and would definitely take one with him again.

Great professor with lectures that were extremely easy to follow! Liked him a lot. The content was hard and the class is only graded on 4 exams + lab grade, but his lectures were definitely one of the best I've had
i liked him a lot

Dr. Vecchiarelli was awesome. If you go to office hours you'll do much better because he often makes test questions from what people ask in office hours. Tests can be tough because you need to know specifics but they're doable. Lectures are interesting and Dr. V is obviously extremely knowledgeable. I wish I could take this class again!

Genuinely one of the best professors I have had at umich. He has dense lecture material but he teaches in a way that helps digest the material much better than other stem class professors I have had. Lab for this class is really easy, and comparatively to biochem or genetics the exams for this class are not too bad.

I like Dr. V a lot. He's really nice and you can tell how much he likes his students and the material he is teaching. But this class is hard. And his tests are ridiculous. And maybe it was just me, but I didn't feel like this class compensated for such a hard semester online.

He makes lectures interesting and truly wants to see us understand the material and gain a passion for microbiology. Exams can be challenging so play close attention to detail, meanwhile the 207 lab is super chill for a science lab. Dr. V is amazing!
New professor at Michigan, but definitely earned his right to be there. Interesting lecturer, and very approachable. Brings in a lot of real-world examples, which keeps the class interesting.
Greta new professor here at Umich. Make sure to pay extra attention to lecture. Lectures are fun and he keeps it moving

I honestly really disliked the class as I am not a big architecture person and was just doing this as a humanities requirement, but Professor Timmermann was able to make this class bearable for me. Attendance is mandatory and lectures are an hour and a half of him talking and nothing else, but he is very knowledgeable on the topic.

Attendance was mandatory and technology not allowed. If you're into art this is the class for you, if not can be a bit boring. Also found the prof a bit rude in class and through email at times. Not very clear instructions and only 3 assignments but did give a lot of time to work on them

Class is fairly easy if you can manage time well and have at least a little interest in the topic, since there are barely any assignments, but he can be rather rude, which made me afraid to speak in class or ask questions. I've seen him lowkey treat students like their questions were dumb when they were just trying to learn.
He was a little rude and unapproachable but was also very unclear about grading progress throughout. Overal, not too bad if you're really interested and he is very thorough

Professor Timmerman is a very nice and thorough professor. HISTART194 is a first year seminar. He lectures every meeting about the history of medieval castles, culture, and artwork and he is very knowledgable on the topic. Even if you are not interested in the subject, it is a great way to clear 3 humanities credits and also learn something new.

The class content was okay, however, this class was listed as a seminar, but students rarely got the chance to participate. There were only two projects, so the workload was manageable, but I had no clue what my grade was until the final grade came out. Grading was also unclear on projects and I never got my grade for any of my assignments.

If you are not interested in architecture/design at all, DO NOT TAKE THIS. He lectures the entire class although it is very interesting material. If you show up and pay attention the tests are cake. I barely showed up at all in the first semester (enough I technically should have failed) and he was cool about it and I still managed to do alright.

Timmermann was a great professor. This class was a nice step away from all of my other harder classes. As long as you're not on you're phone in this class, you will get an A easily. 1 essay and 2 exams is all your grade is, and they're relatively easy. Lectures are relatively enjoyable and Timmermann often throws in jokes. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took histart 201, he does lecture for a while so if you're not interested in architecture or art you should probably pass on this one, his voice is fairly low and kind of a German/British accent that can potentially put you to sleep if you're one to doze off in class easily, He knows a lot about this subject and you will learn a lot in it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Timmermann is clearly an expert in the field of art history. I took the class as an easy, first semester seminar but it ended up being my favorite class. Attendance is pretty much mandatory, but it really isn't a problem because we only met twice a week. Lectures are clear, the guy is incredibly intelligent and workload is minimal.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Timmermann comes off as a rude professor but is very interested in historical art and architecture that I learned a lot in this class. I thought this class was going to be boring, but I've learned a lot and that made this class an easy A for me. If you study comparisons of art and make note cards on each monument, you will pass his tests fine.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy, graded on attendance, one essay, two exams. Fairly easy grader and very interested in the subject (Great Monuments). Most content can be found in the book though.
Very harsh grader that lectures heavily. Looking for specific information that is ripped from both the slides and the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's incredibly intelligent, and the material is interesting, but he was not always the best at organizing the lectures around developing themes. He gives you the exam topics ahead of time, so if you put the time in, you can easily do well. The term paper took a solid weekend, but an A or A+ was attainable.
Love this class. Good intro class for students who don't know much about art history. GSI was really nice. No tests and only 5 quizzes that you prepare for.

Lectures can get really boring but he's a cool professor who is willing to help. Not much reading at all but participation is a MUST. If you have more than 2 unexcused absences, he will ask you to withdraw from the class, no matter when it is in the semester. But cool class, would take again.

Prof Timmerman seems like such an awesome guy. He really got into the material for the last part of the course. Lectures are mandatory for attendance, which kind of sucks, but being that the material was really interesting I didn't mind going. My GSI was awesome and I loved visiting our museums. Recommend taking this class if interested in topic!

You can definitely tell that he's very interested in the subject (especially during the last few lectures) but, unfortunately he has a lot of required material to cover and not enough time. Lots of memorizing but it's not at all a difficult class. Most recent edition of text book isn't necessary. (I went with 7th and was fine. They're identical!)

Previously took HA 272 with an awesome professor in which I ironically worked less, listened more, and enjoyed much more than I did this course. GSI's are more helpful and informative than listening in lecture. Quizzes cover alot of material, so expect to spend hours memorizing dates, names and locations.

Lectures start out interesting but definitely peter out towards the end once you hit Christianity. A good guy and the class is pretty easy. The GSIs really make the class, though, and Jenny is an all-star who understands that it's an entry level course and to cater the material accordingly.

HORRENDOUS CLASS. If you are taking this just to fill a requirement, CHOOSE SOMETHING ELSE. The quizzes are absolutely atrocious. SO much work for a quiz. I have to study longer for these quizzes than I do for my 300-400 level EXAMS in other subjects. It's pure memorization, but a completely unreasonable amount of it.

Art History 101. The professor seemed very nice. His tests were not hard, and he really tried his best to give everyone the best grade possible. My GSI, Lehti, was AMAZING. She gave us candy, baked us cookies, put stickers on our tests (even fuzzy ones), and she was a great teacher. I highly recommend this interesting class and its teachers.

Professor Timmermann ia great.  He loves art and its history; though, sometimes the lectures are a bit dry he describes the art in interesting ways.  He LOVES when students participate so don't be afraid to raise your hand because otherwise he gets frustrated.  I never needed to go to office hours but I'm sure if you did he would love to talk

Here is the driest, most boring Professor I've ever had. In a tiny seminar, he hardly ever invited class discussion (that's pretty weird..) and also arbitrarily assigned us each different obscure paper topics and did not help me with my research. 10-12p SINGLE-spaced?! Ruined my interest in a potentially cool area of art history.

The grades are based on 2 papers and 2 exams. He grades the papers relatively easy but the exams are graded hard (he does give you the 2 essay questions). He expects you to memorize dates and names of cathedrals which all look alike. If you're interested in this kind of stuff then this class will be easy. Attendance is taken.

I took his freshman seminar class and it was VERY easy.  He is a pretty good prof.  Lectures can get a little boring at times, but it is a nice break from all your other stressful classes.  Very little hw and two big projects that were fairly easy.  If you needed help he would go out of ur way to help u.
Great proffesor. Knew the class material very well and was able to teach it clearly. Lectures were sometimes boring, but overall I was very interested in what I was learning.

He did not stick to the schedule. He would post readings a day or two before discussion boards were due. Often, the lectures did not cover the topics scheduled, and he has a tendency to ramble. Nice guy, but disorganized.

We are 3 lectures away from the end of the semester, there is no mention of what the final is, there has not been a single grade posted for any assignment outside of the midterm, and he doesn't reply to an email of it has any importance. Genuinely if I could select my courses again there is not a chance I'd do this course with him.
never take his classes.
Don't do it unless you absolutely have to

I'll agree that it's hard to tell what your grade is throughout the class, but I still loved this class. Idk why Bruce receives so many bad reviews, he's a very nice guy who teaches you a lot, his papers are easy (you can write them based on 1 paragraph you see in the books), & I took notes on my computer every class without a problem. No tests.

He does not grade anything you do all semester, leaving you guessing where you are in the class. You may think you are right on track, but the lack of feedback allows him to throw a curveball and give you a lower grade than you expected.
readings and class are completely unrelated. lectures have nothing to do with topic of class. do NOT waste your time on this class if they don't change the professor.
Oops, I meant Peru, not Brazil.  You'll learn a lot about chewing cocoa leaves and nothing else.

Being a linguistics major, I was excited for this class.  I had a great GSI and I enjoyed the readings.  The prof is completely useless, I didn't go to class and I got an A.  He's obsessed with the field work he did in Brazil in the '70's.  Lecture really has nothing to do with exams or paper.  Go to section and do the readings, you'll be fine.
He's the worst professor I've ever had! He talks in a very confusing, complicated, and roundabout way, and rambles on about things that are boring, like his obession with Quechua.
He is very obscure. Funny man but very easily gets off topic. Talks very quietly.

Enjoys yelling at students for having newspapers or computers in class; draws attention to it and wastes class time. Talks quietly, he makes everything really complicated. He doesn't have anything to do with your grade so make sure you have a good GSI.

Very wordy, obsessed with own field work. Lectures off-track the courses supposed topics, test questions are very abstract. NOT MEANT TO TEACH. I would highly suggest staying away from his lectures or classes.
completely useless, don't take any class with him, ever.
Obscurantist in speech, very clear in publication.  Deliberately confuses pupils.
Not helpful. arrogant. shouln't be tenured.
talks in binary; semiotics made erotic

Easy class, I never went to a single lecture or watched a single movie but ended up with an A. I used chatgpt for basically every single quiz and discussion as well as the final project and both exams

Professor Bodiford was fantastic. He explained all the material clearly and thoroughly and was clearly very passionate about the subject. As long as you attend classes, you should get an A with very little difficulty. It's an interesting class if you're interested in music and science fiction, my favorite class I've taken at UMich!
Good professor and interesting lectures if you enjoy the content, but he grades a little stricter than I thought

Great class, great professor, the sci fi section is phenomenal! I will say though, highly reccomend you attend lectures so you won't fall behind in contents, which honestly I didn't have an issue with because the lectures are so easy to digest.

Fantastic professor and a fantastic course. The lectures were quite interesting and I learned a ton. Assignments are easy too and the projects were actually quite fun to work on as well. My only gripe is he sometimes cuts off people answering questions, and then later gets upset when no one raising their hand to answer questions. But yea he's cool.
This guy is a chiller love him -- honestly a pretty interesting and unique class

The best class ever! I learned so much and the subject was fascinating. I looked forward to every class each week of the semester. The readings were quite heavy but interesting, and his testing was well done and manageable with a little work. I would definitely recommend taking his class!
Although class isn't too difficult, the man is condescending and stutters a lot. Would recommend taking the course when he's not teaching.

At first I thought James was super dull in his teachings, but as the class material gets more interesting so does he. There were a ton of hilarious moments in the class and I'd definitely take James again if I was doing another music class.

Easy and interesting class, decent professor, chill but kinda boring (though he did perform for us once). Lectures not needed to do well at all, just look over slides / assigned readings and know the songs. That being said make sure you participate in discussion and know the songs for the listening quizzes. Really not a hard class, good material
I love this man. Hilarious guy
He doesn't always really seem to know what he's talking about, but the class is super interesting.
Dude will be like this next concept is very very simple and explain that said concept and provide some overly complicated explanation.

Lectures are not clear for understanding the concepts, and he's bad at explaining things and doesn't know how to pace his lectures, spending too much time on unnecessary details while speedrunning through important ideas. Discussions are more helpful for preparing for exams as there are more visual illustrations than on the lecture slides.

I thought he was an ok lecturer, although discussions were far more helpful for preparing for the exam. He crammed a lot of things at the end before the midterm and final, which I didn't appreciate. Other than that, he's funny and seems like he genuinely cares about his students. Not a hard class, but there's a good amount of content.

Professor gave really great examples for every concept which made everything super easy to understand. EECS 484 had so much material covered it was insane, so the exams were quite difficult. The prof also offers connections and rec letters if you do well in the class (A+ or lecture participation). He was very likable and respected among the class.

Lecture and homework content is inconsistent leading to points off that could have been avoided. At one point, lecture and the way they graded exam was literally contridictary. They ended up not curving the class despite the median being much lower than a B+

DO NOT take EECS 484 if you have this professor. While he is a good person, his teaching style is simply bad. He makes the concepts more confusing than they are, and usually, the majority of the people do not understand his explanations. The professor and IAs taught different things, and in office hours, the IAs did not know the right answer. 1/10.

The examples are pretty hard to follow and prof speeds through hard content sometimes. It's not a good indicator when less than 75% of the class has raised their hand when he asks if students understood the content. Spent more time than necessary on basic SQL and not enough time on things like Normalization right before the midterm.

I felt this class was very doable and Prof Mozafari was very reasonable with the exams and grading. Second half of the semester was more difficult, but overall this was the first EECS class in awhile where I truly felt like I understood most of the content and enjoyed a lot of it. I feel like he's restructured some things since previous semesters.
Feels like making confusing concept much more confusing
All were perfect except sometimes lectures were too fast to follow.
Very good

WORST lecturer in Umich. NOBODY can understand his lecture. During his lecture, he usually spend 20 mins to show off his friend's companies. AVOID!!
Hint for other students who wants to take 484: If you get a not good prof like him, just go to watch Berkeley's cs162 recordings. This covers nearly the same stuff as 484 but 500% clear than 484.

Only writes a few words in slides when it comes up important things relevant to exam. Lectures are hard to understand. His ambitious explanation pushed me to watch recordings again painfully. Database is interesting and useful topic, BUT EECS 484 is definitely not.
If there is a time machine, I will drop this course without any hesitation.
Barzan is a very good guy, but I find his lectures a bit unclear to follow. Sometimes he goes over topics too fast (such as BCNF and 3NF), and it would be difficult to fully comprehend them.
Feel like wasting one semester working on something even the professor didn't care about.
Do not want to take classes with him anymore, awful.
Passionate about the course and takes feedback, but there are still a lot to improve. The slides are not self-explaining, had to go to textbook to look for better examples.
