Enthusiastic about the course but teaching has a lot of ground for improvement.
Barzan is a good guy. His words have been helpful to me both in academia and later on in the world of industry. Listen to what he has to say.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Slides are not well organized. Didn't explain things well. I prefer to stay at home and read textbooks instead of going to the lecture.

He did a good job explaining things during lectures. Homework and projects are at another level of difficulty. You have to do some research on your own in order to finish them. Autograders for the first two projects are awful (no feedback). Exams are the most horrific thing, if you can get half of questions right, you are in good shape.

Great class! I learned a lot. Interesting to students of any area because he focuses both on the details of database systems, but also on how one should approach a research problem. Very motivational and very respectful! The homework is somewhat difficult, but grading is fair and helpful. Mozafari is a great guy!
I do not want to take any more classes with him.
he hurt my feelings but made me 10x smarter.

5 homeworks, 1 exam. 
its difficult because most people only take one if any analysis course before this so understanding the first few concepts are difficult. Unpleasant person to deal with in office hours, especially if you're behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Textbook is INCREDIBLY HARD!
Even I have leant Stochastic Process,Stochastic Calculus,Real Analysis,Measure Theory,Functional Analysis, Operator Theory,Partial Differential Equations,Time Seris Analysis,Algebraic Topology,Point Set Topology,and Futures & Options,Mathematical Finance...
I STILL Find the textbook too difficult for Master Students.
Sharp mind, good at talking jokes, clear idea
Did not prepare for classes, used a previous professor's notes, very difficult exams, showed no respect to students.
Writing very messy, that shows little respect to the students. Also, doesn't explain things clearly, atfingall. Worst lecturer I have ever seen.

First, unfair grading among sections. Our section is graded way strictly than other sections. Second, tough lectures which go beyond the book, and you will find them useless for the exam. Third, weird accent.  He does not allow you to use laptops and iPad to read textbook in class. Very harsh person. Will not recommend.

She is a very impressive individual. We had a lot of online classes during the semester because she was busy with her other job. It's hard to prioritize her class if she doesn't prioritize it as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clarinda was unfairly disrespected by the UT' 28 cohort. While her lectures could be monotonous, they articulated new content well. Her case studies were by far the most interesting aspect of the course imo, and the grading was fair. That being said, the take home midterm is possibly the most poorly formatted assignment I've ever completed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ok professor overall. doesn't respond to emails whatsoever. unfair grading system. so many readings. VERY unclear directions almost always. great person very well-rounded person and a cool but bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the funniest and most engaging professors ever. There isn't a lot of work, which is great but you have to do well on those couple of assignments to do well in the class. But overall I'm so glad I took his class.
Amazing lecturer - prof H. is so engaging and also respectful of the content he teaches. Absolute legend of a professor and I don't think I've ever laughed more in a class.

Dr. Hollenbach is so goated. His lectures are very fun and entertaining while also informative. Attendance isn't required for lecture, but it is for section. Your grade is based off 3 exams, 2 writing assignments, and section attendance. Very easy class with practically no work. Exams are very easy and so are the writing assignments.
Attendance for the lectures isn't required but it is for the discussions. He is very funny and makes the content interesting, so the lectures aren't boring. I would definitely take him again!

I LOVED Professor Hollenbach!!! He always made his lectures engaging and pulled in meme references that made me laugh. The GSIs are also super helpful. You're graded on 3 exams (pretty easy if you do the study guide) and 2 writing assignments. I hope I can take another one of his classes!!

Prof Hollenbach was passionate about his studies and made them really interesting for us. He often connected his lectures to pop culture references, making them really enjoyable. Tests were straightforward if you studied the study guide. The only thing is that at times it was unclear exactly what we were to do for the writing assignments.

Pretty engaging lectures, and the tests are very easy if you attend or watch the recordings. Also go to office hours before the tests. He always finds a way to connect everything to his real life and media/pop culture, which is entertaining.

One of my favorite professors ever. I chose to watch the lectures rather than attend class, and as long you watch them, exams are a breeze. Super entertaining lectures and exams were exactly like the study guide. The way he teaches makes it so easy to retain information and it was genuinely interesting. Do the work and you'll get an A.

I, like most others, didn't attend lectures but would rewatch them for upcoming exams and was genuinely so entertained. He used a lot of pop-culture references making the content more bearable, and the exams were extremely fair. He's also very willing to accommodate exam changes and just great to talk to. Would honestly recommend to anyone

This guy is the goat. While I hate to admit I almost never showed up to lecture, I'd watch the lecture videos in my dorm and he made me laugh a couple times. Really energetic and the topics were decently interesting. Exams aren't too hard, but the released study guides are helpful and cover everything. Had cool selfies too and loved Ariana Grande

He is the best professor I've had so far!! He made seemingly boring topics so interesting, and I always looked forward to the lectures. Lecture's aren't mandatory, but you are missing out so much by watching the recorded lectures. He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. The expectation for the writing assignments and exams are clear.

iconic, love him, work is light, i got a b bc i never went to lecutres and barely watched the recordings to my fault lmao. there is a textbook and i never did the readings but im sure you could get an A without doing the readings.
My literal idol.
Prof Hollenbach is the best. His lectures are super engaging and he is clearly passionate about what he is teaching.

i would take any class with prof. hollenbach again in a heartbeat, hands down the best teacher i've ever had. super caring, and made the material incredibly interesting.

lecture attendance was optional but it was so enjoyable i never wanted to skip—prof hollenbach u could make millions as a podcaster

Prof. Hollenbach is a great lecturer, and his expectations are very clear. Easy SS credit. My one qualm is that he will talk rather loudly to his GSIs and answer phone calls throughout the entire exam sessions, which was distracting at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I ended up selecting this class last minute when filling out my course selections, but then this became my only class that I looked forward to. Hollenbach is an amazing professor with a great sense of humor and great lectures. We even watched an SNL skit, Drunk History, and watched some relevant movie trailers. He shows genuine care for students.

Easily one of the most enthusiastic professors I've encountered at UofM. He's always excited to teach us and has a great sense of humor. I highly recommend his class if you're interested in medical anthro or if you just need a social science credit. There is lots of reading, but very clear instructions on writing assignments and only 2 exams total.
Literally my favorite professor I've ever had. Made the classroom environment so welcoming and fun while also being educational. I would take a class with him again in a heartbeat!
HES SO SLAYYYYY I LOVEEE

BEST TEACHER EVER. I am a freshman BBA and I took Anthro101 my first semester and I loved him so much that I am taking TWO classes with him for second semester (im not even a anthro minor) he is so engaging and makes you want to show up to class. readings are helpful for free response but not required. exams are easy if you study. TAKE THIS PROF.

LITERALLY THE BEST TEACHER. I am a freshman business major and I took Anthro101 my first semester and I loved him so much that I am taking TWO classes with him for second semester (im not even a anthro minor). he is so engaging and makes you want to show up to class. you do not need to do the readings at all. exams are easy. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!

He was SO funny and kept his lectures engaging always. He provides a study guide for every exam, so I made a quizlet with everything on each exam's study guide and always did really well. You do not have to go to lectures, but you definitely need to go to discussion sections, as they are honestly a large part of your grade. 100% recommend.

Hollenbach is an engaging lecturer, but he has millennial humor so beware. Ur graded on 3 exams (no final), and 2 writing assignments but none of it was hard. As long as you watch the lecture videos before an exam and look through the study guide he posts you're good to go. I didn't buy the textbook and I still got all the information I needed.

Professor Hollenbach was literally my fav professor to date! He is so passionate and socially aware of what he is teaching and why it is essential. I enjoyed going to lecture everyday and found myself so engaged and laughing during every lecture.

Professor Hollenbach's lectures were a joy to attend; they were funny, engaging, and interesting, and you can clearly tell he loves anthropology. The exams were a breeze, the writing assignments felt a bit tedious but were still pretty easy nonetheless. My GSI was also a pleasure. Overall, a great class and great lecturer!

He made all of his lectures super engaging and made even the most boring topics funny (he's very culturally aware and I enjoyed seeing Moo Deng in lecture). My only gripe with this class would be that I bought the textbook but honestly didn't use it at all (got a good grade anyways). But 10/10 professor! He clearly wants his students to succeed.

Dr. Hollenbach is a great guy and obviously wants his students to succeed. You can get an A in this class without going to lecture, but he tries to make class fun and interesting. Engage with your GSIs-especially for the papers, and you'll excel.
He was a great professor! He made the material really easier to understand, and gave a clear outline of learning material. He was always willing to help, and give advice!

One of Michigan's greatest professors. Professor Hollenbach has the unique ability to create an engaging and personable class while still effectively communicating content. Taking this course with him was a pleasure, and I encourage anyone who has the opportunity to take a course with him to do so. We love you, Professor!

Professor H is truly special. He cares about his students and always tries to make lectures interesting and engaging. He's hilarious, responsive, and intelligent. This class was quite easy and lecture based. Also, he hands out extremely thorough study guides for exams - he wants you to succeed! I cannot recommend him enough!

Professor Hollenbach was one of the most engaging professors I have had thus far. I am a CS major and didn't think I would be interested in Anthropology, but he puts a lot of effort into his lectures to make them fun and it made me love the class. He was also incredibly helpful in office hours. Overall I would highly recommend ANTHRCUL101 with him.
Amazing class! Professor Hollenbach is the best professor that I have had at Michigan!

Hollenbach is super charismatic and easy to understand. Papers are harder than exams, but still relatively easy. I only went to lecture in person on exam days (3x total in the whole semester) and still got an A in the class. His study guides are direct outlines of what to expect on exams.

Ben was by far my favorite professor at UM and im hurt that I cannot take another class with him. He is incredibly easygoing and loves everyone so much. He makes class an incredibly inviting, fun, and comfortable environment. He genuinely needs to be the framework for how every single professor should teach, ive never loved a prof more

He's amazing, super funny and even though lectures were not mandatory, I enjoyed going. The topic itself was sometimes boring but he made up for it. Class is based on 3 exams, 2 papers, and discussion participation. If you follow the study guide, the exams should be fine (mc and frq).I will genuinely miss him blasting music at 10 am
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Hollenbach is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He clearly has a gift for making people enjoy their time around him. Anyone that doesn't rate him a 5/5 needs to get their vitals checked.

Dr. Hollenbach is so great! He makes lectures very fun to attend even though they aren't mandatory. I would definitely take Anthrcul 101 with him if you have the chance. The only thing is that the entire class is based on 3 exams and 2 papers, so you need to be prepared and do well on those to get a good grade.
Very approachable and well-rounded lecturer, definitely incorporates elements of humor in class, study guides provided for exams. A class with him will leave you better than you started.

Professor Hollenbach was fantastic! Very interesting and intriguing lectures. I am not an anthropology major, but he made the subject very interesting for me. I loved going to lecture although it's not required, and his lectures were funny and interesting almost always. The textbook is said to be required, but I did not use it almost at all.

PROF H IS THE BEST PROF EVER. Took his first year seminar on "Cults, Coercion, and Kool-Aid" and it was my favorite. Very informative and manageable class on cults and New Religious Movements. Prof H is so funny and you can tell he really cares for his students. If you get the chance to take ANY of his courses, DO IT. He is the best.
Incredible! Could not recommend more, literally considering minoring in Anthropology after this lol. Study guides for exams made them much less stressful and papers weren't too horrible.

I LOVE HIM. He is so funny, his lectures are always HILARIOUS, and he really cares about Anthropology. If you need the RE credit, are interested in Anthropology, or just want a fun (easy a) class, TAKE IT WITH HIM

The class was very easy the exams were mostly multiple-choice. The papers were fun and not graded harshly. He's a great lecturer and makes the class fun. If you need the RE credit I definitely recommend this class.

This material was really easy to grasp and Prof. H makes class fun for students. He uses a textbook, but almost all test material and textbook material is covered in lecture, so it's pretty straightforward. He always plays music before class and is excited to see everyone.

Professor Hollenbach is so awesome! You can tell he's definitely passionate about what he teaches. The class content is pretty easy, so it's not too difficult to do well in this class and Prof. Hollenbach manages to keep things interesting when it comes to content that could get dull. I would honestly get sad if I ever had to miss a lecture of his!

Professor Hollenbach is AMAZING! He is clearly passionate about what he is teaching, and his lectures are super engaging because of this. Not only is the material super interesting, but Prof Hollenbach is super funny and always makes lecture a good time. Grading wise, his expectations are clear, and he wants everyone to succeed!

take. this. class. you won't regret it and he is an amazing teacher that is passionate about his field of study. very clear on information needed to know for tests and his lectures are not boring at all. if you ever have the chance, take the class.

Prof H is SUCH an amazing professor!! Literally my favorite prof I've had at this school so far. He cares about his students SO much, is super engaging and energetic every lecture, has very fair exams, is very relatable, inclusive, kind, humorous, and makes everyone look forward to attending his class. Really an incredible professor.

Entertaining lectures (also recorded). Amazing prof with a great personality. Graded on 2 essays: a 3-page "thick description", and a 4-5 page ethnographic interview. Kind of tedious, but isn't too difficult. 3 tests, no final exam. Tests have really detailed study guides, so as long as you do it and study that, you'll do great.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had here!! He keeps the lectures interesting and the exams are very fair. I would reccomend Prof. H for any class

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. His lectures are very engaging and he can be pretty funny. Has the students best interests at heart. Exams are pretty easy if you show up to lecture and at least skim the readings. Discussion can be boring, but overall great class.

I absolutely love Prof. H. I took this class as my race and ethnicity requirement and ended up really enjoying it. His passion shines through his lectures and even though the content may not be the most interesting, he somehow finds a way to make lectures engaging. I would love to take another class with Prof. H!!!!

Easy intro class for R/E credit. Most of the content is common sense and it's very easy to get an A in the class. Lectures are recorded and also very engaging- he's really funny tbh. There's a final writing project but it's pretty simple and graded very leniently. I'd consider taking another class of his, he's a great professor.

Professor Hollenbach was wonderful! Although his lectures were not required, I always went because they were enjoyable and he is very passionate about what he teaches. The best professor I have had at Michigan. He also provided very helpful studying tools and information prior to exams, so the criteria was clear. Definitely take his classes!
My favorite professor ever.  Wish he taught more classes

Professor Hollenbach was an amazing and funny lecturer! His classes were fun and intriguing, while also having a lot of information. The tests had clear guidelines, and if you attended lecture or studied, you are sure to do extremely well. Amazing professor!

HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD OMG. TOTALLY RECOMMEND ANY CLASS HE TEACHERS, ESPECIALLY ANTHRCUL 158 (if it's running - its about cults). Seriously, the best professor ever, so funny, relatable, kind, and understanding.
Really good teacher, made material easy to understand and fun. My only regret is purchasing the textbook, it wasn't used at all so I wouldn't recommend buying it.
You know exactly to expect on exam day, and Prof Hollenbach puts in a lot of work to try and make the lectures interesting. He's a nice guy.

I loved Prof. Hollenbach! He is incredibly nice and you can tell he cares about his students. Super easy to get a good grade in this class so long as you try. Says textbook is required, but I hardly used it except for one paper. 3 exams with clear study guides, and one longer paper from the whole semester. Definitely recommend for R&E requirement!

reviews.comment: He was my favorite professor, he really cares about his students and is passionate about anthropology. I loved showing up to class because I knew I would end up laughing and having a good time. His lectures were very interesting, and his tests were extremely fair. I would recommend taking his class, as he is a wonderful professor.

The GOAT! If you take anthro, please take it with hollenbach. He actually makes anthropology, a relatively boring subject, extremely interesting through his engaging lectures. He also holds review sessions the night before exams where he basically gives you a couple questions on the exam.
He's so chill and he really tries to make his lectures interesting, I love him fr

He's really funny and puts a lot of care into his lectures and class overall, though his fixation with chainsaws was a little unsettling.

Highly recommend taking ANTHRCUL 101 with him. It's easy and enjoyable.
Love him, made mom jokes and helped make somewhat boring material super interesting! Best professor, definitely recommend taking his lectures!
Turned what would have been a somewhat boring class into really fun lectures. Loved him.
One of my favorite professors! Would recommend this class to everyone
The professor's discussion on chainsaw is funny.

Professor Hollenbach is very likable and funny. Even though lecture was over 400 people, he made sure to hold review sessions the night before exams. He always ensured office hours were available for students.

Super interesting lectures, Hollenbach was funny and very likable. His lectures were interesting and very understandable, and he did review sessions the night before exams that students could ask questions in.

reviews.comment: Dr Hollenbach was one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He always made sure to make his lectures entertaining.

Super funny professor who uses a lot of memes and pop culture references to convey important themes and messages. Super friendly and approachable. Engaging. Super cool content in Cultural Anthropology. 10/10/.

His lectures are entertaining and contain exactly what you'll need to know for exams. Study guides for exams are very specific, and if you use them you will do well on the exams. He likes to sprinkle in jokes and memes and uses lots of pop culture examples for concepts which is fun as well. Low workload for the class also.

Took this class to get LSA's race and ethnicity credit, and it was great! Would definitely recommend, exams are straightforward and there are few assignments. Professor Hollenbach is great, he is very personable and made going to lectures entertaining because of how eager and fun he is. He made everyone laugh every lecture.

Professor Hollenbach is awesome. He is passionate about teaching and his love for anthropology shows. His lectures are engaging and funny. He uses references that young people will get and really tries to engage with his students. He hosts review sessions before tests, which are super helpful. Anthcul 101 is an easy and fun class 10/10 recommend.
I loved Professor Hollenbach! He was so funny and caring and made lectures really fun. Some of the readings were long but we weren't overloaded and exams were super easy. I'm gonna miss his class!

Professor Hollenbach is a fantastic professor, probably the best I have had at UMich so far. His lectures are funny and very engaging. The tests are really easy and as long as you study for a couple of hours, you shouldn't have an issue. Overall, would highly recommend it to anyone who wants an easy class where you'll actually learn.
Great professor! Although lectures are not mandatory, they are very interesting and enjoyable.

Great class for race & ethnicity requirement. Professor Hollenbach is very lively, passionate, and he explains the material very clearly. Although, be prepared for lots of corny millennial jokes. The readings are simple, only 3 easy exams, and one project. I definitely recommend taking this class with Hollenbach.

Professor Hollenbach is amazing! If you still need to fulfill the race and ethnicity requirement for LSA, take his class!! I found ANTHRCUL 101 super easy, and it was actually a fun class.

Textbook is supposedly required but you don't need it for any assignments, and just studying the lecture slides for exams works well too. He's very clear about what you need to know and what will be on the exams.

Professor Hollenbach is a fairly new to umich, but I think he was amazing. He was actually so funny in lecture, and his slides were self-made and really easy to follow along with. This is an intro class, so the content wasn't terribly difficult. The exams were so easy you just had to follow the study guide. Highly recommend for first years.

reviews.comment: His lectures were really interesting and his exams were relatively easy

Take this class! The class was genuinely interesting and Bender is a great lecturer imo. He blends humanities with science and is very engaging. Ignore his low overall rating - many of his poor reviews are from 2018 or earlier. Some of his exam questions are a little specific but they mirror the practice exams he gives out.

reviews.comment: This class was a good natural science credit course!!! Your grade is 4 26-question exams all added together or your score on the optional final, imo i think the exams were very fair and if you lock in studying for like two days your should do well!! Also Prof. Bender is so CUTIE in his vests and ties lectures were recorded!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you fail this class, you probably do not have the work ethic to attend umich. This is a bare-bones lecture and exam class, every question on the exam is well-covered in both the readings and lectures. Your final grade is an average of exams 1-4, or you can take a cumulative exam over the whole semester and your grade on that is your final grade.

Optional final, 4 exams overall that make up ur final grade. He talks a lot which can make the basic lectures confusing but overall an easy natural science course! provides lecture recordings and make-ups for exams. Go to class and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bender is an absolute gem. He is an very educated man who has a deep, unwavering passion for the things he teaches about. DISREGARD ANYONE who gives this professor lower than a 5. The questions are multiple-choice and extremely straightforward (Ex: What is the name of the bacteria that causes ____?). Take his class. Love him.

Professor Bender is a nice guy, but as someone who attended all of the lectures and did all of the readings I still found the exams to be surprisingly hard. He tests over very specific little details that you wouldn't know to study for beforehand. The 4 exams are the only grades in the course so you have to do well on them if you want a good grade

This class has been incredibly interesting and easy at the same time. Personally, I did not attend all of the lectures, but all you really need to do is read the text that he gives you about the disease you will be covering and then take notes for those lecture slides. There are 4 exams only that are very easy if you looked at the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bender is a great professor, and will not move on until every person understands a topic,especially the more scientific topics.The EASIEST 3 ns credits you'll ever receive, as there are only 3 lectures in the semester that are scientific. If you do the readings and attend lectures,high school classes are harder than this one. Exams are a breeze

If you read anyone saying that the exams are hard because they as little minute details - disregard that. At its core, the course uses an old fashion lecture and testing teaching method, and the topic is the history and biology of diseases. You have to study for exams. But his lectures are so memorable and excellent, you will prob just need to skim

This class is a hybrid between a natural science and humanities course. As a non-stem major, there was only one lecture I had to rewatch, as it focused on more complex biology (but if you've taken a bio class, it won't be hard). His lectures were clear and the exams were simple if you attended/watched the lectures. He's flexible with exams too!

I absolutely loved bio118! It gives such a real-world view to the diseases we all know about today. Bender is brilliant and kind, but either going to class or watching the lectures is a must if you want to get a good grade. So happy I took guis natural science course

Maybe Professor Bender taught differently in previous years, but I really think he delivered lecture material clearly and the 4 exams were simple enough if you attended/watched the lectures and had good recall. He was flexible with exams during the semester I took the class which was really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't understand all of the negative reviews on this page. Bender is a great lecturer and this class is an easy A imo. Grade is based on 4 exams which are not difficult if you do ALL the textbook readings (has non-lecture info), skim slides, and have a working memory. If you can cram the day/night before exams, then this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bender is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He will not help you to understand material, and is completely disrespectful when you're struggling. The actual material is very interesting, but he will test on the most arbitrary details and never on broad concepts. I left the class knowing obscure names, but nothing about AIDS.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. It is not an easy A. Questions consisted of minor details that were irrelevant. Your grade is based entirely on the exams, so it is hard to do well if you don't remember every detail. Many of the questions were never discussed in class. Take something else for natural science.

Tests were non-specific and arbitrary. Some questions were never discussed in class; he will expect people to memorize fragments of his readings posted online as every word has the possibility of being on an exam. About 10 questions were truly related to biology. He had no method of teaching; considering the discussion on fist-ing for 15+ minutes.

Professor Bender is a nice guy, but not a good professor. His tests are very unreasonable and expect you to memorize the most random/irrelevant details. The questions do not test big picture concepts. For example, one question was "What time period did Typhoid Mary infect?"If you have a near perfect memory, you will probably do fine in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most absurd exams that test on minute details instead of the broad picture. If you are good at remembering small details you will do well. Not test of intelligence just memorization. Additionally, most of the exam questions have tricks to them. The class is boring and should have a component other than four exams.

A great course with an awful professor. I loved the material and went to every single lecture, taking detailed notes and studying weeks before the exam and I got an 89%. My friend never went to class and got a 96%. The course is all about luck. You should pray that you happen to remember the most pointless details because those are the questions.

This is a great class for anyone who needs to fulfill the NS requirement. He asks lots of random questions on exams so make sure you do the readings or come to lecture. You really need to have a clear understanding of the material to do well on the tests. I try to figure things out without his help because his explanations are always long/unclear

Professor Bender was an awesome lecturer and explained things very well. Go to as many lectures as you can and read the powerpoints along with as many of the readings you can do and you should get an A. I barely studied for the 2nd exam and got a C, so I had to go all out for the last two to get the grade I wanted, don't make the same mistake.

Easiest class you can possibly take at Michigan. It is also interesting and has a little something for everyone: history, public policy, and some science. With that being said, don't take if you're a science major... the dumbed down explanations he gives for mechanisms of action are cringy.
awesome prof
Good professor, easy class for natural science credit while being interesting if you actually listen and go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Bender is probably one of the most kind hearted people I have ever met. The class is super easy if you are just looking to get a NS credit.

This class was the easiest that I'll probably take at the university. All you have to do is  pay attention and look at the old exams he provides to study for tests. If you are not interested in science but need NS credit, take this class. Bender does a good job of making scientific concepts understandable in lamens terms.

Professor Bender was great. This was his class that he started so he was obviously very passionate about it. It's a good science class for people who don't know a lot about biology. The material was very relevant and very interesting. I don't know how it is with the new professor, but I highly recommend this class.
Really interesting material.  Great professor.  Highly recommended.

SUCH a nice guy. Yes, his tests are confusing and seemingly pointless as relates to the material covered in class, but all you need to do to "study" is look over the lecture slides and take all the old practice exams. 95% of the questions come from old tests, which he posts on CTools at the beginning of the semester.

Very disappointing class. The topic and information has so much potential and Bender butchered it with simplistic explanations and random questions on exams. He focused on the minute (ie llamas=indigenous to the Americas) rather than the overall relevance (the link between domestication and sickness). This made exams  frustrating. Horrible class.

It's not that the material he covers is difficult, it's that he relates it to things that have NOTHING to do with biology. Instead of giving you dates, he'll ask you what period in US History it happened in (i.e. industrial revolution, new deal, World Wars, etc?) tricky tricky man.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. Tests are in now way reflect what is taught and only measure your ability to memorize random facts and numbers. He uses terms like "magic" to explain biological processes. A complete waste of time and not even easy to get an A in. Bender is terrible.

Terrible, terrible professor. Tests generally center around whatever random information he finds interesting and not biology. Some of his classes have a disclaimer that remind students that his material is oversimplified and not true. Tons of stupid history questions. Studying is essentially useless because irrelevant information is on the tests.

My boyfriend took the exam after I brought it home (yes you get to keep them afterwards) and got the same grade I did (3 wrong out of 27) without any knowledge of the material. They're not hard if you look at the lecture slides, but he does throw in random history questions :( By the way--first large animals in north and south america=llama. *shrug
This guy is kind of awkward, but he is SO nice and entertaining. You can tell he's passionate about his job.

I'll look down my row of seats, and not one person will be awake. He will BORE YOU TO TEARS. Seriously. I've had some of the nicest naps of my life in that class. Oh, and his tests are confusing. He sets you up for failure.

Don't take this class. Bender administers tests that just try to confuse students. You can study for weeks and still receive a bad grade because his test questions are so irrelevant. My guess is he an old cynical bitter man who failed his own bio class. It's not worth it. Trust me. Stay away

Professor Bender is a joke. He is extremely vain and not willing to listen to his students at all. I was very interested int he subject material but couldn't stand his lectures. They are boring, dull and at 8:30 in the morning. Bender makes a lot of rules that just aim to boost his ego and make it so he can do less work, and his test are impossible
Professor Bender is AWESOME. He is nice and helpful and gets you very interested.

This seemingly easy class is a joke because he tests you on information that is not relevant and tries to trick you constantly on the exams.  I did not learn much and sometimes regret taking the class.  Bender's exact words, "Am I going to test you on information that we have not talked about...of course!!!"

Take this class if you're interested in infectious disease or microbiology. It's an easy A+. Bender is pretty cool, and explains most things pretty well. Don't miss lecture because he says A TON that's not on the slides. Good practice exams, but some tricky exam questions. Discussion is optional, but good clarification of material and reading help.

I loved this class, and I am not a fan of science. I really learned a lot about AIDS and other diseases (a lot of things that I didn't know). His test questions are kind of tricky, but the class is so interesting. I actually went to every lecture, he's really animated.

Professor Bender makes a 500-student, 8.30am class really interesting!  His lectures are always easy to understand because they usually have a story-like format.  He goes through the lecture slides pretty quickly (which has led to several early releases from class) so I suggest printing out slides beforehand.  Tests are easy if you study.

Take this class!  Bob Bender is the man!  Most of his lectures were interesting, he was clear, and the material was pretty cool.  I can count the number of times I went to discussion on one hand, I didn't do much of the readings, and unless I bomb the next test, I'm going to get an A.  If you needs NS credits and don't like science- take this class
keeps it interesting, very aproachable

I really hate Biology, but I really like this class. He teaches as if the students do not know anything, which can be good to establish basics. Also good if you pay attention in class: a fearful freshman can take this. Expect to do some reading, but he is an interesting man.

Bender has a huge ego problem and refuses to listen to anything that he does not think is right.  His exams are very tricky and do not follow the reviews.  Lectures are long and boring and very hard to keep your attention.  I would not reccomend him to anyone at any point.

It's an easy class, so if you want to get rid of your science requirement without having to learn any...science, then take it.  The tests are pretty easy, but also really pissed me off.  A typical question is "who was president when this disease happened?"  see what i mean about not having anything to do with science?
Great for non science people. The GSI are very helpful and easy to acess Overall, I enjoyed the class the material was interesting and clear.

My advice: never ever go to lecture or discussion. Read his powerpoints, go to reviews. Don't read the book, don't take his tests. Just study hard for the final and you'll do great. He gives old test questions, that eventually mimic the upcoming test questions. I had a C+ in the class, then took the final and got a B+.

Bender may seem entertaining at first but it is a very fake fron.  This is truly a bitter man who in my estimation brings nothing to the table, they should just set up a website with some readings and multiple choice exams because that is all you will get with Bender.  Bender should be avoided.

Definitely an easy science course, so it's great for people who don't want a lot of stress.  Bender is quite quirky, but usually his lectures were entertaining.  Be sure to pay attention to all of his random facts, because he likes to throw a bunch of those on the exam.  Go over old exams because he just rewords most of his old questions.

This class was not as easy as I expected. However, Bender gives you a chance to earn a better grade in the class through an optional final. This class was very interesting, and I feel like I learned a great deal. He is quite entertaining as a lecturer. Discussion was optional, so I never went.

Sure Bender is a little quirky, but the lecture were actually quite interesting and if you go through the practice exams you will know half the questions on his test. Good readings and the easiest 4 credit class I have taken. I highly recommend.

Just read the books, and the lectures and you'll do fine. Never went to lecture did fine on most of the exams. He gives you a chance to make it up in an optional final. Helpful tip: Expect the uexpected on his tests he can throw anything he stated on it.
I hated this class...it was boring, the tests were impossible, and he was confusing. Don't take it.

This class sounded so interesting, so I took it. My mistake. The material is interesting, but his multiple choice tests are impossible. You could study for hours and still not know what is going on. My advice: dont waste you time studying...or even better yet dont take the class!!
This was not an enjoyable class
The class is interesting, but the tests are a little unfair. But overall not a bad class.
No Comments
He takes interesting material and kills it by administering nitpicky multiple choice exams.  it's nice that the section is optional but overall the class is dumbed down by the tests.  don't take it
No Comments

Professor Boland clearly cares about students' understanding and takes time to explain concepts thoroughly. He's also genuinely funny, which keeps lectures engaging. The main downside is that he doesn't provide practice exams or much structured exam prep, so you have to study more independently. Overall, I learned a lot and would recommend him.

Math 425 with Prof. Boland is hard but worth it. Lectures are optional with no recordings, so go to class! He gives great note skeletons. Exams are tough and 70% of the grade, but he curves at the end of course, so don't panic. HW is long and difficult but infrequent. He connects concepts to the real world, cares, and is funny. Would take again!
He knows what he's talking about

He connected all topics to real-life examples, which made class fun. He didn't really explain topics that well in class - you are expected to do the readings/videos in order to learn in-depth. But, he was always accessible during office hours and genuinely made an effort to connect with you!

Pat does an amazing job of creating a light-hearted and constructive learning environment! This was my first calculus class at Michigan, and I am confident that this gave me a good foundation going forward. Highly recommend taking his section of Math 115 if you can!
Super sincere guy, great teaching pace and lecture style. Would definitely recommend

Highly recommend taking Boland for 216. He is a great lecture and makes class interesting. Lecture and recitation do not have mandatory attendance, but both are basically necessary for doing well in the course. Boland knows what he is talking about and is very accessible with office hours as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Boland truly made differential equations very interesting. He's very passionate about the subject and always found a way to apply what we were learning to real life. I would highly recommend taking him for this class.

Professor Boland is easily the best professor I've had at UMich. He's an engaging lecturer, helpful outside of class, and is overall a really great guy. He helped me through a very hard time in my college career and while my performance in this course wasn't what I had hoped, he was very reassuring and available to help me out.
MATH 275. Intro to cryptology. discussion based class. Interesting class. Good teaching style. Good professor. 2 mid + 1 final.
Great person and makes lectures as interesting as they can be while still teaching very well. My favorite professor by far.

Math 351, not 389. Pat is simply the most phenomenal instructor you will probably ever encounter in the math dept. The course is IBL, but Pat incorporates mini-lectures that kickstart everyone into fully participating. Homeworks were plenty, but I learned so much every lecture.

Thanks Pat!
Great teacher, take a class with him if you can.
Awesome professor and deeply cares about student understanding.
Pat is the absolute best and truly cares for his students -- he is always willing to go above and beyond for others. 116 was tough for me but we always did what he could to help me.

I had Pat as a lecturer for Math 216 last semester at umich. He was an amazing professor and was very good at explaining complex topics for a very difficult class. He was also very understanding and always available during his office hours or on the deadline of a particularly difficult homework. As a lecturer, I can't praise him enough.

I took Math 216 with Boland back in the W2018 semester. He was (and most likely still is) an excellent teacher. As a grad student wrapping up my Master's in a different field, I still remember Patrick's teaching fondly. If he teaches a math course you need to take, sign yourself up.

Pat is the first actual Math Professor I have ever had in my life. He is chill with emergencies and his goal is to let students explore more about Math instead of just receiving an A. His IBL lectures are productive and you will never get bored. More importantly, Pat encourages students to think deeper and have a mindset of a mathematician.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Math 216 is a very conceptually challenging course that requires many hours of work. Professor Boland provides great lectures and explains the course topics clearly and concisely in a way that shows you how to solve the specific problems in the course. He is very accessible outside of lecture and responds quickly via email.

If Pat is teaching ever teaching this class again, try and take it with him. Excellent proffesor, knows how to guide a conversation in such a way as to both make learning easy, and also make learning very deep. It is remarkable how many different ideas in mathematics we were able to cover in just 1 semester.

I took Math 116 with Dr. Boland last semester. He is by far the best math teacher I've had at this school. A lot of what he teaches he will show visual representations of some sort which really helped me to understand some of the tougher concepts of that class. As long as you go to class and do the hw you'll get a good grade.

Math 116 was a hard course for me, but I don't think I would have passed without Dr Boland. He is a fantastic lecturer and really loves teaching. He is the first professor at Michigan that I actually have had a real relationship with. A good grade is very possible, but consistent practice outside of class is necessary in order to achieve that.

Patrick is somewhat a good instructor. He cares a lot about his students, and he tries his best to answer all the questions he receives during his office hours. I can't lie though, that his classes are somewhat boring, just like other math classes at the U-M. I really hope the math department could find a way to deliver math courses interestingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best wingman out there ��

Pat made Calc 2 fun and worth taking. He really cares about his students and has a lot of availability for office hours. He always relates whatever topic we're working on to the real world, which I really appreciated. We were up doing work on the board a lot, which I think is a great learning tool and gets the blood flowing. Pat's a really nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 116 was not an easy class for me. Despite this, I was very thankful to have Pat as my professor. He wants to see all of his students succeed and he puts in a lot of effort. He was accessible outside class through office hours which was great. When you take this class make sure you do the readings before Pat's lectures. His RI accent is also great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm going to be honest, this class is rough. But I'm so glad I had the chance to take it with Pat. He's a super smart and funny guy, and cares about his students understanding the material rather than just reciting definitions and algorithms from the textbook. Definitely wish I could take more classes with Pat and his heavy Rhode Island accent.
By far, Pat is the best professor I've had at Umich. His lectures are very clear and organized so that you leave knowing what the most important topics to review are. Highly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: MATH 216 is a conceptually tough course at UofM, but Professor Boland makes the subject matter very intuitive. The exams are challenging and will test your ability to apply fundamental definitions of things. Professor Boland also sends out emails summarizing class material that really help you pick out the most important topics in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pat's a great guy! This course is unecessarily hard, but Professor Boland make lectures enjoyable. He's also super accessible outside of class and often sends emails with useful resources. Also, his Rhode Island accent is amazing: "OOOOOoooscillating System!"

Pat is great! His teaching style may not be for everyone, but he knows what he's doing and is very open to questions. He's willing to admit mistakes and is sure to follow up with an email if he makes even the slightest error in class. Overall fun class with Pat!

I LOVE Pat!!! He encourages students to interact with each other and write on the board (my favorite part of his class). He also encourages making mistakes and learning from them. Class always consisted of a wide variety of examples, including hilarious personal ones. He's a really approachable professor and so kind. STUDY FOR THE EXAMS, THOUGH.

Pat is the best professor I've had during my 1st year. He is a great professor for diff eq, funny, fair, and clear. His office hours are extremely helpful and he is very approachable. He is also very enthusiastic, which made MATH 216 much more tolerable. Definite recommendation!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great diff. eq. professor! His enthusiasm during the class is what made the class easier to engage in and understand. Patrick also explains material well, and if you don't understand it he will try additional examples to help you. One of the most fair professors I've met and he is also really nice and easy to talk to. Go to office hours, it helps!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely nice guy, gives good feedback, personable, helpful
Very easy to talk to, great explanations. You can tell he really cares about seeing his students do well. I really enjoyed working with him.

Teaches using lots of examples, lots of in-class participation and writing on the boards. Very few "lecture-style" classes. Lots of chances to explain and collab in class. Tries his best to explore answers that are incorrect, not just say "wrong".
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class itself was very difficult, but Boland was always able to help. He always responded to emails right away. He does assign very long and difficult homework, but you start getting the hang of it by the end. The tests were very tough, but there was a very generous curve. The lectures were very helpful, especially his many examples.

Boland is a great diff. eq. professor. Very good at explaining concepts, and picks very good examples that have real applications and really make you appreciate the topic. He may not seem very approachable, but he is always willing to help, and go to office hours to get to know him. He even let me make up a midterm on a Saturday. Highly recommend!
He made the class very enjoyable and easy to follow along. Would definitely take more math classes from him in the future.

Pat is concise. He instills confidence into your mathematic abilities. Pat always encourages students to find real-world applicability within the material covered in class, which seems rare among professors here. Overall, Pat is fair, patient, and smart; my level of understanding within calculus has increased dramatically since I've taken his class

Pat's an awesome lecturer! Lecture is dragged out sometimes, but only because he goes through so many practice problems. Math 115 is a pretty tough class, and even tougher to get a good grade in, but Pat is very good at explaining concepts, and always answers questions very clearly. He makes sure everyone understands, unlike my past math professors
Pat is the best!! You need to take his class if you can!! He is so funny in the most fantastic way. He is a great teacher who will do whatever he can to help you succeed in the class!
Best math teacher i have had at the school.  Legendary.

It was his first time teaching the course and I think he did a good job. Made an attempt to connect with this students. Had a consistent schedule. (quizzes Weds. HW Fri.) Very organized and to the point. Very flexible Off Ho.  I would definitely take him again.
Pat is extremely helpful, especially for the difficult course.

I took History 262/Amcult 263 (cross-listed), and while the class was fairly easy, Professor Berrey's lectures were somewhat tough to follow. Mainly just narrations with minimal texts or images. If you're not someone who can actually learn from listening (without written stuff to accompany), this might not be the class for you.

Awesome prof. He doesn't record lectures but I've never struggled to go to his class, since it's super engaging. He's a very easy going grader who just wants to see that you did the readings and showed up, which are also very interesting. Very knowledgeable and respectful on everything he talks about. 

Take his classes!

Professor Berrey was one of the best professors I had last semester. While his lectures weren't mandatory, as he posts the slides on Canvas, I would still recommend attending, as he provides more in-depth information that will not be shown on the slides. The lectures were overall fascinating, and I looked forward to going to them each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super nice and inclusive guy, always makes you feel ready to ask questions and goes out of his way to gas everyone in the class up. Lectures were pretty engaging too.

Professor Berrey was great! He taught very engaging and interesting lectures. American Culture 374 was amazing - probably one of my favorite classes that I have ever taken. I definitely recommend for those who have an interest in American History or even just music. If you attend lecture/discussion and turn in assignments, an A is very achievable.

Prof. Berrey is one of the best professor's I've had. His lectures are so engaging and he makes it clear that he knows so much about the 60's. I absolutely loved this class and I'm so sad it is over. Take it if you ever have the chance. Grading isn't bad at all, two exams and an oral history project, but overall it is worth it.

Professor Berrey is amazing! It's clear he enjoys teaching this class, and his lectures were always very informative! There's a decent amount of readings, but they were usually interesting and easy enough to get through. I would definitely recommend this course if you have any interest in the subject!!

Great professor, super knowledgeable. Loved how this class was music forward which made it more engaging. The only thing is that if you miss a lecture, you're not in a great spot because he posts the slides a week or two later, they only really have pictures, and there aren't any lecture recordings. Otherwise he's a great lecturer on a cool topic!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was pretty good. There is a lot of reading but honestly, I never did it and it was fine. Start the big paper early, you'll thank yourself. The midterm and final aren't bad and easy to prep for. Section is mandatory but easy enough to go to and participate in. Overall not a bad class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and very accommodating. My GSI was a difficult grader, but lectures are chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Berrey is awesome. He is very accommodating to various issues that can occur and is a realistic person. His lectures are interesting and he uses very engaging music. I would definitely take this for RE and HU. If you participate in discussion and pay attention, not hard to get god grades. He wants everyone to do well.

Great professor. I never even showed up to a lecture. You just need to show up to discussion sections and reasonably keep up with the readings. You'll get an A as long as you do that and put in effort in the assignments.

This was my second class I've taken with Professor Berrey & it was amazing again! His course content is constructed in an interesting way and he really enjoys what he is teaching and wants students to do the same. He's understanding to students and can make accommodations when needed. He is accessible outside of class as well. Love his classes!

I was really excited to take this course, and although the course material was interesting Professor Berrey truly cared and was knowledgable, lectures were not engaging. The fascinating readings and unique musical performances meant he expertly curated the course, but I found myself spacing out far too often in lecture to make it worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is awesome, just wished I had a better GSI for the discussion. Professor is very understanding and friendly, very patient when being asked a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken multiple classes with Professor Berrey and he is by far my favorite prof Ive ever had. He is kind, listens to students, and has deep knowledge of the subject. He is a true class act and I would recommend him and his classes to anyone.

My GSI was a bit of a tough grader but I learned so much that all of the work was worth it. The class is extremely eye-opening and interesting. Professor Berrey is knowledgeable and engaging. His lectures are clear and informative. Assignments are creative. He is very respectful of students' needs and warns us about potentially sensitive material.

BEST professor ever. Outstanding lectures: unique content, funny jokes, class-wide conversations. So interesting to listen to & he's also a great guy to talk to outside of class/office hours. Super caring can tell he wants students to enjoy what they're learning. Liked his integration of music through the course too. I can't wait to take him again!

Stephen Berrey is an absolute god. I took politics and culture of the 1960s with this man and I would take it 10 more times. Hes sweet, funny, and tbh a silver fox. Lecture is important and readings are somewhat optional (esp for exams) his tests are blue book but you know exactly what to expect (flashcards help). Only one long writing assignment!

Prof Berrey is the greatest. Really interesting lecturer who makes jokes in class. Also, his dog is so cute! Made his slides interesting. Only 2 exams and 1 essay, which was nice. Discussion is easy, but attendance matters for discussion. Exams were harder than I thought they would be, bt prof Berrey gives you a study guide that is really helpful
My favorite professor. So smart and well-rounded, always willing to help and work things out. If you do the reading and go to class it's an easy A.
Amazing lecturer who made every class exciting. Looked forward to each lecture and the exams were very fair. Take Berrey if you get the chance.

Professor Berrey was awesome. He made course material really interesting and was also super fun and would crack jokes in class. You have to commit some time to study for the exams but the study guide tells you everything you need to know and grading is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. His lectures are inspiring and he is passionate about the material. If you show up to every discussion and participate, it's pretty easy to get an A. The exams and essay are very straightforward

Took this class to fulfil requirements. He's an interesting lecturer, and a funny guy, keeps you engaged. There's only one essay, and two blue-books, and they're pretty easy for a history class. He does give weekly reading, but they take like 5 mins, and you dont even need to read to pass. Overall, as long as you put in decent effort, you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Berrey makes the class very engaging and makes jokes throughout class. Grading is dependent on your GSI, but they are very clear as to what they are looking for and fair graders, so if you put the time in, it is not difficult to receive an A in the class.

Basically your grade depends on your GSI. But Berrey is a cool guy and tries to make lectures interesting. For a non-history student the class was a lot of reading but apparently compared to other history classes it's a light load. One essay, 2 bluebooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Stephen Berrey was an excellent prof for history of the 60's. His lectures were engaging, organized, and interesting. He provided a spotify playlist for our class that included all of the music that we spoke about in class. He genuinely cares bout his students, as he got to know our names and ask us about things we cared about

Generally a really interesting class. Lectures are occasionally boring but you learn random information that you would never learn anywhere else.  He tries to make class fun and crack jokes and show lots of visuals.  It really all comes down to if your GSI is a tough essay grader or not.
Professor Berrey was an all-around awesome guy and a great teacher. He's very knowledgeable and extremely engaging:)
Classes are decision base so it's a good class for first years. Lots of readings, but they are usually enjoyable. Only two major essays and again the topics are enjoyable so not a hard class.
Great Teacher fro first years

Dr. Berrey is a clear, funny, and interesting professor.  Lectures are clear.  He engages students in lecture, but doesn't force or require students to talk who don't want to.  My GSI graded fairly.  Go to class, take notes, participate in discussion, do reading (light load) and you'll do well.

Prof Berrey taught the course with Prof Hughes & was very nice. The class is nice because you learn stuff out of interest rather than because you will be tested on it. There are no tests. We had one midterm essay which was clear cut and the professors were willing to help. He is very nice and a good lecturer. We have a final project, 50% of grade

Professor Berrey is my favorite professor at UM so far.  He's a very laid-back, easygoing guy even if he does talk a little fast during lectures.  I never missed one of his lectures because they're so interesting: he slips jokes in and doesn't take himself too seriously.  He also likes Doctor Who!  I highly recommend taking one of his classes.
Very interesting guy & makes the class fun to attend. Overall, the course was okay -- not boring but not the most interesting either.
Nice guy and entertaining lectures. Sometimes he even makes some funny jokes.  The class was really good and covered a variety of topics; I'd take it again.
Amazing professor! he really knows his stuff, and he's super fun. Lectures are extremely interesting and the discussions even better. He's the best!

Interesting course, but extremely picky/difficult grader (not sure if it was him or the GSI). Usually an A-/A level writer and get about that in most history classes but this class I could never seem to do better than a B/B+

I good teacher, really knows his stuff.  Gives a lot of reading, about two selections each week  X(, but lectures were very interesting including the discussions we had.  If you enjoy learning about African American Culture i recommend this class,  but if you feel this topics is boring then you won't want to do the work assigned.
Lots of reading!!! He can grade very hard so make sure you do everything he tells you to study for/put in your paper.
Very hard grader, almost ridiculous. He knows his stuff but lectures can be quite boring. He expects students to remember dates and names that are almost impossible to remember.

It was a topics course about the African Diaspora and while the course wasn't that interesting, he was still a good professor. I can't say anything that amazing about him, but he's definitely not someone you need to avoid by any means. Go to class, pay attention, show at least a mild interest and it shouldn't be too hard

Dr. Casey is a fantastic professor and really cares that his students enjoy and understand the material. He is very approachable. He is knowledgeable and his lectures are interesting and well paced. The one thing I would say is that I hate the exam format: Choose all that apply questions and weird hard to understand questions
Poorly organized course. He and Dr. Duan have a special ability of taking something interesting and making you hate learning it.

Not a bad prof, but its just a ton of content and the way the class is graded is insane. 94% cutoff for an A and no explicit curve. I've been happy with my studying and my scores all semester, especially given the complexity of this course content, but I still don't think I'm on track for an A or even an A-. Exams are not reflective of lecture.

This class is really hard for some reason. Exams often ask unfair questions that contradict what we learned in class. He is pretty good with dropping questions/giving partial credit. However, the time I spend studying for the class is not representative in the grading at all.

I don't really get the hype. I just feel like everything is all over the place when he lectures and stuff is smushed together. Some of the exam questions make no sense it's mind boggling. I sense a lack of care too when it comes to going over stuff that's heavy on the exam.

Dr. Casey was nice, accessible, and explained concepts clearly. However, he tended to misspeak sometimes which made things confusing. His memorization questions on exams were simple, but his application questions were incredibly difficult. They felt beyond the scope of this course, but he was fair in removing them/giving partial credit.

He is definitely better than Haenfler when it comes to explaining material. I like the way he lectures. The final exam was very difficult. 80 questions with intense application-based questions that required a lot of thinking outside of what we learned in class. 4th exam had a lot of spelling errors and didn't look like it was revised.

I saw lots of reviews saying Dr. Casey had a problem with misspeaking during lecture, but I strongly disagree. Maybe he saw those reviews and took them to heart, because I did not notice any of that this term and thought his lectures were very clear and helpful. Dr. Casey was a fantastic professor and I'd happily take another class of his.

Awesome guy and really down to earth, Dr. Casey is so caring and makes lectures fun. Content is very heavy in this course and can often times be confusing but he breaks it down so well and makes slides very clear. Does make a few mistakes on occasion but otherwise would 10/10 recommend!!

Good lecturer. The class is content heavy so the exams are difficult. You get extra credit from submitting questions on piazza. Has ocassional choose all that apply questions that are difficult. Starts class right at the start time with an iclicker question. iclicker is graded. Class has case studies done in groups before every exam.

My favorite professor I have ever had. He made his classes interesting and one of the only classes I haven't dreaded studying for. He wrote me a letter of recommendation and really cared for me as a student. I wish he taught another class because I would take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor. He is very caring to all of his students. If you have accomodations or need extensions he is helpful. Exams are pretty tough, but as long as you study the slides you should be fine. Overall, he is a truly great professor and I highly recommend!

Professor Casey was generally a good professor. He's very kind and fair when it comes to removing unfair questions from exams and giving good extra credit. He would say information incorrectly a lot of the time and would be very nitpicky with questions on exams, being very specific about things he touched for maybe a second, but mostly a good dude.

Accommodating, kind, and entertaining prof who truly cares for his students. Practice exams are given far in advance and are nearly identical to the real exams, which aren't too difficult. Gives partial credit for "choose all" qs and gives credit back for any qs where the most popular answer wasn't the correct one. Easy quizzes, light workload.

I really enjoyed this class! Dr. Casey is a little silly, and a good lecturer. He doesn't unnecessarily complicate topics and while there was lots of information to cover it never seemed unmanageable. Also its obvious he actually cares about his students and their wellbeing. Do the practice tests, they are very similar to the tests!!

Dr. Casey is by far the best professor here at Michigan. He truly cares for his students and makes sure we understand the material. Definitely study for the exams as they can be difficult but are doable if you put the work in. I definitely recommend going to office hours and taking bio 225 with Dr. Casey!

Professor Casey is definitely one of the best lectures in the biology department. He went the extra mile to address student well-being during the semester and even allowed a dropped test. The tests are NOT hard despite what other comments say, only reason students say this is because they have lack of discipline to study and like to project

While there is some confusion in his lecturing as he misspeaks and backtracks at times, his slides are clear and easy to follow. He utilizes the textbook as a resource but doesn't force you to have to read the book for the exam as they're summarized in his lectures. Exams are tricky but not impossible and he adjusts them based on the class.

Incredibly unclear lecturer. When taking such a detail oriented class like physiology, it becomes really hard to follow the content when the lecturer misspeaks every few sentences. There are typos on assignments and exams (though he does scrap qestions if the majority of students get them wrong). Disorganization made the class unenjoyable.
The first quiz on the syllabus was very nit-picky and in general he is a stickler for his own rules. Very defensive if you ask questions.

Casey writes hard exams compared to other bio profs and has a bad habit of misspeaking. However, he is so responsive on piazza, office hours, email, and is super clear on his expectations for the exams that it's your fault if you do bad in the class. Overall, he is still a great lecturer and prepares you well for the MCAT.

Dr. Casey seems like a great guy, but he is unfortunately not a great lecturer. He has a bad problem misspeaking and saying the wrong things. His exams are hard, but he is fair and gives decent extra credit. The class overall just has issues and he is not helping with his poor lecturing. I have heard he's better for bio 226 though.
Writes really hard exams and frequently misspeaks in lectures. Super nice and approachable guy. Amazing coordinated for 226 but that did not transfer to lecturing for 225. Needs to revamp bio225.

not the worst lecturer, but somewhat difficult exams with minimal practice materials provided to do well on exams, which are a large portion of your grade. Low quality lectures and he misspeaks often. Seems like a nice guy but man they need to revamp 225.
no bueno

Dr. Casey is fine, he uses a case study format to help consolidate the material talked about in class. He likes to use "type A and B" questions on exams where type A is more surface-level and type B is to test your application of understanding. He's a little more difficult than you may anticipate for a 200-level Bio course.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely nice guy,but so often mispeaks during lecture and leaves out important details. Exams are written so terribly and there is not adequate practice beforehand. Says everything on slides is "fair game," so left studying everything and much of it not tested on exams. Wish I took Physiol 201 to actually learn content.

He misspeaks so often that I often have to go back and rewatch sections on the recording even if I was paying attention in class. He is not clear at all and makes easy topics so much more confusing than they need to be because he messes up what he is trying to say every other sentence. One of the worst professors I have had at UMich.

Dr. Casey is an engaging lecturer. He taught the 2nd half of my class. Despite his exams being harder than the first prof's, his lectures were interesting as he included relevant real-world examples. He also talked about his research, which I found interesting. The extra credit he gave was not worth much, but it helps if you're near the cutoff.

Dr. Casey taught the second half of Bio225, and he did a great job. Lectures were well-paced, and he was active in answering questions on Piazza and created many opportunities for office hours. Now and then some test questions felt out of left field, but that was offset by a lot of extra credit. Overall Dr. Casey is a good professor and caring guy!

Dr. Casey was a great course coordinator. Most of the work is done in class (except for small weekly quizzes), and the four larger projects were pretty interesting and not overbearing. Labs were a mix of data analysis and animal experiments, and most didn't take the full four hours. Bio226 is definitely my favorite lab class I've taken here so far!

Lectures did feel disorganized or rushed at times BUT you should be reading lecture slides on your own too. This class is tough BUT if you make an effort and seek help during office hours, piazza, or via email it is super manageable. I am studying for the MCAT and this class single handedly has prepared me for the bio section more than bio171/2.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor did not care about his students or their academic needs. He is very unprofessional and left a lot of his students aggravated and lost. There is zero quality of teaching, and he does not know the concepts or material that he is lecturing us on. Overall, do NOT take this course unless you want to be ignored and forced to fail.

Please note positive reviews left here are from students who took him online, otherwise, he is terrible. You absolutely do not need to take this course to learn the material taught in this course. Absolutely zero quality teaching and gibberish information delivered.

Incompetent professor with poor teaching, lacks understanding of material, struggles to articulate concepts, consistently fails to provide reliable information. Avoid this course, take actual physio. Professor's friendliness does not compensate for these shortcomings. No exam viewing, so you won't know your mistakes. Exams are terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly poor professor as his lectures and exams are riddled with mistakes, contradiction, and inaccurate information. He lacks a solid grasp of the material, struggles to articulate concepts, and consistently fails to deliver information. Despite his friendliness, his incompetence as educator is evident. AVOID if you can, take the other physio
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel bad because Dr Casey is obviously really humble and seems like a genuine guy...but goodness, his exams are an absolute disaster. I was extremely disappointed with this class. For the first exam, I showed up and asked questions at every lecture and studied very hard, followed his review guides--and then the exam was utterly unpassable. Avoid!

Unlike other professors at the University of Michigan- Ann Arbor, he is one of the best professors at teaching. He used a case method style to help you digest the content of the lectures. This class makes you realize the importance of understanding the concept if you want to be a physician someday.

a professor who usually says random things that are not super relevant to exams at all. he likes to test some nonsense questions that are specifically associated with what he said in class.  this course failed to be qualified for a real meaningful physiology course. You learn 0 about how science works in this class.

The only thing good about Dr. Casey is he gives extra credit but that is just to make up for his poor lectures. He mumbles a lot missing out important information and often rushes into finishing up the lectures. He is just okay and to succeed in this course you really need to study on your own and memorize things word to word and apply concepts.

Casey is pretty good! I liked him better than Haenfler teaching. He can be very short and rude-seeming on Piazza responses. He is very good with names and if you make a bit of an effort to chat with him he really tries to get to know you!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible lecturer. He connects lecture material to relevant examples that can be found outside of the classroom. His lectures are very engaging and easy to watch. Everything he teaches is so easy to comprehend. He's also very accessible outside of class (always answering piazza, office hours) and cares about his students doing well.

Dr. Casey was a great professor.
