One of the only professors at Michigan that I've had that seems like he actually cares about his students understanding his content, and tries to make it applicable for their future goals/careers. Very fair and it is easy to get help in this class. Would definitely recommend, it has been my favorite class at Umich.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rambles during lectures about things not covered on exams. Misspeaks often, rarely clarifies what he really meant. This made it very difficult to learn material. He had poor canvas and class organization. Friday weekly quizzes became random days without warning. Avoid taking this professor if you prefer organization and clear speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely phenomenal explanations and engaging lectures.

Dr. Casey was such a delight! You can tell he's passionate and deeply interested in the material which he teaches. It's hard not to love Physiology when you're taking this class! Fascinating subject matter, and Casey has the best anecdotes (not too jargon-y or dense) to make the material really stick.

Dr. Casey was a pretty decent professor, and he's super accessible outside of class time. He is helpful with explaining the challenging topics. That being said, his exams are entirely different from the other professor, and there's not much studying that can be done to prepare for hypothetical exam questions. This class is graded on exams only.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Casey was very accessible outside of class which was the best thing about this class. He truly seems invested in helping students. I will say that the lectures ran a little bit slow and the exams were quite challenging -- especially considering that they are 100% of your grade. But Dr. Casey is very smart and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Casey is not a good professor to have for exam-oriented class. He doesn't go straight to the point and his pacing is bad that he can't finish slides he prepared for the class and he had to rush through material before the exam. He is really accessible outside of class on Piazza and during office hours though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Casey definitely cares about his students. He is passionate about his students but not so much so that he'll make the class super easy. He breaks down the content well enough and when he's writing the tests, his questions are fair, but it can be difficult when the questions aren't just his. Overall, a tough class but definitely doable.

I wanted to like him more, but I got very frustrated with his lectures. He'd often misspeak or give contradictory information. All of his tests had a few questions with multiple answers. At least he was very accessible for clarifications and offered extra credit, but the lectures were just too confusing
Dr. Casey is a straightforward lecturer but beyond that a kind professor who cares about his students. If you reach out while you are struggling, he will make an effort to help you improve.
I really enjoyed having him as a professor he is very clear and to the point in his lectures and keeps them interesting.

I LOVED the second half of BIO225 with Dr. Casey! He is a clear lecturer able to convey difficult concepts in a straightforward manner. He really knows how to teach! (He taught bio and chem at a high school for 10+ yrs so he knows what he's doing.) I enjoyed how he made his exams which is something I can't say about most bio profs at UofM...

Dr. Casey is clearly passionate about what he teaches and is always willing to help students during and outside of office hours. The lectures are very clear and nicely organized and he explains the material well. I liked him a lot and he made the class interesting. I think I'm gonna try to take the lab portion of the class with him too. He's great!

Dr. Casey is super organized and clear, even when explaining tough concepts. You can tell he is well versed in effective teaching and testing methods. He's passionate about exercise and food science which makes his lectures about those topics even more interesting. His exams were fair while still being challenging.

Dr. Casey is so sweet and I loved his lectures more than the other prof for this semester. He's clear and easy to understand. (Reading the book helps a lot for this course.) He offered some cool extra credit opportunities too. Would def take again and actually am in the fall for biology 226. I've heard good things about him for that course as well.

He is very kind. But very hard to understand. I wish Dr. Casey taught the whole course. It was weird to all of a sudden have the test questions come from the textbook instead of lecture. Expectations of what we needed to know were unclear. However I liked that he didn't include choose all that apply questions on exams.

I feel like he just conglomerates a bunch of words on the slides and then spits it back out during lecture without explaining it well. It's pretty hard to understand him as well. Always talks about how concepts are "easy" and this and that, and doesn't really go into detail about anything and requires a ton of self learning on the outside

He constantly says the material is “easy” and tells us to read the textbook. Most lectures feel like he's just moving his mouse around the slides and throwing words together without clearly explaining.
This man just liek to hear himself mumble! Im rewatching recorded lectures and he is actually not making sense and is just putting a bunch of words together. no exaggeration

I learned a LOT from this class and it really stimulated my interest in physiology and medicine as a whole. Dr. Duan is passionate and knowledgable and he was very approachable during his office hours. I recommend making flashcards after every lecture and doing the case studies thoroughly- they are very interesting and also count for extra credit!

Dr. Duan was a funny and knowledgeable professor who explained material accurately. While this class does require outside investments (ie. reading the textbook, making flashcards, etc.), it will pay off on exams, which are straightforward and don't try to trick you. Overall, he was a very fair lecturer and his office hours helpful!

Duan is an extremely kind and always so helpful and patient in office hours. His exam questions are pretty straightforward. If I took this class with an easier schedule, I definitely think I could have done better on the exams.

He is a nice guy and is getting excessive negativity, His accent was understandable. Some lectures were boring, but it was due to boring topics. He could be more engaging and rely less on the textbook. He and Casey should collaborate more so the transition between them isn't so drastic. Exams were usually fair, with some random/specific questions

Dr. Duan does not teach. You go to the lecture to get confused by whatever he says. He gaslights you and commonly says "Biology is very easy" and "just read the textbook". It is very clear that he does not work at all with Dr. Casey, as Dr. Casey frequently stated the textbook was totally optional, and Dr. Duan would test straight from the textbook

I have never been more gaslit than in this class. You will constantly see multiple-choice questions with several correct answers. He requires the textbook and then contradicts it. Slides don't have even half the information you need to know. I've learned a lot of this before, and seeing it presented in this way is incredibly confusing. Don't take.

Avoid. Requires the textbook after already being halfway through the course. Spends most of the lecture telling us to "read the textbook, it's so easy" rather than actually explaining things. Doesn't know how to use iClicker. Barely responds to Piazza questions. Lectures with his back turned making him hard to hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy
Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All he says is "it's so easy" and "read the textbook" for every slide. He doesn't actually teach a lot of the material and relies on the textbook too much. He spends his lectures with his back turned, facing the board, which makes it even harder to understand him along with his accent. Seems as though he doesn't even know what is on the slides.

If you like watching paint dry then Dr. Duan is the professor for you. He is extremely boring and unclear during his lectures, and his use of the textbook after Dr. Casey didn't use it at all was jarring and annoying. I cannot stress enough how poorly this professor taught this class. Biology 225 needs to be revamped. Avoid him at all costs.

Not surprised that a department head cannot teach. His accent + mispronounciations make it difficult to follow his lectures. Has no idea how to use iClicker lol. You will be ok if u have him, but rely on textbook + youtube unfortunately.
Dr. Duan was very understanding, and it was clear he was willing to help and cared for his students. I recommend using the textbook to study for exams, along with lectures.

Dr. Duan was extremely accommodating during a tumultuous online semester. He clearly explains what textbook material will be present on exams and does a great job of providing in-depth analyses of critical concepts. Definitely have the textbook at hand before and after lecture to reflect on what he says!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Despite online classes being a challenge for everyone, Dr. Duan managed to make Bio 225 a really interesting class. He also was always willing to help when students were confused about any material. On top of all, he was extremely enthusiastic and clearly passionate about physiology, and made learning very enjoyable.

Dr. Duan was a great lecturer and is definitely clear with the material he wants you to focus on for exams. The online formatting of this class, however, is not very fun and makes it harder for some students to perform well. There are no "buffer" assignments to boost your grade. However, Dr. Duan is very helpful if you ask him questions.

Dr. Duan is a nice professor. It's clear that he is trying his best, although students must be aware that he is not very accessible outside of class unless you go to office hours. His exam was very textbook and memorization heavy.

Hands down the worst professor I have had at UMich. Incredibly unresponsive to emails / piazza, difficult to understand in lecture, holds 'optional' office hours each week that if you skip, you will miss essential material, and could not give a single damn about his students. His lectures in NO way prepare you for exams, but he doesn't even care
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and really dove into past and current endocrinology material. I thought it was super applicable to my future studies. Dr. Duan is so helpful and open to questions at all times. He really cares about his students and wants each one to succeed!

Dr. Duan's lectures are content-heavy and comprised of the most recent research, however, he is very caring towards his students in that he makes himself accessible to students during his office hours. He even added office hours on the weekends! By the end, you may find yourself with the ability to read research articles more critically.

Dr. Duan is a great professor. He is very passionate about teaching and really cares about his students' success in the course by helping students grapple with the material at office hours. The course is also very well structured incorporating Endocrinology not only from textbooks but also through the latest research articles.

Do not go to lectures, which r big waste of time. Just watch lecture recordings at 1.5X speed and read assigned book pages the day before exam, and ace the exam. Lots of memorization so figure out a way to memorize lots of info in a short period of time. Material on exams is mostly from textbook and lectures. Extra credit on exams is a nice bonus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer and graded on only four exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Duan teaches the 1st and 4th sections of this course. He was slightly better and more engaging than Dr. Xu. This class is graded on 4 exams only, but they arent cumulative and there are up to 8 extra credit points available per tests. No curve. I honestly found the textbook to be more useful than going to lecture. Exams are straightforward.

Dr. Duan is fantastic. His expectations are clear and he is very willing to help if you are struggling. He spends a lot of time going over topics that are difficult and he essentially tells you what is going to be on the exams. This class has a lot of memorization but it is all manageable. He also offers a lot of extra credit on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class after Bio 225 and Professor Duan is definitely one of my favorite teachers at UM! The material was really interesting and we learned a lot of pathways in depth, but also in the scope of real research currently going on. Professor Duan was always available to answer questions and really looks to make you fully grasp the concept.

I had Dr. D for both Bio 225 and MCDB 426 and greatly enjoyed taking both classes. He always make sure to cover the complicated topics slowly, and also spends part of each lecture reviewing the previous day's material. Exams are fair and clear- good guy!

Dr. Duan was a great lecturer! Although his accent sometimes interfered with my comprehension of the lecture material, you can still get by in understanding what he is saying. Be prepared to study ALL the course material mentioned in lecture outside of class. This will comprise the entirety of his two exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Duan is great.  He cares about his students and is always willing to help.  He has many office hours that are very helpful.  Be sure to study.  This content is not particularly challenging, however,  there is a lot of material.  Lectures are not recorded.  Attend lecture.  You will learn a lot from this interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I would recommend any class with Cunming. His cheerful personality and clear way of lecturing made animal physiology great, though the subject material is already interesting. He is also more than willing to get to know his students. Attend every lecture and ask questions in office hours, and you will not find it difficult to get an A.

I took both Endocrinology and Animal Physiology with Dr. Duan.  Classes were not easy.  However, Prof. Duan was always very clear on what he was going to test us on and was always available to help in office hours and before/after class. Additionally, exams were fair, enabling a very positive experience in both these classes.  Highly recommend.

I took Endocrinology in Summer 2015, and it way my best experience in a science course at UM.  The class was small and Prof. Duan was very willing to answer individual questions. He reviewed material he noticed students were struggling with and was consistently available in office hours.  Exams were fair. He made endocrinology very interesting.

Duan is an endocrinologist so he definitely knows what he's talking about in his class. It's very informative and he'll go over things with you if you don't understand it. Definitely a class I'd recommend taking with him.
You definitely need to spend time going over the slides but he makes everything very clear. Awesome class
Tests are fair. But lot of material.

Duan is an extremely helpful professor, and I think that he really does his best to help students by being available via office hours. He is extremely passionate, and he truly does give a clear outline of what you need to know to do well. The readings are most definitely required.

225 requires a lot of specific memorization. Study all the pictures and diagrams that Duan presents.  There is blue review but if youre struggling, go to lecture and his office hours so he gets a chance to know you. He is very passionate about his research & class and really wants his students to succeed. Also, i found the textbook very helpful

He usually teaches half of this course but his exams are much harder. He tests from the book even if he says he doesn't. You have to study everything in the lecture and book and it still might be hard.
Professor Duan was an awesome teacher. You can tell he is passionate about the material and wants his students to succeed.

Bio 225 is a course that relies on lots of memorization.  That being said, Duan's lectures are very clear and the exams are fairly written.  Each exam has a few bonus questions, too.  If you study quite a bit before the exams and stay caught-up on lecture material, this course isn't bad.  Duan does a great job teaching this course.

He was confusing at times, and sometimes he said the wrong thing, but overall he was a really nice person and the way he talked made lecture much less boring than it could have been.  Really tries to help the students, and tries to make the info as clear as possible, even though sometimes his accent can get in the way.

Cunming is a really good guy and professor. It may take a little bit to get used to his accent but he really wants everyone to do well. He takes the time to answer questions and is willing to help however he can. Highly recommend him

Duan teaches the second half of this course, and I like him better than the first professor. His exams are slightly harder, but he's easier to understand. He's  very willing to help students and is generally a nice guy. Lectures are blue reviewed and the class is pretty much just straight memorization from lectures. Never opened the book.

I thought he was pretty hard to understand, so going to class really isn't that useful.  He does a mini review of what was learned last class which was helpful, and he gives extra credit on the exams just like the other professor, so even though the class isn't curved, the extra credit is a lifesaver.  Overall very nice person.

I would highly recommend taking this class. Dr. Duan does a great job of making himself easily accessible to his students. He holds office hours and review sessions regularly. This is a class where your effort reflects the grade you receive. If you attend all lectures, go to office hours and do the assigned readings you will do well on his exams.

Duan is an awful professor. He's the professor that I had the hardest time understanding. You don't need to go to class, and I'd advise against it. Blue Review worked wonders because you can rewind and replay what you didn't understand. He was also incredibly rude to me when I went into office hours. That being said, the tests were really easy.

Duan is underrated on here. He does make an effort to engage with the class, and it's clear he cares about the material. He is pretty hard to understand, but is much easier to follow on blue review. Better than going to class. Exams were not too bad, but hard if you consider there isn't a curve.

This class went from being my favorite class to my least favorite when he took over for the second half. He is a little hard to understand, focuses on weird details, and crams in all the important information right before the exam after going really slow for weeks. Doesn't reallypresent info in an interesting manner. Class is still possible though.

Prof refused to acknowledge students difficulty with the material, especially on exams. Questions were irrelevant, focusing on minute details, rather than testing students understanding. Spent ton of time on professor's own research, on info outside course. Not enough time to cover subjects in the syllabus: skipped lymphatic and resp systems.

Bio 225 is a hard class because of the huge amount of material covered. That said, Prof. Duan is super helpful during office hours and regularly makes himself available for questions even on weekends before exams. He is also very encouraging. The exams also have lots of extra credit (one test had 5 EC questions!).
Duan makes it very clear that exam questions come from lectures AND the textbook, so make sure you read the chapters. Getting an A in his class is attainable.

Bluereview is nice.  All the lectures are online, so attending lecture is not necessary.  However, I would recommend getting the book.  There are about 15% of the questions that are not mentioned in lecture, especially the extra credit problems.  Duan is a nice guy, and a smart guy.  He cares about his students, but this class is difficult. A=94%+

This is a pretty terrible class that a lot of people have to take. Professor Duan is kind of hard to understand because of his accent. But the worst part is his exams. He likes to take random sentences from the book that we're not covered in class and puts them on the exam. H reuses a lot of questions from old exams that were not covered in class.
He was nice, cute, difficult to understand, and made the exams unnecessarily confusing.  I don't recommend him.  Or this course.

Duan was a nice man but he mispronounced words and had a thick accent. The exams are extremely hard and specific and you must apply concepts very strictly and not just memorize words or concepts. Even though exams had extra credit, the questions were hard and it was hard to get a good grade.

This was by no means a difficult course for those familiar with bio classes, but Duan was very hard to understand and very often mispronounced words. Exams always have a few absurdly specific questions, but always include extra credit as well. Going to lectures often felt like a waste of time. I usually just reviewed the slides instead.

Prof. Duan is approachable and open to questions, however, on exams he tells you that he will not try to trick you...which is a lie. Both of his exams had questions that were from one specific line in the book that he never discussed. Luckily, most of his questions are fair, so it's relatively easy to pass, but tough to get that A.

I had a hard time understanding him in class because he mispronounced and misspelled a lot of words.  The exams were hard because he would literally pick out ONE sentence from the reading and ask questions about it.  Seems dedicated though and probably helpful outside of class.

I had Duan for animal phys and for molec. endocrin. Some have found it hard to understand his accent (they should sit in front) and some are disturbed by the lack of a powerpoint.  That being said, professor Duan is one of the most dedicated teachers at the U.  It is not often you will find a researching science teacher so invested in your learning

Really hard to understand because of his accent and his low, mumbling voice.  Skips slides, goes out of order, talks fast.  Starts class 5 min earlier, claims it will end class earlier but it never ends early.  Implied once that this class is only 1/3 of his time and has "other stuff to do"...everyone i've talked to gets frustrated at lecture

Prof Duan is GREAT! I really learned a lot from his class and he uses clear and relevant examples. It's obvious that he loves what he does and enjoys teaching the students. Sometimes his accent makes it a little hard to understand but if you take good notes and pay attention his class is pretty easy. I enjoyed his lectures very much!

Better than Pavgi but still had some issues...was not very organizied during lectures often including slides that we never on Ctools..accent made him hard to understand...exams were more fair than Pavgi's but they still werent always clear...schedules OH etc very rigidly and refused to meet outside those. reviews often at awkward times (Fri 6pm)

His tests were fairly easy, but I hated lecture. I had a difficult time understanding him. He also schedules office hours at incredibly inconvenient times and refuses to meet outside of class or these office hours. Just read the book and look at lecture notes.
recommend take the lab concurrently with lecture; STUDY NOTES and PAY ATTENTION
No Comments

He is good at giving relevent examples and it is obvious he enjoys teaching and puts a lot into it. Unfortunately, he uses overheads instead of powerpoint and this can leave students confused and without good notes to study. He is sometimes difficult to understand and his exams are more challenging
He's enthusiastic but sometimes its hard to understand him. But not too hard of a class.

I felt like the class was poorly structured and assignments were tedious. There wasn't really a point to attending lecture even though she didn't post her slides because she would click through them so quick anyway. I think there could be a lot better organization and setup to this course.

I wanted to love the class, but Professor Gabriel makes it really hard to want to enjoy. Seems disorganized, presents a lot of her own opinions, and her quizzes are SO HARD if you're trying to genuinely do the work for them. Do not take the class with her; take it in the fall instead.
Disorganized and biased in her teaching. This class was poorly structured.

Professor presents her own opinions as fact during lecture and fails to give an overall factual lesson. Overall a harsh grader, and creates unorganized and hyper-specific quizzes that tank your grade. Would not recommend taking WGS220 with her in the winter. I've heard the fall prof is 100x better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have a lot of issues with this prof as a person that I won't describe here, just that she has a lot of opinions that are clearly reflected in her teaching. She's also so disorganized. Links on Canvas take you to the wrong places, and she takes the entire semester to grade simple assignments. Avoid her courses if you have the option to.
This was such a fun and engaging class! Put in the effort, and it's an easy A.
This is a life changing class. I am shocked how much I did not learn about anatomy, physiology, biology, and sex in high school compared to what we got in one semester here.

Cynthia is a very sweet and caring professor and she is very understanding of you come to her with any issues you have with the class. Lectures were lengthy but overall the work was easy to finish especially if you have a group of friends to study with. I would definitely take again.

I really enjoyed having Cynthia as a professor for both WGS 220 and WGS 252. Both about women's perspective in health. This was one of the most informative classes i've taken so far. When I went on a study abroad with her (252), she was really thoughtful when I was having trouble with my sim card, metro, and was just a really down to earth person.

As someone that did every reading sometimes there would be more than one right answer in the multiple choice and she didn't assist in anyway. They are not at all understanding of absences and mark you down for not being able to attend discussion even with an excuse. Do not take a class with her.

I really wanted to enjoy this class. You can tell Cynthia is passionate about what she is teaching and she is a good lecturer, but we were graded on so few things. Getting a single point off on a homework assignment dropped my grade 2%, and the quizzes are incredibly difficult. Everyone who gets 100% on them is using AI.

Cynthia's lectures were so incredibly difficult to stay engaged with. She never seemed aware what was on the slides she was presenting and wasn't very clear during lectures. You don't need to go to class so I would recommend just watching lectures afterwards. Quizzes and writing assignments are so incredibly stressful and specific so be prepared.

realllyyy tried to enjoy this class because its content was so interesting but good GOD the structure is awful. Quizzes were so unnecessarily specific it didnt even matter if u did all the readings/attended lecture; didnt test on our understanding rather how well u can find a needle in a hay stack. Felt like a CONSTANT fight for a good grade.

The content in this class was very interesting and I got a good grade without putting a lot of effort in. Probably also due to my fantastic GSI, who I would give a 5/5. It was a little more intense than your average introduction class, but it didn't bother me.

It's an ELECTIVE course for many, but the work is graded like a graduate thesis. Quizzes are so beyond anal, it's overall discouraging. Never want to take a WGS class here again, given my experience this semester. Cynthia is nice, but how she structures this class is ridiculous and a disservice to the department. Not worth the time or stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WGS220 expectations are ridiculous. Though interesting, it was not worth the STRESS nor the GPA hit from the grading that is intensely nitty-gritty. Dr. Gabriel is a smart woman, however the way she structures this course feels almost mean. Nothing is easy about the work that's expected, and half of the assignments/quizzes felt set up for failure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I believe that for what the class is, it should not be at this level of stress comparable to a core class for my major. Especially, I find it extremely unfair that I have to bring two people to my project during finals week (in the evening) in order to receive full credit, knowing many of my peers and friends are busy with their own classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sets her students up to fail and is overly critical of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Places very strict expectations on students but does not follow them herself. She expects proper academic sources no older than 10 years and based in the US yet gives us Tumblr posts as class reading material. She expects perfect writing on all assignments and no errors in our citations yet makes grammatical errors on the quizzes she writes. Awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dense and she moves through slides so quickly it is impossible to write everything down. This is inconvenient because the tests she assigns require you to remember specific statistics discussed in lecture. The final project is also difficult because of the parameters she sets for your sources which makes them almost impossible to find.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was extremely difficult for an introductory, elective course. The quizzes were too specific and expected you to remember everything we went over in each 2 hour lecture. The readings are also extremely questionable in their scholarly validity. The sources she asks us to provide are nearly impossible to find under the parameters she sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

Things are not always clearly explained, and you are left without an example of a real-world application. If you are good at math, this is an easy A class. Otherwise, prepare to grind out book work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, he was just fine as a professor. He goes over the content well in class and it is pretty simple in nature. Highly recommend to just keep up with the workbook and you will be totally fine on all exams, don't need much preparation beyond that. He was a very sweet person and exams are very predictable in nature, nothing out of the blue.

I'm surprised by his poor rating—it doesn't seem fair. I took Econ 401 with him in Fall 2023, and his lectures were well-organized and easy to follow. Homework was manageable with effort, and office hours were highly convenient, held four evenings a week. If you study, you'll do well in his class. He is also happy to answer questions after class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Idk just not a good lecturer I guess.
Guy is a huge squid and gets his in class problems wrong. switching my major.

Don't take this class unless you have to! The course and course work are useless with regards to what you are tested on. Might as well go to any other class before the exam because it will help you with the exam just as much.

Rushes through important subjects and tends to include things on exams that was not covered in lecture or discussion sections. He is much to lenient with TAs, as mine continuously taught us how to do problems the wrong way. He seems to expect constant participation in OH and Econ Lab for you to do well in this course, b/c he won't explain anything.

I dont know why this guy gets so much hate. Taking 401 as someone who's partied and probably had a little too much neuron deterioration from alc, I realize that he goes through things slowly but not too slow where your ADHD makes you wander off. Hes a good prof for this class and cares about the details
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude blows, reads off the slides for an hour and a half, then gives the most impossible exams.
This class could have been a lot better. He read off the slides and didn't really add much insight beyond that. Would not retake.

I was able to pull my grade up after struggling heavily on the first midterm and ended up with a respectable grade. With that said, you must do the workbook problems/quizzes and practice exams if you want to do well in this class. I learned this the hard way after the first midterm. If you utilize the workbook, the class is manageable.

It's cliche but this class is what you put into it. You need to do the workbook questions, review the slides, and if your gsi is good, GO TO DISCUSSION. You can turn this class around coming from someone who got bad grades on E1 and E2 and pulled through on E3. Use zamzow's microeconomics videos to study.
jj

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 1) His lectures actually are helpful and if you listen you'll know how to start all the workbook problems (you might need to ask for help on harder problems). 2) If you work hard on the workbook problems you'll do well on the exams. The class is so doable if you just do the workbook problems and listen in lecture.

If and only if you do the workbook you will pass the class. I found out this lesson the hard way :(
So, do the workbook and get 10/10 on all of your quizzes and you will pass the class. Do not blow this class off, it will catch up with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is not a hard class if you know how to take it. Very easy to succeed. Focus and prioritize the workbook and if you understand and do all the workbook quizzes you will get a good grade on the exam and that's what matters.

1. Master Lecture Slides - Literally know everything. This isn't as difficult as it seems, yet it is a very important step.
2. Do Practice Exams .
3. Do Workouts.

This class is one of the easiest upper-level courses offered at UM. It is likely your fault if you can't succeed in this course. It's harsh, but accepting it will help you in long run.

Proulx is a knowledgable professor and if you do the workbook questions along with the material each week you should do decent, but its challenging to do well in the course due to the lack of study material for exams. There is only one practice exam for exams and the exam questions can vary greatly, so preparation is difficult. Overall, mid prof.
The class is structured poorly which doesn't help when the content is difficult by itself. Avoid him! Doesn't prepare you well for exams

Absolutely atrocious professor, worst I've ever had at UM. His exams are difficult and most questions have no relation to anything remotely realistic. Also a terrible lecturer, would give practice iClicker problems and 80% of the class would get them wrong. Then would move on without an explanation bc we were "running out of time." Dude's terrible.

Straightforward recorded lectures that are mostly conceptual, unlike exams which are more formula-based, but are useful for attaining some background on the chapter topic. Utilize the workbook, practice exams, and econ lab early on and you should have no problem. Econ lab and the GSIs were definitely the most helpful resource!

One of the worst teachers I have ever had as a student. Lecture material is not conducive to the learning styles of students. With that being said, learning relies almost exclusively on the workbook, as lecture slides are hard to follow. Exam prep materials did little to help students succeed as exam questions covered entirely different material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is extremely easy. I never attended lecture, crammed 1 week before every exam, and my lowest exam score was a 90%. He provides lecture content in a general mathematical form, which is then almost always *directly* applicable to the quiz/exam questions. Look at the notes, use the equations, take the practice exams, that's it.

His lectures are purely conceptual and provide no assistance in solving the workbook problems, which are very difficult and essential to doing well in the class. The course covers a large amount of material in a short period of time and is graded heavily on three extremely challenging exams. Decent person but a horrible professor for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For Econ 401, Intermediate Microeconomics, Proulx did not teach exam material. Instead he taught conceptual aspects of the course which were largely irrelevant for achieving success. Do not take Proulx for Econ 401 if you intend to do well and wish to avoid a very painful experience.
Terrible at answering questions and lectures made me more confused.
Switched majors because of him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Exams are hard. Lectures are confusing because they are usually hypothetical.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Means well, go to office hours if you need extra help.
He is terrible

Proulx's lectures are fine, and he can be quite funny. I don't really know how people expect him to just teach practice problems in a 300 person lecture instead of teaching concepts. Just keep up with the workbook and go to discussion. The exams are really similar to the workbook questions and practice exam. Quizzes are effectively free points.

Dr. Proulx's lectures were pretty funny and engaging, however a lot of the material is pretty hypothetical and you need to keep up with the workbook questions if you want to pass. Exams were very similar to the workbook and were hella easy if you did the workbook questions. He was funny and out of pocket sometimes which made him entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I will start by saying that Proulx is a nice guy and a pretty funny professor. I found that his teaching style didn't really mesh all that well with the way I learn personally- he teaches in a very theoretical way, and leaves most of the computational, mathematic side of this class to the GSI's. He is a nice guy, as I said, but get ready to work.
Great lecturer with weird exams. Exams were similar to practice exams and excerpts from the workbook. a little bit of extra credit from iclicker.

Professor Proulx is a good man and has lots of office hours but his teaching is very lacking. The overwhelming majority of his lectures are taught extremely hypothetically which makes it difficult to understand the material, and thus hard to do the workbook problems. I wouldn't recommend Proulx for Econ 401 whatsoever, take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible. The median was below c-. Exam are too much harder than quiz and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I ever had in my lfie. AVOID AT ALL COST.
Secon week in school, you already can tell he sucks.

Straightforward, recorded lectures, albeit sometimes boring. Practice exams are very similar to actual exams which I found extremely useful when studying. One sheet of homework a week. Attendance is taken by iClickers for extra credit and accuracy doesn't matter. If you've taken AP Micro, Proulx's Econ 101 feels just like a review of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Proulx's lectures are extremely funny and engaging (which is good considering the length of the lectures).  He is accessible to his students and very kind.  Despite this, though, you will want to consider that 75% of your grade is based on three large exams.  Also, the content they cover isn't always what was covered in lecture.
75% of final grade is based on exams. Discussion section was more confusing than helpful. Lectures were dry and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a pretty typical large lecture class, but at the end of the semester Proulx really came through and let me retake the final exam when I messed up the time. Literally saved me for no reason.

Proulx himself is passionate about economics which helps in not falling asleep during class, now, as a person, I didn't like him. As a professor, I liked him even less. Grading. Sucks. Ass. He is not someone you should take unless you're a 100000% sure you like econ because this is the type of professor that makes you want to change majors.

If you are half decent at calculus, just do all the weekly take-home quizzes and practice problems and you'll pass. 80% of the exam questions are very similar to those practice problems(you do need to buy the workbook though, as the version you can easily find online is a little outdated).

Dr. Proulx was definitely not as bad as everyone on Rate My Professor made him out to be. I wouldn't call his lectures inspiring or something completely mind-blowing. However, the way to succeed in this class is outlined clearly from the very beginning, and his lectures are quite clear cut and helpful.
Wish he did more practice problems in class, but otherwise a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Proulx teaches extremely hypothetically, making it difficult to connect what he is saying in class to homework/exams. He is condescending and outright rude to people who ask questions. I'm so happy I never have to take him again. BUT - if anyone is reading these reviews and is nervous, it IS DOABLE. You got this, just give the class lots of time :)

The GOAT professor at umich in my books. Chris Proulx changed my life. He has been the most inspirational and generational instructor that I have witnessed in a classroom. W professor, W life, L wife.

Terrible. Lectures have nothing to do with exams. Speaks very broadly in class and does not prepare students whatsoever for incredibly more difficult exam problems. Hoping and expecting him to never teach a 401 class again.

Chris Tool thinks it's brag worthy to note that many people fail his 401 class. His lectures do absolutely nothing to prepare you for the test. He doesn't even give worked out solutions to workbook problems. He's also super liberal and claims that he'd take a Toyota over a Rolls Royce. Dude's wife left him and now he takes it out on the students

Don't pick him as your 401 prof. I'm currently taking his class and he has done absolutely nothing to prepare us for the exams. He teaches broad concepts in class and expects us to know how to apply that to exam questions. I honestly think half the class has no clue what's going on. Proulx needs to stop teaching this class, it's unconstitutional
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Proulx did a very good job of teaching the material. His lectures were clear and he always made himself available after class for questions. As long as you come to lectures and do the assigned work, you will be fine. Many people were frustrated by their low test grades because they didn't put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My suggestion is that do not take courses taught by this prof

Prof Proulx genuinely seemed passionate about teaching economics and was always open to questions during and after class. I didn't love how the exams were graded, with blank answers counted for more points than wrong answers. Overall, his lectures were clear and all taped online, and the practice exams and review sessions prepped well for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Proulx himself isnt a bad guy and he seems pretty knowledgeable about economics and the lecture materials. However, the class structure is idiotic. It is graded off of 3 stupidly hard exams where each mult choice question is basically 5 percent of the test. The tests were way too hard for the lecture material and I wish homework was graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are long and theoretical, the way he explains concepts can be confusing. The workbook problems/quizzes take time, and he doesn't provide any worked out solutions. Retook this class with a different prof who explained Dr Proulx 1 hour 22 min lecture more clearly in 20 minute video who also provided step by step solutions to problems.

I think Dr. Proulx gets too much hate and his rating is often more representative of the difficulty of the class itself than his ability. His notes are very detailed and exam-oriented. There is not much covered in exams outside of the scope of the notes and the practice exams, and closely following them was an excellent method to do well.
I think because it was online the exams were difficult. It is a relatively fair class, but he does throw some curve balls on the exam.
He is a really nice man. Always seems kind and generous. He explained the course material well and the exam is not hard. Listen carefully to his course and you will get a great grade.

This class is almost solely based on exams. The exam questions do not at all reflect what is taught in lecture (the lecture just covers the basics and they expect you to figure out the rest with optional homework questions). He seems like a nice person, but definitely not someone I would choose as an ECON 101 professor.

Professor Proulx did his best to make the lectures as engaging as possible. The course itself is difficult and the poor reviews are slightly exaggerated. However, I took micro in hs and got a 4 on it and still found myself having to study often. I can't imagine how those with no experience must have felt. Avoid Proulx, choose anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take Econ 401 with Proulx. He is extremely rude & condescending. He puts people down for his own pleasure. Before I took his class I had an advising appointment with him to discuss the major. He told me that I was not smart enough to get through it. He does not want students to succeed & is not a good lecturer. I only have bad things to say.

Proulx is a very nice guy who cares a lot about econ and his students and that shown through even over asynchronous lectures. If you took AP Econ in high school or have any prior knowledge this class is an easy A; I never read any of the textbook chapters or went to the discussions and have a 98%. There are easy weekly quizzes and extra credit

The three exams are worth 75% of the grade and the weekly take home quizzes are worth 25%, which makes exam performance crucial if you want a good grade. Discussion attendance is not mandatory and they are quite boring. You are able to collaborate with peers for the take home quizzes. If you do the optional homework/practice exams you will be fine.

Prof Proulx was very nice and caring, and made himself available if you needed help. NEED to do the homework if you want to do remotely well on exams. Exams can be tricky but he would curve/remove certain questions if a majority of students were not able to get the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He didn't really explain things very well in lectures. I already had previous Econ knowledge so the class was okay for me but if he doesn't do a good job of explaining concepts to newbies.

Really funny guy. Obviously cares a lot about Econ. Lectures are clear, concise, and easy to follow, even asynchronously. Gives lots of examples and weekly quizzes are easy + a good way to check your understanding. Offers extra credit.

I've heard some say that he's okay for 401 because there's a workbook, but avoid him for 101. The exams are arbitrary and the practice exams aren't for the course so there's always material that is irrelevant on them. Just save your sanity and take one of the other profs.

Proulx is kind of a strange guy but overall a pretty good teacher. Exam questions are taken almost directly from the workbook, so if you understand the practice questions you will do well. His slides are good and he explained the material well. Econ 401 is a hard class overall so you're always gonna have people who complain about the teacher.

Dr. Chris is easygoing professor who always care about student involvement in the class and clarity of course contents. I think he usually put tons of models in the beginning stage, but things really get easier afterward due to foundation in the first few lectures. I will definitely recommend you to take his class. (Chris really worths the 5)

Honestly dont get the heat he gets. The class was well-structured, taught well, and I learnt a lot. Tests were not difficult at all. In fact, the materials he uses are so well-made that you could just learn off the slides and get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ok. So he's not that bad. He's very very theoretical. His lectures don't explain everything he may ask you on tests or homeworks. Sometimes it is incredibly frustrating. But he's not the worst. Very theoretical but you can survive his class.

Proulx is not a good lecturer. I had trouble understanding his lectures so I stopped going to lecture after the 2nd week and taught myself the material. However, he does provide you with decent lecture slides as well as practice problems and workbook problems. Do those if you want to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sheesh. This guy is the worst professor at UM. Not only does he negatively affect students but you should just speak to him so you know not to trust him and understand that he teaches economics for a reason rather than do anything beneficial for society. This guy doesnt accomadate you for anything you need, he literally tries to hurt your life

Proulx expects that no student in his class does anything outside of class other than Econ 401 (hence why his syllabus suggests 3 hours of studying for every 1 hour of class time). Expect to suffer if he is your 401 professor, it's best to look anywhere else if you want to succeed.

This is the absolute worst teacher you will ever have. I put so much effort into the class and ended up with a B because he cannot teach for his life and should be let go as any professor at the institution. He's probably really happy he has tenure cause hes the worst teacher anyone can ask for. Your grade will suck and it wont be your fault.

Proulx is a nice guy but he's not very good at teaching econ. I took AP econ in high school but because of how Michigan's econ department works I had to take 101 anyway, so I did well, can't necessarily say the same of kids who had no econ background. It's also graded really strangely, figuring out the grading system is harder than the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You'll get basically the same experience in ECON101 no matter what professor you have. That being said, I would try to avoid Proulx. His lectures were quite hard to sit through, and the slides do the bare minimum to prepare you for the exams. Your success in this class will come from doing many practice exams (and you wont need the book).

Do NOT take Econ 101 with Proulx! Lectures that can be very confusing, and are impossible to look back on after class because his lecture slides are very limited. Exams are way harder than anything done in class or practice exams. Econ 101 is a hard subject without a doubt, but having Proulx as a professor made it much harder than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Proulx may not be the best prof in the Econ department, but he does a fine job. If youre following along in the textbook and doing the practice problems (along with going to lecture), youll have no trouble in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chris Proulx is a good guy who is passionate about Econ. However, he writes a tough exam. If you struggle with hard exams and slightly boring lectures try to get into a different class. This class seems significantly harder than the other Econ 101 classes. I wish I would have listened to the bad reviews and chosen a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The rabbit's lectures are quite theoretical indeed, and I loved all his anecdotes and humor. However, his lectures do little to prepare you for the exam. Save your time - don't use the textbook at all. I survived this class by networking with others who were able to explain problems. Look at the workbook for sure, some questions come from there.

Apparently the anomaly here, but I thought that Proulx was a good lecturer. He does teach the material at a higher level than might be necessary, but he is a good lecturer. He is extremely competent and does explain concepts well even if he is rude. His lecturers are more theoretical than the exams but are helpful for conceptual understanding.

This is a class where you get out what you put in. If you do the work and all the workbook problems, you'll do fine as about 70% of his exam questions are very similar to the book. He's not a great lecturer as he mumbles a lot and many of his slides are hard to follow if you aren't good at calculus, so be prepared to learn largely from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I want to be fair. Proulx can be funny and he can really helpful during office hours. But I can't deny the fact that this class is so stupidly tough because he makes it so. There's absolutely no need to blow through material so quickly while teaching proofs and other things that just needlessly complicate material. 401 shouldn't be bad, but it is.

Pretty much going to echo the feedback here: 401 is a challenging class and Proulx's lectures do little to help. Some people think he's funny but to me he just comes off as pretty rude and his slides will do nothing to help you prepare for the exam in the class. Your best resources in this class are your GSIs/discussion sections and YouTube videos.
Proulx always overcomplicates things and never explains them well. I stopped going to lecture after the second week because I can learn better myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Econ 108 is the Personal Finance class that is an easy A with Proulx. Just keep a spreadsheet of your weekly spending to turn in and a two page paper on what you want to do financially in life. Very easy and he has lots of world experience to add to the class.

Well I may have just failed a midterm but I swear I'm objective. This guy is awful. The material for 401 is moderately hard for sure, proulx makes it way worse. Bad lecturer, over complicated concepts and creates absolutely ridiculous test questions. I don't think a single person did well on that test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I wanted to believe that the hype/drama of ECON 401 isn't true, but it is. Proulx is so smug and not helpful and intentionally makes concepts harder than they need to be. Lecture is not that helpful, instead you should rely on the GSIs because you will learn way more and be better prepared for the tests from them instead of Proulx.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Is unclear and is rude to students when they ask questions. Someone asked a question in lecture as to how he got a certain answer and he responded "like I just did."

Proulx was a really good lecturer. He did a great job of explaining difficult concepts in a way that was understandable. This class rewards those who really work hard on their own time. You HAVE to do the workbook problems even though you don't get credit for doing it. This was an incredibly rewarding class but was hard.
Chris isn't that bad. I would recommend going to his office hours and putting in the work. You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He literally does not explain how to do any problems that will appear on the exams. So basically you teach yourself the calculations. It's a very hard class, and it almost seems like he wants to psych people out, as an answer left blank on an exam is worth 1 point, but a wrong answer is worth 0 points.

He adjusts the class so that, on average, 40% of the original class drops or fails (he said so during the first lecture of the semester). He provides a lot of materials to study, even recorded lectures, but students have to decide what works best for them. THIS IS NOT A CLASS YOU CAN BLOW OFF.

I realized very soon that this class is meant to weed out students from the econ major. Proulx is a very poor lecturer. He explains general concepts but not how to relate the information to solving problems on exams.

I really wish I could like Proulx. He can be funny and clearly knows the material, but he's no good at actually teaching it. I do all the work and reading (mandatory and otherwise) for this class and it's clear that he needlessly overcomplicates ideas -- he'll show a useless proof of why something works, but never actually show how to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I feel like Proulx's not as bad as his RMP score reflects. The class is difficult for sure, but Proulx is a great lecturer and very helpful in his office hours. He tries his hardest to teach you the concepts and will spend as much time as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Proulx obfuscates concepts with unnecessary amounts of esoteric technical language and has a general attitude of "this is how it is because I said so." He offers little explanation of concepts yet designs exams to leave students confused and unsure about the majority of questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Proulx's RMP score is way more indicative of the toughness of his classes, rather than his actual quality as a professor. He's a great guy and you'll do great in the class if you do the readings, homeworks, and workbooks. Slack off and you will fall behind very fast. The class is hard, but Proulx's lectures are engaging & he's always ready to help
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very tough class. Be sure to do the assigned reading BEFORE the lecture and take good notes. Proulx gets a rap for being bad but really how well you do is entirely dependent on how much you put into it. If you understand basic Calc I you can get away with not completely understanding the concepts. Study a lot for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Proulx is funny, endearingly quirky, and for the most part able to convey the material effectively. The tests are pretty straightforward and virtually every question feels ripped from the quizzes in the back of the workbook. You should still expect to put in the effort in learning the material, though, because there's a lot of it and it moves fast.

Class based entirely on math (Calc 1 / partial derivatives). Put in the work (a LOT of work) and you'll be fine- if you at least can answer the exam questions that are straight off the workbook problems, you'll get close to the class median (which was about a 60-70%). Proulx is a good lecturer and slides are super helpful.

Your grade in this class is basically weighed entirely by exams, which are impossible. Exam averages were in the 50th percentile. Lecture slides were overcomplicated and exams were full of complex test questions that were impossible to understand. This class is used to weed out students from the econ major because it is that difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I stopped going to lecture after the fourth one because he's quite dry. However, I thoroughly went over his notes (for conceptual information) and spent A LOT OF TIME doing the workbook. YOU NEED TO WORK FOR THIS; HALF OF MY STUDYING WAS SPENT ON THIS CLASS. You can do well relying on being good at math and not concepts. Not the opposite though.

Proulx isn't that bad. His lecture slides hand you everything you need to know. I think he's a decent lecturer. Doing well in 401 requires a ton of work: do the workbook (at least the assigned problems), homework, quizzes in the workbook, and practice questions provided. Don't get behind on material and you'll be fine.

Exams determined way too much of the class grade. Homework questions were hilariously difficult and worth so little points. If you're great at math you'll be able to figure it out, however with calc 2 background I had a tough time following lectures and the slides were basically statements without explanation and very badly formatted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Econ 401 is a weeder course (not easy), relying on math/quantitative ability rather than intuition. That being said, Professor Proulx covers a lot in each lecture, and pointlessly derives some formulas or gives you the long method when it can be done quicker and easier. It's do-able, if you put the work in. Dr. Proulx is quirky and is pretty dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His class was very very dry and it was impossible to follow along with the material. While 401 is on it's own a difficult class, Prolux did not help make it more engaging.

Proulx really dives into the concepts and aims to provide a DEEP understanding of each and every chapter. That being said, each chapter is packed to the brim with information and requires a very strong calculus understanding. The tests are very hard, and you will be doing a LOT of work if you want to score at least an average "C" on tests.

Proulx gets a terrible undeserved rep. He is an amazing lecturer and clearly explains all the concepts. The class is extremely math heavy and knowledge of calc 3 is very useful. It seems that many studetns have problems with the math portion of the class because the economics is not very difficult. Easy if you're good at math, difficult if not.

If you are really interested in Economics and want to go beyond exam and grades, it is a solid choice. Proulx gives a lot of deep knowledge behind the general concept, which is useful for getting a deep understanding in Economics. But if you just want to get an A and are not very good at math, be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Proulx was not all bad.  I went to most of his office hours and put in good time before the exams to prepare and I did fine.  Its an extremely tough class, but it is definitely doable if you put in the time.  He is definitely a weird dude, but also a nice guy and i actually really enjoyed this class.

As an individual, Proulx is NOT approachable, and he is often condescending to his students. That said, he is an excellent lecturer. ECON 401 is a very difficult class, but doable if you put in the work. Workbook problems and homeworks are very helpful, lectures less so, and the textbook less so. Be ahead in the class, falling behind is very rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lecture slides are so confusing and helpless, and his workbook contains too many long questions which I do not want to work out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Proulx was one of the worst professors I've had for econ. His lectures are extremely helpful. I tried my best to take diligent notes and follow along, but when I came back to them I had no idea what we were learning. The best thing you can do is all of the PS's and HW assignments and workbook. It was the only way I could do well in the class

This class is very difficult but doable if you spend ample time before the exams going to office hours the days of the week before the exam and making sure you thoroughly understand the solutions and principles. Proulx definitely gets a worse rep than I believe her should get. He is just a very quirky guy, but very intelligent and good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you have a choice, just avoid him and wait for another professor in 401. He is definitely okay in lecturing but seriously he covers too much materials in one lecture and when you go back to review PPT, it is really confusing though. Also, I did all workbook questions, quizzes, practice exams but still feel unconfident about the exam.

Honestly, he deserves a better rating. His slides are compact, ordered information from the textbook. He even includes examples from the workbook. His lectures aren't the best, but he tries to make it relatable and funny.  Econ 401 is a hard class itself, so do work hard, go to office hours, get all the help, and you'll survive.
Terrible

You can tell Proulx is intelligent and knows what he's talking about, but the lectures are all theoretical, along with the book for the most part. The workbook problems are easier than the exam problems. Proulx doesn't go over any problems similar to the exam problems. I found it difficult to prepare for the exams. Hardest class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't the most exciting things in the world, but he is not a boring professor. iClickers used for attendance, which isn't mandatory, but you receive extra credit for it. Doing well on the exams has nothing to do with how well you, but rather how the rest of the class does, so pray for a generous curve. Overall, hard class, fine professor.
I think he gets a bad rep. for being an odd character but he is actually a good professor if you look past it. He was very helpful reviewing exam material in office hours.

Dr. Proulx is an unreal lecturer. He gets a lot of mixed reviews but I will make a point of having him again. He really knows his stuff and can put the material into the simplest of terms. Highly recommend.

Don't take 401 with Proulx if you have a choice. He barely gives examples, and when he does, they are far from what's on his tests. To make matters worse, his recommended textbook is useless. It is the first textbook I have seen without common examples. I really hoped the textbook would help prepare me for tests but it's as useless as the lectures.
Proulx does not care about his students.  He is not helpful and belittles his students if they don't understand.  DO ALL THE WOB QUESTIONS.  Try to avoid him if you can.

Dr. Proulx is fine ... they try to fit a lot of material into this course, so his lectures were always rushed. I actually found that the workbook/quiz problems were comparable to the exams, it's just that you have a lot less time during the test - so work to really understand the concepts and then practice!! And go to the GSI review sessions/OH.

Econ 401 was the hardest class I've taken at U of M. Proulx doesn't make it easier. His lectures are purely conceptual, while all of the work he expects you to do is mathematical. He never teaches students the math, which is the whole course, and leaves this burden to the GSIs. On top of that, exams are insane. If you have to have him, good luck.

Not conscientious, which can be seen his giving only 2 hours of lectures a week -- compared to another prof T. Borgers, who gives 3 hours of lectures a week for ECON401. He is never able to finish a single lecture. At the end of each class he hurries to read the remaining slides with little explanation. Exams are easy ONLY IF U R A MATH PERSON.

Exams were very hard, and Proulx penalizes you for guessing on the multiple choice. Lectures were boring, and I did not like his teaching style. He rambles on about examples. The textbook and workbook really helped me get through this course.
Extremely rude and condescending. Unclear lectures with overly difficult tests.  Very unpleasant professor, who should be avoided at all costs.
Don't listen to the professor and buy the workbook. It is useless. The problems in the workbook are way too easy and consist of only long questions. However, the exams are all MCs.

Well guys... it is brutal. Going to class will not help you in anyway. I attended twice and glad I didn't keep going because he can't explain the concepts to save his life. He gives you no practice tests (just practice problems from the book). Pray that you get a good GSI and a huge curve because that was the only reason I passed.

Pretty straightforward-- If you think through ALL the workbook problems then you will do well on the tests.  He throws tricks into the tests but they are mostly within the realm of concepts that you get from doing the workbook problems.  Lectures are basic but discussion is the place to hash out tricky questionsconcepts from the workbook.

The class was quite tough. Proulx did not lecture well and the slides were not too helpful. The most helpful study tool was the workbook (problems and the practice quizzes). If you can understand how to do every problem in the workbook you will be okay for the test, but it will still be tough to get an A.

The biggest piece of advice I could give anyone taking 401 w Proulx is to try to get your hands on a previous semester's exams and to take the practice quizzes in the Varian book. The Varian practice testsnormal problems are not good enough preparation for Proulx's exams, even if you think you know the material.

The reason for 1's all around is that his lecture slides are easy to understand, the book is easy to understand and even the workbook is pretty easy. His exams are insanely difficult and I found myself wondering why he didn't make the other material more difficult. He is actually a great teacher but didn't make our study material tough enough.

While he wasn't the most approachable professor, he certainly gives you the knowledge necessary to do well in what is a difficult class regardless of professor. Proulx explains the topics perfectly adequately for the most part, and with a bit of work on your end you'll do well.
The tests in this class are impossible. I knew the material, but the test never covered any of it.

It depends on the person, I did everything he asked of us and barely passed. I'm changing majors for sure even though I passed. I just can't handle the way these professors make the exams and how little they care about what happens. Each professor I have had here is horrible but this guy is the worst, he just enjoys seeing the students get angry.

It is a laughing matter that Dr. Proulx can teach the most important class in the Economics major. His lectures are dull, he is unclear and he doesn't give his students the materials they need to do well. All tests are purely multiple choice. This may suit some, but I don't think it's  a comprehensive way to learn Econ.

Just don't, he is the reason why i'm not doing econ anymore and I got a c in the class. Absolutely doesn't care for the students and the department doesn't as well. You can see it clearly that he enjoys it as well, it's really weird, he tries hiding it but it's obvious to anyone that he loves every second of seeing a student struggle. GOOD LUCK.

Professor Proulx is one of the worst lecturers you will find at UM. His slides are designed to show off his own intelligence and are full of complex and unnecessary equations. There is no need for mathematical proofs, man! "Rabbit" is a professor who should be avoided if at all possible.

Proulx does a good job at getting the bulk of the information to you, however he does not use relevant examples. For the most part his in class examples are very basic, the homework problems are much more complex than anything he covers in class, and then his exam questions are harder than homework. Helpful in OH though and GSI's saved my life.

Proulx really isn't as bad as everyone says on here.  I think the nature of the material is just more difficult.  If you do the readings and workbook problems as he assigns then then you should be fine.  His tests are hard but they are creative and good if you know the material and concepts well. He also seems like a genuine guy.
Lectures are horrible - insults students' intelligence by using childish examples and clearly tries to show off by making problems complicated.

He over complicates examples during lecture so much that you will leave questioning what just happened. Proulx is hands down the most pompous, arrogant professor I have ever had. His office ours are not helpful leave you with more questions than answers. Avoid at all costs.

Proulx is THE WORST. His slides have so many unexplained symbols and characters; they make lectures impossible to follow. He (admittedly) goes so fast you will inevitably miss important info. He is unapproachable and often cancels OH. Often says "think about it" in lecture and NEVER explains. 2 exams contain info learned in previous day's lecture.

Proulx is a horrible teacher for a horrible course  (101). Overall, I would avoid him if possible. The tests are overly difficult, the book if poorly written and filled with typos, and the class is generally impersonal. I missed a pop quiz because of a family emergency and he gave me a zero with no option for credit.

Everyone says Proulx is the absolute worst. I disagree. He does a decent job of explaining the material and is enthusiastic. Is he really weird? Yes. But if you get off your phone, stay awake, take notes, and do the readings, it isn't tough to get in the top 25% of the curve that gets an A or A-. I managed an A without any previous Econ experience.

Professor Proulx is a pretty boring lecturer and seemed puzzled when asked questions during lectures. However, the class is straightforward and as long you read and study a fair amount it's not too tough

If you think that he's terrible and confusing, you probably will think that econ overall is terrible and confusing and should reconsider your life goals. He's excited about the subject and that shows through his lectures. Not an easy class but you'll be okay if you can understand the material. If you can't, that's fine--you can't ace everything.
The discussion sections have pop quizzes. The questions asked in lecture are usually tricky and somewhat irrelevant to the exams. I recommend utilizing the book and any of the GSIs for clarification.
Proulx is not a good professor. Lectures and homework do not prepare you for the tests. He is not clear on any concepts. Would not advice taking a class with him
Bad professor

Proulx is the absolute worst, you can go to lecture and pay attention and walk out knowing the same amount as if you didn't pay attention, and makes his examples beyond confusing for no good reason. his tests are also purposefully difficult! Don't take this class with him!

Proulx is not good at explaining at all. His midterms are tough and hard to get an A. Textbooks are needed in case you have to know the details. For an Econ101 course his tests are too hard. Don't recommend taking it.

Worst teaching style ever. His graphs are hard to follow, he's boring, and he only gives trick questions that you'll never see on the exams. His class did, however, teach me to be thankful that my other bad profs weren't nearly as bad as him.
Doesn't explain anything well and tests are confusing/hard. He tries to trick you on them...
No. Just no. Lectures are hella boring. The course can become very difficult very easily and it's really hard to catch up once you're behind. So, no. Just no.
Whatever the case may be, I left the class with a good understanding of Econ.

Had him for Econ 101 and 401. Bad idea. Uses very confusing examples to explain simple topics. His exams are full of tricks. Consistently bogs down his slides with so many symbols and characters that you don't know what's going on. Avoid him if you can.

Proulx gets a bad rep just because Econ 101 is really hard. The class requires a lot of work to get a good grade. You have to study for multiple days before an exam, do all of the sample exams, read, attend class, etc. If you put in the effort, you can get a good grade. Most others here are bitter that Econ was too hard and take it out on the prof

Proulx is a terrible lecturer. He tries to be funny in class and is very arrogant. Doesn't go over any of the types of problems on his exams, which are very difficult. The textbook he used was also useless. Try to avoid him if you can.

Proulx is more interested in sounding intelligent than clarifying concepts. He will never explain/demonstrate how he solves problems in lecture which leaves you pretty much SOL. Terrible professor. Perfect addition to the extremely mediocre Economics department at U of M.
