Proulx was the worst instructor I've had at Michigan.  He was an embarrassment to the department, as he didn't seem to care at all about the class.  He didn't put any effort into explaining things well, and didn't seem to care about how his students performed.  Don't ever take him.
Sarcastic, cocky, and not helpful. Don't take him.

Proulx's tests in this class were challenging and full of tricks. The problems on the homework did not adequately prepare us for the exams. I would not take ECON 398 with Professor Proulx under any circumstances.

He explained things decently but didn't prepare students well for the extremely hard tests that he gave.  He also was sarcastic and seemed to lack concern for his students and seemed to teach for the paycheck.  His voice and demeanor were quite annoying.  Avoid him if possible. Bottom line, avoid him if possible.

Proulx is knowledgeable but not a great teacher. I only did well because I took Econ is high school. He repeats himself a lot, uses odd examples, and his voice can be annoying. Often times he would spend so long on the first slides, that in the last two minutes of class he would rush through 3-4 slides.

During lecture, he likes to hear himself talk. He skips lecture slides. He answers his own questions. He is unapproachable. When I went to his office hours, I left more confused than I came. I would not recommend taking any economics class with Professor Proulx.

Responds to questions in a very negative manner that makes me afraid to have things clarified by him. I think he is a smart individual but he needs to a) change his exam questions and b)approach students in a nicer manner.

Unhelpful, Unresponsive, and has a tendency to make things overly complex. When I think of the standard of awful professors, I go straight to Chris Proulx. For both Econ 101 and 401, he was a perpetual frustration. It's not so much that his classes are difficult (they are), it's that he appears more interested in fostering struggle than success.

Proulx is a nice enough guy, but the exams for this class are just heinous. I think he designs his tests specifically to "make you think", but in reality they're all trick questions and you'll walk away frustrated.

This is a terrible class I strongly recommend not taking it. The exams were 20 multiple choice and the questions were more trick questions than testing your knowledge of the material. Long weekly homework assignments that are challenging (not impossible)that are graded for correctness. His voice is also very annoying to top things off.

I actually do like this professor. He is funny and kind. His exam is reasonably hard, and I think its just right. His homework problems and quizzes really enhance your basic knowledge of Microeconomics, which is awesome.
Decent professor. Slightly boring in class but its not too hard to pay attention if you try. The textbook is excellent - make sure you read it.
Definitely avoid him, and try to get Gerson or Malone. His voice is super annoying to listen to during lecture. His tests are significantly harder than the other econ lecture too.

Everybody says to avoid him but his class really isn't that bad. Econ 101 is just hard and people don't like that. I'm not saying to take him over Gerson or Malone but if he is all that's left or if he fits into your schedule better, don't not take econ. Go to lecture., read the book, and try to enjoy his jokes.

Try to avoid him for Econ if you do not have a background in Econ.  His tests are way easier than Gerson and Malone but he doesn't lecture well, is boring, and is awkward.  So, if you have no Econ background, get Gerson or Malone but if you do, have at him!

Exams are difficult. Just make sure you know the material and you'll be fine. He explains everything well (read the text though) and is funny, but his voice is annoying and puts me to sleep everyday. Doing the homework won't help you on the tests as they're not alike.
Not as bad as most people think (especially if you have prior economics experience). He knows his material, and is actually really funny. Class is not easy though.

I did well in this class but I think it's only because I had an awesome AP teacher in high school. The homework and lectures are way easier than anything on the exams. I've heard that Gerson and Malone are better so take this class with one of them if you can.

I went to every lecture, but my after class review was more helpful.  The overall lecture was well structured. I did like the discussion session and the GSI. BTW, in the summer term, he did not provide any past exams for review. That was the part made the course hard.

Very interesting course called "strategy", basically intro to game theory.  Basically all math and problem solving.  He is a pretty good prof. but loses focus sometimes and tells long, unrelated stories.  Homework is important for understanding material.  Exams are tricky.  This course has a more generous curve than other econ courses: 30% A, 35% B

The professor knew what he was talking about but set up the class in a way that related more to his personal life and beliefs than the actual class.  Do not take his class.  He was a hard grader and very stubborn when subjectively grading homework and exams. I also found his voice extremely irritating.

I had him for ECON 398 and 395 (Law and Economics) and he did a great job teaching the materials. He helped me relate the economics theories to the real life situations. Also, his lecture slides are clear and helpful. It's not hard to get a grade as long as you understand everything talked about in class.

I didn't think he was as bad as some of the reviews say, but I think taking AP Econ before made things clearer for me. I had a very good GSI too, so that helped a lot. He likes to use strange examples sometimes.

He is very passionate about what he's teaching. If you're uncertain about something he taught, you should go look for him personally. He could give a better explaination when he is speaking one to one with you. I really think he's a good teacher.

I'll admit, part of what makes this class hard is that its weeder for Ross. Still, Proulx was boring, and his lectures seemed dumbed down compared to what was on the exams. Doesn't tell you your grade,just gives you a range relative to the class, which even the other two don't do. He is arbitrary and stubborn, and that says something in THIS class.

Seemed like a nice guy--a little nervous teaching, though (as evidenced by the slight stutter), but he got better as the year went on. Not very engaging. Repeated things ad nauseum, which was annoying, but HELPFUL. don't go out of your way to take econ with someone else. im taking his strategy class next semester

You can tell he was passionate about econ, and he loved to give examples in class that relates to the world today. However, he often droned on and on. I think I was legitimately awake for only 5 of his lectures this semester. The slides and the book-in-the-making did not help. I think I would've failed if it weren't for my GSI (James).
subject was interesting, but his lectures put me to sleep and the lecture slides posted online weren't much help. the book was pretty boring, too.

Had him for Econ 101.  I feel badly giving him a bad review, but try to get a different professor.  I always fell asleep because lectures were extremely boring, and his voice kind of bothers me.  He does his own thing, not doing what the other Econ 101 professors do, which was annoying.  Book was pretty bad- not in color, which would have helped.

he is a very unclear and somewhat not straightforward in his lectures. His material is different than the other 2 econ lectures (which partner up the same). I would highly reccomend getting Malone or Gerson... their class is structured the same. Proulx does his own thing, has his own tests....

He tries, but he is still boring. His slides always have grammar errors ("when their gone, their gone"), but the iclicker questions are helpful. We are also using his textbook, which is incomplete, lacks a table of contents and index, has grammar errors, and has incorrect answers and incorrect chapter numbers. The gsi is much more helpful.

Problem sets weren't bad at all and don't take that long to do. Lectures are pretty much useless and trivial, if you do anything go to section. If you are interested in Game Theory wait to get exposure in 401 and if you still like it take 409. Overall a disappointing class that I didn't get much out of at all.

I don't know why everyone hates him. Was he the most entertaining teacher ever? No. Was he the easiest? No. However, it was totally possible to get an A, and the stuff we learned was pretty interesting. I'm not saying he was great, but he wasn't that bad. I will say one thing though, he is a bad administrator because nothing was ever posted on time
ugh. never again. his lectures are amazingly boring, pop quizzes are annoying and the midterms are killer
i hate this man.  exams are difficult, homework problems are very hard.  if you take this class make sure you get help from your gsi

Never went to class, never did the homework, never read the slides, still got an A. Econ 101 is easy, just look at practice tests before the test. This guy is terrible though. Boring, unhelpful, annoying accent. Take it with someone else if you have to take 101

I think that at heart, Professor Proulx wants to be a helpful teacher--but in the end he's really just kind of goofy in a not that great way and not that interesting. He stutters a lot, and I think maybe some of this isn't his fault, but it's kind of distracting. If you can, try to get a different professor.
He is hard to pay attention too, and rables on about non-important topics.

The homework problems are hard, yes, but not impossible, and definitely don't take 12 hours.  The exams are pretty straightforward applications of the material.  It's not a memorize the lecture slides class, it's an understand the materials class.

For 398, prof gives 5-7 questions hw each week that easily take 7-12 hours each. His powerpoint lectures are relatively basic and don't prepare you well for hw. GSIs may not provide enough help since professor is very strict. Class itself is not even interesting as one might expect of game theory.
he is good
He's a great professor, I dont care what anyone says. He's enthusiastic about the subject and willing to help out students. Smart guy that knows his stuff, and a good professor to learn from

This class is terrible with him (as all the other comments state). Most of the exams didn't even relate to what we studied and were lectured on... One of my classmates even said he thought he was taking the wrong test at one point when he recieved the second exam on exam day. Better off guessing on the test. Don't take this class.

Ron is so awesome! Super funny and awesome guy, attendance isn't required but I went to lectures just for him. My GSI was also amazing + helpful! Class isn't too bad, but don't underestimate it! If you do all the assigned stuff (even if it's optional), you will be fine as tests are made from that material. Consistency is key in this class!

Prof. Caldwell is an excellent educator. He is thorough, respectful, and makes content easy to grasp. Course grading is very fair, just keep up with material and deadlines. He supports curiosity beyond the syllabus, but also understands student priorities, fostering the desire to learn. Easily one of the best profs I have had. Highly recommended.

I loved this class. Attendance isn't taken since lectures are large, but don't skip because it helps with understanding. Try to find past exams from students who took the class before—he often reuses similar questions. Easy A if you study about an hour outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good and engaging lecturer, sometimes rants about unimportant stuff though
Goated, love this guy

Great Professor, willing to help students at all times, and exams are very much based on lecture and section content. Overall would definitely take again if I could, and one of the best Professor's I've had at Michigan thus far!

Best professor I have ever had in my life. I had never taken econ before and his lectures are so fun, interesting, and he is a deeply caring professor. Always available outside of class and happy to help whenever. Makes lectures very engaging and makes you not want to skip a single one despite being optional. Tests exactly like practice materials.

Really energetic and passionate guy, but I found he was too familiar with the material that he failed to take it slow and explain concepts to people who econ does not come naturally to. My gsi was extremely unorganized and was called out numerous times for giving us incorrect info during discussion- which is bad bc discussion questions are on exam

Professor Caldwell made every lecture engaging and worth going to, even though attendance isn't required. The class was pretty easy, as it was only three multiple choice exams (no final), none of which were cumulative, six quizzes that are online and open note. The practice problem sets are super useful. Loved this class!

Really liked Ron. Good lecturer and if you didn't understand, you were able to ask questions, even for such a large lecture. If you sit near the front, he will get to know your name and will give out Coke and Pepsi during the first 2 weeks. Exam heavy but most questions were the same exact questions as the practice, just with different numbers.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are going to take econ101, take Caldwell. He is such a great person and his lectures are not boring at all. Really cares about his students and if you do the work that he gives and study well, the tests are pretty easy.
Big fan of his lectures. He is clearly very passionate and knowledgable. Provides good real world examples of content we're learning in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron is a great professor! Do the problem sets the week they come out, and start the quizzes early. I went to all the lectures and discussion sections and didn't have to spend much time out of class studying otherwise. Exams are super reasonable if you keep up with the work. Sit towards the front - he will make a point of getting to know your name!
Caldwell I great for econ! He makes concepts easy to understand and classes are fun and interesting.

Professor Caldwell is amazing. His lectures are very engaging, and he explains everything in depth and with various examples. The only reason this class can be tough is by making simple mistakes on the exams, but the exam questions are pulled directly from the practice sets and discussion worksheets. Overall, a great professor and an easy class.
He is an amazing person and really cares about his students and their learning in the class

Ron is hilarious, and I enjoyed his lectures; however, this class is tough and depends on who your GSI is. It's only graded on a few things, and all exams are multiple choice (no partial credit). Go to lecture, go to section, do the practice problems.

While I'm not the most economically minded, Caldwell made this class bearable. He has great explanations and truly cares about his job. I recommend going to optional discussions, as most of the quiz and exam questions come from the discussion problems. Overall, a great prof for a tough subject.

Really great and engaging lectures that made class fun. Also, made concepts feel easy to understand. If you go to class and do the optional homework (problem sets), it's not hard to get a good grade as most midterm questions come from there. Discussion sections are also important and helpful.

Three non cumulative midterms and no final, 6 online open not quizzes with a lowest score drop, and one very short writing assignment which you have two opportunities to do and only your highest score counts. Ron is super nice and made all of the content very clear and easy to understand. I would 1000% recommend taking his class!

Ron deserves every promotion and teaching award out there. Made each class relevant and funny. Kind soul. Offers lots of out of class support. Helpful in office hours and willing to explain concepts over and over. Cares deeply about his students' success and well-being; he meets you where you're at. Don't be shy to ask questions. TAKE HIS CLASS!!
This class is pretty easy. Most of the time spent on this course is before exams. I would highly recommend taking Econ with Caldwell.

I really enjoyed taking 101 with Ron. He made the topics very easy to understand, breaking them down so that the concepts are very digestible. I took AP Econ and I hated both of them so much. However, I actually found a new love for economics in Ron's lectures. I understood every concept. I will say though, that the exams are a bit frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron is a great guy who gives engaging, well-designed lectures. I never dreaded going to his class. His exams were more than fair and multiple choice. You're well prepared for his exams by the practice problem sets, lectures, and discussion section. He also offers recorded video lectures that he did over COVID, which are helpful.

Ron is the best! He genuinely cares about his students' success, answers every question with patience, explains concepts clearly, and gives helpful advice for all assignments and exams. If you have the chance to take his class, do it! :)

Ron is the best professor ever! He is so knowledgeable about his subject & great at explaining hard concepts. He ties everything into a real-world example which is so helpful. He is very open to questions. Attendance is optional, but to succeed you should go to lecture, section, and do problem sets. If you put in the effort, you'll get a good grade

Very easy content-wise. Mostly just memorization. Lectures were huge but he learned the names of a handful of people and talked to them every class. If you sit up front and answer his questions unprompted, you will become his bestie for the semester. He is a very amusing lecturer, even giving out sodas/drinks mid-lecture to people who participate.
Best option for Econ 101. Take home quiz grades are determined by how chill your gsi is. Was very engaging with lectures and interacted with students even though it was very large lectures.

I had to take this class with 2 other hard classes so I didn't allocate as much time as I should've, but Ron is a super nice guy whose clearly passionate about the subject. Even though this is a 100 level class, you need to put in a good amount of effort in regards to studying for his exams. 3 midterms/6 quizzes/2 small writing assignments.

I performed relatively poorly on the first exam and got a 64/100. I ended up getting a total of 3 questions wrong across the last 2 exams and was able to get an A-. If you get a bad grade it immediately takes away your opportunity of getting an A no matter how well you do on the later exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron Caldwell was an amazing professor this semester. His class was extremely well-structured and he is an amazing professor. I would also highly recommend utilizing his office hours when needing help, going over problem sets, the multiple choice question he post on canvas, and discussion practice for the exams.

Professor Caldwell was amazing. His lectures were always fun and exciting. I never skipped a lecture and did well in the class. I bombed the first exam but did well on the last 2. The curve is very heavy. Just show up and GO TO DISCUSSION omg like y'all half the questions are from the discussion.

Ron kept his lectures as interesting as possible and always included people, he was also very funny. The class is so easy if you go to lecture and discussion and do the practice problems. Keep up and the exams are very easy

Ron is great! Engaging lectures and explains concepts in-depth. Do the practice sets and canvas practice quizzes and the exams shouldn't be too bad--he takes questions from the practice sets and uses them in the exams.
Out of all the 101 professors, Caldwell is the best. Take it with him, trust me.

Caldwell's lectures are amazing because he explains each concept so thoroughly, and he's patient with questions. If you do all the practice, he tends to repeat exact (or really similar) questions on his exams. Compared to the other professors this semester, Caldwell is the only one I haven't heard anything bad about, and it makes sense why!

Prof. Caldwell is a very nice guy who delivered interesting and funny lectures. He explained material very clearly and was very helpful if you were struggling. You are only graded on 5 take-home online quizzes, a news article analysis, and 3 midterms, so your grade hinges on only a couple of things. If you study for the midterms you should be fine

Passionate about economics, not his students. Would not recommend having any sort of crisis in the middle of the semester (mental health, family death, etc.) If you catch him on a good day, perfectly fine, otherwise condescending in office hours. Just because you are good at Econ does not mean he was a good professor.
Good professor who seemed to care about students. Attendance is not mandatory for lecture or discussion

Professor Caldwell is the best choice for intro econ! His lectures are easy to follow and he posts old video lectures online.  Quizzes are open note but graded harshly by GSIs. Exams are multiple choice and pretty easy if you do the optional module quizzes and practice questions and go to discussion. Often questions from the practice are on exams.

Caldwell is a thorough lecturer who does a good job of explaining concepts and tries to make sure that everyone follows along. If you do all the practice problems he assigns, go to discussion section, and go to office hours, you'll more likely than not do well in the class and on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed how he would make economics interesting by tying it to a real world concept. I also liked how he would try to remember everyone's name and personalize it. It is a hard class, but Caldwell does his best to teach you what you need to know in simple terms. The only negative I can think of is he gets upset when students leave early.

Caldwell was a great professor and really wanted you to learn. He has engaging lectures, records his lectures because attendance isn't mandatory, holds office hours and is open to answering questions. He tries to get to know you! 

The only worry is grades are from three things: 5 quizzes, 3 big exams, and an article response.

I struggled with econ a lot but I can still recognize that Ron is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and is always open to critiques and feedback. His lectures were engaging and he was always prepared. The grading on the quizzes can be tough but he drops your lowest score. Whole class is based off of about 9-10 assignments.

Ron Caldwell is the professor that made me change my major to economics. He is so honest with his students and genuinely cares to speak with them during office hours. I find him to be a genuine and funny professor with the rare ability to win people over. Nothing but praise for professor Caldwell!

Ron is a very good lecturer (and seems like one of the best for 101). However, I honestly felt like my high school Econ teacher did a little better of a job explaining things. The tests are difficult, but he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. I ended up .1% away from an A+.
Every lecture was hilarious, insightful, and informative. The class is a bit exam heavy, and some of the questions can be a little tricky. I would take a class with Ron again in a heartbeat.

Ron always came to class prepared with interesting lectures and was always more than willing to answer any questions. He went above and beyond for all of us this semester as I'm sure he has for all of those he has taught. I 1000% recommend taking a class with him!

If you're looking for a good prof for Econ 101, I absolutely recommend Ron. He's an engaging lecturer, connects content to the real world, and cares about knowing and helping students. Do the module quizzes and problem sets, and you'll do fine on the midterms, although 75 questions make up 60% of the final grade, so you have to do well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a charismatic professor. Regardless of the class being huge in size, he will do whatever he can to make you feel included in his lectures if you are willing to participate. Teaches content really well and as long as you pay attention to class and attend, you will do good. Curved due to the number of different professors teaching the course.

Prof Caldwell was very interactive and his passion for Economics is very clear. He keep lectures engaging and interesting. His course may be more difficult in comparison to others taught by other professors but there's benefit to it. One critique is that he doesn't repeat questions asked to him, thus the rest of the class cannot hear what's asked.

Ron is a great professor. He tries to learn as many students' names as possible, is clear on topics, and works hard to help everyone succeed in the class. Make sure to get all of your points in this class, and study practice problem sets, discussion section questions, and module quizzes before exams. Loved Ron and had a great time in Econ101!

I really appreciated Professor Caldwell's efforts to make class engaging and his attempts to learn as many names as possible. His lecture slides are also very clear and are posted prior to lecture which is extremely helpful. Additionally, I emailed him with a few questions and he responded almost immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super easy class, barely went to lecture/discussion, and there are not many assignments in total so the class is not very time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caldwell was super funny and down to earth. 101 was harder than I expected, (I took AP macro, but not micro in HS) but I still pulled off an A. His class was more chill than the other 101 profs I heard about. Just study the problem sets and module quizzes for exams. Also every point counts so do your best on the take home quizzes too
Speaks a bit too fast but overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron is a super great guy, he makes lectures as engaging as possible! No final exam, just three pretty short midterm exams (25 questions), and 6 open-note quizzes (open on Canvas for a week), & the lowest quiz score is dropped. If you review optional practice quizzes and problem sets you should be good to go. He also posts lecture videos on Canvas.
Good prof, he doesnt force students to read off a textbook, can answer all your questions in and out of class.
The quizzes and problem sheets are way easier than the exams, so come exam time I did not feel prepared. The exams twist the quiz problems and make them way more difficult.

Professor Caldwell wants you to do well. Much of your grade is dependent on take-home quizzes and short-writing assignments. The 3 midterms are difficult and you need to prepare. I highly recommend Caldwell's office hours, but you NEED to come with SPECIFIC questions in order to get the best help. Engaging, funny, well-prepared.

Ron was great! Overall, Econ 101 is just a tough subject and it takes a while to get the hang of it. There are weekly quizzes that are 4 questions each for 36 points and 3 exams that are 25 questions for 100 points, so there really are not any "easy points" without doing the work to keep up. One large subject / lecture.
Good professor. Very nice guy overall, and was extremely approachable. Not only did Ron dedicate a lot of time to his students, but he was very dedicated to his students and was approachable.

Ron was a solid professor who went into good detail and used real world examples of the economics we were learning in an effective way. Tests are not too bad, make sure to do all of the practice problems and quizzes and you'll be fine.
Great prof very clear, you have to put in work but genuinely enjoyed econ bc of him

Ron is an awesome professor. Engages with his students, tries to learn names even in a big lecture hall, and made a topic I am bad at very interesting. The exams are rough, and there aren't many assignments, but if you put in effort you'll do fine (I didn't but that's my own issue). I don't like Econ (sorry), but I do like Ron :)

Caldwell is such a great guy. I find him to be really entertaining during lecture, but it can be a little tough to follow so his extra videos are good for review. This class isn't insanely difficult but you do have to work if you want a good grade. Would totally take more classes with him in the future.

Ron was one of my favorite professors and inspired me to fulfill a degree in econ. He explains the material incredibly well and provides SO many resources that are extremely helpful for the exam. He was genuinely funny and was so caring for his students. Definitely take ECON 101 with Ron and take advantage of the practice problems he gives out.
Caldwell makes an effort to know each of his students, and he explains the material in a clear and often humorous manner. He is one of the kindest professors at Michigan.
Amazing lecturer and makes an effort to get to know his students despite it being a 350 person lecture. Very available outside of class and helpful when students have questions.

Dr.Caldwell is a great guy who really tries to connect with his students. If you show up to lectures he tries to learn your name and uses you as an example during demos. He is super funny and easy going and always willing to talk about topics shared in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron is a great lecturer. He always engages with the students, and he is very funny. He also does his best to learn everyone's name, and it is impressive how many people he remembers. His tests are not bad, only 25 multiple choice questions. He posts more than enough review material, between his great lectures and all of the resources, pretty easy.

Ron was a great prof for my Econ 101 class. His lectures are clear and engaging and he himself cares a lot about the students, even putting in effort to learn as many names as possible in the 300+ person lectures. Exams were tough but I should have studied more. Would definitely recommend taking an Econ class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calls out specific students in lecture. Not very helpful, despite his enthusiasm.
He is a great guy and loves what he does. His exams are very difficult and do not relate to his lectures.

Caldwell is very rude and comes off as arrogant. He targets specific students in lecture/office hours. I stopped going to lecture and discussion after the 3rd or so week and just watched everything online and got an A- (4 points away from an A). The class is useless and I would just watch the lectures online and not go to discussion. Very rude man.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome class! Lecture was optional, but Ron's passion for econ and humor makes you want to go. He made the lecture hall feel like a classroom. Highly recommend going to office hours to get help or just to talk to him. There are 3 tough exams, but do the problem sets, actively learn in lecture, and go to office hours, and you'll be fine.

Really charismatic guy! Great for a freshman that wants that small classroom feel because Dr. Caldwell makes an effort to get to know everyone's names. He does get off track from really involved students which can be annoying. Presents information clearly but makes exams really hard. Overall, great professor.

Fantastic professor, I would recommend this guy to anyone taking ECON 101. Entertaining lectures, clear explanations, clear grading system, cares about his students. I can't say enough good things about professor Caldwell.

Dr. Caldwell was an amazing guy. He was hilarious and you could tell he really cared about his students. The class itself was hard, as reiterated by the other comments. The exams in particular were difficult. But overall, it was a good introduction to economics.

Professor Caldwell is a great guy, and I had many nice conversations with him. For the most part he taught econ well, but I did not like that how a lot of the lectures was him reading off the slides. His exams were tough for me, but the quizzes we not too difficult. I wish I got a better grade in is class, but that is on me.

Ron is a great professor! If you are taking Econ 101, take it with Ron or you are getting it wrong. There are 3 midterms, 6 quizzes, and 2 article responses, so it is not too much work. Do all of the practice problems that he offers if you want to succeed in his class.

I loved Ron. He is a great teacher and treats his 300 person lecture like its a 40 person class. He truly cared about his students. He knew the names of like 50 people. His exams were tough sometimes but they really weren't that bad. Take this mans class he is the best.

Ron was amazing! He made a large lecture feel like a smaller classroom with his humor and teaching style. He offers great extra help and makes an effort to connect with each student who engages with him. Take Ron for Econ101!

One of the best professors I've had at Umich so far. Puts in effort to learn people's names, making a 300 person lecture feel like a seminar. I highly recommend taking 101 with Ron if you're wiling to put in the work!

Professor Caldwell is a great econ professor. His tests are not that hard and he gives 6 online quizzes that you have a week to complete. He is great at teaching the material and is always open for questions. Highly recommend taking a class with him.

Professor Caldwell is such a nice guy and really willing to get to know his students. If you stay after class and talk to him or sit in the front, you'll get to know him even better, and I really recommend it. Just try to pay attention in lectures and do the problem sets, and you'll do fine in this class. Would take more classes with him.

Ron is a great professor and makes lectures really fun and has a lot of neat tricks to help information stick in your brain. Super nice guy but ECON101 is graded on a curve- that makes it difficult and grading is up to the horrible GSIs. Don't go to discussion, get all material you need in lecture and go to office hours. GSIs will confuse you more.

Dr. Caldwell was a nice person. Any time I went to him for help he was wiling to explain anything I didn't understand; however, I'm not a person that learns off of powerpoints, and that was how he taught his class. He would explain something, then read it off the slide. It was difficult for me to fully understand and I never got it the first time.
Ron is a great professor, his exams are very tough though. Because there are so many people in the class, you. have to go out of your way to get help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Caldwell was a fantastic professor. His office hours were the best. When you went he always went through concepts in detail and made sure you had a solid understanding. The tests are hard, but there are plenty of practice opportunities available.
Excellent lecturer. Quite funny. Tests are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caldwell really cares about his students. When I email him I get a response immediately. Also his exams are really straight forward, I wouldn't call them easy but it if you do the practice sets and module quizzes (making sure you understand everything that you are doing) you will do very well on the exams (I received 100).

Overall great professor. Took him for Econ 101 and class was not hard. Its good to go to lecture but theyre recorded if you dont want to go. Got a B+ cus I screwed up the last exam but it wasnt his fault. Was riding an A all semester with minimal effort and a good understanding of the topic

Even in an absolutely massive lecture hall, Caldwell tried his best to be personable, funny, and caring. While there is a department enforced curve, if you do the optional readings, module quizzes, and engage in class, youll be absolutely fine. The best choice for Econ 101!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ron is an absolute gem, you're missing out if you don't choose him for Econ 101. I've taken AP Econ and this class was super easy and straightforward, Ron was an amazing lecturer and he made me actually want to go to class. He's also very clear about the grading policies and really funny!! Couldn't recommend him more

I did pretty badly on the first couple of quizzes and the first test, but I was able to get to an A by the end of the semester because I watched his recorded lectures and completed all of the module quizzes! Just watch his lectures on 2x speed, do the module quizzes, and skim through the practice problem sets, and you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ron was an awesome professor to have. His lectures were interesting and he made sure to interact with the class. Despite having a class of 200+ people, he made sure to learn as many names as possible. The exams are 25 questions all multiple choice, and they are the biggest factor in your final grade. Highly recommend end of module quizzes to study.

Ron is an outstanding professor. For sure the best choice for ECON101. He does an outstanding job at breaking down topics and explaining what is important. Also, he is hilarious. Looked forward to his class everyday. Very manageable class, take notes and do the end of module practice quizzes. If you don't take ECON101 with Ron, you are missing out.

Caldwell is a great choice for ECON101. I was concerned after reading COVID-era horror stories about his class, but in person he is great. He makes Econ interesting and fun, telling anecdotes throughout lectures. Additionally, while there's a curve for every Econ class, Caldwell's exams are easier than others: all 25 MCQ exams. Econ 101? Caldwell!

Ron is one of the kindest, most interesting professors at Michigan. I will say, however, the tests are extremely important. I messed up on just one exam and did fine on everything else, but I still found it difficult to get my grade back up. I would highly recommend going to tutoring and paying attention to lectures.
One of the best professors I've had so far. Interesting and concise lectures; friendly and approachable. Office hours were nice to attend.
Professor Caldwell explains the concepts really well and the coursework is very reasonable. The exams are non-cumulative and there is no final which is really nice.

I felt the lectures did an OK job at preparing you and the supplementary materials built you up a little more but the exams still had some hard-to-navigate questions, which were challenging due to the virtual format. He was very respectful and excited to meet students too. I would look at the other 101 instructors before you decide who to take.

Look, if you're taking ECON 101 just to pass and get an easy A this isn't the class for you. That said, Dr. Caldwell is the only professor I've seen at UMich that actually cares about their students' wellbeing during Corona. If you don't engage in the class and pay attention you're gonna have a really bad time, if you do, this class is the best.
Ron is cool. Ron is great.

Ron is a great instructor. Although I haven't got a good grade, I take it as my responsibility. As long as you care about the course and decide to work hard, you should be okay. But if you terribly screw up one of the big exams (which was my case), you might have a very hard time getting back on track. Make sure to be 100% prepared for exams.
Ron is the best!! Even during a pandemic with online courses he made sure to be available and helpful.

He is really nice and tries to learn everyone's names even in the online format with hundreds of students. The only thing is that his lectures get very boring and not really engaging having to watch them online, but he is very willing to talk outside of class to clarify points which is nice.

I read through rate my professor and picked Ron because he had great ratings. It was easy at first to understand the concepts but the workload became almost impossible. The first test was so hard that I ended up dropping the class. There was not enough time. He's not understanding at all about COVID. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite professor this semester! If you keep up with lectures & do all the practice problems he gives, you can definitely score well on exams because they are incredibly similar. For an online class with 700 students, the class was run very well & he's great if you meet him outside of class too
Terrible class set up/grading system. One bad test and you're screwed. Definitely would not take any of his other classes if they were similar to this one.

Took his class remotely. Overall great professor; however, if you aren't willing to try on tests, then this class will be a tough time. Do practice questions multiple times because the tests are hard. Don't underestimate the first midterm of the class because the class average was 79% for the first exam.

This class was SO HARD online. I really suggest waiting til in person. There was about 700 students in my class. Professor Caldwell was accessible, and a great guy, but if you got one bad test grade there is no fixing it. Everything is grades by GSI's. NO exceptions on late work or test extensions. I worked so hard and ended with a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: "Ron" was incredibly accessible throughout the semester. He put a lot of energy and effort into the recorded asynchronous lectures (COVID). He made it a point to get to know each one of his students during coffee hours each week. There were plenty of points in different areas of the course to round out your grade. 10/10 would learn with again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An amazing person and teacher - Ron is life-changing. Best professor at U-of-M.

Professor Caldwell was a great professor over the semester. Especially considering the circumstances around the class given the pandemic, he did a fantastic job. He was very accessible outside class and provided resources that included him and other tutors for every student to be successful in the class.

Caldwell is a great professor. Econ 101 is a pretty tough class and the online test formats weren't ideal. However, he explains the principles really well and tests/quizzes are open note. I didn't even need to use the textbook because everything you need to know is in his slides. If you take the class online, DON'T get behind on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Love Ron. This class wasn't as easy as usual online due to the weekly quizzes and your grade being determined by 3 exams, but if you do all of the problem sets and module quizzes they aren't horrible besides timing. He's an excellent, knowledgeable lecturer and even cooler person! Make sure to meet with him outside of class because he's the best!

DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN FOR ECON 101. I was led astray by all the positive reviews saying he is the best econ 101 professor. All of the reviews are pre-pandemic. The quizzes are not how they used to be. I repeat do not take Caldwell. You have been warned.
Course is easy, but professor doesn't give enough time for tests! 100 minutes for 20 questions and each question have multiple parts. I don't even have time to process what the question is asking!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ron is incredible. He really wants to get to know you even with the weird pandemic circumstances and you can find a time to meet with him and talk about anything. The lectures and content are interesting. Grade mostly based on exams and quizzes. Quizzes are easier than exams. Exams very fast-paced. You can do well if you work hard but not a free A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Caldwell is a nice guy, however, given this new format, his class was quite difficult. It is recorded lectures and the majority of your grade is determined by three tests that are very difficult throughout the semester. He is undeniably the hardest econ101 professor, although he teaches you everything, if you want an A, this isn't the class.

Hardest econ 101 professor there is. His class is much more difficult than other econ 101 classes. Don't get me wrong, he's a great guy and actually teaches you (although his lectures can be a bit boring, repetitive, and slow). If you want an A in econ, find a different professor.

I loved Caldwell's class. His lectures were super interesting. He makes sure that you really understand the concepts and explains them really well. You definitely have to work for the grade, but if you want to make the most of your time, take the class with a professor like Caldwell that really teaches concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVE Caldwell!!! Exams are more challenging than some of the other Econ101 professors, BUT it is well worth it for how well Caldwell's fantastic teaching prepares you for higher-level econ classes. Also as a plus, he's absolutely hilarious so you can't go wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There will be people who love Prof. Caldwell teaching style, and people who don't. I am in the former. He is sarcastic, and some people can feel uncomfortable about it. For me, it was sarcastic in a good way. Warning: he is strict ( hard to get an A) but his lecture is AMAZING.

With the stress of this COVID-19 situation that is currently happening, Professor Caldwell is the least understanding out of all of my professors. Students were essentially being forced to move out of dorms Thursday and Friday and most of my classes moved assignments and lectures until next week but Professor Caldwell kept the exam on Thursday.

Caldwell is very overhyped. If you want a class with little homework, then take him. However, I came to lecture, did Problem Sets, take-home quizzes, and I still earned an average grade. Maybe it's not him and I just am not an Econ person. However, I feel I should've received a better grade even if I'm not an Econ person as I worked hard for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: good lecturer, but you will need to take time to study and not just memorize what you learn. You can only get 6-7 questions wrong total on 3 midterm exams to get an A. There will also be 6 take-home assignments that you can work on with anybody. probably the best choice since no final/essay, but tests are fairly tough, so understand material early
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Caldwell is an amazing professor. He is hilarious and caring, he knew my name (mind you that he had 200+ students taking ECON 101), and he is an amazing lecturer.

I loved taking this class. It isn't necessarily an easy A, but if you attend lectures and discussions and study for the exams, you will do well. Make sure not to lose points on the easy things. Prof Caldwell was a great lecturer and very funny; he helped me understand a lot of the trickier topics through his use of examples. Take this class!

I LOVE RON! He is so nice, funny, and a great professor. He is so helpful in office hours and just does an amazing job of teaching the 101 material. 10/10 would recommend taking his class if you're taking econ 101. Also no cumulative final which is a plus.

I was honestly let down by the hype. Caldwell is a decent at best. Lecture are dry and the exams are annoyingly only multiple choice. I never felt he really delved deep into concepts in lecture. Discussion is useful because exam questions are basically the same just with numbers changed. But besides that, discussion didn't actually improve learning
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ron has been my favorite Econ professor at UM so far. He really cares about his students and their success, and he presents the material in a very clear and concise way. His office hours help a bunch. Ron is a teacher who does research, which is a refreshing change to many of the researchers who try to teach. Couldn't recommend enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He cares about students a lot, learning their names throughout the semester, which is refreshing in a huge lecture. His lectures were animated and filled with amusing voice cracks. Honestly, my feelings about this class would be more positive with a better GSI. Unfortunately, mine didn't prepare me well for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class grading criteria is skewed compared to other professors for Econ 101. If you don't like multiple choice tests, don't take. Ron himself is caring and passionate, and really wants you to learn the material.

I had Ron for ECON101, and he was an excellent professor. He does not record lectures, and it is useful to go to lectures. The exams are non cumulative, and are the most difficult part of the class, but they don't need to be difficult. You'll need to understand the material very well, but if you do and understand the homework, thats not problematic
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Caldwell was a great choice for Econ 101. He's funny and made lectures enjoyable to go to. Would definitely take again. The one thing I would say is to take the exams SUPER seriously right out the gate. I bombed the first one and kind of blew my chances of getting an A right off the bat. Pay attention to that and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very willing to open up to his students. Once you get past his zeal for apples and oranges, Caldwell is a great teacher and guy. The class is very heavily based off of the practice tests and if you can complete those, you will do just fine in the class.
He tried to make lecture as interesting as possible and made an effort to learn as many students' names as possible. He genuinely really cares about making sure students understand the content.

Ron makes economics crystal clear as he walks you through the material (he's a natural at lecturing, so his lectures are essential to learn). However, there's a lot of information to understand and memorize, the 3 tests are basically your grade (very easy to make mistakes on them), class is curved to a B median so you will have to work for that A.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ron was a great professor and he really wants you to learn the material. He's really funny and gets to know many students by name.

Does a lot of lecturing but everything is clearly explained. His interaction with students during lecture helps to understand material. Grading is comprised of homework and three equally weighted exams

Ron is absolutely the best prof I have ever had. He is super funny and he explains the materials very well. He genuinely cares about his students, and if you have any concerns and try to email him, he usually responds in 5 minutes with your problem addressed. But tests are kinda hard for me since I did not take any AP econ in hs.

Was pretty hesitant about taking my first Econ course. Ended up being my favorite class all semester. Caldwell does an amazing job explaining somewhat dull concepts and making them seem interesting. If you can get into his class, take him 100%
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ron is fantastic. He explains the material well and in an accessible way, and will answer your questions. The textbook isn't strictly required, but was very helpful in preparing for lectures. The exams were pretty easy as long as you did the practice problems and homework along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grades you on what he presents in class and is a great lecturer (highly entertaining). If you go to class and take good notes and/or review the slides you'll do fine. Best professor to take Econ 101 with.

If you attend lectures/discussions, try on the take-home quizzes, and take numerous old exams, you'll do fine. The optional problem sets are useful too, as he uses some of those questions on the exams. He's a solid lecturer and engages with the students, making the class more interesting. I used to hate Econ but really enjoy it now because of him!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely the best Econ 101 professor. Go to lecture, do the practice problems and exams, and try on the quizzes and you'll do well. Goes off on tangents, but he's a funny and clearly very smart guy who is passionate about his field. He engages with the class and students to make lectures more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Born lecturer who has a way with words. Definitely take him for Econ 101
He's a good professor, but a very tough grader. This class is pretty difficult if you haven't taken AP Econ in high school, and even if you do, it's hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ron is the best professor to take Econ 101 with. This class is very easy if you did well in AP Micro in high school. Either way, just go to lecture and memorize drawing each graph. Each exam is a lot of application of the info, so going to discussion, doing the problem sets and quizzes, and studying is important.

One of the best professors I've had. I had never taken Econ before but he made me as interested in the subject as i'm interested in my major! I disagree with the review below that says exams are hard. Exams are easy as long as you pay attention in class and focus on what 'hints' he gives. The given practice materials are more than enough.

After taking Professor Caldwell's class, I have decided to major in economics! He is such a great teacher, approachable, and willing to help you understand any concept. Lectures are interesting and Prof. Caldwell makes it a goal to get to know his students. If you are able to take ECON 101 with him, do not pass up the opportunity!

HARD exams, unless youve asked around for practice exams from other people you will only have the one provided on canvas to study- which is a lot easier than the actual exam. 90% of your course grade comes from the exams. do the practice work early
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Limited room for error but I covered more content in my high school econ class

Lectures were kinda confusing - added stuff in slides that wasn't necessary and led me away from main points. People seemed to like him, but I didn't really love him. Tests are hard (harder than other teachers' I believe), especially since I had never taken AP Micro/Macro or any other Econ class before. Go to lecture and do practice HW to do well!

Caldwell was a great teacher. He presented the material well and with numerous examples. His tests can be tricky, but if you slow down and break the problem apart, then it is pretty easy to deduce the correct answer. If you took AP Microeconomics in high school and did well, then this class should essentially be review for you.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I came in thinking it was going to be a bad class but i actually did very well because he is very clear in lectures. Office hours are approachable but go early because it lots of people go the week before exams. Definitely go to lectures and you will learn a lot. 10 out of 10 recommend.

Caldwell was an amazing teacher. He understands that some topics are confusing and really simplifies them. He is easily accessible and such a cool guy. I do think that it is not an easy course without effort but if you put in the work you should get an A. Id reccomend going to office hours and looking through past exams to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Caldwell was a sufficient teacher but his exams are really difficult and count way too much for part of your grade. There's not much you can do if you get a bad exam score on any of the three exams that count for 90% of your grade. Each test question is 1% of your final grade. He's a good professor, but if you want an easier A, take Dudley's class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and very helpful. Tests not very difficult.

Caldwell is a great teacher who makes an effort to get to know the students that take his class seriously. He explains topics clearly, and although one of the harder Econ101 classes, it is the best class I have taken at Michigan to date. The exams are only difficult because of the multiple choice format, and if you know the concepts, you'll do well

The class itself isn't hard, but it's easy to get complacent about it. Don't skip lectures, go to section the week before quizzes, go over the practice problems  the curve is friendly, but every point does matter in this course when it comes to grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you have never taken Economics before, then Dr. Ron is your man. He explains the concepts of microeconomics in a very intuitive manner. Go to lectures and you spare yourself tons of headache reading through dry text. Prepare hard for the exams as they are very tricky. Do the practice problems as many of them appear on the exams.

Caldwell is a great teacher who really knows his material. He's very passionate about his subject and tries to make lectures as entertaining as possible. However, he makes tests very hard, hypes up his curve, and his lectures are so long. The quizzes are easy 10's, and there is no final exam. I would not take Caldwell. Other teachers are easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher. To do well do as many practice tests as you can. It is wroth it to go to lecture but I never went to the discussion sections. I took AP in high school but still had to study. Got an A on 2 exams and B+ on the other. Make sure you get all the points from the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Honestly, the class is easy. His final is hard so make sure to study. However, he makes a huge curve for the class. You get in what you put out with him. He really cares about making the students understand the material and I appreciated that.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Everyone says he's the best econ teacher at this university, but not sure if that's true. He isn't really able to explain concepts well if you've never taken econ before and acts as if it comes intuitively to everyone. Tests are extremely hard and you must study hard in order to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Caldwell is a great professor who really cares about his students. The exams were definitely tough and he emphasizes understanding the material over memorization. Review lectures, do the problem sets and practice exam, and you will be fine. I learned a ton and am really happy I took this course for intellectual breadth in engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Entertaining, but wouldn't necessarily say helpful. Tests are hard, limited room for error

Caldwell is so funny, He really seems to care about his students, The class is light actual workload, but you really have to stay on top of the concepts and have a complete understanding of them for the exams. if you sit in the first few rows you can he'll interact with you and keep you on track. Go to office hours they help a good amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Caldwell is an amazing professor. He gave every student in his 800+ Econ 101 class a thorough introduction to Economics. Though there were only three midterms and five quizzes (each midterm is 30% of your grade, each quiz is 2%) and my grade was based almost solely on the midterms I took (which are tricky), I really learned a lot. Great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: So I literally just finished caldwells third midterm and can officially say he is amazing. He is the best prof at Michigan. If you sit in the front feel rows and participate he will use your name in examples and it makes a lot easier to pay attention. Exams are fair. The Gsis suck at least mine did. Try to go go to Luis or Thomas dis. In w2017
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Great professor, can tell he really loves what he is doing. Super funny too. You have to go to lecture to pass. Exams were pretty hard in my opinion. Wording of tests was always confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Caldwell is an amazing professor and makes you WANT to go to lecture, though not necessarily required. The class itself was pretty hard and you have to put a lot of work into it. Discussion was not helpful, but that's mainly because the GSI I had was not the best. Class is graded fairly though.

Caldwell is an excellent professor and really knows how to teach. The content isn't overly difficult but really make sure you study and do the practice problems/practice test. Don't think you can get away with not going to lecture. Discussion was unhelpful and the GSI sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: As people have said, Prof. Caldwell's a great lecturer. His class isn't a joke, but his grading is nothing if not fair. People, despite what they may think, get exactly the grade they deserve in his class. He really makes you want to learn the stuff. Good class.

Sure, Econ 101 is a difficult class, but with Caldwell and solid study habits (the lack of this is the main reason people perform poorly in this class) an A is really achievable. Do well on the first exam.

Ron is a fantastic professor and person. Tries to relate to the students and get content across very clearly. Great lecturer. Exams are very fair and most/all problems are slight variations from the given practice exams and problem sets.

This guy knows what he's doing, super chill dude and really smart and helpful. I will say, however, his tests were kinda tough (all mc, no fr) but he really prepares you well. If you're interested in econ or want to really learn the material, take his class. If you're trying to pass with a good grade and little work, i'd take it with a diff prof.

Ron is great!  After the first lecture you will simply realize this man was born to teach.  Never thought I'd enjoy this class but it was probably my favorite.  He's an awesome lecturer and makes everything so simple.  I thought this course would be tough but I couldn't have been more wrong.  If you don't take econ with Ron, you're doing it wrong
Ron is everything you want out of an econ prof. He lectures well and tests are based off of lectures. Work load isnt bad
Great guy and very easy class. Makes micro topics easy and is interesting and passionate about what he does. If you can get him, take the class.
No need to go to lecture. Just finish hws and review slides before the exam.

Ron is definitely a great economics teacher. His lectures are interesting, and there are no surprises when it comes to your final grade. On the exams he definitely tries to trick you, but the class is curved at the end so that most people get an A or B. Go to class every day, study for the exam, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Class is a joke but take the exams seriously they're meant to trick you. If you wanna take an easy route, just read the book three days before the exams and get an A.
Caldwell is awesome. That said, each question on an exam is worth one percent of your grade. That's all. Good luck!

Ron is a great prof who not only knows his material but knows how to help students understand the concepts. I don't think lectures were mandatory but you should really go. He occasionally hints at things on the exam and they are helpful in general. The hard part of this class is every question wrong on the exams is a percent off your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best professor for ECON 101 without a doubt. Tests are all multiple choice, but are meant to trick you. Definitely your best shot of getting an A in ECON 101. Really cares about his lectures and students and makes himself available outside of class. Exam content is always covered in section or in lecture slides.

Caldwell is the man. If you took econ in high school and did well on the AP tests, trust me, take Ron. Three tests throughout the year with just 30 mc questions. Even if you didn't take econ, his lectures are very good and he explains the information well. However, you may need to go in for help a few times... econ isn't a walk in the park.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Econ 101 with Caldwell was very enjoyable. In the beginning I was worried because everyone says 101's a weed out class with harsh curves. But what I found was that as long as you go to class, discussion, do the take home quizzes and problem sets, and you'll be fine. Also don't even buy the book. You'll be fine with lecture slides!

The best! Econ is a tough course, Ron makes it understandable and explains things very well and very clearly. He is very organized, which a person like me appreciates greatly.  I didn't get the best grade in this course, but I learned a lot and would recommend taking him over any other professor.
Great teacher, and easy class. Three tests, thirty MC and no final. Straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I love Ron to death. He's a great guy and explains everything super well. His slides are great and he prepares you well for his exams. There isn't a ton of homework and he posts optional practice sets to help you understand the material. He's engaging and easy to follow. He cares about his students and wants everyone to understand the material!
Good professor, but exams can be tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Caldwell is a great lecturer, but I almost feel like some aspects of the class were underwhelming because they were so simple. I guess if you're unsure about your talents in econ you should take him, but if you want a bit more of a challenge Caldwell isn't a slam dunk.

Econ 101 is a pretty tough class, but Professor Caldwell clearly outlines what he wants from you. The 3 midterms are multiple choice only, so that makes things a little easier. Definitely pay attention in lecture or else you won't do so well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best econ 101 professor in the Dept and very engaging. Beware of exams, very tricky and tough!!
Good professor all around. I never took an Econ class, and Caldwell teaches a very thorough, but accessible intro econ class

Caldwell is known as the best econ101 professor. However, you WILL need to work for your grade as the atmosphere is incredibly competitive because this is a first-year weeder course. Go to lecture. Take notes. Pay attention. Good luck on the tests.

Anyone who thinks ECON 101 is  a weeder  class needs to take it with Caldwell. Lectures are engaging, he is super clear in his examples, and the tests arent out to get you. really a fantastic professor

Ron is great! His lectures are super clear and he is always willing to help in office hours. The tests are hard but if you do the problem sets, practice test, and visit his/the GSIs' OHs you'll be fine. It helps if you've had calculus since a lot of econ is math but Ron does a fine job explaining the material. 10/10 would recommend.

Caldwell was my favorite teacher this year. He is very clear with his explanations. The only thing that I didn't like about his class is that for every question you get wrong on a test you lose 1% towards your final grade.
Never took econ before but loved it anyways. Quite an easy class, went to a lot of the GSI's OH.
Never took Econ before and it makes sense to me. Overtime I ask questions he answers. He's not into making connections with his students, but he's there if you need help.
great

Caldwell is definitely one of the better professors to have for Econ 101. He's pretty clear, but you have to pay attention in class. If you've taken intro Econ before, you could probably skip some lectures. I didn't and regretted not paying as well attention. Study enough and you'll do fine!

Ron inspired me to become an Econ major! He genuinely cares about his students and explains the material in a fun/interesting way. The tests are tough yes, but if you utilize every material he gives you, you will do fine.  Very little work for this class (6 take home quizzes and study for exams). GSIs were also SUPER helpful. 10/10 would recommend.

Caldwell is a great lecturer. By far the best econ 101 professor as opposed to Proulx, Hogan, Wolfers, or Dudley. Lectures aren't necessary but I think to self-study Econ with the difficulty of the tests, it would be better off going to lecture. Take the homework quizzes seriously as the curve can come down to half a point.

Best professor to take for econ at umich but beware exams are incredibly hard and very easy to mess up on because questions are very tricky. However, if you go to lectures and stay on top of material you should be able to pull through at the top of the curve.
Great lecturer! Made econ 101 much easier to understand. Rushes through material sometimes, but always takes questions in class. Don't be afraid to ask for help, he wants everyone to do well!

Out of all the Econ 101 professors, Caldwell was probably the best one. Lectures go by really quickly, but if you took AP Econ in high school, this class won't be too bad. In his emails, Caldwell sound rude, but other than that, he responds quickly and efficiently. The tests can be tricky, so make sure you don't skim anything and read carefully.

Ron is a great teacher! He really cares that his students are learning and not just memorizing facts. You have to work hard but if you do you'll do well in the class. If you ask questions Ron is more than happy to help.

Ron is for sure the best econ teacher at UMich. 3 non-cumulative exams and 5 small and easy quizzes. The exams are difficult, but the top 25% of the class gets A-range grades at the end of the semester. Really enjoyed his lectures as he made a boring topic bearable. He is very clear and thorough with his lectures and gives good feedback.

The course material was simple enough to understand. The only issue was the high stakes grading. There were three midterms worth 150 points that were just 30 multiple choice questions along with six 10 point quizzes - actually five since one is dropped.  Caldwell is very good at explaining and I would highly recommend!

Best Econ101 prof at UMich! Ron Cadwell is a entertaining professor and really understands the level to teach at for intro Econ students. He is very thorough and his material/lectures are straightforward. Econ101 is soul-crushing, but he makes it bearable, which I am forever thankful for. Here's to a professor who cares about student well-being.

I found the lectures and the material very straightforward, but the exams were impossible. Be careful when emailing him for help because he can be quite rude in his responses. Spend tons of time studying for the exams, especially the first because that one is the hardest of them all.

Dr. Caldwell is a great professor. Very good lecturer overall. Some of the lectures are dry but he lets you know ahead of time. He lets you know exactly what will be on the exams and does not try to trick you. Do the practice problems and attend lecture and it should be an easy A.

This class was hard for me. However I can't deny that Caldwell is a phenomenal teacher. He is funny and it helps keep you engaged. I believe though, that Caldwell covers less information more in depth than other 101 professors. This means that his test questions can be kind of tricky, but I know many students found it fairly easy.

He's a very clear professor and I had a great GSI. I found the material interesting and pretty easymake sure you really understand the concepts! Be sure to get full points on all the quizzes (not hard to do) because the curve is REALLY tight and even comes down to half points.
Amazing professor.  Explains everything really well and is interesting to listen to.  Best ECON professor at the school.

Everyone says Econ 101 is difficult, but that's a bit misleading  Caldwell is excellent - extremely clear, provides thorough explanations of concepts and answers questions well. Attend the lectures. Just listen and you'll do fine  3 exams (not hard, but trick questions), 10 quizzes. Optional practice problems. Try to get Aakash Mohpal for disc.

Caldwell is the best professor I've had here. His lectures are incredibly clear and hilarious most of the time. If you pay attention and take notes in class you don't need the textbook or excessive studying. He tries to get kids to participate in class by learning their names and using them in examples, all in good fun. He is a really awesome guy.
Ron's was very helpful and as long as you put any work in, you are golden.  Go to his office hours if you don't understand anything, he is really good at clearing things up

Ron is (from what I hear) the best Econ 101 prof. at Michigan.  The class is curved so that the top 25% get A's (or A-'s), so it's not the material that makes it difficult, it's your peers.  Ron is really clear and funny though.  He learns students names throughout the semester, which is rare in such large lectures.

I loved Caldwell! He's a nice and funny guy who makes everything seem very clear. If you really understand every problem from the past exams he posts online, you should be fine on the midterms. They're not easy, but they're fair. Highly recommend!

Caldwell is great in lecture. He can be funny and provide good real life examples to keep students listening during class. His tests were all only 30 questions. They were easy, but if you make one or two dumb mistakes, they add up quickly. It is quite competitive, but if you aren't an idiot you will do fine.

The tests are definitely challenging but if you review carefully, you'll be good! And make sure to go to discussion and take notes! I went from getting a 60 on the first midterm to a 93 on the second just by scrutinizing the lectures and taking good notes in discussion. A lot of those problems show up on exams.

Caldwell is fantastic! 101 is a really competitive course with fairly challenging exams, but he makes sure to present the relevant information in an extremely understandable way. Don't skip lecture; the PowerPoints he puts online are rarely identical to what he covers in class. Participate from day one and he'll make an effort to learn your name.

Ron is the man! It is a difficult course but Ron makes every attempt to make the concepts clear and answer everyone's questions during lectures. Always available during office hours and exams are easier than other profs taking this course. Less math, more concepts.

I hear about the other Econ 101 professors and it sounds like Caldwell is the best one to have. He assigns 6 take home quizzes and 3 midterms during the semester. He explains things well and his lectures are pretty enjoyable.

Ron is a really awesome lecturer.  He is very clear about the concepts that will be on the exam, and I never used the textbook.  If you're going to buy a textbook for the class, get the 2nd edition because its only like $10 online and is the same as the new edition.  The exams are hard but certainly not impossible, the quizzes are take home.
Funny, helpful, and cares about his student. It's a big class but he tries to get to know all of his students. Best Econ 101 professor at U of M.

Best Econ 101 professor at Michigan.  He is funny, always cracks jokes, and usually ends class a little short which is nice because it can feel long.  He sticks to the Krugman textbook well enough that if you keep along with the reading and go to lecture you will be fine in class.
Dont take this class

I took 101 with Ron in the spring semester, which I would highly recommend if you're okay with a lot of information in 7 weeks. We only had 2 exams which were each 45% of the grade, but the curve helped out so much. You only needed 290/330 points to receive a solid A. Take 101 with Ron-he is the man. I'd t go back to his class just to say whattup!

Caldwell is the man. He makes Economics interesting and likes to joke with his classes. He's the first professor I've seen at Michigan that knows the names and has a personal relationship with students in a big lecture. It's a difficult, but if you go to lecture and discussion and do the problem sets, it will pay off and it will be worth it
