He was a great teacher. I took econ in hs and didn't understand it very well. Obviously the curve makes it harder to get an A than most classes, but if you wanted to get it, there was no reason why you couldn't. The lectures were clear and he did a good job of explaining the material.

Caldwell was a really nice and interesting professor. He was very straightforward with what he wanted. His tests were basically the same as the practice problems he gave us. Obviously an A is never guaranteed, but if you put the work in there is no reason you don't get an A.

Professor Caldwell is one of the best professors I have ever had.  Econ 101 is a decently hard course, but Professor Caldwell is the best one at U of M.  He is willing to help out students and he even extends his office hours.  Attending lecture is not a must, but it is extremely beneficial for succeeding in his class.  Take Econ 101 with Caldwell.
Great teacher, especially compared to other Econ 101 professors.

Honestly, don't buy the textbook. I never opened mine. Ron is very clear in lecture. He succeeds at making a boring topic somewhat interesting. He's the kind of professor who you can tell is a real person. I HATED the curved aspect of this class. It made me not want to help people out. But overall I got a solid intro to econ. I would suggest Ron.

It's tough to say how hard this class would've been with Gerson or Malone, but I came into 101 with a passion for Econ. Yet, your entire grade is based off the 3 exams, which are VERY QUANTITATIVE! If math is your thing you'll be ok, but if not beware!!!

Ron is a great professor! Econ 101 is a hard course no matter whom you take it with simply due to the curve. If you have to take it, you can't go wrong with Caldwell. His lectures are clear and he obviously enjoys the topic. He'll tell you right away that the book is unnecessary and it's the truth. Just work hard on the quizzes and go to lecture.

Don't take Caldwell if you actually want to learn Econ 101. Clear lecturer and great guy but the material covered in this course doesn't even begin to cover what is discussed in other econ 101s (Gerson or Malone). I regret taking this class with him esp because of the lack of structure the class has - no hw and no practice exams for my semester

Caldwell made lectures interesting and always answered questions until students understood. Exams are very fair and are possible to do well on if you learn the details of lectures/discussions. The textbook is totally unnecessary. I would highly recommend Caldwell for 101 and I really enjoyed the class. Now I am considering majoring in economics.
I think it was best stated:  "If you don't take econ with Ron you are a peasant."  Thank you for that amusing yet accurate comment.

I only went to lectures, did the quizzes (which are take home) and exams, escaped with a B after getting a D on the final (had an A- prior to that). Not a lot of work, not a bad Econ prof. Still needs to figure out how hard to make the exams, but definitely take 101 with him.
Incredibly easy first exam, then things get real difficult. Overall, probably the easiest of econ profs at UofM

Pledgemaster Ron, as we called him. Inconsistent exams, and not exactly similar to the slides covered in class. If you're looking for a good professor, take Ronald, but beware. Oh and completely disregard the "Kindall point"
if you don't take Econ with caldwell you are a peasant

The 2nd exam was hard but he gave us fair warning that it would be much more difficult. Being his first semester teaching at UofM he underestimated us on the first exam and had to crank up the difficulty to bring the average more in line.  He is a great teacher and lecturer very entertaining.

Ron is actually a really god lecturer. He's good at articulating basic principles and he loves what he does. That being said, he got lost a bit this semester and was inconsistent with his exams. Yes, there's a curve with ECON, but Ron had about 30 kids drop the class; unheard of. Take ECON with a more established professor on campus.

Ron is a very good professor and he makes econ interesting, but his exams are extremely difficult. He says that you don't need to use the textbook, but I highly recommend getting it, as some of the exam questions are from the textbook. As long as you're willing to put in some extra work and study a lot for the exams, take econ 101 with ron.
Ron is a really good guy!

Professor Caldwell is great, and I'm so glad that he's come to UofM.  While econ isn't easy, he made it bearable - fun, even! Definitely one of my favorite professors. He's funny, kind, and down-to-earth, and I looked forward to lecture each day.  He is helpful and smart, and almost made me want to switch to an econ major!

Simply put, Ron is a delight. What is there to say about a man with such poise? Well, three things: First, he outlines everything you will need to know. It's up to you to do problems and learn them, which can be difficult. Second, if you are struggling, he can't help you if he doesn't know. Third, be prepared to learn to put up with Ross students.
Ron is a great professor. Some exams are difficult, but perfectly manageable with adequate study time. Take Ron's class and get ready to experience the new world of scarce resource allocation!
Do not take this class. He gives out an easy first exam, and then just cranks up the difficulty way too much. He also cannot phrase unambiguous questions.

This guy comes off as nice, but in reality he isn't. He is not a good teacher. He gives you false by giving out an easy first exam. From there, things go downhill. In addition, some of his questions are extremely poorly written, to the extent that they  refer to multiple things, which in turn makes them unanswerable. Overall, I'd say don't take him
Ron is a good guy .Econ in general is hard so there is nothing you can do about that.

Ron is a good guy. Since this was his first year teaching at U of M, he made the first test far too easy, the second near impossible. Beware the second test, at least for my semester it was on little to no material covered in class or on the slides.
Great professor. Love this guy. He's a champ

TAKE ECON WITH RON! He is genuinely a great guy and cares about his students. He values teaching and makes all his lessons very clear! he promised us that we "will never need to read the book" because he "will teach us everything we need to know" THIS IS TRUE! Unlike other classes that have hours of reading I never opened the book and have an A

In his first year teaching at the University of Michigan since transferring over from the University of Kansas, Dr. Caldwell has certainly made a positive impression on the Wolverines student body. He's an intelligent professor with a clear style of teaching. He's very open to helping out students, too. I definitely recommend him for Econ 101

Dr. Caldwell is an excellent teacher, and he always makes class interesting. His explanations are clear and understandable, and he’s very approachable to ask questions. I often went to his office hours and so he knew my name, even while having two huge econ lectures! If you're taking econ, I would highly recommend Dr. Caldwell.
Chem 130 is overall an easy class, but Crisci made it even better. Great guy, you can tell he truly cares about his students. Worth it to go out of your way to take if chem isn't for you.
Great professor and honestly awesome guy. Teaches tough content in a digestible way. Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed
Ralph is amazing. He's extremely approachable and is very respectful of students. He makes the class fun and wants to see students succeed.

Great professor! Super kind and caring to his students and was super helpful during office hours. All of the GSIs were also very helpful. Grading is very exam-heavy but if you go to lecture, do the homework, and go to office hours to ask any questions, it is very manageable!

Dr. Crisci was a great professor that explained material clearly. He taught with a moderate pace, and exams were very representative of what we learned in class. Homework, discussion, and exam reviews are excellent resources to help you prepare for exams and are even worth a portion of your grade. Just don't fall behind, and you will do well!

He is pretty good teacher, lectures good however sometimes we were a bit slower than other classes; but it was okay because it would be taken off the exam. Not too much going toward the grade just the online chem homework's and the exams. There is e coach extra credit. Also attendance is not required but he does I clicker every class for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good Prof! Did go a bit slower, but we ended up covering everything.

I didn't take chemistry seriously in High School due to Covid-19 and other pandemic related issues however, Dr. Crisci is very nice and helps you understand if you attend office hours. Although, Dr. Crisci is great, he was a little slow compared to other professor and can be unprepared before lectures.

Dr. Crisci was great. He is a fun and caring guy who takes the time to thoroughly explain concepts and answer questions during lecture. If it is your first time taking chemistry or if you didn't take AP chem I would recommend Dr. Crisci for chem 130!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty good and covered everything you need, the only thing is he went kinda slow and took a lot of questions from the class, so our section was always behind for the exams. He is a nice guy and also cracked some funny jokes, and I turned out just fine for the exams by reading class notes and the textbook.

Professor Crisci did a good job teaching the material. His lectures were very thorough and he spent a lot of time answering questions. He did fall behind on the material, so it was always a scramble to learn the info before homework deadlines and exams. It is a difficult class but not impossible if you do the work.
He is extremely nice and helpful! His lectures are very clear. Definitely recommend him!! :)))))
Lectures can be slower paced but he gives very clear explanations.
Dr. Crisci was an amazing professor. He will answer any questions, and is very available.
Lectures could sometimes be confusing but he does a great job of trying to support his students despite the large sizes of his courses

He taught the material pretty well, but was very slow paced, which made it a bit hard to pay attention. He is very open to questions, which isn't always a good thing in a 500 person class, but it was usually fine. Overall, he taught me everything I needed to know.

Professor Crisci was great! He explained concepts very well and was willing to answer questions. It seemed like we were always a little behind, but it wasn't a big deal and did not impact my level of preparedness for the exams. The exams weren't bad at all and covered relevant material.

He was nice and covered topics well but since he was new last semester I think he was still finding the best ways to approach things. He seemed underprepared at times and used up way too much lecture time answering questions, but overall wasn't bad, I did feel prepared for exams.

Seemed like he came to chemistry lectures very unprepared and would often have to re do his calculations and problems that he created himself which made it really easy to lose interest in what he was saying. It seemed like he had better things to do then teach my class and he was not passionate about teaching it at all.

I really enjoyed Dr. Crisci's class. He explained things in very simple and concise terms for people who don't have a very strong chem background. He always made an effort to answer people's questions (even if one person keeps asking), and never makes you feel stupid for asking a simple question. For a first year teaching, he is doing fantastic.
Dr. Crisci was a good professor. Sometimes his lectures were confusing, but he answered all questions and did a good job at helping students. Overall, he prepared me well for the tests.

I had Dr. Crisci during his first semester lecturing at the University of Michigan. Saying this, the only thing that bothered me about his lectures was him answering questions that ended up eating up 1/5 of the lecture time. Other than that, he seemed like a genuinely nice guy and CHEM 130 is what you make of it regardless of your prof.

His lectures are not well organized and he is hard to follow most of the time, with lots of derivations and long winded algebra. He does not prepare you for the homework or tests. He takes a long time to get grades back. He was absent for most of the semester and communicated it very little. I would not recommend his class at all.

Despite what others have said, I actually thought he was quite a good and engaging lecturer. He explained the conceptual side of everything quite well, but that's about it. Evidently, he did not really care about this class; he missed a lot of lectures (making us watch recordings later on) and took forever to grade/make solutions for the graders
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult class, homework takes forever. So much material to cover, lectures are extremely boring. Actually a nice guy, but a bit unresponsive to email and not the best explainer. Everything except lectures were online, so there's more time, but he uses that as an excuse to make everything ridiculously hard. Take in the fall if possible.

He is as dry as the Sahara Desert. Lectures are extremely boring, and the course is disorganized. Exams are take home and not too bad, but bi-weekly homework sets are basically grad-level difficulty and take forever to do. Don't take with him if you actually want to learn gas dynamics. Graded on HW, Exams, and a couple canvas quizzes.

Professor Limbach has all his skill points in the intelligence department and none in lecturing. He is absolutely atrocious as a teacher and explains concepts remarkably poorly, often making no effort to expound on details. The class is remarkably disorganized, with misgraded homework, countless typos & errors, confusing grading scheme, etc. 0/10.

This might be the most poorly run class I have ever taken at this university. The lectures are almost impossible to learn anything from. The grading of the class was miserable, with students having to effectively grade their own homework's due to the extensive periods of time it took to get grades back, and the numerous errors present.

No doubt that Prof Limbach is highly talented and intelligent in his field, but he is also the most abysmal lecturer I have ever seen. Unclear about the content, highly disorganized and does not explain concepts well, sets strange homework questions that are worth an unnatural large amount of points (one HW assignment was 15% of the total grade)!

Professor Limbach is the worst professor I have ever had. He does not know how to lecture and does not explain material even when asked questions. He gives only 5 homework sets that are worth over 10% of your grade each and the average is a 75% on them. His midterm exam was nothing we had seen in class and he does not set you up for success.
I did not enjoy her or her class. I would recommend taking it with someone else.
Not a good environment to learn in.
Did not like her or the class. nicest way I can put it.
Harder than expected
I think this class is not given enough warning for how hard it is.
Did not enjoy this class really hard.
YIKES! No this class was not it. Take it with another professor.
It was hard to get along with here during her office hours.
Do not take it with her in the winter when you are already lifeless. She is definitely a hard grader.
Not a great experience as a freshman in her class. I would not recommend her if you are slower learner
0/10 would not recommend. Hard grader and was very limited with her time.

Although I am aware that 232 is a weeder class and is meant to be challenging, other weeder classes have 1) excellent instructors. 2) Teachers who are aware that their course is challenging yet go above and beyond to ensure you grasp the material. Carla didn't do either. For no apparent reason, she made her lesson more difficult.
I took this class spring 25' and she was not a good teacher. Really hard to talk to her.

I can assure you that every one of the thirty or so people who are currently praising this class as "awesome" are either fluent in spanish or white (probably both). Not even trying to go there, but Carla's microaggression is crazy. Really, girl, in 2025? Uncomfortable surroundings, awful atmosphere, and a terrible teacher.

I'm not sure how she got such a high ranking, but people, please don't! There are other professors who are 1) greater teachers than she is, and 2) better individuals overall. She is difficult to communicate with outside of class and really impolite!

She must be among the most racist teachers I've ever had! The worst person I have ever met. She made it quite difficult for the four people of color in the class to feel comfortable and seemed to be hoping that we would fail. It's a BIG no for me!

Whatever you do, please avoid taking Spanish 232 with Carla for your own sanity! When you go to her office hours, she will watch you struggle repeatedly without offering any assistance. She watched me cry for help physically and metaphorically and laughed in my face, like actually. I also wrote this in my evaluations, yet nothing changed.

DO NOT take 232 with Carla. I can't even fathom how she has gotten such good reviews in the past (which is what made me take the class with her, a decision I greatly regret). Very condescending and acts like she cares about students, gets involved in their personal life. Made me hate taking the language. Unless you are fluent, don't take with her!!

Genuinely loved this class and learned so much, decent amount of work but it was manageable and I feel like my Spanish was at it's best while in this class. We spoke so much Spanish in class every day which really helped me. Carla wanted the best for us so held us to high standards but was super understanding when things came up, 100% recommend!

I thought this professor was really great. At first, I wanted to drop the class because I hadn't taken Spanish in years and in the first week felt that I knew absolutely nothing. But I put in some effort and it was a great and enjoyable class. The only bad thing for me was the fact that the class is four days a week which was a little annoying.

I would recommend taking 232 with Carla to anyone who is fairly proficient at Spanish already. I had a poor Spanish program in hs, so I was a bit lost on the writing component. 

Carla did not offer intensive feedback. She has a particular way she wants things answered. Others have great experiences, just not me. She is a standard Spanish prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good office hours!

If you placed into a high level Spanish for your first college-level language class, take 232 with Carla. There is a fair amount of work but she is very caring and helpful. I never felt like I was being looked down upon for struggling with material, which unfortunately cannot be said about many language profs here. Loved her!

At times I felt that she said things that were inconsiderate of students' situations. In addition, she can be judgmental depending on the question you are asking and or the mood she is in that day. She is mostly in a good mood, but at times seems irritable when it comes to students not understanding the material correctly.

The class was great and I felt like I actually learned a lot of Spanish... which unfortunately is saying a lot compared to other language courses here. The professor is great and she's willing to help out however she can. But I did hate how half the grade is based on a five minute oral exam. Personally, I got anxious and bombed it, so don't do that

Great professor all around, both as a teacher and as a person. She was super open to providing feedback in office hours and encourages effort over correctness. Definitely one of the best options for Spanish 232. I wish I could take more classes with her!

She's a fantastic teacher, always makes time to help students--especially if they go the extra mile to her office hours. She fosters a really inclusive learning environment where there's no pressure to be right, she really just wants your best effort. I wish I could take more classes with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Carla, es una profesora increíble. Enseña muy bien y es maginigica a la hora de explicar las lecciones. 12 sobre 10!

Carla is the best. Her class requires some work, but if you do what she tells you, you will be good. She's super cute, cares about her students, and really pushes her students to speak better Spanish. Highly recommend taking with her!
Fav teacher at this school. Makes class fun with games and videos. Class is easy as long as you do the HW and pay attention.

Carla is pretty nice and really enjoys teaching Spanish. This class does take some work, but she is very willing to talk about what you can do to get a better grade. The exams are tough but doable, and she makes really helpful worksheets. Overall, I would definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Carla is awesome. She does a phenomenal job teaching her class. She's one of the best professors I've had here. She hilarious and makes class entertaining. She's got a couple rules that you need to follow like not using your phone in class and speaking only in Spanish. If you do that, you'll be in good shape. She's the only choice for this class.

Truly an amazing professor. I had her my second semester freshman year and her class completely changed my opinion of the university. She's not an easy grader, but if you go to her office hours she's completely willing to help you succeed. Highly recommend any class taught by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Carla is a really good teacher. She helps students when they have questions. Make sure to speak in Spanish when talking to her and other students as she does watch and listen for participation. She is really sweet and wants her students to succeed so don't be afraid to ask for help. She is not the easiest grader on papers. Still recommend 10/10 :)
Carla is very nice.  She is a tough grader, but I learned a lot of Spanish.  She does have a way of actually making class fun from time to time, and she is very easy going.

My favorite Spanish teacher by far. I actually love coming to class because of her. She is really nice and helpful. Her grading is not super easy, but more lenient than other Spanish teachers at this school. Highly recommend taking it with her.

Carla is absolutely one of the best teachers in the department. She so funny and bubbly and our class dynamic was absolutely amazing. I used to dread going to spanish, but with her, I looked forward to class every day.

Carla is an amazing teacher and a really cool person in general.  This class is a decent amount of work, but the theme of this course (España en contraste) is awesome.  Expect a decent amount of studyingwork but a really rewarding class experience!

Carla is cooperative, caring, and somewhat engaging. She makes this difficult class relatively manageable. Looking through the profs ctools sites, I found that she offers 3 times the study material. If you use the materials that she gives you and put forth an honest effort you'll do muy bien.
Best spanish teacher I've ever had! She is so nice and really gets to know her students.
She is a very lovely teacher and really knows about the subject that she is teaching. She is always willing to help. The tests are hard but overall the class is a good one.

This is my fourth semester of Spanish, and Carla is by far the best teacher I've had. She's hilarious, very easy to understand, and willing to help if something is unclear. Plus, she starts every class with a music video. If you have the choice, take her themed class, it's actually pretty interesting.

Carla is a great professor. The content can be difficult to grasp but she is always willing to spend time helping you understand. She even gives information about study abroad programs to help her students travel!

Carla is a great professor.  You won't waste time in class, however you will do many many exercises and readings.  Some of the material is difficult to grasp and isn't supplemented well by the book or worksheets. Carla does a wonderful job covering what our text doesn't.  And she rightly deserves her chili pepper award.

Carla's exercises are great and get you reading, listening  and speaking. She is very kind and will help any student that needs help in office hours. Also has info on study abroad. She knows the material inside and out and happily answers any questions. Exams can be a little bit difficult but do the practice she puts online. HW everyday counts!
Love this woman. Best Spanish teacher I've had at Michigan.

Carla is a fantastic Spanish teacher. I had a very bad experience with 231 and I was thrilled when I got to 232. Carla is fun and helpful, she made the class interesting and easy to understand. She is very knowledgable and is a fair grader. I would recommend this class to anyone.

Carla is fantastic. I used to hate spanish before this class, but she made it fun and enjoyable for everyone. When I got sick i the beginning of the semester, she worked with me to get me back on track and was very helpful in office hours. Take her themed class, and work hard and participate, and you will do well.

Carla is the worst professor I have ever had, she was very unhelpful during office hours and was very rude in an e-mail to me. She told me that she realized that I was a hard worker and that my work ethic would pay off in other classes. I have never met anyone who cares less about the success of her students.

Carla is amazing. I went into Spanish 232 after two and a half years of not taking/speaking Spanish. I was so scared to start Spanish again but Carla made the class so much fun and it turned out to be my favorite class that semester! She is passionate, dedicated, understanding, and fun. Take Spanish with her if you get the chance!
Carla is awesome!  She has the cutest clothes and she is so nice.  She is funny and a great teacher.  She makes the class fun and interesting.  She is hands down my favorite teacher so far at U-M!!

Carla is a fantastic teacher. She makes the material very interesting and clear. She's incredibly helpful and her tests and quizzes are very fair. She's not incredibly difficult but her class is definitely not a blow off. Go to class, pay attention, study hard, don't speak in english and you'll get a good grade.

I speak on behalf of everyone in my class (Fall 2008) when I say that we all loved her. She is fun, energetic, and she wears the best clothes. Also, she makes really good truffles, and she prepares you well for the quizzes and tests. Favorite class of college so far.
She creates a very dynamic exciting place to learn spanish.

Carla is awesome!  She is super fun, very energetic, and makes class interesting.  She starts every class off with a music video.  She loves it when you participate.  She does laugh at people and is challenging but the fun makes it worth it.
Carla is great!

Carla is awesome! she is really fun and she thinks of new, interesting ways to teach spanish! you get to watch a lot of great spanish music videos and she gives you lots of music on CTOOLS!really great class!
Carla is awesome!

Carla is a great teacher. Very enthusiastic and fun. She explains things well and recognizes and helps if people are having trouble. Lots of homework and busywork in this class, but it's beneficial and helps you get better at Spanish. Be prepared to spend lots of time on homework. Exams are easy enough if you're prepared. Take Carla's sections!

Carla is a great teacher and explains complex grammar concepts clearly.  There is a lot of busy work in the class I took (232) but it really does help you in the end.  Attendance is also mandatory and if you miss more than three classes your grade goes down which sucks when you have to have class on Friday.
Very enthusiastic, makes class fun to go to.

Easy class in general, teacher is passionate, although he could go deeper in topics and make content more intuitive for students, he tries his best ot get students to participate and does his best to help out students. Most people complain but I feel like he's trying to do good as a teacher and not intentionally being a bad teacher.
Not great at teaching.

Pros: three in-class exams ~90% median, very easy to get an A.

Cons: lectures are surface-level, he can't do the textbook problems he assigns, labs can be VERY difficult/long, poor-quality lab hardware screws up results. Buy the e-textbook to see author examples if you actually want to learn the content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture was mandatory but Students were expected to self teach through the textbook and attend lecture to "teach" each other. Garmire was seemingly incapable of doing his own example problems and would rarely answer questions asked students effectively. The only good thing about this class is that the exams were graded forgivingly.

Avoid taking this course and any other course with Garmire at ALL COSTS. He refused to grade the midterm until a month after the due date (take home exam) and has a history of putting impossible circuits to solve on his exams. He rarely grades assignments during the semester. The course is VERY lab and exam heavy. Lectures are not helpful at all.

Drops horrible lectures every time. I always had to visit GSI office hours for hw and I learned more from them. Labs were ok but time consuming. The worst thing is that he gives 3 take home exams, which is meant to take"90 mins," but in fact it did take 6-7 hours to complete it. Do not take 311 with him. You will lose interests in analog circuits.

It was one of the easiest EECS classes I've taken at Michigan, but I also came away having felt I learned almost nothing. His lectures were confusing and full of poor explanations. He was much better in office hours, and very accessible always willing to set up an appointment with you. I've heard he's much better for 311, so YMMV.

It's a course where getting an A is relatively easy but learning something for real is harder. The professor is quite flexible but does not spend much time explaining the materials. Still, you should be good if you can keep up with the reading requirement, which is really heavy considering you have to finish a very hard tome in one semester.

Garmire hopes for his students to learn without fearing for their GPAs. For some, motivation comes from deadlines/grades, which is disastrous with Garmire. I loved the availability of explanations on HW/exams. The project took many hours to complete (many requirements). Final exam very long. Everything open note/no time limit. Graded last minute.

Horrible textbook, useless lectures, and vague grading. Solved only a handful of simple example problems in the entire semester, never touching more difficult ones. HW had infinite retries and gave answers. Labs were a nightmare and time sink. Final project was a waste of time and had grades seemingly pulled out of thin air. Ditto for final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Started the semester with real lectures, then replaced them with 15 minute prerecordings and did nothing during the real lecture. Homeworks don't help you learn the material at all and labs are a complete nightmare because of it. Ended up learning everything from the textbook. Final project is insanely tedious for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Garmire's 312 was the worst course I've taken at UofM. The largest problem was assignment structure and effort by Garmire. HWs had no due date, unlimited retries, and gave you the answers; labs were a joke; our project had no effort in its grading (just got 100); and Garmire didn't do any problems in lecture until just before exams - unacceptable.
His lectures are not very exciting but you learn a lot in this course.
there are 5 quizzes that are more difficult than they need to be and lectures do not help in prep for those quizzes. the lectures were clear, but they were not relevant to what was on the quizzes.
this class is harder than it has to be
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad lecturer; instead of a midterm or final, he gave 5 quizzes.

Dudley was a great professor for this class. You could tell he cared and engaged in environmental economics. While he uses handwritten notes for class, he uses multiple real-world examples that go with his notes, which help relate economics to the real world. 10/10

Dr. Dudley made the class confusing by overcomplicating topics and spending lectures on random material and rushing key points. He was obsessed with catching people using AI and lectures were deleted after two days. Exams were hard to prepare for and didn't clearly match lectures.

For an Econ 101 class it is way too complicated. Writing assignments don't help, and they aren't even graded by the prof. They are graded by "writing fellows" who grade way too harshly for no reason. Tests are tricky. You're better off taking this class with another professor if you want to succeed.

I don't like his grading structure: he gives out three writing assignments and five exams that are twisted compared to what he says in lecture. Even in lecture, I feel like he talks too fast. He does do a good job of explaining the concepts, but it might be too much explaining. I feel like I learned a lot more in my discussions and my GSI.

chat gpt police. He cares so much about making sure you aren't cheating that he doesn't touch on the topics well enough and it doesn't seem like he wants you to succeed. You would be much better off taking it with anyone else as this shouldn't be as difficult for a 101 Econ class,

He focuses too much on not important information during the lecture, and speeds through the rest. I loved econ until I took this class. If you did not take econ previously, you will likely struggle. Take it with anyone else if possible, they are much more likely to help you succeed.

Not my favorite... Lectures were never engaging and I found his teaching style hard to follow. Exams were not impossible, but definitely not easy. He has very high expectations for his students and can be really persnickety. Just always kind of doing too much. Discussion sections are optional as well, which is nice.
Do everything you can to avoid taking this class. This is a class on how to take tests, not on econ. If you're not good at tests, you're cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never explains things in lectures. Just throw things on a graph and doesn't explain how to calculate anything yet expects you to do it on the quizzes.
I'd rather eat dog food for the rest of my life than take another econ class taught by this man. He teaches you nothing yet expects you to know everything.

Dudley is genuinely the worst professor Umich has for ECON. Do everything you can to avoid having him as a prof. His exams are lengthy & u only get an hour to do them. They're filled with trick questions instead of being focused on testing what you know about the content. Lectures are incredibly vague & don't prepare you well for the exams at all.

Worst umich prof ever. Lectures are rarely explained clearly, a lot of class time is spent on unrelated stories instead of actually teaching the material. It often feels like you're expected to already understand the content. Exams are extremely difficult, which makes the course stressful. Have to teach yourself a lot this course. Don't recommend!!

This professor is not good. He claimed he has never curved down but curved us down 3% which dropped all are grades by a letter. He speaks off the board in lecture and goes on rants during office hours and we get nothing done. His exams are bad. You have to read them backwards to understand and they are filled with tricks. I do not recommend.
I really like Dudley, his lectures are super engaging and he is a really funny guy.

This guy is a complete joke take anyone else for Econ101. The tests are moreso reading comp than economics. His 5 quizzes are filled with tricks designed for you to mess up, rather than to test you on how well you understand the subject. Questions are oddly weighed meaning getting 1 wrong can automatically drop you to a 90. He's also very boring.

Professor Dudley's lecture were informative and helpful, however the extreme lack of practice and homework made it very difficult to succeed in the class. Grading was based entirely on essays and 5 non-cumulative quizzes which each build on the last, so if you don't do well on one it is even more difficult to improve on the next.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot be contacted outside of class. Lectures are so boring

He rambled on in lecture a lot and assigned a lot of work. He offers extra credit several times. Overall he's an okay professor, but with all that he offers for grading, if you put in the effort you can easily get an A.

He is an okay teacher. Textbooks weren't required, but it helped more than his lectures did. His office hours help as well. His graders for the writing assignments were really bad. You could follow the rubric completely and still get points off. His tests aren't super hard, but if you get some wrong that have a bunch of points, you're screwed.
Professor Dudley was great! Loved his lectures and quizzes weren't too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He curved me from A to A- :(((((((((((((((((
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you miss anything, no makeups, your done and cooked. Curve at the end can hurt people who worked hard and help people who didn't. Overall a weeder class with a stuck up professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He starts the beginning of the year saying you get a curve. This curve HURTS YOUR GRADE. I had a 92 which got curved down to a B+.

Solid Econ professor. Lectures were good, but would delete the recordings after 2 days so you couldn't watch them later. I'm a little confused why he'd add extra credit if he was just going to shift the grade distribution at the very end anyways. Makes the points redundant cause they were for completion lmao. Cool guy though

Decent guy, lectures can be boring at times. 5 quizzes, 3 short papers. The papers can be confusing at times, but the quizzes are easy. He gives out extra credit when necessary. Changed grade distribution at the very end, which could screw some people over.

He changed the grade distribution at the last second. THE VERY LAST SECOND. AVOID AT ALL COSTS IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR GPA EVEN SLIGHTLY. Assignments are much tougher than all other teachers, and expectations are obviously unclear. The feedback received is very vague and misleading on all other assignments.

Dr. Dudley was a great Econ 101 professor! He is very enthusiastic about the subject and his lectures are pretty engaging. If you do all of the practice quizzes and make an effort to understand everything in each unit, you should be fine getting an A. I also thought the textbook was very helpful in increasing my understanding of the topic.

He is a very nice guy and good lecturer. Went to his office hours a couple times and he was very helpful and eager to teach. The material is not hard but you're only graded on quizzes and essays, so you have no buffer if you don't understand or do poorly.

The 5 quiz format is wayyy more difficult than the other econ 101 classes and I can't be convinced otherwise. Content is much more difficult on quizzes than what is gone over in the lectures and discussions. He will try to trick you on the quizzes. Writing fellows grade everything and will take points off whenever possible. I enjoyed his dialogues.

If you've taken AP Econ you'll do fine in this class. Lectures are just soooooo boring. Professor Dudley is a very nice guy, and you can tell he's passionate about econ. I just don't think he's the best teacher.

He gives extra credit, which is nice. Papers are graded by writing fellows, so it all depends on that. The tests can be hard and don't offer much partial credit, which I found frustrating. I like his lectures, though. It was a good pace to keep notes, and he gave helpful, real-life examples that solidified the conceptual topics for me.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really nice and funny professor. While he often goes on tangents during his lectures, he manages to explain the material pretty well. Although the five mandatory quizzes can be a pain, if you put in the effort and go to his office hours you should be able to get at least a B on all of them.

This class is very easy, the tests and papers are easy, I don't know what others are talking about on here. Dudley seems like a nice guy, he is helpful. Lectures are slow, and sometimes feature strange tangents, but if you go to every lecture, you should have no problem getting an A or B in the class. Textbook readings are not necessary.

Quizzes often contain material that he does not teach you. Lectures are boring and often contain more confusing than useful information as he overexplains simple principles of economics. There is some slack in that if your GSI is good, the class experience probably could be better.
he made me hate econ somehow

The content in the quizzes was way harder than what was covered in lecture and my GSI was not very helpful. His papers are also very difficult as you have to include a massive amount of information in a very small word count.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH DUDLEY!!!! It is not his usual teaching assignment, and he made it clear to us day one that he would not be taking our class seriously. Expected to memorize long lists of random words for the three exams that made up final grade. No practice work given ever, so no homework, but also no non-lecture way to learn content.

I mostly had trouble with the content and not with Dr. Dudley. I just wish that there were more assignments besides the papers and quizzes he gave us. He ended up making two assignments to help people get their grades up, so I wish he had done that from the start. Lectures are a bit boring, but he is kind, respectful, and tries to engage students.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material, classes, and discussions teach concepts well, but don't take the class with dudley. He makes exams and the questions dont match any kind of practice exams or questions or homework assignments. The gsis do more for you than dudley. Take caldwell or anyone else and you'll probably fair better in applying concepts.

He was nice, but often went on rants during class. There were no midterms or finals. Rather, there were 5 non-cumulative quizzes. Each one got harder and harder each quiz. There were 3 writing assignments, but there was first draft, peer review, and final draft for each assignment. Other than these assignments, no homework.

He's a fine lecturer but goes off topic once in a while which I found frustrating with trying to learn. The writing assignments honestly were good for learning the concepts but the way they graded is that they expect more from you than what the rubric asks. I would definitely not take this class again if I had to do the writing assignments again.

Dudley's Econ 101 class is extremely frustrating. Basically your entire grade depends on just five exams, and each question is worth a huge portion of your grade, making them very easy to fail. The exams are much harder than anything covered in class or practice materials. He's a nice guy, but I don't recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His voice is so incredibly annoying I nearly wanted to fail the class because I couldn't bear listening to it. So so annoying.

Overall an easy class that suffered from a lack of homework. There is not much review material, lecture recordings expire after 48 hours, and textbooks often don't align with lecture, making exams hard to study for. Lecture was fine, office hours are helpful, but the entire grade was reliant on 3 exams with multiple trick questions each.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everything you need to know is learned in discussion. The exams are fair, but easy to fail since each question is 2-6 points, so missing one could drop your grade by a letter. Your grade also mostly depends on the GSIs that grade your writing assignment, since some are harsher than others. I did fine, but I also felt unsupported in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were most of information and if you go its great. He is accepting of most things, however, he is test and paper heavy. Lectures were boring and he would go on tangents on one concept and would speed through the rest which made the lectures not worth going to. I would take a different professor.

Dr. Dudley was a great lecturer. However, I found the grading for the writing assignments to be inconsistent and unfair, especially since an 80% was "meeting his expectations." If you wanted an A on the paper, you had to "exceed expectations," which I found frustrating. These writing assignments are worth a large chunk of your grade so be prepared.
lectures were good, but the writing assignments are very dependent on subjective opinions from GSIs, which lost me many points alongside the very broad/unclear rubrics
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecturer Dudley was nice but strict. He was kind in OH but showed a lot of attitude in teaching so many students. Your grade consists of 500 points, 300 from 5 quizzes, and most of the rest from writings. The quizzes were challenging, with limited partial credit, and writing grades were very subjective. He's fine, but take Caldwell if you can.

Dr. Dudley is a good choice for 101. Your grade is made up of 5 quizzes and 3 writing assignments, other than that there is no homework. Old quizzes are provided as study tools which are helpful and each writing assignment includes a first draft where you're given useful feedback.

Best econ professor/class by far: no HW other than writing assignments and studying for quizzes. Quizzes are not bad if you prepare with the content given. Only thing is he is VERY stringent on grades and deadlines. If you miss something you're basically cooked.

Dr. Dudley's lectures are clear, effective, and engaging. His exams are highly application-based, so make sure you fully understand the material, not just memorize it. Your lowest exam out of 5 is dropped. Go to lecture and discussion and you will be well set. This is THE class if you want to gain a strong comprehension of basic microeconomics.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dudley is a good prof and explained complicated topics relatively well. Only graded work is 3 writing assignments, which are a little tedious but not too bad, and 5 quizzes, the lowest of which is dropped. Quizzes are hard though so be sure to study beforehand.

His quizzes are made so that no amount of studying or other review methods will improve your chances of getting a higher grade. The practice guides appear helpful but the quizzes are nothing like it. He believes it is normal for students to fail their first and second quiz instead of changing and adapting his teaching style to raise these grades.

Dudley is a very good instructor for 101. His lectures are engaging for those who don't know econ, but for the people who have taken AP or IB micro the class will feel like a complete rehash and may be a bit boring. The class is really easy, and Dudley cares a lot about students, his office hours are quite entertaining.

Do not take, avoid this class/professor!!! The class format is difficult, the 5 trickly quizzes and pointless writing assignments never give you a break in this class. I found the writing fellows to be inconsistent in grading and other econ101 classes do not have the same heavy workload as this one. Nice guy tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: WOW! TAKE DUDLEY. He is by far the best prof at UMICH. He cares for his students and explains everything beautifully. I wish he taught econ 102! I loved his teaching style so much!
Great professor. Engaging lectures, reasonable assignments, learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Dudley runs an incredibly organized and effective ECON101 section. This section is by far the best, as the only grades are 6 quizzes (one dropped) and 3 essays. Dudley uses intuitive examples and his lectures are very interesting (great for 1.5x speed). When I was wrongfully flagged by the chatGPT detector, he was quick to apologize.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Dudley is extremely passionate about the stuff he teaches and you can tell he loves to teach. He's a great lecturer, the exams were straightforward and the workload is really low. However don't take this class if you're not a good tester, 100% of the grade is exams. Overall CANT RECOMMEND ENOUGH!!!

Econ 370 was one of my easier classes work-wise although our entire grade was based on 3 exams. These exams are just like the notes he gives in class and the past exams, so if you watch the lectures and take notes, you will be fine. He is a super nice guy, just talks really slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dudley was a good econ professor but class is made up of 3 writing assignments-->writing fellows who grade them are so inconsistent so you never really know what grade youre getting. there are 5 quizzes and you can drop the lowest which is good. the quizzes are difficult though so you have to go to lectures, do practice worksheets, redo quizzes
This professors downside was the fact he spoke very very slow

A large portion of the class is writing assignments that 1). Do not teach you anything and 2). Punish you for going more in-depth than basic economic concepts.  I averaged a 99% on the exams; however, ended up with an A- because of the fact that I got a significant amount of points taken off on peer review and writing assignments.
best econ professor at umich

Dr. Dudley is great if you are interested in the subject and keeps class engaging by providing lots of examples. Personally math/science isn't my strong suit, so I found this class more difficult that my classmates. If you are like me, focus on getting high scores for the 3 writing assignments, that will really boost your grade.

Dr. Dudley is very passionate about the subject he's teaching but his lecture can get bored sometimes. But if you gonna take ECON101 take it w him. The class has 3 short easy essays and 5 quizzes no final and you can drop 1 quiz. Make sure you take the past quizzes and past homework to get ready for the quiz as some problems can be rlly tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dudley is a really nice and passionate professor. For Econ 370, he taught a lot without any slides, and would write during lecture on Microsoft OneNote which could make class a little slow. Class is solely exam-based, but they weren't super hard and he provides practice materials. The units of pollution economics and climate change were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Dr. Dudley is a great teacher. He prepared for classes very well. Course content are relatively easy to understand. He is also very responsible after class. When I sent him an email asking about something, he would reply very quickly.

The only thing I don't like is the quizzes, which is 60% of the grade.These quizzes are difficult. Be prepared!

I strongly believe Dudley is the best professor for Econ 101. I was a big fan of how he used quizzes instead of tests and you get to drop the lowest quiz grade. His lectures were very engaging and helpful. He also is easy to talk to...go to his office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear class guidelines and structure. Lectures can be sometimes a little bit boring, but he clearly cares a lot about Economics. He's also very accessible, and an Econ major advisor if you need more information.
Dudley is a great lecturer, very enthusiastic, explains material clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take Econ 101 with Dr. Dudley!! We did not have tests, only quizzes and which are fair (also no final exam). There is no HW in the class besides 3 small-ish writing assignments that people overall do really well on. If you pay attention in lecture and do the practice quizzes/discussion WS you will succeed in this class! Pretty low workload overall

Prof. Dudley is very passionate about what he does! I really appreciate his grading structure (3 500-word essays and 5 quizzes, no exams), which made it easier for me to learn and reflect on the key concepts. As long as you consistently show up for lectures/discussions and study a little, you will walk away w/ a good grade.
Clearly loves what he does, talks to students before class. Class load is pretty high, 3 essays 5 exams, graded on very little outside of those 8 things. keeps your attention in lectures for sure.
Great lecturer - very easy to pay attention to. Also he doesn't assign much homework. However, tests are very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dudley has been teaching Econ 101 for a long time. His lectures are entertaining and informative. As a person, Dudley can be fairly arrogant but is available outside of class to help. I would lean more heavily on your GSI for help on assignments.

Really interesting lecturer and explains everything in a VERY clear way with lots of examples! If you watch/go to all of the lectures and practice the quizzes and worksheets, you'll be totally fine.
One tip would be to watch the lectures online and put it in 1.5x speed, he talks a little slow so it really helps to focus on the faster speed.

Dudley is one of the best professors I've ever had. He gives clear lectures, relates lecture material to real-world examples, and responds to emails quickly. The class is out of 500 possible points, & a breakdown can be found in Canvas so you can always know how many points you have or can still gain so calculating your grade is super easy.

Top, top professor - exceptional at explaining concepts. Yes, there isn't a lot of opportunity to get partial credit on quizzes but he's also not out to get his students. Study concepts and read questions carefully and you will do fine. Definitely recommend taking econ 101 with him.

Prof is fine, but my goodness the quizzes/assignments are AWFUL. Plenty of extremely ambiguous questions that you won't get credit for if you aren't on the same mental wavelength as him (even if you're also right). Quizzes are terrible--getting 2  MC questions wrong puts you at a B b/c there's no partial credit, I've genuinely never seen worse.

Dudley's lectures are pretty funny but still boring, I stopped showing up halfway through the sem and just watched them online. Definitely watch it tho, all the content on quizzes will be covered. The class is graded through 5 quizzes (lowest mark dropped) and 3 writing assignments, but there's enough resources to help you do well if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: super easy teacher. just pay attention in lecture and get an A. not interesting at all, though.

I can't recommend Dr. Dudley enough! He is an incredible lecturer and explains everything in multiple different ways to make sure all of the content is clear. The quizzes and writing assignments are pretty straight forward. Easy to get an A as long as you pay close attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I personally feel that Dr. Dudley does not care enough about his students and his quizzes do not reflect the material that is taught in class. Additionally, I think he gives minimal room to get partial credit on quizzes and is not understanding when one tries to explain themselves. I have never felt so lost in a class and would not recommend it.

Dr. Dudley has been one of the best professors I've had so far at Umich! His lectures are super entertaining, and is always willing to answer questions before, during, and after class. The structure also sets him apart from the other Econ 101 professors, as 5 quizzes (dropping the lowest one) and 3 short essays, really reduces stress about grades.

I enjoyed Professor Dudley's ECON 101 class! His Canvas page was extremely well-organized, and everything necessary for success was always right in front of us. His lectures were long, but they were spaced out with questions to check your understanding in-between. He seemed like a great guy and was always enthusiastic in his videos!

Professor Dudley was a great Econ 101 professor. He explained the material very well, and it was very possible to do well on quizzes and papers throughout the semester. It is not a blowoff class, however, and people have to stay engaged in the class in order to keep a high average. If you are focused and organized, it should be very easy.

Dudley himself was a really great professor and explained Econ 101 really well. But the 7 quizzes that made up the class were unreasonably difficult, and the 1 hour time limit only made things even more difficult. The questions were all short answer and were unlike any of the practice problems he gave. Really struggled with the quizzes in the class

I really enjoyed this Econ 101 class. For the Fall 2020 semester, he chose to do 7 quizzes, all worth 60 points, and would automatically drop your lowest 2 quiz grades. We did not meet for class other than 1 discussion section per week with a GSI, but he had office hours at least 2x a week. His lectures were long but manageable, and well explained.

Dr. Dudley was great this semester - very clear and very open if you had any questions. I wasn't the biggest fan of having 7 quizzes instead of three midterms, but some people really liked it. I would just note the quizzes are much more challenging than the practice materials - if you participate and do a through job on the papers you will be fine

All the lectures were recorded and available to watch on Canvas. Each section had a nongraded mini-quiz to test your knowledge during lecture. He made sure his lectures were clearly understood and that he was approachable for OH or general questions. Would definitely recommend Prof. Dudley, I imagine the in-person version would be be even better.
Asynchronous lecture videos were extremely clear. Grading criteria and expectations clearly laid out before the term starts. Excellent professor.

Professor Dudley was one of the least understanding professors this semester. He was incredibly tough on grading and didn't take into account all the issues that were affecting students. He gave all open-ended questions for all of his quizzes with a small amount of time. If you're taking Econ 101, I'd recommend taking it with Zamzow for sure.
Solid lectures. Incredibly accessible outside of classes. All round great guy.

Dr. Dudley is a fine lecturer and explains complex concepts very well, but he goes off tangent so frequently it sometimes detracts from the material and causes him to fall behind schedule. Tests are fair, but the writing fellows for the written assignments are hit or miss in terms of grading. Put some effort into this class and you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice guy! You can teach yourself 101 with textbook, and the old tests he posts on Canvas are helpful. MWrite essays are beyond useless, graded by undergrads, and there is a major issue of inconsistency amongst them. Not the worst for 101, but not the best.
Very caring & replies email fast. A good lecturer as well, probably one of the best Econ 101 professor at Umich.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: He is a decent lecturer, tests aren't bad, and writing assignments (assuming you put in effort) are a good grade booster. The only reason I gave him this rating is that the lectures and examples are so simplified and dumbed down that they are almost useless for studying. Also GSI'S don't speak good English at all, so do not rely on them for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Dudley is an alright instructor. He does spend a lot of class time talking about himself instead of focusing on the material. Overall, I thought the course was ok.

Dr. Dudley makes the lectures interesting and does a really good job providing examples connecting economics to our daily lives. When studying for exams, make sure to take advantage of the practice tests posted on canvas.

Dudley gets off topic/talks too much during lectures. Stopped going to lecture so I could fast forward through the nonsense. Lecture and discussion are both optional. I did decently well in this class for not trying, so that is a positive. However, writing assignments are graded harshly by "fellows" who are just undergrads. Exams are moderate.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, I relied on his explanations and examples a lot. Classes are recorded so you can watch them online after. Papers were annoying to have but not too difficult. Exams were pretty straightforward and not too hard.
Decent lecturer. Tests are weird and difficult. Practice essays are not helpful at all. You'll have 30% of the grades graded by 20 year-olds. Would not recommend.
He's one of the most caring Econ professors at UM!

This might be one of the worst classes I have ever taken at Michigan. Beware of the hype because you will regret taking this course with Professor dudley. To start out with Professor dudleys lectures are extremely dumbed down and not helpful for tests. GSI is not even fluent in English and makes no sense. You are graded by 19 year olds. Avoid.

He spends way too much time talking about his personal life (and the "connections" they have to the material) but overall his lectures were as interesting as possible for an economics class. The grading system is great and it's really easy to get help or feedback from the GSI's/writing fellow's/him.

Dudley was a great dude. His class was pretty easy. The first two tests everyone did well on, class averages were high B's. The third test slaughtered everyone but he drops your lowest score which includes the final. You also had three papers where you went further in depth on concepts. Every lecture was recorded. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dudley was a solid choice for ECON 101. I struggle with economics in general but was able to pull through in Dudley's class. The tests were fair and the writing assignments were a good grade booster. And he drops your lowest test grade which is so helpful. His lectures were thorough and easy to understand.

Okay, so here's the deal. I absolutely suck at Economics in general, but Dudley made Econ 101 that much less painful. I think with any other Econ professor I would legitimately have failed the class, but Dudley took the time to explain things in lecture and always answered students' questions. Also, don't sleep on the discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Explained things very clearly, and I learned a lot. I started off reading the book and then realized that just paying attention in lecture and attending discussion would get me through. Didn't read a single page the rest of the semester. Exams were pretty fair and anything that wasn't, got taken off.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class, great teaching process, very helpful with any difficulties you may have. Exams weren't too difficult, just study the lecture material well. Somewhat relaxed class environment, but pay attention!
Great Professor

Great lecturer. Explains things very clearly and uses lots of examples (sometimes too much). Lectures can sometimes get boring, but useful in a lot of times. Lectures are recorded, no unannounced quizzes / participation points, so attendance isn't mandatory. Writing assignments are relatively easy and short.

Dr. Dudley as a person is really nice and he takes the time to answer questions thoroughly, but the lectures feel pretty dry sometimes and there are not a lot of assignments in the class so there's more pressure to do well on every single paper and test.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dudley is a solid choice for a Principles prof. Only complaint is that he doesn't have very conceptually intuitive explanations for tougher concepts in Macro, but then, what professor does? He's very available outside class and will answer all your questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dudley is a great prof with a lot of love for Econ. Although his explanations are sometimes a bit circuitous, he is happy to answer any questions and usually picks up on the issue the student was having immediately. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hes a very nice guy who is super passionate about Econ. I really liked this class even though it required more studying than I thought. He is super friendly and very accessible out of class. I wish I had him for Econ 101 instead of the professor that I had. I would definitely recommend taking any class with him.

Dudley is a super humble guy, which really shines through in his lectures. His passion for economics is infectious. You have to work and really know the material to get an A, but it can be done. In case the entire class does poorly (the average grade on each exam was a C), he adds a curve so 35% of the class gets As and 75% get an A or B.

Dudley is a really nice guy who seems to really care about his students. He loves Econ and tries to show us the real-world significance of Econ every lecture. The tests aren't bad at all. Attendance isn't mandatory because he posts all lectures to Canvas. Reading the textbook isn't necessary either. Great guy. 2nd best 101 professor behind Caldwell

Dudley's teaching style is very laid back, but he is an effective communicator of the material needed. He is also very helpful in office hours, and has a good sense of humor. For Econ 101, he is a solid choice

Not too bad of a class but he's definitely made it harder than last semester from what I've heard. His lectures are good and helpful but discussion section is where you actually learn how to do the stuff that'll be tested on. Tests are much more quantitative than lectures. Read the textbook, it helps

Professor Dudley makes the concepts interesting, but his Econ 101 course is not quantitative enough to properly prepare students for Econ 401. The only homework assignments are papers which are then peer-reviewed, and they don't require much quantitative analysis. But he does make himself available to students and his lectures are quite humorous.
I enjoyed Dudley's class. He is a good professor, especially because this topic is really his speciality. My only complaint is that sometimes lectures were just boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Would not have made it through Econ 101 if Dudley had not been my professor. Super detailed yet entertaining lectures. Very respectable professor who genuinely cares about his students. Grading system is fair.
Awesome professor, accessible and fair grading system
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I'm writing this to recommend Econ 370 class! One of the best professors! His lectures are clear and interesting. But I hope he gives more questions in the exam, because each question worth too much! So if you make a mistake, it affects a lot. It's basically whether you don't make a mistake or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dudley's a really nice guy and probably the easiest Econ 101 professor. His class is very manageable if you either go to class or watch the online recordings of class, but a bit difficult if you don't do that. The textbook isn't necessary, but it can help. He also drops your lowest test grade, which helps a ton.
Genuinely cares about his students. Him and Professor Adams were easily my favorites in the department. Made the regrettable mistake of going to my GSI's office hours instead of his.

Dr. Dudley is a great choice for any economics classes. His lectures are clear and he is great at answering any questions. He also gives great real-life examples to make sure you understand the material. Exams were not difficult because there were many sources to prepare well. Take econ 101 with Dudley.

Dudley is a good choice for your econ professor. He does not assign any homework besides 5 400-500 word essays that are peer reviewed before submission. My only criticism is his tests are a lot harder than his lectures. The tests are a lot of math so you have to go to your discussions to learn how to do it. Besides the tests it was very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Dudley!! I honestly don't know why everything thinks Caldwell is the best - Dudley is just as great in my opinion. He is fun and interesting to listen to, and he's passionate about econ. Tests were much harder than lectures though (lots of application and math I didn't expect before I saw the first exam) so go to office hours/discussion.
Great Professor!Makes learning Econ fun! The class is well-rounded and Dudley genuinely cares about students succeeding.
- posts lectures online - class is straight forward. Materials are all in the text book - 3 midterms (lowest is dropped) 1 final - relatively easy course as long as you put in the effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is the only teacher I've ever had that actually makes me excited to learn economics (weird, right?). Not only does he make the class as easy as possible, but I would marry him if he wasn't already married.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dudley is one of the best professors I've had at the University of Michigan. He is super enthusiastic about economics and wants his students to succeed. Tests are fair; he does not test anything not covered in lecture. Workload was light, but you learn a lot. He is also generous enough to offer extra credit; 55% of the class got an A this semester!

I was shocked to see he only had a 4 on here. His enthusiasm for economics is contagious, explanations of concepts are really insightful, and his expectations more than reasonable. The tests are also straightforward and overall the workload was very light compared to other 4 credit classes. I have solidified economics as a major because of Dudley.

Lecture with Dudley was not helpful in the slightest as he just read off the slides and would end up stuck on one small detail for 30 minutes. As others have said he recently changed the format of the class, and the new essays have nothing to do with exams. Tests are way harder than problems done in class and often are worded to trip you up. Pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lecture is pointless he just reads off the slides and rambles. You'e better off just reading the book. The assignments have barely any correlation to the exams so they don't help, and from my experience and my friends' the GSIs don't really care of want to be there. Literally just wait for a spot in Caldwell's class.
The lecture and discussions are very concept based however, when you get to the exams it is all math problems.  The lectures are not helpful.
Dudley is a really good professor. He is very excited about Econ and his lectures are really good. For 101, the grading is fair. You take 4 exams but can drop 1 of 3 and write 5 short papers.

Dudley is a great guy and can be funny in a "dad" kind of way. He tends to ramble in lecture, and the GSIs for the most part are not helpful. He changed the format of the class so there's open ended on the exams. Do practice exams and practice problems, you should be good.
A great professor who makes lecture interesting and fun. Will be honest, if you do the practice exams you don't need to go to class.

Good overall teacher, reading the notes will get you a B, and going to class will push you over the edge. He is good at lecturing and is really helpful when you have a question whether its during class or at office hours. Solid teacher, tests are slightly more difficult than the material in the notes so that is why you should go to class.

Professor Dudley is an incredibly sincere and caring person. He makes all of his past exams and lecture slides available online to students. Tests are fair provided you understand the material. I would be happy take a class with him again.

Dudley could possible be the best econ professor at Michigan. Hes funny and lectures fly by because he engages with students.  Great guy and professor.  Easy class and exams were clear, be sure not to cheat on exams though, he failed a handful of kids in our class that he caught. Also theres  is no homework for this class, just exams.

Excellent teacher and excellent human being. Any professor that genuinely cares about the mental health of their students gets my respect. In addition, the course he taught was interesting and engaging material. He has a passion for his students and for what he teaches, and exams were clear and understandable. Can't ask for much more from a prof.

Dudley is a good professor. His lectures are good although sometimes boring and he explains things pretty well. If you have no econ experience, definitely put some time into this class.  Tests are okay if you read the book, do the homework and discussion activities.  I screwed up big time on the first test and I had to work my tail off later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Note: I took AP Micro in high school I found the lectures very over-descriptive and boring, good if you are bad at econ. Ended up not going to half. Homework takes 1-2 hrs a week, and u don't need to read the textbook. Dudley seems like a good guy, but I never went to office hours. You only need to go to discussion to turn in homework then leave
He's a great guy and is always very helpful in office hours. The tests are difficult, but if you study very hard and know the CONCEPTS very well then you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't bother attending the class. Mitchell is going to waste your time. Plus, he is one of the worst professor I have ever signed up for.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good teacher with engaging lectures, but can get off on tangents time to time. Exams are multiple choice and worded pretty tricky. Def need to read the textbook and do practice problems to do well on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't get the hype. Reads off powerpoint. Questions were so much harder than practice problems but there's no exposure to harder questions so you're screwed. We had major  cheating scandals so it was a crazy unorganized, dramatic semester but if you have to take econ I guess since all profs aren't the best so Dudley's fine.

Dudley's a great professor if you go to lecture with the intention of at least trying to comprehend the material. My discussion section wasn't the least bit helpful, but it was required you attend (ON TIME - VERY IMPORTANT) to turn in the homework. The class is heavily based off of three exams, but they are rather easy if you know the material.

Dudley is one of the best professors I have had. He was fair, would only introduce a curve when it helped students, and kept to the traditional 3 graded tests. His tests are all multiple choice (50 questions) and most questions tested 1 concept. The questions looked familiar from class. He was very approachable and friendly, and made lecture fun!

Did well in this class solely because of my GSI Obeid Rehman. Dudley will teach you the general concepts but the textbook (really well written, actually) and discussion section will prepare you for the exam.

I took environmental econ class with him. He try to be clear when he explains the concept. Willing to be helpful to students during office hour. As long as you study hard before the exam, going to his office hour when you have anything uncertain, you will do fine. There's only three exams no homework.

The only problem with Professor Dudley is that he can go on tangents that end up over-explaining things or going in depth with explaining unimportant things. However, this is just because he is very passionate about the topic, so as long as you focus on the important parts you'll be fine. His textbook is great and if you study hard you'll be fine.
