Jaimie was very nice, but I would not take this class again. A large number of our classes (more than half) were moved to zoom or cancelled, often last minute and the expectations of us were not well-communicated as there was not a clear syllabus with dates.

Super nice teacher and not a lot of work. I did a hybrid class which made it even more chill, fridays always on zoom and sometimes cancelled. Totally recommend for non-english majors who need a FYWR. One of my favorite teachers definitely take her class!!

never been as frustrated as I have in this class. She's extremely harsh with grading, and only gives A's to exceptional writing, so unless you're an author, forget about the A. Talks far too much about politics, and was very passive-aggressive, and ran over time a lot. Didn't find her feedback helpful. Save yourself and take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jaime (she told us to call her that) has been an amazing professor and she cares so much about her students. Highly recommend!!
Ms. Delp is a very caring teacher who grades fairly. Take her class!!

Professor Delp made English 125 the easiest class of my semester. If you can it with her, take it with her. We only did two essay assignments (some other teachers assigned 4+), and the lowest given score across the class was a 90 for both. Overall, a very easy grader, and if you do the small assignments she hands out you'll get an easy A.

Our grades was mainly 2 essays plus some workshops to peer edit papers. I found the assignments very doable (a reflective narrative and meditative analysis), which she walks you through how to approach. There are some readings that we discuss in class to teach us how to write the essays. She is extremely sweet and caring, and super understanding.

Contrary to what everyone's saying, she's a great person but a horrible professor to have for an introductory to English class. The median grade for the class is an A, but to get an A in her class you need to give "exceptional" work even though it's an introduction to English course. Avoid her unless you have a passion for writing, too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Delp was super caring. She took the first 10ish minutes of class to check up on students. She was very understanding of COVID and its effect on us. Definitely try to participate in discussion. Take advantage of her office hours as she provides great feedback on essays before they're due. Be engaged in class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Delp is easily my favorite professor from my time so far at UofM. She genuinely cares about her students and is such a warm presence in class. She provides amazing feedback on essays and is always willing to go more in-depth in office hours. My writing drastically improved during this course, and I cannot recommend her class enough!

Professor Delp is SO nice and she cares about her students so much! Virtual learning is hard but she really went out of her way to make sure we didn't burn out by making one of the lecture sections asynchronous. She also made me feel comfortable writing personal essays and I learned a lot even with a light workload.

Such an amazing teacher and person. Really cares and gets to know you as a person. While you will have to work very hard for an A, it isn't too bad. Go to office hours and do extra credit assignments. Was my favorite teach freshmen year! If you care, she will too.

Jamie is amazing. She is so genuine. I learned so much from Jamie, definitely one of the best teachers I had at U of M. You have to put in the work to get an A. If you care about your writing, she will too.
Great Teacher. Improved the quality of my writing without flooding my workload. Super nice as well. Definitely would recommend for english 125

I absolutely ADORE Jamie. She is a ray of sunshine and her class, although tough, has been one of my favorites in my 3 years at U of M. She is so helpful and always willing to go out of her way for her students - she is passionate, talented, and endearing. She manages to get the best out of her students despite her very high expectations!

Jaimie is amazing! One of my favorite teachers I've ever taken a class from at Michigan! Seriously, if you ever get the opportunity to take a class with her, please do. She cares about you and will make time to talk to you both in and out of class. Her grading system is really fair and just do the work and you'll be good in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Jaimie was amazing and a really great prof, she cares about you as both a student and a person. She also will make herself completely accessible outside of class and she's incredibly laid back but a tough grader. She expects the best from her students so just work hard and do your best and you'll be dandy.
Very encouraging professor who give great feedback in office hours. If you go through the revision process she suggests, you should be fine.

Great class, Jaimien might be my favorite professor I've had so far! English 325 is my favorite class I've taken so far, which is odd for a Computer Science student like myself. Definitely do the readings and be engaged in class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I knew from the first day of class that she was going to be horrible; I am not looking forward to having her for the semester. She made it explicitly clear that an A is exceptional work, even though it is an introductory class for English. So sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Did not enjoy her class. She brought politics into the classroom a few times and it wasn't comfortable because she was pushing a certain agenda... it's one thing to have discussions, it's another to make a student feel ashamed. Not only that, her criticisms were not very helpful and left me feeling helpless as I didn't know how to improve my work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Honestly she's more than just a teacher, she's just the nicest, most genuine person to have to see when you walk into class. Whether you like english or hate it, you can't find a bad thing to say about her. Loved being in a class that was laid back but also drove you to better yourself as a writer and a person. 10/10 recommend. PS she's a dime

By far my favorite class of my first semester of college. You can tell how much she cares about the content and her students, and it drives even a lazy kid like myself to do well. Wouldn't call it an easy A, but if you're a good writer and participate in her class you will do well. She's so lax and going to class was low-key enjoyable.

Love love love Jaime!! I cant say enough great things about her! This was my second course with her (I took Academic Argumentation previously). Jaime is super caring about each student not only as a writer but as a person. Go to her office hours--she is so helpful and specific with creative ways to revise your essays! Best teacher I've had @UMich

Jaimie is so nice and genuinely cares about her students and helping us become better writers. At the beginning of the semester she told us it would be difficult to get an A, and it may just be that I'm a strong writer, but I also went to office hours a ton and she was very helpful. Love her and wish I could take something with her again.

I love Ms. Delp so much. She is the most caring teacher I have ever met in my life. Compared to all of my English teachers that I had in middle and high school, she is by far the best. She knows that each person writes differently and understands that on a personal level. On top of that, she is one of the nicest souls you will meet. Have her!

Jaimien is a great professor. I've never been a fan of english or writing classes, but if you're looking for an ULWR I definitely recommend this class. She's incredibly nice and I actually enjoyed the readings she gave us. You have to participate to do well but the discussions in class are very laid back. Not a tough grader either! Take this class!

Jaime is great. Really nice, really good feedback and class structure. I felt as though I really improved as a writer. During my class we only read short stories and essays, which was nice because if you didn't like what we were on it was over soon. Make sure you do the readings, class can drag and she gets annoyed if participation is low.
She was great! She is incredibly approachable about grade and assignment concerns. The course was the good kind of challenging, not hard though.

Best class I have had here so far. She's so nice and approachable. Definitely go to office hours she'll grade easier if you do. Made me enjoy writing more and not focus so much on the grade. Never was overwhelmed by the course load and there are not any tests!

Jaimien Delp is a solid 7/10 teacher (if such a scale were available). Better than most, but nothing spectacular or noteworthy. She is there to give you feedback when you look for it, and her classes are neither dull nor particularly engaging.

One of the best classes I've ever taken.  She's an incredible teacher and the classes was really interesting.  She makes you work for an A, but it's still possible.  I'd recommend her to anyone.   She's always available for office hours and workshopping really helps.  She 's really into writing with voice rather than being solely academic.

I loved her class! I recommend it to all of my freshmen friends for their first year writing. Jamie makes the class enjoyable and engaging. We read interesting stories and I never feel overwhelmed by her class. Definitely one of my favorite teachers here so far!
Really engaging, you can tell she really cares making her students better writers & avoids wasting their time. One of my favorite classes I've taken at Michigan.

Jaimie is a fabulous English teacher! So nice and is willing to help you with your essays outside of class. She also is very considerate and often let us have workdays when we were swamped and stressed instead of class.
Seriously one of the most down-to-earth professors out there! She is passionate about the class and she works hard to help you out. SO NICE.
Jaime is a wonderful professor! She was very helpful inside and outside of class. I would highly recommend taking any English class with her, I myself am even signed up for another next semester.

Jaime was awesome, she made English class last fall enjoyable and fun to come to! She's super nice and personable and covers the readings from the coursepack eloquently. It doesn't seem like she hands out A's very often but if you put in the effort in your essays and stay engaged during class you won't have to worry about your grade.

She is such an amazing teacher! At first I thought that taking an english class would be boring, but she made it incredibly fun and engaging. She seeks your voice in your writing and not necessarily the typical 3 body paragraph format. Definitely recommend her, hands down!
She was a really awesome professor. She was very helpful with revisions and also very generous. She made this annoying requirement enjoyable! Definitely recommend her.

I love Dan. This is my third time around having him as a professor. He is just a really great lecturer, with super clear (and accessible!) slides that give you everything you need to know for the exams. He has good jokes here and there, and tries to make everything digestible. If you haven't taken a class with Dan, you're missing out.
Nice dude but i don't know why a moral philosopher is teaching a political econ course. We read Marx for one day and spent over a month on random moral philosophy questions.

I took Dan's Intro to Ethics to begrudgingly meet a HU distribution requirement and it ended up being my favorite class that semester. I decided to take another class with Dan to meet more HU requirements. He's such a kind and caring professor in office hours and his lectures are entertaining enough.

Did the moral progress section and was very interesting but lots of reading. The 2 graded assignments (not C/NC) were graded kinda hard but if you go to office hours or send him some emails about it before you submit, you'll be fine. He is very clear, funny, and easy to talk to. Unsure if he'll have this section again but overall he's a good prof.

This was one of the most challenging classes I've taken. Professor Lowe was kind and approachable, but the GSI graded very harshly. Exams were detailed and focused on specific parts of the readings, plus surprise quizzes made it tougher. Not ideal for beginners in philosophy, think twice before taking this if you're not a philosophy major!!

Professor Lowe was a fantastic professor and made this intro to philosophy class that much better. He explained philosophy in a very approachable way, and is also just a kind guy. He made time to meet with me outside of office hours when I couldn't attend. There is a decent amount of reading, but if you enjoy philosophy, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dan!! Dude is an amazing lecturer for a topic that can get easily murky and boring. He is engaging, dumbs things down for easier digestion, and makes actually funny jokes but still can be serious when talking about real-world applications of ethics. Overall just a great prof, hopefully I'll be taking more classes with him in the future.

Dan Lowe was by far one of the best professors I have ever had at Umich. He's insightful and engaging without being biased or persuasive. He's able to convey difficult concepts in simple terms and he made it a point to prove how much he cares for not only his class but his students. His lectures were inspiring and the classwork was easy and fun.
Prof Lowe really is the best lecturer on campus. I am majoring in Philosophy now because of him. Everything is organized on Prezi, clear, and he makes everything so interesting.

355 is basically just discussing essays on modern issues from the left and right perspectives. Lowe manages to make his lectures really engaging and interesting. He doesn't allow devices to be used in lecture, and there's really no need to take notes, so you can just listen to him lecture, which is a refreshing break. There are pop reading quizzes.

He's funny and clear! Attendance not req'd but recc'd, bc 3 question, 3 minute pop quizzes on reading (usually on mondays & weekly), but summarizers can get you out of reading... 6 reconstructions (a=b b=c, so a=c), not super hard. Final essay 6 pgs. The class is so interesting, and helps your argument confidence, great for future lawyers!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures exactly corresponded to the weekly readings and were all on Prezi which made them super easy to follow! Overall the course was structured well and the lectures were really interesting, and as the semester goes on his humor comes out and he's actually really funny. Also my GSI was awesome and made the 2-hour discussion bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. A large percentage of the grading is based on few large writing assignments, but he is available for feedback and willing to help with writing.

Dan is a really good dude. In 196, there was a lot of dense reading. Never more than I could handle, but it was unskippable and a big time commitment twice a week. That being said, 3 simple papers and participation were the bulk of our grade and he'll help you a bunch if you just ask. Dan cares a lot -- I highly recommend taking his classes.

Professor himself gets a bump for his personality, he seems to care a lot about the subject and helps facilitate the class. However, the class itself is a mess. The syllabus hardly is informative, and you're graded extremely harsh with a very ambiguous and uninformative rubric. Just take the intro to philosophy class, this class isn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the material. His class are organized and engaging, though not really innovative. And although I went to class every time, I heard you can set an alarm at the time of the quiz instead of actually go to class. You can get something above 95% on the exam as long as you memorize everything on the slides.

The lectures are very straight forward and so are the reading quizzes. He doesn't really say much beyond what's already on the slides, but the slides themselves are well done so it doesn't really matter. My biggest complaint is that he doesn't allow electronics in class so I couldn't take notes directly on the slides with my tablet.

He puts together a very interesting selection of course topics! Honestly, I had to study a lot for the EXAMS. Nevertheless, essays are graded fairly and the GSI is always happy to help! AMAZING experience overall!

Learning ethics with him is life-changing. He makes the course material very digestible and teaches you how to understand philosophical arguments in creative ways. Awesome GSI as well! He is the perfect professor for this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: PHIL 196 started off as an interesting class with a relaxed atmosphere, but it changed mid-semester to one not deserving of the FY Seminar tag. Papers were graded like we (First Years) were juniors (my 2XX English courses were easier), participation was graded with scales not in the syllabus, and readings were often 40+ pages/week for a 3 cr class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor was nice, but the class itself incomplete. Despite being 3 credits I did more than a 4 credit English course, with more papers and more reading (75-100 DENSE pages per week). The way the grading was done was unclear and inconsistent. Despite being a philosophy "introduction" most vonyrny would've been better suited for upperclassmen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is simply amazing! He is one of the best professors - if not the best! His lectures are full of well-paced learning, great real-world examples/connections, and lots of jokes! He is always easily accessible and loves to answer questions after class or during office hours. Honestly, I am only going to be taking PHIL 361 for him next semester!

He's a great lecturer, and def knows the material very well. If you actually do the readings and go to lecture, it's very easy to succeed in this class. The essays were graded a bit harsh tho, so make sure to dedicate a lot of time into them. Overall fantastic professor who I'm taking next semester, and very interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Excellent professor-- structures lectures well, raises very interesting points for discussion. Get help with papers, he is very smart and happy to talk through arguments.

Professor Lowe is great. I took his class in Fall 2021. He explains the material well. He is always down to chat during office hours and is very helpful. His grades fairly. Also, participate! It is not required, but it makes the class so much more fun when you engage with the great material and think about things seriously! Take a class with him!

Dan is a great lecturer, his Prezis are amazing, very thorough and well thought out. You can tell he really cares about teaching and students. The exams and papers are very straightforward, but certainly challenging. Interesting lectures and readings, no textbook. Reading quizzes randomly throughout the term. Really good GSI this term.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lowe's Great! Knowledgeable, with a clear and engaging lecture style. Class was clean, straightforward, no fluff, no bs. A solid amount of reading, but you could often get away w/out doing. No formal lecture attendance taken, except random reading quizzes given in lecture. Go over his Prezi's before the exams and you'll be alright. Would Rec!

He is super nice and also hilarious! Exams are super reasonable and not hard to do well on exams. Make sure you do the readings bc reading quizzes can help or hurt your grade A LOT - and participate in section! If you do well on reading quizzes and get a good participation grade exams and essays are not something to stress over.

Prof. Lowe is very knowledgeable and his lectures are very interesting, even in an online format. He makes everything relatable and understands the needs of his students well. Everything about class grading is very transparent, and he is great at answering any and all questions. Would take him again!

Professor Lowe is a kind and compassionate instructor. He is always willing to make time for you outside of class. Professor Lowe is one of the best people I have had the opportunity of meeting. In his course, he will teach you empathy not just through his own example in how he treats you as a student, but in how he encourages you to treat others.
Super unreasonable. Really just not a great guy, he won't help you if you need it. Feels like he wants to make it hard for you to succeed. Stay away

Not the worst I've had, but certainly not good. The lectures seem like they're kind of pitched for high schoolers and he doesn't seem that well prepared. Not hard to do well on the essays, but not a prof I'd recommend.

This is the second time I've taken a class with prof. Lowe, I had PPE 300 with him before. He is one of the best profs I've had at umich. His lectures are great and he does a really good job of breaking things down so that they're really simple.

Professor Lowe is an excellent lecturer. His lectures are extremely understandable, even when going over confusing material. Additionally, the way he structures the class is conducive to a synthesis of the material. Pop quizzes are easy, yet still require a read through of the material in order to do well. Essays are graded nicely, but fairly.

This class was my favorite course of undergrad. The content is fascinating and Dan is an amazing lecturer. His lecture style is clear, articulate, and stimulates introspection. This philosophy course has truly moved me and the way I think. Love how this course was laid out. Readings and exams are easy and you truly LEARN.
Very respectful, caring and understanding of her students. Projects are pretty straightforward as well.

She is an amazing person, but she canceled class so often that it gave us way less time than we needed to finish projects. This made the course more challenging than it should've been and caused a bit of resentment. If you get the chance to take a class with her just be aware of this.

I might be an outlier here in my rating, but she was out for maybe 60% of the semester and that kind of disrupted my success in her class. She's also not great at replying to emails. Other than that she's great!
Very clear on grading, helps you improve your work, extremely kind. I highly recommend taking her for this class I learned a lot as well as had fun.
Great Instruction, Super caring, and definitely empathetic. If you are thinking about having her as your prof, I definitely recommend.

SHE'S AMAZING! I haven't had everybody at stamps, but she's one of the best to do it. Well thought out assignments and she carries herself with patience and empathy. Take a class with Katherine if you can!

She is awesome. Take her class. I recommend her!!!!!

I love her personality. (Very caring, understanding, and respectful to everyone.)
Goated professor. Take any physics class with him.

GOATED! In all seriousness, you can really tell that Dr. Weller wants to see his students succeed. He understands that majority of the students taking PHYS 150 are on some sort of preprofessional track and so he provides many opportunities for extra credit and test corrections. He definitely speeds through lectures though so it makes it tough.

All of the lectures have real life demonstrations and are very entertaining. The professor cares about making the class an environment for collaboration and does a good job of it. It's a very positive learning environment and the kind of class you can easily make friends in while learning the material.
Dr. Weller makes things click. He explains things simply and in a way that is intuitive and interactive. Among students, he is clearly the top physics lecturer.
Literally my favorite teacher I've ever had. The class is hard, but Dr. Weller is awesome!
Great Prof.

Dr. Weller is one of the best instructors I've had at U of M. He connects physics to real-world applications in medicine and beyond, making the content immediately relevant. Incredibly supportive and approachable. The difficulty rating reflects the nature of the course, not his teaching. He does everything possible to set you up for success.

Dr. Weller was one of the best instructors I had at Michigan. Physics can be a difficult course, but he had an incredible way of making challenging topics more accessible and understandable. During studio sessions, he made sure we understood the reasoning behind the problems before moving on. Definitely recommend taking Physics 250 with Dr. Weller.

Dr. Weller was one of the best instructors I had at Michigan. Physics 250 relies on short lecture videos, but his studio sessions made the material much clearer. He's very approachable and explains concepts in a way that helps you truly understand the physics instead of just memorizing formulas.

Kind and compassionate person, really helpful during his office hours, and reasonable with his test questions. iClicker is off completion, lots of extra credit opportunities, and the content is difficult but manageable with adequate studying outside of class.

The most supportive and inspiring professor. He cares about his students and their learning. He is easy to reach out too and very responsive on different platforms such as email and piazza. 10/10 would recommend. I wish he was teaching 250!

Great professor. I am taking 250 with someone else and I wish that Dr. Weller is teaching 250 this semester because I got a v.good experience in 150. I am suffering now with other professors (2 are teaching the 250 class and they don't really know how to teach).

Weller was an amazing lecturer -very clear and full of examples- and it's obvious that he is very passionate about what he does. He took feedback and seemed to really want to help us understand the content and do well in the course. He made physics at UMich possible!

Had fun with this class! There were live experiments shown every lecture and Dr. Weller was a very well spoken & hilarious prof! It truly felt like he wanted you to succeed in the class. I found the content to be pretty challenging, but there's a lot of resources and help provided. He's also gets back to emails and questions very quickly.

Dr. Weller was my workshop professor, and was genuinely one of the best, most caring professors I have had at UMich. He took the time to made sure I understood difficult concepts, and he also admitted when he didn't have the answer to a question, which I think was equally valuable.

Genuinely my favorite professor I've had at UMich. He is incredibly engaging and explains stuff extremely well. He's also fun and quirky in a way that makes you care about physics. He's also very receptive to feedback.

Dr. Weller is truly one of the best lecturers at UMich. He is very knowledgeable about the content and willing to help anyone with any sort of question they have. I am yet to find another professor who is adored nearly as much he is.

Best professor I've ever had, period! Super engaging, made jokes and included cool demonstrations in lecture. Midterms were difficult but fair. Homework, discussion, and extra credit makes up a heavy part of your grade. Discussions are graded for completion and extra credit is easy. Attendance is taken via iclicker and lectures are recorded.

Dr. Weller is one of my favorite professors at the University of Michigan. He brings his passion for physics into every lecture and always keeps the perspective of students in mind when teaching. His office hours are welcoming and collaborative, I would not have gotten as much out of Physics without Dr. Weller's commitment to his students' growth.

I went to all of Dr. Weller's lectures this semester only because his lectures were that amazing. He does a great job of explaining concepts, he clearly cares about all of his students, and he is a large part of the reason why I enjoyed taking the course.
He was a great professor and seemed to want all students to succeed. I appreciated his demos in class and how he was always available to help. I highly recommend his office hours!

Dr. Weller was an amazing professor who takes the time to help you understand concepts in office hours. I also really liked how he remembers students' names and is very attentive. The exams were pretty challenging but the extra credit helps to buffer your grade.

Dr. Weller is an amazing professor. His lectures are hilarious and really easy to understand. His exams weren't always easy, but if you do the practice problems, you'll be fine. He is also generous with extra credits and there are a lot of opportunities to raise your grade. I would definitely recommend him!

Very engaging lectures, provides resources to succeed on exams, and good communication. I was scared to take physics, but his enthusiasm made me appreciate the subject so much more. Explains concepts in a way that a 5-year old could understand.

Dr. Weller is a great lecturer. He is incredibly fair, and is always willing to answer student questions. He really does believe in his students, and encourages perseverance. His exams can be difficult, but his grading is very fair and so long as you keep up with the workload you will know where you are in the course.

Dr.Weller is a fantastic person and is willing to help anyone succeed. However, the tests are pretty hard even if you do all the necessary practice, so I recommend office hours (I think this will get better in future semesters).

If you don't have a physics background, this will be a difficult class. However, Dr. Weller does everything in his power to make lecture interesting, and clearly cares about students. He'll easily match and exceed the effort that you put forth into this class. Don't expect the median grade on atlas unless you're ready to work for it.

I love Dr. Weller and personally, he's one of the best lecturers in umich. His office hours are really helpful but the exams are VERY hard. I did all the modules and practice exam problems and still the exam scores didn't turn out well. I think people with a physics background do better in this course.

I can not stress enough how amazing Dr. Weller is as a teacher. Although, physics 150 is challenging course, Dr. Weller devoted a lot of his time to teaching each week, especially in office hours where he thoughtfully broke down challenging problems and approached all questions with true passion for physics and respect for all his students.

Weller was an amazing professor who did a good job of breaking down material. He was always accessible outside of class and went out of his way to help if you ask for it. The tests were fairly hard (and varied in difficulty) but he gives a lot of extra credit. Overall, very sweet guy who really cares a lot about his students.

Professor Weller is good but he needs some improvements such as preparing students more for exams as well as explaining the concepts in a better way. GSI's weren't that perfect and most of the times they didn't know what we're asking for. Overall good but not perfect or as expected.

Dr. Weller is very kind, respectful, and enthusiastic. He actually makes changes based on feedback, like creating video explanations for tough problems. He encouraged us to reach out for help often, and the team had many office hours during the week. This class was hard, but I feel like it was created to where I could succeed if I put in the time.

Dr. Weller is a great professor who explains tough concepts in ways that are easily digestible. Hardly ever, if at all, did I feel as if he put things on our exams that did not correlate to what had been asked of us in lecture or studio. Each exam was only worth 14%, and he offered a heavy dose of extra credit. Dr. Weller for president!

I think Dr. Weller is a great professor! He did a great job at explaining concepts and being engaging! He was also very helpful in office hours. However, I do think that some of the pacing was a little rushed, and I don't feel as though I was fully prepared for the new content that was on the final. Otherwise, I would definitely have him again!

Dr. Weller is a wonderful professor. I feel like there are definitely things that he can improve on in terms of his lecture habits. The exams for the class are hard, so practice the module questions to prepare. I wish he would go over difficult questions in lecture. The last unit we did felt rushed, and I feel like I wasn't prepared to succeed.

Dr. Weller means well but needs to prepare more. His exams feel unnecessarily difficult and don't match what he teaches. He mostly reads off the PowerPoint, and while he offers office hours, the exams are nothing like the practice. I wish I felt more supported and knew what to expect.
Amazing professor, always has an interesting lecture. Anyone saying he is not ready to teach or is bad, must have not been paying attention. Every lecture was clear and answers questions anytime

Prof. Weller was good overall and I believe that he'll be better in teaching physics 150 and in how to prepare students more for exams. Physics is not easy but most of the times he made it fun. His exams are heavy and they don't match the practices or the mock exam and I believe that this is one of the things that he must improve. Overall, good exp

Weller is a good person, happy guy, and overall I think a good lecturer. I stopped attending in person and moved to lec. alternate and watching the lec because I found myself getting way behind irl, too fast. Hard tests, but generous ways to make up grade.
a whimsical man with an infinite amount of doohickeys for physics demonstrations

Dr. Weller is engaging and informative. He may be new to teaching, but he makes material easy to follow. Tests are challenging, but that's part of taking a physics class. I personally liked him a lot. If you use the concepts he teaches in lecture, succeeding is possible.

Very bad experience. I used to attend all lectures and do much more than what we are supposed to do but unfortunately the professor was not ready to teach this course. He do many mistakes and he tries to make fun but honestly it's not funny at all...

Passionate, caring, and makes physics easier to understand and interesting. I would definitely want to take him again. However, despite going to almost every office hour, doing everything provided, and pouring much of my time into this class, I did not do great on the exams. This depends on how good you are at physics but definitely hard content.

This was the worst experience at U-M. I didn't expect this much of studying for a physics course. He's wasn't ready to teach Physics 150 and the big proof for that is that one or more times students asked for something and he didn't know how to answer. Also, he improved his ipad problems recently. Don't take him because you will have hard time.

One of the best professors I've had! Although he is newer, he genuinely wants his students to succeed. He is enthusiastic and funny in lecture and very helpful in office hours. Not all materials matched with exams well, but that wasn't 100% his fault, since he just took over. He listens to his students, and actively tried to make things better!
Neither lectures nor studios were helpful. Don't take with him

Dr. Weller made everything confusing and stressful. This class is not meant to be that hard and that's what most of the students say usually when taking it with other professors. Nothing he said matched what's on exam or homework. This class made me wish to die because it drained me. I would NOT recommend him to anyone.

This class gave me hard time knowing that I used to hear from other students that physics is easier than other classes. As someone mentioned before, he's not experienced at all. For other semesters I recommend him doing quizzes after each module which would increase students grades. UNRECOMMENDED.  Effort for nothing.

Physics 150 is not for him! You must put a lot of effort. He does multiple mistakes which make a student feels lost, and I don't think that we're here to let him learn what to do from our feedbacks or survey that he used to tell us do it. Also, the examples that he gives or even the practice problems are very easy compared to the exams....
Concepts were hard but he was very enthusiastic/motivating
One of my favorite lecturers at umich by far! Made content easier to understand somehow and kept class engaged during lectures! highly recommend!

Amazing professor, clearly cares about what he is teaching and his students, and truly wants you to understand the content. Made the class way more enjoyable than I thought it was going to be. Would 100% take another class with him.

Dr. Weller is amazing and i'll be retaking phy 150 with him again because i did the course as P/F due to personal issues that didn't allow me from saving my A grade. Exam 1 was really hard and that's what at least 90% of students said, by Dr. Weller took our feedbacks into consideration where he made the other exams much better. Highly recommended

Dr. Weller was a fantastic professor. He clearly puts in a lot of effort even for a class full of pre-meds who don't care about physics. His lectures were entertaining, clear, and helpful, and I'd absolutely take another class with him.

Dr. Weller did an amazing job teaching this course. It is tough for me to enjoy physics, but he made each lecture engaging and easy to learn the concepts. This was probably the best physics has ever been explained to me. For attendance, it was beneficial to attend in person, but an alternate option was available if you couldn't.

Dr. Weller is an amazing professor. He takes feedback very well and does his best to make sure every student in his class succeeds. There were plenty of extra credit assignments which contribute significantly to your grade. He is also a great lecturer and made difficult subjects very easy to understand.
I never write reviews but I ADORE this guy!!!!! try and take his class if possible one of the best profs here at UM teaching one of the hardest subjects! he made me love physics again :))

Genuinely the worst class I have ever taken. Dr. Weller is nice, but you can tell he is inexperienced. The lectures do not reflect the homework or exams. I have taken Math 115 here at Michigan, and this class was worse on so many levels. Nothing could have prepared me for the trauma I've endured this semester as a result. You work hard to fail :(
Great teaching style with engaging lectures. Dr. Weller is great at answering questions and takes the time to explain questions so that everybody understands. I would 100% recommend.
Dr. Weller is a great professor. I did not come across too many professors that are as helpful and dedicated as Dr. Weller. Definitely recommend taking his class!!
Very open to feedback!

As someone who has never taken physics before, Dr. Weller does an amazing job at breaking down concepts and taking the time to walk through confusion and questions. Highly recommend taking physics with him, am purposely taking Physics 250 this spring semester to have him again.

Dr. Weller is an awesome person and professor. He remembered all of the students names in a huge lecture just to make us feel respected. He was super helpful and available and truly cares about his students learning. I would definitely recommend taking his course if you are taking physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Explains everything so clearly. Definitely cares whether students are understanding well or not.
Very funny and helpful professor, glad to have taken his class.

Dr. Weller was an amazing professor. I have always struggled with physics, but he explained things so clearly and with enthusiasm in every lecture. I genuinely enjoyed being in his class and I feel as though I learned more than I have from professors in the past.

He is a great lecturer and truly cares about his students and wants them to learn. He also makes sure to keep lectures engaging. If you put in the work you will receive the grade you hope for. This class is hard but definitely manageable with this professor.

Dr. Weller was an awesome professor. 100% recommend for physics 1. He tried to get to know lots of students names and was very accessible outside of class if you seek out help. Enthusiastic lecturer and really cares about his students success.

Dr. Weller has very entertaining lectures that are well paced and filled with practice problems -- both demonstrations and student answered. Overall a wonderful course. The best possible conditions to learn something as difficult as physics.

Despite having a tough time throughout this course, Dr. Weller has been a great professor providing support to his students. He personally met one on one with me after exam to review the problems I got wrong and how to approach them. Overall, despite exams being on the harder side, Dr. Weller does his best to make them fair and the course doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: GOATTTTTTTTTT

Inspirational professor. Definitely loves the content that he teaches, and his passion for the material is contagious. Would 10/10 recommend taking a difficult course like Physics 250 with Dr. Weller. Took him as the instructor for studio and was the central reason to why I passed the course.

Dr. Weller was always kind, compassionate, and humorous with his students. He had an incredible way of making harder topics more accessible, and would always make sure we understood the problems and how to solve them before moving on. He was enthusiastic about the material and made his students care!

Dr. Weller was always incredibly kind and helpful to students taking this difficult class. He made the material feel accessible and would break down problems in helpful ways, giving tips and also making sure everyone felt confident before moving forward.
Dr Weller is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. I have taken multiple classes with him and I wish I could take more!
Genuinely one of my favorite professors. Dumbs things down really well and cares so much for teaching and for his students. Would 100% recommend him for a tough class like Physics.

I'm glad I took physics 2 with Dr. Weller, given how difficult it is in other semesters. He was kind and made sure we had all the resources necessary to succeed. Most exams were proctored but open book. Assignments can be a little difficult but nothing impossible; he made grade adjustments when needed. Overall, put in the work and you can succeed!

I really wish I was able to take Dr. Weller's class in person rather than online in the Spring. You can tell he truly cares about his students and their success. I appreciated his way of teaching and will never forget him as a professor.

Dr. Weller was one of the most receptive professors I have encountered at UofM so far. He was excellent at adapting and breaking down the large amount of content in Physics 250. If you have the option to take him for Physics 250, please do it. He responded promptly, actually listened and implemented feedback, and was a refreshing professor to have!
Amazing professor, taught the contents very well and grades really fair

Dr. Weller was awesome! He recognized our struggles with the course/material and made changes to grading policies to help with said struggles. He also implemented feedback given to him by students, almost immediately, which I really appreciate!

Dr. Weller was teaching this course for the first time, and as a new faculty member at the University of Michigan, he managed to do a great job navigating all this new territory. He is very receptive to his students and their wants and needs. His students and his class are important to him, and it shows.

Easily the best lecturer at this university. Dr. Weller makes sure that each student knows the material and recognizes the difficulty that comes with it. Whenever he saw we were struggling, or unfair policies were in place, he changed them promptly to make it so that it was easier for us to success. THIS IS HOW YOU BE A TEACHER TO STUDENTS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, Dr. Weller is a very good professor. He can get contradictory at times, going back and changing things he said prior. He makes 250 understandable, the volume of content creates the difficulty of the class. He really cares about students, which is a nice change of pace.
Dr. Weller will go down in history as my GOAT. So fortunate to have met this man before leaving the univesity
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best prof ever you will understand so well

Dr. Weller is one of the best STEM professors I've had at UMich. He's incredibly passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students academically and personally. He does his best to ensure everyone is doing well and creates a supportive learning environment.

Dr. Weller is one of the best professors I've had at UMICH. Physics is not an easy class, but his passion and excitement are contagious. He is very supportive of his students and is fair and flexible in the course to ensure we receive the most benefit (eg. posting lectures earlier during exam weeks, taking feedback and applying feedback, etc.).

Hands down the best STEM professor I've had thus far. So knowledgable in physics and made the class actually enjoyable for me (I hate math). I struggled heavily with 150, but through his guidance 250 actually made so much more sense to me. Highly, highly reccommend taking physics with him.

Dr. Weller is the best STEM professor at Umich. It is refreshing to have a professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed. He is super receptive to student feedback and explains hard concepts in a very digestible way. GOAT
Daniel Weller is THE BEST professor I have ever had. HIGHLY recommend!

Probably the best professor I've ever had. Very enthusiastic, kind, receptive to feedback, helpful in office hours, and genuinely wants students to understand the content and do well in the course. I couldn't believe how well I scored on exams and really understood what I was learning. My goat!!!!!

Dr. Weller's lectures are very detailed and clear to understand. All of the studio work, quizzes, and homework is also extremely relevant for exams as well as the MCAT. He really cares about how well students learn and encourages students to come to office hours. I would recommend phys250 with only him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, who explains material well and clearly explains his expectations of the difficult of material for exams, something a lot of the physics department fails to do. Super nice guy, always responds to questions/emails and is readily available for office hours. Highly recommend to take him for your physics courses if you can.

Dr. Weller is one of the best physics professors I've every had. I am NOT a physics person!!! But Dr. Weller simplifies difficult concepts so that I was able to easily follow along with the material and solve problems. He is a passionate, enthusiastic, and kind professor. Love love love his teaching style.
This guy is straight up GOATED. The best professor at this university!
He was really nice, had him for physics studio where we did practice problems, he was always really helpful and genuinely wanted kids to learn.
I will die for this man. goat

Dr. Weller is super enthusiastic, funny, and easy to talk to. He genuinely cares if students understand the material and always takes time to help when needed. You can tell he loves what he does and I highly recommend him. As someone who isn't the best at physics, his explanations made it feel not so hard.

i haven't heard anyone say any bad things about this professor. he's down-to-earth, kind, and very invested in making sure everyone learns something from studio. i loved his explanations and enjoyed his class.
Dr. Weller is an amazing instructor who cares about his students and who always works hard to provide us with the tools and material we need to succeed in this course!

I wouldn't have survived Physics 250 without Dr. Weller. He wasn't even my assigned professor but I went to his office hours and workshops because he was able to explain all the content so much better than the videos. He's super patient with any questions you have and I cannot recommend him enough.
Seriously, one of my favorite professors at Michigan and loves what he does and is very good at teaching physics and going above and beyond

The only one of the Physics 250 instructional team that knew how to teach. Learned more in 1 hour discussion sections from him than in 3 hours of lecture from Eckhause, Meiners, and Yang combined. Really patient and good explanations. Only reason I got a good grade in this class. Absolutely should be the lead instructor for this class.

Dr. Weller is awesome. I had him for my Physics 250 studio and went to his office hours. He made all the hard concepts in lectures seem really easy. The actual lecturer in the class, Dr. Yang, wasn't great, but Dr. Weller's studio lectures made up for it. I'd recommend, if you're taking 250, to make sure Dr. Weller teaches you in some capacity.

Professor Weller is probably the most caring educator I have met. He makes the material really easy to understand in a class that is known to be incredibly difficult at UMich. He is willing to have one on one which truly tells you a lot about him because not many professors do that. Professor Weller is awesome, the physics department needed this!

Dr. Weller always had a positive attitude and made so much extra time for students to learn Physics especially with a difficult semester losing our main professor. He is a great teacher and always broke problems down in different ways that everyone can understand!

Dr. Weller was an amazing teacher and resource during my time in physics 250. His office hours were super helpful, and he explained concepts very clearly. He makes learning fun and easy. I highly recommend Dr. Weller as a professor.
Dr. Weller was a great professor. He explained concepts very clearly and was very helpful. His office hours were great.

Dr. Weller is the best science professor I have had at Umich. He singlehandedly got me through Physics 250. He was amazing at explaining difficult concepts and was the most supportive professor I have had here. He made an effort to know all of his students and I could always tell how passionate he was about physics. Go to his office hours!!!

Dr. Weller was one of the most personable professors I have had at Michigan. He was great during the optional workshops and office hours, and he helped me actually enjoy and understand the course material.

Dr. Weller got me through Physics 250. He explains concepts really well and is to the point. He is probably one of the most enthusiastic and helpful professor that I have met in a physics course. Overall, his specific section made the class a whole lot more palatable/understandable. I definitely recommend people to take his section if possible.

Dr. Weller is genuinely probably the best professor I could ever had at UMich. You can feel his love for physics through his teaching. He is super reachable outside class and his office hours are SO helpful for the exams. I couldn't have gotten an A without him.

Dr. Weller was a very passionate professor. His lectures were always clear, he was one of the best professors I have ever had. His office hours were very helpful and he was always willing to meet outside of class if you needed extra help on the material. Highly Recommend!

Dr. Weller is genuinely one of the most passionate and kind professors out there. His help was literally the only reason why I did well in physics. You can tell that he enjoys what he does and he is really good at dumbing things down and explaining things in multiple ways. I would 100% recommend any class that he teaches in.
Dr. Weller was one of the best professors I've ever had. You won't find another stem professor that cares about their students more than he does. His office hours are extremely helpful.
Good teacher.
Harsh grader for a 101 course and would only speak Spanish which made it extremely difficult for new learners, also never responded to emails
Professor Lavin was truly a great Professor for Spanish 231. I would highly recommend her.

Erin Lavin is great. They care more about students learning rather than grades, so there was often very little or no homework. We had 1 midterm, which we were allowed to correct in class for a better grade later on, and one final that was very easy. For a 400 level Spanish, very easy. I would take their class again and again.

Prof. Lavin is a fantastic teacher. She is funny, smart, and makes class really enjoyable. If you have the chance to take her, I would 100% recommend her. If you're a freshman who got placed into this class, don't stress; she's a great teacher who is always willing to help you if you ask.

Professor Lavin is by far the best Spanish teacher I've had. She's very relaxed, calm, easy to talk to, and funny. She's clear about what you do and don't need to know and will never surprise you with random information on tests. She'll always make sure her students are prepared and have a good time. 10/10 recommend

I took 487 with Erin and it is probably one of the best classes I have ever had. She is brilliant, cool, relatable and willing to teach you what you want to learn. She wants to see you succeed and helps with your Spanish a LOT. Pay attention, feel free to ask questions, participate and you will have an easy A. Must have professor for U of M.

Legit the best Spanish prof I've ever had. Very informative, funny and easy going. You'll leave her class with real-world knowledge. She doesn't like the concept of grades so she's very generous, but you will respect her so much that you'll work hard as to not disappoint her. Everyone should try to take a class with her if possible!

Oh, palabra? I didn't know anything about linguistics before I took her class and now I want to take as many Spanish linguistics classes as possible, preferably with her. One of the funniest, kindest, most intelligent professors I've ever had. Everyone should take a class with her!

Brilliant. She is hilarious and engaging as one could be for a required language course. She tries to keep the class light and enjoyable. Indeed flannel loving, but the blue sweater is better. Laid back and easy going. Easy to talk to, very caring, passionate. Musically inclined yet technologically stunted. Highly recommended.

Everyone taking UM Spanish should try to get Dra. Lavin at some point, especially for a linguistics course. She is brilliant, hilarious, kind, clearly passionate about what she teaches, and is constantly opening students eyes to real-world usage of linguistics. Lots of interesting life stories. Hands down, the best Spanish prof Ive had at UM.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr Lavin is a brilliant need. Loved her class.
Great prof. Dra Lavin is very easy-going and down-to-earth. Flannel-loving. Advice-giving.

Dra Lavin is great. She's very laid back, reasonable, knowledgeable, and understanding. She does what she think will be best for her students. She encouraged me to stay in the course despite initially feeling unsure. She really cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Great person and professor!

Best spanish professor i've ever had. class was rather easy and tests are pretty straight forward too. essays aren't graded too hard. also one of the funniest teachers/professors i've ever had in my life! definitely take 277 with her
I loved Dra. Lavin! She was clear in what she expected and very laid back. Definitely take spanish with her if you get the chance!

Profesora Lavin is so great! She's very helpful if you go ask about something after class or if you attend her office hours.  She's pretty laid back and likes to really get to know her students.  My entire class was trying to get her again for 102.

pompstacular professor! First half was kinda boring, but the second half of the course on pomps were actually very interesting. Ionides is passionate about that second half, so it makes it much more fun

Amazing scholar and decent lecturer. Class is more project focused, with the exception of two exams and quizzes every day. Materials presented are definitely interesting. I think having more engaging lectures covering fundamentals before going off tangent is a plus, but otherwise Dr. Ionides is nonetheless very knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ionides is an expert in time series analysis who is passionate about imparting his knowledge to students. He also takes a genuine interest in students' projects, providing objective evaluations as well as valuable suggestion and guidance. As his student, Ed is always ready to help, offering effective solutions when you encounter difficulties.
Worst professor ever. Class is not related to homework. Project grades are really low.

His online lecture were not helpful in instilling interest in the subject. Moreover, after working hard and be on time with the projects, he graded it harshly just on the false notion.  It is import that you cite each and every line of your project ( Similar to a research paper) otherwise he drops your grade like crazy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not the best lecturer at Michigan

He is a painfully slow lecturer and always appears disorganized and all-over-the-place. The syllabus claims homework is graded on completion if sufficient effort is given but that is not the case. There's a disconnect between lectures, homework, and exams. Stats 401 has been one of my least favorite classes I've taken at Michigan by far.

The whole class is disorganized-he often gets confused with his own notes and solutions. HW rarely has anything to do with lecture content, and asks for extremely specific answers on quizzes and exams. Basically you have to go to gsi office hours or google everything yourself to know what's going on.

Nice guy, tries hard to explain material, but very disorganized, not good at explaining simple concepts that GSI's can do. Tests material that were not taught requiring students to go to extra office hours to know how to do them.
I like this guy. He does everything possible to make lectures good and unenjoyable. Good replacement for sleep aids.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst professor Ive ever had. Unprepared for every lecture. Clearly puts no thought into the class. Some of my favorite quotes: I dont know if the GSIs would mark me down for this answer. (On his answers to questions on his own slides) I dont want us to think about that right now. (When asked what the passing grade on the midterm was)

No respect for your time or personal goals whatsoever. There is no basis for grading such as canvas or rubrics, and is all based on his own opinions. Talks through all of class, leaving you with a huge workload and doesn't communicate clearly at all.

Endi talks a lot in class and will go on tangents for ages, using up a lot of valuable class time. Along with this, he has no respect for your time. Once he kept me for over an hour after class unnecessarily. Avoid taking Endi, or else you will never hear the end of it
Endi will go on tangents about absolutely irrelevant things that have no relation to the class. Due to this, he will often go ten minutes over, and you cant get any work done in class.

He will lecture for 2 hours straight with no breaks in between and expect you to make eye contact with him at all times and contribute to discussions. It's very hard to keep forced and most times he talks about his life rather than the materials. His feedback to you will feel like personal attacks and makes you want to switch majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice and funny, easy grader. Some projects were a bit unclear, but make more sense as you work on them.
Endi tends to talk a lot during class however you are able to complete majority of assignments during class. He is very flexible with due dates and a easy grader.

I think Endi is underrated. He definitely does talk alot and goes on tangents, but overall is a really funny guy. Instructions are pretty hard to follow at first, but he gives help when needed. Is willing to give extensions and is very forgiving. Very passionate about what he does, and wants students to be motivated. Light grader.
Would constantly go on tangents about very unrelated topics and will go over class time because he was too busy talking to actually teach the class.
Somehow managed to insult everyone in the class individually every day. I think he means well, but it's just not translating in any way that is productive to the class.

Would NOT recommend having him for Second Year Studio unless you have to. We didn't actually start on our projects until halfway through February when every other class started earlier, and we had no time to work in class because he spent 90% of it ranting about meaningless topics. Doesn't use Canvas AT ALL & very harsh attendance policy. Awful

This Boomer class is just him reminiscing about ‘days before tiktok' while dismissing student work that isn't immediately connected to his definition of "art". He doesn't teach—he lectures about himself. Feedback? Nonexistent. Questions? Met with condescension. If you enjoy being talked down to by a man stuck in the past, this is the class for you.

Endi goes on long tangents, has vague critiques, is passive aggressive, fixates on the unrelated, does not grade until the semester ends, demoralizes, and often makes offensive remarks. Classwork always becomes homework because of his random asides. If you have a heavy course load already I would advise not to take classes he doesn't specialize in.

Generally, professors at University of Michigan are respectable and reasonable. However, Endi is an exception. Expect to sit through all his useless life stories and offensive comments on you. He will pick on you out of nowhere unless you are a exceptional student who is willing to get down on their knees and treat him like a kind.

Endi Poskovic made countless passive aggressive remarks towards me and other students. He would tell us we have a work day and go on to talk for over half the class period which left us with more homework than normal which ultimately would affect time to do work for other classes. Also,he never clearly explained our assignments,or how to do them.

Class with Endi was a roller coaster. He created schedules for work time that were then interrupted by his tangents or unrelated lectures. His critiques often targeted personal aspects rather than discussing the work and he seemed to hyper-focus on specific elements of a piece rather than provide overall feedback.

Endi was the worst professor I have ever had. Never in my academic career have I had an altercation with a professor, but Endi's borderline and sometimes highly offensive remarks, passive aggressive judgement and blatant feedback about not only you as a person but your work has people running out the door before he comes in after hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Endi is a really nice person but he will talk about the most random topics. He will say we have the whole class to work on something but will then spend half the class taking about some off topic. Very nice guy and genuinely seems like he wants the best for his students. he is also cares a lot about attendance and participation.

Endi is a delightfully odd professor and I wish he could teach all the classes I'm taking. He certainly is easy to send on long tangents but not a word is wasted- very inspirational and tells great stories. He mostly likes to see your work shift or be influenced, so lean into that for his projects. He has a lot to say and it is worth listening to.

Endi is delightfully weird and clearly cares about his students. However, his lectures are very meandering. Even a yes/no question would start a 20min spiel. It takes him months to return projects, and while his feedback is thorough (maybe even nitpicky) in critique, explanations for final grades range from brief to non-existent.

Endi is definitely, one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I would always look forward to going to his class because it was always so fun. He can sometimes go on long rants about things, but if you actually listen to him the things he says are relevant to the topics being discussed. I agree with the previous comment: you'll love or hate him.

Endi is definitely very different from most professors, but in a good way. He cares a lot about students, their success, and growth as artists. His projects push you technically and creatively and he is actively involved the process. It can be difficult to gauge grades sometimes and he tends to ramble but I loved his class!

You'll either love him or you'll hate him. He's a decent professor, but he goes off topic for so long he wastes half+ of most class time talking about an entirely unrelated topic. One thing is he likes things done his way, if you do something he doesn't like, just wait, he will like it when he thinks he influenced it

Endi is hilarious. If you ask to go to the bathroom, expect a twenty minute lecture about ducks (yes, ducks). It is an honor to be in his class and you will learn a TON, and I mean a ton. He has amazing stories to tell you and is incredibly kind and extremely good at what he does. He expects a lot from you.

Endi is very knowledgable. He's a fun teacher and connects very well with the students as well. One criticism is that he sometimes goes off topic when he's explaining things which makes him hard to follow. Assignments are a bit unclear at first and he and didn't provide grades on projects until the end of the semester

Endi is a really great teacher. He is straightforward and tells you exactly what he is thinking. He's funny and weird and sometimes rambles. You'll learn a lot from him, and he is very helpful especially when you need something. TAKE HIS CLASS! Especially if you like printmaking because he's the only one who teaches it!
Hard exams. Too much material. Rushed and confusing. Nice person.

As a non philosophy major, I honestly zoned out most of the time until it got to interesting topics or arguments. She literally gives her exam questions, which are 10 questions and she will only ask 3 on the exam. I will mention, they are sort of paragraph style, but either way its already provided. A is achievable.

Professor Edmonds was great! She was a good lecturer that gave real-world examples and very interesting to listen to. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but if you attend most of them you get extra credit. You're graded on 5 quizzes (which you can check your answers with your GSI), 2 midterms, and 1 final.

This class seems easy, but it's a lot of work. Edmonds gives misleading review guide. Exam means are B-. She is accessible (constant office hrs) but u rly have to fight to learn concepts (unclear slides, bad review guide). Lecture attendance bonus doesn't get an A if u have a low A-. Cool concepts but hard class, discussion was chill not a blow off

Professor Edmonds was amazing. No matter what career you are going into you should 100% take this class, and I feel that I learned so many things that I can apply to my future career. She is very funny and lectures were engaging, but you should definitely read the textbook to fully understand everything. I genuinely enjoyed learning from her.

Anna is such a good professor! All her lectures were super interesting and the course content felt very applicable to everyday life. Her office hours and GSIs are very helpful. The class is also one of the best paced and organized classes I've ever taken. I'd recommend her and her classes to anyone!

you can tell she's passionate about what she teaches, which is a really good trait to have as a professor. she makes the class engaging by paraphrasing and expanding upon what's on the slides rather than simply reading off of them. it helps too if you read from the textbook time to time before class since she restates what's in it each lecture

Professor Edmonds is great! Everyone should take PHIL 183; critical thinking skills are so important, regardless of major. This class is interesting but not hard, has a pretty standard setup of two midterms and a final. Study for a few hours and you'll be fine. Prof. Edmonds also has the most helpful office hours of any instructor I have taken.

Anna is AMAZING! Take this class. The content is so interesting, she is incredibly smart, and the workload is not significant. She and the GSIs want to know you are engaging with the content, and discussion activities are super fun. I've learned a ton from her. Also, gives midterm/final prompts in advance.

I loved this course- Anna is extremely knowledgeable, and her lectures were captivating. Beware of the 'fivers'- there are 6 pop quizzes in discussion sections over the course of the semester. They're relatively easy, but you do have to fully understand the readings to do well on them. Overall, I'd highly recommend the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Edmonds is great. Super upbeat and she's extremely knowledgeable. The exams can be a pain in the neck and there's really nothing counting towards your grade in this class but the exams.

Prof. Edmonds' lectures were so amazing! I found myself really engaged with her content and loved her willingness to help, but the discussions weren't great. The GSI I had struggled to answer some of the material, and was late to discussion a handful of times. Not having a good discussion section really hindered my understanding of the material.

Amazing and interesting lecturer. Wanted to be friends with her. The class has a good amount of work for a 3 credit, but definitely manageable. Very interesting content that feels applicable. Helpful for conducting research and analyzing data.

Anna's lectures were interesting, though my favorite part of the class was the discussion beacuse it was more participatory and evoked more thought from the class. The readings were super captivating, and I still find myself applying concepts from this class to my daily life. Anna's office hours leading up to exams were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anna is an amazing professor. This course applies to everyday scenarios, and the conversations it generated were extremely stimulating. The material will stick with you, and it's a great introduction to philosophy, as someone who's never taken a Phil course before. She loves to get to know her students after class and during office hours!

One of my favorite professors ever. Very engaging in lecture and discussion. Very relatable, funny, respectful and considerate. Straightforward class structure. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Class topics are incredibly relevant to the real world. The textbook is cheap and easy to read. Go to lecture and listen to what she says, instead of copying slides.
Good professor! Very knowledgeable and accommodating for students!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class and Anna is super kind and very knowledgeable about her subject. Would recommend.

I really liked Anna. This course was really fun and I loved the content. The tests are very straight forward as long as you read the text or listen in lecture. I took this course in a really busy and tough semester, so I could not give it my full attention that I otherwise would. Despite that, I felt like I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Edmonds is passionate about the topics of 183. However, I found the lectures went off topic and it took a long time to get to the topics of the lecture. The quizzes in this class were also quite challenging by the wording of the questions. If you want to do well, you need to go to office hours, which is tough if you can't make it.

She was so incredibly personable, and made me feel super comfortable being more casual and real in an academic space. Super knowledgeable on the subject matter, and very welcoming in office hours. Just an all around super cool person who is interested in our processes of reasoning just as much as her own, which here went a long with the course :)
Love

I loved Dr. Edmonds and her entire class. Very interesting topic that she dives into very clearly in her lectures (all of which are recorded). This class is test heavy and most of your grade is based on 2 midterms and a final. I would recommend going to her office hours they are extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love prof edmonds, she's very silly during lecture which makes class enjoyable. She's very caring and helpful for the writing assignments and basically hands you the answers you're looking for. overall the course wasn't difficult if you put in the time and effort to read all the readings!

I love Anna Edmunds so much. She is an incredible teacher, her class was easy and very engaging, and she seemed passionate about what she was teaching. If you have a chance to take this class, 100% take it.

Nice professor that cares about students. Professional yapper- will talk and you will not understand half of it. Pretty funny and passionate. Would recommend going to a bar or being friends, would not reccomend taking this class unless you plan on pass/fail declaration. Exams and quizzes crazy hard and not fully related to lecture.
Loved her class, excited to take more

Best philosophy professor I've ever had! Professor Edmonds makes learning the material very easy, no textbook required for Phil 110. Lectures were recorded and she encourages questions during lecture and discussion. Really helpful during office hours too!

Great professor. Always tries to make lectures fun and interesting, and constantly makes herself available at discussions and office hours. I highly recommend reading the the textbook chapters before discussion and coming prepared to discussion with your questions. She will clear any confusion you may have about the current topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! This course has a lot of terms and 3 exams so it's a little bit hard for intl students to finish exam in time, but she allows me to use google translate on exams, which makes it way better for me! Recommend!
This course and Professor Edmonds are so nice. Materials are interesting and close to daily life, totally different from what I imagined at first.

Dr. Edmonds is great. This is not an easy class, but she tried to make sure that everyone understood the material through plenty of office hours, review materials, exam review sessions, and more. The 3 exams are weighed pretty heavily, so it's important to do well on them. She also tied the material to everyday life, which was really eye-opening.

Easily the best professor I've had. She's a FANTASTIC lecturer and makes a point of keeping things interesting. Her class was phenomenal, and the readings and work really make you think a lot. The workload is not too heavy and the class is very doable. GSI's can be kind of hit or miss.. mine wasn't great but I would still 100% take the class again!

Edmonds is truly a great professor to have. She is incredibly intelligent and keeps things fun and hilarious. She is incredibly engaging. I will say that her lectures sometimes go off the track, though, but I was always engaged. I would go to lectures, read the assigned articles, and participate in discussions and you will do well!

The assignments and grading for this class are very straightforward. The topics covered are very interesting, and inspired me to continue pursuing philosophy! I honestly didn't go to lecture because they didn't seem useful, but I'd for sure recommend going to you discussion sections.

My friends thought this class was easy, but I genuinely had a hard time with it. Prof. Edmonds was incredibly easy to talk to, she was fun, and her office hours were always a blast. I'd recommend mastering terminology to do well in her class. I took it winter 2021, so it was still online. Great woman, and I didn't even like the course content.

Anna Edmonds is by far my favorite Professor I've had. She is extremely passionate abt the subject she teaches and is always willing to make time for her students outside of class. The material is not always immediately easy to understand but her lectures are very engaging and she is willing to answer in depth as many questions as you have.

One of the best teachers I've had at Michigan so far. The material was very interesting, and she was extremely helpful during office hours. It wasn't that difficult of a class, but it's so engaging you'll want to pay attention!

If you can take a class with Anna; do it! Even if philosophy isn't your passion, she's the kind of teacher who inspires and makes it fun. I would definitely take another course with her! So fun, kind, passionate, and makes you want to learn because you want to please her. The best kind of professor!!

I took Critical Reasoning and am now signed up to take her Ethics course this term. I can't say enough good things about Prof. Edmonds. She works so hard to make sure everyone understands. Very smart, very caring, very reasonable, and the content is extremely important and useful. Can't wait to take another course with her.
