Amazing professor, I had her for critical reasoning and that class really makes you think about things differently. Also she's super down for discussions on other philosophy things in office hours or going through homework/quiz problems
Anna Edmonds is awesome. She's funny, kind, and makes the content digestible. The quizzes and homework can be hard- but just go to her office hours and you'll be so set in this class.

Prof Edmonds was the medicine for my weary spirit this term. I actually teared up twice during her 183 lectures - during the election and her last lecture about changing our minds and the truth. She doesn't get caught up in the little things because she just wants you to learn. If only everybody would take this course, the world would be better.

Great professor and great class. Though, I would strongly reccomend waiting to take this course until it's moved back in person. I didn't feel as though I learned as much as I could have if it wasn't online. don't take it winter 2021, but do take it fall 2021 and beyond.
Great professor and great class! Put effort into quizzes and Tophat. Interesting material. Do not be daunted by the metacoglogs and make sure you truly get the material to do well on the quizzes.

Anna does a great job teaching philosophy. Even with the difficult Zoom classes, she makes lectures engaging . She's very understanding when students ask questions in lecture and office hours. Very flexible when giving examples of topics discussed, which makes it easier to understand the concepts.

Absolutely amazing professor. The class is incredibly enlightening, and Prof. Edmonds is a great lecturer. The class is not incredibly easy, it takes a little time to grasp the material, but she explains things really well and is very open to questions. Try to get into one of her discussion sections too, they're great!
One of the most genuine and intriguing lecturers. I never missed a class nor an office hour because everything she said immediately stuck with me.
A very interesting and pertinent class so far. One of the best online setups - really clear instruction and Prof. Edmonds is a wonderfully understanding person to work with during these times.
Incredible professor.

Very nice and willing to help outside of class if you were willing to put in the work, but this is not an easy A class since Anna can be a bit confusing with her explanations. Definitely go to discussion and ask questions as she will explain all the tophat and quiz questions! (she was also very helpful once everything switched online!!)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Edmonds is hands down one of the best professors at UM. After I went through a health crisis at the end of the semester, she was the most compassionate of my professors. Subject matter of the class is straightforward, engaging, and eye opening. Pro tip: try to enroll in the discussion sections that she teaches, very much worth it! :)

Great course, great prof. Definitely transitioned to online teaching because of Corona/Covid better than anyone else. Lectures and working through problems live was very helpful and always phenomenal one on one. Most enjoyable course I've taken at Michigan. Not an easy A - get help on the quizzes and Tophats in office hours, you won't regret it.
She is a fun and knowledgeable instructor who makes class interesting and fun to be. However, the homework and quizzes are pretty hard, so be prepared to spend time on them.

Hands down the best professor I've had so far. Go to her office hours and she's more than happy to help. A genuine person who cares about what she teaches and her students. A must take for anyone in any major.

Philosophy of Critical Reasoning is a must take class. Prof. Edmonds is extremely knowledgeable and articulate, not to mention caring and funny. Shell help you from whatever point youre at and she knows a ton about other fields related to cognitive science. Lots of assignments but not hard to get an A.
critical reasoning was a good/interesting class but beware there's some stats at the end, it's pretty basic but if you're illiterate in math like me it's kinda hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course was the most enjoyable/valuable class I've taken. Prof Edmonds is awesome - clear, approachable, interesting, and funny. Amazing she is able to make time for all her students given how big the course is, but she does. Office hours are packed, but she'll still make individual appointments. You'll actually improve your critical reasoning.
Exceedingly intelligent; entertaining; woke. Her course should be required.

Anna Edmonds is a very respectable person. Her enthusiasm for the class was very evident, and she cared a lot about her students doing well. She cares about what she is teaching, and that makes her lectures more enjoyable. She is very accessible as welllllllllllllllllllllllllllllll.

Anna is awesome in every way. Her lectures are interesting and clear and she is extremely helpful one on one. The last week of classes she departed from the text and it was two of the best classes of college so far. If you get into her course count yourself lucky. Memorable course, memorable professor.

Prof. Edmonds is hands down the best professor youll have at Michigan. Her lectures are engaging and funny. She really really cares whether youre understanding the material. My 183 GSI sucked by I show up at her office hours a multiple times a week and am getting an A in the course. Theres nothing she doesnt know about and this course really

I came into this class considering a PPE major; now I am no longer considering that path.  She was ok, not great not horrible.  I probably would have enjoyed the class if I didn't find philosophy to be a waste of time (spoiler alert: it is).  She's really nice and very willing to meet with students.  Not a difficult class

This was my first philosophy class and I wasn't sure what I'd think.  I loved Anna and learned a ton.  She is sooo good. I'm thinking of majoring in philosophy now and would take another class with her in a second.  She's excellent at teaching philosophy but I also learned a lot about life.   And super funny, which helps for staying engaged.

Excellent teacher, very obvious after listening to her that she's brilliant and knows what she's talking about. Only time I was bored in class was when I didn't do the readings and had trouble following in class. The readings aren't really mandatory but it really helps for discussion. 2 Papers, 1 Final, weekly readings, pretty easy workload.

Anna is truly brilliant. Philosophy is a difficult subject, and she understands that and really wants every student to take something away from the class. It's not easy, but definitely possible to do well. She's not a stereotypical crazy philosophy professor, but extremely rational, not-biased, and makes you want to learn and contribute!

First I had her as my logic 180 GSI and then I ended up having her again for phil380. Her classes were a struggle at first but I ended up knowing my stuff and now she's even writing my recs. Easily my favorite GSI.  Sometimes doesn't respond that well to email but is great in OH and can really help with LSAT logic games. 10/10

I had Anna Edmonds for Knowledge and Reality in the Fall of 2011. I can say with total honesty that this professor probably changed the way I will think forever. She made the material easier to understand, but besides that she made me see what it is to be a kick-ass thinker.  She's tough but she's also almost certainly a genius. And funny as hell.
Anna is great. She's super smart, helpful, and really funny. Papers were very difficult, but her grading was fair and I really enjoyed having her for discussion. I'm really going to miss this class!

Ethan is the GOAT. If you need to take an English class, take it with him. He grades everything on completion but always provides amazing feedback, which really helped my writing. He was also very personable and emailed me when I missed class to make sure everything was okay. Such a sweet guy - could not recommend him enough!

If you feel as though you have not been exposed to writing outside of academia, then this class is perfect for you. Although there is (obviously) lots of writing, the class is not too much of a burden overall. Ethan is GREAT! He is so caring and understanding. You can always ask for accommodations/extensions on your work + gives good feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ethan was a great professor! He made a (somewhat) uninteresting class exciting, and he was genuinely so kind and caring toward everyone in the class. He provided great feedback, and showed real interest in student work.

Believe the  hype, she is an amazing professor. If you take math 525 with anyone but Dr.Wolf you will deeply regret it. She is amazing !! Yes, I said she is amazing twice because the first tiem didn't emphasize it enough.

Amazing professor. Incredibly patient, always super clear about expectations, great at explaining things, and cared a lot about her students doing well. No complaints about her, but the class is set up in a way that makes it really hard. The constant masteries and team hw are really annoying. Textbook was recommended but you don't really need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Math 105 with Dr. Wolf and she was amazing! Was always patient and understanding as well as great at teaching concepts in an easy to grasp manner. She was super accessible out of class if you needed help, and was an easy grader. Attendance was appreciated but not mandatory. Never had any issues with Dr. Wolf and would 100% recommend her!
She was always willing to help everyone, and would take extra time after class to help students.
Easy class. Boring for me because I don't really care for the topic. Professor Toups is friendly and I would take a class with him again

Super caring, understanding professor! Exam resubmissions were so helpful, and his feedback makes the necessary edits straightforward. He said we should be able to earn the grade we want, and makes it possible for students. His approach to teaching the Indigenous history of North America changed the way I'm going to view history from here on out!

Such a kind, inspirational, and caring professor! I learned so much about Indigenous history, and he is so knowledgable and so good at facilitating positive and inclusive discussion. Assignments are varied and fair, and I truly think my writing and reading skills improved. Definitely recommend if you want to learn new angles of American history!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Toups is great! Take him if you can. Incredibly knowledgeable about virtually every topic. Gives great feedback on essays (allows unlimited re submissions). Facilitates great class discussions. Passionate and energetic. Also very relatable and approachable. Really cares about his students and it shows. Highly recommend.

Dr. Toups is an amazing professor! He provides detailed feedback on all submitted assignments and lets you resubmit each assignment. My writing improved so much because of this! He facilitated great in-class discussions and would make jokes during class. Would recommend his class to anyone who wants to improve their writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cho is a super engaging lecturer who made class fun and enjoyable. Like most other Econ 102 classes, your grade is based on just 3 midterms all of which are fairly difficult. With the curve, however, it's totally manageable to do well if you study some. Other than the exams, very little weekly work.

Cho is the best prof ever and super fun. He has great lectures but the discussions aren't necessary to attend. Not everyone does the textbook readings, but they are super helpful. You have to attend lecture because you submit a photo of the lecture hall for credit, but you get a few absences and lectures are recorded.

Ed is an amazing person and makes lectures super fun and engaging. He cares a ton about his students and is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Exams were difficult and sometimes on very niche things from lecture - had to study hard to get an A-. Overall though, great prof and would recommend taking him for 102 if you can. Shoutout Munchy!

Cho loves what he does and makes lecture interesting and fun. His exams are not outrageously difficult. He provides practice exams and answers to discussion worksheets and problem sets so there is a lot of practice material. He doesn't provide the best explanations sometimes, but it's not too bad and the optional textbook helps.

Really chill and funny guy. Found myself rewatching lectures at times if he talked a bit fast or didn't understand in lecture concepts. Memorize any type of diagram he mentions and at least for the first exam it was very conceptual. He mentions grade ranges after each exam, which were accurate. Very funny man
This class was awesome! Munchy is a cat!

Cho explains concepts well and gives you what you need to succeed on exams if you go to lecture (especially rewatching confusing parts)––discussion worksheets help a lot too. Exams are tricky and harder than what you do in class, but getting good grades is possible if you prepare a lot. The textbook wasn't necessary.

There's very minimal work to do besides exams, and the lectures are fun. However, the exams are hard, and grades depend on class distribution. Rewatching lecture recordings and going to office hours helps

Cho is very passionate about economics and his love for it is no secret. HOWEVER, this man cannot teach. Lectures were somewhat entertaining (loved the countless photos of his cat), but he would go on so many tangents that I felt completely disengaged and like we had lost the plot. Don't take if you want to have a complete understand of Econ.
Super clear and engaging teacher. Made me excited to attend class and learn. Loved the storytelling and positivity he brought to each lecture. As for course content, he taught it very well.
Beware that his exams are pretty tricky and challenging. It is manageable to get an A in the class, though. Truly loves his cat so much that it's becoming concerning.
hes just great
Amazing class! Cho has so much personality and is so funny. He makes lecture worth going! Highly recommend taking this class if you can get in!
Easily the best professor at the University... if you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it
An awesome professor! Lectures are never boring, and he is a very fair grader who clearly cares for his students. Highly recommend his classes!

Definitely take it if you can get in! Perfect class, learned a lot about real-world economics. Go to the lectures, it worth it. If you actually do the readings, exams are pretty easy. Really helpful professor. Super easy as a  400-level electives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, made concepts easy to understand whilst adding humor anywhere appropriate. Munchy is a Cat.

Cho is a good prof and communicator. However, I found his Econ 340 class difficult to study for. You are graded mostly by two exams, which include lots of specific questions on readings. The lack of practice and “working out” of problems led me to sturggle in this course. I took it the same semester as Econ 401, and got a lower grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some professors just have a genuine care for helping their students learn and making the classroom a fun place to be, and Professor Cho is the pinnacle of them. On top of that, his explanations are clear and intentional. He cares more about you learning well than being an "objectively" good lecturer. Munchy to the moon.

Had Cho for Econ 102 in Fall 2024, genuinely one of the best professors/teachers I've ever had. He's the goat. And funny, as well. 

80% of his Econ 102 grade consists of three midterms, which are split between 25 MCQs and two long-answer questions. Attendance is also mandatory, but lecture wasn't a huge pain to go to, since he made them enjoyable.

I think Cho is great, but this class was a LOT of work for what we all can acknowledge is a "I'm a senior and need one more class" course. There were multiple readings for every class that are used in the exam so you have to read them. Problem sets are fair but not worth a ton and attendance is mandatory but you can watch online + do an assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ed Cho has so much aura it's insane. Never thought I'd be laughing at economics jokes. He also loves talking about his cat Munchy which is valid.
great guy and teacher. makes lectures enjoyable and actually feels like you are learning. would reccomend 100%

My favorite professor I've had so far at Umich. His lectures are so engaging and funny. Econ can be a tough subject but Professor Cho has truly made me enjoy learning the material. He explains concepts in a very simple and concise way that makes it very easy to grasp. You will not regret taking his class!!
If you are an ECON major, you must take 485! Such an interesting and fun class. However, you will only get this experience if you go to lecture.
very inspirational, been to his class couple times. And I don't even go to this school.
such a great professor. conveyed material in an understandable way, unlike other profs. super nice guy too and super funny.
Cho is my fav econ prof here. He is super engaging in lectures and explains concepts very well. Would love to take him again.

I took Econ 402 with Prof. Cho this past summer, and he was absolutely AMAZING. He was highly engaged in teaching, an excellent listener and explainer, genuinely cared about his students, and always added humor to make the class more engaging. If I could, I would take his class every semester.

Professor Cho brings economics to life with his engaging lectures. The material can be challenging, but using tools like unstuck study, ChatGPT, and the textbook helped me succeed. Overall a great class.
Dude is goated and hilarious, and exams are about average difficulty!
King. You will not regret taking a class with him.
Awesome professor, fun to be around
He is the best economics professor I've had at Umich. His lectures are fun, and he is very eager to teach. I strongly recommend this class and his other courses.

Cho's class was the best econ class I have taken at umich. His lectures were engaging and fun. He presents the information clearly and gave us breaks to stretch and walk around. He also drew graphs on the projector so we could follow along in real time. If you do the psets and can explain the material intuitively you will be golden for the exams.

Incredible professor. Dr. Cho not only knows the material he is teaching extremely well but also teaches enthusiastically and passionately and seems to genuinely care about his students. The class was very manageable, and if you do the practice exams/homework, you will do just fine on the exam.
Cho is a very engaging and funny professor. He definitely makes difficult tests so be prepared to study for his two exams. Not a hard class but also not a easy A+

I LOVE prof Cho with all my heart, but I must say, his exams are HARD. Exam questions were so much more difficult than I anticipated, class average was around 67% for both the midterm and final, which were each 35% of our grade. Definitely worth it to take a class with him though, such an amazing guy and super passionate about what he's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam questions can be ambiguous, definitely harder than I expected them to be, but overall no one does insanely well on them, so boundaries for an A aren't high. Amazing professor tho. Dr. Cho has a reputation for being very good and he definitely lives up to it
Ed Cho is the Lebron of the Econ Department

Cho is one of the best Econ professors at UofM. His lectures are very structured and are easy to understand. The tests can be a little bit harder than other Econ classes as he does some FRQ questions.

I've taken three econ courses with this lovely man in my time at Umich. They have without a doubt been the highlight of my economics degree. If you can get in I really recommend 485, he mentioned that it's his favorite class to teach and it really comes through.
He is one of the most engaging professors I have had at the university. His excitement for the subject is palpable and he brings economics to life in a way few others can.
I love him

Professor Cho is a very lovable professor. He's funny, an engaging lecturer, and very clear in his explanations. However, this class is more difficult than I had anticipated. He makes very hard tests.
This was one of my most difficult classes, but my favorite professor. Connected material to current events a

Dr. Cho was a great professor. The only thing that bothered me about the class was that exam material didn't always reflect lectures, discussion, and textbook material. I felt like I had a thorough understanding of the material but wasn't doing well on exams despite learning a ton.

Goat Econ professor. Very engaging and his lectures were never boring. He explained the material clearly and exams were pretty reasonable if you went to lecture. Textbooks also helped. Take him if you can!

He is not a stellar prof everyone says he is. While his lectures are ok and does its job, he doesnt do much in terms of teaching. He isnt able to answer them even though they are clarification questions on the content he has taught in class. As a result, he would resort to saying go read the textbook or something. Not exactly the best prof
Best professor in the Econ department. Clear material and engaging lectures.
Took it over the summer, went by fast but it's pretty easy to do well in the class. Easiest econ elective ever

I really loved 485 with Prof. Cho. Easily one of the best professors in the Economics department. I cannot recommend his class enough. Use of economic models in places you would never expect to use them. Super funny and personable guy, while also being an inspirational and brilliant teacher.
Hes a legends, by far my favorite teacher I've had so far at Michigan

Overall great class. Professor Cho is a great lecturer and very engaging however the tests are much different than the practice tests. I strongly encourage to not waste your time going to lectures and just read the textbook! Not the worst class ever but prepare a lot for tests.

As a graduating senior, would recommend this class to all econ majors looking for simple and interesting electives. The class was an absolute breeze. Just be sure to attend lectures/watch recordings and you're good.
Hands down the best economics professor at U-M. I think people judge him because of the 'toughness' of his classes but he is an amazing lecturer and advisor. Could not recommend this class more.

I thought this ECON 102 should be easy so I took this class and broadly review the first midterm. Did very bad on the first exam, like a mid B. Then, I started to study hard and got both A for the second and third exam. But my final grade comes up to be an A-, which pull down my gpa. Not an easy course, really need some attention.

I was worried about this class because of it's reputation, but Cho made this class such a breeze. I love how easygoing the lectures are and it seemed like he was trying his best to make the material easy for us.
Took 402 with him last sem and what a gem y'all. He is very endearing and easy to learn from. 10/10

Do yourself a favor and TAKE HIS CLASSES! He is hands down the best professor I have ever had in econ. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches, tries his best to engage the students and makes sure you understand the material. Unlike other professors who put you to sleep with their voice, he will awaken the curious mind in you. Love him!
What a legend! Definitely the best Econ prof I have had as of yet. He is such a genuinely kind person. Highly recommend taking 402 with him :)

Dr. Cho's classes are a reflection of him: Humorous, witty, but extremely passionate and hard working. If you major in Economics, you will find out his classes are "a working lunch break" sandwiched in between classes taught by researchers who live on the cutting edge of the global markets and economies.
Professor Cho is an excellent professor that puts in his work and cares for the students. It is a challenging course, but goes out of his way to answer any questions the students have.

I really wonder why there are so many good comments for Prof Cho. He is indeed nice and kind, but his lecture is rather confusing. Practices he provides are limited and many terms are unclear. Moreover, he chooses to skip some classes or sections, making understanding his course even harder.

Cho didn't really meet the expectations I had based on previous posts. Cho is a very kind, caring, and personable professor. However, I thought that his lectures were sometimes a bit clunky and unclear. The slides were not particularly helpful to review and he often spoke with far too many generalizations. Overall, decent experience, but not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Cho for 402 and took him again for 485. His courses aren't necessarily easy but he explains the material better than any other econ professor I had while at Michigan. Can't recommend taking a course with him enough.

While I ended up changing the course to pass/fail this was of no fault to Ed Cho. The course work is really hard but he does a great job explaining things and making the material accessible to people of different backgrounds. I would not take this course with any other professor.

Something I really liked about Cho's course was how clear he made the grading criteria. His canvas page is always updated with everything you'll possibly need for the class, and it's very organized. His lectures were really entertaining and helpful, and having a decent GSI is also veryyyy helpful. Don't be fooled tho, the class is still quite tough

the tests were weighted pretty heavily but he was a very good teacher and explained somewhat diffiuclt to understand topics quite clearly. he made his lectures fun and engaging and i would take another class of hist in an instant. a worse grade bc of his tests is surely worth it.
Professor Cho is a great person and teacher. He is very passionate about his work, and exams are straightforward and reflect the lecture material very well.
Good lecturer, but very weird exam, even you have worked very hard for it, you don't get a good score you expect. If you want to maintain your GPA, don't take his course.

I changed my MAJOR because of him, he made me fall in love with economics. A very genuine person, and super kind. He single-handedly got me through the pandemic, he is my hero. Also Munchie his cat is so cute.
Not only an amazing person but the best person on the face of this earth, this man is not only a teacher but a therapist. Super funny and easy to talk to, he literally saved my life!!

So funny and by far my favorite teacher at umich. I want to be friends with him, he is just a really good person and very funny. I love munchie too, Professor Cho was my lifeline during the pandemic I cannot wait to take Econ 402 with him this fall!!

THIS IS THE BEST PROF AT UMICH! The best teacher and person ever I took econ 102 with him and I changed my major because of this teacher! I was a very depressed engineering student Professor Cho gave me my life back, and his class offered so much knowledge but also comfort. It feels like your friend is teaching the class and we all love Munchie!!!!

His lectures are clear and not too overwhelming, plus he adds a break into each lecture. The class is almost entirely based on tests and he did not offer EC. That being said, he has office hours almost every day, cares a lot about his students, and has a great personality. It was a good class despite being online, just somewhat difficult for me.
Dudes the GOAT nuff said. Take 485 if you can get it but it fills up fast.

Highly overrated. Lectures are VERY confusing, uses lots of words when few would do. Lectures are mandatory to watch with a little flexibility built in. Lots of textbook and reading needed. Tests are fine if you work hard, but not easy by any means.

Edward Cho is an incredible Economics professor. He is clearly incredibly passionate about Econ, and his lectures are clear and easy to follow. He cares a lot about his students and his cat Munchie. I would highly recommend him to anyone.

I tried to leave a rating before and it wasn't approved. Maybe there are a ton of GSIs who love Cho and report all bad ratings. I'm not sure, but everyone I've talked to who's taken 102 with Cho doesn't like him. While he has a bubbly personality, lectures are unclear, slides are terrible, and he will destroy your GPA. Do better RateMyProfessor.

Professor Cho is the best! His lectures are so clear and easy to learn from and he's the kindest, most accessible professor. The GSIs are great too and the video supplements were SO helpful. The contemporary connections really piqued my interest in econ and I genuinely looked forward to watching lecture recordings (which is an anomaly). 10/10.

Didn't really live up to the hype. Don't get me wrong, he's still a solid prof who explains the material well. Your grade is basically just exams and the exam MC is WAY harder than it needs to be. Discussion section was useless, and the lectures weren't in-depth enough compared to the exams. Prepare to learn a lot on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cho is a very funny and kind professor. He also does his best to make the lectures interesting and easy to understand. He did a great job to converting to an online only format and remained easily accessible. He's a great professor.

One of the best professors at UM. Explains everything really clearly and in a succinct way. Hes also really nice and funny and super accesible in office hours and always willing to answer questions or just to chat. Honestly hes a beast

Professor Cho is definitely the best Econ professor I have had at U-M yet. Honestly, the material was difficult for me, but I can say that he broke things down to be very simple, which eventually helped. I also loved the GSIs this semester; they are so helpful and patient. Cho also let us take breaks during the lecture... he's the BEST!!

Overall, Ed is a great guy and is passionate about teaching. I feel that he does rush through a lot of things in class. Grade is made of 2 exams 35% each and rest HW and Participation. 40% of MC questions on test are from articles, so read them early. Overall, just be ready for about anything on HW or lectures...
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really passionate and caring. Solid choice and great combination of intelligence, humor, and compassion. I'm not sure if his grading scale is as favorable as other professors but ed cho is a great professor.
By far the best UMich professor I've had.
cho is hands down my favorite prof by far! Hes passionate, funny, and helps make difficult concepts easy to understand. You can tell he loves teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought Cho was entertaining and explained the material well. He shows pictures of his cat Munchy maybe every lecture. Exams are not too bad but you have to study and problem sets are completion grade.
Cho is the best professor in the econ department by far. Take any class you can with him while you have the chance.
Overall great class. Cho is passionate and interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Cho's has been my favorite so far, even though it was a lot of work. He does a good job making a large intro class feel smaller than it actually is.

Cho has a habit of overcomplicating basic concepts in his lectures. Though the content itself isn't very difficult to grasp, it takes time to decipher his lectures even if you pay diligent attention. Exams tended to focus on just a couple random topics from the course material, and the free responses were unnecessarily difficult. Overrated prof.

Prof Cho class was one of my favorites. He is pretty clear in presentation, and I ended up actually looking forward to class, which is not very often. I liked it so much, that I wanted to take more of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ed Cho is the most overrated professor at the University of Michigan. Everyone raves about him but his course is so extremely difficult, you are better off taking a "worse" teacher but you will do better in the class. This ruined my GPA

Prof Chos class is one of the best courses Ive taken at Michigan. He always knows how to engage the class, and presents ideas in an intuitive way. His midterms both challenge and reward those who really spend time to understand economic concepts. Munchie will always be my favorite cat

Professor cho is a funny guy but this class is more demanding than it needs to be. Exams go way more into depth than what is covered in class, and difficult concepts are hardly covered due to the fast pace of the course. Unless you have taken ap macro chances are this class is going to be difficult for you, or if you have a light schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cho is a really great person who is fun to listen to during lecture, but that doesn't translate into him being a great teacher. His lectures are very bare-boned and do not reflect what actually shows up on the exam; often the average score is extremely low because we never went over heavily-tested concepts during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Cho has been my favorite professor that I have had at Michigan. I took both 396 and 485 with him, and he is able to convey difficult economic concepts in a straightforward way. He is a great lecturer, and I actually enjoy going to class.
Cho is the man. He has changed the way I read current events, since I can use basic economic tools to analyze events. Class keeps me engaged, which isn't the case for many of my other classes.

Prof Cho is one of a kind. He has a real talent of conveying complex ideas in an intuitive way. I will never forget this class, even though I took it over the summer semester. His jokes are hilarious!

Pro chos class is challenging, but Ive learned so much applicable material that makes it well worth it. He brings an energy that is infectious, and makes you want to actually come to class. One of the best professors Ive had.
Professor Cho is hilarious and very knowledgeable. Hes able to explain difficult concepts concisely, and his cat Munchy is adorable.

Ed Cho is an ok professor, but his exams are unnecessarily difficult. There are only three exams in Econ 102 which determine your entire grade (10% of your grade is based on problem sets/attendance, but this washes out with the curve). His exam questions are extremely poorly worded and only students who've taken econ in high school typically get As

Chances are unless you're willing to dedicate your life to this class you're not getting an A. The multiple choice on his exams is likely to wreck you (and your gpa). But, Cho is an inspirational professor who really puts his all into his lectures. He makes the material accessible and applicable to the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a fine class to take if you know little about finance like me, but at times I wished it could have been a little more challenging. The readings are good at tying what you learn in class to real life phenomena and there are only about 5 homework sets in total so there isn't much work in the class.

Dr. Cho is the best and professor to be. He is always so prepared and energetic during lecture that it makes lecture go by like a breeze. Explains things clearly and gives good examples to illustrate his point. Very approachable and easy to talk to for help. Also, he loves talking about his cat.

Professor Cho is my favorite professor that I have had at Michigan. I took 102 with him then 396 and both I thoroughly enjoyed. He is hilarious, personable, loves getting to know his students, and a great lecturer. His class is the only one I truly look forward to and enjoy going to. He gives great feedback wants you to succeed. TAKE HIS CLASS

Cho is the best Econ lecturer at UofM. He explains things clearly and makes the class actually entertaining so you don't fall asleep, like I do in many other classes. He keeps you engaged and is always open to questions. Highly recommend taking him when you have the option to.

Cho is a great teacher and would definitely recommend him. Pretty straightforward class but he was actually not very knowledgable in financial principles outside of what basic information that pertains to the class. Class moves slow but is very easy if you have any background knowledge in finance.

Cho is well-respected as THE person to take econ 102 and he really deserves it. GREAT professor. Super funny and passionate. Definitely a lot of work though. My mental health wasn't great this semester and the class really sunk my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cho is the absolute best! He's funny, passionate, and makes very difficult concepts very easy to understand! You can tell he genuinely cares about the students and even in a lecture of 400, he still knows many students by name and will say hi to them in lecture. He loves his cat Munchy and brings her up a lot, which is adorable.

All-around great professor who's genuinely entertaining and enthusiastic. He's excellent at explaining everything that's on the exams and especially those concepts that aren't immediately clear. Put away your laptop and pay attention in lecture, because he's the kind of guy that deserves it. Also, Munchie's adorable.

Really passionate and exciting. He is also quite weird at times but in a good way which makes his lectures something you actually want to go to rather than something you feel you have to go to. Each test had a couple really tricky and badly worded questions but they were all very fair overall. Read book, do practice tests, and you will do well

Hands down one of my favorite professors. His class is also one of the few I have where it seems like time flies by. He is great at explaining material and making you laugh. Also one of the more traditional professors who still uses the chalkboard and forbids laptops in class which has actually helped me pay attention much more. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I will be honest, the Econ department at Michigan has some AWFUL professors who should not be teaching. Cho is the biggest exception and as others have said, if you take a class, you should take it with him. Take as many of his classes as you can because he is not only knowledgeable, but also VERY good at explaining things. Best professor Ive had.

Ed Cho is such a cool guy. He teaches well and everything in lecture is clearly explained. He relates the material to the real world. He is so excited and passionate about Econ and about teaching, which makes it a lot easier to pay attention and learn. I wish I could take every Econ class with Ed.

Outstanding professor, engages you in every lecture and makes economics fun and applicable. Exams are fair/somewhat difficult, but he explains everything you need in class. Don't forget about Munchie.

If you can take a class with him, take it with him. He makes learning economics very fun and helps clarify difficult/confusing things in class. He always happens to know what students tend to get and not get. If possible, get to know him as he is very fun to be with during office hours. However, the exams do tend to be a bit on the hard side.
He is a very good and approachable professor. During lecture, he is so fun and energetic, and I am so sad that the semester is over.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: VERY SAD that I will not be able to take ECON102 with this guy. The 300 spots in his class went so fast and he had 0 spots left when the other prof still had more than 250 spots left. )): I am sad

Cho is overall an excellent professor. He knows what he is talking about and when he's focused on the subject at hand, he's excellent at explaining the material. He is also very funny, but can get off topic a little too often. Tests place a heavy focus on current events, so make sure you understand those. Not a very heavily math intensive class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: ED is the man

Ed Cho is amazing- you NEED to take a class with him at UM! He works really hard to make complicated concepts easy to understand. He also tries to connect what we learn in class to current events which makes the class feel particularly useful. On top of that, he's hilarious and shares the cutest pictures of his cat!
Genuinely nice guy and I enjoyed lecture and kind of looked forward to them despite my loathing of economics as a topic

Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. I learned more in one summer semester of his course than I have in 2 years at Michigan. I usually can't pay attention in lecture and need a textbook, but he made lectures clear and engaging and did not have any filler information. Would definitely take again

I hate Econ, but Cho is a fantastic professor. Everyone thinks he is HILARIOUS. He makes the class great. However, the class can be hard, and requires a lot of work. To do well, definitely make sure you read the book and study a lot before tests. But, Cho is a hilarious, great teacher. Would absolutely take him again if I liked Econ, lol

Very funny guy who has worked super hard to be where he is- genuinely cares about students and wants to see you succeed. OH not necessary to do well in the class but he's a good teacher if you're confused. Do the problem sets, read the chapters, listen in class, and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cho is a fantastic professor - very smart economist, good teacher, keeps lectures interesting and informational
Lectures are a blast. He's honestly a great personality, and very good at econ. For this class you gotta do a bit of self-study if you wanna pass, and grading's pretty set and strict.

Professor Cho is well respected and liked by the student body. He teaches the material in a clear manner that avoids confusion, but doesn't take his work too seriously. He constantly cracks jokes or includes funny slides in his powerpoints. The class was competitively graded so it was though, but I enjoyed it overall. I would highly recommend Cho.
Hands down the best Econ professor at UofM!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ed Cho was the best professor I've had so far at Michigan. You need to take his class.
He is amazing. So lucky to have taken his class (402!). The best professor ever.

This class is not hard to do well in as long as you put in the effort! Make sure to keep up with the readings he assigns every week because they're an important attribute to do well on the exam. Also, it is good to review problem sets and seriously understand the exam reviews. Understanding concepts is more important than knowing the math for class

Professor Cho is an amazing guy. He is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had. He makes everything really clear and makes a point to stop a lot during lecture to make sure everyone understands what is going.
Cho is fantastic and inspiring. Tests are fair and lectures are fun.

I absolutely love Cho. He makes lectures so engaging and difficult topics easy to understand. Makes it clear what is on the exams and truly cares about his students. Also, takes breaks throughout lecture to show silly pet pictures-even makes up his own captions. Fave professor here. TAKE THIS CLASS.

He is amazing. I cried walking out of his last lecture. He is the greatest professor at the University of Michigan. I am not even doing that well in his class, but I would recommend his class to anyone.  LOVE YOU CHO

Econ 485 has been my favorite upper level econ class by FAR. There's a reason it fills up so fast. He doesn't post lecture slides or anything online so you have to go to class to get the info - but it's worth it to go. Very minimal homework and exams are really easy. Unfortunately the class barely focuses on the law side of anything

Ed is amazing! His lecture is never dull.  He loves his cat and shows us his cat every lecture. He makes difficult concepts very easy to understand. Workload is the lightest. However, office hour can be crowded because he teaches so many classes. Practice exam should be longer too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Econ 396 would definitely be a great choice if you want to gain more understanding about the real world economy and professor Cho would be the best guider to help you through. Even though the course is running fast, especially in summer term, and we have A LOT OF materials to cover, studying this course would still be enjoyable due to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ed is the best! His lectures are entertaining and helpful. He does take attendance, but I cannot understand why people would want to skip this class. Overall, the class is not too tough and I found it quite interesting.

Professor Cho's Econ class was a joy to be a part of the whole year. Very good at keeping the class engaged. Class can be tough because most students in the class are either in Ross or are Econ majors so be wary of that due to the curve, but the concepts aren't too difficult, especially if you took AP Macro in high school. Munchie is my fav cat!

One of my favorite professors! He's hilarious and very friendly. Made econ really fun and has a lot of corny jokes. His lectures are funny and he uses real life examples to help better relate to students. Even if you're not an econ major, would recommend if you want to better understand the economy.
Loves his cat/ pretty funny guy/ fair tests/ uses iclickers worth 5%/ Lectures are amazing/ teaches very well
Cho is easily the best professor for 102. He was very clear and made the material not difficult. If Macro or Econ is your thing, you'll do very well in the class.
made class really fun. The material  can be hard but he'll giv real life examples that are easy to understand so that you can follow. amazing dude overall

Aside from all the goofy jokes about his cat and brother, Professor Cho made Macroeconomics far more interesting because you could tell how much fun he had talking about the concepts. Really appreciated the connections to real-world events as well. This was my favorite class so far at UofM.

Cho is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of energy. He's very passionate about Econ and it shows. His 102 class fared much better than the other professors, but it's clear that the concepts were very general in Cho's. The textbook is extremely helpful. The tests get harder as the class progresses. I would recommend Cho if you're taking 102.

Amazing lecturer but tests are not easy. Everything he talks about in class (unless specified) can be testable, even if they do not seem to be important. His test questions aren't tough so most students gets high raw scores, but he grades on a pretty tough curve (25% gets an A). You have to be meticulous to get an A.

Edward Cho is the best professor i've had so far at U of M. He teaches in a way that makes even the most complex economics topics easy to understand. He's funny and engages with the students throughout his lectures. He brings a lot of energy to class everyday, and is a MUST HAVE if take Econ 102. I recommend reading the book , it is amazing!

Prof Cho is easily the best professor I've had so far at UM. If you go to his office hours even once, or just interact with him outside of class, he will remember you. He makes the class very personable- despite it have 350 kids in it. He's also an amazing lecturer and integrates funny stories and examples into his teaching.

Professor Cho presents the tough material of Econ 102 in the best possible way. Material is very difficult, but make the most out of the resources given. Take the practice exams and review lecture slides and the article readings and you will be ok.  He also loves cats and especially his cat Munchie so that will entertain you. He is the must have.

Ed Cho is a great professor. He explains things well, engages the students in lecture,  and ends lecture early most of the time. He is very quirky, and has an odd obsession with his cat, but that makes him pretty funny. Very few homework sets, and midterms are very straight forward.

Professor Cho is truly passionate about the subject and that comes across in his lectures.  He is also very funny when he talks about his pet cat Munchie all the time and puts pictures of the cat into random slides.  iClickers were graded for participation, homework was great on effort, so that's 15 percent of your grade that should be perfect.

Prof Cho is a really funny guy and is obviously passionate about econ, and it shows in his lectures. He talks about his cat Munchie a lot, which is great, and takes breaks during the lecture when people seem to be zoning out. All around great guy and great lecturer.

Cho is a great guy, very funny. Loves cats, especially his cat Munchie.  He makes jokes in lecture and it goes by quickly, even for someone like me who isn't a big fan of Econ.  The material is not exactly easy, but Professor Cho is very helpful and accessible. If you are taking an Econ Class, I would highly recommend Professor Cho.

Cho has been one of my favorite professors at Michigan.  Really funny lecturer and pretty easy class.  Homework was graded for effort, iClickers for participation, and exams really weren't that hard, plus they were non cumulative.  Highly recommend him

This class was awesome! I am halfway through it and already writing this review. Ed is the man, his lectures are chalk-and-talk style so you have to go to lecture to get the information but it's no task with his amazing teaching style. Take this class!

Ed is the best professor I have had at U of M. His lectures are clear and I didn't have to crack the textbook once. It is very easy to be interactive in his lectures and he holds office hours almost every day so it was easy to get help from him.

Overall, this is an outstanding class which I consider as my favorite economic class for now. I have learned a ton from the class and this is the first time that I know how to relate the economic models I learned to real-world issues. This makes me become really passionate about economics and want to explore deeper! Prof. Cho is really fun, inspiri

I will make your decision easy: TAKE HIS CLASS you wont regret it. Best professor in the department. This guy was born to teach. He learns everyone's name by the second week. He uses the whiteboard to teach and not boring powerpoint slides. Go to class, take notes, participate, do the homeworks and you will get an A. He will make your life happier.

He is extremely helful and passionate about his teaching. But, he should know that he is the only professor I have ever met who speaks very fast. Because he talked really too fast, I seriously thought to drop his class. I also know another person who were very worried about it. He does not have a good handwriting also. gave me big stress

Ed is a really really nice guy. But honestly, I wish he was more understanding. He often gets really excited about the subject he is teaching and moves at such a fast pace that no one understands. Also, I don't like how he doesn't keep track of grades on Ctools, I am currently studying for the final and have no Idea what my grade is.
I took a a summer term course with him and it was his first at the University. Very different from the more traditional professors here. By far the best and most engaging Econ course I've had here.

He's really hilarious, helpful and nonjudgemental. You can ask any economic or career related questions once you get to know him and he's willing to share his own experience. One thing may need your attention is that the major readings, from WSJ, Economists, etc, are hard to comprehend sometimes, but he'll talk about them in the lecture.

Check the date on this post. Within three years Ed Cho will be a umich Legend. His lectures are engaging and he's hilarious. He writes all his notes on the board. Don't worry if you're not a math whiz or econ expert, this class is meant for beginners. Problem sets aren't hard (18% of grade) and tests are manageable (2 of them).

Ed was definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. I never write reviews of professors, I swear. But Ed definitely changed my outlook and inspired me to further pursue my passion in financial institutionsmarkets. I loved the class and definitely would recommend it, but it is a challenging course. You've been warned.
Do not miss this class. One of my best Prof. ever.

Best professor I have ever had. He is a great professor, and even better all around guy. His lectures are interesting, and he throws in a funny joke every once in awhile. I feel as though his exams are tough, but fair.

TAKE A CLASS WITH ED CHO. He learned all 100 students names by the end. He doesnt post lecture notes online so you have to go to class, but it's worth it--he's a great lecturer. He tells hilarious and corny jokes. He's brilliant and very accommodating for assignments and office hours. Totally fair grading too. Best professor in the econ department.

Powerpoint slides are a terrible disease to the educational system because is making professors more lazy. This guy has all my respect. He uses the blackboard to teach, which is surprising to see nowadays. The workload is above average, but if you go to class there is nothing to fear. He knows every student's name and always helpful! Admirable!
Does not post lecture notes and takes very sloppy notes on the white board that are your only material to study for the exam with.
Easily the best professor I have had in the department. I wish he taught more classes, would go out of my way to take another one of his courses.
Ed is cool, lectures aren't posted so come to class. PS' are graded tough but tests are easy if you come to class

Seriously this guy is the best out there!  He is actually teaching the class and not reading powerpoint slides. Super entertaining and his explanations are incredibly clear. He is always in a great mood and with a lot of energy! He is always willing to help you out. Best Econ professor hands down. Take a bow!

Professor Fink is kind and generally does a good job explaining the material, but the class is set up in a difficult way. Exams are pretty brutal and difficult to finish in time, making up 85% of the grade, with as of now no plans to be curved. Definitely possible to do well, but in comparison its needlessly difficult compared to other sections.

Dropped early. The first day was a recorded lecture from last year (very suspicious). She was unprepared with constant "technical difficulties." HW is incredibly long busy work, and lectures will put you to sleep. You can get an A, but it's painfully boring. Take a different professor for Stats 412 or a different class for the requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Conceptually the class should be easy, but the lectures are incredibly slow. The exams make up 75% of your grade and are ridiculously difficult and there's no sort of in class review whatsoever. Our exam review was way different than the actual exam, and she doesn't let you ask questions during exams despite writing hard and confusing tests.

Boring lectures, nit picky and inconsistent grading (good luck guessing how the exam will be graded differently from the homeworks), ignores piazza, and unreasonably high workload (weekly quizzes and homework assignments, even on exam weeks).

I think Fink just loves seeing students put up lower averages than they did the semester before. She writes tests unnecessarily hard where you will be getting 60s and be average. The class isn't that conceptually challenging but ur better off taking 425 instead of 412 and with a different prof. Fink makes an easy class unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she isnt as bad as these reviews make her out to be. 412 is a fundamentally easy class it is not hard by any means if you put any amount of effort into it. her lectures are not engaging and paced very slowly, but these reviews are dramatic.

Homeworks and exams for the most part follow the lecture material, so make sure to attend lectures or watch the recordings. Lectures weren't engaging. The professor struggles with communication, especially on Piazza. The practice problems often aren't really reflective of the exam, so review homework. The course is also very exam heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are hundreds of reason not taking her class. She is a real tough grader on the exams that makes 85% of the grade. I went to every single (boring) lectures but learned little. She ignored our questions about curve and regrade policies. Taking her class will cause you mental damage and make you doubt yourself.

The lowest score I can give is 1 but I DO wanted to give a 0. It seems ridiculous to rate a professor from her unorganized and less-communication class mode. We've asked for tons of questions regarding grade curves and regrades while she chose to neglect all of us from piazza. Exams are harsh and HWs are heavy. Worst professor I've ever taken.

This is one of the worst classes i've ever taken. Please do not take with her, its very difficult for little reason, unless from now until the grading deadline there are major changes, this section does not follow the atlas historical grading distribution whatsoever. The lectures are hard to understand and the professor doesn't post anything online
The exams make up the majority of the class grade and they're extremely difficult. If you aren't an extremely good test taker do not even bother taking the class with Nadiya Fink
definitely avoid it. Heavy HW, heavy exams, only allowed to bring small note card while other section allow to being A4 paper.

This was my favorite class that I've taken at Umich so far and I'm a junior. THOSE WHO DON'T ENJOY THIS CLASS DON'T GO TO LECTURE AND DON'T DO THEIR HOMEWORK WELL. There is literally only one very doable homework set a week. The lecture lines up exactly with the homework AND the exam. Very reasonable and kind professor. Don't trust the low ratings.
heavy exam no curve no matter the difficulty of the exam, heavy & unnecessary HWs. Take other class if you can!!!

I don't know why she gets so much hate. If you are a math major reading this like I am, this class is 10x easier than most other math classes at UMich. The tests are EXACTLY like the homework, almost exactly the same questions. So study those and you will be golden. If math does not come somewhat easily to you, she may not be the best teacher.

She's very particular about the way she wants everything and gives little wiggle room. She is rude and difficult to communicate with. I liked statistics going into this class, but not coming out. Thank God I passed and don't have to see her again.

She has a thick accent which is fine, but she speaks so quietly and muffled that it is impossible to follow her. Lectures are very boring. Answers questions about material covered in lecture by saying "just go watch the lecture" instead of answering
Does not teach well, makes simple mistakes sometimes, and overcomplicates solutions for no reason, very unclear should not be a teacher

She was not a bad teacher for 412, explaining things somewhat slowly but fairly clearly as well. The pop-up quizzes were extra credit, and the exams were not too difficult if you study the homework and practice exams! There is also a live synchronous zoom which alleviates the slower lecture issue.

Take any OTHER class or prof to fill this requirement I beg you. 75% total exam grade and she will state "second exam grades are always bad" there I no curve, and she knows the exams are too much, the are long and tedious. Will mention putting formulas and work for partial credit on exams but is hardly awarded. will mark points off for any mistake.

GET THIS THROUGH YOUR HEAD. I would genuinely rather take a full power shot to the crotch from a heavyweight UFC fighter than ever see, let alone speak with this woman again in my life. A large portion of the second exam had content that WAS NOT COVERED IN THE PREP. The homework's have a ridiculous amount of unnecessary/irrelevant work as well.

Don't take her class if your GPA matters. teaches more materials than other MATH 425 professor. The grade is not curved. The HW is heavyyyy.
Don't want to take it anymore:(

Overall, professor Fink was a fine lecturer. However, the way she wrote homeworks and tests made the class tedious. The homeworks were way too long despite being 15% of the grade. She also didn't allow us to use basic problem solving methods learned in math 215, a prerequisite, instead making us solve them her way, which also took way too long.

She's a great professor, explains step-by-step, every concept has an example. HW lines up directly with lecture, par for an intro course. The hardest part are her exams which are very thorough, you won't finish if you're unprepared. Luckily the HW and review is very similar. If you're good at standardized tests/time management then you will thrive.

She is tough but fair. She fills in "skeleton notes" for the class which makes it easy to understand where you are and where you are going. Homework is tough and has a lot of proofs. Exams are very challenging but I believe some of the harder questions are graded based on you having the right idea even if you cannot solve. Good class, good teacher.

She is bad at explaining statistics, I wanted to do data science but that out the windows, I hate statistics now. She is boring and deviates from the book a lot. You will have homework due the day before thanksgiving and homework due the tuesday you get back from thanksgiving break (2 days to do it).

Though the class is straightforward, Prof Fink makes it incredibly dull. Slow lectures that feel rushed with almost no time for questions. There is little motivation to understand the field deeply because it feels like we're studying for the sake of completing the course content. We were also assigned HW over Fall & Thanksgiving break and exam week

The homework load for this course is extremely heavy, and no formula sheets are allowed on exams. While the professor is nice, respectful, and thorough in covering the material, the workload is intense for an introductory probability course.

Fink is good at explaining concepts. She also offers and teaches a lot of examples in her lectures. All the problems in HWs and exams are pretty similar to what she taught in classes. The problem is that she just allows a small piece of note and limited time and does not give any curve even though our exam average was D+.

Professor's really amazing at the things she teaches, however, the exam questions are okayish in difficulty but the sheer amount of Ques we get in test is insurmountable and impossible to do. She will teach amazingly well but will expect you to study her course only 24x7.
Personal take, go with someone better, don't risk your GPA. Exams r hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly all the bad reviews are just people getting mad for lack of preparation. Nadiya is a tough but fair professor, she takes the class and teaching in general very seriously, but thats not a bad thing. Exams were extremely fair imo, there are direct correlations from every question to a hw question/lecture example.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stats 412 with dr. Fink is very difficult. 75% of your final grade comes from 3 rather difficult exams so it is imperative that you master the homework. However, as a byproduct of this, it follows that you learn the subject matter very well. Outside of the exams the course logistics are below average.

She obsessed over attendance, she checked it with multiple "Pop-up quizzes" per class. She always compared the sections she taught, and consistently reminded us how far behind ours was (we "asked to many questions"). Lectures were extremely boring, and she failed to give accurate instructions or steps for basic concepts and was a very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class content is fine and sometimes interesting but the professor is rude and intentionally ignores questions asked on piazza.

I took Stats 412 this semester. There are 3 exams that make up 75% of the grade. There is no curve, but she makes your best exam worth a little more. This is probably 1-3% boost, so you need to average 90% on exams to get an A. I would estimate class average to be B-. I was able to get an A, but it was quite difficult. You need to master the hw.

Freaked out at the beginning of the semester over all the comments I saw here. But I actually was able to understand materials covered in lectures (which rarely happens). Tbh exams were really tough and did require LOTS of prep, but manageable. She didn't check piazza regularly so be sure to utilize office hours for questions (she was very helpful)

Stats 412 with Nadiya has very poor communication (piazza avg response time was 5+ hrs). The class material itself is not inherently difficult. The slides as the year goes on also get progressively worse in which you have no room to write your own notes. Having a zoom option was very nice. This class is also very exam heavy (study hard for exam 1)

8 hours of homework per week, plus a quiz, and 2 pop quizzes per lecture. Impossible grader. No curve. Sent an email to all the students not doing well recommending they withdraw- luckily for my ego I had already sent in my withdraw request. W is for winners.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Originally, I thought everyone on here was exaggerating until I took her course. Exams are worth 75% of final grade and they are not curved. Exam times are 80 minutes for a full length exam that should take 2 hours. Do not take the grade distribution on Atlas seriously.
75% of your grade is exams, and they are very long with a short time period to complete them. Also, very high workload for 3 credit class, and at least two pop quizzes every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Fink is a great lecturer and uses good examples in class. However she covers a lot more than other sections and at a faster rate. She is a tough grader and her exams are structured such that you can easily lose points even if you get the right answer.

Nothing that hasn't been said - disproportionate workload, time-crunched exams, she *does* record lectures, but only makes them available to people with a verified absence (no slides, ever). Set a pop quiz to expire in less than a minute and said "oh well." Do not take under any circumstances, avoid the class itself if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Workload is unnecessarily heavy compared to the importance of the class. Weekly homework and quizzes, even on the week of the midterm. Staff doesn't care about answering Piazza questions at all. Enforces attendance through multiple pop quizzes throughout class, yet doesn't release lecture recordings. This professor's pettiness is unmatched.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's just the worst. Enforces class attendance with pop quizzes and doesn't release recordings of lectures or even annotated slides so if you miss a lecture, you're just screwed. Makes exams unnecessarily difficult by making them apply to real life situations despite never doing that format in class, homework, or quizzes. Never, ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The workload is larger than MATH 217. Very tough grader. Please do not take her class. YOU will regret!!

Materials are easy and the lecture is boring. Lots of weekly homework and no review session for exams(still teaching new stuff the day of the exam). Exams are super long with a bunch of calculations. The whole staff team barely answered piazza questions. At least 2 pop-up quizzes per class forcing you to attend the lecture.

Almost every class has pop up quiz and workload is huge. Only incomplete notes are published on to Canvas and need to complete them in class by yourself. NO lecture recordings. Weekly quiz is hard. A torturous class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Fink is an okay lecturer (monotone and not very engaging). Exams were hard, and I had a grading issue at the end of the semester which I had to wait several weeks to get help with (after emailing her).

Exams reviews do NOT prepare you for the exams at all and are extremely hard as well, given the amount of explanation about the content during lecture.
I also see 7 positive reviews rated 5/5 from the past, which were written on the SAME DAY, with a very SIMILAR style of writing, so I'm pretty sure you would understand what that means.

I did my biggest mistake in this school when I was looking up Professor Fink and I thought people were exaggerating. Don't get me wrong, she is a great lecturer and takes her job very seriously. In fact, TOO seriously. She starts and end lectures late, covers a lot more content than other professors, and makes this course unnecessarily hard. Avoid.

The other section got a formula sheet, and had access to recordings. Our section got one side of a 3x5 index card, mandatory lecture attendance with no recordings, and the exam got moved up two days "due to weather."

Do. Not. Take.

I am a straight A student and this was the only B I've received due to the final exam being extremely differnet from previous exam review materials and homework. I actually liked the content and felt that I learned a bit, but the final exam was truly unfair and I don't think my grade is refelctive of the effort I put into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class overall seems to have differing standards each year, as the "cheat sheets" have gone from one page front and back to one side of an index card this semester. The exams are tricky and do not fairy test on things we have practiced, seemingly focusing on specific aspects that could be easy to brush over.

Students are not well prepared for exams and the exams do not do a good job of reflecting the material taught.  Lecture notes are only provided in an incomplete format to incentivize lecture attendance, but a final version is never uploaded, meaning the instructor is purposely withholding important material, which is truly bizarre and unfair.

I really should have listened to what was said here before signing up for this class. Unfortunately there aren't too many other professors offering the course. Lectures are long and drawn out. Exam prep and review isn't very representative of what is on the exam. The class fundamentally isn't that hard, so you'll survive, but she won't make it easy

The instructional team left good Piazza questions unanswered for weeks, deliberately made information difficult to access, wrote a majority MAMC final w/o giving any representative practice material, and are ghosting regrades and all questions about exam statistics/curve/exam contradictions with the course notes despite posting final grades.

Nadiya is a good person but her course style is BAD.
Nadiya is very flexible and accommodating (emailing out reminders, having office hours, etc.); however, content questions were basically ignored by staff after class, the exam answers contradicted class notes, and most questions/concerns about grades were never answered.
Recommendation: AVOID
She is probably the worst professor at this school. I hope no one has to suffer through one of her awful classes. Avoid her if you want to actually learn something in class.

Do not take Fink's stats 425 if you're not super interested in math. Her section is absolutely the hardest 425 section. Fink grades her exams very harshly. Also, you're only allowed a notecard as cheat sheet, so basically you have to memorize everything. Homework is due every week and super long.

Honestly HWs aren't that bad though they take long. Tests are quite difficult though and not curved. They are also quite harshly graded so do not take this class for an ez A. Previously students were given pages for exam notes and now we are given one side of one small notecard so it is far more difficult. Strongly discourage taking her for 412.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is terrible. Monotone, uncaring, and she makes the class harder than it needs to be. If you can, avoid taking her classes. She seems like a nice person but that niceness does not translate into her courses. She makes the notes hard to take, the lectures are too fast, and she does not even ask for feedback. Disappointed.

This is the first time I have ever rated any professor, but she is horrible. You need to go or watch each lecture as the only notes given out are incomplete. Does not provide nearly as much practice as necessary and explains nothing.

Explains content way too quickly and unclearly. Provides little to no practice and support for exams. Exams are graded super harshly and aren't curved at all. Totally disappointed with how this class is being taught and now I'm having to reteach myself everything because I've forgotten/mislearned all the content from lecture.
Her notes were very clear and easy to follow. Clear connection between the lecture notes and homework and exams.

Theres nothing specifically bad about her, but I thought she was very bad at giving lectures, very uninteresting, very monotone and pretty hard to hear.  The issue was exacerbated by the fact that we deviated from the textbook a lot, and so there weren't a lot of other ways to learn the content besides the lectures.

Fink has a good hand writing. I did not attend the lecture. I learn just by looking at the slides and the solutions to homework. The solutions provide a clear way to solve questions with formula highlighted in different colors. The exam is easier than homework, and it has 4 extra credits as well. I'm poor at math but this course is an easy A to me.

I don't get why Fink gets so many poor reviews, and I wouldn't be surprised if every poor review came from the same person. Fink is crystal clear in lectures, and the course content isn't too difficult as long as you study, but that's expected of any class. Homework requires you to think through problems, but that just makes the exams easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Fink is one of the best stats teachers at UM. She is extremely organized and clear and you really learn the material just by following along. She is also very sweet and willing to answer questions that may arise and is rooting for your success. I did so well in her class even after only getting a B+ in calc 3. Cannot recommend more!

One of the best Stats professor at Michigan. Very chill, down-to-earth, great lectures, and is very willing to answer questions. I attribute learning so much in Stats 412 to him, and looking back after taking 413, he prepped me well for 413 and statistics interviews.
There's nothing to say that hasn't been said - Nadiya Fink is an amazing teacher that cares oh so much about his students. You really couldn't ask for a better experience learning Stats.
Fink is a very good professor and explains the concepts well.
Amazing lecturer, one of the best I've ever had. Clear and methodical teaching style and effortlessly facilitates class participation.
Fink is the goat. 10/10 would recommend to a friend. By far the best 412 prof.
Dr. Fink is really a great professor. Lectures are helpful and clear on content, and she engages with students well. Definitely the best professor I've had a UM so far!
Very good professor. I think she really cares about her students and tries very hard to make everyone to actually learn the material.
Worst lecturer, worst grader. Poor content

It seems that FA21 was a rough semester for STATS 412- I took it WN21, and it was fine. The class itself was pretty easy during WN21, and I do think that the harsh ratings from WN21 are an anomaly. There's a clear language barrier considering her accent, but I do think she cares for students and has good intentions :)
Fink is a sha bi lecturer. Withdrawing from her section is the best decision I've made this semester.

Listen to the reviews, I wish I did. One of the worst classes Ive taken at Michigan. She doesnt explain anything clearly and you basically have to teach yourself all the material. Exams are VERY hard to do well on bc of super specific grading and no curve whatsoever. Stats shouldve been an easy requirement and her class rly dropped my GPA.
Sometimes, don't trust your eyes. The reviews don't really tell anything. Take this class and you'll know how good it is.
Have her own set of rules for everything. Don't follow the book or anything online. Only listen to her and how she wants the hw/test to be graded if you want a good grade.
The rating of 2.3 just cannot explain how bad this lecturer is. Rather eat garbage than take this class again. At this point, it's not even a matter of gpa, this class is just pure nonsense.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader
