reviews.comment: Does not explain anything clearly. Uses the textbook but has her own set of rules for grading the test. This class is extremely hard to get a good grade without a curve, especially with no curve and crazy tests.

From the bottom of my heart, do not take this course. No curves at all, class has a B- median. If you mess up once in one of the three tests, your A is gone. Has worse curves than EECS 203. From the 25 courses I have taken at umich, this one was definitely the worst, others are not even close.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Made this class super easy to learn. Had a fun time learning statistics in this class. Tests were super easy and graded fairly.

The class isn't curved, which makes it hard when the exams end up with averages less than a B. Do not take this prof. She does not explain grading criteria clearly. We use the textbook, but then she has her own rules for how questions are to be done, docking almost all points off if not done her way when she doesn't explain how she wants things.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even though she does not curve, this class does not need a curve at all. An A is very doable.
I do not recommend to take her classes, ever. Escape her section at all cost, even if it means late withdraw.

I thought that Fink was a solid professor and I enjoyed going to her section. She explained the course concepts and examples clearly (my own experience doesn't really align with all of these "confusing" "bad lecturer" comments -- she's absolutely fine, at least in stats 412)

It honestly breaks my heart to see those negative comments here. Nadiya is definitely one of the nicest instructors at U-M! She always explains concepts extremely well with inspirational sketches. Also, maybe it's because of my previous A+ in Math 217, her Stats 425 is one of THE EASIEST and smoothest classes I've ever taken - highly recommend her!

For a relatively hard Theory-heavy, Calc-based Probability class, Dr Fink does a great job of taking you through all problems and showing the right way to go about a solution. The class itself expects a solid foundation on multivariable calculus, but the material for this class is covered clearly, with the assumption that you know your calc

Nadiya Fink is the worst. She gives out difficult and long exams and doesn't curve at all. The class median is roughly a B-/C+. Almost 1/3 of the class would fail. Don't take her class if you care about your GPA. She's gonna ruin your future.

Nadiya is a great lecturer and so helpful during office hours; probably one of the nicest professors I have had. Her class is tough, I had to work really hard after taking a 3 year gap from 425 (I'm not a stats major), and her homeworks and tests are quite long. Definitely a really heavy workload but I enjoyed it and found the class rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nadiya Fink is the worst!!! Her tests were extremely long and a lot of my friends received B- or C range grade during the midterm. Her lectures were filled with her calculations which only she can understand. No explanation at all!!! Don't take her class if your GPA matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She explains everything clearly and gets through material very efficiently. She takes her time to go through a practice problem or two for every topic she teaches allowing students to be able to attempt homework problems on their own. She also holds regular office hours and is very helpful in answering any questions you have on the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fink is not a good professor - she is very hard to not only understand but pay attention too. She doesn't phrase things in the best ways and sometimes doesn't handles questions well. Taking it with her, will make you work much harder for your grade. Also the exams are ridiculously hard with a C average sometimes.

Nadiya Fink does not even deserve a chance to teach students. Especially at such a great university. She does not know how to care and help students. NO curves. NO explanation. Almost one-third of my classmates received a C range result in some exams. She failed a lot of students in her class. Don't take her class if your GPA matters.

I wanted to give Dr. Fink a chance, but she honestly confused me so much. After doing just ok on the first exam, I stopped going to Fink's lectures and only went to Gunderson's. I scored four letter grades higher on exam 2. If you have Fink, I recommend watching lecture recordings or going to a different lecture. Also, use GSI office hours for HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Stats 426 with Fink was the worst class that I have ever taken. She is a good lecturer, but she doesnt give adequate practice material, her exams are extremely difficult, and most importantly, her class is totally uncurved. Because of this, a good chunk of my class received in the C range and below. Avoid taking if you care about your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This instructor is a good lecturer but gives ridiculous grade. Medium is C+ to B-, no curve at all. The most unfair issue is that other instructor(s) give much higher grades. Never take Stats 426 with her!!!

To be honest, I've never seen such a horrible teacher before. Almost every one of my classmates was having a problem with the material she taught. She gave these hard, long exam which obviously was impossible to finish and she did not curve the grade. HORRIBLE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst teacher I've had in all of college. The class is difficult, uncurved, and is extremely work heavy even though it is only supposed to be a 3 credit class. Additionally, her notes are hard to read. A good chunk of my class has a C and below and she still refuses to curve. I would avoid taking classes with her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had in two years at Michigan. She does a bad job of explaining examples in class, homework takes 2-4 hours to complete weekly and the tests are impossible to finish in time, let alone being very hard. She doesn't curve either so almost half the class won't pass. I would never consider a course taught by Fink again. Ever.

Try to get Gunderson or do not take Stats 250. Stats with Fink I think actually screwed up my thinking on different concepts in stats and wish I hadn't gone to any of her lectures. Seems like a nice lady but I get a headache trying to constantly understand her.

Homework due every week with about 5-7 pages long, exam is the hardest and longest i have ever taken. The main point is no curve at all, even my class medium was a C. If you have another choice, don't pick her class.

I almost got depression from this class. I did not do really well in the first exam, and I just see no hope in this class. Regardless of how hard and how people perform in this class. This class does not curve. Please if one day she can see those feedback, she would understand how her students feel about her grading.

NO curve. I almost cried. Her exams were sooo long and she took off most of points in an exam question because of only missing minor things. The homework is due weekly and each of them took me around 10 pages of writing. Some of her exam material does not match her homework. If I can give a negative rating for her, I would.

Worst teacher ever. Obviously, she does NOT know how to teach/explain and she does NOT curve the grade given the fact that her exam was long and heavy. One advice on how to learn stats: DON'T take Nadiya's class.

Take stats w/ Gunderson, or at a diff school altogether. Fink does what she can, but she teaches poorly and lacks the concept side of stats that is needed to survive the painfully hard exams. It's unbelievable how much of a waste of time, work, and money this class is, for a widely prereq math class that makes you writes papers and buy hw access.

Of the professors for STATS250, Fink is by far the worst. It came to the point where I had to attend both her and Gunderson's online lectures to understand the material, and then I stopped going to lecture altogether because it was actually hurting my understanding. If you get stuck with her, attend a different lecturer and you'll do much better.

Nadiya FInk is a horrible teacher. Her teaching structure is very unorganized and her lecture is all about computing the problems. NO explanation. NO study guides. Her first exam has an average about C- and she does not curve at all. Straight scaled. Worst teacher I've ever had in my life.
Professor Fink explains things extremely clearly and takes you through problems step-by-step. Easily one of the best I've had at Michigan.

Her lecture is detail-oriented and well organized. And she is good at explaining concepts and computation step by step. I went to her office hours several times and it is really useful. Also I think the workload is okay since it's a 400 level course and there are too many things going on. You cannot learn anything without doing homework.

She gives long, meaningless homework with repetitive calculations, but not enlightening exercises. She also likes to post half of hw online and updated it 3 days later which makes careless students(like me) forget to update hw. Don't ask her deep concepts, she doesn't know either. Her exam questions are organized in a weird way too.
Insane amount of homework. You gotta spend more than 8 hours on homework.

Take this class with her! She explains all concepts clearly and goes through every example problem step-by-step. She's also very helpful in office hours and is willing to help you through any problem. If you just go to class and pay attention you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fink's lectures for Math/Stats 425 were perfectly fine--nothing extraordinary, but she did a good job explaining all of the concepts and doing examples. With that being said, I personally found the content of the course very uninteresting and tedious.

During my semester of stats 250, Dr. Fink moved much faster than Gunderson's class. I always felt like concepts were rushed and never fully understood. It got to the point where I went to Fink's lecture to get the clicker points but watched Gunderson's lectures later on. Take this course with Gunderson if you can.
She was very nice, but the class is very memorization heavy. If you don't memorize the concluding sentences for each test prepare to lose a lot of points.

Nadiya has trouble explaining concepts that should be easy to explain. She is also unwilling to admit when she is wrong (or even worse, doesn't understand why she's wrong!). If you like learning, don't take MATH 425 with her. You will hate statistics and life afterwards. The worst part is that she doesn't post completed notes.

STATS250 is a piece of cake if you've taken basically any math or technical class on campus. Prof. Fink always helped me anytime I went to office hours, and did a great job moving through content at a good pace. Her accent wasn't a problem at all.

Dr. Fink seems like she knows what she's talking about and I think she wanted us to do well, but she didn't really get that across in lectures. Exams are difficult, especially if you do not have a background in statistics. If you take this course, no matter the professor, make sure you review ALL concepts before exams. They will surprise you.
An OK lecturer teaching an easy class.
Very mediocre. Hard class, nothing was very specific.

Nadiya was great for Math/Stats 425. Lectures are very clear! If you go to lecture and do the homework, you will do very well in the class. The tests are extremely similar to the homework problems. Do them! Attendance is mandatory so just go. Overall it was the smoothest and easiest math class I've taken at the University.

Her lectures aren't thorough; she rushes through problems and can't explain the answers clearly. I usually spent days in office hours with GSI's to understand simple concepts. I failed the first exam and dropped the course. Unless you have a background in Stats, e.g. you took AP Stats in high school, I recommend taking it at a community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Quite dated, but not too bad.
It wasn't my favorite professor; I didn't learn much from the class, since it was discussion-based, aside from like three mini-lectures. Definitely a history class for non-history majors

Three 4-5 pg papers, six discussion posts, no exams. 1 lecture per week would have an easy surprise quiz on the readings so you had to read them. Prof. Fields was super funny, and her lectures were easy to pay attention to. Told history like a story rather than listing meaningless facts, I learned so much. No Lecture Capture or slides though.

Literally one of the best professors I have had here. Caring, funny, and really knowledgeable about Russian history. Always encourages students to ask questions and really makes the classroom comfortable

She's so awesome-sauce! Dr. Field is caring, encouraging, and supportive. The course is new, so she's lenient to a reasonable degree. She's clearly passionate and excited about the course and its materials, which is contagious. I actually enrolled in this class by accident and had no background knowledge/understanding, but I already love it! Thx DF
I love my queen Deborah, she is by far my best prof I have had my freshman year. Great and humorous lady that I absolutely adore.
Prof Field is a different professor.  A little hard to understand what she wants in her assignments.  Average grader.  Not a hard class but not very interesting either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Field is a great professor and makes the class interesting. Participation is very important to her so make sure to keep up with the readings. My main critique is that the class is graded on 100 points. If you do poorly on one assignment it can ruin your grade in the class, which is frustrating if you are consistent for most of the semester :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, genuinely made me interested in the course. She is super funny and entertaining in class, and has funny content incorporated into the course. There is a lot of reading and grade is based heavily on participation, but the points are not very tough to get. She is very helpful and provides excellent advice to do better on essays.

This class was super interesting, and I got to learn a lot of different things. The GSI grades everything so make sure you run things by him. There are three papers to write, apart from the participation grade. Overall, I would not say the class is an easy A, but it will become easier if you do your readings and find themes you are interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst class I have ever taken. The prof is nice but cannot teach. The only reason I passed was because I had prior Python experience. Discussion is a waste as gsi's know nothing, projects + tests are so much harder than what he teaches, exams are open-book but still BAD for that reason. If you're an econ major, take Stats 250 instead.

I don't personally believe that this material is best absorbed in the lecture format, but the lectures were the best they could be, given the constraints of what had to be taught. Beyond this, the homework often had to be pushed back and amended, which gave the course a more disorganized and unserious feel.

He is not as bas as all these reviews are saying! Very kind and understanding and cares a lot about his students. His lectures are boring, but he always ensures to go around and help every student who needs it. Don't be afraid to take this class!!
Makes basic stats confusing, and it is actually impossible to stay awake during lecture. Uses AI in the middle of teaching because he forgets what he is talking about.

The worst Prof I've had. This class is so difficult because his videos and lectures are unclear and poorly explain concepts. If you don't know Python, good luck using AI, which is encouraged. Grading criteria on quizzes are arbitrary. Everyone I talk to is somewhere between somewhat confused and completely lost. Don't take!!

Professor Fredrickson is an hilariously bad lecturer who manages confuses himself sometimes. I came into this knowledge with lots of stats knowledge. Professor Fredrickson only managed to confuse me more. When you ask him a question, he unironically tells you to ask AI.  It is disturbing how bad he is. Great GSIs though shoutout Mihir.
Worst professor I have ever had in my whole life.

Lectures were so boring, I felt bad bc I was constantly falling asleep in them. The prof was nice and stuff, but you really don't learn anything, bc AI was encouraged and told to use it if you didn't understand. My GSI wasn't helpful either and communication was lacking on all fronts, very frustrating tbh. I don't recommend this course AT ALL.

The most frustrating part of this course was the lack of communication and timely grading. Piazza would be filled with complaints and questions that were never addressed. No response to emails either. Grades would take forever to be entered. Lectures were incredibly boring; I stopped attending. You use AI for everything. You don't learn very much.
ChatGPT101
I was under the impression this class would teach you Python. I left feeling even more confused and honestly a bit disturbed.
Waste of money

Considering this is one of the first classes I've taken at UMICH, I'm already beyond disappointed with the quality of instruction that I'm seeing. Lectures are not engaging and GSI's aren't very helpful. Abysmal communication with students. Would not recommend taking this class unless you absolutely need to.

This class promises that you don't need any knowledge of Python to succeed but it was unrealistic for its expectations. And as people are saying, this class was organized so badly it's hilarious, and grades come in very late. He is a nice professor who will help you, but I feel like everything is inconsistent, not timely, and not engaging.

He's a solid teacher if you go in person to lecture, but the most frustrating part is how the class is run. Assignments take months to grade making it difficult to know where you stand in the class and he responds to piazza very slowly, if at all. I took 306 and 406 with him, and while the classes themselves aren't that hard, change should be made.
Very kind Professor but course was beyond unorganized and required extensive prior knowledge to succeed while actually learning though states it does not.
My advisor advised me to take this course…but if this is what UMich delivers, then I probably accepted the wrong offer
Being in his class did not teach me anything that I found to be useful or practical. This course was beyond unorganized, and it's frustrating how he ran the class the whole semester.
He deserves jail time for robbing students of their tuition

This class is the most unorganized and stupid class I have taken at UMICH. Hes a nice guy, but doesn't know what he is teaching. The GSIs are the worst as well. Don't take this class if you are wanting to learn anything.

i came in expecting to learn python and statistics because that's what he opened the first few lectures with and even highlighted that datasci will be half python and half statistics. im not sure what happened to that because this class just became vibecoding 101. prof seems like a chill dude, just wouldn't recommend him to teach you anything.
The course was very badly structured, and the lectures were not inspiring at all. The exams and projects were not easy at all. Overall, I wouldn't recommend him.

Prof. is kind, but lectures are boring and have errors. This class fails to teach Data Science effectively. GSIs are bad, too. A spike in difficulty forces reliance on AI for projects, contrary to claims that no Python experience is needed. It's an easy grade since AI is encouraged, but you will learn little and feel unprepared for future courses.

Undoubtedly, he's a very kind-hearted individual & always respectful towards his students. He's clearly passionate about stats but extremely unorganized: opening up Gradescope submissions late, pushing back due dates because he grades late, and switching up quiz formats often. Lectures were hard to follow & he's very unresponsive in Piazza/emails.

I can tell that Fredrickson has a good heart and respects students, and to his credit, I can see that he is quite helpful outside of class. That does not make up for the trainwreck of a class that this was. This is a class on vibecoding & I gained absolutely zero insight on Python or DS. Assignments were random & lacked guidance. Don't take w/ him.

Lecture is so so boring, he is very monotone. Slides are also difficult to take notes on and the projects often had to little to do with what we were learning in class (like more advanced coding). Class was also so unorganized, felt like he and the GSIs weren't communicating.

Never responds to emails, and the Piazza is rarely updated. It was almost comical how disorganized this class was. They grade like 1 month late, and you never know your grade in class. They changed the organization of this course, with pretty difficult quizzes. Most GSIs don't seem to care. Piazza is absurdly filled with complaints

Fredrickson seems like a very good person but datasci 101 is a VERY VERY poorly organized class. Labs were a waste of time. Many ppl complain about the difficulty of this course which is fair; its easy if u have a strong background in stats and programming but impossible otherwise (which shouldnt be the case for a 101 lol). Take at own discernment

This class was literally being rewritten as it was being taken. As a student who knows nothing about Datasci, I was hoping for a simple and straightforward learning about it, yet we were literally the class guinea pigs. Due dates were always wrong, quizzes harder than the material learned. It was extremely difficult to keep up with.

Professor Fredrickson was always available and helpful when answering questions. However, his lectures were difficult to follow, a lot of the slides included bits of code that weren't well explained. The organization of the class was not great, and the material on the quizzes and lectures felt very disconnected.

Mark is an alright lecturer, I wouldn't say he just reads from the slides, he explains well. I think the problem with this class was the lack of organization. They rewrote the course this semester, and a lot was rocky. Quizzes are open note and easy, but one of them was harder than the others and the instructors acknowledged that, but didn't help.

He is very sweet in general, someone who would go home and bake cookies for his family, but not the best prof. Everything on canvas would have wrong due dates. Open notes for all the quizzes. Easy enough to get by with chat but knowledge wise he was unhelpful and confusing. the question forum was filled with questions but rarely ever answered.

this class was actually insane. lectures drag and jump between random topics with no clear point or structure. quizzes feel like guesswork. projects are vague, and labs are useless. we're surviving off chatgpt and prayers. only positive was that studying hard and waking up early for those biweekly quizzes just to get rekt built character.

Amazing! I accidentally missed a quiz and he allowed me to make it up, he is also very sweet and cares about his students. Attendance is easy points, projects and quizzes are open note and there is lots of resources available to help, including directly asking him during the quizzes. i love mark fredrickson he deserves a raise
Dr. Fredrickson is an amazing professor. He's very blunt, but I appreciate constructive criticism

Mark is a good guy. His lectures were presented well. No tests. But his course seemed incredibly disorganized. Piazza questions went several days or more before a response. Go to class or OH to get your questions answered timely. Hastily produced homeworks that sometimes had short, vague directions wasted students' time on unnecessary confusion.
Easy A but not good for actually learning the skills. He's such a boring lecturer and basically tells you to use GenAI on everything. Even exams. Which makes it easy but not very productive

This class is really fun with Dr.Fredrickson, although pretty difficult if you come in without prior Python or statistics knowledge. For the most part, you get out of the class what you put into it. If you pay attention to lectures and lab, the homework is pretty easy. The wording of the questions for weekly quizzes and homework is confusing.

Pretty easy intro course, but lectures were boring. ended up not going to most lectures and still ended with an A. exams were all online take home. weekly hw's that were probably the hardest part of the course, but still not bad.

He's a good professor for STATS 206. The course is not difficult, but a common issue is the varying levels of Python experience among students. Jumping from Python fundamentals in Lesson 1 to using libraries for statistical computation can be challenging for those less familiar with the language.

Cool professor and he really tried to make the class interesting. Unfortunately, statistical computing is quite dry. OH are very helpful, and he is easy to reach on Piazza or email. Not a super high workload, and you will certainly get better with R. He genuinely cares about his students. You get as much as you put into the class.
Love prof Mark! He is a great guy and do care students. Took 306 in winter and 406 in fall with him. All the lectures are recorded.

He's a nice enough guy who is happy to respond to emails, but his lecturing and quiz/exam/assignment writing is just terrible. The beginning of the class was pretty much basic statistics that I've known for years, and yet his style of lecture was so confusing that I felt less confident after each lecture. Test questions are unclear and unhelpful.
the best professor

Mark Fredrickson conducts his class with an unwavering aura of professionalism and composure. He is open to questions and feedback but his explanations are so fluid and understandable that those are often unnecessary. STATS206 is not a difficult class with Mark at the helm. He's locked in.

This class was unnecessarily time consuming and confusing with the constant typos on the homework and lots of code that wasn't taught in lectures and was quickly skimmed over in labs that was just sort of expected to be known. The lectures were also extremely boring and were not very interactive making it harder to grasp the material.

STATS 206 is not a hard course. The class has an A- average; anyone claiming it's insanely difficult just didn't do anything. Homework is fairly time consuming, but work in a group and you get it done. Exams are online, again time consuming but not too hard. Mark is generous with extra credit; sure he isn't the best lecturer, but just do work = A.

Fredrickson is nice but the class is taught terribly. This is the hardest "intro" class I've ever taken, and there's barely any coding taught even though the hw is all Python. Most GSIs are terrible and clearly don't know what's going on in class. I would advise against taking this class but if you do: go to OH for the hw and do the extra credit

I knew a fair bit of Python coming into the course and had a bit of an AP Stats background. Given that I barely spent time on this class, it was honestly harder than expected. Homeworks are impossible unless you go to office hours 24/7 or you get them from someone else lol. But exams thankfully aren't too bad and are online.

Professor Fredrickson was very passionate about stats, but, this class was not what I expected. As someone who had no Python or coding experience, I struggled tremendously. This is definitely NOT a beginner course. HW is very long and difficult and does not cover lecture material. The content was all over the place and lectures are confusing.

I have never done Python before, but I didn't think this class was too hard. Lectures are boring, but attendance isn't mandatory. Questions are worded confusingly often, but GSIs are super accessible and helpful. Labs give answers to HW often. Homework is super time-consuming and difficult, but quizzes and exams are super easy.

I want to be brutally honest, so people know exactly what to expect. He is kind of robotic and very hard to understand at times. This class IS NOT welcoming for people with no Python experience. Even though I had some Python experience, I had lots of trouble. Unrelated to him, the GSIs are awful and unhelpful. Take this class w caution.

Mark is a caring and understanding teacher. He is flexible when scheduling his office hours, extending due dates when homework is released late, and other administrative things. He gives clear answers during office hours. However his lectures can be dull, but 'tis the nature of statistical computing.

Professor Fredrickson was a caring person and was more than happy to answer questions during office hours, but the content was often very confusing and did not relate to what was presented in lectures. If you have not taken another stats class or are not familiar with Python, I would recommend not taking this class.

Lectures don't cover homework and quiz material at all, and there was lots of math in the lectures that we never got tested on. If you have no background in coding, do not take this class. I did okay because I took compsci in high school, but still struggled since I've never touched pandas, numpy, or seaborn (which most of the class is on).

Mark's lectures are extremely boring and overly complex. Lectures never correspond to homework as hw requires extensive coding that he does not teach. Without prior coding or stats experience, the class is too demanding. His grading rubrics are specific to the point where his GSI's had to confront him. Avoid his class and take stats 250 instead.

His lectures can be a little boring and hard to follow through but outside lectures he is super helpful and caring and has office hours frequently so he's almost always accessible. He is also accommodating and really does want you do succeed. If you can get through the lectures then I recommend Professor Fredrickson.

He's a great guy who knows a lot about stats. His lectures can be a little dull, but they're easy to follow. I have never taken a coding/comp sci class before, but as long as you watch the lectures and pay attention in lab you'll be fine. All the exams are open note and similar to the homework and lab assignments we do.

I know he is very intelligent in his field, but the issue this semester was that the lectures were not informative. The lectures did not translate to any test, quiz, or homework assignment. It was truly difficult to put 2 and 2 together because there was no correlation between what was learned and what was given on an assignment.

Shouldn't be labeled as an intro course. Little to no explanation of Python & coding hw that is far too difficult for beginners. Lectures are dense & boring, grade relies heavily on performance in the exams & few coding assignments. Often didn't get the necessary info to complete the hw until a few days before it was due. Nice prof, bad class

Professor Mark Fredrickson is a great professor and very nice person. He is very helpful and understanding. However, this class is a mess. You have to teach yourself python, and you really should have prior stats knowledge. For example, we went over hypothesis testing in one lecture. I would avoid this class.
Great instructor who teaches well. Sure, there are some parts that might be confusing, but he is very helpful when answering questions (during and after classes) and gives great feedback.

It is unfair for this guy to receive many poor ratings. Although Dr. Fredrickson seems to be confusing during lectures, he is willing to help his students in office hours. The class is challenging but interesting, and he gives some extra credits so I don't think it is too difficult to get a good score as long as you learn. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I think that Dr. Fredrickson was given difficult a class, but he genuinely wants to help his students. He receives unfair criticism because the class he teaches is not great, but its the curriculum, not his teaching (at least in my opinion). Class is somewhat hard, but honestly doable. Frederickson cares about his students and is a good guy
Avoid Stats 206 at all costs. Not worth it to take and extremely hard for an intro class. There are better coding classes at this school.

lectures are super boring, data science and coding was not meant to be taught through lectures and Dr. Fredrickson doesn't do much to make it more interesting. Nice guy but wholly uninteresting. I really wish there was more interactive work, feel like I had to teach myself python from scratch. Avoid.

The poor guy got handed a mess of a class in the form of STATS206, it's not his fault this is a horribly written class. Dr. Fredrickson tries his best to be accommodating and help his students out, lecture attendance is not required and you can ask for exam regrades. But STATS206 is a total mess, and you should avoid it. Take another class.

I really like Prof Frederickson and I feel like he really prioritizes helping students learn the material. He is very attentive to Piazza posts and will even respond late at night right before the assignment is due. He is very easily accessible and his class helped make programming less intimidating to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fredrickson makes simple concepts confusing. His homework regularly has typos and is full of confusing wording. His exams are multiple choice questions and essay questions (which are heavily weighted), so prepare to write a lot in a short time. One good thing: he records lectures, so you have the flexibility to watch them when you have time.

Worst professor ever, expect you to write code at the beginning of the course, although he said no coding experience required. And he's materials are blur af, 100% not prepare your for future stat or data science course. Avoid him!

INCREDIBLE professor!! All of her lectures were so interesting and well structured, and she connects with students really well; the class felt like a community. Lots of reading but just reading a summary before discussion works fine. I cannot recommend this class enough. And it satisfies RE req!

You learn so much in the lectures. Discussion was easy to get by with only a summary of the readings. Attendance for lectures is kinda needed to get content but easy to sit through. With so much content thrown at you, they do a great job with testing a small amount where you get to choose to demonstrate what you learned, setting up for success.
So funny, pushes her students academically for sure.

Professor French is such a good lecturer, her lectures are always engaging and informational, and you get a lot out of attending them. I will say attendance is definitely mandatory, you will take a lot of notes and you'll need them. The essay assignments were explained well as was the midterm

Professor French is very nice and funny, and I like the class a lot. I would say the only downside is that there are no slides/information to access online if you can't make it to class for whatever reason. However, her lectures are interesting and tend to run on the shorter side, so attending class really shouldn't be an issue.

Lectures were always super thorough and interesting. If you don't have background knowledge in this course it can be a little hard. You can get by discussion without really reading much of the assigned readings, but that will come back to haunt for papers/midterm and final. Very GSI dependent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor French was a great lecturer and professor. She was always enthusiastic and truly did care about her students. While she did read from cards for lectures, she definitely knew her material when students asked questions. Very accessible outside of class as well. Would take another class with her. Grading was easy.

I actually took History 211 with Prof. French (couldn’t find the correct tag). Her lectures are written very well, and she is extremely knowledgeable on what she teaches. I’ve never been a huge fan of history classes, but she made it very interesting! Papers/exams are not too difficult and other work is minimal compared to some other classes.

Professor French makes an effort to get to know the students. Very knowledgeable, and less formal compared to others in the department (although this is not always a good thing - she often let teacher's pets waste class time). She's witty, but lectures still feel long. Overall, fairly decent.

Professor French is obviously a very seasoned and intelligent professor, who gives great lectures. However, the assigned reading is upwards of 100 pages of dense material per week. She is also a very tough grader, and grades unpredictably on papers. She's hilarious, but i mean you can work very hard and still get a B.

Professor French is my favorite professor at UM. She really helped me discover my passion and she's probably the best thing about my time at UM. She is really honest and tough when grading papers, which makes my writing better! She's hilarious, incredibly knowledgable, and the most incredible lecturer! If you love history, she is the prof to take!

Professor French is extremely knowledgable and articulate. Her lectures are fascinating if not always comprehensive or straightforward. She grades fairly, and is naturally more scrupulous when grading papers that are heavily weighted. She is a kind person who can be rather snooty on occasion.

I hated this class. Your grade is entirely based on several 3-5 page papers, and she is VERY picky and unpredictable. I did really well on the first one and then really poorly on the next, and when I went to her office hours for help, she was condescending and didn't give me any helpful advice. She is entertaining in lecture, but not worth it.

209 was come to class, take notes, leave. Read primary sources. Discuss them in section. However, the 1.5 hours spent in lecture went by relatively fast because she is a GREAT lecturer. There isn't a lot of work, but she is very picky about the papers. (I spent 3 to 4 hours and got a B on mine). Some extra reading. A few "field trips" to the museum
I am no longer a history major because of this professor.  I wish she never taught at Michigan.
Horrible Professor, avoid if you can.

Professor French's lectures are amazing and extremely interesting, which is especially hard to find in a historical survey course. Her midterm and final are a bit challenging and all SAEssay, however she provides students with the opportunity to create the topics that will be on the test. Do not need the textbook at all.

We were asked to choose a topic and start writing our term paper in the very first week of class.  I ended up choosing a primary source that wasn't of much interest to me.  She gave too many personal anecdotes in her classes, sometimes completely unrelated to the class and often wasted good 10-20 minutes of class time.

Professor French is the most entertaining professor I have had so far. She is great at lecturing and makes it interesting even if you don't plan on being a history major. Be warned though, she expects a lot from her students. There isn't a terrible amount of work but what you do has to be quality or you won't pass.

French is a great professor. She knows what she's doing and she is enthusiastic about the subject. She is super helpful in office hours and is willing to clarify anything you need. She does assign a lot of work though.

Our textbook was wordy and chosen because it was the cheapest-not helpful. She talked very fast in lecture and some of her analysis seemed off. One's GSI is the person you communicate with in this class and he/she grades all of your papers. French was not as great as you'd expect at Michigan, but certainly not awful.

I am a chem major, but took her class for distribution. She was exactly what I wanted for a history professor. She loves her subject and makes the lectures like a story (tended to leave on a cliffhanger). Hard grader but I loved the class. Mandatory lecture attendance though.
She is a VERY hard grader. I thought this class would be very easy and took it as a joke. It's my worst grade....I wouldn't recommend it

While a FY seminar on Robin Hood sounds easy, Prof French grades pretty hard, and there is a ton of reading.  Professor is nice and passionate about the topic, but large reading load and hard grader on essays.  I definitely would not recommend this class, unless you are particularly interested in RH / medieval history.

Prof. French is really funny! She's nice, knows so much about history, and makes even dry lectures interesting. Okay, she's kinda a tough grader, but this is college, what do you expect? Lots of reading and mandatory attendance. Overall great prof!

KFid is by far one of the best profs in the aero department at UMich. 325 is a hard class, but he explains the concepts very well, and makes the class an enjoyable experience. He really cares for the topic and his students, and it shows. He has example questions in class to help understand concepts better, and offers class over zoom as well
Great professor for a very hard course. I really enjoyed lectures and felt like I picked up the concepts pretty fast. I don't think I would have passed Aerosp325 if it was a different professor.

By far the most caring professor at umich aero. Spends much time preparing for lecture, teaching style is amazing, and has plenty of office hours where he will make a complex subject understandable to a 6 year old. Homework's and exams are TOUGH, but that's a part of actually learning. You will spend many hours on this class, but you WILL LEARN

Professor Fidkowski is easily my favorite prof in the Aero Department. He knows the material inside and out and has an incredible ability to break it down and make it understandable for new students.

Homeworks are typically quite tough, as are the exams, but they never felt unfair. Read the course notes and go to office hours and you'll be fine.

Great professor! I was very worried going into this class - I didn't feel prepared due to doing poorly in the prerequisite class (AE325), but Prof. KFid really made this course doable. He taught things in a very sensible manner, provided lots of help in Office Hours, had great notes, and was extremely flexible with extensions and coursework.

This class is just really hard. KFid is a solid professor, good at explaining material and work is relatively spread out throughout semester. HW is really hard and is the majority determinant of your grade - but it is certainly possible to do well.
Good professor. Extremely smart.
Poor lecture quality during online school
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor who cares a lot that his students learn. Organized with very clear and helpful lectures, class notes, grading, schedule, etc. Office hours are very helpful and he is responsive on Piazza to answer questions. One of my favorite classes in the aero department so far!

KFid is the best professor! It does not even matter what he is teaching you should just take it (even if you do not think you are interested). His lectures are fantastic and he is incredibly helpful on homeworks. The work is hard, but interesting!

Fidkowski is one of the best professors I've ever taken. Awe-inspiring command of the material and crystal-clear explanations. Great use of peripheral tech like Piazza and iClickers. Super accessible and helpful. Wrote and provided very comprehensive course notes. Gives a lot of very tough homework but you will learn a lot. Go to office hours.

KFid has been one of the best aero professors I've had thus far. His lectures are very helpful, and he genuinely cares that you learn. Homeworks are difficult and you will find yourself in OH often, but they prepare you for the exams. This class is graded very fairly, but nonetheless a difficult class. Overall a great class. You learn a lot.

Fid responds quickly to emails and thoroughly answers questions about the homework. That said, the homework frequently seems impossible - beware an offer to replace the worst homework grade with a new homework's grade. He grades fairly and lectures at a comfortable pace; he genuinely cares if his students learn.

Definitely take KFid's class if you have the chance. His explanations are crystal clear, which is critical for a class like aerodynamics. He's a prof who really cares about his students and a genuinely nice person - he baked us treats for Halloween! Homework is tough, but once you're through with those, exams are perfectly doable.

Prof. Fidkowski taught computational methods in aerospace engineering which was a class similarly offered in MIT. The concepts covered were abstract but he made them easy to understand. He is imo the best lecturer in the department. He replies emails within a couple of hours which helped a lot in getting assignments completed on time.

He is extremely helpful and approachable and is really knowledgeable. I would highly recommend taking any class with him as he is arguably the best professor in the aerospace department. He goes out of his way to help his students and as long as you attend lectures and make an honest effort to learn the material, you will have a great time.

Best Aero professor I've had. Very helpful and explains things well. Homework is very difficult so be prepared to go to all office hours. Never used the suggested textbook, all hw and exam question are based of his notes.
Extremely hard class.  Be prepared to spend ungodly amounts of time on the homework.  Despite the homework being insanely hard, he manages to make the class enjoyable somehow.
Very nice

He is one of the best professors I've had.  The homework can be long but it's really helpful and he's always willing to answer questions. The lectures are well-worth going to, especially if he continues with the Quizdom concept questions.

Professor Fidkowski is probably the most effective instructor in the entire department.  Lectures were excellent and his self-produced homeworks are extremely interesting (though consistently challenging).  He conveys aerodynamics concepts with both clarity and depth, and is always friendly and approachable when extra help is needed.
He is a great teacher. The class is challenging and interesting

Very clear, helpful, and honest with students.  Stresses concepts rather than formulas, which is crucial to understanding aerodynamics.  It's a shame to admit that a second-year professor is possibly the best in the department, but it's been true so far by a pretty good margin.
Best professor in the dept. Very responsive to the class. Always willing to help. Homeworks can be long but help alot with the exams. Fair Grader. Every aero student should have K-Fid.
Great professor, learned a lot from him. He really cares about his students and tries to help them and get feedback from them.  Lectures are pretty interesting and worth going to

Professor Warneken made the class more bearable. The topics weren't too difficult, and the lectures were usually sorta funny. Strict no phone/computer policy and will call you out, but lowkey just pay attention or don't go to lecture since attendance isn't mandatory. Sometimes he covers things in class that aren't written on slides so I would go.

Dr. Warneken's policies are very strict and I honestly wasn't a huge fan of the way he taught the class and called out students. But I would say the way he presents information is pretty engaging in a certain kind of way, especially since he makes a lot of jokes.

Super fun professor and an easy class. The content was interesting on its own, but Prof. Warneken made it even more enjoyable. Some parts felt a bit too easy or like common sense, but overall it was a fun and engaging course.

Professor Warneken was great and I loved this class. The readings can be a bit heavy, but not unmanageable. He posts study guides for each exam, which were pretty straightforward. Strict no technology policy but his lectures were engaging and super funny. Would take again!

I enjoyed Dr. Warneken's lectures bcs he told good jokes, & the class is super easy if you do the work. Papers are actually enjoyable, & exams are straightforward. However, he's oddly strict abt his policies to a point that's pretty unusual, like making everyone show their IDs to enter the lecture hall or calling ppl out for having a laptop out.

Does not respect students and his policies are so rigid. He will stop a lecture and individually call out people if he sees a phone. No access to lecture recordings unless you're basically deathly ill or play a sport. At least he makes some good jokes

Professor Warenken was able to teach avg, his lectures were sometimes funny, pretty straightforward. However, his policies were absolutely terrible. He doesn't allow any laptops, and posts the slides 24 hours after class ends, and his canvas was disorganized. Too much work for advocating for SSD, very stingy about having everyone to learn his way.

Class is pretty straightforward. I attended lecture for the first month or so and just stopped showing up since the exams were pretty easy as long as you took the notes after he posted them the day after.

PSYCH 250 was overall well organized, and Dr. Warneken explained the material thoroughly and clearly. He's pretty funny too. If you did all the readings and notes, showed up to lectures and sections, you should definitely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is fine however if you have in class accommodations I would be prepared to fight with him for them. He will give you up to 200 pages of reading per class but to be honest I just would read like 20 pages and it was fine. Only 2 major papers and no tests.

I honestly loved taking Dr. W's class, and feel that I learned a lot for an intro-level class. He really tries to make lectures interesting for students, and always tries to get a laugh. The grading is very easy, there are about 4 online exams and 1 paper. He does have a strict no-tech policy, so be prepared to bring a paper notebook to class.
He is a great professor. He keeps lectures interesting and his exams and very reasonable. When I took the class the exams were online and taken outside of class.
Very straightforward class. Easy to understand and you know whats expected of you. He makes exam prep very easy and is super nice :)

Felix was the best professor that I had all semester. He gives great lectures and they are so interesting. I would 100% take this class again. Attendance at lectures wasn't mandatory, but I still went to almost all of them because he is great. Tests aren't that hard either which is good.
Professor Warneken is a great lecturer and his class is very clear and straightforward. His tests are pretty clear and easy as long as you keep up with the lectures.

All of the lectures were asynchronous but you could still see that he made the information class-specific and tried to be engaging. The material was straightforward and really interesting. Overall a great class.

Professor Warneken was amazing. His exams are exactly what is in the lectures. He even gives you a study guide and jeopardy before each exam to help you succeed on his exams. Overall a very easy and interesting class.

He's clearly passionate about psychology, is very knowledgeable and is a great teacher. I could tell that he respects student contributions to the discussion. I love that he read every reflection I wrote (2 per week) and provided feedback. He's clearly woke too i.e. during the election he was empathetic about missing class.

Professor Warneken isn't strict, but is formal. Treat him with respect. Sometimes there was material on the exams which were covered in chapters and lectures after the exam and it was difficult to study because GSIs had no idea what was on exams. Still, you could tell that Professor Warneken really cares about his students!

Dr. Fogleman is wonderfully thorough. While many of the concepts she touches on are implicit considering we're all participants of society, she, throughout the course of class, puts them all into context to each other and genuinely sends you off with a deep shift in perspective which helps bring insight and lucidity to your navigation of life.

I had Dr. Fogleman for SOC 302. It was her first time teaching the class and she was extremely kind and caring and receptive to feedback. Grades were very clearly defined and she was overly nice in her efforts to make the class as effortless as possible. She made the final exam optional when most people were doing quite well in her class.

Sweet person but an awful teacher. Takes 45 minutes to explain things that could be said in 5 minutes. The content itself is extremely easy to comprehend. However, her grading is extremely annoying. She grades papers based on her opinion rather than the quality of your writing and takes points off for no apparent reason. Also a super boring class.

Nice person, horrible professor. Super disorganized. Very harsh grader. Takes FOREVER to grade. Expectations are almost always unclear given the way she grades. Grades based on how she would write. Posts assignments very last minute. Lectures are useless (reiterates readings and yaps for 80 mins). Can't reach outside of class. Would not recommend!!

Grading is extremely hard and super unclear. No rubric for the semester-long paper, and it seems like she grades each draft based on whether or not it's the way she would write it. Feedback is never given on time and she's constantly changing due dates. Very nice person, but wouldn't want her as a professor ever again.

Professors is very nice and was receptive to feedback during office hours. Lectures felt unstructured and a waste of time. Deadlines were sometimes confusing. She mentioned it was her first semester teaching post PHD graduation which explains some of the disorganization. If the class at a GSI next semester I think it would improve a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice person, horrible professor. Everything was super disorganized. Very harsh grader for no reason. Expectations are almost always unclear given the way she grades. Posts assignments very last minute. Lectures are useless (just reiterates the readings and yaps for an hour and a half). Technically "easy" but would not recommend at all.

really nice but extremely nit-picky grader. group projects are weighted heavily. MAKE SURE to get good project partners, it will make/break your grade. basically everything is group work. lectures are pointless. difficult to reach out of class. take a different class if you care about your GPA. Only people who could do well are Soc majors.

Grading criteria was never made clear and took points off for the smallest things. Lectures weren't clear and she often went on tangents that didn't relate to the topic at hand, but then proceeded to ask us to provide written reflections everyday. Everything was in a group and even if you wanted to work alone, you couldn't.

Harsh grader on things like proposals, lecture was very irreverent, and group project heavy (you get one group). When she gives feedback, it is basically "do this not what you did". There was no clarity in anything in this course. She goes on tangents that are not relevant. Way to hard for the credits you get and for the course.

She didn't provide rubrics for assignments and seemed to make up the parameters as we went, even for a semester-long project. Lectures were unengaging and often off-topic. Everyone I talked to felt confused about the content and assignments. Nearly everything was group work, and reaching her by email was nearly impossible.

Very tough grader while lacking clear grading criteria or instructions. Took off points for the smallest details but failed to give constructive criticism. Bad at responding to emails. Lectures were hard to follow and pay attention to. Almost every assignment required group work. Nice person but she made me passionately hate this class.
An incessant yapper who is incoherent most of the time. Introduces hard-core sociology theory with very little set-up. Group projects for everything. Would NOT recommend x20
Assigns important coursework on late notice. Nitpicky grader on small details. For me personally, she was hard to follow in lectures and would often go all over the place.

Always wants students to talk. Yaps, A LOT. Very chirpy. If you hate group projects or care about your GPA? Don't take this class as 90% of the work is group work and group projects, and is not "curved" to reflect individual effort. Posts assignments very last minute, and still expects completion. Overall horrible experience, but "easy" class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I thought taking an 8 am Spanish class was extremely daunting, but Laura brought so much energy and passion that I forgot I was up so early. Overall, she's a great explainer and wants you to succeed.
Spanish is hard, but Laura is a fantastic professor. I had her for 102, she was great. Now, for 232, I'm back with her and she is just as good as last year.
She made taking a 9 am course (four days a week) very enjoyable.

She is someone who knows how to teach, especially when dealing with such a broad range of students. You'll find her to be very understanding. She makes class enjoyable, even when taking it at 9 am. Overall, great semester.
Hate the language requirement but Laura made spanish fun, would take her again!

Laura is such a caring teacher and she made me look forward to going to Spanish class. She gave us lots of extra practice resources, prepared us well for the quizzes, and made the class fun. Would recommend.
i absolutely love her, she is the sweetest soul. She cares about her students so much and makes sure we learn and do well. One of my favorite proffers here at umich

She's great. Super nice, and makes practice sheets and vocab sheets she isn't required to make. She is very helpful for accommodating conflicts and very personable. Excellent teacher, always has great answers to any and all questions.
This professor seems very flaky and temperamental.
So kind, made me enjoy spanish class!

Laura is the best language instructor I've had. I found that her teaching methods worked well, and I didn't need to cram for the final to do well. I can look back and say I actually learned Spanish this semester and did not just "get through" the class. I do recommend going to office hours after speaking tests to get feedback, and go to class!
She's an amazing professor. Be clear grading, and is very helpful if you communicate your needs. Use office hours, and participate. Attendance matters.

Laura has been such an amazing instructor! My mom passed away this semester, and Laura was so understanding and helpful, which I can't say about all my instructors. She is enthusiastic, dedicated to teaching, and provides lots of resources to help students study outside of class. Laura is one of my favorite instructors that I have had in college!

Laura was a great professor who was obviously very caring and passionate about Spanish. She gave great instructions and the class was fun. I highly recommend getting her as your professor for 232 if possible.
Laura Gess is an amazing teacher! She's super caring, helpful, and patient with her students. She's also really funny and engaging- definitely recommend her for 232.
Had her for Spanish 232. She was awesome. Highly recommend
Fine professor. His class is too much work to be only 1 credit. A little much on how he expects students to understand this particular class as most are not astrology majors...

I really loved the class material, but he just felt uninterested and not excited to be teaching. However, he clearly was knowledgeable and knew the material well. I did not enjoy going to class each week because I knew he would be unenthusiastic. This class was fine for an easy credit, but if you really like this material, I wouldn't recommend him.
Great professor with good explanations. Fun 1-credit class with clear expectations, interesting course material, and not too much work. Many options to earn credit. Would recommend!

I really liked Prof. Gultekin. At times taking this class I was very lost but reading the textbook definitely helped with the exams. The labs and homeworks were difficult but also weren't really relevant for the exams which made them easier. If you are looking for an easy quantitative reasoning requirement like I was, I would not take this class.

Good professor, but many concepts take time to understand. He had a demo in almost every lecture and used iClickers as extra credit which both helped a lot. If you are interested in astronomy I highly recommend this class (I really enjoyed it), but be prepared to put in some effort if you want an A.

Goes through lectures fast but he does a good job covering subjects that are hard to grasp. He has demos which are fun and does a good job answering questions in lecture. iClicker is used. I recommend taking this class but make sure you study and read the textbook.

He has a tendency to make people feel bad about doing independent work/ will force you to get into groups or stay after to work on pointless group assignments that don't really contribute. He adds in random questions and tasks that are unrelated to the course, like having us send him pictures of his childhood hero out of his own enjoyment.

I stopped going to lecture after the first quiz and still ended up with an A. There's a lot of homework assignments but they're graded lightly. Lab assignments were annoying but pretty easy usually, don't miss discussions because that and labs are a good portion of the grade. He's a nice professor though, and the ones I did go to were entertaining
Lectures were so much fun and very entertaining. The hours goes by really fast and he helps to understand material gone over in textbook. Love this professor!

A surprisingly difficult class, given that it was an intro course. Spends a lot of time on topics that are maybe above the paygrade of a new astrophysics student, and there is a LOT of content you'll need to have memorized. Might be best to take the class for fun as an upperclassman, rather than at the start of an astrophysics degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Interesting class.

Thought this was going to be a blowoff, but it proved that it requires some work. Exams were online and we could use pretty much all resources, but if they were in person I would've been in trouble. My GSI made sure labs were an easy 100

He goes through topics a bit too fast during lecture, but he is very clear. He tries his best to help with questions and makes the material quite easy to understand. As someone that struggled heavily with physics during high school, he made learning the basics to astrophysics easy for me. Make sure to study the slides!

Go through lecture slides too quickly to make everything clear. There are too many topics to cover for this course. He is good at answering questions by the way. He tried to help students, but he is just too busy. The reading quizzes are just boring. He spent a lot of time in class deriving equations that you may never use. But GOOD prof overall.

Clearly tries really hard to be relatable to the class and make sure everyone gets good grades. Explains things really well and has helpful slides that he posts after class. Overall, I really liked him as a prof and wished he had taught the whole class instead of just half!
Ver

Boring lecturer. Goes through lecture slides rapidly. Tries to cover too many topics within the semester. Doesn't narrow down the topics you'll need to know for the test. Literally, gave us 155 topics to study for the final. Might as well study an encyclopedia.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Meg is so sweet and supportive, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. The class includes three essays, a final presentation, and regular annotation assignments but they were all very manageable. She grades generously and gives helpful feedback—you will have the best time if you take 125 with her!
Great! It is a little more work-heavy than other courses. She actually cares about her students and is very understanding of issues and grants extensions for coursework if needed.
Meg is AMAZING! 10/10. Every day was fun, educational, and a treat. She is so kind and obviously loves her job. You need to take this class!

Meg is a super welcoming professor who truly knows her stuff. She is so engaging and actually cares about her students' individual development. Homework is pretty light, and the essays are very manageable if done as instructed. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is genuinely one of the nicest professors I have ever had in the world. She isn't as harsh as a grader as she may seen and there's lowkey a lot of busy work. But, she made me a better writer and it is an easy class to get a good grade in!

Meg's awesome, although I'll admit it took more effort on my essays than I thought to get an A. If you want a free A, you should look at different classes or professors, but if you can match her energy and actually want to learn to write better, this is a great class and it's not TOO difficult. Gonna miss Meg a lot but I won't miss the work.

Oh my soul, Meg was absolutely wonderful. I loved her class and it came as such a comfort during my first semester. Meg has wonderful insight on how to develop critical reading and writing. I felt like every article we read was purposeful in what it taught us to better our craft. I also enjoyed getting to choose our own topics for each essay.

I loved having Meg for English 125, highly recommend. She genuinely cares for her students and encourages collaboration. She takes time to get to know you and be a guide for her course. By far my favorite professor I have had.
Brings incredible energy and enthusiasm to every class. Super fair grader if you put in the effort. Meg is the goat

I took two classes with Prof. Garver and learned so much from both. Her classes tend to be small (around 20 students) and each class is hands on and engaging. Prof. Garver gives good feedback and isn't as harsh a grader as she claims. She is so kind and energetic!

This was my favorite class of freshman year! The instructor is incredibly nice, caring, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. Classes are always fun and interactive. There is a lot of busy work, but it ends up being helpful in the end. She's flexible and offers extensions for major assignments.

I loved her class! There is kind of a lot of busy work but it is easy to accomplish. She claims she is a harsh grader but I did not really see that. She also gives extensions on major assignments if you ask. She is a great teacher!
She was honestly the most caring and inviting professor that I had during my first year. Very flexible and accommodating. She wants you to succeed.
Pushed me, in the best way.
Meg is nice and a great person but I wouldn't wish the workload on anyone. This class added too much stress to my schedule.
She was amazing! She did a great job explaining everything, and was super understanding!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Madame Gjata is the best French instructor I've had my entire life. This class is not easy, but she was always very helpful when you came to her with questions. She also really cares about her students and their success. If you have the opportunity to take 231 with her PICK HER, she is the best 231 teacher.
Awesome French professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was a lot of work but she really cared about student success. She also cared a lot about class participation and growth throughout the semester.

Dr. Gjata is an amazing professor! Her grading is fair, her explanations are clear, she gives helpful feedback on assignments, and she creates such a supportive and welcoming environment. The French 231 is challenging, but she makes it interesting and enjoyable. I learned so much and feel much more confident in my French. Highly recommended.

Prof. Gjata was incredibly caring and truly wanted all of her students to succeed. French at Michigan is generally very demanding, expect 1-2 hours of homework daily in addition to recitation. The material can be a lot, but the assignments were not graded too harshly, and Prof. Gjata gives great feedback.

Madame Gjata cared a lot about participation, but she emphasized that students don't need to be afraid to mess up and would give nonjudgemental and very helpful feedback. I would definitely recommend taking her for French, as she cares a lot about creating a classroom environment that everyone is comforting speaking French in.
Madame Gjata is super sweet and she cares deeply about every student. She wants whats best for everyone and her teaching is clear.

Madame Gjata was an amazing professor! Although her grading on participation was harsh at times, I believe that it more-so because of the French department's strict guidelines. As long as you complete the homework with effort and participate regularly in class, you'll be set up for success.

Took French 101 (not 103) with Dr. Gjata. She is one of the best professors I have ever had. She cares about teaching so much and you can tell. I hope to have her again during my time taking French at umich.

Professor Gjata is the best professor I have ever had and she is very knowledgeable. I enjoyed being in her class every day. Dr. Gjata is an exceptional professor who made the class engaging. Lots of group work, but fun. Her passion for the French is contagious. Always there to support each student's success. I highly recommend Dr.Gjata to anyone.

Dr. Gjata is so kind and helpful. I took her class with French 101, not 103. The French department at umich assigns a lot of work, so be prepared to do a lot for your A. But, if you have the opportunity to take French with Dr. Gjata, take the opportunity.

I am horrible with languages, but Madame Gjata is one of the most caring and helpful professors I have ever had. Every language class at UMich is going to be challenging, but Madame Gjata always did everything she could to help make the class easier and going to her office hours was incredibly helpful as well
She is a great professor, and she is really caring. There was a lot of homework, but it was all very easy.
Professor Gjata is one of the most caring people I have ever met. She was always willing to help students understand the material, and she did a great job at making the class as easy as possible.

Probably good for the regular classes but do not take an elective where she makes the syllabus. Super disorganized. Way too much material, often couldn't find what she was looking for. Bounced from subject to subject in class, which made it difficult to engage. Impatient if not answered quickly or as expected. Stressful vibe.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gell was an amazing teacher, and after her class, I feel much more confident in writing and speaking German. There are daily assignments that take time, but she is lenient if you need extensions for anything. She always provided helpful feedback on assessments and took time to work with students who needed extra help for certain topics.

Professor Gell is very caring. She works hard to ensure that assignments are graded quickly with feedback. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the topics that her classes are themed around, so class always felt fun and informative. I would definitely take another one of her classes.
So amazing and caring. Incorporates culture into class too. Great professor

Wow I love German now. I never thought id be so greatful for the LSA language requirement but Frau Gell made German 101 an amazing experience and I seriously feel like I will continue to learn and love German.

I normally do not write reviews for professors, but I feel that it is necessary for Frau Gell. She is truly one of the best professors I have had at UofM. Super kind. Super funny. Extremely lenient and attentive towards any problems you may have. I have never cared to read a comic book before joining her class, and somehow she made it enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Frau Gell was an absolute gem to have for a German prof! She always kept lectures interesting and they felt more like a lively discussion than a lecture. Class was graded on homework assignments, quizzes, and essays, and she gives clear feedback that makes it easy to learn how to improve.

Make sure to check that her class counts for the ULWR if that's what you need. She was rather disorganized. The sudden changes to plans were kind of exhausting by the end. Bookwork is where the grammar learning happened.

prof gell can be kinda disorganised sometimes, but in a good way- sometimes class just becomes a cool discussion in German so we get carried away! she's very chill and understanding and will give you extensions on hw if you need them. she makes German fun and tells really hilarious stories. overall I recommend!
Nothing short of an amazing lecturer. If you're lucky enough to get her for any German course, you're in for an amazing semester!

You get what you put in. She is a good teacher and facilitates your learning well. You can BS a lot of stuff, but I wouldn't recommend it. She cares about her class, and students respond to that. Her plans for a given lesson can sway considerably, for this reason the course sometimes feels a bit aimless. The real lessons are in the assignments.

Frau Gell is amazing. She is always willing to meet outside of class and wants students to learn as much as possible. She is hilirous and a great teacher.   She is not strict on due dates for assignments. In 300 we covered a lot of material but was great to help understand German grammer. This class is an easy A as long as you learn the grammer.

I am so glad I had her as my first german teacher, because she made me love the language and want to continue it! She's one of the best teachers I've ever had and effortlessly made such heavy content seem so easy. She made everything about class fun and even brought the whole class together. Take her class!
Peace, Love, Frau Gell

Frau Gell is a wonderful teacher! She is extremely supportive and super relaxed. She is very lenient on assignments and throughout in her comments! The class itself is wonderful even taking it as a freshmen first semester! Participation is mandatory as it is a 300 level class; however, Gell does not push anyone to speak if they do not want to!

One of those teachers so great they come your friend. Phenomenal instructor, great mentor, and kind person. She gives excellent feedback and is very engaging. Her presence alone inherently motivates others to seriously learn the language and have fun while doing it.

I took her German course on film in the summer and it was amazing. It had great movies and discussions and the class was geared towards our ability not expectations. She's also really nice and it's hard to not like her. But literally show up, know the few words a week and you pass with an A. I got over 100% final grade
She is the best language teacher I've ever had, through middle school, high school and college. She makes it fun and easy to learn, something that seems difficult to most language teachers.
I love Mary Gell. She is one of my favorite professors at U of M. I wish she had been teaching 102 when I took it. Amazing, helpful, and worldly.
Frau Gell is a saint.  She let me turn in work probably 2 weeks late and still gave me full credit.  She is the most understanding, fun professor I've ever had!!

I have taken many courses with Frau Gell (German 300, 326, 306). I always got an A and had an awesome time! The homework is easy and she's an easy grader.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but you've got to go to most of the classes. She's super nice easy to talk to. If you're looking for a challenge -- Look elsewhere! She usually uploads PDFs of books.

Mary Gell is an angel; I almost didn't take German and am so glad I did.  She makes things so clear, is always available for extra help, and understands that students have lives outside of class.  She's honestly the best.
Mary is great. She's fun, nice, and super easy to talk to. I will definitely try to take a class taught by her again.

Mary is kind, friendly, funny, and she is really willing to help you do well in class. I think that she is a better lecturer rather than a discussion leader. Everything is straightforward. Not light readings, but mild works. This is a class where you can easily see the payback of your effort.

Excellent professor. My class was 7-9 at night (which sucked), but she made it worth it. Very funny and willing to help. The class was easy to do well in as she is an easy grader and the assignments aren't too hard.
Mary is a great teacher! She is very helpful and her class is very easy but you still learn a lot. Online vocab quizzes, grammar quizzes, and weekly 200 word essays are all very manageable.

Mary is amazing. Wonderful professor. Very chill. Very understanding if you turn in homework late. She is great about explaining and clarifying if something is too difficult to understand in German. I would totally take her classes again.
she's freaking amazing. she's funny and so nice and full of energy.  but not cheesy. you'll really enjoy going to her classes.
Best Professor ever!
Katie is TOP 1 professor at UMich. She is super chill and flexible regarding deadlines and other commitments. Take her English 125 class if you want the freedom to write about anything you want!
