She was incredibly enthusiastic and passionate about the subject which made the course really enjoyable. She went a little fast sometimes but overall the tests were easy and it was an overall good course. Would recommend!

She is such a wonderful professor! She's the kind of professor who makes you want to go to class, and who truly cares about her students. Very PPT oriented, but she shows LOTS of videos, too! She really does give you all the tools you need to succeed in the class. I highly recommend both this class and this professor.

Fantastic professor. Very enthusiastic and makes you LOVE the subject (mostly a class about life). Wants the best for her students, exams are easy, only two papers the whole semester. Recommend to anyone!
Such a great professor! Enthusiastic an easy to follow. She gives you all the materials you need to be successful.

Kovelman is a great professor! The class is really easy: the exams are only based off of her slides which she posts online before every class, so technically you'd never even need to go to lecture, but I always WANTED to go to lectures because she's so funny and shows cute movie clips. Very enjoyable and easy class.

Kovelman is a good teacher and loves Dev lang. She is very power point oriented, but breaks it up with video clips. Sometimes she just has too many slides and at times contradict other slides. The class is pretty easy, there are no exams however the quizes are worth 20% of your grade.
Henry told us to write him reviews... but yk what he's acc the goat and deserves 5 stars... Take him if you want an A and want to listen to cool stuff twice a week
Great professor, very friendly, funny, and easy going. I really enjoyed the lectures and he always made class light hearted and interesting.
His lectures are engaging and split into three sections, which the lecture quizzes are based on.
Very funny professor and enjoyable class I highly recommend

Unfortunately, I found the lectures tedious & unnecessary for success in other parts of the course. Clearly a cool guy & knowledgeable, but the lecture style was mind-numbing & the quizzes were asinine. However, the discussion section & assignments were interesting & I enjoyed them.
Henry is really really great! I've taken both his minds and brains class as well as his addictions class. He is really phenomenal please please please take his class!

This guy is great. His classes are very interesting, and he is a great person to chat with in office hours. It's clear that he genuinely cares about his students and his teaching philosophy is very purely academic, with a strong emphasis on learning for it's own sake. Always a joy to go to his class, and I'm excited to take him again!

This class was so easy and Dr. Cowles' lectures were super interesting. There were 2 readings/week that were probably around 40ish pages total. 3 papers, the longest of which is 1500 words. Once a week we did collaborations in lecture, and I really enjoyed these- these mostly involved designing a product or an ad related to our topic for the week.

I've never wanted to listen to hour long lectures until having Cowles. He is so knowledgeable and engaging with how he delivers his content, and it is always very in depth in that he covers social, economic, historical, and modern information to provide a very holistic education on each subject. I could go on and on about how amazing Cowles is.

Prof Cowles is a cool guy, obviously very knowledgeable. Lectures could be a little boring but definitely could be worse. The papers and going to section are what really matter so ask your gsi for help when writing and you should do okay. Get the lecture attendance points as well. Overall, pretty easy class with a light workload and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: HIGHLY RECOMMEND, lectures are engaging and interesting. They all feel like an amazing TedTalk. Cowles encourages you to interact with the material and make connections, you feel like you are really learning and not just going for the points. I looked forward to lecture each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool dude
Super engaging lectures. Makes himself available to workshop essay drafts with students. Would highly recommend.

Professor Cowles is extremely knowledgable and gave some of the most engaging lectures I ever heard. He is very smart and funny, and I would definitely recommend taking this class if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely would recommend to anyone. Insightful lectures, very passionate, very clear, very responsive.

Best prof I've ever had at Michigan. Very aware of what students want to learn and makes lectures so captivating. Readings are very well chosen and you'll actually want to read them (+ they're not long). Wish I could take this class with him again!!
Cowles is a really great professor. Makes class super engaging and entertaining. Wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best class I have taken. HIST265 was so captivating and Prof Cowles made the material very accessible- always uploaded recordings of lectures along with slides. 3 papers and 2 small easy weekly quizzes based on lecture content. Point-based class. Talk to him about your paper outline before you write it!!! He gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cowles is INCREDIBLE! The workload is manageable and he continuously got students' feedback in order to improve the course

I would agree with the last comment and most comments already on here. I want to note tho that sometimes I dose off when he lectures and he can sometimes go in circles. Other than that I would highly recommend!

HIST265 was the best class I have ever taken at Michigan.  he is so interesting and is so passionate about everything he teaches. He is very cognizant of what students need and want and has made numerous changes to grading policies because students have asked/ to make things easier. discussion is not super hard, just participate and do the work.

Professor Cowles is a good professor. Works are reasonable. If you put in the efforts, you will get an A. Both the professor and his GSIs are very understanding and accommodating. Would recommend his class.

Dr. Cowles is respectful, smart, and does a great job with this whole class. Yes attendance is mandatory, but you will want to go to class. The material is interesting, and he does a great job listening to students feedback and changing things if necessary. The GSI was also great. Highly recommend him as a professor and this class!

Prof Cowles is great! He made the most engaging recorded lectures I've encountered since the pandemic started. He's clearly very passionate and knowledgable. He asked for (anonymous) student feedback multiple times throughout the semester and actually made changes to the course to reflect it. He's quirky and makes dad jokes, but that's a good thing

I really loved this class. The lectures were really interesting and he would make adjustments to them if people asked him to. He's pretty funny and him and the GSIs made the class really interesting. They graded through participation and 3 essays so you have to make sure you put in the work to get an A but its not meant to be your hardest class.

quirky guy and the lectures are very abstract, but the class is easy enough! small group collaborations each week with other students on zoom. cowles is strange, but cares for his students and makes it pretty straight forward. Wouldn't say this is a typical psych class though if that is what you are used to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: American Addictions was one of the best classes I took at U of M

TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE!! Professor Cowles is outstanding and there wasn't a minute of lecture where I was bored or hanging onto every word. He is very insightful, funny, and the class is very clear and interesting. Also, shoutout to my GSI Alex, if you can, get him as your GSI, he is seriously the best.
Wonderful human inside and out

Dr. Cowles was honestly one of the best professors I've had at UofM. He's extremely knowledgable, passionate, and engaging in his lectures and structures his course in a way that makes you eager to learn. Especially during the transition to remote classes during the COVID-19 crisis, Dr. Cowles was SUPER understanding, helpful, and prepared. A+ Prof
Professor Cowles is actually the best. He was such an engaging lecturer -- very organized, clear, and funny. Everyone should take this class at some point.

Professor Cowles is hands down the best professor I've had thus far. His lectures are easy to follow, he's pretty funny and relatable to young people, and it's not difficult at ALL to get a great grade in the class. Although there are weekly writing assignments (about 1 page double spaced), they're pretty much graded on completion and interesting.
What a guy. Lectures passionately and knows his stuff. Take good notes during lecture and study them and you're chillin.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: American Addictions was a really cool class. Cowles is the most adorable lecturer and he really cares about his students. The class is also very light in terms of workload so you can take it if youre taking it with other difficult classes

The class was super interesting, it has been one of my favorite classes to take at Michigan! You need to do the readings to be able to participate in discussion and help your group with the weekly op-eds, but the readings are very interesting and you don't have to read very far in depth (skimming is okay, even encouraged). Grading isn't tough

Professor Cowles is amazing. He truly cares about his students and his lectures are fascinating. He does lecture with little words on the slides, so it's important to listen, but he really is very knowledgeable. Would 100% take this class again!
Henry is great. He is very knowledgable about the topics discussed and his lectures are really interesting. The workload is very light and attendance is not mandatory for lectures.
Great professor. He really cares about his students and I feel like I learned a lot. His lectures are really interesting so you should show up. Also super cute and kinda jacked hmu Henry

He's a walking philosophical textbook. It is as if I selected all of the text in John Stuart Mill's "On Liberty" and had Siri read it to me. You won't understand what he says, nevertheless the readings that are assigned. Take at your own risk.

He's super nice and funny in lecture, you can really tell he loves teaching this subject. His lectures are organized well, but he doesn't really put words on the slides, so notes definitely need to be taken throughout lecture, because the powerpoints will tell you nothing. Would take again, he was amazing!

Cowles is one of the kindest and most fascinating people I have ever met. He truly cares about you as a human being and going to his office hours really helps if you are confused by the material because its done on a 1 on 1 basis. Theres probably like 2 words on each lec powerpoint so your notes come from listening and writing down stuff he says
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cowles is manages his time and organizes the material well. He talks fast and has little written on his slides which can be frustrating but hes knowledgable enthusiastic & funny. Theres a lot of reading & a short response due every week but its fairly manageable. U can miss key stuff when u miss class tho:/ He cares about u doing well & is nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: very nice person---really messy structure, unreasonably hard quizzes every class. Exam is 60% of the grade which is completely ridiculous for a one credit course (earth104). I always went to lecture and still didn't learn anything, because the questions were a memorization game of arbitrary facts and not about understanding content.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very understanding about deadlines and absences. I enjoyed the class but lectures can be boring. No work outside of class, straight forward tests, definitely an easy natural science credit.

Although the grading is relatively easy, this is probably the worst experience I've had taking a class at this school. At least 4 assignments weekly, and deadlines are inconsistent and hardly communicated.

Hendy is a fine teacher, she's very passionate about science but her lectures can be extremely dull. Content was interesting, and we did have some out-of-classroom activities which were nice. Her in class work assignments weren't hard. Her tests were easy and were all questions seen before. Extremely easy natural science credit.

This is the worst class I've ever taken. If you ask questions, GSI's will tell you different answers than Hendy. Hendy will answer questions, but in a condescending manner. Assignments guidelines and deadlines change all the time, if they are given at all. Discussion might as well be a separate class than lecture. since

Professor Ingrid likes to use documentaries in EARTH 333. Part of class time is lecture, and the other half is watching docus about the ocean. Some days there are no videos. Discussion section for the class is just meeting with one of the GSIs (who are really awesome!) and you work on the term paper. Tests are diagrams and questions from homework.

Professor Hendy just loves science and teaching. She cares for her students and actually makes boring topics like ice seem very interesting. In-class activities after every lecture, which will either be easy or heinous, and no in-between. Overall, it's an easy class to get a natural science credit, with a midterm and online final.
Not the most exciting lecturer, but the class is easy overall, and a good natural science credit. No homework at all other than studying for exams.

Took this over summer term, kind of dry and I don't feel like I learned that much about the oceans. A lot of it was VERY QR based and took the fun out of learning about marine/ocean life. Class isn't mandatory but you WILL need help to be guided through the incredible amount of busy work that there is. Hendy is nice but I wouldn't do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you're interested in oceanography this course provides a lot of information and you can learn a lot. But lectures aren't incredibly helpful and mostly rely on slides. If you really want to learn, it's in your own hands. There are a couple group projects and they're graded hard. Exams are graded very hard, but otherwise not a hard class.
Class is super easy, but very dry

The lectures are lectures but they're interesting if you care about the topic. Prof Hendy is kind of a quiet talker so make sure you're listening but she really knows her stuff. If you go to class and put in an average amount of studying you should be fine.

Her lectures are extremely boring and hard to follow. Whenever she teaches, it just looks like she's in her own little world talking to herself at the front of the room. Even when she uses a microphone, no one can understand her because she mumbles and has an accent. Easy exams with everything straight from the powerpoint, so it is an easy class.

Going into the class, I thought it would be an interesting class. She is very boring during lectures and she will grade your tests as she pleases. It's about 10 lectures per midterm. Memorize everything on the powerpoint and you should be able to get a B/B+.

Pretty easy class as long as you show up most of the time. She puts lectures online so you can follow in class, which is nice because she sometimes is confusing. She word for word gives you the exam essay prompt(s) and the essays are a good chunk of the exam. Overall she's not an outstanding teacher, but the class is easy. P.S. don't take the lab.

I took this class as an easy natural science, but it ended up being extremely confusing and difficult.  The exams required you to memorize dozens of random diagrams and graphs and were way too difficult for an intro course.  Also, it was almost impossible to understand her or to read her handwriting.  If you need natural science,take something else

She's a really nice person but not a good lecturer.  The class is pretty easy, but Professor Hendy mumbles and just generally doesn't make sense.  Still worth it if you have to take it for your NS/QR requirement.

The class was easy, little work and the content was easy. She is rather hard to understand and follow. I found the course to be very interesting but her presentation of it was a bit dry. If you have intrest in the topic, it's a great class. If you don't have intrest in the topic, avoid it.

Ingrid is a bit difficult to understand at some times, but overall interesting class. A lot of different topics covered but not too in depth. If you go to class and pay attention, you will get a good grade. She grades on a huge curve.
She is plain bad. Can't understand what she is saying. It seems she is unsure of the material herself. Keeps forwarding and rewinding the video clips. Avoid her.
This class has little to no work, but the final was NOTHING like the review. Parts matched up, but the questions were may more in depth than she ever taught. Few people got As. Mostly got Bs

Very interesting class.  I learned a lot.  She was a little spacey at times.  You can tell she loves coral reefs.  The final questions came right from the quizzes and she tells you exactly what you need to know.  An easy class and very interesting.
The final was HORRIBLE! nothing like the exam review sheet. If you don't need to take it don't

had her for mini course coral reefs. I loved it! she was super nice and her lectures basically told you exactly what was going to be on the final! She also gave mini quizzes that ended up giving away answers to questions on the final. If you need an easy credit and want to learn about the ocean definitely take this course!
Great proffessor. Very, very nice and very helpful.  Class counts as a QR2, and couldn't get any easier. Take this class!

Class should have been easy and interesting, but definitely wasn't.  Had to teach myself much of the material & tests were harder than expected, but curved. Optional final (open book). She's very hard to understand during lectures
Physics has never been easy for me but he genuinely was more than willing to help me understand small concepts whether during studio or in office hours. Highly recommend.

I didn't have this professor for studio but he is an extremely great teacher. I would always to his office hours for extra help on module and mock exam problems and his explanations are always direct and clear. Even people who have no basis in physics like me can understand immediately.

Dr. Chahrour was my physics studio lecturer and he was fantastic. Explains material very clearly and is visibly passionate about the field. His office hours were even better. He often had a large group but always made sure every question was answered. His instructional method is great, very socratic, makes students really engage with material

Dr. Charour was honestly a pretty great professor/studio lecturer. He explained things in a way that actually made sense. Honestly, he should've been the main lecturer for Physics 150 imo. He really knew the material, was passionate about it, and cared about making sure we understood and did well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved having him for the studio, but his office hours were even better! Really great at explaining things and makes sure that each student has an equal opportunity to ask questions.
I had him for studio but he was amazing at explaining things in office hours. Take his studio section if you can!!
By submitting everything on time and giving a decent amount of effort, it's very possible to get a B or higher. Class accomplishes multiple distributions and upper-level writing at once.

This professor was genuinely one of the best I've had. he was extremely approachable, funny, easy to talk to, and always willing to help. Office hours were helpful, emails were answered quickly, and they truly cared about student success. The class was clear, fair, and enjoyable. Highly recommend!

Ahmad is a very fast responder, even outside of class. He makes class feel really lively and really helps the atmosphere feel fun. He also clearly conveys all the information about the material. I would definitely take a class with him again!

Super nice and understanding!! Also very interesting and funny in class lol 
Prepares presentations that go over content taught in lectures which is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very personable guy who communicates the material well. Has an interesting demeanor and very accessible.

Ahmad is the best GSI I've ever had. He's funny and brings a vibrant atmosphere every class period. He helps us understand the content as well. That fact that the class would rather listen to him lecture than watch a video when given the option once attests to how wonderful he makes this class be. He's young so he's able to relate to his students

she's nice but not a great lecturer. pretty easy A but heard she was a rough grader on other people. she also has no clear guidelines or instructions for many assignments as well as quizzes. no practice problems and review slides are eh. class was not very interesting so only take if you need it as a req.

Professor Ivanova is not the best lecturer; however, she is very passionate about the field of biophysics and it shows. Her lectures may seem long or boring, but I feel as though the times I learned something new made up for it. It is very doable to earn an A in this course if you follow her instructions as I believe she is fair with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ivanona is an terrible teacher, her lectures are so boring and there is no flow to the class. Her lectures also don't correlate to the course topic itself most of the time and we tend to veer off in so many unnecessary directions. Her grading makes no sense and it is always unclear what she expects. For a 100 level course, it is challenging.
I took BIOPHYS 370 with her and it was not good. The exams were so much harder than the other content and she read off of the lectures.

Took biophys370. This prof uses filler words like um so frequently lectures are hard to watch. Slides are terrible. We get like 10-15 practice questions per exam and she doesn't bother to give any answers. Tells us to use AI to help ourselves. Like you cannot be serious. Don't even bother asking for a mock exam.

It pains me to write this because Dr. Ivanova is such a kind person however her lectures are horrid. I fear she doesn't know how to explain things at a basic level and I am left too confused to know how to ask a question.

Disorganized lectures, HW that was difficult to do (especially with no help from the prof), and way too much R coding for a supposed "no coding experience necessary" class. She is a nice person, but this class was an absolute waste of time. Take something else if you can.

Do not take this class unless you have R coding knowledge. She says that this is not a coding class, but many of the assignments were coding. She was not helpful when answering questions either. The lectures were very disorganized and assignments were difficult.

Magda's a nice person who is clearly passionate about amyloid research. Unfortunately, her lectures are disorganized and quizzes are difficult. On a given day, there's only a 30% chance that she actually recorded the lecture and posted the slides. The class isn't demanding, but it can be stressful when assignments are due.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: yo shoutout kali tho she cool man
They were the worst instructor I have ever had, I cannot wait for this semester to finally end so I can regain my sanity and get a break from hearing those babble "lectures."
Avoid plss
The worst.
The combination of Kali and Dennis Simiyu made for one of the least enjoyable classes imaginable.
just not great
Worst lecturer ever!!!! Worst class I've taken yet!!! Enough of Kali Israel!!!! Worst teacher ar Michigan
The worst professor at UMich? No. I believe that is Chris Proulx, but she is close. Or they. Not sure.

I will always remember this class, but for the wrong reasons. The insane ramblings each class were to be expected, but sometimes they came with a child-like outburst towards someone unfortunately seated in her/their midst. Kali couldn't teach, simply put. At least she was easy to trick into grading highly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As soon as the add/drop deadline passed and I was still in Kali's class, I knew I was screwed. When she rambles, hold on tight; you are in for a long ride. Would not wish this class on my worst enemy.

She has no teaching skills whatsoever. The highlight of this class is the outbursts she has, where she is nearly brought to tears with rage over people seemingly not paying attention to her endless yapping. There is a LOT of comedic subject material just looking at her trying to convey any information about a topic.
What an absolute nightmare of a human being Kali is. Her teaching style is almost as wretched as her wardrobe.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Should not be teaching at this level. If she cared about students she should resign
How she teaches at the University of Michigan is something I will never figure out. I am pretty sure she reviews herself to balance her rating. SHOCKING, DO NOT TAKE

This class was a mess and left learning nothing. There is no way of seeing your grade until it is put into the grade book after the semester. Missed class? Late? Get ready for her to make snide comments about you to her students. Unprofessional but a very easy A.
The worst professor at UMich, closely edging Chris Proulx for that position.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst prof i have ever had. Awful

I truly believe that this professor is the worst in every sense of the word. Firstly, she does not use lecture slides, and all the lectures consist of her talking, but this professor does not have the skills to teach a class this way. Assignments are unclear, exams too, and she expects participation when she talks all lecture. MSU level teaching

This class was extremely easy. There were only two assignments: a final project and a final reflection. Attendance was mandatory and participation was key. That being said, the criteria for grading was not very specific but as long as you put some effort in you were fine. If you're looking for an interesting topic but an easy class this is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was so confusing for no reason. You get practically no guidance or proper rubrics for any assignment. You are expected to “participate” in her lectures, yet there's no opportunity to ever contribute but a brief moment where she stops fumbling over her words. That moment will be taken by one of the same two teacher's pets. Terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared for yap like you've never experienced: this class is so boring. She is extremely unclear on assignments and has few communication skills. Her slideshows (if she even bothers) are lame, and she never engages with the class. AVOID.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. Besides the fact that you pointlessly talk about "walking" for 3 hours and terrible time management, there are no clear instructions for assignments. Then there's zero feedback to know if you're doing it correctly, just some arbitrary grade she slaps on at the end with no explanation (even if you reach out to her).

Please don't take this class. I didn't read the reviews here and I took this class, she is so bad. She speaks non stop for 1.5 hours and I feel like I am witnessing verbal diarrhea. She doesn't use any slides or diagrams and just spits out useless facts that have no connection with each other or any aspect of British history.

Prof Israel is the most out of touch professor I've ever had. She has no concept of how students interact with her lectures and doesn't care if they understood them. Her lectures consist of a 1.5hr stream of consciousness where she continuously rattles off facts non-stop with maybe one 30sec break for questions. Avoid Prof Israel at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgable about British history. Decent amount of readingtypical of a history class. Lectures were important. Rarely used slides, mostly for pictures. She did not post slides or lectures online and the lectures contained different, yet complementary info to readings. Grades mainly based on attendance/participation and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Israel clearly knows what she's talking about but as a student, you are supposed to write papers on what she says combined with fictional readings - which is hardly history. I was commonly frustrated with Israel's bias and how we saw zero reliable sources for her statements in this class. If you care about history, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I decided to become a History major because of Dr. Israel. You can tell that she is prepared for lectures, knows the material well, and wants to make sure you know the whole history. Lectures can sometimes be dense with new information, which makes attendance a must in her class, but it is incredibly worth it if you're willing to put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kali Israel is amazing. She's lecture heavy, but keeps it pretty interesting save a few bad days when she acknowledges its just stuff she needs to include. If the British history class seems like something you'd be into, TAKE IT. If you hate wars or history, steer clear. She's really accessible and will even read your papers and help before its due
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Here's all you need to know. You need to be a good writer to take this class. You don't have to actually read the books but you have to come to class and take notes. She rambles on but the material is interesting only if you're into history. She is weird at grading but if you work hard on papers you could pull an A- / B+. Not a blow off
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's a lot of reading entailed with Professor Israel but I've never had a more passionate and informed professor. Extremely captivating lectures and interesting readings make the papers not too bad to write

I've taken a few classes with Professor Israel and I can't recommend her enough. A really smart and inspirational professor. She grades fairly and you can tell she's extremely passionate about the material. She also selects great books, too!

Use of powerpoint is on the low side and lectures can be a little on the boring side sometimes, but she's definitely knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches and is very helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Israel lectures without any visual aid nearly every class. Extremely hard to stay awake sometimes. Assigns a lot of books that you need to cite in depth on essays, but I got away with finding quotes to cite online. She does keep track of attendance, so you do need to attend. She is very passionate and knowledgeable  about the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: All lecture but if you zone out for a second you're in a different decade. She obviously knows a lot of material but drones on and on. So hard to not to fall asleep. Biggest issue with this class was my GSI at the time. Really socially awkward and unknowledgeable. Even if lectures are interesting, the grades come from her so she ruined it for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Israel is incredibly knowledgeable. However, her political viewpoints are clear and you would be hard pressed to write any paper that didn't reflect those viewpoints. Also, the assigned reading, while interesting, conforms to the professor's politics. This made the class seem a bit too one-dimensional.

Scottish History. Professor Israel is amazing at constructing a historical narrative. Her classes were so worthwhile because of this. A lot of the information given in class was never used, but the themes were incredibly important. A lot of reading, but all phenomenal reading. I have three new favorite books. She is a must-take for history majors.

The professor was very insightful when you talk to her in office hours. Her lectures can be pretty boring because she has no powerpoint to follow what she is saying. Make sure you read the novels in depth to do well on the papers. If you are not very interested in British history, you probably should look for another class.

I really enjoyed taking British history with Professor Israel. The class was heavy on the social aspect of history and you'll learn a lot about the plight of the working class. Paper guidelines were fair and allowed students to think critically. Overall, not an extremely demanding class but it wasn't an easy A either. Be prepared to read!

Scottish history. The class met once a week for three hours, which was a lot of history at once but not too bad. There's a ton of reading though... one week she assigned two 300+ page books and only discussed them briefly. Other than reading, a pretty easy and interesting class. Three short papers... just be sure to take her side when writing them.

British History Through Film and Autobiography; very easy class (I'm an engineer and needed a 300-level humanities course), I got by on reading only 3 or 4 of the 11 books (like most of the students).  Only 3 essays in total with no other assignments, and Professor Israel is happy to review and correct them before you submit.

Modern Scottish History. Interesting when not talking about religion or politics. Amount of reading grew annoying quickly, though I'm an engineer. Easy grading, but more short papers than the syllabus lets on.

Her readings, though extensive at times, are at least captivating if extremely depressing, and attendance in lecture is mandatory which is annoying but can make getting good grade easier due to participation grade. Interesting perspective but heavy on social history esp. working class and youth during WWI.

It was supposed to be English and History, but we never discussed the books in a literary sense at all. Her lectures consist of her talking for 1.5 hours without slides or any kind of discussion. She assigns excessive amounts of reading, that were then never discussed in class.

Professor Israel is an amazing professor. She is captivating and extremely knowledgeable. I look forward to every lecture. She delivers her lectures with a passion and a drive that lacks with many other professors. I always felt like there was a point to being in class. I looked forward to every lecture to learn more and learn with more interest.
Average professor, fairly undemanding/easy course. Lecture was very boring but attendance was always taken. I needed it for R/E and it was okay. Not too difficult but not a fun class.

Professor Israel is by far my favorite professor at U of M.  Her lectures allow you to really get a sense of feelings, and opinions of the people during the time period.  She made British History seem exciting.  The class is based off of essays, and attendance, so it's not too difficult to get a good grade.

She made British history seem really personal.  Definitely focused on the human face of history and the social context.  Clearly a knowledgeable professor.  Her class is essay based, so if that is your strong side, it should be fairly easy to get a good grade.

I loved her!  She covered TONS of information and made it sound like nothing, made everything very easily digestible, and she was never boring.  The readings are interesting and you will need to at least skim them for papers, otherwise not totally necessary.  Really, going to this class was just a treat.  Take her, you'll love it!
I had her last semester after randomly switching in. I actually really enjoyed her class ad learned a lot. Definitely would take it again.

Professor Israel has a remarkable way of covering a vast amount of information, while still infusing nuance and detail into her lectures. Her integration of the poetry, reflections and art of historical subjects gives texture and warmth to her portrait of such a broad, complicated and violent time period and place as WWI and WWII Britain.

Very Interesting class, she can be a tough grader. My advice is to change everything that she marks you down for in the first paper on the next two papers, even if you thing she is wrong. A lot of reading but know exams only three papers and two map quizzes.

Very good lecturer. Inclined to social history but that seems true of the whole department. Lot of readings, some great, some not so great. Papers were not easy and required mainly thought and writing skill more than research. You will learn a lot and improve your writing.If you want a throwaway course and an easy A, look elsewhere.
Best professor I've had at UM. Incredibly knowledgeable, genuine, helpful, and enthusiastic. Lectures are detailed and moving, material is fantastic. Overall fantastic epxerience

I absolutely love Professor Israel. She is a wonderful teacher, VERY knowledgeable! Her lectures are detailed and you will take a lot of notes, but you will learn!  She does not believe in tests, so you will be writing a few essays for this class. If you enjoy history, Prof Israel is a great choice. I'd take her 100 times if I could.
Horrible, horrible, horrible teacher. Rude and nasty to students. Taught us nothing of any value the entire semester and left us frustrated and disillusioned.
LOTS of reading.. But enjoyable! Class is Wednesdays 1-4, but we usually got out pretty early. Prof Israel is very passionate about what she does!!! Take this class!!!
This class has a TON of reading, but it's really interesting. Prof. Israel is way knowlegeable and a cool person to talk to. Definitely recommended if you have any interest in Scotland!!
Worst professor ever. Unbelievably narrow-minded, won't even listen to anyone who doesn't agree with her completely, boring lectures, just generally an unpleasant person.
took her first year seminar on scotland and it rocked
prof. Israel is the worst professor I've ever had.  She picks on students for personal reasons and is completely boring and incompehensible.  Avoid her like the plague.

This is an interesting history class.  She knows a lot and can be informative but the lectures are VERY boring....hard to keep your eyes open.  The lectures are mandatory (take attendence) but it is a pretty easy class.  Easy A or B.
Way too longwinded, talks for so so long about generally nothing. Has her own viewpoint, and won't even think about other ones.

Poor professor.  Her lectures are scattered and repetitive.  She's very biased towards the sociological approach to history, as reflected in her approach to papers.  You could sell out to her style and get an A, but I would avoid this class.  There are many other fine history courses where you can get an A and actually learn.

she's got f***ing awesome taste in music but this is lecture is more boring than the average funeral.  i slept through every one and managed a B+. attendence is mandatory....for the lecture!  can you believe it? at the college level?  the discussion is a joke.

She's a very cool woman, smart and funny in her own way. The 90-minute lectures were pretty painful at times, though, and be advised that a lot is based on the (extensive) readings. Still, a good class, and a very good prof.

Very boring, disappointing and long. Since the whole  class was based on papers, I didn't know really what to write down in class. She gives a TON of reading in very short periods. She gives alot of random information and details for a survey class. I would rather take an exam then write papers
Lectures are long and talkative
Prof. Israel rocks and she's smarter than your usual English prof. and wiser that your usual History prof. She reads and lives more than you do, so listen up.
She is an awesome prof

Kali Israel is not a good professor; however, she went to Rutgers, and since I'm from New Jersey I will not be too hard on her. Don't take her for anything tho, she is an unfair grader, though I did well in her class :).

Would often go on tangents in lectures that would be confusing and/or above the class level. Does not believe in past exams or practice questions. Clearly very smart and too smart to be teaching this class. Lectures are often hard to follow and hard to take notes on
Rather difficult

Avoid this teacher at any and all cost. Obviously is extremely smart and knowledgeable but not good at explaining concepts. Exam questions have multiple parts tat depend on each other so a wrong answer on part A will lead to wrong answers on B, C, and D. I made one small adding error on part A of a question and ended up with an 87 as a result

He was terrible at explaining hard topics, and wasn't there for the entire first week of class or other various times throughout the semester making it pretty hard to figure out what is needed to know
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's a pretty terrible teacher, and seems too smart to be teaching the class. He will TRY to help you if you're confused but usually can't even understand what you're asking. The class is very hard and his lectures are very fast moving. Very focused on proofs instead of actually making sure people even know what's going on.

Very knowledgeable and passionate about math. Assigns hw with good intentions. Gives hints about problems to encourage thinking. OHs are fun and helpful especially when you are collaborating with other students. Lectures are sometimes confusing -- ask him questions when you are lost, he will explain. 285 is challenging but you learn more than 215.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He clearly knows a lot of math, but he has trouble teaching it. Teaches extremely fast, and teaches lots of material that you don't even need to know, so it's a gamble as to whether what random thing he's writing will show up on a test or homework. So, tip is to write down literally everything he writes on the board no matter what. GET STUDY GROUPS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I cannot express how lost and confused I felt taking this class. He went through topics in lecture so much faster than I could write anything down. All the material was completely abstract, and the exams looked like gibberish. This was the hardest class I've ever taken by a LANDSLIDE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable and smart and does prepare what to say in class. The huge problem with him is that he seems to focus on his presentation performance in every lecture. Whenever a student asked questions he hurried. This prof needs to change his attitude from being self-satisfying academic to listener to his students if he likes to be better.

285 with Prof Tobasco is hard. Lectures are fast-paced and proof-based. He goes beyond regular calc3 and talks about some concepts in mathematical analysis and measure theory. Exams are tough but you can do well if you truly understand the materials (or at least understand better than others do). His class is HARD but you learn a lot if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is quite challenging but not to an unreasonable degree. Also, tests are very hard but are graded fairly based on level of actual proficiency. Lectures are nearly all proof-based which is not helpful for the hw but gives an idea of what the tests will be like (but not directly related). Overall a great challenge and an alright professor.

Lectures are fast-paced and hard to understand. He assigns the hardest homework without building up first, and the class does anything but help you learn. I barely know more about calculus 3 now than when I first started - although khan academy has helped - and I'll probably forget it soon anyway. The class is pointless and he is an awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: A pretty terrible teacher, 0/10 would recommend. Throws in "challenging" problems on the exams that we have not learned before. Lectures are confusing and largely irrelevant. To this day I don't believe I have ever solved a differential equation. Do not let this man ruin your life.

They made this class really hard this semester. It was so hard for me to follow the material. You definitely need to filter out some of the things he says to figure out which ones matter for the homework, labs and exams. Otherwise, he's fine.
He's alright I think but the class is real hard
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Villa-Palomino is kind, smart, and makes every lecture worth showing up for. He genuinely looks out for your mental health. Take this class!
Absolutely fantastic professor! Class discussions were very helpful and consistently deepened my understanding of the material. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Julio Villa-Palomino!
Phenomenal professor! Dr. Villa-Palomino's lecture style created a welcoming environment and generated productive discussions. This class expanded my understanding of mental health and wellbeing.

Dr. Villa–Palomino is an amazing professor. His lectures and the discussions in class helped me engage with the material. Readings were meaningful (some a bit long). The grading was fair, and the assignments weren't too hard. I genuinely looked forward to coming to class!

Dr. Villa-Palomino's course on the anthropology of mental health was eye-opening and really challenged the way we think about mental health. Sweet and caring professor that made all of us feel seen and supported. One of the best professors I've had at Michigan. 10/10!

Dr. Villa-Palomino was a good professor, I was not a fan of the "discussant" presentations, where a student would teach the class about a reading; it felt repetitive to read something then come to class to have another student teach me about it. Grade consists of four papers, 3 smaller ones and a final, grading was not super clear. A good professor

Class is super light. Lecture is not interactive at all but professor is clearly passionate about the material. Everything you need for the exams (which, along with participation, is the entire grade) is discussed in your discussion sections. As long as you memorize the professors interpretations for the passages given, you'll easily get a 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is so light. Come to class because you have to, go to discussion and just memoroze the passages and it is so easy. It is literally not hard to get an A. You just memorize what they give you on the slides and it isn't hard to do so. Take if you want an easy humanities because it is worth it. Also, he makes some jokes so its fun.

Prof Ready is good, he's passionate so lecture is interesting. No HW, just tests and attendance (iClicker and disc). Tests are easy if you're not expecting an 100%. The rubric and his interpretations you have to write about are very specific, thats all. This means lots of minuscule point deductions add up.

if you are not interested in greek mythology, do not take this class. prof ready is rude and does not care about his students. The GSIs who grade your exams grade very harshly and you must put EXACTLY what HIS interpretation is, not yours. You essentially have to memorize his exact points (18 passages 7 sentences each) in order to get MAYBE an 85%.

Professor Ready has word-heavy slides and spends the whole time reading in a monotone voice. Additionally, his tests are based on passages from class and you must give his exact interpretation on the test or will be heavily marked off. He doesn't have office hours or seem to care much about his students. He never answers questions in class either.

Prof. Ready did a great job with this course. He is clearly passionate about the material and gives interesting lectures. This class will greatly broaden your understanding of classic Greek literature. Half of the grade is from attendance on iClicker, and the other half is from discussion/exams. Pay attention in lecture and you'll be prepared.
5 Test from the readings, everything on test is gone over before exam during discussion. Good professor and class.

Professor Ready is a great professor and Greek Myth is also a pretty easy and enjoyable class. Half the grade is attendance in lecture (done through IClicker) and discussion and the other half is from the 5 tests (non-cumulative). Tests are pretty easy and Ready goes over the entire readings in lecture.

This was by far one of my favorite classes and favorite professors at Michigan. Only had six problem sets and two tests, which were all graded on an upwards curve. Tests were very accurate to what we did in class and never too hard. Professor Osgood was always available and willing to help out when needed. Definitely take a class with him!

While the course and content itself was difficult for me, Professor Osgood made things very easy to comprehend. He is extra explanatory in lecture and makes sure to go over everything once, and even twice. Only graded on problem sets and exams, but both exams are not meant to trick you at all and closely reflect homework. Overall a great class!

Iain is a great lecturer. He simplifies game theory well and makes the class easy to understand. Lecture attendance is mandatory, but also worthwhile. Course is graded off of 6 problems sets and two exams. Homework isn't difficult and exams reflect homework pretty accurately. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Osgood is a great lecturer. Be prepared to sit for an hour and a half just to hear him talk about political economy. There's always a reading to do and more often than not there's a pop quiz on the readings. There's also two essays, which are graded solely by your GSI; who you have as your GSI will determine your essay grades.

Professor Osgood is very knowledgable but I sometimes found his lectures hard to follow. Pop quizzes were relatively straightforward. I had a very caring GSI. I felt that papers were graded toughly and not enough direction was given. Exams are a ton of studying but if you put in the work you will get an A. He did not seem willing to help sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relatively straightforward introductory course on political economy. The professor is unclear in lecture when explaining materials, instructions, and in communication. Grading criteria are arbitrary though inflated. Professor Osgood demonstrates passion and knowledge but is a poor lecturer. The only thing that is consistent is the inconsistency.
Great professor and makes international economy a very interesting subject. I want to take more classes in this area because of Dr. Osgood. His research also relates well to topics in the class.
awesome and jolly guy

Good professor, but exams were super hard and covered a lot of information. Ridiculously hard to study for, and the essay grading was harder than it should've been. All in all- Iain and my GSI were super informative and always there to ask questions, but I will not be taking another int econ class again...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: STOP THE INHUMANE TREATMENT OF STUDENTS WITH YOUR READING QUIZZES!

Such a good lecturer and really passionate. He makes class really interesting and is overall a really nice guy. There are reading quizzes that are annoying and you have to be sure to participate in discussion, but overall the class is really great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Osgood is a really clear and knowledgeable professor. He is well prepared for class and his lecture slides have lots of graphs and models (most of them made by himself) to help with learning. The tests for Polsci 369 aren't difficult if you study the concepts he gives you. The papers should be easy to write if you pay attention in class.
No more reading quizzes!

Great professor, great lectures. Introduces both game-theory-solving techniques and real-life games. Homework problems can be fun and thought-provoking. Great class, but make sure you attend all the lectures.

Iain is great professor, and his teaching of Game Theory was a breath of fresh air at UM. His courses were clear, his grading was fair, and his lectures were enjoyable. It's one of the easiest recommendations I can give. As long as you go to lecture and take notes, you'll spend less than 2 hours on homework every other week.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had at Michigan. He's a great lecturer who doesn't waste time assigning content that doesn't matter. After we were supposed to submit the online midterm at a specific time, he personally emailed me to make sure that my exam had been submitted the right way. This guy actually cares about his students.

Iain is amazing! He teaches clearly and has a great sense of humor. He also picked great GSIs that helped us do well in the class. Exams were straightforward and he gives out study guides. There are pop quizzes for the readings, but he doesn't grade them too hard. Definitely take him!

Professor Osgood was an incredible, fair teacher. He did not assign outside reading, just two exams and six problem sets throughout the semester. He simplified game theory to actually be understandable. Pay attention and engage in lecture, and you will do great!

His class is pretty lecture heavy but he tries his best to make the lectures as interesting as possible. If you go to his office hours, you will feel that he is genuinely willing to assist you and make sure that you do well in the class. The content of this class is really useful too. Take his class!

Professor Osgood is great. The class itself was pretty interesting, though the lectures sometimes got boring after awhile. Tests are pretty easy if you are willing to prepare definitions to words/concepts that he gives you in advance. My only complaint is that the pop quizzes are disorganized and the grading criteria for attendance is unclear.

Super energetic and passionate about the class. In-class quizzes, if you miss 8  0% for participation so you have to go to lecture. Slides have everything you need on them so you don't have to take notes. 2 easy papers, easy tests. He's accessible and even my GSI was awesome. The class is super interesting too -- 100% would recommend.

Incredibly interested in the subject he teaches. Very enthusiastic to teach and likes to apply lessons learned to current issues. Provides lecture notes for every lecture so note-taking is optional. Engages students constantly to try to keep them involved. Very open to meet after hours if you need help. Very nice and friendly guy as well

Unfortunately, Professor Spitz is not well versed in teaching this class and many labs were outside his realm of expertise. Lab reports are graded relatively fairly, but do not expect a good grade without putting in a lot of effort. Results matter, and outliers will lower your score.

Cares a lot about his students and loves physics a lot. If you have experience with the topics covered in class, then all the course concepts are pretty easy, but the explanations might be a bit quick if it's the first time seeing it. He does a great job of showing where concepts are used in higher level physics. Homeworks can be long sometimes.

This is hands down the best professor Ive ever had in my life. If youve had bad teachers in the past that made physics feel like a chore, he will make you enjoy it again. Hes extremely good at explaining things and ACTUALLY understanding and answering your questions and his teaching method rules. Definitely take his class.

Josh really understands what it's like to be a student and is thus very understanding and empathetic. He is really encouraging and wants to see everyone succeed. Go to his office hours and get to know him because he's really cool and a very friendly guy.

Josh is an amazing professor. In class he really makes sure the students understand the material, and if you have questions he will make time for them. No matter what class that Josh is taking, I would highly recommend taking it. He wants his students to do well and will help in any way he can. Genuine person who really cares about teaching.

Josh is hands down the best professor I have ever had.  He is so patient, kind, and above all a great teacher.  There are some teachers in your collegiate career that change your life.  Josh is one of those teachers.  Go to office hours to talk about him about anything.  He listens and offers advice if he thinks he can help.

Josh is really great. He's a new professor, but obviously cares a lot about his students. He really grew into being a professor this semester (this was his first class). More than willing to help you during office hours and knows this material can be very difficult. Very understanding and just a cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Jim is an awesome professor. He genuinely wants his students to do well and gives great feedback. I'm not a heritage speaker but I felt incredibly welcomed in his class learning environment.

Jim is awesome! He's a really good teacher, very accessible outside of class, and super fun to talk to during office hours if you like to get into the more specific stuff about Arabic. It's also helpful that even though he's obviously fluent in Arabic, he knows what it's like to learn it as a second language. I stayed in the 8 am for 102 for him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Jim (nickname) for both 101 and 102. During Arabic 102, he definitely expects you to speak a lot more Arabic than 101. The whole class is in Arabic in 102, but it isn't harder in terms of material and workload. Jim is amazing. He's always there for his students and I wish he'd be my Arabic professor for 201/202, but he's really good teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jim (nickname) is the best professor for Arabic learning. He is great and really knows his Arabic. He is always there if you need extra help and really tries to enhance your Arabic. He's very organized and tries to crack a joke once in a while. If you really try and do your homework, getting an A in Arabic 101 is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great, interdisciplinary professor who helps students think critically about the various perspectives one could take on any given topic mentioned.

Best professor I've encounterd yet. He cared about his students and was very passionate about how sociology applies to the real-world. He doesn't just read off slides, and his study guide is accurate in terms of what to expect on exams.

Loved this class. Very interesting topics. Optional readings and lectures. Only a few graded assignments and 4 short quizzes. I would recommend you go to the lectures because Professor McGinn is so entertaining to listen to and he's very knowledgeable.
Terry is so nice and a great lecturer. This class is super light also. Strongly recommend!

Professor McGinn is a great professor. The writing assignments are manageable, and the exams align with the study guides he provides. Attendance is not necessary, as the information you need is in the slides; however, his lectures are enjoyable, so you should definitely go!
Decent class, somewhat boring lectures, and attendance is not mandatory. Reviewing the material is quite easy from the slides, and the exams are pretty easy.
So sweet and attendance is optional! Just mandatory discussion once a week but its literally so easy and an hour long. Exams are very straightforward, study the slides and you'll be fine!!!

amazing professor who lectures in an engaging way, provides many resources to succeed, and tests fairly. he made me really interested in sociology even though I thought I had no interest before I took the class.

Dr.McGinn genuinely cares about his students. He constantly asked my peers and me how we were doing, etc. He gave interesting lectures and is very passionate about the topics. He provided straightforward guidelines and told us what would be on the exams. He gave clear study guides. I would definitely recommend him for Soc 100.
super easy class. attendance not required so never went to class, watched all the lectures a few days before and always got an 100 on the exams.
I did not speak much in this class but wow I loved Terry. He is such a sweet guy and we only had 4 quizzes, 2 papers, and 1 group project that you can also do alone. No final as well. Great guy.

Best professor I've ever had. I came in undecided, and this course made me declare my major as sociology. He is an incredible professor and a genuinely interesting person. Attendance is not required, and most of my friends got decent grades (a/b) without doing most of the readings. He is genuinely interested in the content he teaches.

Terry is a great lecturer! He uses stories and real-life examples to clarify ideas and keep students engaged. He's always open to conversation and willing to help, and his classes are both productive and easy to follow.

I love Professor McGinn! If you can take SOC100 with him please do! Genuinely learned so much and he doesn't just read off slides. Everyone always felt so comfortable to speak up and have discussions about topics. Open about his political opinions but was unbiased when actually teaching.

Good lecturer and funny guy. You can tell that he has gone through a lot of personal work to breakdown bias that he's been taught, allowing him to teach sociology well. He's very good at teaching the content unbiasedly, despite heavily disputed topics. His tests are very straightforward and overall it's a pretty easy class.

I normally dislike any kind of humanities class because i'm not very good with memorizing, but this class was life changing. He was so funny, so kind, and made his lectures engaging for all of us. when it was test time, he didn't spring anything surprising, you just had to make sure you studied. my advice is to make flashcards with the key notes!

He gives great lectures, engages with his students, and keeps things interesting. The exams are as straightforward as possible, and he tells you exactly what you need to know and review. No surprises or trick questions anywhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof McGinn is the sweetest man and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Exams were an exact replica of the study guide and because of this, no one would go to class. However, I think McGinn deserves an audience and you should go to class because it is actually interesting.

I love Terry! He is a great professor and he cares about his students. I went to office hours to go over a quiz and he was really nice and willing to help. The class is 4 exams and he doubles the highest score and drops the lowest. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

Terry is a great lecturer and clearly very knowledgeable about the subject. Attendance is not mandatory and you can easily get an A without going to class (watch lecture vids). The class is only graded on exams (50%), two small assignments (5%), and discussion attendance participation/attendance (20%), and a group project done in discussion (25%).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and amazing guy and always available at office hours to review exam material. There are 3 exams, 1 group project (in your discussion), 2 small assignments, and discussion attendance and that makes up your grade. Just an overall great college professor and I'd take any of his classes.
This was the easiest class I've taken at U-M just make sure to check canvas every blue moon so you don't miss any assignments. As long as you review study guide before the exams you'll do fine.

Terry is a kind and supportive professor, but the course content felt a bit scattered at times. Nonetheless, study guides and review sessions made exam expectations clear. The group project could use a bit more oversight however, as each GSI seemed to have her own grading criteria. Overall, SOC/DIGITAL 285 is an easy and fairly interesting course.

Terry is a charismatic, genuine professor who makes surface-level content enjoyable! It's an easy class but not mini-course easy. Exams are short, mixing content and application, so you'll still need to study. Your worst exam (out of 3) is devalued from 20 to 10 points. You don't need to do the readings or attend lectures if you watch them online.

The course content is fine, and the professor is super supportive, but the grading system for group presentations (25% of grade)is a big issue.   In our section, Erika Arias graded harshly—our scores ranged from 20.5 to 24.5, while other sections the lowest score is 24. The whole process felt more like busywork than a learning experience.

Terry is a very enjoyable professor who I would recommend taking. While lectures can often be very simple, he manages to make it entertaining and interactive with appropriate and engaging contemporary examples. Exams are easy. There is reading homework but honestly you can skip the readings and just listen to the lecture and be fine.

Terry is a great professor and lecturer. His slides and lectures are clear, and he divides grades into 3 exams and one group project. The exams are very reasonable (and in my experience, pretty easy). All the readings that are relevant to the test he teaches in lecture, so really no need to read them. He's also really funny!!

It was a very easy class. Terry is the sweetest old man and cares about what he's teaching. The tests were very straightforward and easy. You don't even need to show up to lectures to do well. 3 exams and 1 easy group project in discussion. I would 100% take a class from him again.
Lectures cover all test material. No surprise questions on tests.

Professor McGinn makes the material engaging and fun. His study guides are super helpful - combine them with unstuck AI for easy exam prep. Attendance is mandatory but the workload is reasonable, and he's a cheerful, approachable instructor.

Terry was an enthusiastic professor that made boring material interesting and fun to learn. His slides were a bit wordy, but he gave a list of key concepts at the end of each lecture, which told you exactly everything you needed to know for exams. He is the best professor to take for this class!

McGinn is my favorite professor, he grades easy and seems like a cheerful old man.  I like his enthusiam and how he makes the class nice and easy so we can learn but also enjoy and focus on other classes stress-wise.

I love this guy. He's so nice!
Basically, as long as you do your study guide and study it the night before the exam, you are guaranteed an A. Very straightforward tests, and he is a wonderful lecturer! Take him if you get the chance!
Easiest soc 100 professor at Michigan, you don't need to attend lectures and there are no essays or assignments. Terry is also funny and keeps lectures simple and engaging.

Terry is a great professor who you can tell is passionate about sociology. He is funny and engaging, however attendance in lecture isn't needed. The class is graded on 3 tests, discussion and thats like it. I felt this class was more work than I was told, but it is by no means hard.
Great professor, great lecturer, very engaging and down to earth. Take any of his courses if given the chance.

Would recommend SOC 100 with Terry! I enjoyed his lectures and appreciated his study guides. Everything you need to know for the three quizzes is on those study guides, so be sure to review them thoroughly.

Great professor. Really knows his stuff. Encourages conversation and wrestling with material. Grade based on few assignments, but assignments are pretty easy. Lots of reading, but the reading isn't super necessary for understanding material. Just pay attention to lecture and study guides.

The class is super easy and he is a really nice guy. You are not tested/asked to apply concepts as much as you are asked to memorize facts and people so if you like that or want an easy A take this class.

Terry is such a sweet guy and his classes are extremely manageable! He also loves to interact with students and get everyone engaged with the content. In terms of grading, both SOC 100 and 285 are structured around short non-cumulative quizzes, which he provides a study guide for with everything you need to know. Super chill, would recommend.

Always came to lecture with a pretty good attitude and talked about sensitive subjects in a well thought out matter, giving room for differences in opinion. No one ever got offended. Exams weren't that hard, but assignments are graded on quality, so don't slack in the class. Otherwise, it's a pretty easy A.
He was super kind and respectful of students

Professor McGinn explained the topics very well, and although there were a lot of readings, as long as you paid attention in lecture you'd be fine. All of the topics from the readings you needed to know he covers. Also, he gives you a guide before exams of what the key points you need to know are, and they're very helpful.

Terry is a great lecturer with clear expectations.  There were four quizzes and two assignments (a presentation and paper) that counted towards your grade in addition to attendance (though you could make up for the classes you miss).   This class and the quizzes are very easy if you keep up with the lectures and review the notes.

Terry is adorable and a decent lecturer, though they can be a bit of a snoozer. Luckily, attendance isn't required and this is one of the easiest classes you will ever take. Grading is super easy and there aren't really any big assignments. No cumulative exams or midterms. Terry is kind and caring, makes everything super clear.

I love Terry! He is super engaging with the students, and if you ask him a question he doesn't know, he'll research it personally and get back to the class about it. He finds ways to keep the class engaged even though the workload is very low and the grading is generous.
Take Sociology with Terry, easy / fun class and he is the sweetest. Brought us candy for Halloween.

Probably one of my favorite classes and favorite professors here at UMICH. Dr. McGinn is very knowledgable and is very kind. Even though I knew/was familiar with many of the topics covered in class, I was always eager to hear his perspectives and even the experiences of my peers. Great class and not hard to get an A.

Incredible and passionate professor. Presents info super clearly, and lectures are very engaging. He's a very fun and nice person and very approachable. This class made me decide to major in sociology. Would definitely take another class with Terry!

Very interesting class. As a minority I kind of already knew this stuff but I love to hear it be taught. Also Terry was super nice and understanding. The exams were super easy if you understand the study guide questions. You don't need to purchase the second textbook, honestly I didn't read anything but some of the first book.

Great professor. Assignments were discussion posts, 2 papers, and 3 exams. Gives you a study guide for exams with exactly what you need to know. Papers graded by GSI's. Lectures are recorded so you don't have to go.

Discussion attendance required lectures were recorded. Terry was an amazing lecturer even asynchronously, some of the GSI were better than others but you can understand the material just from him. Some discussions didn't seem very tied to the lecture which was annoying bc we had to attend, but that didn't really impact understanding of the material

Professor McGinn was a wonderful professor! He's very passionate about sociology and broke it down into easily understandable concepts, and he was very clear about all the class expectations. Lecture attendance is optional, and the assignments were pretty easy. Easy A class that piqued my interest in sociology!

I would recommend taking SOC 100 with Terry! He was a really great professor, and his class is easy to pass with an A. His exams are all straight from lecture material and never have any trick questions.

Professor McGinn's lectures are engaging and he always adds personal stories to make them more fun and relatable. Reading is unnecessary since all of the information is covered in the lecture slides. There are three exams and lowest grade is dropped. Easy A.

Terry gave engaging and funny lectures. You can tell he really cares about the content and makes sure everyone understands. He often adds his own interpretation into lecture and tells stories that make the content more memorable. Grading is not harsh, one group project and an essay but nothing very difficult. Lowest exam grade is dropped. Easy A.

He is an amazing lecturer! Truly helped me to enjoy the class, the course, and the material. He is super caring with his students and very understanding professor! Would highly suggest any sociology course with him :)

Terry is an intelligent and kind professor. He gave the class a clear structure and had an exact breakdown of what makes up the final grade. Overall, the lectures were informative and to-the-point, and the content of the tests was very representative of what was covered in lectures. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

Terry is a great lecturer and his SOC100 is a very reasonable class. Show up to class, take good notes, and you should do solid on the tests. GSI's are responsible for about 50% of your grade (group project, paper, etc.). discussion attendance is required. Not my personal favorite class, but simple, solid class for social science credit.
I just want to say this man accidentally missed a discussion section so he bought everyone giftcards. Truly just a nice guy teaching an interesting class! Take if you have the chance.

This is my first year at Umich and Terry has been my favorite professor so far. His classes are so entertaining and he really cares about his students. I also got lucky with my GSI and they both were amazing and super lenient during the pandemic. I would love to take another one of Terry's classes. I am sure the in-person lectures are even better.
Terry rules. nuff said

Professor Mcginn is easily one of my favorite lecturers at umich. He really cares about his students and his lectures are straightforward and really easy to understand. He also goes over the main points of all the readings in lecture so if you cant read them it really isn't a big deal. Sweetest guy and a great professor/ easy grader.
Terry is the best! SO approachable and really tells a story in his lectures. All around 10/10 guy

Not often you find a professor that makes you feel like a friend without having met them, he is that prof. Very easygoing and interesting, and makes an effort not to be pretentious. To top it off he is very informed of the topics he teaches, and backs up examples in lecture with real world experiences. Fantastic class and prof.
Super nice prof who is genuinely passionate about sociology and loves to teach! He was always willing to clarify class content and is overall friendly

The course is dry, especially online. Terry is a nice guy though who seems very caring and knowledgeable. The assignments are pointless and the instructions/difficulty/grading vary significantly across the different sections. The course is fine but would recommend Psych 111 or Anthrcul 101 over it.

Lectures are detailed and uses plenty of examples to clarify basic concepts. The class has A LOT of reading though so be prepared to take the time to read. I took this class online and it was pretty low-stress. He covers the key concepts during lecture so if you miss a reading it won't hurt, but I would recommend doing the reading when you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance taken randomly in lectures. GSI was extremely shy and rude when approached with questions or concerns. The whole class was graded out of 100 points which makes it tough to get a good grade if you mess up on anything. McGinn definitely cares about his students, but this class is unreasonably hard for a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terry seems like a decent guy but Soc 100 was unbearable. Don't take it if you don't have to, but if you do it's super easy if you put in minimal effort. The content is just super annoying. Prepare to spend an entire unit on communism. Also, the GSIs were laughably bad.

The examples and stories that Prof. McGinn tells in class helps solidify concepts. His slides oftentimes don't tell the full story, so paying attention during lecture really helps you understand material better. This class is super low-pressure if you study well before tests and put in the work. Overall, I recommend taking this class with him!
