Worst GSIs, unorganized lectures - other soc profs are easier

Second class with Terry and it was once again a great experience. SOC285 - Soc of the Digital World is a super interesting course and counts towards the digital studies minor. Graded on 4 quizzes, group blog, and group presentation. Quizzes were not too difficult and group projects were relevant and fun. Terry always made class fun!

The most boring lectures you will ever attend. There were only 100 points in the whole class so you miss a few here and there and your grade drops so much. He did random attendance checks so also go to class. There were four exams and a paper to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely boring. Terrible powerpoints, not very clear/well put together. Nice old dude with lots of personal life stories but they usually aren't relevant/helpful for the class. GSIs are awful. Worst GSI i have ever encountered for SOC 100. Weird point scale for the class.

he randomly takes attendance which counts for credit. tests are dumb easy but you still need to study for them. hes a great, interesting speaker but its really easy to miss information since theres too much text on the slides and he walks up and down the aisles of the lecture hall making it hard to fully engage
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terry is a great professor lectures are interesting and full of his life stories and the class is really easy, only take SOC 100 with him!!
Great teacher, but the grading scale is very rough. EVERY POINT MATTERS IN THIS CLASS. Study hard and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: terry is a nice prof but the study guides and tests do not always match up well, you go into the test expecting one thing and are sometimes blindsided by what is actually on it

Terry is my favorite professor at U of M!!! I've taken his soc 100 class and a smaller class soc 455 and loved him in both. He is funny, charismatic and wants his students to succeed. He is very knowledgable about sociology and you will learn a lot from him!!

I took soc100 because it's a pre-med course now. Not as easy as I expected. Straightforward quizzes- go to lecture, take notes on his stories, set aside 45 min per week to do the readings - you'll do fine. Essays/group projects depends on GSI, so get your points from quizzes/attendance. Strange guy, but he's fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I came in thinking Soc 100 would be a super easy class and that the exams would be common sense. That is not the case. You have to study a bunch and memorize names and historical things for them. Also, the class is only 100 points and your grade depends so much on your GSI. I didnt learn much from the class either. Mcginn is a cool professor though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terry wasn't bad. He lectures were very boring and the class was graded out of very few points. The problem was the GSI's. They were all horrible and tough graders. His exams weren't awful if you approached the answers from what you think he would choose and not what you think the actual right answer is.

I only signed up for this class cause it was the only one that fit in my schedule. The lectures are dry and the material is boring. The class is graded on very few points, so it makes it hard to do very well in the class. In his tests, he hides very specific details from readings that don't pertain to the concepts from class, making exams hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: first exam was hard but then I learned how to study and did rly well on the second one. got kicked out of class once for laughing... perfectttionnn. I do like Terry though. He's really enthusiastic.

Terry is a great professor! I highly recommend taking his soc in the digital world class for a distribution requirement or if you're a soc major. Class structure is varied, which keeps class interesting, and he is very helpful in office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: love terry!! super charismatic and cares about his students. Class was harder than I expected, but I definitely learned a lot

Terry was a great lecturer. He had a lot of stories to tell which made it easy to remember information. Tests were super easy; just memorize the lecture slides and you're golden. Easy class overall. I put in very little time or effort and got an A. However, this class is graded on very few points (100) which proved difficult for some students.

Terry was great! His lectures were informative and unbiased. He's pretty funny and made sure to include examples on different levels to adhere to different types of students and their learning. You don't have to do the readings as the test content is lecture-based. Grading is based on few points and your GSI determines a significant chunk of that.

Terry was a solid choice for Soc 100 - his lectures are interesting and he provides some really cool insight to certain situations. If your mind easily grasps natural science concepts and not social sciences like mine, this class won't be easy. Your grade is heavily determined by how much of the slides you memorize and how nice your GSI is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrys a cool dude. Made lectures interesting with personal stories. Lots of memorizing and reading (save a group project and paper). Graded on very few points. I put in a lot of work and still almost got an A-. Large part of grade comes down to whether your GSI is lenient or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terry is the man. The guy is very intelligent and knows his stuff. His lectures are unbiased and entertaining and the requirements for class are pretty clear. Also, you don't have to do the readings to get an A, just pay attention and study the lecture slides, but they're pretty interesting and can't hurt to do
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Terence is great but the class is not an easy A. Lectures were super interesting as Terence always told stories that related to the topic. But the class is graded on close to nothing. 15 pts/exam, 10 pts for paper, 15 its for group project, rest are participation pts and total100 pts.

Terry is great and a superb professor. Do not take this class for an easy A, although classes are only 2 days a week, there is quite a bit of reading and the exams focus a lot on that reading. Its a point system though so if you do poorly on the exams (like me) you will still be able to gain quite a few point elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DON'T take SOC100 if you want an easy intro class. The material isn't difficult but is graded on few points. An A- isn't too bad to get, but an A takes a solid effort. Lots of reading and memorizing slides. The problem is that it's so easy to lose points. Miss 2 questions on a quiz and your final grade is already down by 1%. Definitely overstudy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terry is one of the best professors I've had at this university. He's kind and incredibly knowledgeable. You DEFINITELY have to show up, do the readings, and put in the work. But if you do, you will be sure to get a good grade. Plus, he's always willing to help outside of class if you need it. He sometimes gives EC for attendance as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: not a very respectful person; not too difficult to do well in the class but definitely did not enjoy classes with him- extremely dull and ppt heavy
terry's awesome
terry's the best for soc 100

Lectures weren't awful, but they also weren't very informative. After a few classes, it becomes clear that he acts pretentiously as a façade to cover up some sort of guilt. He projects his insecurities on traditional students in a condescending manner. At the risk of sounding mean, he's spineless.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terry is a cool guy and teaches interesting classes but he definitely isn't a hard grader. You don't have to do a whole lot to pass the class but there's interesting content. He's a nice guy but definitely not a life changing class and it didn't really push me

If you took SOC 100 with Terry, then you will recognize some recycled content from the class put into a new context with SOC 295. That said, Terry is an exceptional professor, really cares about his students, and is fun to listen to. Just get used to hearing the same story three times. Also, most people are on their laptop most of the class.

Terry was just awesome. Very genuine guy that gives lots of interesting personal antidotes in class that relate to the topic of the day. The class is not heavy a heavy load but you genuinely learn a lot. I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is interested in what sociology is/ just wants a board understand of the subject.

Amazing professor- very engaging! Provides you with the knowledge and space to think critically about what is going on around you. Pushes you to take what you are learning in class and apply it to your life. He is the professor that inspired me to become a Sociology major. Not hard- tests all based solely on lecture (he posts slides as well)
Jeez, Terry is amazing.  His lectures are fun and engaging--you can tell he loves what he teaches.  Life-changing and inspirational professor, one of the best I've ever had.
Good professor with interesting anecdotes to enhance concepts. Getting an A- is easy, but to get an A, you have to put in real effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Terry was an awesome professor. Each of his lectures are very interesting and he provides tons of real life anecdotes about sociology. I can genuinely say I learned a lot about the world through this class. It is hard to get an A though because the class is out of 100 points total. Would definitely recommend.

Terry is a great professor. He may seem a little intimidating at first, but he just has an old school style. He brought our class in sweet treats on multiple occasions. His class outline is very clear and straight forward. However, it is hard to get an A because the course is out of a total of 100 points, but it is still definitely do-able.
Terry's lectures are awesome and convey the material very clearly.

Terry is great. His lectures are very well done and he is interesting to listen to. Your grade will definitely come down to your GSI, however. In my class, the general consensus is that two or three of the four GSIs were good (not 100% certain, I had a fantastic GSI). Will be taking future courses with Terry for sure.

I took this class thinking it would be fun, interesting, and a GPA booster. I was wrong. There is TONS of reading that you have to do in order to do well. You have a long paper that's graded strictly and a group project which he gives minimal guidance on. And not to mention it's really boring! We spent all of the semester on the history of soc.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: For only a 100 level class, I had to work way harder than I had hoped to do well in this class. I studied for the exam by memorizing the lecture notes and that was not enough. You need to do the readings and pay attention to his lectures because there will be things on the exam that are not in the lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor is a pain in the ass. Plus, he is really rude.
You can get by without reading if you focus on the powerpoints. All of the tests are based on what's on the powerpoint. The tests can be slightly tricky. An A- is achievable but A will need work.

Terry is an awesome person, and has tons of anecdotes that make class interesting. My only problem with this class is there is no room for doing bad on an assignment since it's a 100 point grading so if you don't do that well on one of the quizes that's only 30 questions it's easy to drop several percentages. Also, the grader wasn't him for essays.
He is a great professor, however the GSIs can be hard graders. If you attend lecture and study the study guides, you'll receive a good grade within this course.

Everything on the tests are on his lecture slides, which he posts online, so your guaranteed A's on the test if you study the slides. His lectures can me a bit sporadic at times but he keeps everyone engaged because he is so enthusiastic about sociology.

Terry is an awesome guy. Very knowledgeable and kind. The grading is straight forward but it's hard to get an A. The quizzes are more-or-less memorization tests and the papers are not bad at all. He's a great guy and makes coming to class worth it.

Terry is the best professor I've had at this University. Lectures are engaging and insightful. Quizzes are simple and straightforward if you study. Papers are graded fairly and pretty open-ended leaving room for creativity and critical thinking. Participation in class is not required, but makes coming to class more enjoyable.

T-Mac is the man! He is so cheerful and is a gifted lecturer. I would recommend taking the Soc. Topic course on Sex, Religion, and Money. The way the class is set up, it is difficult to receive a solid A. Tests are tricky and there are assignments graded by GSI. Work hard and you should do well.

Terry is a great professor. He engages his students, loves when students participate, and makes really funny remarks. Lectures are pretty interesting and there isn't too much reading. Also, the 4 quizzes are pretty straightforward as long as you look at his study guides, so there's no final/midterm you have to cram for.
Amazing professor! My absolute favorite this semester :D  His tests were only 10% each and there were 4 of them so the class isn't bad.

Soc 100 is a class that is very conversational, at times lecture can be vague when trying to figure out what is on the exam.  I read the books when assigned and the day OF the test I went through every lecture and read them out loud.  It got me A's on the exams, and there are only 3.  Also, my GSI was really chill and layed back, so that helped.

Terry is an amazing professor. I never got bored of his lectures! If you go to his office hours, he is always nice and patient with you and he takes his time to talk to you personally to get to know you. Would recommend taking his class.

If you've thought aboutresearched stuff like this before (sociological topics like feminism or racism), this class is much easier. It frames the arguments you've seen into an academic perspective. Memorize the slides & exam is golden.  The discussion sections are mostly GSI-led, so pick your GSI carefully (Linroy rocks, btw. He's chill).
Tests aren't relatively difficult and Terry is a great guy.  Though the GSI's are tough graders on essays and group presentations.  Discussion sections didn't help at all.
Exams had nothing to do with the material and assessed unrelated questions to the topic of sociology. He is a pretty cool person and does provide entertaining lectures on a relatively boring topic.

Terry was a great lecturer. The material in the class is very dry and abstract. Attendance is graded. Grading system is terrible. 100 points total so EVERY point counts. There are 3 exams, one paper and one group presentation. GSIs are strict with grading & exams are nit-picky. You will have to work hard for an A. Overall, I would not recommend.
He is very funny but better take his tests seriously: Meaning, memorizing the lecture slides or otherwise good luck in guessing multiple choice questions.

His grading system makes it almost impossible to get an A if you don't ace every test, come to every lecture, and get full credit on papers. The content can be interesting and he is a nice, interesting guy, but this class is much harder than necessary. Also Evan the GSI is absolutely terrible so do not choose him for discussion.

The content of this class was very easy. However, there aren't enough points offered so everything has too much weight. There are only 3 15pt tests of 30Qs that are reading quizzes- not testing theories, concepts, or ideas. Ex Q: What was the ex used in chapter 3; who wrote which article? Absolutely ridiculous for a class that should be an easy A

Terry is the bomb. This class is so interesting and he's very good at treating students like adultshis peers. He's very intelligent and wise; he has some of the most interesting stories. My favorite class and favorite teacher by far at Michigan, it's the one class I'm actually excited to attend! You'll do fine as long as you pay attention in class

Material was dry but Terry made it relevant and easy to digest. He held review sessions after every 4 lectures, and responded to class feedback throughout the semester when the curve was abnormal after the midterm. Exams are not difficult if you pay attention to what material he emphasizes.  Sweet and energetic. Take good lecture notes & you're set

McGinn is great! He is very helpful and will try to schedule a time to meet up with you if you need help. The way grades are set up, it is a bit hard to get a solid A. If you answer all the questions on the study guides he gives, you will do just fine on the small exams he gives. He is a great professor and I would def recommend this class.
This class was pretty interesting but Terry gives the most unnecessarily difficult tests of all time. 30 impossible multiple choice questions per test. Only take this class if you have to.

I was originally very interested in the class, but it turns out the lecture discussions are just boring and poorly structured. Quizzes don't truly reflect the materials on study guide. Grading on the reaction paper is not very fair.
Such a cool professor, but the class was very boring. Section was super structured and a lot of the stuff taught in class seemed easy, while the exams were a little harder.

Favorite professor so far at UofM! Very engaging and funny lecturer, he blends theory, current events, and personal experiences very well in his class. Readings are manageable and lectures build upon them very well. If you come into the class with any interest in sociology or religion, you will love it, and it wont be that hard. Great prof!
Awesome teacher, with very helpful office hours. He knows his stuff, and is always willing to clarify whatever you may need help with. Take a class with him!

Lectures didn't necessarily have anything to do with exam topics. Very all over the place. He was nice, but most of the class was based on biographical information of sociologists--almost nothing on sociological topics. Definitely not an enjoyable class.

Terry is an awesome Prof! This was my 2nd course with him, and I want to take more. He is very laid back during class, and gives really clear course outlines, that he will change if need-be. We had 2 really fun group/indv. music projects, quizzes, and a take-home final essay. You don't need to know anything about musicology. Take a class w Terry!

Very clear in both the expectations for the class and in teaching the class. I learned a lot during the semester, and he presented the information in an understandable way. The grading can be a bit tough, but he is very open to helping you to do your best.
Terry is an interesting teacher. He lets the students make their own grading rubric, decide on what they want to learn, and then teach each other. It was really group oriented class.

Terry is a great guy and very willing to help his students. This class has a lot of reading, be prepared to do 20-50 pages per class. That being said, it's not very hard to do decent without completing all of the reading. The part I enjoyed the most was learning about Terry, he's led a very interesting life. Definitely take a class with him!

He was a fantastic instructor. He was always willing to help during office hours. He also encouraged students to talk during class and add their opinions. His class was interesting and the material was presented clearly.

Lecture became boring (maybe bc it was 1.5 hours) but he tried to keep the class engaged. The quizzes are very easy. Study the slides. All of them. Overall, he is a nice guy, and he likes participation.

I thought Terry was a great guy but the curve in the class is the most obnoxious thing in the world. You end up hating everyone in the class as you compete for the 100 points that are given. Every point counts and you think the class is easy at first but by quiz 2 you will be studying for hours so as not to miss a single ? on the nit picky quizes

This is easy class with a light workload.  I stopped doing the reading halfway through the class and my grade didn't drop at all.  Lectures are boring but useful.  All you need to study is the slides on his powerpoints and you will get an A.  Terry is a nice guy and this is a good class to take.
This class was pretty easy.  Lectures were sometimes a little dry but Terrence is always willing to help and clarify any questions.  Overall a good class, I would recommend.

Great professor. Really took an interest in his students and what they had to say despite the fact that he was teaching in a large lecture hall. People may complain about the curve but not hard to get an A at all if you study the slides thoroughly and take notes during class. Readings help but not completely necessary.

Great professor, kept the lectures interesting. Funny and always in a good mood. Make sure you do the readings. Exams (he calls them quizzes) basically follow lecture and readings but definitely not regurgitated. You need to be able to internalize material and understand every aspect of it.
Boring lectures. Grading scale not very fair. Didn't help that my GSI was garbage. Terry is really nice though.

Attendance is mandatory via iClicker.  You don't need to read the textbooks.  The class is incredibly boring and most people just play on their computer.  The only way you can keep up is if you look at the powerpoint to see what he is talking about.  Frivolous grading system--100 point class, every exam is 15 points....

Friendly, generally cheery guy. Lectures were relatively straightforward but if you looked only at the powerpoints, you wouldn't understand much about the class. He is willing to help and wants students to do well by asking if they understand the material. The bell curve grading is weird and the 3 assignments don't seem relevant, but they're doable
This class was fascinating.  If you like religion or learning about crazy cults you should deffinently take this class.  It was the class that got my interested in sociology ( I am now a soc major).

Terry is really knowledgeable and a great teacher.  He works hard to make sure his students understand the material.  The class is pretty easy.  It helps to do the readings because he tends to use stuff from the beginning of the semester to reinforce concepts later on.

Terry is a fun guy. His lectures were fun and interesting. I didn't do any readings but did study the slides for the quizzes and I made a B+. Go to class because he takes attendance grades. Overall good class and I plan to take another sociology class with him.

The class was mildly interesting, and skimming through the reading was enough to get by.  However, he grades on a ridiculous curve and also when the end of the semester comes, he takes the class average as well as section averages and adjusts all the grades to meet that-we had a few percentage points taken off of our grades, our GSI was even upset.

This was one of the best classes I have ever taken at U of M. I never got that feeling I get when I learn useless information because everything was so relevant and applicable to real life. Terry is very clear and understanding and always willing to help. The class is not a stressful class at all (3 quizzes and a paper) and it is pretty fun overall

Pretty good taecher, makes lecture extremely interesting. the one thing i don't like about him is that he uses powerpoint but he goes out of order (of the slides) A LOT and sometimes makes it hard to follow.
Fairly easy class, quiz questions were directly from lecture slides & notes taken during class, takes attendance randomly, had a bad experience with my GSI but he is an excellent professor.
Lectures swing between extremely boring and very interesting. Class is pretty simple. Make sure you study the details for the tests

He made lectures interesting, tests were a little harder than i expected, i put in a lot of time doing the readings and it turns out i didnt even need to read them when it came down to tests...overall good class though
loved topics presented in class
I like to refer to him as T-Mac... I thought he was a pretty awesome lecturer. He made the class pretty interesting.
Easy grader, but doesn't really know much. His quiz questions insult student's intelligence - he asks questions like "what page number is this concept discussed on?"

Great professor.  Really interesting lectures.  Likes to hear what students have to say.  Pretty easy grader.  You don't have to read the textbook or readings at all - whatever he goes over in class is what will be on the quiz.  Highly recommended teacher.
Terry aka T-Mac was a great lecturer!! Just stay on top of the readings and you'll get an A. Highly recommend him

Terry is a great lecturer, witty and intelligent. However, when you're taking notes he's wont to say "this won't be on the quiz" - IT WILL. So write everything down. Not too bad of a class, but if Jamie is your GSI be careful if you appeal a grade; she will not be so kind after that
Great instructor, Interesting Class. However, the curve was annoying [25% A, 50% B, 25% C]...Not too heavy of a workload - mainly just multiple readings
he's really good and my favorite professor this semester! i would recommend him to anyone and he's not a very hard grader either
terry was my favorite prof this semester and he's really good, i'd recommend taking him for anyone, he really got me to like sociology and he's not too hard of a grader

Grading is ridiculous.  Lecture is simple, however sometimes boring. If you take this class make sure you don't have Jamie as your GSI, she is awful. Terry is interesting however fairly liberal and often teaches through his own views.  Overall a decent class, would be better without Jamie.

He's a pretty laid back guy, but sometimes he can snap. When he has a bad day he will take it out on the whole class. The workload is extremely light and the tests are a breeze if you do minimal reading. Sometimes the lectures go off on tangents, and they rarely reflect the reading or test material.

His grading system sucks. I got a 93 on the first quiz (2 wrong FYI), which was a 69th percentile, so I was getting a B, even though I had a NINETYTHREE!  And on that first quiz he asked us the page number of a concept, not what the concept was...

I couldn't stand this class. Terry taught in a way that always seemed patronizing to me. The class had a lot of potential, with interesting topics, but I found it completely useless and pretty annoying. It felt like a big waste of my time.

Terry is a very good professor.  Class is sometimes boring, but he can be entertaining, too.  Quizzes aren't too bad, nor are the two papers.  You do have to come to class though because attendance is often taken.  You don't really have to read the books, because he summarizes them in class.  Grading isn't overly harsh.

Terry is a really cool and understanding professor. His quizzes are easy, but he limits the amount of A's he grants for overall grades. His class is interesting and often shows cool movies and brings in speakers.

Terry is by far my favorite professor ever.  Sadly, I have now taken every class he teaches at the University... but if he decided to pick up a new class, I would take it.  I took his religion class with almost no interest in the subject, just because he was teaching it...I loved it!  Take a class with Terry before you leave the University!

ALSO HAD HIM FOR 305. TERRY IS VERY INTERESTING AND AN OVERALL COOL PROF.  HE IS MORE EASYGOING IN TOPICAL CLASSES LIKE SOC OF RELIGION THAN PREREQS AND REQUIRED COURSES.  HE HAS AN INTERESTING BACKGROUND.  HIS OFFICE HOURS WILL ALWAYS PROVE TO BE INFORMATIVE AS WELL AS ENTERTAINING. IF YOU GO TO CLASS, IT'S PRETTY HARD TO GET A BAD GRADE.

a little unorganized..but pretty nice and very easygoing...if you come to him with a problem he is helpful and the gsi's are great to ask for questions...overall pretty its a pretty easy, relaxing class and mcginn is good
Many people's favorite sociology professor. Funny, can be sarcastic, can occasionally be testy. Definitely good at his subject. Doesn't grade too hard.
Doesn't believe in A's yet quizzes are fairly simple. Lecture's pretty much just a summary of the reading but there are times when we get into some pretty interesting debates. Not too bad overall

The class was really easy and he presented material clearly. I just wish he'd gone beyond what was in the book for his lectures mroe often to make it interesting. I don't need to pay tuition for a book summary. Overall, a good teacher adn a nice guy though.
Good professor. I liked him.
Excellent teacher. Made classroom discussions interesting and engaging. Coursework was clearly laid out. Uses a "grader" to evaluate papers.
Lectures easy to understand, nothing to hard to comprehend.  Simple tests/quizzes.
Take his class.  He gets all the points across easily and makes class interesting.  Very easy.
Had full knowledge of the subject.  Very detailed and great teacher.  Enthusiastic for a seemingly uninteresting subject.
He's a really good teacher, he knows his stuff and makes the class enjoyable. I would recomment taking his class.
No Comments
his class is intersting and he does different activites in his lectures. he is very opinionated and will argue or makes you stand by your comments
Great teacher, but not much consideration for opinions outside of his own. Puts alot of effort into the course, and it shows
No Comments
Good
Its obvious that he loves the subject and enjoys teaching it. TAKE HIM
Terry is awesome. Only teacher I ever had that really cared about the content of his class and how interesting it was. great readings, very interesting. Terry actually works hard.

This class was awesome. Money, sex, religion...what more would you want to learn about? Terry uses great examples to illustrate his points, and the books are actually interesting to read! This class was a welcome break from the rest of my awful schedule. TAKE THIS CLASS (esp if you need a SS credit)

the class is retarted. There is a quiz on the content of the syllabus thats worth half of what the final is worth. stupid grade sysytem. Terrys a nice  guy but a horrible teacher. Have not really learned anything about soc. quizes are on non-soc book's content rather than thier relevence to soc.
He's not very good with getting feedback about grades, but is very energetic and interesting. Although the class is a hodge-podge if information, it's fairly reasonable.

I wasn't excited about taking a sociological theory class, but I'm actually enjoying it. Terry is so friendly and always eager to hear what students think. I didn't like having a quiz every class period, but it did motivate me to do all the assigned readings.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Took Mark's cult cinema course this semester, and it's by far my favorite I've taken with him. He knows EVERYTHING about cult/exploitation, and I always looked forward to seeing what movie or clip he'd show next. He tells lots of personal stories too, and they're usually absolutely ridiculous (in a good way). I'll miss being in his class!!!
Mark is charismatic and incredibly articulate! The kind of professor that you can build a really great friendship with if you speak up and are respectful.
He is just so mean to students. I have never felt more uncomfortable in a classroom.

I have taken two courses of FTVM with Mark, 353 and 441. He is always well prepared with the content of the course, and also tries to understand and respond to your personal opinion. He is very nice and caring to students. The fantastique and horror topic he taught for the upper level is awesome. I would recommend that everybody take his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i didn't know it was ever possible for someone to have as much insane film knowledge as this man does😭
One of the smartest professors and a entertaining and funny lecturer.

topics covered for class can be dense and there are lots of readings, but he breaks them down really well. he almost always has a wacky anecdote related to the lesson too, which makes it memorable. very encouraging to students who participate in class. chillest guy i ever met tbh, truly the goat of the uofm film department

Mark is one of the smartest professors that I've ever had. The topics that he explains are so complex, yet he communicates them in the most digestible way. I always have a great time attending his lectures, and leave every time feeling like I've learned a lot. Mark is great.

I learned a lot about the history of cinema, and I liked the readings though there were quite a few of them. Good selection of movies as well. Would take another class with him as a good lecturer with tons of humor and analysis of films thrown in. A little disorganized but overall really enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kligerman is good as they get.

He's disrespectful and if you're even 1 minute late to class expect to be chewed out in front of the entire room. His classes are the worst I've taken and it sucks that FTVM students have to take multiple classes with him. HEAVY READING and pointless, hard-to-follow lectures have nothing to do with the quizzes or exams but attendance is taken.
I would take a bullet for Mark! He's one of the funniest people around and just a great professor. He's so passionate about the material and learning, I loved attending every class of his.

If you're a film major, Mark is THE professor to have. He's passionate and knowledgeable about all of the content and can keep students' attention extremely well (my friends and I keep a google doc of all the wacky things he says). The workload (esp. readings) is very heavy so if you're not extremely passionate about film, be wary of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This professor was an absolute mess. He showed us graphic content without any trigger warnings. His "class discussions" revolved around him lecturing at us without power points or visual aids. He did not foster a comfortable environment and I never felt encouraged to participate. Overall, I would NOT recommend taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One the greatest classes ever taken. Readings are heavy and sometimes complex but generally managable. Two exams are not as easy but he posts review sheets for every chapter so you know what to expect. Two papers, and grades depend on GSIs. Hilarious, well-organized class, also helpful in office hours. Work hard and you'll learn a lot.

Mark Kligerman is easily one of the best professors at UMich. You can tell he cares so much about his subject and about his students. Every day of class is filled with laughs and his lectures are actually amazing. Took contemporary film theory with him and he made the class one of my favorites.

TRULY the best professor I have had in my time at Michigan. The funniest man you will ever meet and so engaging. In lectures I would hang off his every word. Take as many of Mark's classes as possible, because no professor can teach you better than he can. So knowledgable about everything TV and passionate about his students. I love this man.

Mark is an absolute gem of a professor, the type of person you want to write down at least a quote a day from the hilarious things they say. He is also such a kind individual, even if the workload is intimidating and quite difficult. Make sure to go out of your way to meet him because it goes a long way in making class easier. One of a kind.

Love Mark! Had the pleasure of taking his class last semester and this semester. Incredibly smart and eloquent, but also funny and engaging. Really sympathetic too, which is helpful considering he assigns a lot of reading. His humor is a bit eccentric and provocative, but you get used to it.

He's very funny and knows his stuff BUT there are lots of readings. You need to do the readings to do well on his exams. His lectures can be hard to follow sometimes, because he's just sooo smart. Sometimes I have to dissect what he's saying because he talks really eloquently very quickly. But I would take him again because he's very easygoing
Best prof I eva had
I'll second the crush. Mark's a great guy and is really passionate about the material. Readings were difficult, but lectures and group work helped a lot.

I've had three classes with Mark and he is such a stellar prof. Also I have a substantial crush on him. Lot's of dense reading, but he clears everything up during lecture. Took his histories, and his theory, which I thought would be dreadful, but actually really liked it. The smaller the class the better.
He's intense but a great professor.  If you keep up with the work you will do well and learn a lot.

These were two history classes (pre-New Wave and post-New Wave) and he was awesome. Really funny and very insightful. Once you get used to his style of teacher, the classes become really interesting. Highly recommended.

Kligerman is hilarious.  Has me laughing every class.  Very easy to pay attention because he's entertaining and really passionate about the topics.  The theories in class are tough but he is really helpful in breaking them down.  Two papers and he says there will be an online final.  Not too hard for and ULWR.

Awesome professor. Im a in undergrad, and Ive never taken a SAC class till 455. He loves participation, and trust me you will too. Quizzes are based on the readings for the week so READ. He wants you to do well so just do the work. Its not much. You get the same points in participation as you do on the exam and paper. LOVE KLIGERMAN!!!!

Be ready to participate if you enroll in Mark's class, he does a good job of keeping students attention and remembers all their names. His humor is unlike any professor I've had in the past. He is unafraid to give his honest opinion on any topic. Great Prof.

Mark is one of the best professors I have ever had. I took SAC272 (Classical Film Theory) and SAC355 (The Road Film) with him. I wanted to take a third class with him before I graduated but his lectures conflicted with my work. He is funny, quirky, very knowledgeable, and very interesting. But you have to be prepared. You need to do the readings.

Lectures are a great combination of high level analysis/discussion and deadpan off-kilter humor. Film and reading selections are consistently thoughtful and interesting. Makes an effort to keep the whole class engaged and participating. Very solid professor.

French Cinema: Great class. Some of the materials covered was review from various other classes, but you get to go indepth on FNW, Poetic realism, 2nd wave, occupation cinema, etc. Mark's a great teacher and really fun to talk to. I strongly recommend this class to SAC majors. He likes participation though, so have something to say.
Really funny!! You have to do the reading though or you will be totally lost. I will definitely try take Contemporary with him. But overall I would suggest the class if you're a film major!

Kligerman is clearly an intelligent teacher, and his lectures are interesting if you're prepared and can follow what he is saying. He's a nice guy who loves when you come to office hours. Pop quizzes were the worst, but participation is key and can really help a grade. really interesting guy who has a lot to say.
Funny and interesting but there's a lot to cover and the pop quizzes are brutal.
kligerman is funny as hell. his class is a lot of work, but if you love film, you'll love his class. he's a great man

What a great prof! Really willing to get to know his student and really helpful and understanding if you make an effort when confused. He says the craziest things during class- I wish i had made a quote list. Definitely the best I have had at SAC and I highly recommend him to anyone, even if you aren't a SAC major.
He is a fun guy. Often starts class off with a random statement and then sayd "just kidding." Classic theory is difficult, but Mark is a solid guy and respects you if you partcipate.

I've had better lecturers in SAC, but the class wasn't bad and Marks a really nice guy.  He knows what he's talking about, which is a plus, but I found him pretty repetitive in lecture (aka. goes over the text VERY in depth and repeats his points over and over)
Mark is a great professor, extremely engaging and knowledgeable about a plethora of topics
Mark is a great teacher. His classes are a little difficult but he is willing to help you out with anything you need.
He is a hoot!

He's so funny and interesting. I always looked forward to his class. I absolutely adore this professor! Definitely one of the best, if not THE BEST professor I have ever had. Oh yeah, and he's oddly adorable...Like David Schwimmer.
Kligerman is a solid professor
He actually made contemporary theory interesting. I hope he teaches classical again soon.
Great scifi film lineup and good class discussion. Looking forward to horror in the fall.
The best professor I have had in the film department.  He leads extremely interesting discussions, and is also a really funny guy.  I definitely want to take more classes of his if I can.
One of the best teachers I have ever had
The guy basically gave us the questions a week before the quiz. How can you be more clear? And insulting the way he looks in a public forum seems like sour grapes.

He's not a bad prof, but he's not funny, he's certainly not hot, and I've yet to be impressed by his "clarity."  Perhaps it's just this new class offered, but readings are long and arduous, lecture points are numerous and all over the place, and we were ill-prepared for the "quiz" (should've been called a test).  Not the greatest experience.
Mark's hilarious and his lectures are fun, clear, and engaging. His stories of his childhood are priceless.
Uh oh...I thought I was the only one who thoughts he was cute. I guess not! But seriously, he's made theory really interesting and accessible, so I definitely recommend this class.
Funny as hell, cute, smart, and yeah, he remembers your name the second you say it

Mark learned everyone's name the first day. Most teachers don't know our names even at the end of the semester. He's also a really good teacher. Teaches theory clearly and with great enthusiasm and insight.

Adorable, dry-humored, very intelligent teacher.  Made even the boring texts seem useful and put together a great film line-up.  I would recommend him to anyone looking for a fun way to get deeper insights into film texts.
Nice and an amazing teacher.
Dead-pan humor that can liven any lecture, a firm grasp of the material, and a very interesting film line up.  What is there not to love about this guy?  Doesn't hurt that he's sardonically adorable.

great sense of humor bordering on strange, which was definitely a plus- will ask random questions in the middle of class keeping things interesting.  work is always straightforward and many film examples are used during clas
No Comments
No Comments
Kligerman is also my hero.

Knows his stuff very well and is able to engage in relevant discussion on almost any topic.  A hilarious lecturer; often started lecture with a frank appraisal of his well-being.  Not afraid to voice his opinion on the movies he watches, but that makes him more down to earth.

Professor Riles moves through material quickly without explaining it enough. Homeworks are incredibly challenging, lengthy, and differ a lot from in class examples. Refuses to post lecture notes or videos unless you have a doctor's note, and even then only for two days. Tests were hard but more manageable than homeworks.

This class was an absolutely miserable experience. Lectures were dry and quiet. He wrote very small on the whiteboard so if you weren't sitting at 3 specific tables in the classroom you couldn't read the board. Claimed that the tests were based on the homework, but were much harder. Graded harshly too. Do not take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was unnecessarily rigid for class attendance. The work and reading was unreasonable. Office hours were useless. Also, he felt condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor. Riles never post lecture recording unless you are sick, and postpone homeworks due to the first day of holiday. Office hours are useless, each time I leave his office with more confusion than I went in. This class for sure is hard, but his midterms and final made it unecessarily hard. The final's median is 60. 15% homework and 85% exam.

a few facts:
He copy the book on the board, with indiscernible mumbling.
He would lecture on 1-7 for the first 11 weeks, and use the last 4-5 lectures to speedrun everything in chapter 8, 9, and 11.1 which are the real hard stuff.
He taught 405 many times and gives a median of B using a 32 years old guildline, despite grade inflation in every uni.

No lec notes posted, low voice, making the class experience totally a mess. The tests are very hard. Ready to challenge yourself?  His median grade of this course is never above B, while the median of this course on atlas is A-! That make sense since he is a prof who would still ask for homework on the day of the test!

if you want a prof who always smiles, speaks softly and write slowly, but you don't care about no any lec notes, very tough exams, still has hw in exam week, and has never given a median above b, then go for it. I might have done too many bad things before, i deserve this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Riles is a clever person and has extremely strong physics intuition. His lectures are fast-paced, but if you read the textbook before his lectures, you would definitely enjoy his lectures. His homeworks are a bit time consuming but they help a lot in understanding qm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: WN23. Riles is a gifted lecturer and a clever physicist. Definitely read the textbook between lectures. Practice exams and HW problems will prepare you for exams. He grades very generously, and still will curve the class. No cheat sheets allowed. He is also kind and forgiving. He is understanding of your troubles, so don't hesitate to reach out.

Riles is a very kind man and a respected physicist. His lectures are very good and offer insight beyond the textbook. The textbook *must* be read if you want to understand QM, and if you want to succeed you should read and then go to lecture. Exams are easy, just know the HW problems that you have been assigned. Cheat sheets allowed.

Keith Riles is a great lab professor, if you dont understand a concept he doesnt mind taking the time to help you get it and he always has something insightful to add about conversations about physics happening in the classroom, regardless of the topic. He explains things clearly and grading of reports is fair. Would definitely recommend

Keith is a great lecturer! His lecture style is very clear and concise - he always knows what to write on the board, and he is great at answering questions. His office hours are also super helpful, and he was always up for discussing your questions - even if they were about things in Quantum not directly related to the homework or tests. Great guy!

Riles is a pretty average teacher. He does flipped lectures and lets you practice coding for extra credit. Overall, if I had to take Physics 140 over again, I would choose Keith over any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom, so class is spent doing i-clicker questions. Youtube videos were used for homework lectures (about 20-30 minutes long). Riles makes it clear it isn't an easy course, but he is very helpful in office hours. He is a quieter, more reserved professor. Helps with coding extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom and numerical modeling (coding) used, unlike the other 140 lectures. However, the coding provides a pad to your grade and helps out a lot in the end. Riles is more of a quiet teacher but is extremely smart and has concise explanations if you talk to him in a small group or one-on-one

Professor Riles's class has a nice format with the online lectures, short Q&A session, and then practice problems. The coding assignments were also great grade boosters and fairly helpful. 80% of exam problems came from practice exams, MP, and in-class problems, which made studying much easier. Finally, Riles's demos were extremely entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Riles is great. Thought the notorious python assignments would be awful, but they give a great grade boost and aren't too bad.  Riles really knows his physics as shown by his involvement with LIGO.  Overall, it was an absolute an honor being taught by this man
I had no problem with Riles. I really liked the format of doing online lectures and problems in class. He clearly knows his stuff and can explain things fairly well when asked questions

Sure it's a difficult class, but Keith wants all of his students to learn as much as possible. Keith's class has the highest averages because of the free Python grade boosters as well. Everything in the class is reasonable and with enough effort, anyone should be able to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: You can tell that Professor Riles is really passionate about Physics. The demonstrations during lecture are engaging and the weekly programming assignments were pretty fun. He is a little quiet and reserved which can be confused for dryness or apathy but at least in my opinion he seems to really care for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My man Keith knows a ton of physics, will tell you it straight up, and will expect you to know it on the exams. That's it.

Had him for Physics 140, Newtonian Mechanics. His section is also kind of weird because we did Python coding exercises,  and were the only section to do so. So there was an additional homework assignment, but they were usually pretty easy and were like 15% of the grade. His section usually has the highest averages.

I absolutely loved Keith Riles. He was passionate and extremely willing to give extra help outside of class/office hours. VPython assignments are a piece of cake & extra credit is offered. My one recommendation is to thoroughly look over the lecture slides. That is where you'll find upcoming exam problems. Not all the slides are covered in lecture.

This classroom was a flipped. You watched daily lectures on your own and then tested those concepts via clicker questions in class. He drops around 5 clicker days, so you can miss some class. The videos were honestly not that helpful, he always made things way too complicated and it got confusing. The class also requires weekly VPython Assignments.

Very difficult intro course. Lectures are online and class is just practice problems, but attendance is mandatory. Only professor that assigns programming homework which is a nice grade boost but takes time to learn. Average test grade is usually a 60%. Join an SLC study group ASAP.

He seems like a nice enough guy however the style which he teaches has really taken the passion I had for science out of me and I am rather disappointed in his dryness with the material. Feels like first priority is his research and all else follows in suit. Strongly recommend a different professor if you're interested in science.

I don't understand what people don't like about Riles. He was my favorite professor freshman year and one of my favorite teachers ever. The class is very difficult, but the hard work is worth it to understand the interesting topics discussed. The computer homeworks are a pain, but worth it in the end. I would not change anything about this class.

Riles teaching method involving watching his lecture videos the night before and in lecture he just goes through iclicker questions, so its mandatory that you attend lecture. In my opinion, I would suggest Uher for 140. But Riles has python homework assignments that boost your grade which is nice.

Riles is a good professor who really wants you to learn, however the Numerial Modeling projects are extremely time consuming and do not help your understanding of the material. Beware of his tests--they contain normal physics questions replaced with programming questions and those questions are quite tough compared to other sections' questions.

Although his class involves programming that took extra time to do, he is a great professor and willing to help in office hours. His lectures are online that you have to watch before class and then you do clicker questions in class for participation points. The clicker questions and Python are good grade boosters because the tests are hard.

A lot of people talk bad about Keith Riles but I am extremely glad to have had him for Physics 140. I thought he was a very good professor, clearly extremely intelligent, will always help you if you have a question. Yeah lectures are just iClicker questions but it prepares you well for exams and makes you think about the problems presented.

I didn't like the recorded lectures. They were clear but if I had questions you had to wait until the next day to ask. "Lectures" consisted of answering iClicker questions. The exams are tough but if you do enough practice exams you can do well. The computer homework was super annoying but it helps your grade a lot. Mastering physics sucks too.

Riles is a great Professor and a really nice guy. Riles teaches using lectures that he makes himself on Youtube (they are super clear and really informative!) his exams are hard, but he will help you outside classes anytime. Really nice guy

Professor Riles has been one of the best professors I have had at Michigan. He is always ready to help outside of class, and you can't ell he works very hard at his job. He prepares very clear well-thought out lecture videos which I'm sure take a lot of time. Overall this class was tough and the exams were hard but Mr Riles is a great guy and prof.
i don't learn anything. he gets all his work out the book and doesn't obtain any knowledge. he is very disrespectful.

Sorry guys, but I do not recommend him. He gives Numerical Modeling labs that are a GIGANTIC waste of time and all you basically do is iClickers. That's pretty much it. And they're not very helpful when preparing for the exams. His Youtube lectures are very dry and the tests are notoriously tough. Get into Uher's class if you can.

Dr. Riles uses the reverse classroom setup, which I personally don't like. You are supposed to watch 10-30 minute videos before every lecture, which most of the class doesn't do. He mostly just goes through examples during class that you are required to answer with an i-clicker. He knows what he's talking about but I don't like the class setup.

Keith is a really nice guy, and easy to understand, but he makes you do VPython programming assignments every week that are such a hassle. Luckily, they're an easy way to boost your grade, and makes the exams worth a smaller percent of your grade than other sections. The exams were really rough. I would definitely recommend Keith though.

Modeling labs were easy. iClicker questions in class. He is a great guy and tries to help you understand, but he often tries to "brute force" solutions in class and the way he solves problems in lectures can be more complicated than necessary. Difficult class.

He really doesn't teach at all. Be prepared to try and watch some unnecessarily lengthy and dry youtube videos that he prepares to take the place of lectures. In class, it's only iclicker questions, all day, every day. Basically, I found him to be useless as a teacher, but a nice enough guy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DID NOT TAKE AP PHYSICS. His lectures are all youtube videos that he doesnt post until the sunday night beforehand. Each class had 15-30 minutes of video to watch.. (x4 = 45 min to 2 hours of video a week!) He skips explanations/ gives REALLY CONFUSING ANSWERS. His class scores 10% lower than THE COURSE AVRG on exams.

Very nice guy but not the best at explaining physics concepts. Youtube videos are clear, but he spends too long on easy examples and when the problems got more difficult we would run out of time and not figure out how to do it. His exam averages were typically lower than other sections.

Gives videos to watch beforehand so you focus on practice problems in class(familiarize concepts) - videos are 15-30 minutes long and easy to follow. Vpython programming was annoying, but 4/7 assignments have extra credit(which isn't hard if you go to office hours). Full points on all EC, grade bump of 4%! Also makes exams count less towards grade.

Physics 140 is tough, especially if you haven't had any previous experience with mechanics. Riles is a good professor, but he is not the best. His explanations can get quite sophisticated and the iClicker structure of the class is useless, students just hear other answers. The comp assignments are a time-drain, but they are worth it b/c of exams.

Keith Riles is one of the nicest and most helpful professors that I have ever had at Michigan. He is always willing to help students in office hours or meet with them outside of class. His demos are always interesting and they help students gain a good grasp of the material. Riles made 140 my favorite class of the term.

Hes a nice teacher but it seems like he doesnt realize how much harder his class is than the other physics classes. He doesnt lecture in class so you have to watch youtube videos outside of class which aren't that helpful. On top of that we have to program in vpython which is extremely hard and a waste of time. As an actual teacher hes not too bad.

I can be around a nice person, watch youtube videos and not learn vPython for free which are the sole things Riles class provides you. He does not lecture, vPython does not help students and is borderline impossible with no instruction and on average his exam scores are lower. Be prepared to work 3 times as hard in his class just for an ok grade.

He's a nice guy, but literally the worst teacher. He does not even teach. I'm not paying hundreds in tuition to be told to watch youtube videos. He skips over explanations and the ones he does give are hard to follow. Multiple times he's told me I was wrong on a clicker question so I changed my guess and my original answer had been right.

He does not give lectures in class, you must watch youtube videos before hand and all that is done is class are practice problems. The problems would be helpful if he actually explained the answers thoroughly. He often says things like "you can go over this on your own" or "you will have to know how to do this problem, but we won't go over it now".

Didn't teach. Didn't explain. "Pilot" class for python in 140. Worst idea ever. Didn't learn a thing and spent hours writing code. Okay prof if asked questions, but never even lectured in class. They were all on youtube. Aka, more homework time. Pretty useless.

very thorough. if you can adopt the thinking and methodologies he demonstrates during lecture then you'll do very well in the class. this is a very challenging course, however, and you should plan on doing ample practice problems.

Riles is a great teacher for physics but the course itself is really tough. Throughout the semester, Riles is helpful, but for the exam review, he goes over problems you already have solutions to. He's hilarious with demonstrations.

Physics is tough with Riles. He spends too much time writing problems out the "brute method" way, instead of showing the easy way to solve it. My friend and I have been able to solve problems in a few minutes while he takes 15 minutes. He gets annoying and doesn't answer student's questions. If you have AP Physics C background, you'll be okay-ish.
loved him! super clear about EVERYTHING

his lectures are worthless because he mostly wastes time simplifying problems, and the only reason you should go is for iclicker. This class is hard and you need to use the book/book problems if you want to get above a C+. Also, the homework is worthless for teaching you anything and it is just a major chore (it takes hours). Class is set up badly
This teacher is a joke. If possible take it with Uher. You might actually learn something from lecture if you take Uher.
He is an average teacher but this class is soo hard and the system that is set up is not conducive to learning take it somewhere else if at all possible, u of m physics is no good
The class is hard. Make sure you do the problems in the TEXTBOOK. I did not Professor Riles at first, but he actually is a really nice teacher.
Great professor! Willing to answer questions about practice exams at all times. It is easy to see that KR is enthralled with physics.
Was willing to answer questions and meet outside of class. 126 is harder than 125 but you shouldn't have a problem if you do practice exams and either pay attention or read the book.

Professor Keane is really chill and explains the lectures very clearly. The first two exams are harder than the final (which was all mcq), but overall fine if you study. Make sure to ask gsi's for homework help throughout the semester.

John is a GREAT instructor, however, the class SUCKED. Do not take this class if you do not have to. They made everything so much harder than it needs to be. They recently changed the curriculum because people were passing too well. All our exam class averages were like 50 and 60%. The way they explain the material is odd.
He sometimes goes really quickly over hard material and spends more time on easy stuff. The class itself is pretty easy though, you can do pretty badly on the exams and keep a good grade.

Organizes tough subjects and concepts into concise notes containing clear examples to further your understanding of said concepts. He is also very kind and easygoing. If you need to take STATS 250, would highly recommend him.

Absolutely loved Prof Keane he's super nice and responsive to any questions plus you can tell that he knows what he's talking about. I highly recommend him for stats regardless of if you've had experience with it and def do the ACTIVE approach for BOTH lab and lecture my grade was significantly higher bc of it. Overall 10/10 prof love him

John Keane is one of my favorite instructors I have had not only at Michigan but in the entirety of my academic career. He clearly knows his content well and is very capable of communicating this knowledge to his students. I like that he doesn't just read slides word for word–– his class is more interactive and easier to remain engaged.

I loved Keane as a professor! He was very accessible outside of class, just email him. He's so kind and so funny. His lectures were easy to follow with his guided notes. Ask questions if you're confused. Very accommodating to students who need it.

I was dreading taking this course until the first day of class when Professor Keane's presence alone showed me that everything will be okay. This class was hard but I know I learned a lot, so credit to Professor Keane for making such difficult material digestible even at 8:30 am.

LOVE LOVE LOVE!!! Dr. Keane is an amazing professor, lecturer, and all around great guy. Lectures were clear and entertaining and he provided adequate feedback. Class itself isn't difficult as long as you do the work. Highly recommend.

I didn't always attend lecture in person due to being a traditional approach student and having an exceptionally busy semester, but I felt the instruction was excellent in both online and in–person formats. Dr. Keane is very eloquent and explains topics that can be very nebulous with concrete examples.
Absolutely fantastic professor. Super knowledgeable about the subject matter and teaches clearly and engagingly. Would love to take another class with him.

Lectures are super easy to follow along with, practice exams and concepts packets are helpful in preparing for the exams, homework/pre-works/group works are reasonable and not overly difficult, amazing course overall

Probably one of the best professors I've had at UofM. Lectures were clear and easy to follow. Exams can definitely be a little tricky as there is very specific wording to use on short-answer questions; however, your grade is cushioned with homework and lecture activities. All in all, great course!

this guy rocks! stats 250 gets a bad rap here, but because keane's lectures were so clear, I spent little time studying outside of class. the exams are difficult, but luckily there is extra credit and homework/lab points that give enough cushion to get a good grade.

Dr. Keane is very eloquent and a good lecturer. I have never taken stats before, but with Dr. Keane, it was doable. Also, do not be scared about coding or R Studio; there is almost no coding, you just need to plug in numbers into equations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just like the other ratings, chill prof, great lectures. The first two exams were slightly harder than I expected, but the final was significantly easier. There isn't a textbook, but there is a note packet. The packet helps w learning concepts, but not with keeping them retained.

Not having a textbook make studying harder. Lectures were VERY clear. In-lecture examples were often so well explained that I only felt the need to watch one. Lab assignments were less daunting than I expected them to be---really not a problem at all, as long as you use office hours.
John Keane is an amazing teacher! I enjoyed going to his lecture every Tuesdays and Thursdays, and never found it boring ever.
Great professor who truly knows and loves the material is teaching. He also has a sweet dog! Highly recommend!

Professor Keane makes his lectures interactive, and his notes are very clear and organized. The weekly homework and group work reinforce concepts we learned in lecture. Overall, a great professor to have, very communicative and excellent at teaching.
Dr. Keane was an amazing professor who clearly cares about his students! He's a real one. 10/10 would recommend to a friend.

Professor Keane is one of the most helpful professors I had. He throughly explaining any questions I had. Groupwork, prework, labs, and case studies were easy. Make sure to watch lectures, but if you watch those you should be able to do great on the tests! Also an A is considered a 90% and above, and they round to the nearest whole percentage.
Great class, taught by Professor Keane. He makes class engaging and the content easy to understand. I enjoyed taking the class with him.

John Keane is a really good professor and explains things very well, the actual class content was the issue for me. Lecture, homework, and case studies focused on applying the information learned in lecture, but the exams themselves were purely conceptual, and you applied little to nothing. Study the concepts and watch the lectures.
stats 250 goat. gonna miss jkeane!

John gives baller lectures. They are very informative about the content we need to know in class. Paying attention and following in the notes is an excellent way to learn in class. Take this guy if you can.

John Keane was put on this earth by god to lecture stats 250. The entire 300 person section was enamored by him. For many people its the only qualitative reasoning class they will take in undergrad and he's well aware of this.  The content digestible without sacrificing material.
stats 250 goat, i'm not even in his section and I go to his lectures instead + he answers every question well

Professor Keane was always enthusiastic and clear with his instruction. I did not expect to feel as engaged and interested in this course's material as I ended up being. It is undoubtedly a useful class for anyone who is going to deal with any type of statistical analysis in the future, including pre–med students like myself.
I felt this course was taught very well. Despite being expedited with spring term, I still felt that I understood all the content very clearly.

Best lectures ever. John Keane is an incredible speaker and there was never a dull moment in his classes. He is sensitive to levels of student understanding and genuinely wants every student to succeed. Would definitely recommend this professor.
The quality of instruction in this course was very high, and I really enjoyed the lectures. Everything was explained clearly and thoroughly.

Although I was not excited to take this class and would not say I am excelling in it, Keane is by far the best math lectuer I have ever had, and did a great job conveying information and overall did a great job leading the class.

Great professor who explained concepts clearly. Heavy workload. GO TO OFFICE HOURS to compare HW answers w/ GSIs, select the ACTIVE lecture/lab approach, & do ALL the extra credit to maximize points! Only reason I was able to get A. Stats is a difficult subject but Dr. Keane makes it significantly more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was a great professor. He covered each topic remarkably, and I felt like I walked away with few questions, if any. If you do have questions, I highly recommend the Piazza! I will say the first half of the semester is basically AP Stats, so it was a breeze for me.

Best course I've taken at Michigan. He's is an excellent professor and a great person. He's engaging and genuinely super helpful. He wants his students to succeed and does such a great job of teaching the material. I took AP Stats in high school and still thought he had such fantastic extra insights to add even though I knew most of the material.

Great lecturer. Funny and upbeat. Very engaging. Course pack is mandatory, but not helpful on its own, so go to lecture or watch the recordings. Many small assignments tally up to 15-25% of your grade depending on the course approach you select. I recommend doing the active approach to limit exam stress and get good practice problems for exam prep.

Dr. Keane is a very nice guy! Very upbeat, enthusiastic, and caring. The grading on the other hand is an absolute nightmare. Spend as much time as you can on practice problems for the exams (which never follow the practice exam format). UNDERSTAND the concepts and go to office hours weekly for homework and help. It's manageable but very tough!
Decent Lecturer with somewhat entertaining lectures. Graders for this course are very harsh.

Professor Keane is an amazing lecturer! He is very thorough and understandable. I took Active approach for lectures during the whole semester and thought it was helpful to my understanding of the material. A little bit almost everyday made homework and exam quite easy. Totally recommend!!

if you're doing active approach (going to lecture for credit) TAKE KEANE!! if not, you can watch his lectures anyway so it doesn't really matter. he's always enthused, and the class is a really easy A especially with the grading scheme

Prof Keane was amazing! If you have to take STATS250 make sure you take it with him! He is super kind and explains material very clearly. Choose active approach and he walks around and answers questions during that time. If you're lucky, he brings his dog before exams! He was one of the best profs I've had at Umich.

John Keane is a great professor. Stats is a hard course but he makes it interesting and easier to understand. The grading is clearly explained, and it's not hard to get an A or B in this class. Advice: choose active approach, it allows for more room to better your grade and it doesnt take much time at all!

Prof. Keane was a great lecturer who explained things very clearly. He always took care to ask every couple of minutes "what questions do you have so far?", and was always around before and after lecture to help students with their assignments. He has a fun personality and even brought his dog to class a few times. Would recommend.

I LOVE JOHN KEANE. He's one of the best professors at the University of Michigan, especially for first-year students.  His knowledge is invaluable and provides clarification whenever you need. His lectures are very active, and he encourages students to participate frequently to enhance learning. I 100% recommend taking STATS 250 with him.

JOHN KEANE IS THE BEST. He is such an amazing lecturer, he is so clear about what he is saying and explains everything so well. The course content itself isn't too hard, as long as you put in the work to learn the content and study for the exams. Teacher-wise, I wished Keane would teach all of my classes because he is awesome.
He was amazing. A lot of extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gives you a choice between active/passive lecture and lab participation, but I would choose active. Very good lecturer, with lots of energy at 8am.

Professor Keane was a great instructor and very friendly. He always had great energy, even at 8:30 am, which really showed his passion about the course and desire to help students. I enjoyed taking his class and learned a lot.
He's smart and personable. Good class. Annoyed I had to take 250 since I took AP Stats, but that's not his fault.

John Keane manages to teach a subject matter, I have no interest in learning about, in a format that keeps me coming back for more. If all classes could be instructed in the way John Keane does, I would be a better student.

Dr. Keane is an outstanding lecturer! Wow, he is very articulate and has clearly invested effort into making each concept clearly understood. He is personable, approachable, and very effective at answering questions. I really appreciated how he would turn our questions around or provide an analogy to encourage us to think more about the concepts.

If you can take Professor Keane, absolutely do so! He was born to teach and makes the content so easy to understand, coming from a student who's never taken a stats course. However, I will warn you that there is a lot of homework and assignments that go along with this class; stay on top of it and go to office hours for help if you fall behind!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: THE GOAT. Dr. Keane's lectures were engaging and very understandable, and I enjoyed the class quite a lot. He's very friendly and incredibly well prepared for lecture. If you're intimidated, STATS 250 is sometimes hard but I would recommend taking the active approach and going to lectures, because groupwork is a lot of the times just free points.

Prof Keane is a fun lecturer. He is very theatrical and knows how to keep up interest. Class has a ton of hw which you should def go to office hours to get help with and active approach is basically free points and forces you to go to class which you should anyway.  Exams are hard so make sure to do well on lab/hw by going in person.

I was nervous about STATS 250 because I had never taken a statistics course and I had heard stories about the course difficulty. I know people who have dropped out of the university in part because of this course. I was completely surprised. It IS a workload and the content is foreign to me, but Keane is an incredible instructor.

He managed to make stats actually interesting at 8:30 in the morning, he felt like my peppy soul cycle instructor and it was awesome. He funny, uses time efficiently, and explains things well, love that guy!

Professor Keane is an amazing lecturer. For 8:30 in the morning, he has great energy and makes sometimes-boring topics more engaging and entertaining. I would 100% recommend taking this course with him.
he's a really good lecturer - from pacing, flow, tone, etc. - if youre attentative.
Super engaging lectures and very down to business. No time wasted. Bonus: he talks super clearly and crisp so you can speed up his lecture 2.5x and still understand every word. 100% love this guy

Professor Keane is easily one of the best lecturers I've ever had which is crazy to say about a statistics course. He somehow managed to make stats engaging and digestible at 10am. He's the type of lecturer that would inspire someone to switch their major, so if you have the chance take STATS 250 with him.

If you are taking 250, TAKE KEANE! Everyone w/ other professors watches his lectures too! His explanations are always so clear and understandable for someone who isn't good at math/has no stats background. Also, choose active learning for EASY points. Yes, you have to go to the lecture, but it was so worth it for my grade at the end.
John Keane is pretty goated he is a very good teacher who is very well spoken. Nothing more he could've done as a professor to make the class better 5 stars for him!!

GOAT. Super engaging. Makes content actually super interesting. I do not like stats but I really enjoyed the way this class was set up and the way Keane teaches. The 8:30 lecture is so worth it. Take the active approach and go to class, it will help you so much.
Keane is the GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am very fond of Prof. John Keane and his teaching style. He is extremely clear and engaging. I would be lying if I told you that going in I expected to enjoy lecture, but Prof. Keane has done a fantastic job at making the class genuinely interesting without deviating from the material.

Dr. Keane is probably one of the best professors that I have had at UofM. He speaks so clearly and explains the concepts very well. If it wasn't for him, this class would've been very tedious.
