If he's teaching the class, I'd recommend doing the traditional method because if you understand the concepts in class, you will have no problem in the exam.

best lecturer for stats 250. made hard material easy to understand. if you're not math oriented and have to take this for a prereq, take Keane! His office hours are great and doesn't make you feel stupid. 100% recommend.

Yes, a lot of materials are covered in each lecture and the workload is not low, but he is definitely a good lecturer. He explains concepts pretty well, and I find his lectures easy follow. Just don't learn the materials in the last minute and you'll be fine. To be honest, as long as you keep up with the work, this course is an easy A.

The class was very well structured and Prof. Keane was always prepared for class. I would recommend finding a good group of people to sit next to as group work makes up a large part of your grade if you choose the route that makes your grade less test-percentage heavy.

STATS 250 was not an intro course. As someone who hasn't ever taken a stats class, this class was VERY difficult for me. While Prof. Keane was nice, the class size is so big that most of the time you end up going to the GSI's for help. Sometimes he explained things well and other times he could be very confusing and I had to resort to YouTube.

Prof Keane is an amazing lecturer and explains every concept thoroughly. If you show up to class and take notes using the course pack it is very easy to succeed in my opinion. I did the active learning approach and I would recommend going this route if you plan on coming to lecture, there is ample time dedicated in each lecture to finish group work

Professor Keane is a great person and his lectures are very engaging. The content is not difficult, but there are quite a few assignments, so you need to stay on top of your work. The exams were not super difficult either, and are much easier if you study using the homework and practice exams. Overall great professor and very manageable class.

I absolutely loved Professor Keane's teaching style! He explained difficult statistics concepts in a clear manner and made sure to reiterate concepts. That being said, this course had too many assignments: weekly homework and labs, essays, pre work and lecture group work, tests. But, it is definitely a doable and easy class!

NOT AN EASY A. Way too many assignments every week and exams are pretty hard. Also extra credit doesn't help at all (max 1-2%). Was just at the cutoff of an A- and A (like so many people) and they don't curve so yay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Keane is an amazing professor. I highly recommend the active learning approach he offers along with attending lectures, as he really does a great job of explaining the material in a concise manner. I have never taken stats before this course, and I don't think I would have done as well with a different professor. There is also ample extra credit.

Professor Keane is an amazing teacher, all though I do struggle with anything dealing with math he did a good job explaining it to me so I could understand. He has met with me after class to talk about my fears and he has given me very good advice which helped me tremendously if I enjoyed math I would take his class again!
Probably the best professor I've had at UMICH guy loves the subject and is one of the most concise lecturers I've ever had.

The lectures are very content heavy, really hard if you have it at 8:30 am :( Stats is a lot of work be prepared to spend so much time in office hours to get any work done. The homework is hard and the class examples aren't always super helpful.

This class is really enjoyable with Keane as your professor. He makes sure to check-in with students about questions and the class in general is really easy to understand and get a good grade in as long as you do extra credit and the work. The class is work heavy so be prepared to spend some time on assignments.

Funny, very enthusiastic and clearly passionate about the subject. Attending/watching lectures is important because he walks through slides and notes during lecture but the slides are still left blank in canvas, so you won't have the answers to topics/practice problems unless you watched lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Stats 250 overall is very annoying - weekly homeworks and lab work. However, Keane makes is more enjoyable. He is obviously very passionate and will go through multiple examples throughout the lecture to give you a sense of how to apply the equation/test and not just leave you to figure it out by yourself

STATS 250 is annoying not because it has hard material, but mostly because of all the annoying busy work they give. However, Professor Keane makes this class a lot more enjoyable. He is obviously very passionate about statistics, but he doesn't overcomplicate anything. His lecture are clear and prepared. He helps out a lot during class exercises.

Professor Quist is a great guy who has a true passion for teaching. We would do beginning questions every class to get to know our section better, which I enjoyed. Overall, he cared a lot about the students' well-being and I highly recommend him to anyone. I had him for STRAT390, which is a section class, but would take any class of his.
ts pmo shlawg

Kramer Quist is by far the best professor I've had in my time at Umich. He puts in more time and effort than any other professor, and it shows in his lectures. I would take any class you can with this GOAT.

I had Professor Quist for STRAT 290. The class was quite interesting and much better than I thought it would be on day 1, though the consulting project could sometimes be annoying. He is very knowledgeable and took class discussions in interesting directions.
Kramer is the man and I would take this class every semester if I could.

Kramer is very knowledgeable on this topic, and the class is super interesting. He doesn't allow electronics, so be prepared for that. Participation is very important and he may cold call you. Not too much homework besides readings and pre-class assignments. Group project wasn't bad, but the exams were pretty difficult.

Chinmaya often seemed dismissive toward underperforming students, which created an uncomfortable learning environment. I also found his speaking style difficult to follow, and I felt that lectures focused too much on personal research and internships rather than the actual course material. Overall, I would not recommend this instructor.

Chinmaya is a nice person, but not suited to be a teacher. He is 10-15 min late every lecture, and talks very fast and in circles. Does not explain anything terribly well. If anything, I would not go to lecture and just try to learn on your own. Good Luck.

Among my section Chinmaya was very controversial, but I very much enjoyed him. I do feel like he sometimes over-complicates things, but he has taught me to think about math and problem-solving in a new and profound way. He was also very fun to joke around with. He is ALWAYS late though, but only by about 5-10 minutes.

Professor Kausik is probably the worst Math professor I've ever had. Calculus I should not be made as confusing, which is partly the course coordinator's fault, but it's just a course that is so horribly structured. Kausik talks extremely fast, trips over his own words, and confuses himself and the entire class. Just avoid taking Calc I here at all
Tests are hard (average on mcq of a test was 33/40, which is the same level as an weeder eecs class test median)

Don't take this for R/E credit; there are other easier courses. Very rigorous group project due around the same time as the final, the tests have alot of content. The class isn't super hard, but a burden if you have other hard classes.
marked my inclass assignment for ai, when i was in class and did it truthfully. slow on grading. not super hard to get A but exams aren't super easy either.

Don't take this class to fulfill an easy requirement. She makes the class difficult - there are ZERO unexcused absences - only mini lecture assignments that you can get late credit, the group project barely has points so even if you do bad on the exam it won't help. The exams are so difficult, even if you study questions are niche and nit picky.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stuckey is a good professor, and this class makes getting an A very attainable. She doesn't take attendance in lecture, but if you miss a class, you will be confused/behind.
LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE HER. TAKE THIS CLASS

I absolutely adore Dr. Stuckey. She was the most fabulous way to start my morning! She is engaging, clear, and her class is structured so easily to understand. It has some work and reading, but all entirely manageable. She is so helpful, and if I could retake WGS 325, I would.

Professor Stuckey is so lovely. I was always happy to start my day with her class; lectures were engaging and fun and you can tell how passionate she is about what she teaches. The class was relaxed and enjoyable and I learned a ton. I highly recommend you take a class with Professor Stuckey if you can!

Professor Stuckey was kind and engaging, and she and the GSIs care about students. Lecture recordings must be obtained from her, so attending lecture is pretty necessary for doing well on exams. Exams are detailed but not bad if you pay attention in class. The group project was a little tedious but interesting, and you have a lot of freedom.

took for an easy race an ethnicity credit; but it was NOT! worked on a long, consuming group project throughout the whole semester (i don't like group projects), exams were long, and she tried to convince you to revolve your life around anthropology. i suggest any other r&e credit

Great professor overall, very passionate and caring. Super easy class as long as you go to lecture. The only tough thing is the group project, but even that's really that bad. You don't need the textbook, just do the other readings, but she usually goes over them in class anyways.

This isn't an easy A. Going to lectures and doing the assignments is big (I missed a couple early, and it dropped my grade by 4% at the end). The exams aren't bad, but studying is a maze. No material was given other than a sheet with topics on it. However, she gives out a lot of extra credit near the end of the semester to raise the course avg.

I never showed up to half of the lectures, the other half I didn't pay attention to, and I didn't read the textbook. I still got an A. The only time I had extensive work was for exams where I had to cram study ~10 hours to get an A, that might be a con for a lot of people, but it's something that works for me. Good class, I just have ADHD, lol.

Really great prof. Very kind and you can tell that she genuinely enjoys teaching. Lectures were engaging and easy to follow. Ethnography project is a bit of a pain but you're at least given a lot of creative freedom. Quite a few reviews touching on exam difficulty but it seems pretty standard - if not easier - compared to other classes.

Im convinced everyone giving 3 and below are just LAZY. Exams r extremely easy if you pay attention in lectures just write down things on the slides provided. I barely did any of the readings just paid attention when they were reviewed in class. Barely any assignments and plenty of E.C. opps. Its a 100 lvl class and that is reflected appropriately!

She makes class really interesting & has enthusiasm. You can do well in the course but need to really write down everything from lectures because you're tested on small details. The project is cool, but its unfair that other profs have an easier final assignment from what I've heard, wish I'd known that.  If you want an easy class, take a diff prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Stuckey is kind and enthusiastic about her class. I took Anthro101 mainly for the HU/R+E credit, but it was actually pretty interesting. Slides are posted if you don't go to lecture. Readings and review materials are easy, and I found the exams to be about the same. Final project is a little dense, not awful. Some extra credit. Overall good.

This professor made a 100 level course feel like a 400 level course. I took this class as an easy distribution credit, but ended up stressing over this class far more than my other classes. Take Anthrcul 101, but not with this professor. She is very sweet, but blamed our low test scores on the pandemic (which makes no sense).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ok, so class is really interesting and the prof has good energy. I learned a lot BUT she expects you to basically dedicate your life to her (intro) class. tests are hard & graded harshly. For final project: I've heard other professors have a writing assignment or something easy, not a full on project. While it is a cool project, it is A LOT of work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is not the content one should be learning or expected to understand for a 101 class. Tests are tough and expectations are not made clear. Content is not accessible outside of class.

Do not take anthro 101 if you want an easy or even medium class. The lectures pour an insane amount of info on you, readings are unreasonably long and boring, and exam review materials are a joke compared to how hard the tests are. Fought for my life in this call while getting an easy A in calc 1. (like bro what)

She makes the exams super test heavy and she gives so much content in a 101 class to the point where it's frustrating. The exams are super specific while lectures are extremely broad. The lecture has barely any structure and it's so frustrating. It's not only me who feels this way I have talked to so many people this class that are frustrated also

I felt like Stuckey was really invested in all of our semester long projects and was eager to help us succeed, and also committed to making us all comfortable participating in class discussions which make up most of class. great course if interested in anthro and ethnography. guest speakers were also interesting and relevant

This class was amazing (her lectures), but honestly, your grade depends on who your GSI is. They grade so harshly and the exams are reasonable but a little frustrating because of how short time we had and how much they expected.

Everyone needs to take Childbirth & Culture!! I thought Leigh did a good job teaching, and the information she taught is so important for everyone to know. There's only a midterm, final, a small final project, and section participation. All grading is done by GSIs, and mine wasn't super great so that was frustrating. Overall, a super great class!

Prof. Stuckey is such a wonderful lecturer. She brought so much genuineness and personality into the class. I would recommend Childbirth & Culture to anyone. It was reading heavy and attendance helped a lot (but not mandatory). You can't really glean what you need for the exams from the Google slides so take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE HER CHILDBIRTH AND CULTURE CLASS!! Prof. Stuckey is amazing and Anthrcul 325 was literally life-changing. Her lectures are incredible and so interesting. She is very responsive to student feedback and encourages participation in a variety of ways. There's a lot of reading, but as long as you skim & go to lecture you'll be fine. 1000/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved learning from Professor Stuckey. She is clearly passionate about what she teaches. The class wasn't easy, you have to work for your grade, but I really enjoyed all of it (save for how long we spent on the topic of bones, but that's just not my thing.) I highly recommend this class.

Prof. Stuckey had such good vibes and turned me from a potential anthro minor to an anthro major!! She def assigns tons of readings that are sometimes repetitive/kind of irrelevant but otherwise I love her!

Dr. Stuckey has been an amazing professor. She is kind, and cares about her students. Her lectures are very interesting and engaging, I wish I would have taken this class sooner, she truly sparked my interest in anthropology and childbirth. The only downside is the readings, some of them are very similar and she assigns a lot of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoy this class and Stuckey is a great professor. Lectures and content are interesting. It is reading heavy as to be expected but you can get away with skimming or even skipping, just brush up before tests. Most reading content is covered in lectures. Some might find this class biased but I think it provides a new perspective.

Dr. Stuckey is super knowledgeable & definitely knows her stuff, but she was not a great prof. When students participated in class discussions, she'd sometimes make unnecessary snarky comments. She wrote really discouraging feedback for some of the essays I wrote. I stopped reading feedback on my papers after having her as a prof bc of the anxiety
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Stuckey was a wonderful professor and lecturer. She covered incredible topics in her childbirth and culture course and even brought on some very interesting guest lecturers. This course helped me identify my career goals and passions. Content was emotional at times but she did a fantastic job covering it. Highly recommend her for this course!

Do not listen to people who say anthro 101 is an easy A. Exams are very difficult and averages were low. This class was so disorganized. No cohesive plan for discussion sections. Some GSI's gave out weekly graded assignments and others never gave a single assignment. Extremely dry and boring class. I didn't learn a thing all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Stuckey is a great lecturer, her class is SO interesting, and above all she is incredibly considerate of students. I had some personal issues arise that really affected my midterm and she was so kind in trying to accomodate me and allowed me an additional opportunity to showcase what I knew. I appreciated her as an instructor so much. Take 325!!

There's a textbook but you don't need it. She assigns readings that are discussed in class. She provides study guides so if you study you'll be fine. For the last weeks, she assigns easy 250-350 writing assignments instead of an exam. The group project can be annoying but that's any group project. She encourages us to reach out but I never had to.
Worst professor takes 3 weeks to grade exams
Easy class but trying to convince all students to be anthropologists throughout the class got really annoying
Forced us to do a group project for the final and randomized groups giving us no control over the final project
Dull Lecturer, who gives inaccurate info

You don't need to buy the textbook, just look at the slides for lecture. If you're looking for a blowoff, you'll be fine as long as you go to discussion and get the assignments on time. Know everything on the study guides and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Stuckey was very knowledgeable in her field. Lectures were always informative and helpful. She is a diehard NC fan so beware Duke fans. You don't really have to read the textbook as the exams cover the lectures and separate readings. I took this strictly for the R&E credit but ended up finding some interest in Anthro thanks to the class.

Took this class to fulfill the race and ethnicity requirement but ended up liking the material. Professor Stuckey is awesome. We didn't have actual quizzes but we had a short writing assignments every week which was pretty easy (150 words or less) & we had a few days to do it. I didn't do any of the readings and still passed with an A-

I could never connect with her as a professor. If you are not extremely passionate about ethnographic methods, you will suffer and I definitely wouldnt recommend this class. During last two weeks of class, you have to write a 25 page paper. It was very overwhelming. The best part about this class was the engagement from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took this class for credit but I ended up really enjoying the material. This is one of the few classes where the professor made the class enjoyable and engaging online. There were no exams this semester which was super nice too, just a big project at the end of the semester. Definitely recommend this class and Stuckey.

Professor Stuckey was so passionate, engaged, and fun during lectures that you couldn't help but become interested in the material. Exams were based on exactly what was covered and emphasized, so they were super easy to study for and do well on (coming from a poor test-taker). Grading for everything is also very lenient.

Prof. Stuckey was absolutely fantastic. Prof. Stuckey so caring and understanding I 100% recommend her. There were no exams in the online format of the class and she made gave a reasonable amount of assignments so there were plenty of opportunities to raise your grade if need be. Take her class!
She was very nice, caring, and fair. Her lectures were always interesting, and the class is very doable. I would highly recommend.

Quite understanding during COVID and gave weekly writing assignments instead of exams which was nice. Brief reviews of readings and lectures will get you by for these but the content and her experiences are pretty interesting so I'd recommend watching them all.

Leigh and my GSI Eryn were AMAZING. Love love love them so much. Class was super easy with 250-350 word writing assignments based on lecture due every week. Thoroughness +clarity+organization 10/10. Longer papers were graded quite easily with effort/creativity reflecting grade. Learned so much in this class, it was super inspiring <3
Great professor, would definitely take again if given the chance.

I'm gonna be straight forward. She's a nice lady, but she's a bad professor. Extremely dry material and boring lectures. She's an extreme leftist so beware of that when enrolling for the course. Get ready for a lot of trash units about "toxic masculinity" and all of that trash stuff that UMich so heavily tries to push onto us. I would avoid Anthro.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the first class that I have taken where I felt like the instructor genuinely cared about students' success. The GSIs were also super helpful. She incorporates videos in her lectures and this helps to make the class more enjoyable than it already is. She gives study guides for the exams, and they are SUPER helpful! Favorite class thus far!

Leigh is such a sweet person and is really good at lecturing. Lecture slides as well as most videos/movies watched in lecture are posted online but I have noticed she generally goes into further detail in lecture than just what is on the slides. The GSI's were phenomenal and really set us up to excel in the class.

I loved taking Professor Stuckey's class! The only class where I actually liked doing the readings because they were relevant and interesting. She is a great lecturer, and also shows lots of relevant/funny videos to illustrate her points. Great prof!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Lei tended to spend 5-10 minutes speaking about a single slide that had a handful of bullet points on it. This made it very difficult to follow along and stay engaged. On average, only one student asks or answers a question every 2-3 weeks, which makes lectures dull.
Worst professor I've ever had at uni, so unaccomodating and explains concepts at such a high level it is hard to follow. Test questions differ from hw assignments and there is barely any practice.

This is possibly the worst professor I've ever taken a course with, despite the fact that he is quite knowledgeable about the concepts, he is awful at explaining them. If you ask him any questions, he'll respond to you with a scuff as if you're stupid for even asking him. Run, don't walk.

Qin obviously is one of the most educated finance professors at Ross, but that precisely might be his downfall. The lectures are dense and very technical, and he seemingly has little care about how his students perceive his lecture style or teaching methods. His voice is difficult to listen to, which makes everything worse.

The worst BBA professor I've had. His voice is grating, and he chose to explain things from a very academic perspective that was too applicable to real-world examples. His lectures lacked details, and his in-class problems did not reflect the exams. Exams were online, no partial credit, and our exam grades were consistently in the 60% range.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst Ross professor I've had in my undergrad BBA career thus far. His voice is grating and unnerving, and he explains things academically rather than using real-life, applicable examples. His lecture slides lack detail, and his example problems and homework do not reflect the exams. The exams are online with no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lei is clearly an intelligent man who knows finance, but he fails to clearly articulate concepts discussed in class and often rambles. DO NOT take finance with him - unclear syllabus and exams account for 80% of your grade. Sends you way too many emails and does not use Canvas.

Easily the WORST professor I've ever had. He truly doesn't know what he's doing. Our overall class median was a 66% and exams are worth 80% of your grade. No partial credit, and definitely no extra credit. I read the book and understand the concepts—but it doesn't matter, the exams will test you in ways he didn't prepare you. Truly terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid taking this class with him unless you want to learn how to use the financial calculator and not excel. Professor clearly knows what he is talking about and is very smart but one of the hardest classes I've taken at ross and no excel made it more annoying. 4 midterms, 3 worth 40% and final one worth 40% on its own, lots of homework
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE FIN 300 WITH HIM. He only lets you use a financial calculator for exams, no Excel. The final is worth disproportionately more than the other exams. Also, his voice is grating which makes watching and listening to lectures unbearable. Really one of the worst classes I've taken at UM.

Though Qin obviously is an expert and is well organized, his lectures are so difficult to follow and he goes on tangents that leave us lost. He sometimes comes off as passive-aggressive, though I don't think he intends to. I taught myself most of the material and don't think I gained as much knowledge as I should've given this class's importance.

Great professor in terms of getting the content across. Accessible outside of class as well, and includes relevant examples in class that helps you understand how to apply formulas, etc. Test averages are relatively low, but the class is curved and you get to drop an exam if you do all the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took awhile ago when class was online. He deliberately lied to me about participation - said if you watch every lecture within 24 hrs of the recording, you get full points. I did this and still got screwed. When I confronted him at the end of the semester, he said he "didn't want people to game the system." This should be grounds for leave.

1.He will be mad at you if you do not follow his plan which you simply don't know in the first place.
2.The real exams are hard and he doesn't want to provide any resources for you to practice those hard questions. 
3.His lectures are confusing. For quick and full understanding, I have to refer Investopia, which explains 100 times better than him.

Not accessible outside of class. Got angry at me because I waited for half an hour outside his office and ended up telling me to leave before I could ask a question. You can tell he's smart but he's pretty bad at lecturing and the exams are nothing like the lecture material or practice problems.

DO NOT recommend at all. The professor is okay to reach out during your class time, but whenever you want to talk to him to ask for suggestions for your study or anything that is outside of the class scope, he will definitely not help you at all and will not respond to you. Never care about his student and be prepared to get no response from him.

FIN 475 is one of the most frustrating courses I've taken in my four years here. He often fails to explain difficult concepts intuitively. To make things worse, he spends little time covering formulas that are heavily tested (often without examples) but chooses to go off on tangents that add little depth/value (news headlines).
Difficult and outdated material. Can't explain concepts clearly.

He says "Which implies that" a lot but often fails to really explain what he's talking about. His explanations are subpar at best and often leave you more confused. This is supposed to be an introduction to Finance but the pace and how lucid the explanations are do bring about frustration. If taking this class, be prepared to be left confused

Some of the worst lectures I've ever attended. He moves way too fast, and doesn't explain things as he goes on. His lectures are him talking to the screen the whole time, with no engagement of the audience and no expression at all. I found this class very hard to follow and the exams are extremely difficult and all had low averages.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: FIN 302 is a great class for anyone who wants to explore business/finance. Professor Lei's lectures are quite fast-paced, and it might be easy to get lost during them. However, he does a great job introducing complex topics. To really grasp the material, read the chapters IN DETAIL and do all the HW problems twice. Not too difficult if you do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His content and exams are hard so study the lectures and do practice problems extensively before the exam. He does allow you to have a cheat sheet for the exams, so be sure to write down all the key formulas and concepts on it.

Very organized professor. Wants students to do well. However, kind of more work than usual for a 3 credit class. Moves kind of fast in that a lot of material is covered but stay on top of lectures and spread out your studying and itll be a very rewarding class. The practice problems help but it helps having a conceptual understanding from lectures

This class isn't super hard but Qin doesn't help his students out a lot. He rarely covers all of the material in lecture so it falls on students to learn themselves. His lecture slides are confusing and his explanations are vague. Discussions help with calculations. Mandatory attendance is terrible because lectures are useless. Wouldn't recommend

Great professor, questionable exams. Heavy on MC which I dislike. Mandatory attendance. Very easy material if you try to somewhat study or have past experience in finance. Reminiscent of ECON101 in that the material is easy but exams make it seem difficult. Kind of strange exposition of options I'd say. Cares about you and course website is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Qin Lei is the most organized prof I've ever had, and you can tell he cares about the subject material and his students. Mandatory attendance is annoying. The class is also very math-heavy, and as such can be tough for some students, but it is also very fair- you get out what you put into this class.

Fin 302 is challenging, but manageable if you study enough. The exams are tough. However, Qin Lei is one of the best professors I've had at Michigan. He is very organized and teaches well. The best thing about him is how much he cares about his students. Have questions? He will spend as much time needed to explain. Need anything? Email & he helps

This class is difficult, especially the exams, & his lectures can be boring. But he is a great and organized professor. You can drop an exam if you get a 100% on all of the online hw. I put that he was caring because one time I got a 95% on the hw and emailed him asking if I could still drop one. He said "do not worry" so he cares about students

He's a good professor but I don't like the structure of this class. Two one hour lectures and one discussion is not enough time to over content.I feel like I am teaching myself the entire course, because of how fast it goes. The tests are also designed in a way where you can either do really well or really bad

One of the smartest, most professional, and organized professors i've ever had. Speaks fast in lectures but offers so much outside help and resources. Learned a lot! 4 exams but you get to drop 1 exam which is really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Qin is very organized, respected, and straight forward in his approach to the class. He has a great website, where he hosts everything you need to be successful in the class. He is VERY responsive and helpful if you need it.
Such a nice professor that cares about student. Willing to help. You can count on him. Cool guy.

Dr. Lei is an incredibly smart guy.  His class is well-organized, and his communication with his students is fantastic.  The nature of the class can be somewhat difficult, but Dr. Lei generally does a good job of presenting/working through the material.  The tests are not easy but are fair.  There is homework, but it is not very time consuming.

Professor Lei is extremely passionate about his teaching and his course. He provides so many opportunities for his students to succeed and truly cares. One of the best professors I've had at Michigan. Class is extremely useful. Michigan alum, too!

If I went to lecture without doing the readings, I would feel lost and confused. But if you do the readings, lectures are great and clarifying. He was an excellent professor, really smart, and always willing to help students out. He and his TA's hosted at least 10 office hours on days leading to exam day.

Does not do a great job of explaining material to students in a clear manner. I found his lectures confusing and had to teach myself most of the class on my own time. He focuses entirely on teaching financial technicals through the use of a financial calculator with little focus on conceptual or theoretical details.

Very difficult to understand and does not teach material clearly at all. His Finance class is basically a class on how to use a Financial Calculator. He gives very little explanation of actual financial concepts.
In my opinion, not very good at communicating concepts in an understandable manner. However, it could've just been that I am bad at Finance. He is very open to help in office hours however.

Though it was a ross course, it only gave 24% A range, and 7% A. The material was harder than before, and the exams were harder, while the grade was based on CUTOFF scores. Even in the math department, we did not have such low A range rate. He was crazy.

Professor Vandenbossche creates an amazing classroom atmosphere, clearly displaying her care for each student. She is extremely knowledgeable about all of the readings and facilitates interesting discussions. She provides a ton of feedback and is very available outside of class for help if needed. I definitely recommend taking one of her courses!

Great professor to have during my first semester at Michigan. The readings were interesting and manageable, and discussions were engaging. She was very accessible during office hours and consistently gave helpful feedback. Getting an A is achievable if you stay on top of assignments and use her feedback.
Absolutely love Lisa. Could not say enough amazing things about her. Not an easy A but it is so worth it to take. She is amazing and genuinely cares about you.

Dr. Vandenbossche has been absolutely amazing! I took my FYWR in one of her ENG125 sections, and I have learned so much about writing, reading, and healthcare. I love that the class is blended to teach content about stories in medicine as well as fundamental writing skills. I would highly recommend!

Amazing professor! She is a lot of fun in class and makes the three hour time block enjoyable. But, she is an extremely harsh grader. If you are looking for a FYWR that will be an easy A, do not take this class. There are many other teachers that give everyone a 95. To get a an A or A-, she expects a perfect paper.

Dr. Vandenbossche is one of my favorite professors at U of M. She was so kind and supportive, and she truly wants the best for her students. She kept classes interesting and made me want to pursue writing throughout my college career.

Professor Vandenbossche is amazing. She truly cares about her students and gives thoughtful, helpful feedback. I grew so much as a writer in her class. She makes every lesson engaging and meaningful. Because of her, I'm now pursuing a double major in English. One of the best professors at Michigan!

Dr. VB was awesome! She cares so much about her students and is so enthusiastic about what she teaches. I would try to get to know her better one on one, I know she has a lot of interesting things to talk about. She was a great teacher for a first-year writing class, and I genuinely think my writing improved because of her. She's also funny asf.

Dr. Vandenbossche is the best professor that I have had in college so far. She clearly cares about all her students and she makes the class a really positive and social environment. I can confidently say that my writing has gotten so much better because she has been SO helpful with how to write and revise essays. She is the best!!!!!

Professor Vandenbossche was lovely! She made the classes fun and interesting, and always made herself available to her students outside of class. I learned a lot about writing and reading techniques. Take her class!

Professor Vandenbossche is amazing. She's the kind of person who will go out of her way to be helpful, she's very accessible outside of class, and it is clear that she cares about her students and their class performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved having Professor Vandenbossche! She was always so willing to help students. You can tell she cares a lot about what she teaches. The readings she selected for our classes were pretty interesting. Whenever I attended her office hours, she gave me helpful feedback. If you have to take a first year writing course, I 100% recommend her.
if you want to have an exam free class with an awesome professor, take this class. i love lisa vandenbossche.
she is a sweetheart and is always willing to help you

Professor Vandenbossche was so sweet and fun! Nobody really wants to take a three-day intro English class, but she actually made it enjoyable! I enjoyed the assignments and the topics she chose and I learned a lot. The class is mainly graded on papers, but she is super helpful with them and gives a lot of class time to work so it is all doable!

Going into this class I didn't know what to expect, but Lisa is seriously amazing. She helped me grow as a writer and was always there to give helpful feedback in and out of class. You can tell she genuinely cares about each of her students as she is always smiling and always ready to help. I LOVE Lisa, take her class or you're missing out!!!!

Prof Vandenbossche is amazing. She teaches students how to structure papers, and actually gives good feedback and works to help students improve their writing. There are not many assignments, but instead you take a paper that you've written and workshop it quite a bit with peers. She is very chill, funny in class! Love her :)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. I had low expectations for the class because I've never liked English classes but she made it worth while. She is very helpful with feedback on papers and is happy to work with students outside of class. She brings good vibes to the class and tries to connect with all of her students. 10/10 professor in my book.
Exams can be tricky, but the lectures are really interesting. Go to lecture, and discussions.
she's only reading off the slides and exams are tricky
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone not interested in dev. psych, I loved this course. She is a very engaging and passionate lecturer, caring, and clearly outlines everything you need to know. Exams are simple, and you get an index card. The two projects are also pretty straightforward, just a little more time-consuming. If you are thinking of taking this class, do it!

TAKE HER CLASS! I was kind of nervous coming into this class and after syllabus day hearing that lecture slides wouldn't be posted. After the first exam, I realized that it what really helped me excel. Ward is a kind and humorous professor and will definitely leave a lasting mark on you for your time at Michigan.
EASY class! there are 4 online exam super easy if you take notes on lectures! there are 2 projects which are time consuming but not hard. 10/10 recommend taking this class
She was delightful. EASY A.

Dr. Ward is a great professor! The class consists of 2 papers and 4 online exams, which were not difficult at all. She does provide extra credit questions on the exams as well as lecture outlines to take notes. If you take this class, be prepared for the psych kids to literally never stop talking while she's lecturing -- it drove me crazy.

Dr. Ward was very nice and always helpful when I had a question. PSYCH 250 was incredibly easy with her, exams are online, open note, and timed graciously. It is a very interesting class and she communicated well with the class. Definitely recommend!

Professor Ward is the most entertaining professor that I've had at University of Michigan thus far. Her lectures are engaging even though I'm not particularly interested in psychology. She said she would offer us extra credit and didn't but that's my only complaint.

Dr. Ward was an amazing lecturer. She explained everything clearly and her class was very well organized. The exams were mainly over lecture content so it is important you attend them! She has a lecture outline with everything you need to take notes on so it makes it super easy! It was a very interesting and very amazing class! I loved it!
Trust me, just take the class

Dr. Ward was great for PSYCH250! I would take another class with her again in a heartbeat. I always found her lectures really interesting. There wasn't a lot of contact between her and students since it was an asynchronous class, but whenever I reached out to her, she was super nice and helpful.
Dr. Ward was extremely understanding and always ready to answer any emails.

I loved having Dr. Ward. She is very helpful, knows what she is talking about, and is very accessible. She is also just a very kind person. Her lectures are amazing, although sometimes outdated, and I love developmental psychology. She is willing to give extensions and extra help where needed. I highly recommend her and this class.

Ward is an amazing professor for psych 250. Her lectures were always interesting, though she does not post her powerpoints online so coming to lectures is important since some of her test questions are based on the lecture. I used the book to study for her tests and the lecture notes helped too. Papers were fairly easy, only had to do two.
Prof. Ward was great! Lectures were straightforward and so were the tests. Show up, take good notes, and study a little before tests and you should do fine!
Super easy class -- show up and take notes on the lecture outline that she gives you. I didn't even ever read the textbook or have to do any extensive outside work for this class.
interesting lectures, great personality; she gives you outlines for note taking so just go to lecture & take good notes and you'll do great
Very great professor, tests are straight forward, if you go to lecture, take good notes and stay on top of the readings you will do fine.
he is so chill. take this class

Professor Larry Ruff is one of the easiest A's you can get. Lectures are recorded and exams (including midterms and the final) are online. The class is very manageable and great for distribution requirements, though it may not be the best choice if you plan to major in geology.

Professor Ruff really wants to see students succeed and designs the course as such. He's super nice and passionate about the topic! While he doesn't take attendance, going to lecture will make the tests so much easier for you. No homework, just multiple choice exams with plenty of time and participation exercises on Canvas.

This man is the second coming of jesus christ. Best professor of all time. Such a nice guy. So understanding. More professors need to have the same attitude as Prof. Ruff. He is just happy to be here and has a genuine passion for what he teaches. Would give a limb for this man. Thank you for everything, professor.

Professor Ruff was super passionate about what he taught in EARTH205, which made the course enjoyable. The lectures can be slow, but he is very understanding and gives plenty of opportunities to get a good grade in his course. If you need NS credit or have any interest in Earth Science, I definitely recommend taking his class.

Professor Ruff is obviously very interested in the topic and a super nice guy, but the entire class is just group presentations. The only grades you get that matter are the midterm and final, which are both online open note. One of the easiest classes I've ever taken but super boring.

Professor Ruff was very invested in this class and you could tell that he really cared about the subject (Environmental Geology). The class was mostly run by student presentations, that he would build the tests off of, but he would interject and give both feedback and more information on topics. A great class for the natural science requirement.
Not very caring. Poor slides preparation. Only graded by three exams. No practice or homework at all before the exam.
A great professor includes a lot of images in his lectures that are very helpful.
One of my favorite natural science teachers so funny!
A gem of a teacher !
All I can say is he is amazing !! Love this professor.

Larry Ruff is an amazing teacher. You will not regret his class. I took Earth 205 a mini-course with him. He is so knowledgeable and his lectures are very very detailed but the exams only require you to know the base knowledge. An easy class but the knowledge I gained was amazing, and he is a great person and professor one of my favorites for sure!

Very nice and super easy class, but still interesting! Dr. Ruff is a very nice person as well. The whole class is taught through student group presentations and he does a good job of creating the tests and quizzes based on those presentations.

This class consisted only of student made/led presentations. He never actually taught us. Dont take this class unless you want to be taught solely through other students poorly made google slides presentations. Although the class was easy and had very little work, it is not worth the easy A. He also would end class 15 minutes late every day.

Larry is someone who is very knowledgable on his subject. He knows a lot about various earth systems. My biggest critique is in the class structure; each lecture is done through group presentations, but attendance outside of that wasn't counted. There would actually be times when there were just as many people in the audience as presenting.

Not worth my effort to wake up and show up at 10am for. I took this pass/fail so I went to the very first class and the final. I am a senior who already knows a lot about volcanoes and earthquakes, so I breathed and passed (studied for 10 minutes). It may have been difficult if I didn't already have knowledge. Take P/F or not at all. very boring
Boring class and whole course grade determined by only one final exam. Wouldn't take again

Professor Ruff can be funny at times, but if you are not interested in Geology or the topic of the class, you will have a bad time. He can be very boring and does not post grades until the end of the semester. He uses group slideshows to teach the class and then makes the exam off of that. Considering that most students didn't try, made exams hard.

Do not take class with Professor Ruff. He is an extremely boring lecturer and went on too many tangents. I am really bummed because I was so excited to learn about volcanos and earthquakes -- but the class could have been taught in such a better way that was actually interesting. Exam counts for your entire grade - my GPA dropped.

I took this course of volcanos and earthquakes for credit to be full time, even with attending lecture twice a week (so monotone I could barely pay attention) I did poorly on the 50 question exam that was the ENTIRE grade. He gave us 3 exercises but none counted for credit. Overall wouldnt have taken instead of a different minicourse if i knew.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do not take his class. Just don't do it. Would rather sit through a women's studies class than this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I needed to fulfill some last-minute credit requirements to graduate, and I chose Earth 105 because I liked the topic. Unfortunately, I've been really disappointed. He started this class with a tirade about why we should care about his minicourse, but he never stopped. His syllabus is confusing and lacks info. His lectures are unorganized.

Larry lacks enthusiasm or interest in the class and students. He gives little to no information about the exam and consistently tells the class to use their "collective intelligence" to answer any questions. His Powerpoints are unorganized and have no information. He speaks in a monotone voice all lecture. Must cram and learn on your own for final.
Not an easy A; not an easy class. Lectures are hard to understand and slides have little to no information on them.

Larry is easily the worst professor I have ever had!! I have never rated a prof on here but felt it was my duty to review him just so other students do not have to endure the hell that is his class. He tells you not to study because exams will be easy but makes exams extremely difficult and then does not curve. Worst course/professor

Larry Ruff is very knowledgable about the earth and really cares about the environment. He is passionate and wants to help future generations save the earth from itself. There is no homework besides a powerpoint presentation every four weeks (very easy). The only tests are the midterm and the final. If you put in the slightest effort you will pass.

In my term, over 50% of the students received As. (He emailed us the grading statistics). As long as you do his many projects and memorize the lecture slides, you will get an A or an A+. Larry Ruff is a good, considerate guy (No Homo). Class discussions are as unbiased as you can get from any University. Spend your class time on studying the slides

He is not clear on his expectations for the group presentations, which are very low once I learned his expectations at the end of the term. Your grade is determined by the two exams. He has low poster and final paper expectations; you get an A by completion. Memorize the lecture slides in class to be more time efficient. Exams are student lectures

This is hands down the worst professor I've had at UM. There is no organization to the class at all. Powerpoints are not helpful and neither is attending lecture. Ruff refuses to answer any questions at all regarding anything. His answer is always to "figure it out yourself" or "ask other students." Avoid this class like the plague.

This guy literally doesn't know his head from his ass.  I would rather take a class taught by a group of insects who grew up in the USA about Israeli culture.  I mean this guy is about as valuable as a broken urinal.
Worthy
this guy is the worst.  i don't know how he ties his own shoes in the morning.

worst teacher ever, confusing too and bad lectures. hes so rude and arrogant and wont help when u ask a question. he says "go figure it out yourself"- word for word. his tests are not bad but there is SOO much stress because u have to learn everything urself because his lectures suck and u panic. most kids get a B, not an easy A.
Larry is an absolute legend. His classes are truly entertaiing. I couldn't care less about this class beyond the entertainment of his lectures
Prof. Ruff is extremely knowledgeable and very approachable.

I did not enjoy this class. I have been fascinated with natural disasters my whole life and thought about making it a career, but this class completely turned me off of it. His teaching is terrible and very confusing.

I usually dont have a problem with professors being condescending and rude, so long as they are helpful; Professor Ruff, however, was rude and completely resistant any form of constructive class discussion.
if Prof. Ruff doesnot respect the course he teaches, but treats this minicourse as a joke himself, then this class is a joke.
I took this class pass/fail and would definitely recommend it to people who need an easy NS credit.  The few times I went to lecture it was pretty boring but the prof seems like a really nice guy.

He's awesome! This is what a mini course is supposed to be like-- just come to class and you'll get an A. I don't see why all these people are complaining. He's hilarious too and he seems as if he really wants his students to enjoy the subject of geology.
Prof Ruff is the most useless professor I've ever had. He refuses to help students and gives no direction for his class. Not a very hard class, but he's a terrible professor.

Very confusing. Didn't learn much from his lectures. He is cool at first but I lost interest after the 2nd day. The class needs to be structured better. He needs to be more exciting, produce quality powerpoint, and stay away from the jokes because they wear out quickly. Not worth your time to take this class.
He is horrible! I have no idea what is going on in this class.
I expected to get an easy A in this class; however, that was not the case. Though I worked hard, I found this to be one of the harder seminars. I would recommend another NS seminar

This is what a mini course should be. No readings, just go to the lectures and you'll get an A on the exam. I didn't even look over my notes before I took it. He makes it clear exactly what you'll need to know. And if you actually pay attention, which no one does, you'll catch all of his ridiculous jokes and have fun.
This class is very easy.  There is little homework.  The professor is easy going and likes to joke a lot.
Larry Ruff is the man! He knows his stuff, his minicourse is easy, and although he does ramble he is super entertaining, I laughed a lot! Definitely worth taking a class with him!
Good ol' Larry Ruff.  Everyone at U of M should take at least 1 class with him.  He rambles on about a lot of nonsense, but its funny and the exam is easy.

best teacher in the world. seriously have no idea why i failed this class, it was so much fun! larry is literally the man! i can't believe that people are being mean about him. His lectures were UNBELIEVABLE. although i was always confused, i loved his jokes. he is such a kidder. Im so sad that this class is over, i no longer have any reason tolive
The easiest A you will ever get... But is it worth the emotional and psychological toll that is Larry "I like rocks" Ruff? No.
He was a good professor and very interested in his topic
very very easy class. never came to class, and showed up for the exam, got a B. i shuda got an A tho.

I attended ONLY the final exam. Did not go to even one minute of any lecture, not even the first one. I downloaded and began to look at the slides an hour and a half before the exam. There were about 60 multiple choice questions. VERY EASY A!

Prof. Ruff is an interesting man, to say the least. The class was very, very easy and he really wanted everyone to get an A. He often goes on rants about insurance which wastes class time. Overall, class was easy. Wishing I took it graded.
Just study hard the day before the final and you'll get an A. The class was a joke.

I'd rather play in traffic than take a class with him again.  He doesn't explain anything ever, is a complete buffoon, and expects you to know things that he never talks about for the test.  Stay away at all costs, he is not worth the time of day.
Larry is the man. Best proffessor at Michigan. OH CRETACEOUS!!! know subduction zones.
Rambles on.  A lot.  Likes to keep talking after class ends.  Knows what he's talking, but an easy minicourse.

GeoSci 148 was incredibly boring.  Professor Ruff just talked his mind and tried to make the class interesting...but he failed.  He doesn't have any rubric or proper grading system.  Don't bother buying the textbook.

The class was easy grading-wise. You want to have the right classmates to have the session lively. He knows his stuff and is also interested in social issues/mitigation, and gives valuable points&opinions. Sometimes his answer to the question carries on too long, but over all a sweet professor.

MITIGATION,MITIGATION,MITIGATION. that is all you need to know for the class, its very very easy but at the same time a bore. luagh at his jokes and he'll love you. EASY FRESHMAN SEMINAR, W LITTLE TO NO WORK.
Larry is the man.  The class was ridiculously easy, but extremely boring.  Larry loves Mountains, Basalt, and Feldspar.  Take this class.

Larrys a nice guy but he doesn't know how to teach very well. Throws alot of information at you but the tests are a joke. A few powerpoint presentations and 2 tests = entire class. VERY easy but be prepared to be bored and to not understand what he is looking for in terms of grades!
larry is the man. in his own little world, yet dumb jokes that are kind of funny and a pretty easy class overall. book has no use because everything comes from him. take for a b/a grade

Larry Ruff is a very very nice guy, and you can tell he has a genuine interest in geology, but he doesn't have a hold over the students at all and I often feel like nobody is paying attention. He also tends to respond to short questions with unnecessarily long answers.  He is a nice, funny guy, and his class is very easy
He SUCKS!!!!!!!

I had him for a minicourse in gelogy expecting it to me interesting, but it was quite the opposite.  His lectures are completely unorganized and chaotic.  I leave his class feeling more confused than when I came in.  He generates abosolutely no interest whatsoever, and he is terrible at teaching the subject of geology.
"ahh Cretacious"
Easy, loves geology, focused on what you learn not about the test

He rambles most of the time, but all you have to do is show up. The easiest "A" i've ever gotten! Pay attention because he throws random questons in and if you answer them it gets you on his good side

Everyone's right. I felt like I was in 3rd grade again. Boring, rambles about the same thing every class. If you take this, don't buy the book. Go to lecture, even though you'll want to pull all your hairs out because you'll need the notes for the final.

this was a mini course and was totally pointless.  Prof Ruff just rambled on and made not much sense.  the class was boring, an easy A but boring.  take only if u need a random 1 credit of natrual science
teaches like you might be in elementary school, then expects you to come up with crazy connections between things for homework. He does seem grade his part of the test easier though.

I'm not sure if the course was easy or not because we never got our midterm back the entire year. This is the most unstructured course in this university. He decided to have a final a week before finals week and nobody was available to take it.

Like most professors Larry knew a lot of information about the subjects, however I felt like he taught the class to 6th graders. I felt like each class period was a waste of time and I didn't learn anything new. I also felt like he constantly tried to undermine the other professors.
No Comments
Grades everything so harshly will find anything to take points off
Take anyone else.

Great person and very caring, but in class I often felt unwelcome and singled out. She can come across as condescending, and it made me hesitant to participate. She's also tougher than other professors who teach the same class, so I'd recommend taking it with someone else if possible.

Liana is an amazing professor, especially for a language so hard like Arabic. She is really clear in her instructions and understands the material thoroughly. She does give a lot of homework, but thats not really her fault, its the department who assigns the assignments. She grades very fast and always gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Liana was one of the best professors I have ever had. She is truly kind and caring, and it was clear that she wanted her students to succeed. She wasn't a harsh grader at all and gave really important feedback about your work. She even made her office hours right before our quizzes so we could ask her last minute questions. Highly recommend!

she's a very tough grader, almost unreasonably so, and she has accused me of cheating twice. I was quite intimidated by her, and the amount of homework assigned was a lot, and it was quite difficult as well. Her class was also quite hard to sit through and i was bored and restless. some activities would have been really nice and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Liana truly cares about students and wants us to learn Arabic. She does encourage questions, but sometimes comes across as intimidating and expects you to understand something after being explained, although students sometimes need something to be explain in different ways. Gives detailed feedback which I appreciated

Liana communicated the expectations for every assignment and had a very clear/accessible Canvas page. She prefers to stick quite closely to the textbook, and really focuses class on the content of a given chapter, with limited references to dialect outside of the dialect days. The speed and detail with which she gives feedback is really amazing.

In my experience with Professor Reading, she genuinely cares for the well-being and the success of her students in and outside of class. Yes, she may be strict, but with a level 5 language like Arabic, it's helpful to have someone to keep you disciplined on your studies along the way. The feedback received from her is generally in-depth and helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: As a Arabic language major, I feel it's important to take an instructor's feedback and apply it to do better in the language. I appreciate instructors who take time to give feedback. However, Professor Reading's grading and feedback is quite harsh to say the least. Rather than visiting office hours to get help, I would just not interact with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Reading is by far the hardest language professor that I came by. Although she is passionate on the subject, it's not a very welcoming environment. Many others and I were intimidated just being in the same room as her. The amount of times students, with less experience in Arabic, have gotten brain farts when asked a question, is countless

I want to preface this by saying the Arabic Department, in general, does not make learning Arabic a good experience for anyone. Liana is truly one of the most difficult professors I have ever encountered. She has a well-structured class, and you always know what to do. She grades though is picky about the smallest things. Would not reccomed.

An amazing instructor who is passionate about her subject and students. The course is difficult, but Liana makes it a joy. She fosters a sense of community in her classes, and there is a spirit of camaraderie amongst her students that is unique to any class I have taken at UM. I cannot recommend her highly enough.

Liana is a great teacher and really cares about her students. She really wants her students to learn Arabic well and I appreciate that. If you can get Liana for an Arabic class, definitely go for it, she is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class itself sucks, but Liana is an angel. Best professor for Arabic. Truly cares for you.
Liana was a great instructor. The department has strict guidelines which she had to abide by but overall she was great.

Seriously she is the best teacher I have had at UofM. Truly cares for her students and takes into account overall performance. Always goes out of her way to check on you and make sure you are doing well. I was extremely fortunate to have her as a professor for all of my Arabic classes at umich. DON'T SIGN UP FOR ANY OTHER PROF.

Liana is the sweetest. You can tell that she truly cares about her students and their success. I was a heritage speaker, so this class was easier for me compared to most other students, but this class was still more of a challenge than 101. Liana takes your whole performance into consideration when calculating your final grade. She's THE best.

Liana is amazing. She's so kind and interested and inspirational. I wish I had her as my Arabic professor from day one. Unfortunately with the regime change, she had to comply with the craziness a bit, but she still let us breath. If I had another certain teacher, my love of Arabic would have been left in the halls of the MLB.

Extremely helpful! Always available for office hours and really wants her students to succeed. If you are truly dedicated to learning the language then take her, she's amazing. She does teach a little more in depth in comparison to the other professors but she is a fair grader. Very do-able.
Probably the best foreign language teacher I've had. You can tell that Liana really cares about her students. She makes it easy to learn, even though the class can be tough.

Liana is among the best foreign language teachers I have ever had.  She is passionate about Arabic and has an interest in you learning it.  She likes to get a lot done in class and checks anything you write thoroughly, making it kind of difficult to get an A.  Anybody that had trouble with her was likely just troubled by the language itself.

Good teacher but all we do is homework and check homework. Great teacher when she teaches. should put less emphasis on homework and more on teaching. quizzes were extremely particular but doable the exams were very difficult but good teacher.

For 210, great professor! She explains material clearly, gives good examples, and really wants students to succeed. I definitely think the way she set up such a difficult course really worked for me with all the resources she provided. For 211, I feel like the grading was unclear a lot and the quizzes were unnecessarily hard. 210 > 211 for Nolta!
Nolta is good, but not as good as people say she is. I also didn't find her lectures as helpful as her office hours were.

Amazing professor probably the best I have had. You have to be willing to put in the work though this is not an easy course. Do the text book problems do all of the worksheets she gives you, go to office hours. If you genuinely do all this you will be fine. She really cares about her students and loves what she teaches!

Biggest thing is the grading structure over all, it's so ambiguous and subjective. I earned full points in almost half the labs and ended with an A-. While I know someone who only received full points on two of the labs and received an A. She's a good teacher but don't even bother trying to appeal you're grade either.

she's very passionate about chem and cares about her students. she explains the labs very well and her chalkboard writing is super clear and easy to follow. i've heard she's great for orgo 1 and 2 as well.
OMGGG I'm obsessed with Dr. Nolta's lectures. She's the best professor I've ever seen in my whole life...Chemistry is so easy with her. The course just started and I'm super readyyyy cz of Dr. Nolta

Dr. Nolta is very nice! Lectures felt all over the place and rarely useful for the lab itself. Inside the lab, often times there was confusion on what to exactly do-but most were fun. The quizzes are challenging- often covering stuff in detail that we barely touched on. The notebook grading is ridiculous though you can't get lower than a B overall.

According to GSIs, every week's notebook submission is graded by different standards which are rarely revealed to us. The grading is outsourced, and they are clearly unable to handle such heavy amounts of people taking this lab course. 210 and 211 are not synched whatsoever. It feels like Nolta talks to us like we're children. Terrible course!

Extremely hard course because you learn so much content, but so worth it!! They set the grade averages to be the same across all biochems, so why not take the one that you learn the most in? Nolta is the best professor I've ever had. She explains everything so incredibly well. She is caring, funny, and personable. Brough us treats after every exam.

I found this lab very frustrating because it was unclear what was required for our submissions. I also had a difficult time getting accommodations from Dr. Nolta, which added to my stress. The 3-hour lab felt more like a humiliation ritual. I'm not sure how much the class changes each semester, but I had a pretty bad experience.

This class is the most difficult I have ever taken but I love Nolta. She is a very nice and caring person and really makes an effort to know her students by name. She even brought in donuts for us on the last day of class. Just a very cool person and extremely knowledgeable.

Sooo nice! Love Nolta and she truly cares about her students, which is really refreshing. Class is by no means the most exciting, but she does her best to make it worth your while. Definitely recommend.

Her lectures were a joy to attend, I can tell she loves what she does and her lectures prepares you well for lab. Lectures aren't mandatory but they help significantly. She's not the one being the tough grader since GSI's also grade, but getting full points on a lab is rare! Make sure you read the syllabus and notebook guide and you'll do well.

I don't think the current Orgo Lab structure sets students up for success. There aren't enough resources available, and we're often expected to figure things out entirely on our own.  The environment is stressful rather than educational IMO. In my section specifically, my GSI was not helpful and just made things even more confusing.

Dr. Nolta is amazing! She explains concepts to students in a way that everyone understands, even using analogies from outside of science. She truly cares about her students and lectures with clarity, which is important in such a difficult class. Her exams were also reflective of what she taught. I 100% recommend her if you're worried for Orgo 1!

Her quizzes and assessments do not reflect what she teaches in actual CHEM 211 lecture. She will briefly cover topics and then expect you to know intricate details for the quizzes. Also the lab manuals are confusing.

Dr. Nolta is the best teacher on campus. She records everything—lectures, office hours, even FN Orgo—and replies to emails super fast. Attendance isn't required and the textbook is optional. She provides a massive archive of past exams. I skipped like all lectures, watching all recordings and taking practice exams to succeed. Highly recommend!
wants you to succeed in this class. many many resources avalible. I'd LOVE to have her again.

Really amazing professor. She teaches very well and is a great resource for anything science-related. If you go up and talk to her she will know your name within a few days just because of how personable she is. What she asks of you in Chem210/211 is very clear and if you have any problems she is pretty understanding.

Her FNs were AMAZING! Seriously couldn't imagine myself surviving Orgo with any other teacher. Her lectures made sense and she made sure to highlight the important stuff. Exams weren't too bad and as long as you attend all sessions (even if not mandatory) and study, you can do well. Oh, and also gave us the biggest curve. DONT PROCRASTINATE
Nolta is the best professor I have ever seen. She cares so immensely about her students. Her lectures focus on theory,

i loved nolta! made a hard class easier. she has lots of extra OHs and records them all and posts optional worksheets on canvas so there's always something to reinforce material. do all of her practice exams because they are very similar to the actual exam (which i found very fair). she does do notes with chalk. pick nolta u wont regret

Dr. Nolta is the best lecturer I've had at UMich so far. Chem 210 is challenging and TONS of practice is essential. Luckily, Nolta is eager to help always. She makes herself very accessible outside of class! She also posts the exams she writes so start practicing early. Go to her Friday OHs, join an SLC group, and you'll do great with Nolta.

NOLTA IS THE BEST! Honestly, this class was a breeze compared to other lab classes! Pretty straight forward, and you get out pretty early! The pre-lab, in-lab, and post-lab submissions were pretty annoying though... We did not get a lab practical though, so that was great! Overall, NOLTA IS THE GOAT!
you'll understand the hype if you take orgo and lab with nolta. she genuinely is one of the best professors i've ever had. so kind and so knowledgeable. very grateful to have taken it with her
Nolta was a phenomenal professor for this lab course. Her lectures are very insightful and helpful so even though attendance isn't required they are definitely worth attending!!!

Nolta is a phenomenal professor for an array of reasons. She is incredible thoughtful and caring and she always has her students interests at heart. She offers endless amounts of opportunities for students to get help by holding tons of office hours as well. Additionally, her lectures are very informative, fun, and easy to follow along.

An excellent prof for Orgo 1 made this difficult course so much better. It is a lot of work, but she makes this class doable, exciting, and engaging. If you can take this class with Nolta 100% do it, she wants her students to succeed. You can do very well in this class using the canvas resources and office hours.

Nolta makes ORGO so much more digestible than any other professor teaching the course at UofM (I would know, I had to take the course with Tuttle before taking it with her!). If you need to take Chem 210, absolutely take it with her. She is engaging and entertaining and deeply cares about you doing well in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's really nice, but the syllabus doesn't explain much, and I don't like her teaching style. She always emphasizes the basic concepts but skips over explaining the difficult ones. She also doesn't provide any practice during lectures—you have to do all the practice by yourself afterward.

Nolta is a caring person, but she tends to overwrite lab procedures, making them confusing to read. A lot of times, you have to dig through the procedures to understand what you need to do. Her lectures don't help with the labs; they mostly review Chem 210 topics. The quizzes are extremely difficult, and you have 0 clue what your grade is.

Nolta is hands down the best professor I've had here. Though orgo is tough, she makes it just a bit more bearable with her humor. She genuinely cares about her students and knows many by name. Content is hard to understand, but Nolta does her absolute best to help everyone understand it.
amazing lecturer, unclear grading guidelines but should avg out to an A. makes chem a lot more understandable

Dr. Nolta is amazing!!! She makes every lecture engaging and provides an unmatched level of nuance and clarity, breaking down the most challenging concepts into digestible pieces. Dr. Nolta is always available by email for questions and even responded to me late at night during finals week. I truly cannot say enough good things about her!

This course wasn't necessarily difficult, but you have no clue what grade you have throughout the entire term and what you end up with is definitely GSI dependent. Her lectures are clear on how to complete the labs, but there are some content topics that are important for the quizzes (with a failing average) that she doesn't explain very well.

The grading of Chem 211 is very GSI based, and there was no way of knowing where your grade was at until final grades were released. That being said, Dr. Nolta was helpful in her lectures but there weren't very clear guidelines for what was expected on labs.

Although I believe Nolta was a great professor during lectures, taking her lab is like walking down a tightrope blindfolded. Class is completely GSI-based and if you end up with a GSI like mine who grades in emojis you have no real idea of how you are doing in the class + even kids who did well on labs ended up with bad grades due to the curve.

Professor Nolta is amazing. She explains the material for every lab section very clearly and answers questions nicely. She has a great sense of humor and makes lecture fun. Your GSI matters more for this class; I hope you get a good one. The grading scale is mysterious, and you won't know anything about what your final grade will be until the end.

By far the most genuine and caring professor. Really great at explaining what we need to do for lab. Very descriptive and has a lot of fun with using color on the blackboard. NEATEST HANDWRITING EVER. I must say, grading system is really mysterious and you just got to hope you have a great GSI. Other than that, try your best and you'll be fine.
