There's absolutely no concrete rubric for this class. The entire semester I had no clue what my grade was. There are two quizzes throughout the class, on material barely covered, that both average a failing grade. In the beginning of the semester it was stated that there's no outside work, but those two spec supplements took at least 8 hours each.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very obviously knows how to teach the material and did it well. The only issues I had with this course were due to the mysterious grading system, but a lot of reassurances were given on the matter, so just make sure to complete all the work assigned and you should be fine. Oh, and I still don't know what a mass-spectrum really is.

I thoroughly enjoyed Dr. Nolta's lab class. She would explain what was expected for pre-labs. She would answer all questions and she cares for her students. 2 gripes with the class is that assignments were graded by a GSI. Also there were 2 difficult quizzes that covered previous concepts in great detail, so beware of that. It was great regardless.

Dr. Nolta herself seems to be friendly, but this lab course was terrible. The grading scale is a mystery. The GSI gives emojis on lab reports. There are no lecture recordings, but the quizzes are extremely difficult and heavily test your memory of small details or deeper understanding of concepts she only briefly touched upon during lectures.

I truly enjoyed chem 210 as taught by Professor Nolta. She is incredibly clear and explains concepts in a well-planned manner. She also goes above and beyond outside of lecture hours to help her students, whether by email or during review sessions. I would definitely take another class with her if I had the opportunity.
If she is teaching, who is running hell. No words other than that will be said!

Honestly, yes this course depends on your GSI, but the general grading for 211 is really unspecified. You won't really know how you're doing until the end and the quizzes are tough. Lectures were good but it's difficult to understand what your future grade will be.I wish she made that more specific, and found a new grading scheme.

I found her lectures clear, focused, and engaging. She also gives lots of resources/practice exams, grades quickly, is very responsive/approachable outside of class, and is also a really caring person. Overall an awesome prof, she's the best 210 lecturer IMO.
Best professor I have ever had. SO approachable and available, eager to help, and generally cares about each of her students. She makes Orgo accessible to everyone, which is not an easy thing to do.

Prof Nolta is an amazing prof for Chem210 in the spring. She gives every piece of information you could ever need. Explains things clearly and records everything. Anything you could need is posted and at your fingertips, she really does her best to make sure you understand the content. Overall glad I took this course with her.

Dr. Nolta was an amazing professor! She truly cares about her students, taking the time to learn many names (out of a 400+ person lecture). Her tests were difficult, but if you take the practice tests provided, it is easy to do well in the class. Strongly recommend going to workshops and or office hours. Easily my favorite professor so far.

She's very sweet and knowledgeable/passionate about chemistry, but 211 was a big mess. There is no clear grading criteria and the quizzes were incredibly hard. Because she lets all GSIs grade extremely differently, I probably had to put in at least 4-6 extra hours a week compared to my other friends with a different GSI to get the same grade.

Nolta is very kind in lecture, but kind of overrated in her explanations. In fact, I stopped going to lectures midway and would only watch them at home and mainly learned from Soellner's topic videos I found from a friend. Her exams are a little easier than other prof's exams I heard but her teaching is somewhat vague for me.
Did not explain ideas well at all. Quizzes she gave had absolutely nothing to do with what we talked about in lab or lecture, felt very unorganized. A lot of people like her, I was very disappointed.

She is a very good lecturer and tries her best to keep the audience engaged as much as possible. However, the exams were really challenging and cooked my GPA for the worse. You need to be heavily invested in the course material to do well.

Dr. Nolta was a great professor! This class can be really difficult, but she did a good job of making it as fun and interesting as possible. She was always accessible outside of class and truly cares about her students and wants us to do well.
So funny

dr. nolta is easily the best professor at umich! i was terrified of taking orgo but she made lecture so much less intimidating, almost to the point that it was easy. she is so accessible outside of class and you can tell she puts her heart into everything she does, and provides a multitude of resources. orgo with nolta was the best choice i made!!!

Nolta is THE. BEST. professor I have EVER had. She is so kind, responds to emails efficiently, includes so many opportunities for practice and asking questions, and she is just all around the best prof I've had by far. Orgo is a difficult class but I promise it is a much better experience when she is teaching. Couldn't recommend her more!!!

Nolta is an amazing professor and an even better person! The way she teaches makes everything organized and interesting, yet still fun and exciting. It truly feels like she wants to be teaching and wants you to succeed! For orgo lab, be weary of the two difficult quizzes she gives on canvas, but everything else will be graded by a GSI.

Dr. Nolta is hilarious and it is genuinely so fun to go to lecture and watch her and Gunther perform these cool experiments! Lab participation obviously matters, and pay attention in class for things that will be on the two quizzes. Nolta even popped into our lab every couple of weeks and would talk to each student individually and give feedback.

Dr. Nolta is the best! Her lectures are extremely clear, easy to follow, and overall hilarious!  She is such an approachable and outgoing person as she kindly helped to resolve a conflict between me and my GSI. In the class itself, the grade is determined by your GSI. There are also 2 quizzes that despite being open-note are extremely HARD.

Professor Nolta was simply amazing. Her lectures were engaging, easy to follow, and helpful in regard to the lab itself. She has a great sense of humor and is very approachable. Grading is primarily based on 2 quizzes and GSI-graded lab work. While quizzes are open notebook, they were tough. Keep that in mind!

Nolta is great! She is funny, she knows what shes talking about when it comes to lab, and she will *most of the time* keep you engaged in lectures. She sometimes goes off on little chem tangents and you have no idea what she is talking about, but at the end of the day, you just ignore it and move on.

Nolta is so passionate about what she does! She made lectures fun and interesting for us while also providing us a clear guide of what we will see in lab! She made note taking so easy and lectured at a very good pace. Heavily based on how your GSI grades lab work and 2 quizzes. These quizzes were online, timed, open note, but VERY HARD!

Orgo is known as a difficult class, but Dr. Nolta makes it enjoyable! Your grade is based entirely on 4 exams that aren't multiple-choice (this is for all orgo professors). Dr. Nolta is very accessible outside of class and holds several office hours every week. She encourages using the coursepack because practice is the best way to pass this class.

Phenomenal professor, Dr. Nolta has consistently gone so above and beyond as a professor this past semester and I could not recommend her more. She is personable and so accessible. Despite the material being incredibly difficult, she does everything she can to help us understand and prepare us for her exams.
Great professor! Explains things really well and makes a daunting class like orgo actually worth learning about!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: One of worst experiences had in a class. Unnecessary amount of work. Quizzes are incredibly difficult & asked questions/terms that was not covered during lecture. Lab reports & pre-labs are all up to your GSI. Was never even sure what my grade actually was because there was no defined grading scale in the syllabus/addressed in class.

Dr. Nolta is by far the most engaging, enthusiastic, and friendly chemistry professor I've had. I hated chemistry before this class, but Dr. Nolta helped me find the joy in it, and I'm very grateful for that. She taught with great clarity & her lectures were never dull. She's very down-to-earth in her teaching style. She also has the cutest cats!

The chem dept legend! Great lecturer, and is a great teacher in lab. Always trying to help students, and you can tell she cares a lot. Grading was pretty unclear though, and mostly done by GSIs. PS: 353 (ULWR) is completely GSI taught

Prof Nolta is the BEST! She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to enjoy chemistry and truly understand the material. Her lectures are fantastic and she helps motivate you to learn difficult material. However, post labs are a lot of work and are usually due 48 hours after lab, so finding the time can be difficult.

Amazing professor. Cares so much about her students. She gives 2 tough quizzes during the semester, but they won't impact your grade too significantly in the long run. Give good effort on lab write-ups and you will get the grade you want.

She is so funny and cares so much about the students and has the most first-grade teacher vibes!! The quizzes are super hard and don't have much to do with the material (do outside research), and the grade/lab has more to do with the GSIs than Nolta, but she is incredible :)

I would rate her a 5 if it wasn't for the unnecessarily hard exams. She is extremely funny, nice, and caring, however the exams cover topics we hardly touched on or that were not explained to us well. To do well on the exams you have to do some of your own research, showing up to class will not be enough. love her though
"This won't be on the exam" is a lie. Do not believe it. Hilarious professor though.

Dr. Nolta is probably the best chemistry professor at U of M, and one of the best professors all around. Her lectures are absolutely amazing. Lectures weren't even required but I would make sure to come to every one of hers just to be inspired.
Queen
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta is a very good professor and is really dedicated to her students. However, in chem211 you need to worry about your GSI and their grading style.

Dr. Nolta is a really nice person, but her exams for 351 are notoriously hard. Doing the old exam questions she provides and going to office hours are really helpful to prepare for exams. Even if you can't come to office hours, she records them and can answer a question for you if you email her ahead of time.

Best prof I've had at umich. No joke; you will laugh, you will cry, but you will learn insane amounts about biochem. Ask her any question: I promise she has the answer. If she doesn't, she will make a slide about it next lecture. Tell her you are struggling; she will teach you how to improve. Incredibly hard course but prepares you for any to come.
Professor Nolta always made lectures super fun and interesting. She was caring towards students, always made things clear, and gave you exactly what you needed to be prepared for the lab.

Honestly, the GSI matters more for 211 than the lecturer. Regardless, Nolta was a great lecturer, she has super neat notes, and provides you with the info you need for the class. Sign up for labs based on times not professors though, because you only see the lecturer for an hour a week.
Requested a regrade and got harsh comments about my work that I had never received during the semester.

This class comes with a sizable workload, but Dr. Nolta goes over the experiments and related concepts in detail before lab. She is kind and also accessible outside of class. My only issue is with the two course quizzes, which were very fast-paced and seemed unnecessarily difficult. With that said, they weren't a major part of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Such a great professor! Lectures were clear, straightforward, and very well organized. She loves interacting with the students, so the class is not boring at all! Also very accessible for help by email, after lecture, and even during labs.

This class involves a lot of tedious work (prelab and postlab every week), but Nolta's lectures make it easier. She is extremely clear, and doesn't go too fast like many profs. Overall great lectures, but the labs are often tedious and the weekly lab reports get really annoying. There are also two random really hard quizzes. Ok class, good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta is hands down one of the best professors at this university. She makes a point to form personal relationships with her students and makes lectures engaging. Also, she explains chemistry concepts very clearly which is helpful because a lot of organic chemistry concepts can get confusing fast. Register for her class if you can!
Lab is hard because you have to be so specific in your reports. Despite this, I loved Nolta's lectures and she is also willing to help with any chem topic, not just Orgo 1 lab. Love her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking this class with her, her lectures were very clear and easy to understand and were able to hold my attention well. She lectured in a way with infectious excitement about the topic and seems to interact with students well even though it is a GIANT lecture section. I would love to see more profs like Nolta in the future :))

Nolta is an amazing professor. But, when it came to online learning she took a very ridged approach. Her lectures were longer than the class period would be, quizzes were very difficult (even open note). I don't think her approach was equitable. It seemed that she shifted away from teaching concepts toward enforcing specifics which's disheartening

While she may be a great professor for Orgo, she did not show an ounce of respect towards her students in biochem. Her lectures were almost 2 hours long/day when the class was only scheduled for 1 hr/day. She made the exams extremely difficult "due to our ability to use outside resources". Do not take her during the pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta is the best professor I have had so far at U-M. Took this during the spring semester and was one of the select few to get an A. The exams are hard, but DO THE COURSEPACK PROBLEMS when they are assigned, attend EVERY office hour session to check your answers/ask questions, and use all of the resources she provides!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nothing can be said about Dr. Nolta that hasn't already been said. Take her course and you will never regret it. She is brilliant, extremely approachable and knows organic chemistry like no one else on Earth. Not only does she explain well in class, she does all of the practice problems PLUS extra practice PLUS practice exams in office hours.

Dr. Nolta would upload a ridiculous amount of recorded lecture each week and expect students to decipher what the important aspects were. She refused to meet 1-1 with students and made it obvious that mental health was not a priority. She would dismiss student's concerns and even laugh at them and make fun of questions asked during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of material necessary for this class and she does not outline what the important parts of the material are in the lectures. She is unwilling to meet with students outside of class, and does not seem to care for students' mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta's excitement and passion for the subject was infectious, which is particularly impressive when limited to pre-recorded lectures. She wants to help students understand, so don't hesitate to email her or ask questions during office hours. Be prepared to work hard! Nolta's exams are challenging and cover an immense amount of material.

Nolta is one of the best STEM profs there is. Extremely well-paced lectures with tried-and-true teaching methods. She truly cares and really wants to make the material stick. Orgo is rough no matter what, but she's super accessible and loves what she does. The material is hard but Dr. Nolta is a gem. If you have to take CHEM210, take it with Nolta.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta was really understanding during the COVID-19 pandemic, while the lecture recordings could sometimes be a bit lengthy, they covered everything we needed to know and they were easy to follow along and understand.

The BEST science professor in all of University of Michigan. She made even gen chem concepts click while in Orgo. She's outstanding. Her lectures are clear and well-paced. She will do everything to make sure you understand by holding office hours and review sessions and more! OUTSTANDING!

One of the best professors. Even with classes being online, Dr. Nolta made lectures easy to follow and made it clear what topics we should know. Quizzes accurately reflected the lectures and labs were easy to write and follow.

Prof. Nolta is so so so great. She teaches the material so well and her lab section was taught extremely well, being entirely remote. Her lectures were extremely organized and she addresses questions well and ensures you understand the material. Highly recommend and she's such a great caring person.

Dr. Nolta's Chem 211 class was definitely difficult and involved a lot of work (that sometimes was confusing due to the online format), but overall her genuine dedication to students, willingness to help, and passion for chemistry made this class a wonderful experience. Dr. Nolta is the ideal of what a professor should be like! Lots of work though.

I know this has been said a million times but Dr. Nolta is by far one of the best. Everyone loves her and all the good things you hear are completely true. I was so nervous about taking this lab course but she has made it so bearable and so much fun and ive learned so much. She is so kind and so dedicated to teaching and always happy to help
Dr. Nolta is incredible!! Things can be tough when labs are online but she is always available and willing to help. By far the best teacher I have ever had at UM!

I have her for orgo labs online. Ive emailed to ask a question or two, as the remote lab results are sometimes hard to find, and every time she was very rude, not very formal, and it made it harder to ask questions If you have disability she isnt great. She was rude when I asked for an extension, and forced me to share details of my disability.

Dr. Nolta is the best professor I've had. Orgo is really tough no matter who your prof is, but she gives you every single resource for success. She's super kind and understanding and receptive and her lectures were actually fun to attend even though I hated orgo. AND she goes over the entire coursepack. Dr. Nolta is truly a wonderful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: best prof I've had yet! shes so nice and explains everything with logic so it makes sense to you. its a hard topic but she makes it very do-able -- you just need to put the work in. She also answers emails really quickly and can always tell where you're having difficulties

Nolta is a great prof but 211 is SO GSI-dependent. The class doesn't have a clear grading scale, so it felt like our final grades were determined arbitrarily. Definitely do your best on all the assignments no matter how insignificant you may think it is, especially the online quizzes. Their importance isn't stressed as much as it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I thought I'd absolutely hate orgo but Nolta made the class so enjoyable. You can tell she's a genius yet still an amazing teacher. Loved orgo because of her. Nolta goes above and beyond to help students digest the content, but you also need to put in the work to practice problems. Tests are do-able if you dedicate your life to the coursepack.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never had a professor who cared so much about her students. After dropping orgo in the fall and then taking it with nolta in the winter, it was probably the best decision I made. Yes the exams are more difficult, however she teaches the material so much more clearly. TAKE ORGO ONLY WITH NOLTA I am so serious. Friday night orgo saved my grade

As amazing as Nolta, her exams are very difficult. If possible, I would recommend taking orgo in the fall and then just coming to nolta for help understanding the material. The exams are much much easier in the fall semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing. She's the best professor I've had at a university with so many amazing teachers. Yes, orgo is hard and will always be hard, but I have never seen someone so driven to make sure that her students do the best that they possibly can do. She gives more than enough resources to succeed, and she inspires her students to work hard for the class.

Nolta is one of the best ever. She cares very much,so don't be afraid to talk to her or email her any concerns. The tests are not easy and you MUST prepare but her recorded office hours and 12 practice tests makes it more than possible to do well, just have to prepare+do problems on your own by starting early. Orgo I takes commitment, not genius

Nolta is the way to go if you have to take orgo. This class is still super hard, but it's a bit better having her teach it. Her lectures are great, but if you miss any you're screwed. Definitely buy the course pack and work through the whole thing because the only grades for the entire class are the 4 exams. Shifted grading scale (80% is an A-).

Nolta makes orgo easy. I absolutely bombed this class but that's totally on me since I hardly put in any work. If you go to Nolta's lectures and office hours, it's literally impossible to get anything lower than As.
Dr. Nolta is AMAZING! Her lectures are so engaging and she is always willing to answer questions. Orgo 1 is hard, but Dr. Nolta makes you want to work hard and learn the material.

Easily one of the best professors at this school. She cares so much about the subject and her students it blows my mind. She will memorize names at office hours and respond to emails within 10 minutes, and her lectures are like works of art. The lectures are much more simple than exams, so get the coursepack and practice that to no ends.
Beware. The happy people with Nolta are myths. this is the worst class i've ever taken. Unnecessarily hard for no reason. Do. Not. Take.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are going to take organic chem (CHEM210), you should take it with Dr. Nolta. Attending or watching her AMAZING office hours and workshops is key. You will probably never meet a professor who works so hard to teach and help students master challenging topics. Finally, for success in the class, do course pack and practice exams. That's all.

This was one of the few classes where the professor goes above and beyond what is expected of them for the benefit of their students. I've taken Chem 210 before with a different professor and barely passed and just thought I was bad at Orgo. With all the amazing resources Nolta provides, I am holding an A and understand Orgo more than ever.

Nolta was amazing. She is exceptionally good in teaching chem 210. For 211, I found it to be really GSI dependent. For me, my GSI was a bit clueless and never really told us how we are being graded until the end of the semester. But, Nolta as a person is amazing and I would highly recommend taking any chem class with her.

I didn't even have orgo with Nolta, but she still held office hours for orgo and recorded herself doing practice problems. So much more helpful than the lectures!!!! She goes so far above and beyond and is so willing to help you understand things without being condescending. I am horrible at orgo but Nolta is the only decent thing about it.
What can I say that hasnt already been said? Nolta is amazing and great at explaining material for lab and for Orgo I in her FN Orgo sessions. If you can take Nolta for either, TAKE HER.

Dr. Nolta is easily the best professor I have ever had in college. She is kind, personable, and has devoted her life to making chemistry as comprehensive and as fun as possible. Her FN Orgo series for Chem 210 was a lifesaver for me, and it was always a treat to show up to lab lecture every Monday. Love, love, love her!
Amazing professor. First choice for chemistry anytime.
Dr. Nolta is God. I didn't actually have her for chem 210, but she holds office hours every Friday and records them and they are the only reason I'm doing as well in this course as I currently am.

Dr. Nolta is the MVP of the chem department. She is an engaging lecturer and truly cares about her students. She responds to emails within 20 minutes and is often available in actual lab sections to answer questions and help out. She also recorded coursepack problems for chem 210, even though she was only teaching 211. She goes above and beyond.

Before the course began, during the course, and while I was DAT prepping 6 months later this professor was available to answer questions. She truly has a passion for organic chemistry and her students success. Organic chemistry can be a challenging subject, but she makes it easier to comprehend. She's super organized and such a fun professor!
Dr. Nolta is AMAZING. She makes chemistry fun and cares so much about her students.

Dr. Nolta was pretty helpful in preparing us for labs every week during the lectures, but sometimes left things confusing and left us with lots of questions for the GSI's. Not really her fault, hard to speak about both the chemistry concepts and lab mechanics both in a 50 min lecture. She was light-hearted and lecture was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hands down the BEST professor I have ever had at this University! She is tough but very fair with her students. She's one of the kindest people you'll ever meet. A lot of people say her exams are harder but after taking a lot of practice tests you will be just fine. She literally gives you seven practice exams to work with. Take advantage of them!

Dr. Nolta is simply an incredible professor. She finds ways to make orgo lecture entertaining - she kept me engaged nearly all the time. She truly cares about her students' success. Highly highly recommend.

If you have to take orgo, you have to take it with Nolta! She is the most engaging, caring, and genuinely enthusiastic professor I had freshman year. Basically to get an A you need to commit to the coursepack practice and attend some of her workshops/office hours. The woman dedicates her life to her students, so you can give some of that back!

There are not enough good words to describe Nolta, she deserves every single bit of praise that she receives. I only pulled a B but that is purely due to my lack of studying/spring semester being a bit rushed. She gives everyone the ability to get an A for sure and is just the nicest person of all time.

I have never left a review of a professor but I came here specifically to leave one for Nolta. She is amazing!! I never liked chemistry before this course but she made organic chemistry actually kind of fun just because shes so passionate and cares about students. Always go to her office hours and do the coursepack problems and youll be fine!!

Nolta is hands-down the best professor I've had at umich in any subject. She is an unbelievably caring and devoted teacher and LOVES what she does and the subject she teaches. Don't be intimidated by the rumours; orgo isn't that bad, and she is there for you with resources and workshops for the coursepack. Nolta made orgo fun and really cool.

If youre one of the unlucky bunch to have to take orgo, like myself, take it with Nolta! Not only is she a phenomenal explainer with great notes, she is very accessible out of class and answers emails in minutes. Thanks for a great semester, Nolta!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nolta is the absolute GREATEST. Even though concepts in orgo are completely new and sometimes difficult to grasp, Nolta goes out of her way to help students. Besides 6 hours of extra weekly RECORDED workshops and office hours, shes also extremely responsive to email questions- she literally responded to all of mine in less than 10 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Nolta was a great prof--definitely cared about her students and knew the material well. In order to do well in her class, however, you pretty much HAVE TO attend/watch an extra 4 hours of lectures (office hours & workshops) per week because that's where she goes through actual problems (what matters for the exam). Kinda frustrating, still good prof

She explains things perfectly & holds like 6 hours of RECORDED office hours per week, going over solutions IN DETAIL. I came in absolutely HATING chemistry. She also grades on improvement. I got a B on all the midterms but an A on the final, so she gave me an A in the class when I really should've had a B+ (based on percentage) TAKE HER CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have had in college. Always going out of her way to help students as much as she can.

I love Dr. Nolta. I pretty much changed my major to biochem because of her. The way she teaches is effective for a variety of learning styles, and she's clearly so engaged in the material and finds everything fascinating, and has the ability to impart that on students, as well. It's the best.
It's a hard class, but Nolta is amazing, I love her so much, best professor ever!!!
Best professor of all time. Use all the resources she provides on canvas and watch all the recordings!

I love this crazy cat lady with my whole heart. Her exams are more challenging, but she's such an amazing and engaging lecturer that it makes up for it. She goes out of her way to be accessible and gets to know many of her student my name. No lie if you email her a picture of a problem you're stuck on she'll get back to you in minutes.
I hate chemistry, but Dr. Nolta is the reason I'm still pushing through. She is an amazing lecturer and you can tell she is 100% committed to her job.
her notes are SO perfect and she keeps lectures very entertaining

She is literally the best human ever and is so nice. Talks to you like you're an equal and is always willing to explain a concept to you, even if you need her to 584329085 times. This was the first lab I have taken that I actually enjoyed and I believe a large part of that was attributed to her.
AMAZING HUMAN BEING!

Nolta is the best professor I have ever come across in my entire life. Orgo is v tough but she makes it understandable and actually enjoyable. She is cute and quirky in her lectures and even gave us candy bars at her workshop one time. She goes over the entire coursepack which is so incredibly helpful. Go to her office hrs+every extra workshop!!!

Dr. Nolta cared about the success of her students. I bombed the first 2 exams, but did very well on the final 2 and received an A for showing an huge improvement with my test scores. She also provides A TON of resources and additional help in-person and over email. Highly recommend, especially for the spring/summer semester if available.

Can't recommend her enough. She made me want to go to orgo lectures (not just because of the need to learn material, but because her lectures are actually quite enjoyable to attend). I laughed a lot in this class, and she seemed to really care about her students. Make use of many of the resources she provides (ex. past exams) and orgo will be fine
She is the best and most caring professor I have ever had. Made orgo so much fun! Her notes are amazing, too!

Very informative class but requires memorization of SO. MUCH. INFORMATION. where studying usually ended with rocking back and forth while laughing uncontrollably. Exams are about 20% multiple choice and 80% short answer questions and are brutally specific, but compensated from a huge curve and by having Nolta. I wouldn't take this with anyone else.

Nolta is 100% WORTH THE HYPE! If you can, wait + take orgo w/her. Teaches in a way that's easy to understand + notes are beautiful (color-coordinated!). Genuinely wants you to succeed + has lots of resources to help you. Nicest lady, makes lecture fun and engaging (songs of the day every lecture that relate to material). Gives out candy 24/7 also

Nolta is an amazing professor and a very kind and genuine individual. She wants each and every one of her students to succeed. I struggled with orgo in the beginning but as I reached out to her the better I became. It's really worth it to go to her extra office hours/workshops, and use all her past exams to review for tests . Take orgo with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Nolta is the sweetest professor I have ever had. She is soo caring and wants you to do well in the class. Her lecture boards are BEAUTIFUL and easy to follow. I would recommend going to her office hours/go aheads/workshops. I found those to be more helpful for the exam than lecture. I found her exams a lot harder than the practice exams though.

I love how Nolta obviously cares about her students and how they understand the material. She knows it's hard. But she is so willing and available to help students. Her enthusiasm truly knows no bounds and that is amazing. She's also pretty OCD and makes fun of that a lot, which is super cute. She has so many resources of her own as well as others.

Dr. Nolta is just a wonderful wonderful human. I was terrified of taking orgo, because I didn't like gen chem much, but she made me LOVE it! voluntarily signed up for orgo 2 next semester because I just can't get enough. Might change to biochem or chem major. She is very clear, but office hours are what really seals the deal. Go to all of them.

I hate chemistry a lot but actually enjoyed this class. Nolta is one of the best teachers I have ever had and is very caring and welcoming to students who struggle. If you have to take orgo, she's worth waiting a semester if you have to.

Orgo is very difficult, in general, but Dr. Nolta will show you your way through the material. She makes lectures understandable, her office hours are sooo helpful! GO TO THEM (coursepack solutions!) Her exams are "tough," but they are really just comprehensive and wanting to know if you can do the material inside and out.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: I've heard that in previous semesters the chem 216 lab has been difficult and time consuming but Nolta made going to lab every week a very pleasant experience.

Dr. Nolta is one of the best professors I have taken here at umich. She cares so much and her lectures are truly an experience that I wont forget. Her extra OH (which she doesnt have to do but still does) are amazing and I recommend going to them. Introduce yourself to her, you wont regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best

Nolta made the most difficult class of my life very enjoyable. She really wants everyone to do well, and cares about each student even though she teaches hundreds. She gives out gifts at the end of the year and writes very clear and beautiful notes!

Dr. Nolta is the best! Great at explaining topics, cool lady, quickly responds to emails, office hours podcasted, completes the coursepack with you, has like 10 practice exams for each exam. She teaches concepts and reasoning skills, as well as how to do problems. With the expanded grading scale, there's no excuse to get lower than a B- (60%)

Honestly the greatest professor I have ever had. Her lectures given teach you the very basics, and she details everything in her office hours. She even does the coursepack with you, making it so much more useful for studying. Her exams can be difficult, but she provides all of her past exams as practice. Hard work will reward you in this class.

I have never had a professor pour themselves into teaching as much as Nolta. She truly cares about her students and goes above and beyond to provide them with helpful resources. If you have the opportunity, you MUST take orgo with her. She makes the class manageable and inspires you to work hard.

She's an amazing person. I never got to know her personally and I wish I did. I've never been a great chem person, but the way she teaches makes it impossible to not understand. The exams ARE hard because of how great she teaches, but I would say its worth it without a doubt.

Nolta is known to be a great professor. I agree, but there are faults. For example, I feel her lectures/notes are too unorganized/weirdly ordered. So that wasn't the best thing ever. However, I loved her workshops, especially the fact she actually gives coursepack answers before Exams (unlike other profs).
Probably one of the best professors (if not the best) I've had so far in college. Definitely take your lecture with her if you can! Excellent lecturer and genuinely cares about her students.

If you have to take orgo, definitely go with nolta. Any problems I had with this class and her lecture were with the chem dept. making this class so damn hard. She's adorable and will give you stuffed animals and candy. Tips for success: watch office hour podcasts and use her website for extra practice tests. Do them ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Nolta is definitely the best professor at U of M! I came into orgo terrified and not knowing what to expect but Dr. Nolta has made orgo one of the best classes that I have ever taken. Dr. Nolta truly cares about every single one of her students and her dedication shows. Go to her office hours, workshops, and lectures and you can succeed in orgo
Dr. Nolta has been my favorite teacher so far. She made Orgo1 bearable and her lectures were always on point. She is very friendly and super understanding.

best teacher I've ever had. She spends countless hours outside of class podcasting practice problems and ensuring we all understand the material. If you are taking Orgo1, take it with nolta, you will not regret it!

Podcasts all her office hours and weekly workshops. Genuinely cares that all her students do well, hard exams but definitely the most AMAZING professor I've had a UofM. If you're taking orgo you have to take it with Nolta.
She is the best professor I have ever had. If you have to take ORGO, do everything you can to get her.

She's by far the best professor I've ever had. Wasn't originally gonna take Orgo in the winter but I'm so glad I did, she's such a gem. It's a hard class but if you go to her office hours/workshops/go-aheads you'll be fine. You can tell she really cares about her students
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I'll ever have at Michigan. I've never been so interested in a chemistry class before (and usually I hate them). Would 100% recommend taking a class with her. She's so understanding, helpful, and intelligent. The definition of what a professor should be.

She is absolutely awesome!  Yes, Orgo is a very hard class but she is very understanding and always willing to answer any questions. She does a lot of coursepack problems during office hours and even in class. And often after an exam she will have us do the wave in lecture :D

For a class as hard as Organic Chem, Nolta puts in the maximum amount of effort to help her students succeed. She does a great job explaining the material so people understand all the underlying concepts rather than just memorizing reagents and reactions. Tests are really hard but Nolta is the best teacher i've had at this school yet. Super funny
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love Nolta! She is such a good teacher and she is so caring for her students. She puts in a lot of time outside of class like working on coursepack with u and gives you the answers. She makes orgo fun and understandable. I actually really enjoyed it! Make sure to do her old exams as practice for the tests, those help a lot

Nolta is the best professor I have had at michigan. She has made me actually enjoy doing organic chemistry and going to lectures to learn the new material. Her tests are hard but she has so many resources to do well that getting an A is manageable if you put in the work.

I freakin' love Nolta! And this is coming from someone who didn't do too hot in her class. Once you accept the fact that you're not going to get the grade you probably want/usually get in classes you'll be fine. GO to her office hours/blue review!! She goes into so much more depth - they're honestly more helpful than lecture. She's a very fair prof
The fact that her rating is this high and she teaches orgo says it all. Quite possibly the best teacher I have ever had. Sure the material is hard but Nolta makes it more than possible to understand.
Best Teacher At the University, period.

Dr. Nolta is absolutely one of the most amazing humans I've ever gotten to know. Yes, this class is hard. But Nolta makes it worthwhile. Take the time to go to her office and get to know her, because you'll appreciate the class so much more. She's passionate about biochem and about what she does, and it shows. A TRUE gem.

Prof. Nolta is one of the real gems at the university. The class is very hard. I thought that people weren't serious when they said to know every detail and word on each slide, but that is absolutely the truth. However, she is extremely helpful outside of class. Email her at any time with any question. She is one of the few profs that truly cares.

Probably one of the hardest classes in LSA. You basically have to spend an extra 2+ hours every week to attend her Go Aheads/OH; otherwise, you'll be learning stuff the day before the exam.   Later exams get harder with a lot more memorizing. You get food on the lecture after each test though. She's super helpful and replies very fast to emails.

Professor Nolta is an amazing professor but and even more amazing human.  She is kind, brilliant and truly tries to help each individual student in any way she can.  She's always available to answer questions and is so easy to talk to.  Hardest class I've taken here but worth every minute with Nolta.

Don't listen to people who complain about the difficulty of the class. I received a B in both organic chemistry courses, and earned an A for chem 351. If you want to do well in this class, you really need to study weeks in advance of the exam, right when the material is presented. Nolta is caring and respectful, and answers emails within minutes.
I love Nolta! One of the best professors I've had at Umich. Also the hardest class I'e taken here by far, but there's a curve, so it's okay. Worth it!

Never had a professor like her. The biggest hard-worker that I've come across. While her exams are not easy, the work she puts in surpasses the difficulty of this class by a large margin. Nolta is one of those highly intelligent geniuses that also knows how to teach. At first I was dubious of her, but I ended up absolutely loving her and Orgo 1.
The best professor I've ever had by far. Her ability to cut through the mess of complex terms and actually explain things to you his amazing. Hard class but you'll definitely enjoy her lectures

I don't like chemistry, but Nolta was the best teacher I have had to date. Very interested in the material and very energetic. She knew the name of every student. She knew the material very well and was always willing to help if you needed it.

I loved nolta freshman year! her lectures for lab were super easy to follow, it might be hard to show up but I highly recommend! She gives a lot of the answers for quizzes (which you can usually use notes on, how awesome!). She engages with the students and always cracks jokes. Very neat, always answers question, passed with over an A.

Much harder than the other two intro biochem classes since those taking it weren't scared off by 351's reputation. Mechanisms/extra material were tedious. Exams were naturally brutal. Her slides were confusing as well, though she means well. CHEM 451  was easier than this.

Had her for lab. I didn't do as well as I would have liked, but this was more my fault. Her lectures are clear and she repeats important material. It's a fair amount of work for a 1 credit course, but as long as you pay attention and make something of an effort, you'll do fine.

This was definitely the hardest class that I have taken at umich, but it was also my favorite class. Nolta is awesome and does everything that she can to help you, but her exams are brutal. Expect to work your ass off for a good grade in this class.

Nolta is so much fun! She is clearly passionate about teaching the material, so her enthusiasm is contagious. For Chem211, you definitely need the lab notebook, as it has all the experimental procedures in it. You also should attend lecture because it adds a lot that is not in the notebook. I learned a lot that helped me in Chem210, as well.

Nolta is the best in the chemistry department! She's interesting and explains the material really well. I had her for orgo 1 lab, so just one lecture a week and it was really easy stuff. Hopefully I can take another class with her in the future.
Dr. Nolta is the best professor in the entire world! Take a class with her!!! She should be teaching chem 210 every term

Don't take biochem unless you're taking it with Nolta. Sure Nolta's exams are hard af but you get to suffer with your entire class. Don't buy the book and just memorize EVERYTHING, even the tiniest details, on her slides and you'll be fine.

Yes Nolta is great but not only are you responsible for 80 slides per week, the exams that cover this material,  particularly short answer, are quite brutal. It's what happens when virtually everyone in the class likes biochem and is happy to put the work in. Take the mcdb or biolchem version if you can, not even Nolta makes this worthwhile

Nolta is a great person, but she will wreck you. She includes way way too much material in lectures and the only way to get all of the information is to check with the textbook. Her exams are BRUTAL and although I learned a ton, I felt like I was learning to take her exams instead of the material. I love her as a person, but not her teaching style.

LOVE. DR. NOLTA. All of the great things you hear about her are an underestimate. She's an incredible professor who knows orgo like the back of her hand and will go above and beyond to see her students succeed. You have to work for it because the exams are difficult but she makes the class better just by being Nolta. Also go to office hours!
It was hard. 11/10 would do again.
Nolta was my favorite professor so far at UMICH. She's friendly and hilariious :D
The best professor I've had at Michigan so far. Her office hours are very helpful. Very nice and takes time to make sure you understand.

Best professor I've ever had at Michigan (4 years) in any department. Very hard class. Her go-ahead lectures and open office hours (6+ hours extra per week) are very worthwhile and helpful. I've never seen a professor work so hard and care about her students so much.

Dr. Nolta is one of the best professors I have ever had. She teaches tough courses, but she does everything in her power to help her students and make them feel as comfortable as possible.  If you have her for any course, you will not regret it.
Was a little apprehensive going into the class, but Dr. Nolta took the time both in and out of class to help any student that sought her help.

She takes the time to make sure that you understand the material that she gives. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS I cant express how important it is to go to her for help the moment you are confused! I wish she taught 215 .

Nolta is the best prof at UM, hands down.

Dr. Nolta is the best! She also learns everyone's names. She's won a bunch of teaching awards, so she's actually the best. I didn't do too well but it was still my favorite class I've taken.

Amazing!
best orgo teacher I've ever had!!

take nolta for sure for orgo 1 and 2, she usually teaches orgo 1 in winter and 2 in spring, she is by far the best.
Go to her office hours.  It's still a difficult class, no matter who is teaching it.  Attend all lectures.
No Comments
The MOST awesome prof I've had at U-M!!  She's fantastic.  I highly recommend her.
awesome, definitely try to get her if you can, and always go to office hours
No Comments

Dr. Sanford is a fantastic lecturer. She lets you know exactly what's expected and covers a lot of content through MANY practice problems. She's also just all-around really good at what she does and has a lot of passion for the subject. Very organized, compassionate, and eager to help.
Amazing teacher, does practice problems, will stay after class to answer any questions.
Took CHEM 210 in FA'24, and I loved her. If you read ahead, her lectures are great reviews. GO to her OH, since they're long (1hr 30 min) and on Zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chem 210 is a difficult class, but professor Sanford is a queen and her knowledge with the subject helped greatly. She did move a bit slower than the other professors but I never felt she missed certain topics. Stanford also provided some nice humor that helped the class stay awake regardless of the dull subject matter and the 8 AM meeting time.

Professor Sandford is pretty good overall. This was her first time teaching 210 after a long time and it showed. While she lectured well, she often lagged behind other lecturers in teaching. She answered questions very well and was a good lecturer otherwise. Just supplement with lecture videos of other professors so you are on track.

Professor Sanford was decent for 215, but I wouldn't recommend her over Coppola. It seems that with the new coursepack, she wasn't as prepared as she would've been in earlier semesters. Certain topics were left out or very briefly mentioned without explanation, but they were on the exams. I'd suggest Coppola if you want to know all of the details.

Like CHEM210, CHEM215 is a very challenging course, and grades are determined exclusively by four exams. With that said, Dr. Sanford is an excellent professor, and her lectures are like no other. She manages to fit so much valuable content in 50 minutes without rushing; she is also great at answering questions. My GSI (Naish) was fantastic as well.

Dr. Sanford is truly one of the best professors I've had at Michigan. Chem 215 discusses some tough material, but Dr. Sanford makes it clear and comprehensible. She made orgo as enjoyable as possible for me. This class wont be easy, but if you have to take it, make sure you take it with Dr. Sanford! She's awesome!
Such a great lecturer, really cares about the topic and is good at clearly explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Sanford is awesome. You can tell that she's really passionate about organic chemistry, and her lectures are awesome. They're not too fast or too slow, and she explains difficult concepts very clearly. The class is hard, but that's not Sanford's fault. It's just a terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanford was great for Orgo 2. Although she can speak very fast and stutter, she conveys the material very clearly and is always on top of her stuff. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While Prof. Sanford talked very fast, the pace of the class was sometimes painfully slow. We got through just the basics of everything and you really needed to go to study groups or work hard on your own to understand all the other information. Tests were definitely harder than Orgo 1 but still manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: teaches super fast but not bad overall. however made a lot of mistakes that were either not made by others profs or corrected in SLC study group. which made it difficult to people without access to these resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Sanford was an awesome lecturer. Although she speaks loud and fast, you will get used to it after a week or so. I highly recommend taking orgo 2 with her if you can because she is very knowledgeable of the material. Also, emphasizes what students should know for exams. She is very approachable, and she is willing to help students!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanford is very knowledgeable about organic chemistry and is excited to teach. She talks very quickly so be prepared to follow her at her pace. Accessible in office hours. No-nonsense professor. You should attend lectures consistently to not fall behind on the material. Three exams and cumulative final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Sanford is nothing short of an amazing professor. Her notes are clear and detailed, and the lecture material is reflected in the exams. Long story short: if you are taking Chem 215, you absolutely CANNOT go wrong with Prof. Sanford. She's also personable, approachable, funny, and a chemistry wizard.

Sanford is a force of nature - brilliant, funny, and charming - and I highly recommend her for any class. 419 isn't hard if you've taken 210 and 215. All the material is covered in depth in the lectures, and the problem sets and quizzes are very representative of the exam content/format.

Sanford was absolutely amazing. 419 is a really interesting class that places Organic in a very practical context, and Dr. Sanford goes out of her way to make material relevant and interesting (although she does have some convoluted tangents). Exams and problem sets are challenging but fun and fair  definitely an awesome upper level Chemistry clas

Sanford was a great lecturer-- the material was interesting, she was funny, and explained things clearly. You will get a good grade if you put in the effort. The only thing is she seems a little unavailable--Overall though if you need a upper-level chem elective this is a great one to take!

Professor Sanford is amazing, all-around. She talks really fast, but she explains everything very clearly and often tells funny stories about her own experiences and career. She's extremely supportive both in office hours and outside of class. One of the best professors I've had at University of Michigan, 1010 would recommend.

Melanie is such an inspiration. Besides being an amazing career scientist, her passion for conveying her love of chemistry to her students is apparent. The sense of community the class offered was facilitated by both Professor Sanford and Dr. Pérez. The extra work is worth it 100%. Orgo II changed my life.

An amazing professor and has been by far the best I've had so far at UMich.  The class is A LOT of work, especially in the last month, but grade wise the class will probably get you a better grade than regular Orgo 2 just based off the fact that the class isn't 100% exams (it's like %50).  Great class though.

This class is HARD, and at the same time it is probably easier than normal orgo 2... While the exams were extremely difficult, they only counted for around 10% of your grade (except the final). The other points come from weekly quizzes ranging from easy to insane and an SSG project (which is super time-consuming but not hard). I loved it though!

Professor Sanford is a great professor. Her lectures are clear (for the most part), her knowledge is deep, and her passion for teaching is obvious. Her exams and quizzes vary from fair to challenging. While 215HH has a huge workload, it is a bit easier to achieve a higher grade because only 60% of your grade is determined by major exams.

Prof. Sanford was my lab lecturer, and I loved orgo lab. She is obviously brilliant, and good at explaining things. I always understood the material from CHEM 210 better in 211 lecture. She speaks very fast, so be ready to take notes quickly. Your grade is totally based on your GSI, though.

I struggled through Orgo I and when I took Orgo II I thought I would have difficulty as well.  However, Professor Sanford totally changed my mind about the course and helped me do way better. She teaches stuff that is only necessary, and really prepares you for the exam.  Go to every lecture, she makes it worth your time and is really helpful!

Easily my favorite professor in the entire school. Coming to class was actually enjoyable because of how much she loved organic chemistry. Explained things in ways that made everything seem much easier-definetly recommend.

Dr. Sanford was my favorite professor this semester hands down. I was registered for a different section of the class, but attended her lecture twice a week when I had free time. She made orgo II comprehensible, which is a difficult task. Take this class (or any chemistry class) if she's teaching a section... you won't be sorry!

This professor is AMAZING. Her lectures are clear, she reviews almost every lesson so it is very hard to fall behind, and her awkwardness and sense of humor make the class so much more interesting to attend. She is also a world famous organic chemist! Googling her and reading her wiki page made me that much more thankful to be in her class!

Great professor! She taught clearly. Everything in the exam is in her lecture notes and coursepack. I went to every lectures and a weekly study group that helps me with coursepack. Got an A without lots of works!
Hard class, but best professor for it. She's literally amazing

I was very scared of this class after not doing so well in orgo 1. But she made orgo 2 very manageable. This semester was her first time teaching orgo 2 and I had a lot of fun in this class. I am doing better in orgo 2 than I did in orgo 1.

Professor Sanford is an amazing teacher for Orgo 2.  Dr. Coppola is a tough act to follow in terms of quality and she knocked it out of the park.  This is a hard class and she was able to explain the material in a logical manner. DON'T believe the hype that Orgo at Michigan is impossible. The teachers are great and will get you that A if you work

Orgo 2 with Professor Sanford made way more sense than when I took orgo 1 with someone else. She's incredibly organized and outlines each lecture beforehand. She's clear and explains things thoroughly. Plus, she's really funny.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS CLASS! She is so helpful. I started off bad on the first midterm, but she helped me so much that I did so well on the next two midterms to bring my grade by a full letter (based on the orgo 1 scale from last semester). Now I'm confident that I can do very well in this class, thanks to her!

Made orgo 2 so interesting.  She is absolutely hilarious and extremely smart, and explains things perfectly.  I don't even read the text book, and I'm getting an A in this class right now. (I got a B in orgo 1).
She is amazing! I cannot think of a better person to teach this class!
Not an easy class, but yeah she explains the stuff better than the other instructors this semester.
I think she is a great professor. Yeah that first exam was rough. But she is clear in her explanations and is definitely better than all the other orgo 2 lecturers this semester.

This class changed quite a bit. She does explain the stuff well, and yeah she lists certain coursepack questions you should be able to do. However, the material you expect to see on a given exam is very inconsistent with in the past. This is not good because now practice exams are literally useless in helping you prepare.

She's actually pretty good at teaching the material. She does make some mistakes, but you can still learn a lot from her. The only complaint I have is that this semester the course is not very organized. Now you can't rely on practice tests to prepare for exams.

Excellent professor. Great explanations of DIFFICULT concepts and reasonable expectations (but still expect to study hard to do well). I highly recommend taking a class from her while you're at Michigan. Your chemistry experience won't be complete without it.
Mel's my hero.

Although I was first skeptical because of her nervous, hyper appearance with frequent stuttering, I grew to appreciate the way she explained things. Very clear and very understandable. She taught the class exactly what we needed to know, and when some GSI's would take her place, it wouldn't be the same.
Best professor, very helpful both inside and outside of class, knows her stuff very well, genius in field of chemistry but has trouble adding :P

Professor Sanford is the best lecturer for Orgo 1, hands down. She teaches everything very well so that everyone can understand even the most difficult concepts. She prepares you well for the exams by giving lots of example problems, which when you take Orgo 1, you will see how useful it is for the exam. She's also incredibly smart and nice.

Sanford is the absolute best! She explains things so thoroughly and clearly. Her lectures are extremely organized and interesting. She knows exactly what she has to do for everyone to understand. She prepares you really well for the exams! <3!
Difficult class, would only recommend if you did really well in Chem 210.  Good professor though- office hours are helpful but sometimes she doesn't understand your question.

Sanford is a great teacher. She really knows her stuff and gets excited about it.  She loves to give little tidbits of fun facts that make lecture bearable. One of my favorite profs for freshman year.
Professor Sanford is an excellent teacher!  I wish I could have her for Chem 215.
Professor Sanford is really funny. Even though she'll make mistakes sometimes, give her a chance, and you'll learn a lot from her. Go to office hours, she's super down-to-earth and helpful.
Melanie Sanford is by far my greatest professor this year.  She made my freshman year wonderful and eased me in to the world of chemistry.  GO BLUE

Professor Sanford is awesome. She does a terrific job of explaining things and is willing to answer questions mid-lecture, but not too many. She is also very funny and INCREDIBLY involved and excited in teaching each lesson. Really. Great.

Professor Sanford has a clear understanding of the material, and is one of the only orgo lecturers who will really go over a concept and not just zip through it. I have more trust in her than in any of the other professors. I recommend her section!

Sanford was a pretty awesome teacher. I think that a lot of people find the course hard because they are not willing to treat the class like they should... a problem solving class! She had a very clear understanding of what she was teaching and could explain things really well!

Sanford tries really hard and overall does a pretty good job. She messes up occasionally, but it's rarely on something important and always has to do with something you should have known anyway. She's really nice and her explanations are pretty clear. She tells you what you'll need to know for the exam and does problems relevant to the exam.
wonderful

Excellent teacher, though the material was dense, she was always  interesting in lecture. She was new to Chem210 when I had her so she wasn't entirely familiar with the exam grading, however if you went to her office hours she would do coursepack problems and sometimes she would do problems that were very similar to problems that showed up on exams

The whole CHEM 210 class itself is set up rather poorly, as is the style of the exams.  As for the teacher: kind of unclear; doesn't directly explain many of the concepts involved...she just gives a few of examples so as to "get the gist of it"; sometimes doesn't cover some material that appeared on exams.  Overall, not up to my expectations.

Stanford is notorious for telling students wrong information causing them to make mistakes on the exams. Most of the time when asked a question should would tell a student to look in the book.  She is an awful professor. I did better not going to class than I did when I went to her lectures.
Great lecturer, very hard class though.
I think Sanford's awesome. She explains everything pretty clearly and she is very energetic, which makes the student be more into what she's saying ( as opposed to falling alseep!)

Very nice, helpful. Make sure you study with people with other lecturers though because occasionally she will misinform/not inform you about important things for the exams. Notes on the board are sometimes incomprehensible because of numerous arrows. One awesome thing about Sanford is she discusses real life applications of organic chem.

Sanford is a great teacher, knows what she's talking about. Does make a few mistakes while speaking, but if you can't figure out that she accidentally said the wrong thing you shouldn't be in the class. Very helpful, and wants to help students understand. Class is difficult, but not because of bad teaching, only hard tests.
Great teacher.  Cares about students, is engaging as a lecturer, and very smart.

The hesitations are endearing and her slip ups actually help you understand what is going on because you are able to catch what is wrong when she writes it on the board.  And her handwriting is impecable...I've never seen anyone write so legibly on a chalk board

Sanford is a great teacher. She's not so great at drawing chair structures of cyclohexanes or determining bond angles, but she lets you know that these are faults! The negative impact on learning is minimal. She's really funny and truly loves her subject.
Great teacher.

I love Sanford! She is very excited about teaching and her lectures are clear. The exams are also pretty reasonable, this class is probably easier than the regular orgo 2 w/ gugelchuck, although it's a lot of work.

Professor Sanford is the only Professor at the University that has shown true interest in what she is teaching.  By no means is the class easy, but you actually feel like you are learning something when Professor Sanford teaches.  Her class is great, and I have gained a whole new outlook in organic.
Professor Sanfrod is an amazing, charismatic, and very clear professor, and as other people have commented, sparks or rekindles love of chemistry.
She makes you pay attention.  If you aren't, you'll miss the whole class.
Professor Sanford is very clear and easy to understand.  She is helpful and interesting.  She is also energetic and cares about students.
One of the best professors I've ever had.  Actually taught useful information and not just theory.  Dr. Sanford made me remember why I love chemistry.
No Comments

Can come off as confusing. I expected more from this class based off the name of the class since it seems interesting but it's just the same as any other psych class. Also with the use of top-hat... I didn't enjoy it at all.
Dr. Tronson is clear and thorough. The material isn't super interesting, but it is challenging and it's nice to have a professor who teaches such material with so much enthusiasm and clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Tronson is an expert in her field, and it really shows. She is very organized and thoroughly covers each topic before moving on to the next. Very many quizzes (1 per class), though these were fair and doable so long as you keep up with readings. The exams were dense, but she was always very willing to hear out your thoughts behind iffy answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Tronson was extremely knowledgeable  on the course material and always encouraged students to ask questions, but the daily quizzes and the constant readings (some of which were several dozen pages long) was a bit excessive- too many lecture slides!

Very knowledgable/fair grading! Its hard to understand all the material because its so in depth. She expects you to think above and beyond the readings before we even cover the subject matter. If you like to be challenged in thinking this is a great class! I enjoyed this class it taught me to think outside the box.  You have to work hard for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Prof. Tronson as a lecturer, just was not a fan of the course itself. Every 3rd-ish class was a workshop/group discussionday, which I don't rock w/. She's extremely personable+helpful, and has this very certain, almost sly, quickness about her. (Also you can prob get full pts on all the bi-weekly quizzes w/o doing any readings)

Dr. Tronson gave amazing lectures and seemed to be very prepared for her classes. She also seems very attentive and really wants her students to understand the topics, so, if you don't get it, ask it again and she'll explain it as many times as needed. Also, go to her office hours, they're useful. Honestly, it was my favorite class that semester.

Dr. Tronson knows a lot and also does research on the concepts discussed in class, however, she isn't very good at teaching a well-structured course. Lectures seemed disorganized and even contradictory at times. I honestly feel like I didn't even learn that much.

Natalie comes to class SO prepared its great. She always makes her slides very detailed and its very helpful. You have to read before coming to class, because there are daily quizzes. During her lectures, she discusses a lot of things that aren't in the readings, so it's very important to go.

She's a new prof, without experience; a researcher with lab insight but cannot teach a well-structured course. We all know those survey courses that go over a scattershot of topics without any coherent, larger picture: avoid Psych 443. I hardly learned anything. Nice person though!

I am so glad I took this. Professor Tronson is great! She really has a lot of knowledge on the topics that she teaches and she made the class interesting.  The class was focused around reading research articles and discussing them in class.  Do the readings, participate, and you'll do well in the class while learning A LOT!
One of the worst labs ive ever taken. We did the same 3 experiments over and over again, with completely randomized grades.
Grades are based on a toss up, and often rubrics wont even be explained.
have no idea what grade will appear at this point.
Unclear grading system that makes it impossible to know your final grade until like the day before the semester ends. Makes a 2 credit lab much harder than it needs to be.

Atrocious class structure. If you want an A, you must go beyond what is provided in the rubric (she doesn't follow the guidelines). Rubric guidelines alone will give you a 3 at best; 4+ comes from a non-standardized amount of extra effort. Regrade requests are often meaningless unless you have objective evidence of fault, and she is very demeaning.

This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken. The grading is so unbelievably unclear and the professor makes it nearly impossible to succeed in this class. Be prepared to put at minimum an addition of nearly 5 hours each week aside from in lab just to be given a 2/5 on your efforts for the week for no reason.

Grading criteria are unclear, making full points nearly unattainable. I maintained A-level work all term, but the final quiz and practical lowered my grade significantly and without explanation. The class content is straightforward, yet grades are artificially deflated. The instructor is condescending and actively works against student success.

After releasing our final "lab practical" grade we were told we aren't allowed to see what we got marked down for. All we know is she could've just rolled a dice for the grades. If you are taking this class with her next semester pray for your sanity and expect it to be worse than you may even think. The worst professor I've ever dealt with.
Worst class I have ever taken at UMich, this class ruined my 4.0 I had going for 2 years through orgo 2 and biochem!
Tries to take points off to artificially lower the class median. Hard to do well as expectations must be fully exceeded to get an A. Dr. Nguyen is also condescending to students.
her grading is designed to make u not get a high grade. They take off points for nothing. If you meet with her she is somewhat condescending. I wouldn't recommend taking her as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough grading on individual lab reports. Earning a 5/5 is nearly impossible. The recent quiz was regraded after submissions with a different key, which lowered scores. Regrade requests were strongly discouraged by mentioning how almost all result in a lower score. Be prepared for a strict and extremely frustrating grading style.
Keep In mind that rate my professor keeps taking down ratings.... there are more bad ratings that you arent seeing
I honestly have no words
Grading criteria very unclear, doesn't seem like she likes students or cares about their success, seems annoyed when students ask questions
what is this grading structure bruh she better curve this

very harsh grader, save yourself and take with someone else. don't expect help, high grades, or a good experience. I have never been angrier than i have in this class, and my blood boils thinking about how BAFFLED i am that she still teaches here. She forgets that she was once a student struggling through college, and that is the biggest crime.
It feels like she doesn't want her students to do well. Too bad this is required for so many people.
plz for the love of god reconsider signing up for her lectures when you register for classes
have never felt so defeated in a class

To say she is a tough grader would not be true because that implies that there is an objective grading scale on which she can be tough. I prefer the words "nonsensical grader", I would have better odds winning roulette in Vegas than guessing my post-lab grade. It feels like she just rolls a 5-sided die for grades.

It is very difficult to get full points on any assignments. Post-lab questions are not covered in lecture, she just expects people to know. The maximum grade is 3/5 if you do not submit a conclusion, yet if your conclusion is bad enough it can drop you grade to 2/5. Why is a blank conclusion worth more points than a bad conclusion?
I'm gonna be honest this class is a bit challenging, but nothing a tuff guy like me couldn't do.
The class itself isn't hard, it's just that the grading is not good. You'll rarely get a 5/5 on your post-labs and the quizzes are really hard for no reason even after studying immensely.

On labs she asks post lab Qs that she doesn't go over in lecture, and aren't even talked about in chem 215. She just expects you to have the chemistry knowledge of a chem PHD, and I am literally a just a freshman. She told us that 60 minutes was enough time for our entire lab practical because a GSI was able to do it (literally a chemistry GSI)
the quiz answers were literally wrong?? She says no regrades for this quiz which unfairly impacts so many people because of her mistakes. NEVER take this class with this professor
Unfair, so much effort for a 2 credit class with unfair and unrealistic grading. Take honors
i just can't believe how all she wants is for us to do bad. it's really upsetting. Like support your students don't bring down.
Be prepared for incorrect answer keys for quizzes with no regrade requests. All this for 2 credits :(
Take the honors course, I repeat, take the honors course with Poniatowski, even he is fairer than this.
Postponing this course and redoing your schedule may honestly be the better option if you want to avoid an unnecessarily punishing grading experience.
I can't believe this is the only option for orgo 2 lab.

She wants students to fail. She seems easy-going in lectures, then is rude and dismissive over email and when you ask questions. She expects you to find expected data when there is none on the sites she gives. She has very harsh rubrics, they are not clearly outlined, and the graders often miss included items and take off points.
not great not as bad as could be
needs to be banned from teaching this class again
Please. we all know the prof or one of her GSIs wrote those 5/5 ratings.
While the historical median for this class is an A I am not sure that this will reflect the median of Dr. Nyguens class. It's almost like she wants people to not do well, I dont really get it.
This was the worst class ive ever taken at the university
I love class thru and thru yay thu
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She wants all of her students to do poorly. You can do everything right and she'll still find something wrong with it. I have accommodations for certain things and she disregarded everything, saying that they don't apply to Chem labs. She does not want you to do well, disregards actual learning, and will stress you out.
Literally find any other professor to take this with I'm not joking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've never been more infuriated. Do EVERYTHING POSSIBLE to avoid her. Impossible to get a good grade on post labs, pointless office hours, doesn't care to help you. Very obvious that she doesn't want ppl to do well. If you have her...good luck
