Probably the worst professor I have ever had. Actively goes out of her way to make everything harder for students, from unnecessary clicker questions to hiding extra credit points in announcements. The post-labs are impossible. You could put in hours of work and still get a 3/5. Do not take this class. I wish I had taken the honors lab instead.

Worst prof I have EVER had. Don't even bother asking questions because you will receive a condescending attitude. Spends more time during lecture tricking you on the iclicker than actually teaching useful material. You will rarely/never do better than a 3 or 4 / 5 (if you're lucky) on the post-labs no matter how much you try. Stay FAR away from her
Very unclear what is expected of students,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are reading this before registering for classes, push this lab off another semester and take it with a diff professor.
Most stressful and least favorite class I've taken so far. This class should be an opportunity to learn, not to worry about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, I'm not trying to be mean, but Dr. Nguyen you need to understand that how you structured this class did not help our learning. We stressed every day and never understood why we got the grades that we did. I promise you I know my stuff. Does my grade reflect that? Frustratingly no. You need to fix this class.
Very good professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The grade distribution is shockingly low. Do not take this class.
Not a great class. Very unsupportive learning environment. Did not feel like this class taught me anything. It only gave me anxiety. Cannot wait to be done.

Do not even bother asking for a regrade on your lab. She will likely mark it down even further and find more "problems" with your lab. Some examples of problems I've noticed from my and my friends lab:date missing, incomplete title, wrong order of pages, etc (I know theres worse im not remembering). Do not take.
Bad experience overall. Grades on her own established curve to only award a certain number of perfect scores.
Grading very inconsistent and unforgiving.
Grading is so inconsistent, but if you have a question or want a regrade might as well just not even try. She will not help and tell you it isn't her fault.

She does not care about you, one time she told me when I went up to ask her about a grade, "I can't help you, I will forget about you in 5 minutes." If you put in the maximum effort, you will still get 4/5 max on the lab, and there is no way to tell the grade you have until after you finish the class.

Uses underinforming as a technique to spread out grades. Grading seemed to be disorganized and arbitrary, a GSI even said they were told to only give out ~3 perfect scores per class. Seemed determined to make students the enemy, and was extremely rude when handling regrades
actually what is this class. do not take.

There is no way of knowing what your grade is in this class. If you put in work and effort, you will still do poorly. The lab practical was not fair and had no clear grading scale. I recommend staying away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Their grading system is rough and she does not seek to help out. I reached out to her via email and was very rude and condescending. She would not let me see my lab practical and gave me some attitude when I asked to view it. Also, she does not know topicity at all, and decided to put it on the final when she couldnt answer questions herself.
Are we serious? The practical compares your percent yield with the rest of the class and that's how you're graded?? So much for learning. We get punished for things out of our control.

I have a better chance of knowing my grade using a random number generator than trying to understand my post-lab grades. No matter what you do you will always get a 3 or 4 out of 5. Even the gsi's have said that she makes them limit the amount of 5s they can give out no matter how good your post lab may be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: bad and loves to fail people even when rubric is followed to perfection and feedback is followed for next lab
Harsh grading scale
do not take

Easy lab class turned extremely difficult. Grading criteria is almost never clear. Consistently doing something on the lab will get you points one week and no points another week. Professor claims to curve grades down to keep grade distribution low. If avoidable, do not take with this professor.
What a ridiculous class. Unclear grading. Who knows what I'm going to get in the class at this point. An A in Chem 215 and for what.

I put hours into this class and attend every lecture and still am receiving a 3/5 on every assignment. There are no consistent grading scale for the post-lab assignments, and all she cares about is trying to trick students. She is condescending during lecture.
Not a great professor she made this lab incredibly difficult for no reason and her grading makes no sense
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Genuinely feel like they want me to fail. This is a 2-credit lab, are we being for real?
She cares more about the grade distribution being low than her students actually learning the content. Only take 216 with her if there is absolutely no other option.

Probably one of the worst professors I have ever had at UofM. They claim to give you guidelines on how to a pre/post lab but then you can NEVER get a 5. I have gotten a range of scores on them and the feedback has quite literally been the same. Get out while you can
What a joke of a class.
I got points off on a point lab for shade being in my post lab in a scan. I dont know what to do at this point lol. Laughing through the pain.
I wish I could rate her even lower.

This is the worst professor I have ever had in my time here. I did well in chem 215 yet I am doing worse in the lab. She does not care about her students and wants them to fail. She purposely tries to trick her students and grading is impossible even if you do everything on the rubric. Avoid at all costs.
She needs to teach something else. 216 is not supposed to be this difficult.
I wish I could leave a 0/5 on this.

I had the unfortunate displeasure of having Dr. Nguyen for both Orgo 1 and 2 lab. In both classes, she was disrespectful towards her students. She constantly condescends to us, and questions are met with snide answers and the response "you should know this already". She has manufactured an inhospitable learning environment with impossible grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class needs to be revamped because what in the world. Genuinely harder to get an A in the lab than in the lecture. If you do everything asked of you, you'll probably get a 3/5 on every lab. How to get the 5/5, I couldn't tell you. Very disheartening to put so much work into a class, which is literally just a lab, to have it end like this.

Demonstrates consistent incompetence in terms of actually testing the understanding of her students. Nearly impossible to receive full credit on labs/assignments because she is grading for absolute perfection, not for the criteria provided in the rubrics. In addition to being unhelpful, she's downright condescending to students who ask questions.

This class could be so simple and educational, but instead she spends her time having us pick between c and e for true or false and fabricating data. The only thing she cares about is not having work. Any questions are answers with extreme sass, she does not care at all about her students. The GSIs are great, but they are forced to follow her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the most unclear class ever. The rubric is there and if you fill everything out directly to the rubric, you will NOT get full credit.

Never felt like my grade for a class was more out of my control before. Dont take ts. Material isn't that difficult and I know what i'm doing every lab. Grades for post lab submissions are marked down to 4/5 for the most random reasons. also more concerned about making the most elaborate weird iclicker questions for lecture than teaching material

Just told the whole class that our grades for the final lab practical will be partially based on our percent yield compared to the class's average percent yield for each compound. Essentially just told everyone we are going to get marked down if we don't fabricate data.

She is the definition of making things harder than they need to be and deflating grades for no reason. Take the orgo lab with another professor. Also, most of her ideologies are just backwards or plain wrong
She doesnt seem to want students to learn just wants to give out bad lab grades. Its a very unfair class.

I've never written a review before, but she has proven to be very disrespectful, uncaring, and unaccommodating. Never have I had such a difficult time with a professor. Simple questions are met with annoyance or non-answers. Written lab report guidelines aren't well followed despite following procedure 100%.

She's impossible to talk to and  condescending. Responds to questions with attitude instead of helping. She makes mistakes in her lectures and we get penalized for pointing them out and answering correctly.

she spends more time trying to trick us on iclicker questions that don't count for credit, than helping us succeed in lab. i put so much effort in to my post labs each week, but still continue to get low scores. she wants to lower the median grade of the class to ruin our lives. be warned that you will be spending HOURS working on post labs
genuinely what is wrong with her... i need to sue for emotional distress.

Grading is not based on your ability to read the professor's mind. Hidden criteria she doesn't tell you about or will act like certain things are optional when they aren't to get a 5/5. Abysmal lab protocol and course organization. Impossible to know what's expected of you. Making course grade median much harsher. You will learn nothing.

Never in my life have I had a teacher that genuinely doesn't care about learning and only cares about points on a rubric. The problem isn't harsh grading its the fact that this woman isn't even a good teacher content-wise. Rude and too good to answer questions or actually teach anything. Don't take this class if you want to learn.

Such a pointless course. They take off points like they're getting paid for it. You can do everything right according to the rubric and they'll still find something to take off for. Genuinely doing the most for 2 credits. Idk why they think people care abt lab.
This professor is condescending toward the students and she limits the amount of 5s the GSI can give and now no one dares to give out 5s. They simply deduce points for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've taken at this school. I did amazingly in CHEM 215, and yet none of that is reflected. My GSI literally said she made him regrade because his scores were too high. Ridiculous class, the grading is so harsh; even when your GSI says your work looks fine, you still will get points off.

Run away. GSI informed me that she only allows a certain amount of 5/5 on asgnmts they grade, resulting in you being graded down for either no reason (literally no comments) or due to extremely picky/irrelevant mistakes, extremely subjective - no rubric. Don't try oh bc she's unwilling to have constructive dialogue. Wants to decr class avg 4 no rea

I found this course significantly more challenging than expected, even compared to Chem 215. The grading felt very strict, and I often lost points which I felt were lost at random. At times, explanations during lecture differed from what was expected for post labs, which cost points. I found interactions with her to be quite unhelpful.

This class is so utterly ridiculous I don't even know what to say. The grading is totally random each week, every time I ask a GSI for help they don't know what's going on, and the spec lab is a joke. Impossible and the printed material is wrong and corrected mid-class. Getting an 80% on a 5-10 pg assignment for one error is actually insane.
I prefer to have a stroke than to have the lab.

Quizzes are graded very strictly, with inconsistent partial credit (some high-point questions have none), so small mistakes cost a lot. GSI are scared to give out 5/5 for postlab. This prof is consciously controlling students grade to be within C+ to B, so she won't curve it up. For who wishing to keep a solid GPA, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!

The grading in this [2 credit]class is unnecessarily confusing and feels designed to keep averages low rather than help students actually learn. The quizzes do not reflect the level of depth given in lecture. She also has too much sass with students, which makes it uncomfortable to ask her questions. Only took her again after 211 because I had to.

When my friends took her class in 2025 apparently she was amazing, the grading criteria was clear, and her lectures were clear. This semester all the changes she has made are really bad, everything starts to look similar to Chem 211, including the grading (which is the worst part). The GSI's are scared to give 5/5 on the post lab.
Treats students like they're not allowed to ask questions, feedback takes forever to receive, and grading is unclear. Save yourself the headache.

I had her in 211 and somehow 216 is worse. While there is a clear grading scheme this time, it doesn't seem like the graders even follow it. She can be quite condescending to students who are asking genuine questions. Once again, she seems more focused on grade distribution than learning.

The grading scheme in this class was very confusing and frustrating to everyone. It seemed like she was more focused on making a tough grade distribution than having students understand and enjoy the material. The quizzes were insanely hard for the details that we were taught. Would not take again, but here I am taking her in 216...

This is the worst, least flexible, most disrespectful teacher I have ever had. She could not care less about students, implements a grading scale that is fully based on GSI feelings that day, and is overall disrespectful. Feels like she is happy when she sees her students not do well.

Very unclear grading system - I had no idea what my final grade would be until posted. Does not really care about students, quizzes were not reflective of what we learned in class, and the class was unnecessarily stressful.
She's by far the worst professor in all of the Chemistry department. Lectures are nonsensical and often wrong, and she's is very uncaring about her students.

Very disrespectful to students and the class structure is not organized. The grade you receive weekly for labs is based on vibes not your work. In lab GSI's don't know how to answer any questions but when grading will take points off for everything.

Her lectures were very unhelpful compared to the lab. She often seemed unprepared for lectures, as it often felt like the students knew more than her during lectures.  The grading is very ambiguous, as although there's a structure unlike 211, it almost feels like lab grades are taken given at random.

Dr. Nguyen made mistakes making the quizzes and refused to give me points back when there was a problem with the question itself. She also questioned me when I had to be excused from lab due to a religious holiday. The grading criteria was very clear, though.

Better grading system than 211 but they just hand out random scores. She made several mistakes on quizzes and had to be corrected multiple times in class. She would pop into lab sometimes and it felt like she was looking for mistakes students would make.

I'll give her the benefit of the doubt because I think this was her first semester, but her class was very disorganized. Students would have to correct her during lectures because she didn't know the answers to her own problems, and quizzes were unclear and unfair (and had to be corrected multiple times). At least her grading was clear, unlike 211

I just don't get why some teachers like to make everyone's lives harder. Quizzes had questions that you literally could not solve (NMR matching) and she would have to regrade them. Better solution is just to make sure to put out coherent quizzes to avoid stressing everyone out. I would not recommend at all if you have the choice.

Kinda fast and hard to keep up with at times. Grade pretty much solely depends on GSI. You could get  2/3 on all labs (A- work acording to them) and still get below an A- at the end. They post a rubric for lab submissions but are very stingy with 3/3s and their feedback is so vague. Should be fine if you look prepared and get your GSI to like you.
Easy class and GSI's are great, but good god she is horrible. Made mistakes in our dry lab and also screwed up the quizzes. Also just not helpful when you ask her questions
Most disorganized course and disrespectful to students

He's a great teacher who knows that people normally take his class for fun or because they have to for a credit requirement. He has lots of passion for teaching film and treats students with respect. Not gonna lie though, some of the screenings are boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Noble-Olson was great...class not so much. Maybe just not a fan of film theory, but I found the concepts to be incredibly difficult and frustrating because of how little we were graded on. But Matt was always good at engaging in conversations with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Noble-Olson's Detroit class, FTVM 335. I really liked the movie theater history project, it was probably one of the most unique assignments I've done in any FTVM course. It's a group thing, though, so keep that in mind if you're thinking of taking this course. Overall, 335 has a light workload and it's a fun class. Would recommend!

had a great time in this class! matthew is super approachable and fun to talk to if you have more interest in action cinema. the theory readings he assigns can be tricky but they're p much graded for completion on perusall. the course has 3 papers but they're nothing crazy, 1000-1500 words

I found the material covered in class to be very interesting, although at times they were a bit tricky to comprehend. Overall, this course was taught very well and I was comfortable when asking questions.
One of the hidden gems of the film department. Very knowledgeable and will entertain any discussion in class which can be really fun.

Matthew was one of my two lecturers for FTVM 150—a decent professor and a nice guy. After lectures, he's easily approachable and willing to answer questions. However, he tends to say "uh," and "um," a lot when lecturing. Not a big deal for some people, but it's hugely distracting and detracts from the class experience if you're like me.
Makes theory readings interesting. Only knows a handful of the student's names, though. I realize that is hard, however. I enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: mean, short tempter, easily fustrated, creates a stressful environment

Professor Nucci's demeanor was quite dismissive and created a high sense of pressure to the point where I felt uncomfortable speaking in fear of being heavily judged by him and my peers. As a freshman new to Ross where participation matters most, this slashed my confidence. A heady air of competition and bragging is encouraged in the classroom.

This professor is very impatient & easily frustrated, creating a tense, uncomfortable environment. Very ironic for a communication teacher. Expectations are so vague & grading is extremely strict & feedback feels blunt not helpful. Participation grades depend solely on hand-raising, adding pressure & is honestly unfair to those who have anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nucci is a good lecturer & leads discussion real well in this course. I like his feedback on presentations & written communications. He goes through case studies & real life examples really well. Overall, pretty engaging class & challenges the soft skills. The RIS part was not too bad either, and just study the slides & course content for the quiz.

BCOM is a terrible class, but Nucci made it palatable. He was very energetic when presenting and always had an anecdote about the subject. He grades very harshly as he wants to drive home the material. Make sure to frontload all the writing you do, and you will do reasonably well

I don't like leaving bad reviews, but AVOID Professor Nowicki. She is incredibly rude in lectures and makes the most extreme backhanded comments you have ever seen. Tons of homework on the weekends, but not much during the week. Lectures have iClicker, so attendance is mandatory.

really liked Dr. Nowicki. She genuinely wants the best for students and really supported me when I needed it. The class also helped me in my research labs! I plan to take her higher level classes after 173.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Nowicki is passive-aggressive at times, but her lectures are exceptional. She takes the time to answer questions and truly cares about students. You don't need the textbook, but do the PQ sets. GO TO ALS!

She is not a good professor. I don't like to write negative reviews, but I am just self-teaching myself all of this as we're given 2+ hours of lecture to study before every week and class time, which is mandatory for attendance, is to just do practice problems. I don't think her teaching helps the structure of the class
Very passive agressive
beware of iclicker
Didn't love this course but Nowicki does a great job at explaining things clearly and theres so much extra credit offered
Professor Carly is the best professor and her her lectures are very interactive.
....Overall, my favourite professor.
This class was super fun and it worked to me as a relief. Professor Carly is super knowledgeable and I learned many things from her.
Labs were too long and I believe that this is what they should adjust (3hrs!) but Dr. Nowicki is professional and she'll let you love science.

Professor Carly is the most professional professor I've ever seen! She cares about her students a lot and she biology very enjoyable and not boring at all. She made everything easy to follow. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

This is the second time I have taken a class with Dr. Nowicki and she is undoubtably my favorite professor I have had here. She is incredibly caring and goes out of her way to ensure students are mentally and physically taken care of.

I didn't really interact with Professor Nowicki, but my GSI was great and he made the class enjoyable overall. The grading system is points based so it's really easy to succeed and get an A. I would recommend!

While Dr. Nowicki could be condescending at times, she always outlined exactly what was expected. The grading system was very forgiving, tests were fair, and there were lots of opportunities to get extra points. The field trips were super fun and engaging. Labs were a little tedious and were very dependent on your GSI (shoutout to my goat Kai).

nowicki is a great instructor. she genuinely loves her job and cares abt students' wellbeing. the class is never boring; we always have something different going on like a group project or field trip. its cringe when she tries to appeal to a younger audience but lowk funny too. lecture is mandatory with iclicker; u can skip some and be fine

Lectures are not insufferable but she does seem very passive aggressive and annoying at times. The review for tests are nothing like the actual test but you only need 375/460 total points to pass and that is an 81% so thats very generous. The three-hour abs however are painful to sit through. I would take again.

Comments about her attitude are not exaggerated, but you only need a 375/460 to get a 4.0 in the class, which is an 81%. She likes to brag about her kids being smart and it passive aggressive sometimes, but if you can look past that, her exams are honestly fun but she has questions that will trick you. However, they were not exceedingly difficult.

These reviews seem pretty exaggerated. Bio173 is an easy A if you show up and do the work. You need 375 points out of 460 total offered for an A which is pretty generous. Exams are a little weird but all multiple choice so it's not too bad. She's not a great lecturer but you don't need to fully understand everything she goes over in lecture for lab

Avoid her. Awful class structure and has two exams for a lab course. The exam wording is extremely vague and she gives out "Practice exams" with free responses when the actual exam is multiple choice and has nothing to do with practice ones.

She likes to make her essays reading comprehension tests instead of biology ones. She is insufferable to listen to in lecture and she makes the worst analogies to try and "relate" to the class. If you can take a class NOT with her it is a personal victory.

Her lectures really are not terrible, but I do not agree with the way that the class is structured at all. Nowicki requires us to stay in lab all 3 hours, regardless of productivity, and to be entirely honest--is not the friendliest. Honestly probably would take again if was the only choice, but def not on my own accord.
Even for question like what is your favorite part of the class has a correct answer...
Good class. Easy. Carly gives bot

She was a very engaging lecturer and good at explaining concepts. She was straight to the point (which may have come off as condescending to others), but this was refreshing to me as it was clear what I had to know or not. I appreciate the emphasis she put on science communication. The class was also easy to do well in.
Confusing exams, boring lectures, iclickers graded for accuracy where only 10% of class gets right.
Class was not difficult to get an A. The lab is pretty okay, but she is such a passive aggressive and condescending person, would be so much more interesting without her lectures!

She is an alright teacher and 173 is a pretty easy class. Expectations are very clear but unfortunately she has a habit of going back on her word. Class would be less stressful if she was an honest person.

If you've ever wanted to relive high school, this is the class. She talks to everyone like we're 15, polite yet condescending, and exams are so vague, it's just about decoding her wording. There are exams instead of lab practicals and way too many random assignments for a LAB course. Good luck, being a required class,sadly, there's no escaping her.

i ain't even out of her class yet and im already so sick of these papers. labs aren't hard at all, its the follow-up assignments that'll kill you. plus its wild that your grade is determined basically by your exams, since lab attendance doesn't count for much. shes also incredibly passive aggressive and her lectures feel like shes yelling at you.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a okay professor but the exams were full of trick questions, and it felt like I was being assessed on my reading comprehension and not the content itself. Most of the time you're just trying to decipher what the question is asking you. Also the flipped classroom is a waste of time.
Lectures tend to be slightly annoying.
gave me the worst bubble guts of all time after eating that fiber one bar for an experiment.
I took her Bio 171 class Winter 2025, she was super clear about course expectations and was always willing to answer questions during office hours. Be sure to stay on top of readings and discussions!
Legit questions are written like riddles. You can understand everything and still get marked down.

This class may seem easy, but the tests are confusing and full of trick questions. I read every recommended textbook section and still struggled. The content isn't hard, but the way it's assessed is unfair. Nowicki often didn't know answers to her own questions and made frequent mistakes in lectures and office hours.

Dr. Nowicki cares deeply about her students' learning and is always willing to help! My advice is to take advantage of office hours, make sure to take THOROUGH notes on the lecture videos, and utilize practice exams and practice question sets as much as possible.

Dr. Nowicki was great! She is the best 171 instructor. In lecture, she does exam practice problems and spells out to students what they need to know for the exam. Expectations are very clear. She is great at explaining course content and always respectful to students. She gave lots of opportunities for students to ask questions during lecture.

I liked the ALS sessions for the most part. I found them to be informative and I felt like I retained information from them. I will say sometimes Dr. Nowicki could be pretty passive aggressive but other than that she seemed very caring for her students.

Flipped classroom model with heavy homework, and has difficult questions on the exam that revolve around subjects she mentioned in one sentence in the lecture. Not to mention, prepping for the exam is basically nonexistent besides 2 practice exams, everything else is 10 times easier than actual questions. Wish I didn't have to take her class again

Dr. Nowicki gave pretty good lectures and was usually pretty easy to understand. Sometimes she wasn't the most clear and would kind of talk in circles, but if you focus on the central idea of what she's saying and don't get fogged up by the extra words, you'll understand. She does flipped classroom which takes a lot of time up outside of class.

Flipped style wasnt bad, and the ALSs were nice to go to if you still needed extra coverage on a topic. I would often not attend and just answer clickers from home. She occasionally made discouraging comments towards our exam scores or our understanding when we *just* learned a new concept, but besides that she genuinely was a overall good prof!

Flipped classroom setting made it difficult to really learn the content. The mandatory ALS was 3x a week and would often only go through a couple questions. She was regularly talking down to students for asking questions or not seeming to understand the content. She would mention the high fail rate of the test and then not curve.

I love Prof Nowicki. She is very straightforward, focusing on the big picture stuff which is good for the broad material in 171. She's good at simply explaining tough material and she's very approachable and I find the review sessions before the exams SO helpful. TAKE HERRRR

Im not sure why people say that this professor is hostile or rude, she is incredibly nice. The class is structured very well so although there is a lot of material, it is still clear what the path to success is. It is vital that you watch all of the material, and the exams can be pretty tricky. Overall, she definitely cares for student success.

Personally I found every time a person had a question it was met with hostility,  I also found that the professor does not explain the material further in ALS as it was supposed to be. I also found that her comments about the preparation of blue books to be very harsh and created a negative environment.

Carly explained the material very clearly and in a way that was easy to understand. The lecture was entertaining, especially for an intro bio lab class. Exams weren't that bad, and followed the practice exam on canvas as well as the study guide. If you have the option to take this class with Carly I would recommend you do.

The other, not good, reviews are just because they were when she was a new prof. The difficulty is because this is a weeder course, not her. She really truly cares  not just about our success but really understanding everything. If you don't understand something, she's ready to explain it 100 different ways until you do. 1000% recommend.
Absolutely fantastic prof. Honestly my favorite here. She really truly cares more than most. She expects engagement and effort, and will make you a better student by the end of the semester.

Overall, this was a very straightforward lecture and Prof Nowicki clearly communicates content. I wouldn't say that lecture itself was enjoyable, but I had a great GSI which made lab fun. Make sure to keep up with deadlines and communicate well with group work partners. Most grades weren't published until end of semester which was annoying.

As long as you stay on top of deadlines and make sure to communicate with your lab group on projects an A should not be hard to get. For exams, Dr. Nowicki makes sure to provide lots of review material and I found that the exams were very similar to the practice ones she'd provide. Overall very chill class.

Overall this class was not bad, def easier than any chem lab here. Actually study for exams (they are similar to the practice ones). Grading takes a while depending on your GSI, but you should be familiar with what you're getting. Pretty easy/ fun lab.

Dr. Nowicki is a very good lecturer and you can tell that she really wants you to understand the content. Lectures are graded based on iClicker participation. Her office hours are very helpful and I would recommend attending them if you have any questions or need clarification on anything from lecture/lab.

Lectures are engaging and I walk away from them knowing what's expected in exams/labs. 2 exams taken that were VERY similar to the practice test/study guide. The lab report was pretty difficult but manageable. Concepts felt easy with previous intro bio knowledge. Only annoying thing was a delay in grade releases, but went ok for me.

No point in going to lecture as the first half is always filled with whining. Treats her students like middle schoolers by yelling at them during lecture for being on their phones and micromanaging the required fieldtrip. Has an attitude and is unpleasant to be around. Would highly recommend taking this course with another professor if possible.

Very disappointed with how she withheld the grades for all of the major assignments besides exam 1 scores till after taking exam 2. She is unprepared for the class as she is dealing with issues outside of the school. If you could take it with any other teacher, I would highly suggest doing so.
Lectures are mid, ppl do iclicker from home.. The actual coursework/labs were really fun. 2 exams, both are barely worth anything, no final. She does have a bit of an attitude

Overall, this was a good course -- very straightforward, material was covered well in lecture, I knew what was expected of me. Prof Nowicki was good & I'd take her again, but nothing made the lectures exceptional. Loved my GSI and had a good time in lab.
Professor Nowicki treats her students with respect and hosts very interesting and engaging lectures. I had a lot of fun in her class!
She was nicer than Dr. Kurdziel, but due to the reverse classroom style, it doesn't really matter how she teaches. To be honest, I found "class" incredibly useless and did iClicker from home.

This was the first semester that Dr. Nowicki taught this class, and it showed. It often felt she didn't know what she was talking about or got confused and had to be interrupted by the other instructor. Aside from this, she seemed very kind and interested in what she was teaching. The flipped classroom had her not teach the bulk of the material.

This class used a flipped classroom model, so lectures were online. Dr. Nowicki hosted ALSs three days a week, and they were pretty informational. You could get points for going, but there was no penalty for not attending, so that was nice. Overall, she was a good teacher and explained the material reasonably clearly.

Dr Nowicki was very nice in my experience and always seemed willing to help students. The "flipped classroom" style of the course scared me at first but really wasn't bad. The in-person learning sections each week are helpful but not necessary if you are already comfortable with the material.
Dr. Nowicki is a great prof. Super understanding and was very informational. She didn't make students feel bad when they asked questions too!

Professor Nowicki treats her students like high schoolers and is constantly disrespectful in how she talks to them. The Canvas and Assignments are also disorganized and points given are usually unclear, they often post the wrong rubric and change it last minute. If I didn't HAVE to take this class I would have dropped it.
Very energetic and thorough lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Nowicki. Although I often felt that our lectures were rushed, it was often due to technical issues and difficulties rather than a lack of preparedness. The course could have been formatted better, but Professor Nowicki is definitely passionate and knowledgeable about her field!

Seasoned in lecturing and made sure respect was given to guest speakers (rightfully so). The class itself was insanely easy and all thanks to her and the GSIs; the study guides were clear, the QnA recordings were helpful, and the course content simply wasn't that complex. Good way to ease into UMich science courses in my first semester here.

Dr. Nowicki was a great professor that explained material clearly and confidently. Exams were worth only 20% percent of your grade, and the study guide and practice questions were very helpful. The guidelines for every lab and assignment were clear and easy to follow. However, the class had more work than what is expected of a 2-credit class.

Carly Nowicki was an exceptional lecturer. She was stern and straight to the point when talking about what would need to be known for exams and lab reports. She also had many guest speakers and gave many opportunities for undergraduates that we're looking for labs/information about biology. Would love to have her as a lecturer again in the future!

Fairly straightforward class, exams are mostly similar to past practice exams and together worth 20% of grade. Have a good group to complete a lot of the group projects, and you will be fine. One thing that is really annoying is that lecture attendance is required and tracked through lecture quizzes but you only need 85% accuracy on all of them.

bruh this was a stressful course. Like the first exam, it was based on things that she only mentioned for one or two seconds during the lecture. Also, she yelled at us numerous times for packing up early. Like, we have back-to-back classes, are u kidding me!!!!!

Dr. Nowicki was probably the best intro course professor I could have. She was kind and understanding, and had ways for us to contact her though we were an 800 student course. Most of your grading comes from GSI's, but during lecture she's very eager to teach and always has interesting things to talk about. A third of your grade is participation!

Dr. Nowicki was a really good lecturer and made sure to drill down what we needed to know for the exams. She comes off as a bit intimidating but she's genuinely really sweet and cares for all her students. She gave us the chance to do multiple wellness checks and was always very understanding. This class was pretty work-heavy for 2 credits, though.

Professor Nowicki was great and definitely cares about her students and their learning, however lecture was often very tedious and students felt talked down to. It often felt more like a middle school class than a college course. However labs were really fun and the class wasn't too bad overall. Except for the tone in lectures, it was a good time!

I loved taking Bio 173 (as a Bio major so I'm a little biased)! It's very lab heavy and there's a lot of work involved but if you keep caught up with everything then it's a class that's hard to do poorly in.

173 is a lot of work disproportionate to the credits (long lab hours, tests, occasional group projects) Lab experience and grading varied a lot depending on the GSI. However, the lecture part of this course was always great. Carly was a fantastic, enthusiastic lecturer. She clearly wanted to support us all in our science journeys--not weed us out.

Dr. Nowicki was a pretty good professor. Lectures were a bit too fast but they're recorded. Your grade will depend on your lab and GSI. There are few assignments so make sure they're the best they can be. The material for tests build throughout the questions so understand the connections between topics. Not hard if you put in general effort.

Carly was a great professor. She did lecture very quickly (I would personally say too quickly to take notes in class), but since all lectures were recorded this really wasn't an issue. Lab grading was fair but very GSI-dependent. Only 2 exams (free response style) but they followed the lecture and lab procedures very closely.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nowicki is super funny and the lectures are all recorded so you don't have to go to lecture, but I'd recommend it. Exams are pretty chill too, BIO 173 is a pretty easy A class if you put in a little effort.

Dr. Nowicki is amazing! I really look up to her, as she is obviously very passionate about biology and wants to share that passion with her students. Her lectures weren't bad; she's a bit of a "no funny business" person, but she's quite kind and caring. The class was super easy imo, and not a lot of work at all.
Prof. Nowicki is amazing! I loved the way she gave lectures. She made sure everything was super clear but also engaging. She is so kind and an amazing professor overall.

Dr.Nowicki is great! This lab class isn't too demanding, literally no prelabs no postlabs, one lab report, one easy presentation, a group project, and two exams but as long as you fill the study guide and do the practice questions you should be fine. GSI team was pretty chill this spring. Nowicki loves to help and is very open to questions.

The class is mandatory for most undergrads doing something in bio, 800 people in it, so dear God why is a large project calory counting? This should be called eating disorder 173. More than that, grading is arbitrary as there is not a clear standard for the GSIs, and for 2 credit hours it is too much work. Nowicki is brilliant though, I mean it.
Dr. Nowicki was fine for BIO 173. She explained concepts clearly, but her class felt like more work than necessary given that it was only 2 credits.

Dr. Nowicki was very knowledgeable about the subject matter. She could come off as a little cold and non-understanding during the online lecture, but once we got to meet her in person it was clear how kind and helpful she was.

Dr. Nowicki is clearly passionate about the subject matter and teaching in general. She goes out of her way to make the class engaging. However, she did seem to gloss over students' questions instead of actually clarifying. Also, her grading scale seemed a little off (one 10-minute casual presentation was somehow worth more than our final exam).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Bio173 is mainly a lab class, but Dr. Nowicki lectures to prepare you for lab and for the quizzes. She is a concise lecturer and is available twice a week for office hours if you need help. Overall, the class grade is mostly GSI, but I would recommend always attending lecture even though it's not mandatory to prepare you for the quizzes.
mediocre lecturer, boring, but is ok. bio 173 has way too much work for only 2 credits

There are 2 quizzes that are based on lecture (and some lab) content. Carly lectured fairly well to prepare us for the quizzes, but I highly recommend taking BIO 172 and 173 at the same time. The quiz questions are short answer, so write down EVERYTHING relevant because it can be graded a bit critically sometimes. Grades are mostly GSI-dependent.

Her class was far too much work for a 2 credit intro biology lab. I spent more time on this than on my orgo lab. Also, she said that HIV was created in a lab?? The class is pretty easy its just too much work for two credits
She is very accommidating and gives good lectures!

The class is easy and has few assignments. Some days took all 3 hours and some days we finished early and could leave. All the pertinent information is online, but attendance is required. Dr. Nowikci came across as being condescending and disrespectful and impatient towards students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Nagata is a great and knowledgeable professor; you can tell she is passionate about the material she teaches. The course itself is very eye-opening and forces you to confront your own beliefs about mental health across the globe. A lot of readings, exams are easy and open-note/material. As long as you go to class you'll have no issues with her.

Dr. Nagata was incredibly accommodating/easy to reach outside of class. Reading heavy! Exams are open note and super easy (half of questions are on readings & half on lecture content). No laptops (not super enforced); iPads are allowed. Topics are super interesting and eye-opening. Would definitely take the class again if I could
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class that had a very unique topic. Grammar on papers and reflections is graded! Exams were pretty reading heavy. Lectures were very interesting, warning she does talk fast and doesn't allow computers.

Perhaps one of the most accommodating professors. I struggle with a disability and caught COVID during this course. Prof. Nagata was very flexible with how attendance participation would work with me being out of class for a while. The content of the course (Psych and Culture) was very informative and eye opening!
Very informative and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredible content. Engaging readings. Lectures are a bit slow, but Professor Nagata is clearly knowledgeable and passionate about the course material. I learned a lot and broadened my understanding of this topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes. It's a must! Quite a bit of reading, but the readings are engaging and interesting. Dr. Nagata is kind and helpful. The concepts and info covered in this class is super eye opening and relevant, definitely made me question and rethink my previous assumptions about culture and mental health
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I took mental health and culture with Dr. Nagata online during the COVID-19 pandemic and the class was 100% asynchronous. Lots of research papers to read and papers to write, but she is very generous with the grades she gives and very kind with the feedback. I loved the content of this course and learned a lot about inter-cultural mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Donna is not the best lecturer I've had, but she's still a really nice person and is willing to help students outside of class. Participation matters and so do the readings. There's no textbook, but there's a coursepack that costs around $40, and the rest of the readings are posted online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved taking Mental Health and Culture with her in Spring. She clarifies the readings during class and the slides she has uploaded has partial information in them already filled. Take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Must attend lectures since most of exam is questions directly from lecture. Very interesting lectures though, she uses a lot of anecdotes from her work experiences as well as videos. Must also read textbook because some exam questions are directly from book. Overall, very reasonable class and very interesting to learn actual clinical psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Nagata is one of my favorites. She's engaging  and genuinely cares about her students. Sometimes she references her own work/experience which is funny and interesting. I took the class in the spring. 2 exams, 1 paper. She's always willing to help and really seems to value input. Nice person, great professor.

She makes even boring topics interesting with stories from her experience. Going to lecture is pretty important because her exams are pretty specific (espcially the short answer part). Also, for the exams, make sure you can distinguish which info came from lecture, and which info came from readings! As long as you put in the work, you'll do well.

She is really sweet and approachable. She gives partially filled out lecture slides before each class but you better have extra space because there can be a lot to fill in. I found her exams tricky... You really have to read the textbook because there are some specific questions from the text.
Very good prof. She brings treats to class sometimes and is very engaging and open to questions. What a sweet lady!

Interesting class and interesting professor, she really tries to interact with the class so that the lectures don't seem so long. Exams are pretty much straight from lecture and a fairly easy as long as you study.

Dr. Ahmed is very knowledgable, however this needs to be a 400+ level class. Especially since majority of the students transitioned from Psych 230 to this. His exam is also very hard and he doesn't cover all the materials on the slides, even if he does, slides does not include things we can use to prepare for the exam.

Dr. Ahmed is a nice professor who clearly cares about his students and willing to elaborate on questions. However, this 300 class is harder than any other 400 course I've taken. Most of your grade is drawn from only 2 tests which are extremely difficult. Great guy, but wouldn't recommend this class.

A humorous, knowledgeable, and respectful professor. Never comes off as condescending or arrogant. He will repeatedly explain the same concept throughout the course to ensure you understand. A lot of readings, but he often spent the entire lecture guiding you on the thinking behind the papers instead of quizzing you on the small details. The GOAT!
You have to read a couple scientific papers for each class but they can be pretty interesting once you get into the habit of it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It should be a 400 level class. The exams were the worst part of the course because many short answer questions are unclear. Even you understood the material super well, you may mislead by the vague expression of the questions themselves. The lectures are well organized, but the pre-class assignments are pretty heavy.

I am working with Dr. Ahmed in his neuroscience lab - he is an AMAZING professor who is understanding and well-respected by all who know him. Dr. Ahmed explains concepts clearly and is available outside of class. He is an expert in his field but NEVER comes across as arrogant - a dignified, knowledgable professor whom everyone should get to know!

I will start by saying this course has a heavy workload, and moves FAST even if you have some background. However, Okuno sensei is the best part. She is hilarious, understanding, and passionate about teaching Japanese. She seems to genuinely care about her students. If you show up to class, do the homework, and review frequently you'll be fine!

I had Okuno-sensei for RCLANG 196 + 296 and am truly grateful for her guidance, support, and enthusiasm to assist her students in learning Japanese. She makes the lectures engaging, incorporates fun projects, and provides endless opportunities for you to apply your learning. Truly my favorite professor of all time. HIGHLY recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was intense, especially coming from no prior language experience, but Sensei is amazing. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is humorous, kind, and clear in her expectations/grading. Participate in class (study outside of it) and you'll be fine.

Not just a great professor, but an amazing human. I wouldn't have made it through the '20-'21 online school year were it not for Okuno. She made one of the most difficult languages offered by the RC fun every single day. If you need to fill a language and you're considering Japanese, you won't regret her class. I wish I had the time to do it again!

Okuno Sensei is the favorite teacher I have ever had in my life. She is extremely funny, caring, and a fantastic teacher. She teaches very difficult coursework in a way that is easy to understand and if you are struggling she is ready to help. This is the kind of class you take because you want to try hard and really learn a language.

Okuno-Sensei has been by far the best professor I've had here at Michigan. The class is intensive with a TON of work, but she always ensures that we all are on track and learning the material. One of the most respectful, kind, and approachable people I've ever met. If anyone deserves a raise, it's her.

Due to the nature of the class, there's a LOT of homework and near daily tests/quizzes. But if you put in the effort, she won't let you fail. Such an incredibly kind, funny, and caring woman. Wants to get to know all of her students and see them succeed. Fosters a wonderful, supportive, light-hearted class environment. But get ready to work.

I can concur with the other reviews that Okuno sensei is one of the best professors I have ever had.  If I could, I would take all Japanese with her. It will challenging yes, but that is because the course will pack two semester's worth of Japanese into only one. But the results, as well as the learning that comes out is nothing less than fabulous.

One of the best professors at U of M. You can tell that she really cares about her students and wants them to do well. The class is challenging due to the fact that it is an intensive language course, but Okuno sensei is always encouraging and ready to help her students. She is hilarious and energetic, and I had so much fun in her class.

She goes above and beyond to ensure her students are passing and even more. She truly cares about that class and you can tell in her teaching. Additionally, she is humorous and makes class interesting. the reason for the difficulty of the class is because of the fact that it is intensive language. It cannot be avoided.
Honestly the best professor at UMich
She is so sweet. Good lecturer and always able to meet.

Tina ist die Beste!!! She is very understanding of absences and it is very easy to makeup attendance in the class. As long as you participate and do the homework, you'll do great. She loves her students and teaching Deustch.

Tina was a great professor. She was always so kind, sweet, and understanding. Participation was super important, and you were able to "make-up" up to 10 days throughout the semester, but I would not recommend skipping. She made learning German super fun with different mnemonics or songs to remember vocabulary or grammar by.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is quite possibly one of the most caring and understanding people I have had the pleasure of meeting in my entire life. Incredibly sweet and really wants to help you succeed, the course itself is a bit work heavy and requires a lot of studying but that is a flaw across the entire german program. All in all one of my favorite profs ever.

Wasn't great prof. nitpicky with P&P's and much more strict than other profs for German. Had harder quizzes than other profs and wanted alot more out of you. expected everyone in class to want to take German(when most take it for the distribution). Very nice but not great compared to many other profs in the department. take other profs is possible.

Professor ODonnell was truly the best language professor I've ever had. I was initially apprehensive about taking a college German course with no prior experience, but her genuine care for her students quickly eased my concerns. She created a welcoming, fun space, fostering confidence in every student rather than promoting competition.
I'm a college dropout, and I wouldn't take this professor again. I think he cares more about his work than his students and that really really hurt me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Omar teaches at a really nice pace, and I honestly found the content super interesting. The class is mostly theoretical, so make sure that's what you are into. As a bonus, he gave a good amount of pretty doable extra credit assignments during the semester I took the class.

EECS 490 is meant for those interested in theory and research. Negative reviews seem to dwell on how the class doesn't prepare you for industry— yes, expect that when taking a theoretical course. Professor Omar is in turn a great professor. He goes quite slowly during lecture, which gives plenty of time for students to ponder and ask questions.

I had to take his class because all the other ULCS classes were full. There's low enrollment for a reason... few people want to learn about PL theory, and nobody wants to do PL theory homework for 15 hours a week. He clearly cares more about his own research than teaching.

It is disconnected with reality.Basic concepts won't  make you a pro of any pl.Use functional pl to write an interpreter of another is lame.Derivation is like "if one frog has two eyes and four legs, how many do two have?" questions in primary school.Omar is OK, but he researches on teaching like Rust visualizer. It won't prepare for your career.

Prof. Omar did a great job of teaching EECS 490. I enjoyed his lecture style; live note-taking with no slides is perfect for the kind of material being presented. His lectures were clear and informative, though the material itself can be a bit repetitive towards the end of the course.

EECS 490 is my single favorite and the single highest-quality course I've ever taken at U-M. Prof Omar is great, and gives amazing lectures. The concepts taught are very interesting and sometimes mind-blowing. The assignments are of suitable workload. There is no complaint I can think of this course.

He's a really good lecturer. The class gave me a new perspective on programming languages, what they are and what they can be. The material isn't taught enough at University of Michigan, which tends to focus more on low-level systems.

He's extremely passionate about programming languages and it shows. Instead of lecture slides, he uses hand written notes, written in real time during lecture. While this may sound terrible, it's actually a huge plus because he knows the material well enough to do so, you have time to take notes, and you know exactly what material is important

Really passionate about what he teaches, and it shows! Keep it up, doing a great job with 490 so far, can't wait to see how it grows in future semesters. Puts a lot of effort into the course and takes student input often.
Cyrus is really nice as a person and kind to students, however the curriculum is absurdly difficult and not enjoyable. Not at all what I was expecting from this course.
Good and knowledgeable about his subject. Easy to just watch lecture recordings. Not very exciting but does what is needed.

He definitely knows his stuff. Tests are 90% of the grade, but only 6 homework assignments the whole semester, and you don't have to read a textbook, which is nice. The tests are very fair, and there is nothing on them that was not covered in class, also similar to the ones in the past.

Oleg was a great Professor, who had a very structured and well-thought out course for 402. Don't get me wrong, 402 is a difficult course. However, Oleg (along with his GSI, Majdy) were very helpful in making sure all concepts were broken down into simple terms and that they were easy to understand. This was a great course and I recommend Oleg!
taking another class with him loved it

I like Econ but I found this professor a little boring. It was hard to stay focused at all times. Otherwise, Professor Zamulin was a very good teacher and I have no problems with him as an instructor.

Dr. Zamulin's lectures are how economics should be taught in general: An underlying theory supported by numerous real-world examples not simply shown for the sake of giving examples, but helping students understand the logic behind the concepts they learn. The emphasis on understanding is what stands out more than professors who like dry MCQs

Good lecturer. Knowledgeable and teaches a very traditional style class. No attendance, useless textbook (find a PDF if you really want to read it), but 3 exams determine your grade. Go to every lecture and take good notes and you'll have no problem getting a good grade. Don't doze off in lecture because you can miss a lot of info in a short time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy. However, beware that he can be hard to understand from time to time and frankly I didn't get much out of going to lecture, just him going on about nothing. If you take his class, be prepared to teach yourself the whole thing.

Great lecturer, explains clearly, and is so sweet! He lights up the room with his smile and is genuinely passionate. If you're considering 102, but are scared of the tests, he gives us all the tools to succeed: you can do it if you use them! I also

He's very funny, I enjoyed the lectures. Some were dry, but he knows his stuff. He has done pretty much all of the stuff he teachers, as he worked at a large Russian bank for a long time. Great professor.

Not the worst econ professor but not the best. Problem sets and exam studying took a lot of effort and I found it hard to get a grade that equated to how much time you put in. Zamulin is a nice and qualified professor but some exam questions were far fetched and required a lot of intuition. Section was useless but reading the book was helpful

Very doable class. Do the problem sets and practice exams, and you should do fine. I did pretty poorly on first exam because I did not the practice exams, but did well on the last two exams bc I actually did the Problem Sets carefully and practice exams. MAKE sure you understand the lectures, they get harder and more abstract later on.

Dr. Zamulin has great and passionate lectures. Despite only making up 10% of the grade the homework is the most important part of the course as it prepares you for the exams. Master the homework's starting from day #1, and you will do great in the course.

Amazing Professor. Compared to most Econ courses, this was more of a story, where topics were explained through US Economic History (current and past). You can tell he has a vast knowledge on the material. Exams are hard but doable, need to study a lot (makes it easier if you go to lecture and understand how he walks through the problems).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting background

Oleg Zamulin is one of my favorite teachers I have been fortunate enough to have at the University of Michigan. He is one of the first teachers I have had in college who has done something outside the classroom of meaning. Although I struggled in his class, I still learned much and will always appreciate my time with Oleg.

Intro Macro isn't the most interesting subject but unfortunately, the lectures didn't make up for it. You are graded by 3 tests (90% of the grade) and they are tricky but there is a decent curve to make up for them. As long as you're above average, you should get at least an A-

Professor Zamulin is brilliant and incredibly organized. The class is exam heavy, but the short answer portions of the tests are very nice to have. The problem sets are extremely helpful for the exams. The lectures are solid, but lack charisma. The slides are very useful. The details of the curve were not well communicated, especially at the end.

An organized and respected professor! He likes to engage with and get to know students in class by asking questions. He is definitely too knowledgeable to teach 102. He will integrate 102 concepts with real economic events. He also does review questions at the beginning of each lecture (very helpful). A funny professor. Go to his OH!!!

Prof. Zamulin is a good professor, however the problem sets are quite long and take time. Exams are fairly difficult and require a good amount of studying, but if you take and study the practice exams you should be ok. The curve is also generous at the end.

Dr. Zamulin is a solid lecturer with incredible macroeconomic experience. Problem sets are long and difficult, but walk you through each concept and is graded for completion. Practice exams resemble the midterm and final fairly closely. If you study the problems and practice tests, you'll do fine on the exams.

Oleg is a great professor who is really really knowledgeable and cares a lot about his students. His lectures are great, though the material is sometimes dry, and he's super accessible outside of class too. The class is tedious, but not as hard as people say, as long as you put in the work and give it the time a 4 credit class demands.

Well in teaching materials but terrible exams and problems provided. The practice and actual exam have a huge gap. You must prepare to reach the problem from another level out of your normal mind. It is difficult to maintain a high grade on each exam. Cause the problems are so random.

Professor Zamulin is an incredibly knowledgeable macroeconomist with great industry experience. He takes pride in helping his students understand concepts and explains topics very logically. Exams were appropriate in difficulty and if you put in sufficient effort you will be very successful. He is definitely my favorite Econ professor at Umich.

Zamulin was a great professor. Pretty funny guy and considering that W23 was his first semester teaching 402 I think he did a great job. Almost all of your grade is exams but the final specifically was 40%, make sure to study and know your stuff and you'll be fine. Would definitely take one of his classes again.

Zamulin is tough. He is knowledgable and has plenty of experience. His lectures can be long and boring at times, but if you pay attention and keep up on homework and prepare for exams heavily, you will do fine. He is difficult and requires a lot of hard work, but an A is manageable. Also, he's pretty funny and approachable.
He's a great guy. But he teaches and makes tests like Professor Proulx (albeit without a workbook this time around). That's all that needs to be said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a boring professor and talks so slow. I would have such a hard time staying focused in lecture, and a majority of the time, his lectures were so broad and vague that they did not help me with the homework at all. Once I got the answers to the homework problem sets, I was able to learn from those, but his lectures did very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very knowledgeable, learned a lot and enjoyed his connections to his experiences outside of academics.  enjoyed his lecture style and humor. class is curved, so you just need to be above avg.

I have to agree with the other ratings. He's a nice person, but his lectures are convoluted and confusing. The discussion section is the only reason I understood the material somewhat. I've done well on the midterms, but the final is cumulative and worth 40% so my grade could be an A or a B which seems unfair.

This class was awful. Professor Zamulin seems like a nice man but his lectures are vague and extremely dry. Often super hard to know what is expected of you and final exam is 40% of final grade AND cumulative. I would highly recommend taking 402 with a different professor. The class is on a curve which is nice but it is still incredibly hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Class is difficult, but it should be because it's 402. Lectures are boring, hard to follow, and too shallow for the exam.

The worst part is that Professor Zamulin is very intimidating and condescending during office hours. He seems agitated whenever he answers questions that students have outside of lecture.
Anyway, the final grade is curved, so why care about the exam score if you can outperform others?

Prof. Zamulin is a nice person, though the material is difficult, it's up to date and useful. Some part will deviate from Mankiv's textbook, but this will add extra work to professor and I don't think he did this for himself(I mean, directly reading the book and official slides is the easiest). He is trying to make us learn a better content.

Do not take 402 with him. He is the worst professor and the exams are impossible to get a decent grade on. He includes problems on the exams that we have never covered in class. It is really difficult to get partial credit too. Just do yourself a favor and take 402 with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad instructor for an interdisciplinary course. Taubman Architecture department students are advised by academic advisors not to take his classes. He creates a harsh environment and does not allow for any small mistakes on assignments even with unclear instructions. Very mean when asked a question.

I would never take his class willingly. He does not teach but rather switches ideas from class to class in order to assert his dominance over the students. He answers questions with an attitude. Takes attendance at an arbitrary time, and if you are not in the classroom space within that time (ex. bathroom, printing...) he will mark you as absent.
temporarily witheld.Will post after finals
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The studio course has potential, and many concepts were covered. If you enjoy fabrication and want to explore this aspect of design in studio work, I'd recommend it. However, Professor O'Geen's demeanor can be challenging at times; he expects respect but does not always extend the same to students.
She's one of the best professors i've had here and really cares about her students. Grades fairly and does whatever she can for her students to do well.

Paula is a fantastic teacher! She always puts in effort to make classes as engaging as possible,  and just generally has a great attitude. The class does have a good amount of homework, but it does pay off and I've seen my Spanish improve since starting the semester. She does appreciate participation, so I definitely recommend being active in class

Nice professor, but doesn't seem to understand that none of us are native speakers of Spanish. She commonly calls out students for not being able to pronounce words perfectly and harshly grades oral exams over it. She also accuses students of "memorizing" ideas that are repeated during the oral exams, but not sure what else they could do to study.

Amazing person. It's a practice-based class and she makes it fun to come to class and talk in Spanish. I would take advantage of that opportunity and share your ideas as much as you can even though it's hard to in another language. Really do the homework and learn the grammar, and your grade will be fine. She's super understanding as well.

I was unfairly graded because I submitted a paper that was written too well. She also provides no rubric for participation and is quite strict. Speaking out multiple times in class and participation in small groups is not enough, apparently. If you want to be graded very strictly then by all means, join this class. Otherwise, look elsewhere.

Hands down the best professor in the U of M Spanish department. Extremely caring and comes to class with an enthusiastic smile, ready to teach. Class itself is mostly online work w/ in-class group convos & discussions. Generous grader, offers helpful feedback. Very approachable, friendly, & understanding when it comes to any issues. 100% recommend.

Profe was so caring and always seemed excited to be in class. I did not get a lot of Spanish-speaking experience in high school, so I was very nervous to go into a class with heavy participation, but all she wanted was to see improvement in your skills and I achieved that. The workload is extremely light for this class as well.
Such an amazing professor for 277. She was very warm and caring and made the class easy, very flexible if you miss class or need accommodations.

I had Paula for 277 last semester and she was really exciting. She engaged me with Spanish, and she was pretty receptive to feedback as well; me and her bonded over Spanish music. This class was grinding VHLS and that was kinda meh. Otherwise I recommend Paula for Spanish but I can understand that the experience may be subjective to the student.

Paula was my favorite professor this semester. She is super enthusiastic about teaching and doesn't assign too much homework. She is super understanding of any extenuating circumstances and really cares about her students. I wish she taught more advanced Spanish classes so I could take her again!

She made a 8-credit class about as painless as possible. I looked forward to her class most days, even at 9AM. Yeah there was a lot of work, but it was never too bad. The journals are actually fun to write and she genuinely responds to them. She's also very accessible outside of class. I would stay after just to chat about random stuff. Great prof.

She was one of my favorite professors the year I had her (in person learning). She has a lot of availability for office hours and gives really good feedback in your journals. Make sure to participate and study (she does give pop quizzes in person)!

Such an amazing teacher!!! I had her for Spanish 231 and 231 and absolutely loved her. The classes are not too hard but she makes it very easy for students to understand. Highly recommend her for any Spanish class.

One of my favorite teachers! She is so kind and helpful and really does want you to do well. 232 isnt an easy class in general, but she always answered any questions I have. She was a genuinely great professor, her lectures were engaging and she keeps it interesting. She cares about her students and is great at her job. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Paula makes the class interesting and I enjoy going to class - that's hard for a prof to do, especially when the class is 4 days a week. She gives really good feedback and gently corrects mistakes when speaking - it is a comfortable environment to speak spanish in because she does not judge or make you feel judged. She wants her students to do well

Professor Ostreicher is a decent professor, but his teaching style didn't work well for me. I often had to review the slides after class because the explanations sometimes felt overcomplicated. Some exam questions also covered topics that weren't emphasized in lectures. Class was a bit boring, but it gave a helpful intro to future business courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For IOE 425. Lots of industry experience, very motivated to teach the class, and just an overall great guy to talk to. Lots of heavy group projects though so don't procrastinate. Midterm was the only knock on the class. It was super dense and didn't feel very fair, but can easily make it up with projects and participation. Overall recommend!

Be prepared to hear about Toyota. Dave is a nice guy and very knowledgeable about some of the topics however other topics he could not really answer any questions. The projects in his class sometimes had vague instructions but he didn't design the class so not really his fault. Overall not that hard of a class and he is very personable.

Dave was a relatively laid back professor but he's definitely a yapper… while this was his first time teaching the course he was thoroughly prepared. Handles inquiries in standardized manner, referring most questions to the BA100 teaching team to ensure fairness. Answers questions but will tell you to Google things he doesn't know the answer to.

Didn't take SAC311, but I can't change it for some reason. I took FTVM210 with him and he is a great guy and is really helpful in creating and crafting your screenplay. Yes, you are graded on pretty much two assignments, but he will give you a ton of ideas and help to get those to be well graded. Very fun class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was very interesting and engaging. He's a very tough grader and you're graded exclusively on your screenplay with no consideration of attendance or participation. If he likes your screenplay, you're golden, if not...
Tough but good!
No Comments

My favorite orgo lecturer. She explains topics clearly and genuinely wants students to succeed. Orgo is still a rough course, but she's definitely the best professor to take. She's also kind of weird in a funny way like she was teaching her kids about bbls.

I absolutely loved Dr. Tuttle. She cares about her students and chats with them when there's time before class, and tries to get to know as many students as possible (or at least gets to know names.) I took 210 and 215 with her, and Dr. Tuttle explains topics very clearly, and gives advice if you ask for it, and overall I enjoyed her teaching style
She's a decent teacher, the class is just hard. Don't ever try to email her becauses she's the most passive aggressive person ever and honestly I would never go to her office hours because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is a thorough lecturer, who walks through concepts in such an accommodating way for first-time learners. She is the best out of all orgo professors.

Tuttle is really clear with her lectures for orgo 1 and 2. obvi orgo is really hard but she explains these difficult concepts at an easier level.
