However the problems she does during class are pretty easy so I'd recommend doing the textbook problems. You won't have to do the textbook readings though
best ochem lecturer at michigan, hands down.

CHEM210 is a hard class no matter who you take it with. Tuttle does a great job explaining content in a digestible way, but she often does so through examples, which forces students to find out themselves why her examples work the way they do. She has a passion for Orgo, just be prepared to do some reading/self-studying in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her notes are organized and easy to follow. She usually went past the class time and sometimes left off in the middle of notes. She used examples to teach instead of explaining the overarching ideas, leaving it to me to go back through notes or listen to other professors' lectures online to organize the main concepts which, she should have done.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the love of God, just take Orgo I with Nolta in the winter. Avoid Tuttle at all costs. She makes exams way harder than what's covered, not to mention vague lectures w/ basic examples that don't truly reflect the material's difficulty. Her condescending, rude behavior doesn't make it any better. DRILL ALL THE PRACTICE QUESTIONS & START EARLY.

Tuttle is organized and has very clean/easy-to-read notes. I never felt prepared enough. Of course, you get what you put in, but lecture wise, I had a hard time following. She teaches like she's lecturing to a group of middle schoolers. That may be nice for some, but it just didn't align with my personal learning style and made it difficult for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: good teacher, bad atittude towards students, made final way more difficult than practice tests and this is coming from someone who attended all lectures, understood all umps and homeworks. tests should reflect course material

Dr. Tuttle is the most organized 210 lecturer, her slides are handwritten (easy to read) and color coded. She used to teach middle or high schoolers which is why I think she is so good at explaining very difficult things in a digestible way. She does tend to go over time at the end. She does "Fall Watch" every Friday which I found fun.

Dr. Tuttle is the best lecturer for Orgo 1. Her lectures were organized and engaging. Also, she taught the fundamentals very well. I feel like she falls a tad short on certain concepts but overall breaks things down in a digestible way. Do as many textbook practice problems you can and every single practice exam given. Literally. Practice everyday.

Honestly, Dr. Tuttle is a good professor. She's definitely way easier to understand than other professor's. I think orgo is just a hard class and requires a lot of practice. I wish the exams were just a little easier though. She taught quite well though.
I would watch Tuttle's lecture whenever Coppola's was confusing because she's super organized and color-codes everything. She's very good at dumbing down the content so everyone can understand

professor tuttle ily

seriously though do lots of practice problems (especially practice exams) and you'll be fine

Dr. Tuttle is a good professor but she rarely ever finishes her lectures on time and is always rushing at the end of class to cram content in. Not to mention we learn content up until THE DAY BEFORE the exam. Also, exams are WAY harder than the practice problems done in class. You have to do a million practice questions to feel remotely prepared.

Good prof but in lecture can go pretty fast & be hard to keep up with. Overall pretty caring, but nothing overly notable in my opinion. Recommend reading textbook lotssss to keep up with content that Tuttle may not discuss deeply in class.

Tuttle is great! Lectures are engaging and helpful, but don't expect to pass without the textbook and maybe forming a study group. This isn't really on her, but there's so much content to cover that it's difficult for her to explain everything as detailed as she'd want to. If you want a good grade, use all resources available alongside lectures!
open a bible and pray to God.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She generally cares about her students. Her explanations are good and she goes through the content well, but goes very fast. Please also be aware that she calls out people for talking/being a little disruptive and will threaten to kick you out if you are causing too much commotion. Authentic and has the respect of a lot of students.

She is a solid professor who provides you with a foundation of what you need to know for the exams. That being said, she does not prepare you well for exams. You have to learn by yourself from the textbook and the practice exams. To her defense tho, there is so much content covered in these two courses so it is hard to get through everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is a great organic chemist but a poor course administrator. Lectures were poorly paced and often contained errors. She was also consistently vague about what content would be most relevant for the exam despite the accelerated 7 week semester. Dr. Tuttle often uses a condescending tone with students as well, which only makes orgo harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Chem 215 in the spring term. It was fast-paced, but I liked the way it was ran, and the most critical content was focused on. Dr.Tuttle likes to answer questions in person, but she will stay as long as needed after class, and she is always sweet. I would recommend getting to know her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is by far the worst prof I have encountered at Mich. She was rude and dismissive anytime I voiced questions about course material. I loved this course, regardless of her terrible attitude towards students who genuinely cared about learning. Stick to the textbook and teach yourself, Dr. Coppola knows best. Don't avoid her term, but beware

Dr. Tuttle was a good lecturer and could explain concepts well. However, the difficulty of the lectures did not translate to the difficulty of the test. She also would not show the mechanisms for some problems in class, which could be very frustrating.  DO ALL THE TEXTBOOK PROBLEMS AND PRACTICE TESTS, if you want a good grade.

Tuttle tries to encourage students but it always feels disingenuous. She takes a long time to get through concepts and lecture often feels redundant. Although I attended lecture in-person, I had to rewatch almost all lectures after class to learn the material as, in lecture, I often zoned out by the time she got to new concepts (20 minutes in).

She was very passive aggressive and condescending towards students. She explained material clearly but it didn't transition well to what was tested on exams, and she wasn't good at pacing the material so big concepts were frequently taught the day before the exams

She is one of the most arrogant professors I have encountered at Michigan. Her lectures are average, compared to the other orgo profs at Michigan, she is constantly falling behind schedule, and lectures like a high school teacher. She is aggressive and straight-up rude when you approach her about anything regarding the course, no room for success.

Dr. Tuttle is incredibly knowledgeable of organic chemistry and is extremely confident in her teaching. I found her lectures to be extremely informative. She explains stuff very clearly and I enjoy her note-taking method of writing stuff out on paper. She will also call you out in lecture if you're talking/disrupting class.

I had Professor Tuttle over the spring and she was the least helpful professor I have ever had. Her topic/lecture videos were fine, but she was not helpful at all during office hours. She only approached the larger groups and when I went up to ask if we could discuss a question, she told me to ask someone else first. Overall really frustrating.

Don't be mistaken, this class is HARD. However, Tuttle explains the fundamentals well and breaks down content in depth. Compared to other orgo professors, she does not go over as wide of a variety of examples in class and likes to use the same reagents over and over again, which makes exam style and textbook problems feel more foreign...

Dr. Tuttle is incredibly smart but makes content digestible. It is clear that she is passionate about what she does and wants her students to succeed. I thought her notes were a little disorganized at times but overall a great professor for 215!

Absolute best professor I've had yet at Michigan. She's funny, lighthearted, and always has a smile on her face. She truly relates with all of her students. I predict most of her negative reviews are more a reflection of the rigor of the course as opposed to her teaching specifically.

Dr. Tuttle's lectures were clear, well-spoken, and easily understandable. It's apparent she truly cares about the success of her students and her passion for chemistry is contagious. Don't be mistaken -- the course itself is extremely challenging, but Dr. Tuttle sets her students up for success and creates a positive learning environment.

Dr Tuttle is genuinely the best professor i ever had.
I'm convinced all the negative reviews are from people who don't keep up with the material and want to rely on yhe professor solely.
She also has 1000+ students so don't expect her to spend hours teaching you personally a concept.
She cares A LOT, insanely knowledgeable, and very inspirational.

Hard class, but thats true regardless of professor. She had pretty lecture notes, but they rarely addressed actual practice problems which made exams and practice 10x more difficult. She's also really passive aggressive, and I always felt stupid after I interacted with her. She seemed nice, but not so much one on one. She also falls behind a lot.

My absolute queen Dr. Tuttle, if you have to take orgo I would 100% recommend taking it with her. She has a light-hearted and humorous sense that makes orgo seem much less intimidating. I think any frustration with her comes from people not keeping up with the course, and then getting confused in lectures when she expands upon concepts.

Professor Tuttle really saved my orgo grade. I was originally enrolled in another professor's lecture, but I found some explanations hard to understand. I started watching Tuttle's lectures and the way she explained concepts made them much easier to understand.

She is well versed in the subject, but  there were often times where Organic Chemistry was up to the learners interpretation. No doubt she is great in this field, she's wicked smart+for sure knows what she's talking about, but lectures were all over the place. We'd revisit a super vague explanation two lectures later after being left in half etc..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Liked Professor Tuttle but she was just difficult to approach. Was always passive aggressive when I asked questions, but otherwise I liked the way she lectured for 210. The way that she groups information for 215 is a little difficult to follow, but overall clear if you do the textbook problems too.
The exams are challenging and are much beyond what is covered in homework or even practice exams. She is very blunt, but a good lecturer, but fails to get through content quick enough.

Honestly, I tried my best to like Dr. Tuttle. She was consistently passive aggressive and often made me feel stupid for asking questions, even though I asked GSI's who referred me to her because they were unable to answer. I had an amazing chem 210 experience with a different prof, which is how I knew that Dr. Tuttle was not a great professor.

Prof. Tuttle was an amazing orgo lecturer. She clearly has a world-class understanding of chemistry and is excited to teach it. Lectures move quick but are easy to follow. Only issue is that she is difficult to establish a relationship with outside of class when many students are looking for letters of rec. Would def take her lecture section again.

Dr. Tuttle was an incredible professor and I truly enjoyed her lectures. She came to every class very prepared and taught the material well. She helped me do well in a notoriously hard class. She also cares a lot about her students and interacts with the front row before class + makes an effort to know the kids that go to office hours.

WN24: Dr. Tuttle is a great professor who tries her best to make sure you have everything you need to succeed.  She is very passionate about the material. However, I do feel that Dr. Tuttle focuses too much on concepts instead of actual examples that are tested on exams. The exams in this class are pretty difficult. Other than that, she's great!
do not take 210 with her. worst professor I've had
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have had in my college career. She is the least understanding professor I have ever encountered, has no empathy for you, and will not work with you if you are having issues. If I could take this class again I would do everything I could to take it with literally any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are precise and she's nice. There were not many other positives. She and the other profs are stingy with points, tough graders, and cover material like their students also have a PhD. The course material is end-heavy. Exams extremely difficult. Hardest ever class for 1/2 the students. Felt like they killed passion for the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo II was a tough class, but Tuttle made it better. Her lectures take you step by step through mechanisms and concepts in a clear, concise manner. Her recordings were great study material and she knew the names of most students in the lecture hall. She talked WITH you, not AT you.

Tuttle is by far the best professor I have had at Michigan. She truly isn't just extremely knowledgable of the subject at hand, but truly passionate about YOU understanding/succeeding as well. I had her for CHEM 210/215, both of which I do not think I would have done nearly as well in if not for her. Her lectures are amazing and her office hours >>

I've gone to all the orgo lectures and Tuttle is definitely the best. She explains things pretty clearly, she rarely makes a mistake and if she does, she fixes it. The class itself is pretty hard and people tend to take it out on the profs, but she is a good prof and an even better person. Also she color codes everything which is nice

Dr. Tuttle was the best professor I've had at the University of Michigan. She truly cares about her students' success and provides all the resources necessary to succeed. She makes a difficult course engaging and fun, and you can succeed as long as you attend lectures and use the resources she provides.

Dr. Tuttle is a solid CHEM 215 professor and she does a good job of giving you the tools you need to succeed. However, having Dr. Soellner for CHEM 210 I did feel that Dr. Tuttle's style focused a little too much at concepts and less on actual practical examples that can be useful for the exams. But maybe that's just my preferred style.

If it weren't for Dr. Tuttle, my grade would FOR SURE be an entire letter grade lower than it is. This class is HARD, but she is absolutely incredible at explaining the material thoroughly, but in simple terms so that we can understand her. She's also super kind and sweet. Take CHEM 210/215 if you can - it'll be the best decision you make!!

Dr. Tuttle was a very caring, smart lecturer for CHEM 215. The content covered in this course is very difficult, but Dr. Tuttle helped lay a good framework for the exams (since she wrote them this term). I can tell that she genuinely wanted her students to do well!

Orgo 1 was very difficult for me. Tuttle's teaching approach works for me, but I understand it is not for everyone. She lays out the groundwork so we understand entirely. Her notes are great and she is on top of everything. I wish I had taken her class for 210, but I am glad I had her for 215. She enjoys the subject but can sometimes be too much.

Dr. Tuttle is the best teacher I've ever had in my life. I have found that her lectures are significantly easier to understand than other lectures and she genuinely wants her students to do well. Because of her, I looked forward to attending a class that people usually dread. She made orgo interesting and was super knowledgable about molecules.

very plainly the goat of chemistry lecturers at umich. i had dr tuttle for her seminar class as well as orgo 2 and she is probably the most caring teacher i have had, during or before college. massively appreciate her effort in helping me get back on track this semester, she truly cares about her students and is an amazing teacher.
OH MY GOD. I CANNOT. SHE IS THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER EVERYONE IS GOING TO FAIL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is quite literally the best professor I have ever had. She is the reason I did well in Orgo 1 and I am taking her now for Orgo 2. She is so clear and does such a good job getting you to understand how mechanisms work instead of just having you memorize everything. She is amazing.

Professor Tuttle was very kind and genuine, but I felt like her lectures didn't prepare me for the exams. I also felt like her section of the course often got behind and raced through new material until the very last second. Be prepared to do your part of the work and you can succeed!

Tuttle was seriously a lifesaver this semester. I wasn't originally in her section and was struggling so much until I started going to her lectures and everything became so clear from the way she explained things. She's very kind and makes an effort to get to know students which is pretty rare in such big lecture settings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle was amazing and I am so grateful to have had her for Orgo I. Sometimes she would go a little slow in lecture and would spend a little to much time talking about the heliums but the content explanations were top notch. Soelner's Topic Videos + Tuttle's Lectures + Lots of Practice = passing Orgo!!

Dr. Tuttle is very knowledgeable about orgo and her lectures are very well done and clear. I know several students who stopped going to their registered sections to either attend Dr. Tuttle's lecture or watch her lecture recordings. I am hoping to continue onto 215 with her. The course is tough, but Dr. Tuttle will give you your best chance.

Tuttle is amazing! She takes the time to get to know her students if you sit in the front rows or go to her office hours! Her lectures are concise and clear, and also provides additional videos online for those needing additional resource. Broke down concepts to be easier to understand and made taking a hard class more manageable!

Dr. Tuttle cares about her students more than any other professor I've had at UofM. Although orgo is a huge class, if you sit in the first two rows, she will learn your name and make an effort to get to know you. Her lectures are clear and she genuinely wants her students to succeed.

I took orgo II and failed. Shes different in that she teaches how to think and approach problems. Orgo II is more about having basics down then applying to any problem while orgo I is about understanding the most difficult problem to repeat. Gives amazing prelecture content videos (well organized, clear).Highly recommend her for spring/summer class

I had Dr. Tuttle for Chem 210 and I liked her lectures so much that I took her class for 215 as well. She uses lots of colors, examples, and real-life applications (shout out to Fall/Winter/Spring watch) to explain the different concepts. I recommend creating condensed outlines of important content before each exam to get the bigger picture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is an enthusiastic lecturer so the hour passes quickly. She writes and draws very fast so sometimes it's hard to keep up, and will sometimes rush through important material at the end. But, you can tell she's really interested in what she's teaching and everybody enjoys Fall Watch. Practice is probably most important for the class.

Chem 210 is a 'weed-out class' so it can be hard to separate Dr. Tuttle from the class. The actual class is very difficult and graded by 4 exams. As for Dr. Tuttle she is decent and a nice person. Her lectures sometimes don't cover all the required material
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is a tough class no matter the professor. I was worried based off her previous ratings that Dr Tuttle would be bad, but was pleasantly surprised. Her lectures involve explaining topics and writing on a doc cam as she goes. I highly recommend reading (or at least skimming) the textbook and doing practice problems to fully understand the topics.

Orgo is a hard class but Tuttle is a great lecturer! She's also accessible outside of class so if you get the chance try to meet up with her. Taking her for 215 next semester and I'm excited. Got a B in the class because the subject is hard, but she made me excited for lectures every day. She's super enthusiastic and smart.

Great lectures that explained the concepts we needed to know in the perfect amount of detail. Posts all of her notes online as well as extra videos if there's a complicated topic. Doesn't focus as much on practice problems during lectures but is helpful during office hours. You can tell she loves chemistry and cares about her students!

Best professor for Chem 210. Many of the other professors didn't explain as clearly as she did. Don't waste your time reading the textbook but make sure to do all the problems in the book and you'll do well on the exams.

Really good when it came to explaining material for exam 1 and the final, not so much for the rest of it. helpful topic videos for most subjects. as long as you attend lectures consistently and keep up with the assigned book problems, the class shouldn't be difficult.

Dr Tuttle is a really great lecturer if you're a visual learner. If you take her section, I recommend doing the associated readings before, since she does a lot of practice problems, and knowing the theory behind them beforehand is helpful. Although the subject material is difficult, she makes it very approachable and provides tons of resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tuttle does a really good job of explaining complex concepts clearly. People get frustrated when they aren't doing well in her class (it's a really hard class and flawed in a lot of ways that are beyond her control) and write her poor reviews but they don't really reflect her teaching in my opinion.

I took organic chemistry with Dr. Tuttle, and the class is known to be difficult but Dr. Tuttle made it easier to understand. Her lectures are paced very well as she writes down notes and works through them with you and she is always clear, concise, prepared, and knows what she is lecturing about. Recommend Dr. Tuttle for 210 and 215.

I really enjoyed Chem 210 with Tuttle. She was very clear and started with the basics before providing examples during lecture. She also provided online resources and pre-lecture videos to supplement understanding. Keeping up in the textbook and attending her lectures worked for me
Dr. Tuttle's lectures were great and she cares about her students. You have to self-motivate a lot in this class, but if you do, you'll be good.

I took this class over Spring term (flipped format). Overall, I think the class wasn't too bad. She provides good notes, but I feel like we didn't focus as much on practice problems. The ones she reviewed in class were way easier than the book or the exams. The discussion was useless because we just went over homework problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was based solely on exams. Lots of practice problems. I watched Wang's lectures for some and I liked the way Tuttle taught and organized the information. It was a lot to work on, but they also boost grades for significant improvement on exams (by a letter grade). I always struggled with chemistry and feared orgo and it was not awful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: incredibly inefficient teaching style. I don't think she was bad at explaining, however, the choice to give 30 minute prelectures then say NOTHING new in class is why nobody would show up to lecture. Watching Wang's lectures was FAR superior.  only gave a 2 because she is nice and invested in student outcomes.

I think people say rude things about Dr. Tuttle because they don't take the time to learn chemistry. Her notes guide you through the homework, which has the same mechanisms you learned with new reagents. Take her advice and learn about the overall mechanisms rather than specifically memorizing reagents in practice problems and you will learn a lot.

I took orgo last sem. w/ Wolfe and like Tuttle's lecture style more. Others say she's more difficult but I think she goes into more depth and details, which is really helpful. Practice problems are also a must for this course, they are super similar to the exams (in-chapter questions, end-of-chapter questions, plus exam reviews).

Dr. Tuttle really explains concepts very well in comparison to the other Chem 210 lecturers. She actually cares that you learn the material. Additionally, the exams she makes are straightforward and basically from lecture. I highly recommend taking Chem 210 with Tuttle.

A lot of people say negative things about Dr. Tuttle, but I really believe that those people didn't take advantage of the lecture content or practice materials provided. I never went to office hours or discussions really, but the practice materials alone allowed me to succeed in the course because they are so similar to the exams.

No answers are given to the course pack so you cant even see if you are on the right track. Only few answers are given. Lectures were horrible and despite attending in person lecture, I learned nothing and had to watch them on my own multiple times to grasp something. Exams were extremely hard and the curve is not enough for mostly D averages.

Contrary to a lot of what a lot of people on here said, I actually didn't mind Dr. Tuttle's method of teaching; office hours are offered fairly regularly and despite the difficulty of the course, I found that her way of explaining was pretty clear and helpful. If you do the coursepack/old exam problems that are offered, you'll be set :)

Very bad at explaining! Does not take time to help out students who don't understand. Just overall a bad professor, but sadly the only option at umich so you have no choice if you want to take orgo 1 or 2

I've never given a bad review and I feel terrible, but this class was not it. The material in lectures/course meetings sounds simple as you're learning it, but it's not good preparation for/representative of exams. She didn't take any concerns seriously, even with very low exam averages. Watch Professor Wang's lectures - she was my saving grace.

For a 3credit class, the amount of unhelpful lectures we have to watch is astounding. only does the basics of each type of problem, then expects u to know how to do way harder problems on the exam unhelpful in oh and doesn't care when class averages are at a historical low. Worst professor I have had in umich. don't take her waste of money
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tuttle was overall a great prof. Although the course meetings were similar to the lectures, it was helpful in reinforcing my learning. She is clear in her explanations, and her lectures were good at explaining the concepts. Just stick to a schedule and you'll be fine.

Tuttle has been getting a lot of hate, but it's unwarranted. She doesn't give specific solutions to problems in OH, and she says that in the syllabus. Go to a GSI if you want specific problem workups. She does, however, break down material in a detailed way and provide though processes for her solutions. DO THE WORK, PRACTICE, AND YOU'LL BE FINE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tuttle is not nearly as bad as people on here say she is. She does a good job overall with the lectures. Her course meetings are not particularly helpful though because she just repeats lecture content. It would be much better if she focused on practice problems. Office hours can be helpful, but she only lets you ask conceptual questions.

Dr. Tuttle has clear, concise pre-recorded lectures and is well organized. Her synchronous lectures are mainly a review of the pre-recorded lectures and rarely goes over practice problems in class. If you want practice problems in class and helpful office hours, pick another professor. If you learn from good lectures, Tuttle is a good choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you do the work, youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tuttle didn't teach 70% of her lectures for this semester (it was a GSI). She's not easily accessible and she refused to give me clear reasoning when I emailed her about a question my GSI couldn't answer. I stopped trying to contact her after that. She's not a terrible lecturer, but tbh she's a last resort. If you have another option, take it.

-Office hours are at inconvenient times and repetitive/non-specific - spends 15 minutes on one student's question -Lectures are repeats of recorded material, no problem solving -I succeeded due to spending hours with Wang's materials -Refuse to address questions in class/email -Background distractions during lecture -Choose a different prof
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm willing to bet the comment below was written by Tuttle herself because I find it incredibly hard to believe that anyone thinks she was a decent lecturer much less a good one and I know for a fact that her office hours are useless because she doesn't go over coursepack problems (because she probs doesn't know how to do them herself lol). 0/5
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tuttle is a great professor! The coursework is heavy and tests can be hard if you don't study. But that's typical of any ochem class. Dr. Tuttle made sure that students were well-informed. Her lectures are very thorough and clear. Her thought process is easy to follow, and she holds lots of office hours. Use all the resources & you'll succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a college as renowned as UofM for its chemistry department, I am quite surprised that they allow Dr. Tuttle to be a lecturer. I'm going to be straight - unless you already know organic chemistry, take a different professor. She does not prepare students for exams. In fact, she seems to take pride in failures. For the sake of GPA, just don't...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'll never forget going to her office hours and asking about a coursepack question, only to hear her say she "only answers questions about chemistry" and listening to her reteach me the lecture material for 20 minutes. If you need help ask Prof Wang.

Tuttle often falls behind in course content compared to Wang. She doesn't provide any examples of problems in live sessions and rather reiterates the lecture that the students have already watched. She's very nice but you can't ask her to help you on the coursepack which is very frustrating. Wang is a better professor overall as she prepares well.

Not only does Tuttle assign 3x as many prerecorded lectures as there should be each week, but she also is incredibly inaccessible and does not care whatsoever about the students taking her class. During the synchronous lecture meetings twice a week, she basically skims over the lecture material again and never goes over exam level questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tuttle is terrible. She doesn't do practice problems during the synchronous session and instead repeats the lecture. I can tell she is lazy because of the way she approaches this class and her inaccessibility outside the classroom. 1) there is no answer key to anything and 2) if you ask for help on a problem, you won't get it. Wang is better!

While Dr. Tuttle seemed adequately prepared and presented clear notes, she often fell behind and covered less content than other professors. She did not work through exam-type questions in class. Halfway through the term, I stopped attending Dr. Tuttle and went to Dr. Wolfe and Dr. Montgomery instead, who prepare students much better for exams.
La Diabla.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is the best and absolutely amazing! I love her so much! Would 100% take this class again and any class she ever teaches! She is is such a great teacher and I learned so much in her lectures. She is so encouraging and made me excited to learn Spanish! She is the best professor that I have ever had and I am going to miss being in her class!

Olga is one of my favorite professors at U-M! While her class does require some effort, Olga is incredibly supportive and knowledgeable, which made the class pretty manageable for me. You can tell Olga really values her students and wants them to succeed. Her in-class analyses of the texts were also super helpful for succeeding on papers.

Olga was very knowledgeable about Spanish and explained the material well but outside of class was incredibly awful to work with. She was constantly rude and condescending to students. During the first week of class, she even told "you are not smart enough to be here".

Olga  is very effective at getting you to learn the material, because she threatens to drop you from the class if you aren't successful. She is brutal and sometimes hurtful with feedback. I learned a LOT in her class, and managed to pass with 8 credits. Grammar matters a lot. Go to office hours, it's important to her and may impact your grade.

Olga is my favorite professor at umich. She is caring and respectful, honest and intelligent, and only wants the best for you. She has an enormous knowledge of beautiful Spanish literature, poetry, and films, and in her class you are blessed with receiving a LOT of it. Highly recommend. I love her.

Olga is a great professor, but you need to work in her class. You have to read and PARTICIPATE in discussions or she will call you out. However, she will also help you learn Spanish and will help you understand readings. The best thing to do is go to office hours and just talk to her about your life, because she genuinely cares about her students.

Olga is one of the best people! She made me feel welcomed and that I was important to the group. She's a tough teacher and that makes you better. She gives you the resources you need to succeed. I've taken five classes with Olga. The key is to schedule time to go to office hours! My Spanish improved so much over the three years I had her!

Olga's class will definitely teach you Spanish. She is very caring and funny, always available outside of class and wants you to come to office hours. However, be ready to read and be even more ready to participate because she will call you out! However, Olga wants the best for you and you can tell she really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Olga is a really compassionate teacher and is readily available for outside help. There are definitely a lot of readings, but that should be expected for a Spanish readings class. If you are in the RC and just passed RCLANG 294 or just want to improve your Spanish beyond the minimum requirement for LSA I strongly recommend this class.
OMG I love Olga, she's amazing. Her class was super interesting, although there are a lot of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Olga is a wonderful teacher! She's super caring and clearly invested in her students' success. I loved my time in her class (although it was demandingto be expected) and I have learned an incredible amount of Spanish thanks to her. I highly recommend taking her class!

Olga is amazing. She is such a caring person and a really great teacher. I would definitely recommend going to her office hours to practice talking with her. She works really hard for her students and is just a great person. The class is pass fail too.
Very kind person. You are lucky if you get Olga. Very caring. Go to her office hours and chat with her, good practice and always fun

Olga is amazing (in the Residential College at the University of Michigan all Professors go by their first name). You mainly work from the course pack. I advise meeting with her regularly in her office hours to get accustomed to her accent and so she knows you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olga is a decent prof. Most of the class is just doing readings and then talking about them philosophically. You have to contribute to the conversations or she tells you off. Whole grade is based off of in class participation and 3 essays on the readings that she'll write for you if you go to her office hours. Also, she's terrible with technology.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olga is brilliant, knowledgeable and kind. She is definitely someone you can go to for help and except sympathy. That said, she has high expectations, gives a good amount of work (essays and reading), and you MUST be prepared to think actively/participate every class. Mutual respect btw her/students is evident. Gives good feedback, I learned alot.

I came into this class (City Imagined) thinking that it would be interesting. I was wrong. Olga is very passionate about her subject, but is incapable of listening to opinions different from her own, and struggles to understand when students don't grasp a concept immediately.
Incredible class if you want to learn the language thoroughly and fast. Tons of work but worth it.

She is an amazing teacher! The class was extremely difficult for me, but if you work hard you can pass. Olga will give you as much as you give her, she cares about the students. She wants us all to learn Spanish. She even remembered facts about my life after our conversations. I love her and I am so happy I took the class!

She is one of the most amazing professor! She explains the grammars clearly and she helps every student to understand the grammars perfectly. Indeed the workload is heavy but you will not regret taking this course with Olga!

Olga is amazing. She is extremely helpful and truly wants every student to succeed. She is a perfectionist and wants each student to speak with fluidity. Attending office hours helps a lot also. If you really want to be proficient and know Spanish then work your butt off and with the help of Olga you can get there.

Olga is AWESOME. She is a really sweet and understanding prof, who makes the material exciting and fun to learn. I especially loved how much Olga cared about us as students. She gave amazing feedback to papers and commented thoroughly on our reflections. The mark of a great teacher!

Olga is wonderful! There's a fair amount of reading, but the essays are reasonable and I really didn't think the class was as hard as people are making it out to be -- maybe just because it wasn't my first readings class, but I thought it was a normal difficulty level.Material is interesting and Olga is funny and sweet. Participate in class!
Olga is a fantastic teacher and explains grammatical concepts extremely clearly. Tests are challenging, but she is happy to help you if you put in the work. I loved her and the class.

Olga is an amazing teacher. The class is a lot of work but she really cares about her students and wants them to learn and understand. If you put in the work the class is rewarding. I would advise avoiding taking other difficult classes while taking her class but it's worth it. She is clear and the class is interesting.

Olga is without a doubt a COMPLETE GODDESS. She is so intelligent, graceful, beautiful, helpful, and elegant. Everyone wants to be her when they grow up. And her reading's class about Spain was excellent- it really changed the way I view history, country narratives, memory of a nation, etc- take this one if you can because it's the most structured

Olga is an excellent instructor; her grammar lectures are extremely clear. She genuinely cares about students' individual progress. However, be cautious - she can be somewhat stern regarding her definition of politeness. She especially frowns upon people who do not eat all food on their plate at lunch tables or those who yawn/zone out during class.

Class was extremely difficult but completely worth it thanks to Olga. She truly wants you to do well and cares genuinely about your opinion on the material. She wants you to open your mind, and if you do that and work hard, you will succeed in the class. She was always helpful and kind to me.

Great prof - Leads discussion very well, super helpful on papers, and the workload really isn't that bad. Go to office hours before papers to get feedback, and try to make at least 3 contributions to discussion per class. Would recommend.
Love her.

Olga taught me so much this semester. She is really willing to help and is extremely invested in your education. The readings are difficult but really interesting if you take the time to read them throughly. I can't say enought about her it was such a great experience!
No Comments

Olga is very sweet.  Her class was a lot of work compared to the other readings classes though.  She presents very interesting ideas, but often expects too much from the students in analyzing literature.  If you take a class with her, expect tons of reading and 6 page essays with difficult topics.

Olga is an amazing teacher and person and her class was incredibly interesting.  Although she grades hard, she is one of the nicest people I've ever met and is willing to give extensions so that you can turn in a better paper.  There is a lot of reading and if you do it and participate, you're grade will be a lot better.  Overall -- amazing class!

It's really difficult to learn in this class because the teacher talks down to you instead of leading or pushing you in the right direction. Brutal grader. Nice person, very knowledgeable, worst teacher ever.
if you enjoy life dont take her

She honestly seems like a very nice person and very well educated however i don't know if a professor is the right career path since her instructions are really ambiguous and she grades like your gpa doesn't matter
RUNNNN AS FAST AS U CAN, DROP IMMEDIATELY, BE SCARED, WAITLIST OTHERS IF U HAVE TO, JUST DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. My entire class is drowning, and she is the rock tied to our ankles that is drowning us.
Just saying the first INTRODUCTORY assignment had an average grade of 68% and this was 10% of our grade by the way. Run.

This class is truly a battlefield, in all honesty, she's well respected in her field and she knows a lot. but on the other hand she grades like a monster, nothing is ever good for her, instructions are so unclear and she will have you writing a research proposal in 3 days and make you decide on a project that you have to do for a month and a half.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never in my 19 years of life met someone so unable to give unclear instructions. Ask a question and be prepared to be left more confused. This class gives me so much anxiety, and when I tell you, YOU WILL NEVER know what you're doing. The professor said she hasn't taught this class in four years, and it's OBVIOUS.

This professor does not provide clear instructions in her assignments, and when asked for clarification on the assignment, she is unable to provide good clarity. I do not recommend her class, as it doesn't feel like learning or improving on creative processes as an artist.

Her instructions are unclear and her clarifications rarely help. Her class is a product design class not a creative process strategies class you will be writing multiple page long proposals with annotated bibliography.
Class should be called sticky notes and storyboard. If u like that this 4 u.

this class was unlike any other stamps class i have taken. this is basically like a psych ux research course. name feels misleading. feels like professor has no respect for the arts, or artists. you will not learn anything about design, or any valuable techniques. i came in thinking i would learn how to better use figma. don't be misled.

I really enjoyed her class. I can tell she's really knowledgable on what she teaches. She can give some harsh critiques, but it never feels demeaning, it feels like she wants you to be the best you can be. She also really cared about the students in my class outside of school. I had no trouble understanding her accent, but maybe that's subjective.

This is the worst course that I am taking in this term. You could tell she walked into class with no plan. She just rambled on nothing and we learned nothing. It is also hard to communicate with her because of her accent. I won't take any of her classes again.
Strict attendance policy, and yet he is always late to the class

Dr. Paloff (and POLISH326) were freaking fantastic. The amount of passion and expertise Paloff has is aspirational. He is also one of the most caring and hilarious professors I have ever had. Very relaxed classroom environment with a guy who truly cares for your success—I only had a few nightmares from the stop-motion films. LOVED!!
Great guy, very respectable and treats his students like humans. The papers might be longer than other classes at the 300 level, but he makes them manageable by giving tons of creative freedom.

Actually the best; my class was a seminar so we talked a lot and it was always super engaging, the time would fly by and we take the time to really talk through things so I feel like I learned a ton. Very flexible and understanding, we read so so much but it was okay. Easily my favorite prof.

Generally, this is a very interesting course as I decided to take it to account for my humanity distribution. The workload is a little too much for a non-major distribution intro level course. In short, fun class, kinda heavy workload, a pretty solid choice if your schedule isn't too bad and you are interested in the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Great personality and really knowledgeable on the subject. He's a guy who cares about what he's doing and is really easy to get along with and understand and the class honestly was a lot more fun than I anticipated and I truly enjoyed it.

He is a funny guy. I respect that he isn't out to push any agenda. That seems to be rare in this university. He lets you redo papers and if you are trying, he will help you out. He is very passionate about his work and pushes for honest students. This school needs more professors like him.
Highly recommend Professor Paloff. He is so inspiring and so thought provoking.

Not a bad prof but the work load was excessive for a 100 level class. We had half a dozen novels, movies, and short stories, plus two essays and an exam. Definitely wasn't an easy A and though I found it interesting I wouldn't recommend this class for someone trying to fulfill their humanities requirement. Ben clearly cared but work was too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great lectures - really gets you thinking. You do actually have to the readings to be able to participate in discussion, and there is a participation grade. Not a super heavy work load. Ben incorporates real world issues into a topic that you would not conventionally think represents our world (i.e., zombies).

Paloff wants you to become a better writer. Honestly, I feel he boosted me by half a letter grade in my other classes with his brilliant writing advice. If you work for it (infinite resubmission), you will get an A, and he cares and is an absolute blast.

Mr. Paloff gives very constructive feedback. His aim is to make you a better writer. We have some deep, random discussions and some readings and exercises, but other than that he gives you lots of freedom in your two papers. Some interesting films and books, and I learned a lot, but writing the papers was very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Just a really passionate, intelligent professor who cares about his students and is extremely interested in the material he teaches. Don't expect an easy A but expect thought-provoking, entertaining lectures and the opportunity to earn an A if you are engaged in the material and willing to rework your writing.
Fantastic professor. He's compassionate about the material, compassionate about teaching, and compassionate about his students. I looked forward to every lecture he taught.

Go to his lectures, he's an engaging, extremely educated, really funny professor. I looked forward to lecture, and discussion too. This is a central/eastern european cinema class and he broke the movies down piece by piece, making the papers you have to write easier. Limitless resubmissions because he genuinely wants you tp improve your writing.

By far one of the best professors I've ever had.  I've reevaluated my entire way of thinking.  He's a super cool and interesting guy, open, honest, and hilarious.  You're missing out if you don't take at least one class with him.

Professor Paloff's class changed my life. No, seriously it did. I've never had a professor who seems to be as interested in his student's thoughts as Paloff did. He provoked me and made me rethink my positions every time I entered the classroom. Spend a lot of time digesting the material and engaging Paloff, you won't regret it.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Extremely nice and cool guy. Also, one of the most intelligent men I have encountered.

My favorite teacher I've ever had. Prof Paloff is an amazg lecturer, and makes the class really interesting. He lectures with powerpoints, so make sure you take good notes and write down key terms and the midterms will be easy. He's a really cool guy and the class was really enjoyable.

Paloff is one of the best professors I've had @ U of M! I am a science major so writing is not my forte but he made the class very entertaining and was very helpful. I thought the class seemed overwhelming at first but definitely worth it! One of the best classes I've taken !

One of the best professors I have ever had. He cares so much about each and every person and genuinely wants everyone to do well. He will also do whatever it takes to clarify anything/help with anything. MUST take this professor if you can.

Dr. Paloff is the best professor I've had at the university. He puts so much effort into making us better writers through all of the feedback he gives on written assignments. He's a very charismatic teacher and is very engaging during class. I would recommend taking any class with him!

He gives you lecture handouts for every class with key words. He explains everything and is very clear about it. Super funny so it makes class entertaining. He helps you out a lot with your papers if you need help and if pretty flexible about due dates.

I took my FYWR with him and he was awesome. (It was an English class that focused on Slavic Lit) I will definitely take a class with him again. He actually helps you become a better writer, that's why his class isn't easy.
Really fun, educational and entertaining guy. You have to work for your grade, but you can resubmit papers multiple times so you can earn an A if you put the time in.
Grades papers hard but you can resubmit them as many times as you want. You don't need to read any of the books and class is just him being entertaining. Easy fywr.

A nice and entertaining guy who knows how to relate to students, but the concepts he brought up were pretty vague and he didn't clarify much. This wouldn't bother me so much, but he didn't explain any of the written assignments, both of which were worded vaguely and unclear. Besides that, the material was pretty interesting and class was fun enough

awesome teacher & awesome guy. he really listens to what his students want, and actually takes student opinion very seriously. he took our input about future syllabi & even our arguements on how the class was graded. he gives amazing feedback & made us all 10 minute videos about our final papers. great freshman class! on a sidenote, do the reading

The most caring, passionate professor I've ever had. Besides the first name calling, and the family dinner table atmosphere of class: -we get 4 pages of detailed notes on each essay we right, ON TOP OF lavish marginellia imprinted on our essay -we can rewrite our papers ad infinitum -he made each us a 10 minute video critiquing our final paper
A really inspiring teacher.
He's just an awesome person. He's willing to digress during discussions, but when he gets back on track it's entertaining. Taking his class was definitely worth it.
Pretty nice prof, lectures are very entertaining
What a tremendous teacher
Avoid this prof if you can! Otherwise, you regret!

Professor Park is generally pleasant and easy to approach.

He's quick to agree when you ask for a recommendation letter — which sounds great, until you realize he might write something that quietly undermines you.

Just make sure you know what kind of support you're actually getting.

The lectures move too fast, and the homework, made by TAs and GSIs, is mediocre. The exam was difficult, but the grading is very lenient. I appreciate that he offers what is probably the only computer graphics course at UM. The schedule is also quite flexible—we're basically free starting from mid-November. Can take this course for fun.

Throughout the semester, course materials lacked clarity, especially in assignments and grading. The instructor showed minimal interest and patience in student questions. Communication was poor and there are no office hours. The teaching quality fell below university standards.
Great professor. EECS442 got adapted to be a little bit more cutting edge with radiance fields

I left one of the earlier reviews. It turns out to be a grading error affecting about 10
% of students. It got fixed, and a lot of students receive A range scores following previous distributions. This is the first term Professor Park is here, so I think some mistakes made are totally normal
Worst course ever taken in the eecs department
Worst prof that ever exists umich. Worst class, period

Very poor lecturing. Grading is ambiguous. From piazza, it seems that a score as high as 96 corresponds to an A- without anything stated in the syllabus and an illusion that there would be a curve down given the 70 exam median which ended up being a curve up . I got greater than 93 and also got A-. Worst class taken in umich
Unclear/confusing homework and harsh grading (+ no regrades for their grading mistakes
Homeworks unclear, spec and starter code often contained mistakes. Piazza will be your best friend.
unclear homeworks

Prasad is a good professor who cares a lot about screenwriting and the specific stories for everyone involved in his class. I will say though sometimes he'll give bad advice but other than that he's a good professor
Professor Prasad is a great professor who sets up his class in a way that both trains you for the field but also teaches you a variety of the essential elements of screenwriting
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really good. Only issue I had was with the grading system. The way online quizzes are set up, you have to input the correct answer EXACTLY as Prasad did or else you don't get the points. Other than that, very good; lots of workshops but they're helpful, very smart about course content, funny enough.

I really like this professor. His expectations are clear, and his lectures are clear w/ lots of examples. The readings & scripts are interesting and easy to understand. You work in groups pretty much everyday in this class & he gives different writing exercises based on the concepts in the week's reading. It's a fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good advice for an intro class. Overall helpful prof.
Of the two 310 professors, he was the one who gave feedback on everything. Cares about his students' success. Very passionate about screenwriting.

He seems like a nice guy, but he's not very willing to give advice. And even when you take his advice he'll give you a low grade. Even if you really work you ass off if he doesn't like your ideas or think you're a good writer you don't stand a chance.

The evaluative tests are easy, but the teacher is unbearable. Pretentious to the point of surreal. Perhaps it's what he's going for, but seriously - don't bother. Your ideas will be less appreciated than the screenplay grammar of your work. Take it and perhaps he will make for a good antagonistic character outline in one of your future pieces.

Doesn't give good feedback. Could care less about your idea as long as you mess up some small part in the formatting he marks off. honestly, if you're really interested in film and money isn't an issue don't go here. Overall, they (film department) have equipment but not talent.
He's pretty chill. He's passionate about film. A stickler for the rules though.

Read a feature length script + wrote our own short (only a few pages) working in a group once a week.  Not too tricky if you do the work which isn't very demanding.  Sometimes can give harsh feedback on your writing but it was fair and he says he does it to make you better.  I believe it.  Put effort into your writing, you shouldn't have an issue.

Great class. Prasad was very nice, works hard to keep class interested. We watched a lot of short clips in class that illustrated the topics we went over clearly. Go to his office hours! He's much more approachable in that setting. Sometimes a little scatter-brained when leading class, but I think he commutes from Chicago, so, understandable.

Some of the reviews are pretty unfair; overall, this class is one of the better-run math classes. Though she has a thick accent, I never really had trouble following along, and overall, I thought she did a good job working through and explaining the material and making it understandable. Taking 214 with her is not something to worry too much about.

I think a lot of the reviews are pretty unfair for Professor Sun. She was pretty good at explaining the material and working through problems methodically. She would stop and ask if we had any questions frequently, and was accessible outside class. Her accent is sometimes difficult to understand but you get used to it fast.

Exams were fair, weekly work was manageable, and projects were nice as they helped cushion grades. That said, lectures were not helpful. I had trouble following the math during lectures and ending up using the textbook to re-teach myself the concepts most weeks. I'd recommend taking another professor but you'll be fine either way.

Ignore all the unfair reviews. She is kind, prepared, and provides great note skeletons. Exams are fair, reflect lectures, and allow notecards. The only issue is the language barrier that can make understanding some concepts a bit difficult. If you attend lecture, follow along, and study properly, an A is easily achievable. You will be fine.

Lectures are genuinely incomprehensible and impossible to understand and follow. Also, required attendance through iClicker. Read the textbook since lectures aren't helpful, and study a ton before exams.
difficult to understand lectures, better off reading textbook
Incredibly unclear lecturer and impossible to communicate with outside of class. I would seriously try to avoid taking 214 with this professor by any means necessary. LOL

There's definitely a heavy workload in this class but Zhao Laoshi is such an amazing teacher. She has a ton of energy, offers a lot of opportunities to earn points and extra credit and overall just makes a difficult language a lot easier to learn. My favorite chinese teacher I've had here!

I have had this professor for ASIANLAN101, 102, and 201 and she is amazing. She is very caring about students and always excited to teach us new material and give us nuance on real-world usage of words. She is a very generous grader, so it's not hard to do well.

She is probably one of the nicest and caring teachers I have ever encountered in my life. She is a great teacher and an even better person. Do not hesitate to sign up for one of her classes. I really can't put into words how nice and understanding she is and how she truly cares about her students and class.

I'm unsure of why there is no option to pick ASIANLAN101, but I enjoyed Zhao Laoshi so much I made sure to prioritize having her for this second semester of Chinese. She makes learning super fun by playing games at the end of practically every class. She also has us engage with classmates, which is great because we see each other five days a week.

Overall good, but some of the political opinions she inserted into class were uncomfortable and unnecessary.  Though politically correct in the US, the topics that were brought up from the assigned videos were not related to the language itself.

She is my favorite teacher ever. Best teacher I've had since Kindergarten and she has so much respect and love for all her students. She's also really fun and we play games in class! Definitely take her!

Quili laoshi is the best!! She's so sweet and makes class so fun. We always play a fun game in the last five minutes of class too, like Kahoot or Blooklet. The class is easy to follow and the workload is very manageable. It's one of the only classes that meets five days a week, but I don't even mind because it's so chill. I highly recommend her! :)

Seriously, one of the best in UMich's Chinese department. Smoothest online class I have; you can tell she worked hard this summer to make sure this semester went well. Really recommend the class. Approximately weekly quizzes and about 4 hours a week of homework outside of class, not bad at all for a 5 credit.
Zhao laoshi is one of my favorite professors at umich! There is constant testing in this class, but it's always very clear what to study. 10/10 would recommend

I really enjoyed Chinese with Zhao Laoshi. The class itself is time consuming, so prepare to be constantly tested. Participation is crucial in this course. She never makes you feel uncomfortable speaking and though she often corrects students, it is never done in a discouraging way. I'd definitely recommend taking Chinese with Zhao Laoshi.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved taking Chinese with Zhao Laoshi. She is so kind and funny and supportive. I never felt anxious talking in class because she works hard to make the class environment comfortable. Be prepared to make mistakes and be corrected often, but in a constructive way. The entire Chinese Language department at U-M is phenomenal.

If you're taking Chinese at UMich and not doing your best to take it with Zhao Laoshi, I don't know what you're doing. Zhao Laoshi is the best, and I've absolutely loved having her as my teacher. She pushes you and makes sure you learn, but she also is very understanding and has realistic expectations. Plus, she's the kindest person ever. 10/10.

Incredible professor. While I haven't had a bad professor for Chinese at U of M, Zhao Lao Shi is definitely one of my favorites. She will push you, as ASIANLAN 201 and 202 require a lot more listening and writing comprehension, but you will learn a ton. Great experience, kind woman, and definitely worth taking a class with!

Great teacher!!! My reading/writing skills improved significantly after taking her class, and so did my speaking. She gives many mini vocab quizzes each week but they're very easy if you study for them and just memorize the characters.

Absolutely fantastic. She's a great teacher who cares about her students. Do some preparation before class, since she will call on everyone at least 2-3 times, which keeps everyone engaged. You will need to put in some effort to do well, but she's not too harsh of a grader and your Chinese skills will improve a lot.

My Chinese improved rapidly after taking her class. She is extremely nice and caring to all her students and she made class extremely fun. That said, her class is relatively an easy A if you set some time aside to study some vocab and sentence patterns. Also, she is an easy grader. Quizzes and Tests are pretty easy.

Professor Zhao is an amazing teacher with an extraordinary ability to effectively connect with students. Her kind and fun personality helped me to improve my Chinese speaking/writing/reading abilities. Tests are a bit difficult at first but as you get used to them (and the weekly quizzes), they become fun. You won't regret taking class with her!

I love Zhao Laoshi! I was slightly wary at first because her syllabus makes her sound strict, but she's a cute little lady who's incredibly easy going. Her class isn't too hard as long as you put in some work. Tests aren't very hard and she's a very easy grader. Class can be slightly boring, but I would love to have her as a teacher again!

I love LaoShi, she's the best.  Super cute and friendly.  The class is set up so you have 2 vocab quizzes per chapter and a unit test for every 2 chapters.  PARTICIPATION is MANDATORY in class!!!  It's very organized so you know exactly what is expected out of you.  There should be no problem getting an A.

Zhao LaoShi is excellent! I had Gu LaoShi last semester and was kinda wary about taking this class but Zhao LaoShi is equally funny and helpful, and the class is a lot of fun! She teaches you exactly what you need to know for quizzes and tests, and does so in an interesting way. She makes sure that each student gets their voice heard.

She is so awesome!!! Just as good as Gu lao shi. She really cares about her students and is always very happy. Very nice grader and I have really learned a lot in this class. I'll miss her a lot! Take her class!
Zhao Laoshi is very understanding and is not nearly as strict as her syllabus states. Tests are quite hard compared to 104. Lots of essays and you present your essays in class as well

Zhao laoshi is super nice and lenient on grading. The difficulty of the class depends on your prior knowledge, so the amount of studying required varies. She's always willing to help though. Everybody gets called on at least twice a day, so you can't really zone out. I enjoyed the class, and my Chinese definitely improved. She's a great teacher!
Requires 100% attendance. If you need absense, you have to provide doctor notes.

The class material itself is not hard, but Dr. Qiu is not a clear grader and seemingly grades without solid rubrics or expectations. Attendence is measured with random pop quizzes, sometimes given if he sees there are not many students in class. There are many lengthy and dense readings, and a single final project makes up 50% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is only exciting because of the super fun labs, led by fantastic GSIs. On the other hand, lectures felt more like a comedy routine than a botany class. YQ overcomplicated pretty basic material, and students hardly paid attention. But the class wasn't too difficult, and he was definitely a character, and I would recommend this course.
Super passionate and informative, but super unorthodox and unclear about course structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked this class. No matter what, do NOT skip class. Throughout this course we had a total of 2 pop quizzes, which account for 10 percent of your final grade. Missing class one time drastically dropped my grade. The lab is super fun, but the lectures don't really connect very well to the lab section. Also, pop quizzes are quick but not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love YQ. Probably my favorite class and lecturer at UM. He truly is like an uncle you have fun conversations with. He loves talking about his garden and about herbal medicine. Lectures are chill, no exams or quizzes really. Take as a nice class filler and get to know YQ!

I feel the whole class loved their time with YQ. He feels like an uncle who tells stories. He has a huge garden at his house and loved to talk about it. LAB WAS SO FUN!!! We had Jacob and he is THE BEST!!!! You get free plants, food, etc. I recommend the course. There is one mid-term & a final project.
Awesome and funny guy. Lowest grade he gave all semester to anyone on any assignment was an A-. And everyone got A- or above for a final grade. Take 212 with him for an easy credit filler.

You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches, although he can be a bit confusing at times when answering questions. Although quizzes seem to pop up randomly they were all very easy and most of the course felt like a completion grade. Nobody knows what his grading methodology on papers is but it seems to be if you had fun so.. have fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: YQ really cares about plants and botany in general, and this enthusiasm is evident in his lectures and activities. He can be a bit harsh sometimes if people don't understand directions for assignments and ask for clarification. The course isn't very cohesive across lab/lecture, so that gets overwhelming and confusing at times

Bought the textbook before class started and in the first lecture he said we'd be fine without it or with a different one... he does a great job of making the class interesting while you are still learning legit stuff. As long as you pay good attention you should be fine on tests. Encouraged us to make wine for our personal semester projects.
Great guy, easy class, interesting material

Just go to class and you'll be fine. There are pop quizzes but otherwise no one would come to class because most people aren't actually interested in the material. It's not hard and definitely underrated.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Honestly, he seems like a decent and honorable professor until it comes down to grading. None of it makes sense, you receive grades that don't correlate with your amount of effort or the actual assignment itself. I'm not sure how he does it, but it's one just big jumbled up huckaboo if you ask me. I warn you, do not take this as a credit filler.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Excellent Teacher! I took his class Fall 2017 and loved it. He incorporates a lot of real-world examples into his teaching, which makes his class very interesting! Read the papers and powerpoints well, as there will be pop quizzes!
YQ was great! He's really made an effort to be very relaxed and approachable in and outside of class. He isn't at all like any of the old reviews rate him here. Lab is also a blast.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: YQ has worked really hard to improve his ratings, he's much more respectful, has reformatted the class and tries to be really accessible. His exams and pop quizzes are not really fair, just expect to not do great, but the lab is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: YQ is by far the most energetic professor I've ever had, and he's a lovely guy with the misfortune to be teaching a sadly dull class. He does what he can and I'd certainly rather be learning from him than your typical lecturer, but botany is a difficult subject to pay attention to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: YQ is an awesome teacher! Super chill and relaxed. It was a great class!
Fantastic class discussions. Casual teaching style and very approachable. Really had a good time in his class.
He's so nice and is super passionate about what he teaches.  Always excited to go to his class.

I have never been more insulted by a professor. His class was 90% talking about how stupid American students are and 10% muddled lectures based on slides that look like they were designed for graduate classes. The exams were horribly unfair, a complaint I never thought was justified till I took this class. Multiple students in my class reported him

I was very excited about this class, but it soon turned out to be one of the worst I have taken at U of M. The lab was one of the best classes and I wish that people could take it separately because the lecture was useless. YQ's slides were confusing and no one knew what was relevant.

AVOID!!!!!!!!!!!! The book that was assigned had interesting information, but he never once referenced any of these interesting things. He used personal information through the entire class that contained little useful content ignoring important concepts. Could not follow though process for power point, no clue where the info came from.

I changed my entire schedule to take this class because I loved the subject matter. After being in this class, I would change my entire schedule again, but to avoid at all costs. The GSI's and lab are great for my botany class but the lecture does not teach anything. I've lost all interest I had in this topic.

Initially, I thought he was quarky and funny. Then I found out he would only post year-old lecture slides rather than the ones he would actually be using? Then he spent half of each lecture discussing his philosophy on education and why current undergraduates would make for crappy graduate students later? It was absolutely ridiculous, so I dropped.

He started off by advising my class to look up things we didn't understand on wikipedia. Never have I ever heard a professor recommend a student teach themselves the material using wikipedia! His lectures were unorganized, he didn't emphasize any major concepts (instead he focused on plants that never popped up again), and no one could understand h

He complained about the people that didn't show up to class to the people who obviously did. And those who went to every lecture but could not understand anything he was saying or read his writing, were at a disadvantage, as well because he wouldn't post all the slides. He made it clear that he didn't want us to do well and didn't answer questions!

Supposed to be an intro class for non-science majors. Qiu was a condescending ass. He wouldn't tell us any info about the exams. During the midterm, a lot of students were confused about the wording of a question (he doesn't have the best English skills), and he brushed us off saying that the question was "perfectly clear." NOT

Unless you need to take this class don't take it.  It isn't a hard class- Dr. Qiu, while nice and approachable, is not a good teacher.  Better to take a class that you might actually learn something in over the course of four months.  This class was a waste of time and you will not come out knowing much about plants, fungi, or bacteria.

I'm currently trudging through Plant evolution, which has little to do with plants. Much of every lecture is devoted to Qiu talking about how surprised he is that undergrads can be intelligent, or talking about how amazing he is at creating power points and being a scientist in general.  An absolutely terrible class. For the record, my grade is ok.
Really nice guy, good professor. His assignments aren't difficult. He even says he's not there to trick you, he just wants you to learn the important points.
Today was the first day of class and her accent is super hard to understand. I didn't understand anything and she's kind of unprepared. I believe that i'll drop this course.
fantastic professor. clear and easy to understand, made physics 250 feel easy. would take any other courses she teaches.

prof yang is incredibly knowledgeable and is a great teacher. i enjoyed lectures and found her class to be engaging. the material is hard, but if you focus during class and do your work, you'll be fine.

Professor Yang is a great professor and is good at breaking down the more complicated derivations that we come across in class. I thought her chalkboard lecture style was engaging to follow, especially compared to slide decks. She gave extensions or homework modifications when asked by the class as well. Overall not a high stress class either.

She's a great professor, although her lectures can be unclear at times. She's very understanding and a easy grader, but expectations may be unclear at times. That's alright though she will make sure you pass the class.

My favorite professor!! She is so caring, always willing to help, and her tests and assignments very clearly reflect what we have learned in class. The workload is very manageable and expectations for assignments are reasonable and clear. Take her class if you can!
you will love her. so sweet and caring and just brightened my day every day. she's a great teacher and genuinely cares about you and your learning. her class is fun, rewarding, and not too much work.

I LOVE Liu 老是。She was so caring, patient, and funny, and really took her time to calmly explain each topic and even break down the characters and sayings. We did some fun stuff in class, like watch funny Chinese videos, and she was just so so so kind. The class was tough, but that's to be expected. I wish I could take her for every Mandarin class.
Great prof! I felt like I grew so much in this course, and she gave really great feedback! This class is a lot of work, but as long as you put the effort in you should be fine.
