Qian Liu (qianlw) is extremely caring and treats her students like her own children. I had a lot of mental health issues while taking 204 and she listened to me and gave a lot of good advice and encouragement because she went through the same thing. The class does have weekly homework quizzes but it's manageable for heritage speakers.

Qian Liu is the best professor I have ever had, possibly the kindest person I have ever met If you really care about learning Chinese, I highly recommend taking this class. The workload can sometimes be a little bit on the heavier side but I guarantee your Chinese will improve tremendously after taking this class.

Qian was the funniest, most chill professor Ive ever had. He was a super easy grader and its not hard to get an A if you put in minimal effort. His teaching style was hard to understand at times and a bit unorganized, but overall he was great.

One of the most caring and patient professors I have ever had. She is extremely enthusiastic and genuinely cares about each of her students. I never liked Chinese very much but I looked forward to every class with her.
Very understanding teacher but grades tough on essays and tests
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a very kind teacher who gives you feedback and is accessible during class and during office hours without making you feel lowly. Also, she has a lot of energy when teaching Chinese and makes class enjoyable. However, there are frequent vocab quizzes that add up and the exams do get quite hard. Also, she can be a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is a very good instructor. I always looked forward to her lecture, and although there are frequent vocabulary quizzes, we always knew what characters were going to be tested and at the end they helped me stay on track in this class. She is very accessible for help, although the exams may be a little hard.

Best chinese teacher I've had out of 6 teachers! She gives really helpful feedback, she grades hard but fair, and challenges you in a fun way! She just has one of those warm personalities that makes asking for help easier. Puts effort into her lesson plans. You must show up to class to get an A. Biweekly presentations, weekly vocab quizzes and hw.

Amazing teacher who is very patient and kind. Doesn't make you feel dumb when she gives you feedback about your Chinese pronunciation or sentence structures. You should go to office hours because she'll practice Chinese with you. Weekly vocab quizzes and regular presentations. Also she's super pretty! :)

She's an amazing teacher and person, really supportive of near-native students expanding their Chinese capabilities. She's a tough but fair grader.   Go to office hours if you need extra help; you won't regret it. It's also fun to chat with her about life in general.  I'm excited to take 204 with her again!
She was always super helpful and available.  Really friendly, Relatively difficult grader though.

She is so adorable! Although she is a tough grader she gives heavy weight on participation. She is clear in her directions, easy to communicate with, and very helpful in office hours. My Chinese improved significantly and I loved working with her. One of my favorite teachers.
A little strict in grading but I love her because she's super cute and nice! She's very understanding and is genuinely interested in getting to know her students
Good teacher that kept class interesting. Lots of class participation and group work. Homework/studying everyday though. Make sure you participate and she likes you and you'll have a fun time!
Harsh grader but clear lecturer and very helpful; always willing to meet with students if they needed help. The fact that she's good looking as hell is a bonus.
Wants completely novel ideas for the project. Rejects almost everything.
He is very clearly a smart guy but his lectures are incomprehensible and he spends a good chunk of the class talking about his own achievements rather than using that time to teach students??????

Some of the worst lectures I've attended. His slides are terrible, the way he teaches is OK at times but confusing most of the time, and any visual examples he draws out are usually incomprehensible.

I was honestly disappointed and felt like I wasted so many hours of my time. At Michigan there's no reason to have a lecturer this bad.

Professor Stout seems like a nice guy outside of class, but was extremely rude to his students. He often talked down to us asking a genuine question, and was unavailable over email, often never responding. The content in lectures often lagged behind the homework. Lectures didn't match homework, and little help for the final project. Overall bad.

I don't know about high level class. I am taking EECS 376 right now. And his lecture is the only one I can understand. He goes into details and provide clear explanation. Also he is patient with questions. I would recommend him if you take 376.

I can tell that he is smart and experienced: This is from his lecture and OH. But he is an awful instructor: lack of slides makes it hard to review, his lecture is not well organized, etc. In all, I think he is rather enjoying talking to himself instead of teaching students. Plus, the grading policy of homework are really weird.

Quentin is a bit behind the times when it comes to effective use of modern teaching techniques and technology. He means well, but there's improvement to be made. <- My review after finishing the class. 586 felt like an assault on my brain and attention span every day I was in the class. <- My review during the class

Frankly speaking, he's not that bad. Yep, his class is not well-organized, HW without solutions, GSI plays smartphones at OH and I don't know how ge gives the credit. But he is energetic and his HW is actually great... it forces u to think if u don't overhear others' solution at OH.
If no one takes his class, then he can retire. It is good for him and us.

Everyone seems to be hating on Stout here, but I honestly thought he was a decent teacher. He's definitely not the best, but he's not the demon that people make him out to be. I appreciated his humor and enthusiasm.

What we should do: If you want to take his class to learn something, unfortunately, it will only be a waste of time. If you plan to take his class to satisfy some requirement, find alternatives. If you are taking his class, do the teaching evaluation. If you took his class, report him to the school and ask someone else to teach.

He never released HW solutions but had students present their own solutions in front of whiteboard, maybe so that he could reuse same problems in the future. What's worst was that most of the time he didn't comment anything on the wrong solutions students presented. I knew because GSI confirmed my other solutions were correct during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Student who are taking or took his classes must come together and report Stout to the college for him not being able to teach classes! United we stand divided we fall !
Utterly useless.
Arbitrary lectures, pointless answer for your question, don't care about teaching nor research. What can you ask for from such professor?
Avoid him at all cost! He doesn't care about students.

Professor Stout can be a bit confusing at times, especially in 587, where almost everything are unrealistic parallel concepts that lack real world applications. Your grade will be the final project (HW are a joke) for which can be really hard to get a topic approved and the grading can be a bit arbitrary. Thus the grades are mostly from B+/A-.

I started out the semester with Stout but was quickly confused  by his lectures. His teaching was hard to follow and his examples were difficult to understand. He's not necessarily a bad professor, but I had a difficult time learning from him and ended up switching to Lee's lecture partway through the semester.

Stout is a brilliant and cool guy, but he is not the right professor for EECS203. His lectures were off topic and unhelpful. He spends half the class philosophizing about the content instead of giving you useful information related to exams and HW. I switched to Lee and instantly started learning more. HW and exams got easier after I switched.
For EECS 203 he is pretty disorganized and his lectures are hard to follow. He is okay at teaching when you ask questions but he isn't very good in lecture.
Most people will get a B+/A-. It is very hard to get outside this range.
Very boring, but material was fairly straightforward.  Honestly I didn't get much out of this class even though he preached everyday about how we would use this class in everything we do.

Stout is an ok teacher. He is a nice guy, but his lectures are kind of boring. It is a class about computer theory, which I think is kind of boring anyway, but his lectures never really grab my interest. Just make sure you go to the gsi's office hours about the weekly homework and stay for the whole time.

ENTR 530 is such a great class. Like many others, I had no idea what to expect; but we were blessed with relevant case studies for patent law, guest speakers from every industry, and group work that didn't just seem boring and painful. The class is highly engaging, on the easier side, and very informative; Quinn is a great professor and lecturer.
Fantastic professor and class; had no idea what to expect going into IP strategy and patent law, but ended with lots of great knowledge with a fun experience along the way

Chris is absolutely someone you want to take a class with if you want the word from a true expert in the field of IP law. This class was not an easy A - he definitely makes you work for it, but for good reason. You'll learn a ton in his class, and he brought in some great guest lecturers as well. His passion for educating students is very apparent.
Dr. QI is the GOAT!
Dr. Qi is amazing. Delivers clear content and exams are open resource. He is patient and accessible outside class.

Well meaning professor who truly knows what he's talking about. Very helpful in office hours and wants you to succeed. Might lecture a bit fast, but always uploads his power point slides on canvas. Very responsive to feedback if something in class isn't working.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Hard to follow sometimes. Flies through power points like no one's business. Nice guy, good office hours. Strange class format.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Amazing professor for EECS 270! The material is pretty tricky but he does a great job of fully explaining things during lecture. He clearly cares about all his students and wants everyone to succeed. Lectures are engaging and helpful, so I would go even though attendance is not mandatory. Overall had a great experience.

This guy is a legend. He is so flexible if you talk to him, and he's saved me multiple times on assignments I was not able to complete. His lectures are so clear, and he carries eecs270. If hes teaching 280, I'd take it with him immediately!
there were two professors for eecs 270 fall semester, the other guy retired. the other guy was decent. razak is amazing though. super super clear lectures

Funny guy that makes lectures fun and digestible. Really cares about his students. Beware of difficult exams but the grading scale set to 84% for an A by default makes getting a good grade in this class very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Writing this before the final so my perspective is not skewed because of my performance on the exam, as I do believe he's a fantastic lecturer. He did lose me sometimes in lecture, but that's because the course itself is quite conceptually challenging. He tries to make things as digestible as possible, and is pretty funny to boot. Highly recommend.
Honestly, my favorite professor at Umich.
Amazing teacher for EECS 280, explained the concepts super well and with some jokes too

I really like the sense of humor. Exams and homework were well-designed. However, I found it difficult to follow the lectures, especially when he didn't stick to the slides. Sometimes, I struggled to distinguish which points were important and which were not. But that might just be me—I've heard other students say his lectures are easy to follow.

He lost me at times during lectures, but that could be my own fault; the class period was right after lunch haha. But he gets the material across well and he's pretty funny. Classes run long -- I encourage him to take more breaks during lecture, perhaps just 5 minutes halfway through so everyone can reset their brain.
He's a great lecturer who was able to make the dry material of Computer Networks sound pretty cool. I saw people call him Tim Duncan of lecturers which sounds pretty close.

Amazing lecturer. He explains things very well and is super funny. You can attend any of the lecturer sections regardless of the section you're registered for, and so I highly recommend attending/watching his lectures.
Amazing lecturer who really knows what he's talking about and knows how to present the information in an understandable way

Professor Razak is a very talented public speaker, which makes him a great lecturer. He is thorough and clear every time. 100% would take again for future CS courses, and HIGHLY recommend for EECS280.

Best CompSci lecturer I've had. Explains everything in an understandable manner and somehow finds a way to remain engaged with his large class. He is also very approachable and answers questions well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very engaging and I find him to be very humorous! He provides necessary information very well and with examples that are explained. He answers questions thoughtfully.
I will mainly remember Professor Razak for his exceptionally good analogies from things in computer science to the real world.

Lectures were excellent and funny. Introduces concept by devising a case where its use helps solve a programmer's problem. Also heavily focuses on asking questions to students to keep them engaged and correct mislearning. Lecture content directly helps in completing concurrent projects, which in turn build understanding for exams.

He's a really good teacher and explains complicated concepts very well. He engages with the students a lot during lectures and has a lot of funny stories to tell about his family and career in Qatar. He's new in umich eecs but I would DEFINITELY take him over the other eecs 280 lecturers.
hes nice

His lectures are interesting, and he's always funny. He often asks questions, which can sometimes slow the lecture down, but he makes sure everyone understands the material. I was worried about going to his lectures because he was new to teaching at UofM, but I am glad I did.

This professor was amazing. From the first lecture, he was engaging and funny and kept me interested in this class even though it is not my major. He asks a lot of questions to the class which I found helpful and answers all of the questions that the students have.

She changed the format from online exams to in person half way through the course. Was mad that nobody cares about her class so purposely made the exam super difficult - the average was a 64 and she refused to curve it. Would never take a class by her ever again.

Dr. Rosenbaum is amazing! She did switch multiple choice section of the exams from online to in person, but in the age of AI, I believe that to be perfectly reasonable. She's very helpful, enthusiastic when answering questions, and It's fun to listen to her lectures! This class was the highlight of every week.
just mean for her joke of a class
Switched our exams to in person after our first two exams which were open-book and online. Ridiculous.

Having taken Psych 368 with Rosenbaum and Anthrbio 201 with a different professor, don't take 201 next semester with Rosenbaum (or any anthro class with her). She was strict and didn't post lecture recordings. Her lectures were fine but her harsh approach brought down the mood of what could have been a fun class.

Amazing lecturer. She's clear, engaging, passionate, and made primate behavior fun to learn. The open book exams and grading was fair. The essays were hard and without much support honestly but I appreciate that Stacy read through and gave feedback on them on top of the GIs - somewhat harsh feedback, but useful nonetheless!

The lectures were informative and interesting but it wasn't easy to know what to study for exams, especially with guest lectures every few weeks. The papers were challenging but very doable and Rosenbaum made herself available for any questions. I wish this class incorporated more active participation, such as iClicker practice questions or polls.

Definitely recommend this class! Dr. Rosenbaum is super knowledgeable, very well-spoken, and makes her lectures super engaging. Your grade is determined by 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are online, open book. They are fairly straightforward imo. The paper rubrics and expectations are clear and are touched upon in class frequently! 10/10

She is a great lecturer but these exams were no joke. Often pretty confusingly written with a lot of inference based material. Even with going to office hours and doing all the work + bonus work I struggled quite a bit. Got perfect scores on the homework, section assignments, and attendance and this still put a dent in my gpa. Proceed with caution.

Prof. Rosebaum is a great lecturer and knows her stuff. She's respectful, quick to respond to emails, and answers questions well; however, don't let her open note exams fool you, they're NOT easy and the majority of info can not be found on the lecture slides so focus on the textbook. She does offer extra credit (adds up to 1%).

very rude and disrespectful when communicating with students. she didn't even try to understand what I was asking her and answered with a very immature retort. she thought she ate when she in fact did not. super condescending. lectures are fine, but her one on one communication skills are not it.

Don't take this class if you aren't a science person. I took this for a NS credit, and now i want to kms. they changed all of the "late" work that they accepted throughout the semester, so now I am going to fail. if they were going to take away points they shouldn't have waited until the last minute. completely ruined my night. thanks stacy.

First, Prof Rosenbaum clearly cares about the topic she's teaching. She's so passionate. Lectures are interesting and she always answers questions. GSI's are amazing. Tests are pretty easy as long as you organize your lecture notes (its open notes). Overall, awesome class and prof.

Anthrobio personally just wasn't for me, but Professor Rosenbaum was always giving you the opportunity to succeed which was awesome since it I didn't always understand. Do the optional readings because they're on the exams.

I took ANTHRBIO 201 for my nat. sciences requirement, and it turned out to be a great class! Prof Rosenbaum has enjoyable and understandable lectures even for those not majoring in the field, and she is really helpful in office hours. Exams are open note and pretty straight forward. There are a couple reading-heavy weeks, but nothing unmanageable.

Dr. Rosenbaum is amazing. Tests were difficult and you definitely need to put work into the papers but her grading criteria is very clear and it's more than possible to score highly on papers if you follow the rubric. Lectures are interesting and she is extremely respectful of students. People feel comfortable asking questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have met in college. She is very condescending and shows no respect to other subfield in anthropology major. She is very rude, hard to communicate. I do respect the efforts she has put in her classes, but I hope she can learn how to talk and write properly and politely, instead of urging students to do x y and z.

All the other reviews are facts. Would recommend literally any class she teaches she's an amazing teacher. Expectations and material are super clear and easy to understand, plus her lectures are genuinely interesting and I am not at all a science fan.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best and most intelligent professors I've ever had in my life. I'm telling you right now TAKE. HER. CLASS. I have never met anyone else who could make a 1.5 hour lecture about evolution so interesting. Her lectures are always well-prepared and structured and she gives you all the tools and advice you need to do well in the class.

i absolutely love her. definitely cares for & understands her students, very communicative, straightforward. sometimes the test questions can be worded a little vaguely, but just try not to overthink it (can be difficult). reading heavy but she goes over all of it during lecture & adds stuff; read the book, watch her lectures and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenbaum is a good lecturer. Her lectures are clear and informative. The class has weekly multiple choice quizzes consisting of 2-3 questions. There are four exams each covering one unit. The exams consist of multiple choice, T/F and short answer questions and are pretty easy since everything is open book during COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Rosati is truly knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, which makes the class fun. The course has 6 readings per week + online and in-person discussions with no exams. I enjoyed her lectures, but she can get so passionate that she rambles and sometimes cuts students off when they are speaking. This made it feel one-sided at times.

Overall very fun course and great professor. There are three group presentations but they aren't hard. Lots of reading, but the empirical papers are interesting. She clearly loves what she teaches and that makes the course so much more fun. Would recommend.

Solid professor. Dr. Rosati clearly loves what she teaches, which always improves a class. Doesn't allow electronics in class without a good reason, prefers pen and paper notetaking. Getting access to lecture recordings is like pulling teeth, so just show up to the lectures. 

Overall good course and good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: NOOO, just no. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Take her psych class if you want to stress over anything. She pushed me away from psychology, despite the fact that I intended to major in it. Also, be prepared for her examinations' multiple-choice questions are like 5 or 6 (like both A and B) (all of the above) (Both C and D). Take any other psych class except hers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosati is a great professor and makes the lecture accessible to all students. But the exam is very tough, and she will catch plenty of detail in the exam. If you want to fulfil your requirement, try to avoid taking this course.

Attendance mandatory in sections. I didn't love Rosati and classes were slightly dry at times with the depth she went into primate systems, but it was nice w/ humans at the end. I didn't study as much as I could've, but found that exams could be more nuanced than other professors. Make sure to pay attention in class & study the little things.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rosati is super knowledgable and makes lectures accessible to all students. The content in lecture is really interesting and she allows opportunity to learn through lecture, videos, and readings, which are all super helpful in the class. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely smart, approachable and fair in her exam writing. Very considerate and clearly has a passion for what she teaches. There's a lot of reading and it helps to do them, but she also gives a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very easy to get a good grade. However, the way the material was presented was uninteresting and uninsightful. They did not seem to know the topic very well, and would often forget to cite information they were presenting as fact, which was really strange for an academic professional. Maybe interesting if you're entirely new to the subject.

Prof Streeters class was a great topic taught by someone who doesn't seem like they know what they're talking about at all - which is weird bc some of the readings are her published works. People would ask questions mid lecture and she would say “I'll get back to you on that.” Not very entertaining and always seemed unconvinced by her own slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Streeter uses the specifications grading system. I had never been in a class with this type of grading before, but after being in this class I think I prefer it. Most of the assignments can be redone for a better grade and the criteria to receive an A are very clear. Professor Streeter had interesting lectures and a reasonable workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: worst prof ever. dont take phy 140 with him if u didnt take any physics classes in hs

Physics 140, the best way to begin your day. Professor is very energetic and cares about the material he is teaching. Always leaves room for questions and is available for office hours. Class does move at a fast pace though.

Yuri Popov is the best way to begin your day. He made the 9am lectures fun, and he is absolutely hilarious. The class is pretty difficult, but he is so much fun. And this review is closed. And it's closed. And it's real closed.
Lots of content and little explanation for the course material. Professor just does not seem to care a whole lot about the students.

Lectures are extremely fast, don't try to take notes as he's talking. Just try to focus and take in information. Not great at answering questions without a condescending tone. Tests are all multiple-choice, but felt fair for the material. Great professor though and extremely passionate. Also, he's iconic for UMich engineering students.

If you like multiple choice quizzes with no partial credit and can keep up with faster pace lectures, Popov is great. But I suck at multiple choice and the lectures went way to fast for me. I learn by examples and Popov did examples, but they went way too fast and required a little too much pre-lecture reading for me to gain much from them.

I didn't like his personality but other than that it's a pretty easy class. If you didn't take this in HS then I can imagine this being much harder but if you pay attention and start the homeworks early it's manageable.

genuinely the worst professor i've ever had. he was rude and condescending both in person and in emails. the exams were absolutely brutal, and the average grade on the final was in the 60s, which wasn't much different from the other exams. he teaches super fast and expects you to know everything, even the bizarre trick question stuff he does.
Clear lectures that are extremely helpful, and enthusiastic about office hours, though learning materials costs a bit higher than average. Definitely would like to take his course again if possible!

Professor Popov is quite condescending to those who asks questions. Additionally, attendance is taken by iClicker quizzes, which means you may not even get full marks for attendance. Every question feels like a trick question, and the average on his 4 midterms was 10/15, 17/25 for the final. All multiple-choice with no grading for work.

MAKE SURE TO TAKE AP PHYSICS 1 OR AP PHYSICS C BEFORE TAKING THIS CLASS. There is so much content in this class that you are significantly behind if you didn't take either of these classes. Yuri Popov is extremely fast paced but reasonably so because there is so much content. Some days I felt like he was evil and the MCQ tests are HELLLLLL.

I took the 9am section which eventually caught up to me towards the end of the semester. Though attendance is via i-clicker, you get substantial credit for just answering. I had a pretty decent ap physics teacher in hs, yet Yuri still elevated my understanding of physics. Loved his demonstrations.

Homework took a long time, as did reading the textbook. But there are lots of resources (I went to the Physics Help Room for my homework all the time). Class can be stressful because of the i-clicker questions (4 points for a correct answer and 3 if you get it wrong), but the 6 lowest grades get dropped. Course materials were expensive.

Great lecturer and explains things clearly. His enthusiasm makes the class one to look forward to, and he does fun demos. Your grade is pretty dependent on the exams (which kind of sucks), but the questions are very reasonable and similar to the past exams he posts. Overall, this class was enjoyable, and I will definitely miss his travel photos

Yuri is a great lecturer and the best way to start my morning! My only complaint is the structure of the exams: 15 multiple choice questions with no partial credit. But I guess you get what you sign up for. As long as you're on top of your homework and pay attention in lecture, you'll be fine!

I suck at physics and never got an above average grade on any of his exams, yet you can't dislike the guy. His lectures were engaging and he is so well versed on all the material within the class. While I'm so glad to be done with physics I, I'll miss his jokes and travel pictures.

Great lecturer. Makes everything very engaging and gives more than enough reason to stay awake and learn at 9 a.m. Homework can be tough, but if you can ace homework then you can ace exams. Everything on the exams was covered at some point in class. No trick questions, no bs. Great guy, difficult course, he makes it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, exams are reasonable but definitely can screw your grade if you make some mistakes, attendance is mandatory
It was indeed the best way to begin my day

Having this class at 9am sucks, but Yuri does the best he can to make lectures interesting. However, the content is very hard to get a full grasp on, and at times the lectures felt like they didn't go in-depth enough on it. The homework is also way harder than the problems in lectures/exams. However, in terms of PHYS140 Yuri is the best it gets.

The professor is pretty great, but sometimes he moves through the content very quickly in the lectures. This was difficult for me because I had physics at 9am, and as someone who is not a morning person, I had to drag myself out of bed to answer MCQ with a physical iClicker for attendance. Not to mention it is test heavy and typical median is 10/15

His lectures were condensed, poorly explained content that is not helpful if this is your first time learning physics. Exams are short, multiple choice, and very hard to do well on. Prepare to spend a lot of time and energy on homework and teaching yourself the content
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Popov is a very experienced and informative teacher. However, the materials for the class can be pricey, which is inconvenient. I don't count that against him as a teacher, but I would keep it in mind before taking his section.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly find his grading to be pretty unfair. All exams are mcq with no opportunities for points back, and the averages are 10/15 per exam. Additionally not only does he grade attendance, but as it's by clicker questions you might not even get a full mark for attendance technically. Also he seems condescending.

Yuri is a great lecturer and knows the material very well. However, he has little respect for his students and can be very condescending to his students in lecture and during office hours. Physics 140 requires almost $200 worth of access codes just to begin working on the material and there are 5 exams (4 mid. 1 fin.) worth most all of your grade.

Really dedicated professor, and very down to earth. Not the most flawless when it comes to conveying information in lectures, and the homework can be difficult. He cares about students and is willing to work with you if you have problems, quick email replies as well.

Dr. Popov was a great lecturer.  He was incredibly funny and made the 9 am lectures bearable.  The class itself is difficult for sure, but if you work hard to stay on top of everything and attend lectures, it will be okay.  Go to the physics help room as much as you can.

Yuri is one of my favorite lecturers EVER. Where the class falls is the sheer amount of content, and the expectation of prior physics knowledge. However, this is not Yuri's issue, and he truly does his best with the content he has. Totally an A+ lecturer with a D+ class.

Great lecturer, but awful teacher. His slides and explanations are amazing in class, but he is definitely very condescending and tends to look down on students when they are confused. He preaches dropping out of his class at the slightest inconvenience, which is not exactly very motivational. Word of advice: don't to take it to heart.

He seems condescending in his emails and when you talk to him. At first you seem like it'll be fine or its just a one time thing, but he's like that most times. He looks down on you when you don't understand something and doesn't fully let you speak when you're trying to explain something to him.

Yuri might be one of the most condescending professors here. It's not that he doesn't know how to teach the material, but when you don't understand something he isn't very helpful and looks down on you as if you're less. I don't really recommend him at all, he should be teaching a much higher level course with people who deeply understand physics.
He's not the kindest over email. He will not play favorites. Everyone gets the same emails it's your responsibility to read them.
Dr. Popov is so iconic and anyone who's ever had him will forever remember his catchphrases! He is as good of a prof as you can get for 140, but still a really hard class to get good grades in.

I walked into this class having a very weak foundation of physics. I understood physics significantly better with him. His exams are a roll die. The first two exams and the fourth exam were fair. I felt his teaching wasn't as good for the third exam, and the final exam extra topics. But overall, great professor. Attendene is required to do well.
I LOVE YURIIIIII
Really fun and enthusiastic professor. Just make sure to attend lectures and put effort into homework, and you'll be fine. Exams were pretty easy and the curve is nice.

If you did not take AP Physics in high school, DO NOT take this class with Prof. Yuri. He speeds over material and spends 80% of time on practice problems and 20% on actual concepts. So lectures are effectively useless, but you must be there for participation. There is no partial credit on tests + I-clicker responses are graded so don't mess up!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking this class with Yuri Popov. I have never been in a physics class where physics was taught on a slideshow that went 100 mph. He flies through concepts, no blackboard to actually understand concepts. The exams are only multiple choice, so no partial credit. Most fail the exams. Not a good Prof. for physics.

I fought for my life in this class. Exams are brutal (half the class fails every one) and homework takes hours. 

Popov has a slight accent. I wouldn't call him rude but he is def not polite/nice (kind of scary...). He always started class with cool places he traveled to which was cool. However, the required $200 of class materials was not cool.

Knowledgeable, but can't teach. Homework is difficult, iClicker is graded off of accuracy, and your grade  heavily relies upon exams which are MCQ's so no partial credit. Can't answer student's questions. Heard from students that he would tell you you shouldn't major in engineering if you are struggling in his office hours but told us to reach out
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Popov always made the class enjoyable despite the difficulty of the material. He does a great job at explaining things and is always willing to answer questions. There are a lot of opportunities to get help in this class from Dr. Popov and the learning assistants. Despite this, the class is a lot of work so be prepared.

Amazing professor, easy to understand but asking questions during lecture results in answers that may not be understandable at the moment so prepare to go to office hours/ physics help room. The material itself is difficult which is why people may rate him lower but overall couldn't ask for a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Yuri is very funny with is dry sense of humor. I think he's a great guy and very flexible but I really don't think he is that GREAT of a lecturer. He will zip through concepts VERY quickly. If you want a good grade take GREAT notes and write down all equations as presented in lecture. GO TO CLASS. Good luck!

Yuri is great at teaching the material in a way that is easy to comprehend each topic. The class is lecture-heavy, and participation is mandatory due to I-Clicker use. The exams are only multiple-choice, which for me hurt my grade more than it should have, but the rubric is fairly relaxed and exams are based on questions from previous exams.

He's a very nice professor, and one of the funniest professors I've had. The only times his class wasn't engaging to me was when the fact that it was 9am really caught up to me. I really enjoy physics, so it was a lot of fun. He was also very happy to receive questions during lecture.
Very good lecturer. Explained material thoroughly while engaging students with demonstrations and iClicker questions.

Best lecturer I've had so far. Makes physics clear and interesting. Funny guy too. Most students seemed to enjoy being there because of how good he was at lecturing. Grade was super exam heavy, but Yuri prepares students well. Highly recommend his lecture, class is not too difficult for a physics class, not much hw/studying required.

Good professor, he can teach very well. But, there is a lot of content, and without an AP physics background, it can be hard to get a good grade without extensive effort. A lot of people in this course are taking other engineering courses/math so it can be hard to put in that much time. The four midterms and final are also most of the grade.

I REALLY wouldn't take this class with Yuri. He lacks respect to students and can be very arrogant. Too lazy to grade tests, so it's all multiple choice, hence no partial credit. A bad score can really hurt you. Class is not curved, lots of homework, trick questions during lecture that ARE graded. Save your time and get a different instructor...

The only complaint about his class is that the tests are 100% MCQs (many question are variations from old exams tho). Outside of that, Yuri is a fantastic lecturer and could be quite simply termed "a god among men." Would highly recommend over the phys 140 studio based section. Phys 140 with Yuri was in fact the best way to begin your day!

Not sure why some complain about him being rude. When people pack up early, he gets annoyed because he's still trying to teach and can't over the hundreds of backpacks zipping up. Lectures rarely ended late. He answered questions well in lecture, just sometimes had issues with hearing people in the back. Overall, one of my favorite professors.

Yuri is an amazing professor. He clearly knows what he is talking about and teaches very well. Physics 140 was very hard due to the format of the exams. There is 5 exams all 15 questions multiple choice, no partial credit. This makes it very hard to get a good grade in this class. Homeworks take a long long time. Practice, practice, practice!

Engaging (Go to office hours REGULARLY to figure out how great he is), Knowledgeable, and Fun. You could absolutely succeed in class by literally following what he says (which you should):
- Read Textbooks
- Clearly understand how to solve relevant problems
- Do practice exam
- 3 Problem Roulette Questions per day

Don't listen to the haters. GL.

Yuri likes to throw temper tantrums when his students pack up at the end of class. If you take his class (which I HIGHLY discourage) plan  extra time to get to your next class. His lectures are useless, and he asks iClicker questions designed for you to fail, which wouldn't be so bad if attendance wasn't graded on accuracy. STAY AWAY!!!

Dr. Popov is quite disrespectful towards students. He always judges students harshly when they answer wrong and is not very helpful or seems to be open to helping students. His lectures are very fast paced and hard to keep up with. He is very good at physics and knows his stuff, but I would rather learn from a different professor.
Lacks respect to students

Prof Popov is an incredible physics professor. The lecture is the same every day--powerpoint slides and iclicker questions, but he always tried to make lectures interesting with demos and jokes. The class can be fact paced and content heavy, but he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. I definitely recommend taking Physics 140 with him!

I liked Popov as a professor, but 140 def doesn't feel like an intro class for people who have never taken physics before. 4 midterms with 15 multiple-choice questions (no partial credit) didn't help me out. While the exams were hard, Popov kept me entertained throughout lectures and explained everything well. (140, the best way to begin your day!)

Professor Popov was a wonderful start to my day. He is funny, heavy on demonstrations, and explained everything with a true passion. The course itself is very time consuming and difficult, but he made learning physics fun by his sheer interest in the field.
He flies through everything so fast, it is difficult to catch up, especially in my case since this is my first ever Physics class.

He didn't always explain things the most clearly and could be mean to people who tried to participate in class. I don't really like how the class was taught, it just didn't work for me and sometimes it felt like he wanted most of us to fail.
defnitely an upbeat professor but the test pacing was really hard to keep up with.

AMAZING prof. Explains everything clearly. HW can be difficult/long. Make you purchase ~$100 worth of things. Every class follows the same format: Lecture w/ practice problems that he goes through, iclicker live questions (not worth that much, you can get a lot wrong and still be fine), and then demonstrations. He is available for office hours.
Great guy
Great professor who knows how to make class fun. Main drawback is that he runs through lecture incredibly quick. If you blink, you will be a unit behind.

Prof. Popov is a good lecturer who knows his stuff and explains it clearly. If you need to take PHYSICS 140, you should take it with him. I am not a big fan of the iClicker component of the course, but who is I guess. Challenging but doable exams make up most of the grade.

I don't love the way that this class is taught. There's a lot of homework and required effort for what is an intro class. Lectures are pretty good but have required iClicker questions that sometimes feel like gotcha questions are don't allow the students to be prepared for them. Overall, the class isn't terrible, but isn't great either.
I personally do not like the set up in class. Lectures, two different types of homework, participation grade...

he may be one of the best professors/teachers I have ever had in my educational career. His great lectures let me actually comprehend what I had been unable to understand in HS physics. A lot of the grade is participation (homework/in class clickers) and yes each exam question is very impactful, but study a bit and it's hard not to pass the class.

Spent more time trying to crack jokes instead of explaining the material properly. Also threw many trick questions into the i-clickers to make us lose points. U of M doesn't seem to have any good physics instructors.

Yuri was a super entertaining lecturer, who definitely knew what he was doing day in and day out. His lectures are super important, as there are I-clicker questions and that is the only class time to learn. His class was hard as it was my first physics class, but if you put the time in you can obtain a B, even after botching and exam or two

Amazing professor, is extremely prepared and knowledgeable in the subject. Attendance is not "mandatory", but  always go because the class moves extremely fast. Also almost half your grade is in-class participation and homework - those might make the difference in whether you pass the class or not.

Prof. Popov seems like he has taught this class a million times. Every lecture feels well-rehearsed, and he is ready for any questions/obstacles that come his way. Exams/HW were difficult but not impossible, it really came down to how much time and effort you put in. He really means it when he says "three practice q's a day make a difference"...

Professor Popov can change difficult introductory physics to something you enjoy learning daily! Enjoy the class :)

+ Detailed lecture slides w/ clear work. Gives great explanations along with slides w/ interactive clicker questions so you are engaged. Dedicated to help you during office hours.

- None. HW may be heavy, but it helps you learn.

Professor Popov is an excellent lecturer who uses class time by going over topics, sample problems, and using iclicker questions (for credit!). PHYS140 is challenging, as the homeworks take a long time and exams require both good intuition paired with strong physics knowledge. Read the textbook, go to class, and practice with extra problems.

Great professor, clearly cares about the subject a lot. Came across as a bit harsh at the beginning but loosened up quickly. Gives lots of fun demonstrations during lecture and answers all questions clearly. It's an intro physics class so there's going to be a lot of work. Some of the clickers are pretty hard, but you get 3/4 points just for trying
He loves physics and you can tell. I recommend going to office hours and utilizing all the resources available.
Teaches a tough class, but is a great prof. Knows the material in and out, gives good lectures, and gives great explanations for help in office hours.
Hard class but it's physics so what can you expect; he was very understanding and was willing to work with me to find a solution and help me pass. Also emails back fast and is great at office hours.
pretty good prof, teaches the class well enough

One of the worst professors I've ever had. This class is supposed to be an introduction into physics but Yuri does not give any insight on basic rules of physics. Rude and condescending to students and the exams are ridiculous for only 15 ?'s. He goes too fast in lecture and doesn't know how to teach. GSI's are far better at teaching than he is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He has a very interesting personality.  He makes his lectures fun and his demos are cool.  Makes physics very understandable.
Best Professor Ive ever had

Be prepared to work extra hard because some of the assignments were pretty challenging.

Grind problem roulette and past exams if you want to do well.

Reads off slides he recycles each year rather than writing things down. Too many clicker questions and online homework that he doesn't even touch. Makes a good subject a nightmare. Have a good routine because you will be stressed. He is also very rude and disrespectful to students despite thinking he is funny. Way too many tests that remove fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Avoid this class if you can. Exams were especially difficult because they were 15 Qs of MC and out of 15 points (all or nothing answers). It also used Mastering Physics which took hours to complete. I went to the help room frequently but rarely got adequate help. Professor is not approachable and did not accommodate for me after a temp disability.

Yuri is a super entertaining lecturer, but I will say without previous knowledge of most of the material it can be hard to get through. He sets the expectations for the class at the beginning of the semester. Make sure to do FLIP IT hw it can be easy to forget. Try to get daily practice in the best you can. The exams are really hard.

Popov is dedicated and respectful to students and a nonpartisan grader. Beware though, this is an intensely difficult course that half of the class will need to retake. Be prepared to spend as much time as you can in office hours. Do not take unless you are an engineering/physics student or you will fail.

Yuri is an absolutely hilarious and amazing professor. Although his class is quite difficult and the exams quite hard, he is a great teacher and you will learn a lot. Do not expect to get an easy A, you will work very hard for maybe a B or B+. He has great demonstrations and you will learn a lot. Would definitely take another one of his classes.
He is not a nice professor. Yes the subject is tough, but he makes it harder.

Prof. Popov is an excellent lecturer. He explains concepts clearly and tries to not make the class hell on earth. Physics 140 is a difficult class in general: the exams are tough because of no partial credit (all multiple choice), and it’s physics, but if you put in good effort you will do well. I’m convinced he is a physics genius.
Definitely not an easy class but lectures were interesting and exams are doable as long as you study for them

Popov is an experienced lecturer who knows physics very well and genuinely wants his students to enjoy the class. There is a lot to keep track of in this class, but if you are able to stay organized, much of the class grade is about completing assignments. His office hours are helpful, and he genuinely wants you to succeed.
Hes a super funny dude, but the class can be pretty fast-paced at times. Dont expect to get an A.

Quizzes every other week that are more like tests. Reads off everything from PowerPoint slides rather than writing everything out. Expected way to many problems(MP,FIP,I-clicker,Problem Roulette,etc.) rather than getting us to actually understand the material. Exam averages were super low. By far one of the most toughest professors to take physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A friendly and accessible professor. Classes were informational and concise. Office hours were helpful and nice to attend.

There is lecture 4 times a week and the homework is tedious. It often took me 3-4 hours just to do the homework. There are quizzes every 2 weeks which is annoying. The lectures are fine but he moves way too fast, and I didn't enjoy the mandatory iClicker questions, especially since they were 10% of our grade. Difficult course, would not recommend.

The class was pretty difficult, however, what is expected of you is pretty clear. All the homework is laid out in the syllabus. Yuri does help answer questions. My biggest complaint with him is sometimes he moves too fast and you don't have time to get all the information in the slides, but he uploads the slides later so you can always go back.

Dr. Popov is extremely on point when it comes to teaching. However, lecture slides are very difficult to follow(would like a blackboard). Recommend to avoid if unreliable internet connection. Also clicker heavy. Quizzes every two weeks are stressful. Homework is annoying online and tedious(would prefer paper). Pre-lectures were often redundant.

Yuri was very knowledgable about the subjects and made sure there was some type of office hours every day (whether with him or a TA). Make sure you read the textbook before lectures and you'll be good.

He's ran this class a million times and it shows. Streamlined, lots of resources, difficult, but you get the grade you deserve. He even bumped me half a percent because of covid. All around top lad. Physics 140 really was the best way to begin my day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Profesor Popov is great at instruction. He always has demos and makes jokes during lecture. The online version was very hard to pay attention to, and he could be un-empathetic at times. The class is difficult, but do-able if you pay attention and put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professors.

Yuri was a wonderful and entertaining professor. Although the content of the class was tough and you have to participate every day, Yuri still made such a boring subject bearable and fun to learn about. My only complaint is that the quizzes/exams are much more difficult than any of the material covered in lecture/HW.

Physics is a hard subject for newbie, and lectures are very important. With this professor, you must listen closely. Missed something - better read textbook, or youtube it from other lecturers. Mr Popov is very unwilling to read email, containing newbies questions. Anyway want to know the subject, Popov is right for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough guy. Can't understand what's his subject about

He's a great lecturer. My only complaint is that he doesn't seem too patient when answering questions. Also, he doesn't exactly seem happy when he answers questions either, it's almost rude or condescending.

He is a great professor; one of the best at UMich. Out of all of my classes, Professor Popov handled the COVID-19 situation the best. I understand the content that was taught after we moved online just as well as before. The lectures are mandatory, but if you find a couple of friends in the class, it's enjoyable.
G.O.A.T
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good morning good morning this is physics 140, the best way to begin you day Sometimes it's also the best way to end your day cuz you have midterm
This man in captivating and makes physics more enjoyable than it should be. Good guy who thinks he is the smartest in the world. He is very funny and wants students to do well.
Yuri Popov is an amazing lecturer and an all around good guy. He teaches is an interesting way, and whether you enjoy physics or not, you'll enjoy this class. Much Respect.

Best way to begin your day by far. I'd recommend sitting in the front of class so you can see the demos better. Yuri is a good teacher and passionate about physics. If you don't have a strong math background, this class will be much more difficult for you, but it is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Popov is one of the best professors at umich. If you pay attention in lecture and think about the clicker questions you will easily get an A. Popov cares about his students and makes 140 very interesting with all of the demos. The class is actually interesting and I rarely felt bored in class. Best way to begin your day!! Popov is a great professor
Yuri is a great professor, can come across as intimidating sometimes but truly cares about what he is teaching and how well his students understand the information. 10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach

While Physics 140 was the hardest class I've ever taken, Yuri is truly the best professor. It is obvious that he cares about the success of his students and loves what he does. I have definitely never struggled more in a class, but I still enjoyed going to lecture everyday. Really makes physics enjoyable, even though it is a tough weeder class.

Physics 140 is by no means an easy class unless you did some intense stuff in high school. Yuri is just a great guy, not necessarily the best prof that makes physics cake, but take him. You wont regret it. It really helps if you do the reading and take the prelectures seriously, but around 49% of your grade is based on hard work rather than genius.

Yuri made Physics lectures fun, with all of his demos and real life examples. He is very unique as a professor and you will never get the feeling that he doesn't care about what he is teaching or who he is teaching it to. Make sure you participate, the class is difficult, almost impossible if you do not show up.
I love Yuri - best lecturer ever.
Great teacher.

Pretty good lecturer, aside from mocking students who answer questions incorrectly in class, which discourages everyone except a select few from participating. He also makes snarky comments about other topics during lecture and can be extremely rude when spoken with or emailed individually. Would be a great prof if he had a little more class.

He does have an accent, but it's not hard to understand. His lectures are extremely helpful so I don't recommend skipping. He's very funny and does care about those students who put in the effort. Yuri is one of the must-have professors at the university. Physics 140 with him is definitely the best way to begin your day.

Dr. Popov was probably the best professor I've had. His accent pretty much never made it difficult to understand him. His lectures were never boring, and he was great at explaining a lot of the weirder concepts in Physics 140. Overall, would definitely recommend him as a professor if you have to take Physics 140.

Yuri is a great lecturer, although his Russian accent can be hard to understand at times. Physics 140 is just a hard class, but Yuri tries his best to make sure that anyone who wants to do well, can. He is really funny, and "it's the best way to begin my day".
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Physics 140 is for sure the best way to start your day, and if you don't know why I said that you are missing out. Go take Yuri's class. He's is funny and makes the class enjoyable and is always ready to help outside of class. Best Teacher of my freshman year.
Very good professor, but the course itself is quite a lot of work.
Really enjoyed Dr. Popov. Excellent lectures, didn't assign too much homework. Good sense of humor and explains concepts well. Thought the course was quite easy, in part due to his good lectures.

Professor Yuri Popov was absolutely amazing. Not only were his lectures the best way to start my day, but he ensured that everyone in the course understood the material, and if you didn't, he would take the time to ensure that you do (given you take advantage of office hours). He is a really chill, really smart, and really funny individual.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Popov is one of the worst professors I have had. He focuses his class on lame jokes, and mocks students when they ask questions. He is also not understanding, and not willing to help his students. During some lectures it seems he focuses more on political rants rather than teaching. Do not take Physics 140 with him, the worst way to begin your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Physics 140 with Yuri was the best way to begin my day. His lectures are a bit fast, but definitely enjoyable, and he is great explaining the hard concepts.
His class was the best way to begin my day. Lectures are a bit fast, but definitely fun to attend.

Best Physics professor ever, anywhere, hands down. You will ROFL the first class and stay cheery all semester. Flip It Physics quotes are by far the best part of the week, and he does clicker questions in the most amazing way. Take Popov, you will not regret 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Pretty good at giving lectures (though that may be the same for all the other physics professors). Tries to be funny. You won't be bored in class (that much). Easy A though other might not have thought so.

Loved loved loved Yuri. Had him as one of my profs for physics 160. He was funny and helpful. Also does a lot of the grading so check your work with him. You can get A's on vpython assignments if you just put in the time and get help. He's reasonable about grades and really wants you to learn. Also just a very likeable guy.

Prof. Popov is such a cute Russian guy. He explains concepts really clearly and has some pretty cool demos. I've emailed him with a question before and he gave a really detailed reply. Definitely the best way to begin your day! P.S. MasteringPhysics is useless; cram at least 150 problem roulette problems per exam if you want to get a good grade.

Yuri was a great Physics 140 lecturer. His demos were really cool, and really helped to conceptualize the concepts. Yuri also made an effort to squeeze in extra office hours when needed, and took time to explain concepts and problem in office hours.  Be aware though: Physics 140 is HARD, and you need to work hard to understand concepts early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's definitely the best way to begin your day
This rating is low because I just hate physics in general. Professor Popov, however was a great lecturer and I'm glad I took his class.

Most kids who take this are required to take it. The workload is what you would expect from a physics class, and you have to go to lecture if you want pass the tests. That being said, the Professor is one of the best and makes this class interesting and fun. There are tons of demonstrations that help clarify tough topics. Best way to begin my day.

This is my first physics course at um, the course has some material covered in calc3, though I haven't got to calc3 yet, but still you can do fine in this class, you get to learn a lot of coding which is really nice!
The best Physics 140 professor -- fast paced but really funny and enjoyable.
Good lecturer, energetic and funny. Several exams, in class participation, and weekly homework.

Yuri's a great professor and a funny guy. Some people don't like him because they feel like he's  yelling at them when they get something wrong but he just naturally talks loud and is very passionate about problems. If you need help on a problem he usually just does it for you instead of explaining it, but he's super funny and good at explaining

Popov was adorable! Really did make Physics the best way to begin your day. He does a great job of explaining the basic material in class. His lectures are not too in depth, so if you're good at physics, they are potentially useless outside of i-clicker points. He is also a ton of help in the Physics Help Room. I went every Monday.
Yuri was always very detailed in his explanations and always approached the class with an energetic and fun attitude. Would recommend for sure.
Yuri Popov is "the best way to start your day!"

His class is the best way to start your day. FUN. If you do the readings and take all of his advice seriously,which involves solving mastering physics problems yourself, taking practice exams under time pressure, etc, then you will do fine. I slipped up my first exam and it was the easiest one, then i took his advice and did great.
Physics 140 is a tough class.  That being said, if you want to do well on the exams, take Uher.  If you want a fun time in class, take Yuri,

Professor Popov is a good professor, his class is very difficult. Weekly homework assignments are time consuming, and tests were quite hard. That being said, Professor Popov gives clear lectures and examples in class that are very relevant. There were times that I would miss something in class, but slides are posted online after each lecture.

Yuri is a pretty good professor - uses lots of examples in lecture to explain concepts. I struggled with the class but it wasn't due to him. Exams are hard, but the practice exams he gives out are really helpful. He does have an accent, but I typically struggle with accents and I could understand him with ease. Iclickers make lectures mandatory.

Yuri is great. He could explain those confusing materials with deep insights. 406 is a course with a lot of math, but he could tell us the physics meaning behind the math. He is not the kind of teachers that just copy the derivations or equations from the textbook to the notes, and from notes to the blackboard.

Yuri is great. He is very  helpful, he cares about his students, and his homework is concise and helps you learn the material. It is not just tedious busywork. I would definitely take a class taught by hum again.
Fantastic professor with amazing knowledge about the subject and a hilarious sense of humor.
Yuri is the best teacher at U of M. Physics 140 is the best way to start your day

The best way to begin your day and the best professor I have had at U of M. He tells you what you need to know (the concepts) and how to apply them for harder questions that pop up on the exam. He is a chill, down to earth Russian who makes physics a ton of fun and easy to understand!!!

Professor Popov is awesome! Very glad I had him for Physics 140. This is a tough class, and the exam problems can be difficult, but Prof. Popov is entertaining in lecture, works hard to make sure students are understanding and is a generally a very nice person. Would highly recommend him for this class.
Yuri's 140 class is so interesting. If you study hard you can easily get at least A-

Yuri is a really cool guy, but not quite the best at teaching an upper level physics class. He  can confuse or miss crucial information that finds its way to the test. Good feedback though. His use of Microsoft Word, iClickers, and grad level questions for a 400 level physics gives pause.
Yuri does a great job making concepts interesting to learn and easy to understand. He's clearly passionate about what he does.
Good lecturer. Cool experiments. Great class participation model.
Great physics professor.

Definitely the best way to begin your day. His lectures were often engaging and had a lot of demonstrations. if you make sure to read the textbook and try not to google too many mastering physics answers, you should do well.
Great lecturer! REALLY cares if students are learning and is more than willing to help outside of lectures. He allowed me to meet him during spring break and tutored me one on one for a week!
Lectures were entertaining and engaging. Do the readings before lecture and you will enjoy it much more! Physics 140 was truly a great way to begin my day.

Yuri is very passionate about teaching this Physics class.  Attendance is expected and iClickers are used for points each day (taking attendance, too).  He always answers questions in class and is well liked by the students.  Exams are generally pretty challenging, and the grading is straight scale.  I definitely recommend Professor Popov for 140.

Tons of HW but very helpful, not only towards learning but also towards your grade. Pretty fast paced so make sure to pay attention all the time and take lots of notes. Exams are quite hard but if you study enough you'll be fine. Will have office hours and help if you ask. GO TO CLASS EVERY TIME! Good luck if you're taking this class!

if you dont have a solid physics background from high school, dont take yuri's class.  lectures are like he assumes students already have an understanding and he skims over some major topics. exams are extremely difficult

Yuri is a very clear professor. Office hours should be attended if you want to excel, but like most physics courses at UofM, you get out what you put in. You won't have to deal with any vPython nonsense, though.
He is super awesome and funny. I really enjoyed his lectures.
His accent is cool and not difficult to understand.

Yuri was amazing. NO interest in physics before taking this course but his class was very interesting. He's energetic, he's enthusiastic, he's absolutely amazing. Highly recommend Yuri if you have to take 140 at michigan

Physics 140, the best way to start your day. Not really, but Popov made this class entertaining and clear. He was certainly born in the old Soviet Union, so he has an accent, but he is completely understandable, even for a guy whose first language isn't English, like me. Many people complain about the difficulty of the course, but it n't that bad.

This is definitely the best way to begin your day!! Physics is not an easy subject, but he makes it easy!! Definitely take his class, instead of other section which requires you to work with python programming.

Physics 140 isn't necessarily the best way to start your day, but Yuri makes it entertaining. His examples are useful. iClickers and Mastering Physics questions are annoying, but it's part of the class. Exams are completely fair (though not necessarily easy). He was willing to explain anything asked. Very knowledgeable and passionate about physics.
Good help and writes out problems online but difficult class
I liked popov. good professor. exams and mastering physics were tough as nails but he did a good job teaching the class.

Not sure why he's getting such great remarks. He absolutely flies through material and assumes everyone understands each step he's taking even when it's incredibly complicated. That coupled with he's accent make this class much harder than necessary. Yuri is a nice guy and is very approachable, though, but I wouldn't say he teaches well.
Yuri is the best. He makes mechanics fun. His demos are very cool. It was truly the best way to begin my day.
Good professor. Fairly clear in his lectures and puts on some pretty cool demonstrations. Exams can be a little tricky.
Yuri is the bomb. Explained all of the topics very thoroughly and always had awesome demos. I really enjoyed having him as a professor.
Yuri is awesome. His demonstrations are extremely clear. He makes physics fun. There could't have been a better way to start my day!

Yuri is an amazing professor. If you take Physics 140, make sure you take his class. It is definitely the best way to start your day. He throughly explains things and drills topics into your brain. Excellent class. Excellent man.
Great teacher for a tough class. Mastering physics really sucks, but go to class. his examples are helpful and his explanations are clear.
He's just really passionate. So willing to give you resources to help you succeed. It really is "the best way to start your day"
This is Physics 140! The best way to begin your day!

Amazing professor. His class can be challenging but he makes sure everyone keeps up with the material. He expects effort but we also had the highest exam scores compared to other sections. Highly recommend taking his class

Dr. Popov is amazing, he is very enthusiastic about physics and teaching. While he does have an accent, after a day or two it is not at all hard to understand. His sections of physics have harder iClickers than the others but they also have high exam scores than the others. I highly recommend taking his class.
Solid prof with a very interesting and nasal-y accent. Likes to repeat things nonstop, but overall good at teaching
He was great.  Clear explanation of topics.  He really likes to teach unlike most professors.  Great guy if your taking Physics try and get in his class

Good professor. Slight accent that took about half of the first lecture to get used to (he kinda sounds like Gru from Despicable me). His pre-exam reviews were generally not helpful (Go to Uher's, he just gives out answers). Other than that, really good professor, would recommend over Uher. Had higher averages despite not giving answers to exams.
Yuri is a great professor!
Best way to begin your day!

Yuri is a great teacher.  After you get over the accent, you will enjoy his class and find that he is helpful and always asks if there are questions.  Yuri even took myself and some other students to lunch for doing well in his class. Yuri is smart, funny, and generally a good guy, I would recommend!
He's a pretty good professor. Humorous and very clear on everything.

Even though he has a Russian accent, I got over it within a few days. After that, he was a very good professor. Clear on explanations and prepares you for the exams. Seemed kind of rushed at times, but its the universities fault, not his. Throws a joke in there once in a while. Reading and doing problems helps, but is not mandatory. Overall- 8/10
He is a really good teacher. He explains everything in debt. He does have an accent but understanding him is not an issue.
fantastic, amazing professor
fantastic, entertaining professor

A great teacher. He explains the material well and is willing to go out of his way to help you. He uses demonstrations and humor to keep the class interesting. His in-class exam reviews were usually not very helpful though.

He's a great teacher who explains the material clearly and concisely. He does have an accent, but I didn't have a hard time understanding him.  The tests are fine as long as you actually attempt to understand the homework and do the practice problems/tests that are provided. Great class!

Great professor whose used a perfect combination of demonstrations, conceptual questions, and practice problems in lecture. At times his lectures took unclear tangents, but he was definitely entertaining enough to keep the entire class engaged for the full 50 minutes. "Welcome to Physics 140, the best way to begin your day." Yuri's awesome.

A good professor for the material. I had no problem understanding through his accent. Material is not too challenging, though you should still put some work in. As long as you do you Mastering Physics (without cheating!), attend lectures, and (at least) scan the book, then you will be fine.

Good professor. Explained problems fully and takes time to teach students outside of class. Although he has an accent, I had no trouble understanding him. Mandatory attendance because of iclicker questions but they are easy marks. Tests were more difficult than I expected but easy hwk marks let me get an A still.
He's a great professor for the class, he covers the main topics in lecture but you must use the book if you want to get a good grade.
Truly an excellent teacher.  Totally makes you view physics from a more mature and thorough perspective.  The class was hard, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.
Good professor. He is passionate and helpful. It's very easy to follow him in the class. I'm glad I had "the best way to begin my day" last term.

Great Professor! He does a very good job of conveying the material, and will take time out of lecture to answer students questions and make sure they completely understand the material. Exams were difficult but also very relevant to what was taught in class. Overall great professor.

I really enjoyed Physics 140 with Dr. Popov. The material can be challenging, but I was always able to understand his lessons and he really cares about his students. I always felt well prepared for exams. This class really is the best way to start your day.

Professor Popov is a really great teacher! He is energetic and engaging about most topics and is very willing to work with students outside of class. After going to more office hours and asking him more direct questions after class, I began to understand the physics much much better.

Great professor who knows his mechanics well. Funny, I look at all of the newer reviews and he has gotten mostly positives. Maybe he changed something in his teaching; I know iClickers were new and those REALLY helped: "mandatory" attendance plus real-time feedback. Truly the "best way to start your day"

In my opinion, he is great teacher. I enjoyed his class a lot. I liked how he explains the material and how he uses experiments to explain the suject. Mastering physics is also pretty helpfull. I didn`t have any problem with his accent(as some of here says). And it is really the best way to begin your day.

once you get over his accent it is extremely easy to follow along with lectures. I sat in on other physics lectures this term and by far thought Yuri did a much better job in teaching. still physics is physics so many people will struggle with material. if you read the assigned topics before lecture however it makes much more sense.

Really cares that the students understand what he is lecturing on. The i-clicker questions really help with comprehension. Demonstrations are also pretty cool. "Physics 140, the best way to begin your day"

After you get used to his accent, he's easy to understand. His jokes and quirks are pretty amusing. Make sure to go to class as there are daily iClicker scores, and I'd recommend reading the book even though he posts his slides. He's great at explaining the material. Exams are hard but doable.

Guy knows his material, but isn't that great at conveying it to the students. His accent is difficult to understand at first, but you get used to it. It's not the end of the world if you get him, but he probably shouldn't be your first pick, either.

He is difficult to understand, but seems to know what he is talking about. Would be a much better lecturer if you could understand his heavy accent. To stay focused in lecture try to count the number of times he says right.
30% of grade is on stuff you can get a 100% on. His lectures don't help at all but you have to go to get clicker scores. Exams are very hard.
Adequate.  His accent wasn't a big deal but he could not relate the material at all to anything besides physics. Would not recommend without a foundation of physics understanding.
He explains things really well,  his English is excellent despite his accent. Definitely hit up his office hours if you can.
Pretty well Knows his stuff...Maybe his accent got better but I understood him. Better than going to a lecture with a professor who don't really can't answer your questions.
I like him. He pretty knows his stuff well. Not sure if his accent was worse...but I understood him fine.
GSI for physics 160--pretty useless and i couldnt understand him. meh.
ok professor
No Comments
