Super cool teacher and course! A lot of reading, but very worth it because I love medieval history. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about her subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Medieval Animals: Assignments instructions are unclear (yet long) and grading rubric is a guessing game. Very forgetful with putting in grades, checking attendance (mandatory), and posting materials on time. Slides don't mirror lecture (and hard to see during class), and no recordings. Not as "open beginners" like course book said.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Excellent class (Medieval Images in Between). She's a great teacher and is totally respectful of her students. I really enjoyed the specificity and randomness of the class, and how she integrated analysis of the UMICH campus into the major project.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures: I found her very funny and engaging. She took large group participation seriously, but it was worth it. I thought she was very clear and I think I learned more than I expected from a partial term class.

I took SLAVIC290: Films from Kosovo with Professor Aleksic, and she tackles the topic in a very easy to digest manner. She's passionate--and knows--what she's talking about, and she goes beyond just the technical aspect of film analysis. The coursework was very easy to manage as well, and there's a lot to learn in taking this course. 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had her for a COMPLIT class. Tatjana's class was occasionally puzzling, but interesting for the most part. She is VERY laid back during discussions (you don't have to participate if you don't want to). However, your participation grade at the end will take a hit so try to speak up on occasion. Overall, she was a very funny and easy professor.
Tatjana is extremely knowledgeable and very passionate. Loved taking her class!

Super great and understanding professor. The class itself wasnt difficult and the exams were open-book/online. Awesome if youre interested in the refugee crisis and global immigration, and a pretty easy A. I really enjoyed the class and Professor Aleksic and would totally recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She really knows her subject and class is very interesting. If you do the readings and participate in class you'll get an A. Fantastic teacher, hope to take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Get ready to read. I think we read 5 books and every class she gave us excerpts (around 50 pages each) to read and discuss in class. Final paper of 10 pages minimum. The class is awesome I learnt a lot and I love prof. Aleksic. She know a lot and she loves to make you think about everything twice and question everything. Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tatjana was my favorite professor freshman year.  Very sarcastically funny, but she wasn't mean.  She corrects your papers hard, but if you listen to what she says, you'll come away with an A, even if your first papers stink.  Be ready to back up your arguments.  She is also just an interesting person, loved talking to her.

You either love her or hate her. I love Tatjana, it was a great class. She is so inspirational. I was so mesmerized by how knowledgeable she is. She is very passionate and in the essays she expects you to write what she said in class. It is very nice to talk to her outside of class and in her office hours. Great professor, but much better person.

Tatjana is a great person, and her specialty is Serbian vampire legends. It seems sometimes though that this class is more about her personal history than vampires. After the midterm we didn't really learn anything new, so the final was the exact same. Her GSI Matt was great, they were both willing to listen to our voiced concerns.

Professor Aleksic is a very caring and passionate professor. She wants her students to do well and is very willing to help in any way possible. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. This is the best way to finish with an A in this class. She seems tough, but if you're willing to put in the work, you'll do just fine.
very enthusiastic about the material and really likes people who talk and participate a lot in class; but she has little tolerance for cell phones in class, so watch out for that.

If you're interested in art and cultural movements of the 20th century, you'll like this class. Our discussions were divided in half between what we read outside of class and student presentations about things like pop art, postmodernism, the music of John Cage and Phillip Glass, etc. I found the class very stimulating, just be careful with essays.

From the syllabus, this class seems a easy and seemingly interesting class. However, despite there being a handful of assignments, they are graded as harshly as the genocide we read about in class. If you take this class, GO TO OFFICE HOURS before essays are due, she'll basically tell you what to write. Expect to work hard in this class.

Asserts all of her own opinions as if they're fact.  Very arrogant, pretentious, and comes in complaining about something different each day.  Absolutely hated going to class; she singled students out in front of the class frequently.  Ruined literature for me.
She expects too much from freshmen and expects life altering conclusions from papers. Not a great teacher.

Not the easiest class but it was manageable. The beginning was rough because she's very specific about how she wants the papers written. She doesn't leave much room for interpretation so don't be too ambitious when you write your papers. Listen to what she says in class, incorporate that into your paper and GO TO OFFICE HOURS
Prof. Aleksic is very knowledgeable and helpful. She can be difficult because she wants to see her papers done a certain way, but other than that it was a great, thought-provoking class.

class was alright. don't be fooled NOT an easy alternative to eng 125. if you really enjoy abstract literature and enjoy deep analysis you'll enjoy, she expects a thorough analysis in papers. unless truly interested in learning about diff kinds of literature/literature of the balkans i don't recommend slavic 151 yugoslav post yugoslav short fic

Her freshmen seminar about myth and history in the Balkans was wonderful! She truly tries to inspire her students and improve their writing skills as well. It is nice that she takes the time to comment on graded papers on ways to improve for next time.

lectures aren't very good. never finishes the slides, kinda all over the place and usually youre better off just reading the slides posted instead of attending lecture. exams are ~1hr, not very hard. a lot of extra credit is available tho. homework is graded either 0, 1, or 2 pts but somehow i get decimals like 1.8 (violating syllabus)

not a good prof at all, SUPER unorganized. didn't release practice exam answers because he "ran out of time"... wdym you "ran out of time"? how? at that point just say you don't release answers, dont give a lame excuse. lectures are sometimes helpful, but mainly all over the place. doesn't rly use canvas, uses own website which is quite buggy

Professor Sun really cares about his students and replies to emails very quickly. However, the homework load is way too heavy, and the lectures are extremely hard to follow. Sometimes the material taught in class is fairly simple, but the homework is especially difficult.

Yuekai is one of the best professors I've had at UMich. His lectures focus heavily on mathematical proofs and machine learning theories, but he explains everything well. The midterm was fair, with questions very similar to the problem sets. If you thoroughly reviewed the assigned problems, you would  be fine with the midterm. Good luck!!

Yuekai is one of the best profs I've had for statistics courses. The midterm is closely aligned with homework questions, so thoroughly understanding the assignments will prepare you well. While the material is challenging and the homeworks and project are time-intensive, you'll learn a lot if you stay focused and put in the effort.

Quality of lectures was all over the place. Understanding linear regression, MLEs, and lagrangian multipliers beforehand would be beneficial, professor did not really explain these well. HW is very time intensive, but doable with OH. Exam was heavily based on HW, and this was explicitly clear. Project was doable, but unclear grading criteria. 6/10
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Yuekai is a nice guy but his lectures were not very clear and any time a question was asked the answers were very vague. Homework is difficult and time consuming, and the median exam grade was about a 65. Office hours are basically crucial if you want to know what's going on on the homework, and having STATS 413 already was super helpful.

The class was tricky because the content in lecture was semantic definitions while the homework covered mathematical definitions and proofs so you basically had to go to office hours every week but he was very lenient with extensions and pretty generous with partial credit so it worked out. Definitely prepare to spend a lot of time outside of class
He talks well and understand student.
The grading criteria is vague. It's not that hard to get an A in this class though.

No matter which course it is and no matter what he tells you at the beginning of the course, stay away. All grading criteria are vague and he cannot be reasoned with. What is more interesting is that he interprets feedback from students as "frustrated messages" and publicly claimed so in the Slack channel.
Lectures were heavy, homework was heavy. If you are aces in linear algebra and proofs, you will love him. Otherwise, his lecture was a nightmare.

If you have to take this guy, be prepared to go office hours. Few people can do his problem sets on their own, but he will show you the homework step by step. Course is extremely difficult and I would say it's an 600-level course instead of 400-level, but if you spend time on the material, you will definitely learn a lot.
A theory guy. Should be prepared to learn some statistical theory rather than application. If you love statistical theory you will love him, otherwise avoid his section.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sun does not convey the knowledge in a clear way. And he is so much interested in math proof which make the consistency of the class decline. Also, for half of the homework, the only way for average students to finish it well is going to his OH(usually for difficult homework, there are about 30 students waiting) cause it's too difficult.

I dont think Ive worked harder in a class, but I came away a better and more confident statistician. Prof Sun is nice and accessible, but you definitely have to go to OH and be proactive in reaching out (to the prof or to smarter classmates) to do well. Dont take his class if you want an easy A, but its inspirational if youre ready to work.
Its been a displeasure being his student this semester. I learned nothing. Please dont let his inadequacies as an instructor dissuade you from further study of this elegant subject.

Professor is nice but this class is horrible. He loves machine learning and wants to cover a lot of machine learning materials in his section. During lectures, He speaks too fast to be understood. If you want to really learn something, don't take his class. He will always play some maths and discourage you from learning statistics.

He is very smart for sure, very responsible. 413 is a hard class, I won't argue that, and I struggled. He tried to introduce a lot of new concepts which I think is great, but his homework and exams don't connect like the other classes do. Still, you would do great if you understand the concepts. He is always willing to help. Great person and prof.
Prof. Sun doesn't explain things clearly. Most of his lectures introduce new concepts which are deep. But he doesn't do well on the introduction. Got a good grade but won't take his class again.

Worst professor I've taken at umich. Always trick us with intensive math and proof. MATH 525 (Probability Theory), MATH 451 (Advanced Calculus I), MATH 217 (Linear Algebra), STATS 426 (Theoretical Statistics), and STATS 306 (Statistical Computing) are recommended before taking STATS 413 with Yuekai Sun.

When I say "solid professor", this only applies for students who already excel in rigorous proofs, which I am. For the other type of students, it can be frustrating. Prereqs (STATS 412) won't be enough; be ready to learn on your own. Difficult homework/exam. Grading scheme makes no sense (80% exam total). More exposure to applications will benefit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I cannot say it's Yuekai's fault to be too smart, but it is his fault to assume all his students are as smart as him. A terrible organized class that most topics are uncorrelated with regression. All his homework and exam are extremely difficult for undergraduate students. Bad curve. Recommend taking other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He knows his section is more difficult than any undergraduate level statistics class but he claims that STATS 413 is SUPPOSED to be hard. Consider taking this course with other professors.
Professor is nice but the class is horrible. Consider taking this course with other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Escape his section at all cost unless you have got a Nobel Prize in mathematics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A good professor but an extremely difficult class. He made me PTSD in data science. Won't take any courses with him in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I feel Professor Sun is a bit out of touch with his students. Nearly every assignment he gave was so difficult that it could not be done without GSI help. He also focuses the course more on rigorous math rather than applying stats to real-world applications (what I thought the course was about). Do not take his class unless you want a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is okay, but do not recommend it at all unless you want to be a mathematician or statistician in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His class is difficult for the students not good at math. I recommend stats 426 should be taken as an enforced prerequisite. It's necessary to go to his OH (at least GSI OH) to do problem sets and prepare exams. If you want to get an easy A and are not confident about your math skills, take someone else. But will learn something real if study hard.

Literally the worst professor Ive ever had. I learned nothing the entire semester. The homework is unbelievably hard, and almost impossible to do without office hours. Office hours are frequently canceled at the last minute before important deadlines. In the past, STATS 413 has had a very light workload with no exams, now its the opposite.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Never really explains the base level of why he is talking about something, while always saying "here is a high level view of what I am talking about." In short, don't take this class with this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yuekai is one of the smartest, if not the smartest professor I have ever had. However, he assumes that his students are aces in linear algebra, and you often end up doing more linear than stats in this class. Unless you really like stats or want to be wow'd by someone's knowledge, avoid this course for your own sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are a performance art beyond my appreciation. Smart guy, but assumes you got an A in all the prerequisite courses.

He assumes a ridiculous amount of prior knowledge. If you dont do all of the reading carefully and take notes for hours before lecture, you will be completely lost during lecture. His lecture notes are helpful, but lecture is confusing and not great.

Yuekai is crazy smart. The class is definitely hard, but motivating. His lecture notes are clear and he knows what he's talking about. Go to office hours for homework if you are confused, as the material is going to be on the test. Be ready to learn and work from the get-go.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is difficult but professor is pretty nice, except I think he cut me off once at a stop sign in Kerrytown.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: To really pass this class and get a good grade, you just need to find a smart smart smart classmate who is willing to teach you before the exam. He curve nice in the final but just need to study hard. In conclusion, if you don't understand the class, that's totally normal. You just need a smart friend who should be a math major.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a definitely smart guy so it is very hard for him to express his idea accessible to lots of students. Not a very well-organized class and lecture notes are not helpful. He presented a bunch of weird mathematical terms, which is quite difficult to undergraduate level students.

He's very smart and friendly, also offering a lot of useful resources, but the class is taught at a very high level that can be confusing and difficult for a lot of people. I wouldn't say this is a fault on Sun's part, but rather a lack of experience with university stats undergrads. You'll need to study the material a lot, but he is there to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Exams are horribly complicated, but Uribe was always a nice guy who did his best to help you understand the material being taught and show you the beauty of mathematics. He could be a bit confusing at times, but overall, a good man. Would suggest going to multiple Math 215 lectures per day for the best results in this class.

Had Uribe for math 215.  Went to his lectures in the beginning and they seemed fine, helpful.  Went to Weis instead and never went back.  He cares about his students but his lecturing can get pretty confusing and I found it hard to learn from.  Grading scale is usually much nicer than on canvas. Get a tutor!! Recommend Kahn academy.

I took Uribe for Math 215 last semester as my first semester here. I'm sure if you took prior math classes at michigan that it wouldn't be as difficult as it was for me. This class tested my love for math. Homework is much harder than the textbook. Midterms even harder. Final MUCH worse. READ THE TEXTBOOK! Go to lecture

He is literally my favorite professor in Michigan! I didn't have any background with manifold/topology before taking this class, and I probably wouldn't survive it if he is not teaching it. He makes the class really organized. He cares about his students and if you want to learn, he would like to help as mush as he can.

Probably wouldn't be surviving this class if it was any other professor, Professor Uribe cares about the way the material is presented, paces the class well, and is very good at imparting an intuition of what's happening.

I'm almost certain he's writing the proofs on the fly -- he does make some small mistakes, but he wouldn't be doing that if he was dictating the proofs from the book. The class is well-structured, and he rearranges the way the book presents the material for it to be more intuitive. Please read the textbook before going to class, it genuinely helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Uribe is FANTASTIC. He covers material well and encourages the development of mathematical intuition. He chooses examples that are mathematically interesting and balances theory and applications. He also does an excellent job of explaining why something works when the proof doesn't necessarily show why. Highly recommend.

Professor Uribe is a wonderful professor. I took 285 with his this past winter, and I truly learned a lot. He is a very warm and friendly person with a nice sense of humor. It is very obvious that he cares about his students, and he often takes pauses during lectures to ask if students are understanding the lecture and to clarify any confusion.
Really nice guy but not a great teacher. Goes on many tangents and really isn't very clear. Ended up getting a tutor and watching khan academy.
Nice guy, but not a great professor. Go to a different lecture or use Khan Academy/Youtube
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Uribe is the most adorable grandpa from whom you could ever hope to learn calculus. He teaches the material in an intuitive way and clearly cares a lot about his students. Go to lecture, pay attention, and the material should make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: He rushes through material a lot and does not realize that he skips important things. Gets distracted and starts a new topic on the side before coming back to the topic at hand. Homework and exams are very difficult
Fun, great class!

He is a very harsh grader! Makes a lot of mistakes in lecture and exams are either too easy or too difficult. My first and second midterms are above the average a lot and I got an average at final. My homeworks are good but I got a B!!
Very helpful for such a difficult class
Homework was very difficult but exams were fair assessments of what we learned. Does his best to teach but doesn't realize how hard the material really is.

His lectures are very unhelpful because he goes at a very fast pace and fails to explain the material properly. He also doesn't have very engaging lectures as you'll find half the class asleep at any given time. He definitely means well, but I learned all the material on my own using the textbook.
very unclear lectures. he's really sweet and wants to help his students but he's to smart to see why we can't understand.
very unclear. contradicts himself. doesn't want to help his students, even in office hours.
Great teacher. Very helpful in office hours.

Professor Uribe is an excellant lecturers whose primary goal is always the success of the students. Although he goes fairly quickly in lecture, he is excellent in office hours and makes seemingly difficult concepts very easy. If you complete the homework diligently and attend section religiously an A will be within your grasp. Recommended.
He is a good lecturer and gives great office hours.

He goes over material in class pretty fast, but once you take a look over the notes, or start the homework, things become pretty clear. He is better in his office hours. Nice guy though; if you are really struggling, he will try to help you out.

Prof. Uribe is a busy man, thus his lecture reflects this.  He rushes through concepts most of the time (esp. important material that he doesn't feel like deriving).  Do not get me wrong, he is great in office hours, but as a professor, he needs to re-evaluate his abilites to teach others.
Genuinely Him. Only about 1 month into class and he's already known as professor mo (motion).

I absolutely love Udo as a person. I took this class with him and did well. Although the assignments and assessments were very difficult for an intro earth class, he supplied so much extra credit opportunities and the option to not take the final if you were happy with your grade that it worked out fine for me. He is so much fun to listen!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expected students to have a much better understanding of course material than we actually did. Only gave very brief and confusing explanations, then expected us to immediately complete complex assignments. Homework had vague instructions. Even GSI had difficulty with it. Course expectations were unclear. Study guide for the midterm was inaccurate.

Professor Becker is nice, but cannot teach. He seems to forget this is an intro level course with his lectures and even after asking questions I cannot follow his explanations at all. There are no reading materials provided to give context to the material, and half his quiz questions have nothing to do with the lectures. He is also bad with email.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Here's the thing about professor Becker, I'm not quite sure what he was teaching but I sure loved to listen. He  went through "earth basics" very fast and spent a lot of time on topics above an intro earth classes understanding. He's also unorganized which was annoying. Fun dude to listen to, not the best instructor.

Udo Becker is really sweet, but he talks slow and it is difficult to understand. Most of what he puts on tests and quizzes is what he explains verbally and you can't find it on the slides. I recommend downloading the slides and adding notes, it also helped to watch his lecture recordings in 1.5x speed. He is an easy grader and forgiving

Becker seems like a decent enough guy but I would not take this class again. I sent him 4 or 5 emails throughout the term to clarify the grading of the class because it is so vague and he didn't respond to any of them. There's also way too much material that is difficult for a non-science student like myself. Do not take.

Dr. Becker is a nice guy who is clearly interested in what he teaches, but his lectures are super monotonous and hard to pay attention to. Most the time, no matter how hard you try, you won't be able to follow what he's trying to explain. On the quizzes and tests, there's material that wasn't even talked about in class. Lots of extra credit though

This professor has no idea what he is talking about. Constantly asking questions to the class when he is supposed to talk about that to students. Strong accent and workload skyrockets towards the final season. Strongly not recommended
Disorganized and frustrating. Goes off on randoms tangents a lot and you don't know if they're relevant. Luckily the class wasn't too hard but he is not my favorite.

Udo was sometimes unclear in lecture, but this year he was good about stopping and addressing the class's concerns if they seemed confused. He also cut some topics in order to go more in depth. The homeworks are difficult, but he puts clues in the lectures and the slides. They really make you think, which helps you to learn the material. Hard exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you don't go to class you won't pass. For his mini-course he offered 6% extra credit by showing up, which I seriously needed. Although it's a mini-course it is not a blow off at all. If you haven't taken chem and don't like earth avoid this class at all costs. As well as him. He is dry, and really didn't offer any extensive explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The homework assignments aren't that bad, and he takes a lot of homework questions and copies them exactly on the exams.  He also gives you a ridiculous amount of extra credit, while also curving the class really nicely.  Also, he was a really quirky and interesting guy.  I actually really enjoyed this class, and it was because of the professor.
Difficult class that requires a lot of work. Professor rambles on in lecture and bases a lot of his lecture off chemistry which he requires you to have a solid understanding of.

very difficult class. if you're looking for a blowoff class this is NOT the class for you. the lectures are extremely hard to pay attention to unless you seriously love earth. otherwise udo is a nice person but not the greatest prof
If you don't take notes in class you will not pass. Weekly quizzes, which are actually kind of hard. Lots of information to cover in just two tests. Teacher isn't very helpful.
Udo is great

At sometime during this semester I actually felt I should've taken it Passfail because things we learned aren't so easy as I never do the reading. Fortunately there are lots of extra credit chances that will make up for your previous quizzes. Grades are only quizzes and 2 exams, so don't really need to show up. Plus Prof. Becker is a nice person.

Great minicourse! just memorize the slides and you will get an A. He offers thousands of extra credit and most of the questions included in the online quizzes are part of the final exam. You must do well.

He offers so much extra credit so the students in his class can be successful. I even missed a homework assignment and he reopened it so I could take it. He's easy to approach, helpful, and wants his students to understand what he is passionate about. Take this not only for the A, but for some interesting information!
Easy A two credit course. Excellent professor. Reminded me of high school earth science class.
udo becker is the worst professor i've ever had.
I was actually interested in this class, and am majoring in Environmental science, which helped. Exam was worth 70%, and I got over 100% in the class. Interesting and easy 1 credit class.

lots of readings for a one credit mini course.  Udo is certainly knowledgeable but he severely overestimates the chemistry and physics skills of his students. the final exam was very challenging and he conveniently left down the day before it was given.  avoid if possible.

The course was technical when it came to chemistry and physics, and way more work than the one credit I am receiving for it.  Also, Professor Becker is not good at explaining the concepts when it comes to answering questions in office hours, and many of the questions asked on the weekly quizzes are not included in the lecture material.
Udo is awesome!!!!!! The class is fun!!!!!!

Take this class pass/fail, if you do otherwise you will be extremely mad at yourself.  Quite frankly I wouldn't take this class at all because it was so much work for only one credit and quite honestly the topic is brutal.  Takes it far too seriously for so little.

This class is more difficult than I would have expected, material wise.  There are 2 quizzes, but most of your grade comes down to the final.  Only take if you're legitimately interested in the topic.

WAYYYY too hard for a 1 credit course. this guy's nuts. very specific, awful organization on ctools and lecture/resources titles. material should be for a 3-4 Credit class, not an intro Geosci course. IF you for some crazy reason decide to take this course for the love of God take it pass/fail.

This mincourse ended up being a lot more difficult than I thought. He gives 2 pop quizzes (one is extra credit) but they are hard and he grades them hard. He knows what he's talking about, but doesn't always explain it clearly.

He writes really poor exams and requires way too much reading for a 1-credit course. If you don't do the reading, you will miss a lot of the points. The study guide was helpful but most of the questions were easy to misinterpret and the granularity of the exam was almost to the point of being inane. Every class was more like a PSA than a class.
Udo Becker is the best thing happened to University of Michigan Geology Department in last so many years.

Udo gives boring lectures and the majority of the material is over everyone's head. However, the exams and final project are fairly easy, as well as the laboratory, which will give you a high grade. Udo himself is a good, funny, oddly dressed person. You must go to him to get help, he will just cruise along whether the students understand or not.

Awesome.  One of the coolest and funniest professors you'll have here.  He tought 231 with Rod Ewing, both were great as was the class - will never forget the fieldtrip to Bancroft, Ontario via the University minivan Convoy.

He's funny and his clothes are always the talk of the class.  He's very smart and concerned for his student's welfare. The lab for this class is annoying but not hard.  He will make you participate in class.
Great 1 credit mini-course.  He was sort of boring during lecture, but the material was presented very well.  Just try to stay awake, and make sure you take the extra credit quizzes.

Dr. Jakob is very knowledgeable about biochemistry at a deep level, which shows in her lectures. The content can be challenging, so staying on top of the material is really important to succeed in the class. Going to office hours is especially helpful; she does a great job of explaining concepts more clearly and answering questions.

Dr. Jakob is harsh but efficient in her teaching; she won't coddle you, but with a lecture class of 250 students, I don't think anyone would expect her to. She is efficient in office hours and willing to meet outside of the scheduled times. I loved how she worked with you to find an answer rather than simply giving it to you.

Exams align closely with concepts Dr. Jacobs emphasizes in lecture. This class is application of orgo and intro bio. Office hours helps to work through problem solving similar to those on exams. Problem roulette is also very helpful for additional practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Jakob was confusing at times, and I felt she could've organized content better. However, when I rewatched her lectures, they made more sense. Her exams were difficult and had nipicky questions, but were doable. She is also very engaging, which makes learning easier.

Dr. Jakob is quite engaging in a way that is difficult for a topic as information-heavy as biochem, and explains material well; however, she moves quite fast and packs a lot of information on each slide. Her exams are also pretty hard and nitpicky. Lecture recordings are your friend.

I enjoyed Dr. Jakob's lectures more than Stockbridge, but she can definitely be confusing at times. I think the lecturers for this course get bad reps because the class/exams kinda suck, but I think Dr. Jakob did a decent job. My only complaint is she likes to laugh in students' faces when they get questions wrong in lecture, not a fan of that.

Extremely unclear and disorganized lectures/lecture slides. Very nitpicky, specific questions on exam, could literally be from 1 bullet point in a 50+ slides lecture. Unclear what material is actually being tested and to what depth. Very hard to understand and confusing lectures. Badly written/confusing exam questions. Despised this class.

Goes through materials quickly, but does a good job going in-depth and avoiding just reading off the info from the slides. However, she uses a laser pointer a LOT and its faint so you can't tell what she's pointing at. I've missed information because she will only reference it with the pointer and not speak on it again. Overall a decent professor.

Dr. Jakob is very knowledgable and puts in a lot of effort, but her lectures were sometimes hard to understand the first time around. She was enthusiastic and likable, and while I wouldn't say she was the best professor I have ever had, I also think it is feasible to do well in her class if you put in the work.

I enjoyed this class. Not unexpectedly, you have to put in effort. Rewatching the lectures helps. Her exams are doable if you study. Sorry but a lot of whiners here that you should not listen to. Put in effort and you will do just fine.
calls on people

The amount of things I want to say makes me speechless. I am still in shock and i hope no one goes through what I did w/ her. She was so confusing and would start sentences but not finish them and her ideas were so unorganized. Class content was hard in a way that is still manageable but SHE made it impossible. Accent is fine btw

Whoever recently gave a positive review of Dr. Jakobs got paid. Yes, not surprisingly, the material is hard. But it's her exams that are simply unfair and unjust, giving us questions that were written so poorly. Stockbridge is 1000x better, it's literally just HER. DO NOT TAKE HER EVER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the last review was def made by dr jakob herself don't listen to it lol. listen to the bad reviews she's terrible. she tries to justify her questions by saying we have a cheat sheet so it can't be that easy for us, but at least make the questions reasonable and doable. actually the worst professor ive ever had.

Do not listen to the negative comments. I very much enjoyed this class. Dr. Jakob is entertaining and explains the material well. Too many seem to think that they can get into medical school with minimal effort. It shouldn't come as a surprise that Biochemistry is hard and requires some effort.
would rather be tortured than to take another mcdb 310 exam that is never reflective of the material we have been taught. take the other biochem unless u have to for ur major
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible prof take it with anyone but her as she makes the exams so f-ing hard. She barely explains in lecture and just talks about beer. I did well in this class bc I study really hard not because she was a good professor.

Dr. Jakob is actually the woat professor. She skims past important content in lecture, makes exams impossible, and always says 'oh you should know this don't use your cheat sheet or notes' when we literally just learned it. Also her practice exams are never reflective of her real exam she reuses problem roulette for them. avoid her 100%.

I honestly really enjoyed Dr. Jakob's lectures. Though she can be slightly confusing at times, she is very funny and engaging. Upon rewatching lectures they make much more sense. I do not think that is her fault I just think biochemistry is inherently a complicated subject and it takes a few times to absorb everything. Would take with her again!

She was a kind professor with great style, but I got nothing from her lectures. She clearly has a deep understanding of biochem yet does not convey it in an easy to understand way for beginners. I taught myself this whole course and only went to lecture because it was mandatory. I would stay away from taking biochem with her.

Dr. Jakob is very knowledgeable about biochemistry and took the time to explain how biochemistry was applicable outside of the course/human body (such as brewing beer), which I thought was cool. However, I definitely struggled the most with her exams. Problem Roulette is your best friend in this course - drill it every day if you want an A.

Dr. Jakob is extremely knowledgable but she tends to move to slow on lectures so you're always behind schedule and trying to catch up before the exam. In my opinion, she didn't explain concepts well and often goes on confusing side tangents that aren't a part of slides or content. Will cold call in 600 person class. She has amazing outfits though.

Definitely a hard course to begin with but her fast-paced, convoluted lectures did not help. To learn anything I had to watch the lectures back at least twice, sometimes on .8 speed. Also, I hated the cold calling, makes the already huge class even more intimidating. However, I appreciated that the textbook wasn't mandatory.

How is she still a prof! Explains things in the most unclear way. Overcomplicates things. Says the wrong molecule on accident all the time. Runs out of time and then just spends like two seconds on the last few (very important) slides. Honestly impossible to get an effective learning experience. Really unfair to people who want to take the MCAT.

Dr. Jakob is a nice person but a terrible lecturer. She moves way too quickly in a disjointed manner. Chucks around this microphone cube that ends up hitting people to cold call. The worst part is that most learning happens with the textbook but attendance is required for these useless, lengthy lectures. Do not take this course with her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She zooms through lectures so fast that you get lost within the first ten minutes. Her explanations are not clear, she wastes class time by either joking about throwing the cube around or by including content in lecture that we will not be tested on. She is very friendly one-on-one, but her lectures and exams are incredibly difficult to understand.

I'm a senior and she's by far the worst professor I've had. Doesn't explain concepts at all. I've been a strong science student all of college (A's in both orgos, pchem, etc) but there is just no way to understand something if it's not being taught to you. She is sweet but just does not remotely know how to teach. Really not fair to students.

Not a very helpful professor. Bad teacher, doesn't know how to explain concepts, just throws great amounts of information at you. This course is very slide heavy (must know everything on the slides) I do not recommend taking this heavy memorization/material workload class with such a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The most awful professor. She cold calls and requires attendance which takes away time from us teaching the content to ourselves and instead forcing us to come to a rather useless lecure. Also teaches up to the last days before the exam and includes it all on the exam, with hard and unreasonable questions. Sadly, not very understanding or kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Jakob is the worst prof I've ever had. She either just reads off of the slides or makes it more confusing by saying one thing, and the slides say another. She also requires lecture attendance, so its a huge waste of time when I could be studying in a way that would be MUCH better for my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are almost impossible to understand and she cold calls on people throughout the entire lecture. Need to do so much outside of class to understand since she makes 0 sense and contradicts herself a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she is unbearable to listen to and makes students chuck microphones around to answer questions

HORRIBLE and ATROCIOUS lectures. Legit nobody can understand anything in lecture. She also cold calls on people by making students throw a heavy microphone around (def not safe). It stresses everyone out and makes it hard to focus on lecture. She also did a fake iclicker question to catch people who were clicking outside of class. Worst lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: well known to be a bad lecturer

Great prof!! Very engaging lectures for potentially boring/heavy material. Prof Jakob included outside info to engage students in how biochem translates outside of class (brewing beer, diseases...). Fast paced, but willing to re-explain and answer questions. Kept students engaged with i-clicker and frequent "cold-call" questions.

Although entertaining, lectures feel very disorganized. MCDB 310 has a lot of material, which does not mix well with added personal stories and frequent tangents, making students lost and confused. She often has to correct herself or backtrack because of speaking too quickly or incorrectly.

Dr. Jakob's slides are much clearer and better formatted than Dr. B's, but the pace of her lectures is much slower. Her project assignments required lots of work, and she was often unclear in her speech during lecture. The material she presents that contains outside applications does appear on exams, so make sure to understand it.

Dr. Jakob is eccentric and unique, but truly cares about her students. She is the first teacher ever whose office hours I've attended, and she truly made it worth it with how clearly and concisely she explains information. Biochem is a tough class, but put in the right effort with Dr. Jakob and you'll reap the fruit on her exams
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ursula was a great professor. She really engages with the class and tries to get them involved with the material by walking around cold-calling during lectures. She is actually very funny too and tries to joke around. That being said, sometimes how she explains material is confusing, but she will try her best to reexplain if students do not get it.

Her lectures are not super clear, however, her slides are perfectly laid out. Makes memorizing easier. She walks down the aisle and makes people participate in lecture, so either sit far away or don't make eye contact.

She's not the worst or the best professor I've had. BioChem is going to be a tough class no matter what and she was an okay teacher. Her flow of information was a little off in lecture and she was definitely confusing. But, she was nice and approachable. She's not as bad as some commentors are making her out to be, but she's not that great either.
Dr. Jakob is a super nice professor who genuinely cares about teaching.  She's pretty clear in lecture and helpful during office hours.  Definitely the more likable one between her and Dr. B.

Jakob is 10x better than Balazovich. She cares about her students, she explains material clearly, and she will always pause to re-explain herself if the class is struggling to understand a concept. She will ALWAYS tell you exactly what you need to know and study to get through the class.
Don't really understand the negative comments, Jakob was a good professor who explained the material well and in a relatively simple way

I feel many people who rate on this site have a negative impression of professors who teach difficult classes (particularly pre med classes!). Biochem was a tough class, but Ursula explained concepts well the majority of the time. Yes, you needed to know almost everything on her slides, but that shouldn't be surprising for a biochem class.

Everyone here needs to calm down. Ursula is an amazing professor and always willing to help in her office hours. She makes things easy to understand- but you have to put in some work yourself! No one said biochem was going to be easy, you really have to study. Her exams were fair- she tested over exactly what she said she would.

nice lady who doesn't stress concepts that will be heavily tested, and rather tells us useless things we don't need to know. wouldn't even tell us the avg for exam 3 because it was so low, im guessing. the reason for the low avg correlates to her teaching ability.

I disagree with the post below.  She is actually a nice person and cares about how you do in the class.  She is clear in lecture and tries her best to help recap what you should know/study.  Overall, I liked her more than the other prof for this class.

This lady absolutely cannot teach. Do not take this class with her. Exams are poorly worded and set up to fail you. They test the most minute details. She rushes through lecture slides every day and simply does not care about student performance. She's there simply to be there, not to truly care and teach and make a difference.

Although she is a German, but I could understand her English no problem (unlike some Indian prof. in the University). Very helpful to students and answer question emails quickly. If you read her slides and refer to textbook, you will be totally fine for the class. Persons who gave her bad ratings probably just want good grades without studying.
Ten chapter in 2 classes?  She cannot and should not teach.  She does not care about student performance or learning.  Obscure test questions not covered in class.  You teach yourself.
She is not nearly as bad as the previous comments describe. I found her questions to be easier than Dr. Bs. Her accent isn't that bad, or even comparable to half the math department.

So they expect to give you in this class the whole world of biochemistry in 3.5 months....this is one of my worst classes ever...i struggled so much and you should take this class solo in a semester if u wanna do good.tests have hard questions that u never expect they would've asked abt b4 the test. Teacher is nice  ,class is hard

She lets the graduate students make mistakes on grading. She would not give me credit even though my answers were correct. She takes off 5 points for units which are already given in the question. She lost my regrade and told me to stop wasting her time asking about.  IMHO she is one of the worst person I've dealt with.
Worst teacher at michigan. Its OK to be hard but its not OK to be confusing and teach crap and then make mistakes on grading
Absolutely horrible. Will not discuss grading scale. The previous person is right! Rude and the accent makes the class unbearable.

Very confusing. When I was in office hours, she was very condescending and expected me to know my answers. Hello, if I knew, I wouldn't ask! In fact I saw two students come in to get their forms signed so they could drop the class. This just shows you how bad it is.

Dr. Jakob is very approachable. The class is do-able despite what ppl say. It is easy to understand her, ppl that say otherwise are deaf. Just make sure you read and KNOW the lecture slides! Definitely possible to get an A just attend lecture and read the book. Exams are geared towards detail but the detail comes from the notes not the book.
No Comments
Good instructor.  Pointless to go to class except for a few MCAT practice questions.  Memorize the notes and refer back to the textbook if you have any questions.  Requires a lot of time.

Nice lady. Her german accent wasn't that bad. She's pretty straightforward and doesn't try to trick you on exams. Her slides are slightly messy, but really tell you what to focus on. She makes jokes in lectures and they are actually funny, but her lectures could be really boring at times...
Hard class, really nice lady, though, and was more than willing to help students. Little difficult to understand her accent, but all her lecturenotes were online.
She is really hard to understand because she has a strong German accent, but she is funny and sweet.  Everything you need to know is on her lecture slides and she is very straight forward.

She is really nice and very funny in lecture. She doesn't go as fast as Balazovich, which is nice. She only wants you to know the very basics of biochemistry and does not try to trick you on the quizzes/exams at all. Very straightforward, even if her powerpoints are slightly messy.

Very strong accent which made it hard to understand her. She was helpful and friendly to approach compared to Satan (Balazovich), but she was vague to questions. I would also like t suggest picking out new GSIs whom don't state on the first day, "I don't care about you since I am going to med school and you aren't" to the discussion class.
Biochemistry professor. She was clear, and lectures were kept as interesting as possible. Friendly professor who answered emails quickly.

Unhelpful and rude when it gets to legitimate concerns. Follow-ups often went unanswered.
A large portion of the grade depended on group work while the team is randomly assigned.

Mike is the father of mech eng at umich. Only bad part about 250 and 350 is how difficult the exams are. Open homework policy is great and he fully explains homework questions in office hours. I think he knows the names of every person in the major. Great guy
ME250 was a very poorly organized course. You will be fine if you just follow the lectures, but I had a bad experience
Very nice and passionate professor. The final exam felt unnecessary and lowered my grade.
Respectful, clear professor who makes his expectations clear. Heavier workload mid-semester, but grading was as expcted.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everyone loves Mike. I had him for 250 and currently have him for 350. He's very willing to answer questions, teaches very fluidly, and knows designing/manufacturing well enough to teach it in a way most people can understand. One of the profs who acts like they actually want to teach!

Professor Umbriac was a good leader for such a cornerstone class. Lectures were posted online and were easy to sift through. The final exam for this class was kinda salt in the wound after so many hours of work into the project, but it was managable. Definitely take notes with lectures and save yourself the cramming time at the end.

Good class, learned a lot from the project. Most useless final exam I have ever seen. I think it only exists to justify the pointless hour and a half lectures on things we don't use on the project. Empty studying during finals week when I could be studying for other things.

Umbriac is the goat. Great prof with lots of stories of real engineering experience. Lectures are a mix of online and in-person, explains concepts clearly with lots of examples. Throws in a healthy amount of jokes and encourages students to ask questions and give feedback. Class was a blast and I would take anything with him again in a heartbeat.
Will always love taking classes lead by Mike!
Boring lectures, but incredibly kind person. Class is primarily project-based, where a lot of direction and guidance is given.
Mike umbriac cares deeply about his students and is very helpful in office hours. He was an excellent professor for ME350.

ME250 has a very large workload, but you will learn a lot in it.

He is a good professor.
Never responds to email.
Good professor, presents material clearly. Class is mostly project based.

Professor Umbriac, in the few times I interacted with him, was extremely kind and helpful. It was obvious that he cared a lot about the course and cared about making it fun for students, despite the huge workload. Just like many other students, I think this class will be one of my favorites in my ME undergrad, and that is partly due to Umbriac.

Took 250 years ago (2019), and really realized how unhelpful and unwilling to assist students who are working hard on the project. Often throws rude comments like, "I'm not the one who should answer this question," or "Ask the GSI" even the GSI had troubles helping the team with CAD design. Also, unwilling to help lecture materials he presented!
Kingpin of ME250 and ME350. Mike is one of the best professors I've had, however, both 250 and 350 are so intense on project-work that you'll end up interacting with the GSIs more.

Horrible professor. Acts like a dictator who is in control of students. Lots of work that is pointless. Stop using "I was at Ford" like it's a glory or showing you are above everyone. He needs to learn how to respect students and consider their workload before bragging your background. Please stop.

Mike is a great guy and a joy to be around. His lectures are fine, but honestly, the material he teaches can be just as easily learned by scrolling through lectures slides for 15 minutes, so I didn't go very often. He's helpful in the lab and is genuinely interested in your projects.

Mike is a great person, cares about his students, and is helpful during office hours. He's experienced, especially from his time at Ford. Overall, I learned a lot and ME 250 may be the most useful class I've ever taken so far (ever). His exams are difficult so beware. As for the class, groups are a hit or a miss, but I got lucky with mine.

Great professor. Yeah the lectures are boring but there's no way to make this material interesting so I don't blame Mike for that. He knows his stuff and how to teach it, he's a nice guy, what else do you want?
Mike is a really nice guy who cares about his students. His lectures are a little boring, but his office hours are helpful.
Great teacher, super friendly. Willing to get to know students and help out.

Mike is a VERY nice guy who enjoys what he does (whether it is teaching his students, or did I mention FORD?). His lectures are helpful, although this class isn't conceptually difficult, it takes A TON of time out of your schedule!!!
The course seems disorganized and really easy to get lost. Lecture slides were the only source to prepare for an exam but I found it insufficient.

Very good lectures, albeit long early in the morning. He does give a stretching break, however. Very knowledgeable about the design and manufacturing process. He will also help you out in lab if he happens to be there. You can pass on the course guide, I never used it.
Never had a more boring or pointless lecture in my life. Did you know he worked at Ford?

Mike is the man. His lectures are really interesting and pretty easy to understand. He was helpful in office hours when I went, and will never pass up a chance to talk about his time working at Ford, so be prepared for that.
Mike is a fantastic lecturer, and takes sincere interest in your ability to learn. If you're having any trouble, go see him outside of class - you'll be fine.
Umbriac is the face of mechanical engineering. Rather boring lecturer but extremely smart and helpful when it comes to knowledge and teaching design
Very helpful professor and very down to earth. Easy to talk to and understanding of the outside world and what you will actually need to know to succeed.
He is actually extremely rude and it interrupted my ability to learn.

Mike was the best lecturer/professor I've had! He is very interested in the subject, and is willing to spend a lot of time outside of class to help you. His enthusiasm shows, and it makes the class so much better.
Great Professor. Always willing to help students outside of class. Lectures with many industry applications from own experience. Very easy to keep in contact with outside of class.
Very Responsible to Students. One of the greatest professors ever seen. Clear lecture. Great Project.
Umbriac is extremely helpful in lecture and very accessible out of class and when working on the project. He is, in general, a very nice reasonable guy and I highly recommend him.
He's great and will answer any and all questions.
Although some lectures are boring he is very helpful. He will answer any question you have and help with any project. He was also great for ME 250. Although both classes took up a lot of my time.

Umbriac is a great professor: he is helpful and homework is very straightforward (with the help of the lecture notes). He makes the lectures interesting by passing around example parts and using videos to show manufacturing processes.  Highly recommended.

Prof. Cable was extremely knowledgable on everything related to the course. There isn't really a more qualified professor to teach this class. Lectures were easy to follow, interesting, and not too content-heavy. Only qualm is Prof. Cable can come off as rude/mean sometimes, but it's not intentional & doesn't take away from the learning experience.

This class is really fun! As an arab, I was able to gain new information around the arab world it's self. I feel like this class has hints on what is going to appear on the exams. I would say do all the lecture activities as it will help your grade out! I would say that Prof C is really nice and this class had the lightest work.
Professor is strict but gives many hints towards the quiz. Very knowledgeable and interesting to learn from. Much respect for them.
This class could have been better but only with a change in Professor. They can be very abrupt and are more interested in being a stage actor than an actual educator.

I think that Professor Cable is very passionate about the work they teach. They also care about their students being attentive and taking this subject matter seriously. This is why they come out as a little harsh to some. However, class content was always thoroughly explained and talked over in class. I plan on taking more classes in the future.

Prof is so clearly passionate about the information they teach. To some students, they may feel a bit abrasive at first but once I gave them a chance I loved this class. Lectures are engaging, the readings tend to be short/fair in length, I learned so much valuable information from this, and tests were very fair. I highly recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Cable was very unwelcoming and oftentimes rude. Lectures were uncomfortable because students were afraid to ask questions - when questions were asked, Cable usually had unhelpful and condescending answers. For a college course I paid for, I'm incredibly disappointed by the poor classroom atmosphere, distasteful material, and unaccepting prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I made an account just so I could post this. The worst class I have ever taken it was amcult 215. Literally just he complaining the whole class. Did not learn anything. The was would call on people randomly because no body wanted to answer the questions. When you did answer he questions she would rip on you a lot of the time.

Prof. Cable is an exceptional educator. Grades were determined by reading responses, a very fair midterm, and an optional final project. Prof. Cable cares greatly about their students and is easily approachable. However, they are pretty inaccessible outside of class. If you have any questions, make sure to ask after class! Highly recommend!

Professor Cable was an excellent professor and person. She was always extremely prepared for class and treated all her students with respect. She was extremely caring, aware of the difficulty of learning in a pandemic, and was always made sure we were comfortable with the information we were learning.I took her Media Activism class this fall.

I usually enjoy earth and environment-related classes to the point that my intended career path is in the area, but this class sucked. Do not take it. Tho he is a very lovely man, the content is confusing and rubrics for the required projects are hugely unclear. Sometimes, the whole class would share a look in solidarity b/c we were all so lost. 😭

Udo puts a lot of value on office hours, and kind of expects you to come. Despite EARTH427 being advertised as a mineralogy class, my section (also the first section ever offered so YMMV) had several units & a field trip on hydrology and water chemistry. Strong physics + chem background is an asset in EARTH427.

Awesome, laid back guy who knows a lot about his subject. Total dad jokes. He's a fairly lenient grader and homework is pretty much nonexistent. If you show some effort, he will make sure you do well.

Dr. Ujeed is the first professor I've ever felt compelled to write a review for. She makes Buddhism an engaging and accessible subject, even for students with no prior background. I took her class during my freshman year, and it was without a doubt one of the best courses I've taken at this university.

Excellent teacher! Very fun and engaging lectures, especially for ASIAN 250. Highly recommend if interested in learning about Buddhism in a fun way. Little bit of reading but it will be throughout the course. Not much assignments and the workload balance is great. Definitely recommend 10/10.

Dr. Ujeed is a lovely professor. She taught classical Mongolian with immense passion. However, the class was not advertised as a language class, which was very confusing. It was also very fast-paced for an introductory language course.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing. Such a sweet person and professor.
Easily my favorite professor so far, she's so bubbly and positive. Even for taking her 8am lecture, her class had a fantastic energy.

Definition of the goat. Do practice exams and you'll be fine. Homeworks are on mastering physics (dreadful) but shes very very helpful if u ask her questions and wants to see you succeed. Had some fun demos, no required attendance but you should definitely show up if you wanna do well. Overall incredible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Physics 160 with Professor Sih was straightforward and fun! Lectures were sometimes unclear and tough to follow at times, but she is very open to clarifying questions and is helpful in office hours. Previous quizzes and tests are provided, setting clear expectations for every exam. There are modelling-based coding projects too. No set attendance.

This is a very difficult course and there is a lot of work involved. Professor Sih bases the grade mainly on quizzes which tend to be more difficult than the homework. Coding is an important part of this class. Concepts were not always explained well in class and there was no textbook. Very much a teach-yourself style through in-class questions.
Really easy grader and great at explaining the material
Quiet but clear lecturer with great demos. Very helpful. Very responsive. Works hard to answer questions in and out of class. Interesting assignments.
Not the most entertaining lecturer but very clear and has fun demos. Really helpful in office hours. Really cares for the students. The class had a ton of work but was definitely worth it!
Great Professor.  Really enjoyed this class.  Had to work, but completely worth it

Lots of reading - I found reading and lectures boring. Dr. Kivelson was far from bad but I don't feel the need to take another course of hers. Grading criteria is vague for all written assignments and difficulty probably depends on your GSI. Attendance is a big part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her expectation setting for essays is not great. Overall it should've been a fun and interesting class but was not. My GSI would respond rudely to comments she did not like in class and gave me the exact same grade despite seeking out and using feedback. Great class concept though.

You're graded on attendance to lecture and have to complete readings biweekly. However, the lectures were very boring and dull, with no interactive or interesting aspects at all. No one participated in lecture other than the same two people. This class would be good for a hardcore history major, but to others it may be a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm a lecturer now, but I'd take Professor Kivelson's class again in a heartbeat. The courses are lecture-heavy and a lot of reading will be assigned, but it was all worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class content itself had nothing to do with Salem until the end of the course, and despite some of the information being kind of interesting the lectures themselves were dreadfully boring. If your GSI was anything like mine, sections will be a waste of time. Prompts are vague and GSI's hardly know what's going on.

A pretty interesting class overall, but grades were made up of mostly essays. I would say the lectures are actually very important to go to/watch, especially with history not being my thing -- weekly quizzes in discussions were not common sense, and detailed notes from lecture were necessary for me to do well on them. Otherwise, workload not bad!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was mostly graded by a few large essays (graded primarily by the GSI). Lectures were not useful if you did the readings as they usually just summarized key points. If you do the readings, I would forgo going to the lectures. Your GSI will be the one that drives learning. Kivelson does a lot of research if you are interested in that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While I do believe that Professor Kivelson is incredibly intellectual, her lectures are very boring. I took this course because it seemed interesting, but it was definitely not worth it. There are so few opportunities to actually show off your knowledge, and even the best papers aren't A-worthy. I wish I had known this before taking the class.

I took the history colloquium on Russian Witchcraft with her and it was a mess. No structure, no real teaching on how to write even tho it was an ULWR class. Extremely hard to get an A on papers despite this. She is accommodating re covid, etc but despite initial understanding, will dock your participation grade. Dont recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great! Only critique is that the class focuses on way more than just Salem (also a women's studies course). Look at past and recent syllabus to get a feel before signing up. She is one of the most passionate professors I've had, and takes time to get to know and help students. Papers are difficult to get higher than a B without prof/GSI consult.

Kindest professor ever! I took her Witchcraft class online and enjoyed it. The lectures are long, but are usually interesting. We wrote 4 papers (1 being the final) and had to use our readings in them. Our final was a fun and pretty open paper, similar to the others. Super chill! Grading depends on your GSI, but the professor grades some randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Kivelson is really lovely and I thoroughly enjoyed her class on the History of Witchcraft. She's super passionate about the subject, and has extensive knowledge on it. Before discussing potentially triggering subjects such as rape she would always give us a warning, and is very diligent at outlining each lecture's structure at the start.

I took History 375 and History 432 with Professor Kivelson last year and can confidently say Valerie is hands down the best teacher I have ever had. She is wise, beautifully spoken, and so so caring. I learned a tremendous amount, greatly improved as a historian and writer, and grew as a person thanks to Valerie's positive presence in my life.

Valerie was very engaging and made lectures very fun to go to. The material was super interesting, and she does a good job teaching it. A fair bit of books were required for reading, but it was not unreasonable. No exams, only 4 papers.

Prof Kivelson was an amazing history professor who is knowledgable and passionate about Russian History. She went above and beyond and met with me to provide feedback beyond what I needed to get a good grade, and helped me improve my writing. She cares about her students, is interesting and engaging, and I would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Beware, old reviews are irrelevant as the course structure/assignments have changed (I learned the hard way). Class was very disorganized, the syllabus is a poor description of what you'll actually learn in the class. GSI's and professors are on different pages, making grading vey confusing. Least helpful group of faculty I've encountered at UM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Kivelson was a superb professor in her Medieval Russian history class. You have to stay on your toes with the readings and participation, but she really made the material come to life. She was understanding as well when I needed extensions. Makes you work for your grade, but I found her class to be a rewarding experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kivelson is clearly very passionate about witchcraft, but her lectures are often scattered and boring, resulted in spotty attendance. The class is not tough, but at some points can be excessively feminist. The first half of the class focuses on European witchcraft and the second on the more interesting Salem witch trials. Easy humanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kivelson is a nice lady, but a terrible professor. Her slides are so disorganized they are hard to follow. The prompts for writing assignments are vague and even the GSI's can't explain what they are asking for. Grading is harsh. At no point in the semester did we talk about Harry Potter or other movies like the course description said we would.

She is an incredibly nice woman, and is obviously interested in her topic. She is also very opinionated without trying to force her opinions on other people, which is a nice skill. The class itself is a bit boring at times, but then again, the lecture was at a terrible time in the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took History 375/Women Studies 375 and it was amazing! It's the History of Witchcraft and is largely focused upon gender issues, which is where the women studies crossover comes into play. Kivelson has amazing lectures, includes a powerpoint filled with pictures and film clips. No finals!! A take home essay at the end and some pop quizzes.

Kivelson is really great, and I'm not sure why her rating here is fairly low.  She takes the time to get to know students and is very friendly and warm.  She also integrates pop culture, art, and theater into her lectures, which makes the material more interesting and approachable.  She gave a number of opportunities for extra credit.

Kivelson's class relies heavily on class participation but she doesn't shoot you down completely if your answer isn't completely right.  Also I'm pretty sure she knows the name of everyone in lecture, so she puts in the effort.  She is more than willing to answer questions and is super approachable (coming from a student afraid of office hours)

This was a great class and I do not understand all of the bad reviews. Why do people even come to this college if they expect to do absolutely nothing and get an A? Prof Kivelson let you know what you needed to know for exams and I found the material very interesting. What you need to know is very clear and emphasized. Make sure to do the readings.

Kivelson is fun and tries her best to make lectures fun. They are sometimes all over the place but I recommend this class to anyone who is a history major or a non-history major. She has good content and is willing to help any student who wants assistance. Show interest, and guarantee the GSI or she will be willing to grade you easier.

Please, for your own sake, do not take a class with Valerie Kivelson. Her lectures drone on FOREVER, and still yet leave you wondering what the hell the class was about. Blue Book exams are TERRIBLE and nobody should be subjected to her course.

Don't bother going to lecture after midterm. Relies way too much on student participation even in a huge lecture. Some weeks devoted to things hardly related to witchcraft - fairy tales and mccarthyism. Should be a 3 credit 10 week class or something. Everyone just dialed it in the last few weeks. Grading is ridiculous for such simple content.

Professor Kivelson has a very narrow mindset.  She does not allow for any individual thought, rather she is interested on if you can spit back the information that she gave you.  Lots of boring readings and many papers in which the feedback is awful.  Would not recommend taking this class, for you will not do well.

Val is very interested in the material that she teaches. Her interest radiates through her while she lectures. Although class can get a little dry on occasion, it's worth taking it to get the A. The GSI you get may effect your grade. If Scott De Orio is an option, choose him. He is a wonderful GSI.

I took this class my freshman year and it very relatively easy to get an A. Going to class is recommended, and I actually found the lecture material interesting, as well as Kivelson's way of presenting it. Although. She does like a lot of student participation during her lectures, which can get annoying.

Fine class. BUT val does not know how to give an organized, clear lecture. A lot of times you feel like she is BSing and her powerpoints look like they were made by a 5 yr. old (crazy colors, no organization, lists often start at #2 and you are like "what?"). Plus, she makes up words to sound smart (ex. climactical change instead of climate change)

She is a great professor. If you go to office hours to discuss writing assignments, she is very helpful in improving your understanding. Professor Kivelson is extremely nice as well. I was unable to go home for Thanksgiving, and she actually invited me over to eat dinner with her family and relatives, which was fun!

I thought this would be an interesting class, but its really just awful.  Half the lecture is spent listening to student's reactions to readings/pictures, and the other half is a really sweet professor talking about a whole bunch of bull.
Not a good class! I thought this class sounded like an interesting humanities course, but I was mistaken. Unless you are history major and like dull class I do not recommend taking this class!
Interesting class, and she's super nice

Prof Kivelson means well, but she's incredibly dull.  I thought History of Witchcraft would be an interesting humanities credit, but it becomes old really quickly.  For the most part, the readings are extremely dense and there are a lot of them.  This class is definitely better suited for history majors, and not science students.

Kivelson is an incredibly nice (and sometimes socially awkward) professor, who's always willing to help. Meeting for office hours can be useless unless you come prepared to discuss specific topics, as she typically won't provide significant feedback.  Tons of reading, but otherwise a very good course - highly recommended.
She is absolutely the nicest professor I've ever had. She does expect you to work, but she's always willing to help you. The material is very interesting as well. Definitely recommended.

I took her freshman seminar on witchcraft, and I loved it. There is a lot of reading and a lot of papers, but most of them are just 2-3 pages, there's only 1 long one. You can probably skip out on some of the reading, but I'd try to keep up for the most part. Doesn't take attendance, but again, I wouldn't skip very often. Discussion is very helpful
