I had her for a freshman seminar on the history of witchcraft. The actual topics were pretty interesting, but monotonous over time. Kivelson is a total sweetheart who seems to really want the best for her students, but there's a lot of reading and papers. The actual class is strictly discussion, which she WILL force you to partake in.

Prof. K made things really interesting and the material was fun to learn about. I did probably 2 of the 500 readings all year and missed 1/3 of the lectures and pulled out a b+. Don't expect to be able to use the lectures posted online if you don't go to class though, she makes them impossible to understand without her presentation.

This is a great class. As long as you do the reading and pay attention in lecture, you will be fine. Like any prof., she expects you to be prepared for class, and she is incredibly nice. Exams are challenging, but not impossible. You will be expected to interact-participation is 25% of your grade. Lots of Disney movies! This class was a lot of fun!

I had never taken a history class here before, and I found History of Witchcraft to be extremely interesting.  Yes, there's a lot of reading, but for the most part it's fun stuff.  Valerie is a nice professor and will go out of her way to talk to you ... we also got to watch great movie clips :).

Every single day was a discussion section. Unless you like to talk constantly and read about two hundred pages a week, don't take this class. She doesn't seem to realize that most people don't have a Male Russian Witchcraft background and gets frustrated if you don't agree with her. She expected us to buy $400 worth of books and bring them to class but some of the books we hardly used.

She seems to be completely oblivious of her tendency to cut down other people's ideas and originality. I wish she would have changed up the class format every once in awhile. Class discussion EVERY day was really tiresome.

Contrary to the previous few comments, I really liked Kivelson.  She may have been agrumentative with a few students, but that's only because those students were probably full of themselves.  Kivelson's a fine teacher.

I was extremely excited to take this class -- it was a mistake. Originality should be avoided at all costs. If you want an a, spit everything she says right back to her. She doesn't set up discussion that well. Don't go to office hours. Also, she always prefaces  her political views with, "I don't want to interject with how I feel.." Frustrating!
She seems very nice, but she gets very snappy if you don't agree with her. She expects you to know everything about everything! There is a lot of writing in this class...beware

She had a way of tearing students down.I felt like if anyone had the guts to say anything outside the box she would shut them down.She seemed to lack respect for her students and was very harsh.I wouldnt recomend her classes to anyone for that reason alone
good class if you enjoy the topic
Great professor. Extremely intelligent and aware. She will challenge you, but if you can handle it, be prepared for a great course and a wonderful learning opportuinity. Highly recommended.
Great Prof!  Just do the reading and pay attention, and you'll get involved in very interesting discussions

Has a way of setting up unhealthy class dynamics. Too much sarcasm. Rather than encouraging the smarter thinkers, she feels threatened by them and gets sarcastic and dismissive. Also - beware of setting your own course on paper writing. Any hint of originality will be swiftly punished.
Fantastic teacher, very engaging -- I would recomend her class, but only to those who aren't afraid to try hard and think outside the box. I learned a lot about writing from her.
No Comments
Nice lady.  Very critical on exams and papers... so good luck.  She does a good job teaching material that is essentially inaccessible.
when I first heard her speak, I was all, "whoa, she sounds like a mouse." She has a really wavery voice and she's really small, but she's probably one of the better profs here. I really liked her! :)

very nice lady, but she grades our written exams as if we are supposed to be fluent Spanish speakers, and I do not know anyone who has received above a 85. The same goes for the regular exams; nobody in the class got an A, and she does not curve anything. Don't take this class if you care a lot about your GPA.

Prof Maria is truly passionate about teaching languages to students. She is a caring individual and wants to see you do well. Her grading is extremely fair and she is supportive in class if you have a slip up while talking. The class itself is extremely difficult but manageable, I chose to take it as a P/F but had I kept it graded, I'd have a B.

Profe Maria is from the DR and is super excited to teach her native language to her students. The only thing that I disliked about the course was the lack of Spanish speaking in class, as in my previous Spanish courses here at Michigan were speaking heavy.

Profe Maria is the sweetest! I totally recommend taking her courses because she is so kind and you can tell that she genuinely cares for her students. She's not a terribly harsh grader, and there's only like a few "big" assignments throughout the semester. 10/10 love her!

amazing professor! clearly cares about her students and wants you to succeed. she always seems eager to teach and greets the class with a smile. makes lectures engaging and does her best to clarify any confusing topics. i would absolutely take a class with her again if possible!

She's so nice and caring. I love her and her class. She does a good job at explaining when students have questions. She also always seems to be excited to teach. I would take her class again if I can for my next Spanish class

One of the best professors I have ever taken a class with. She genuinely tries to establish meaningful connections with all of the students in her class. The essays and readings are both super interesting. Learned a lot from her class.

don't be intimidated by her because she seems intense, she's super nice and actually very flexible. the only thing that sucked was that the entire class was graded by like, three assignments, so it was super hard to get an A. but the assignments weren't difficult and the class was interested. i'd highly recommend. she's also super funny lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: difficult and passive aggressive

I loved Dr. Uehling's class on humanitarian dilemmas, she is very knowledgeable on the topic and super passionate. We were only graded on 4 assignments, but she seemed to follow her rubric guidelines and provided feedback on points missed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't know why her rating is kind of low on here...Dr. U is a great professor, and 401 was a super interesting class with a manageable workload. Definitely recommend!

I had Dr. U for both Intl Studies 101 and 401. I wasnt the biggest fan of her lecture style in 101, but she was an amazing professor in 401! She was engaging and the subject material was very interesting. She was also caring and communicative if something came up. I would definitely recommend 401 with her!

Dr. U seems like a nice person, but her lectures aren't the most engaging. If anything, there might be a problem with the course: since it's an introductory course, it has to be vague. She definitely shines when she can go in-depth on a topic, but she can't with this class. Reading isn't required, but it's good to have a book for reading quizzes.
I found this class to be fairly simple. While some students didn't like her lecture style, I found it quite clear and concise. She says what she means, and class typically ends early.

I was not a fan of Uehling for 101, but when I had her in a seminar setting for her Human Trafficking and Smuggling 401 course I absolutely loved her. She's accessible outside class too. The course is discussion-based and graded almost entirely on participation, with two short papers (which she gives really good feedback on). I love her!

Very monotone and boring lectures but the material is interesting so it makes up for it. There's also a good amount of guest lecturers so she isn't teaching all of the classes. Offers a study guide for exams which is pretty similar to the actual test.

I honestly enjoyed this class. I do see what some of these other reviews mean, though-- she's not a very interesting lecturer and is kind of all over the place, but if you're interested in the material it's not bad at all. Midterms were exactly what she says in the study guide and if you do the work you'll do fine in the class.

Uehling gives plenty of grading guidelines, but as far as I can tell, she grades completely arbitrarily of these guidelines. She provides rubrics, but fails to give you any sort of feedback on why you missed points. Email communication is terrible as well. Usually professors of upper level classes care, but it seems like Uehling really doesn't.

Class is easy. Majority of your grade is comprised of the quizzes but they're all online and straightforward. Midterms were a joke. I probably wouldn't skip lecture because although she mostly just reads off the slides, sometimes she might say an important thing now and then. For a woman with a lot of credentials, they sure don't translate.

Greta's class left something to be desired. The material was interesting enough, but the class is graded on few things (participation, one paper, one project). Your participation grade is completely arbitrary and grading on papers and projects are unclear. Don't expect to be in contact with her to resolve any questions or issues on grading either.
Interesting class but she is a boring lecturer who literally reads off the slides and always seems like she is confused about everything.

I took this class because I was considering an international studies major. After taking this class, I can't say the same. The lectures, while I attended every one, were dry, long, and unnecessary to pass the class. The quizzes are easy, but the tests are really hard as the questions are very specific. Only take if you want to major in it

I had Uehling for international studies 101 which was just OK, but then for 401 she was AMAZING. The class was super small and she was always really engaged and encouraged every one to be active. The assignments were fairly easy and she is a very fair grader (if you put the effort into the paper you will get a good grade).

I actually really enjoyed Dr. Uehling's class. The guest lecturers, though painfully biased at times, where a nice change of pace given that we didn't have to listen to the same person every week. The class itself was relatively easy, graded solely on reading comprehension tear-outs (the reading was straightforward/interesting), a paper, and exams.

INTLSTD 101 is probably the worst class I've taken at UMich. Way, way too many guest lecturers (including listening to a pre-recorded lecture from a poli sci course) and the tests are so specific in questions that you're not sure what you're supposed to study for or not. Subject matter is so vast that it gets very confusing, overall a terrible time
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is really impossible to prepare for exams, since her lectures (actually no cuz she doesnt even gives lectures) are vague but the questions on the exams are super specific and picky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and often pretty boring to sit through. There were way too many guest speakers that added to the course's overall confusion. Lectures are not recorded. The discussions were perhaps the best part of the course. The worst was having to listen to a pre-recorded guest speaker's lecture for the lecture. What was the point??
Way too many guest speakers and tests aren't clear

This class was ok, the material is too broad and at times insubstantial, and there are WAY TOO MANY guest lecturers that sway violently between horribly dry and interesting. But the textbook was actually pretty good, and the class is one of the easiest classes I've taken. Shouldn't be hard to sit through

100% not recommend taking her class unless you're an international studies major. The lecture is super dry, and way too many guest lectures which make it super confusing. She made you buy the textbook which is edited by her for $80. Note you HAVE to buy a new one because of the tear out questions on the book. Buying a used book is NOT an option.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Greta was very nice and clearly new what she was talking about. Her experience in the field is obvious. However, her slides were too specific for learning about such broad subjects. It was mainly memorization of her slides. Greta is also very biased, bringing in guest professors that were very clear about their personal political views.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: As a new International Studies major, I was excited for this class only to be let down. She seems nice but the class is so broad with such little detail that it becomes hard to stay invested. The text book is a rip-off, if you have friends in the class split an online textbook. It is only used for one online, open book test. Take it if you have to.

Take it if you need to; otherwise, it's not an enormously interesting class. She knows her field but the course is honestly just stringing things together and there generally isn't much depth across all topics. Lecture slides are a bit scant in terms of text/content so going to lecture can matter. Study guides cover everything you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class was fairly easy. Probably put 10 hours of work into class the whole semester and did not go to any of the lectures. The one paper is graded extremely easily. If its an easy A you're looking for, take this class, If you're looking to learn, maybe look elsewhere.

Class is broad but honestly felt like I was just learning a bunch of facts. Can't really apply the information to anything outside of class. Decent lecturer, but very bias and emphasizes weird topics (we had to learn about mythical creatures for half a lecture once). Overall, it was alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: - Uninformative powerpoint presentations (lots of picture, little text) - Text book is additional reading. Does not cover in class material - Little resources for class material - Graded on 1 paper and 2 exams

Reading quizzes are super easy if you have an online book. Talk with your GSI to get a better grade on your essay. Go to class because slides barely have any information on them. A lot of guests lectures which keeps it engaging but makes exams confusing.

Professor Uehling is very knowledgeable in her subject, and she makes her lectures interesting by adding media and current events. That being said, this class was difficult for a 100-level course. The exams were long, frustrating, and often contained questions that caught us by surprise. Good content, but definitely not a "blow-off" class.

Really hard class :( information-heavy lectures with occasional guest speakers that make it even more confusing. Exams cover literally everything and anything, so you have to take detailed notes on every little thing she says. Make sure you have online textbook so you can command + F on reading quizzes (which are open-book). Really hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Greta. Class is easy, but you still learn so much and have truly meaningful conversations. She's great and has so much experience working on humanitarian issues.

I'm confused why everyone is saying that this class is hard. I had a great GSI who basically told us exactly what would be on the exams. Yes the class is vague, but its an intro course. Greta has had a super interesting career and I found her lectures enjoyable. The reading quizzes were super easy and I did well on both exams.

This class should be 4-5 credits instead of 3. I'm taking 4-5 credit classes that have significantly less work than int'l studies. She really jams a lot of material (6 whole modules) in only 1 short semester. The material is kind of vague so preparing for the exams is extremely difficult. I wouldn't take this class if int'l studies isn't your major

Reading quizzes every week - unnecessary nit-picky questions. Exams are very difficult. If int'l studies isn't your major, you'll probably fail it. She's not a good lecturer. Email responses are vague (ex. one time I just got a "no"). She doesn't care about her students' success. Lectures are boring and the material provided is extremely vague.

I would strongly urge everyone to NOT take this class with Dr. Uehling. Her lectures are extremely boring and information-heavy and she speaks extremely quickly, so it's almost impossible to take notes. Her lecture slides, which she posts on Canvas, are very vague and will not help you study for the midterms (which are hard-friend and I failed it).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Greta has actually been one of the best professors I have had at the University of Michigan. Her work is beyond inspirational and she's very motivating. She's very knowledgeable and passionate about her work as well, which definitely gives her an advantage in lecture because she always kept me engaged. She's very big on participation!

She's very strict about her grading policy since she never rounds up anyone's grades. Be aware of the fact that she is not empathetic. If you ever ask a question through email, she would complain and possibly say an inappropriate things as an instructor. Never had a professor like this ever before. Well, good luck if you MUST take her.

Greta is a great professor!  She seems very invested in this class and seems to know her stuff, especially about the Humanitarian Module and the Human Trafficking module.  I had a great GSI who really knew her stuff.  Go to lecture and take notes on what she says and less on what is on the slide - only way to do well on exams which are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Greta is an interesting professor.  Her class is pretty easy -- not an easy A but if you put in some effort, you'll be fine.  Her GSIs (Graduate Student Instructors) are total hit or miss.  I was lucky but my other friends were dead.  Greta's lecture can be a bit too fast but make sure to get what she is saying rather whats on the screen.

Greta is really kind and has lots of interesting and applicable experience. If you are interested in the field, she's a great person to hear from. Her lectures are very informative but can sometimes become a little boring. There's not much work, but it means that the midterms count for a huge part of your grade and are very long and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Uehling is a great knowledgeable woman. She shares her experiences from her work with the students during lecture and that's always an interesting day. She can be a little boring and monotonic sometimes but she almost always lets the lecture out early. Easy A!! Her guest lectures are pretty interesting too. She's pretty great!

Boring lectures with lots of powerpoint. Nonstop guest speakers, which I guess is okay because she's not the best, but they're boring too. For such an exciting topic this class is dreadful to sit through. Plus you have weekly reading quizzes for no reason, since we never talked about readings. Nitpicky test questions. Hope you get a good GSI.

This class takes a very broadscope look at International Studies, it doesn't go indepth on any topic. The info is interesting and Uehling conveys a strong sense of interest in her career field and regularly makes antecedents to her previous work with the UN. I found the class very interesting, easy, don't' bother buying the book tho.

This class was very easy. I'm not sure why others are saying different. The quizzes are only on the assigned readings and the midterms are only on material from lecture. The midterm was super easy because it was exactly what she said in class. Not a ton of reading either. Quizzes are online so theres plenty of time to go back  and read for answers.

I really did not like her class at all. Her lectures were not engaging and her GSIs really did not give consistent lessons from section to section. The first midterm was incredibly difficult, and by the time of the final, the majority of the "required" readings were completely disregarded. I honestly do not think I learned anything useful.

Uehling is less than academic; meaning uncharacteristically unintelligent for a UM professor. She would frequently fail to back up information that she had on her slides, and seemed uncomfortable with the information in HER OWN CLASS. Test average is lower than expected for a blow off class (79%). AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Professor Uehling was the WORST professor I have ever had at the University of Michigan. All of her GSIs are CLUELESS. They are unaware of the subject matter of the class. Her tests are nearly impossible. She just reads off of the lecture slides, and refers to them when you ask her questions about the study guide.  Last test average was a 79%.
Greta was one of my favorite professors! Her lectures are AMAZING, but you'll probably have to study a little bit for exams. Take this class! Quizzes are easy.
Uehling is nice and makes it clear what she wants from you. However, the class is very broad. It is still interesting. Expect to work for an A, but it definitely isn't impossible!
I took 101 with Greta and wasn't a fan; however, her 401 class is easy since it's enjoyable. I really enjoyed 401 and would recommend it to other INTLSTD majors.
I was interested in this class to begin with. It was very basic and fairly boring. Study the lecture slides, and you should be fine.

I've had Uehling twice now, and while I wasn't a huge fan of hers in 101, I definitely enjoyed her 401 class a lot more, as I think her teaching style is better suited to smaller classroom sizes. This class was really interesting and not too hard - I'm glad I took it with her. I would definitely recommend it for the 401 requirement.

The slides have almost all the information that are on the exams, but the short answer questions require some elaboration, and that's where your lecture notes come in.  However, it was hard to take good notes since Professor Uehling didn't speak very fluidly and rather read off the slidesher notes.  Overall, the class was pretty easy but boring.

Prof U's class on human trafficking and smuggling was pretty easy and didn't require much effort to get a good grade. Mostly in class discussions. Prof U was clear and helpful and the work load was manageable

Prof U has a lot of info to cover on a very broad topic, so the class was very easy. Felt like I was in high school. She published her powerpoints from lectures but you still need to go cuz she will say things not written that you'll be expected to know for the exams. Never needed extra help.
Class is kind of easy, interesting subject matter, Greta Uehling rants and most people really do not like her.  Still the class is kind of cool.

Professor Uehling is knowledgable with an experienced background in her subject.  She isn't the greatest public speaker, but she does her best to help the class, and there are several guest lectures that make it very interesting.  The class is easy and the textbook is hardly used.  I learned a lot about parts of the world I'd never imagined.

She talked really fast and her lectures were unorganized. She never stopped to ask for questions and she has no sense of humor. She would try to make jokes and it was almost pathetic. Very boring. Not a good lecturer at all.

This class was really boring! I had a hard time going every week.  She talks really fast and never seemed extremely interested in what she was teaching.  Her powerpoints were full of examples that never made sense for what we were learning.  DISLIKE

Greta is very kind and passionate about what she is teaching. She speaks very quickly when she lectures and it is difficult to take notes, but she posts her power points and the exams are based off of those. She is not the best lecturer but all the guest speakers were interesting. I thought this class was very interesting and I would take it again.

Professor Uehling was great! The lectures and the material are supposed to be broad - its a survey class, duh. And for once the prof is about big ideas instead of making us memorize facts that will be forgotten. I was blown away by some of her research she shared: child smuggling, sex trafficing, self-immolation. And she made it make sense

Professor Uehling's lessons were disjointed. She did not communicate well with the GSIs. Module papers were incredibly broad, but GSIs had unclear expectations that made seemingly effortless papers hard to get consistent grades on. Section was pointless, lectures by Uehling were uninspired unless she was talking about refugees (her passion)

Quizzes were super easy. Low workload. Module papers were a pain because the prof wrote vague essay questions and the GSI would expect a very specific module paper. Her lectures were boring, and all over the place. Guest lecturers were better. Section was pointless, my GSI couldn't even speak English properly. Not an easy A,but not super difficult.
Professor Uehling is amazing! The lectures are some of the most interesting I have had at U of M. And while the subject matter is broad - its 101 - duh! Few professors could span that breadth.

Not a bad professor, but slightly boring. She had a few guest lecturers which were more interesting than her lectures. She's very nice though and her discussion section was actually very interesting. If you take this class, try to get her discussion. If you study for the exams, they aren't that bad. Almost no homework either, which was a plus.

Greta is a nice lady. The class has the potential to be interesting; however, she simply reads off of her notes and powerpoint slides (and uses the example of the deportation of Crimean Tatars about a thousand times--it's her main area of expertise). Tests cover too much material. Discussion sections are not helpful. Would not recommend.

All she did was read off the slides - sometimes I think she didn't even know what she was saying, but blindly reading them and pressing "next". The material was too broad to be interesting. She gives really good study guides.

Greta is a kind person, but lectures were lackluster, and a mile wide and a foot deep in information. However, the class requires little work, and every now and then there are fascinating guest speakers- but I would not say that this class is a representative introduction to how interesting international studies can be.

Professor Uehling is really boring and doesn't know anything outside of her own field, which is a small community in Ukraine.  She reads directly off the slides and you wouldn't need to go to class, except they sometimes take attendance.  The papers are easy but the tests are hard because she's so boring in class and doesn't keep your attention

The class (CICS 101) is somewhat interesting, but is WAY too broad to keep your focus for long. Furthermore, Professor Uehling is unfortunately rather horrible. If she didn't have her PowerPoint presentations with her in class, she would probably have nothing to say. I would NOT recommend her, with all due respect.

This is a relatively easy class, if one studied for the tests. There is also relatively little assignments other than 2 papers which make up 40% of total grade. However, there is so much content that you will unlikely learn in-depth knowledge about the topics covered. Some lectures could also have be improved.

I preferred the guest lectures over her own. She definitely knows the material, but has a hard time making it interesting. Two papers and two exams in the class. Papers weren't too difficult, exams we're moderately difficult because it covers a ton of material. Overall, a decent class.

It's hard to rate the professor since most of the lectures were given by guest lecturers. She goes through the information quickly when she does lecture, so you always have to look back at the notes posted. Midterm was sort of a pain to study for since there were many short answers

CICS 101 was an awesome intro course. The readings weren't overwhelming and the assignments and quizzes were straightforward. Uehling is really very clear and has a lot of experience and cool examples in lecture. But she's not one of those professors that just rambles about their trips- she actually ties her work into what she lectures about.

Overall, CICS 101 is a great class with little work and straight forward assignments.  Uehling does a pretty good job with lecture, but can be a little dull sometimes. She's very clear and has a lot of experience to back up what she's talking about. She's also very accommodating to students if you need to ask her questions.

Sometimes interesting, sometimesnNot terribly interesting lectures but otherwise it was a good class, and she's a good professor. Not too much work. Sections are fun. Just study for the exams. She gives good study guides.

I think this was her first time teaching the course. Easy enough, lecture attendance was completely unnecessary, but interesting if you went. Quizzes can be done with the readings open. Exams are common sense. The two papers were simple enough. Hardest part about the class for me was its 8:30 discussion. Apart from that, easy and interesting.
2 exams, 2 papers, quizzes every week. Sometimes the hour and a half lectures drag on but Uehling has an interesting background and knows what she's talking about.
Professor lacks empathy for students
Its a good class and she is approachable.

I think Dr Yixin is a good hearted professor. she is very knowledgeable, but her exam is very tough. Claims that it is similar to past exam, but reality it is much harder. She is very kind and generous, and I wish she teaches the classes with more motivation! So much potential but I think for now needs improvements

Easy midterm, lots of coding. She does a great job of explaining deep learning concepts in an intuitive way. Involves some linear algebra but in general not too bad. The final has coding and was a bit tough, but the grading was generous so not bad.

Since this is the first time she taught this course, the grading criteria for some homework question and the final report may not be super clear. But given the generous grading scale (same as historical distribution on atlas), that shouldn't matter that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Coding focused course with some math/stats concepts. Multiple choice midterm but final has coding questions. All coding homework. Decent class and grading.
Interesting course. Final is a bit tough but the grades are eventually okay
Very generous and passionate professor. Very clear lectures
Chill assignments and quizzes. Deep learning course, mostly programming focused. No requirements for attendance.
exciting material. The professor is very nice and very responsive to student feedback.
very passionate professor
Helpful and caring professor during office hours. Very receptive to feedback
challenging course but practical. lectures include many practical demos. learned a lot.
passionate teacher, heavy workload, but interesting class
weekly homework; quite a learning curve at the start but get much better post midterm. content is interesting.

So, so confusing. This was one of the most disorganized classes I have ever taken. The lectures are confusing, the topics are all over the place, and the homework does not cover what is taught in the class. Also, as this was marketed as a theory class, the emphasis on learning new coding languages, especially for the final, was really frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: weekly quizzes; weekly homework.
fine lectures. interesting class.

The class is quite disorganized, and Prof Wang certainly did not deliver the contents well. I understood those, only because I am already familiar with stats theory. The homeworks are easy Google Colab assignments, which I don't think matches what's taught in lectures.

Her lectures are confusing. Her homework assignments are confusing. Even the solutions to the homework are confusing. Her office hour only makes you more confused. Overall, she is a confusingly terrible professor. Through the semester, even if I get an A, I still have to say I never understood what she talked about. She wasted my whole semester.

She was a terrible lecturer, and her lecture slides/examples were difficult to follow. Her iteration of 451 was too bad-structured since she wanted to reorganize the course with more materials but did a really bad job in integrating them. Take it only if you don't care about statistics but only need an A/A+ to boost your transcript.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know why there are some good ratings for IOE classes when we are discussing Yixin Wang in the STATS department. Avoid this professor at all costs I am going through hell right now in one of the easier classes I've taken at this school because of how unorganized and confusing this professor is. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.
The class covers some interesting and deep material. But Needs good preparation and hard work to understand. Enthusiastic instructor. Easy homework.
Easy grading but I learned close to nothing as the lectures are unclear and theoretical. Super easy homework. Can feel her enthusiasm but don't know how to teach.
First half is awfully boring math. But the latter half was more practical and interesting about the practice of deep learning. Weekly assignments and weekly quizzes and a final project.
The course material was challenging. But homework was easy. The instructor was very enthusiastic.
Reasonable midterm. No finals. Easy class.

This class's prerequisite does not prepare me well to take it. I don't understand most of the stuff she was talking about and even the textbooks assume you already know a lot. The class is disorganized and quiz questions are not covered in lectures. You can definitely tell she is enthusiastic about the subject and is willing to help tho
The class is way too theoretical. all statistics theory; nothing actual about data analytics.
Completely useless class. Everything shown in class are theoretical stuff. If you want to be a statistician, come. Otherwise, avoid at all cost.
She seems enthusiastic about the material. The course has no exams.
Fair

Class is highly disorganized. She tends to cover many fancy stuffs in class but doesn't explain them clearly. Lectures are useless, or the professor herself is useless in learning course material. She doesn't quite want to answer students' questions in great detail but in a vague sense. Definitely avoid at all cost.

Lectures are unclear and theoretical, but homework is mostly practical. A high workload class, but the workload doesn't come from the practical nature of Bayesian statistics, but the annoying pre-lecture questions and post-lecture quizzes. Can somehow feel the professor are enthusiastic, but she really cannot teach. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: one of the worst professor. There's a quiz in every single class. Hmm—I don't want to go into too many details, but I believe his grading is highly subjective (depending on whether or not he likes you).
Very nice professor, makes sure his students understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Dr Weiss as a professor for Math215! He used drawings to explain a lot of concepts, and spent time making sure he explained concepts clearly. His office hours are also incredibly helpful for homework help or conceptual questions.
One of the best professors I've ever had

Math 215 is a very independent and time-consuming course with challenging material. The homework is difficult, but Professor Weiss explains concepts clearly and his lectures are easy to follow. He is straightforward, which is appreciated, and the recorded videos are very helpful. Overall, the course requires consistent effort outside of class.

Michael Weiss is the greatest calc 3 professor of all time. He saved us from the examinations from another planet that Dunworth gave us. Was behind on pacing all year but it is justified because you need to prepare the students for the wrath of Dunworth. Funny as well.

Simply put, I passed Calc III because of Weiss. His clear, logical explanations of concepts that other professors explained way too abstractly helped me "decode" some atrocious exam questions that would have otherwise left me still pondering what they were asking in an exam hall to this day. Would HIGHLY recommend him for any math class

Great lecturer, took my 15 yo sister to a lecture and she understood. He does run out of time at least once per week, so you will have to watch additional instructional videos (which are great btw) to keep up with the class. Tests were hard but there's dozens of practice exams available. Weekly problem sets are tough but lots of office hours open.
Best Math215 Professor in the entire Umich math department. He uses lecture time to do lots of examples with us so that we understand the content the best we can. He is the best.

Weiss is one of the better lecturers for MATH 215. However, he would often run out of time and spend some lecturers diving deep into practice problems that were either unnecessarily complicated or extremely simple. He went very in depth with some topics, maybe too in depth, making the class watch videos outside of lecture because he ran out of time

Loved his class. He gave good commentary on the material, provided videos to watch outside of class, and I think went more in depth than his peers. He's also very nice.

Despite this, the class itself is quite challenging and was by far my most difficult class this semester.

Professor Weiss is a very clear and engaging lecturer who provides extra videos when concepts need reinforcement. He is extremely accessible and genuinely cares about his students. When my friend and I emailed similar concerns, his detailed, thoughtful response stood out compared to a one-sentence reply from another professor.
Weiss is my favorite Math professor that I have had so far at Michigan! Incredible lecturer and explains very difficult concepts in a digestible way.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By far the best math 215 prof, explains everything really well
Weiss was an incredible Math 215 professor! He explained everything in detail and took time for questions. Definitely an amazing professor.

I took 217 in the Spring half term. To no fault of Weiss, that class is not built to be taught in such a short amount of time. That being said, he was very accessible and incredibly helpful and encouraging, and did a great job at setting expectations. I highly suggest taking 217 with Weiss, just don't take it in the Spring if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best prof for 215 but that isn't saying too much… Could tell he was really interested in the material and was a good teacher one on one but was always behind on content. Also, his office hours were super helpful—he just always showed up 15-20 min late.
He saved my GPA and understanding of the class in the end. I am forever grateful to this professor. He is a bit disorganized, but well so am I
Math 215 is difficult class, but Professor Weiss explains the material very clearly and is always happy to help students with any questions they have.

Dr Weiss was teaching the class for the first time and was juggling teaching 215 as well, but was by far the best math teacher I've had in terms of patience and explaining concepts until students understand. As far as math department standards go, he is well above the norm, and I highly recommend taking him (and 205) for future students.

I understand MATH205 is a newer course, but the professor lacks any actual preparedness for the class. He wasted a large part of the semester stressing the importance of graphing to a group of students majoring in statistics, data science, and social science. When faced with his ineptness, he combats students with passive-aggressive behaviors...

The best 215 professor. Although the class is hard, he explained everything extremely well. Going to office hours is a godsend and he is always so willing to explain things again and again until you understand them!!! 1000% reccomend!
Great prof, the best of Math 215, featuring well-prepared, clearly explained lectures.

Phenomenal prof. Class is inquiry-based learning, but whenever he gives explanations or lectures, he makes the math seem very intuitive/approachable. Extremely likable and easy to talk to for help. The homework and exams are brutal, but he offers a fair amount of help on piazza with clear hints. Great professor teaching a hard class.

Dr Weiss was an excellent teacher and gave a really strong understanding of calculus. He took time with the concepts to make them as intuitive and understandable as he could. This does have its downsides though, as he will get through course content slower to better explain and then has to rush through the last bit before an exam. But overall 10/10

Best lecturer on campus for a calc class I've had (umich students know that most calc I-IV instructors are...questionable). Takes the time to meet students out of class (very accommodating). He's the type of instructor where it feels like he could teach a kindergartener this math, he can explain it in so many ways. I miss profs like this :(
fun and explains material clearly
Absolutely amazing professor. Yes calc 3 is hard but he explains the content very clearly and is very supportive of his students. This class made me fall in love with math.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 215 is really hard and lots of work, but Prof. Weiss teaches it about as well as one can. Lectures are dense and not really interactive, but if you pay attention, he explains concepts clearly and connects difficult topics well. His office hours + Piazza are very helpful for completing written homeworks, which can take hours.

Really great lecturer. Calc III is so hard but I genuinely enjoy it in his class. He does a great job of working through tough concepts and making them feel accessible. Would absolutely take another class with him again, best math prof I've had so far. Way more enjoyable than Calc I or II here at UM.

I had a decent experience overall with Professor Weiss, despite MATH217 being the most difficult and misery-inducing class I have ever taken. He knows the material well and offers very clear explanations. He does have a bit of a short fuse, however, and I witnessed him snap at a few students this semester. Stay on his good side!

Michael Weiss is the best math professor I've ever had. Calc 3 was a difficult class, but he made it clear what everything meant and explained concepts clearly. Before his class I wasn't even sure if I liked mathematics a lot, but his class made me fall in love with the subject material.

Dr. Weiss explains concepts so thoroughly and really helps you understand the reasoning behind every concept and technique used in calculus. A very accessible professor and willing to help his students, you can tell he truly loves teaching math. Be prepared for him to change the way you approach math, definitely one of the best out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Altogether, I liked Dr. Weiss. Maybe it was just my past experience with calc in high school, but he made MATH 115 very easy // although, he does goes off-tangent A LOT.

OK, so I took Math 215 last year but just got on rate my professor and needed to give Prof. Weiss a shoutout. Math 215 was the hardest class I have ever taken, and I barely passed, but that wouldn't have been without Prof. Weiss. He made the material seem do-able and he was always willing to help. 10/10 great guy, Math 215 as a class: 0/10

Michael Weiss is by far my favorite professor that I've had so far at UM. He explains difficult and abstract concepts in a way that makes them very clear and easy to understand. He is always willing to help and has a very unique way of connecting students to challenging material with the least amount of struggle.

Dr Weiss is an outstanding professor. I took his calc III class and although it is an incredibly difficult course, I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures and learned a ton from them. He truly cares about his students success and has a deep knowledge of the material.

Calc 3 is a pretty tough class with lots of new concepts. The exams were awful, but that's not the fault of Weiss. Weiss is a very clear and interesting lecturer, who loves using examples and visuals in Geogebra to get you to learn. He's also a super nice guy. If you have the choice to take a math class with Weiss, do it.
You thought you had a better choice but NO you don't. He is the better choice - the best choice for math 215 (if you are not an exceptional math person).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very boring class, uses lots of examples, but not the basic details that we need for each concept. Not very responsive to email, hard to reach out him outside of class.

His lectures are very clear and he never lost my attention throughout the class. My main issue is I had trouble keeping track of what was expected of me and often had to resort to other sources to learn how to solve the homework. He does a great job in teaching the textbook material, but could be better for preparing us to do well in the class.
easily the best prof i've had at umich, i never leave ratings for professors, but she is literally so amazing that i have to leave a review! if you're looking for a FYW class, 10000% recommend her!!

I took English 124 with her this semester. I would recommend anyone who has to do a FYWR to take her section of English. She's an awesome person who cares a lot about her students and always gives detailed feedback on essays. If you have time, show up to her office hours because she's an enjoyable person to get to know outside of the classroom.
TAKE. THIS. CLASS. You will quite literally not regret it--- Adelay was a Godsend.
She so good

I absolutely adore Adelay and the dynamic that she has with her students is unmatched. I think what I appreciate most about her is despite being our professor, she treats her students like her peers or equals, and she often tells us that she learns as much from us as we learn from her. She is energetic and so personable and TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take Adelay's class, DO IT!!! She is so kind and understanding. Her class was the highlight of my semester. The workload was very light so it fit well in my busy schedule. She truly cares about her students and makes class feel like family!

Adelay is one of my favorite people ever, she is truly so amazing as a person and a professor. If you can, you should definitely take her class! She is really the most caring person out there for her students and I am so appreciative for her. She also structures her class very well. I would look forward to her class everyday and am sad to leave.

I LOVE Adelay! If you can get her for this class, I would definitely recommend it. She is the sweetest, kindest person, and truly respects her students and wants them to learn. I genuinely looked forward to her class and I'm sad to leave. Lots of reading, but they're pretty enjoyable and light. Just put in the effort and you will reap the rewards.

I loved taking her class. She is extremely caring and understanding. The readings she assigns are unique and the class is designed like a Socratic seminar style with lots of collaboration. Overall, she is the best teacher I have had so far, and I find myself reminiscing on her class. She also gives excellent written feedback and notes!

She is an amazing teacher, very caring towards her students and checked up on all of us individually throughout the semester. She assigned a solid amount of readings but they were all interesting and didn't feel like busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING! Was the most caring person, and I definitely recommend taking a class with her if you have the option. Makes the first-year writing requirement seem fun and interesting!

An absolute gem. I was a little nervous to take an english class for the first time in a while. She cares about you and your mental health. She is so understanding and although there is a fair amount of work, everything is very clearly laid out as far as what is expected. If you don't take her class, you are missing out.

Adelay is an absolute saint. She brings an upbeat yet chaotic energy to every class and handled everything thrown at us in the COVID semester with understanding. She loves what she does and truly cares about her students. A really easy grader, but still provides solid feedback to make you into a better writer.

Adelay is the most empathetic professor I've had. She has you submit a cover letter with each paper explaining not only why you chose to write what you did but gives you the opportunity to explain what you were going through while writing it so that she can grade you paper accordingly. If you're on the fence about taking her course, do it.
Greatest English teacher! So kind and gives great feedback on papers. She wants you to focus on your writing so she grades rather easily.

Best teacher ever. She offers an incredible amount of feedback, grade easily, and even brings snacks for the class. She also lets you create your own rubric as a class for each essay so you know exactly what to expect. Don't take 125 without her!

Adelay is incredible. She cares so much about what she teaches her students and she always comes to class full of energy and a smile on her face. I learned a lot in her class, she is so special and just wants everyone to learn. She always put a smile on my face.

Adelay is absolutely amazing - a really fantastic instructor and great person. Go out of your way to take her. She is an easy grader because she wants her students to focus on their writing, not their grade. TAKE HER! She is so kind, willing to meet you halfway, and she really is a good teacher. I've learned a lot in her class and felt happyinclass

English 125 with Adelay was, without a doubt, one of the best classes that I've taken at UM. She genuinely cares about each and every one of her students and is determined to make sure everyone learns. This class was a blast and something that I looked forward to every week. To anyone looking for an English class, you can't go wrong with Adelay.

TAKE ADELAY'S CLASS she is the best human being in the whole world and she actually cares about her students so much its crazy. I know this class is a requirement and a lot of people take it just as the requirement and think they'll just have to suffer through it but if you take it with Adelay you don't have to suffer through it I promise!

Adelay always showed up to class excited and ready to teach. She brought enthusiasm and pure joy every day, and she cared about each student's experience equally. She is by far the best teacher I have ever had in a class, no contest. If you have any chance to take her, I suggest doing so. You will not regret it and the class will be unforgettable.

Best professor I've ever had. She is the most caring soul I've ever met and she really loves her students. She gives back really good detailed feedback on papers. She also wants to give everyone an A so she is always willing to put in extra time with you to get you there. She also takes into account your own class schedule and personal issues. love
Adelay is absolutely amazing! She is so enthusiastic about teaching and tries to get to know all of her students. It's clear that she genuinely cares and wants every student to succeed.

Adelay is an excellent instructor and really cares about her students. You can tell that she takes her time when she grades essays and gives copious amounts of insightful, helpful feedback. She is highly personable and willing to go out of her way to meet with her students. A few times she brought snacks to class which is always a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Adelay is very enthusiastic. She puts in more work than other 125 instructors and she expects more from her students in return.
Great teacher! Would definitely take her again. Respects students to the fullest.
Overall great teacher. Adelay is so cool and respects each and everyone of her students. Take a class with Adelay!
Fair grader and nice guy. Weekly readings, but they are not due until the end of the semester. Make sure to check his announcements because he posts readings and due dates outside Canvas.
Mr. Welch is such an engaging teacher. I look forward to his class every time because of the energy he brings. If you are looking for a laid-back, caring teacher, Mr. Welch is your guy.

Mr. Welch is an awesome and engaging teacher. He cares about every student and encourages everyone to make an effort to participate in class. A part of his grading scale is overall improvement, so if you incorporate his feedback, you should get an A. I recommend that anybody who has the opportunity to take a class offered by Mr. Welch do so.

Professor Welch is absolutely amazing. He is very passionate about literature and giving students feedback. He is so thorough for each assignment, doesn't give insane readings, and grades VERY fairly. He also has the most inviting and eccentric character. I'm not the biggest fan of English, but I would take another class if it were with him.
Can tell he cares about material. He makes jokes often and his inclass activities are usually interesting.   I found the homework material and readings pretty boring.

I love him! We had some interesting projects and I felt like he always graded pretty fairly. He was always accessible and loved giving quality feedback which I appreciated. He's a little awkward but he's super smart. Overall, I felt like I became a better writer because of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you need to fulfill your FYWR I highly recommend taking this class! Prof. Welch is a very kind and understanding person. He grades based on improvement so you can still get an A regardless of a bad score at the beginning of the semester. There are readings every class (attendance is required), but they're very simple. Great guy and funny af.

Mr. Welch is an amazing professor, and I would recommend anyone to take his class. It was interesting and engaging, even for someone who doesn't like English. The grading is simple, and you always know what is expected of you, but he gives you almost full freedom on every assignment.

Professor Welch is such a great teacher. He grades on improvement, so even if you get a C on the first assignment, you can still end with an A. Attendance is mandatory, but you can skip as long as it doesn't become repeated. You'll have plenty of time to complete assignments, just make sure you communicate with him if you need an extension.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor. He's a bit awkward, nice, and open in class and during office hours. Won't call on students, so participation doesn't really matter, but it's nice to have people talk to keep the class engaging, especially since it's a small class (20ish students). Class was often boring, but it was easy - just do the work, which was light anyway.

Professor Welch is a great professor. He really cares for his students and wants them to succeed. Throughout the semester we did several projects that had little guardrails, allowing for us to make them our own. Overall, a good course and professor.

Overall, Shawn Welch is great. Most others in my class rarely ever participated or engaged with him, so their experience reflected that. But talking with Professor Welch about the subject matter makes the class infinitely more enjoyable. He thrives on student interaction, yet he doesn't quite enforce participation enough. The work is light too.

Super nice guy. Very weird. Doesn't really care that much if you miss class as long as you tell him. Graded us on improvement. Never did a reading before class and was fine. Started a project the day before it was due and got an A. Very easy.

Mr. Welch is a good professor, but boring at times. He wants students to lead class discussion but he doesn't force participation. So, often class was silent and boring. He doesn't lecture, the class is analyzing texts (children's literature for my class) and there were 6 assignments (3 small writing ones and 3 bigger projects).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was really good at explaining course concepts and super accessible outside class. Very highly recommend if you are taking EECS 183 and are taking the c++ section.
Very good professor for introductory courses

Bill is a great guy and lecturer. The hardest part of this class is the last few projects. The staff is very helpful if you get stuck on them. I found eecs 183 challenging because I've never coded before but Bill did a good job explaining things during lectures.
Bill is a great professor! Super nice and caring to students. Pacing during lectures can be a bit inconsistent, but manageable.

I didn't end up needing the lectures, but when I attended them, they were thorough and he was clearly caring despite the large class, always answering questions before moving on. The class itself is fine, though the sharp increase in project workload can make it feel like a weeder.

Professor Arthur is one of my favorite professors so far. Very friendly and funny. Only downside about this class is having to do 5 projects (first 2 are easy but the last 3 can be time consuming and difficult)  but besides that this class is pretty easy if you pay attention.

He's definitely beginner friendly and his lectures were typically engaging and interesting. By textbook I'm referring to the zybooks, which I think was an amazing resource and helped me understand the concepts, with his lectures expanding more on said concepts and showing more examples. This course is set up nicely and I enjoyed the group projects!

Personally, I didn't find lectures very helpful since we used zybooks to learn the content before going to class. However, I still went to ask questions and get exam review practice. Professor Arthur was the absolute GOAT and he was a very easygoing professor. For anyone without prior coding experience, Professor Arthur is the man to have.

I loved Professor Arthur! He was always extremely willing to answer any questions, and explained everything very well. The class is very work-heavy, with lots of homework and very time consuming projects, but he was very helpful, and I am glad I took this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures are very good and understandable, especially as a student with no prior knowledge. He does go fairly slow, but I appreciated that as someone who had never coded before. He is very nice and respects his students, I would definitely recommend him!
he is a nice person, but he sometimes cannot explain things clearly during lectures. There is too much unnecessary homework (zybooks and codelab), which is really annoying.

Professor Arthur is a great lecturer and really cares, but EECS 183 wasn't the best for me. There is always something due like Zybooks, labs, projects, or exams (even for a 4 credit class). Labs and lectures are required, but you get some drops. No final exam which is nice. Stay on top of work, start projects early, and study super hard for exams.

Explains complex concepts in a clear way that people new to cs can understand, and also made it fun. Lectures were basically word for word from the online textbook, but still helpful. Projects were got increasingly more difficult, but nothing too bad. Easy A imo.
Great lectures, he's really friendly and explains concepts very well, in a way that guides you through his thinking and leads you to the answer. Funny guy, too.

EECS 183 was a lot of work, but he was a super chill professor. He had office hours where you could come and meet with him directly, too. There's extra credit for turning in the projects early. Overall, not hard to get an A if you do all the work and study for the exam, but it was a lot of work.
I do not like this man. He is mean. He makes me sad.

Awesome professor & very nice, passionate guy! I hated coding going into 183, but Bill's class became my favorite and inspired my CS minor. Lectures are engaging & he clearly wants everyone to learn. The course moves pretty fast, but he does a great job of breaking it down. Very helpful at office hours too. HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking a class with him

Amazing professor. Class could be difficult without prior coding experience but he does a fairly great job at going through all the concepts and providing extra help where necessary. No complaints about the teacher at all.
Very nice guy and held engaging lectures. Made it very easy to do well in the class and was always willing to help or direct students to where they can get help.
Good lecturer and awesome person. Was annoying to wait for several weeks for exam 2 grades but it was because he didn't require his staff to work over spring break

Bill is amazing, he's super sweet and very knowledgeable. His lectures are helpful. As someone with no prior coding experience, lectures were taught well. The class is a bit of work (code lab,zybooks and lab assignments every week + 4 projects throughout the semester (also 2 exams), but manageable if you start on time. office hours are helpful

Professor Arthur is a nice person, but I found his lectures to be subpar. The unclear lectures combined with the terrible setup of EECS 183 made the class time-consuming. This is partly out of his control, but the monthly projects were nearly impossible to get feedback on, requiring me to sit in online queues for hours.

Bill was a wonderful professor! He is extremely kind and caring and wants everyone to succeed. We do have iclicker during lectures for participation points along with zybooks and codelab homework. I would recommend you to start early on the projects, especially after project 2 so that you have enough time to finish. All in all, a very doable class!

I loved Prof Arthur! He was very enthusiastic and his passion for computer science is very obvious. He is very engaging and is willing to answer any and all questions. I would definitely take another course of his if I could!

Bill is a delightful, down to earth person, and his lectures really sparked my interest in computer science and engineering. The class can be intensive, but if you use your resources, you will do fine. He quite obviously loves what he does and the people he does it with. I would HIGHLY recommend him for EECS183. Also, his voice is weirdly soothing.

Prof. Arthur explained things really well and the class was pretty interesting/not too hard for a non-CS major w/ no prior experience. Sometimes he was a little condescending when answering in-lecture questions which was annoying but I liked his teaching style. Study for exams, get a good group for projects, and you'll be fine!
Make sure to study for the exams. Everything else in the class is fairly easy.

Zybooks (you have to pay for this) is definitely useless and doing it is a waste of time. Professor Bills is good at communicating with students but sometimes he is not so good at explaining things clearly. Will recommend skipping 183 and going straight to take 280 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: W. Arthur is a W professor. He is very energetic and enthusiastic when it comes to his lectures. He is very approachable and helpful when it comes to questions. He has a great sense of humor and makes coding enjoyable.

tests can be tricky if you don't pay attention...one of the only classes I have had where the multiple choice is harder than the free response. Get ready to hand-write code too (sucks), lol.

I got a 103 in this class. Workload is chill if you plan accordingly and start ahead of time. Do the code labs and zybooks early, lecture is kind of pointless

Really awesome professor who explains concepts clearly and respects students. The projects for 183 do require a lot of work and time management but if you follow the schedule timeline you should be good! Overall a really fun class that made me more interested and excited in computer science. Lecture attendance and lab attendance mandatory.

Really nice professor!! Good at explaining, so definitely attend lecture as much as you can. Projects get more difficult as the semester goes on, so start early and ask for help. Exams are also difficult, but I would say start studying early and take practice exams. Probably the best professor available for EECS 183 so I would recommend taking him.

Bill is a super nice and super helpful teacher. I felt that the class was graded extremely fairly and that he was always understanding if something came up. Get started on projects early and be sure to use office hours as necessary.

The main reason I would not take his classes again is computer science hasn't been my favorite. It's pretty easy to get A if you do your work, but the projects were bad, especially since the office hour queue was often 4+ hours long. If you get a good group, the project will be easier, but a bad group/partner could mean a lot of work for you.

Professor Arthur was a good teacher and always seemed to explain the concepts pretty clearly to me. There's a clear structure to each assignment and project. I wish there was a better way to do office hours as the queues would sometimes get way too long, and you'd end up having to wait 3 hours for one simple question.

I had no coding experience going into EECS 183. Professor Arthur is a great lecturer and professor, but the class itself was difficult for me. Office Hours queues are so long that they basically become inaccessible most days, especially if you have other classes and extracurriculars.

Bill was a great professor. I thought he taught EECS183 extremely well, and that the course was well structured. Make sure to go to lab (attendance points are really important), and start working on projects earlier rather than later. Overall, the class is a GREAT intro to CS and its very possible to get an A.

Very structured class. Clear guidelines, although the spec can be a bit iffy at times. Bill was great, engaging and fun. Kind of sucks that attendance is mandatory though. I will say though that maybe teaching C++ as the language for an intro level CS class isn't the smartest idea, but that's not Bill's fault. TAKE BILL FOR 183!

As someone who had never coded before 183, I struggled in this course. Prof. Arthur lectured and gave practice exercises in class. I understood the information, but sometimes struggled to understand his explanations for exercises. Office hours are always available, but the queue can get really long. Highly recommend starting projects early!
Straight up fun lecturer, very engaging.

Bill is a great engaging lecturer and answers questions well. EECS 183 has so many resources outside of class, so anyone can succeed. Do all the work and start projects early, and you'll do fine. Lots of people I know ending with >95% and many with >100%. Only tough parts can be exams, but if you study and have been paying attention, it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Explains concepts very well and is generally available outside of class and quick to respond to emails.
10/10 prof. Some of the projects were a bit tough but his enthusiasm in class helped me push through :D

Great professor, very clear lectures. Also very accessible during and outside of class. I had no coding experience, but was able to do well in EECS 183 by putting in the necessary work. Arthur facilitates this for all of his student.

A very nice person and give very clear lectures. As a student who have learned CS a year already in another language, I can tell that this course is tough for beginners. You'd better study and have some CS background before taking this class. Tests are though. If you have the background, you can take the course like I do: Never attend class and lab
I love bill

Amazing professor. His lectures were very well detailed and welcoming, but I found them to be boring sometimes and I stopped attending towards the end of the course. By doing the projects and putting time into them, you will learn SO much about programming. I was surprised to see we used object-oriented programming, which was awesome.

Bill was amazing! I never coded before and got an A. It takes time but if you put in the work and follow the timeline its pretty easy. Hes an amazing prof, gives great lectures, and super helpful outside of class. Such a nice guy and genuinely gets excited about what he teaches.
Great professor, I learned a lot about coding in this course.

Bill was very excited when he gave lectures and made the lecture a lot more interesting than other professors. Although you do not get to know him on a personal level, he seems very caring and genuine and like a good guy.

A fantastic entry to coding (C++ and python) if you have never received any experience. There are many chances for extra credit, the homework and projects are not difficult but require setting time aside to complete. Professor Arthur writes the exams and ALWAYS wants questions and your curiosity. Never be scared to speak up and ask for help!

Bill really made sure that we understood what we were learning and how it applied in a real world context. I found that he made lecture interesting. He was also always open to questions. I would recommend Bill as a professor.

I came into EECS183 this semester having no previous coding experience, and Prof Arthur's teaching has made me begin to consider majoring in computer science. Excellent lectures, he's a great guy and very understanding, but of course, the class is a lot of work. Projects are hard but totally doable. Exams are challenging, but again, totally doable.
Fantastic asynchronous lectures for EECS 370. This guy is saving my grade!

Bill was a great professor and made me feel comfortable despite not having much coding experience before college. He was very caring and willing to spend extra time with students to discuss their grades and progress. The material was difficult at times but it was always engaging to learn.

Great professor that makes coding fun and approachable to everyone, even if you never had prior experience. Projects are time consuming but doable, and he is always willing to help guide you through projects outside of class. Overall a very time consuming class that can be infuriating at times, but he is one of the best to take it with.

I came into EECS 183 with no previous coding experience, but despite this Bill made the class enjoyable and perfectly doable. Bill is truly passionate about computer science and wants to see all of his students succeed. This course takes quite a bit of work but you will get out what you put in. I highly recommend taking this course with Bill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Bill Arthur is amazing! He is the best professor I have had and he made me always want to go to lecture.

Arthur was a good professor. He made the lectures interesting and he was sarcastic and made me laugh. Get a good planner because you won't be reminded about the many, many assignments and projects. His iClicker questions were very hard. He would test us, then teach us. It was hard for me to get iClicker credits despite attending most lectures.

Start the projects early and you will be fine. You only need 40 iClicker points and after that you don't have to attend lecture. Find partners for final project as early as possible. Exams are easy A if you practice writing code on paper.

Professor Arthur is a real gem! I had him over the summer and in EECS 183. He not only presented lecture materials clearly and was incredibly organized, but he goes above and beyond to share his path to success and offer many advice for his students. If I ever get into grad school or obtain a job, it was all due to his inspiration!

Fairly easy class with a pretty heavy workload. A good lecturer but most of the materials taught in lectures are already covered by Zybooks (the pre-reading assignment) so the lecture is sometimes dull. Overall a solid choice though.

I enjoyed Bill's lectures most out of the EECS 183 professors. He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about Computer Science. EECS 183 is a great choice for an introductory Computer Science class whether you have coded before or have no experience.
Bill yells and calls names at students. That is not nice.
Lots of projects and homework. Talks too much rather than teaches the materials. Didnt enjoy this class. Only good thing about this class is that there is no final exam.

This class is real tough. Professors are not there very long during office hours, and TAs are rude and know almost nothing helpful. Better to hire a tutor at the begin of term. This class made me sure that I am not going to take EECS anymore.
Oh man. This class was tough for me, but Prof Arthur was always incredibly patient and clear answering all my questions. I highly recommend!

Bill is a genuinely great guy and he made my introduction to coding very enjoyable. I'd recommend this class to literally everyone, regardless of concentration. Projects were quite easy, but make sure you start them early so that you don't have to worry about debugging on a deadline. Final project was very interesting.
Best intro EECS prof. Got me started in programming. Explains things clearly and answer student's questions. Passionate about the subject.

He is the best EECS183 professor out there. Don't think twice. The other people are average compared to him. He is very fun to talk to and incredibly smart. Loves to talk and talk and talk...... but its all interesting stuff. You will enjoy this class!

If you have to take this class, take it with Bill! He is infectiously passionate about the material and knows it inside and out. He's a great lecturer and always engaging no matter how early class starts
I was in a different professors lecture but went to his whenever possible because he was such a good instructor and made it really fun.

If you wanna get yourself into learning introductory CS, Bill's the guy! His lectures are really helpful for students to understand the content especially the i>Clicker questions. Whenever a student has doubts in lectures, Bill will make sure they are clarified right away. I don't intend to major in CS, but he made me start to like CS as a hobby.

Arthur was a great professor and I recommend eecs 183 to everyone because coding is a great skill. Only need to go to 10 lectures and get iclicker points and can skip the rest if you choose (theyre recorded). Very project heavy with very clear grading criteria and hours upon hours of office hours each week. Made me want to major in CS!

Definitely a great guy who likes the topic a lot. Didn't find the class too challenging after taking AP CS in high school but there were a few concepts that were new like input/output files and python. Pace of lectures was a little slow, but definitely liked the format. Bill is very knowledgeable and clearly likes teaching. Would recommend.
The class is hard no matter who you take, but definitely take BIll if you can

If you're gonna take EECS, people say Bill is the best. I'd say he did a really good job up until the final project, which wasn't laid out as clearly as I would have liked. I came in with no CS experience and didn't find the class too hard or heavy work-wise, except for 4 projects (10hr ea). Take the class pass fail and avoid the final project.
Great introduction class to coding with a very good professor and amazing IAs to help you. Be mindful of the class project load and difficulty of exams though.

Harvey Munson is the man! I had never taken CS before and I was very lucky to be in Arthur Miller's class this semester and have learned a lot. Bill Murray knows his stuff and is a really approachable guy. Robert also structures the class in a really cool way where you can attend any lab section. 10/10 would recommend  taking James Franklin's class
Very enthusiastic and respectful!

He explains material very very well and is very helpful during lecture.  However, his lectures do get very boring at times and dry (his small amount of humor doesn't make up for it). He also goes on tangents sometimes which aren't fun. All in all, he's still a pretty good lecturer so I recommend if you're just trying to understand the material

Professor Arthur was one of the best lecturers I have ever had.  He is very respectful, helpful and supportive when you are struggling.  I struggled in the course so much and I reached out to him multiple times and was left with hope that I could still succeed in the class.  I have never coded till his class and now I am considering minoring in CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I didn't know any cs before the course but I still felt like the class was way too slow. He goes really really slow. Someone else might be more engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Arthur is a caring individual. He always lectures with a smile and is always willing to answer any questions. Lectures are very heavy so reading is a must. iClickers are done daily for pts. The class is work load heavy so be prepared to do so many projects and assignments. Office hours and lecture recordings/slides are easily accessible
