You can go to any EECS183 lecture, but I think he was the best professor if you're actually wanting to learn the content.
Really understood the material he was teaching and was thorough enough where all the students understood the concepts, but didn't spend too long on anything.
Fun, engaging and never boring. You won't regret taking EECS 183 with this guy

Bill Arthur was a great professor in my opinion. I entered EECS 183 not knowing if computer science would be for me and now I want to major in it! Professor Arthur keeps his lectures engaging and covers important material more than once (return type, function name, parameter list). Overall, a good guy presenting engaging material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I heard he is the best instructor of eecs 183, and I think he is, although I haven't taken the other two professors' course. He is passionate about the course and explains everything clearly. The course material is actually too easy for me as I have already self learnt, but other fellow students say they learnt a lot.
Bill is great! He made his lectures easy to pay attention to and somewhat interactive. He also is very helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I found it to be an easy class b/c I took AP comp sci in high school, but  even if I hadn't, Bill did an excellent job of emphasizing the key points during lecture. Really preps his students for the tests, and he couldn't be a nicer guy. Very enthusiastic and fun to listen to. Only class I never wanted to skip.

EECS 183 is a tough class, but they fortunately allow you to go to any lecture. Go to Bill's lecture, as he is clear and very good at answering questions. Explains material in depth, and most importantly doesn't go too fast. Funny, patient guy who is there for his students. The biggest mistake I made was not going to his lectures sooner.

BEST EECS 183 professor, absolutely no doubt about it. Lectures are very clear even though they are a bit long. Bill is always super enthusiastic and nice. His office hours are also very helpful and it is worth going even if you don't have a project due soon. Even if you don't register for his lecture, you can go to any, so go to Bill's lecture.

Very engaging OUTSIDE the classroom. Please trust me in that it's very lucrative to meet with him in his office hours! They're almost always empty, and I was on a first name basis with him in the first 5 visits. Not gonna lie: it's a difficult class. Also a super USEFUL class. 1010 would recommend looking at CodeAcademy first for familiarity.

Due to the design of the course itself (at the moment), it is possible to take EECS 183 and pass without having attended a single lecture. However, Arthur's lectures are very helpful and he is very good at driving home important concepts and the importance of important concepts, all the while making his lecture entertaining.

You definitely have to go to class or she will be upset and start looking at you different/grading you lower even if your quality of work hasn't changed. also she was fighting a lil too hard to say the n word as a yt person ngl

This was my least favorite class I have ever taken. If you aren't gifted as both a writer and a mind reader do not take one of her classes. She constantly changes due dates as well as moving around the final exam. Little to no rubric and expects you to know exactly what she wants. If you don't participate in every conversation you will be gradedbad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Santamarina is a wonderful teacher. She is more than willing to help if you go to her office hours or email. This is not an easy class, but you will leave with a much greater understanding and a much better writer.  So take you won't regret!

Professor Santamarina is a passionate teacher. She regards her students well and considering the amount of reading in the class there is an equal amount of writing. If you are interested you will leave it with no regrets.

Professor Santamarina prefers to be called by that, don't make the mistake I did and call her by her first name. She is very knowledgable about what she teaches and also very passionate. There's a fair amount of writing in this class, essays for your exams and little, short, reading responses. I had little interest and the class was very dull to me

Professor Santamarina is a wonderful teacher. She has an enlightening way of teaching and is always willing to help. This class is for those who find the topic interesting and should not be seen as an easy A. You  will improve your writing and emerge a much better student.

Prof. Santamarina is an amazing teacher. Her insightful thoughts and clear discussions will challenging those who don't pay attention. She is incredibly helpful and kind. She has high writing standards but you are guaranteed to learn. I would suggest not to take her class if you want an easy A.

Santamarina is a prof. who will definitely challenge her students to go above and beyond. To receive an A in this class, your writing has to be perfect. If you're looking for an easy A, this is not the class to take. On one of our papers, the highest grade anyone received was a B/B+ (and only one person in the 15 person discussion got that grade).

Professor Santamarina seems better-suited for small class teaching than lecturing. She does seem very knowledgeable but has a habit of jumping all over the place in lecture. Sometimes very hard to follow, especially if you are not particularly interested in the subject.
can get off topic at times but offers good information; pay attention when she's speaking to avoid getting lost

Felt like her lectures were sort of all over the place. She's a very  nice person and pleasureable but not the best lecturer. Seems like she's more adapt to teaching in small sections rather than lectures. They are changing teachers next semester though and I've heard him lecture. He is awesome so I'd encourage taking the course.

She isn't bad, and she can get pretty entertaining when her moral/political views start sneaking into her lectures.  I have no real complaints.  The tests are more than fair, but GSI's easily find ways to not give you full credit.

personally I loved professor santamarina! this was a first year seminar and I highly recommend first year students to take a class of hers. she is helpul, informative, makes students feel comfortable. great topic of class, interesting literature. nice lady who more importantly is great at her job.
nice, but felt threaten a lot when student questioned her

Homework is usually a bit of reading and/or a short film to watch. Weekly tests consisting of questions from both the homework and the current day's lecture. You are graded by a points system, meaning if you reach a certain point threshold, then that determines at least the floor of your grade for the semester. Would highly recommend.

The goat. It wasn't really about fraud and manipulation in a psychological sense, but more from a historical and media portrayal perspective. Either way, it's an easy 1-credit class. You take quizzes about the reading/ class but they're easy.
Super easy and fun class. He has many opportunities to get an A, so there is no way he to do badly in his class.

Piotr is such a great professor. Attendance is not mandatory but you don't want to miss a lecture because they're very interesting if not very organized. I learned a lot about Polish history and culture and the material was always given to us.
Piotr is one of the best professors I've had at UMich, he cares about his students a lot. His office hours are very helpful, and he's a really funny guy.
easy and fun class. His teaching is always easy and relaxed, he tries his best to make non-intensive classes for SLAVIC 290. I took him twice, worth it both times

Piotr was really amazing. Lectures were great and interesting and projects weren't too difficult but you definitely have to try. However, he doesn't use canvas and there is no clear grading scheme. Make sure to watch the lectures the day they come out or you'll miss something, he organizes his classes different from every other teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Piotr's classes are always quite funny. No matter what, there is always something entertaining in his lectures, and the homeworks that he grades on are incredibly easy if you just show up to class, as he talks about all the questions.

Piotr is my favorite professor. He truly cares about his students and their learning/success. If you show up and pay attention, you will do well in the class. I would take any class he offers in a heartbeat.

Easy two credit class but grade was based on best 4/5 assignments with strict threshold for getting an A. You have to pay attention very well in class. Westwalewicz was funny and nice, however, if you are struggling with assignments, he will not help much. It was an interesting class and didn't have a heavy workload, it could just be  annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Piotr is a fabulous instructor who genuinely cares about his students. His style proves the antiquated dogmatic pedagogy of drilling and testing students to death doesn't always create a meaningful learning environment. Here, you actually engage in deep discussion about the world. Piotr shares real life experiences that hit home. Trust his process.
I LOVE HIM. Such a good 2 credit class, watching lectures is actually really interesting because he is so passionate. Super accessible outside of class too!
Very nice man!! Funny, forgiving, understanding, and ends class early. There's a test every week but he will do literally everything he can to get you at least a B+.

THE BEST INSTRUCTOR. I seriously have no complaints. Piotr kept me going when I got frustrated and confused and he offers many extra credit opportunities. Also just a super funny and charismatic instructor. If you can take any class with him, do it.
Nicest dude you'll ever meet. Fun lectures. Only downside is having to turn hw in in-person outside his office door but honestly can't complain because it made me wake up before 1 on Fridays
Very fun 1-credit class, professor is passionate about the subject and the class is very interesting. Would recommend
Really interesting class taught by an interesting guy. Take him if you have any interest in Eastern Europe. He's also really nice to talk to outside of class if you see him in the halls.

This class is amazing! I learned so much in 1 semester. Quizzes are decently easy if you study. Lots of in-class participation. You can tell he loves his job and really cares about his students. If you're taking a language, take it with him.
Absolutely amazing anyone who takes one of his classes will love him.

Piotr is one of the best professors I have ever taken a course with, and I have taken 5 classes with him at this point and keep coming back. The material is fun and interactive and he cares about your engagement and interest in the material. He is also one of the most accessible professors I've had and he is always willing to meet outside of hours.
I loved Professor Piotr's Slavic 290 class, his style of lecture is very informative and fun. He is easy going and is always willing to help each and every student.
Best Professor at UMich. Take any of the classes you can with him (Slavic 290, Slavic 151, Polish 214) You won't be disappointed.

Hated writing in high school but this was probably my favorite class I took as a freshman. Such an insightful, helpful, & funny teacher. Lots of interesting discussions & he's not looking to be right he truly wants your perspective. Moderate amount of writing & somewhat abstract concepts, but for me this made it more interesting not more difficult.

Very caring professor. He wants you to succeed and he is very accessible. You can text him at any time. He also drops your three lowest grades you have a lot of leeway and opportunities to get an A. Overall, awesome professor.

This class was supposed to be about nationalism and Eastern Europe but we literally only talked about pop culture in Poland. Lectures consisted of watching videos accompanied by his ever present commentary. It was more like watching news with your angry uncle than actually sitting through class. Unreasonable work load even if it is graded easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Piotr cares about his students as he will make to talk for office hours regardless of how busy he is. I would make use of his advise since he gives useful detailed advise during personal conversations. Slavic 151's topic were a little confusing. Piotr often would drag out discussions until the class made a specific point he was looking for.

Took this class with him my first semester and from what I've heard about the other first year writings, this is one of the best ones to take. There are 4 main papers that make up 80% of your grade, they're usually 5-8 pages. Going to lecture is mandatory, and there are small writing and reading assignments. There's make up assignments/papers too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took this class for my FYWR after looking at what other students wrote about him and most of it is true, but there is some things that have changed. There was 4 papers 6-10 pages long, decent amount of short writing assignments (but you only need to successfully complete 4) and in class participation DOES NOT MATTER. Take it if good writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Okay, Piot is very nice and funny. He's a great guy. Don't get me wrong. But this is the most boring class I've ever been in. Piotr doesn't read english well, so if you write a bomb. com essay, you'll get a C. Frustrating. You have to write very simple, with short words. Like, what should be a C essay. It didn't help to further my education here.

He is a caring, sweet person and you should definitely take his slavic 290 class. Graded by 6-8 in-class short quizzes which are easy if you pay attention to what he says. Also offers an optional essay if you're not doing good on the quizzes. Overall, his slavic 290 was a good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Piotr is an absolute beast. Show up, watch music videos, write 2 essays, get an A+. He presents the material to be very interesting as well. Just show up and put an ounce of effort and get an A. Best class at U of M.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Piotr is the GREATEST. Super nice guy and the class was insanely easy but really interesting. We only had two papers, and if you were happy with your grade on the first one you could write the second one as pass/fail. I highly recommend taking a class with Piotr, easily one of my favorite profs.

Piotr is my all-time favorite professor. He's insightful, funny, and the class is incredibly easy. Just show up to class (attendance is mandatory) and you'll pass with flying colors. Seriously, I got an A+. He tells funny stories about his life (which always relate to the lecture topic), and is so approachable. I love this man.

Such an easy class. 3 papers, but only counts top 2 scores so if you do well on the first 2 then you don't even have to write the third. Have to attend every class but don't have to participate. Not super exciting material unless you're really into music videos, but definitely super easy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Christ, do not take this course. If you do, take it pass fail so the impossible quizzes don't matter as much.

Do not take. The worst minicourse at Michigan. He makes it seem like it will be impossible to not get an A, but he MAKES IT IMPOSSIBLE. He's a hard grader, the quizzes ask ridiculous questions , and you frankly don't learn much.

Amazing professor- seriously one of the most insightful and inspiring professors I've had. I took this class to fulfill my first year writing requirement and absolutely loved it. He made the content extremely interesting and thought-provoking. I plan on taking more classes with him in the future. Don't miss your chance to take a class with him.

Piotr is awesome, Slavic 151 was my favorite class. The class fulfills the FYWR but is a lot more fun than some of the other writing classes. You watch videos and listen to music all the time and you just follow along in the course pack he prints. He is hilarious and really wants you to get a good grade. Highly recommend taking any of his classes!

Funniest teacher I have ever had. Wants you to get an A in the class, he drops half your lowest grades and the longest paper you write is 4 pages. Class mainly consists of watching videos, so you don't have to pay attention and there are no readings. He's funny and really nice, wish his other classes didn't have full waiting lists right now.

Piotr prints off coursepack materials for everyone before class so you don't really have to buy anything, and his classes are pretty easy as long as you do the work. 221 language class - if you're not there, you won't know what's on the weekly tests. lots of songs used! 215 - couple papers, 4 simple presentations, no tests. Moviessongs in class

Piotr is one of the best professors out there! He is engaging, fun to be around, and very knowledge about Poland. Not only are assignments interesting, but this class is extremely easy.  Piotr gives you multiple chances to get the best grade possible and only uses your best scores to calculate your final grade.
Piotr is a unique professor who is very down to earth, and loves giving out A's to his students. Go to class, take notes, you will get an A. Great professor, great class, I highly recommend it!

The class was REVAMPED. It is pretty difficult now. It is no longer an easy class. The class is also really boring. I'm sorry Piotr was not up to par in teaching either. The class is one of the worst classes I've ever taken.

bro, this class is no longer a blow off. everyone gives him 5/5 because everything is so easy but he must of gotten mad because each semester as teh course gets more developed he adds in more work. this past semester there were 2 papers and a final and attendance was mandatory. bro

Best professor at the University of Michigan. Polish 214 is a must have for everyone in the University. He makes it easy for everyone to get an A, his class is the most interesting and fun class offered at the University. Great, absolutely great professor.

Easy class.  Piotr is great!! He gives everybody the opportunity to get an A and he is really fair.  The topics you write about are clearly stated in lecture and he loves originality and creativity.  He is such a nice guy and really knows a lot about his subject.  I really enjoyed having him as a teacher.

This dude is so great for so many reasons. I will name two. He honestly values creativity and free will on the part of his students. He actually lived through what he is teaching about (regarding the Polish Rock class). The class is awesome, you spend most the time listening to music that you otherwise would have never discovered. Don't miss class.

one of the best classes at UofM and there are lots of great classes here, Piotr allows you to ask questions without needing to answer them, he lets you think critically, encourages you to disagree with him and relishes it when you do, overall amazing teacher, class is also very easy and highly entertaining, as is Piotr

Piotr is an EXCELLENT professor for an EXCELLENT course; nowhere else at the U of M will you find a course and professor combination as awesome as this one. Piotr is very laid back and humorous, and makes class extremely interesting. Assignments can actually be fun to do, and he is very, very helpful if you need any assistance. TAKE HIM!

only in college could you find a class like this and its very interesting. piotr is an excellent lecturer and he really wants his students to do well. yes, its an easy A, but you do have to make sure that your response papers are thoughtful and grammatically correct to get that A. i wish i could take the class again, i loved it so much!
If you can't get an A in this class, quit school.  Seriously.
Easy class and fairly interesting.  Just make sure your 1 page papers are grammatically correct and you'll have an A.  Good job Piotr.
I love piotr!!!! Hes the best teacher ever!!!!

Too bad this is a minicourse. I was not interested in the course at all but took it on a whim. Piotr is da bomb. Very organized. Attendance mandatory. Easy to get an A. Definitely opened my eyes to many things. I didn't think the two hours dragged by like some people have said. Highly recommended. Plus, he wears soccer gear to class = baller.

Awesome teacher, and great class (if you like new-wave post-punk polish rock).  I had him as a substitute in another class a couple of times, and he definitely is good teacher even outside of this music minicourse.  He tells you right away that it's hard not to get an A in the class.

Best class ever! I learned more new things in these 6 sections than I do in two semesters worth of math. They should make classes like this for every European country and their artists, and they should all be taught by Westwalewicz (even if he's Polish). Lecturers, use Westwalewicz as an example of what you should strive for.

Very enthusiastic about the material.  However, class seemed to drag on for a long time.  I am not saying it was boring, but it was not something I was deeply interested in.  Nevertheless, I would definately reccomend him.  Attendence is required, 4 short papers and an optional project.  Very reasonable for a 1 credit course

This is the easiest course on earth.  Imagine a course in which there are no tests and the longest papers can be is one page!  Just go to class and be inventive.  Too bad it's only a mini-course.  Professor is a wonderful, funny family man.  Highly recommended.
Overall, great teacher, but some might not like him because of his test based teaching style. I personally enjoyed taking tests.
He is hard to understand and mind numbingly monotone. I did not enjoy attending this class and felt I had to self teach myself 90% of the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs

His lectures are quite awful. He speaks with a very thick accent, mumbles, and stutters making it very difficult to understand what he is saying. On top of being a terrible lecturer, he is not very enjoyable to be around. Any questions or interactions with him are met with either a condescending/rude response or a extremely awkward answer.
His passion is contagious. Lots of funny stories, very humble and extremely approachable. Never had such a utopian learning environment before. Please stay the same.

based. very cool and relatable. often asked me about the instrument I had to bring into class for my jazz minor. dude was just cool and fun to talk to. as a professor, he talks a little funny during lecture, but he knows what he's talking about. takes good notes and enjoys answering questions.

Basically my grandfather. Super passionate about his work and about teaching/helping students. Such a fun guy to be around and talk to. Helped with work for a project outside his class and seemed disappointed when we eventually had to leave. Genuinely the realest, nicest, and most caring professor I've met here.

Insane level of passion for engineering that is infectious and rubs off on the entire class. No matter what the topic is, he always has a way to connect it to a real-world project that is both fascinating and inspiring.

Really good professor, probably the best professor I've had so far at UofM. Even though I took the class remote the lectures felt better than most of the in-person ones I've had. He explains content very clearly and does an amazing job with example problems. Exams felt very fair and represented the homework difficulty very well. Highly recommend!
Amazing lecturer, funny real-life examples, dedicated and passionate. Takes the time outside of lecture to chat with you.
You can still pass the class with 20% on the exam. That's how much he curves. NO ONE EVER FAILS HIS CLASS. EVER.

Always uses planes/helicopters as metaphors and tells hilarious stories in lecture. Lectures are a bit slow, but they are usually entertaining and they are necessary. Book was helpful for the open-book exams, not necessary for anything else really.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Liang is a great guy. He tells at least one completely irrelevant story each class, which helps liven things up. He curves up so not many people fail, and he genuinely cares about his class. He's an EE by trade and does a great job teaching an ME class. Highly recommend Prof Liang!

He is the best professor in University of Michigan. His lecture is clear and he has sense of humor. He is really helpful in his office hour, too. There is no surprise in his exam. He only make problems that he told you to in the exam review. I highly recommend him for fluid. If he is not teaching fluid wait until he teaches. No Liang, No fluid!

Great guy. Speaking with some Chinese accent but easy to follow. The content of the course is informative yet kind of too general, hence you might not learn a lot unless you want to work in the photo-lithography field for electronic devices. Be prepared for his cold jokes. Homework is not very easy yet not a lot. Generous grader, you know that.
Best Professor I've met.! Very excellent professor who really care about teaching. He has his own way of teaching that make the complex question become very clear and simple.

Best Prof I've had at this Uni so far. Lectures are truly amazing and well structured. If there was an award for teaching, this man deserves it.  Homework can be a little tricky at times but the GSI was extremely helpful. Class material is not simple but if you take it with him, you will learn it well. Just don't miss class.. Wicked plane drawings

Favorite teacher I've had so far. He explains everything very clearly and his notes are so well organized. He's very willing to help out and has lots of office hours. The exams and homework are extremely fair and he gives lots of partial credit.

Xiaoming was a really sweet professor. It's clear that she loves what she teaches and is genuinely passionate about it. I heavily appreciated her physical demonstrations almost every class! My one comment is that she is a bit hard to understand at times but to no fault of her own.

She is so kind and provides amazing feedback. Highly recommend!
would very much recommend

Hui is one of favorite professors I have had so far. Professor Hui knows English, the review below is wrong. She is really understanding about assignments or mistakes. I had two instances where I forgot to submit my work. Prof. Hui is a very friendly professor. She is also more forgiving in her grading. As long as you follow her standards you will almost always be given full marks. And my favorite point is that she posts all the slides and standards in advance on Canvas, very clear.

Her English is great, that other reviewer just cant listen. She knows what she's doing and is very helpful. Assignments were clear and straightforward. She is kind and understanding that students have lives outside of class.

Lectures are so dry and boring. Yes, the quizzes were open note, but had so many double or triple negatives you could get stuff wrong just by getting confused. She's nice enough. If you're looking for an easy A, go take planets and moons instead of this class

Huang cares about her students and genuinely wants them to succeed. Definitely take this class if you're looking for an easy A natural science class. The lectures are dry but, if you only care about your grade, then this class is a definite yes from me.
She is definetely my favorite professor! I enjoyed her lectures so much and she is really nice and always so caring of her students. I would love to take her lectures again!

Yasuda sensei is so kind, and is always open for questions with a smile on her face. She is so funny and great at teaching and it makes every class worth coming to, and encourages making mistakes. I hope I can have her in another class someday.
She is very encouraging and nice. She encourages people to make mistakes and never shames anyone for getting anything wrong. She is also funny and very good at teaching

I was worried Japanese would be hard to learn, but with Yasuda sensei teaching, it's a breeze. Everything is so much clearer when she explains it in lecture. I absolutely love her. I had her during the 2020-21 school year, both fall and winter semesters. She is an incredible teacher and made Japanese learning so much fun; having class every week day is no problem when you have Yasuda-sensei. I hope to have her for 400 level Japanese!!

Yasuda Sensei is an amazing teacher! She explains everything very thoroughly, answers questions easily, and is overall very enjoyable to be around. She is super easy to approach and always emphasizes that making mistakes is okay and important to continue learning. Be prepared for each class because she will call on you.

Yasuda Sensei is super sweet and a very good teacher. She explains the material clearly and enthusiastically while maintaining a sense of humor, so while you have to attend every lecture, it's not too terrible. Would absolutely recommend.
She makes a very welcoming environment to participate in discussions, and stresses the fact that it's alright to mess up. She's also hilarious in lecture with her love of Roger Federer
Yasuda sensei is one of the most kind-hearted people that I have ever met. She makes class fun and enjoyable while still making sure that everyone understands the material.
Always has a smile and is willing to help you. Very approachable, which is good for a language course. Wishing that I could have her in every class

Yasuda sensei is awesome. I took the intensive summer course with her, so there was a ton of work to do in a short span of time but she made it a positive and engaging experience. Yasuda sensei is really sweet and funny, and she's super accessible. If you get the chance to take a class with her I recommend that you do!!

Yasuda-sensei is wonderful, she's super sweet and really cares about her students. You're gonna have to participate a bunch, but she's never intimidating and is always open to questions and helping you with the material.

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, great teacher overall, but you have to work to get the grade.

Yasuda-sensei is one of the most clear and kind lecturers that I've had at Umich. Although she will force you to participate, she's super funny and considerate about it. Lectures are clear, concise, and go by fast. One of my favorite classes.
Yasuda-sensei is amazing! She's funny and very supportive. She wants you to succeed and will help you get there. Take this class!

Even having her as my lecturer for two terms in a row, Yasuda-sensei is still as fresh, entertaining, and excellent as before. Awesome teacher! Funny, kind, helpful, clear, very approachable - easily one of my fave teachers here. Yasuda-sensei is the best! She's hilarious and super adorable. She's very approachable, loves to help, and understanding.  The class reqs are very clear. Many EC opportunities. Excellent lecturer. Involves as many students as possible in a manner that is not disruptive or distracting from the individual learning experience. Allows all students to interact with each other in short and natural bursts to practice speech and hearing with each other. Willing to help students who need it or ask for it.

She's very easy to understand! Most people in this class have some basic knowledge of Japanese, so she may move quickly. If you've never studied much Japanese, you'll need to study a lot. If you have self-studied, you may need to occasionally study new vocabulary. There's homework but it's very short. Class is honestly the best part of my day.
Absolutely awesome professor.  She cares a great deal about students.  She's also one of the funniest women I have ever met.

Very nice and really passionate about teaching her students. I can tell that they she tries to be as understanding as she can about mistakes and wants to make every student feel welcome. Also she has a good sense of humor!

Amazing professor. Very clear lectures. It feels like almost everyday we introduced new material and yet it never seemed overwhelming. The grading has been quite forgiving. I highly recommend this course and Yasuda??.

Deeply knowledgable about math & statistics. Will be tested on things covered in lecture, so don't miss class. Moves fairly quickly in class, but you will learn a lot. Try not to take her 8am class because it will be hard to focus if you're sleepy.
Proofs heavy! Not recommended!

Prof. Young really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She's able to make relatively dense material easy to digest. In both her 523 and 524 courses I easily obtained an A. You can either write down what shes writing on the board or listen to what she's saying, but you can't do both. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Young is very personable and admirable. Her class is challenging but if you go to every class and take good notes, you will find the materials all build up very naturally and make sense. Tests are a bit tough, so you need to know the stuff well and allocate your time wisely.
Brilliant teacher. I love the way she organized her notes. Requires effort to ace the class but her notes are really relevant to Exam C.

Be prepared to write 4-5 full pages of notes each class.  Quizzes each week are pretty easy but the test are tough, like most math classes (ie average in the 60s).  The kicker here is she does not curve the class.  She is known for failing about 13 of student.  Wait till Winter semester if you are a below average student and want to pass 523.

She is a decent teacher and has very organized notes, but the exams are difficult and she's giving almost half our class Ds because that's all we need to 'pass'.  Also gives basically zero partial credit on exams which makes them very hard to do well on.
She is helpful and really cares about her student. Grading is fair. her teaching style is amazing.

Professor Young really cares about her student and would like to extend her office hour if you need. Grading is fair. Try to focus on every point she mentioned in class. I like her teaching style a lot!!

I had her for both Math 520 and 521 and I thought she did a great job explaining the concepts. Most of the time, she tries to explain the intuition behind concepts so you don't end up just memorizing them. A lot of students think her classes are difficult because of the straight curve, but really, she's pretty lenient with quiz and exam grades. :)

I thought Prof. Young was pretty good Prof and a nice person. Assigned HW but not graded, instead we had a quiz each class with a HW question on it. The exam questions were very relevant as well, no curve balls.

In the class I took: 1) Homework was not graded, instead there were quizzes each week with one problem from the HW. I thought I would hate this, but it was actually kind of nice. 2) Exam questions were either modified hw problems or problems from notes. 3) She went over HW problems in class.

Professor Young is one of the least helpful professors I've had. While her notes are good and she goes over homework in class, she doesn't seem to care about the students. She won't take the time to help those who struggle and she doesn't curve at all. Horrible class.
quizes every week. Does not curve class at all. Okay lecture, but not helpful during office hours. Would not recommend. Require lots of self studying.

Her lecture notes are clear and well organized.  I like how she will take requests to go over difficult homework problems in class.  Her exams are challenging, but many students still score very high.

Prof Young is the worst math professor I have ever had.  She is completely unapproachable in office hours and actually keeps her door closed.  She doesn't know how to explain the concepts to people who haven't already passed SOA exam M.  She lacks personal skills with students.

reviews.comment: Challenging and fun, Prof Zurier works hard to see all the students and their specific knowledge to contribute to the class. Gives a lot of responsibility to the student.

The material was dry, and her presentation of it was worse. She's one of those profs that thinks this is the only class on your schedule.  The term had zero structure to it. Not a fan of this professor. Expectations of Art Historical knowledge were not clearly stated at courses' start. She drawls on in lecture, although the material is interesting, she unfortunately kills any interest with her teaching style. Would not take this class again.

Worst professor of my entire career at UM. The subject matter is interesting, but she presents it in a confusing, unorganized way. I've attended every class and still can't see how she organized the class. Focuses completely on memorization instead of themes/movements. The beginning of this class was very interesting. However she is very disorganized in her lectures and power points.Got assignments and exams back longggg after we turned them in. She is so painfully boring and the discussions she pushes us towards are sometimes not relevant to the overall purpose of the class. The subject was fascinating to me at first but now that I am in the class, it really is a downer. She treats the subject in a very elementary way.

Worst professor i have ever had.  She is not helpful when you ask questions at all.  She definitely knows what she is talking about, but has no idea how to tell others about it.  Terrible people skills.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
Her interactions with students suggest that she does not have much experience working with humans.  Perhaps she would do better with farm animals.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had at U of M. She treats her students like simpletons and doesn't respect anyone's opinion but her own. She assigns a ton of work and is very slow to get it back to students, as well. Unless you absolutely must take a class from - DON'T!

Brilliant woman, knew the topic very well.  Lectures were boring as sin though informative.  Not the most forgiving grader, though.  Definitely worth it if you're interested in Art of the American Century, but it's a definite commitment.
Not good. Boring, tons of writing and not fun.

I do not doubt that she has a kind heart with the best intentions, but this class edged on painful.  Incredibly interesting subject matter, yet her teaching style sucks the life out the topic.  Her standards are high, and although there are no exams, it is just not worth it.
Horrible. LOTS OF READING (that you need to do!) Worst Art History class I've ever taken. Don't think that interesting subject matter can make up for her awful teaching skills.
not at all considerate of students' time. shows up late every day and doesn't end on time. her people skills aren't the best, but at least she knows  her art history.

Prof. Zurier, while boring, is very willing to meet with students outside of class.  She makes an effort to be available to students, although her personality is a bit drab.  If you're looking for excitement, turn back now, but it's a fairly easy A, and she knows what she's talking about (despite countless errors during lectures).

She reviews soooo much throughout lecture.  the first half of the lecture is always a rehash of everything leading up to this one, so all the concepts are completely laid out for you.  Only tough part is memorizing the lists, but I guess that depends on who you are.
lectures are interesting.  she's not hard; it's just that a lot of memorization is required.

Very interesting lectures!!! Does a great job tying everything together. Reserved at first glance, but a great communicator and very approachable. Will have lunch with you - take advantage of it! Fun to chat with. And an easy A. A favorite class and a favorite professor.
THE WORST EVER!
Probably a brilliant researcher, but posesses no people skills whatsoever. Not suited for a classroom environment.
She's a damn good teacher and her class is really easy.
Worst teacher I've ever had.

Zach was an incredible GSI. He was very careful to make sure that his entire class understood what was going on in each unit. He asked for feedback frequently in order to make adjustments to his teaching, and went out of his way to host a study session for the final exam. Math is difficult and Zach did everything he could do make it more doable.
Overall his test on the Prime factoring system was the easiest part and that's just the beginning . Dude, I cant state enough about how the Micheal project sucked To do, and the straw one too.

reviews.comment: The only part I enjoyed was the toy straw experiment but I liked when he helped us with the forum

reviews.comment: Awesome and informative professor and class, I would take class from him again. Many assignments pass/fail. Highly recommend!!

If you want to learn something this class isn't it, but it is a super easy A. Go to the discussion but the lectures are not needed. Half the class is pass/fail and the exams are easy if you memorize the terms.
He's great. Even teaching an intro class he is so entertaining and explains concepts clearly. Def take a class with him if you can!
really good teacher

Easiest A of my life, every assignment was pass/fail (turning it in was a pass), and the two exams were multiple choice and noncumulative. Fascinating topics and lectures, the discussion section was really fun too.

reviews.comment: MY GOAT. dr. zeglen is genuinely one of the best professors i've ever had. he's super open, honest, and well-educated. my only complaint is that he was pressed for time but spent most of the time in dumb group discussons, because i'd rather just listen to him talk. all assignments are pass/fail. the readings are hard but amazing - focus on those!

This class was super easy if you attend lectures. Prof. Zeglen is a good lecturer and engages students. all assignments except for the midterm/final are pass/fail which is really nice. midterm was super easy, final had some confusing questions, but overall, very easy class with minimal effort needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's biased but makes it obvious so I was never bothered. He is so knowledgable. His lectures are good and I've learned a lot about the general field of intl studies. Exams aren't bad, just a lot of memorization. He just switched to the assignments being Pass/No pass so that's easy. Amelia Wittig is a fantastic GSI, so engaging and kind.
Very easy class. Almost all of it is pass/fail except for the multiple choice midterm and final. Lectures are interesting, and all of the information is easily digestible.
all assignments were pass/fail except for the midterm and final, exams sometimes had oddly specific questions that were briefly touched on, but overall easy class

Dave is such a great professor! His lectures were always super fun & engaging! They're not mandatory, but I'd recommend going because he doesn't explain many examples on the slides and verbally explains them instead. Assignments were P/NP, so they were really easy & tests were straightforward enough. Discussion was also helpful, IMO.
Prof. Zeglen was the best prof ever. His lectures are super engaging and he is also hilarious. No textbook and very minimal reading. If you study, class is super easy, and also fun to learn.

Dave is excellent and very knowledgeable about international studies. Although there is no iclicker or credit for going to lecture, it is very important to go as he will give information not on the slides during lecture. Dave is a great professor and very kind and caring towards his students!

Dr. Zeglen is a great professor! He makes everything super digestible and easy to understand. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory. But helps so much for comprehension of examples. Your grade is based solely on 2 exams, 2 papers, and Section work (i.e., Self-reflections). Honestly, if you go to class and section every week, exams are easy.

Dr. Zeglen is definitely opinionated, however he is very knowledgeable about the course material. His lectures are engaging, and most of the assignments are for completion which makes the class very stress-free. There is also a lot of vocabulary to memorize, so be prepared for that!

He is very knowledgeable and knows what he's talking about. You can tell he's passionate and cares about his students. I've also taken 101 with him and it was the reason I became an INTLSTD major. Would definitely take his classes again and again.

He is so knowlegdable and passionate about the topics he teaches, he knows so much and wants you to learn and understand what he is teaching. I have taken 3 of his classes now and do not regret a thing—one of the best professors at Michigan for real.

Easiest class. Zeglen knows how to break down concepts and make them digestible. Super well-informed and does his research. Tests are simple if you can memorize quickly. Papers are graded by GSIs. Definitely recommend taking the class through him.

He is very funny and lectures went by so fast. Although he is pretty biased in lecture, it doesn't impact learning. He is extremely knowledgeable in his field and a great lecturer. Also very respectful to all students. Would definitely take another class with him again.

Dave was an excellent lecturer, extremely engaging and willing to respond to questions. He was also my section professor instead of a GSI, and discussions in this section were very valuable to my understanding of the course. Super knowledgeable guy with strong opinions, I learned a lot from him. 10/10 take this class !!!

He is extremely biased. Not that I disagree. One time he said, "If other professors in the _ department tell you _, just don't listen they do no research and are clueless." Prolly why there are no recordings. He needs to realize other people have opinions. He also makes up a lot of terms to explain his reasoning. The terms don't exist online.

Zeglen offers an interesting take on international studies, and forces you to think critically on institutions that you might have previously assumed were protecting people, rather than hurting them. Class structure was weird: exams were the day after Thanksgiving and fall break, and required a ton of somewhat pointless memorization.

Prof Zeglen is a good lecturer and brought in really interesting topics/perspectives. Exams are mostly short answer (he gives you a list of like 25 and picks 5). Lectures aren't recorded and you can't get everything from the slides, so I definitely recommend going. He took attendance once with a QR code.
Worst professor so biased. Only take this class if you are good at memorizing, you don't learn anything from this class. Such a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance was technically required, but he only took it once. Grades were determined through two exams, two papers, and section participation. Dr. Zeglen is SO knowledgeable about International Studies, and he does a wonderful job at explaining concepts instead of just talking at us. He has a great lecture presence and will answer all questions!

Zeglen's lectures were really good and not boring at all!! For the exams he'll give you a study guide of short answer questions and will choose 5 of them to be on the exam! The only bad part about this class is that the exams were on the Mondays after Fall Break and Thanksgiving break. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory until like after fall break.

Dr. Zeglen is a great professor who cares about students and will make time outside of class to talk. He is passionate and knowledgeable about the material. Class discussions are engaging and build on the assigned readings + the workload is very manageable. I highly recommend taking a seminar class with him.

Course material was very interesting and professor did a great job with lectures. Two exams and two current events essays which were fairly easy to do. GSI Amelia Wittig is THE BEST!!!! Best discussion class—very engaging and so so nice.
zeglen was a easy class to take as a freshman, his lectures were somewhat engaging. exams are exactly what he gives on the study guide and done in class

BEST CLASS EVER! He was an amazing lecturer who was extremely knowledgeable. This class is graded on two exams & two papers. You can rewrite your first essay. The exams are easy. He gives you a study guide with 20-25 questions you memorize, and he picks 5 to put on the exams. The discussions were my favorite part, GSI Amelia Wittig is the best.
Awful teacher gave a final exam on the day after thanksgiving break

David is a nice professor who really does want to share his knowledge.

However, you're only graded on 2 essays, 2 tests, and participation. He put up a QR code for attendance once but everyone I know got the link to the form from a friend who actually went to the 10 am lectures...

He also gives tests right after fall and Thanksgiving break
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad teacher overall
He was bad, plus a final right after Thanksgiving break
Absolute abysmal teacher. Would stay away at all costs.

AMAZING professor. I loved loved loved professor zeglen's class and looked forward to it everytime. his lectures are actually interesting and he was extremely knowledgable and passionate on the subject. just go to class pay attention and take notes and youll pass with an A. definitely a must take professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zeglen was a great lecturer with lots of personal experience with some topics. He seemed to really care about the material and the students in the class.

zeglen is the best!!! super knowledgeable and passionate. you know exactly what's gonna be on the tests so just memorize the definitions and examples he gives you. i would just spend like four or five hours the night before the exam studying and would be totally fine. papers are graded arbitrarily depending on gsi, so beware of that.

Honestly I love Dave, his lectures were so interesting. There are 2 three page current events paper and they are so so soooo easy to write (I would do them the day of and get high 90s). Two in person exams but he gives you all the questions beforehand. Not only did I enjoy listening to him but also looking at him hehe.

Very good professor, taught what you needed to know in a clear concise manner, would definentaly recommend taking this class as it broadened my perspectives on international relations. The GSI's were the ones grading assignments and they were definentaly hard graders, but don't let that discourage you from taking the class.
Dave was an excellent professor and a great leader during the strikes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave was an awesome professor to have, lectures were completely optional but everything I went to was very interesting. A few of the lectures don't really have any relevance outside of the class, but he's a super cool guy with some really interesting life experiences, I would absolutely take more classes with him

This guy is interesting and his lectures are insightful and actually interesting to sit through. With that said, he's incredibly one-sided in his viewpoints and centers his lectures around his opinions.

Love Dave so much! Actually cared about us learning and being interested rather than giving us pointless assignments. I loved the current events essay and wish I could take this class again. Easy course load and very interesting topics

Love Dave so much! Actually cared about us learning and being interested rather than giving us pointless assignments. I loved the current events essay and wish I could take this class again. Easy course load and very interesting topics.

I loved Dave. He clearly cares about his students and shows this through the class discussions. There was a good amount of reading required for each class, but they were very useful as he includes guiding questions with them. I would take his classes over and over again.There is one midterm and one final paper (8 pages), but they are not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Zeglen is a fantastic professor who is super passionate about the material he teaches. The lectures are engaging and he does a great job of including current events in the class concepts. I highly recommend taking a course with him.

This was the worst class I've ever taken at U-M. Zeglen extremely biased in almost all his teaching. He was often unwilling to explain class concepts further and reacted hostilely to students that disagreed with him. Lecture was often based solely on his opinion with little evidence/support. I never read the textbook. It made no difference.

Lectures were interesting, but very biased at times. He had a habit of teaching his opinion or the side he agreed like it was fact instead of teaching about both sides. Some of the lectures, including one on the Politics of Study Abroad Programs, didn't really seem to have much real-life importance. Overall, a decent class.

Lectures were all over the place, and it took my GSI over a month to grade the first paper and the midterm. His lecture on orientalism showed clear lack of knowledge on the subject (he couldn't give literally an example of orientalism except yoga), and he would randomly bring up Israel and Palestine in lecture but not connect it to course material

I love attending Zeglen's lectures. He is a large dude and has a deep voice, but don't let it fool you. I know he's a teddy bear on the inside. He draws a lot of his knowledge from his experiences, and is very well versed and well cultured. Highly recommend.

I found the lectures interesting but even though I agreed with his opinions, he was extremely biased and only presented his point of view even when it had shaky evidence. He also doesn't respond well to opinions in class that go against his which on occasion created a hostile environment.

Had him for INTLSTD 101, super easy class, 2 exams & 2 short papers. He said he'd take attendance at random lectures throughout the semester but never did. Interesting guy, worked at some NGO monitoring human rights in North Korea and has a couple lectures about it. Exams are easy bc questions are directly from the review sheet. 10/10 professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave always offered extra credit on the exams and would give you a selection of questions ahead of time that he then picked from for the exams. Overall, not a difficult class, but I enjoyed my discussion section and the material.

While this was a straightforward class and the easiest I've taken, looking back, I take issue with how much of his own opinion Dr. Zeglen baked into the lectures. Even the definitions of key terms were obviously not impartial to anyone who's been exposed to the concepts before (a Marxist perspective was force-fed on very many of the concepts).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good lectures- he is passionate and well-versed in the material. Exams are not hard, he gives possible questions ahead of times and it is all based off the lectures. He talks fast imo and most of the info isn't on the slides so it can be hard to review. There are 4 current events essays but the rubric is simple and it's easy to do well on them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zeglen was very clear in his lectures and provided a lot of examples, but make sure to take notes because a lot of the information is not included in his slides. For every exam, there was a clear study sheet with all of the possible questions he could ask. The only other things graded were 4 essays that were about current events.

For an intro course, Zeglen is exceeds expecatations by providing good, contextualized content while often offering his own take on the matter. Not much pressure to attend lecture, but it's definitely worth it and will make getting a good grade much easier.

Professor Zeglen was super engaging. He presented many of his opinions alongside material but he always made the distinction between the two clear. He is also fun to talk to and his exams and essays were fair.

I LOVE DAVID ZEGLEN. Coolest person ever I love going to lectures he's so funny. He has an eyebrow piercing. I want to be him. This class made me feel so smart. Highly recommend. God bless him. #livelaughlovedavid
Expectations are clearly outlined. Not a hard class to do well in if you show up to lecture and take notes. Professor is funny and makes class interesting.

Such interesting lectures. He's super clear with how the exams will be and even gives out a study guide. Make sure you go to lecture and take good notes though because he doesn't put much information on his slides.

Dave is an awesome professor. Fun lectures, extremely knowledgable and approachable. Assignments include 4 short essays that you chose when you turn in, short interesting readings, and 2 exams (he gives you all the possible exam questions ahead of time and answers your questions about them). I highly recommend Dr. Zeglen.

Great proffesor in terms of caring and knowledge. However when it comes to teaching a class and interacting in order to further learning a strong weakness is there. Very hard to learn and unserstand the key points for exams.
Zhang is so smart but he should NOT be a professor. Some people should realize their strengths and weaknesses.

The problem is not George, it's CBE. They try to fit so much into the curriculum but students don't actually retain the information. He was ok, still better than Lee McClain imo. Grading scale consisted of: 15% homework (6) 25% midterm 15% Quiz (exam 2) 45% Final I had to teach a lot of the content myself but he curves heavily (rightfully so).

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Zhang's half of the class was well taught and more straightforward than the second half. The homework, practice problems from lecture and the quizzes reflected the types of problems on the exam. He explains the material concisely and to solve problems it's important to understand the logic that he used to solve examples in class.

Professor Zhang is an awful professor. He makes himself very poorly understood, when a student asks a question he goes off on tangents, he's never clear about the exam material and seems to be the professor that teaches once every few years to keep his research since he dislikes student interaction. His exams are also impossible and unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang knows genetics very well, he just does not know how to teach it. The class required to memorize formulas, so one would think the highlighted formulas in the lecture slides are the ones to memorize . However, this is not the case, any formula is fair game. I recommend taking the class during winter, or any time when he does not teach it.

The only reason I understood the material was because I went to GSI office hours. He does not explain concepts well in class and doesn't set clear expectations for exams. States that you don't need to know details but his exams are all details. Glazes over lecture problems he expects students to know, doesn't prepare you for difficult HW problems
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He cannot explain hard concepts at all. Very difficult class. Spends a lot of class time going over history of genetics that is not on the exam.

He's a really funny guy and walks the class through almost every iclicker question and while not giving the answer he makes it obvious. His exams sample his old exams heavily. Has trouble getting through all of his lecture slides. Class is hard but the book problems help.
George is a great guy. His exams are a good reflection of his i-clicker questions and the easier of the book questions. I'm not sure why everyone complains about him.
The class is boring and waste of time. Dr. Zhang simply sucks! He did not agree to write me a recommendation letter even when I got an A in his class.
Took intro genetics.  He never understood why the class average was low, he thought his questions were easy

Hard ass class.  Did not curve. Gave me an avg grade even though I got an A on the final. Does not want to answer any grade related questions. In other words, you suck leave me alone, I do not wish to associate with you! I'm busy relaxin on my research. I hate teaching

Bio 305. I stayed up until the first exam. The average on the exam was around a 60%. The course was not supposed to be curved so I opted out while early in the semester. His lectures are dry and borring and he lacks any form of personality. Its like being taught by a robot.

One of the worst class I took since I transfered. Unclear, tests extremely hard math concepts despite the class being geared for bio students who aren't engineers. Take stats before this class. I learned it the hard way.  If you are good at math, his section should be bearable   Comparable difficulty to physics II
Lectures are extremely boring. Not helpful at ALL after class. DOESN"T KEEP HIS WORDS, and just not appoarchable overall. Exams are pretty hard.

He's knowledgeable, but he didn't seem interested in teaching and sometimes confused himself on his own practice questions during class. The exams in his half of the course were notably much more difficult. I highly recommend using Problem Roulette and exams from previous years to study.

Genetics is a difficult class, and Dr. Zhang was not very good at explaining concepts. It sometimes felt like he couldn't explain certain questions, and he would sometimes get the questions wrong in class. Tests were also very difficult!

Genetics is a very hard class, and I didn't feel like Dr. Zhang helped to make it easier. He frequently misspoke during lecture and struggled to explain some concepts to us. We often got to discussion entirely confused, only to be saved by our GSI's explanation. He's a nice guy, but not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The half of genetics taught by this professor was brutal. Lectures didn't tend to be helpful since the material is dense and the speed with which we were expected to learn it was approaching breakneck. Didn't provide nearly enough resources to achieve the level of knowledge expected from us on the exams, which were a little insane content-wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang's half of genetics was extremely difficult. Obviously learning styles are very different but I found his lectures to be very hard to follow and the exams to be harder than many of the other classes I have taken here at UM. Don't underestimate this class and assume that you will be tested on very small-scale topics!

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang taught the first half of genetics. His slides were great, and he was clear about expectations for the exams. I didn't read the textbook, and just did the practice problems at the end of the chapters and listened to lectures, which was enough to do well on the exams. It was about the same difficulty as Dr. Dus' second half of the class.

I would strongly discourage any student from electing courses with Professor Zhang. His deficient instructional style demonstrates his disrespect for students and his inability to understanding students perspectives and learning styles. My experience in BIOLOGY 305 has been extremely regrettable.

Dr. Zhang did not sufficiently explain his slides or the course material to students. He did not welcome questions from students neither did he care to genuinely assist students with understanding course material. His exams were not representative of the material covered in class. I recommend that you don't take classes with him.

I thought Dr. Zhang's half of the class was well taught and more straightforward than the second half. The homework, practice problems from lecture and the quizzes reflected the types of problems on the exam. He explains the material concisely and to solve problems it's important to understand the logic that he used to solve examples in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Without a doubt the worst professor/ class I have ever taken at the university. The exams are ridiculously difficult and content explanation in class is extremely poor. The only thing that keeps anyone afloat in this class is the textbook, SLC, and GSI. I am shocked the university allows the students to suffer through this course.

I am never the kind of student to blame a professor for my grade.  But I would just like to warn all students taking the class two things.  1) Zhangs lectures covered far more material than were on the tests, and 'mastering' the material did not really help me.  2) He reuses questions so find practice exams (other students will be using them).

I found his exams to be challenging and detrimental to my grade, but I can definitely say that I learned something by attending lecture, listening to him, and reading the sections he assigned. I enjoyed him, even though my grade now sucks.

Horrible. Hard exams, completely misrepresentative of the information presented in lecture. 25 multiple choice, so every question is essentially 1% of your grade. Accordingly, your grade is nothing less than a crapshoot.

The content that she went through in the lecture could have been a lot easier, but she explains everything in a very complex way. If you study before the tests by going through the slides and using the readings, you will do well.  A chill 100 class just seems to be more confusing than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I disliked the way she speaks to you during office hours and her common response of "everything's in the lecture." She says one small thing and expects you to remember it for an exam. Still, shes passionate in what she does and I enjoyed listening to her lectures, I just had multiple bad experiences with a passive aggressive attitude.

Very light-hearted, open-minded professor. Breaks down heavy topics in a easy to understand and light-hearted way while remaining in an academic & professional tone. Her lectures are optional to attend and are recorded. Even so, I always love when I attend them.
rude and condescening

You'll get an A+. She cares about what she's saying. You don't have to go to the lecture, really, but you should because she's so knowledgeable. She may not come off as warm and sweet but her grading gives a lot of grace
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very passionate for what she teaches about and helps you learn about sociology in a fun way! She likes to make jokes during lectures and make the content understandable, especially when readings can be heavy at times. She worked with me through a difficult life period and allowed me to thrive in her class, definitely take!

great lectures, multiple choice on exams could be difficult but salam was very understanding and willing to curve/give extra credit. great professor, you could tell she really cared about her students and the material she taught.

Prof Aboulhassan was one of the most inspirational professors I've had. Her lectures were always entertaining and inspirational and the readings made me want to learn more outside of the class. The quizzes are pretty hard and you have to pay attention to details of all the readings. Overall loved her and would recommend for an intro soc class!

Conceptually not a very hard class. The tests, on the other hand, are very difficult to get A's in. One or two multiple choice questions wrong on a test can impact your grade a lot, and often these multiple choice questions have two options that appear correct. Lots of readings during the semester and Salam a knowledgeable lecturer.

The content isn't hard, but the tests are difficult. The multiple choice portion of the tests are hard to get right. You can read the whole reading and understand it and still feel like two options in the multiple choice are right, and this doesn't just happen sometimes, it happens all of the time. Lots of readings, but they were interesting.
interesting lectures. funny.

Salam's lectures are great and really informative. There is a lot of reading, but GSIs explain it clearly, and it's not difficult information. The exams correlate with the readings and her lectures, and they aren't difficult. The final paper was an interesting process, and I enjoyed writing it. Overall, she's a great lecturer and cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a chance to take Soc 102 with her, please do! Her lectures are hilarious and informative, everyone goes despite attendance not being mandatory. The exams are very easy and the GSIs provide a ton of help with the study guide. There's a lot of reading but it can be manageable if you plan correctly.

I had a very positive experience taking this class with Salam. She does a great job with lectures and letting students know what they will be tested on. The only thing I didn't love was that the readings can be long, and the exams mostly cover them.

Prof. Aboulhassan is so funny and interesting. Her lectures are always interesting and often incorporate her personal life. She swears often but I thought that made her funny and relatable. She grades fairly and is willing to apply curves and give extra credit. She is very open to feedback from students on anything relating to the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Soc 102 - Very engaging, passionate lecturer. the course was honestly pretty disorganized but assingments/grading were easy enough that it didn't matter. prof cared a lot about students and the topics at hand, I had a lot of thought-provoking conversations in discussions.

This class is fine if you keep up with the readings. The readings assigned are extremely interesting but rarely discussed. I would have loved more opportunities to discuss the readings themselves rather than random topics. Salam is passionate and approachable but extremely pessimistic. She tends to go off-topic making it difficult to contribute.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly, very easy class to do well in if you do the readings/ notes. Readings are long but on occasion, very interesting. However, she constantly brought up how “easy” she was making the class for us and that things would be changing. She was an impressively pessimistic person but not necessarily mean or unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Aboulhassan is one of my all-time favorite professors at Umich. She just wants her students to succeed, and she's very clear about expectations for the class. Just read and attend discussion, and you'll get an A. She's also one of the realest professors here, and super funny.

Speaks eloquently. Facilitates really great discussions. Cussed sometimes, no one cares though. Her experiences are countless and her resulting perspectives on societal concepts and issues were completely unique to my world thus far and really interesting. I could listen to her speak for hours, and our university needs more people like her.

Is very obviously a childhood prodigy. He teaches very quickly and you have to keep up. Since keeping up is hard, he is very very helpful during his office hours and during the time that he is in the Math Learning Center. Go ask questions.

A pretty great professor overall. It's obvious he's genuinely passionate about what he teaches, which makes learning from him a lot less dull. At times he may go a bit fast or go off on a tangent, but always asks if anyone has questions. Extremely accessible outside of class, and puts in regrade requests for exams on behalf of students.

Dr. Zieve does a lot for students and is pretty much always available outside of class. He shares a lot of useful test prep and strategies, and as long as you read the textbook chapters beforehand, his lectures are easy to understand and very helpful. Overall a very knowledgable mathematician and intersting guy. I'm super glad I took his section.

Dr. Zieve is a very knowledgeable mathematician but sometimes gets carried away in lecture. He makes random comments about people in class and their grades but overall he's a nice person. Just beware because he assumes students know some of the things he explains but does care about how his students do and grades fast. Not the best or worse in 116.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zieve isn't the easiest to follow during section/lecture. He's very well-versed in the subject, but is prone to making simple mistakes + assumes students know certain things (when many may not). However, one-on-one Professor Zieve is amazing. He will help you through any problem in class, and I highly recommend going to his office hours.

He's an incredibly good mathematician and if you can figure out what he's saying in his lectures, can give great insights into the material. However, lectures were very confusing and only somewhat reflected the ideas in the homework and tests. He doesn't seem able to communicate with struggling students (me) and help them where they're at.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He would do one example per class but every single time, without fail, would make some error halfway through that completely changed the method to do the problem and then spend 30 minutes trying to find the error, making it totally pointless to listen the first time, and then he would rush through the redo of the problem and move on abruptly.

Does not explain concepts clearly. Does not use slides at all and just writes really small on the chalkboard. Tries to "smoothly" transition between topics but ends up blurring them all together to the point where you don't know how to actually use the info in homework or on exams. Spends 90% of the class on proofs you do not have to know for exam.

Professor Zieve is very smart and many of his remarks (mathematically or otherwise) will help you a lot in the long run. Very accessible, advice on general stuff is good, tho not so helpful with specific problems. Be cautious though if you dread self learning, because homework often cover things (or use tools) not clearly stated in lectures.

Lack of clarity, even though I know he's very smart. The grading standard of exams is confusing. Final exam is the most confusing part, questions are easy and has obvious solutions, but require very detailed justification, for which how detailed should it be to be considered as "very detailed" is unknown. Got A except the final, which lead to a B+
Probably the worst experience Ive ever had with a math prof.

Easily the worst professor Ive had at U of M. He doesnt care about his students at all, and gets very frustrated and demeaning as soon as anyone has trouble with any of the material, and he doesnt understand exam pressure. E.g. he gave us a quiz on doing simple addition and other arithmetic after our first midterm. He is extremely disrespectful.
Interesting and patient, curve is good.

If you're a comp-sci major that needs linear algebra credit I would rethink taking his class. Zieve is smart but this class was not suitable for me who had not learned linear algebra before. He was not able to re-explain concepts more clearly when I did not understand something for the first time. I would have preferred to take MATH 214

Zieve is the best professors at Umich. He's insanely smart and knows what he's doing. During exams, he will take the test with us then post his solutions online after the exam is over. He's a great teacher who cares about his students test results and fights against unfair grading. I wouldn't have passed the class without him. 100% best teacher!!!
Really nice prof

To be concise, he knows what he's talking about, so you can always keep asking until you learn and he'll make sure you do. He organizes previous exam questions into chapters for you to practice, and he gives out practice questions and gives u feedback if you actually hand them in. He's super chill on homeworks and grading too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Incredibly good at math. Really goes beyond and helps students understand how tests are structured and how to get an A.
He wants you to succeed.
I'm pretty sure he's a model. In terms of math, you'll learn more than you ever imagined.
Very dreamy; sometimes hard to think about math, but then he proves great theorems out of nowhere.
He is like 'Shifu' in martial art. You learn everything you need from him.
He's great.

Mr. Zieve is a pretty awesome professor. He was always willing to sacrifie time to help his students. He listens to students and gears his class in a useful direction. He is also a fairly funny and civil guy. I would definitely recommend him for any level course.
Zieve is an awesome, kawsome, saucesome math man. But you should refuse to turn in homework unless he brings you food/cookies. On the first day of class, ask him to prove 1=0.
Prof. Zieve is brilliant, helpful, enthusiastic, and funny.  By the end of the semester I went to office hours and class just to see him.  Take any course you can from him!  He's great!

Worst professor I have ever had at the University. Took months to hand back/grade simple assignments, and was not easily reachable by email. I took this class to fulfill my credits, but there are so many different classes I should have taken rather than this one. Boring class, even worse teacher.

Natasha is extremely caring and accommodating. However, her class felt VERY disorganized. The readings were very different compared to what we were expected to know in class.
