Directions on assignments and exams were unclear, and grades were given more than a month later from when they were due. Attendance was also mandatory!
Passionate and caring. Great class.

Had her for Ling210. Professor Abner is clearly caring and accommodating but class felt disorganized. Material in readings was too complex compared to what we were expected to know in class, which created confusion. Assignments felt like guesswork since we didn't have practice applying some concepts. Attendance was mandatory and no textbook

I'd recommend taking this class because the content will be relevant for the rest of your life. There was a lot of reading, although she did make the readings slightly less in response to student feedback. She was very accessible outside of class, although she wasn't super approachable. Yellowdig posts were annoying but not super time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She obviously cares about her students and is very welcoming when it comes to office hours, but the assignments build off of each other and it takes 2-3 weeks for her to grade them/post answer keys, so you don't know what you're doing wrong until it's too late. Also relies a lot on readings to teach the material instead of her own lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Natasha is an nice woman who is clearly passionate, specifically in disability studies. She brings in guest speakers which is entertaining sometimes. The biggest drawback of this course is the insane amount of reading; 20-30 pages of reading a night is typical, so be ready. Boring lectures too, very dry and one can easily fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Thoughtful and thorough.

Prof Eiler encourages class discussion and helps us push our thinking. The class didn't have a ton of structure or tangible content but Eiler was able to maintain class discussion. She could have been stricter about assignment criteria and deadlines. Nice woman though and very approachable.
Three hours goes by fast as this course is highly engaging. It does require you to complete work outside of class prior to the in-class discussions. Prof. Eiler was fabulous!
Enjoyed the engagement and access to the professor for consultation outside of class-time. She really cares.
High engagement!

Professor Eiler is lovely! Super great guidance both in and outside the classroom (career-wise). So much experience in and passion for the field. My only complaint is that the Canvas page was a bit disorganized--readings for the week not released until the day before class, and assignments were sometimes confusing and/or released late.
We loved Abigail and I thought her teaching was relaxing.
Abigail was a really nice teacher. Everyone was going through a hard time that year. Thanks Abigail.

During the course Professor Finlay only lectured for about 15 minutes max and then had the students attempt to try math problems that the students were not prepared for. The exams were difficult and the class did poorly. It should also be noted Professor Finlay went on a teaching strike and the students still had to complete all assignments.

I learned so much about global health from this course that will be useful to me in my future career.  The course was well organized, and Dr. Wagner has lots of experience doing applied global health that he brings to the class.

I am really interested in public/global health, but this class was awful due to Dr. Wagner. He explains concepts poorly, exams focus on obscure details from unrecorded lectures, and he's condescending and hard to reach. Even our GSI said he ignores feedback and makes exams unnecessarily difficult.

Rude, passive-aggressive, and disregards students. Exam content's extremely ambiguous, and assignment guidelines are not clear at all. Course's all over the place due to his recent wish to "make the course harder" so people could be better prepared "for their career." Regardless of what place you are in the class, he'll expect you to "be an adult."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a nice, passionate professor. We had a few larger assignments and two weekly reading quizzes (super easy). Exams were a bit tougher. They were open time limit, open resource, etc. but would have such specific questions that the answers could be impossible to find, including in the lecture recordings. Overall a decent class and good prof.
He's such a sweetie big fan. he really cares a lot about this course and the content and he and the GSI were super flexible and understanding with everything
She does things differently than the other module instructors

In this class, we got to try a lot of different things like the TV Lab and use a robot. Zain always made the lectures super enjoyable. You got one free unexcused absence but other than that, you were expected to be in class. I thought sometimes her feedback was more tough and a little unclear but she offered lots of support to make you successful!

In hindsight I absolutely loved having Zain as a professor. Whilst taking the class I found it tough and Zain to strict, however it allowed me to produce great work that I was proud of. Sometimes she was mean to fellow classmates but I went in and took everything she said with a grain of salt and she seemed to warm up to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Abby is genuinely a good person and caring professor, but the downside is that she reads off her slides to the point where you don't need to attend lecture or even watch recordings. That being said, it's a super easy A (easy exams). Discussions are two hours long and mandatory though, but they were always super fun.

Abby was a great professor! She cares about her students and is very accessible and accommodating. Lectures are recorded, so I watched them in 2x speed. 2-hr long discussions can be daunting, but I actually enjoyed talking with my classmates! No assignments except for 3 easy exams that are 100% off the study guide, 1 project, and weekly posts!

Professor Dumes was one of the nicest professors I have had so far. She cares a lot about her students and is available if you need extra support. Her lectures were mostly just her reading off of the slides, and they were all recorded, so attendance was not mandatory. Discussions were 2 hours once a week, but I really enjoyed the material.

Class was pretty easy, the lectures were her just reading off the slides so attendance not mandatory. The tests were textbook, so they were easy as long as you have general knowledge of the chapters. The discussion is 2 hours long once a week but is very helpful. Textbook is helpful but you can pass without it. Extra Credit opportunities given.

Easy A and exams were common sense. Lectures were very bad. She read word for word off the slides and there wasn't really any point to attending lectures. She posts review guides before exams so if you study those concepts you'll do well on the exams.

Professor Dumes is very kind, and her lectures are incredibly easy to understand. All of the test material is based off things that we study in class, although I recommend that you study the readings that she gives you as well. I highly recommend taking this class with Professor Dumes.

I wouldn't recommend the course. Grading standards were not clear and my GSI provided minimal rationale for the grades I got. There was some amount of reading but It wasn't needed to do well. I would take a look at other RE courses before taking this one unless you really want to take it. Dumes was a nice instructor but the course was not good.

LOVED ABBY!! She's extremely caring and kind and her lectures are great with the added videos! The content is super relevant and very informative. The exams were word for word from the exam review sessions and nothing was a surprise. Definitely recommend her and I hope I can take other classes of hers.

I LOVED Professor Dumes. WGS 240 is a super laid back class, and I thought I wouldn't be interested in the topics, but I found myself really loving her lectures and wanting to read the outside readings. She is super passionate and caring for her students, even though this class was online. I highly recommend her.

Abby is the sweetest and most caring professor I have ever come across. She really cares about her students and made the course topics engaging and educational. 10/10 would take a class of hers again.
Abby Dumes is one of the best professors at U of M. She is so kind and really cares about all of her students.

Everyone should take this class with Professor Dumes--she is a great lecturer. She uses lots of video clips in her lectures that help you connect the information to real-world applications. It's not a very difficult class, but the material is interesting and presented in a friendly way.

Dumes is an amazing professor. She clearly cares about her students and is very well prepared for every single class. The class itself is very easy, yet very interesting and informative. Definitely made me consider minoring in anthro.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have never studied for a test in here and I have gotten an A on every single one. Just show up to lecture and listen. I've missed a few, but she always posts lectures online :). The exams are very reasonable, there are amazing guest lectures, and the GSIs are helpful. Highly recommended that you take this with Dumes because she makes class fun.
Her lectures were always super interesting and the tests were easy. I never did the readings, just show up to lecture and you should pass.
An easy, basic introduction to anthropology. I did really like how she brought in guest lecturers. Just show up to lecture and pay attention and you'll be fine

Super nice and informative. She puts all the slides online and has review days in class that really help for the exams. If you show up to class (even though she doesn't take attendance so you don't have to) you'll do fine. If you show up and do the readings you basically don't have to study for the tests. Overall it was a really interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Dumes is great, shes very helpful and always comes across more humble than most professors. Workload is easy, lectures are a little pointless because she just reads off the slides. Overall, very approachable so if you need help with your grade its always a possibility!

I am an engineering major, and yet this was my favorite class this semester!! It was easy, but also super interesting and informative. This class was really cool because Dumes uses a lot of modern day examples (like dabbing, etc.) to help us understand terms. Make sure you come to class though! Dumes tests on videos she plays in class.

Absolutely amazing. Reem was one of the few professors I actually enjoyed working with. She knows her material well, and wants her student to understand and succeed in whatever field they are studying. She is always there if you need someone to talk to or if you ever need help with work. I highly recommend taking a course she teaches.

One of my favorite professors I have ever had. Reem is so sweet and in the classroom she tries to make her lectures interactive and fun. I always enjoyed coming to class as Reem always wants to help you and wants you to be a successful student.

At first I thought I was way out of my comfort zone taking Reem's "Not Quite White: Living In America as an Arab" class but she made it fun. Reem is one of the sweetest professors I have met and is willing to help in any situation. I would 100% take this class again. Reem is funny, very encouraging, and welcoming. Take CSP 100 with her if you can!

Reem is an amazing professor who is willing to help you whenever you need it. She is funny and really generous towards her students. I learned a lot from her teaching habits being a student in her Arab in America: Not Quite White course. We had a mixture of lectures, discussions in small groups, share out loud, but in all I had a great time.
Prof Bol is amazing and her grading is very fair and she's very understanding + will give bonus points
It was a good course, I liked the diversity of topics included and the exams were pretty simple.

Professor Bol is a fine professor for Chem 260. She is very dry when lecturing and I didn't like how she often rushed through important material, but I never thought she was being unfair on any of her quizzes or exams in terms of testing the entirety of the material. I wouldn't take her again thought simply because she is so boringgg.

Professor Bol taught the second half of Chem260. Like in the first half, lectures were difficult to comprehend due mainly to how densely packed the slides were. It is easy to lose points, as no partial credit is given on quizzes and only some on exams; this can add up since there are not many graded components. Practice exams were not provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Behrad is the most understanding professor at Michigan. He truly cares for and gets to know his students so well. I had Behrad for four semesters, and he knew my schedule outside of Persian. I gained a good understanding of reading and writing while taking his class. He encourages participation but never forces it. He supported all of his students.

Behrad is one of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever taken a class with at UM. he genuinely wants to see you improve in farsi and will do whatever he can to help. If you're interested in the farsi language, don't miss out on his class.

Agha Behrad wants you to learn Persian more than anything. He is extremely flexible when it comes to turning in homework and will always give you the benefit of the doubt. Easy A classes. I'm so happy that I took him for a few semesters with Persian. Wish he taught the upper levels too!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Behrad was a wonderful teacher! He takes his time with students and walks you through every lesson and mistake along the way. He is very understanding of student health and will help you do everything you can to succeed. Truly deserving of the phrase, "A Real Gem." (Textbook is available free online, though is necessary to have access to!)
Behrad is awesome! SUPER funny, always my favorite class to go to. He's a pretty easy grader as well. Just make sure you're studying your vocab outside of class if you want to learn anything.

Behrad is an awesome professor. His class is easy to succeed in as long as you put in an effort. He appreciates students coming into office hours and is more than willing to help. The class this semester had three exams and homework once or twice a week (which was never too difficult).  He's also hilarious.
Very nice and willing to help. Makes class fun and interesting. I learned a lot more in one semester than I thought I would.

Behrad is such a personable person. He loves to learn about his students and always has a funny life experience to share. He always has some insight into the linguistic root of a word, determining its origin based on cues from various morphemes and phonemes embedded within the word. I was an average caucasian with no experience and loved this class

Iranian/Persian or not, Behrad will become your best friend if you let him. If you need an A, take this class, because you will learn Farsi with minimal effort and he always gives out extra credit. Tests are straight out of the book, so it is easy to study. 4 tests (easy to study for), biweekly hw (copying text), and attendence = A+.

Behrad gives great stories behind how words came to be and describing how they connect with other languages. If you try, you will do well. He is very helpful and wants students to come in to office hours if they are falling behind. He will do anything to get you that A.
He is very disorganized- Poor presentation of learning materials.  He has no passion for what he is doing.  He is the most boring language instructor.  Be careful!!!
I sincerely enjoyed this class! He made learning Farsi an interesting and easy experience.

This class is fairly straightforward but I kind of knew most of the techniques that were described. Dr. Aguilar is good, not very exciting but not boring. Seems like he is pretty tough for the undergrads!
This was a great class and Carlos was a super professor! I liked the group project and thought the class was fun.

I really enjoyed this class even though it was hard at times. Two things I did not like were the lab and how the tests were long. I felt Dr.Aguilar was a good teacher and thought the small stories and demos he would thread into the class were creative.

This was my favorite class that I have taken at Michigan. Professor Aguilar was great and really liked the way he walked through some of the material. The work in the class wasn't too demanding and it was really fun! I had a great group and Professor Aguilar was pretty helpful when I had questions. All together I would recommend the class and him!
I learned so much in this class and really enjoyed meeting with Dr.Aguilar outside of class. He was always kind, tried to make jokes and was helpful for our class project.
Professor Aguilar was nice and a good teacher but his tests were tough!

I really liked Dr. Aguilar and thought he was super nice and down to earth when I would talk to him. I emailed him about applying to med school a year after class had finished and was surprised he remembered me. He helped me with my essays and application and wish more professors were as helpful as him. 221 was tough but I learned a lot!

Professor Aguilar was terrific and kind! He met with me outside office hours several times to talk about grades and helped give feedback about my career plans. He has been my favorite BME professor so far!

He didn't prepare us for the tests at all. Said he was going to do more examples after his midterm evaluation and we still did 2, at most, of basic problems that were examples of the easiest questions from tests and would have other students explain them. I don't care about food or him being nice, I care about actually being taught the material.

Professor Aguilar is the first professor I met who genuinely cared. He would bring food, do demonstrations in class, & share stories about his work. When I asked about help for tests, we discussed strategies to prepare. He also made sure I was okay mentally. Some students were critical of his tests, which were hard, but he was great overall.
Professor Aguilar was great! I enjoyed his lectures, and the ways he connected the material to real world applications. He was a tough grader but thought he was fair.

By far the worst professor I have had so far in my BME classes. He goes back on his word constantly in terms of expectations and assignments. He tests on material that he specifically said will not be assessed. He complained to students about his poor post-midterm evaluation but did little to fix the complaints that students had against him.

Professor Aguilar is a good teacher, in my opinion, he cares about the learning of his students and will help you along the way if you are struggling. However, there is not much homework for the class, and exams are weighted heavily. The class material is challenging but Dr. Aguilar will help you understand if you tell him you need help.

I never knew what was going on in Aguilar's class. He did not prepare us well for the exams and lectures were off topic at many times. He's very passionate about his research which is great, but he did not seem qualified to lecture/teach. Mostly everyone in my section was confused all the time because he was always unclear.
great professor

He's a really nice dude and cares for his students. Only thing is that his lectures aren't too in depth and the way the class is structured, you have to watch prelectures before coming to lectures. He's a tough grader? I don't know if he sets the rubric but grading is tough in this class. But he's caring and will help you.

Prof Aguilar is a great lecturer who does his best to interact with the class as much as he can. That said, you'll want to interact with him as he grades partially on class participation. He obviously really cares about the material and making sure you leave class knowing what goes on behind the curtains of equations and principles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very tough grader, exams are difficult. Make sure to go to office hours for homework, even if you know how to do it, you will lose points on things such as not drawing a diagram or not writing knowns from a problem. Although class is 40-50 students, make sure to participate in class, 100% attendance does equal 100% participation. Overall, average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tough but good professor.

Each class starts with a student presenting on the most previous reading assignment, the class has discussion in small groups, then the groups share their thoughts. He encourages all ideas and is very kind. He is passionate about the class topic "the Anthropocene" and grades fair or easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pedro is one of the kindest professors I have ever had. He constantly reminds us that he is there for us if we need support. He is super passionate about what he teaches, and it is clear that he puts his heart into his work. I adore him, and I'm so sad that I'll likely not get the chance to take another class with him.

Pedro is amazing. He has a huge breadth of knowledge and applies it to every work we read in class. He's amazing at explaining complicated topics and often brings in his own life in Spain as examples. Very fair grader with clear expectations. Too bad he's going to Notre Dame next year- I wish I could take another course with him.
He is adorable and the classes he teaches are super easy and I LOVE HIM!

Pedro is a grad student, so he relates really well to the students in the class.  He is really informal and extremely adorable, friendly, and helpful.  I looked forward to going to his class every day and felt that I learned a lot. His office hours, held in a coffee shop, were fun to go to. I definitely recommend any class taught by Pedro!

His lectures are great. I learned a lot during the lecture. I recommend attending lectures cuz he sometimes drops extra credit opportunities. One thing I didn't like was the lab organization. It jumps from simple amplifier to TIA/LDO design with 10+ transistors. People without prior layout/cadence experience can be tough. Exams were very tough.
I was interested in the course and learnt a lot.

Smart and nice guy, but hard to get in touch with outside of class. Lecture was easy to follow. Tests were open book but way harder than the homeworks. Labs were very poorly organized, and did not effectively prepare us for the final design project which was also poorly organized. Never taught us how to methodically size transistors..

He is very helpful and funny. But the course is very poorly structured. The lecture/homework and exam content can vary a lot. Exams felt more like an “gotcha” than actually testing the content taught. No lecture notes provided too. Additionally there was no tutorial provided for projects for simulations.
Afshari is a great lecturer. The course can use better instructions for the projects, but overall, I learned a lot.

Impossible to succeed without prior knowledge/experience. Exams are completely different from homework and no practice problems given either. Project specs are that of a high-quality industry-level, which is impossible for a first-time learner to gain experience to adapt to. Nice person but CANNOT succeed without prior knowledge/experience.
You won't learn much. The class is badly organized, the professor isn't available outside of class, and there's no feedback on homework or tutorial in labs.

He is pretty knowledgable and he is willing to help out students if you ask him. He's also quite light hearted and funny. However he does go by quite fast in class so you read the textbook and do lots of revisions outside class to fully understand the material. Tests are also quite long so beware. But overall he is quite good.
Afshari is knowledgeable and great at his lectures. He is not very available outside the lectures and his office hours. I learnt a lot from his lectures.
Afshari is very knowledgeable and his lectures are good. However, he is completely unavailable outside lecture and never responds to emails.

I was nervous about taking EECS 215 this semester but Professor Afshari made it a good experience. His lectures can be at times slightly difficult to follow, however the textbook for the class is really good and the majority of the homework is taken from the book. Professor Afshari is really approachable and genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice guy, incomprehensible lectures and poor communication with students.

when he bragged about his research and the 2 companies he owns i should have switched out of his class. the only positive about him is he is obviously very knowledgeable, but as for passing that knowledge to the students, he does a horrible job. he is not available outside of lecture, and his answers to questions in lectures are very condescending.
He was not good. Did not respect students time and did not answer any questions outside of class. I do not recommend taking any class with him

EECS 215 with Ehsan Afshari is my worst class at Umich so far. An organizational nightmare. Afshari never responded to student concerns over class logistical issues and seemed absent at all times other than lecture. Never made an attempt to hold office hours or reach out to students. He knew the course material but taught the class terribly.

Seemed nice enough in lectures, but I asked him for an extension on some HW, and initially he said it was okay, I just needed to also send it to the IA. When I asked for their e-mail as well, he got super upset and called me lazy, and said my HW was "unreadable" so he would no longer accept it. Came off very condescending.
Excellent lectures, very knowledgeable, and fun.
Great lectures. Very knowledgable.
One of the worst professors that U of M has to offer. Unresponsive, unhelpful, and uncaring towards students. He's almost impossible to reach outside of lecture and never responds to emails.

For your own good, please avoid him. Entering the semester, I saw all the bad reviews he had but thought How bad could it be? Well, it is terrible. He is an unhelpful teacher and he is by far the worst teacher I have ever had in all my life.  Ignore 5 ratings from his apple-polisher graduate students. I am very sorry for his own grad students.

This guy is terrible. I can't comprehend how he even got his Ph.D. He's extremely disorganized, literally unresponsive to his email and very careless. He provides no support or feedback on HWs. DO NOT TAKE ANY COURSE WITH HIM.

This guy literally never responds to emails. Avoid taking any classes with him. I have a hard time believing that he's one of the ECE grad advisors. I honestly feel bad for any grad students that have to rely on him as an advisor.
Good lecturer but very poorly organized
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Focusses a lot on developing intuition which is very useful for circuit designers.
Great inspiration. All classes should be like this one.
OH MY GOD! Horrible professor. You bet barely can find him outside class. Even he does not regularly show up at the class lectures. No response to emails! So Careless!

Not organized at all. Lab works were basically nothing. You design an inverter and suddenly have to design full system. No feedback. No replies to emails. Only good thing was himself being very nice guy only in a classroom.

Nice person. Respectful of students. Great expertise. However, the class was an organizational disaster. Received virtually no feedback on HW's, labs, exams, & project. Lectures were subpar. Never responded to emails. Had 3 weeks to do our MDE and 1 for research paper (during MDE). By far the worst & most disappointing class I've taken at Michigan.

I had Britta at Vassar and really liked her. She's funny and knows really weird but cool things. She's also really understanding of actual human life problems, she definitely cares about us. You will be given plenty of exercises but not that many things are graded. I wish she wouldn't assign such expensive books.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: I could be bias on this review because I dislike history classes to begin with but probably one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. She is very monotone and rambles on reading word for word on the powerpoints. Her weekly quizzes barely match the readings assigned which makes them difficult to do well. If you can avoid this class, do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Professor Ager at UMass Amherst, and I think it was her first semester here. I was dreading this class, but she made the information more appealing and is obviously very passionate about what she does. You won't need the textbooks very much in this class, and she's a really solid choice if you need to take a history course.

Britta is one of the best professors it has ever been my luck to learn from. She truly cares about her students and will go the extra mile to help them. She is an extremely lenient grader and takes into account her student's struggles. I previously hated Latin, but she actually made my final semester an enjoyable experience. BRITTA IS THE BEST!

I was not looking forward to the 4th semester of Latin. But then came Britta. She is one of the coolest professors I've ever had and makes the class very interesting. Her laidback and fun personality makes the material more open and relatable. I STRONGLY recommend this professor. She made a dreadful class enjoyable and I learned a lot.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking a class from. She genuinely cares about her students and their success, and she will work with them whenever they need help.  I highly recommend her to any student for any class, she will go above and beyond and try to make class fun, and she's a very lenient grader

Britta is not only one of the best professors I've ever had in any subject, but she is also one of the most genuine and caring individuals I have had the pleasure of getting to know. She is extremely knowledgeable, receptive, and invested in the success of her students. She even made Latin, which I previously hated, fun. Excellent professor.
Horribly boring class! Was supposed to be on Roman Sports and Daily Life, but was more like a history class. Not interesting at all.

I was nervous to take the fourth semester of Latin because I've never been good at it. I was lucky to end up in Britta's class. She makes me feel extremely comfortable, and therefore I'm not scared to volunteer or ask questions. She lets her students get away with a lot, but in the end, we're learning, and having fun with it, so who cares?
Just boring as hell.  She rambles on about random stuff on power points.  I wanted to learn about Roman sports and it was the least amount of stuff she talked about.  She is so monotone too.
Seems unsure of herself, rambles about topics which feel irrelevant to the class.  Very poor experience in a class I was previously excited to take.
Horrible professor. Take an interesting topic (Roman Sports) and just makes it absolutely boring. Even her jokes are so unfunny. I would NOT recommend any class she teaches.

Great discussion leader. Really knows the books and tries to get the students talking. If you're obvious about taking the class to fulfill the ULWR, she'll probably torch you. If you are interested in the material, or at least try to be, she'll be one of the most helpful discussion leaders you'll have.
Not my experience at all.  Our discussion section was great.

She is a GSI. Avoid her! She is not particularly knowledgeable, completely unresponsive (won't even answer emails) and unavailable if you need help. She is always late in returning assignments. In fact, sometimes she doesn't even return rough drafts of papers before the final version is due! Despite this fact, she is an extremely hard grader!
Bad teacher
enjoyed the class a lot. need to read everything that is assigned.

I would not recommend this professor to anyone.  He seems to think teaching is inconvenient for him. He talks down to students and acts as if helping them is beneath him.  His directions are unclear at best. He's not here to teach, that's for sure.

NRE 510 is manditory for first year MS students, which is too bad because it's an awful class.  Arun is nice, but totally unclear.  He could or would not explain his indecipherable problem sets, and then marked down students who didn't understand.  The exam was worse, confusing and poorly worded. The entire class failed and it had to be curved.

Vanessa is by far the most encouraging and inspirational professor that I have had at U of M. She pushes students to learn about their relative interests while still sticking to the course material. I wish every professor cared as much about their courses as Vanessa does.
She is extremely nice and helpful.  She prompts your interest in the material and she engages you in discussion.
Awesome teacher! You learn a lot with out stressing out!
best professor I ever had. being a grad student I had tons of them.
Awesome professor! Very helpful. Prepare to work hard for it, but you'll learn a lot.

Professor Agnew is a brilliant cultural theorist. She is also an amazing mentor. At the graduate level she is challenging but extreemly fair. Her sense of humor is also appreciated. Her course on the history of German musical thought was much more interesting than many of the courses offered in the music department.
pretentious, annoying, hard grader, insane. stay away.
she was okay. it just wasnt very interesting.
Love Ahmad. He is a super tough grader, but it was fun to be in his class. He is super casual and it is possible to talk to him about anything. love you ahmad < 3 uwu
Incredibly condescending and unhelpful in class/office hours. Essentially self-studied and got an A+ without him.

Ahmad was good at explaining concepts, and he was very flexible with office hours. He also made an effort to get to know his students despite our fully remote class. Although Math 115 is a difficult class, Ahmad will thoroughly go through any questions and weakness you have to make the class easier.

Professor Ahn is a genius. This class teaches soooo much, and you will gain expertise in Excel and business analytics that will be unmatched. Lots of homework assignments that often take many, many hours. But it's worth it if you are interested and really want to master business analytics, machine learning and Excel!
He makes statistic less scary, but he gave us a lot of homework. He is a nice guy too.
Good
Makes stats so much fun
Humor used extensively in class.  He makes an otherwise dull subject (Stats) more enjoyable.  He's personable, hip, and has a great smile.
BEST TEACHER YOU'LL EVER HAVE.  IF YOU RATED HIM BAD CUZ YOU GOT A BAD GRADE YOU'RE AN IDIOT

This is a very difficult and time consuming class by nature.  Ahn is the best of all the 301 profs.  He makes bus. stats as fun as it can be!  And like he says, if you do all the homeworks and go to every class, your final grade will at least be in the B range.  TIP: Pick smart hw partners and do NOT buy the book!!!
The class sucked royally, but Ahn's antics made up for it.
Ahn is very entertaining and made business stats as fun as it could possibly be.  Overall one of my favorite professors at the business school!
ahn is by far an amazing prof, makes stats interesting with fun pop culture references and is just a cool, jolly guy
No Comments
No Comments
Easy minicourse on Marcus Aurelius's meditations. The class is very easy to get an A in, however I don't think I would take this professor for a full term course because she seems a bit disorganized.

She cares so much about us students, super accommodating and understanding, encouraged and supported us, made me infinitely more confident in my Greek skills! Made sure everyone understood before moving on, explained things thoroughly, made the texts relatable and engaging, held office hours all the time. One of the best professors I've ever had!

(GRK301) 1st, she chooses favorites very quickly, and if you are not one of her favorites, you will know. She treats least-fav students rudely in class, and is far more strict with them regarding time limits on tests, etc. 2nd, she simply does not have a strong command of the Greek language. Constant grammar mistakes, poor explanations.

Sara is sooo disorganized and when she is going through something, everyone knows. Her lectures are quite chaotic, but they can be entertaining. It was an interesting first take of a class at Michigan. I don't think the Honors Dept has her teach Great Books anymore, but she was something. Her GSIs were incredible. They improved my writing 100%

The grade for this class is entirely based on your GSI (in my case at least) and going to lectures was not necessary beyond a certain point. This Professor is clearly very passionate and knowledgable about what she does, but lectures were muddled, unclear, often way off topic, and disorganized. She is a very kind and earnest person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not many points, so each is worth a lot. She was very interested in the material which made the class more enjoyable. If you try to be interested, then you will become interested!!

Absolutely amazing experience. My favorite curriculum for any class I have ever taken. Not a "show up and get an A" class, but if you do a reading then write the paper and demonstrate understanding you will get an A, nay an A+. Very minimal level of work needed to do well. She's very fun and unique, and really means well by her students. 3 papers
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor had unorganized lectures and often ran into unnecessary technical difficulties. Slides were unconventional and she often went on unrelated tangents. Seldom did the lectures help write your papers. I got by using spark notes instead of doing most of the readings. Discussion sections were much more useful.

She's definitely a character and sometimes gets side-tracked in lectures. She is obviously very smart and knows what she is talking about. Attendance for lecture was not mandatory, you definitely don't need to attend them to get an A. The course has a ton of reading but she understands this and gives you specific passages to look close at.

This is an extremely easy class if you get a GSI that's an easy grader. However, Professor Ahbel-Rappe's lectures didn't seem well-prepared and most weren't especially interesting. There is no reason to show up to lectures - if you go to your discussion groups and put in a little bit of effort on the essays, you will get an A.

Sara is very passionate about the material, but her lectures often seem all over the place and have little correlation to the books read. She often references books not included in the curriculum and is very disorganized. Sara pressures confused students to participate and is disrespectful when she does not receive her desired answer.

It's obvious that Sara is passionate about her subject materials, but class management and preparation could use some work. It took until almost the end of the course until students were grasping the material that she was presenting, and she tried to facilitate discussion on topics it was obvious we weren't clear on. Not the best ULWR.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Sara is great but her GSIs suck. This class, "Magic and Witchcraft", may seem like a joke but the assignments are graded pretty harshly by the GSI. Also, I don't know if Sara and her GSIs even talk about things because when I emailed them, they all say something different. But I guess Sara isn't the one grading, so listen to the GSI.
She is extremely knowledgable but she really has no idea how to handle teaching a class. The class is an easy A but don't expect to learn anything or do meaningful work.

This class (Ancient Medicine) actually turned out to be quite a bit more interesting than I thought it would be. Dr. Ahbel-Rappe is a bit scatter-brained at times and STRUGGLES using LectureTools, but shows a genuine interest in the material, makes lecture interesting, and is always willing to help (She's also hilarious!). Class was pretty easy.

I cannot even begin to explain how beneficial taking a class with Prof. Rappe has been on my life. Besides being an amazing teacher, she legitimately cares about her students grasping the sometimes difficult concepts in this philosophical course. She constantly evolves her teaching style to best benefit the student.
Sara is one of the best professors I've ever had at U of M.  Definately take this class.
Great class- I learned so much had fun doing that. Class lecture and discussions were interesting and very helpful toward understanding this material.

Sara was an awesome professor, and made Plato more interesting than he already is. She gets very much into what shes lecturing, and always wants to hear other perspectives. She also is very helpful in office hours. Easy grader.

I took this class to fulfill a philosophy requirement and had no interest in it before this class, but she turned out to be the most interesting professor I have ever had, and I have taken three more classes with her, she's that great. You'll love her. She may be a little hyper sometimes, but it makes class that much better.

I had this professor in the mid-90s. She is the smartest person I've ever met. But sometimes she'd go on and on about The One, till one day I crumpled up a bag of Doritos, threw it at her, and walked out. She seemed to favor one kid in the class, named 'Shu. I loved 'em both!
Best professor I ever had. So interesting and full of knowledge. Class is entertaining and informative. She goes on tangents that are endearing and fascinating.
I learned a great deal. And the class was hysterical!

sara is one of the most intelligent people i have ever met. she really knows what she is talking about; however, in her brilliance, she is sometimes scatter-brained. she talks extremely quickly (and sometimes is hard to listen to), but she is very thorough. there was a lot of last minute reading, but i didn't mind because i learned so much from her
Very intelligent woman but she likes to interupt and unless discussion is animated, class is pretty boring.

Ron was a great professor, but the class is pretty difficult. Start preparing for exams early as they are worth a large part of your grade. Overall, he really cares about his students, the tests are just difficult to prepare for.
Nice guy but takes the class far too seriously and gives very little leeway to students. Avoid if you care about your gpa and just want to get your lsa requirement

Ron was quite rude to the students in his class during lectures, and I found him to be the toughest and most unforgiving grader of any Spanish professor I have had at Umich. He ruined my love for spanish, before him I was considering minoring in Spanish, but I no longer have a desire to. Worst professor I've had at U of M.

Ron was great! I only had him for 1/2 of a semester because he had to go on paternity leave and was really sad for him to leave. He really honors hard work and participation. Def not the easiest grader, but like I said if you challenge yourself and work hard it will not go unnoticed. I learned a lot from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ron makes you think beyond who you are. He's a great teacher. I've learned a lot from him. I would recommend him for anything he decides to teach.

Prof. Ron is an amazing professor. He makes class go super fast and wants everyone to do well. All of my past professors have been tough graders so I've never strongly noticed his tough grading style as seen in the other comments. Just practice for the exams and you'll be good.

I placed into 232 without speaking Spanish consistently for about 4 years, even so with my background being very little. Ron made the environment super relaxed and friendly. He was also very clear on expectations.

I really enjoyed having Ron as a professor. Despite not personally enjoying Spanish 231 and getting a B+ in it, I found Ron's class to be much more enjoyable than 231. He does a good job teaching material in class, repeating concepts to ensure everyone understands them, and making them fun. I would highly recommend him for 232!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed spanish 232. I think Profe Roosevelt is a great teacher. He is very organized, accessible, and encouraging, however, he is a tough grader. I worked really hard in this class and maybe should have been in an easier level but we made it work. He made me want to continue taking spanish classes

When my semester started, it had been about 5 years since I had last taken a Spanish class. Ron did a great job of starting with the fundamentals and helping me grow from there. The class was challenging, but the rest comes naturally if you show up and participate. The oral exam was stressful, but I did fine because he didn't expect perfection.

Really liked this class and learned a lot about linguistics having never taken a linguistics class before. Some of the concepts and tests were a little hard, and I wished we had done just a little bit more practice with them, but he was very kind, understanding, and made the lectures interesting.

Participation matters A LOT! He takes it very seriously, so I suggest participating at least twice a day. He makes sure all students understand the content, and provides a lot of helpful resources when studying for exams. He's honestly the best spanish prof I had so far, even tho this class is hard because his teaching method is the best.

Ron is a great professor. I had never taken a linguistics class before and he made it very interesting and easy to understand in 298. He's very funny and keeps the lectures quite entertaining. You can tell he cares about students. One weird thing is that technology is completely not allowed in class, but it's worth it. Highly recommend this course.

Ron is an awesome professor. While some of the content in the class may be difficult, he truly cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He does a great job at teaching the material by making the class interactive. Definitely take a class with him if you can.

Ron was really great at teaching linguistics and made the topics  interesting. There is reading to do before class, but the material is repeated information from class, however if you don't understand a topic it's good for clarity. He is definitely a hard grader for homework (hw=exam q's), but as long as you put in effort you can get an A.

Prof. Roosevelt is the best! Took 277 this semester and it was the only class that I was always excited for. Workload is very doable and the content is taught very well. 10/10 would take another class taught by him, this dude is the goat.
He was funny and willing to work with students, but its a fast moving class and he was not forgiving if you miss anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I was pretty nervous about taking Spanish up again after a couple of years off, but this class was super engaging and Prof. Ron made it fun. Very heavy on Spanish grammar with lots of writing activities and some smaller homework assignments, but you're able to use a dictionary so long as you cite. We also got the chance to socialize (in Spanish ofc

Not an easy A for language credit, but Ron gives clear explanations, thoughtful answers to questions, and brings a funny positive energy to class. Definitely recommend for anyone interested in Spanish grammar.

I was fortunate enough to have Ron for both 103 and 230 and he was by far my favorite professor during my time at U-M. He will make the subject incredibly interesting as long as you put in some time and effort. If you want an A+ for simply having a pulse, he may not be for you. If you want to actually develop new, valuable skills, he's your guy.

Although I came into this class expecting to hate the language-learning process, Professor Roosevelt somehow got me interested in not only the Spanish language, but also linguistics. His teaching style, enthusiasm and personability transformed this from a class that I was looking to avoid to one that I couldn't wait to attend almost daily.

Had Ron for Spanish 230--8 credit class. For studying Spanish 8 hours a week, a professor can make or break your semester. If you're willing to actively participate, you'll enjoy coming to class everyday. Ron takes the class very seriously but is also very laid back. Willing to joke around and have fun. If willing to put in the time, you'll be okay
Seriously best teacher

Ron might seem tough at first, but he does everything for a reason and explains all of the methods to his madness. He is not just there to get you your required Spanish credit; he is there to give you better language skills and knowledge about different cultures. I'm so grateful for Ron and this class, and because of it I am now minoring in Spanish

Class with Ron was always a good part of my day. He clearly loves Spanish and though he can be a bit of a tough grader, he is always happy to help you understand the concepts in office hours/outside of class. Would definitely take again

Ron is a really sincere and good guy and I greatly enjoyed his class. That said, it is pretty tough and he will get you out of your comfort zone a little bit. But hey, taking risks is what school is all about and Ron knows that. He was a great choice for the fourth semester.

If you are not confident in your Spanish do not take a class with Ron. However if you are good at speaking and really want to learn Spanish like have a passion for the language you can do well. Ron's a cool person but if you are not confident in your speaking this is not the professor who will make you more comfortable speaking.

I never liked Spanish and was only taking 232 to finish my language requirement but Ron has made me consider taking 270 because of his enthusiasm. He is a tough grader, especially when it comes to participation, but if you try, you can do well. His workload is very manageable- two 325 word diarios every 2 weeks, and short online activities nightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Beware when taking a class with Ron, he does not care about his students. IF you are good at Spanish you will probably do ok in the class but, if it is not your strong suit he will not be of any help. DO not expect him to help you in office hours they are pointless. There are a lot of good spanish teachers here so I would try to get someone else

I asked Ron for advice for the final and a few other exams and he gave little feedback. For the final, he actually sent me the same e-mail he posted on canvas pointing me to the study guide, which I had asked in my e-mail for more specific study strategies. If you're not strong with Spanish/language, do not take with Ron.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is structured like every other Spanish class however, if you struggle at all with Spanish his class is not for you. He does not create a welcoming atmosphere if you are not great at speaking Spanish. Even if you are trying your best, you will not receive good participation grades, effort is NOT taken into any consideration for grades.

Many people love Ron, but I was not a fan of his attitude. I will say I struggle with Spanish and talked to him multiple times on how to better my grade. I would not recommend Ron to students that want to finish up their language requirement, he is a tough grader, and I do not think he is the most friendly when trying to attempt Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Fantastic teacher who cares about his students and makes class interesting

Ron is the best prof I've had. I didn't like Spanish at first but he made me really appreciate the language and now I'm considering a Spanish major/minor. He can be tough but he's a lot of fun, knows his stuff, and everything he does makes you a better Spanish speaker/listener/writer/reader. He keeps class moving and is overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ron was a great instructor--he has such a vast knowledge of Spanish and he really cares that his students gain a quality understanding of the Spanish language and the culture in Spanish-speaking countries. Ron is hilarious and connects with his students really well. Such a great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ron was such a great professor!! You could clearly see the genuine interest he has for Spanish and his students. I loved learning slang and hearing about his experiences abroad. He's strict about ONLY speaking in Spanish which really sucked at first but you get used to it and my Spanish is sooo much better now. I would definitely take him again!

If you have to take 103 at U of M, TAKE IT WITH RON! I hated Spanish in high school, and Ron made every class not only interesting, but fun. He made me like Spanish. You need to go to class, because practicing  learning w/ languages, but if you want to ease the pain of a 4-day/week class, take it with one of the best profs U of M has to offer.

AEROSP 215 with Johnson has been one of my favorite classes I've taken at Michigan. He is an engaging lecturer that makes efficient use of class time. Lectures are better in person but attendance isn't mandatory and everything was recorded, which I appreciated. The homeworks can get long but are manageable and great practice for quizzes.

I like Prof Johnson, he's funny and respectful. But I really don't like the fact he doesn't give practice exams because they don't have the "bandwidth"? I get that it takes time but the lecture slides used are from a past prof and the HW is mainly problems from a textbook. Not sure where the time goes for this course but practice exams would help

So glad I took this class when I did. Johnson literally one of the top 3 in this department in terms of being an amazing prof and caring about students. He made 483 truly amazing. I learned a lot about spacecraft design and made a final product I'm really proud of. Johnson provided numerous resources as well as extra credit. Love this class.

Professor Johnson is a really great professor. You can tell he cares about his students. We had a hard matlab project but he had a lot of office hours/resources to help and pushed back the deadline by like a month because he realized the project was harder than expected. I loved him as a professor and would gladly take one of his classes again.

I have never taken MATLAB in my life, I took Rob 102 for Engr 101. I struggled so hard with Project 2 and 3, I hope to god he never chooses to do this ever again in his life. He made all of us miserable unless you actually know MATLAB.

Professor Johnson has worked with education research in the past, and it is very evident in his courses. He is passionate about helping his students and he has a great feedback system. Very friendly and approachable. Perfect guy to teach introductory Aerospace and Statics courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Johnson is so good! His lectures are interactive and really help you learn. The class itself is pretty homework heavy, and there are lots of tests and quizzes so make sure you devote time to Aero 215. His grading on exams is very nice. Partial credit and error carried forward will save you so much. He grades you on Aero215, not on math mistakes.

Dr. Johnson is the best professor I've ever had at UMich. Take AEROSP215 with him, you will not regret it. Very clear and concise explanations of the material, and very accessible outside of class during office hours. There's plenty of extra credit, and if you study for exams you should be fine. Start studying maybe 7-10 days before the exam.

Dr. Johnson is sincerely both an incredible professor and great person. So much so that I came here just to leave a positive review. It is obvious throughout class that his goal is for the students to actually learn the course material, and also that he genuinely cares about each individual student. If you have the option, take 215 with him.

Prof. Johnson is the best professor I have had. He is always engaged in the class, cares that the students learn, and is ready to spend extra hours for anyone who needs it. His research is in education which goes to show how much he cares about teaching. Take this professor!

Johnson is the man. He records his lectures, posts his notes online, works tirelessly to help students through office hours, and responds to e-mails promptly. His tests are quite fair. He has a strict homework late policy but rightfully so, as he posts solutions afterward to review if you want. Wonderful professor, best of the semester. Hard HW.

Johnson is a new instructor who cares a lot about his students and about improving the course. Rough late policy but gives opportunities for extra credit. Has some things to learn but still a lot of fun to learn from. Very responsive to student feedback. Clear explanations. Very friendly and approachable. Get ready for dad jokes. Lots of dad jokes.

Dr. Johnson is an amazing professor who really cares about improving his course. He teaches well and is constantly taking and acting on suggestions. Overall I love his class and would definitely take another class with him.
Professor Pierce is great, he really cares and is very helpful.

Such a great guy who loves to share his passion! Will get much more out of the class if you go to lecture, but definitely not necessary. His lectures work well as an addition to reading the book / previous notes, but if you rely solely on them you will fall behind. Luckily the HWs are easy and short for 4 cr. so you have extra time to read.
Great professor overall. Always brings his passion for physics to lectures.
Aaron Pierce is the greatest professor in the continental United States
Best professor I've had so far! Clearly loves physics so if you do too, take his classes with him.

Aaron was a great lecturer! Definitely go to class though, as his powerpoints were largely images that he explained verbally. 116 had one midterm, a final project, and some easy HW assignments. Midterm was curved. Project was time consuming but graded very leniently. Awesome, knowledgable and funny guy teaching a great course. Would recommend!
Really nice, and eager to help!

Go to office hours if you're struggling. He'll never make you feel like you asked a dumb question (even if it really was dumb). He's very nice+helpful+knowledgeable.  Take good notes; don't just copy what he writes on the board (when you look at it later it'll probably be incomprehensible. You need his verbal explanations of the formulas+pictures).

Legend says that he understood the ABC conjecture before anyone else and gave solutions through mystical visions. Some say that he appeared to Shinichi Mochizuki in a dream (he was the one who conceived the entire field of Inter-Universal Teichmuller Theory). Some theorize that he might also be the vision Ramanujan saw before cracking partitions.

Pixton is very knowledgeable in math. Sometimes his lectures are just too advanced for undergrads which also is in part the material. He is a generous grader but there lacked some clarity sometimes. Material is hard for the course.

When Grass Man Ian attacked the class, Pickstone saved us all. While the sheafs were quasi-coherent, Pickstone was more than coherent. “This is OUR class” he cried, rallying the communist diagrams behind him. Immediately, his magnificent hair rose on its ends and the Grass Man Ian fled in terror. I'm rating him 2 out of 2.
Pickstoneee my loveeee

Only a few areas where Pixton could add some clarity to his lectures. However, his method of lecturing worked well for me. Generous with grading; curves of 20-30% to exam scores, waiving quizzes, and incorporating effort into grades. Occasionally appears frustrated when students can't answer his questions in class (maybe somewhat justified lol)
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No curve. No extra credit.  Quizzes are ten percent of our grade, midterms are 50 percent, and the final is 40 percent. Homework does not count towards the grade. do not take the class with him, as the syllabus was completely of his design and not standard for the class. The professor turned the easiest class at umich into something that its not.

Being foreign, my Thanksgivings are usually lonely, but this year Aaron invited us students to dinner. He roasted 67 turkeys and when I inquired about the amount he explained that 67 is a prime number, launching into a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis that sent me into such an academic delirium that the only words I can now utter are "6" or "7".

I was trying to draw all the homeomorphically irreducible trees with n = 10 on the board outside class, but I couldn't quite do it.

Pixton was mopping the floors nearby & proceeded to solve it with his mop. I asked him how and he said that my Gordon Wood was good, but I forgot about something called "Vickehs." 

I do like them apples, Aaron!

He is the universal property: I was never worried about being able to put my thoughts into words, since all my thoughts factored through his mind. He was even able to grade my homework before I had written it up. He also discovered a new prime when he said that our methods generalized to any field, including the field of characteristic 10.

yuh ma boi aaron pixton mad tuffington. I was sad he make me happy.
If aaron pixton has a million fans i am one of them
if aaron pixton has 1 fan I am his only fan
if aaron pixton has no fans I am dead
i love aaron pixton the goat fr fr
he like so mathy like idek
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had long since stopped believing in Santa Claus, but on the night of the 25th, something changed my mind. I saw Aaron Pixton drinking milk from my fridge and leaving behind a note with a brilliant solution to a math problem I had been stuck on. When I approached him, he told me this was his winter break side hustle. He's amazing!

I was rolling a boulder towards the Grand Hilbert Hotel when I met Pixton, upon which he informed me that the hotel had infinite rooms but was full, so they may or may not be able to accommodate me and my boulder. He then vaulted my boulder 10 km so that I could try again later. Great guy, really put my happiness into perspective.

My boyfriend Arnav was bullying me at every lecture, which ruined my class performance and made me depressed.

Luckily, Dr. Pixton was also a part-time clinical psychologist who taught me that some problems are unsolvable, like the Goldbach conjecture. He solved the conjecture anyways (I'm still bullied) but I'm now a resilient man. Thanks Aaron!

When challenged to explain the concept of infinity, Professor Pixton started a lecture that lasted for weeks, demonstrating it by counting non-repeating decimal places of Pi in real-time. I aged considerably during the lecture, but now I truly grasp the concept of "forever". Truly a genius lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While struggling with a problem on algebraic topology, Pixton claimed he could simplify it by introducing a new dimension--Pixton-space. Curious, I followed his guidance, only to discover he had tricked me into proving P=NP using abstract knot theory. Now I'm touring the world explaining how Pixton's joke revolutionized computational mathematics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor, but he has this really annoying habit: when working on homework problems, occasionally I'd get really stuck. With no warning, Pixton would materialize behind me, whisper hints into my ear, and then disappear before I can reply. Don't get me wrong it's helpful, but also a little off-putting.

After a rough night in Vegas, I was on the brink of losing everything. As I was about to bet the last dollar to my name on roulette, Aaron Pixton materialized behind me and explained that he knew the movement and position of every atom in the casino, allowing him to predict all the spins. He then proceeded to win 30 consecutive spins ($1 billion).

Before flying home I decided to stop at the McDonald's in DTW. Right before I bit into my Big Mac, Professor Pixton broke through the ceiling and obliterated it. In a thunderous voice, he proclaimed: "NEVER eat at the McDonald's at DTW" before vanishing. It seems the Lovecraftian horrors that lurk at that restaurant will have to wait another day.
With his devilish wit and captivating charm, Professor Pixton is undoubtedly one of Earth's finest specimens.

I began to wonder how Professor Pixton was able to accomplish so many incredible feats, so I asked him what his secret was during office hours. He revealed to me that he used his knowledge of the Banach-Tarski paradox to construct multiple identical copies of himself, and that there were actually hundreds of Pixtons in the world. A brilliant idea!

I'm in student government and one day I was worried because we would be voting on an extremely controversial bill. When I vented my worries to Aaron, he volunteered to help me out by ingeniously spending hours detailing his proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, effectively filibustering the bill. We have now come to a complete standstill. Thanks Aaron!

I was playing in a Dungeons and Dragons campaign this year, but my DM (also in Pixton's 465) contracted a terminal illness and was unable to finish the campaign. Luckily, Professor Pixton took a week to watch all of Dimension 20 and memorize every rule and mechanic in every sourcebook so we could continue playing. Thank you Professor Pixton!

This semester, I wanted to start working out, and Aaron volunteered to be my personal trainer. Aaron's personalized gym routine for me was my homework, and the final was a grueling full-body fitness test. Because of university policy I was given a failing grade since I hadn't learned any math, but thanks to Aaron I achieved my true goal.

I knew that professor Pixton was a genius when he used principles from algebraic geometry to construct the Ship of Theseus and then replaced all of its parts. Unfortunately the bell rang right before he finished the proof, and he had to immediately leave because his private jet flight to Dubai was leaving soon (he was meeting the Sheik).

I was instantly captivated by his charming voice and tone. Every word spoken to me was understood immediately and from the beginning I was immediately propelled into an A grade. Would gladly recommend to all future students.

After a torturously hard semester, I was worried he would set a really difficult final exam. Luckily, there was only one problem on the test: prove that the real part of every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function is 1/2. We had seen this problem before on our homework, and I solved it with ease. Thank you Aaron!

After bombing both midterms, I was at risk of failing this class. I talked to Professor Pixton about it during office hours, and he was generous enough to offer me an extra credit assignment: find an uncountable set with cardinality strictly less than the reals. His class had easily prepared me for the problem, and I finished it in an afternoon.

Before I took this class I was a devout atheist. I rejected religion and wandered through life with no beliefs and no principles. However, after discussing this with Prof Pixton, he told me that he was in fact the second coming of Jesus. It all makes sense now. I have now been reborn as a new man, filled with new purpose and strength.
Pickston, my love. I thank you so much
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class meets at 8am in the mornings. I am absolutely not a morning person. Luckily, Professor Pixton always made sure we got up on time. Every morning, he would personally come to each of our apartments to wake us up. Sometimes, if we did well on homework, he would even bring us breakfast in bed. I never missed a day of class, thanks to him.

One morning I ran into Professor Pixton, and we walked to class together. On the way to class, however, he wanted to stop by the neighboring homeless shelter. He proceeded to take solid gold ingots out of his backpack and handed one to every person he saw (including myself). I've never quite met anyone as selfless as him.

Last few days has been windy and cold. I am exchange student from Siberia. No money for coat. Long walk to class. Luckily, when Professor overhear about my troubles, he let me move into his apartment and drive me to class every day. I sleep on mattress next to couch. He even make me his favorite American dish (burger). I am forever in debt to him.

I went to Prof. Pixton's office hours and told him that I was struggling to visualize concepts in class, such as the donut/mug example. He informed me that humans are actually homeomorphic to both due to their digestive tracts, and then grabbed the student next to me and continuously morphed his body into a donut. It was so much clearer after that!
My favorite BTS member.

Aaron is a tasteful man. I was once talking to him about the works of Dostoevsky, and he managed to draw a connection between his works and the symphonies of Tchaikovsky using a lemma he derived in math 475. And did I ever mention that he proved the Riemann Hypothesis in class? Crazy.

Prof. Pixton is an absolute beast. When I was watching the world cup, I told him I was sad because France might rob Messi of his last chance to win, so he personally took up the most intense athletic training regime known to man and joined the Argentinian team in disguise. When Prof. Pixton scored the winning penalty, I cried.

My man Aaron is the chillest mf out there. After the final, he threw us a pizza party in his 4-bedroom apartment (where he lives alone) and as a bit of post-class enrichment he showed us a bit of his current research which developed from his ingenious proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. I've never quite met another professor as awesome as this guy.

Great professor, super chill guy. Even taught me a couple of advanced chess tactics during office hours when I told him I was into chess. Class content was reasonably interesting and he was very willing to help out in office hours when I was struggling. Couldn't recommend him more!
The class served as a good intro to number theory, and professor Pixton taught it well. Go to office hours for extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: My son took Aaron Pixton's class last semester. Three days in, he was able to form a bijection between the Riemann Hypothesis and the meaning of life. I don't know what he discovered, but he now lives in the mountains of Tibet. On several occasions men in black suits and shades have shown up to inquire his location, but I know as much as them.

Do NOT take any class with Professor Pixton. He is such a genius and incredible teacher that, after one semester of classes, the entire field of combinatorics now seems like a triviality to me. Math is no longer fun. Not to mention, he proved the Riemann Hypothesis on the first day of class. Absolute monster of a human.

After breaking up with my boyfriend Arnav, I felt quite sad. That is, until I took Prof. Pixton's class. Despite math being so hard, Pixton's charisma completely penetrated my understanding. He was like a father, breaking the problems step by step, until the whiteboard completely exploded with math equations and filled me up with knowledge.

One day in class, professor Pixton overheard me telling my friend Arnav that I was nervous about my open heart surgery later that week. He then proceeded to obtain an MD in the span of three days and applied to be my surgeon so that he could be sure that I was in good hands. He was so skilled that I didn't even need anesthesia or pain killers.

An old adage states "You catch a man a fish and he eats for a day; you teach a man to fish and he eats for life". I don't really know what this means, but I do know that professor Pixton proved the Riemann Hypothesis in class.

On the first day of class, Aaron solved a Rubik's cube in 10 seconds and linked it back to his research in algebraic geometry. Then, we had a little bit of time left so to pass the time, he proved the Hodge conjecture as a bit of enrichment material. We then proved the rest of the Milennium prize problems the next class. What an incredible man.

At first, I was a bit intimidated by Professor Pixton, but he is genuinely the nicest man I've ever met. I ran away from home in the middle of the year, and professor Pixton was the one who took me in. He mentored me throughout my stay and landed me a job at google. Truly a life changing experience.

This course was very difficult throughout the whole semester, and for a long time I questioned if I was cut out for it. However, on the last day of class he revealed that he had actually taught us the material of Math 465, 565, 566, 669, as well as the Riemann Hypothesis all in a single semester. I have my PhD now. He's brilliant!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As a homework problem, Prof Pixton asked us to prove or disprove PNP. When I complained that it was too hard because it was a Millenium Prize Problem, he proved the Riemann Hypothesis in front of the whole class to show that Millenium Prize Problems are no harder than textbook problems. Truly brilliant guy, I'll never look at math in the same way.

In class, we computed every single Ramsey number, and then proved the Riemann Hypothesis. Professor Pixton is the most brilliant man I've ever met, and I know that he will go down in history as not only the best mathematician in modern times, but also the most caring father.

Professor Pixton single handedly proved the Riemann Hypothesis in class and ever since then, I have never been able to see mathematics the same way. He showed me a new way to approach the field and after taking his course, I now have enough prerequisite knowledge to graduate with a PhD in mathematics this semester. Thank you sir.

I contracted a terminal illness over the course of the semester, and Professor Pixton took the time to show up to my hospital bed to bring me a personalized get-well-soon card and a bouquet of very nice flowers. A gem of a professor. Nicest guy I've ever met. I don't think I've met another professor who demonstrated as much care and respect as him.

He is good for an upper-level class. The fact that he didn't post lecture notes or make his lecture videos readily available made it a bit challenging, but his lectures were awesome. He gave good examples and his proofs are easy to follow. Helpful during office hour. Final exam was very easy.
Read the textbook like a bible, this professor is a real gem though. Loved the class.

I love Dr. Pixton, he is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures have inspired me to the point where I have decided to become a math professor, such as him, in the future. He has been a mentor to me, nay, a father.

Aaron Pixton organized this course very well. He made it informational yet still manageable. The lectures can get a bit heavy, so be sure you understand the previous one before going into the next day. He is manages to make rigorous proofs very understandable and provides a lot of feedback to make sure you can get it right.

Aaron Pixton is the G.O.A.T. He was super down-to-earth and showed that he cared about his students. Your grade in the class is based on a holistic view of all your assignments, so if there's a single test or homework bringing down your grade then he'll likely take that into consideration when giving out final grades.

Although 465 is one of the easier upper-level math classes, it's still a lot of work. Despite this Aaron Pixton made the material easy to understand by giving many examples during lecture. He was super helpful (especially during office hours) and responds to emails really quickly. Would take a class with him again.

The concepts in math 465 can be tricky, but Aaron Pixton does a good job of providing examples and proofs during lectures. He does lectures on the chalkboard and there are no slides or anything, so if you don't take notes you can't refernece lectures again. If you don't do well in the first half don't worry; graph theory is a lot easier.

Aaron Pixton was an extremely well prepared and friendly professor. He really formed a friendly environment in the class. The pop quizzes were really hard but he was very easy to talk to. Would totally take another class with him, had lots of fun.

465 is a concept heavy course but professor Pixton is very well prepared and nailed it with lots of examples. He is also very accessible out of class and provides lots of alternative office hour options. Explanations are clear and concise. Definitely take him.
Absolutely awesome professor. Incredibly fun in whatever class you take with him, doesn't care about grades at all, he'll work with you.
Amazing professor! Loved his class. I would absolutely take it again in a heartbeat. Super caring and knowledgeable. One of my all time favorite classes.

Amazing professor who clearly loves what he does, and is so willing to help anyone, whether or not it is related to the class. His lectures are great too, very interesting and useful. definitely my favorite class of my first semester!

Lectures are entertaining and lead to good class discussions.
