Professor Ridley is happy to chat with students after class, during labs, or during office hours, and seems to really prioritize his students. Professor Ridley is funny and very passionate about what he teaches. My only complaint is that the grading criteria was not always clear
Great professor with jubilant personality that loves what he teaches and I learned so much and had a great time in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great

Mr. Ridley was one of the best parts of my semester. I had him for the Rocket Science section and he was phenomenal. His lectures are amazing and will make you laugh; you can clearly tell he enjoys his job and the content. A lot of group work and not that many assignments, but still a great class! Highly recommend!

One of the most fun and interesting classes I've ever taken. For an intro level class it was remarkably well paced, with fewer assignments than most other ENGR 100 classes but with assignments that felt important and useful. The skills taught in this class have put me ahead in nearly every future class in my engineering career. I highly recommend!

One of the best professors I’ve ever had. He is very interactive and gives us some control of the lectures (lots of class wide discussion). There is a good bit of work involved (especially second half of the semester for section 980 — rocket science), but it’s pretty easy to do well. Look for his name if he teaches a class you want to take.

Ridley's section of eng100 was probably the highlight of my first semester. Workload was enough to keep you aware of the class but never busywork. The group project that formed the main grade of the class was incredibly fun and challenging, forcing you to learn, make use of the material, and work with your group to make a good final project..

Professor Ridley is one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. He was great to get to know after class, and was always willing to listen and talk to me about anything (whether it be academic stress, personal life situations, etc). I learned an incredible amount from him: He explains things clearly, and knows when we need a break.

Dr. Ridley's ENGR 100 Section 950 (Electronics for Space and Atmospheric Measurements) is probably one of the best intro to engineering classes you can take. You are exposed to a wide variety of different engineering disciplines, but be prepared to work your butt off on the project.

Aaron Ridley is the closest thing to Grandpa Rick in Rick and Morty. He is simply put a genius at space engineering! He often cusses in class and is super chill. The class can be tiring sometimes, but is overall really easy. By far the best professor I've had!
Ridley was a funny professor who was great to learn from. 10/10.

Professor Ridley was probably the best professor I have had so far at Michigan. He is incredibly smart, astoundingly funny, and shows great care for each of this students. His teaching style keeps students engaged with funny and relevant anecdotes, and is efficient at making class incredibly enjoyable. I could not recommend this professor any more.
The class was a blast, and the professor is very good at teaching the course material. Would highly recommend.

He was consistent with his expectations for the course and made class interesting on a daily basis. He understood that most people weren't aerospace engineers and made the content easier to understand. Even though it wasn't really mandatory to go to lecture, he made you want to.

Seriously one of my favorite professors. The guy is a NASA consultant and a friggin genius yet he's great at explaining things and making class funny. He's full of interesting knowledge. Wish I could take another class with him.

He is a personal professor teaching a really easy course.  He tends to just read off of the lecture slides and do a lot of wild pointing with his laser pointer, but he gets through a lot of material in the semester and all of the tests come directly from the lecture slides, so class isn't that necessary.

Honestly, I didn't go to lecture too often (not necessary, 99% of necessary info for homeworkexams is on the lecture slides) but the times I did go were interesting and intriguing.  Exams and homework are very straightforward, grading of the final paper is fair. Exams aren't that tough, but don't underestimate them-- there can be a lot of detail.
Awesome class, absolutely one of the most enjoyable lectures to go to, extra credit, easy essay grading, easy homework (get friends to make it easier), and exams are easy too. Awesome experience.

The exams were not that easy, for some reason he makes the exams curved making them tougher and then everything else is not curved. I don't understand the reasoning behind this but it's whatever. The class is easy but the exams can be a little annoying at times, remember dates is not cool.
He's Pretty cool. I loved the class. Just Study for the Exams and do the Homework. Attending Lecture was helpful because he gave a few exam questions before hand.
Ridley is the man. Its that simple. Take this class if you have any reason to at all.
Strongly recommended, easy class, A+
About as easy of a science class as I could imagine. No reading, you never have to go to lecture but its pretty entertaining. Homework and tests are very straight forward and not difficult.

The class is fairly easy, and he's very easy with grading the exams which are multiple choice, a few fill in the blanks and a few drawings.  He makes sure just about everyone passes.  There are weekly online homeworks that are easy and straight from the lecture slides.  Awesome class!
Not a blow off class...it takes some studying. Most get a B/B+
He's awesome guys
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: While Aaron seemed like he hated us the entire semester, I think he just wants to retire. Aside from that, he gave us free points when we were in dire need.
He literally cured my cancer

Big Man AG was truly a force of nature. Lectures felt like TED Talks powered by espresso and righteous academic fury. A true academic weapon with integrity and wisdom beyond his years. A true wizard. 

Class was legendary. Learned a ton. Lost a piece of my soul. Would take again in a heartbeat.

Mr Gunn was really quite outstanding as an instructor; lectures were always creative and concise. He always looks out for his students and was a rather relaxed grader. Homeworks were kinda brutal, but he would always give you the solutions so long as you completed it beforehand. Class was fun but destroys your soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron Kall is by far the worst instructor I've had during my four yeas at the University of Michigan. The typical lecture consists of Aaron summarizing a Youtube video, playing that video, then re-summarizing that video. He refuses to use Canvas to communicate relevant course information or due dates. All grade feedback is handwritten and illegible

Aaron Kall is by far the worst instructor I have had in my four years at the University of Michigan. The average lecture consists of him summarizing a Youtube video, playing that Youtube video, then re-summarizing the video. He refuses to use Canvas to post grades or communicate important due dates. All feedback is handwritten and illegible.

This was a very disorganized class. I was excited to take this class but that excitement quickly wore off after the first month. Aaron has an unclear vision of how he wants to run the class because he has no experience teaching. He doesn't respect students' time by always going over time, every class. Also, grading is biased and lacks consistency

Literally the best professor I have had in the school of nursing. Her workload was light and she had clear expectations for everything. She is so nice and accommodating. I had her for my first clinical rotation and for N262 in the same semester and I would take her as my professor again any day. Angel sent straight from above.
Prof Accurso is so sweet. I had her as an instructor for NURS 234 and 262. She is clear with her expectations and they are very reasonable. She is very knowledgeable and a wonderful instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Middle semester update, it's unfortunate she is not empathic when you come to her with concerns. Is very conservative with "fairness". Needs to improve empathy but I cannot give her a unfair rating because of my personal interaction with her. Will come back and edit this, but I hope she improves.
This class is textbook heavy. Definitely buy the book and READ it. Turn in assignments early if you can, as Accurso is strict about deadlines. Not an awful professor just a difficult class.

Professor Ackerman is an amazing professor. Lectures could drag on a bit, however he would sprinkle in jokes or just random absurdities that would get the entire class laughing. You always knew what to expect in the class and exams were not too difficult. If you are looking for an easy way to fulfill a requirement Ackerman is the way to go!
A+ totally recommend.

Dr. Ackerman is a perfect example of the University of Michigan academics and education.
Dr. Ackerman set the expectations clear on the syllabus from day one; three exams (lowest exam grade dropped), section points for lecture attendance, discussion points for attendance, and an extra credit 5 page paper.
One of my favorite UofM professors. A+ rec.

No electronics in class, participation mandatory with exception of TWO absences. Discussion review sessions weren't helpful. During exam one not enough were printed and half the class had to wait 30 mins in silence, there was no curve, just reduced the amount you were graded on. Lectures went to the last min or over every time which made me late.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ackerman was always very prepared and had a very logical, clear lecture prepared every day. If you've taken AP psych you'll notice that a lot of information is similar which makes this class easier. 200/250 of the points come from exams so it's important that you memorize all of the terms.
Nice guy. 3 exams and you can drop the lowest.

Ackerman gave great lectures. We all love him although this course is a bit tough. All of the contents are so organized and attractive. The only thing is that the pace of his lecture is fast and there are lots of content every week. But as long as you keep up with the course content and review them before each exam, you will get a good grade.

This was the best class EVER!!!!! Prof Ackerman is so passionate and I genuinely loved learning about evolutionary psych. It's so informative but not difficult at all. Would recommend to anyone and everyone.

Ackerman is a nice guy and though the material is cool, endless lectures can get dry and it was tough to pay attention. Class doesn't get interesting till late in the semester, as we spend 3 weeks on "research methods" that we've already learned. Discussions are underutilized as a rehash of lecture, and you can only pass exams by memorizing.

Tried hard to stay focused during lectures, but just couldn't. Material was kind of interesting but each lecture felt like hours. Not much work outside of class but exams are HEAVY on amount of content. Study hard for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ackerman was a great professor, he always provided study guides for our exams and he drops your lowest exam score, he even hosted the review session for exam 2 during the GSI strike

Professor Ackerman was one of the most engaging professors I have had. His lecture content is made interesting through class examples and overall a great lecturer. The class was graded heavily on exams, but if you pay attention and take notes on the slides you should be successful!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ackerman makes lectures for the material very engaging and interesting for students. He is clear about material. Tests are a bit difficult, so know your stuff, but lecture iclicker is helpful in gaining understanding of material and expectations for exams.

Professor Ackerman was really good at teaching the material - I did, however, find myself feeling like I lost out on a fun opportunity for in-person learning (this class would have been really fun to see my classmate's reactions on some of the topics) - but that couldn't be helped, obviously! Definitely recommend him to anyone interested in psych!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Ackermans lectures are the best. He delivers it in such a way that makes you want to learn more about the topic. On top of that, he's very good at explaining concepts. He also wants you to succeed in his class. If you have the chance to take his class, you should.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I literally rave about prof Ackerman to all my friends in the psych major. if you have the chance to take a class w him, TAKE IT! you won't regret it, he makes lectures engaging, understandable and genuinely interesting, and I found him hilarious.

Dr. Ackerman is easy to engage with. His lectures are very straight forward and so are his exams, so as long as you're paying attention, take good notes, and go over them before exams you'll be fine. I wish he offered more classes, I took his social psych class and loved it and I followed him to 385 which was super interesting too. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever had from the last 5 semesters at Michigan. His lectures are extremely interesting and engaging and he is funny without trying. 10/10 recommend taking any class w Josh, you will definitely enjoy it. I wish I could have more classes taught by him.
Best psych prof ever. Prof Ackerman is very knowledgeable and apparently passionate in his field. Although we are having online classes, his lectures have always been engaging and interesting.
Very organized and good at explaining things in lecture. Exams are average, but good policy on those. I would say an average professor, not horrible but not amazing.
Amazing professor! Very clear and easy to understand. Not only is the class interesting, but Prof Ackerman is really great. Attendance is mandatory, but that shouldn't be a problem. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved having Prof. Ackerman so much! His lectures were always really interesting, and he always worked to make sure that his slides were engaging and entertaining. He does a really good job of making materials available online, such as lecture slides. He has a really good sense of humor too, which is good. He does take attendance though!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lectures are mostly mandatory (clicker points made up 20/250 of the total points) but listening to Josh is seriously like a ted talk everytime, especially when you enjoy the material. Tests arent hard, just do the study guides and youre set!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His class can be extremely easy if you just go about it the right way. He gives a review guide before the exam, however, it is in your best interest to MEMORIZE THE LECTURE SLIDES. One exam gets dropped, the first exam I only studied the review guide and didn't do well, the second exam I memorized the slides and did very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Ackerman is fantastic. PSYCH280 is an easy class that you could just blow off & not pay attention in lecture, but Ackerman's lectures are super interesting. His lectures are interactive, fun and sometimes shocking. Hopefully I can take another one of his UL classes in the future. Side note--get Martha as your GSI, she's equally as great.

Dr. Ackerman is absolutely the best professor at the school. He gives very inspirational and content rich lectures while he is interactive with students. The course is super fun and practical as well. Highly recommended!

As I'm writing this review, I'm getting sad thinking that this is my last week of lectures. I loved the material covered in this course, and Ackerman is a great professor who knows his stuff very deeply. Every lecture is very interactive, and it honestly feels like I'm at a TED talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pretty good
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super passionate about his field of study so the lectures are all very engaging. Pretty much your entire grade is based off of 3 exams so study a lot for them but they aren't too bad. Overall very interesting class and good professor.

He knows his lectures very well and breaks everything down so that you always understand everything, and he uses real life examples to help you really connect the material. 3 tests (get to drop lowest/not take one), 3 journal assignments, iclicker points for attendance, 1 extra credit assignment, light reading, no textbook! Study lectures for test

Professor Ackermann is very knowledgable when it comes to social psych and it shows in his lectures. His presentations are interesting and can actually relate to human life which is hard to find in a psych class! If you study the lectures you will get good grades on the exams, and you're allowed to drop one exam. Would highly recommend his class!

he makes lecture fun and the content is really interesting. always answers questions and clearly knows the subject well. he's very approachable and willing to talk after class. takes attendance but I honestly wouldn't want to miss a class anyway. as long as you study for the exams and do the journals you will be able to pass.

Dr. Ackerman is very passionate about his subject and demonstrates a lot of knowledge regarding his field. He doesn't post study guides, but the exams aren't that difficult and all the slides are posted online anyway. A big part of your grade are the three journal entries, and they're strictly graded according to the criteria he gives you.

Ackerman was a great professor who really made the material interesting and captivating. If you have an interest in social psychology or evolutionary psychology this is a class worth taking, if only because Josh really makes it an interesting class. It was a 9 am and I still attended nearly ever lecture

Dr. Ackerman provides a really awesome perspective into evolutionary psychology. I took a seminar on sex, survival, and evolution with him, and it made my mornings! You can tell that he has a passion for the material and that he tries to make class interesting with cool studies and examples!

Professor Sahin is one of my favorite Professors in the Department of Religious Studies. He is very passionate about his work, he is very approachable, and very caring towards his students. He has the ability to break down complex ideas and make it very easy to understand. I would absolutely recommend his courses :)
Sahin cares more about their students than any professor I've seen. Truly cares about how you do. Sincerely wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Sahin was the best teacher or professor I've ever had. They really care about each of their students and it really comes across. They were constantly willing to help, and does not believe in grading (everyone gets an A, which I thought would make me slack but definitely did not). If you get the chance to take a course with them you should.

Written for Winter 2024-25 semester for EECS 493

Actually shocked to see Professor Ackerman have such a bad score on RMP. He's genuinely a great dude. Don't understand the hate. If you hate how EECS 493 is, hate the class and the many lecturers, not just Ackerman. Easy class. Ackerman makes the dead easy lectures better by being cool.
quiz and quiz answers make no sense. This professor should have lower rating than Edward Ionides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackerman and his EECS 496 class was honestly one of the worst classes I've ever taken. His syllabus and grading criteria are unclear. His assignments have unclear rubrics and he gives out arbitrary grades.
Not clear grading criteria, difficult to assess expectations

He's not a great lecturer, but as a professor, he was okay in terms of class administration. We often had class administration complains because of the other professor of this class, and Professor Ackerman would usually help to fix the issue.
Absolutely horrible communicator, has no idea where students' understanding is, WORST EECS professor in the department WITHOUT QUESTION
You don't learn anything on EECS 493 and the grade is so bad. I think he is the worst professor I have ever seen. Do not take his class unless you want to waste your time.

Ackermans User Interface course is comparable to (Insert your least favorite LSA course here).   If you hope to learn about programmatically building user interfaces, or about current design trends, then this is not the course for you.  If you like memorizing flash cards, and regurgitating useless information to do well on exams, then take UI.

The course itself isn't too interesting but easy to understand. He tries really hard to make the lecture more fun. Assignments are done using the Qt framework, which isn't explained in class, so you need to do a lot of your own research. Although, grading isn't too tough.

I really couldn't say what exactly it is about his lecture style that makes it so boring, but it is. I learned a lot about UI during the class- from watching YouTube videos so I could manage the homework. Lectures are pretty scattered and don't have a clear path, and he tends to assume you have prior knowledge about UI programming, web design, etc.
Mark was pretty funny and lectures were entertaining, but not educational. I felt like I learned nothing and lectures helped not at all with exams.

It's teachers like Mark Akerman that make you want to drop out of school. He acknowledges that he's the most boring lecturer and doesn't do anything about it. Was really interested in the class, professor completely ruined it. I have a 3.5 but might fail this class. Couldn't really care less anymore.

I was really looking forward to this course, and it was fine for the first half.  I didn't learn a single thing the second half of the course.  In fact, the review sheet for the final was the same as the review sheet for the midterm plus two or three additional things.  Waste of my time.
great course and interesting man
great course!
funny man and interesting course!
Great! Excellent! Hard work but so wroth it.
Great teacher! Fun class, fun guy. Truly enjoyed the course, but was very challenged.
brilliant guy, good sense of humor. wish he responded to email.
He is the Best!!!!!!!!!! and I mean it
Very entertaining teacher. Makes lectures interesting. One of the best EECS professors, hands down.
Very good lecturer, always kept things interesting.  Stories and chalkboard more than just Power-Point.
I would have liked to know more about new kinds of interfaces.  He has a good sense of humor and seemed to genuinely like us.
Good about answering questions and fielding students' concerns.  Great availability.
Overall, pretty good - lectures somewhat lengthy but covered the important information.  Tough - but what can you say, it's EECS.
Has read world experience in subject matter, not experience in teaching.

Dont even think about it... completely incompetent teacher and useless for all intents and purposes.  Assignments are hard and given in language more cryptic than the incomprehensible examples he gives in class.... enjoy!

Several instances where she was quite rude when making corrections- very uncomfortable vibe in class & doesn't foster active learning. She is very set in her opinions.
Not inclusive to those with different learning style. 85% of final grade is based on public speaking/oral exams when it's just a film class.
Still a decently easy A but NOT enjoyable

Elena is by far the best teacher I've ever had at UM. If you have a chance to take a class with her, you should! She's engaging, informative, and deeply cares about her students and helping them succeed. Seriously a gem of a professor.

Elena was a real gem here at UMich. I took her for both 277 and 295 back-to-back. She makes Spanish all the more fun to learn and genuinely wants you to know the language. She is a tough grader mainly because that is what the department expects of you, but truth be told, you become better at Spanish for it. Wish I could take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Elena is the best professor I've had in college so far. She really cares about her students and she is really easy to get in contact with. She usually answers emails within an hour or two, and provides clear explanations for any questions you ask. She schedules additional office hours when exams are near. Overall, very helpful and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: My section of 492 is about bilingualism. It is seminar style with the students and Acrisio taking turns to present papers and lead discussions. The breadth of topics covered was great and I learnt a lot. Pretty minimal work for most of the semester but there is a 2500-3500 word term paper, which Acrisio is more than happy to help you with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Acrisio is the best! I really enjoyed his 492/792 class, and he always had plenty of information to share on the most diverse topics we covered. He was available outside of office hours, a fair grader, and the workload was quite manageable for the subject matter and level. Definitely take a class with him if you get the chance, you won't regret it!
Semantics turned out to be more interesting than I thought. The class was really laid back, we got to do graded work with other students in class, and other assignments were fine.

Lectures can be dull, But Cris really loves teaching and the subject which makes it easier. He makes it a point to learn the names of every student and always offers help and makes you feel welcome to ask questions. Holds many review sessions for homework and tests. Some weekly work and recommended readings, but not mandatory. Show up for class.

Acrisio was enthusiastic about syntax, which can be a dull subject for those not into linguistics.(misconceptions abound re: linguistics) I took 315 in the summer, which was super chill. One time we took an exam with coffee and bagels on hand and it was awesome. He was always willing to clarify and explain things further.

Acrisio is such a sweetheart but not really that great of a teacher. His lectures are dry and boring and it feels really awkward to participate even though he really wants you to. He cares about his students, but I don't think I'll be taking another class with him if I can help it.

Acrisio is adorable and really wants you to do well. He tells bad jokes and really makes sure that he gets to know the class and that the class knows each other. The material is interesting, but lectures were a little boring. He is definitely there to help if you are confused and an A is definitely attainable.

Acrisio is a very nice guy and tries to lighten the material with bad jokes in an endearing way. The material in this class is a bit complicated at the end so I wouldn't recommend it if you don't have at least some linguistic background. The material itself is naturally very dry so unfortunately there's not much to do to make it more interesting.

Acrisio is a good guy, but this class was so incredibly boring that I completely lost interest in linguistics. The material was presented in a far more complicated manner than it needed to be. If you're not a linguistics major, do yourself a favor and do NOT take this class.
He was really clear and an extremely easy grader. I wasn't looking forward to taking the class but I found it to be incredibly easy.

This class is worth taking.  A lot of BBCS majors take it because it's the only class that doesn't require prerequisites but the subject is kind of cool: Syntax! Acrisio may be dull at times, but he can be funny too. There are no surprises. He teaches you what he wants you to know, and then you're tested on it. An 'A' is DEFINITELY ATTAINABLE!!! :)
This class was okay. Professor Pires is a good instructor, but there was way too much obnoxious group/partner work. Who has assigns a final paper in linguistics as group work?

Dry lecturer, I found myself doing crossword puzzles in class. I agree that the group work was more annoying than helpful. Exams were easy, graded the paper harder than the exams. I wouldn't go looking for more of his classes, but I wouldn't be too upset if I got him again.
His tests are easy, the group work is annoying, and the lectures are boring.
this course was interesting, but I was not crazy about it. Most of the course deals with ambiguity in language...
This was an excellent course and I had a lot of fun taking it! In-class group work helped helped me understand the material better(but there should be more of this work).
If you like formal stuff about language, you'll like this class. DON'T take this class if you intend NOT to show up to class -- the guy asks people to do group work as part of your grade.

Wow, this was a terrible experience. I would not recommend taking linguistics (with him) if you do not have to. This is the most dull subject matter presented in the most dull way imaginable. I really do wish I could get back the hours of class time wasted in this class this past semester; oh wait, nevermind, those were good nap time hours.

He is a good guy who means well, but LINGUISTICS IS HORRIBLY BORING. One of the most worthless classes I've EVER taken -- shame on me for taking a class that is not even required for my major. Super easy until after the 1st exam then it's pretty much 'uhh WTF?' I would never go if it weren't for the in-class assignments that affect your grade.
Acrisio is a sweetheart and is very committed to helping his students.

He's a really nice guy, very excited about Syntax. The only problem is that he talks like a dictionary. So if you did the reading and didn't understand it, you won't undersand lecture either. If you did understand the reading, you wouldn't need ti show up except for the pop quizzes. Discussion sections before exams saved my grade.
really difficult to pay attention and follow his lectures. he has few points and never answers your questions directly.

The man looks like Mr. Bean, sounds like Kermit the Frog, and teaches like a preacher.  He just babbles and babbles until you finally raise your hand and ask "What is your point?"  The work load is fine, but the class is very boring. Half the class just stopped coming after the first exam. He is a nice man, but the course was dull.

He's a really nice guy, and you can tell he really knows his stuff, but the class is kind of boring.  And he's not always crystal clear in explaining things. Still, I recommend taking his class. Don't let me deter you.
Acriso is a nice guy but his class was so bad!  It's hard to say anything bad about the person, so I'll just say don't take the class

ok he gives you like 22,000 pages of notes online to print for lecture the next day but only can make it through ohh..maybe 3? but ya gotta know it all.if you get a C on the midterm but work hard, go to lecture, and do extra credit you can pull off an

Acrisio's classes move VERY slowly and no matter what the class, he seems to like to begin it with child language acquisition.  His classes are so easy that you can get behind in them cuz you'll want to just stop coming to class.
Acrisio is completely devoted to undergraduate education, assumes his class has interest in the subject, and teaches so that everyone learns the material.
OSU Rating

Absolutely fantastic-and this is coming from someone that HATES the subject of English. Professor Acosta-Hughes actually made this class fun and interesting-you can tell he really really loves what hes talking about.

Really nice guy, really boring class. I pretty much showed up and watched Prison Break the whole class just to get the attendance points. I never did the readings and the exams were fine because they are mostly over vocab. This class is a nice easy A, as GEs should be. Just cram for the exams and you're good. This is an OSU review btw. Go bucks

I took Greek Tragedy from Prof. Acosta. He's hilarious and very sweet, and very inept when it comes to technology. His lectures are interesting and entertaining, and he tries to get the class involved in discussion/performance of the plays. We were supposed to write 7 papers, but ended up only writing 4. Easy Class, but fun :)
He was terrible and pretentious
Excellent teacher!  He was especially good as a GSI for the honors section.  Not a difficult class, except the 2 page papers due once a week can be annoying.  Highly recommend

phenomenal professor, class is a much better alternative to english 125 for the 1st yr writing requirement, work load is consistent, exams are easy if you study and this guy is the absolute man, if he were 20 years younger we would be best friends. very well dressed, as he will tell you, PHENOMENAL CLASS, HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!
AMAZING. take CLCIV101 if you're interested in it at all. Acosta-Hughes is brilliant and even though the 2 page papers are a drag, his lectures are great
Well dressed

This was a great class.  I was in the honors section, so Professor Acosta-Hughes was my the head of our discussion section.  He is a really nice guy who is very clear and fair in his grading on the papers and exams.  There is a lot of reading towards the end and a 2-page paper due every Friday, but it's very manageable.

He is professional and passionate about his subject. He slips humor into his lectures to break up the density. His voice is very smooth and flowing and can cause you to temporarily zone out, so it helps to focus on his powerpoints to keep track of what he is saying.

He knows everything and more about the subject and he makes it interesting to learn. He makes a lot of jokes that are hard to understand but it keeps you awake. The only problem is his lullaby voice.. take a voice recorder otherwise you might be tempted to sleep.
Very open to discussion, and extremely approachable! He is also very passionate about his subject, which helps to make his lectures interesting.
Always open to discuss topics with students and help them understand the material more fully.

A truly enthusiastic and engaged teacher who seems to care deeply about his students. Though the reading got a bit much at times (it was a literature-based course), he tried to adjust to fit our abilities. The discussion was always great too. What a delight!
Acosta-Hughes is funny, clear, and engaged. I definitely recommend.
Liked the class, put in the work.  He was really nice.
Good class, but his voice was so damn soothing i fell asleep every day.  He gets props because its been 3 years and i still know what "sparagmos" means :)
i hate this proffesor
I could hardly pay attention, the man is fine.
Professor Acosta-Hughes is a Great Professor
Wow, this class is way too easy.  Do yourself a favor and don't buy any of the book (unless you actually want to read them).  You can get an A simply by going to lecture and/or discussion.
hilarious!
The class was fine, but I wished I had taken Great Books instead because I would have learned more.  Your grade depends on your GSI, obviously.

Excellent professor, amusing, love the accent and enthusiasm.  Very knowledgeable, I learned a lot, even having had significant background in the class.  I however, did not like the grades being totally dependent on the GSI.
Pleasant.
This class blows. Period. If you like memorizing random Greek words for no apparent reason, then I guess you'd enjoy this class.  Take Great Books if you have to!
No Comments
Ben's kindness is surpassed only by his brilliance and helpfulness.  And he's amazingly outgoing and kind.  He's very suppportive, and he's a soft-spoken guy who is easy to befriend.  A great man.
easy material,grades dependant on gsi. he spoke very quietly and with a funny accent which made me need to sit up front.
Did not really help out much and didn't want to get involved in matters of grading fairness.  overall okay teacher. grades are really dependent on gsi and not prof
a pretty good professor, but i felt i could have gotten more out of the class.
My goat. So sweet, provides genuine feedback in a constructive way and understands that everyone has a different style.

I put lectures cause what he says before you start drawing is really helpful. I feel like my sketching has gotten so much better. This class has been invaluble in my artistic development. Very personable, and says hello outside class. Talks to every single student throughout class. You can make up drawings but its better to draw in class for input.

By far the best professor at STAMPS. His lectures were clear, useful, and hilarious. I didn't want to take Drawing Visualization as a 3D artist, but he inspired me to improve. I often stayed after class to practice, and he stayed late to help. Truly a caring, motivating professor.

Probably the best professor I've had so far during my time here. He gives good feedback and plenty of time to do your work. Best part: he doesn't give any homework. Well, except for the final project, but he gives you like a whole month to do that. Highly recommend this professor, very cool and epic

Prof Deva was amazing for Drawing Obs. He believes that art shouldn't be graded, but is instead a learning experience. Your grade will pretty much be your attendance. He also gives fantastic feedback on your work and is just overall great to talk to. 100% would recommend.

I loved Prof Deva's course. He truly cares about each of his students, and his main priority is always to ensure that you are progressing and developing your skills. Would highly recommend taking a course with him!

Adrian was lovely to have in class! He had so many good insights and I really felt like I learned a lot from him. He was excited to talk about everything he taught and offered us a lot of freedom on the final project.

Adrian is honestly the best art professor I've ever had. He proves that classes don't need to be stressful and difficult for you to learn a lot. I learned and improved so much in this class mostly because I wasn't stressed out constantly and because Adrian genuinely cares, is super passionate and inspirational, and gives very good advice.

Incredible teacher! I learned a TON during his class and he made me actually want to show up (considering it was an 8am that's a miracle). Super kind to all students, offered great advice, respected all art styles. Very light workload, basically the only assignment was the final, and you had plenty of time to work on it so everyone got a good grade
super funny guy, very passionate about art. gives great feedback. favorite quote from him; "drawings should be good."

Favorite class this semester! Deva knows what he's talking about & gives excellent critique, passionate about the art & genuinely has his students' best interests at heart. Very few turned-in assignments, graded on attendance. Bit vague at times, might be frustrating if it's not your kind of art, but this class got me out of bed in the morning :)

Adrian is THE BEST. So nice, so funny, great teacher too. Gives awesome feedback, and is really attentive to his students and how their work is going. He is very organized, doesn't assign much homework, provides great help when needed, is respectful to his students, and has great project assignments. HIGHLY recommend.

I took ArtDes 105 with him and he is honestly a phenomenal professor! He pays attention to the progress of each of his students intently and gives great advice. He is overall very friendly and considerate and at the end of the day just wants his students to improve and do well.
Adrian was really kind to students. He gave good feedback on our observational drawing. This wasn't my favorite class, but I have nothing bad to say about Adrian.
Never showed up on time, made faces. complacent at best
Never on time, always on his phone and condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This whole class was created so that we could be free labor for his sister, Ashley Fure's, ensemble that was coming to town.  We were encouraged to be innovative with the materials but none of that was used in Ashley's production.  Adam is not good with feedback and didn't reimburse for expenses.  Beware if you take his classes.  Very slow to grade
Passed French 103 effortlessly with the help of Dr Dula who GENUINELY wants you to succeed.
Dr Dula was great! Always ready for class and her teaching style was great for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dula is the best French professor that Michigan has!! She is kind, understanding, and really wants you to succeed. Yes, it is a French Class at Michigan, so there is a lot of work, but it's ultimately to help you understand the language better, and Dr. Dula will absolutely take the time to help you if you are struggling. HIGHLY RECOMMEND :)

Any french 232 class will have the heavy workload but Professor Dula is a great teacher for this class. She explains things well in class and cares about her students. Even though the work can be challenging at times, it will be like that no matter your professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best French professor I've had. I really enjoyed being in her class, she does a great job at creating a welcoming atmosphere. You can really tell that she cares about her students and puts in a lot of effort with her explanations and feedback to help students learn.

Prof. Dula was amazing! She always made sure multiple times that everyone understood the concepts that we were learning. She explains things very clearly and overall was a great professor for FRENCH 231. Her feedback on written assignments is fairly clear, and she doesn't grade harshly. She also thoroughly prepared everyone for all of our exams!

I absolutely love Prof. Dula. She is so caring for her students and she never feels condescending or gets down on people for their mistakes. I feel really supported in her class and she helps all of her students grow. There's a lot of homework in the class but she is really understanding that the French department has some unrealistic expectations

I learned a lot of interesting things from his lecture videos! The class is asynchronous and completely self-paced, which is great for a spring term course. He made the final exam optional and quizzes made up the rest--or entirety--of your grade.

Overall, Prof Simon was a good professor, and this class was interesting. 90 percent of your grade comes from pop-quiz questions throughout the lecture, which is easy if you attend every lecture and pay attention. I didn't always pay attention, hence my A- lol. Should be an easy A+ if you pay attention, no effort outside of lecture necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Simon and would take class from him again. He went through material somewhat quickly but it was clear he was very confident in the material he was teaching and made it known exactly what points were most important for us to remember.
Will never take his class again. Signing up just for to rate him.
clearly knows his stuff but this guy is a dee eye see kay who argues with college kids with a terrible attitude
If you want to get an A, don't attend his class.

Argues with students often and is quite rude/stubborn. Grade is based on 5 quizzes during a 2 hour online lecture. Gives students very little material to be successful in the class. Would not recommend taking a class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you encounter any unpleasant things in life please don't vent your frustration on your students This is the worst teacher I have ever seen at UMICH. He shows no respect for students, argues during class time, and even changes the grading rules near the end of the semester, making it impossible for most students to achieve the grades they desire.
If you made anything wrong and you definitely won't get an A, even worse grade. There is no place for argue.

This is the most engaging course that I've learned the most from (I'm no where near an Earth major). Anyone who gives him a 1-star is making their political bias clear and can not cope with a difference of opinion. He uses broader implications of politics on energy infrastructure, calling balls and strikes on both sides. A-Dolla is the man

Brings politics into discussion way too much, in a very pushy manner. Is also very rude to students- got into a full argument with a student during class, and had very negative and condescending responses to several students asking normal, respectful questions from the start of class.

He has very clear laid out guidelines for the class and sticks strong to them. As long as you are paying attention to lecture, this class is extremely simple and easy to follow. Argues with students but is fully justified as students are trying to make excuses to get around wrong answers and teacher is sticking to clear rules.
Keeps deleting all bad reviews but always argues with students.
By far the best professor I had in my undergrad. Do not miss the opportunity to take a course with him.

Professor Simon is unaccommodating, unhelpful, and rude. His lectures consisted of him rambling about unrelated topics the entire time and I learned absolutely nothing. When I encountered pretty intense issues with a group project, he did not care whatsoever or do anything to help us resolve the conflict. His class was easy, but a waste of time.
Clearly likes Earth Science, Easy Grading, take him if available.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loves to bring up his objectivity citing that he does not care about politics yet brings them up or alludes to them often in his lectures. He is blunt which is not something I enjoy in my lectures. I want to learn about technical science, not why liberals are dumb for not supporting open-pit mines.
Easy A+ and a fun class imo but not all of it was exactly an "Intro to Research" as most students would expect.

If an incoming student asked me about MRADS I would tell them to absolutely NOT join if Adam Simon is the director. The class is supposed to be "intro to research" but Adam spends most of class lecturing about wildly inappropriate personal stories without any relation to research. Uses scare tactics to influence students about their freshman year.

The expectations for this class could have been better stated. Assignments get a 0 if they are 1 second late, and each assignment or quiz is worth 5% of your grade. Dont miss them, but theyre easy enough. To people calling ALA Adams Life Advice well, yeah. Youre not going to agree with all of it, but he has some gems of wisdom.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adam thinks he's better than you. Although okay in office hours, he's unaccommodating, gives off-topic lectures that often go overtime, consistently posts HW late, and fluctuates between pure busywork and unreasonable deadlines. MRADS is good, but ALA 104 is by far the worst part.

Avoid this professor if possible. Adam is extremely rude and condescending towards students, especially in his canvas announcements. I received very little constructive feedback and would not consider this course beneficial to my writing abilities. There seemed to be a lack of communication between Adam, the GSIs, and the students.

Adam Simon is a good lecturer and a funny guy. He was able to make the lectures engaging and relatable. At times, he got into politics a little too much, but it wasn't too bad. I found that the textbook that was "required" wasn't of much use to me. Exams were about 90-95% of the grade, but a good class overall.

Loved to say he doesnt care about your political leanings and looks at issues objectively, but opens and closes the term with lectures using stats from the World Bank about poor peoples quality of life. If you can look past his capitalism fetish, his lectures are in depth from a scientific standpoint; great even for people outside of EARTH
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was a really knowledgeable, funny professor and he made lectures as interesting as he could. Hes definitely not afraid to share his opinions, but it made the class much more entertaining. Tests were very easy if you went to lectures.

I did well in this class but found Adam to be pompous and abrasive. His lecture slides never had any words on them, solely pictures or videos, making studying for tests extremely difficult. He is a very engaging and dynamic lecturer, however, he is inaccessible due to his holier-than-thou personality.

Adam Simon is the most engaging lecturer I have experienced. He knows the material and teaches it with ease. He is hilarious and keeps the material relevant and easy to comprehend. The exams are straightforward - if you listen in lecture and use them to study you will do fine. Lecture quizzes are easy. Discussion is alright but could be better.
Changed my life - best professor. If you don't work hard, you won't get an A.
Amazing lecturer and knows a lot about this topic. Makes a bland topic fun to learn and interesting.
Outstanding professor. I would recommend Adam Simon to anyone who is looking for an interesting earth science class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adam Simon is hilarious and makes very dry material entertaining. He is extremely helpful and engaging, while also one of the most savage people I've ever met.

Prof Simon is engaging and knowledgeable. I went to every lecture and did minimal studying for the exams and ended up with a B, which felt fair. The material was much more interesting than expected from someone who had little prior interest in rocks. Simon can be blunt and polemical, but is thought-provoking and non-judgmental.

I took his EARTH 380 class in Fall 2017 and learned more about the environment, energy, resources, and economics than I have from any other class I have ever taken. Prof. Simon's lectures are always entertaining and informative, and he treats his students like peers. Good stuff.

Adam's lectures are great and very informative. He works to challenge your views on our modern society, but he definitely has a "love him or hate him" type of personality. Sometimes his jokes are unbearable, and other times they are entertaining. However, he claims to focus on facts but then injects personal opinions into almost everything he does.

Adam knows what's up. He will get up on that stage in CCL and preach an incredibly informative lecture that challenges your perspective on the reality of modern society. He has strong, logical,  progressive views and is not afraid to make them known. Understand the broad concepts/trends/few key values and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really good class. Adam can be hit or miss with some people, but I thought he was really fun to listen to. Truly a caring guy. Go to class and take notes. Miss class? Good luck.   Discussion was interesting. Definitely not as good as the lecture, but was an "okay" supplement to the course. Wish it were just the lecture.

He obviously knows a lot about what he's teaching, but I found his lectures preachy and I think he tries way too hard to be the "cool professor". I spent hours every week doing boring calculations for the section project, for as heavy as the workload is you really don't learn much.
Loved this class. Amazing lectures which are taped and posted on the canvas site.

God has blessed us all here at the University of Michigan with St. Simon. He has the wit and knowledge to make any subject interesting and enjoyable to learn. A very engaging and contemporary lecturer it seems like everything he says sticks with you. Also he has a pierced ear and it turns me on.

Adam is wonderful. Funny, smart, prepared, his lectures were very entertaining and engaging. The second exam I thought was the hardest, but he was most passionate about that subject. Go to class, watch the lectures again and take notes, go to every discussion and you should for sure get an A. Book not necessary to buy. Pop quizzes in lecture!
He makes the material interesting.
great class

This is one of the best classes I have taken at U of M. It really opened my eyes on the issues it brought up. You have to go to class to pass, but Adam is a great lecturer and makes it well worth it. The project wasn't great but it was in the first year and really isn't too hard.

Professor Simon changed the way I view many environmental issues. His lectures are entertaining and very insightful! Earth 380 has been of my favorite classes at Michigan. I would definitely recommend taking a course with him!

Lectures are surprisingly interesting and Dr. Simon presents the content humorously and enthusiastically. However, I didn't see the value in discussion, and the project (new this year) was a lot of work. If you want to do well on his exams, showing up to lecture is a must.  I learned a lot in this class and I definitely recommend it!
Great lecturer, super interesting material and he presents it really well. Didn't enjoy the work we did in discussion, really just wished I could have only gone to lecture and listened to him talk
So much homework! Discussions are different than lecture. Trying new project. Still many kinks

This class recently incorporated an alternative energy project that requires an enormous amount of time. I am taking an upper-level chemistry and physics course with this class and find myself dedicating the most of my time to Earth 380. Unfortunately, the discussion section does not cover any of the same material the lecture does. Would not take!

Dr. Simon makes this class enjoyable, although his lectures are long. The class consisted of 5 quizzes and a final exam. They were very easy, but that may be because Simon allowed us to take them all online outside of class. He made this decision on the spot, so, you may not be as lucky. Take this class. It's an easy A
Simon is the best.  Funny and engaging, he always is prepared for lecture and is very fair with what he covers on the test.
Adam is a great professor, and truly cares about the topics he teaches leading to some very insightful lectures.
Adam is the man. The class is really interesting and nothing is too difficult. I could recommend this class more.

AMAZING CLASS! GREAT PROFESSOR! I am en econ major, and had no environment background and this class went very well for me. The slides are clear and he is great at explaining. HIGHLY RECOMMEND ANY CLASS WITH HIM!

This class is great, and is all about how much you want to learn. You can attend class and slack off and still get a good grade, because exams are easy and are based entirely on slides. But you'll want to pay attention, he's a great lecturer. Exams are multiple choice, and attendance is necessary due to pop quizzes, though they're very easy.

Adam is a great professor! He is very clear while lecturing, and makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Going into office hours to get help on your essay topic is really helpful and he is easy to converse with.

Amazing class! Adam is a great instructor and makes complicated information easy to understand- he really helped to make connections to the bigger picture! His essays had a prompt, but students got to pick what to focus on. I learned a ton from this class, and my writing really improved. Definitely recommend.

This is an outstanding ULWR course; Prof. Adunbi is exceptionally insightful and well-informed, and his thoughtful approach to controversial topics makes the class genuinely moving. While some readings are dense, simply showing up brings real clarity to pressing environmental and societal issues. Your grade is based on two essays and participation.
Professor Adunbi is very smart and super into his research. I personally found much of the course to be boring but it is a very easy ULWR so I recommend.

Prof Adunbi was very nice, but this class was boring. I hardly ever paid attention in lecture, but it didn't matter at all. Only 2 major assignments (essays), which were graded very easily. I never did the readings for class, either, and did just fine. Great ULWR. Seems like a lot of work when looking at the syllabus but it is easy a high A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unresponsive

Prof. Adunbi comes to lecture & reads his prepped notes in front of wordy slides; I personally didn't find his teaching style engaging. Syllabus claims to ban laptops in class, but not enforced. 2 papers + attendance make up most of your grade, but attendance-taking method in lecture changed weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class had no structure of what was expected from the students. The lectures were really boring, and the assignments were not clear on what was expected. I recommend taking a different upper-level writing if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were essentially only 2 assignments for my whole class.
Only graded on 2 papers throughout the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor with interesting lectures. The class has one main paper that is made up of smaller assignments throughout the semester. Grading is fair and assignments are pretty straightforward. Best ULWR to take.

The attendance is mandatory and the professor will call you from 100 people in class to respond to questions. No devices and he will literally come to you in class to make sure that. If you want an easy A this is definitely not what you want. If you want to satisfy the distribution this is not an ideal choice. Still, you can pass with some efforts.
Hard to follow and treats students with a weird attitude. Insanely reading heavy course and lecture attendance was mandatory even though nothing beneficial was ever discussed.

this is a ready-heavy class, but if you're someone who doesn't do much of that, make sure to pay attention to his lectures and take good notes. those will come in handy. prof. adunbi is a very knowledgeable man who tries his best to make the material enjoyable and useful. two main writing assignments, one medium-length, one long.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Adunbi is truly a master of this subject. His lectures require attention but are broken down into digestible chunks, plus he is very engaging and cares a lot about his students and their understanding of the subject. I'm very grateful I got to have him as a professor, since he teaches well and is definitely a leader in his field.

The material was interesting and Dr. Adunbi was very knowledgeable about all topics discussed. It frustrated me how harshly the papers were graded (go to office hours before the first paper!). The professor often calls on individual students in 80+ person Zoom lectures, which I didn't appreciate. It made attending class unreasonably stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a super great professor, however the essays are graded pretty harshly. Despite that, as long as you go to class and participate in section it isn't hard to pull out an A. Class can get boring sometimes but content is pretty interesting overall.

Professor Adunbi is a wonderful and charismatic man that wants all of his students to succeed in understanding the material. He enjoys getting the class involved in lecture, and he loves a healthy, respectful debate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Personally, I struggled to stay engaged during the long lectures. The reading load felt heavy at times because the readings are long, dry, and only marginally interesting. However, Dr. Adunbi is definitely an expert on oil, so if you're truly passionate about the topic, then take his class. Plus, he seems to truly care about his students.

Grades are 2 essays & some reflections. Lectures can be long & ambiguous. Per his own words, Adunbi teaches because he is an activist - some may like that but others don't. Lectures are subjective & like listening to someone share their opinions rather than learning factual info. Content is still interesting whether you agree with him or not.

Adunbi is a really smart, interesting guy. His lectures are long (he reads off the slides) but the class covers interesting topics in environmental politics. Come with a strong knowledge of critical theory/philosophy and you're golden. Participate in lecture/discussion. Only need to do 2-3 of the readings. I really enjoyed this class.

This class was pretty simple. Some topics are more interesting than others and the overall workload is light. Lectures can be a little hard to sit through at times but the discussions were nice to listen to. There's a lot of assigned reading but as long as you know the gist of the readings you'll do fine on tests and reflection papers (2 each).

If you want to be bored for an hour and a half every week then this class is for you.  Yes there are few assignments but he grades hard and doesn't tell you what he expects.  Your grade is very dependent on them too.   He has an accent so it is hard to understand what he is saying.  Reading are hard, boring, and long.  Not suggested.

Human Rights has always been a passion of mine, so the class was a really big shock when I figured out the whole class was complicating HR. Prof Adunbi helps to get very interesting discussions going in class and helps them along; however the readings discussed are often long and dry. This class has few actual assignments. I highly recommend it!

Friendly and seems like he actually wants to get to know students. Lectures are decently interesting, but his lecture slides have far too much information on them and are hard to follow. I would recommend ignoring them and just taking notes on what he says. A pretty good class overall.
Very friendly. But does not give clear directions or expectations for assignments.
Adunbi has an amazingly unique perspective on human rights and when given all the information, you view on the subject will forever be changed. Absolutely critical influence in any you activists life

Professor Adunbi is extremely knowledgeable in his subject area. The class was great and opened my eyes to the deeper societal issues caused by the addiction to oil in developed countries and the disparities it causes in third-world countries. We were required to do six one-page reading reflections and one final paper 10-15 pages. No exams!

He shows any help to students who are struggling through this course and gives great advice to students for better improvement. He offers students extra credit for grade improvement. If you want to learn how to write better, learn from him.
good and fair but participation was required, plus a ton on homework writing assignments.

it was actually ENGL-2110-L02
Prof. Sneed was awesome. Super lenient, great feedback, super helpful. The online course was super easy to navigate, and he made everything relatable. If I could, I'd take him for every class. This is my first time rating a professor and it's cause he made this semester so achievable. Amazinggg
Grading scale is difficult. Incredibly sarcastic and makes you feel dumb if you ask questions. Rolls eyes a lot and makes side comments.

Adam's class is super difficult, but if you show up and do what you need to do, you're guaranteed a B. Sometimes the course load can be intimidating, but you always get it done. Office hours really help too!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He may be a tough grader but if you put the work into it you WILL become a much better writer. He's a really nice guy and SUPER funny so class is never boring. He's also super helpful if you go to his office hours and just talk out the assignments with him. The class isn't easy but you can do it.

Yes, he's a difficult grader, but the class isn't impossible. He recognizes the effort you put in and curves your final grades accordingly.  He'll push you and you WILL become a better writer, whether you like it or not. You're a Wolverine; there's no such thing as an easy/blowoff class, even FYWR. If you can't handle the heat, go to State.

Adam is an absolutely impossible grader, to the point where I was even discouraged from working hard. He actually told the class on the first day that he would only give out 2 A's (for course grades). The workload was EXTREMELY heavy for a FYWR, and I did not enjoy the class at all. Do yourself a favor and take someone else for your FYWR.
The harshest grader ever.
Please don't do it to yourself

I could tell she really cared about her students, and the class was very interesting! She was very kind and understanding, and was interested in us and our thoughts. Rubrics for assignments can be unclear, so definitely go to office hours in preparation for projects. Class discussion helped with the readings, and exams were fairly straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Adhikari structures class around discussion and engagement with themes/concepts. Assigned materials are thoughtful + diverse and putting in a couple of hours a week goes a long way in learning about histories/social conditions, etc. She brings a lot of energy but will meet you where you're at, especially if you talk to her.

I genuinely did not enjoy this class because of this teacher. She provided no rubrics or criteria for the only 2 projects that meant anything to the class. Also, she gave NO opportunities or put any effort into helping students. Her grading simply inconsistent between different standards, but her explanations regarding lower grading do not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you like being anxious about your grades, not knowing what is expected of you on every assignment, and ending up with lower grades with no explanation, Professor Adhikari is perfect for you. Throughout my experience, she proposed questions, never provided context, and was irritated when we didn't get the right answer. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, she was one of the worst teachers I have ever had. She constantly insists on writing essays a certain way, yet fails to give us proper instruction or even a rubric. Despite asking for criteria, she continues to grade based on "how she wants it written". If you think this is going to be an easy A then don't take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are more like guessing games where she is looking for one correct answer in an open-ended question. Gives feedback on assignments that don't apply to the rubric, making it impossible to get a good grade. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We were graded heavily on a few assignments without having a clear rubric to go off of. The instructions for pretty much everything in the class was unclear, so you never really know what is expected of you. If you are looking to get the humanities credits out of the way with an easy class, do not take any classes with her.

Professor Chaney has a lot of experience in his field, and I honor that. However, this class was supposed to be about building community and learning how to work with community. This class was rather just a three hour lecture of trivial philosophical tangents and had little to do with peer engagement.

Only lectures for the three hours, very boring. Treats students as colleagues, which can be both good and bad. Hard to access out of class. Took interesting content and talked around it for the full time. Group project is the main thing you work on which is very surface level. I don't know what I learned in this course.

He is the worst professor I've ever encountered in my academic career. He does not teach, talks in circles about topics irrelevant to the course, and is extremely disrespectful to students. Multiple people in my course contacted the dean to report him. Avoid at all costs. This man has no business in the education setting.

I'm not sure where all of the bad reviews came from, because I love Adisa. He's a really chill teacher and is super approachable and relatable. He has an unorthodox style of teaching, but he's a really easy grader and has some interesting points to make. I do wish we had more guidance on the semester long project, but I really enjoyed this class

Despite the bad reviews, I loved Adisa. He was vague in lectures at times, but was really inspirational. I could easily get away with skimming readings. Only a few short papers, and he graded super generously. Wish he had given more guidance on the semester-long group project and he wasn't good about returning emails, but overall really fun & chill

This class would be good if he actually taught. He talks in circles and assigns about 100 pages of reading each week. Each class, he randomly calls students to the front and you have to "teach the class" based on one of the readings. They are picked at random so you never know. Students teaching? Isn't that HIS job?! This is how EVERY class goes.

No text but about 100-300 pgs worth of articleswk that must be read in case randomly chosen to present to class. Readings are interesting but not helpfulrelevant to the class. Lectures are nonexistent, and instructor is not open to class input. Assignments are not clearly explained and large group project that has to be done out of class only
Completely useless as a professor. Gave way to much work to the students, then did not lecture at all. In a lecture formatted class.

Is not helpful at all. Very disrespectful and defensive. Does not answer questions well and sees them as a threat to his authority. Is insecure as a professor, does not take feedback or requests. Not sensitive to student's needs or opinions. Very unclear grading and assignment requirements.
Prof. Ames is very kind and understanding. If you participate and do the homework, you will be absolutely fine!
Lots of homework, but great professor.

The class is VERY participation-heavy in verbal French but Prof. Ames structured the class well enough where I was never really afraid to participate. Don't blow off the daily HW before class because it truly furthers your understanding of the language and HW is used in-class discussion. Prof. Ames is also super accommodating and understanding!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alan was the best French teacher I've EVER HAD. He is so clear with his lessons and always pushes us to be better students. He is very accessible when you do not understand something and gives us opportunities to better our french in and out of class. He is also very kind and respectful and I will miss him dearly next semester!!

Professor Ames is by far my fav French instructor! He is always willing to help his students and is very easy to follow in lecture. I was a bit daunted at first with speaking French in class, but he was very patient with all of his students! I def recommend his class overall-- the exams and hw aren't difficult and I def learned a LOT in his class!
Very nice and funny prof, but this class is definitely as hard as you make it. Lots of homework, and while attendance isn't mandatory you miss a lot by even missing one day.
Great at introducing the language though it seems daunting at first. French at umich tends to wait post-course signup to tell you who your instructor is, so if you got him you're very lucky!

Very helpful and thorough. He gives clear explanations in class, but help is also offered every day during office hours. Even the more introverted students can learn and get a good grade. Great French instructor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was so genuine and kind, my class had a really great time learning from him! He explained things very clearly and in-class activities really helped with learning French. If you're more of an introvert and don't like speaking in front of the class, his structure of class really helps with that so that everyone feels comfortable speaking out loud.

I love prof Ames, he is so nice and teaches really well! I think I improved my speaking skills/french overall a lot more than I did last semester in 231. Only thing I would say is the homework is graded for accuracy and the Canvas assignments don't show you your errors, but other than that he was great. I always knew what to expect in class.

Alan Ames was a great professor who gave plenty of opportunities for students to participate and improve their French. He also gives helpful feedback and time in class for students to ask questions on vocabulary and grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ames was really helpful and always available for any questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Alan Ames. He really makes you participate, but is understanding if you don't participate everyday. He makes the class bearable, and I actually looked forward to my morning French class everyday. You have to try hard to get an A, but it's not too hard to do.

There is a ton of homework associated with this class on VHL, but that's not just because of Prof. Ames. He works really hard to make sure that everyone understands what he's saying and is really open to questions. He cares about people learning the language, is extremely patient, and you can tell he is really passionate about French!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ames is a real gem. He is extremely kind and helpful. I can tell that he truly wants each and every one of his students to succeed. Participation and preparedness is extremely important. Exams and homework were generally not that hard if you put in the work. Overall, this isn't a tough class, but you have to be dedicated!

I was never a good French student in high school. So, when I saw that I had to complete four semesters of French, I was worried. However, Alan Ames has been great. He's a nice guy with a caring persona that makes you feel comfortable to talk in class. (Or outside of class.) Even when you mess up, he'll just brush it off like nothing happened. GOAT.

Alan was a really solid choice for French 232 because he really challenges you to participate and speak in class, but is also very caring and understanding. Nobody is near fluent in 232 and he does not get down on people for their mistakes. He really helped my speaking confidence grow.

One of my favorite professors I've had! Alan is so so nice and supportive (which is important for a language class) and class went by quickly. Gave a decent amount of work but it was definitely feasible. Totally recommend him!!

Alan was honestly one of the best professors I've had at Michigan. I am usually a bit self-concsious about participation, especially in language classes, but Alan made it feel like we weren't being judged if we made a mistake. There was lots of work but that just how the course (Fr232) is set up. If you can get him 10/10 would recommend!

Alan is awesome and one of my favorite instructors at the university! He always makes class fun and is more than willing to help you succeed. I was initially concerned about taking Fr232 but Alan was always very encouraging, explained the material well, created fun activities for class, and was also available to answer any questions.
Alan is an angel sent from heaven to make us all smile and feel amazing inside even though we suck at French and I would sell my soul to protect him.

Alan is an AMAZING french lecturer!!! I had him for both french 231 and 232 and was very helpful and kind to me throughout. He never made me feel self conscious about making mistakes in class when speaking out loud which was something that was a problem for me in 103. If you get Alan for french, you're a lucky duck.
Alan is the most flawless angel on the face of this planet!

Alan was the BEST french professor I've had at Michigan. His accent is great, he was always so nice to everyone. He expects you to participate and will call on you if you don't, but what french teacher doesn't? He's always accessible at office hours or appointments, and really gets to know the students which is helpful. My favorite prof.

Alan Awesome Ames truly lives up to his middle name.  Everyone who's giving him bad ratings has never had an actually bad french teacher because Alan legit made me look forward to class. He also grades super quick which is nice
Alan is a great guy but can be a bit of a tough grader and doesn't give As in participation readily at all, loved the class though
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: yay have fun take this class yes @Alan good choice

Alan is super kind, but less so when he's speaking to you in English. He is generally not a tough grader but is when it comes to participation. He has a harder time understanding your French and explaining himself in French that other instructors but he's always happy and prepared.
