Really helpful and pretty easy grader. He wants everyone to pass and he made sure that everyone participated. He does not like when you don't come to class or you're late.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had in my time at UofM. She has a weird complex about not posting lecture slides or recordings. Not an accessible professor at all. If I weren't graduating this semester, I would've taken another class to satisfy my requirements. At least her GSI is good.

Incredibly confused by all the bad reviews. She has dry humor, yes, but is not at all rude, condescending, or unwilling to teach/help outside of class. Seems like these reviews are coming from people who don't come to class and get a bad grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The other reviews are not lying. This is the worst teacher I've ever had. She's very passive-aggressive, and her humor is very dry. She does not want to teach and shows it. She does not post lectures/record on Canvas? I've never had a teacher do that. Unfortunately, this is a required class for many, as it was for me but she needs to be fired.

The worst professor I've had in three years at the University of Michigan and it's not even close. VM creates an incredibly uncomfortable classroom environment and makes it clear she doesn't want to be there. She's rude to students and has no interest in answer questions insightfully. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

She provides no support and is rude. She does not respond to emails, does not have office hours, and doesn't provide a rubric for assignments worth 20% of your grade. I would not recommend her course. There is no support and an overwhelming number of assignments will be graded harshly despite her not providing any support at all.

The class topic itself was incredibly interesting, and I am glad to have been exposed to the concepts within it (arch science is very cool). However Professor Ventresca-Miller was abrasive and rude to us. I don't think she likes people much, she certainly does not have a lot of patience for student questions.

I needed to take this because it was the only class to satisfy certain credits and I was worried about it because the other reviews on here are awful but I actually liked her a lot. Lectures were informative, grading was harsh but criteria was pretty clear, and it was easy to follow along with the lectures. Lots of opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ventresca-Miller is rude to her students, gives poor feedback, and expects large improvements based on said feedback. One of the worst classes I've taken at Michigan both in terms of poor teaching and nonsensical organization. I know it's appealing cause it's ULWR but seriously, take the other AnthrArc class for the Anthro req.

VM is passionate about her work, but lectures are boring and essentially info dumps from the textbook, so the book is essentially useless. The course is not graded on much besides 2 papers that do not have clear prompt. Lectures do not supplement the papers and you are completely on your own on research and writing. Do not take for arch or ULWR.

Textbook and lectures are completely useless, she just talks about her own work. Super vague about grading criteria and then extremely rude and unhelpful feedback. WILL mark you down on things that she doesnt comment on. Also, you have to do extensive research for papers, no citing the textbook. Save yourself the misery and dont take this class.

If I wasn't already in love with archeology, this course would make me want to never take another ANTHRARC course again. The professor was rude to students throughout the course, her grading on papers was so unhelpful, even the lectures were random and confusing. I honestly regret taking this class.

You are graded on 3 exams so don't skip extra credit if you do not have a background in college biology and chemistry. Covers surface level information, but the amount of topics you learn is a lot so the class is mostly memorization. Lamanna mostly reads off slides, and sometimes incorporates fun activities during lecture to understand concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are confusing. Her office hours were ok, but I found tutoring to be the most helpful. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: grade is based on three exams, do the extra credit, lamanna is a very confusing lecturer and it was hard to understand what she was talking about and what you need to know for the exams, prior knowledge in chemistry is extremely important to do well on the exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Lamanna for 415. I think she made the content very doable and her exams were not too difficult. Just make sure to study her slides, because everything comes straight from them (and it's not too application heavy).

USE HER SLIDES TO STUDY. Very clear and comprehensible slides that gave appropriate amount of detail. Would often leave her lectures confused, but the slides helped immensely. Tests are straightforward, extra credit generous.
Definitely a really hard class & will require a lot of work outside of going to lecture. Professors were great and really accessible outside of class. They truly care and want you to succeed!

I really enjoyed Allison's lectures, more than Stuckey's for sure. She did an excellent job at breaking down concepts and reinforced what we needed to know for the tests. For any students about to take this class--DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it will save your grade. Also the practice tests are very similar to the actual exams and help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked her a lot more than the other professor, but only because I thought her slides were a lot more coherent. She was nice and gave us candy and was honestly just really sweet.

DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! Lamanna is very smart, but doesn't explain material the best. the tests are very difficult, and she never finishes her lectures. Go to class, but you will still have to re teach yourself everything before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance was not mandatory, lectures were recorded and posted. Grade is only based on 3 exam scores, so do the extra credit! Lecture slides were very clear with everything you need to know. As long as you know know everything on her practice test and problem sets, you will do good on the exams.

Somewhat similar to the other professor, but I thought her slides were easier to follow and had everything written out. Sometimes we wouldn't finish in time, so we had to watch recordings, which was pretty annoying. Her practice exams match the actual thing, and as long as you know how to study, this course won't be too bad. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although this was a genuinely tough course, I greatly enjoyed it because of the proximity and access you receive to the professors as they are the ones who teach the discussions. You have to study lots, but if you stay on top of the lectures and ask questions during discussions, you will do well. Lamanna in particular is also incredibly nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Allison's lectures more than the other professors. Will help if needed and is very helpful during office hours. The textbook is not needed for this class, I did not crack open the textbook onece!

Prof Lamanna is a very clear professor and very caring about her students, I'm really not sure why ratings are so low. The course mirrors very closely what is needed for the MCAT (so exams are all MC). She lectures well, and this class DEFINITELY requires work, but if you put in the time, 415/515 with her is completely reasonable.

Most of what you need to know is written out on the slides so attendance isn't necessary, but it's helpful. Sometimes she wouldn't be able to finish the lecture so we would have to watch a video which was annoying. Grades are the average of 3 exams but she gives a fair amount of extra credit and her practice exams are similar to the actual thing
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer. Only grades off exams. Studied and attended office hours but nothing seemed to work. Should be given for 3rd years and up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Allison was amazing! She's incredibly smart and has a talent for breaking down complex topics into simple, easy-to-understand explanations. Her lecture slides were long but extremely helpful. Her practice exams closely matched the actual ones, making studying easier. I absolutely loved having her as a professor!

Dr. Lamanna was very helpful and her explanations were clear. If you missed lecture, everything was on the slides. She sometimes wouldn't finish each part of lectures so you would have to learn some stuff on your own. Overall, she is great at explaining things, and her practice exams were very similar to your exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content was not easy, but you can achieve a good grade if you dedicate a good amount of study time outside of lectures! Lamanna really showed that she cared by incorporating cute, hands-on activities in lecture. Her office hours are also so helpful - you can ask a specific question or just listen to her answer other peoples' questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am an A student and this is the only class I got a B, due to a lack of foundational knowledge for chemistry, and studying habits. She may sound monotone, but she actually explains things well. Slides were clear, and her practice exams were similar to the actual exam. Slightly better than Stuckey, I really wish I had gotten an A so badly :(

I think that Lamanna was a better professor than Stucky was. Her slides were easy to read and had all information you needed. She explained things well, and I always knew what was expected of us for the exams. This class is tough and requires a lot of studying, but just take the practice exams and go to office hours and you will be fine.

reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Talks way too fast in lectures but records. iClicker, but lowest five removed. Unnecessarily hard homework, a friend said office hours were helpful/he always finished his hw in OH. Study a lot for the exams - not cumulative, but tricky wording (MC+short answer). Can buy old textbook edition, textbook only needed for homework (read only 1 chapter)

He talks fast, but Adam's incredibly passionate about economics and honestly entertaining to listen to. Go to class and discussion. Do the homework every week and do the practice exams. You should get an B+/A- if you just do what's expected.

Material is very interesting but he covers a lot in each slide during lecture so be sure to go. Also be sure to read the book because my grade on each exam was correlated to how much I read the book. Exams are tough so be sure to put in the time for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Decent at presenting. Attendance is scored by iclicker questions and he gives you five days to skip.

I love Adam! He is a very passionate lecturer and keeps you engaged. He lectures incredibly fast, so it's hard to keep up with him. If you put in the work though, you'll do fine. He records his lectures and is great at posting slides before class. He is very knowledgable and uses a lot of real life examples to explain the content.

Stevenson is a very eccentric guy. On stage he talks fast and hard, but the over-the-top behavior can make class more engrossing. During lecture it can be hard to keep up, and the content is rather thick. Class required memorization of equations and deep understanding of the topics to do well. Certainly harder than other profs, but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very smart. He keeps track of attendance. His lectures are recorded so i rewatched them. He rushes through the material very fast. You have to put in work. The homework is somewhat helpful, although it doesnt connect to tests. Tests are very hard especially in the limited time. Work everyday if you want to do well. Stevenson makes it hard.

Stevenson is very knowledgeable and excited about microecon. The class can be challenging, which is good preparation for Econ 401. It is very important to stay on top of the content and readings of the class. Make sure you give yourself a few hours each week to do the homework well. There's a lot of math, but it's not too bad if you pace yourself.

ECON 102 with Stevenson is very MATHEMATICAL BASED. I highly recommend you to take this with him if applied algebra is your strong suit. Be prepared for annoying weekly homework that can take 2.5 hours to figure out. Lectures can be long and is based on graded iClicker points. I only used the textbook to do homework. All in all, it was a good class

Stevenson is very knowledgable but he often rambles on and his powerpoints have 30+ slides each with 2 or 3 paragraphs of information on them. This is a very hard class and requires a lot of work, Cho is much better

The class covers a lot of valuable information. It's good to have a basic understanding of the economy regardless of your major. Prof Stevenson's exam and hw questions would irritate me a lot, but he is passionate about what he teaches.

Stevenson is one of the better professors I've had in the Economics department. I was hesitant to take 102 because I found 101 difficult. However, it is not super difficult to do well in 102 if you put the work in. Stevenson may ramble on a little bit but I'd rather have a professor who over explained something rather than under explained.

Adam Stevenson was the best professor I've had at UofM up to this point. He is very knowledgeable on Macroeconomics and covers huges amounts of material in lecture. Study hard for the exams because they are difficult and will test your knowledge of everything you learn. Tough class but if you put enough work in, it is manageable to do decent.
He explains his topics well. Textbook didn't help as most of his content isn't even in there. If you study well enough you'll do okay. Old exams are very helpful.
Stevenson is kind of eccentric but he explains all of the topics well. The exams are very fair and It's pretty easy to do well as long as you review the lectures and study old exams.

Pretty average all around. He's definitely excited about Econ but sometimes his explanations just ramble on. The tests are not as bad as people say, they're very similar to the old exams online and grades are curved generously.

I took ECON 102 approximately 3 years ago with Stevenson. I would describe the material and structure of his 102 class to be extremely well crafted. He is a really passionate lecturer. I majored in Economics because of him and how well he introduced some of the major Macro topics.
Worst Prof ever, textbook sucked not helpful at all

This class is tough. You'll have to study, but the curve is generous. The more you study, the better you'll do (this is true for most classes). I never read the book (I only used it for homework). I ended up with an A+

Stevenson is very energetic and you get the sense that he cares about what he does. I've recommended him to a couple of friends. However this class is graded on the Econ curve which ensures that at least 40% of the class will get a C or below. Be wary of that stat, I killed Econ 101 and barely pulled out an A- in this class.

Stevenson is passionate about economics. You can tell that he is smart and knowledgable about the topics. His course is not necessarily fast-paced, but it is difficult. The exams have multiple choice answers that take thought to process each possible answer. The exams also have free response that can leave you clueless how to answer a problem.

Stevenson is one of the best teachers I've had so far and really knew what he was talking about. He gives clear, in depth lectures and lays out what is expected on the test. He is a nice guy and even though the class is somewhat difficult, it isn't hard to get a good grade if you put in a little effort
The lectures were very boring, but he made the material easy to understand. The tests were relatively hard, but that is pretty common for an econ 102 class.

Econ 102 is definitely a hard class and Stevenson's exams make you work for your grade. His exams are curved but they are not easy, especially the short answer portions. He also covers material very quickly, but he does but the lectures on Blue Review. He really has a passion for teaching, and it makes the class much better than expected.
The class is basically mandatory, but Adam's exams are tough. It is graded on a scale though.

true sharks should be able to get an A in this class.... not hard at all. I didn't go to a single lecture and got an A in the classs... prob could have gotten an A+ but I had other stuff to worry about. he also curves unlike dudley- so take stevenson for sure.
Tests are tough but he is an incredible professor, who prepares you for the exam. If you want to take econ 402 ever, take 102 with stevenson

He moves very fast and covers a lot of material each class. Exams are very tough, the curve is small. He is knowledgable about the subject but often overcomplicates things. It is a hard class, but manageable if you are willing to put a LOT of work into it.
You have to do a lot of work if you want to do well on the exams which are hard. His lectures can be hard to follow because he moves SO fast.
He is not a nice guy.  He purposely makes his exams way harder than necessary and he is not helpful at all. I worked my butt off and ended up with a B+, which was my worst grade at UMich thus far.

Adam is a great professor. His tests are hard, but they are fair and he earns the right to be tough because he explains the material so well. He covers the readings quite thoroughly in lecture so you often don't need to open the book. Favorite prof in the econ department!
I've heard a lot of bad things about him and understand none of them. He's one of the most straightforward professors at this university and I think he's very entertaining in class.

Adam is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject but he overly complicates things and the class is ridiculously hard. His grading system makes it hard as he returns the 2nd exam grades after the drop/add deadline.

He is a very passionate and smart lecturer. There's hw problems every week, which can take a while but are not terrible. The 3 exams are pretty difficult, but if you pay attention in class and study, you will do fine. Contrary to the other comments, he actually said in class that he is Keynesian, and thus, liberal. But he tries to remain neutral.

Adam is a bright guy. He knows the material and is clear in delivery, but he makes things extremely complicated. As others have said, he's blatantly conservative, and lets his opinions be known. The exams are extremely difficult, but if you put a lot of time into it you can escape with a B+/A-

Adam enjoys overly complicating things. The tests are very difficult, probably more so than they should be, although not entirely unfair; if you really study hard you will be okay. He is blatantly conservative, condescending, and super egotistical. Unhelpful in office hours. There isn't that much homework, but it's very tedious and takes time.
Extremely into himself. There are math questions on the exams that are not covered whatsoever in lecture.

Definitely knows his stuff, but makes his exams mostly math based and gives zero explanation to the math, while spending the entire lecture time focusing on things that are made pretty clear by the textbook. Would not recommend, there are easier Econ 102 professors here.

The new homework required and written parts to exams can catch students buy surprise at certain points. But in reality it's the same difficulty as 101. His test will make sure you know he material. Show up. Pay attention. Ace the homework. Use it all as study guide and ace the class. Remember lecture tools is your friend.

I was really happy with Stevenson as a professor. The class was hard, but it's going to be hard no matter what. He was a really clear lecturer but he speaks really fast and I didn't have time to hand write everything I wanted to. He puts ppts online with his notes so that's really helpful. Overall I liked him as a professor and would recommend him.

Great Professor and i'm saying this as a student who got a C in his class. His class is hard, exams are even more challenging but I learned a ton and as long as you don't take many other classes with it, you'll have plenty of time to study the heap of material he throws at you.

Stevenson's a very organized professor and he tries to keep his lectures interesting. Regarding exams, I thought the second one was okay, but the third was hard. It's probably because I liked the material for the second portion more than third. But either way, you do need to put in time for this class. Also, the textbook really isn't necessary.

Stevenson knows what he is talking about but he is sometimes very boring and loses you in the lecture. His slides are pretty useless although the graphs are good.  His tests are extremely difficult and it makes his class very frustrating.

Stevenson definitely knows material in and out, but his lectures are at times very dull. He does upload the post-lecture slides and the lecture recordings online, and I rewatched parts of those for the exams. The exams can be either okay or impossible. The second exam was the most difficult exam I have ever taken.

He posts lecture slides AND audio online which is huge. He does everything he can for his students to succeed. That being said, the exams for this class fluctuate between fair and downright heinous; very hit or miss.

Very knowledgeable and clear lecturer. He's my only professor who posts the lectures online (the entire lecture..video plus sound..) which is incredibly helpful. He also seems to be genuinely passionate about teaching, which is unfortunately a rarity at the college level.

Adam is a good guy who knows a lot about the topic.  He loves to talk forever though, and the amount he tries to plow through in the last five minutes of class is a little much.  Also, the second exam was the hardest thing I've ever taken.  Average was a 32/60 or something like that.

Stevenson speaks fast and can be dull at times, but if you can manage to focus, he is a great lecturer, very clear, and passionate about economics. Use your GSIs, they're generally pretty good if they speak english.
Stevenson is really solid. He knows and explains the material well - it is NOT an easy A, however. You have to study a lot to do well on the finals- always go to review sessions.
I thought that this was a great class. Professor Stevenson does an excellent job at presenting the material and I found lectures to be very interesting, though exams were kind of tough.

Probably the most boring lecture i've had at U of M. It doesn't even matter though as the exams will be completely new things. Some GSI's are good, but mine was terrible and did not care about the students who did not grasp the topics.

A very charming but not really good professor. He sounds very legit in lectures, but you'll never understand the stuff when you start studying. Very heavy workload, ridiculously fast pace, unclear. Killer combination with engineering classes.

He definitely makes the class WAY harder than it is. I didn't actually hate it and did well but for some people, this class can be hard. I used Study Edge to review and prepare for the exams. They have chapter reviews and concept videos that helped me get the hang of things way faster. I did their practice problems and those were EXTREMELY helpful!
Makes the class unnecessarily complicated. You will learn one formula the entire year and then on the exam he gives you a total different formula. Take pass/fail if you can.
His lecture slides are boring and hard to follow which makes lectures painful to sit through. had to teach most of the material to myself

Stevenson really knows his stuff. He posts recordings of all of his lectures online, which is extremely helpful considering the difficulty of the material. It's not an easy A, but the GSI's were really great across the board. If you put the work in you should be fine
The lectures are interesting, the exams are tough but fair, but the homework assignments are difficult and way too long.

Stevenson is a nice-guy professor who is more than willing to help students who try. His tests and homework are challenging, but he doesn't try to make kids fail or test on things he doesn't teach. Even in large lectures, he does a decent job remembering people if they come to office hours.

I was in his Economics of Education class, and he is definitely one of the most organized and clear teachers I have ever had. Everything is on Ctools, including recorded lectures and tons of past papers! Doing the readings isn't really necessary. If you do the past papers and go through lecture slides thoroughly and you'll do well.

Stevenson is very organized and clearly knows what he is talking about. However, the homework and exams are very difficult. Much studying and frequent office hours visits are required to receive a good grade in his class.

Stevenson is a good professor.  Class was very interesting.  "Required" readings are easy to ignore. 6 homework sets through the semester, but they tend to be lengthy. Exams are multiple choice and short answer and were more difficult than I expected.

Hardest class i've ever taken. Professor Stevenson is a nice guy but and a good professor, but goes so fast sometimes. The work load is extremely heavy and at a certain point the tests are so hard that they're just cruel.

Adam is a really nice guy and a really good lecturer, but the class is hard. It's not too difficult to get a good grade, but it is a ton of work. Make sure you read the book. And count the number of times Adam says "Fine!" during lecture. Also, he's NOT Canadian, regardless of what anyone says.

Professor Stevenson is definitely a great teacher, but the exams are quite difficult. He offers the basic concepts of new material in lectures, but the homework and exams take it to another level. If you're up for the challenge, I would recommend him.
Great professor. Hard exams. But if you study enough you'll do well. His lectures do enough; you don't even need to read the textbook (although I'm sure it's more helpful)
Good professor. Teaches well. Exams are hard though.

Loved this class with him!! I took it over the summer, loved how much I learned about education. Class isn't too math-based (I'm not good at math so I'd know), there's also a good deal of remembering educational trends and theories. I love his passion about the subject.
Pretty bad. Super fast and very unclear.

Stevenson is really goofy. Homework is not very clear, especially the problems he writes. Kind of has a standoffish attitude when dealt with in office hours. Tests have questions on them that come totally out of left field. They are also way too long, you can know the material and still do poorly due to a lack of time. Take at your own risk.

Decent professor, but the class is hard.  Don't take if you haven't taken 101 (he says 101 is not required, just recommended - it should be required).  Best way to study is to look at homework questions/answers, even unassigned problems.  Prof seems a bit bitter about not being tenure-track, though.
HARDer than econ 101! He goes pretty fast in lecture though he posts the lectures in ctools. Exams get progressively harder. BUT he is a really nice guy
Same difficulty level as 101, MUST study AND do homework. First exam is more review, second and final are difficult. Dry lecturer and make sure you get a good GSI
Class can get a little dull at times, but otherwise it's not too terrible. Posts all his lectures online so you don't really ever have to go. There is iClicker attendance though.

I'm an ECON major who got a B in 101.  His lectures are quite possible the most boring things I have ever attended, but if you can pay attention then you should do fine.  Decent lecturer, great slideshows, I have taught myself the entire class.
Goes WAY too fast through the lecture slides. I don't feel that the material is that difficult, but still struggled with it because he fails to explain the intuition behind the important concepts.

AMAZING lecturer, his slides are a great resource for studying, HWs always have a "real-world" application/meaning behind them. He makes sure you learn a LOT of applicable material in this course. One of the best professors I've had at Michigan!

The concepts are simple but he glosses over the important stuff and rambles on about many things that are irrelevant.  he goes too quickly through the lecture slides and his exams are nothing like any of the practice exams.  Not the best econ teacher I have had here at Michigan.
Nice guy.  Hard class.  Really energetic guy.  Funny if you get a chance to talk to him in person.

The class starts out fairly easy. The first exam is basically all 101 review. The second exam is pretty easy too. It gets much harder for the final so don't slack off towards the end of class. Doing the practice exams are the most helpful ways to study, so make sure you understand all of the questions on them.
no comment

very clear and interesting professor. He likes to connect real life scenarios to the class discussion. The first two midterms are ok, but the final is very hard. The class ends up being approximately curved down 10% (total points) (80% A-, 70 B- etc...). Overall, you will probably get similar grade to 101, and the tests are more straight forward.

He is a clear lecturer and is very good at explaining hard to grasp concepts. I would suggest going to lecture in order to do better on exams. The second midterm and final are hard, but study hard and you should be fine. I love econ now.
He is a very good lecturer, crystal clear, good examples, engaging.  Found the subject matter somewhat dull (liked 101 better).

GREAT professor! After this class, I was more interested in Econ. He is an engaging lecturer and explains his material well with clarity. It is nice to have a professor with much passion. Econ 102 has been my favorite class so far! Even though it was a challenging class, it was ultimately very worthwhile and I learned a lot.

Overall Stevenson was a pretty decent lecturer. The work isn't easy but it definitely is doable. Its way easier than 101 but the only hard part about it that the curve sucks. There is only like a 5% curve. My only suggestions is go to office hours if you have any questions because most of the GSI's suck.

I really liked Stevenson.  The material is interesting to me, and he is engaging.  His voice is not boring, he is animated, and his mannerisms make me laugh.  I thought grades and exams were completely reasonable.  I'm taking another class he is teaching next semester because I like him a lot.
Good professor/lecturer, very clear, even makes points several times over for you to understand. Exams are fair, helps if you understand the material rather than just memorizing it

Stevenson is great. He videotapes his lectures so you  can go back and watch themas he draws the graphs, which are GREAT review for the exams. Overall, it's a fairly graded class and I thought it was more straightforward than 101. Pretty much if you do the articles and HW, you'll get a 3rd of a letter grade bump. Two midterms and a difficult final
Stevenson's an awesome prof! Take Economics of Education, Trust me, its so enlightening about the education system, its kinda easy, kinda hard. Its a fun 300 level Econ class.

If you don't need to take this class dont. 101 was much easier and this just flat out sucked. Ive never studied so hard and done so bad. Final was horrible and cumulative. Take it if you need to otherwise avoid.

He uses lots of lecture slides, posts them online, with notes, along with podcasts of the lectures - all very useful for studying. Lectures are interesting because he applies the basic 102 models to complex economic issues. A lot of professors won't bother with that.

if you took econ 101, this class is not a shocker in difficulty. Not a walk in the park, but definitely not impossible either. It takes work, but if you got a B or better in econ 101, you should be able to do the same in this class with less effort. Overall, Great Guy and Great Class

He's a good professor: goes at the right speed, lectures are clear and easy to understand. But agreed, DON'T take this class for fun. It will kill you, esp. if you're not a "math-science-know how to apply stuff to problems" person. If you're like me who learns by memorizing things , don't take this class. It will destroy you.

stevenson is an interesting guy, but just sometimes hard to take seriously.  his lectures aren't that important, the GSIs are more so what matters. the exams are tough, even with the curve, many people still do horrible. only take this class if you seriously have to!!!
Best 102 professor.  Fun teaching style, interesting lectures.  Exams are pretty hard, but your grade is relevant to the class average so it doesn't matter.  Highly recommended!
hi professor stevenson!

Adam was really enthusiastic. His tests were too hard, but he curved the grades at the end, so it turned out okay. He also screamed the whole time and could use a lesson in speaking with a microphone, but overally it was a good experience. My GSI (Noah) was AWFUL and Adam was happy to help me instead.
If you are okay with basic algebra, you would have no trouble whatsoever.

Lectures in a clear but interesting manner - hand motions make him look like a dictator at times. Slides have what you need to know. Tests are hard and stresses math (bring a calculator!), but the curve is generous esp. with the homework bump (1/2 a letter grade!). Would recommend anyone strong in math to take it. Remember: practice and SLEEP WELL!

Great lecturer and his slides are incredibly neat and informative.  However, the tests were apparently too easy first semester so he made them fairly difficult this time.  I felt like he was asking us to draw inferences in the short answer instead of actually teaching it in class.  Grades are curved in the end though, so you'll be fine.

Good teacher and interesting lecturer. But, he doesn't understand how to write a test. His tests from first semester were very easy. He made our tests really hard. He needs to figure out how to write an appropriate test for the material taught. He doesnt curve tests but curves overall grades, and if you do the all the hw you will get a grade bump

This class turned out to be a complete fluke. It appeared that Dr. Stevenson was attempting to make up for all of the good grades that he gave in his first semester class and make the exams too difficult. It was not a good experience at all.

This was his second semester teaching this class.  The practice tests from last semester were extremely easy compared to the tests from this semester. The class average ended up being a 70 which was curved to around a B-.  Two tests and one cumulative final. Make sure you understand the material very well. Make sure to do the HW for a grade bump.

This man explains economics with impeccable clarity.  Exams are reasonable and if you do the homework your grade gets bumped up a level higher.  His slides are very helpful as well and he is good about keeping the Ctools page updated.  Doesn't require attendance to lecture or section, which is nice.

i honestly liked him all the way until the 2nd midterm- at which point he gave us an exam that was so irrelevant and confusing that 10% of the class dropped immediately afterward (and got w's on their transcripts)

New professor that keeps things interesting. From what I've heard from everyone, Miles Kimball is horrible -- don't take your chances with him. If you do all the HW you get an automatic grade bump at the end of the semester (A- to A, etc.). The course is curved at the end to meet the Economics department criteria.

New professor that keeps things interesting. From what I've heard from everyone, Miles Kimball is horrible -- don't take your chances with him. If you do all the HW you get an automatic grade bump at the end of the semester (A- to A, etc.). The course is curved at the end to meet the Economics department criteria.
Great Lecturer, thoughtful, friendly. I looked forward to class!
I like him. He is enthusiastic and his lectures are rarely boring. The midterms were a breeze.

Extremely helpful during office hours. Interesting and very clear lectures. He repeats important points a lot so that students can understand better. Plus, I could see he was doing his best to make sure students can really learn something out of his lecture. Pay attention to lectures than textbook. Exams are not hard if you studied (except finals)

I had him in fall '09, which was his first semester teaching this class. So he lacked some experience with grading, and exam policies. But i found him to be very pleasent during lecture and I did not mind going. Presented material clearly---Id say a good man to learn economics from! very enthusiastic
He doesn't curve, so if you aren't good at taking exams, or don't understand the material 100%, you're screwed. They grade the short answers really harshly as well. Lectures weren't boring though.

He is extremely arrogant and doesn't really take the students concerns into account for grades. If you get a good gsi you should be fine, but if you don't your screwed. Also short response on test are graded very strictly and you will get random points off even if you answered it right, but just not their way with their terminology

If you can get past his left-winged garbage he is a great professor. His lectures are clear and his tests are pretty fair and follow his lectures pretty closely. Reading the book isn't very helpful, except if you are really struggling to grasp some of the concepts in class. The biggest downside about the class is there is no curve so be aware
He is a chill professor. He makes random cheesy chokes, kinda funny.

Yes, he's quite a socialist but versus other econ professors in the dptment I will gladly take him because you don't even need to read the book if you get his slides. At times he goes retardedly slow and I think he forgets he's teaching at michigan rather than OSU. Just LABEL your graphs on tests and ur straight for an A

Full blown socialist, when he isn't espousing his far-left ideology he actually does a decent job at teaching to the textbook. His "custom" lectures should be avoided at all costs unless you enjoyed The Communist Manifesto.

Really enthusiastic and clearly cares about the subject. He makes the material easy to understand.If you have a basic understanding of economic principles the course shouldnt be too difficult. He really does his best to make sure everyone understands. His lecture notes are very thorough and clear.One of the best econ profs ive had in my 4 years!

Pretty good at bringing the material across, unfortunately he is about as left-wing as they come. Which, as an econ professor, is a detriment to taking him and especially his "custom lectures" seriously.
he is very straight forward in explaining things. very clear!

Allie could be teaching 'watching paint dry 101' and I would still take their course. They've always made me feel safe, respected, and valued as a student and encouraged me to pursue what I was passionate about. Classes were very well structured, and I was never confused about homework/lecture material. If you get the chance I highly recommend them

Was reflecting recently on my time in Alli's class. They showed me empathy and kindness that I did not receive from other profs at stamps. Alli has a special ability to tailor the assignments to the unique artist that each student is. I am very thankful for them.

Really lovely teacher and very accommodating and understanding. They really try to work with the students to make sure the class isn't too stressful but we still learn a lot. Allie also gives a lot of good feedback on each assignment, not just a grade. Grading criteria is clear and achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Allie is super kind and they are always open to talk, they gave help outside of class often and worked to create an inclusive and positive classroom environment! Grades in the course were fairly distributed with a heavy emphasis on participation so if you show up and complete every assignment on time you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Allie is amazing! Very kind professor who creates a very welcoming environment during discussions. They also did a great job at breaking down really intense readings. As long as you do most of the discussions/quizzes and participate youll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Allie has to be my favorite professor at Stamps. They always make time for their students, and are always in an upbeat or understanding mood for classes. If you bring up a valid topic you think should be discussed in lecture, Allie will encourage you to follow up with it. When I was just coming into being queer, Allie told me about good resources

Lectures often feel disorganized, and explanations are not always clear, which creates confusion among students. Overall, I believe the course could benefit greatly from clearer instruction and more supportive engagement with students.

Lectures were boring and hard to understand, he changed our class's midterm to in-class w/o notes because we weren't participating enough in class. Labs are fun but you have to have a good GSI teaching you. Grading criteria is vague.

You have a lab due pretty much every week. One midterm, that was open note and take home. The lecture portion is basically a stats class, and Prof. A is very nice. The labs though are hard if you your GSI doesn't teach well. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! The class was fine, great if you are bad at math and don't want to take a hard QR1.

Dr. A is very kind, and you can tell that he cares a lot about his students! The actual lectures are a bit boring, but the labs are very useful. The assignments can be difficult, but they are overall manageable, especially if you go to office hours. The class is mainly about concept application, so its perfect if you're not great at math.

I have really enjoyed Dr. A's 301 and wish I would've took him for 201 also. The projects are manageable, but the timelines are pretty quick. Lectures are a little dry, but its very obvious he cares a lot about the material and student success.

Great professor, but the work for the course may be too much. I was in office hours every week and it became very rough to manage when a time conflict arose. The professor is fantastic, however. I just don't think a lab assignment every week was necessary, at least not one that's so lengthy.
Dr. A really cares about student success and does his best to make lecture easily understandable to everyone. You'll learn a lot without being overwhelmed by the new content or assignments.

"Dr. A" is a solid professor and an even better human being. He is deeply invested in student success both in and out of the classroom. He will go out of his way to meet with students to discuss class topics, lab assignments, or even career advice. 
Lectures are on the slower side, but that's because he tries to cater to as many students as he can.

Dr. A's lectures were a little slow moving for me, but he goes through each line of the script of code for that week's lesson, which can be super helpful if you are unfamiliar with R/Python. I found it difficult to stay focused given I already had knowledge of Python and R. The labs are super helpful for review, and the GSIs were really great.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. A means well. While his lectures lack in clarity, the labs make up for it. The class gives you the opportunity to learn practical skills in Python, Excel, and R. The midterm was pretty straightforward as well. My biggest tip would be to choose your lab GSI wisely because their help make or break your lab assignments and coding projects.

Dr. A clearly cares a lot about student success. I didn't find lecture to be that helpful since a lot of it overlaps with Stats 250 content and he doesn't have the best slides. Labs taught me a lot about Excel, R, and Tableau, and he was always accessible for coding help. Projects weren't too bad and taught very useful skills.
No Comments

Professor Sinha often told us of his adventures spent fighting in the trenches of the jiangxu war of 1987. He uses colorful powerpoint slides as well as guests to demonstrate his points. If I had  to sum him up in one word, I'd say herbivore.

Really easy. I was really impressed because he is an Indian guy, and he spoke Chinese very fluently, and with a flare. Some might call him colorful, I think he is quite vivacious and at times grotesque. EASY!
Had him for lab.  He didn't do much.  Most people just walked in to turn in their homework then left.
cool
very helpful and willing to take time to explain concepts
Truly interested in making sure people who want to will understand not only the formulas but the math behind them. Very enthusiastic about math.
explains stuff well.has a good sense of humor.
fine
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Akhavan makes ME 320 needlessly difficult - homeworks are long, tedious, and graded harshly. The midterm was three hours long, worth 40% of the final grade, and put 12% of the class into the "withdraw or fail" range (her words). Akhaven certainly knows her stuff, but lectures are technical and hard to follow. TAKE A DIFFERENT SECTION

This was the single most fulfilling course of my collegiate experience. On top of teaching more difficult math-she exposes you to the types of simulation-based modeling expected by top engineering organizations in the field. Akhavan is brilliant--the coursework is VERY challenging. Lower than deserved ratings likely due to slackers.

Honestly not as bad as everyone makes her sound. 420 is a ton of work, but honestly they tell you exactly what to do. You will 100% have to be in most office hours, but its pretty easy to get an A if you simply do the projects. One nice thing is a lot of the projects is just waiting so you can do other homework while the simulation runs.

Throws handwritten notes on a projector and eats while lecturing. Uses examples from the book. I ended up dropping her class, so I only have limited experience with her lecturing, but I needed something from her the next semester to address a registration/bureaucratic situation and got minimal cooperation. Gives 1/4 pt for answering Questions.

This class and Akhavan herself were both terrible. She describes the projects as being "full month projects," yet gives a week and a half. I spend a minimum of 45 hours a week on this three credit tech elective. Avoid Akhavan at all costs.

This is the worst class in the ME curriculum. Many students share this sentiment. It is over 40 hours a week on tedious projects, where you don't learn any software or fluid mechanics. The GSIs are not helpful and grading is meticulous. Furthermore, Akhavan shows no interest in this class or teaching students. Avoid this class at all costs.

I am very dissatisfied with her teaching methods. She uses old notes with many examples straight from the book. It's hard to keep up with her in lecture because you're stuck interpreting her handwriting, and she's off reading her notes word for word. Most importantly, her exams are extremely difficult and impossible to pass. Avoid at all costs!

She admits her notes are chicken scratch then rushes them through a projector. Cancels class on short notice then speeds through notes to catch up only to end class 20 min early. She’ll awkwardly notify the class how old and ill she is. Read ahead to ease note taking. Don’t take pictures of notes during class or attempt to debate with her!

This teacher canceled class 5 times 10 minutes before class started. she lectures off of lecture notes that she probably wrote out a decade ago.Parts would be randomly crossed out and  had food and water stains. The only thing good about the class is that it's massively curved. She treats you like a grad student.

This lady is brilliant. Her lectures very clear and she helpful outside of class. The homework is long and difficult but makes sure you know the material. More homework than other fluids professors. Class is curved to a B+ so just beat the average and you should get at least an A-.

This lady is one awesome genius. She's a master in her field and very helpful to those who seek out her help. Not to mention, she is hilarious. We had a fire drill one day in which she poked her head out of the classroom door and then just walked out and up to her office leaving class w/o saying a word. Funny lady and very smart.

She seems very tough at first and is. But, she is a VERY good teacher. her notes are crystal clear. Just make sure to attend class. It's tough sometimes b/c class is at 8:30a. But, she is very helpful and the class is highly curved, so it seems like everyone is doing poorly at first. Again, VERY GOOD TEACHER!
I like her a lot
A lot of derivations, but she's not terrible
No Comments

She LOVES to derive EVERYTHING and gets caught up in the mathmatics of every theorem. She likes class participation and if you have an idea as to what is going on stop her and make her look at the big picture.She's very intelligent and likes to help.
No Comments
Genuinely the best, most caring professor I've had. He organizes his slides in a way thats easy to understand and does his best to accommodate all students. Honestly a great guy and professor.

He is the professor I have had at teaching. I feel like he truly cares about the students and them learning the content and not just getting it done. He mad studying so much easier because he was so good a teaching.

Very intelligent, genius. VERY FAST speaker slides are organized. Some videos in class didn't help as much, but he was great. Both professors for N245 were equally as great. However, no recorded lectures, and 90% grade is exams. Kaplan was VERY difficult, prepare for it in advance. Use CoursePoint to help with NCLEX practice questions. Study often!

Sharma is committed. He is genius; passionate about infectious diseases but speaks very fast so it's ok if you don't get everything down sometimes too quiet / hard to hear. N236 is slightly harder than what people say, requires HEAVY memorization, difficult to balance this class since this is the hardest semester of the entire nursing program.
dr Sharma is a really nice dude and his lectures are super clear. exams are EXACTLY like his lecture slides so as long as you review his slides you will be fine

Dr. Sharma is one of the best professors I have had here. He is super down to earth, cares about his students, and is very receptive to his students thoughts and concerns. He gives you everything you need to know for the exams, its a lot of content but nothing is meant to trick you. Once again he is just an awesome guy! really enjoyed his class

Sharma is a great lecturer, all of his explanations are clear and I don't leave with any questions. The grade for N236 is solely based on quizzes and exams, which requires a lot of memorization of different infectious organisms. Sharma gives you all the information that you need in the lecture, so if you take good notes and study you will do fine.

Absolutely love Sharma. Very fair in terms of expectations and exam material. Takes feedback from students seriously. Really respects his students and their time so makes sure to keep things as clear as possible.

Dr. Sharma is so sweet. The lectures have a lot of information which makes this class difficult, but his explanations are clear and you can tell he wants everyone to do well. He's always available if you have questions and exams are straightforward if you study the lectures. Would definitely take another class of his!

Professor Sharma is great! He's super clear and makes his expectations for your learning known. He gives interesting lectures and he's a super likable sweet professor! Microbiology isn't everybody's first choice to take but he makes it bearable.

He gives clear and concise explanations. He is willing to help outside of class. The class may be a bit difficult due to amount of content but it's manageable. The slides help prep for exams. Exams are straightforward. The only critique is that he talks fast during class so it can be difficult to get the information in time.

Best professor I've had in the nursing school so far. Super clear about expectations and resources for students having trouble. He works hard to keep students engaged during class despite the heavy course load. He expects a lot but if you put in the work, you'll be fine. (I recommend taking lecture notes before class, he talks fast)

Dr. Sharma is the best professor you'll have this semester. His lectures are super well organized and he's always very clear about what information is important. His exams are straightforward and not difficult at all if you follow the lectures.

Dr. Sharma is very intelligent and well-spoken. His lectures are concise and easy to understand. The exams in his class were not very difficult as long as you pay attention in class and study from the lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sharma has amazingly clear lectures. He is available and understands that nursing students aren't microbiologists. By highlighting parts of the powerpoints, he makes the most important part for exams clear (although they are only highlighted on the recordings). The class was work heavy for 3 credits, but I attended during COVID, so grain of salt.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's the SWEETEST. Very pleasant and encouraging.

I have had few professors I appreciate & respect more than Dr. Sharma. He is passionate about teaching. He is respectful of his students & while he expects you to work hard & do well, he is never trying to trick you & makes it clear he is there to help. I would recommend him to anyone & hope I can take more of his classes in the future.

Best professor you will ever have. The nicest and sweetest. His exams are very straight forward and as long as you show up and listen you should get all of his questions right. He doesn't force you to remember minuscule details, but expects you to know the key concepts. Overall, love him and he's the best
he is excellent
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: All in all, I really enjoyed Prof. Akaaboune and his lectures.  He is extremely knowledgeable and genuinely cares whether you understand the material or not.  At times, he can be a little bit confusing, but I think he is overall a great professor.  The class itself is pretty chill– 2 exams and a group presentation.  I learned a lot in this class!

Passionate/kind scientist, ineffective professor. I genuinely disagree with comments saying he berates students. However, I agree he is disorganized and offers zero exam prep/guidance. Jam-packed lecture slides make studying overwhelming. Only recommend if you're willing to risk your exam grades, it's a chill class outside of exam weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever had at this university. He has no idea how to use technology, will not respond to emails sent regarding class material, gives no guidance and no rubric for grading. His exam study guides are not relative to the exam, and are released 12 hours before the exam. He berates students during presentations.

He is not very well prepared and couldn't give us answers to questions about the course structure. He made our first exam the day before and had no idea what kinds of questions he was going to put on the exam, so we had no idea what to expect going into it.

Great professor overall and learned more in this class than any other Upper Level Requirement MCDB courses. The content itself is very interesting, and you also learn a lot regarding how to read and understand research.

Definitely the worst professor I've had. He constantly contradicts himself, assigns 80 minute student presentations with no rubric, and he berates students during them with impossible questions that no undergrad could possibly be able to answer. grades from september still are not in in late november. run as far as you can from this prof

Absolutely inaccessible outside of class - completely ignores emails. The guidelines for the course are unclear, and he keeps changing things. He contradicts himself constantly, so I'm not even sure if the things I'm learning are accurate. He says "you don't need to memorize this" and "there will be an exam question on this" on the same slide.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Akaaboune can be very nice and helpful. He is extremely knowledgable about the content he teaches which is a huge plus and rare especially when these courses are taught by profs that engage in research. Would take 451 again.

Akaaboune is no doubt the worst professor I have ever had during my time at UM. He is rude, disrespectful, and goes out of his way to make us feel bad about ourselves. Plz do not take this class if you have any other options, every exam question is short-answer and asks you to design experiments that many graduate students don't even know how to.

Prof. Akaaboune seems like he would be chill, but classes and exams on Zoom were unbearable. He doesn't know how to use Zoom, his test questions are so poorly written, he rarely understands students' questions/concerns, he can be very condescending, he didn't hold office hours, and we barely got through half the planned material. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible. Do not take. He was not understanding and very condescending. Very confusing lectures. Only graded on 4 exams. The average of the tests were very low (70s).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is absolutely no structure to the class. He is not helpful with questions. What is expected of you is not clear at all. Lectures are beyond confusing and very dense. I would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Akaaboune is one of my favorite professors at Mich. He cares so much about his students doing well who he see cares about doing well. Sometimes just showed up at his office for office hours and he always made time to help. Go to his review sessions before exams he wants to help those who go do well and understand what will be on exam.

Great guy really knows his stuff. Very refreshing to see a professor who worked incredibly hard for his position and who genuinely cares about the well being of his students. He is a fair grader, you reap what you sow. You can tell Professor Akaaboune loves his job.

Akaboune was incredibly unorganized. He did not post grades until the end of the semester. He did not follow his syllabus. He provided no rubric for presentations or projects. He wants people to understand material, but was very poor at explaining even basic concepts to students. He asks convoluted questions and has difficulties answering questions

Couldn't understand anything that he said- there's a huge language barrier. Even when I did understand, his lectures were very disorganized- almost as if he hadn't even written the slides.  He moves through lectures very slowly, spending way too much time on easy concepts, but often skipping the vital information that would make the material clear.

Professor Akaaboune was great. Very helpful and always tried to make sure students understood the material. Most of the people complaining were probably just lazy because his exams were exactly on the material covered in lecture.

Nice guy. This is what all science classes should be like in my opinion. Forces you to think like a scientist. I took 418 w/Denver and he basically just asks you to regurgitate a large volume of material. Take Akaaboune if you want to actually learn something and prove your intelligence to this university.
Class is mostly straightforward if you go to class regularly. However if you have questions, take them to the GSI. His review sessions are useless and unhelpful.
Professor is always willing to help students. His lectures are clear and if you come to class you will do well on the exams

Much easier to connect with than Hume, that is, after you bypass the minor accent barrier. Same format as the first half of the course, but it seems the level of intensity has decreased and everyone is finally comfortable studying for this class.

Attendance isn't mandatory but you should go to get notes. Lack of teaching skills but he knows his stuff. I honestly hated this class, it was too specific to their research and not interesting to me. Exams were difficult and had a curved grading scale but this was the first class so they may change that. Overall, doable, but not exciting

Dr. Akaaboune is a decent professor.  He definitely knows his neurobiology, but he is not the best at explaining some topics.  He is a very nice guy though and is willing to meet outside of class to clarify any concerns.
Don't need to go to class. His lecture slides generally have everything you need to know but lacks focus and the exam itself is even more vague. He's a nice guy but just not a good professor.
"What does mean this" pretty much describes my experience with this class.

Worst professor and class I've experienced at U of M. No structure to the class, and exams were based on two 50-minute exams which were very difficult to understand due to a huge number of typos and grammar/language issues. Save yourself a massive amount of frustration and avoid this class - I would not take this class again under ANY circumstance.

Very awful class, do NOT take it from Prof. Akaaboune.  Only 2 exams, no practice exams, no study guides, no review sessions outside of class. Very lazy professor and it shows. However, he is entertaining sometimes during lecture. The 2nd exam seemed to focus on memorizing small, random, useless details. Will explains thing a 2nd time if you need i

The professor is willing to answer students's questions; however, his exams are poorly designed!!!The first exam was too long; the second exam was too detailed. The material taught in this class was too specific on the muscular disorders. Many other important aspects of the neuronal physiology were not covered.

Awesome professor and class.  He does have some trouble with communication but his powerpoint slides are very well done, and he is quite willing to explain things multiple times.  Really wants you to do well in class.  Must attend lectures though to do well

Do not take MCDB 422 from him. Terrible communicator; difficulty explaining even basic concepts. His lectures are random; the class has no structure. You have no idea what you are learning or why. His tests are absurd, testing memorization of the most obscure, useless facts. I am disappointed again; U of M has failed to provide a capable educator.

We have so many professors who demonstrate no real ability, outside of research, to communicate their ideas to undergraduates. With Akaaboune, this problem is magnified 10x due to his near incomprehensibility at times, and his inability to stay organized. The class was light on interesting material and on point opportunities.

Was unable to figure out how to use ctools correctly and almost never posts lectures before the date of the lecture. Show up, take good notes and study for the exams and you will do well. Akaaboune is amazing lazy and it shows in his lecture and grading styles.
Easy Class, Make sure you attend Lectures. Exams are based entirely on lectures.
he is great. i learned alot in his class.;)
Dr.Akaaboune is an excellent professor and very friendly
No Comments
Doesn't speak English or explain ideas very well.  Exams are directly off lecture notes. Book is not necessary.
Worst professor Ive taken at Michigan. Went to other professors to ask their opinion of me because I submitted three labs late. Absolutely subjective and unfair in grading.
13< hours of week for this 2 credit class. Gives consistently low grades and no feedback... Avoid

Carl is one of the worst professors I have ever had at University of Michigan. If you want to take this class be prepared to work 10 hours on a lab report just for him to give it a C+ and give you absolutely no helpful feedback except for "this is terrible". Extremely condescending, out of touch, and expects you to read his mind about what he wants
Take a course with him and you'll know

Worst professor I have had in three years at UM, by far. Condescending to the point of student abuse. Rants non-stop on irrelevant topics. He may have been an OK instructor 60 years ago or so, but now, seemingly well into his eighties or nineties, he is an unqualified disaster of a professor.

Physics 391 is by far the worst class I've ever taken. I've heard that some other sections can be better, but avoid Akerlof at all costs. The lab reports are way too long, and the lab manuals are confusing and poorly written (even though Akerlof writes the manuals). I probably worked about 8 hours a week for this two-credit class.

First off, this class is an absolutely abhorrent amount of work. Weekly lab reports with analysis. However, you do learn a lot about various lab skills and least squares fitting. He knows his stuff for the most part and is a good experimentalist, but can be condescending. Gave everyone an A for the presentation. Not sure how letters go to grades.

Horrible.  You'd think the guy who wrote the lab manual would be a good lab instructor.  WRONG!  Incredibly condescending, always talked for so long that it was hard to finish the labs.  Time pressure was the only hard part about this class.
Very respected and comprehensive. High expectations for students.

Miriam was a great teacher to have that I learned a lot from. That being said, she is very hard on students, demonstrated through her tough grading and strenuous amounts of homework. Overall, she cares tremendously about the progress and learning of her students.

I am a science major and hate languages, but Mme Akoto made the class so much better. There is a ton of work, but it is regulated among teachers, so you would get that with any French class. I would 100% continue studying French if she could be my prof. Definitely would recommend going to her office hours and participating a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Throughout the class prof. Akoto was great! French 231 is a lot of work but she was super nice and always gave feedback on exams and writing. Would totally recommend taking 231 with her because she helped so much and made it a lot easier!

I got Prof. Akoto halfway through the semester because my previous professor had maternity leave. She wasn't the worst professor, but she wasn't overly engaging, and she was TERRIBLE with communication. None of my class knew what we were supposed to do for oral exams. Don't be surprised if she never answers your emails.

French-231 is brutal. The workload is unreasonable and the profs have to teach the exact same lessons for all the classes. Students must learn all content out of class which takes up a ton of time. The only reason I was able to get through this class was Dr. Akoto. She goes above and beyond giving detailed feedback. Go to office hours if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This man is useless as a teacher. His penmanship is atrocious and it's nearly impossible to distinguish between variables that look even slightly similar (think E and epsilon), making it extremely difficult to take accurate notes. He dodges questions by asking his own question and moving on. He SHOULD NOT be allowed to teach.

I don't think he's a bad person, I just don't think he should be allowed to ever teach. Every decision he makes about the course is designed to lighten his own workload. He won't grade homeworks, and STILL hasn't graded two exams (it's November!) and if you go to OH to ask questions? "You need to do this yourself!"
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were awful for this class, he uses someone else's slides and very often stumbles over the material in the slides/loses his train of thought. He mumbles a lot. He gets annoyed when people ask questions during lecture. Exams are fair but he was not that helpful during OH. I don't doubt he is smart but he shouldn't be allowed to teach.
Very caring and taught information well. Exams were difficult. Was helpful during office hours.

Akhoury was a very good professor. He was very clear with all of his info and the exams were very difficult but fair. He was also very helpful and kind to his students. Only thing to mention is that he did sometime mumble during a lecture. Other than that he was a great professor.

I'm very surprised at all of these ratings. Akhoury has been one of my favorite professors of all time. Exams were very difficult but fair. He was very kind and clear in his teaching. This may be untrue, but I have a feeling most of the bad reviews are from students who didn't do well in the class. It is a hard course! I definitely recommend him.

Hands down worst prof I've ever had.  His exams were a mess and he used someone else's power points that he hadn't even reviewed before lecture.  He was totally unprepared and has no idea how to explain things to a 100 level student. Avoid him at all costs

Had him Spring 2014, his teaching ability isn't particularly noteworthy but overall likable individual. Lectures involved mostly reading directly from the Powerpoint. However, he is helpful if you ask him questions after lecture. Problem Roulette and practice exams are your ticket to an A in this class, focus your studying efforts on them.

Dr. Akhoury is a very inconsiderate and somewhat careless professor.  He often times mumbles during lecture.  He also quite frequently makes mistakes on exam questions that will cause you to waste a lot of time on them.  If you try to email him or meet with him outside of class, it's nearly impossible.

He would be great to laern QFT from if you could just chill in his office and have a dialogue. In a lecture format, he doesn't get much done (6 lectures behind by end), emphasizes weird things and ignores important parts, goes in an odd order, and picked a textbook that was literally the EXACT OPPOSITE approach to QFT. Good teacher, bad lecturer.
Akhoury is a great guy and knows that this course is a challenge for many and makes the material needed very clear and simplifies his exams to be fair questions.

I was nervous about taking this class spring term. However, it was a great decision! He recognizes that the material is difficult, and keeps his exams fair. Taking it in the spring term meant that the three exams each only had 10 multiple choice questions, so you have to watch your points.

Professor Akhoury was one of the most caring professors I have had. He took into account that the class was condensed in the spring semester, making the exams very reasonable. He is pretty clear on most topics in the class, yet for some topics he seems to speak softly at the lecture slides. Overall, this class was much better than physics 135.

The issue I had was that Professor Akhoury was one of those brilliant individuals who is not too savvy with teaching. However, exams were definitely fair. He was very accomodating with our group in terms of question fairness and material tested. He was very clear on which lectures would be on the exam. Have no fear, I've had much worse.

Don't get me wrong- Akhoury is brilliant in physics, and this material must be chump change to him. However, that's the PROBLEM- he breezes through slides & explanations and somehow expects everyone to understand. You have to study hard outside of class- that's expected in physics. But if Youtube can teach me material better, that's rather sad.
He just mumbles while he reads off the lecture slides and gets very aggravated when you ask questions. You would be better off buying your own text book and just reading that. Avoid at all costs.

Worst professor I've ever had at the University.  Can't explain a single topic clearly.  Laughs at the class when his Iclicker average is a 20%.  Exams are unfair. Do not take this class with him if you want to understand anything that you "learn".

Useless as a professor. Completely unprepared for class and when he doesn't know something, he skips over it. He rarely got demonstrations to work and he stared at the PP slides and read them to us for 2 hours. Not a good class.

Every comment here is right. His exams sucked, but he did say he'd curve them a little, I don't know if he did. He is not good at answering questions or emailing back to you. Average on first exam 4/10...lecture/discussion mandatory because of iclicker points. Not a fun or easy class! Don't take it with him!
This class is supposed to be difficult, yes, but he was just unfair.

His exams were very difficult and in the middle of the semester he told everyone that the exams were too hard because the average was a 3/10. I felt that he was an unfair teacher and with his curve I still got a D+ when I did all my work
Great class and interesting contents
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Akin goes above and beyond for his students. He's always willing to meet up outside of class. Extremely well-read in the subject material. Provides a good in-depth analysis into the material. Gave me a new perspective on anthropology. I highly recommend this class.
Meh. His lectures are really boring. He can't look you in the eye.  He tries to be nice, and so he just gives you the answers.  The topic is hard, but it should be more interesting.

If you go to class, take notes, go to office hours (key to success), and do the readings you will get an A in the class. This class is super easy if you take the time to meet with him at office hours because he will summarize the exam topics and help you better grasp just the material you need to know. Very nice and understanding too!

Has an attendance sheet in the beginning of class that you have to sign. One paper that is easy if you set up a meeting, he will basically tell you everything you need to write. Two essay tests but he gives you the questions to practice beforehand.

Akin is very willing to help and provides clear answers.  I found his lectures boring and dull, but it is important to go because the notes from lectures are needed for the exams.  Overall a decent class that has a light work load.
Professor Akin is very helpful and passionate about his subject.

This was a great class and I am sad to see it end! Attendance of the lectures is very helpful, and he basically tells stories to whole time. Prof. Akin is very knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff. Exams are very easy, you get the questions ahead of time to prepare. Taking good notes is the key to success!

Definitely take this class! Professor Akin taught some very interesting material and he is a great professor. The class is not too hard, but there are some complex and very interesting topics. Attendance is not enforced, but you have to attend every lecture since exams are off of lectures. Very good professor with lots of great field work.

Prof Akin is very sweet and helpful. Need letters of rec? Then get good grades and attend his office hours. Exams are straightforward - gives a list of possible Qs. Must go to lecture! Although he's a boring lecturer. Do the readings and remember what he says about them in lecture - useful to exam. Take VERY good notes.
No Comments

This class is very easy, and Akin is very kind and helpful. Readings are completely unnecessary, but attending lecture is VERY important. If you go to lecture and take notes, the class is an easy A. Class consists of 2 exams in which he gives you the essays ahead of time and 1 research paper.

Professor Aidala was great and made physics a little more bearable. The resources for the class are easy to access and her lectures are great. She does tend to ramble on with review from previous lectures though which is not very useful in my opinion. You can tell she cares a lot about the students even though the exams can be challenging.

Professor Aidala was difficult to understand at some points. I believe she is one of those professors who is incredibly intelligent but has a difficult time simplifying the material for beginners who are just learning. I wouldn't recommend taking 240 with Professor Aidala, though she would be a great resource for older students.
Dr. Aidala gives a clear expectation of what is expected. However, she is often at conferences and could focus more on examples in class.

Professor Aidala is an amazing instructor. She explains difficult concepts clearly, keeps lectures engaging, and truly cares about students. Her effort to learn everyone's name and create a welcoming environment is rare. One of the best professors I've had at Michigan. She's also super cute and I love her shoes.

She's been teaching this course for a while and her experience shows. Her examples and definitions are clear, and she made the course content feel easy, even though Physics 240 is an objectively difficult course.
I really liked her. I think the physics studio is much better than the lecture, from someone who has done both. The lectures are fine, but you can get an A if you really work at it.

240 studio is not a bad class, I would say easier than physics 140 by quite a bit. However, professor aidala is a quiet lecturer, and gives long reviews of the last lecture at the start of each lecture, and thus class always extends past its time.
