Facilitating discussion is not hard, kinda fun.  I seriously recommend this class.  I started thinking about changing my major because of it (and I did change it).

Amal was a really nice woman and her class was fairly easy, except for when it was your turn to facilitate discussion. The  stories in the coursepack were usually pretty interested, but entirely too long. If you haven't read or have no contribution to the conversation she will call on you. overall, the class is pretty chill i learned a lot.

Amal is an amazing teacher.  She gives easy A's as long as you pay attention in class.  She knows when you are not listening or you haven't read and she will call on you, so be prepared.  She has an interesting perspective because she is from Sudan.  I definitely recommend her!

this seminar was very non structured. it wasnt too bad because you just need to come to class prepared to participate once or twice. she will call you out if you haven't read though. groups have to facilitate discussion every class which sucks when its your turn. she grades kind of hard for it being a seminar but the topics were pretty interested.
At Valparaiso university she stole money from her students so she and her daughter could take a free trip to Disney world under the cover of calling it a public health clinical.

She is so sweet and very passionate! There are participation assignments that can only be completed if you attend class, so attendance is mandatory. Overall, she grades fairly and is super kind and bubbly!

Nurs 372 is by far one of the most irrelevant nursing class that is even offered in this program. Mind you this professor is very condescending and is not understanding. She ignores emails and when she does reply she is very passive aggressive and lacks empathy. This course is very homework heavy and does not relate to medical surgical nursing.

Dr. B was kind, well-informed, and understanding with me. She was regularly available and encouraged questions. Work on the CAT assignment early and often! It ends up being over 100 pages. However, her expectations could be inconsistent across students and across the semester. This may be due to her being new to teaching this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super sweet and caring, just make sure you are participating in class. She makes a point to be as accessible as possible, and even gives out her phone number to make sure she can be reached with any questions.

One of the least consistent/clear grading I have ever seen from a professor. She would tell us to implement "Consumer Behavior" terms in our assignment without ever giving us clear direction of what "Consumer Behavior" terms even mean. Amy Angell is an extremely nice person but do not have her as a professor unless necessary.

Amy is sweet and cares a lot about her students. The entire class is one large group project, and the lectures have almost nothing to do with large assignments. This is one of those classes you forget about, and then once a month, you have some massive group assignment that you dedicate your life to. Good for client experience, bad for sanity.
Amy Angell grades based on how much she likes you + The grading criteria is arbitrary, and she is a little featherbrained
Bad project, irrelevant to the class materials and textbook concepts. Unhelpful and slow response when being asked questions. Stay away this course at all cost

Unprepared, unreachable, and unhelpful. Slides were recycled, but never finished by class time. Outside work is fine, but the inconsistency made it impossible to coordinate with Amy and her clients. Mediocre students who do bare minimum, dislike reading or taking notes, and require the least input would fare well in this class. go bobcats !

Professor Angell flaunts her independent consulting projects yet often times confuses basic marketing concepts. Several times during the semester students had to correct straight up wrong information she was sharing. I would avoid

Angell is one of the worst professors I've had at Ross. I am unsure how she even assumed her teaching position, given she merely reads off her slide decks lecture after lecture and struggles to properly answer questions related to real world marketing application. Her grading system is both arbitrary and unfair, as she clearly has class favorites.

Amy is the best professor Ive had at university of Michigan and her hands on project for promotional client campaigns gave me an opportunity to get real industry experience to help with my desired career path. She truly cares about students and the making sure they succeed in their project last to help out the local Detroit small businesses.

Amy made the class extremely competitive for no particular reason by weighting participation at like 23% amidst COVID. Need extensions - forget it. Requires you to use a tonne of pseudo-scientific diction, "CB terms," that she mostly came up with herself. Nothing to learn in this class, but you'll write a blog so there is that. Watches Fox News.

One of the most caring professors I've had. Incredibly accommodating and willing to work with you to help you get the best experience possible out of the class. For students who've already taken MKT 300 and Psych 280 (social psych), maybe stay away from this class because there's a lot of overlap. The client project is a super useful experience!

Amy is the most sweet and caring professor. She is very understanding and flexible. She is willing to help you and tries to make the class a pleasurable experience for every single person. I have learned more in this one class than in my whole college life.

She truly cares about her students, as long as you also put in the work. Show up to class and put effort into the assignments and she'll bend over backwards for you, she even let me use her office for a job interview. She gives kind of a lot of work but its manageable and pretty on par with other umich classes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amy is an incredible human - she cares about her students like no other. Class itself is very heavy in outside work for a 3 credit course (case studies, pop quizzes, semester long group project, create a blog). Learned a lot, could've learned the same with less work. must really like the material to do well. unclear, subjective rubrics.

Amy is the most caring professor I've ever had at Michigan. She's incredibly sweet and as long as you do the assignments based on her rubrics you will do well. She always has funny stories to share and she genuinely cares about her students. Make sure you do the readings because her pop quizzes are a little difficult, but only 8% of the final grade

BA200 is such a subjective class. It can be incredibly annoying and frustrating - it is a reality for all teachers and all sections. But Amy by far the best BA200 teacher. She cares about her students and will advocate for them like nobody else. She is so sweet and a pleasure to work with. Definitely worth taking BA 200 with Amy.

super nice, but doesn't always specify requirements and expects you to do assignments a very specific way. Will knock off points for very minute details such as not including a secondary resource for a particular question/comment (even when this was never specified in rubric/assignment requirements). Takes forever to give feedback on assignments

Prof Angell is very friendly, very personable, very easy to get along with! But she doesn't share all information with the class - expects students to ask for information to receive it. Hours of class time is wasted waiting for 1-on-1 team meetings. Material in lecture not directly related to assignments. Vague, poorly written rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I selected Pavlov to be a reference for a job and I got it! She's a great prof.

Dr. Pavlov is one of those professors you can tell really cares about her students. She is extremely down to earth and knows no one wants to be in the class, but she helps make the most of it. If you can, I highly recommend you take TC 496 with her.

We turned in a 2000 word essay a couple of weeks into the semester. I am writing this finals week after the class has ended, and still have no idea what I got on an essay which is a significant portion of my grade. She claimed she had the grades done weeks ago in class and still hasn't entered them. She makes this class harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Like most people in TC300, I only took the class because it's required and I ultimately did not want to do it. Pavlov still managed to make me look forward to going to class because she's incredibly personable and genuinely cares for her students. She gave excellent feedback on assignments and is willing to help outside of class.

Gives out very few assignments, which is nice, but she doesn't grade any of your work until the end of the semester. That means there's no chance to know or fix your grade. She grades really specific while not offering much time out of class. In a 1 CREDIT course, she expects you to write a 2000 word essay due in the middle of finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: All-around great professor.  Very nice to deal with.  Gives good feedback.  Fair and accommodating.  Class structure is very clear.  Attendance does matter.  Just do the work and you'll be fine.  Amount of work required was reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ms. Pavlov is one of those rare instructors who seems to be on the students' side. She makes sure assignments are never tougher than they need to be, though the class inherently has too much work for the credit given. She's a cool, caring, helpful instructor and I'd take every required TC class with her if I could.

Not my favorite. This class was WAY TOO MUCH WORK for a 1 credit class. Pavlov did not grade over half the assignments until after the semester was over. You would think you are doing very well until those assignment grades show up after the final exam period is over. Not hard to get an A range, but really takes a lot of effort to get a solid A.

Dr. Shell is a passionate professor who truly cares about her students. While Michigan math is known to be difficult, Dr. Shell does a great job at explaining the material. She is a tough grader, but she offers lots of extra credit to boost your grade and is a very understanding professor who will support you in whatever you need extra help on!

She was very caring and wanted her students to do well. Lots of homework, and you have to do problems on the board in class but honestly, I just think it helped me more. For this class, the exams are going to be hard no matter what, so I would rather have a professor who helps me more than one who gives less work. I recommend her for sure.
Very understanding, explains thoroughly, great professor

Dr. Shell-Gellasch is a very kind teacher. You can tell she loves her job and what she teaches. I think the class would've been better if there weren't structured timelines not from her. She definitely knows how to teach her subject. We were always up and moving to make sure we were engaged in learning. Extremely accessible outside of class time!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
UM math notoriously bad, but this professor made it worse. The material is super easy, but class time is wasted. Dr. Shell gets sidetracked and confused really easily and makes things more confusing than it ever needs to be. (tip: She doesn't actually look at your team homework drafts) AVOID HER.
-- see her other ratings from Eastern Michigan uni

This is one of the best classes at Ross, and Professor Young is amazing. She's so incredibly caring, down-to-earth, funny, and pushed us all to get meaningfully better at public speaking. She gives so much great feedback, and gives a lot of personalized attention. I highly recommend this class, but definitely wait to take it with Professor Young!

Professor Young is a fantastic professor. I have some complaints about the structure of BCOM350, but that's not her fault. Class is engaging and everyone is encouraged to speak. Go to her office hours for help and individualized guidance on presentations and your written assignments- she's super approachable and understanding. Gives great feedback
Amazing Prof! Would definitely take again. Don't give up if you do a bad job on one of the assignments.
Best professor I've ever had! She really knows what she's talking about, and is kind to new students.

Chelo was an amazing professor. She was very respectful of her students and it was clear she genuinely cared about us as students and as people. She puts lots of time and attention into her lessons and you can tell she really wants us to learn. Chose to have her again for Spanish232. Definitely harder, but she's still a great professor.

Professor Digon is by far one of the best professors I've ever had in undergrad. She made learning Spanish very enjoyable and did her best to ensure we all understood what was expected of us. She was very kind and easily accessible outside of class. Overall, 10/10 experience. I absolutely love her and will be taking my next class with her!

Prof Digon Arroba was by far my favorite professor this semester. She is incredibly kind and understanding, and truly wants all of her students to succeed. The class was 4 times a week with a good amount of homework, but that's pretty standard for the Spanish classes at Michigan. Overall amazing professor, wish I had her next semester!!

Professor Digon is the best teacher of my entire life. If you can, TAKE HER CLASS She is kind respectful understanding & grades fairly. Appreciate that expectations are 100% clear. She lets students know what to study and explains well. 1000/10. Absolutely AMAZING. wonderful professor and wonderful person. Best part of my college experience so far.

The content was always very straightforward and easy to understand, and I think grading was pretty lenient. The class involves a lot of speaking practice which is of course very helpful in developing one's skills. Overall, I genuinely can't think of any criticisms.

IF YOU NEED TO TAKE SPANISH 232, TAKE IT WITH CONSULEO!!!!! I was dreading taking this class, but her Spanish 232 topics class was actually enjoyable and productive. I learned a lot, and she is always willing to help her students. She is a fair grader and truly wants the best for her students.  I could not recommend her more.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chello is one of my favorite professors! She is such a sweet woman, and she genuinely cares about every student. She made our class feel like a community, and I did not dread attending her class four times a week as I did with 231. She really made class fun and a safe and comfortable environment. If you can, definitely take this class with her!!!
So sweet and makes sure her students succeed, spends time working on conversational skills in class and clearly cares so much about her students

Prof. Digon is so sweet! She truly cares about each of her students & is easily accessible outside of class. She takes the time to teach every concept introduced in class and will put in the effort to catch you up if you're behind. Truly one of the kindest & respectable professors in the entire Spanish department- don't hesitate to take her class!
Genuinely my favorite professor ever she was so sweet. I wish she taught Spanish 232

Profe Digon might be one of my favorite teachers ever! She was super kind and genuinely cared that we understood the material. She was so sweet and considerate. I struggled a little bit with the class material, and I always could ask her questions for clarity. She likes to have students speak often, but she is so clear and an excellent teacher.

Prof. Digon (Chelo) was awesome. I really liked her class and I think I found her 231 class easier than Spanish 103. She was always kind and respected all her students. She genuinely seemed interested in helping her students. Would highly recommend taking her.

Professor Digon was one of the best professors I have had so far. She is very caring towards student learning and is good at working through problems with students. She brought fun topics to class as well. Highly recommend.
Professor Digon was amazing. She is so kind and understanding. She takes class very slow, and makes sure everyone comprehends what they are learning before she moves on. Would highly recommend her.

Prof. Digon is such a kind and smart teacher. Like most students I'm just taking this class to get the language requirement done, but she made it enjoyable. She's clear at explaining things, brings engaging activities to class, and it's obvious that she cares about all of her students' success. Be prepared for some cold-calling though.

Prof. Digon is so kind and truly has students' best interests at heart. I did not struggle in the class but I believe she was very accessible to those who did. She always tries to make classes fun and engaging, and will take time outside of class to come up with fun activities for us. Take a class with her if you can!

Chelo is an amazing Spanish professor! I was definitely nervous as this was my first college Spanish class, but she was super kind and effective at teaching different parts of the language/culture. Exams/quizzes were fairly easy and she always provided enough resources to prepare. I'd love to take Spanish with her again!

Professor Digon was by far one of my favorite professors ever. She was so sweet and caring and was always patient. She really cared about your learning. She was funny and I would definitely recommend taking her class.  The exams were not bad and she always made it clear what was going to be on it.
If you have her drop. Her lectures have no structure and she cold calls when you can tell the whole class is confused.

Where to begin. Wanted to understand Pricing, but professor was chaotic and noncommunicative. Didn't post critical information, didn't reply to emails, relied only on TAs for grading. Knows her stuff, but is so over-the-top in her self-regard that it's almost like a satire. Just an awful experience.

I took Aradhna Krishnas Sensory marketing class because it was the only one available in the B-school world. Theress no question of Krishnas intelligence & research abilities. She has a lot of information & experience to share. However, she has an attitude problem & isnt an effective teacher because of her hubris. I didnt learn much from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a great Professor and a wonderful person as well. When I was in difficulty, she helped me. With respect to the class, it has cutting-edge contents. It is unique a think....where else you can find a sensory marketing class?

I started to love marketing with her class! She is incredibly proficient in her field and can answer any question asked. She supports theory with examples from real world to make sure that students really understand the topics. Her class is entertaining and engaging.

20% subjective participation grading plus condescending when she doesn't agree with your answer. You can get As on all the assignments and project and have participation screw you out of an A at the end.
Terrible clarity, Doesn't know much about the subject, Very defensive when answering questions and the worst attitude!!!
Awful human being. Yells at students for leaving class for any reason (i.e. bathroom, sneeze attack..etc.) On good days her attitude towards students is tolerable at best. On bad days...watch out.

Fantastic professor! Extremely intelligent and informed about her industry. Very engaging in class; wants her students to pay attention and will call you out if you're not. There's no reason not to pay attention, though, because she makes class entertaining and fills lectures with fascinating content. Very accommodating to student needs, too.

Mean-spirited and nasty individual. Does not know much about the 'real world' of marketing. In fact, she gets very defensive if you know more 'real-world' marketing than her. I learned nothing new in her class. She is so full of herself!!!
He was the best man at my wedding.
he's mcgoated and mcamazing and I'm so mcexcited to mctake his mcclass mcagain.

Raj is, in my opinion, a truly great teacher. He is knowledgeable and passionate about development econ, and that tends to rub off on you, I think. I never go to office hours (in general, not just for him), but he seemed approachable, and would always jump at the chance to  answer questions that I had after and before class. Great guy, mad respect.
Do the readings otherwise you will have no idea what is going on during lecturediscussion. Exams seem to be easy, but grading is tough and you need to be very specific in your answers.

Definitely my favorite Econ class. Always looked forward to the lectures; the subject matter was really interesting, but it was Raj's passion that made these lectures so great.  Unfortunately, the GSI my semester (D. Morar) was a very poor and unclear grader. A lot of people received grades they didn't deserve (both high and low).

I'm so torn on this class. On the one hand, Raj is a phenomenal prof who inspired a great deal of interest, and always gave subtly-insightful lectures. On the other hand, this was the toughest class I've taken. Prepare for lots of challenging reading and 6 really long problem setsessays. Ultimately maybe worth it.

Raj is clearly passionate about what he does and tries to spread that passion to others. He expects you to draw upon readings heavily in class and for quizzes and exams. We had "pop" quizzes that were usually announced about a week in advance. More qualitative instead of quantitative overall.

Raj is a good teacher, he advertises the class as one of the hardest offered at UM, but I haven't found it to be any more difficult than 401 or 402. The discussion section is absolutely useless which is a shame. The only thing that bothers me is Raj talks SO quietly and often trails off, and in a big lecture it makes it impossible to hear him.
Raj is a great prof.  Very interesting to listen to.  The readings make you think.  He is very interested in talking to the students. Best Econ prof I've had at UofM

He is one of those few economics professors at this university who actually aspires to inspire his students, goes out of his way to encourage students to discuss the concepts with him in office hours. The class was great, and made me understand the basic economics models a lot better. Highly recommend.

She is very knowledgeable on the topic, and comes from a good place when teaching. She is super kind and understanding. Lectures are long and slides are wordy. Class format and assignments were simple and understandable, however the exam questions were worded weird that multiple students did not understand.

Overall this class was fine but the professor was often late to class (like… every day) by 5-10 minutes and seemed kinda unprepared sometimes. There were also a few questions on the first exam that were worded weirdly that no one was getting right but they were not removed from the grade when they should have been, in my opinion.

I had Prof. Hassell for Comm 307 (political comm) and loved her and this class. She is so passionate about the subject matter and totally changed how I engage with news/social media. The assignments were fun and easy while still engaging course materials. Would recommend to anyone, Comm major or not.

Ariel is a great professor, super knowledgable and makes the content clear and easy to understand. I took my capstone and two other classes with her and would definitely take another. She's super accessible and willing to meet with you if you have issues.

She's really knowledgeable about everything she teaches, and makes grading really clear. She's open to feedback and will spend time going over things students ask about in class and will do extra review or talk about other topics if the class wants it. She doesn't post her slides so attendance is basically mandatory but her lectures aren't boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ariel is upfront about what she expects and does not give a super heavy course load. She seems really nervous when teaching and stumbles over her words.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was really helpful at providing interesting information in consumable ways. She also just generally cares and does a lot of engaging group work. I usually hate speaking with groups but she made the topics so interesting that I liked her a lot. Would recommend her for every class she offers. Relatively easy course too, but the information you re
Loved Ariel and this class. Inspired me to go the more political comm route. Will be taking my capstone with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Hassel is a great professor. She makes class interesting and picks readings that are actually relevant to discussion. The class setup is great and makes it easy to get an A if you try. It's just 2 midterm papers with a final presentation & paper. She is a fair teacher and I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Ariel is great! Knowledgeable, respected and makes class enjoyable. Readings were lengthy but topical and interesting, and the grading structure was clearly defined from the beginning. A solid choice for the senior capstone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Ariel is great! Her lectures are clear and interesting, and she grades fairly. Two take-home midterm essays and a final paper, but no exams! Readings are fair and not totally necessary for class if you happen to miss a few.

Very passionate about Greek, however class struggles from sociofugal design and somewhat unorganized Canvas page. I have showed up for a meeting a couple times to find that she was not there and did not receive any explanation via Email, Canvas, etc. Quizzes are hard so be sure to study. Very very sweet woman though and definitely very educated.

I really enjoyed this course for its content, and Prof. Leontis for her personality. However, I have major concerns for this course. First, it has a huge lack of structure and communication. Second, this course doesn't publish final grades, only individual. Lastly, the pacing is incredibly inconsistent which really killed my motivation to succeed.

Professor Leontis is one of the best professors I've had at UMICH. She's super caring and really wants you to get the most out of the class. She also allows you to apply things in Greek Culture to your own so it's a super informative class. She will always expect you to do the readings but generally she is so understanding.
She really cares about teaching you Greek and want to see each student succeed. One of the best classes I've taken in undergrad.

Very manageable class. You're graded by 4 papers (the last one is a blog so it's shorter), a quiz and in-class blue book, and attendance. For almost every paper, you get extra time to submit past the official Canvas due date, so it's pretty easy to get them done. If you're looking for an ULWR or academic breadth, this is a great class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Intimidating at first, Professor Leontis is an excellent professor who really cares about her students. She really helped me improve my writing. Go to office hours!! If you take CLCIV 121, expect a lot of reading and attendance in class is mandatory. Overall, I would definitely recommend to take one of her classes- you'll learn a lot!

Very hard class but fantastic. She turned me into a great writer and taught me to love The Odyssey and I have a greater appreciation for literature now. READ READ READ. Always go to class. MAKE SURE TO START YOUR JOURNAL ON THE FIRST DAY.

YOU HAVE TO GO TO CLASS! THERE ARE PARTICIPATION POINTS. On top of participation points a lot of the in class discussion is very useful when it comes to the essays you will have to write. She is also a tough grader when it comes to essays but she is happy to help you with anything you need to succeed in her class.

Good professor (knows her stuff), gives good feedback, but assigns A TON OF READING, and often gives extra assignments last minute. Attendance is mandatory - enough skips and your grade drops a letter grade. You will have to do a lot of work for the class.
She was a very difficult grader who often got mad at the class for not doing well. Liked to blame the students.

Professor Leontis is an extremely good professor.  She assigns many interesting readings and expects you to be prepared for every class.  Leontis is a tough grader but she really cares about her students and is willing to provide help when needed.

Professor Leontis is extremely knowledgeable about the subject, and presents it in an interesting fashion. Although, she sometimes has "bad" days in which she will call on people (who don't raise their hands)to answer extremely complex questions. Writing assignments are pretty simple (easy A), which surprising since it is a ULWR.

No experience with her other classes but this one was the single most useless class I've ever come across. Participation grades suck when the class is boring and useless enough that you shut your mouth in order to stop from saying something insincere. Strongly advise steering clear
Great teacher. Class is interesting but be prepared for her to call on you randomly.  A decent amount of reading.

I cannot stress enough how brilliant Professor Leontis is and how much she cares about her students.  She can be tough, her class was endlessly interesting and she uses the course materials in integral ways that really help develop understanding of the subject matter.  Also, she really prepares you for writing assignments and exams.

Professor Leontis is amazing.  By far the best lecturer I have had.  She does assign a lot of readings, but usually they are too bad.  Come prepared because she will call on you, but this really helped the class to be more fun.

Prof. Leontis is very knowledgeable about everything she teaches. She does assign a TON of reading, but they are all important to the lessons she teaches. The way she teaches class can be confusing if you aren't prepared for class. Always expects student participation. Doing the work is important to understanding her lectures -always willing tohelp

this class goes throughs some really interesting information but the way in which Artemis delivers it kills any enjoyement. If you plan on taking this class, take it with a couple of friends, your going to need someone to complain to about the enormous amounts of reading allotted each class period.

This is my second class w/ Artemis (and I plan on taking another next semester). Although she is very intimidating at first, she is one of few professors who genuinely cares about the progress of her students. Yes, you actually have to do the work to do well, but she does everything she can to help.

While she is demanding when determining grades, Professor Leontis gives a very good lecture and is genuinely interested in students learning and enjoying the material.  If you put in the effort, you will extremely enjoy her class.

Nice Woman. This class is small and fun. She is very patient and is willing to help you learn basic greek conversation. The class is only credit/no credit but it is a lot of fun and really easy. Take it!
artemis really knows her stuff and i found her lectures very interesting.  she is very helpful and clear in class and is always willing to help.

Artemis knows her stuff! Her lectures are boring, but often times she shows clips from movies, which makes the class more exciting. She is rather intimidating and will call on you unexpectedly, but she offers a lot of help if you need it. She also prepares you well for exams by giving out the terms and questions to know. P.S Her readings are boring
His methods and logic was confusing, and didn't knew excel skills would get you picked for his GSI. His GSI and decision making is to be questioned

This course was a lot of work, but Art made it interesting and really tried to make sure each student understood what was going on. He was pretty flexible with office hours so that you could ask any questions you had. The one thing is this class was a semester long group project and was a heavy workload.

His personality is wonderful, but the teaching does not meet student expectations. The grading criteria change every week, grading is subjective, and the class content does not relate to homework and quizzes. Be wary of taking his class.

Extremely vague instructions for homework and took off points from a new made up rubric. Lectures are mostly off topic about his experience in the auto industry. Hours of work for using an extremely outdated simulation and homeworks consist of hours/days of tedious data collection which drained me from actually applying anything I learned.

ISD 522. Avoid at all costs. Spent 30 hours a week working on this class. No Rubrics so assignments are vague and confusing, like trying to hit a moving target. Gives feedback on an assignment then grades the assignment under a completely different set of rules. Assumes everyone works in the car industry. Rate my Professor asks for Pros: NONE.

Rudest professor ever who automatically assume the worst of you. Had to be most useless course I have taken at UofM with very outdated material, pointless assignments and boring lectures. You learned nothing about real life design. Over ideal "LEAN" approach. Crazy amount of videos to watch with repeated contents and no useful feedback.

WORST FACULTY MEMBER! THE MOST DISRESPECTFUL, DISCOURTEOUS, RUDE AND MANIPULATIVE PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! I have already reported him for language abuse in emails and outside class. Despite having SEVERE medical handicap this Professor tried to purposefully drag my case and harassed me via email despite me delivering all project work. HORRIBLE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Instruction is confusing, often go over time during the lecture. Give useless feedback in the assignments

He wasted so much time talking about how he used to be the president of the Mustang fan club. He was constantly showing up late to office hours and gave vague feedback. He said no prior part design experience was needed before taking the class but then expected you to be an expert on a part that he assigned you. His assignments had major errors.

Lessons are not needed to pass the class but are suggested. The class is not very hard, but you have to interact a lot with the Professor to understand perfectly what he asks you. He really likes giving really life examples and is very specific when asked a question. However, the class content could be boring for some.

Professor Mandair ran an incredibly unorganized class. The expectations and grading were very unclear throughout the semester, leaving many students confused about their grades. He would rarely lecture, instead opting to let us discuss content in class. While I understand his goals, it left many still confused about the content after the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So comparable with the rest of the professors at U of M. Very unorganized and always changes his words
Lectures never align with the syllabus. All his lectures and words are out of context. Not sure what he is trying to convey through his lectures.

Dr. Mandair was honestly really cool. Most of the complaints are more directed at the GSI, but he's clearly very passionate and dedicated. It's not a difficult class to do well in. Just show up and put in some effort and you'll be fine. Fair amount of reading but his lectures are fun and his lecturing style is super engaging. Would def take again.

About 20 pages of reading and a 300-400 word discussion post weekly. Grades came weeks after the final assignment with no feedback, making improvement tough. My first assignment got my highest score, and without feedback, I couldn't improve. Not the worst class, but there are probably better options. No final, the final is a podcast.

This was the worst ULWR class I have ever taken. Not only was the course material all over the place, but the grading system was absolutely abysmal. The was never a clear rubric given to us about grading, and the GSI for the course did not grade any of our assignments until the last week before finals.

Dr. Mandair is one of the best professors at UM. No matter what discipline you are going into, his classes make you think in ways that will leave you a more reflective thinker. His classes have left me amazed by how much other classes in the same realms missed or left out. He truly cares about his students, their stories, and their perspectives!

majority took this course to fulfill the ULWR, however it is not an easy A (95% cutoff!). Furthermore, no feedback is given on points lost during weekly discussions. Provided syllabus was incorrect in terms of grading policy and assignments, quizzes/overall course structure. The GSI and professor were not on the same page. lots of jargon
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Extremely unorganized. GSI and professor were not on the same page. Syllabus was not followed. Feedback was shallow and rarely given. There was no structure or order to the topics covered.

Loved coming to Arvind's lectures! It is an ULWR class, so you can expect to read and write a fair amount every week, but I was eager to come to lecture every day! There is a group project at the end of the semester which I personally didn't love, but it also wasn't unfairly difficult or anything. Very interesting man, loves engaging with students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: professor mandair was super accomodating. I got covid during this class and he moved the last couple weeks of class online without missing a beat. I was in quarantine still able to attend class through zoom and not miss any assignments. A lot of reading and homework but not that bad. If you put in the effort, you'll do well in this class

Probably my favorite class of the semester. Definitely a bit of work, but nothing anyone can't handle. The lectures were interesting and engaging and he delivers well. Class material is never boring. As long as you pay attention and read the powerpoints, you'll get a good grade.

Prof Mandair is a great lecturer and went with the syllabus. As long as you stay up to date you will do great. Last 2 weeks we went online and our class zoom meetings were actually more enjoyable. the people who didn't like the class were people who were just lazy. Overall, would 100% recommend.

The BEST professor at UofM. His passion for his subject matter is inspirational and motivating. Gives amazing lectures and is truly the most understanding professor. Unlike other philosophy professors, he tries to understand your way of thinking and challenges it, rather than forces you to think just like him. His classroom is a safe space for all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very disorganized. No clear course objectives. All over the place with course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Mandair leads inspirational lectures and discussion with heavy personal insights! His background and experience lends to his research and courses. He respects every student and creates a great class environment. Very understanding of student difficulties. Participate, do readings, and a great grade guaranteed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mandair is extremely passionate about what he teaches and wants to inspire that same level of passion in his students. He brilliantly conveys Asian religions as philosophy and tries to show you the value of a global humanities education. The class is easy and does not require anything but a willingness to grasp complex philosophy.

Professor Mandair is a clear example of a professor who is invested and engaged in his field. His genuine interest in what hes teaching both inspiring and really helpful for the learning process. Hes pretty easily accessible, and you will gain leagues more out of the course if you ask questions during class. The accent helps!
he is amazing and inspirational

Professor Mandair is an excellent teacher, although he will not spoon feed his students. In order to do well in this class, you have to be prepared to read and write quite a lot. In addition, it will not be on easily comprehensible topics. The corollary is that you learn loads. Would recommend.

Professor Mandair is brilliant.  His coursework is challenging to understand but really helpful.  It's not a blow-off class, but really rewarding in the end.  He's really understanding when it comes to grading and one of the best professors I've had here.

The course material and readings are fascinating for "Religion and Violence in a Secular World" but he requires everyone to make a documentary in a group of 3-5 people. We did not get to choose our groups and he does not understand the amount of work editing and composing a doc can be. The syllabus was useless. No dates. Hard "quizzes"/exams.
Amazing professor. I learned so much in this class about Sikhism. He also has an awesome British accent! Very easy course, not too much homework.
His lectures are interesting.  However, if you don't have any background in Hinduism and Buddhism, the amount of information is overwhelming.  Not just an easy A.
Really recommend this class for anyone interested about sikhism.He grades fair on the essays and knows an enormous amount on the subject. Also has a cool british accent

Professor Mandair is a great professor.  He doesn't follow the course guide very well, but I found the class really easy as long as you study for exams.  Exams are exactly what the study guides lay out. Highly recommended class for Race and Ethnicity credit.

Make the most out of this class--he has more to say if students participate. Some readings are SO confusing, but don't procrastinate and you'll be fine. Grades easy on the essays, just write anything you're thinking, he likes that. Notes are very clear. Don't take the class if you're not interested in the subject--you'll just become frustrated.

Professor Mandair is very friendly and really gets you thinking. At first it may seem frustrating- he is very philosophical, so it takes time for his reasoning to make sense. I know this class has made me look at problems more carefully and critically- a great class, and a great professor.
Professor Mandair will make you think outside of the box.  Engaging class only 3 essays and 1 final.  Read everything, pay attention, and pay attention!

The class was very intriguing which led to many interesting class discussions. He assigns readings now and then from the book as well as posting some on ctools. There is only one exam, and 3 papers. He is helpful and the workload isn't heavy. Pay attention during class and you'll be fine.

Before going to this class, realize that whatever it is listed under it is Philosophical in basis. Everything will somehow have to do with philosophy. If you're good at it, then you will love this class. This professor has written the most organized and well thought notes (and it's readable!). Try and have an open mind! :)
He changed the course syllabus from a Religion Violence Media Course to one that emphasized SO MUCH on philosophy. Totally changed the course syllabus.

Dr. Arnall is a wonderful professor who will work with you to help you achieve your goals. While this class may not be the most traditional Spanish class, he's understanding that many who take this course are not Philosophy/Comp Lit majors and work with you to grow those skills.

Prof was passionate about the topic- and it showed. Attendance was Zoom/In Person, and I loved and took advantage of the flexibility. Felt like prof really appreciated class participation, and would let students lead the way with class which I appreciate in an upper-level course. Content wasn't easy per-se, but prof really helped guide and clarify.

I took spanish 488 with gavin and i thought it was a great class. It had 2 discussion posts per week and two 5 page papers for all of the grades in the class, and attendance isnt mandatory. Gavin is very nice and respects students and their time and I would totally recommend taking his class as it is very light work wise.

Gavin is both knowledgeable and chill, a rare but good combination. He's young so it doesn't feel like you're getting talked down to by someone stuck in their ways. Your grade revolves mostly around two 10-page papers that require close reading of class texts, which are usually pretty out-of-the-box and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Gavin's really chill. He's a liiitle pretentious (Princeton grad, speaks like 4 languages including quechua) but it's very subtle, nothing to worry about. Very relatable because I think he's in or just out of grad school; empathetic to students' situations (extends deadlines past Spring Break if requested, easier assignments at end of semester)

Professor Bucsek is so good at relating concepts to intuition. Every lecture she breaks down a lot more of the complicated concepts and makes them much easier to understand. She's also extremely respectful and caring and so easy to talk to.

By far best professor for 211. She skips unnecessary explanations and gives more useful derivations and equations compared to other professors. Expectations are very clear and exams match topics discussed in class. If you study well for the exams and go to office hours for homework then you'll do great in the class.

Professor Bucseck is amazing! Super caring and understanding. She provides great handwritten notes for each lecture and writes reasonable exam questions. She also occasionally makes funny comments, making going to class enjoyable.
She definitely made it onto the Mount Rushmore of Michigan Professors. She has earned a GOAT status. ASHLEY GOATSECK

Cares about students and is willing to accommodate when needed. Cuts bs problems out and tests general concepts on exams with simple straightforward problems. Extends deadlines to concur with class lectures. Absolute goat professor.
Ashley is one of the most caring professors on campus. I have never felt so cared about by a professor until her. Take the theater and incarceration class; she is 100% the right person to teach it.
Incredibly intelligent and dedicated professor. She has a wealth of knowledge about prison reform; in addition to that, she is an amazing person. Highly recommend for any field of study.

I took the Atonement Project in the Residential College my first semester of my first year, and it was the best decision I made. Ashley is one of the most wonderful people I've ever met. Next to being an insanely awesome teacher, she's also an incredibly talented actress. (See her one woman show if you get the chance.)

It will be by far the most difficult BBA class to date. She did a good job of cracking jokes to lighten the mood; however, it is such a long and boring lecture and its so easy to only start caring about the midterm and final right before. Midterm and final are your entire grades and depending on your section the average could be below a 70 or 85+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Not a tough class neccesairly, just something that catches BBAs off guard.

Best gameplan for this class:
1. slides before class for 30 mins (use AI to help you get general feeling for content)
2. pay attention in class (try and participate at least once but otherwise just listen)
3. try and rewatch lectures after class
4. do hw (actually do it!)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very challenging, and I often felt unsupported when asking questions. Responses were harsh and focused on the curve, which made it difficult to seek help and left me more confused rather than clarified.

Very monotone. Never started class with "hello how are you?" and didn't look to make a personal connection. She wasn't very sympathetic when answering questions. Overall, the class was kind of interesting, and she was very obviously smart. The long classes were pretty miserable and I never once looked forward to class,
Professor Astashkina was great in my opinion. Class is fast-paced at times, but if you pay attention, you should be fine.

TO301 is going to be a difficult class regardless of who you have as your professor. I felt that Prof. Astashkina explained material clearly but since the class is fast-paced, I had to rewatch lectures and go over my notes for things I missed. As long as you put effort into this class, you will be fine.

Astashkina was a great professor and really cared about her students. The class has A LOT of content and materials to help you learn. If you put in the time to practice and understand the material you will do well. If you are struggling she is very willing to meet with you outside of class to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Astashkina is very good at explaining class material and makes it clear she cares about her students.

Kate is hands down the best professor I've ever had. She is the most caring, dedicated, and articulate professor at UM. Her lectures are clear and she works so hard out of the classroom to make sure you understand the material (study guides, review sessions, office hours, email). I could go on and on, but Kate makes a hard class feel easier.

Asenka Asenova made her lectures/content accessible and clear in class and on canvas. The biggest challenge of the class was the grading scale (2 exams make up 75% of your grade). Although Asenova was a strict grader, she always made her expectations clear. If I had to take 251 again it would be with her.
The tests and content were hard but the lectures were very good considering the subject matter

Asja is a great professor, and she does a fantastic job of teaching difficult statistical concepts. Her exams are quite tough, but she curves them. All of the homework is challenging, but it prepares you well for the exams.

Honestly, she puts in more effort than other econ professors but grades incredibly hard. The proofs are abhorrent. She gives you the impression she cares about you as a student and then completely soul crushes your dreams. The grading scale of the class is atrocious.

Do yourself a favor and don't take econometrics with anyone else. She is the best- very accessible outside of class, and her lectures are structured in an interesting and cohesive way. Go to office hours!
Amazing. Top professor. Clear criteria, digestible lectures. Nothing to complain about.

I love Asenova!!!! Throughout this course I was just amazed at how she can make something like advanced econometrics so intuitive and digestible. I was able to do well in this course with watching the lectures and minimal studying because the lectures are just that good. The bad 251 raters are just stupid. Sorry.

Professor Asenova was the best professor I met during my four years of college. Her lectures are so well structured, coherent, and clear that I was never confused in this course. She was so nice during office hours and she posted videos explaining concepts that were frequently asked by the students. She genuinely cares about students and it shows.

If you plan to take the course and focus on the course only, take it. Asenka is a great lecturer. But don't have any further interaction, she is mean. Either refuse to offer any help or make beautiful promises, then break them to destroy your hope.

Asja is very clear about grading and tests and explains material well. Assigns long homework problem sets, but they're very useful and similar to the tests and quizzes. I felt a genuine understanding of basic econometrics after taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Asenova is the best professor I have experienced in the Econ department and one of the best at the university. Her lectures are easily digestible and she genuinely cares about her students learning. Her practice exams and quizzes reflect actual exams and quizzes. If you pay attention in class, you will pass without much trouble

Best economics professor I have had. She is sweet, engaging, and helpful in class. She is amazing at explaining concepts and cares about teaching her students well. She prepares you for exams very well, and practice tests are almost exactly what is on the exam. I would 100% recommend her!
Good professor, made everything understandable. Her homeworks were pretty long, but they were helpful so I'm not mad about that. I'd take her again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher, good lecturer. But exams were way, way harder than expected, especially because the practice sample exams were much easier. Exams were 14 pages long. Homeworks are not too bad though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures are easy to understand, though she covers a lot in each lecture. You may be scared by her if you read the syllabus, but she is super nice. I experienced some personal hardship this semester and she was extremely thoughtful! I wouldnt make this semester if it wasnt because of her help.
Asenka is really organized and truly cares for her students. Just email her if you have any questions and she will try her best to answer you and make sure you understand the material well

The logic behind a professor who bases the midterm off of homework assignments and quizzes BUT THEN when classes convert to online (due to covid-19) makes our final exam 18 pages long and nothing like the homework and quizzes makes zero sense to me. Boring lectures, terrible teacher.

Up until the covid-19, things were not bad at all. Post covid-19, things became harder. The final we took almost had nothing to do with what we learned in class. Took 3 hrs to finish and didn't know half the stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The final is nothing like the class and worth half your grade. Up until the final, the course is incredibly easy; lectures are very slow, and homeworks essentially just go over what we did in lecture. Then the difficulty spikes on the final, where you'll see topics that were never covered in the course.

Asja is nice and explains material carefully. Unfortunately, this is a very boring class (material doesn't help). I've also never seen a professor make so many typos on emails, homeworks, quizzes, and even exams. The typos aren't just annoying, they're extremely distracting.
really liked her. Definitely recommend.

Asja is good, and if you pay attention in lectures, you'll do just fine. That said, as a teacher in the broad sense, she can be frustrating. Even the most innocent of insightful questions are shot down out of hand in her class, so there's little motivation to think beyond the scope of her lectures.

Good teacher. Very clear on expectations for overall class. Have to take advantage of all the resources she offers. Covers a lot of material so staying on top of discussions, homeworks, and practice problems will prepare you well for exams as she doesnt throw you many curveballs.
Good professor. Pretty easy exams!

Went to her office hours to get a test explained and she said I was wasting her time. Wow, I cant believe I pay out of state tuition for a Michigan degree with lecturers like her (and shes not the only one).

Probably the most boring lecturer I've ever had. Although the course material didn't help either, her monotonous droning was unbearable. That being said, attendance is voluntary other than for quizzes and exams. She also uses the same quizzes and exams year after year, so buy a CourseHero subscription and you'll be good to go.
Asja makes Econ 251 the easiest Econ class at Michigan. Very helpful and tells you everything you need to know to succeed in the class.

Asja is an amazing professor. Textbook is not required as she gives really detailed lecture notes and practice tests were really helpful for the quizzes. Aside from that, it is clear that she cares a lot about her students. Definitely take 251 with her!
Asenova is a terrible lecturer. Avoid this class with her if you can. She does give very good notes though, which I was able to use to study for the exams.

She's a very good professor as she explains things very clearly, but this also leads to very boring lectures. The exams are easy but the homework assignments are long. She's pretty well organized - except she doesn't post her handwritten lecture notes on canvas, she only posts microsoft word versions of the notes that she makes for herself.

A very dry and boring class, but I suppose the material is important if you are considering economics research. The exams were not that difficult and homework and practice exams prepared you well, though the homework sets were pretty long. Do not get the textbook - her typed and handwritten lecture notes provide all the necessary information.

I have never seen a professor make this many mistakes on practice exams and homeworks in my life. Her formatting makes 0 sense (goes from part 1 to part c to part 4 then back to part b) and her answers are often incorrect.
Mediocre professor. Her class is extremely boring and honestly nobody is paying attention. Exams are basically the same as the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at Umich. Provides detailed class notes and explanation. The class is not fast-paced and she is willing to answer questions after class with patience. Good for beginners in stats and econometrics. Besides, as a foreigner, I like her voice which is very clear for me.
Lectures are *really* boring. Textbook is definitely not necessary. Asja does right up amazing lecture notes so you probably don't have to go to lecture either.

While the subject may not be the most interesting, it is clear that Asja puts in a ton of work for her students, providing typed and handwritten lecture notes, practice problems, lots of office hours, and summary sheets of concepts. She seems nice too. Don't get the textbook for this class. It isn't necessary and her notes are better anyways.

She's a very effective and prepared lecturer, unlike some of the veteran Profs in the Econ department. Her lectures are very prepared and thought out. She makes sure to effectively explain the material in the easiest way possible. Overall, great professor. Take 251 with her.

Asja really is the best, I've never talked to anybody who's had her and didn't like her. She puts an INCREDIBLE amount of work into her lecture notes, section materials, and homework solutions. She cares so much about her students that, if you have a request, she will always try to fulfill it. I just love her so much (so I guess I'm biased).

She is the best instructor I have ever had in my two years at Umich. Textbook is not needed cause she provided detailed notes. Hw is kinda heavy but every hw will help you a lot in quizzes and exams, be sure to do them and review them! She explains the concepts very clear and she is a nice person. Quick email replier and accessible outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer. She puts in the additional effort trying to convey the syllabus across to the class. Her classes might be dry but she ensures that she's reachable outside of class too. However, although discussions were optional, GSI was not up to standard and really rude. But Asja always ensured that she was reachable outside office hours too.

She's great, and I think having her for 451 would be better (I'm not a math person though). There are only a few complaints I have. One is that both of her textbooks are listed as "optional" on the syllabus: you absolutely do not need them. She also has some difficulty getting control of the class, but that's because the students are discourteous.
Amazing lecturer. Take 251 with her if you can. Clear on what she expects from students, and if pay just enough attention to her lectures, you're sure to have an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is not hard to do well in as long as you're a math person (60% of people get A- and above). While there is a lot of homework, it is relevant for exams. Her final reviews are helpful, too. You definitely don't need to go to class to do well, but I recommend it unless you're good at figuring things out through posted notes and lectures.

She is one of the few professors in the econ department who actually explains the concept really clearly. She doesn't assume students to know everything. Her lectures are crystal clear and exams are just more lengthy homework on time limit. Try to go to review class before the exam since she gives hints and explains common mistakes students make.

Great professor. She's great at explaining it clearly and making her expectations clear. She'll stop the whole class and go over material if a student doesn't understand it. Her classes are extremely helpful to go to and her exams reflect what she teaches. would recommend.

Super Easy A.  Just study the practice exam solutions and lecture notes and you'll be fine.  No one really goes to lecture and she doesn't seem to care either.  Can be an annoying grader (nit picky) but not enough to detract you from an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very easy class because she bases the homework directly off of her slides and the discussion section handouts. The same applies with the quizzes and the tests. Definitely recommend her. Easy A if  you just study the homework solutions and look at practice exam solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice professor and lecture is entertaining

This class was surprisingly easy, mostly because Asja posts extremely clear notes online after lectures and bases the homework off of them directly. She gives practice exams before the midterm and final that are basically exactly what you'll see on the real exam. I never went to discussion and had no trouble understanding concepts. Very easy class.

Great professor and great lectures. Everything is very organized. I liked rewatching lecture recordings. Homework takes a long time, but office hours are helpful. Exam difficulty was fair, and the grades are curved. Prof. Cohen has a good sense of humor and gives intuitive examples. Great addition to the math department.

He always provides intuition for what we're learning and avoids overcomplicating the topics. Everything is recorded, so you can always go back to rewatch lectures. There are no surprises on the exams (though there might be a couple difficult parts), and he grades fairly. Definitely one of my favorite math classes.
Overall a good class, and the GSIs are very helpful.. The curve is definitely not the same as shown in Atlas(median A-). The median is probably around B/B+
Great lecturer, lectures are all recorded, and gives great intuition for virtually all topics
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The materials being discussed in math 474 are really helpful in the sense that they give a rather comprehensive framework of mathematical finance beyond the more "toy" model we've seen in math 423. Asaf is a great lecturer. He pays lots of attention to intuition and clarifies many things in the textbook.

Very clear lectures and homework solutions. Exams are similar to practice exams and homework. Extremely dedicated to students (his two gsi's were told to hold extra weekly tutoring sessions to do practice problems). The best part is that u don't need to take the class synchronously. I only watched the recorded lectures.

Lecture notes are constructed from scratch and straightforward to read. Both lecture notes and HWs are super helpful for exams. Skiped all classes and learned all the things from lecture notes over the final week and got an A+. Frankly speaking, Math 423 is one of the easiest math courses at UofM, and Asaf is definitely the best among all sections.
Only read PowerPoint, kind of boring. Curve was not nice.
He is as genius as Kolmogorov, and his handwriting is so clear.

Professor Ashforth is a phenomenal professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable and wise, and has great insights into Africa, as well as its context in global health. If you don't like to do your work, participate, actually think and use your brain, and write - then don't take this class. For everyone else, this is an exceptional seminar class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Adam did not make the classroom feel like a comfortable place, but attendance was mandatory. Also only grade was 15 page paper that we had very little instruction on. Do not recommend him at all, worst class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ashforth was a funny man who always made the class an interactive place. Beware, attendance is mandatory and mostly lecture-based, not discussion. 20-page paper is not too difficult if you seek help from him, but guidelines are somewhat unclear. Pay attention, be respectful, and follow the guidelines, and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 50% of your grade is a 20-page research paper graded based on "best effort, however "best effort" isn't defined. The expectations were unclear and there were minimal discussions surrounding the paper. He claims he's gonna teach you how to write a research paper, but he doesn't. This isn't a discussion-based class, he lectures the entire time.

20-page paper to complete for our entire grade. Gave minimal guidelines and most of us in the class were very confused about expectations and how the paper would be graded. Most of us were waiting for some type of instruction, so the majority had to work over Thanksgiving to get some done. Hardly discussion based, mostly him talking.

Dude is an absolute authority in his field, and hilarious in class. The whole "one paper per semester" thing is perfectly reasonable if you know what you're signing up for--you spend the entire class preparing for it, and he tells you it's the case right from the get-go. Definitely a tough grader, but by no means unreasonable.  Highly recommend.

Finished today my last lecture in Professor Ashforth's AAS 326 class and he is an amazing man. Funny, witty, intelligent, sarcastic, and just an extremely down to earth guy. The class was small and discussion based on different topics that we were able to choose from. 1 research paper and 2-3 small in class assignments was the workload! Great guy!
Assigned one long paper due at the end and didn't teach the class anything. He is not a good teacher and has unreasonable expectations on his students. Do not take this class.

After my first encounter with him I no long plan on it. I was unable to make it to class because my roommate had  our shared car and my phone was smashed so i couldn't uber. He was extremely uppity about it saying "if you're going to miss a class tell me before hand"... I sent him the email when it became evident I would not be able to make it...

Dr. Ashforth is probably the most down to earth prof you'll meet. I have never had him in class, however, therefore he probably is a little nicer to me. You can tell he is super intelligent, knows his field really well, and wants his students to learn. He gives great life advice too. Truly amazing guy.

I took his South Africa FYS last year and loved it! It's highly discussion based with very little reading. He's a great prof. The research paper is no big deal if you start it early enough, and it's really the only work all semester for that class. Highly recommend.

Super interesting class. Dr. Gearhardt is my favorite professor I've ever had at UM! Very caring and fun. She makes the topics even more interesting and goes out of her way to help students outside of class and make sure we understand. Holds review sessions before exams and is very open for office hours. Papers take time, read the books early.

Dr. Gearhardt is the best professors I have had so far and is the best lecturer. She is so engaging, kind, and knowledgeable. She is the reason I showed up to the lectures. The tests weren't too bad, there were pre lecture quizzes before each lecture that were 15 questions each based on the textbook. 3 chances per question. SHES THE BEST

Dr. Gearhardt is the BEST professor I've had at Umich, hands-down. She is so caring about her students, willing to answer any questions you have, very accessible and friendly, and her exams are very straightforward and easy. As long as you take notes in lecture and skim the book (she does make questions from the book), you'll do fine!

Great lectures. Dr. Gearhardt is very interesting to listen to. She clearly outlined exactly what she expected of her students. Dr. Gearhardt cared if you learned the material, not just memorized it. I really enjoyed her Psych 270 & would take more classes with her. Dr. Gearhardt is very knowledgeable & gave insight/examples using her own research.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gearhardt is a wonderful lecturer, researcher, and person. I have had the pleasure of working with her both in PSYCH270 as well as PSYCH404 (independent internship) and she pours her *very knowledgable* heart and soul into her work. She knows everything there is to know about intro psychopathology and is incredibly accessible outside of class!!

Psych 270 with Gearhardt was great. She is an amazing lecturer overall. She's incredibly funny and very knowledgable in the subject area. The class is difficult and there are iClicker questions every class, so it is important that you show up to every lecture. I would highly recommend her as a teacher to anyone.

Dr. Gearhardt is such a good professor and makes people actually want to come to lecture. She has a ton of knowledge and is also really passionate about the subject matter. There is a lot of material to memorize, especially all the disorders and symptoms, but if you read the textbook and watch lectures the exams aren't too bad.

This was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Umich. I think that her teaching style definitely had something to do with it. She's very enthusiastic and passionate about mental health. She incorporated relevant videos to keep the class engaged. The exams aren't very difficult; the questions are very straight forward.

Dr. Gearhardt is the best professor I have had at this university. She cares that her students do well. Her exams are 65 mc and 4 short answer. Memorizing all the symptoms helps because that's mostly what the short answer consists of. VERY interesting material, would definitely recommend this class!
Great professor. Really wants students to do well. A group of us found out she also really likes cheese, and she gives extra credit to students who share thoughts about cheese in class.

I had Dr. Gearhardt for a seminar class specifically about addictive behaviors. Easily one of the best classes I've taken at umich so far! She's really engaging and interesting; most of the grade was participation & she's a really easy grader. We had to read a lot of scientific articles, but you can just skim them so it's not bad. Not much homework

Extremely interesting subject matter. Ashley is a good lecturer and each GSI leads one lecture per semester in their specialty. We read two novels that required us write case studies. Show up to section. Memorization of symptoms is a necessary skill.

Dr. Gearhardt was hands-down one of the best professors I've ever had! She is there for her students and GSIs and makes things as doable as possible for everyone. Great and interesting lectures, and made the material relatable to everyone. Would definitely, 100%, take a class with her again!

Professor Gearhardt was super enthusiastic and knowledgeable on the topic of abnormal psych! There are iClicker questions in lecture so attendance is mandatory. Always go to section. As long as you read the textbook and go over the lecture slides before the exams, its very easy to do well. Papers are a little harder but still pretty manageable.
Her lectures were great! She made all the material really interesting and her exams followed what we learned in class and read in the book. Highly recommend this class with her.

The best teacher at this university no doubt about it. iClickers were graded so lecture was mandatory. Exams are easy so long you pay attention in lecture and read the summary in the book. Papers a little tougher, but the gsi's don't grade hard at all. 15% of your grade is based on attending section, so GO. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Ashley is one of the best professors I've had at the university.  She can easily relate to her students and I find myself actually excited to attend lecture.  Tests aren't difficult as long as you read and come to lecture.
Show up to class and read the textbook before the exams and youll be fine
Favorite class at UofM! Great professor: very nice, passionate, and loves student input. Have to go to class and participate.

GREAT professor!! I took Psych 477, and it was a great and VERY interesting class. Professor Gearhardt was really helpful during office hours also, she basically wrote me an outline for my paper. Class participation is really important, and attendance is mandatory because there are daily i-clicker questions for credit. I wish I could have her again

This was her first semester teaching so I wasn't sure what to expect, but she was great! 477 was a paper, a presentation, iclicker presentation points, and points for reading responses. She's slated to teach 270 next semester and I know she'll be amazing. Take one of her classes! You'll definitely learn a lot!

I love professor Askew. She's super kind and her lectures are so interesting. Loved hearing about all of her experiences with the Maasai. You can really tell she's passionate about the course material.

This was my first anthro class and after her course I am looking to take more. Prof. Askew was tech savvy, very passionate about anthro, and limited homework to easy reading. I ended with an easy A and would take a class of hers again.
Professor Askew is kind, considerate, and treats students with respect. She is an expert in her (many) fields and is a great teacher.

She was a great teacher that went above and beyond for her students. Professor Askew made class fun by constantly engaging students in discussion, and she was very knowledgable on the topics discussed. As long as you show up to class, participate in the discussion, and can write one decent paper, you will get a good grade in this class.

This course was a first year seminar about Rap and Radicalism. Kelly is a very nice person and treats students with respect. She assigned a lot of readings, but most of them were pretty interesting. She doesn't expect anything more than you to show up and discuss the readings. VERY easy class, good prof.
Interesting class. Professor Askew was friendly and had interesting stories to tell, but sometimes lecture was dull. It was easy to do well in this class.

I had high hopes for this class, but I was quickly disappointed.  Professor Askew isn't a bad lecturer, but she's not incredibly engaging, which makes it hard to pay attention in class.  Her stories about Africa were interesting, but they didn't seem very pertinent to the material we were covering.  Regardless, the class really isn't that difficult.

Do not take this class. I took it as an easy Social Science and Race and Ethnicity credit NOT WORTH IT. There are much easier classes that you can take. Thought it would be an easy A, BUT IT IS NOT AN EASY A. She was unclear about what we would be tested on because she spends so much time talking about her trips to Africa.

Overall pretty good class. Somewhat interesting and super super easy. DO NOT BUY THE TEXT BOOK. You can go online and read extensive chapter outlines on the books website for free; just read them and the slides and your golden.
She was a great lecturer. The GSI's could care less about the work, i never went to lecture and pulled a B.ALOT OF READING, AND LECTURE MEETS 3X'S A WEEK.ONCE AGAIN ALOTTTT OF READING.

Fairly straight-forward lecturer and makes concepts clear, but all grades in this class are determined by a GSI. Not too many essays for what I expected from ULWR, but there are 2 exams and attendance is taken in lecture. Overall a good class covering a wide variety of topics. She focuses on African art from where she conducted her research

This class is boring. Most people slept through or went on facebook during the majority of lectures. If you want to hear someone read directly from the textbook, share stories about vacations she went on (paid for by your tuition), or pretend like she knows anything about biology, then yes take this class. Or maybe you just need LS&A credit

Hmmm...nothing really special to say about her. She was a good lecturer, had a few interesting stories, and was overall just okay. This class is not that hard... pay attention in lecture and go to section and you'll be fine. I never read the books - a waste of money. Everything you need for exams they cover in lecture and section.
Had her for Anthro 101 and I loved her!!!! She's such a joy and loves the topics! I love how real she is!

I went to her with an issue concerning my GSI and she totally dismissed my comments. Instead of listening to my feedback about the situation, she attacked me and said there was nothing she could do because the last discussion section had passed (even though the class will be offered next semester). Boring professor who doesn't listen to suggestions
