SUPER helpful and knowledgable; class can get kind of scatterbrained though (we started learning C++ even though this class is supposed to be entirely an intro to Python). He really teaches you the fundamentals of programming though; I'd recommend this for any beginner or first-timer in programming, but not for one who has had experience.
very nice amicable professor
Challenging class, but I learn A LOT!

Good class, good prof. If you are lost on a project, go to his office hours. You'll have to wait a while, and then probably still spend a few hours thinking about it afterwards, but he will get you thinking in the right direction. He's very relaxed about his lectures, so you can do your own thing in class if you know what's going on already.
This class is really good and Prakash is very helpful.
Easy class. Good prof.

Very easy class. He was great about meeting outside of class time and very good at clearly explaining things. Python was very easy to learn and I never had to go to class. I highly recommend this class.

Boring.  Doesn't respond well to questions, but rather explains what he thinks you were asking.  Also doesn't like it if you choose a different approach to something, like SQL.  I was very disappointed that this was more of a BTREE C++ course than databases. I hear he is better for Operating systems.  I would avoid him.
Clearly explained concepts from the book and knew the subject matter very well. Was always willing to help during office hours and via email. Would definitely take another class taught by him.

It's a given that he's not as good as Chen, but now that Chen is no longer teaching 482, he's all we have.  A decent professor who didn't seem to live up to the horrible billing others gave him, but not amazing by any means.  Was helpful in showing us why we were failing the autograder a few times, but wasn't overly helpful

Christina is a very smart, caring young woman. She will take the time to remember your name and call on you using your name, even in a huge classroom. She knows exactly what she is teaching and will explain it to you if you need help. She allows the students to solve the problems out in front of the class so we can better grasp the material.
Christina was the best math teacher I have ever had. She was so helpful (go to office hours). Even when I wasn't in her class, she would help me with math. There isn't enough good things I can say!

Christina was a fantastic GSI. By far, she was the best teacher I had for my first semester. She is extremelly caring and considerate. She really wants you to do well in the class and is willing to take the time to make sure that every student understands concepts. I was lucky to have her, and really think I would have done worse w/o h

AP Calc was hard for me in high school but Christina made it so much easier! She really cares about her students & is extremely accessible outside of class; always willing to help with questions. She's very personable and is clear in lecture, willing to go over concepts again if they seem to be tricky. She's the reason I'm doing well in the class.

Christina is great. Highly recommended for Math 115! Christina is really superb at explaining the material in depth and answering questions. She is hilarious and realizes the class can be painful, so she does her best to make it engaging! She is VERY Accessible and holds reviews before all exams. I would not have survived in this class without her!

I feel bad for prof Atchade. MA213 is extremely basic and is a waste for him to teach. You can tell he is knowledgeable about Stats and is held back by how basic the class is. If you have taken AP Stats, you won't have to learn a single new thing. Reading the book each week is quicker and easier than going to lecture. MA213 does not need a prof.

Professor Atchade is not a great lecturer for MA213, intro to stats. There is only a midterm and a final, but he teaches very basic material that one can read in a night from the textbook. He does not have a routine for teaching and writes out what he says on the board. Expect to just read the textbook and get the material learned yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: By far the worst Stats professor at this university. After the midterm, the class completely changes from learning about statistical computing to Stats 426 related proof material. The final is all proofs, is extremely difficult, and has nothing to do with writing code. Good luck to any future students who have to suffer through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class completely switches what it is about after the midterm and the final is nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's a bit of a tough grader, and the exams are pretty challenging, but it's a really fun class and the topics are very interesting. It helps to go into the class with a bit of coding background, and his curves aren't generous, but it's an enjoyable class overall.
Think more about how useful this class is than your grade.  This is supposed to be a tough class but you can learn a lot.

Well, this is a very useful course and you will learn a lot from it. The final exam is challenging but interesting. This course requires prerequisites in mathematical stats  , therefore, if you think it's hard, it's better to learn more in stats426 or 525. In general, professor Yves Atchadé is very nice and helpful especially in his office hour.

This class was very difficult. However, between Professor Atchade's lectures and labs every week, I was able to learn so much. Professor Atchade took time out of every lecture to ask for questions and explain any concept that wasn't clear. I got more out of this class than any other upper level statistics course at the university.

I believe teaching's no picnic and isn't a easy job for anyone. BUT Yves is an EXCEPTION - he had a thick accent, couldn't explain materials clearly and wasn't helpful during office hours. Codes on slides are often wrong. Tests are VERY different from course materials & are often based on other courses (eg Math525). Please AVOID him AT ALL COSTS.

The worst and unfriendly professor ever! He is really bad at lecturing and expected you understand everything from his lame ppt. Moreover, he said that he only allowed 3 students at his office hour and he asked me to leave his office once.  Hard homework and exams!I have no idea why he is still teaching this class!  The worst class ever!

The final looks nothing like the practice exam.  The exam relies heavily on your own knowledge from other classes (stats 426 math425 math525).  Very hard to concentrate his class, spent most of the time trying to understand his accent and illogical sentences. Codes in slides are full of errors.   Avoid him if you have a choice.

If you really listen to what Professor Atchade talks about in class and do your homework by yourself, then it is not that kind of difficult. The truth is that so many people during class played with their laptops or chatted on facebook. Professor Atchade did help students in office hour, so please do not put unfair words on this professor.

This is indeed a difficult course, and Yves' accent might make is harder. But he is overall a good teacher. The materials covered are useful and he explain them fairly clear. Those rate him low: you guys can get a much better grade if you pay more attention to him and spend less time on facebook during lecture

I went to this guy's office hours asking for more homework problems, so that i could get more "graded" feedback. I wasn't asking for extra credit, just extra work so I could nail down these concepts. He told me that wasn't his responsibility; it's my job to study the material.  Let me be clear here, this man is no teacher.

Not a good teahcer!He knows a lot but he just doesn't know how to teach.His English is really bad,never asks students if we could catch up.Even worse,he is not welcoming students during his office hour,says he can only have three students in his office at a time. We are not allowed waiting in his office!No textbook at all!

NOT THAT BAD OF A TEACHER..  This class IS hard.  But for no matter who teaches it, students are going to complain.  Dr. Atchade was very helpful in office hours and class.  The projects were difficult and the exam was hard, but he does curve the class.  Very kind and caring professor.

His teaching style was very unclear. This class could have been really interesting, but what he said was often needlessly convoluted. There was also the time that he emailed the class 2 minutes before class was supposed to start saying he couldn't teach that day, and then tried to reschedule the class on our own time. Not a good prof.
Without doubt the worst professor I have ever encountered. He should be banned from teaching. Avoid at ALL costs.
Avoid him at all cost. Seriously.
This guy makes probability much more difficult. His teaching style is unclear, and hw questions and final exam questions did not follow his lectures at all. Avoid him at all cost.
No Comments
He's absolutely terrible.  Material covered and material expected to know for the final exam were 2 different things entirely.

I never write scathing reviews of professors in any context.  Their job is harder than most of us realize.  This case is an exception. His lectures were incomprehensible.  He did not attempt homework before assigning it, so he would mark wrong answers that he said were correct in office hours.  Exams were irrelevant.  Avoid at all costs. Seriously.
Class was not interesting and her style of teaching was not helpful for me. She seemed unprepared and not enthusiastic about the material.

Prof Atkinson is great. She clearly makes an effort to make the subject easy to digest and tries to sprinkle humor into her lectures. I enjoyed her class a lot. As long as you pay attention in lecture and go to discussion you'll do well. I felt like everything on the exams was reasonable.
The course itself isn't very difficult. However, prof. Atkins isn't able to foster an enthusiasm for the subject within the class. Lectures tend to be long and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easiest A ever. Lectures are pointless, just review the slides and you will get an A on the exams.

A brilliant professor that had to teach a class that is known historically for its difficulty and incoherence. She recognized this weakness in the class curriculum and discussed her plan of action for improving the class for future semesters and provided two extra credit opportunities to help students. Would definitely take another class with her.

Came to Virginia Tech and taught AOE 2074 which was a very difficult class especially with no prior programming experience. Lectures weren't helpful for some assignments, and exams were difficult so big curves were applied. Attend class!!! There may be surprise extra credit opportunities to boost your test average. Expects a lot from her students.

Atkins now teaches at Virginia Tech AOE 2074. I went to every class and her lectures are dull and don't make much sense. If you are not great a coding this class is a disaster. The class contains zero lessons on how to code in MATLAB which are all of the labs, HW, and tests. I knew how to code and struggled. She also didn't round my 92.8 up to an A

I have an decent coding background in languages like JAVA and C++, and I found this class extremely difficult. MATLAB syntax is incredibly hard to grasp and Ella does a very poor job of teaching anything. You would expect more from the head of the aero dept., but her course was extremely poorly executed.

You get too much homework that will take you hours to figure out because she explains nothing in lecture and the homework's worth nothing in comparison to the tests. She always acts condescending and mean, so if you have the option, don't have her as a teacher; this is specially if you don't have any cs background. You will be lost and fail :(

One of the worst professors at Virginia Tech. It is impossible to enjoy ANY of her classes. Hope you like spending hours on matlab and poorly created tests. Insurmountable ego. Will go on about how easy kids have it these days when she existed eons before computer-inept professors created detestable programming assignments. Low test averages

I swear if I could cut off my left arm and 3 fingers of my right hand, I would still be in less pain than taking this teacher. Her style of teaching is ridiculous; I have never seen someone with a rolling backpack, grandma skin, and no rizz beat so many souls into nothing. I would rather try to grab a toaster and play bubble bath than do this again

VT Professor is now, egotistic, mean, and grades incredibly hard. Teaches very basic concepts at an insane level because shes "done this for 40 years and we have it easy" avoid this class or take it w another professor. She teaches but shouldn't teach anything in a college setting. She should see a therapist to get her ego in check.

Textbook definition Narcissist and has an ego too big to realize the test averages of 50s might be a reflection of her own lack of teaching ability. If you go to her for help she will tell you that, "you are clearly not smart enough for Aerospace" and will go on about how much she was challenged and how young people can't handle it.

Huge joke
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has inspired me to drop out. I should have known from the second she zoomed into class with her rolly backpack that the class was not for me. If you cannot code be prepared. I can't bear to look at a computer anymore as now I have ptsd from Matlab.

She's currently a professor at VT, and no, she can't teach. I sit in class and I'm like BRUH. If you have no prior coding knowledge it's the worst, even kids who have coded are still confused on her tests. Fun fact she fell off the stage during class so at least that was fun.

This professor teaches at a very basic level but expects extremely high standards with regards to homework assignments and exams. If you are a PhD student, this course is a lot of work. Please dont take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ella Atkins is one of the worst professors I have ever had. She does not explain the projects enough and you are forced to ask dozens of follow up questions. She spent 10 min talking about a topic that made up half of exam 2. Exams require you to write dozens of equations on cheat sheets only for you to find that you forgot the one on the you need.

For an introductory course, Professor Atkins explains the material as though you are in an upper-level course and have an understanding of the basic principles on the topics she teaches. Her lectures are mostly derivations and lack understandable examples. Also be prepared for lots of Matlab homework and projects.

This class is trash garbage due to the professor, the content is mind-numbingly easy but she makes it difficult by explaining things poorly or changing up coordinate systems on the fly. The projects aren't difficult conceptually, but she will give you half the information you need and she blatantly doesn't care.

Aero201 give's Ella Atkins a bad wrap, the homework will have you working your brain hard and saying "I hate matlab". But the blame belongs to the content, there is a lot covered in this class especially for an intro class. Ella is very caring/understanding, course notes are amazing, and you'll learn a lot; if your struggling just speak with Ella.

Atkins doesn't really care about the class. Her curriculum is extremely outdated and very much focused on planes. The projects are extremely time consuming. They are impossible without using piazza, as instructions are frequently wrong. Exams are often on unimportant material from class just because they are easy to write questions on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ella Atkins is a very knowledgeable professor. However, it doesn't translate well to an Intro Aerospace class. Often, I found myself googling for extra information as her notes are very dense. There was definitely a lot more Matlab coding than I thought, so prepare for that. You will find yourself working more than you would expect for three credit

This is a 3 credit class, and it's more work that I've put in to almost all the other classes I've taken. There is no textbook, no course pack, course notes and lecture slides barely provide you with useful information on assignments and projects. Formula cheat sheets in exams are basically useless because there are so many and you'll forget some.

Her lectures don't prepare us well on solving problems she expects us to know. So a lot is learned from the course notes provided. But for Dubins path, there was nothing taught to me that really prepared me for anything she expected us to know. It's very frustrating overall.

Course is taught only through lengthy derivations while the exams test content that's not taught but should be 'intuitive.' Project specs are very vague and all assignments are needlessly long just for the sake of it. This class is for less credits than my others yet takes way more time.

Atkins is a pretty good professor, she knows her stuff and is helpful if you have a question for her. Her notes are really well developed, if you read those and do some practice problems the class isn't a big deal. Prepare to do a lot of Matlab, but nothing insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She puts on this incredibly nice persona but deep down she is feeding on our tears. Homework is only difficult because it wasn't covered and is poorly worded. It literally took a group of 12 of us 14 hours to figure out how to solve the problems. Her lectures are putting the notes on the projector and scrolling, while talking about something else
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ella Atkins is a sorry excuse for a teacher. She clearly has no regard for her students or for their learning. Her project are ridiculously time consuming for the sake of being time consuming.

Prof Atkins is nice when you have a conversation with her, but her teaching style is not good. Her lectures are: rewriting course notes/useless derivations. Then her exams are basically, "Did you write that one equation from the 60 pgs of notes on your notesheet?" One good thing: Matlab projects/homeworks make up more of your grade than the tests.

The only issue is that her lectures are just reading the course notes, so I honestly work on other homework during class. Otherwise she is great and really cares about us. She's best if you meet her outside of class and have 1:1 conversations with her.

She gives poor and obscure explanations of topics, and often gets sidetracked yet expects her points get across. While it's clear that she understands the material very well, she lacks the ability to effectively convey it to her students. Additionally, she requires all coding homework assignments to be turned in on paper: be ready to print a lot

Prof. Atkins has very high expectations, for sure. ROB 550 has probably one of the heaviest workloads you will experience, but at the end of the day, you will be proud of what you accomplish. There may be better choices for instructors, but Prof. Atkins definitely knows what she is doing, and she is not one who you must avoid for ROB 550.

Lectures were dry and full of derivations w/ very few examples, mostly just writing equations from online notes on board. Would upload homeworks and projects late and had multiple revisions regularly. Projects were unnecesarrily difficult, considering she gave almost no examples. GSI had to clarify or correct problems at least five times on final.

"AERO201 with Ella Atkins is looking both ways before crossing the street and getting hit by a Boeing 747."  AERO201 has a set curriculum and Professor Atkins tried to teach it. I don't blame her for running a derivation-based class--it's true to the notes. I do blame her however, for writing tests whose content is disjoint from that of lecture.

Horrible. Boring. Unprepared for lectures. Unprepared for homeworks and projects. She said in class one day, "You guys complain about no examples, but have you guys looked through the notes?" Listen, we want you to supply us more than the ONE example you supply in the "notes". We want you to show us how to use and apply what you "teach". AVOID!!

She provided lecture notes which were very helpful but the lectures were more about writing  equations than explaining concepts. The homework and especially the projects were tough with some things not really covered. Every homework was released late with an average of 1.5 days and a max of 3.9 days.
Terrible teacher- makes the course work significantly harder than it needs to be. Proof-based lecturing so it doesn't really help with homeworks or projects.

Atkins has a clear enthusiasm for aerospace, but she does a poor job teaching it. Her lectures are only confusing derivations (straight from the notes) and she provided no practice problems outside of the homework sets, which were often hard. Poor organization; homeworks were often posted late and with errors. Is willing to help you in OH though.

Course had lots of good material, but Atkins did a horrible job teaching. Lectures were not interesting, and generally, she just went over derivations. I don't think she's gone through a single example. The class is badly organized. All homeworks have errors, and she always fails to upload homework on time (often times days after scheduled).

Interesting materials, practical projects, however awful teacher. The course could be much better, more helpful and much lesser bulky if she had not frequently miss the classes and had guide us properly. Abrupt changes in classes, unclear homework problems, missing links between materials, she is also a stubborn grader.

Prior programming (eg HS class) is almost a must for ENGR151. Much of the material was rushed, and I remember a few times where we would learn concepts after they were useful on a HW. Atkins doesn't have good time management in lecture. I learned a ton in this class, but expect a lot of work (I spent 10 hours/day Fri-Sun for a few HWs) and use GSIs

For your own sake, do not take this class if you're not willing to put in the work (30 hours one weekend). This ended up not being a difficult class to receive a good grade in because of a high curve, but you will have to do a great deal of learning on your own and Ella is not necessarily the best resource for explanations. Use the GSIs heavily.

Homework is hard and the exams are even harder. Make sure you have prior knowledge and a high interest level as you'll get completely lost if you don't. Go to class as her lecture notes aren't useful and material is gone through very quickly. She explains stuff as if you're not learning it for the first time but the tenth. Use the GSIs!

She assumes that every student takes her class to challenge themselves. She changes assignments last minute, and gives an insane workload. For the project, some groups spent 30+ hours over a 5 day span that included the weekend. Grades take 3+ weeks to get back. Stay away from her, shes batsy.

Atkins is a good Prof. Her homework is hard, her exams are even harder, but overall she is a good prof. If you like aerospace, and are into programming you will enjoy her as a professor. If not, good luck. Advice: go to office hours. Her class becomes much easier by doing so.

Overall a good teacher. I came in with a strong background/interest, the projects were difficult enough to be interesting and her frequent tangents were almost all cool. However, if you have no interest in the subject, you should probably avoid her. If you do like the martial, you will enjoy her as a teacher.

To the guy 2 below me, where do you get off saying Ella's a decent teacher??? 90+% of lecture is listening to her irrelevant tangents, there were zero example problems presented in class, exam reviews have nothing to do with the exams themselves, the textbook had typoed formulas, homework was never explained properly, the list goes on and on and on
Simply put, Ella is a horrible teacher. If you have her for a class, run away. If you can't run away, crawl. If you can't crawl, just kill yourself.
She's a decent teacher and very enthusiastic. Homework is often very difficult and not well explained -- expect to spend 10+ hours some weeks. Exams are do-able and the class is curved fairly.
Words can't describe how much I hate this lady...avoid her at all costs

This is class is now known as AEROSP 201, which is a bit easier than Aerosp 245. This class was taught by her 2/3rds of the time and 1/3rd by guest lecturers. Homeworks were a bit confusing at times because of how the class was taught. On the other hand she did curve the class by a lot which makes the class really hard to fail.

She knows her stuff, but she goes off topic from time to time. Sometimes she does not properly teach the material she wants you to do in the homework. So beware of that. On the other hand she really curves the class so it is really hard to fail the class.

Words cannot describe the level of disgust I have when Ella and teaching come to mind, or shall I say lack there of teaching. If you have her as a teacher drop the class, if you need the class, switch majors, if you don't want to switch majors, transfer schools.

As others have stated her class was way too hard.  Other sections focused on the logic of programming while using basic skills, while she took an in depth approach that was way over everyone's heads.  Even after coming out of the class with a B I still don't understand the material.  Also she wears her pants distractingly high on her torso.

I've never taken a class at UM that was so disorganized and unnecessarily difficult. A ton of material is covered in lectures, yet you leave feeling helpless because they provide little to no examples for homework. This class is ridiculous, and if its only purpose is to steer people away from the Aerospace department at UM then I say job well done.

She makes class unnecessarily hard! This is an intro class and even students who have taken more advanced classes say the material she expects us to know is far beyond what we should. She does not explain anything related to the homework she gives you (which is ridiculously long). BE PREPARED TO TEACH YOURSELF EVERYTHING!

Ella finds pleasure in giving out needlessly long assignments and is either too lazy to bother explaining them properly or she?s just an ass. Regardless, I highly recommend dropping a class if she?s teaching it.  To make sure you get an A, make best friends with your GSI and go to his office hours whenever available.

A difficult class, both to teach and learn. Many different subjects and concepts are introduced at once. She curves the class fairly. The homework and projects take copious amount of time. Many times you'll have hard time figuring out what you're supposed to be doing, so take the responsibility to go to her office hours and expect to work hard.
Ella Atkins is an enthusiatic soul..she loves disserting into semi-related stuff..do take this class as an alternative to engr101 when it is offered. You wont regret it. Kevin is a good GSI !
Ella Atkins is an enthusiatic soul..she loves disserting into semi-related stuff..do take this class as an alternative to engr101 when it is offered. You wont regret it. Kevin is a good GSI !
She's tough, but that's to be expected since it was the advanced section. Good with extensions and extra credit. Plus she's pretty amusing, especial on the class chatroom.

awful. have her for 151, advanced programming. her notes are completely unhelpful, her assignments are really difficult (about 30-40 hours a week on just this class). i taught myself programming in this class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ATKINS, just skip to eecs 280

Ella is a very "enthusiastic" individual. For this reason, she should not be teaching intro programming classes. Are assignments were unecessarily hard, because she thought it was fun for us to waste our time on pointless programs. DON'T TAKE 101 WITH HER.
oh god, this woman drove me crazy! she made 101 unnecessarily hard and she encouraged the GSI's to grade too strictly. She wasn't very helpful during office hours too

Even though this class as listed as "101" it was still over my head (i never took any class remotely related to programming). All lectures are recorded so its no biggie if you miss class. HW's weren't too bad but the 2 projects were EPIC so beware. Unless you're truly serious about programming, consider another section.

I was in her advanced C++ section for engr101, and we did a bunch more stuff than the regular section. She is a good teacher and I learned a lot, but the assignments were not well written (at least for the advanced section) and it was not always clear what exactly we were expected to do. I guess I would recommend her, but you'll have to put in work

She seems to know what she's doing but for the students who really don't know what they're doing, she does not know how to bring herself down to their level. her class is harder than it should be (i've been told by a EECS learning center tutor that a lot of stuff i was doing he didn't learn in engr 101).

I don't think Atkins has any idea what she is doing, and probably writes all her assignments, projects and tests in 5 minutes. Instructions are never clear nor do they include everything you need to know and sometimes she posts incorrect examples/test files. Lecture is just a place to sleep.

Horrible notes, no powerpoint only her tablet pc that she loves. I only attend lecture to work on the homework and for a quick nap in Stamps. GSI's will be you're true teacher, Kevin is an awesome GSI. Knows everything very well and can explain in easy to understand manner.

I already know C++, but the assignments are usually unclear enough to the point where you get points off for stupid things that you shouldn't have.  Her section is also run completely different than other section.  Another Engineering professor has recommended Holloway instead of her... I've never had Holloway, but I would have to agree.

She isnt the best reason, but there is no reason you should not get a 100 on the projects or hw. once you go to office hours, the understanding is fine. it really depends on your gsi. her test are not the easiest, but if you just learn to read code, which isn't that hard, you can pull off b's on the test
one of the worst teachers I have ever had.
No Comments

Second class... first class Typography where we designed compositions for her book - and now designing work for another member of her family in Branding. Prepare to experience her haughtiness and superiority with poorly planned classes.
I learned more watching youtube videos - than from her "teaching".
absolutely the very best at teaching so very little.

Overall I got a good grade at the end of the class, sometimes things were not clarified in how they were graded. She gives lots of feedback if you ask for it and it's helpful. She also gives plenty of in class time to work on projects so take advantage of that. She is also very nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took me several weeks to figure out that she didn't actually hate us all and could be quite friendly and encouraging, just with a very calm professional demeanor that came off as cold. She does things very by the book. Had some of the best critiques ever in her class, though. Mixed bag for me but really depends on if her teaching style is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Audrey sets up her class by letting student figure out the assignments for themselves, which can be intimidating at first. Her humor is very dry and she can seem scary, but is actually extremely amicable and cares a lot for her students. She loves to interact and give feedback, and her critiques are incredible.
Michal teaches with a sense of humanity which is humbling. I appreciate her teaching style and would take the class again. She involves a field trip near the beginning of the semester.
This is the second class I've taken with this professor. Easy grader, but she doesn't put in a lot of work.

The class is very disorganized. Does not give clear direction to assignments. Be prepared for last minute assignments and limited time to turn them in. For a one credit class it was a very heavy workload. There were a few lectures but they were not beneficial. Good at responding to emails quickly. Very tough grader. Not worth the time.

Dr. Michal was awesome! The class wasn't too much work, but all the content was super interesting. Dr. Michal did a lot of in-class demonstrations, which were fun; in general, she did a great job of making the content accessible and exciting. There's a group project that makes up most of the grade, but it isn't too much work.

weekly discussion quizzes were pretty easy, and exams which were held online came mostly from the slides and examples from lecture. The readings posted from canvas were extremely long. Make sure not to fall behind on lecture material, and fill out the study guide with lecture notes and whatever is from the readings. Not an Easy A, but very doable.

Psych 240 with Professor Michal was fine. Exams had some tricky questions but were pretty standard and were all multiple choice. Surprisingly, the peer reviews were the most harshly graded. This class was fine but it wasn't perspective-changing or super interesting. It was hard to take notes because most of the lectures were examples.

Dr. Michal is so great! Her class is also super easy (no exams!). Weekly assignments but all manageable. Her lectures are also engaging, since she includes relatable videos from movies/tv shows and demos that get the class involved. There is a group project at the end, but nothing difficult. She's also a sweetheart, loved her and her class!

Super easy and engaging course. Weekly easy assignments to make sure you're not falling behind, and one big, though manageable, project at the end. No exams is a relief. Dr. Michal's lectures were great!

Prof. Michal uses Calendly for her office hours so it's really easy to see her if you're struggling. No exams but lots of little assignments that are pretty easy to complete as long as you keep track of them. Readings are sometimes long but really interesting! Her lectures are fun and incorporate videos and demonstrations that make them engaging.

If you attend class, do the iclickers and you will be fine. no exams, weekly reflection papers (super easy) and weekly quizzes (get 70%, receive full credit - <70%, half credit). Dr. Michal is super smart but the class is kinda dull.

This guy has all the credentials to teach thermo but with none of the ability to convey basic information. He seemed to read off the powerpoint solutions to two problems every lecture. This was the first class I skipped completely to just read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Apathetically unhelpful
Just go to one lecture, after that they're all the same. Homework was given two days before it was due, the project we got zero feedback on, and the exams were guesswork and Unit matching.

Atreya seems nice, but when it comes to actual teaching he's useless. He will never do examples, so get ready to learn on your own. Also just go to one lecture, then he repeats that lecture for the entire semester, with almost no new content.

Professor Atreya is like a grandfather who can't teach anything. He just says to "do the monkey business" and you get the answer while pointing at a powerpoint. I read the book and got a tutor to avoid his disorganized lecture slides. That being said, his curve is generous. If you can take him and attend the other professor you will beat the curve.
It's a joke that this man teaches here.
No one goes to class because he is THE WORST professor I have ever had. Avoid him at all costs if you want to actually learn something.
A very helpful professor, he would answer your questions in details in his office hour. Though the course is difficult, if you spend much time on it, you will get good score.
His classes are absolutely useless...He DOES NOT TEACH what so ever.  He just wastes your time while he reads from a power point, which you will fall asleep during.  You must avoid him!!
Too hard,not clear enough

This course is absolutely miserable. Attending lectures is useless. He uses nothing but powerpoints which make you fall asleep. He doesn't care about the course, or what you think. He doesn't seem to care about teaching in general, very disorganized. Avoid him like the plague.
Avoid his classes. No interest in his teaching, used almost 10 textbooks!!! His exams were reasonable and he is a fair grader....However attending his classes made my life miserable
Poor delivery.
Graduate level combustion course.  Take the one from Aero. It is much better.
Worse ME Proferssor EVER!!!!
take borgnakke! Aretya sucks!
SUCKS! Check his rating done by umich and see yourself.
Helped me out in a pinch.  Considerate guy.
Great professor.  All you have to do is pay attention and work hard, I don't know why the other guy is complaining.  Take this class!
Can't Teach!! Aviod his classes like the plague!! Annoying as hell!! Not helpful outside class!!
good prof
try areo combustion instead
No Comments
He was very open to communication and always in the mindset to help

A knowledgeable professor who seems to genuinely care about the topic and believe in your success. He emphasized improvement and creativity while also helping you to learn the software. He was hands-on with a steady feedback loop and playtests. Keep in mind the course load IS heavy.

Professor Yarger is an amazing teacher. He gives a lot of career advice and resources, while also creating interactive and fun lecture environments that teach important concepts. 494 has a pretty intense workload, but all the feedback from assignments and guidance during office hours is really helpful and pushes you in the right direction.
Only letting me select EECS 494, but I actually took EECS 440. 440 was fantastic, fun, light course load relatively. Austin is the GOAT!

This professor is incredibly passionate and teaches very well. The workload in this course is heavy, but if you enjoy game development, everything feels very logical and meaningful rather than overwhelming.

Prof. Yarger is an incredible professor. He gives tons of career and internship advice, shares great resources, and truly cares about students' success. The workload in EECS 494 is intense, but he's super supportive throughout.

Austin genuinely wants his students to succeed and do well in his classes. He not only offers thoughtful advice on the your games but also provides opportunities for extra credit. His lectures are informative, showcasing different games and their mechanics that influence player decisions. The concepts he presents are helpful for your final game.
Prof. Yarger is really good at teaching, he was very proffesional and very patient with students. And he always help students to look out for job opportunities.

Professor Yarger is one of the most inspiring professors at UM! His lectures are engaging, his feedback is thoughtful, and he truly cares about students' growth as game designers. The class is challenging but rewarding, and you'll leave with real skills and a love for game design. Highly recommend if u feel interested in game area

I took both EECS494 and EECS498 with Prof Yarger and absolutely loved both courses. His lectures are always very engaging and you can genuinely feel his passion in every lecture. He's always there to help, and while these 2 courses are famous for the heavy workload, it is definitely doable with how supportive Prof Yarger is throughout the semester!

Austin Yarger is my favorite professor at the University of Michigan. He is passionate about his courses as well as the game development community on campus as a whole through the creation of new courses, support of student groups, and the passion by which he teaches his current courses. His courses also heavily provide creative freedom.

Professor Yarger is easily the best professor I've had during my time at UM. I took both EECS 494 and 498, which were some of the most challenging and rewarding classes I've taken. His lectures are engaging, the work always aligns with what we're learning-- nothing is extraneous or wasted. He's knowledgeable and provides fantastic feedback. GOAT

This is indeed a review for VR class Austin is teaching as well. His approach to lectures and projects is highly engaging. He gave us the freedom to explore new features in different game engines. If I could start over, I'd take all three of his game development courses.

EECS494 has been one of my favorite courses I've ever taken. Professor Yarger's lectures are incredibly engaging, and he truly cares about his students' success. The courseload is fast-paced-- 494 is the second-heaviest CS class here for a reason-- but you learn an unimaginable amount. His project feedback is thoughtful, and he's always accessible.
GOAT, go for it

EECS 494 is my favorite class at Michigan. I appreciated how it's more freeform & subjective compared to other EECS classes. Yarger's feedback on how to improve a game was consistently super helpful, and his passion for the topic was contagious. Sometimes rubrics made grading expectations sound higher than they were, but it wasn't a huge issue.

Austin was one of the many bright points in EECS 494. He has an ineffable enthusiasm for video games which rubs off on both the rest of the staff and the students. As a recent student, he was empathetic and supportive of many struggles that students might encounter in this class. Lectures were also very fun and interactive. All in all, awesome!

austin is a blessing. he is one of, if not the best EECS professor i've ever had. he is enthusiastic and consistently shows that this class and its students are a priority for him. despite the class getting larger over the semesters, each project still gets great individual feedback. it's a LOT of work, but its so rewarding!!!

The absolute best EECS professor I've had here. He's extremely passionate about game dev. Even if you're not interested in game dev, I'd recommend taking this class because trust me, he will get you super excited about it. His lectures are fascinating and fun. He's also super nice and very very encouraging. He's left a lasting impact on me.

Hands down the best CS instructor I've had at Michigan!! Austin is extremely passionate & knowledgeable about game design, and he brings this enthusiasm to every lecture. He genuinely cares about the well-being and opinions of his students. As someone who doesn't come from a gaming background, the class still felt very accessible and interesting.
Austin did a great job presenting his lecture material and keeping it interesting. There were often in game demos in class which were both fun and effective at explaining game design principles.
Professor Yarger was passionate about the course material and genuinely wanted students to succeed.
Austin is an awesome professor that really cares about his students

His lectures are easy to understand and fun, but sometimes arent immediately useful for projects. He suffers from DKC music addiction and doesnt seem to sleep very much either. You probably won't either, but you can look forward to learning alot about game dev. RIP hair.
Very enthusiastic and easy to approach.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Austin is one of the most impressive instructors I've had. Not only is he unquestionably knowledgeable on every topic he teaches, but his genuine care and effort that he invests in the class is unlike most other professors at the university. His lectures are some of the most engaging you'll have, and though the class is a challenge, it's worth it.

Austin lives and breathes game development and it shows. Over the course of the class, he really pushes you to make a game that is interesting, polished, and fun. It's a lot of work but it's a really fun process and it's the kind of thing you want to work on. He's a caring guy, very invested in making the class great and the students successful.
RCDRAMA 102 is an introductory improv class. This class taught me all about improv, and the professor encouraged me to step up and participate in many games.

I took her pilot class and I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would, but she was fine. Personally, I don't get along well with her teaching style, but I think overall she's a passionate and great professor.

This was an improv games class open to rc and non rc students. Truly such a great experience and Dr. Audrey made this class so fun. Definitely take a class with her - she cares so much about her students and has a wonderfully positive attitude that makes everyone feel welcome!

I've never met anyone with more knowledge of Early Modern drama than Audrey Becker. Her passion for the topic shows and she finds different ways for everyone to connect with the material. She pushes you to improve as a student, writer, and performer, and she can adapt her critique based on your experience in theater performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Planned a lot of helpful projects and activities that were engaging and truly helped with learning about theatre and acting. Gave great feedback about performances and encouraged a community space so it never felt awkward performing in front of peers. There was a lot of reading, but the plays were interesting and engaging to dive into as an actor.

For an introductory class, the grading scale felt unreasonable (95% for an A). Weekly papers are short + lectures elaborated on the readings so you could get away with skimming most of the readings. No tech, but in class notes don't really help since the midterm + final + essays were based on terms in his study guide (remember ~200 terms per exam).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of work for an intro to asian studies course. If you do all of it you'll be fine but don't do this class with him if you don't want to do a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dense readings used to write weekly papers. In lecture, he would say non-english words in and overly accentuated accent that is uncomfortable. Quizzes were on materials that had to be learned outside of class. Multiple choice on exams were very specific and subjective and he did not provide any resources to practice, even when asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Weekly essays and readings that are pretty heavy, refusal to give any resources outside of lectures, and the minimum for an A is a 95 for an INTRODUCTORY class! Calls people out for having technology in class and forces students to write handwritten notes. We had one major quiz besides the pop quizzes, and that was on resources OUTSIDE of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had a very enjoyable time in Asian 235 w/ Prof Auerback. It was a very easy, yet interesting class. Granted, he only lectured and the GSI wrote exams and graded weekly 1.5 page papers based on week's reading. Exams were easy, papers were tedious but weren't graded harshly, attendance is mandatory. No technology allowed in-class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst class ever — ASIAN 215! The lectures are confusing, essays are due every week, and the professor is hard to communicate with. Nothing from lectures shows up on quizzes or exams, the study guides don't help, and both the professor and GI grade harshly. The professor also uses different accents for international words - so annoying!

Dr. Auerback is very passionate about the subject, and the lectures are very interesting! However, the class is a ton of work, especially for an intro. There are a lot of assignments, and he is not very forgiving when it comes to class policies. Also, you have to put track changes on in word, which is annoying

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The workload is absurd.1500+ pages of reading, 500 word essay due EVERY SUNDAY & TUESDAY, multiple presentations & a midterm/final that total 5000+ words. No useful writing feedback & grades everything the last week. His expectations for the effort students should put into a 3 credit INTRO ELECTIVE are severely out of touch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For a 3 credit introductory course, it has weekly essays, 2 long essays around 3000 words, and presentations based on reading. The time commitment is huge, and the professor is not giving up to date feedback. Our writing assignments are not graded until the final week. He is also not friendly when I talk to him during OH or through email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Auerback is a very knowledgeable scholar. He knows a lot about the subject and is very helpful with recommending sources for writing papers. However, he takes forever to grade, and eventually the hours of work you spend reading and writing each week end up being graded for completion, which is frustrating considering the work you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class wasn't difficult but had a decent amount of work as far as readings and weekly essays. He took a long time to grade things so eventually our essays were graded on completion rather than quality, which was fine but annoying given how much time they took. Super knowledgeable and passionate professor, though, which I appreciated.

Professor Auerback is one of my favorite professors here. He's extremely intelligent and kind. He's not that clear about his grading requirements, but that's because he will give you an A if you put in any effort. I learned so much in this class without having to stress about my grade. As any other Asian Studies class, be prepared to read.

Professor Auerback is ridiculously intelligent and an expert on Buddhism and Japan. Intro to Japanese Buddhism was great because he is able to help us understand some tough and esoteric text. My only criticism would be that he takes a long time to grade things... but things happen. If you want to know a TON about Japanese Buddhism, take his class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No bonus credits, no textbook, no examinations, but intensive reading. You really need to spend some time on reading and writing response assignments. Professor Auerback would be extremely helpful when you are working on your take-home paper. He could provide you with an unimaginable number of sources for your research.
Exams are pretty easy. Not hard to get bonus credits and full participation credits. No take-home essays are required.
Weekly assignments are easy, and it is not hard to have full participation credits.

I absolutely love him! His class is so engaging and he is the one who really make me fall in love with Japanese culture! He is not 'humorous' but he has got a sort of the nerdy funny which is very cute. He really like Japan and really wants to let students know more about this country.

Excellent Professor, thoroughly enjoyed his class. He has a very sweet personality and he genuinely cares for his students. He is incredibly knowledgeable about Buddhism and Japan. One of the best professors I have ever had at UM.
Helpful and very approachable to talk to about any subject. This class was reading intensive, the class sessions are helpful for understanding the material.
He's a great professor and a  great human being. He's incredibly helpful on even non-academic matters and genuinely cares for the welfare of his students. A diamond in the rough at UofM.

Focused too much on philosophy during second half of course and expected us to read dense assigned texts and work on research practically 24/7. Class did not focus enough on research or writing methods. A hard grader with unrealistic and unclear expectations who hands out too many negative criticisms but not enough feedback on how to improve.

Prof Auerback is a very articulate and intelligent man. If you have a genuine interest in Buddhism, you will love his class. He's a very friendly and approachable person, so don't be afraid to ask questions! Seek help early if you're struggling and you should do just fine. Overall a positive experience!
Prof. Auerback is incredibly fluent when it comes to asian studies. His Intro to Buddhism class was awesome. I learned a lot. He is really well organized and great with questions. TAKE HIS CLASS!
A very helpful, smart professor.

Prof Auerback is a great instructor. I learned an incredible amount about the study of history; every History student should be lucky enough to take this class. The course can be demanding, but is well worth it. Prof A gives back even more than he requires and goes to great lengths to be helpful and prepare good lessons. The archetypal small class.

Professor Auerback is possibly the most confusing professor I've ever had. He's way to smart to be teaching an introductory class about Buddhism. He's awful at breaking stuff down and assigns WAY too many readings. Not to mention the GSI's are clueless and the exams are blue book. I HATED this class. Take my advice and DONT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

This prof expects students to work hard. Class was challenging, but the time and energy he displayed kept me going when I got exhausted. Prof clearly loves the topic, and loves sharing it. Take any class you can with him.

Anyone who makes a negative comment is likely too lazy or incompetent to appreciate his value as a teacher.  He is incredibly smart and articulate, and his course was well structured.  He is not an easy A, though, so expect to work.

I can't understand why everyone's giving Micah such low marks. He's a really great professor; his classes are very interesting for anyone that has an inkling of interest in Buddhism.. Reading might be a bit much but come on people it's college... Overall one of my favorite classes at the university. Forget all these other people; take the course!

Eastern thought is immensely complex.  It is far more experiential than technical.  Given that, Auerback is a really solid professor.  The material is incredibly difficult to teach, but he is really understanding and chill with his students.  The GSIs can kind of suck though.  They seem to have less of a clue than the students.
Yes, there is a fair amount of reading. Yes, some of the material is rather dry. But overall, it's a fairly easy class. Just study hard for the exams and there is no reason why you shouldn't do fine.

If you either value your free time or your GPA, then don't even think about thinking about taking this class. Somewhat interesting material, but the amount of reading assigned is beyond absurd for any level of any class in any field, let alone a 200-level intro class. Prof is decent but doesn't respond much to students' reflections of the class.

Professor Auerback is one of those nice guys, who is just bad at this job.  He never clearly answers a question and manages to make students less prepared for tests then if they didn't go to class at all.  He says it's a good thing when students are confused and doesn't seem to mind when students are totally lost.  DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES!

My ONLY really bad experience at UofM in the past two years! The man is intelligent but seems not to grasp that this is an "intro" class to a subject that is intensely complex. He teaches it as if we were all experts already. The reading workload is unquestionably uncalled for. Don't give up on taking the class, just don't take it from this guy.

I left this course hating Buddhism.  HUGE waste of my time!!! I could not for the life of me understand his lectures.  His advanced vocabulary is incomprehensible.  On the midterm, I could not answer one of the essays because I could not understand the vocabulary he used (not vocabulary related to the material that we learned...)
Intro to Buddhism was pretty easy-going, and I learned a bit about the religion and its history. Micah is pretty chill.

Unless you already have a great understanding of Buddhism this class will not be helpful.  Professor cannot express what he knows and instead just confuses everyone, and GSIs are the least helpful I've ever met at the University.  Heavy reading also results in a negative feel for the class
I feel that Prof. Auerback likes to test trivial details. The GSIs don't seem very educated in this area.
This class was ridiculous and a waste of time. By making students lead discussions, he was encouraging the GSI's to be useless and lazy; which mine was.

This class is kind of difficult for a 200 level class and you might be scared at first, but the prof is very willing to change based on student need. Be very honest on the midterm review and he will actually change the class based on what you suggest. there's a lot of reading but little writing. GSIs aren't that knowledgeable.

Professor Auerback knows what he's talking about. The class is very interesting and engaging, however there is significant reading for a 200 level class. The first half of the class and the first midterm were rather easy, while the second half is much more complex and difficult. Discussion sections are helpful. 3 short papers must be written.

she is so knowledgeable it is almost intimidating but she is so nice that it cancels out! she is very eager and open any and every question, and is very forgiving and generous on exams. sometimes a lot of homework, but nothing unmanageable. i didn't really care for linguistics until this class and did find it much more intriguing because of aull!

Mind blowing class!! Dr. Aull does a great job of breaking down everything you've ever learned about English in high school and reformatting your thinking to be more progressive and accurate in the writing world. Makes strong connections w/ her students too. 10/10 professor!!
Although the class is pretty challenging, Dr. Aull provides useful feedback to help you improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It is hard to get high score in her class, but you don't always get A (take this advice seriously as a FY student in UM). You will learn more than you expect and ready to be challenge. Many supports and insight and I recommend her class for anyone who want a class more than a FYWR. She make me interested in linguistics even I am not good at English

I took English 305 as a three-hour course. I would normally have trouble focusing, but Dr. Aull's lectures were so engaging that I never had any difficulty. She's extremely articulate and clearly very passionate. She would always take time to thoughtfully answer every question, and you could tell she values her students' opinions. Take her classes!

Inspirational is the best word to describe her. By far my favorite professor at University of Michigan. She is an incredibly deep thinker, but does a fantastic job of translating her concepts to terms the students can understand. I chose her class because I had extra credits to fill, and she nearly convinced me to change my major. Highly recommend!

Dr Aull is an amazing teacher! Definitely the most difficult class I took, but totally worth it! Might end up with a B or C, but the insight and writing skills you acquire are invaluable. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you really CANT miss her class if you want to do remotely well. Awesome lectures, approachable and friendly. A "must" if you can!!
none
No Comments
Professor Laura Aull is very pleasant and a great teacher. She works very well with each student and keeps discussions engaging and though provoking.

Laura is a great teacher and her class is interesting.  She is very personable, willing to meet with students outside of class, and responds to e-mails quickly.  Her class is challenging, but if you put forth a lot of effort you should be fine. If you don't mind a challenge, I definitlely recommend taking the class.
Unclear and definitely avoid if you can

Audrey is an AMAZING Spanish teacher! She really cares about making connections and regular conversation with her students. She encourages participation which is part of your grade for each individual Unit. If you take this course, participate, study hard for exams, and be truthful in your writing assignments to succeed!!!!
She is truly an incredible professor and I have learned so much this year!
Audrey is an amazing professor! Made learning a new language 100x less intimidating. She was really understanding, and always brought a lighthearted, upbeat, attitude to class.
Took ENGR 100 (not MechE 250)

I took ME 250 with Prof. Austin-Brenman and absolutely loved it. There is ofc a lot of work but prof. Austin-Brenman is really a great lecturer. Material is in depth and very well structured while lecture is still lighthearted. Overall an amazing teacher.

He seems like a great person, but it is so hard to learn from him. He jumps around concepts, dodges questions, and misses scheduled meetings without warning. He knows his stuff, but getting that information from him is the equivalent of dumpster diving for treasure. Class itself is very reasonable.

Prof is not very clear on explain the important concepts of the class. I often has to go to the office hours to get clarified on the lecture. Also he seems to miss quite a few office hours. It is very difficult to get the help outside the lecture.

Professor Awartani is incredible. The course includes complex but necessary readings that encourage meaningful engagement with historical contexts. While the workload itself is not heavy, the readings balance it out. Active participation and weekly attendance are essential to getting the most out of the class, and are required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super kind and caring but a lot of reading. Only a few short essays and two group projects throughout the semester, but there are usually hefty readings + reading responses every week. Would totally recommend for an easyish humanities credit, but be prepared to read and participate.
The nicest Professor you will ever have! She is so relatable and gets what her students have on their plates. Her lectures are really interesting, and I learned so much in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The most caring professor at UM! Loved taking her class. Had one final project we worked on throughout the semester, and learned so so much, definitely recommend taking amcult 204 with her if you can.

He never responded to any emails and had no office hours, which is very problematic when the course is fully online. It's been almost three weeks since the final paper was due, and he still hasn't put in a final grade. Canceled class a lot and didn't really ever teach, mostly just talked at us. Easy class though... I guess. I wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was very disengaged and talked wayyyyyy to much. The assignments were just for credit. Did not seem as if he checked them. It was just a waste of time.

Professor Awkward is a lot of fun. We read a lot of interesting books. The class definitely moves quickly so you need to be diligent about reading if you want to be able to write the papers. The papers aren't super intricate though, we had a lot of freedom to take them in whatever direction we wanted. Discussions were great!

There are many things I'd like to say about Professor Awkward.  He's rude, boring, unorganized, has anxiety breakdowns, is reluctant to help students (he shooed me away with his hand), uses seriously inappropriate language, and is just overall the WORST professor I've ever had.  The class itself was an easy A, but that was it's only perk.

He stands up front with about 23 yellow legal pads and reads notes off of them. The rest of the time, he reads directly from or paraphrases the novels we were supposed to have read for class. So basically, lecture is a total waste of time...and he takes attendance every day. Material was easy, finding motivation to go to class was hard.

THE worst professor I've encountered at U-M in 4 years. Not only does he always seem blatantly unprepared for lecture, but also overreacts when students enter or exit the lecture hall - though, for whatever reason, he has left his own lecture early MULTIPLE TIMES without explanation. Abrasive and unfortunately his lectures seem like an afterthought

I could not stay awake during lecture for the life of me. He rambled for an hour and a half, over-reacted to students leaving/coming in the room, AND took attendance every single lecture. Completely unorganized and unstructured class. Too much reading.

I doubt he's ever prepared a lecture before class-he just speaks what's on his mind. Not organized, forgets things all the time, cancels class, pushes back paper deadlines, he actually changed the date of our final exam because he was not "ready". Interrupts students when they try to talk. Doesn't engage the class. I'm surprised he still has a job.

Awkward cancels class often, is unprepared for lecture, and extremely boring. English 313 had an interesting topic of Oprah and easy novels to read, but I would not take a class with him again. He doesn't have office hours, he never knows what is going on, and is completely unorganized.

Cancels class and assignments a lot, so if you're into that you might enjoy his class.  But he didn't seem to care much about the course or make any lesson plans.  I can say with certainty that I learned absolutely nothing in his course.  Also, he took 2 weeks instead of the maximum 3 days to post our final grades.  Easy class, but really useless.
An extremely disengaged professor; not recommended.
His last name is a bit uncomfortable...
No Comments

Absolute GOAT. One of the best professors I've had here at Stamps so far. Extremely lenient on things, very understanding, and overall just an incredibly fun and entertaining professor (Really, he's fun in a way that keeps your inner child alive and kicking). Plus, you actually gain a lot of great animation experience from his class
Love love love Avery. He's super fun and entertaining.

Avery is by far the best professor I've had at Stamps. Super fun guy and will help you further your portfolio no matter what you're interested in. He cares about his students so much and is such an amazing person to be around let alone have teaching your class. Highly recommend taking any class that he teaches.

I LOVED having Avery in class. He genuinely cared about the students and understood how work heavy animation innately is as a course. I was sick quite a few times and wasn't able to come to class, and he was always understanding. Coming to his class was something I looked forward to. I would definitely take another course with him if I saw it.

Avery is such a good guy and he takes your creativity way more seriously than deadlines. He is also so much fun and brought us chocolate for critiques and did a Mardi Gras parade around the school with us. In a place where a lot of profs make class really stressful, it's nice to have a prof that makes art fun again.

An extremely awful experience. He was very bad at lectures. Relied on textbook and other resources to study. Homeworks were a nightmere, very long and difficult. Exam questions were also super long and difficult. 

If he tried to deliver lectures differently and actually cared for students to understand, I may have had a way better experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The most terrible teacher I have ever seen. Never prepare for his class.
Really an awful teacher. Even being absent for classes for up to three weeks for many different tricky excuses.

An extremely smart professor just doesn't always translate key concepts to the students.  His lectures leave much to be desired and do not help much on homeworks or exams where you mostly have to teach yourself from other textbooks.

Lectures are good, but I feel he doesn't prepare well enough sometimes. He helps a lot in the final project and seems extremely knowledgeable. The homework assignments were tough but you learn a lot solving them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor focus more on the project than the lecture.

The lecture sucks. The professor prepared little for the lecture and there were lots of mistakes in the lecture. According to this, I will give him 1.0/5.0. However, he would help you a lot if you cannot complete the final project. Finally, I rate him 2/5.

Extremely knowledgeable, but utterly disorganized and unstructured. Assignments were very long and time-consuming.  Final project was chaotic with circuit designs changed a week before submission. Audit this class or wait for Professor Hofmann to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Never been more overwhelmed by a class. Midterm avg. was 45% for undergrads. Problem sets took over 20 hours each. PS avg. of 6/10.1 month for our final project, requires controls knowledge and PCB design, not covered. Lectures not helpful, expects you to "figure it out" with no guidance. Had 1 OH/wk. Won't tell us what's on final w/ 1 wk left.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr Purkiss became one of my favorite professors at Umich after I took WGS 322 with her. She is very warm and genuinely cares for her students. WGS 322 was very organized and the criteria for assignments were clear. The material is very interesting and I was always excited for this class each week. Highly recommend WGS 322 & other classes with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Purkiss assigns readings that you'll actually look forward to reading, then creates a safe and supportive discussion environment to talk about the readings. She provides a lot of positive feedback and makes you feel cared for while also maintaining a professional relationship with you. WGS 322 is a must-take!

She is such a good teacher take her seminar classes. Took time to learn all of our names by the second day and truly cares about all of her students. My favorite professor at University of Michigan so far. All pre-health students should take WGS 322

I'm SHOCKED that no one has rated Dr. Purkiss yet. She's an incredible teacher who puts thought into every single assignment and piece of feedback she gives you. All of us in WGS 332 look forward to coming to class and feel comfortable participating during discussions. If you are pre-health you absolutely must take this class, it'll blow your mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Evrard was such a kind and down-to earth teacher when I had him. You can tell he deeply cares about his work and he loves talking about technology which is such a central part to his class. Be warned, however, that he will dissect your work and group projects for this class because of his vast knowledge of the course

In Physics 210, Gus was very fun and caring. He demonstrated awareness of current groups, policies, statistics, and physics. Gus explained that he did not want grades to be a fear factor in this course and provided extra credit opportunities accordingly. Gus prefers shorter project reports, FYI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Gus was a great prof, and this course was actually quite fun. It included a lot of cool demonstrations, clear lectures, a field trip to the campus power plant, and cookies baked for us by his wife. Assignments were pretty easy, and projects allowed for a lot of freedom in topic choice and execution. I definitely recommend taking one of his classes!

This is his first term teaching this energy class. Good sides are: hes extremely nice, knowledgeable, gives extremely helpful information even after the class ends, kept a doc of all the useful things we might need reference, easy grade. Bad sides: I think energy is not really his area, he focuses more on astronomy or physics, class a bit boring.

Great lecturer. Prof Gus is an incredibly approachable and caring professor, and I couldn't have been happier. Physics is not the easiest course but he makes sure his students have all the resources and help they need; would highly recommend him.

Gus is a good guy and a fun lecturer. He cares about how much students learn and gives great feedback. In a class that is mostly dependent on how much effort the student gives, he is there to help anyone who needs it. (He is also a genius and can make you feel dumb because of his overwhelming knowledge bank).

PHY 112 is nice and Gus is a great person! He might be unclear and far off topic sometimes, but he's an amazing human. He wants his students to learn things. But this course is harder than a first year seminar should be. We had papers and group projects that takes a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He can be a little disorganized and confusing, but he's genuinely passionate about his job, willing to help out students (even complete noobs), and the subject material is quite useful and interesting if you put in some effort.
really enjoyed this class. there is little discussion in class which would be helpful, but he is passionate and open to criticism.
Class time could be more organized, but he is a fun and passionate professor

Enthusiastic, entertaining, and very clear.  He makes class enjoyable by being laid back, cracking jokes, telling stories, and doing experiments, all while getting the material across to the students.  He and other professors are very helpful with programming and you really get the hang of it later on.

Interesting and fun class, but a little unorganized. I believe that this was due to it being the first time this class ever existed. However, Professor Gus was really into what he was teaching and I was able to learn a lot.
Incredibly approachable and helpful prof. Lectures might get a little confusing sometimes when he goes off a tangent, but still, its interesting!

Very intelligent, but unfortunately could not always communicate the material in a way I could understand. Always willing to help however, so definitely go to his office hours. Exams are hard, but he gives lots of partial credit. Cool guy overall.

Gus is a great lecturer and he is very, very helpful in office hours. Yes, he puts the students out of their comfort zone by giving hard exams, but since his main concern is helping students learn, he gives great hints for how to study for them beforehand. Take the hints seriously, and you'll do well.

Good professor, though he sometimes assumes the students understand things that they obviously don't.  It's a tough class regardless of which professor you get.  I'd say take it with Gus if you get the chance

He is an awful professor. He wastes class literally 3/4 of his class time with demos and student presentations which he should be spending trying to prepare his class for the exams that are too long and difficult to finish in an hour. Has difficulty following his own notes when in the time he does spend lecturing. Would not recommend this class.

Evrard is very hard and I wouldn't advise for anyone to take his course. He is very into theory and likes long boring derivations on the board. The tests are very hard and rely a lot on material only taught in class. He often states the textbook is too easy.
Gus is a pretty cool dude. He knows his stuff, but doesn't always explain things that clearly. Homework is very doable but tests are hard. Take advantage of his office hours.
Cool sense of humor. Classes were fun

The lectures are good for demonstrations and not a whole lot else. Unfortunately, the Qwizdom policy makes it pseudo-mandatory. The discussion section is definitely the best place to practice and ask questions. The exams aren't all that difficult.

The guy is hot, no doubt, but uses lecture time to show statistics and do cool demos instead of explaining concepts. To get an A in his class, you will need to use ALL available resources: Discussion section professor (if you have a good one), the textbook, the student solutions manual, study groups, and most importantly the Help Room.

Great Teacher, Very Enthusiastic, Very Helpful.  Lectures are mandatory but useful for understanding. Nice guy, really wants you to understand the material and succeed.  Exams are brutally hard, self-admittedly.  Do the problems in the book and pray for a B...

Overall this is a fun class and an interesting teacher. The demos are especially good. However, the thing that gets me is that the exams are unfairly hard, even to the point that the GSIs have trouble deciphering some of the problems. Be wary of that.

Good instructor, overall.  Well paced lectures which covered the major topics of the reading (but you still need to read the book).  Not a bad experience for a huge intro lecture course.  Gus included some interesting demonstrations and quips about cycling.  Tests were tough; homeworks were canned problems from textbook publisher.
Gus is very clear, and occasionally injects some very profound details about the universe into his lectures.
Interesting guy, the subject is hard though.

I graduated from Michigan last year, Gus is one of my first professors, and remain to this day, one of my most memorable professors. He cares about you, how you do in the class, how you learn, he could probably sit with you til 4 AM and explain to you about physics. He's a brilliant researcher and a great teacher.
There was a lot of homework and the tests were pretty hard, but Gus was a good prof.
The best prof I have had so far.  Very clear, lots of fun in lecture. A really nice guy who was super helpful.
Pretty awesome.

Hard exams (and all multiple choice--gross), but a really nice guy, and very understanding and laid back.  My only complaint is that his explanations were a bit too theoretical for my taste (which might stem from him bein an astrophysicist).  I prefered my discussion leader's explanations, which were more analytical and to the point.
