Hard exams, but great lecturer. If you have to take this class, I'd take it with Gus.
PROF GUS IS SO HELPFUL!!! i was going through a rough patch and he was totally considerate with pushing back some of my work and he's HILARIOUS!!

Gus is a likeable guy and his lectures are enjoyable, and, for the most part, informative.  Sometimes he goes off on tangential derivations that make no sense and take half the class period, but he's pretty good at explaining quizdom questions...
rocks my life
Gus is an awesome teacher.  He has great demos in class and clearly loves physics and loves teaching.

Prof. Evrard was great at answering all the questions, he's obviously a brilliant guy, but he pays attention to students. I think this school needs more professors like him. At the end of the day, students go to college to get an education, and Gus does a good job of delivering the key concepts in a lively manner.
Excellent teacher!
Great all around!
Stupidly hard exams, even worse they are multiple choice.  No university should ever give straight multiple choice exams.  As a lecturer though, this guy was quite good and I'd recommend him.

Gus was a great professor, and the demonstrations were very interesting. Physics was rough though, especially the exams. Mastering Physics online problems that were due every week took forever to complete. If you have to take this class take it with Gus.

He's a good teacher. Does a good job at explaining all the concepts with cool demos. He's very animated. However, his exams are pretty tough. And those webhwk sets take forever. This course takes up a lot of time.
He is an amazing professor. I highly reccomend him. I'm not saying that his class is easy but he really knows what hes doing and what hes talking about and hes a great guy.

Let me say this. This class is all indepedent studying so read the stuff before lecture. His class is hard and I'm saying that right now because I took Physics AP in high school. His tests are tough but if you practice and work hard enough, then you should be able to get at least a B or preferably an A.

Gus is a good guy, and he knows his stuff.  The only problem I had with him was the fast that he went waaaayy too fast covering the material toward the end of the year.  If you have him, get ready for the exams because they're tough.  Overall, he was a good professor and is willing to help whenever he can.

Coming from someone who never took high school physics, and w/U of M's overall reputation for difficult physics, Gus was a good professor to have.  He lectured efficiently and clearly.  Sometimes he went a lil' fast and was hard to follow, but for the most part, he was a good & enthusiastic teacher.  His exams can be tough though, so study hard.

Gus is the most terrible professor that ever was.  Physics 140 was way more painful than it needed to be, he never used lecture time efficiently, was never clear when he was lecturing and was all around terrible.  I don't know what other people are thinking on this website, but he is probably the worst human being i've ever met.

Gus is an awful professor.  If lecture was not part of my grade, I would have never gone because his explanations are so short and fast that it's difficult to follow if you haven't read the book beforehand.  All resources, book, help room, professor, are not helpful.  Class was much harder than it should have been.

very good prof. he is very helpful and very clear. he teaches his class with a lot of enthusiasm so it is as fun as physics can be. he does a lot of good demos. if you can take gus, do. his exams are very fair.

He's a really good prof. He moves through his lectures pretty quick sometimes, but he always post the slides on ctools so you can get the stuff you missed. Always does good examples & lots of demos. His exams are very fair, make sure you know the material and you'll do fine. Is very concerned over how students are doing in the class.
He is a really good professor.
Great examples during lectures, colorful teaching style.

He is a great teacher and really seems to love what he is doing.  Physics is extremely painful for me, as I have always hated it but it's required for my major... and I got lucky and picked Gus.  If you go to his office hourse he is so willing to help.
He is willing to help if you go to his office hours. He is understanding and more importantly fair.
Overall, I suppose he was a good professor.

Definitely funny/entertaining and well spoken prof.. Good demonstrations every lab relating to the material. CAP can take up your nights, but makes u learn the material... Curve is a humdinger.. But Evrard doesn't come off as someone who wants to fail you
Generally not too hard.  Curve is a bit ridiculous.  Great teacher.  Excellent demonstrations.
If you have the opportunity, get Gus as a teacher. He explains things well, and he's a funny guy. Very enjoyable!
Great teacher.  If you have the chance, attend one of his lectures outside of class.  He is an astrophysicist for a reason.
great teacher.  This guy made physics sweet...imagine that
Good teacher. Knows his stuff and his lectures are pretty good. the curve can be rough at times
Excellent teacher, probably the best that I have had at Michigan.  Class is difficult because of curve, not poor teaching.

Extremely intelligent professor who knows his stuff.  His tests were difficult and you really had to understand the material to do well.  He explained all the theories well and even had cool demos to illustrate.  The demos about gravity were way cool.

I think, but am not positive, that he was a great teacher. He sounded sure of himself, but I was clueless at all the derivations he wrote on the board that he could have been BSing and I would never have known. Other, smarter people seemed to like him too
One of the nicest profs out there, he really cares about the students.  He really didn't know me well but he went out of his way to write me a letter or rec.  Outstanding person.

Don't listen to the other person, Gus was one of the best teachers I've had at U of M.  He was very into teaching and knew what he was talking about.  The course was challenging, but because he was such a good teacher, it ended up fine.
Horrible

Prof. Demond really isn't that bad. She's a little intimidating and very old school, but overall knows the material and knows how to teach it effectively. Exams are hard, but that's just how the class is.

Prof. Demond is very old school with her printed out notes and written homework. She always gives a good review before exams so you know exactly what to expect. However, she is not the clearest person when it comes to teaching and wastes a bit of time trying to explain things again and typically failing.
Prof. Demond is super clear. You know exactly what to expect on exams and what her expectations are. The class was very old school with handout and overheads.

I thought the class is very good. The topic is very interesting. I like her teaching style very much. She goes over the material on the board very specifically and does a lot of example problems. The exams are difficult only because it is very long and I was prepared for it because of her lectures and the HWs. I do recommend her class.
Took this class in the fall of '05. It was quite difficult but mostly because of the subject matter and not the professor.  I found when all was said and done I had learned alot.
After extremely difficult, oddball homework assignments and huge amounts of reading material, I found myself really unmotivated in this subject area.

One of the worst God-Awful professors this school has somehow managed to employ in a teaching capacity.  I can't even describe it in words... If you have the misfortune of having to take one of her classes, you'll see what I'm talking about.

This instructor was extremely disorganized and unprofessional. He made multiple inappropriate comments to students outside of class or as comments on their papers. He was also very narrow minded when it came to paper topics. Would not recommend taking this class with him at all.

I previously wrote a review on Yamil and would like to tell all those reading it to disregard the previous comment- it was a product of anger &misunderstanding. Truthfully, I think he is a very nice guy and a good GSI- he's very passionate!

I had Yamil as a GSI for an Arab American studies course. Not only is he scattered and confusing in his teaching style, but he is not willing to help his students because he is too busy. If that wasn't bad enough, he is extremely rude and unprofessional.?I wish I had more characters- I would elaborate more!
He was not helpful. Wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you have a strong background in Intl security and Conflict.
He is not helpful! Do not take his class unless you have a strong background in International Conflict and Security. He's insensitive to student needs!

Rather dull lectures and boring class (despite the interesting material), however, great feedback on papers--although usually quite blunt as well. Has vast knowledge of the material, but class can still be very slow and unexciting.
She's very knowledgeable and helpful, always willing to go the extra mile if you are too. She does rely heavily on the reading material though.

She definitely needs to learn TIME MANAGEMENT skills.  She never returned tests promptly or posted material online when she said she would.  Plus she would always stop in the middle of lecture to talk about random things that usually never related to class.  Easy teacher, but I don't have much respect for her
Anne cares a lot for her students, which makes the class easier. She knows what she is talking about.

Anne's more of a friend than a teacher, which isn't always good. We never got back a single graded assignment, which drove me crazy. Email responses are weeks late, or nonexistant. Reading material is paperback novels which she assigns on very short notice. Good books though. I think she forgets we're in a structured society, opposed to Madagascar.
Easy for a nat sci credit. She genuinely cares about the students and really tries to make class interesting.
Easy A, but he LOVES to talk about himself. Only teaches w/ books he's written himself.
He is full of hot air. Talks endlessly...mainly about himself.

Yeah. I did not like the topic of this class, it sounded interesting but I was BORED the entire semester. People spend more time on the internet then they do paying attention. He is a nice guy and very passionate!
HARD. THE TESTS ARE HARD!!!

Great Professor.  He always makes class interesting and he is pretty funny.  If you take a class with him, you will enjoy it.  There are 3 exams and only 2 of them count towards your grade.  There is no papers, but there are 10 quizzes.  If you do the reading, you will do fine in the class.

What an amazing professor and human being. You can tell she really enjoys her work and students. Her classes are always full of meaningful conversations and she is one of the most understanding professors I have had. I would 100% recommend taking her

This is one of the best professors I ever had !! She is such a passionate person and loves what he does and her students. She leads with empathy and makes classes so interesting always going the extra mile to make sure students understand and are engaged!! She rocks !! I would take her again and again!! Love her

I love Ayesha. She prioritizes accommodation and respects students' needs. This class taught me much about social work and hands-on community help. Although the class is three hours, she gave breaks as needed and emphasized being able to step out of class or leave early.

Ayesha was very flexible for due dates and took feedback from students. She's a quality person and had really good assignments. We had one semester long group project where we made a recommendation to the Ann Arbor human rights commission on an issue in Ann Arbor. It was awesome getting real world experience.
I had professor Ayotte for FR231 and 232, although there is lots of homework and stuff, you can tell she cares and wants you to succeed in the class.

She is super engaging and fun, and made me actually enjoy French. I would have considered minoring in French if she taught classes beyond 232. It's a lot of homework, but my French has never been better, and I learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really liked Ayotte and I actually think I improved my french with her. There is HW every day but I think it ends up helping in the long run and it didn't take me too long. Study before the exams but I found her grading to be fair and didn't mind the class. She's down to earth and sometimes funny - would definitely recommend her as a professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: can be hard to get full participation pts but i think that's just the nature of french courses here. she was always open to answer my questions irl or via email. she's very nice and clearly cares about and loves teaching

Overall she's good at teaching the content so it was easy to learn, but her methods can be very frustrating. She lays out everything in a calendar, but frequently changes it including moving quizzes the day or days before which caught me off guard. Lectures aren't recorded and she doesn't post slides so reviewing for tests is incredibly difficult.
Dr. Ayotte was great. She was very passionate about her work and making sure everyone had the right information.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ayotte was a great teacher for FRENCH 103! It is clear how much she cares about students learning the language. She always came prepared. She was easy to access outside of class as well. A bit intense sometimes but kind. Lots of homework but that is just how FRENCH 103 is set up since it is a flipped classroom.
Prof Ayotte is tough but truly wants her students to learn and master French. Get ready to work your butt off for this class, but you will learn a lot with Prof Ayotte.

I really loved French 101 with Dr. Ayotte! She's very enthusiastic and does everything she can to help you learn. You have to participate and speak a lot in class but she creates an environment where you don't have to feel bad about being wrong. Just put in effort and you'll be good. I never dreaded going to class. Can't recommend her enough!

I really really enjoyed Dr. Ayotte's class. I found that with paying attention and attempting to participate, it was made much easier. There's really not as much homework as it seems like, it was manageable. I found her to move at a fast pace, but a pace that I felt was very beneficial to the course. She explains concepts very clearly.

She was a tiny bit mean sometimes, but a good professor and very knowledgeable. There was a very unfair amount of homework for this class. I needed it for my language requirement so it was super frustrating to have to spend hours on French a week but overall it was alright.

Professor Ayotte was always respectful and knowledgable about the content we were learning, and I'd recommend her as a professor. Participation is very important for your grade! French 231 at umich is structured as a flipped classroom right now, so be ready for the homework load to be very heavy and time consuming.

I had her during her first semester at UMICH. Participation is necessary and you BETTER bring the textbook to class. She often plays favorites, but its mainly based on participation. Her class was HW-heavy, but if you do not do it, you can't particpate in class. She wasn't my favorite, but she knew what she was doing and I'd take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Instructions weren't posted on Canvas, causing confusion. Classes often started or ended late, and students were called out for lateness or multitasking, creating a discouraging environment. Clearer communication and respect for schedules would have greatly improved the class.
Great professor. Easy class that covers what premeds need to know

Very useful class.  Rams really cared about the quality of our submitted work, gave us a lot of resources to do well, was really really helpful to the students who wanted to go the extra-mile, was always flexible.. all around great professor and class.

Rams is one of the hardest working and most knowledgeable professors in Chemistry and Biophysics at Michigan. He consistently treats his students with the respect of an equal ? a very admirable quality. He is extremely approachable, caring, and supportive of his students ? always willing to give guidance when/where needed; he is a natural teacher.

Dr. Ramamoorthy is an outstanding research advisor.  He truly cares about his undergrads, and makes sure that I learn the skills I need to learn to be a successful researcher. He wants to see his students succeed, and he is very enthusiastic about everyone's projects.
He was nice enough.  Pretty clear, and helpful to students.  He cares about his students' futures.  He also grades pretty easy.

He's kind of an idiot. He reuses his Chem 453 stuff for Chem 463, so expect a lot of protein folding information. He also forgot to put in our book order, so we didn't get them until late January. He makes you do problems on the board and also uses some of the class examples on his exams - like word for word. Good luck!
Great guy to have for an advisor. The research that his lab does is very interesting, and you will learn a lot of valuable research skills by working for him.
He is extremely good in his work

Lectures make sense after you review the material in the book.  He loves to breeze through derivations, don't get hung up on them, just understand the concepts behind them.  He means well even though this sometimes it seems like he's being mean.  He will make you go to the board to do problems so you get over your fear of being wrong.

Very unpredictable and lazy. His tests aren't supposed to be that hard but sometimes he gives these unexpected questions with a lot of points that people get right for guessing right. So because he is unpredictable he is either very hard or easy depending on how well you catch on with the prof's teaching method and type of exam problems.

Sogabe sensei is all-around a great teacher. She's very engaging during her lectures, always open to questions, and conveys the material clearly. Be prepared to participate and speak entirely in Japanese. It's difficult at first but it really helps your speaking skills to develop.

Sogabe sensei is wonderful and has really helped me better understand the material being taught. She's very engaging in her lectures and keeps the mood of the class fun and lighthearted. Be prepared to participate and speak fully in Japanese. It's difficult at first but it really helps you improve your speaking skills.

I've had nothing but good experiences with Sogabe-sensei. Expect to participate, speak only in Japanese, and come to class prepared, but these all help to improve your language abilities tremendously. She's very funny and keeps class engaging with her enthusiasm. On assignments, she gives great feedback and is fair in grading.

Sogabe Sensei is a sweetheart and an excellent teacher. She speaks rather quickly, which could be a problem if your Japanese understanding is not the best. She can be a tough grader, but whatever, she's great at what she does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sogabe-sensei was great despite there being mandatory attendance, lots of hw and forced participation. This forced me to not be lazy and I truly believe this heavier handed approach bodes well for those who genuinely want to learn japanese. No cake walk but given how different the language is from english the class always felt do-able.
Sogabe-sensei is an amazing professor. Make sure to speak with her about office hours if you need extra help!

SHE IS LEGIT PERFECT... It's hard to get into her discussion sections after the first year due to the fact that she is the best teacher ever (which means something because UM has the best Japanese teachers)

Very sweet and clear during recitation! Always there to help you out! However, she /will/ make you participate, so come prepared. Honestly, this class was my favorite to go to, I always left in a good mood. More like SogaBAE.
Funny and nice. She talks pretty quickly, but teaches pretty well in recitation.

Very funny, sweet and helpful. She seems to really enjoy teaching and was a lot of fun. She is also very willing to help out any student to comes to her with questions, and explains things very easily. If you want to learn, take her class! It's not a guaranteed A, but you will learn a lot from her!
My favorite GSI of all times.
Great instructor! Very helpful and really cares about her students! One of my favorite classes!
I recommend

The best professor I have ever met! He is always available and stayed until very late to answer each student's questions. As a student, I can see his commitment to the course and he is very diligent to teach every class.

Awful professor, didn't even care if the class learned anything, just burping numbers on the board. Group projects were a disaster, no grading criteria, nor explanation. Usual professor that makes exams with things he didn't teach, always arguing with students. As a pro now I realize that most of his material was useless for real pro life.
Great prof.  I recommend highly!
Goker is real nice.  He sticks directly to the lecture slides.  Textbook is optional.  Tests aren't tough and GSI helps a lot for HW help.
well prepared, keeps calm and friendly atmosphere. hardest working person. the kindest person anyone would ever meet.

Goker does a great job explaining the Production and Supply Chain material.  He does a great job of picking out the important stuff from the chapters and simplifying it.  It’s possible to not read at all and do fine in the class, the material is pretty straight-forward (and he does a great job teaching).

I don't know if I am talking about the same Goker as the people who rated him above, but his class is terrible, and he is difficult to understand.  The homeworks are very difficult, and his lectures are very boring.
One of the best professors in IOE dept., smart and confident, be very helpful to students inside and outside of the class, and very charming!
No Comments

Always ready to go out of his way to help students even in class...and sometimes ends up not having enough time to do all what he wanted in a lecture. Very available. Exams and howework are challenging and long so beware. Overall a good professor.
Best professor at UM, very kind and understanding and the topics covered in class were very interesting!!  Highly Recommend!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very nice lecturer, super generous grading. It would be even better if attendance is not mandatory. Still highly recommended.

This class was really good and very informative. The beginning of the semester was very much based on online textbooks and assignments revolving around that, but after the midterm, the workload lessened.

Prof Azmeh is kind and a good lecturer, she always tries to keep the class interactive and interesting. I did have some issues but I'll give her the benefit of the doubt since it was her 1st semester teaching! This class was fairly easy so I'd recommend it if looking to fulfill HU reqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Never had a more chill teacher. Hilarious lectures, always encourages participation, and taught us how to juggle. Genuinely reads and responds to every submission, doesn't care about silly things like personal pronouns or grammar, and I'm fairly certain my entire class ended with an A+. Please give her the respect she deserves!

She is genuinely one of the funniest teachers ever and emphasizes socratic learning in the classroom and doesn't really assign a ton of work outside of class. We never had to read outside of class and assignments were spread out so I never felt overwhelmed.

Dr. Bardolph is extremely relaxed, comical, and understanding; her lectures are more socratic, chalkboard-based. She's made me more confident in my ability to critically analyze rhetoric across research studies, classical texts, and modern media. Grading is mostly weighted by 2 essays (with revisions) plus attendance. P.S. you may learn to juggle!

Dr. Bardolph is amazing! She made the lectures interesting and enjoyable. I really enjoyed my time in her class and the things we discussed have helped me a lot. She is very friendly and always willing to talk about literally anything!

Professor Bardolph is genuinely one of the best professors that the school has to offer. She takes a seemingly mundane and boring class (ENG125), and adds so much complexity and thought into how to develop our rhetoric to gain a better understanding of writing and academic inquiry. Also an extremely sweet lady and clearly cares for her students!

Very light workload and engaging lectures made her class the highlight of otherwise tough days for me. She assigns work qualitatively with succinct but thoughtful guidelines I found nice. Hands down the perfect FYWR class you could take.
Such a great professor for first-year writing (ENG 125). Interesting topics are discussed, and not a class that will cause you any stress.
One of the best professors the universities has, hands down.

Prof Bardolph is so sweet and cares so much about the well-being of her students! She barely gave any work outside of class. The class was not super helpful in improving English skills and focused more on rhetoric which is not what I had expected, but she made it pretty enjoyable. Class is very very easy and not much is missed if you skip lecture.
Professor Bardolph was amazing! She is extremely passionate about the topics and her students' success.

She has trouble conveying simple ideas to students and makes frequent mistakes in lecture. It seems as though she does not double-check her notes before class, which I found to be rather unprofessional.  Overall, a sub-par lecturer and mathematician.

Though she is not the best lecturer, and she does have a turkish accent, the material is not too difficult to learn on one's own. As long as one does their online homework, they should do fine. Learn the material on your own, then come to lecture to do practice problems which are rather helpful. Do no expect to learn in lecture.

She is not a great lecturer, but not a bad one. My only problem is that she would make simple calculation errors during lectures, but don't make those errors on the exam or you will be penalized horribly.

Makes tons of mistakes on during lectures and therefore, is really hard to follow. You have to teach yourself a lot out of the book.  I have a bunch of friends in the class that don't show up anymore and just learn from the book.

Her lectures are simply uninteresting and difficult to follow. She makes a fair amount of mistakes and doesn't stray very far from her notes. She also has a tendency to answer questions not by directly addressing the question, but by repeating the last couple minutes of lecture, which is generally unhelpful.

Hard to understand her accent, hard to read her hand writing. Often during class she makes computational mistakes. I stopped going to class, and instead read my book during the time I would have been in class. I had improvements in homework, lab, and test grades.
Wastes time during lecture, unclear explanations, makes computational errors several times every lecture. The worst professor I've had so far, do not recommend.

Really disliked her teaching - lectures were unclear, she skipped two sections' worth of material because she was so behind schedule, and the number of mistakes she makes is terrifying. It was almost painful to see her teach. Ended up going to another prof's lecture instead. She made MATH 216, supposedly an easier class, a struggle to get through.

She sometimes has a tough time explaining concepts and doesn't always write very clearly on the board, but she is clearly trying to improve. Overall a very nice teacher who cared whether her students did well or not. She just has a few things to work on.
Cannot count on the lectures because she is unclear and hard to follow. Her writing was so light on the board. She is unwilling to post her notes.
Probably the best of the Calc IV professors at umich. Everything that appears on the exam is covered in lecture. It is important to read the textbook before lecture or else you'll be lost.
Professor Bulut's lectures were sometimes hard to follow, but she meant well and cared about the success of her students.

I thought she was a great teacher who really understood the topics and made them easy to understand. She was unintentionally funny which made lectures interesting. I could tell that she really cared about our understanding of the topics. Yes she would make mistakes, but who doesn't, and she encouraged us to tell her when she did make a mistake.

She was a lot better than people give her credit for. She meant well and wanted students to learn. She always wanted students to participate to show that they were keeping up with the material. Also, the test averages for her classes were higher than for the other sections with different teachers.

Not very good at explaining material and rushes toward the end of the lectures. If you take this class with her you def. need outside help (internet or office hours, textbook sucks) and can't rely on the lectures. I heard she's good 1 on 1 in OH but I prefer to learn my math via clear instruction in lectures so I ended up disliking the class...

Professor Bulut was a pretty good professor. She was very dedicated to the class, always prepared to lecture, would really, really want to see her students succeed. Though she sometimes went too fast in lecture (especially at the end of class) her office hours were SUPER helpful. Make a point to go to office hours - she gives you one-on-one help.

She has a slight accent. She really wasn't a great lecturer. Often made mistakes on crucial concepts. Over the course of the semester she got better however if possible I personally recommend another professor if given the opportunity

TERRIBLE! I learned more while teaching myself from the book than ever I did in class. She teaches in the least common-sense way and forces people to participate in a big lecture. If they answer questions incorrectly she is condescending and says "this is easy" or "you should know this". She has an accent but in my opinion it wasn't too bad.
Best professor I've had. Very clear in her explanations. Definitely take her

A very unhelpful instructor. She frequently claims that “this is so simple” even though she constantly make computational errors. She does not explain examples on new topics and is very hard to follow her work (a 9 looks like a g, while a g looks like a p in her writing). She embarrasses students for an incorrect answer never questions her own work

Possibly the WORST professor I've ever had. She wastes so much time in lecture asking questions about things we haven't learned yet, and says "this is easy" when it's actually not. She makes computational mistakes all the time and the flow of lecture and the way she explains things makes no sense.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR IF AT ALL POSSIBLE! Her lectures are unhelpful and often confusing. Rather than answering questions, she just tells you that "it's easy" and "you should know this" (even if it's completely new material). She has a thick accent, so it is often hard to understand her. Do yourself a favor and avoid her.

Worst teacher I have ever had.  She frequently insults students and complains when students (involuntarily) are forced to help and are wrong.  Thick accent.  Lectures are verbatim from the book and she still make mistakes computationally.  When she is wrong, she looks at her notes and says that the student is wrong without considering.  Avoid!
Not only is she unhelpful when it comes to explaining even basic concepts, but she is consistently rude to students who ask questions, saying "you should know how to do this already."
not super great. fairly thick accent. lectures weren't that good
Unhelpful and poor at explaining, doesn't understand questions and inadequately answers them. Would not recommend

He has good lectures, is willing to answer questions, and dedicates a lot of time to practice and drilling. He also is accessible outside of class, but the main issues are he is very strict with attendance and the homework and quizzes are graded on a check system that only he understands (so you never know your grade in the class).
Look up AI Lawsuit for Greatbooks at umich

His lectures just had nothing to do with our essay prompts, which was our entire class grade and also incredibly difficult and unorganized. A different teacher came and taught for a week and she was much better than him. Would be a good class otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Dufallo's lectures had nothing to do with our essays. Grade depends on GSI, but if you go to him to contest it, he'll take the side of the GSI without listening to your argument. Currently a lawsuit regarding the fact that he wouldn't hear students side of an "AI Scandal" where all the students didn't use AI and he refused to hear them out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overall pretty easy class but it very much depends on your GSI. I had Carrie and she was an easy grader fortunately. Lectures were pretty interesting and funny at times. Readings were interesting!

Prof. Dufallo gave really in depth lectures. He is clearly very knowledgable on the subjects he is teaching. This course is really book heavy (9 ish books) and has a lot of papers. Your grade is dependent on your GSI and they can take a really long time to grade papers which can set you back. Great class if you're interested in classics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Dufallo was one of the most passionate professors I've had. He clearly loves the topic, and that shows through the class. The reading was never excessive. However, the general organization of the class was tough to navigate, and the prompts felt extremely vague. Professor Dufallo was very flexible, though, and willing to help if needed.

Prof Dufallo is very knowledgeable and passionate about his subject, but the reading assignments are excessive and unmanageable, you are expected to read a book in 2 days to spend one lecture discussing and never revisit. Paper prompts are obscure and difficult and never relate to what we do in class. Nothing felt consistent. Grade depends on GSI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Dufallo is a great classics professor, but as a first year writing course his lectures often become misguided regarding the essay prompts. Grade depends on GSI. Strict technology policies and he also as a rather strict AI policy, as a bunch of kids this semester were accused of using AI falsely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed attending Professor Dufallo's class! I appreciated that he clearly likes the material and wanted us to enjoy it, too, and I feel as though I learned a lot. The discussions were interesting, though they could get a tad boring at times, and the essays weren't overly difficult. Participation is a huge percentage of your grade!

As someone not super interested in Classics, I'd say Prof Dufallo did a pretty good job getting me engaged. There is a decent amount of reading, but I'd say it's pretty manageable. Pay attention in lecture, he gives good prompters for your essays. Didn't love the no electronics policy or limited office hours. Otherwise, good prof.

Honestly, Dufallo was my favorite professor of my first sem, and this was a course I won't forget. Not only did I learn about Shakespeare, I also learned about society in general. This was a great course, taught by someone who was encouraging and supportive of whatever the class did. Dufallo is super cool, gives big Shakespeare dad energy.
It is clear that Professor Dufallo loves the classics and was very excited to share his knowledge with students. I felt encouraged to ask questions and pursue the material further.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great books is a course with sooooo many papers but it is my favorite course of the semester. Dr. Duffalo is so engaging and his lectures are awesome, even at 9 am. If you are an honors student who does not like to write or read, do not take this class. But I loved this class so much and will recommend it to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Dufallo is very knowledgeable about the classics, and his expertise definitely comes through in his lectures. Sometimes, though, the lectures can feel disconnected from paper prompts, leading to the lectures seeming a bit misdirected. Quizzes for every lecture. Don't necessarily have to read the assigned readings throughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Exudes Shakespeare dad energy (Take him, youll understand lol)
Really enjoyed the open discussions/lectures, its mainly him walking everyone through the chapter that was assigned and then adding in connections/context. I lowkey just read the SparkNotes/lit charts for the entire semester but as long as you understand what happened youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made Shakespeare super enjoyable to learn about, very nice and caring - he never pressured anyone to talk and never made anyone feel like their point was wrong. We had really fun & interesting discussion and debates, and he grades pretty easily on essays while giving good feedback. Definitely looking to take another class with him in the future!

I really liked Prof. Dufallo, despite not caring that much about the class. He was obviously passionate about his work and treated his students with so much respect. Shame he's a classics prof, as I would take more courses with him if I could.

i only took this class because it was the only first-year writing requirement still open. i ended up loving it and still remember his lectures over a year later! very inspirational course but not too heavy in workload.

I am not a fan of Greek literature, but Professor Duffalo did an amazing job at keeping it interesting. Ill admit, many students tend to skim readings and read summaries, but it doesnt really impact your grade as long as you generally know whats going on in the readings (which Duffalo often summarizes). The papers were surprisingly fun to write!

Two lectures with Professor Dufallo, and two discussions with a GSI each week. Lectures were always very engaging. There were iclicker quizzes for attendance every lecture. Lots of reading and 4 papers + revisions. Both the professor and GSIs were always available to meet and help with papers. A great class if you come prepared to read and write!
A lot of dad vibes, he makes Shakespeare enjoyable to talk about and never makes anyone feel like their point is bad or wrong. A pretty easy grader, but gives good insight for good writing.

He's SUPER knowledgeable about his field. This class had a lot of papers and readings, but honestly, you don't have to do every reading to do well in the class. He seems like a super nice person, although with virtual semester I didn't interact with him much. Enjoyed it for a class I didn't want to take, great prof overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great class discussion. Duffalo combines ancient Rome & Greece with Shakespeare in an interesting manner. Essays are graded generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I took his 1st Year Seminar, COMP140. Liked it so much that I took CLCIV102, then CLCIV350. Now I'm minoring in Classics. Lectures enjoyable, slides aren't pretty but are posted+useful. Essays are kind of tedious at 100 level, but graded fairly; exams are comprehensive but straightforward. Basil's a great guy who clearly loves teaching the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dufallo did a good job presenting the material, which I found interesting. He seemed interested in how well his students did in the class and open to discussion about exams, lectures, etc.

Great professor who cares about students. Does well in making material interesting that may be dry to some (Roman history). Not too hard if you keep up on readings, go to/participate in discussion, and use the history well in papers

I love Dufallo! I took CLCIV350 with him specifically because I loved his freshman seminar (COMPLIT 140). He's so passionate about his lectures that it's impossible not to be engaged. Essays are super easy A's if you know words and have a basic understanding of the material, and he tells you exactly what the exam will be. A great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Basil's a sweet dude. He knows more about Greek and Roman history than any one I've met. His test was surprisingly a bit tough but if you pay attention in class it's not too bad. The course is a bit dry but if you like history it can be really interesting. The readings are relatively short and not extremely important. All in all I learned a lot.
this was a good class if you are interested in the subject matter but if you arent then you will be bored

I had Dufallo for a CompLit class on Shakespeare. Given I like Shakespeare, it was a very interesting class. We read 5 plays and wrote 3 papers. He graded the papers pretty easily. The only other grades were very simple weekly blog posts and participation. If you like Shakespeare, I recommend the class. We spent most of the class time in discussion

Professor DuFallo is an interesting, engaging and passionate lecturer. He presents information in a clear, concise way and lets you know what's important/ what's going to be on the test. I recommend taking his classes!

PROFESSOR DUFALLO IS AN AWESOME LECTURER! The class was very interesting and engaging, and he went out of his way to explain things and engage students in active discussion. Even though there is SOME studying to be done, its nothing hard that you can't revise for the day before. Best humanities distribution you'll ever take!

Professor Dufallo's class was extremely interesting and he is so knowledgeable. I have no idea why people seemed to miss lecture a lot but they missed out on some great lectures. I would highly recommend this course. It was not super difficult and I learned so much.
No Comments

Really enjoys teaching poetry, and gives a lot of credit to students' ideas and interpretations of Latin poets.  A fair amount of reading was required, and class time was spent translating line-by-line, which was helpful.  In depth discussion of poetry took up much of class, but it was a breath of fresh air from having to translate all day long.

Basil is the worst professor i've had at Michigan.The class is terribly boring.Basil took a facinating subject like Roman History and made me hate it. There is a midterm and a final. Both require you to know over 200 terms.Ridiculos.There is an essay component to both exams, and the final has an additional long essay. Way to much work to do well.

Terrible class. Professor took an interesting topic and made it extremely dull, dry, and boring. There is a midterm, final, and 2 6-page papers due. A ton of material has to be known for the midterm, and even more for the final--totally ridiculous to expect any student to retain the amount of info that you have to for the final. STAY AWAY

Some lectures were really interesting and some not so much. The class was really fair, the exams weren't that tough. I took it honors, and the essays were graded pretty harshly, but other than that the class was pretty easy. He posts most of lecture info on Ctools. I enjoyed the class. Duffalo is interesting, funny, and loves the subject.
No Comments

This is an easy class. Prof Barzilai is nice, but her lectures are a bit surface-level and don't bring much depth to the topic. She relies heavily on student discussions to fill the time. Honestly, I didn't feel like I took away much from the course. Homework is graded generously.

Professor Barzilai was an amazing lecturer and teacher. If you have the chance to take Conflicts and Comics with her I couldn't recommend it enough, just know that you will have to participate and you will have one group presentation! Overall she is lovely and accommodating, and very open to feedback. Take the course!

Professor Barzilai genuinely cares about her students. There was a lot of reading involved in this class, but if you are passionate about Middle Eastern culture and conflicts, the readings go by quickly. She is accessible and displays colorful passion for the subject and artform. She is open-minded and encourages genuine discussion.

Maya's lectures for Jewish Film History were well organized and prepared. She was very knowledgeable. Her lectures are very participation/ discussion heavy, which is nice.  She is very caring and is conscious of the variety of viewpoints in the room. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Maya was great. Make no mistake, she has little time for goofing off and a keen sense of who is actually participating. If you show up and treat the class like a joke, she is unforgiving. However, if you demonstrate you're willing to put in the effort, she is incredibly kind and accommodating. Just be ready for some very blunt feedback.

Maya was alright at best. Her requirements are very vague and her worksheets that she hands out do not prepare you well for the quizzes and tests. Overall, she had good intentions but her execution was poor.

I feel like she knows a lot about the specific subject matter she specializes in but not a lot about the material surrounding it. In her Jewish Comic Books course, it felt like she knew a lot about comic books but not a lot about the Jewish theology that went in to the making of those comics and it showed in the discussions.

Nice lady who cares about the subject matter a lot. Can seem a bit condescending at times but that's just her personality. She wants students to do well. Just follow everything in the syllabus and you'll do well.

Maya really wants her students to do well. She sometimes can be unclear about requirements of assignments, but really all she wants of you is to participate in class. Going to office hours DEFINITELY helps, more so bc she'll probably give you a better grade on a paper. Overall I would recommend her. I had her for a small section and really like her
Don't treat it like a high school class or you'll get a B and feel silly. She's nice.

The class is run in Hebrew.  There is a super relaxed atmosphere, and it's comfortable to practice your Hebrew.  You have to do the minimal homework/readings to participate in class discussions, but like..you can get away without doing it until the (short) essays and 2 tests.  Maya is a nice person and 301 and 302 have been good experiences.

Great professor. Highly knowledgable about theoretical statistics and offers great advice. He occasionally goes on tangents during lecture, but always comes across as warm and helpful. Relatively low-workload class if you pay attention in lecture, fairly methodic exams.

Mouli is actually knowledgeable and kind. However, he tried to teach us too many concepts, and was kind of disorganized. The intention was good though, and the concepts he taught were actually pretty interesting and shall be useful in statistical research. For first-time learners, it did take us efforts to reorganize and understand the whole story.

The homework problems are well designed. However, completing the homework alone is not sufficient preparation for the exams. It is important to also spend time summarizing the key points from the corresponding textbook chapters. With sufficient effort, the outcome can be very good; without it, performance may suffer significantly.
He is a very kind and knowledgable professor, but he is quite disorganized. Tests and HW are quite difficult.

Easily the funniest professor I've ever had. Very entertaining lectures. The homework and exams are very tough since Mouli is quite crafty when writing questions. When you solve a question, you get a massive dopamine hit and life becomes good again. Strongly recommend you take this class with him.

Mouli was one of my favorite professors I've ever had, and is a hilarious guy who doesn't take life too seriously. His exams and homework are definitely very challenging, and this one of the hardest classes I've taken at U of M. However, if you really put in the work you will learn a lot.

Great theoretical statistics professor. Homeworks and exams are extremely difficult, but figuring them out feels like solving a challenging puzzle - satisfying but frustrating. His lectures are okay, but truly shines in OH, as he links each underlying concept in more depth. 
My only caveat is he's occasionally disorganized, so be prepared ahead.
Best class and best professor ever!
Prof Banerjee is the best. He explains everything in a very clear manner. He is also very entertaining and funny. 10/10.
Prof Banerjee's lectures are always informative and entertaining. Best Statistics professor at UM.
Prof Mouli likes to grade the midterms.

He is funny and seems like a great guy. He goes really fast, but cares about students succeeding. GSIs grade everything, which is pretty standard for stats, but can be reached outside of class as well.
Best class I've taken as a PhD student at U.M. I always looked forward to his lectures. Take his class whenever you get a chance (stats undergrads: please take STATS 426 with him if possible!)
His courses are taught but truly helpful and inspirational. You will love the course if you truly love statistics
Banerjee really needs to enunciate more clearly and pause often between concepts.  Otherwise, he would run on and on and on.  I thought he would have improved his teaching techniques by now.

Your favorite professor's favorite professor. If you are a serious Stats student you will like Mouli, if you are trying to skip class and cram for exams you will not like him very much. Overall good but the textbooks/readings he assigns are terrible
Assigns tough homework problems but you learn a lot as a result. Generous grader. If you're comfortable with math/stats his lectures are good

Out of all of the professors I've had at Umich, he is the worst by far. He doesn't give clear indications of what sections of the text book are being covered, he doesn't give any idea of what will be tested on the exams, and gets frustrated with you when you ask questions in lecture or office hours. He is extremely unclear and condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are an information dump about his entire knowledge of statistics, with little regard of the fact that he's supposed to teach. He talks too fast, so it's easy to lose track of what he's saying, or if what he's saying is even relevant. He also tends to make his explanations too complicated, making me question whether he knows his stuff.
Take Mouli for Stats 425. He is an awesome professor. Respond email quickly and treat student with respect. Amazing lecture and a little homework.
His course is hard, but he is a generous grader. He cares for students' success. His course is tough because he is so intelligent, and he doesn't become aware he makes things challenging.
He goes so fast and is quite rude to students in class. Homeworks are incredibly hard and so are the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Moulli is a good professor, if not a little fast. It is clear he understands what hes talking about and is definitely willing to spend time with students. Personally, it took me a second look at the notes and a rewatch of the lecture before I really followed along. Maybe not the best teacher Ive ever had, but certainly a brilliant prof

Run. He is the worst professor I ever had. His own style of teaching is very confusing and hard to follow. He used a lot notions without explain what they were, and his exams and homework are extremely difficult. If you can't avoid him, my suggestion is to try to understand every problem appeared on homework and exams and go to GSI's office hour.
He is very good.

Don't want to comment on the quality of the lectures. He spent one-third of the semester on 425 (prob.) stuff and ended up having no time left for hypothesis testing. And usually, we've got to learn a load of course materials on our own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures were extremely unclear, he constantly jumps around. I came out of lecture more confused about the material. The exams were way harder than the practice exams he gave out. He gets visibly annoyed when people can't keep up with him on the material. At least he gives a decent curve.

His lectures are confusing. His homework and practice exam questions are confusing. Even the solution to the homeworks and exams are confusing. His office hour only makes you more confused. Overall, he is a confusingly terrible professor. Through the semester, even if I get an A, I still have to say I never understood what did he talked about.

The worst professor and human I have ever met. Hard to understand. He expects you to know everything and gets frustrated when you ask questions in office hours. Poor communication- does not answer emails, does not communicate about lectures with students, etc. I would suggest doing everything humanly possible to avoid crossing paths with him.
Great Professor, confusing material but he's a very generous grader. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A masterful professor. I took his class some time ago, and I still reflect on it as one of my best college classes. I know a lot of people do not like him, but (I think) it is because the class isn't easy. That does not make him a poor teacher though. After all, I want U of M to be a place where the best students are challenged to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: His notation is so confusing, and he does not make any indication when he switching to a new concept or problem. He doesn't specify what any symbols mean either. Definitely recommend looking up stuff on the internet if you are stuck. He cares about his students' success, and can be helpful in office hours.
Focuses on the theory, and homeworks can be tricky. However, exams were fair (tested only on questions from homework or lecture) and were heavily curved.

Bane of my existence. I have never had such a horrible and unclear professor. He does not describe concepts clearly and homework is generally vague. Either stay away from his classes or get Chegg  The final was two questions worth 40% of my final grade. Upside, the class is heavily curved.
Mouli is a skilled lecturer; he presents the information clearly and grades fairly. Although some of the material is tough to grasp, it's clear that Mouli cares about his students' success.

Lectures were kinda incoherent and lacking in structure; math was written on the board but there was no explanation of how it all tied together. Not much correlation between what was covered in class and on the exams/homework. Office hours changed every week, making it hard to get help.

Banerjee basically wrote proofs on the boards the whole class and spent very little time actually teaching the material on the exams and homeworks. Therefore, when we were given actual problems, most of the students had no idea what to do. Also having 80 of the class based off of 3 exams is outrageous. Please avoid.

Be prepared, this prof doesn't pull many of his punches.  Expect this course to be very theoretical, and quickly paced.  A couple of good points are the statistics notes he posts on the web.  If you miss something in class, it's rather easy to read over the notes and understand it on your own.  He covers few proofs, so be prepared to work them out.

Topic is very theoretical. He talks fast, and is passionate about statistics. But the lectures are hard to follow if you don't prepare before class. Homeworks are a great deal of work. Open book exams make exams easier. Not many topics covered (about half of what is listed on the course guide) but goes in depth.

Pretty tough.  HW is very time consuming and somewhat frustrating.  Exams are more of the opposite, they are reasonable.  Teaching style could be more clear.  Hard to pick it up the first time in class.  He is good for offering challenges, but if you want something easy, you should check elsewhere.

The amount of readings given for this class is inconceivable for a three-credit course. The first class she said that there won't always be readings, that is a lie. There are multiple readings every class. She says that there will occasionally be pop quizzes. Also a lie. They are every. single. class. Attendance is mandatory. 

Passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Koremenos was very frequently late in arriving to class, which is bewildering. When she did finally show up, she was repeatedly rude and condescending to students, especially to anyone who asked completely legitimate questions during class. She clearly did not want to be teaching. She should go find a different line of work.
doesn't explain grading criteria and couldn't work a computer to save her life

Objectively one of the worst profs I've ever had. Extremely unorganized and unprofessional. Consistently late to class and late to posting assignment instructions. Overly harsh grader for an intro course. After saying all semester there wouldn't be a final, she decided to change her mind on the last day of class and have one anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst ever, changed everything last minute and graded harshly based on an assumption that the class was using AI. Did not even give us a review for the final and changed all of the weights for the assignments and the final after she promised the final was only 10% of our graded.
Not very clear, changed syllabus at the end of course
Worst professor I ever had

While it pains me to rate Professor Koremenos this low since she shows a clear love for political science, the grading for this class is completely unacceptable. Multiple students have received Fs on writing assignments without clear reason as to why and a final was added on the last day of class. The class was extremely disorganized as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrendous professor who was unorganized, rude to students, and overall made the learning environment difficult and frustrating. Consistently stressed the importance of our homework assignments, writing assignments, and group projects because there was no final exam for the class, then surprised us with a final on the last day of class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She changed our final assignment on the last day of class. She never went by the dates she set on the syllabus and released assignments much later, and never gave extensions. For an assignment, she made us read HER book for an assignment. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This is your final warning.

This was the worst course I've EVER taken. She is extremely disorganized and unclear. At the end of the last class, she announced that we were going to have a final, even though the whole semester she claimed we should work harder because we WOULDN'T have a final. Nothing was ever graded in a timely manner, and was insanely hard for an intro class.

The structure of this class is vague, and I didn't learn much about world politics. She focused most of the class on two main group projects. One was related to world politics, and the second was on solar geoengineering- way too much time was spent on research that has little connection to world politics. She added an EXAM the LAST day of class.

Terrible professor, never had a clear plan. Changed instructions, and decided to give us a final exam the last day of class. Awful instruction, the class made no sense most of the time. Take literally any other intro polisci course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Randomly decided the last day of class that we were having an exam. Not accessible outside of class at all, does not host consistent office hours and won't respond to email. Clearly does not care. And, she'll be rude to you about being confused by the super unclear and hastily made instructions for assignments.

This is probably the worst class I've ever taken. Koremenos was severely underprepared for lecture and our assignment. She made instructions very vague, even for our big group projects that are a good portion of our grades. She changed instructions to part of our first group project the day before it was due and after I had already submitted it.

She's Very smart but doesn't belong teaching 100 level class. Has no idea how to use technology and assignment directions are always extremely unclear. Directions are typically posted after assignments have already been started and even then are unhelpful. Avoid and take American politics or comparative politics, trust me.

She is a very scatterbrained person, who primarily focuses on her own theoretical framework. While this could be interesting content, it is not fit for an intro level class. The assignments given do not focus on anything in the textbook, rather her own book which is not a page turner.

She is very passionate about political science, but the class is so extremely disorganized. There are no exams and instead, it is just papers and group assignments. However, the rare time she posted the assignment prompt on time it was not even the correct one. Save yourself, do not take this class with her.

Professor K is highly unorganized and unclear. She is late to post all prompts and assignments and is unclear in her directions. She also lacks clear communication with the GSI. This has been my least favorite class so far at UMich. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Professor Koremenos IS an expert in political science. However, she is not fit to instruct an intro class. Her lecture style stems directly from the textbook, and she makes attendance mandatory for every class. During my term, she fell behind in posting materials without fixing any due dates.Take any other intro course, or you will loathe polsci.

Miserable class and miserable professor. She is the worst and I recommend you take literally any of the other 3 intro level classes for the POLSCI major. Her grading is not clear and is overly harsh considering they are usually not based on lecture material and lectures are all over the place and terrible anyway.

Poli Sci 160 has no exams. Just group projects and individual writing assignments. The information covered in lectures and homework assignments is just not useful for the group projects or writing assignments. Don't bother reading the textbook, either. Prof Koremenos is nice and passionate about world politics, but does not teach this class well.

Literally just reads from the slides and gets mad when no one understands what she is talking about. It's an easy A class, but there are a couple papers that she doesn't explain well that are hard. Worst professor I've had.

She's pretty terrible, the department should not be letting her teach this intro class. She picks favorites and just is not a good teacher. Grades way too harshly for such dumb 100 level class. As interesting as world politics sounds, she makes this class miserable and you should take American and Comparative politics for your major, not this!!

Horrible professor. Disorganized, taught stuff that was not relevant to the textbook or the class, and basically gave no work before spring break, while loading students with weekly papers or projects each of the last eight weeks of the semester. In addition, she graded insanely harshly, taking off points for minor deviations from the prompts

Dr Koremenos is disorganized, unpredictable and unhelpful... Her lectures are like she's reading straight from the powerpoint notes and it was hard to email with her about anything. The gsis are the only ones who knew what was going on/were helpful. Avoid this class if you can

didnt give us a syllabus until a month in. syllabus was incorrect. writing assignments were given without clear instructions until halfway into the writing process. came in during exam week for presentations because class was poorly planned (not enough time because we did nothing for all of march) and assigned writing prompts after class was done

Do not take this class unless you're a serious student who is willing to work hard and read up on the issues at hand. I found myself spending considerably more time on work for this course than on many of my others combined. But the work was intensive, rewarding, and informative. If she likes you, she will be your best ally.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. She gave us multiple group projects with less than a week to do them. The MWrite program was poorly organized as well, and the graders did not know the material very well. She makes it very clear that she thinks students are entitled, and that heavily influences her grading. Do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I wish she would have told us in the course description that this was an M-Write course; I never would have taken it. We had to write papers based on "scientific evidence" from the lectures, when there wasn't any. She was also always late due to a "technical issue". If it happens every day, then sign on early! How hard is that?!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The lectures were surprisingly clear but the lack of organization was stressful. No full syllabus or rubrics for assignments, no clear link for Zoom/BlueJeans (switched between the two all semester), GSI & Prof were not on the same page, assignments were due at the same time, & constructive criticism was not taken well. Frustrating class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof K is a really nice woman and it is clear she cares about her work and this course, but it was often disorganized. dont take this class if you dont care about the topic. the content itself i liked, but finding expectations for assignments etc. was the difficult part

I found Koremenos to be disorganized and unclear. Due dates and descriptions of assignments were not given or changed frequently. No syllabus was given to start and when it was it did not match the Canvas due dates. She made tons of assignments due together and was very rude when hearing student's concerns. A very tough grader for easy concepts.

Fully online. While I should note that Prof. Koremenos was always kind and hard-working herself, the class itself felt very disorganized sometimes. Due dates and paper assignments (some of which, 3-4 in a week) were often unclear, and it was occasionally difficult to get in contact. Brilliant, brilliant woman, but online class didn't work great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: More than a month and a half into class, and wrong Zoom and BlueJeans links are still being sent out. I'm sure the GSI strike didn't help, but Professor Koremenos and her GSI are somehow still struggling with the online technology. Would not recommend taking this class while it is still online due to her incompetence and failure to prepare.
The professor's expectations were very unfair and unclear, especially in light of the Pandemic.

Koremenos taught all her own theory, even thought the designated textbook was much more clear. Although I think she we would be great at upper level 400 Polsci classes, I am not a major and she did not know her material well. Students correct her on topics quite often during lecture. Want to get an A? Hard, but possible and not clearly defined.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Exams were so arbitrary and all she talked about was her own book. Don't even know what I could've done to prepare because the exam questions were always so vague. You also never knew what to expect with the pop quizzes. I'm disappointed because the course content was interesting but Koremenos presented it in the most boring way.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof Koremenos ended up being one of the best professors I have ever had. She draws real life examples to help you memorize concepts; and while the reading is usually rigorous, the expectations for what you take from them are manageable. You do have to come to class for pop quizzes, but you are not penalized for wrong answers. She is great.

This was my favorite class at Michigan. Prof K allowed the class to be flexible according to her students' interests and current events while still providing a great foundation that lead up to our final paper (personal research). She has inspired me greatly to continue a career in academia. I can't recommend her enough.

I'm sad to see what people have written about Prof K. She teaches her theory because it is thorough and foundational. You don't have to write down much from the slides if you do the readings. If you are actually interested in IR and aren't just taking this as a blow-off, Prof K can be one of your greatest resources at U of M. Go to office hours!!!!

It pains  me to rate Prof. Koremenos this low, because I think she's a good person and cares about her students. It isn't a hard class, but it was boring and the material was common sense to the point of dissuading me from taking another political science class. This was her first time teaching 160, though, so I hope it improves with time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Koremenos takes an extremely interesting topic almost unbearable. She teaches her own theories which takes away the objectivity of the material. Lectures are boring. She also goes through the slides too fast, and then she leaves out the important information on the ones she uploads online making it difficult to study effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Koremenos made one of my favorite subjects pretty boring. Lectures were very dry and repetitive and the grade was based mainly off small 10 question pop quizzes. Wouldn't recommend

Professor Koremenos is more concerned with her own attendance numbers than the success of her students. She doesn't post powerpoints to the student site, and goes through them far too quickly in lecture, preventing students from taking complete notes and making studying difficult. Large portions of grades are determined by pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Literally this is the most boring class I've ever been to. She drones on about obvious, common sense ideas that you don't even need to be taught. We literally just learned directly from the textbook and the only reason to go to lecture is because of the random pop quizzes given at the end of lecture that are stupid easy. This class waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was an excellent class and Prof. Koremenos is a very dedicated, intelligent Professor. I learned more in this class than I have in most others. A large part of our grade was a big term paper at the end of the semester, for which we conducted independent research. Prof. Koremenos helped me learned valuable research and writing skills.

The International Relations seminar section titled International Law: What Do We Know and How Do We Know It? with Barbara Koremenos was by far one of the best classes I've taken at Michigan. She cares deeply about her students and is more than willing to help if you take the initiative to go to office hours.

This class was very disorganized and unclear. I feel like it had so much lost potential. The professor was nice but the class was just so unstructured and based mostly on her own writings. I would definitely NOT recommend anyone to take it. The many group projects and quizzes were just confusing, plus there is a 15-page final paper.

I agree 100% with previous reviewers. She seems like a nice person, but she's way too disinterested in teaching. Quizzespointless group assignments keep you busy, lectures are absolutely meaningless, and there's a 15pg final paper. I learned nothing I didn't already know from previous PS classes. I don't know my grade and classes ended today...

One of the worst professors I've had at Michigan. Class was slapped together, and NOT about Public International Law at all. Not a heavy workload but I also didn't learn much, have fun, or become more interested in the subject matter.
Terrible.

This class is completely based on her own research, so you will learn very little about actual international law, aside from reading a few international agreements. Her expectations are unclear and grading is extremely arbitrary. Overall, a very frustrating experience. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS OR ANY OTHER CLASS SHE TEACHES.

The single worst class I have taken in my four years by far. She only teaches and assigns her own work-which is heavily weighted with statistics. Her lectures are remarkably dull and her slides are seemingly put together by a 5 year old. I spent the entire semester trying to meet with her and it was like pulling teeth. DON'T TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!
she is simply uninterested in anything else but her own greatness and importance
Unbelievably frustrating to prepare for class.

Very disorganized. Often has 'partial' powerpoints to make you come to class and take notes. Can be opinionated at times. Grading is somewhat arbitrary. She's very nice and will take time to listen to you, but the lack of real guidance makes it very annoying. Also she likes to talk about her own research a lot. Not one of the better courses in PS.

The class is entirely based on her previous research. She assigns her papers and occasionally throws in someone who agrees with her theories. Purposely makes student's life more difficult than they need to be without any clear benefit to the students or education in general. The purpose of the class is to train coders for her future research.

the material is interesting, but can be repetitive. she has a one year old child who dominates her time and she often comes into the class scattered. she knows her material well though, and is helpful if you go to her office hours. go to class and take extensive notes and you'll do fine on the midterm.

This was a pretty bad class.  I was really interested in the subject, but she just likes to talk about her own theory and that’s all you end up learning.  She’s quite scatterbrained, lectures too fast, and puts 5000 words on a single power point.  Also unhelpful in office hours. Great note-taking and a lot of studying are required to do well.

Prof is a bit scattered at times, but she's clearly distracted somewhat by her current pregnancy.  Pretty much disorganized, but always very kind and helpful when you can pin her down and get some face time.

This topic is interesting and this is a great class for World Politics. However, she often is opinionated, lectures way too fast, and then does not provide notes. You have to read and attend lecture. Most students who did well originally ended up with bad grades on the midterm because it all isn't clear and she grades hard. Worth a shot!

She seems very knowledgeable about international law but is not a very good lecturer.  If you do what she tells you to do, you will do fine in the class.  Before the midterm, she told us to look back at a few specific readings, I did, and did fine.  My biggest complaint is the bad lectures that may or may not come up on the exams(you have to read)

Class is interesting and thought provoking. Koremenos is energetic, really easy to get along with and very helpful. Grading is a bit arbitrary, but as long as you can back up what you did, she's pretty flexible.

Kids who got the highest grades on the quizzes ended up with Cs and Ds on the midterm. Arbitrary grading. She often seems shockingly aloof from the class. Whizzes through notes, which she then doesn't provide. Focuses little on actual law, and more on her "theory of rational design," which means you'll learn little law, but plenty of her opinions.
She is great! Sometimes she assumes we know things she hasn't taught, but she is extremely interesting, very knowledgeable, and a HUGE help at office hours!
GREAT teacher!! she's really nice too! You may feel a little lost sometimes, but if you visit office hours, she is more than helpful.
She gives a lot of homework and can grade sometimes harsh but allows for resubmission and gives really good feedback. Also very nice and helpful!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Surprised her ratings are so bad...I really enjoyed Visualizing & Depicting with her. She's a sweet person and the class was fun. Very illustration-based but I've heard it's more graphic design based with other professors.

If you plan on taking Visualizing and Depicting, don't be intimidated to take a class with her. Despite the reviews, she is apparently significantly better in this class. While her grading can be strict at times and expects you to share her interpretation of things, it's worth it. She's fun and will be there to help you when you need it.
Doesn't deserve the low ratings here. She is a wonderful and caring teacher and is very passionate and great at what she does!

She is overall passionate about 2D, but her instructions for assignments were very unclear and sometimes had me and my classmates wondering what we were supposed to do for days on end. She also would make multiple assignments due on the same day and graded them very harshly.
