I don't get why she has such a low score. Yes, her lectures are long but she's such a sweetheart and you can tell she puts so much thought into her student's experience. Also her way of doing crits are my favorite.

She is a wonderful person, brings a fun and open energy to the class. The projects were pretty easy, though some ate into time that could have been better used on other things. Overall, she's a chill person and easy to get along with, show her respect and she will respect you.
She talks so much. Her lectures literally never end.

She's a very nice individual, but her class can be a hassle. The projects are boring and more time-consuming than they are worth. She teaches very objectively, giving very detailed instructions that must be followed. If she can't connect with your work, then you will get a lower grade. Do not buy the book she recommends; you will never use it.

I had a pretty good experience with Patricia. While she didn't give much time in class to work, she had many feedback sessions to help us with our iterations and was there every step of the way if we had questions. She would pull from her own funds to provide materials for students to explore with and clearly cared about the class.

While she does have a reputation for being a harsh first-year teacher, I enjoyed having her class. The work was not particularly interesting, I did learn a bit in this class. Take if you want to build a close connection with your professors

Grades completely unfair. She is extremely kind in class and then will give you zeros on assignments that have unclear criteria. Classes are boring yet frustrating due to her teaching methods. If you want to stay sane while taking this course, do not take her. Unfair reasoning as to why she takes off points. Cannot back up her claims.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.She will tell you your material is okay in class and then proceed to fail you on an assignment.She disregards the amount of time it takes to complete projects and makes you redo it several times.I have spent 5+ hours on a single assignment just to be told to redo the entire thing.I have had several mental breakdowns due to her.

harsh grader, passive aggressive when asked questions, interrupts when you're presenting or explaining things during critique 
lots of work load, harsh grader even when there was a lot of clear effort put in
 not completely unreasonable, cares about her students, gives lots of feedback but only after the entire assignment is submitted
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's nice, caring, understanding, is a great resource for you inside class and outside class. Her guest speakers are great. The workload is a lot and she expects you to commit lots of ours outside of her class. Take her class in a semester where you have more time and you'll enjoy it a lot more.

Great professor with cool assignment briefs.  There's a lot of complaints about workload but literally every other Wednesday she would hold short small group meetings instead of classes and the rest of the time would be yours.  Very accommodating & will work with you.  Just make sure to not get butthurt during critiques and manage your time wisely.

Boring lectures and material. Extremely harsh grader without setting standards of what she wants. Very disrespectful on students and their time/ other classes/life. Unreasonable. I would not recommend.
The content are boring (because they are boring, it is not easy to get good grades)..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Suck! Very harsh grader: very harsh if you do not satisfy her taste seldom articulates clearly her demands during the critique

One of the most caring teachers I've had here. She genuinely wants whats best for her students and actually cares. Incredibly talented artist, and an even better teacher of art. She can teach anyone to draw.

Very nice and gentle, kinda motherly. Has a lot of feedback to say for your work. While she's friendly and analyses your work a great deal, she can be frustrating. Has a clear set path she wants your work to go and will grade a bit harsh if it doesn't go that way. Overlaps dates of projects so you're always working on two at a time. That can suck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is overall, a nice person, but is very inconsistent in terms of grading. She will tell you that your project is good and then mark you down for things she never mentioned she had problems with. The good thing is you can always resubmit every assignment, however, there were times where I redid a decent amount and only got back a single point.
Ridiculous amount of work! But overall a nice person but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Patricia is very nice. This was her first time however teaching a non-majors course. She was very lenient this semester and I'm not sure if that is how it always is. She was always willing to help you out and very understanding.

Patricia outlines her assignments meticulously, and that's really helpful.  But there are many, many assignments which take up to four hours to do each.  Also, don't take this class if you don't like critique or subjective grading.

Patricia Beal's projects are very interesting,the only issue is that is gives her students a ridiculous amount of projects throughout the semester especially. She gives better feedback on paper than in person which doesn't help when you have to make corrections when you have to worry about the next project due the next week or even the next class.

Amazing teacher. She has a motherly demeanor. She's very helpful during critiques and is more than willing to further explain concepts that are being covered in class. Her one down fall might be how gentle she is- not everyone respects her because she doesn't really resemble an authoritative figure.

She is not a great Spanish teacher, extremely nitpicky, and if she does not like you, she will make it known and make the class environment unbearable. She does not like it when students take their allowed 6 absences, and she emails your advisor to let them know how you are doing in the class as a college student. She is a very hard grader.

The class itself is pretty easy, but she is an oddly harsh grader. Very punitive grade for small mistakes, and she was not forgiving at all and did not take into account the effort to meet with her. Overall for how easy the class is she is too hard a grader

Really good professor, I found 232 to be easier than 231. She is very sweet, funny, and knowledgeable. Lots of kahoots, quizlet lives, cross-word puzzles. Exams are the same format as the practice exam, so very easy to prepare for. Participation matters, but you become very close with your small class, so everyone feels comfortable. 100% recommend!

Marlene is very caring and patient with everyone in the classroom. She is a tough grader, I got random points off assignments, but overall a good professor. Make sure you participate and come to class. She makes them as engaging as possible and we played Kahoot and Quizlet games sometimes. Overall good professor.

My only issue is that she's an unfair grader. I felt that I participated a lot in class yet I never got above a B for participation. Additionally, what homework needs to be done before class is very unclear. Another thing that bothered me is there are multiple incompletes in the grade book for in-class work but I have done everything.

I had her at 9am. She woke me up every day and she made class interesting and engaging. She cold-calls and makes sure everyone speaks, which I thought was helpful in the development of my Spanish. The problem is she is an extremely harsh grader compared to the other Spanish 232 teachers, and ultimately my grade suffered as a result.

Marlene made spanish super fun. I am not usually interested in this subject, but she played games in class. She was also very good at creating conversations in Spanish. She asked students questions that really helped them understand. She is very good at explaining and very kind to students.

Online homework nearly everyday. Quizzes every monday. Caring professor but I didn't feel like she taught the material well, or at all, at times during the class. Heavily pressures you to speak Spanish in class but opened to questions. It was rough that everything was online. Just dedicate and apply yourself if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Marlene is a great teacher. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is a hard grader and is very particular in how you write. However, she tries to make class fun with Kahoots and team competitions!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nightly homework that is mostly a waste of time, she is either extremely cheerful or acts like someone peed in her cheerios, (mostly the latter)..& there's no in-between. Barely any time to complete exams she writes. Rather disrespectful/obnoxious to students in general in the classroom. Total opposite of what I expected, and not in a good way.

A very nice and approachable person, but average as a teacher. Classes are always group/partner activities, and she regularly randomizes your partners (introverts beware). She often assigns more homework than what the course requires (mostly busy work). I don't think she's a bad teacher - it's just that the UM Spanish department has better options.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Beiza was fantastic: very sweet, fun, and class was fast-paced enough to force you awake for a 9 am class. Lots of conversation activities or other fun games, but thorough practice with material. First Spanish class I've taken in four years, and it was a fantastic one.
Bi weekly journal entries and nightly homework. Probably 30 minutes of hw a night, exams are pretty hard and you need to study for them. Oral exam grading is very fair and not difficult.

I love Marlene! We got a good amount of homework every night and bi-weekly journal entries, but it was definitely manageable. I feel like our class really created a community and that my spanish improved a lot. Would definitely recommend her as a spanish 232 professor to finish off your language requirement!

Marlene has a good heart but I find her to be incredibly patronizing. Every class we all have to say "Buenos dias profesora" before we can start, we have dictation quizzes with sparkly stickers on them, and sometimes she hands out "participation candy." It felt like I was in 3rd grade.

I had her class at 9 am and if it was any other professor it would have been terrible. She was funny and had an engaging class. She is a tough grader on tests and gives consistent homework but your Spanish will improve as a result of her class.

I absolutely LOVE Marlene. I have taken previous Spanish classes the last 2 semesters, and she has been my favorite teacher by far. I feel comfortable participating in her class. In the past, I was always anxious going to Spanish class, but now I am actually excited! She gives a lot of extra practice and is overall very helpful teacher. Love her!

Profesora Beiza is wonderful. She is a native Spanish-speaker, and she is very patient and understanding with new learners (such as myself). There is a lot of outside-of-class work, but it's all worth it when we get to do fun and engaging activities during class time. I really felt that our class formed a community with the help of Profesora!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Berwanger was amazing. She was kind, approachable, and genuinely cared about her students. On multiple occasions, I reached out to her regarding circumstances beyond my control, and she was always understanding and willing to work with me. Her grading was fair, and she consistently prioritized student learning, so I 100% recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Berwanger was truly amazing. She was kind, approachable, and genuinely cared about her students. On multiple occasions, I reached out to her regarding extensions and circumstances beyond my control, and she was always understanding and willing to work with me. Her grading was fair, and she consistently prioritized student learning!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Paula was a very nice professor! I did like her, but the lectures were a bit dry. She mostly read off the slides. The exams were also really easy.

Paula was lovely. Not sure why people are saying you won't learn anything from her; she taught tons of history, material, and various aspects of deaf culture, + if you do the readings, there's even more to learn. The students I overheard complaining about her are also the same ones who barely showed up to class anyway... so some food for thought.
Super sweet, but you won't learn much of anything unfortunately

Slow and boring lectures, read right off slides, posted slides. 3 exams, open note, take home, 2 weeks to work on. Most of answers are in the reading, not the slides or lectures. Readings are usually long and dense. Very nice though and tries to be funny. Pretty easy class.
Very defensive and a mean person, ASL should be taught by a deaf individual to teach true deaf culture. Often drifts off topic and very rude when asked questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very defensive and often stressed. The higher-level ASL courses are a waste of time - lots of random things instead of learning new signs. Unprofessional - tends to talk about your personal issues in front of everyone and to your peers. Swings between being super kind and very very rude. Do not recommend this professor AT ALL.

Paula is a very kind, lovely, and understanding professor. She's overall really thoughtful about your life outside of school. You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and is a great source of knowledge. She's an easy grader and theres rarely any homework. Just don't take advantage of her, because then everyone will hate you.

She is a great professor, very passionate and creates a welcoming environment. She does seem stressed at times and often that makes her a 4 not a 5. Amazing person though, learned more in her class than all of high school. She seems to care more about growth and development rather than perfection which is great for a language.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The absolute best professor I have ever had. She really cares about all of her students and their success. She's a very easy grader and extremely understanding. 10/10

Paula is just incredible. Be warned- this isn't a class to take if you're not going to put in any effort. She's not a difficult teacher but does expect a certain level of participation. Always willing to meet outside of class and is more than generous with redos and extra credit. Not enough room to talk about how wonderful of a teacher she is!

Paula is probably the best professor I have had at U of M. She is the most caring woman, and wants every single student to do well, to the point that she gives us so much extra credit. She is always willing to meet with students after class, and gives the opportunity to repeat assignments you didn't do well on.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Paula is a great professor and does a good job making the lectures interesting and encouraging group discussions. The workload is minimal but you still learn a lot.

Paula has been my favorite professor during my whole college career. She is an overall great person and is very passionate about ASL. She is an easy grader as long as you put a little effort into assignments. To say something about her character, at class parties she brings sugar free candy for me because I'm diabetic! Very thoughtful!

I really can't say enough about this professor and this course. She is not a tough grader, but she expects effort and participation. She will not be afraid to call you out if you are always late or never prepared.  I really enjoyed taking this course - without all the stress, it was fun and I learned a lot. She is a great person and professor.

Paula is simply amazing. A very hands on professor who enjoys teaching ASL. Classwork/homework is manageable and make sure you prep for the exams. Having a partner can be very helpful. Overall, wonderful class and great professor!

Let me start this off by saying that I like Paula as a person. But as a teacher, don't expect to learn much unless you're really good at self-motivating. She's far too easy on students, and the class is a blow-off. If you want an easy lang req, take it. If you want to actually learn ASL, try a community college

Paula is great. She's dedicated and knowledgeable about the subject and clearly loves what she does. Easy grader, but tends to get defensive if people don't make an effort. She gets off on tangents easily, but I still think I'm learning a lot. She isn't tech-savvy and you may have to email a few times before getting a response. Ask early for recs!
Really sweet. Easy exams. If you  pay attention you're bound to pass.

The class is very reading heavy but it was interesting. She's very passionate about the topic and that keeps the class engaged. She grades extremely easily, I don't think anyone got less than a 95% in the class. There's one poster presentation that takes about 10-15 minutes to put together.
Paula is probably the most engaged/engaging and best professor I've had at UofM. She's incredibly passionate about the topic and keeps the interest level up.
ASL was great! Love Paula and the class, theres really no way to do poorly in her class.

I had Paula for 2 years and I thoroughly enjoyed learning from her.  While she can be defensive at times, she is a great teacher with extensive knowledge.  The workload was totally manageable.  I am going to miss this class!

Extremely nice and funny.  Even though you have 2 hours lecture but it doesn't feel like 2 hours because you're constantly signing in this class.  Not a difficult class to get an A.  She understands that you have classes that can give you heavy workload so her class workload is very light which is nice.

Paula is a very nice person, but she becomes easily defensive & is very unprofessional. 3rd & 4th levels of this class are filled with wasting time by talking about random things & more help should be given with the work as newer signs are no longer being learned as before. You probably won't have a problem with her, but just be a little cautious
Paula is by far the most down to earth person you can meet. i took ling 250 as well. take her, and you wont regret it.
Paula is...a character.  I'm always entertained!  She's very nice and helpful.  However, the class is supposed to be conducted exclusively in ASL and she talks way too much.

She is the most dedicated professor I've had yet here at Michigan and its obvious she really cares about the state of the DEAF WORLD. She is also very easy to work with if you had problems getting a passing grade in this course you probably arent Michigan material! WORD EM UP
shes not very helpful outside of class and i think she picked favorites a lot
She was not nice at all
Amazing professor; devoted to a program that she created; does not handle slacking from students and co-teachers.

The professor is passionate about the subjecct.  However, the class has a great deal of reading, and it is not all useful.  The professor is a little crazy--at first is very helpful, but then goes off on time wasting tangents.  Try to get Teri Kales.
I can't stand this woman.  She assign way too much reading and a 20 page take home final "paper."
Tries to get students any extra information they need; rightfully does not go the extra mile for students who aren't putting in their share of effort.
No Comments
No Comments

Megan was absolutely phenomenal as a professor for Writing160. I consistently felt supported throughout the course, and was offered many resources for all three of the projects. She truly wants her students to succeed and do their best work, and she is understanding an flexible. 10/10 recommend.
Extremely caring and flexible. Would take again!

very sweet and rly cares about her students. takes the time to give individual feedback to everyone. class is very easy you're allowed to do projects based on what you're interested in. def recommend for a fywr
Very nice and understanding professor. Class work is graded on completion and allows for a lot of creative freedom.

Megan was an amazing teacher for first-year writing. She leads engaging discussions, and makes the students passionate about the topics through her own, clear passion. She is a timely grader, extremely communicative through emails and office hours, and gives great feedback on assignments.

Megan is a great teacher, she made first-year writing fun. At first, when I saw the class was on linguistics, I was a bit annoyed, but she truly lets you explore anything you are interested in through a very unique lens of language.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Behrend a lot. Her in-class discussions about the literature were engaging and allowed students ample opportunity to contribute as well. She was very communicative and responsive outside of class, and her grading on major assignments felt reasonable. Would definitely recommend to anyone interested in higher-level English courses.

Though I wasn't a fan of the content of the course, Dr. Behrend made this course something that wasn't horrible. The course is mostly discussions, which are quite interesting. You do have 3 essays that she is a harder grader on. You have to know what you are talking about. She overall really cares about her students and wants you to do well.

I had Dr.Behrend for English 140 (Medieval literature and romance). I honestly didn't know anything about medieval literature beforehand and this course was a great intro into the topic, but it would help to have background knowledge of the Middle Ages. There is a new reading assignment for almost every class, but they are usually very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really great teacher! Seems a bit new to teaching, but you can tell she's super passionate abt her job. My class had a really heavy workload (cuz apparently the class before had said the workload was too light, thnx for that), but it was do-able. Let us pick our own topics for essays, so they were fun to write. Lots of peer review tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Megan was an amazing teacher. She has an extremely positive attitude and really listens to her students. She also really cares about getting to know you as a person. As long as you contribute, put in the effort, do the assignments on time and well, and are respectful, you will enjoy this class and most likely get an A.

Megan is a newer prof and Writing 160 a newer class, but it was amazing. She cares so much for her students and about her job. Her grading rubric is a bit unclear, but you can also go over it with her. As long as you much effort into the projects, you will do fine. I really got a new and refreshing experience with her class!
I usually hate English and Writing classes, but she is so good and nice that I loved writing and reading

Megan is one of the most passionate teachers I've had. She is incredibly devoted to the learned and improvement of her students. While sometimes she can be frustrating with her lack of consistency in grading and "undefined" rubric, she really cares about your learning and skills improve drastically. I think having her is worth the extra work.
The professor is narrow minded and will retaliate out of proportion. Even when she is at fault. Watch out.
Extremely helpful, Really Great to work with
Totally willing to help even the evening before exams.  Very likable and works hard to teach clearly!  Exams were very long - the full 2 hours.

Prof. Bhattacharya is an amazing professor - extremely knowledgeable in the content he teaches (he wrote the textbook for the class, wow!) and he places a heavy emphasis on UNDERSTANDING the material rather than the grade you get. Nice guy, funny jokes, would recommend taking his class!

My 320 experience: lectures 1-5: no idea what is going on finally read textbook, realize its not the difficult. First Midterm - analytical, basic, like HW Final - Conceptual, if you paid some attention in class you'll be fine Overall: I was often lost during lecture, but doing HW and occasionally reading led me to an A

Great professor and super funny. Really cares about students truly learning and understanding the material. Homeworks were pretty hard and the midterm was rough. But he made the final very easy. I was one of the dumbest in the class and ended up with a decent grade, so I imagine the smart kids all got easy A's. Good class to take.

Without a doubt the best professor I've had thus far in college. He has his days where he can be a bit of a ****, but its a class that he clearly has figured out how to teach from start to finish. Hes got a great sense of humor and really focuses on teaching whats going on rather than just rely on equations.

Arguably the best professor I have had in EE at U of M. He LEGITIMATELY cares about his students and always has time. He does not have a set time for office hours but is ALWAYS, I mean ALWAYS in his office available to help students. Overall, the only professor I would give a solid 10/10 to.
By far the best professor I've ever encountered and universally recognized as one of the best researchers in the field.  His book is also fantastic.

This class starts out extremely quickly, but it gets a lot better closer to the end. The beginning of the class is the "basics", and he covers all sorts of crazy, unrelated topics. After you get that, it all comes together. Good stuff.

Showed up late to class everyday (830 am start).  Answered questions in class / office hours very rudely - expected students to be experts in material after listening to his lecture.  Would argue material in discussion with the GSI, no coherence there.  Exams were very easy, open book but not an enjoyable class or one that I learned anything in.

he is an excellent prof. Really knows his stuff and knows how to explain it to students. MAKE SURE YOU READ THE BOOK! The exams are open books/notes and are pretty hard but his grading is pretty linient too.  I learnt a lot from this class and overall the course material was interesting.

Overall a very good professor.  Will likely learn a lot and learn it well.  Expect difficult exams and difficult HW. Expect a sometimes condescending attitude.  Had a tendency to be mean to kids who were not only confused but had no indication of solving confusion themselves. Hates non book readers.

Overall, he is a decent prof. class is entertaining, has good GSI's. I'd take 320 with him. Exams are hard, and so are HW, but don't worry he is lazy, and does not change the HW or exams, so if you know someone who has take 320 with him, ask them for their old HW and Exams and you will get an A+.

Professor Bhatia is misleading about her grading scale and assignments. She offered an extra credit opportunity for attendance at an even she hosted, but did not actually give points to those who attended. The maximum you can receive in attendance is a 90%, even if you go to all the classes.

She was a great professor. Clearly knew what she was talking about, but wasn't just interested in spouting her opinions but hearing about others too and tried to tailor the class, to an extent, if there was an area that seemed to spark a lot of peoples interest. 100% would recommend

Hate this lady. You definitely can learn a lot if you pay attention. I feel very well versed in Indian history. VB though is a conniving, artificial woman. The maximum you can get in participation or attendance is a 95%, making getting an A almost impossible. When I confronted her about this, she threatened to lower my A- to a B. Just don't.

Pass on this class. Professor Bhatia was in the middle of writing a new book and clearly had not prepared for her lectures. She made the second half of the class sessions were all student presentations so she wouldn't have to write a lesson plan. Kind of funny actually. Respect the hustle

Funny to see a teacher with a clear bias against white students because normally it's the other way around.  My friend who is smarter than me could barely get a word in without being told she was wrong.

Blatantly lies. She offered an extra credit for attending a guest speaker and writing a "short note" about the event. Went to the speaker(2 hours)and wrote the note(1 hour), and didn't get credit. Emailed her about this and she said that my summary of the event was not "analytically accurate." I asked 5 others from class and not one got credit

She is very straightforward and an overall sweet lady; however, the grading in her class is unfair. The highest grade you are allowed to obtain is a 95% on all assignments, including participation and attendance, even if you attended every lecture, and you need a 95% or above to get an A. Most people get an A minus, but an A is not obtainable.

Asian 336 with Prof. Bhatia is fun. She brings in many aspects relating to the topic and has great interaction with class. Beware, She expects you to read a lot! The articles she brings to class are unique and help clearly understand the topic. Her grading is a little strict but she guides you on how to write complete and good papers.

Varuni Bhatia was a wonderful professor. She actually engaged everyone with the material, brought a lot of viewpoints into discussion (and the entire class was essentially discussing the readings) and your grade is almost certainly an A if you try on the presentation and the two papers. Wonderful class, wonderful prof, would take again.
Professor Bhatia is intelligent, encouraging, and kind. Recommend.

VB is super sweet and enthusiastic about the material. The midterm was easy because she provided a study guide, but the final exam ended up being really difficult. We had to learn a lot of the material for the final from the textbook by ourselves. But overall, I learned a lot from this class and I would recommend it to others.
She's adorable. I actually wanted to go to class regardless of the fact that it was mandatory. Exams are easy. Section is  useless, it's too bad that's mandatory too.

Professor Bhatia is very nice, and she explains things quite well. The exams are pretty easy, the only thing that I think is hard are the grading of the modules. All in all, I learned a lot from this class and I don't regret taking it. (you DO need a 94.5+ to get an A though...)

She was clear about everything and the class was easy except that she used a crazy grading scale. Needed a 95 to get an A which was ridiculous!! Class was interesting, but could have been MUCH better if she made her points clearly and without all of the umms.

Prof. Bhatia was very clear in her expectations of the class, and the coursework was very manageable. Class participation is a major part of the grade, but you can "contribute" in a number of ways. Very thorough in the different modules. Class was kind of dull sometimes, but overall I'm glad I took it.
Professor Bhatia is passionate and kind. She's very easy to work with and makes herself available to students as much as possible.
Excellent course! Changed the way I think about religion in South Asia

Seriously the best class I have taken at umich. Lectures aren't mandatory (you don't need to go) class is graded by 3 essays and discussion attendance. If you like art/photography at all 100% take this class- super interesting. I would seriously take this class every semester if I could.
You won't regret taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The class material can be a bit heavy and could come off as boring if it's not something you're explicitly interested in. On the other hand Matthew Biro is so nice. Like he's such a good person and he's very understanding if you have stuff going on.

Prof Biro was an awesome art history teacher. He clearly knows a lot about the material and goes in depth. It is certainly not easy material to understand so I would not take it if you are looming for an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Biro clearly knew what he was talking about. But his class was quite boring. Lectures theoretically had the occasional interesting content but he drones on and on in class I struggled to pay attention and/or understand. He was sometimes funny. I don't want to take another Art History class; either content or him was Too analytical about things.

I was really looking forward to this class, but Professor Biro was too dry for me. He is clearly a genius and loves art so very much, but his lectures are not the most engaging. A bit monotone. I appreciated what I learned so much more after the class, when I saw the art in museums in person. GSI was great though!

He really knows his stuff but unfortunately this class was SO pointless. We never used either of the 3 textbooks, the lectures had NO correlation with the exams, and the exams were INSANE! Memorizing 100 photographs by name, date, and photographer for 20% of the exam. Do NOT take this class. I had to work almost as hard for HISTART 112 as ORGO!!!!!
He puts all his lectures in MP3 format up on Ctools... which makes me not come to lecture. Horrible idea. One of the most boring lectures I have ever attended. Love my GSI though.

This man obviously knows a lot about his subject, but his lectures are so boring that you can't pay attention. Also, he weirdly refuses to pdf his lectures, so you have to click through tons of slides. Don't bother with the books, go lecture and go to section, you get everything you need to know.
great prof decnt class don't buy books I opened one of them maybe three times. Do go to section and particpate it will help.

You definitely do not have to go to lecture to do well in this course. I went once. There are only 2 exams and 1 paper, all of which follow the same exact format. Just study the slide comparisons he sends out before the tests, research the works on them, and you will be more than fine

I feel compelled to right because I am sitting in the class right now. UNBELIEVABLY BORING. He speaks in monotone and goes on and on and on. Class is easy, I haven't purchased the textbooks because his lecturers are a reiteration of the textbook, and then section is a reiteration of the lecture. Make sure you can withstand his banalness.

Incredibly boring class. He is a good, enthusiastic prof. but eventually I stopped going to lecture at all. Easy class however, which probably made the class less painful. Don't waste money on any of the books, I opened them maybe once.
I wish I had gotten more out of this class - instead my main goal was to not fall sleep during every lecture.  This class isn't difficult, but it wasn't as interesting as I hoped it would be.

I'm an alumni, 8 years out and I still think of Matt's class.  Nurturing, smart, fair, and genuinely in love with what he does.  One of my best experiences at Michigan. Try finding another art history professor that truly loves art...I dare ya.

Lectures are extremely boring but available on m-scribe (if you can stay awake and pay attention through the 80min of it) so attending lecture is optional. Lots of memorizing pictures and dates, exams fairly straight forward and nothing unexpected.
No Comments
No Comments

You don't need to memorize alot of pictures, his lectures are interesting and directed strait towards the test. Even if you have no backround in art/photography, the class is still easy. He wants you to do well.

The text is ridiculously boring and practically unnecessary. The lectures can be interesting and Matthew Biro is enthusiastic about the material, however, skipping a few lectures won't hurt you. You don't have to go to lecture very often or read (at all) in order to get at least a B+ on exams.
he mumbles during class the entire time and when people participate he will tell them to speak up and use their Ross voices if they are not as loud

I didn't take LHC with him but can't choose the right course for some reason. Had him for Business Law. Big fan of Professor Bishara--very kind, very knowledgeable, and very supportive. Would definitely recommend taking a class with him. Very engaging professor, very helpful when it comes to academic/life advice!
Bishara is arrogant and impudent. He makes the material dull.

The class is expected to be easy because it is an introductory class, but it seems it's not. For exam 2, I was halfway through, and I am sure half of the class didn't finish the exam. Homework is also longggg..

Decent professor. I didn't go to lectures because he often went off topic and on long tangents. But he one of the most understanding and caring professors I've had so far. If you completed the last take home exam late, he would still take it. Overall a good professor in terms of understanding but an okay teacher.

This class has a heavy workload for a 2 credit class and exams are a speed run since there are usually 4-5 questions and 50 minutes to solve. Sharqi is super accessible and tries his best to teach the breadth of material, which there's a lot since it is an overview of some of the math and science concepts used. He is kind and understanding though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Sharqi's lectures are a bit tough and will require that you read the provided course notes. The exams are like homework questions and if you make a good cheat sheet, you will be fine. He is very understanding of circumstances and does his best to accommodate everyone's needs. Many opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Consider self learning as the professor does not teach content relevant to homework and exams very well. 
Understanding content is easier with practice exam keys instead of attending exam review sessions as he will make errors.
Never expect to finish any of his exams as in the allotted time.
The exams look nothing like lecture slide material.

He's nice, but this class was actually ridiculous. MANY hours/week on hw, tests were genuinely impossible to complete in time. CANT STRESS ENOUGH HOW MUCH TIME I SPENT ON HW. NOT a 2 credit workload. Tests were so hard he had to add a 20% extra credit section to one, and for another basically avg scores with 100. Concepts were not explained well.

He is a new professor who I feel doesn't fully understand the content he's teaching. Occasionally, he asks students in the class to explain concepts when he can't explain it well himself. During several lectures, students asked numerous questions on the same concept and we left more confused than before. The notes are more helpful than the lecture.

Although this class is a little tough, I still feel like the workload is typical for that of a 2 credit class, albeit it is on the higher side of the 2-4 hours per credit hour rule. The exams are a little difficult because there is not enough time to complete them, and make sure you study the course notes that they give you and you should be fine.

This was not a 2 credit class, even by engineering standards. Spent days on HW assignments, and might I add he refused to curve the class, instead you have to spend hours doing extra credit assignments on top of said HW that already takes forever. Pray you have a good IA, his office hours are worthless... and so are the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Biggs is really nice and deeply cares for everyone. He speaks a bit too fast, but he's awesome. I think the main issue is the lack of clarity in the homework. Homework would sometimes require you to use formulas that weren't mentioned in lecture, only adding more to the confusion when completing the homework. Nothing like mass and heat though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In the lectures, the professor failed to define many variables and lacked any flow in his line of thought.  Not great at simplifying conceptual explanations. Homework was very helpful until it stopped relating to lecture content. Homework had long simulation problems that took hours to learn and then implement.

Homework was not like exams or lectures, was way harder. Had us perform complex Aspen probs that we didn't know how to use (2+ hours for that problem alone each week). Long paper/project (who uses 1 spacing and 11 pt font for a three page paper?) with unclear guidelines. Said he wouldn't curve the class start of sem (the avg is a 75). Nice, but bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's honestly pretty blunt and can come across rude which makes her hard to approach at times. You have to get above a 60% on each exam to earn credit, which can be extremely defeating. Definitely a class that requires so much effort.

I had a great time with Dr. Bird - it's very clear what you're expected to know and the 4 exams aren't too difficult. Gameful approach made the class pretty easy to get an A in - you have to show up to lecture though (2 absences allowed before every absence drops you a letter - e.g. 3 classes missed, max grade you can get is A-).

First off, part of the issue with my grade was that I wasn't as locked in as I should've been the semester I took this course. But, there is no reason to end lecture short by 20-30 minutes every class and just rush through the lecture and not explain things deeply. She is also a little curt, and not the friendliest (by her own admittance).

Feeling discouraged because, according to the recent exam statistics, about 1/3 of the class got less than a 60% on the most recent exam, which I woulldn't normally think is something crazy but if you get less than 60%, you get 0 points, even if you're like me, who got a 55% after lots of study. Good prof. but get ready to not get credit for effort

Dr. Bird was a great professor and knows makes lectures fun because of how much knowledge she has on all the content. Gradecraft class so you get to pick what assignments you do. There are 6 exams but as long as you get above a 60% on all of them and attend every class you can get an A+.

Bartley is a great teacher and makes all the content very easy to understand! Honestly I think people gave him bad reviews just because they're not used to college level exams. I have taken the Fall final as practice and it is really not that bad. As long as you stay on top of lectures and homework it is easy to do well in this class.

I didn't even have professor Bartley, but I watch all of his lecture recordings and it is the single reason why I passed this class. If you stay on top of the content, you will do fine. Exams were pretty hefty and sometimes there would be things they said would not be on the exam be worth 10 points on the exam. Spend time out of class studying!

Ignoring everything about the final exam last semester, Bartley is actually a good teacher and a great lecturer. Does a good job explain concepts and going over practice problems. Provides all of the resources necessary in Canvas to ace exams. Put in a little bit of effort and the class will be an easy A
Great lectures!
worked very well up until the last exam, very difficult, still did well, make sure to study and do extra help office hours
He doesn't prepare you for the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your final will give you nightmares. Make sure you know how to draw acids. If you have a bad chem background, get 20+ hours of tutoring.

He has better lectures than Poniatowski! Don't listen to the final exam hate tbh. I was a victim of it myself but I did really bad on the first exam before I started going to Bartley's lectures instead of Poniatowski's.
Everyone complained about the final exam but most people still got good grades.....

Ok so he handled the class kinda terribly. The lecture honestly didn't prepare me for the exams at all so I was doing a lot out of class. The only reason I'm giving a two rather than a one is because he is very nice. The lecture is engaging and he is willing to listen and help if you have specific questions.
Talks really fast and doesn't prepare you for exams well. Whether you go to lecture or not your going to be confused on the content regardless

PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY WORST TEACHER, WASHERNAW COMMUNITY COLLEGE HAS BETTER PROFESSORS. "DOCOTOR" BARLETY AVOID AT ALL MEANS !!!!!!!! DO NOT TAKE, FINAL IS AN ENTIRELY DIFFERENT CLASS. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE. DOES NOT TAKE ADVICE JUST SAYS WE COMPLAIN ALL THE TIME> DO NOT TAKE.

Dr. Bartley was a great lecturer and professor! I felt like he was always super clear and direct when teaching, and the homework questions and worksheets made for discussion really reflected what was taught in class. I also appreciate that he dedicated class days to review before each exam.

Bartley has single-handedly taken an entire 100-level class to the shadow realm. His exams are far harder than practice exams and often don't match the format/difficulty. IGNORES ALL CRITICISM OF THE COURSE WITH COPY PASTES, GIVES THE HARDEST EXAM OF ALL TIME, NOTHING LIKE THE PRACTICE AND LECTURES, NO CURVE, LIFE IS BAD.

Yeah, let's give 30 points of questions on a new thing we just added to the syllabus 2 weeks ago, that sounds like a great idea. Dr. Bartley is truly one of the best professors I've ever had. He is the kindest, most patient instructor, and it's so clear how much he cares about his students' learning and well-being. If you ever have the chance to take a class with Dr. Bartley, do it. He's the sweetest professor and an exceptional human being. Highly recommend.
His tests look nothing like any of the practice test or the homework or anything gone over in class

if u have to take chem 130… switch majors. seriously. gave us an entire final on the one chapter we barely covered. bartley shut down piazza after students were complaining test was nothing like content in lecture, and nothing like practice exams. this man needs to find a new career.

Horrible teaching skills, horrible communicator, and horrible test writer. Do not take this class, as the final has no correlation to the course or practice material. Bartley is incompetent.

Bartley is simply not the GOAT. I've had a lot of problems with this course this semester, and honestly the biggest is the fact that the materials they give us (practice exams, problem roulette) literally do nothing to prepare us for the current exams.
