reviews.comment: Chem 130 with Dr. Bartley is brutal. Homework and discussions seem easy, but exams are nothing like practice. He shuts down feedback, can't handle complaints, and nothing's curved. Smart teacher, terrible class. You'll feel prepared, then the exam will destroy you. This is a class structure issue, and Bartley is in charge of that.

I understand adding in unfamiliar questions that require critical reasoning, but it is in no way fair to make the majority of the exam like that when we don't spend any time on those types of scenarios. I am super dissatisfied with our "cumulative" exam and the lack of resources and instruction to prepare for such an exam.

Exams were leveled up from what previous exams looked like. Dr. Bartley and faculty did not provide comprehensive lectures or study material regarding this level of material. I was blindsided by the first exam and the next two were okay. The final was insanely hard and was around 25% based off of a 14 page supplemental with few practice problems.

One of the hardest classes I've taken so far. Professor Bartley mostly just reads off the slides during lectures so there is no point in going to class. The hw, umps, and discussion (depends on your gsi) are really helpful. The actual exams are always like 10x harder than the practice exams so be careful with that.

This semester they decided to switch content. Exams were harder than practice exams and problems that we were given. Bartley gave easy examples and didn't provide help and when we claimed that exams seemed to be unfair he was rude and condescending stating "rather than complaining list problems that didn't seem "fair". =
DONT DO IT this class SUCKS, gsi's SUCK and tutors BARELY HELP like if you don't have a test tube UP YOUR ASS JUST DONT!
Dr. Bartley was such a great professor. He made his lectures super engaging and fun, despite it being on chemistry. The content itself was difficult, but he was always accessible to answer questions.
My favorite professor in UofM. GOAT!

Dr. Bartley was my first ever professor at Michigan, and I will never forget just how welcoming he was every time we started a lecture. He was clearly very passionate about chemistry, and wanted us to enjoy his class just as much as he enjoyed teaching it, which made for a great experience.

I LOVED my chem 130 section. Bartley made it feel like high school again, in the best way possible. He taught everything very in depth, but also at a pace that always kept the class moving. He would always be sure to tell us what was on the midterm and final, and even had review lectures! He is a professor that truly wants his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy who is great at explaining. Would recommend him out of any other professor for Chem 130.

Incredibly caring & knowledgeable! While he moves quickly, it's also worth noting that each lecture is pretty heavy, so skipping classes or not completing the textbook readings will cause you to fall behind (hence my grade). However, there are plenty of office hours and time after class to ask him for help or questions, & he really goes in depth!

Dr.Bartley is a good chem professor! I took the CSP section and I thought it was great. He made good use of our extra time and practice. Chem is already content-heavy but he doesn't overcomplicate topics in lecture and is pretty funny. He knows well what will be on the exams (he writes them). He makes time for questions in lecture. Would take again

Dr. Bartley is super nice! Lectures were ok, could've given more practice problems in class but it was ok overall. Chemistry is tough and you just need to practice problems as much as you can. Understand things conceptually. The exams mirror almost exactly the exams from the prior semester- STUDY THOSE! Go to the SLC for drop in tutoring! HW was ez

Dr. Bartley was super nice, but we went through things very quick, so it was sometimes on the students to teach themselves certain topics. He made it very clear what would and wouldn't be on exams too, which was helpful. Not the most accessible outside of classroom hours.

He teaches very clear, and is funny during some lectures as well. The lectures are very fast paced due to the heavy course content, but he breaks it down and makes time for questions. He is by far the best option for general chem professor, and he writes the exams as well. I would take him as your professor if you can!! The others are confusing.

Bartley honestly just seemed like such a great guy. He always came to lecture with a good mood and explained material well. Exams were pretty light if you did the homework with little outside help and did the practice exams. Only down side is that he talks the ENTIRE lecture without breathing it seems so you can get lost if you're not locked in
Dr. Bartley is a very kind professor. He is more than willing to help outside of class and re-explain any topic. He definitely enjoys what he teaches, which made lectures a lot easier to listen to.

Professor Bartley was really engaging, and his lectures are easy to follow. Even though the lectures were big, I was still interested in the content and what he was teaching. He prepares students well for the exams and has a lot of resources and practice assignments that I thought were really helpful.

He seems like a great guy and knows the work really well. The class isn't the easiest because of how work heavy it is, but Dr. Bartley clearly knows what he's doing. The class in general is tough because they go through a chapter a week, but in comparison to what I've heard from other classes, Bartley does great.

He's a good guy above anything else. He was going through some serious family stuff this semester but was still making jokes and had enjoyable lectures. He loves to let you know what to study for before an exam which made them more straightforward. But please beware for some mistakes in exams as they cost you time even though full points are given.

Bartley was an amazing professor. Lectures were delivered well and he always made sure we were aware of what we actually needed to know. Homework every week with multiple attempts and PODs were great practice material for the exams. Exams were not bad at all if you put in the effort to study. Would definitely take again if given the chance.

Professor Bartley was awesome! There was a very clear and fair grading criteria, always told us what will and won't be on the exams, and was an overall great lecturer. He always explained concepts well and thoroughly without overcomplicating. He's very chill and understanding and cares about his students.

Dr. Bartley overall was a decent professor - very straightforward about what was/wasn't going to be on the exams. He did skim pretty quickly through some topics in lecture. Good at narrowing stuff down & didn't waste time on unnecessary material. Do all the practice exams on Canvas, keep up with the HW, & you'll be all set for class.

Dr.Bartley is an amazing prof and does an awesome job at teaching. He is super honest and clear about what will and will not be on exams. I attended his office hours quite a few times, and he is super kind and explains things one on one phenomenally. If you take CHEM 130, do it with Bartley.
Good lecturer -- made learning very easy. He's very down to earth and clear about what will and won't be on exams. Definitely recommend him for Chem 130!
Overall a great professor. He explained the concepts in an understandable way and was open about what material would or would not be on the exams.
Overall, it was a good class and the lectures were helpful. Dr. Bartley was always willing to answer questions after class and he explained things clearly.

Dr. Bartley does an exceptional job guiding lectures, is very accessible outside of them, and provides plenty of resources to understand the coursework and prepare for the tests. Make sure to pay attention during the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bartley is awesome!! Chem itself might not be interesting, but I thought his lectures were very engaging. He is fun to listen to, and you'll be surprised how quickly the hour will pass. Definitely try to get him as your teacher!

Bartley is kind, funny, and teaches his material very clearly. His class is exactly what an entry level chemistry class should be. It's not a free A by any means, and you will have to work hard, but there is never any mystery surrounding what you need to study for the exams. Homework is reasonable and relevant to exams. Definitely take his class!

He made Chem130 bearable! Every lecture was clearly taught and easy to understand. He truly cares about the needs and wellbeing of the students and is very knowledgeable about the subject. He is always prepared to lecture and explains things very thoroughly. I really recommend taking this class with Bartley!

Dr. Bartley knows exactly what he is talking about and explains the content in a very digestible manner. He made it pretty clear to me what would and would not be on the exams. He was even having some family issues this past semester but never let it impact his quality of teaching or accessibility and I really commend him for that.
He was a great professor! He made the material really easier to understand, and gave a clear outline of learning material. He was always willing to help, and give advice!
He was a great professor! He did a great job at explaining material and interacting with students. He was always willing to help and give advice!

Dr. Biteen is a great professor. She is clearly very passionate about what she's teaching, and she makes pchem concepts much more digestible and easier to understand. She also walks through problems with you and is great to talk to. However, personally, I found some of her lectures to be boring, but that might be due to the material itself.
She is such a good professor. Not only is she great at teaching chemistry, she's also a really good person. So inspirational seeing someone like her.
Prof. Biteen is one of the best professors in the Chem department. She's always caring and full of patience. She made thermodynamics very organized and pretty easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's so nice and helpful, she has your back when the going gets though and comes through for you.

Biteen is probably the best professor I've ever had at Umich. She explains concepts very clearly and walks you through tough calculations. This really helped me with the math, which I was worried about. Chem 461 had the potential to be the most difficult class I've ever taken, but Biteen made it so much easier and more enjoyable than I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor. She puts in a lot of work to make the content less daunting and is super easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She is a nice professor, but she needs to get her slides more organized. I love her class even though I don't learn anything from it.

If you show up to class and read the textbook you'll be fine. Sometimes forgets to cover what is in the textbook and the material will show up on the exam. Can be tough to understand what she is explaining when in a 300-student lecture. Very clear when you ask a question at office hours though

Class was ridiculously difficult regardless of professor, but Biteen did not help much. She is obviously very qualified and knows the information but does not convey it well. Class is fine until exams, which are made unrealistically difficult.

While I recognize Professor Biteen's skill and knowledge in the field of chemistry. I personally was not ever blown away by her lectures, or her explanations of the subject. She is a perfectly fine lecturer, and you will learn what you need to learn, but don't expect to be excited for every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chem 130 is honestly just an annoying class. I felt it was designed to make it harder to succeed. Prof. Biteen's iClicker questions were pretty easy, but she made a lot of mistakes in lecture. Additionally, her lecture notes got less useful as the semester went on. She seems to be a nice person but I didn't think she was the best lecturer.
If you are looking for an easy A, do NOT take Chem130 unless you have to. If you cannot avoid the course, take it with Professor Biteen because she is good at explaining difficult concepts.

Biteen makes a lot of mistakes during lecture, but she almost always lets the class redo the iClicker questions until a majority gets it right. Otherwise she was nice, much better than the other professors. Exams tore everyone a new one though.

Here's the deal. You're probably taking Chem 130 because you have to and Biteen is a perfectly fine professor to take it with.  It's a challenging class and the lectures are pretty vanilla, but if you're decent at Chemistry you should get at least a B.  You want Bartlett if you can get him, but Biteen is a solid backup.

She's kind and will answer all of your questions. She occasionally makes no sense and often confuses her words, but if you point it out or go to her office hours, she clarifies. Very sweet and caring, makes cute little jokes here and there.
Biteen is the best! She structures her lectures and the discussions so well, you cannot help but do great! She is really funny and really loves her students. Could not recommend her more highly!

Very sweet and caring. She goes at a pretty reasonable pace and is very open to helping people with questions so the lectures and iClickers were fairly easy for me (I had some previous experience with chem honors in high school). The tests are a little challenging though and aren't curved.

Dr. Biteen has it together! Extremely available for student needs outside of class. I met with her literally every week outside of office hours to ask questions and talk material. Obviously loves her students and wants them to succeed.
Makes at least 3 mistakes per lecture. Feels like she was a high school teacher with a class average of a C- and was pulled up to the bug leagues and can't handle the pressure.

You have to show up to every class because you must answer iClicker questions for a grade at every lecture, and it only counts if you go to your assigned lecture, you can't go to another and answer the questions there. Biteen is woefully unprepared, barely knows how to use PowerPoint, many of her iClicker questions are wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's new to U of M, but she seems to know her stuff. She goes through the basic chem slides all the other teachers go through as well. She was very nice and is willing to answer questions. iClicker attendance is recommended since they can give you an extra 4% boost in the class. Exams are actually pretty  hard though since she doesn't write them.
She just reads off the slides in lecture and this isn't very good if you ask me. She also has an odd sense of humor

Julie's lectures are very helpful and she prepares you well for the exams. The exams are a bit tricky so you will have to do a lot of practice problems like she recommends. Tends to make lame jokes often and overuse the phrase "sanity check". Overall, very helpful and clear professor, would recommend.

Not a terrible professor but tended to just read off her generic powerpoints during lecture. Really nice person and helpful during office hours. If you can get Sipowska, take her instead. Sipowska writes the tests and her section typically did better on the exams.

Although Gen Chem is not an easy class, Professor Biteen is a great teacher who cares a lot about her students. She explains very clearly and really wants to make sure everyone understands. Go to her office hours early on, she is very helpful and understanding.

Professor Biteen is a great chemistry professor. She is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about chemistry. She goes through the chapters at a good pace. The exams are very hard, but you can do well by doing lot's of practice problems from the book and that are provided online.

Professor Biteen is one of my favorite professors i've had.  She is extremely enthusiastic and cares so much about all her students. She always makes sure every understands concepts before moving on.  Exams are difficult but if you do a lot of practice you can do well.  If you're going to take this class, take it with Professor Biteen.
Proffessor Biteen is by far my favorite professor that I have had at Umich. She explains everything very well! The exams are difficult, so doing practice problems is a must!

Julie is the nicest prof. She is really enthusiastic about chemistry, but she also takes into account that not everyone knows as much as her, so she goes very slow and gives many examples. However, discussions are horrible. I switched discussions three times, and all three of my GSI's could not teach.

Julie is really nice and enthusiastic about chemistry. Most of the class is review of AP Chem, exams are difficult. If you want to skip class, do so early in the semester because it will be more valuable to attend lecture later on when the material is more difficult.
Extremely good professor!! Very nice and willing to help. The discussion was horrible, switch out if you have David Rowland. He was extremely rude and did not help at all.

Class is mostly review if you took AP Chem, so the lectures are kind of boring and redundant. Newer material covered in later chapters. Prof Biteen is really nice and enjoys what she's teaching, which will benefit you if you have questions. Discussions weren't bad, either.
she liked to tell jokes that were terrible
Awesome professor. Really enthusiastic and knowledgable. Eager to help, and really nice when you go to office hours
Great teacher, really knows how to explain concepts in a way everyone understands
Very good professor. Extremely clear and very expressive so you'll never fall asleep during a lecture. I recommend everyone to take her section if they're doing Chem 130.
Clear, nice and caring...
She is very helpful and really takes the time to explain difficult concepts! Great Professor!!
Really nice! Explain everything clearly. Couldn't tell this is her first time to teach this class!
She explains everything well. It is an enjoyment to have her class.
She`s the best professor I ever met

Worst class I have ever taken by far, 100% sure that any grad student would've done better. She read straight off slides for lecture, which were just screenshots from the solution manual. Only 5 people out of 30 were attending lecture after the first month, and every time you asked a question in office hours she would berate you. umich pls fire.
Great prof, good curve. Exams were tough but not un passable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are just Professor Zhou reading off a slideshow that they opened on Canvas. The homeworks are just book problems. She never walks through problems on a white/blackboard, only talks through them on the slides. I would never take a class with this professor again.

The class is pretty tough but its a 400 level physics class and the material is heavy. She does her best to make sure that her students are set up to succeed and is genuinely kind and helpful if you need it. The book is necessary to understand the lectures and the homework, but the homework is pretty close to whats in the book.

Bing Zhou has very high expectations for her students. She may not be the best lecturer, but she is well-prepared and very thorough in her lectures. The practice problems she gives before exams are a  good representation the exam - make sure to go through those thoroughly. She rarely smiles, but when she does, it lights up the class.

Bing Zhou is very smart, but not a good lecturer. Her lectures skip over parts that would help student understanding and are scattered. She almost always does not understand students questions and makes mistakes when writing equations that often lead to confusing notes. Read the book, and good luck. If you can, wait for someone else to teach it.

Professor Zhou was truly one of the worst professors that I have had at this school.  She expects everything to make sense the first time around and is very condescending in her explanations.  I was a solid A- average honors physics student going into this class, but completely bombed this course.  Definitely avoid her and try to get someone else.

Pay close attention to what is covered in the review sessions because that is what will be on the exams. Lectures are not particularly insightful. Instructor did not recognize student difficulty with the material. Beware of homework sets they are often long and painful. If you can take the course with someone else do so. Your grade will thank you.

She's quite difficult to understand and doesn't really explain things - just reads from the slides and expects it to make sense, which often it doesn't because these are fairly difficult concepts. There are also a lot of mistakes in her lecture slides which can be very confusing. If you use the book and go to office hours, you'll be alright.

She is a nice lady and this will probably the only compliment I'd give her. Her lecture notes are straight from the publisher and not organized at all. A formula from one slide will not match up with the same formula 3 slides later. She changes what she says completely depending on what the slides say. You'll do okay if you go to every office hour.

Bing is totally awesome. She's smart and funny and very approachable. My favorite Bing quote: "Going from 3 to four dimensions is like going from fortran to C - you start counting from 0" hahaha lectures are fun

Very nice and extremely helpful. The textbook is horrible, but she does such a great job explaining things in lecture that you don't really need it. She is a little hard to understand at first, but you get used to it as the semester goes on.
Very nice and helpful overall.

Bill was a great professor during the summer semester. He truly cared for his students and you could tell it too. I wasn't the best student due mental health issues, Bill was willing to take actions to get you where you should be. I've never had a more awesome professor at my time here in Michigan.
Very kind and attentive; has lecture formats and slides on Canvas for various types of learners.
Dr. Gehring is such an amazing professor! If you have the chance to take his class do it!

He is so sweet and is such a good lecturer. He makes the content understable, even when it can be confusing like parts of the brain. The exams are really straightforward and he does curve them to help everyone out. He wants to get to know you so I recommend office hours or at least emailing him, he wants to hear from you!

Bill Gehring is an amazing professor who clearly cares about the course and students. Only thing I will say is that the demos in class do come in the exam so participate and don't brush them off. Exams do require a lot of studying but aren't impossible. He also encourages AI and includes assignments that teach us about it. Great for BS credit.

Gehring is THE BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD at uofm! His psych 240 taught me how to actually study and I learned so much in the class despite it being online and fast paced spring semester! He's an amazing lecturer, easy professor, and an amazing human. Its easy to do well in the class and to enjoy learning the material without dying of stress.

The first year seminar was organized with a reading (you had to turn in notes) the day before lecture. This was the only graded content during the semester and was graded very easy. You must follow the guidelines to get full credit. The paper was the only major assignment that was easy. He asked you what grade you deserved at the end and I got that
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm really grateful to have had Dr. Gehring as a first semester freshman. The class presented us with ample resources and connections within the University; the work prompted me to think about my academic goals and personal goals. I definitely look forward to having class with Dr. G again - he's warm and clearly invested in his line of work.

Professor Gehring is one of the greatest teachers Ive ever had. Especially during the pandemic hes been super understanding. He clearly cares about his students, and his classes are very interesting. The content you learn in this class is so important and applicable in real life, I implore any freshman to take this course, you will not regret it.

Bill was SO nice and a good lecturer, he even bought the entire lecture froyo! The class itself was pretty straight forward and the GSIs and bill himself were accessible if you needed help. Totally would recommend.

Dr. Gehring is one of the best professors Ive had at UMich! He truly cares about his students and wants them all to succeed. He holds plenty of office hours, including some at Amers where we can get froyo/coffee, as well as optional FroyoTalks to get to know students in small groups. He also provides plenty of resources beyond slides. Loved him!

Professor Gehring is one of the most incredible teachers I have ever met. His entire approach to conveying information and knowledge is unique, and is structured to help the student learn and succeed in class. As if that wasn't enough, Professor Gehring is extremely approachable, and is great to have a conversation with. A must take.
Great prof!

Bill honestly was one of my favorite professors here. He was really funny but also clearly knowledgeable about psychology. He loves taking students out to get frozen yogurt and often has office hours at Amer's where he will buy you frozen yogurt just for showing up. There are 3 exams and 3 take home assignments, all of which are super fair.

Professor Gehring is great. He cares about his students and wants to make their lives easier... There is good review material for exams and he always tries to find ways to improve his teaching and make students' learning experiences better. He loves his students so much he even takes them to Amer's for froyo. Great guy, great professor.. so sweet!

Professor Gehring is extremely talented and empathetic. He finds ways to disseminate the course knowledge very effectively, and the way the class is taught is incredible. He sets his students up for success all while helping them learn the information, and actually enjoy it.
Professor Gehring is such an all-around great guy. He cares so much about his students and you can really tell. If you have a chance, you must take a class with him!

Dr. Gehring is a really great professor, his class was a great gateway to college. He really does care about his students and is interested in their lives. Best professor I've had here at UMICH (he even took us to get frozen yogurt one day during class).
He is the best. Definitely take one of his classes.
Great lecturer and a charming guy. Makes material interesting and engaging. Hosts coffeetalk with students outside of class to get to know students.

Lectures optional, tended to be boring even thought he seemed to have a good personality so it was prob the material. Quizzes every discussion section keeps you up to date on lecture material. Necessary to know info from lecture well to get a good grade on exams!

I absolutely loved Dr. Gehring and his genuine care for each and every student. The interesting material covered in lecture was underscored by his passion for the subject. Exams are fair if you pay attention in lecture and review the study guide. I highly recommend 240 but take any class you can with Dr. Gehring, you won't regret it.
Bill is a genuinely great man. Take any class of his if you have the chance.

Dr. Gehring is literally the best professor. He is intelligent, funny, and gives every student a fair chance at success. There was never a dull moment in his class. The only down side is during lecture, you may get distracted by his good looks and completely forgot you're supposed to be taking notes.
took a first-year seminar with bill and it was great. he's a really good teacher and a really cool guy who genuinely seems to care about his students. looking forward to taking more classes with him!
Take any class with Bill. He enjoys teaching and will make you enjoy learning

Bill is awesome! He's so funny and really REALLY hot. But he is also a wonderful professor. He's really good at explaining the concepts we learn about and he's definitely willing to meet outside of class for any extra help you might need.

Bill is my favorite professor at the university.  He is without a doubt the most accommodating professor I've ever had, and he truly cares about all of this students.  I had the privilege of taking a seminar course with him so I was able to interact with Bill often. I strongly encourage taking any course you can with him.

Probably the best professor I have ever had.  He is charming up on lecture and you will love his classes and experiments.  Materials are not so hard.  You will need a bit of study and everything will be fine.  He puts a lot of resource on CTools.

Perhaps my favorite professor at Michigan so far.  Gehring explains things really well and provides students with many resources to succeed.  His exam review sheets are thorough and accurate.  He makes class enjoyable and is a funny guy.  I highly recommend taking his class!

Professor Gehring is awesome. I'm in Education so this class was really relevant to me, although I felt out of my element at times. His work ethic is impressive. He really seems to enjoy teaching, which is fantastic. Take good notes, study frequently and you'll be fine!

Gehring is an awesome professor and he makes the subject very interesting without convoluting it too much with details. His assignments/tests are tough, but fairly test your knowledge (even on multiple choice exams). Studying the RIGHT way is hard, but key to doing well. I recommend flashcards.
One of the best professors I've ever had. It's not an easy class but he makes it very interesting .
Prof. Gehring is one of my favorite teachers at the University; every day I learned something useful and outside of his required field of teaching. Take a class with him if you can.
Really nice professor, knows a lot. Got an A pretty easily. His review sheets and podcasts are really helpful, and participating in discussion is essential. Know the experiments he talks about!

I've been at U-M for 3 yrs now, and Bill is definitely the best professor I've had! He loves what he does, and he genuinely cares about his students. Lectures were made fun and engaging with demos, music, and "clips of the day." Tests arent hard if you study his review sheets. On top of that, he's nice to look at. :) I love this man!

Simply the best. Bill is personable and genuinely a nice guy who cares about his students. There are no papers, your weekly workload is light, and the class is interesting and informative. If you want to do well on his exams, just make sure you understand all the concepts on his review sheets. If it's not on the sheet, then forget about it.

Trys to make everything interesting. Sometimes he explains the most confusing parts in a confusing way, but for the most part simplifies everything nicely. Really cares about cognitive psych, and is always excited. Plays fun music, funny videos halfway through class, and in-class demos

Great professor! I loved this class. It is set up to be an easy A. You do not have to do the reading. Bill is very interesting and knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. He teaches what the students want by asking about subjects they would like to study and asks for their opinion on hw assignments. Take this class if you get a chance

Extremely smart man. He made the material really interesting. This class was definitely worth my while. We always had really good discussions. I always enjoyed going to his class. He is really intelligent and it shows.
material isnt the most interesting thing ever but he does a great job trying to make it entertaining for an hour and a half. not hard at all if you know the review sheets for the exams.
Excellent lecturer, material is a bit dry but he makes going to class worth your while. Really funny, class is enjoyable and has a light work load. Recommend it.

Fantastic Professor. Very insightful about the subject matter and great at instigating discussions. One of the best Profs' here. Writing assignments are informal ways to keep the dialogue going. Mind, Brain, and Evil taught me more than I thought I could get out of a Psych Seminar. Definitely take this class.

Amazing professor.  My favorite so far.  Really easy class.  You don't have to do the readings but they are really interesting.  Writing assignments are really easy since they are very informal and short.  TAKE THIS CLASS!

He was indeed an unbelievably great professor. I enjoyed every minute of his class and his "clip of the day" always helped because we had a few minutes to relax and laugh out loud. If you have to take a mid-level psych class, definitely take this one!

Bill is a very good professor. He is fair and tests are pretty easy. The material is relatively easy, a lot of common sense stuff. Although, there are some areas that get pretty confusing. Lecture is long, but he makes it interesting so it goes quick. Enjoy this class!!
One of the best professor I've had here. Makes really hard stuff sound easy and tests are pretty fair as well as the assignments. Take advantage of coffee talks to get to know him.

Gehring is an amazing professor - the class itself is a little rough given the amount of technical material, but he genuinely wants students to succeed and makes his lectures very accessible.  His lecture structure (with the break for Clip of the Day) makes the long lecture easy to get through - tough class, great professor!
He is very funny and does a great job keeping the class interesting despite the actual topic being boring
He's a pretty helpful teacher. The lectures don't seem too necessary as long as you keep up on the readings, and the sections quizzes are harder than the exams themselves.
Awesome professor, explains material clearly, very interesting topics and great class even though it is tough.

I LOVE THIS MAN.  I would date him actually if the oppurtunity arose.  He is very clear in his lectures (which I recommend you attend) and who wouldn't want to - the clip of the day makes every lecture worth it. The class is rather mundane but I am glad I took it because, let's be honest, I am in love with Bill.

His teaching strategy is one of the most effective I've seen in such a large lecture. He keeps the class attentive by telling jokes and taking a break for a video "clip of the day" every class. He still manages to present large amounts of information without seeming rushed. In person, he is amiable and articulate. He has coffee with students.

Absolutely loved him. He brings in methods to make a not so interesting topic, fun. If you study his study guides for the exam, you'll breeze through the course. He is the coolest prof. I've had here at Michigan and would definitely recommend him!!!

Very interesting seminar and Gehring is great! Watched a lot of movies but they were all very relevant and interesting.  This seminar really got me interested in psychology and I'm planning on taking his psych 240 class later

Course is not easy (covers lots of ground, heavy reading), but he teaches in a way everything falls into place. You never walk out from a lecture feeling confused. Takes that extra step to get to know students better - his coffee hours are awesome.
professor gehring is amazing! you will love this man. he is well organized and has a great sense of humor. i definately recommend this class!
BEST professor ever!!!!

Seriously, the coolest man that there is. I'm not a psych major, rather I took the class for science credit and it was great!! It's not a walk in the park, but you can do well if you study the notes and read the chapters pretty carefully. He doesn't want to trick you at all. Cool guy! I chatted with him during office hours a couple times.

This man is amazing. His lectures are not only extremely easy to follow and clear, he helps to keep students entertained during class, which helps keep students motivated. If you can, definately take this class with him.
excellent.

Seriously brilliant lecturer, and genuinely nice person willing to be very generous with his time. No slouch or pushover on tests, but fair. If you get the chance, take one of his classes, it's worth your time.
Loved him and his clips of the day. The class was easy and his coffee talk made every student feel like he actually cared about meeting students in a large lecture.
Pure professoring badass.  The man knows how to present information clearly by using humor and in-lecture experiments.  Highly recommended.
No Comments
Awesome professor and class. I wasn't looking forward to the course but he made it interesting.
awesome professor, made boring material interesting, enjoyed clip of the day, taught the material very well, i love the man

Bill is the hottest prof I've had at UMich...AND he's a great teacher. Clips of the day...funny stuff from ebaumsworld and other funny websites make the hour and a half go by a lot quicker. I wonder if he's single...

Great professor, good sense of humor but still gets stuff done.  I took biopsych and it was nothing like this, so if you are not pre-med or not naturally scientific, I recommend him.  Also has a weekly coffee talk with a few students, which is really cool.

Cog psych is one of the harder psych classes you will take here, but Gehrig at least makes it interesting, and he is really funny!  Don't let the above statement fool you, you will have to study in this class :)

Extremely talented lecturer and overall funny guy.  Like many others I had to take this class, but it really hasn't been painful.  The text is bad, but he does an awesome job with the material, is very helpful, and writes exams so that you can succeed.  I had him for 121 too, he's the best prof ever

One of the best classes I've taken here. Took it for the Natural Science credits, and I wish he taught more classes! Finds ways to spice up the otherwise dry material, and isn't too hard on the eyes either :)

I didn't want to take this class at all and put it off as long as I could, but once I got in it I loved it! Not because of the material, but because of Dr. Gehring's teaching style and humor. If you have to take this class for your psych major, definitely take it with him.
i didn't want to take the class at all, but now that i am in it i love it and it is definetely due to him.
I didn't like the class itself, but he was great.  The clip of the day is always fun.

Cognitive science sucks, but he makes it relatively interesting and easy (boring text though). And - not that this matters - he's probably in the top three of the most attractive profs that I had in four years at Michigan.

Mind brain and violence seminar- easiest class at the univeristy. you go in, listen to him talk or watch his cool videos on psychopaths. no tests or quizes. one final paper- thats it. really down to earth cool guy. take this class.
No Comments

If there are any incoming freshman reading this that are somewhat interested in psychology, crime, or violent behavior, I HIGHLY recommend taking Bill's first year seminar (psych 121: Mind, Brain, and Violence).  The class is AMAZING.
ditto to everything above
Great teacher who really writes his tests in a way that makes a high grade very possible.  If you go to lecture, you never have to open the book!

I would genuinely never take 461. Ever. Actively googling "how to late drop a class". All written on a chalkboard. Very disorganized flow of ideas. Unsure of expectations. Lecture recordings are recorded but not made public because why would he make resources available to his students? Must request recordings when absent. No late homework allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This guy is a nice person and all, he does care about the students and tries to give feedback if you ask for it. HOWEVER getting any type of straight answer out of him is like pulling teeth. I have to ask him the same question at least 2 times to get a clear response. Some of the content is really confusing, and he doesn't do his best to help you.

Although the required papers are hard to read, Prof. Bleakley is a caring professor and always discusses the papers' ideas during lectures. So I would say this course is interesting and not that difficult as long as you catch up with every topic in class.

Material is interesting and I would even say that Bleakley is a good lecturer. However, every graded assignment (only 6) was SO utterly frustrating. Hw is about recreating models with vague & confusing instructions. Exams are super random and vary wildly in difficulty, also no practice material provided besides old exams (+they're not helpful)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at umich ever. Extremely disorganized, no slides, use handwriting instead. Use very strange and unusual symbols to represent the economics terms instead of what other professors usually do. Choose other courses plz. Run always ASAP
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't seem to prepare for lecture and mandates a lot of assumed knowledge that is closer to a graduate level than undergraduate. If you are not excellent at the modeling side of economics avoid his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is the worst professor I have ever had. He pretty much gave lectures from whatever he was thinking, with little to no structure every time. The course material should have been reserved for grad school, not college students, and he was terrible at explaining everything. The exams were impossible and he even said that a 68% was too high.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams in the course are much more challenging than other classes in the Econ department. Lectures are slightly disorganized which makes it difficult to prepare for exams. However, raw scores are curved very generously. Topics are interesting & prof is very knowledgeable.

I found the content in 461 to be deep and engaging. The professor draws much of his content on the mandatory reading. If you are able to adopt your learning style a little bit to accommodate his hand done notes, I think you will find that he is incredibly insightful. There are easier courses to take but I'm not one to obsess over a letter grade.

This class was very easily the hardest class Ive taken at Michigan. The lectures consist of him scribbling down him deriving equations, even though he had slides with them already derived. There were typos in everything including the exams. Once a topic was covered, it was never covered or connected. The final was 90% the first few lectures. Avoid
Simply one of the hardest courses I took at Michigan and severely math intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's Awesome

Lectures are done free hand, off the top of his head. Homework is Stata heavy, with little to no direction on coding. His exams consist of a couple of questions, with parts A B C D etc. If you cant do A, you cannot do the rest. Tests represent very little of the information presented in the class. If you care about ur mental health, don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bleakley is clearly here to research, not to teach. Lectures were directionless and disorganized with very few slides. Exams and homework were absurdly hard: 1st midterm average  56%, 2nd midterm (which he said was too easy) average  69%, homework graded harshly on correctness. Never clarified course grading/curve policies. AVOID IF POSSIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dont show up  you fail. lectures are very unorganized and confusing. They are mostly him writing equations on paper. Very math based: No joke, he took the partial derivative, log, and full differential of an equation in a one lecture. Spend SO much time on homework. Hardest econ class Ive taken (Harder than 401 and 402) RUN AWAY AND STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is confusing. He doesn't post lectures or slides online or in an organized manner. His lectures are unclear and uninteresting. Attendance isn't required, but most of the lecture is just him writing on the board, so you won't know what he talked about if you miss class. He's unclear about grading and expectations. Kind of pointless class.

For first few months of the semester, he had a high expectation from upper-level students so he explained the concept with extra details. This obviously confused the students but he simplified things at the end. I went to his office hour every week and got help for the problem set and understanding the concept. Exams are similar to problem sets.
Professor Bleakley is obviously very knowledgeable about Economics and Growth but is unclear in his explanations and leaves out important steps and background information in these explanations.

Waited until I graduated to make this judgement: Officially THE WORST Professor I have had.Simply put: Unwilling and unable to help one improve, unclear grading, memorization-based learning, dismissive, purely exam-based course grade, homework dissimilar to exams, does not explain concepts rather write definitions on board. Doesn't belong at UMich.

Prof Elliot only writing what is on the book during the lecture. It feels like there is nothing different between learning by yourself at home and listening the lecture. Anyways, the teaching skills is just awful.

Lectures were copied straight from the textbook, but example problems only covered the basics of the topics. Harsh grader on exams, and had poor explanations for grading. Explanations in class were vague, and I understood concepts better after teaching myself them.

Dr. Blackstone was a great professor—he explained everything clearly, graded fairly, and was always there to help with questions. He is sometimes a little bit blunt, but it's kind of funny. Great professor but not an easy class.

Fell far below the general standard of honors math. All exams (80% of our grade!) regurgitated problems from the textbook; studying became memorizing 100+ problems rather than LEARNING & ENJOYING math. Lectures copied from textbook. I started doing SO MUCH better (D -> A) once I started teaching myself from the textbook instead of going to class.

Pros: very intelligent professor; tests are fairly graded and cover exactly what you studied; lectures often clear up any confusion from the book and usually very thorough

Cons: 80% of grade from 3 tests and the final; sometimes vague in answering questions; homework may include topics not discussed in lecture/book; no practice tests provided
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor and course! The course uses ODE and geometric point of views to explain a lot of mechanical and physics phenomenon. The professor is very nice and always prepared. Office hours helps a lot for those who do not know much before. I learnt a lot even without taking much courses in analysis and geometry. Very inspiring overall.

Professor Bloch is a great guy that challenges you in the hw assignments, but grades leniently and give fair exams. His lectures are very interesting and he has a very subtle humor. One of my favorite classes.
This was a really interesting class with a  nice combination of math and physics and  clear lectures.
The Professor really seemed to care about the students in this class.
Helpful in office hours and class
I stopped attending lecture after the second exam because I was not learning anything in class. I taught myself for the rest of the term. Laplace was difficult without a good teacher.

He's a nice guy but just a really bad lecturer. Exams and homeworks are not hard, but he fails to explain even the basic concepts in class and you don't know what he's even talking about most of the time, the only good thing about the class is the book, which he did a good job choosing for the class
I'm not sure why people like him so much, while the exams and homework aren't too hard, he is an awful lecturer. Extremely boring and very confusing. You're better off just reading the book.
Professor Bloch is very helpful during office hours. His lectures are sometimes confusing, but he really wants his students to do well and always is willing to meet in office hours.

Bloch is the man. During Calc 3, I hated it but now looking back it was actually a really great class, I always liked Bloch he's pretty good at teaching and is helpful, if you're going to take applied honors Cal 3 definitely take it with him

Bloch had very useful office hours and would help explain the written homework, review questions, or recently learned concepts. Class was not always helpful, so go to office hours if you don't understand him. The book was often just as helpful as he was with general concepts. He sounds like Nigel Thornberry from "The WIld Thornberrys."
Great professor! Very clear teacher, homework and exams are about what you'd expect from Calc III. He's a past department chair and you can tell.

Professor seems like a kind person, but lectures were pretty boring. The weekly quizzes weren't exactly tough but pays attention to minor details, some that are even irrelevant. Overall, class wasn't hard since there were no exmas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was fine. There was little direction, though. Lecture heavy with lots of group paper reading and presenting on it. Other than that, thee class is graded on an exam and a paper. Very knowledgable but the class was confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Blum has a lot of interesting career experience and passion to share. However, the restructuring of this course didn't work for me, personally. I would attend lectures but still do poorly on the weekly quizzes. With last-minute extra credit I got an A+, but feel I learned very little. Not the best intro to a really cool subject matter.

I took this class a couple years ago and he was a perfectly good teacher. He explained everything pretty clearly (it was an intro class so not much extreme detail) and seemed invested in student success and open to questions. Lab was not great but other than that it was interesting and he did a good job helping you understand it.
He was a very kind, funny guy, but his lectures were pretty long and boring. The class was pretty easy if you went to the lectures and paid attention.
I really enjoyed the material taught, but the lectures were very boring. It was really unclear what we would be tested on so we relied heavily on the GSIs to tell us what to study.
Professor is nice, but the lecture material is unclear. If you read the textbook chapters it's a little better, but difficult to know what to memorize for the test. Frustrating to take notes.

Easy, especially if you go to lecture and pay attention. Discussion activities are easy and can be done at home and turned in later (aka lab attendance is optional). Gives you all questions prior to exam. Interesting lecturer, great teacher!

Blum's class is great. Incredibly easy. No textbook. Lecture is "required" but you don't have to go. There are 2 tests and minor presentations. Exam questions are given in advance. Take Geog 201 if you want an easy A and a natural science credit.
This course is pointless. In class student presentations make it so that you don't learn anything. Joel is great, but the gsis aren't helpful. And the lab has nothing to do with the course. Avoid it
Awesome prof. Clearly enjoys what he's doing and that makes learning that much more enjoyable as well. Always helpful and willing to explain things for greater clarity.

Wonderful, wonderful teacher.  I went to Camp Davis not expecting much, but Joel made what would have been a boring geology class incredibly interesting.  He shows a true passion for what he teaches and does a great job of conveying important information.  I would recommend him to anyone looking for a great learning experience.
Joel is absolutely awesome! He is passionate about the subject, teaching, and really enjoys getting to know his students. I would absolutely take another class with him, and definitely recommend him!

Joel is a wonderful teacher. He spells out exactly what you need to know for the test on his lecture slides, and it is quite possible to get a great score on the test without reading the text because of the thoroughness of the lecture (still, the book was fun). Very accessible teacher and loves his work. Strongly recommended teacher and fun class.
cool prof.  real easy material as long as you know definitions.  he loves geography.

Really nice guy and a great professor. He is easy to listen to and easy to follow. Plus, he does not expect too much-- you leave his class knowing a lot but it was not painful to get to that point. I highly recommend him.

Blaauw is very knowledgeable and a good professor, but the organization + administrative aspects of his courses make it difficult to recommend. He only taught during the final ~4 weeks of the semester. The class was primarily led by GSIs who did their best. Additionally, his exams are extremely difficult, with class averages often below 50%.

David Blaauw hates children. Genuinely fostered the worst taught class I've ever had the displeasure of having. Next time you plan on teaching a class, actually commit to teaching it. Ever see him for 312 or 427 avoid because he's not actually teaching it.
terrible class with no structure

reviews.comment: Unfortunatly he isnt a good teacher

reviews.comment: tests are nothing like the practice or lecture material
he failed literally the whole class
just nasty exams man.
Tests are a joke and are worth an infinite amount and have NOTHING from lecture.

reviews.comment: Tests are SO UNFAIR DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM

reviews.comment: Just dont take a class with this guy man the gsis run the class hes just gone.
Why does the exams have word for word questions from some random fabrication process mentioned for 2 seconds in lecture 1?

the average for the exam was a 45 and there was 0 circuits involved it was all random fun fact questions on circuits and it was nothing like the TWOOOOO practice questions released like why are we getting set up for failure. why are there 0 good learning materials?
Labs are incoherent and completely different from lectures and exam content is NOWHERE to be found it just appears on the exam somehow

reviews.comment: AMazingly stupid lectures that is

- DOES NOT GIVE YOU EXAMS BACK TO REVIEW 
- DOES NOT TEACH ANY MATERIAL COVERED ON EXAM
The Gsis ran the class he disappeared after day 1 unfortunately otherwise he wouldve been a great teacher :(.
Not even teaching the class, the GSIs teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most intelligent Profs I've had at umich. Explains concepts well and clearly. Super friendly guy also
i called him the flying dutchman because he talked so fast. but he's pretty solid
He is pretty freaking awesome. If he is teaching a section of a class you need to take, CHOOSE HIS SECTION because he is awesome.
Prof. Blaauw makes EECS 215 tough but fair. He emphasizes intuition, but he still shows many concrete examples in class. All in all, his lectures were great, and he's very helpful. I learned a lot.
awesome!
He always asks if anyone has questions and goes through the material slowly. Easy grader

He pre-records videos for each chapter in replacement of lecture, but he still has lectures to discuss articles. Lecture times are mostly for office hours. The biggest challenge was definitely understanding him because of his thick accent. He frequently made errors in his answer key for exams. The class's grading scale is nice though. 85+  A

I was really excited to take this class as I thought it was an interesting topic. However, I had a very hard time understanding him because of his thick accent. Even his writing was unclear at times. The class was all exams that were heavily weighted towards multiple choice. He was willing to hear student concerns and accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes not that bad and honestly if you put in a little work youll do fine

The worst class I have ever taken in the econ department (which is saying a lot). Extremely boring, material is pointlessly difficult, class drones on and on. A 1.5 hour lecture feels like 5 years. Will NEVER take a class with this guy ever again

Blanco was completely unorganized. There was no clear grading scheme and he made the test extremely hard. The hw questions he assigned were useless in helping to understand the material for the test. He was a very tough grader despite the already hard test. He also has a very strong accent and cannot explain class material clearly. The worst!!

She was an amazing professor who made coding accessible while still teaching statistics basics in great lectures. The homework was purposeful and her grading was clear and helped you improve. She genuinely cared about all her students and our success and was ready to help people solve issues with content and the class in general. I learned a lot.
Prof. Bloome is a clear lecturer and a genuinely wonderful human being. She cares about students' learnings and is really accessible for OH.

She is incredible. Many of the students enrolled were unaware this would be a coding class, but she promised us day 1 she would work just as hard, if not harder than us, to ensure our success in the class. She exceeded every expectation I had for this class, having no coding background whatsoever. Very approachable and personable. Go to OH!
Good lecturer, very fair with grading, accessible to students if they need help
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Bloome is amazing! I was apprehensive to take this course because I don't like math, but I am so happy that I did. She explains topics to make sure that everyone understands. There isn't too much homework and if you put in the work it will pay off. She does research as well on gender income inequality which is great. Office hours are good

I'm majoring in Sociology because I never wanted to take math again, so I was terrified of this course. Professor seemed intimidating at first, but also REALLY smart, helpful. By the end I really came to like stats and learned a lot about how to work w/ data. Make no mistake, this is hard material and you will be challenged. But the payoff is huge.
Seems nice and helpful if asked for help, but would throughly murder you with her exams. Would not recommend.

Horrible, worst experience I've had.  Took this to get out of a math credit since I'm not a math major, and it was ridiculously hard for an "elementary statistics" course.  Unclear in her lectures, lazy, and gives hard tests that look at whether or not you can read trick questions and teach yourself.
Kind of snotty. Would not recommend. The tests are rather easy, especially with the curve. Gives off that ivy-league grad vibe like she treats you like you're dumb.
Ben was an awesome GSI, he gave great feedback on papers and was always very respectful. Would highly recommend.

I had a great semester in Professor Blankenship's class! As long as you did the work that was expected and participated during class, it was possible to do really well. He offered extra credit assignments and was very respectful of the students. I learned a lot because he organized great class discussions. Great professor!

Ben is a pretty good person to do research with and work under, however he can be incredibly flaky and unresponsive to emails. He is very smart and very good at his research, which makes him incredibly busy which is why he is so bad at responding I think. Very easy grader.

Ben's a great GSI! You can tell he cares about his students because he's always offering additional help, direct feedback, or walking around checking up on tables during lab. Best GSI I've had at UMich so far! Grades fairly (and according to rubric) and you can always ask for feedback on the papers. Prepared for class and office hours are flexible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ben was easily the best GSI that I have had at UMich. He came to class prepared, and he was always willing to answer students' questions or meet during office hours. He truly wanted his students to succeed, and his calm personality helped the class run smoothly even when discussing some of the more difficult topics. I would highly recommend him!

Ben was an awesome GSI! He was very cool and collected during class and I was so fortunate to have him! He explained things very well and was a fair grader for sure. He wanted everyone to pass and also went with the flow for a lot of things. Would recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ben was a great GSI, always had extra office hours to help give feedback to students about writing assignments. Always had very clear powerpoint slides for every discussion session to help keep concepts clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ben was a really chill GSI! His discussions were super fair, and he's always willing to help outside of class. He goes over concepts with you during class in depth and is overall a great GSI. I would highly recommend taking his class!

Ben is an amazing discussion leader and chooses excellent readings that will really help you build an understanding of the ways our education system impacts the individuals within it. One of the best classes I took in my entire college career.
Ben was such a great GSI! I learned a lot from him and appreciated that he was always there if I needed help. I would definitely take his class again!
Ben was a great discussion teacher for Psych 290. Important to show up and participate though.
He is great!
Great GSI! His section really made the lecture better. Really fair grading, do the work properly and you will get your A.
Great GSI and very interesting class. Definitely recommend

Ben is the best GSI I have ever hard. He is not so much as an "easy grader" but more so understanding and VERY FAIR considering the level of the course. He is very easy to talk to and responds promptly. He really looks out for student's best interest. I can't thank him enough for a great semester!!!!!!!! A+++++++++++++++++++++++++++

As an engineer, this class was incredibly uninteresting for me. However, Ben was a great GSI. He was fair on grading, responded to questions well, and made understandable connections to the lecture content in discussions.

Ben was a great GSI for Psych 393. Always was nice and had clear expectations. He didn't lecture really, rather it was all about class participation and group exercises. Definitely recommend any class you could take with him!

Ben was great for Psych393Polsci 330! He was so helpful, and always had examples in section to help students understand the lecture material. Also, he always had interactive activities in class to help students immerse themselves in the material. "Online" participation (via twitter) is fun. DEFINITELY TAKE THIS CLASS -if you like psych of politics
Solid GSI, makes a really boring David Winter lecture enjoyable. One of the better psychology GSIs that I have had at Michigan. Good grader
Bodwin was goated but lecture and homeworks were a lot of busy work although this was due to the class. Everything else was great though
great prof

Bodwin is by FAR the best 203 lecturer. He's easy to listen to and on the 2x lecture recordings really sounds like Jesse Eisenberg! I didn't go in person to class so I tried all three lecturers and he stood out as the best. Take the advanced version of the class and the last 10 minutes is always a fun/weird puzzle. super interesting.
Professor Bodwin was great! Really enthusiastic lectures and willing to answer student's questions.

Professor Bodwin is such an amazing lecturer! Even though the class itself was rather difficult, he made lectures engaging and entertaining, and I looked forward to coming to class every single day. Even though attendance wasn't required, I still showed up to his lectures because he really is just that great of a teacher. 100% recommend for 203!

Pros: 
- Great async lectures
- Good speaker, and answers questions well
- Writes a lot of the homework problems, so office hours are helpful

Cons:
- Writes the hardest discovery problems
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. Extremely passionate about his job and teaching the students. Very caring/respectful and quite witty, always in a super infectious good mood. Wish I had him for all my classes. Made some tough material easier to understand.
Very clear and awesome lecturer, loved the bonus lectures and the pop-up office hours after classes! His great sense of humor is a plus too

203 was the hardest class I have ever taken in my life. Homework was unnecessarily long and exam median grades were 60% before the curve (thank god there was a curve). However, Bodwin himself was a great professor (I watched his lectures) and he made learning the content feel fun at times, although it was a difficult class when I took it
Lots of hw and three exams - but his lecture is so caring and respectful. Really, a man of honor.

Prof Bodwin's enthusiasm and nerdy charm made discrete math absolutely wonderful. He took the time during and after lectures to answer as many possible questions as he could and clearly cared about his students succeeding at and enjoying the material. I would not hesitate one bit to take him again. Also, his Twitter is funny if you're into math.
Engaging and interesting lectures; Makes a hard class easy.
Engaging lecture and the bonus topics were great
Great, clear lecturer who can make even complex content seem intuitive. Very flexible with deadlines, and seems to genuinely care about teaching.
nice and clear lecturer.
Hugely knowledgeable, makes lecture interesting

Professor Bodwin exudes an infectious enthusiasm for this course and delivers entertaining, thorough, and clear lectures all while demonstrating genuine respect and kindness towards his students. My favorite professor so far.

I disliked the content/class and found it to be conceptually difficult, but honestly, I passed because of Bodwin's lectures. Dude is an amazing lecturer that is actually passionate about discrete math.
Probably one of the best professors here

From the first day of class you can tell this guy loves what he does. He is a very enthusiastic and chill professor. I loved his witty jokes from time to time. he really seems like he cares about his students. He is also a pretty good lecturer, makes sure the class is engaged and offers to slow down or speed up depending on the feel of the class.

Bodwin was an amazing professor and it was very obvious that he has a strong passion for this subject as well as passion for teaching it. He's very clear in his slides and puts lots of emphasis on answering students questions and making sure all concepts are completely understood. For some pretty complex topics, Prof. Bodwin can always explain them
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His lectures where pretty clear and makes sure his students understand the material.
Fantastic professors and where to find them.  �� Took Professor Bodwin last winter but did not find an Um option back then. Great lectures, inspirational teaching, and a role model. Phenomenal.

Professor Bodwin is one of the nicest and humblest human beings I've met. He's brilliant at his work, but at the same time he does a good job at gently introducing difficult topics, and he was generous on grading and curving. I struggled a lot initially, but he and the staff supported me and helped me get my act together. A gem in UM CS.
Loved her!

Mara is a sweet teacher, easy to understand, and inspirational. She had daily participation quizzes and would give answers with thorough, helpful explanations in class. She's always willing to answer questions, especially during what she calls a "chat break" during each lecture. I would definitely take another class with her in the future!

Amazing professor. She is knowledgeable about her subject, and you can tell that she is passionate about it. She's very kind and approachable. The class has a small workload, with only a few exams, 5 homeworks, and a 3 question quiz every class, which you get the answers to in class. Exams make up most of your grade, so make sure you study.

Bollard was a great professor! She made lectures pretty easy to understand, and she was very passionate on cog sci! Your grade is based on lecture quizzes (which we discuss in class so it's pretty much easy perfect scores), 2 exams and a final, and 5 homeworks (best out of 4). Honestly, just study well & you'll be good. Take this class w her !!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's amazing! Lecture recordings and slides are always posted, which makes reviewing considerably easier. Exams are not designed to be particularly difficult, but some questions can trip you up a little. The content was fascinating as well. Definitely a must-take class while you're at Michigan!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bollard's introductory cognitive science survey was a wonderful introduction to the discipline. We get a fairly broad but shallow overview of concepts in cognitive science, phil. of mind, ethics, decision theory, etc, and they are unified in an interesting and memorable way. This course is a good way to gauge your interest in cognitive science.

I took this class for fun as an easy A, but it turned to be more effort than I intended to put toward this class. Lectures are extremely heavy and the readings are very long. Only take this class if you have to, dont take if you arent a cogsci/pysch major.

Professor Bollard gives amazing lectures that explain all content very well. Also, everything important from the readings she explains in lectures (so imo you don't have to do any of the readings). She's a great teacher and I highly recommend her!!

I sometimes found her lectures hard to follow in-person, but when I went through and watched the recordings, they were always very useful and clear---more a problem of Cogsci 200 being a large, lecture hall class. 
The few times I talked to her after lecture, she was always very generous with her time.
Not using a textbook makes studying harder.

Honestly stopped caring about this class after I P/F but Mara seems super sweet and you can tell she knows her stuff. Sometimes things can be a bit unclear, but for the most part she's decent! Lectures were a bit boring sometimes but honestly the accent makes it more engaging lol the guest lecturer she brought in for a bit def was not the best tho

Amazing professor, amazing class. Lectures were engaging and interesting, Mara is highly intelligent and knows how to break down topics to understand with ease. Take this class with her 100% if you can!

Dr Bollard is absolutely amazing! Clearly very passionate about the subject and her enthusiasm makes lectures that much more interesting. Topics covered are very interesting as well. The class itself is relatively easy and well structured. I recommend the class and professor!

She is so sweet and available. Very passionate about cogsci and makes you passionate as a result. Totally recommend taking the class if you're looking for something easy and doable. Go to lectures, and you'll be fine. Go for it!

Mara is very passionate about the subject material, and she is keen on providing students with opportunities for success. She is a decent lecturer, making it easy to understand the content. However, she can be quite boring at times. The exams and homework are pretty easy for this class.

This was a very lenient course; Mara is very clearly passionate about the subject and provided students with opportunities to learn more about cognitive science outside of course. Lectures were clear.

Homeworks and exams were way more difficult than what we learned in class. This was a 400 person lecture, so it was not engaging at all. Wouldn't take again, but it was a low course load. Bollard is good but the way she taught this class was poor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mara is the most engaging professor I have had. She is very interesting and makes the content very easy to understand. The exams are online, but you should know what you are doing. I definitely recommend this course.

She is great! Readings are pretty short, but you still learn a lot. She does a great job of making cognitive science accessible and interesting to those who are unfamiliar with it. The grade breakdown was really fair; homework, quizzes (which you practice and get answers to in class) are all pretty much graded evenly.

Awesome professor. Very light workload but still learned a lot and found the content interesting. She does a great job in her lectures of explaining concepts in a way everyone can understand and is extremely kind and thoughtful if you need help.

Mara is so sweet! She answers questions enthusiastically and never makes anyone feel stupid in class. Most of the grades are based on 5 homework assignments and 2 exams, but there are also graded quizzes (she gives the answers in class though).
loved mara! great lectures and she was super super kind

Mara is a good lecturer. She was very nice, respectful, and clear. It is clear that she really cares about and is passionate about the content.The class was all open note and and we had a good amount of time to do the homework. As long as you take notes you will be able to do well.

Mara is one of the nicest professors I've had; very accessible outside of class and really cares about learning.  Class is interesting for some units and incredibly boring for others.  She gives you all the quiz answers and exams are open note.  Homeworks are much harder than examples from class! Easy A if you pay attention.

Mara Bollard was a funny and passionate lecturer and she made hard concepts more digestible. As long as you pay attention in lecture this should be an easy A, she literally tells you all the correct quiz answers. Super interesting class, but since you cover so much, I found myself loving some units and absolutely hating others.

Thought this class was very easy to understand and informative. As long as you go to discussions and lectures and take notes you should be set. She is very clear and passionate about the material. Discussions give very helpful study guides and go over weekly homework assignments. Learned a lot from the class and some was review from psych 111.

Mara Bollard definitely cares about the material and the students, but wow is COGSCI 200 boring. Like, the most boring class I've ever taken! And to think I wanted to major in cognitive science before this class. Mara herself seems nice, but she was never able to make the course content interesting, in my opinion.

Wonderful course(will become 302 soon)! Wish this class could've lasted longer. Mara was amazing and very understanding, helpful, and genuinely cared. The way the class is set up ensures that you learn all the material, and the classwork directly translates to the homework then to the exams.

I loved taking this class with Professor Bollard. Lectures were interesting and informative and all the work we did felt like it really solidified my understanding of the concepts. Professor Bollard is so knowledgeable.

She's very nice and definitely doesn't mind working with students. She made online classes more interesting and was always motivated even though it was an early morning class. This class covers a lot of things just not with much depth, so it's a lot to remember. I didn't enjoy the class very much but that's because of the material. Mara was great.

Mara was great! She is very kind, and she definitely cares about her students. At times, her lectures could be slightly confusing when trying to translate them to the homework assignments. However, the GSIs and Professor Bollard are both available to help rather quickly. Quizzes (2/week) and homeworks(1/2 weeks) have plenty of time to complete.

There are home work problems every two weeks that are less than an hour, short readings before lectures and lecture quizzes after each lecture. I took this class first semester of freshman year to try something new and now I am considering majoring! Grade has a lot of components so you do not need to stress about the midterm and final (open note).

Interactive format, which is necessary for online classes. Great discussion sections and interesting lectures. There are a fair amount of reading assignments, but they are fun and short. Easy to score if you put in efforts. Would recommend 100%

She's AMAZING!! Nothing more to say. The most unexpected class of the semester and it turned out to be my favorite class! Her entire team is the best example of a well-run department during Covid. The class was really fun and interesting. She's also extremely sweet and great to talk to.

She is always full of energy in her lectures, and the workload isn't too difficult. I definitely recommend taking this class, especially with this awesome instructor, for anyone remotely interested in cognitive science.

Im so glad to have had her for my first semester after transferring. Shes engaging, very friendly, and the course content is very interesting. She does a good job of making complicated topics digestible. Definitely take her. Shes especially accommodating during the covid situation and actually helpful.

I love Dr. Bollard but not CogSci 200. Her lectures are cheery, clear, and charismatic. She has 3 graded iClicker questions per class, but it is easy to stay engaged. Tests are fair, drawing heavily from lecture slides. HW readings are short. If you (for some reason) want to take CogSci 200 (don't), take Dr. Bollard. Also, her accent is amazing.
