reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I cannot stress enough: Dr. Bollard is one of the kindest people I've ever met and she is an amazing professor who cares about what she teaches as well as her students. She has very clear grading criteria, and this class is also a super interesting one worth taking (a pretty easy A). I will jump at any chance I have to take another class with her.

Mara was truly a great teacher. You could sense her excitement about the material every time she started lecturing. She loves when you come to her office hours and wants to get to know her students so that she can teach them better. Highly recommend!

Mara was an awesome GSI. She made discussion enjoyable, and for nearly every class provided a handout that compiled everything from the lecture that would probably be important for an exam. She is a very good grader, and gives genuinely great feedback on assignments. She helped make the class significantly easier and enjoyable!
Rigorous but nice professor. I think his version is much better taught than proulx if you're considering grad school.
Very kind man but unfortunately a strong disconnect between what is taught in lecture and what you need to know for homework and exams.

Mandatory 8:30 AM lectures with no recordings make attendance and staying alert a challenge. The course is graded almost entirely on four long-answer only exams worth 24% each, (96% total.)

Proulx offers recorded lectures, extra credit, and three exams that total 75% of your grade. His exams are also entirely multiple choice.

No Contest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Without a doubt, the best economics professor I have ever had! Incredibly supportive and always willing to help students grow and improve.

Tilman is not the highest paid prof in the econ department, but I'm sure he appreciates the compliment in a previous review! Cons: his exams can be difficult and lectures can get a bit "in the weeds." Pros: he is committed to teaching economic theory and loves his field. You'll come out of his course knowing more than students in other classes.

In terms of 401 professors at UMich, he is one of the best options. Think he is easier than others, but thats really not saying much. He writes the book used for class. Exams were really hard but again, 401 at UMich. I would recommend him over Proulx any day. Be ready to learn the material on your own, since lectures are boring and not helpful.

I regret I took him instead of other prof. His exams are a lot different from other profs... Other prof gives mathematical questions, so students can solve it if they prepare. But he asks you to explain things by yourself on the exam. I heard he started doing this recently and his exams were okay before. Please take other prof if you aim to get A.

class was insanely difficult with Tilman. He is extremely understanding and a genius (he's the highest paid econ professor at UM). However, he doesn't really understand whats difficult for his undergrad students, so his exams are very difficult to do well on. Do not take unless you have a VERY strong calculus conceptual understanding.

Probably the professor to have if you are taking 401. Exams are difficult but there are resources like practice problems, lecture notes, and homework will help prepare for them and he is accessible outside of class and on Canvas. Just keep up with the materials and you'll do fine. GSI was bit of a downer though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Tilman's circulates lecture notes which help to a great extent in understanding course material. Be sure to constantly keep up with the material - homework, practice problems and past exams are a good way to review course material. Exams are challenging but doable. Lectures aren't dry and he keeps students engaged.

He's trying a new teaching method starting this semester which is not working. You have little to go by for what's going to be on the exams. I don't think he intentionally tries to make the exams impossible but he doesn't understand what's difficult for people so the exams are end up being extremely hard. Probably shouldn't teach undergrad.

Class material is very hard and his lectures dont help at all. Just rambles and expects students to understand the material. Ended up just having to learn the material on my own. Exams were very difficult and the class average was below a 50. For the hardest class in the econ major felt like he did little to make it easier.

Easily the best professor I have taken a class from at Michigan. Crystal-clear in class, and really helpful in office hours. Truly cares about his students. I only got a B-, but it was very well worth it and I would take another class with him any time.
do not need textbook. All multiple choice questions. But it is the hardest course i have ever taken. Lecture is useless and no extra credit.

Tough class and not a great lecturer. I learned most of the work on my own and class is curved so my grade had nearly nothing to do with his teaching. Was hard to learn from his lectures and ended up just studying independently to do well in the class. Textbook was completely useless and waste of money

If you're going to take 401, take it with Tilman! He was fair, and made a bunch of jokes that wouldn't be funny unless they're coming from a  Professor. 401 isn't as awful as everyone says as long as you stay on top of it and try. Also, take advantage of pooled office hours if you think you're struggling.

Realizing how good I had it compared to 402 with Cravino.  I thought he was one of the best Econ professors I've had, he explained things concisely and was entertaining in lecture. 401 like most Econ classes is one where you have to work through the problems on your own to understand, but his lectures were  useful and discussion was very much so.
It's a hard class but he is a great lecturer.

After not passing this course, I have taken it with another professor starting with the letter P, both of these professors are pretty horrible but tilman was absolutely worse. Disregard most of the ratings before the fall semester of 2014 as he changed the entire system to writing only, no multiple choice, all written exams. He was ruthless to me.
not good

Tilman was a great professor for Econ 401. It's a tough class and requires a lot of work, but he provides lots of extra resources to make sure you succeed and wants to see all of his students do well. Very helpful in office hours and responds very quickly to forums posts and emails. I would definitely recommend taking 401 with Tilman.

He is a fantastic professor.  He explains material clearly and concisely in a positive manner.  He knows what he is teaching really well and is confident with the material.  Overall, great experience with a great professor.  Plus, he wears purple sweaters!

One of the worst experiences of my life, my GSI would grade really tough and when I complained to him he went off on me during office hours. He grades really tough, all you need to know before taking this class is partial derivatives, chain rule, product rule, first and second order condition and you should be fine. He FAILED 30 STUDENTS, UNREAL.

Hard class.   He is a good prof. He cares and gives students lots of time.  Most people teaching econ aren't really even profs, they are lecturers.  All econ majors need this course for the degree - absolutely the best person to take this course with. The lectures can be really funny.

What an incredible professor! His clear, well thought-out lectures and attentiveness to the students, I was able to grasp a lot of very difficult subjects.  Spent extra time on the harder concepts and stressed those concepts until he was sure the students understood. By far the best econ professor I've taken at Michigan.

You need to go to lecture for this course; the side comments are  very funny.  He changed the exam style from previous years and got rid of multiple choice tests.  Being good at math alone will no longer get you the grades.   First Prof  I've ever had here in a large course that is really accessible .   He seems to really care that we learn.

Lectures are just him making quiet, awkward jokes to himself. His slides are as barren as the Serengeti.  If you don't go to lecture the slides will be even more confusing, but he does post the slides. The assignments are graded way too harshly and the only reason I was ever able to do them correctly was because of the GSIs. He does seem friendly.

I really hated Econ 401, but that's because I hate Econ. Tilman is awesome. He is very clear in lecture and he makes little awkward jokes to himself and it's super funny. Tests are difficult. Grading is tough. But Tilman is a cool guy.

He is very nice during his office hours and is considerate of the gradings. If the GSIs graded your midterms too harshly, you can go to his office hours and talk to him about it,and he will even give you points (as long as you justify clearly and give good reasons).

Dr. Borgers is amazing. He makes his lecture interesting. For this year, he changes his method to teach and test. There will be no multiple choices. Although the problem set is flexible, it is very interesting and not too hard to learn. You will benefit a lot as long as you put efforts in thinking.
A bad lecturer but a very helpful man in person. Class is decently well organized and not exceptionally difficult.

Tillman is an absolute textbook genius. Don't let the class get over your head, dont EVER fall behind and don't be afraid to ask specific questions. He will always be able to answer. With trepidation avoided. You should succeed in this class.

Tilman is amazing. He makes students laugh a lot, which is really nice considering the rather dull material. His lectures are very clear and certainly helpful. Class is difficult but if you put the effort in, you will do well.

Tilman was an amazing econ teacher! The class was definitely not easy, but he made it very clear and was very willing to offer help to students. He was also very funny during class - made me actually want to go to lecture!
This professor is amazing! His lectures are straightforward and he makes hilarious side comments. Homework is based on effort and if you're good at math, the class will be easy.
This guy is the best, he's really clear and very funny. If you take this class take it with Tilman, almost everyone loves him. The course isn't easy but it's nothing to be afraid of.
Great Class. Great Professor. A lot of material is covered... but if you are good with math, it will be pretty easy.

Tilman is such a boss I graded him as hot for fun. Aside from that, the class isn't insanely difficult, it just covers an insane amount of material with respectable depth. Studystudystudy especially section problems before tests and all will be ok!
He's a good guy, and willing to laugh at himself as well as his mistakes. Class is pretty hard though, final was really rough

If you have to take Econ 401, I truly cannot imagine there is a better professor. Tillman is the man, and he is quite funny. He explains the concepts in their simplest form in lecture, section problems get slightly more difficult, and then even more difficult with HW. As long as you stay up to date with the topics, you learn them, and you do well.

Tilman is a really good professor who really knows his stuff. He's amazingly funny and laughs at himself a lot. I had the pleasure of being in the honor's section taught by him and always enjoyed his teaching and jokes

Tilman is a boss.  Coolest dude.  It's a very difficult class, but you need to take it for the Econ major.  If you need to take it take it with Tilman.  Very good teacher who understands the difficultly of the class and is always willing to help.

Great and interesting professor. He makes me love econ and Germany! Pay 100% attention to the class and try to understand everything on the slides and go to office hour. It's not a hard class, but you need have the attitude.
Easy
the best professor i've ever seen in the econ department!

Definitely take 401 with him and not any of the other profs. Lectures are crystal clear and also really funny. Exams are fairly difficult, but there are so many opportunities to get help plus solution explanations for all problem sets and practice test questions are posted. Most organized class I've ever taken :)

Even though most lectures aren't that useful he's a great teacher. This guy really knows his stuff and he is really funny. The only time I ever used the textbook was to do the HW. Study the problem sets for each topic really well and take the practice exams to prepare. Exams are doable if you're willing to put in the work for each topic.
difficult material. but he makes it much more clear. I don't think lecture is mandatory, but i highly recommend going because he is a funny person, and is very knowledgeable about the subject.
Lectures barely skim the top of what you need to know for the exams. Textbook is almost completely useless. Therefore, you have to learn everything in section and office hours. Exams are really hard.

Great professor. Really understands the material he is teaching and knows how to teach his students. He is also very helpful in office hours. Take 401 with him if you need to. The exams are also extremely hard but fair.

I took his econ 401, he is one whose 401 must be taken at all cost! If you want a decent grade, take his 401, if you want to understand materials, take his 401, if you just want someone who you can talk to with ease, take his 401.
Great professor. He's funny and wants to help his students. I would recommend taking his course for whatever he's teaching.

He is a good, clear professor. Very approachable and attempts to lighten the mood in class. He genuinely wants to not fail people, which is a nice attribute of a professor in a class meant to discourage econ majors.
Crystal clear lectures. Lots of extra problems from previous years clsses. Easy if you bother to show up and listen.
He is a nice guy and tries his best, but I can barely understand him and lectures don't help much at all for exams. It's a hard class but his teaching has not made it any easier.

401 is notorious for ruining GPAs and changing people who previously were Econ majors but Borgers does a wonderful job with the course and grading. Previously the course averages were 50% but with him it's actually in the 70% range. Very helpful and approachable. If you have to take 401, take it with him.

Amazing professor.  401 is a ridiculously difficult class but he gives you the tools you need to succeed. Gives detailed answers questions from email or online forum.  Extremely organized class with lots of practice (section and homework) problems for the exam. Textbook helps.
Tough class with very helpful professor.  Be sure you are well prepared.  Excellent, funny lectures.   He personally answered email questions with long, clear responses.

MATH 215 is an difficult class, due to Dr. Dunworth writing very hard HW and tests. However, Dr. B was an great professor given the circumstances. He taught very clearly and was great at answering questions. Unfortunately, he tended to rush through some lectures, and the problems he did in class were very easy and not reflective of the HW or exams.
Professor B was a very straightforward lecturer in 215 last semester. He was approachable and patient with my silly questions at office hours.
Prof. B was a good professor. The class was very diffcult but was not his fault.

Professor B was an incredible professor for Calc 3. This course is challenging, but I feel he explained it rather well. You can tell he has a passion for teaching and for Calc 3. His lectures are great, and he posts his notes. He is very accessible with office hours and via email. He also stays after class to answer questions. Highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is super hard, but it's not really his fault. Dunworth writes the tests and homework and they are brutal. The curve was very good, but still a B average for the class. Dr. B is a nice guy and always ready to help, but sometimes he can rush during the lecture. Not a bad guy, just a horrible course in general.

Honestly I think prof. Bongiovanni is one of the best professors at Umich. He is so organized, prepared and passionate about what he is teaching in lectures. Furthermore he actually cares about his students and stays over a few extra minutes to answer any questions or doubts. WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS OUT THERE!!!!!

Honestly one of the best professors I've had in the ME department. He really cares about you actually learning the material instead of memorizing or trying to use pattern recognition to solve problems. Exams are very resonable. He's also pretty good at explaining stuff.

He is a very understandable professor. Content is tricky, but he teaches everything in a way where if you follow his steps, you will get a lot of partial credit on the exam even if you mess up. Care about students performing well, and will bump grades if you are close to cut-offs.

Prof. Popa is a very calm and collected person who explains material very clearly and at an appreciable pace. His exams can get tricky at times, but he grades based mostly on process, so arithmetic errors aren't a huge concern on exams. He also has two engaging MATLAB group projects which further our understanding of the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great professor who taught the materials clearly. Also, for the exams, he gave you full points if your approach and fundamental equations were correct even if algebraic errors are made later in the work.

Overall a nice guy who knows his stuff and teaches well. Made a point to learn the students' names. Very responsive to feedback. For example, some students asked that we work on more examples and he dedicated Fridays to working on exam style questions. Easy to reach at office hours. Exams, grading, and grading scale all very fair.

Another perspective which is completely opposite of the review below me. The class was great. The exams are easy, he grades lightly, and he wants to help you learn the material. He is an overall nice professor who definitely cares about learning his students' names. I loved that Professor Popa went into depth in the derivation of formulas.

This class was awful. We were not given a practice exam or questions to study from for the first midterm. We got two practice exams and no answers for the second. Dr. Popa tries to make the material engaging but often lectures above that of an introductory ME course. He is very receptive to feedback and tried to learn all of his students' names.
Assigns the most homework and project in history, that you'll need to spend over at least 10 hours after class each week just to complete all the homeworks.

While EECS 492 definitely got harder than past semesters, Professor Bogaerts was a great lecturer. He was very caring and thoroughly answered questions in class. I highly recommend going to class in person, as the content is a lot more digestible this way!

DO NOT TAKE EECS492. This is the most content dense class I've ever taken. As an INTRO class, there is enough content to divide this course into two different ones. Exams are unfair and nothing like the practice ones. Lectures were packed with content and equations/graphs that were not talked about enough. Take 442, 388, or 445 instead.

DO NOT TAKE FOR EECS 492! The class has been completely revamped and there is double the content crammed into the course with more depth and harder exams. The exams are nothing like whats shown in lecture. And this man just glosses over every mathematical formula during lecture like its nothing. Don't take this class or you will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Despite provided online lecture, I went to in-person lecture just for Bogaerts. He was always kind and inspirational and you could tell he really wanted us to succeed. Although attendance was low in lecture, he always taught with the same amount of vigor and passion. His mantra "you belong here" actually helped me a lot over the semester.

Amazing guy that makes you happy to come in and learn every class. He makes everyone feel so welcomed to ask questions and clearly spends a lot of effort on making the class an inclusive and immersive experience. It's always a relief to have a prof as nice as him to brighten the day.
He makes difficult problems easy to understand. also very kind!

Lectures were very informational and engaging. He obviously cares about the material and his students, and is very accessible outside of class hours. Great teacher for EECS 280, as long as you pay attention to lectures then you should be prepared for everything. He makes every student feel valued, and is willing to answer any question.

His teaching style was perfect for my learning style. I found that as long as I take good notes during class, I am able to keep up with the content, and he does a great job at simplifying otherwise harder concepts. He also makes sure every student feels welcome, and his office hours are a great place to solidify concepts.

I would say that this class is pretty hard for people who have no coding experience. I took AP CSA in highschool so for me it was pretty easy. However, the pace is incredibly fast for newcomers. Bogaerts was an amazing teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and is ready to take the time to help students outside of class as well.

Great professor and overall good guy, can be a bit experimental and freeform with lecture style and content, but the material is overall solid stuff - definitely helpful for high level coding patterns.

Beyond that, he has very clear grading criteria and is happy to help you do the best you can. 10/10 would take again.
The format of this class really didn't work for me - it was hard to follow along with what was happening. More structure would have been better.

Excellent lecturer for the data-oriented mastery course. Allows for a good deal of flexibility within the project specifications and provides ample support during and outside of class. Allows students to really concentrate on the project all semester and minimizes distractions. Provides time in class for group work, if needed. Good guest speakers.

Attend half of the lectures and get all late penalties waived, an absolutely wild deal but helps immensely with planning around other classes! This also means grading will take longer. Many assignments have clear rubrics and extra credit opportunities. He'll help prep for coding interviews, and the labs try too. Lab time could be made more valuable

David Brick is extremely knowledgable on Hinduism and encourages participation. His class was amazing and was one of those classes that actually makes you want to go an listen. The exams were very easy as well and he posts a study guide before the exams that is extremely similar to the exam. Getting an A is easily attainable.

(Took for Sanskrit, not ASIAN225) Had a ton of fun in Dave's classes. Great teacher, very knowledgeable about Sanskrit and its linguistic history. Funny and kind. Classes were definitely grammar-heavy, but I liked that. Class was easy, but if you're really invested in learning, that's perfect — never worried about my grade, and I learned a ton.

Brick is kind and helpful.Did not at all feel like an introduction class during the first few lectures - felt as though basic/beginner knowledge is crucial for understanding the course but it was not provided. Lectures are reused b&w text heavy powerpoints, which is fine but not ideal. Exams are short answer which makes grading slightly arbitrary.

Professor Brick is extremely knowledgeable about Hinduism beyond the scope of the content of this intro course. His lectures are engaging as his passion for and knowledge of the subject is clear, while also being interactive with opportunities to ask questions. Exam content is quite predictable as he provides a comprehensive study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a Hindu student taking an Intro to Hinduism class, I was a bit apprehensive about having a non-Indian non-Hindu professor, but David Brick completely dispelled those worries. He understands a lot about the religion and approaches material with a knowing appreciation for the religion and culture. He's also really funny, sometimes even on purpose.

Professor Brown has good intentions but she is very cringy and hard to listen to. She knows a lot about what she teaches, however students find the course material uninteresting. She is a very kind person, but I would not take again.

Nightly readings of ~20-30 pages and they are just the most boring readings I think I've ever encountered. I don't think this is necessarily Professor Brown's fault, but If you want an easy A, take another Honors class like 241 because this class is just busywork on the most uninteresting topics and it's unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Brown had to step in and take on this course last minute, so I respect her for that. Her classroom style is very hands on and involved, but the lectures were somewhat disorganized and relied a lot on sometimes inane student participation. She tries a lot to be the "fun" professor, which meant the content and learning suffered.

What more is there to want?

A+ prof

I took the class online which meant we didn't get to cook and try food during lab (as would happen during non-COVID years). It was still fun, though, as the grading was split across different creative assignment options. This class encouraged me to engage with my Asian heritage, and I learned more about food in a historical and cultural context.

Great class that I'm sure would have been an even better experience in person. Due to the size and nature of the course I didn't get much chance to interact with Prof. Brown, but nonetheless can say she is undoubtedly one of the most caring at the University. Gameful grading that was made even less stressful when she reduced the cutoffs.

Asian 258 is an awesome, outside-the-box course. There are food labs where you go actually make the food you're learning about, which is really fun. Discussion can be a little boring since it's just a review of the lecture. Dr. Brown is hilarious and an incredibly engaging lecturer!

Solid teacher who cares more for you as a person than as a student. The class was about TCM and she really got me interested in the subject. Discussions can sometimes feel long but she always make sure to take breaks if needed. Always flexible and willing to accommodate if you need anything.

Usually classes that are easy to do we well in, I often also feel I didn't learn that much. Not in this case. Grading is easy and straightforward. Miranda is affable and very friendly. Basically the class consists of weekly readings and writing summaries. Each class, we just discuss that weeks reading. Readings are very short and usually engaging.

Not as easy as before, but still manageable to get 4.0. Offers extra credit which really does help your GPA. Weekly writing assignments are really annoying, but it helps for writing three main essays. Also, you have to go to discussion every week to receive points. However, the lecture was very inspirational and great. I really enjoyed this class.

She gives extra credit if you get 99% or 98% iclicker questions right. There is no quizzes or exams. Short response about 500 words every week. And three essays. The creative project will be given full points. It's easy to pass but if you take it as graded, you need to put effort in. It is not hard. GSIs and Mrs. Brown are extremely willing to help

Awesome professor with entertaining lectures. Make sure you use your laptop to ace the iClicker questions (she gives extra credit) The weekly assignments can get a bit repetitive sometime. Also go to office hours to get essay feedback / advice. I would definitely take this class if you want a good grade. Requires minimal effort for 4 credits.
Knowledgeable and helpful

easiest class I have ever taken at UM. You get 5% just for going to every lecture, which basically makes it out of 105. 3, 3 page short papers and a creative project (got a 100/100 on it). There are weekly reading questions but I just did them in lecture because well I had to go to lecture to get the extra credit! everyone i knew in it got an A+
Easiest A ever. Take courses with brown if you want an easy fluff course to fill your humanities/social studies requirements.
Awesome class. Definitely recommend it. Professor Brown is an amazing teacher and if you go to the lectures, the reading homework is really easy.

The class is easy but work is involved. Readings every week for a weekly HW. GSI's heavily determine these grades - I had a hard GSI so I had to put effort into the HW. 5% extra credit is given if attended all lectures! I recommend having Miranda check your essay, she's an easy grader & Miranda is one of the most adorable prof ever!! I <3 her. #FTW

She's a nice professor. It is fun to have her lecture and I really enjoy her question discussion part during the lecture. She answers students' questions clearly. Overall, a very fun class~ Btw, if you attend all the lecture, you get 3% bonus points for your final grade.
An interesting and fairly easy class. She is kind of flakey and brings up personal issues but knows a lot and wants to be helpful. Final paper requires several drafts but an easy grader.

Her lectures are boring and you won't learn much of anything. Once people realized that attendance was not mandatory in order to get an A, they didn't show and then she made it mandatory.  Most people just surf the web.  You really don't have to do the readings for the course, just do the paper topic readings. Waste of time but an easy A.

The class is really the history of medicine taught by comparing ancient Chinese and ancient Greek/Roman practices. Value of discussion depends on student participation. Paper subjects were interesting. You will take out what you're willing to put in.

This class was not difficult at all.  You have to attend lecture and do two presentations. You also have two paper drafts worth 10% of your grade each and two final drafts worth 20% each. Discussions are boring but you can be proactive and engage in it.  She's a cool person with personal issues but don't let that stop you from taking the class.
She's a great professor. The class is interesting and easy. Just go to the lectures that you need to write your essay about.
Easy effin class... entertaining

I love this woman! She's pretty funny, considering ancient Chinese history is not, and she was really nice and helpful. There were only four 750 word papers and two 10-minute PowerPoints (pass-fail!) in discussion. It was a great class, and everybody should take it! Love it!
Didn't learn much but got an A

The workload is very light - only four 500 word papers.  You definitely do not need to read as assigned as long as you study the question you are writing about.  I learned close to nothing from this class.
grades are based on two take home essays 50% each. discrimatory grading by gsi's and no chance of a regrade. lectures and discussion don't help you in any way.
No Comments
No Comments

very energetic and loves what she teaches, she wants to see you do well and was very helpful. exams where take home which made it nice expecially going into an asian history class not knowing anyone or anything about the culture.
No Comments
No Comments
Very easy class. Lectures are boring, and you really do not need to pay attention. The lab days are really nice; they will basically set you up perfectly for the project.
Easy to understand even with no previous coding experience. He's good with giving you extensions and is very supportive of mental health. All in all, super kind and knowledgable.

The class might be a bit tricky if you've never done programming before, but there's tons of resources if you ever need help. Professor Miller does good lectures that actually makes the material make sense with relevant examples. He's easy to approach and ask questions to both in and out of class.

I took this class because I had heard it was an “easy A.” While it may be an easy A for students who already know coding and have the energy to deal with it, not for me. The class ultimately felt like an extra chore. Workload was not heavy; difficult if you aren't familiar with Snap coding. Class was challenging without prior coding experience.
Knows what he's talking about and clearly passionate about what he teaches

I was worried about learning early English Lit, but Gina's lectures are engaging and accessible!! I definitely felt my writing improving by the end of this class, I learned a lot that I still remember today, and she's overall an incredible teacher.  Definitely reccomend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gina is very strict both with attendance and group discussion. If she doesn't like what you have to say she will publicly dismiss you. She was incredibly rude and condescending about extensions and accomodations. I wanted to like her and her class as I loved the topic and think that she is extremely smart, I just couldn't get past her attitude.

She is one of the least understanding professors. Very strict about being on time to class and does not take assignments if you are not there exactly when the class starts. Multiple people were kicked out of class for being a minute or two late and got 0's on the assignment, even if you had a reason for being late or a note. Would not recommend.

This was one of the harder classes I've taken in the English department, but Gina is such a brilliant and incredible instructor. I loved learning under her, even if I didn't exactly love medieval studies. I would certainly take a class with her again, I feel like working under her I improved as a student and an essay writer.

I've never written a RMP, but I had to for Gina. In four years at U-M she is easily the best professor I ever had. She is brilliant, hilarious, caring, and kind. Her classes are incredible and she is U-M's most thoughtful professor. She truly cares for her students. Her grading is precise and fair: When you get a grade, you feel you earned it.

Gina's class was my favorite this semester because of how funny she is, and she tries to involve all the students when discussing the readings. The papers can be challenging, but she has outlines and peer review days to make sure you succeed. The directions for all her assignments are also very clear, so it's easy to make an A if you participate.

Gina is great! She is very strict about attendance and late work, but her expectations were always laid out well on the rubric. Gina is hilarious, passionate, engaging, and gives great feedback. Though I had to watch several movies and read A LOT for ENG290, I enjoyed most of these works. If you're a horror fan, this is a must-take class!

I LOVE Gina but I will say the course description is misleading. It gets you with the "lovers and fighters" when 'lovers' comes few and far between and "fighters" comes from medieval times. Course load was also super heavy with old English readings, papers, and Midterm + cumulative Final (NOT easy). If it was any other professor I would've dropped
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Read one of Gina's previous syllabi before you take her. She is a funny and engaging lecturer and refreshingly candid about what to take notes on ("This will/won't be on the exam" is common). That being said, she is SUPER picky about deadlines and attendance, and her writing assignments have a very particular (yet clear and detailed) rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Gina is great, and her lectures are hilarious and engaging. She really knows her stuff, and her classes welcome open, low-stakes discussion.

That being said, she is an incredibly harsh grader, and doesn't always give the best feedback. Her course policies are STRICT, and she is not the most forgiving... Zero tolerance for late work and tardiness.

Gina is hands down the best professor I have had so far here. Her passion for her work is evident in the way she connects with her students and runs class like a conversation instead of a lecture. She picks outstanding readings spanning across the horror genre and I honestly don't have anything negative to say. Show up on time and dive in!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Absolutely love Gina. If you're a horror fan this class is for you. Her lectures are group-discussion oriented which is very engaging. When you raise your hand to add to the conversation she genuinely listens and adds onto your point, which I usually don't see profs do. She's really good at deep analysis of literature and film as well!

She's very condescending and has a superiority complex. I missed one class the whole semester due to health problems and she had a hissy fit over email and then sent a reminder email about getting doctor's notes to everyone in the class.

Gina is an amazing person with an incredible in class dynamic. Her feedback for essays is a bit confusing, and she doesnt really seek to help you improve. But the our GSI was amazing with feedback and super helpful, so it canceled out at the end of the day. I would 100% recommend this class to any horror fan. Gina is awesome
The grading for essays in a 200-level course was ridiculously harsh. The feedback given on the essays was helpful in no way either.

Obviously very passionate about the material, but short and uninformative lectures leave a lot to be desired. She's a harsh grader for papers - I agree with other reviewers that said you absolutely should not take her classes unless you're a good writer, because she doesn't give you very many chances to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was genuinely so excited for this course and she was SO condescending. And she gave me bad grades with no explanation (mind you, she doesn't teach at all; she just assigns readings). Though she claimed you needed no experience with the subject matter, I could tell she favored students who had more knowledge coming in. So yes, I dropped the class!

gina is one of the best professors i have had at u of m. she is clear, makes you laugh, and incredibly brilliant. if you need a pre-1450 class for english, take 450 with her. she makes the material sound interesting and not as intimidating. can't recommend her classes enough!

I took her class because it was an intro to horror but she teaches nothing in the class. We just summarize what happens in the readings which is fine but then I might as well just stay in my dorm and not go to class and I'd get the same out of it....

Gina's class was amazing to learn more about Horror. She's engaging and funny, and the class atmosphere reflects that. She's a HARD grader though, if you aren't used to writing you might struggle. Go to office hours for help on papers. Although she's usually chill she's really aggro about being late, even 2-3 minutes, it's a obnoxious.

Her lectures are engaging, funny, and make the material easy to understand. She offers extra credit and room for creativity (we had a pinata drawn and quartered on the final day!) Be careful about your participation and preparedness for class by having the readings printed out.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gina is always so energetic and enthusiastic, making going to class a joy, and she really knows how to relate to her students. You can tell she takes time to give helpful and encouraging feedback on assignments as well. Thankfully she doesn't force you to talk in class, though there is a fair amount of reading and a steady flow of assignments.

Gina's a rockstar. This class was super fun and even though it's a lot of reading, the material is really interesting and the class discussions make it better. You'll have a better time if you participate in the discussions, and it'll also make the papers easier. Just utilize her if you need help with writing; she's very helpful!
I love Gina! She's an amazing and very humorous person however, while the content in the class is extremely interesting if you are not a good writer DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Really fun and enthusiastic. This class was super interesting and Gina kept the discussion going. She's super funny and very good at bringing up the "red-hot" topics like sexism and racism.

Gina's a fantastic, enthusiastic professor who cares about her subject matter and respects her students. Lectures are consistently fun and engaging. Participation  in class discussion is not mandatory, but it'll make you will want to participate.

Gina is amazing! Definitely one of the top 3 professors I've had at U-M. The class topic (horror) is already interesting enough, and then she takes it to another level by being witty, entertaining, and caring. She makes a point to learn all of her students names as quick as possible, and leads a dynamic discussion. Oh, and ghost hunters visited.
Not the most interesting material, she makes it better. If you show interest you will do well. Hard to not get an A if you show her you want one.

Gina is dedicated, very intelligent without any egotism, and extremely interesting. My first class with her was "American Working-Class Women," which was valuable on so many levels: it improved my writing, exposed me to writers whom I wouldn't have read otherwise, and was a total blast. I liked her so much that I'm taking two more classes with her!

Gina is probably the best professor I've ever had. Even if you're not interested in the material, she makes it engaging and relevant. She's overall just a wonderful person and cares tremendously about her students and being the best teacher she can be! I agree that she's a little tough, but if you take her class (which you should), you will grow.

Overall, a very difficult class. Gina is great and has a real passion for the material. She wants to learn, but there are just a lot of small assignments that make the workload more than a 3 credit class. I learned a lot and am happy I took this class. if you take one with her, be prepared to take constructive criticism. I grew a lot in her class.
Gina is incredibly enthusiastic, and the class was worth going to everyday, if you're interested in the materials. Moderate workload, but she's a fairly tough grader! Great class overall!

Amazing lecturer with such passion for the subject; makes learning Middle English simple and, surprisingly, enjoyable! HEAVY workload (2 Major papers, 5 smaller essays, 5 quizzes, 1 Research paper, 2 Translation assignments, 2 Exams) but it's really worth it. People say it's impossible to 4.0 her class but I have in every class I've taken with her.
Gina is great! Really fun class to attend. Highly recommend her horror stories class.

Gina is enthusiastic and wonderful. She is interesting and interested, and she really made the class enjoyable. Even though I hate writing essays, I actually didn't mind going to class. She's also very helpful if you just ask.
Gina could teach Watching Paint Dry 101 and make it interesting and hilarious. Would recommend to anyone.

This class is hands down my favorite course I've taken at UMich. Gina is hilarious and extremely enthusiastic about an already interesting topic. She's a tougher grader but is more than willing to meet with you, analyze your work, and help you tweak your writing skills. This course is probably the most fun out of any other class I've taken!

Gina is amazing.  The class was actually FUN to attend (even without mandatory attendance).  She teaches you to really analyze texts and improve writing skills.  She is a tough grader on big essays, but VERY approachable and helpful. I would recommend this class to anyone!

Although the workload is a bit heavy and there is a lot of reading, Gina presents the material in the most accessible way possible. Her humor and passion for the subject is so inspiring and it's crazy how she can make everything relateable to pop culture. As a person, imagine Ellen as a teacher and it's Gina Brandolino inside of a classroom :D
Everday was interesting and fun. She's so quirky! I learned a little about writing too. Very easy. Quizzes are frequent but easy as well. She is very open about adding or removing texts.

Gina is an amazing teacher! You really get 1 on 1 time with her and she is very helpful. She is funny and real down to earth. She promotes participation, but in her class there's no reason why not to participate. One of the best professors I've had so far!

Gina is fantastic. You have to do a lot of work for your grade, but if you pace yourself it isn't nearly as daunting as it seems in the beginning. Excellent lecturer - very enthusiastic - and very personable. She has a very easy-going demeanor that makes for a great class atmosphere.

Gina is a great professor and is so easy to talk to and come to with help. When going over essays she's not scary at all and really helps you on how to revise your essay. She has many many handouts to give you tips on anything. I highly recommend her

She is a really hard grader and may expect a little too much of her students but once you figure out what exactly she wants you'll be fine. The readings were mostly interesting and Gina is pretty entertaining.
She grades harder than I would've expected for a non-ULWR class

TAKE HER CLASS. Gina is wonderful.  The readings are enjoyable and the workload is managlable.  She does expect you to participate in class discussions. If you have questions, she will always help you and give you very helpful advice.

After taking Gina for 3 eng. courses(315, 298, 450), I must say that she is an excellent professor! It does not matter what the course material consist of, I promise she will make it interesting! Certainly not the easiest class, it isn't very difficult either. She is very insightful! She's a cool and down to earth type of person. TAKE HER COURSE!

Gina is by far the best teacher I have ever had, Not to mention she's a great person. She's always willing to help or simply talk if you needed it. She really knows what she's talking about. She studied english for 17 years or something like that. She makes everything clear and has a handout on any issue you might be having

Such a great teacher.  She was really willing to help me and her classes directed you toward a thesis for the papers.  She chose a great selection of books, ones I use in other classes.  Would recommend her to anyone. I hate going to office hours but she made it worth my time & really improved my papers.

She is thee best teacher I have ever had! She is not afraid to tell it how it is and swear in front of the class, which I love! I highly recommend taking her because she strengths your writing abilities. The readings for the class are very interesting.
Wonderful teacher. She's super fun and really interesting. I loved going to her class. If you were ever confused, she was willing to work with you and even give you extensions.
Very good lectures and cares about his students.

I genuinely love him do not listen to what other people say. he is genuinely funny and will not let the annoying people just sprout nonsense and pretend they're smart - he will call them out. also, its like very easy to do well if you literally READ THE TEXTBOOK.  for chem 215, i genuinely watch his old lectures from past semesters. he is so clear!

Coppola is very knowledgeable about Organic Chemistry. He takes the concepts very seriously and explains everything quite well. Doing book work outside of class is necessary for a good grade, but if you do everything you're supposed to, you will be well prepared for the tough exams.

130 must've been a different world from 210, because he was amazing for me in 210. He formats his lectures as a historical story and is very passionate about what he teaches. He's very accessible pre and post lecture. Amazing at explaining 3D concepts and difficult topics. You'll never be bored in a Coppola lecture.

His lectures were fast paced so I personally found reading the textbook beforehand to be very helpful. He's a very passionate about organic chemistry and was happy to answer questions about practice problems before or after lecture. At times he rambled, but for the most part he stayed on topic and the material was almost always explained clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Obviously, Orgo is a tough class, but I enjoyed it. His lectures were engaging, and you could tell that he really has a passion for the subject. He does tend to get sidetracked in lecture with some random stories, but it was always worth going to lecture. If you're already lost in chem, take Tuttle; if you know a little orgo already, take Coppola.

One of the best professors I have ever had! Truly sparked my interest in chemistry. Come to lecture! Come to his office hour! He is so passionate about the subject; he often gets sidetracked with other topics in chemistry, but it only serves to increase interest in fields related to what we're doing i.e. biochem. Strongly recommend Dr. Coppola
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about chemistry, but he overcomplicated things for Chem130 because he is used to teaching orgo, plus he doesn't use slides (just uses a notebook and pen) so he can go on tangents. The final exam was awful this year. However attendance is not mandatory at lectures so I just went to other professors lectures or self studied.

Prof. Coppola is a great guy and so helpful in many different ways. I asked him questions almost every lecture, and it was rare that I walked away still confused. Additionally, you can tell he genuinely cares about what he teaches, with his office hours stretching late into the night with no complaints. Orgo is not hard as long as you work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Coppola is acc the goat I love him sm :') Trust me when I say he's the best teacher I've ever had. TAKE HIM
Go to EVERY lecture/office hours & read textbook/do all practice probs. He taught the subject so well that it made exams easy. His class always had the highest test averages. I WISH he taught Orgo 2. Words can't describe how much I love him.

This class in general was awful this semester. Coppola definitely cared for his students but sometimes he would go too much into the history of the lesson. You have to listen carefully in order to not get lost in the lecture but overall, he was a good professor.

While orgo chem is his bread and butter, Dr. Coppola is very knowledgeable about chemistry in general and has THE BEST EXAM PREP LECTURES. He gives fantastic feedback if you read the textbook and have specific or complex questions. He might give you more information than what's needed to pass the course, but that will set you up for future classes.

Coppola's lecture style, while straightforward, can be hard to get used to. He lectures and writes lecture notes on a piece of paper as he goes. Make sure to sit near the front. Lectures are comprehensive but he moves quickly and skips topics, so review notes afterwards and self-study. Solves test-like problems in class and gives exam tips.

For 210, Dr. Coppola freaking rocks. He is such an eccentric and charismatic guy. Genuinely one of the coolest professors I have met. His passion for organic chem is unmatched. His textbook is great and the practice problems prepare so well for exams. 210 is hard, no way around it. Hes very Socratic, if that's your learning style, you will love him

Very good professor overall, lectures are technically optional but if you want to do well, its best to participate in class it will help you. You will find his office hours way more helpful than your discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Choose to attend lecture with this charismatic guy who knows his stuff. Because he respects you, he teaches at a depth that requires you to keep up. There's a reason why he gets the highest class average on every exam. Also, his OHs are amazing, like a more chill lecture with a few tangents, and you can learn a lot from other students' questions.

He writes instead of using a slideshow, which is fine; however, his handwriting is unreadable. It got to the point where many students did not attend lectures due to this. The class itself is not too bad; the book helps a lot. Not the worst professor, but there is better.
I think he is very unprepared for class and I would not recommend taking chem 130 with him
Coppola is a great lecturer who is very passionate about what he is teaching. He comes prepared to every lecture and makes chemistry fun to learn.

As much of a shitshow Chem 130 was this year, Coppola was actually a great professor. I stopped going to lectures like halfway through the semester, but I still watched the recordings of his lectures. My only complaint is that for more complicated topics, his explanations would get very confusing, but that could just be because of the topic.

The entire chemistry department needs to be lobotomized. I had Coppola as my lecturer—I stopped going after the first week. He teaches like it's the medieval era. Cut your losses and just read the textbook. On a positive note, he is oddly whimsical.

I had him for Chem 130 this semester, and honestly, I started watching other professors' lectures instead. I know this guy means well, but he was often behind the other lecturers simply because he writes everything down on a piece of paper during the lecture. Overall, though, Chem 130 was highly disorganized and not uniform.
His lectures are very deep in the content compared to the other lecturers and I think having those complex lectures is what gives his students more of an edge on the exam. Very straightforward guy.

Prof. Coppola knows what he's talking about. Although he expects students to know a lot of the material already, and goes extremely fast with his notes, making them hard to follow. I strongly recommend doing lots of practice problems. Pay attention to the ones he likes to do in his notes. A tutor helped me digest the material; tests are very hard.

Prof. Coppola definitely knows his stuff. When it comes to teaching he is not good if you're new to the subject. From his lectures you could tell he was pationate about the topics, but he expects you to be as knowledgable as him, making it hard to keep up. I eventually used the other professors lectures because they were actually understable.
I never wore my seatbelt while driving to school because I wanted to die before making it to his class

Coppola knows his stuff, but his teaching style can be tough to navigate. Attend every class, read the textbook closely, and use resources like unstuckstudy ai to prep. Exams are challenging, but put in the work and you can succeed.

He was very knowledgeable, however tests were extremely difficult. If you do not do practice exams you won't do well. Also do not request regrades, when I tried more points were taken off instead of added.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Coppola for Chem 215 and he is not the best out there at all. He is clearly knowledgeable but his notes are  unorganized and if you don't go to class you will fall behind fast. Exams are extremely difficult so make sure to do as many practice problems as possible. I could tell he had a big ego as well. My recommendation: avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is, to begin with, an extremely arrogant instructor. For instance, a class where 23% of the students fail does not always mean that you are an excellent educator. Although he is rather impolite, I would absolutely suggest taking Orgo in the summer with Nolta or at a community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: How can you fail 23% of the class?  And that is after >10% dropped!  This is an outrage and should not be happening.  Historical averages are unfair, because clearly exams vary in difficulty from year to year.  If 1/3 of the class does not pass, that says something about the lecturer, not the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Coppola is great in terms of his passion for chemistry and lecturing skills. Course grades are determined by fixed historical averages meaning there is no adjustment for exam/semester difficulty. I scored ~top 15% in each exam and recieved an A- while a whopping 23% of my cohort recieved a failing grade (D/F). Read the textbook and study hard.

If you have any other difficult classes whatsoever do not take 215 with Coppola. This class requires undivided attention in order to perform well. Was much harder than 210 and Coppola's exams were very very difficult. 23% of the class failed if that tells you anything. An obvious pre-med weeder class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Coppola is a great prof. He is very knowledgeable on the material and he explains what you need to know in detail. He is a step up compared to other organic chemistry professors.

He is either a hit or miss. I didn't like him at first because he tends to skip a lot of steps in lecture, but he is clearly experienced in teaching the course. He writes hard exams though, and you can never expect what is gonna be on there. He is a funny guy and very personable in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell he is very experienced. A lot of time he answers questions before they're asked. He is willing to give criticism to the class if he thinks it is valuable. Very familiar with organic chemistry and rarely makes mistakes or causes unnecessary confusion in class.

Absolutely incredible. As someone not very excited to take orgo, I was very pleasantly surprised.  Lectures were always interesting and he was very clear when answering questions.  Would highly recommend his office hours, even if you aren't in his lecture. He is also the author of the textbook and the practice questions in them are so helpful.

Here I am, DECADES  later, commenting on Professor Coppola. 
I took his organic chemistry class in 1986 and to this day, I remember his obvious love of teaching-at 8 am every morning. 
I am now a physician and came across a patient whose granddaughter was recently also a student of Professor Coppola-what a small world.
Take the class and enjoy.
Bad lecturer
Literally wrote the book for this class. Class is hard but put in a lot (i mean a lot) of work and you will do well. Do all problems and exams in book and canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Coppola for 210 and 215 and he was great for both! You can tell how much he loves the subject and it made me love it. He wrote the textbooks and compared to the other textbooks I have used at UM his are excellent and allow you to slow down and take in the material
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chem 215 was my second semester having Coppola, and he is a fabulous lecturer. 215 was more difficult than 210 in my opinion, but still very doable if you stay on top of practice problems/reading. Coppola gives excellent book problem explanations after class if you walk up to him, so take advantage of this!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really inconsiderate of students who have accommodations for disabilities; doesn't really explain concepts during lecture and always quotes his textbook (that you're forced to buy btw)

For a nervy freshman, Coppola was the ideal professor to ease me into organic Chem. His high quality lectures coupled with the ample amount of practice problems in his textbook are the keys to succeeding in his class. I ended up with a 95 with 4-5 hours of studying a week. An A is feasible if you do what he recommends.

Coppola teaches the course in an "old school" fashion with the blackboard and chalk, but I ended up enjoying this method. Be prepared to show up 5-10 minutes early to lecture though - he writes things on the board before class starts and it can be hard to catch up if you show up on time or late. The textbook problems were very useful for exam prep!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken- had to withdraw. The textbook was not required but highly encourage getting it and making sure you don't have any other difficult classes the semester you take any of his classes. Tests are brutal and at a much higher level than 210 be ready to do every single practice problem in existence to pass.

His lectures are vague, his textbook (stupidly expensive) is so boring and complicated. This man made this class far more difficult than necessary. He's knowledgeable about chemistry, but is awful at teaching and his textbook is horribly written. "If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough." Albert Einstein.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chem 215 is a hard class but can be succeeded in if you keep up and ask for help. Coppola isnt the clearest lecturer, so relying on the textbook was sometimes necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Brian is a wonderful professor. You can tell that he enjoys what he does very much. The class is tests only, and it will be tough. It is a lot of information coming fast. Do your practice problems and you should be set!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall I am proud of myself for pulling through with Orgo II, but I did that myself. Throughout the term constantly being reminded if you aren't doing well with the exams, I'm not trying hard enough is seriously disrespectful and not understanding of our situations. Do better, Coppola. It is possible to do better in the course, I am proof of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unlike most of the other orgo professors Coppola didn't offer many online resources, but luckily you can access the other section's online resources (which I did). Coppola does, however, give super helpful answers after class and at office hours, which I can credit as one of the main reasons I did well. GO. TO. OFFICE. HOURS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He does a very good job explaining the material, although he is old-school (I like that but some might not). His lectures cover almost all the material in the textbook, which is unsurprising considering that he wrote it. Generally decent guy, although not as approachable as some. The curve in the class is quite generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favourite professors of all time. Incredibly engaging, positive and inspiring. He makes you fall in love with organic chemistry. He knows the course is difficult, but dumbs it down appropriately for college freshman who have just have come in. His passion and energy radiates across the hall. Sadly, not many professors can outdo him

Orgo is extremely hard and Coppolla doesn't help. He doesn't do practice problems in class so get ready to do them on your own. He is extremely smart and kind, but it did not help me as a student. Going to his office hours helps a lot, but it is hard to speak with him individually. Only nice thing is that he wrote the textbook and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Coppola is one of my favorite professors. His passion for the subject is refreshing and inspiring, and he genuinely cares for his students and teaches the subject in detailed ways. His textbook complements his class, and you should definitely be prepared to read it if you want a good grade. You'll have to work hard, but an A is possible.

Lecture is overly textbook heavy. He wants us to read the textbook before the class, but the textbook is too wordy and hard to read. It is better to do practice problems from other professors, listen to their lectures, and use his textbook problems for practice before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Organic Chemistry is going to be difficult wherever you take it, but Dr. Coppola really cares about his students and it shows in his lectures. He posts exams from previous years, as well as keys, which give you a really clear idea of what will be on the exam. I feel lucky to have had Dr. Coppola as a professor, and hope to have him again!

Fall 2019. In my opinion, he's the best professor on campus. His words are actual gold. The rigor and format of the class is meant to install habits to promote true learning. The course was def tough, but once I adapted to it, it felt amazing! This man was responsible for the majority of my personal growth in college through a single class.

The online exams were ridiculous. For example, there will be a questions with 15 answer options, 4 of which being correct. The question will be worth 20 points and if you miss one answer option, you get 0 points. I realize it was a difficult transition to online; however, he dealt with this very poorly, with about 30% of the class dropping.

Im giving him such a low score because of how he has handled this semester. He has shown nothing but elitism and no consideration towards his students. He has no problem blaming students for not understanding the new format on the exams. Blames you for everything. Promotes students dropping. 27% dropped the course this semester. Horrible teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Well, he's a personable guy, pretty easy to get along with, lectures "seemed" good, exams hardly correlated, and you have about zero study materials considering the coursepack has no answers to check. The lowest grade I've received in 95 or so credits yay. He chose to add a lot of naming into exams, unlike every other year.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Coppola is a great professor! He makes you work for your grade, but his exams are doable if youve put the time in. His final exams also tend to be more general and slightly easier than the midterms to make up for the volume of material. He is willing to help students learn organic chem but will not spoon feed you answers. I loved orgo with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So I took Orgo 2 praying to the lord above that Coppola wasn't teaching it, but alas he was and my semester was boned. Never have I ever hated a class more. Now, not only does the class itself suck, but Coppola teaches this ish as if we're all trying to become organic chemists. Also, HE DOESN'T PROVIDE KEYS for the practice. What's the point?0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Coppola is a solid professor and a nice guy. There's no sugarcoating the fact that his tests are hard though. You need to study A LOT to do well on them. Though it's pretty easy to get B/B-, but if you want the A range, it takes lots of effort

Coppola is a great professor. Students who claim he isn't most likely did poorly in the class due to their own shortcomings, not his. He definitely doesn't spoon-feed you the material, but he gives you all of the resources you need to succeed in the class. For 215 in general, I recommend finding a practice exam plug. Ask around and you'll find one.
He is pretty funny and teaches well but sometimes organization is an issue. Honestly great overall, it is just hard to have anyone after Nolta for 210.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I cannot believe the difference between taking Orgo at Umich and at a different University. Coppola is so nice, but I never had any experience with orgo and he teaches as if you do. I never felt like someone actually explained material to me, yet they expected me to know what they were talking about. In my new class Ive gotten 100% on all exams.

Absolutely incredible. Probably the best teacher I've ever had in my life. Not only does he explain the material in an engaging and clear way, but he is also willing to answer questions beyond the syllabus, which has helped me understand many concepts better. He also only uses the chalkboard, which I found much more interesting than powerpoints.

Incedible lecturer, explained organic chemistry in a way that even my parents would understand. Very accessible and helpful for outside of class questions. Related the material to every day life and made it seem relevant and interesting.

Coppola is a nice guy, but he is very fast and assumes you already know a lot about the topic. That being said, he clearly loves his job and is so on top of his work. He responds to emails almost instantly and is very punctual. He does not give out answers to the coursepack, but there are practice exams on nolta's website you can use.

He cares incredibly much for his students and is always energetic during lectures. During the office hours before the exam, he stayed waaaay past the the regular hours and answered every single question though it was really late. Coppola is extremely admirable and teaches in a way that is succinct and, as much as orgo can be, interesting!

The best chemistry professor on campus period. Organic chemistry is hard, but his explanations are detailed and thorough. Remember to use multiple sources of information, including your peers and textbook. There's a lot of work to do, but you're in good hands. He's definitely a role model for anyone who learns from him.

Coppola is a good professor but he isn't always clear in the way he presents the material, going in depth on things that aren't relevant. A few general notes about orgo it takes WORK, stay on top of the material and do ALOT of practice exams if you want an "A", also get your questions answered and don't hold on to misconceptions. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's really helpful, he looks strict but he's actually nice.

I thought Orgo would be very hard, but Coppola's straightforward and logical lectures made the material itself seem not so hard. Amazing professor. He always incorporated real world examples into lecture which was cool. If you follow along in lecture, do the course pack, and put in time for studying you will be fine.

Brian is an extraordinarily intelligent, dedicated, & experienced professor. If Brian says it, it will be covered by the exam; his lectures are succinct & he does not stray from the subject matter. Brian uses examples that explain difficult concepts quickly and make them easy to remember. If you have a choice between professors, choose Brian.

Coppola lectures can be boring, but he covers only topics that will possibly be on exams (unlike other profs), as well they are recorded and posted to his website. The class is inherently difficult, but joining a SLC study group and doing about 5 hours of studying outside of that before exams will allow you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Out of all the profs for organic chemistry, Coppola is def the best choice. Then again, I must warn you that I basically thought he was speaking a different language by the end of the semester. This class is by far the hardest class I have ever taken, and I hope I never have to go through something this terrible again
Coppola is an AMAZING lecturer. He writes the exams too, so being in his class is probably for the best. Lectures are recorded so attendance in class isn't mandatory. He's probably a genius.

If you want to do well in this class, dont do noltas exams (way too difficult, her pages in the coursepack are in text font arial). Dont get too attached to lecture. They usually are the justification for the answers. Coppola writes very fair exams with an occasional trick here and there.

Dr. Coppola was an inspiration. He convinced me to join the honors study group, and that is how I met most of my friends at the university. I didn't know how much I would enjoy organic chemistry because I've always liked physical chemistry better, but one semester after taking Coppola's class, I became involved in organic chemistry research!

Literally the best professor at UM. He's funny and says random jokes at times. He's like the funny uncle everyone wished they had. He has such a clear and distinct voice that grabs attention so lectures are never boring. I wish he would teach other chem classes so I could take his class again.

He's good and all, but i don't understand why he sells course packs. They could easily be available online like calc's and physic's practice exams... They're just old exam questions, so it's not like he's slaving over these things. A little scammy if you ask me. Only gripe though, so i guess that's good?

Coppola was alright. He tended to go fast during lectures, and only covered the most difficult material 2 or 3 days before the exam. Fortunately, Chem 210 has countless resources that help you. Tough class, but put the effort in and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Coppola has been my favorite professor so far and teaches chemistry so well. He is very clear and always makes sure to answer questions during class, after class, or in office hours. I had his class at 8am and he always kept my attention and was very captivating. I would highly recommend taking his class if you can.

Amazing person and professor. Really knows how to teach. Funny. Kind of fast sometimes but his lectures are recorded so you can re-watch. For the first two exams he covered the hard material really late (2 days before the exam) so it's better to be ahead and allow time to practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Coppola is honestly an amazing professor. He teaches chemistry so well and everything in his lectures is extremely clear. Truthfully, you don't even really have to go to lecture because his lectures are recorded and he posts a panoramic shot of the chalkboard. Don't believe the scary things you hear about orgo; it's honestly not that bad.

Professor Coppola is an amazing instructor. He really emphasizes thinking through problems and provides a good understanding of concepts. Biggest advice is to go to his office hours because he explains concepts in a much greater detail and really helps out with the course pack problems. Orgo is hard, but this man makes sure every lecture helps!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a phenomenal and inspiring professor

Coppola lectures and makes his notes hard to decipher. He wrote the textbook and you'll need that and the course pack to pass the class. He is helpful but doesn't always explain stuff well. Someone else would probably have been a better prof. GSI's are sometimes useless, all down to luck, but you can go to whoever you want. 4 exams are all the grad

Brian Coppola is an amazing teacher and human being. I loved every second of his class even though its not the easiest class. He really knows what hes talking about and knows the clearest most concise way to explain it. Honestly the man is a sympathetic genius who wants you to learn and wants to teach.

Very passionate about Chemistry, and a pretty good lecturer if you keep up. It helps to read the textbook and stay ahead, as Coppola typically doesn't teach the hardest topic until the week before the exam. If you want to get ahead on the coursepack and have time to practice, it helps to self-teach and go to lecture as review.

I did not like him at all, his lecture notes were helpless. I used other professor's notes for exam preparation since Coppola's notes were useless since it's like a lecture for those who know orgo very much, his lectures shows that he doesn't care that much about 300-500 students per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Coppola puts chemistry into a greater context. If you attend his lectures / take notes you'll actually learn so much more than just how to pass tests. He is very passionate, very knowledgable, and really great lecturer. That being said, you have to put work in and know how to study.

Dr. Coppola teaches in a very technical manner, using scientific jargon for the plurality of his lecture. If you don't understand an earlier concept, he simply gets upset at the class and usually refuses to review the basics. You must come prepared to pay attention to lecture material that you have hopefully reviewed prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Coppola is one of the best professors I have had in the sciences. He is very passionate about teaching and truly cares about if his students understand the material. His lecture style is great. He made a class of 300 students feel like 30 and found ways to make the class interact with the material while cracking jokes the whole time!

Coppola was a great professor. He was very passionate about chemistry which made me want to go to class and learn. He gave really difficult examples during class but it helped for the tests. Going to his lectures and doing the course pack were the most helpful to do well in this class.

Unfortunately, Orgo is the ultimate weeder course at UM, and everyone knows it (despite what the Orgo professors claim in their beloved course pack). This class has several absurd rules, to put it mildly- no answer key to the course pack, no partial credit on exams, and so on. It's incredible that there are no course pack answer keys!

Dr.  Coppola is an award winning professor and cares deeply about his students. He has a very deep understanding of organic chemistry, his instruction is profound, and the course's exams are- never unreasonably, always appropriately, but still sufficiently- intense. With effort you WILL succeed, 70% of us got a B or higher so stop freaking out.
