Coppola was a pretty good professor overall (especially considering the other professors at U of M).  You can tell he has lots of experience teaching this class and he's a very good lecturer. The concepts are difficult and the class is pretty fast paced though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: At times his explanations can be really helpful, and other times they make no sense. He sometimes seems to forget we don't already know what he is teaching us and will often using chemistry vocabulary words without first defining them.

With captivating lectures, Coppola makes it easy to like orgo. But the class itself isn't easy. What I found helps: work on the coursepack early on & with others; join a study group; attend every lecture; ask questions. Coppola teaches in a conceptual way, so his answers to questions aren't straightforward, but help you to approach future problems.

He teaches the class like you already have a background in it. Moves very quickly and it is easy to get behind. I highly recommend going to his lectures, listening to his audio recordings as you go over your notes again, and doing everything else possible to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Coppola is obviously very smart but I feel he is so smart he has a hard time articulating tough concepts to students. One thing he did that I didn't appreciate was start a chapter with examples we could only fully understand after the whole chapter had been taught. Overall he's decent but if you can, take Schindler, Nolta, or Naryian.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's clear through the way Coppola teaches that he is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about chemistry. Orgo is obviously a difficult class, but he explains concepts very well with background information, includes humor in his lectures, and is great about answering questions during class and office hours. Plus, he literally wrote the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His notes are somewhat messy but his lecture are really engaging and he helps simplify the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Coppola is a great lecturer. He speaks real fast and writes on the chalkboard also very fast but that's because he has a lot to teach and not much time. The book is helpful for gaining a basic understanding but he teaches you what you need to know. Plus he writes the exams

Coppola is so knowledgeable in everything he is teaching. The way he explains stuff and goes into more detail than the other professors is very helpful. He had two lectures so when I couldn't go to one, I would go to the other. Definitely the best of the 210 professors.

Its Organic Chemistry. It's the hardest class I've had so far but Coppola does a good job teaching it. You can also access Schindlers notes (canvas) which are great. There is 4 exams and the 3 and final count for more than 50% of you grade. USE GSI OFFICE HOURS. My GSI was Daniel and he was the best but Jessica is also really good. Good luck folks!

THIS MAN IS A LEGEND. I seriously love him and am so sad I won't have him for 215. Despite being head of the chem department at U-M, he's a very humble man and teaches for this level. He writes the exams, so going to his section is extremely valuable. He does his best to answer all questions and goes out of his way to address student concerns.

He is a fantastic professor. He is condescending if you ask a dumb question , but you will not forget that experience. So it is totally worth it in the end. His exams are brutal, but with his teaching you will understand the material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class itself requires a lot of work outside of lecture in order to be really successful - unless you're just insanely intuitive or have some sort of background in organic chemistry. I found Coppola to be a better professor than the one I was assigned for lecture so I went to his office hours and lectures when my schedule allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He does a great job of explaining difficult concepts and always adds a bit of humor to his lectures which is nice. A word of caution though: he scribbles all over the blackboards like a madman. If you try to copy down everything he writes, you will miss the entire lecture. So just pay attention during lecture and use another professor's notes.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Coppola. His lectures were incredibly clear, he was very friendly one on one, and he loves teaching. Exams required A LOT of prep, but they were always reasonable. The first day, he recommended always reading a chapter ahead of lecture - this was crucial since some major content doesnt get covered until a few days before the exam

Dr. Coppola gives off an air of arrogance but once you get over that he's a nice guy who really wants to help students. He likes to challenge the thoughts of students. Will stay after class, even after the next class in the room has started, to answer questions. Don't complain about the tests being "impossible" bc he won't have it.

Very charismatic and knowledgable, and the lectures were pretty engaging. Orgo is a challenging subject, but Coppolla writes the exam and the coursepack so DO THE COURSEPACK and you should be in pretty good shape.
Worst chemistry prof I ever met in college. Lectures were pointless and exam was hard. Also not giving answers for the course pack was so stupid

More concept focused, would not recommend if you are into doing exam practice type of questions. He is a clear lecturer, but I did not feel prepared for exams.  Coppola writes the exams, so get used to the way he writes them!

Coppola taught what he needed to like any other professor. The rest of the course is based on how much time you put into it. It's not that bad if you take advantage of the study groups, slc office hours, and course pack. Find a smart group of people and compare course packs a few days before each exam. Also take nolta practice exams.

Coppola himself kind of oversees Chem 210. Orgo is also taught partially by GSIs or older students, depending on how you study for it. The exams are extremely tough but the grading scale is forgiving. Coppola gives great lectures, but can assume that students are immediately comprehending all that he is saying. I was lost in lecture several times.

Some students may call Prof. Coppola the best of the 210 professors, some may call him the worst.  He has a teaching style that requires paying close attention. He'll cover a lot in one hour of lecture, and he's incredibly knowledgable in organic chemistry. He always seems happy to talk about his topic.

The only impact on your grade are exams. That being said, you MUST attend lectures. I personally loved Coppola; the guy has a lot of energy and enthusiasm for 8am lectures. However, try out the other professors. Find out the ones that work for you! Go to multiple lectures a day if you need to. This class is hard, but DON'T give up if you fail exams

The class itself is pretty challenging.  Get ready for tons of coursepack problems.  But Dr. Coppola himself isn't a bad professor.  He knows his stuff pretty well, and seems willing to help you when you need it.  However, his lectures are a bit fast-paced.  Use all other resources along with his lectures and you'll not get anything lower than a B.

His lectures were quite clear overall and had good energy for an 8 AM class. CHEM 210 requires a lot of discipline and independence to do well . The only grades are exams so it's up to you to learn how you study. However, there are a lot of resources to do well. Highly recommend joining an SLC study group.
Worst Chem Prof. ever! I lost my interest in Chemistry after taking chem 210 with him.

Puts materials that are only covered in Monday review sessions into exams. And sometimes I even find questions that are not covered in any of them. Probably they are taught only to some students who go to his office hours. So overall hard to get an A+. However, he is still a clear lecturer from whom you can learn a lot!

I did not like Coppola. All he cared about was his "superiority" over his students. Makes very demeaning CTools announcements. Everything on exams is either all or nothing. Unwilling to help with coursepack questions after he decided not to provide an answer key. I regret not waiting a semester to take this class with Nolta.

Professor Coppola was an amazing professor who really takes the time out to see that students will do well if they really want to. Go to GSI office hours (or his) and complete the coursepack and POD's throughout the term and not just right before the exam. Coppola is a super nice guy who is willing to help anyone who puts the effort in.

His lectures are extremely sloppy and disorganized but still worth going to. I read every section assigned and did every practice problem in the book which was a huge help. Attend lecture as much as possible and go to his office hours. He puts problems on exams that he only covers in office hours. Bit of a superiority complex but good nonetheless.

Professor Coppola is a long time professor and writes most of the material for the class. He gives quick problems to check knowledge but skims over stuff taught in previous classes involved in said problems. He covers lots of material in each class and somewhat quickly, but not too fast where you can't take notes. Clear and focused during lectures.
He's very smart and he knows it. He's an alright professor, not as good as everyone makes him sound. I often went to other lectures in addition to his for clarity.

I just finished taking both Orgo I and II I took I with Nolta and II with Coppola, Dr. Coppola definitely makes you work for the grade, but that is what separates the A students from the Bs and the rest. Organic Chemistry is a course that requires strong attention to detail. But all in all Dr. Coppola is an amazing professor, I actually enjoyed him

I did not have an enjoyable experience. Yes, orgo is hard and is supposed to be the weeder class for pre meds, but Coppola makes it a point to reinforce his superiority over the students. Sometimes you ask a question and he WILL make you feel stupid. A lot of his CTools announcements come with a demeaning tone. Take orgo with Nolta instead.
Coppola is amazing! His tests are tough, but if you go to lecture and do the course pack you should do just fine. His lectures were the best part of my mornings.

Good guy, had entertaining lectures. He knows what he is doing but will not spoon feed you material.  With any tough class if you put the work in you will succeed, but do not expect him to hold your hand along the way.

People here seem to like Coppola, but he just didn't cut it for me. This is the hardest class 've ever taken, and I say that as a freshman. The lectures were useless and very unorganized in my opinion. Reading the textbook and doing as many coursepack pages is possible is way more important for getting a good grade. Wouldn't recommend Coppola.
Coppola was an amazing teacher for CHEM 210. He made going to 8 AM Chem lectures worth it, and I would absolutely love to take another class with him.

If you show up for all lectures, join a study group (RECOMMENDED), and put a good amount into this class, you'll at least get a B. Doing the course pack would be the best option but he won't give you any help with it, which is extremely unfair. The textbook is of no help. Exams are hard so start studying early. USE NOLTA'S SITE.
This guy will take away you're interest in chemistry.

I did not have a good experience with him. Coppola is one of the most demeaning professors I have ever encountered, and you can see that through quite a few of his emails. Refuses to go over coursepack questions. He makes exams harder because "the average was higher than he wanted it to be". I wish I had waited to take this class with Nolta.
Definitely knows his stuff, and is a good lecturer.

Because lectures are immediately following his orgo 1, there are always many students asking questions when we just sit there waiting. Sometimes even 20 minutes are gone. So he don't have time to go into the details of many mechanisms. But anyway his exams are ok if you do as many coursepack problems as possible. Use the tutors in SLC!
Coppola is one of my all time favorite profs. He presents the material so well and so organized. Do not skip class and take notes and you'll be fine. Textbook is useless. Join a study group

Coppola is an awesome professor with a great personality and sense of humor. He is extremely knowledgable and chem savvy. Many students find his lectures to be not quite as linear as Dr. Nolta's but it's still clear. The hardest part of taking the class this semester is he did not offer office hours because he also taught CHEM 210...

Terrible professor not so clear about the concept, messy material, hard but useless exams... Do not take Orgo at UM. Textbook was useless and there were no answers on the coursepack which made me really hard to take advantage of it.
I can only hope to be as passionate about something in my lifetime as Coppola is about chalkboards and organic molecules.
Not my favorite professor. Teaches a lot of the exam material the day before the exam. Refuses to go over coursepack questions when other people do. Sometimes very demeaning.

Writes too fast, talks while he's writing, doesn't give you time to write down what he's saying, and makes frequent mistakes that go unnoticed unless a student catches them. Notes are confusing. Do not take this class with this professor.
Great prof. Really wants you to do well. His love of the subject really woke me up at 8 am

One of my favorite professors at this university, by far. Dr. Coppola is one of the most helpful teachers, he knows exactly what students need to have a successful semester. He's great at actually teaching the material, rather than just forcing memorization. His lectures are very organized and easy to follow. If you take orgo, take it with him.
While he's an intelligent guy, I found his lectures to be confusing and disorganized. A lot of the times, he'll jump into a reaction before telling us what he's actually trying to teach.

Professor Coppola is extremely intelligent. However this can be a disadvantage because he often flies through the material. His class is very interesting, but there is a lot of material. Take good notes and go to his office hours. Also, write down the things he says out loud. He often times will say important information, but not write it down.

Coppola was engaging and hilarious. He was very clear-cut about his teaching material and broke down complicated concepts into very manageable sections. Despite all the terrible things I've heard about Orgo 1, my experience was pretty easy thanks to Coppola.
Hands down the best organic chemistry professor here.

A fantastic professor. He takes something that can easily end up being boring & gives fascinating lectures about chemistry. Yes, the class is tough & so are the tests, but you really learn the material.  On tests, he doesn't ask you to regurgitate what's in the textbook (or class) but rather asks you to apply what you've learned to new situations

Not my favorite professor. Likes to make students feel inferior to him. Writes harder exams because "people did too well on the previous one". Grading is almost always all or no credit. With Nolta it may be not be easier, but she will probably be more caring about your success.

Coppola is good enough to make the lectures understandable, but is always concerned with reinforcing his superiority over students. Not the most approachable in my opinion. Would've rather taken this class with Nolta even if it meant waiting another semester.
Kinda confusing guy. Seems like he's all over the place on his lectures, but the tests are pretty easy so it's not too bad.

He's a good option if Nolta isn't teaching this class. He explains things well enough, but like everybody said he often waits until the day before to teach a lot of the exam stuff. He's not the kindest person and you can sometimes tell by the tone of his emails.
Awesome.

I loved this professor. He was very clear and funny, and always tried to make class exciting, even though it was 8:00AM in the morning... As many people have said before, a drawback is that he would still be teaching a ton of new orgo stuff right before the exam, so make sure to do the coursepack early! I did not use the book at all.

Favorite professor at the university thus far. Energetic, hilarious, and genuinely interested in chemistry and your success. By far the best 210 lecturer-- I was enrolled in another and chose to attend his daily because he was no much clearer and smarter. Tests are hard (all orgo tests are), but if you do the course pack (he wrote) you'll be fine!

Coppola is a god of chemistry. He has been teaching for over 30 years and I attest every bit of info that I learned from his incredible teaching. He will go above and beyond to make sure his students understand the hardest of concepts. There is no comparison to him. If you are going to take a class as brutal as orgo 1, make sure you do it with him.
Orgo 1 is very very difficult, but you won't get a better prof than coppola. he's good, but be prepared to go ham.
Very clear and helpful. Exams are tough, and a lot of the material covered on them is learned a few days before in class. Best way to study is to destroy the coursepack.

Coppola is by far the best professor I've had. His passion for chemistry shines through during his lectures, allowing you to both enjoy and understand the material. Make sure to ask him any questions, he answer them very clearly.

An amazing person and professor. He is enthusiastic, clear, and hilarious when he teaches. Your lifelines are his Monday discussions, course pack, and podcasts (in the Ctools tab).  His exams are hard, but fair. MAKE SURE YOU REVIEW MATERIAL BEFOREHAND ON PODCASTS, ESPECIALLY BEFORE EXAMS (TOO MUCH OF THE EXAM IS COVERED 2 DAYS BEFORE THE EXAM).

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR! Coppola is hands down the best teacher I've had at Michigan. Extremely clear, helpful and enthusiastic. Makes lectures so interesting. I don't think I would've liked Orgo if it wasn't for him. It's a hard class, but go to his lectures (even if you're enrolled with another instructor) and you will enjoy and understand it.

Coppola is brilliant, witty, and very helpful during office hours.  However, this class is hard as hell.  Get the coursepack, find extra exams with answer keys, join an SLC study group, and take it with Coppola.  That way, your life will be slightly less nauseating on your way to picking up your graded exams.  Good luck, children.

An amazing teacher who can get the concept across if you try hard enough to pay attention. He teaches how to think like an organic chemistry, not what to memorize. The exams do require a lot of practice. Get the course pack.

Professor Coppola is an incredible professor; his 30+ years of experience in organic chemistry and dedication to teaching makes this class an extremely enjoyable experience. The exams, while not easy, are fair: they test your ability to solve problems, not memorize facts. If you take Chem 210 at Michigan, make sure you attend Coppola's lectures.

His drawings of molecules are very clear and his explanations are descriptive and easy to follow. I would really recommend doing the course pack because the exams are similar. The only thing I would want to change is the fact that he doesn't give us an answer key for the course pack. Makes it hard to know if you are doing the problems correctly.

Professor Coppola is an amazing lecturer. He explains the material very clearly and has a way of making the information interesting. He is also extremely helpful with answering questions, so make sure to go to his office hours!

I heard great things about Dr. Coppola, so I made sure to take his section. He's the best of the 210 professors, but I'm a little disappointed. We don't start important topics until right before the exam, and I don't begin to understand things until I ask friends or read the textbook. This class made me not want to major in chemistry anymore.
Coppola was great at explaining things in lecture. The only down side was that we often didn't cover a significant portion of the exam material until the lecture or two right before the exam.

Dr. Coppola is fantastic. I took his section of Chem 210 last fall and, as an incoming freshman, had no idea what to expect. He presented the material clearly and was willing to revisit difficult concepts (especially at the open discussions... go to those!!!). He's teaching sections this fall (Fall 2013) so register for his section if you can.

Nothing like starting your day with Prof. Coppola at 8AM. He's really a great guy and he tries his hardest to manage a course taken by ~1400 students every fall semester. The evening Q&A sessions are great and even though he won't give you the answers to the exam coursepack it's great that he even takes the time to put one together every semester.

Dr. Coppola is the best lecturer I have had at UM. He will make you enjoy going to chemistry lecture. While he is very adamant about students doing the Coursepack without his help, he will go out of his way to explain something to you if you ask him--even with all of the students he has. His exams, while challenging, are fair.

I miss having him. At first, I was really scared to take orgo 1, but I ended up doing okay. The class was hard, but manageable. He usually manages the curriculum for both chem 210 and 215. Now that he is gone this semester, orgo 2 has become very disorganized. I wish I could have him again.
He is a very good teacher and teaches you everything that is on the exam- nothing surprising ever popped up. DO THE COURSEPACK!!!
Funny guy. Enjoyable to listen to. Seems to genuinely care about your success.

I ended up getting a B+ in this class, but I still enjoyed taking orgo with him. His lectures were pretty clear and although you will struggle with the coursepack, he made me enjoy the subject at the end of the semester when I disliked it at the beginning

Dr. Coppola is the best teacher at the University.  After taking his class it is clear why he has won award after award.  His lectures are the farthest thing from boring because he tells a story instead of reciting facts from the book.  This class is naturally hard due to the subject matter.  However, there 10+ resources available to get an A.

He is pretty clear in lecture, but once it comes to trying to prepare for the exams, you have no idea how to do this and that. He will refuse to help you with coursepack questions. Exams are very unpredictable. Our third midterm was unreasonably difficult.
He's a great teacher, but his exams are killer. Good guy though.
Great professor.  He is light years ahead of the other chem 210 professors.  His lectures are well-organized and very informative.  I would highly, highly recommend him.
He is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He never has to stop and look at his notes or to look up a problem. He really knows what he's talking about.

Professor Coppola= simply amazing. He is super nice, and I feel like he is approachable with any questions. His lectures FLY by and it's my favorite class this semester. He by no means "easy", but it is Orgo. His lecture was by far the most helpful in comparison to the other teachers. Overall- great.

Professor Coppola is an excellent teacher. He takes a topic that everybody fears, and can make anyone understand it. Everything he teaches, he teaches like a student would think. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry, which makes it way more interesting to learn about. He makes it worth waking up at 8am
I loved Coppola. He was not my actual professor but I would wake up early and go to his 8 am lectures everyday! He is absolutely wonderful!

Amazing professor. Teaches the content very well, and makes sure to tie all the lectures together by reviewing slightly in the beginning of class. It doesn't hurt that he is the one that writes the tests! I hated the coursepack because of the lack of answers, but I got A's on the first 3 tests by doing Nolta's practice tests (google nolta umich)

He explains chemistry in a whole different way. I really enjoyed him, but you can't just use him to get you the grade. Need to attend discussions and do your own practice. He explains CHEMISTRY, not just example problems. I really admire this guy as a teacher and a person. He's also won almost every teaching award there is, FYI.

Always a day behind the other professors in lecture and content. He does that on purpose too I feel like. If you want to be not behind and up to date on the info before the exam, go to other lectures.

He is clear and explains things well. The class itself is absolutely terrible and so hard but he somehow does a better job than the other professors helping you to understand the material. Very helpful and very nice.

He's good.  Notes are clean, and explanations are clear.  Very passionate about orgo.  Side note, if you are engineering/problem-solving oriented you most likely will not need the book, just go to lecture, do the course pack and perhaps ask someone who's taken the class before if you have questions.

Coppola was a good teacher. He gives very thorough explanations that you can apply to any problem, not just a specific one in the course pack. His notes were disorganized/hard to follow. He also was always behind in terms of material compared to other teacher. His weekly night reviews were very helpful though. Overall I liked him as a teacher

Dr. Coppola is a good guy, but not the best teacher. A lot of my friends loved him and I respect that opinion, but I found him to be unorganized and a real mess in giving notes! He is willing to help you one on one, though, which is something I respect. Overall, not worth getting up at 8am for though....

this class was a real struggle for me! i'm just not an orgo person. i think coppola did an okay job teaching it, but he was out of town quite a few times, and wasn't always available for meeting one on one. i also went to mcneels lectures and found her notes to be more organized, unlike coppola's. all in all, an okay teacher..

Incredible teacher, one of my favorites at the university so far! He really knows his stuff and has a lot of experience teaching it to students and it shows. He knows where students will struggle and teaches to that. Listen to everything he says at the beginning about how to succeed in his class and go the reviews, they help a lot!

Just a solid teacher. Clearly there to help. Clearly this is his calling. The weekly review sessions were very helpful. A key thing for me in this class was NOT copying everything from the board, but to absorb his thinking as best as possible. Then, do practice problems from the book. Thanks for the great semester.

Coppola is super good at explaining things.  His teaching style may seem sporadic at first, but be patient, there is a method.  He circles back around and all of a sudden everything is clear.  He knows what stuff is the hardest and spends the most time on that.  That's why you have less review than other professors.  I highly recoment.
awsome

I found Coppola to not fit my learning style. If you need clear, organized notes, this is NOT the way to go. I found McNeil and Montgomery to be better at giving organized notes. Coppola goes off on random tangents a lot and I found that we were cramming in material the day before the exam instead of reviewing....

He's a really good lecturer but I can never pay attention to what he's saying because I'm too busy trying to copy the notes, which are really hard to read.  He seems like a great teacher but in a room with 400 students he needs to write bigger and clearer! BIGGER!!!!!

I think Professor Coppola is amazing.  I started out with another professor and quickly found out he was definitely the one to take.  His podcasts are also a great review.  He says everything very clearly and logically.  Very organized.  It was worth even going to 8 o clock lectures.
He's good and an interesting lecturer.  He goes at a much faster pace than other lecturers but is good and very approachable.
His podcasts are amazing.  I never went to class.  I just studied from the book and watched the podcasts at 1.5 speed!(saved soo much time)  best way to study for orgo.
Pretty good prof, but could get sidetracked on random questions that were not important.  Also spent too much time on nomenclature.

Not that great - Some like him, but don't think he is so great. I hated his style, he never writes all the important things on the board and goes too fast. Doesn't cover all material either. Steer clear, and go with Nolta. If you're stuck with him just read the book and don't hurt yourself going to his lecture, it will help in the long run.

Coppola is an awesome teacher, definitely your best bet for Orgo 1 unless Nolta is an option. He is very clear and explains things REALLY well. If you work better with concrete notes, however, than Wolfe might be better. But if you're looking for someone smart, interesting, and overall the best professor for this class, choose Coppola.
Very logical and clear, makes orgo comprehensible and organized. very helpful, and definitely helped me learn difficult concepts thoroughly
Without Dr. Nolta's extra review sessions, Orgo would have been even tougher. Coppola is ok as a prof but not worth getting up at 8 for; my study group taught me more than he did.

A great professor. Makes Orgo easy to understand. He doesn't go too fast, so that you have time to take in those information in an hour. And yea, I agree with the comment below, he's not arrogant at all. Bottom line, enjoyed the class.

Coppola was incredible.  His lectures are extremely structured and precise.  People from the other lectures would wake up to come to our 8am lecture.  If you're taking orgo at UM I would definitely sign up for Coppola.

Very good professor, but really arrogant. It's his way or the highway. He doesn't seem to care about the students half as much as Nolta does. Very unapproachable, he never signs his emails or personally addresses the student,and are always one sentence "I don't give a crap" kind of statements. Like I said, good prof, but as a person, an ****.

I thought Coppola explained things wonderfully and made even difficult concepts much more clear.  His lectures were helpful and easy to follow, and I didn't think he was arrogant at all.  I'm not sure where people are getting that from.  Personally, I prefer him to Nolta any day.

Seems like a nice, funny guy, but comes off as quite arrogant at times. Gives a coursepack full of good problems, however there are no answers, so you have no idea if you're doing it right. You really have to hunt to find the answers...either from the GSIs or Dr Nolta. I really don't understand why they are so hush-hush about the coursepk answers.
Kinda arrogant, but a really good lecturer.  His explanations are clear and to the point.  I don't regret waking up for his 8 am lectures.

ive heard a lot of people really like coppola but i was not a fan. he never seemed like he wanted to teach us he almost seemed like he was talking down to us. he lectures are quite dull. id recommend NOLTA to EVERYONE shes the most amazing professor for this course coppola cant even begin to compare. he also doesnt write too many notes on the board

Coppola was great. The subject matter was new for me, so the things we learned were really difficult but Coppola was easy to follow and I enjoyed attending his lecture even though it was early in the morning. His knowledge of the subject and organization during the lectures consistently amazed me, and I would strongly recommend his class.

He's a pretty good professor. He definately knows his stuff and is clear when he explains it. I thought he was better than Nolta... she's good but a little disorganized... his notes are crisp and clean and easy to follow. I highly recommend him.
Coppola is pretty much amazing, although many people will tell you that Nolta is who you should take this is not true. Coppola teaches you in a concise easy to learn manner. He is an orgo chem god.
in my personal opinion, he is better than nolta

Easily the best professor that exists for chem.  His lectures are great; they explain everything really well, are not muddled and unclear, and make the class easier.  Yes, his tests are hard, but hey, take his lecture and you are OK.
No Comments

It's a hard class and you must attend lectures. He does a good job of laying out the material. I liked his humor and didn't find him that arrogant, but I could see him coming off that way. I say he is definitely a good teacher!

Excellent Professor! I found his lectures to be very helpful. He presented the concepts in a straight-forward manner and did not oversimplify things. The tests were also very fair. I think some people may take out their frustrations with the class on him. However, you will do well if you put in enough effort.

He is incredibly arrogant and unhelpful.  He would randomly not be at lecture and would have a sub (who was horrilbe) do his notes.  He also decided to go to China the week before and including our final exam.  Take it with Nolta or Koreeda if you can.

Coppola may be an OK teacher (he seemd Ok as a freshman, but later on, I had some actual GOOD teachers), but he is arrogant to a fault. And he really doesn't care about student's as much as you would think, he cares about HIS students (the ones who work for him and the ones who suck up to him). Average teacher, I didn't like him as a person.

Ok, yeah we all know he is an amazing professor, his C.V. listing his thousands of teaching awards displays that quite well. Class is hard as hell, no kidding, it's orgo...But if you pay attention, and study appropriately, it really isn't horrible.

He will give answers to the coursepack, but you have to be really extreme to get him to do so. One guy went in for the kill and we followed, a miracle happened. Anyway, my score went up 10% after switching to Coppola (from Matzgar), not a coincidence. He slowly crescendos during lecture until he is super loud at the end. I never fell asleep once.
not a fair professor. He makes the exam so that his class does better than others. He did not want to give answers to the course pack.

has a very high ego. in his lecture, he speaks only to the kids who understand the chem. he does not present it in a way that everyone (even those not real good at chem) can follow.  I recommend Nolta...
not a very helpful guy

Absolutely beautiful lecturer and I hate chemistry. Thoroughly enjoyed the lecture - was so clear I barely had to read the book (got an A-). Could teach orgo to a rock. Going to open disc. not that helpful unless you have very basic questions. Extremely organized and logical, if you need to take orgo, do it with him or nolta.
No Comments

Dr. Coppola is evidently smarter than any aspiring chem major will ever be--he really knows his organic chemistry and teaches it in a way that makes it easy to comprehend.  The material is not that hard--the "orgo" fear is all hype.  Go to office hours if having trouble--he won't touch coursepack, but he is very helpful otherwise.
Wow...this was a very hard class. He makes it even harder.

Coppola is the best professor I have ever had! Not only is he engaging but he teaches topics in more than one way so if you don't always understand the first time you are guarenteed to the second time. He is also a genuninely nice guy. The only problem is that he did not hold office hours.

Coppola gives excellent lectures, but he goes way too fast.  Don't expect to be able to actually process anything he says during lecture.  You will not have any time during lecture to think about the material, only to frantically copy down what he says.  However, the lectures are extremely helpful when you go over them a second or third time

best teacher i've had at the university so far. cute old man with major bling. he REALLY knows organic chem backwards and forwards, it's evident in lecture. DO THE COURSEPACK. go to Nolta's review sessions. He really wants EVERYONE to understand. he's your best bet for orgo.

Excellent teacher, he pretty much lives to make sure his students understand the material.  He eases up the orgo material by connecting it to biology and even word etymology.  Does a really good job of giving examples, explaining mechanisms, etc.  Go to his open discussions if you have questions, do the coursepack, it reflects the 3 exams very well

U-M sure picked a committed professor to teach orgo.  The guy even knew enough to answer my friend's question of how electrons get accross nodes.  However if you want to do well on the tests, do all the coursepack problems and go to Nolta's review sessions.  Also take advantage of the podcasts and re-listen to the lectures to get everything down.
amazing teacher, very clear, coursepack is good, go to the open discussions
Tests don't reflect coursepack at all, but really good idea to go to his q and a sessions.
pretty good lecturer, but sometimes assumes that his students know beyond what they really know. you really gotta study for this course.
Coppola is an awesome professor and really cares about his students.  His lectures keep you engaged and are stimulating.
A professor with real competence and substance.
excellent prof! although he's quite mechanical ( unlike Nolta) but he's equally helpful and really knows what he's doing.

Although I will admit that Coppola can be very complex in his teaching, he is a very nice person and he is willing to help and explain concepts to students...he's even willing to meet with students if necessary!!!
Good teacher, easy to understand. Most importantly, his exams are very fair. He only tests on what he covered and does so clearly.
great prof great class
No Comments

Brian communicated all of the material well during his class, but he's not as wonderful as everyone tries to make him.  Nolta is as good or better, so don't think you have to kill yourself to get to his classes if you have time for Nolta.
Best teacher ever
good
the BEST teacher I have ever had!!!
very unprofessional and unhelpful... unorganized and uncaring.. hate him
horrible class and evil exams but he knows what hes talking about and communicates the material effectively in lecture
Orgo has a really scary reputation but taking it with this guy made it actually fun

Coppola is the God of teaching organic chemistry, at least at U of M.  The material is very difficult but he somehow teaches it in a way that you can understand.  Overall, he's an excellent professor.

hard class with hard exams, but most of the stuff on the exams is what he teaches in class, unlike some other chem profs (Gugelchuk). He is a fun guy with a great personality and you will be happy to attend his lectures.
Awesome lecturer, made it worth getting up super early to go to his section instead of wolfe or matzgers
Coppola was an extremely good teacher.  The material was hard, but he taught it in a way that made it very understandable.
great educator but the most arrogent person i have ever met. thinks he is gods gift to the world. if you can deal with that, then you will do well.
Best chemistry professor at U of M.
best teacher I've ever had.  Explains things well and thoroughly.  His teaching methods are really the best I've ever seen/experienced.
Great guy, willing to help.  He actually makes this stuff fun.
This class was hard, but he was an amazing prof.  If you sign up for the class w/ another prof, just go to coppola's lectures cause it's worth it

Entering this class was very painful at first...but though the material is brutal, this man is a wonderful teacher. You could never appreciate coppola more than if you ended up with glick for your second year of orgo.
wow...i was in another lecturers class before coppola, and wen i switched i could UNDERSTAND wat was goin on..dont miss class..but he is THE professor for chem 210, DONT MISS OUT!!
He's teh r0x0r, and so's the 215HH.
Great prof.

If you're going to criticize someone for being arrogant, you should spell 'ridiculous' correctly.  This man is the best educator under whom I have ever studied.  He is passionate about teaching.  Take his classes.  All of them.  Work harder.
The class was really hard at points, but in the end, it was worth it
If you don't want to work, you'll hate his class.  But if you are really into what you are doing and have the guts to give it all you have and then more, you'll love it.

The best chemistry prof I have had here. Lectures clear and informative as well as an accurate representation of the type of problem that we would see on an exam. Very easy to learn from and willing to answer questions.
hard class but he is very willing to help; class was very fun
Best professor ever

Coppola is arrogant and his lectures are ridicules.  Yes, he's smart and well versed in Organic Chemistry but he acts as if you should also be an Organic Chemistry genius even though this is your first organic chemistry class.
His lectures are amazing, but his Double Honors Orgo II class is freaking impossible.  The grading isn't bad, but man, you kill yourself for that class.
No Comments
Too bad all science profs aren't like him.
No Comments
Awe inspiring.
No Comments
No Comments
The best organic chemistry professor.
Chill class with barely any work outside of class. I liked him and it was a very manageable class.

I didn't enjoy this class. It was pretty boring and not as fascinating as everyone makes it out to be. If you're into linguistics, this class is for you. If not, don't take it for elective credits, it's not worth the headaches and harsh grading.

Good professor, a lot of readings that aren't really necessary, lowest grades dropped. You do need to watch lectures though, and at times there can be too many examples shown. The class is fair, although your final grade is revealed toward the end which is also kind of annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, really funny, nice, and answers questions! Although assigned readings are boring, you don't really need to read them (Sorry Dr.Brennan)

Good prof, fun class! It really increased my interest in linguistics and cognitive science. The lectures were interesting and accessible (lecture recordings posted). I really appreciated the clear grading scheme and specifics about deadlines and late deadlines. The exams were also fairly easy + lowest one dropped. Overall, I recommend this class!

Condescending and paranoid about everyone using AI for some reason. Lectures were mandatory and boring yet there was no other way to learn besides rewatching lectures and trying to connect the dots on your own because GSIs were useless as well. Genuinely turned me away from an interest in linguistics.
LOVE Brennan! This class really deepened my interest in linguistics and neurolinguistics. Really kind and goofy and cares about his students.

Overall this class is pretty easy. I am not a linguistics/cog sci major and was able to understand everything fairly well. Discussion sections are pretty chill just turn in the worksheet and you should be fine. I hardly went to class and still ended up with an A.

I'm surprised at how low his ratings are! His lectures are different than the standard PowerPoint, but I did not find it difficult to adjust. I have had very little linguistics training, and I was able to keep up with linguistics majors. He has also been flexible and willing to help. Definitely would recommend Intro to Neurolinguistics overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is not what it claims to be, it is technical linguistics, it is extremely confusing, the GSI's are no help, the grading is abnormally tough and makes no sense, and the lectures are droning and do not help in learning. This class was the bane of my existence this semester and I do not recommend it AT ALL. Prof Brennan is also not nice.

Professor Brennan is really awesome to listen to, especially if you're interested in the subject. He's super knowledgable and gives amazing feedback which is helpful with complicated topics in class. Would absolutely take again and this class was super easy.

Professor Brennan was a good lecturer, however, sometimes I would get bored because he has a tendency to drone on about topics. Textbooks are required, however, he provides a free version to the class. Discussion sections aren't a big deal, so showing up doesn't matter (as long as you do the worksheet). Overall an easy class but do pay attention.

nice guy but in all honesty just a below average professor. Grades super weirdly and will take points off on rough drafts of your papers and projects even when you go to his office hours. His grading makes no sense and his seminars are extremely unengaging. If you gotta take ling103 just don't take it with him

I really enjoyed these lectures and always found them interesting. There are three exams and five problem sets, but the lowest of each get dropped and the iclicker quizzes are only graded on participation so it's really not hard to get a good grade.
Not great
Jon's lectures weren't exactly engaging, and you have to memorize a lot of linguistics for the tests. However, he was a funny and nice guy.
Nice guy. Course definitely challenging but interesting.

Lectures start to drag as the semester goes on, but there aren't any exams and Dr. Brennan's sincere enthusiasm for the material really shines through. Barely any homework at all. Take the class for literally the easiest A you can imagine, and learn some interesting info along the way.
I love Dr. Brennan!! He was so enthusiastic during lecture, and he made the class very entertaining. Almost made the walk to Lorch at 9am bearable!

Yes, this class is often taken for an "easy A", but I'm glad I took this class because of how caring Brennan is. He is a super knowledgeable dude who has a lot to share. Youll get an A most likely but it's a good idea to just show up and absorb his information without pressure to be tested heavily on it. They can be a little dry but I would reccome
Got an A so you should too ;) Also don't take this class if you're going to show midway through in the morning (I'm talking like 30 mins into class)... They notice and it's highly disrespectful.

Jon taught intro to Neuroling, and he really did an excellent job! He was clear in his descriptions and gave us a lot of time to review the concepts both before we moved on and as we prepared for quizzes. The material was difficult, but he was great at explaining each part and how they fit together. Definitely recommend!

He is very knowledgable and energetic, which helps when this class is early in the morning. Attendance is taken every day and does count. Homework assignments biweekly but they are only a couple questions each and just help to buffer any low scores on papers. No exams. 4-5 short papers and a final paper. Workload is pretty reasonable. Def recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jan was awesome! The class was interesting and the grading was very fair.
One of the best professors I've had at umich, take a class with him if you're able to!

This class is super easy but you don't learn a lot from it. The entire class is based on group work which can be annoying at times but you get more than enough class time to finish the group work. Every assignment is based on completion, not at all hard, and the grading is clear. Jan is always accessible outside of class which is nice

english 126 is pretty unique at umich so I'm not sure how his other classes are graded but he is a kind grader, does actually read everything you submit, class can be a little boring. You have to try to not get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: John is a great professor; focuses more on effort and actually spending time being thoughtful with the material versus grading. Offers extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Buckley was super chill, and his course really challenged my perspectives on homelessness. Very reading-heavy in the beginning and writing-heavy at the end, so complete optional assignments early on. He is a fair grader who makes it easy to get an A if you try; I would definitely recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes professor Buckley's assignments are unclear, but he is extremely caring and willing to work with people. The class itself is not hard if you participate, and Buckley is a great guy.

Outside of some lectures feeling useless, every lecture is engaging. John Buckley is hilarious and he doesn't even realize it. Everything in his life is so bizarre but in a cool way. He wants everyone to be a great writer and he is very passionate about what he teachers. You will learn the best from him if you listen to him and follow what he says

Professor Buckley was a great teacher who truly taught me to think a lot more about the unhoused populations and the many circumstances that lead to homelessness. Through this class, I was able to learn more about Groundcover News. The only critique of this class is that it's a lot of peer reviewing. Optional assignments are necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Buckley is a great teacher; his 221 class was focused on interesting topics, and the assignments were engaging.  Essays are graded on completion, and the workload is not bad at all. Would definitely recommend.
The only class I was excited to go to all semester was English 126. John is brilliant and has amazing insights into English and the world as a whole. Would definitely recommend.

Class is based largely on peer review and peer editing. Attendance is mandatory, but listening is not. Buckley tries to teach in a funny lighthearted manner, but all it does is take away from the usefulness of his teaching. Class feels like a lecture with 18-22 students. Feedback is vague and not helpful. Assignments graded on completion. Rambles.

Great lecturer that actually teaches you very valuable lessons for writing / life. A bit of a harsh grader, but work is very manageable and if you put effort in you will be fine. Not as easy as the other teachers for this course but he bakes you treats and I'm extremely happy I ended up with him. High quality teacher that challenges you (good way).

John Buckley was the best english professor ive had for ENG126. There were many assignments during the sem all graded by completion. Completing all assignments automatically gets you a B+, then do 3 optional assignments to get an A. The writing assignments were all very easy/ interesting and he is funny and bakes cookies for class.

I took English 126 with John. Papers are graded on effort so it's easy to get good grades but there was a significant workload. Highly recommend this course if into social justice. Grades papers and responds to emails in the hour. Genuinely cares about his students and will bake you cookies! Class can feel a little long but I highly recommend!

Lectures were interesting, he's a tough grader but overall a great teacher! 

Make sure you participate often in class (10% of ur grade) as that can bump you up a letter grade :)
Good guy, cares about students. Tough grader and does not give out 100% grades on essays so beware.

Majority of your grade is determined by 4 papers (analysis, argument, research, open letter) and a letter, but if you turn in rough drafts and peer reviews on time you will get full credit. Buckley is a great teacher and teaches you alot about writing and new techniques. Took his 8:30 am and was always engaged. Barely any reading outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: John's been an understanding teacher who takes the time to truly care about his students. The syllabus will look intimidating, but he's much more lenient in his actual grading. The one thing he won't go easy on is a lack of effort; whatever you're writing, make sure it's your own words and not something robotic.

Professor Buckley was a pretty decent professor. I always looked forward to his class since he would crack jokes here and there. Hes a tough grader, but if you attend OH, its gonna make things a lot easier. 4 papers in total - each worth a certain percentage of your grade;

John was funny in class, sometimes he laughs more than we did but it kept it light and entertaining. You learn a bunch of writing techniques which is good. Peer reviewing was a good class choice because it is helpful. He chooses fairly interesting topics for essays. He is a pretty tough grader so you definitely have to put in the work.
Has a great sense of humor and makes class fun. Makes you work for the A though.

He's an extremely straightforward grader--do what he asks and get a solid A-/A. He isn't great at promoting discussion or analysis though, and isn't great at teaching you how to actually write. If you come in as a good writer this is an easy A, if not, prepare to put in the work. Meet with him outside of class to get good feedback.

Overall, John really cares for his students. However, he is an extremely tough grader (especially the first two essays). His grading is illogical and (based upon canvas) only gave A's for the last 2 essays. The entire class received A-'s or lower for the first two essays (class average being a B-/B). Don't recommend if for FYWR if you are STEM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Buckley is a nice instructor, and it is quite enjoyable to be around him. I like that he allows us to read and critique other students' rough draft essays, as it allows me to get the feedback of multiple people and allow me to see how other students write their essays. The only downside I have is that he is a pretty tough grader.

I have really enjoyed this semester with him. He encourages you to write about your interests/your major in the essays, and uses a lot of peer revision and discussion techniques. He has a weird personality, but I definitely recommend this if English 225 fulfills your upper level writing!

He's a funny guy and definitely knowledge about writing. Only thing that irks me is that he is a seriously tough grader, almost seems like he'll give you a lower grade on your essay just because its a higher level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She may seem intimidating, but Heidi is awesome! If you show up to class and put in the effort, you will easily get an A. The extra credit is very easy, and exams were online. It felt like a lot of pressure sometimes, just practice outside of class. The TAs were also very helpful (use their office hours for practice).

Heidi was tough, but when you're getting a license to help save lives, you have to be. She was excellent at providing feedback and facilitating class participation. I would take her class over and over again!
This class was fun, and Heidi is a good teacher. However, she can be loud and sometimes it may feel as though her comments on your work is personal (it's not, that is just her teaching style).

Heidi was a really fun professor to teach emergency response. This class has a lot of hands on activities and you have to go to class in order to get the certifications at the end of the semester. Each person (with a partner) gives a presentation for two topics in the course but as long as you meet with her she will tell you what to include.

Professor Heidi is very educated. She teaches everything very well and you will leave this class very educated. I loved this class for learning more about how to care for emergencies. She does make sure to practice a lot with us; but she does expect us to know the answers and she is pretty caring for situations. She will let you make up if needed
Heidi does all she can to ensure you get a good grade, don't be stupid and you'll do fine.

While it is easy to get an A and more of a fun class, Heidi is stressful to have as a teacher. She consistently calls on random people to answer questions but also gets mad at pretty much anything anyone does. I guess it can be good for learning but I found her to be pretty rude and impatient most of the time. Her class definitely is an experience.

Heidi is so caring and she truly wants the best for all of her students. Training her students to become the best EMR is her biggest priority so she cares more about you learning the material than she does about letter grades. Also offers extra credit. Take her classes. She is awesome.

Heidi was so rude to our class and gave so much attitude when we asked questions. Sure, she's an easy grader, but she makes you feel dumb at times. She basically has the students teach the class through presentations we had to sign up for. I would recommend taking this class with another professor if you could.

Heidi had become one of my favorites from the get-go of all my previous educators. She is one of the most caring professors I have experienced, she wants you to not only know the material but to be able to understand it as though you could recite things with little hesitation. Participation matters because her feedback is so inciteful.
Heidi cares about everyone in her class and her class is so useful! A lot of hands-on experiences.

Dominique is amazing. I've never met a professor so encouraging. I struggled in this class, but she was incredibly helpful. It's easy to find office hours with her, and she gives amazing feedback. She really wants to see each and every one of her students succeed, and you feel it every day in class!

I took French235 but wasn't an option to choose. He was a really nice teacher and very caring. He is willing to meet with students outside of class and is very helpful. He takes note of who participates and often cold calls so I'd recommend answering questions when you feel confident so he doesn't call on you, then it's pretty chill. Overall great
Dominique is a very fun and caring professor. She's very easy to meet with outside of class, and she does her best to make grammar presentations fun.

Dominique is a great professor. She's really sweet and kind, and she's aware of how boring grammar lessons can be so she does try to throw in some jokes or break up the monotony, which is appreciated. She always has office hours and is very accessible by email.

Dominique is an okay professor whose classes are made great by her personality. She is such a caring teacher who genuinely wants every student to succeed. Her teaching methods do not work well for me. I felt like the RC teaches you half of a French class. Lectures covered the material in a way that made no sense to me. She's still an angel though.

Dominique is one of the best professors I've had so far! She makes it clear that she wants everyone to succeed and will devote as much time as necessary to make sure every student is at their desired level. Her feedback is extremely thorough and she always lets students know what they need to work on the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dominique is truly so caring about all of her French students. She provides so many resources on her canvas page and in class and will reach out if she has concerns about your performance. While class is occasionally boring, she can be very funny, sometimes unintentionally, but still. She is very understanding.

Dominique is one of the best professors in the RC. I am so glad I took French for the sole opportunity to take her course. I will be taking more of her courses in the future. She genuinely cares about her student's success and does not hesitate to give advice. She is very reachable outside of class. She is the best!

Dominique is so sweet and so caring as a teacher. Her lectures were usually boring, but, to be fair, they were about grammar rules. She always was very approachable and clearly eager to help students whenever or however they needed. Her feedback on compositions was really helpful, and she does a fantastic job of managing all of RC French. Love her.

Dominique is a fantastic professor and amazing person as well! Took both readings and RCLANG290 with her, and she truly cares about her students. Very accessible via office hours to speak about any issues you might have. Tough grader for essays, but gives good feedback and is understanding of how stressful being a student can be.

I cannot say enough good things about Dominique. She is not only an amazing educator, but she is an amazing person as well. Her office hours are extremely helpful and she is there to help you! She makes learning french fun and I definitely improved because of her. Would highly recommend taking any class with her!
Dominique is amazing! Very conscious about workload and explains difficult and dense reading materials clearly!

Dominique is a prof you'll remember.  She looks out for her students, especially those who are committed to the RC French program.  She will let you know if you're doing well just as she will let you know if you're messing up--so be careful.  All in all, she's a great prof who takes pride in her work and grades accordingly.

Her lectures are fun and animated - even through dry grammar points. Questions are encouraged. She makes a point to remember every student's name and tries to accommodate all learning styles. Office hours seem may seem scary at first, but they're very relaxed and helpful for your specific problems+good practice for proficiency- Highly recommended!

Not an easy A by any means, but Dominique is one of the greatest educators I've ever encountered. She made having conversations with a native speakers comfortable, she's funny and so incredibly helpful. I would take a class with her every semester for the rest of college if I could.

Dominique is the reason I know French now and was able to study abroad. I chose the RC for the intensive language and she made it worth it. ALWAYS there to help, both after class and especially in office hours, she gave me tons of resources and advice on course   planning too. The class is difficult, but that's why its intensive. She's 100% gold

Ok, Dominique is the nicest woman that I've ever had the pleasure of meeting. She's warm and hilarious, and really cares about how her students do in class. That being said, she occasionally will speed through difficult grammar points in class. However, you can always ask for help. She's great. :)
She's super sweet! But very frustrating. Not very clear when answering questions and doesn't tell you how to succeed. It's a very much figure-it-out-on-your-own kind of class.

Dominique is super sweet! She is ALWAYS helpful and legitimately does everything she can to help you succeed. She cares about her students not just as learners, but as people and her office hours are just as much how you are doing outside of class as in the classroom.

Dominique is the cutest person ever!  She's always so bubbly and she makes learning French fun.  She has a great sense of humor and you learn so much from her class. She's very theatrical in the way she talks so it's super easy to understand her, even at the beginning of the course when you don't know that much.

LOVE THIS WOMAN! She is so sweet, and really wants her students to do well. She is willing to do as much whatever it takes to get you up to par for proficiency. A lot of grammar makes lectures very dry, but it's all necessary. She's also hilarious!

I adore Dominique!  She is such an engaging professor, and so helpful.  The class can be a bit boring sometimes, but she's really funny.  While it can be hard most of the time, Dominique will help you get through.  Take her class!

She was a great teacher. She was approachable and hilarious during class. I loved her at first, but as the class went on, I got bored because I had already taken 7 years of French previously, so I scored well on tests, but my accent wasn't up to par, so I didn't pass proficiency , which I thought was ridiculous and it made me hate French.

Dominique is probably the best professor I have had so far. She is incredibly entertaining, open to questions, willing to explain herself, caring about her students, funny, and an all-around wonderful person. I want her to teach me French forever. Take her class. Just do it.

Dominique is fantastic! She is hilarious to listen to and really cares about students doing well. If you have problems, go see her because she will help you work through it to pass proficiency! She is such a nice person, and very easy to talk to if you have questions.

Great professor!  Funny and helpful.  The only thing is the structure of the class is a bit tough.  There is a coursepack and textbook, both of which are confusing in themselves, but you also have to keep skipping between the two to find what you need.  The exercises in the coursepack are usually way above the student's level. But you'll manage. :(

Domonique is *extremely* sweet, helpful, and friendly. I took her RCLANG 320 Friendship class and I enjoyed it. Most of it is opinion, and Domonique is very open to different views. If you need help with papers, feel free to email her or go to her office hours. I'd take another of her 320s in a minute
Dominique WILL get you through profiency! She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. One of the best all-around teachers I've ever had.

Dominique is a very challenging teacher, but she has a lot of charisma in class that balances it out. She's funny and her lectures are informative even when the material is difficult. Stay on top of your notes and assignments and you should have no problem passing proficiency.
not very helpful, cold.

RCLANG290 Fall 2006. 100% passes for proficiency. Yes you read that right - every single person in this class passed the notoriously tough proficiency exam. First time this has ever happened in the history of the RC French program. Says something about Dominique's teaching doesn't it? Thank you Dominique - we're all grateful to you.
enthusiastic, definitely positie. cares about your ability to learn french
She made me love French! Dominique is one of the most amazing teachers I've had!
she's an excellent professor, very approachable, very understanding and overall she's great!!
Dominique is an excellent professor.  She teaches the language very well and is easy to get along with.

Dominique is cute, helpful, and very funny.  I am impressed by her ability to actually care how we're doing, and her attempts to motivate us.  She's like your favorite high school teacher, the cool one who you miss now that you're at college.
She's so cute! And she made me love french. I <3 Dominique!
D. is a great teacher!  If you get a chance to have her as a professor, take it!

dominique is hilarious and does a great job of presenting the material so it is relatively easy to understand.  has a great knowledge of french and she knows exactly what she is teaching and how she wants to go about it every time.  excellent professor.
She's awesome, very experienced in the French language, very helpful, exciting.
Homework was easy and class was chill

People really like him for some reason, but every time I have interacted with him, he's been really rude and mean-spirited. Idk if it was just specific to me, but I've heard students with similar experiences. It can be really disheartening when you have to hear people chanting his name at the introductory lecture series when you know how mean he is

I was very disappointed in Bill's class. He has very little organization to his classes, and deadlines are non existent. He proposes random projects with no end in sight, and announces things in class that are never put on Canvas. He is a nice guy, but if you are Type A in the slightest, you will struggle to appreciate anything about his style.
EVERYONE LOVES BURGARD!!!! (but very few love the lecture series). I think it's aight. Its really give or take, it all depends on the speaker.

Bill Burgrad is a character in the best way possible. He is a caring and understanding professor, always respectful of people despite different backgrounds, and is a genuinely funny and real guy. He's awesome and knowledgeable of so many things and encourages learning in every way!! I love this guy shoutout Bill.

You need to follow what he wants, and he will give you good grades. 
He does not care about your style of drawing. 
He does not respect what you think if you challenge his idea.
He will be rude if you keep sticking to what you want. 
Change everything to what he claims to be correct then you will get an A.

Bill was my favorite prof for all of freshman year. He really cares about his students and it shows. He will give feedback on projects without being harsh...he actually wants you to succeed. I would recommend him to anyone! Some of the material in this class is very perspective heavy, not fun but definitely stuff that needs to be learned:)

The workload is fine and lighter than other professors, but if you come in not having a very "corporate" art style, you basically have to cope and start doing that style. I've seen him misgender students multiple times. Also fairly impatient when you are struggling to understand a concept.

Bill is probably one of the most memorable professors at STAMPs. He won't hold back in critiques, but he gives constructive criticism and specific things to fix. It's not a *lot* of homework, but you do want to designate time for it because some of them can be timely. Bill is friendly and supportive but won't give you leeway to do not try.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be prepared for lots of technical based assignments! They are tedious and have very little room for creativity at the beginning of the semester but loosen up near the end. Critiques are tough but he is specific about what he wants. My drawing definitely improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bill is an amazing professor. He gives a lot of work sometimes, but if you keep up with the homework it's easily manageable. He gives pretty clear criteria for all of his assignments and is lenient on allowing you to resubmit work for a better grade. Bill's great at answering questions and giving advice. In general he's just super fun to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I struggled in this class as I found Bill to be condescending and impatient. He will teach something twice and if you dont get it, good luck. He can be funny and chill but if youre a bad procrastinator, you two will most likely not get along.
The kindest and most understanding teacher I've had in a while. He has really helped my drawing skills without stressing me out and he's super flexible. One of the best art teachers at STAMPS tbh.

Absolutely love Bill and his class! He's such a chill and relaxed teacher but is also informative and skilled in his subject. If your someone who gets offended very easily you might find his critique really harsh, but he always has his students interest and heart in mind. Follow his guidelines and hell give you a 100%. I'm gonna miss him next year

He comes off as a bit dopey, relaxed, he talks kinda slow and drawn out, but man does he know his stuff. Critiques with him are straight to the point. "You did this this and this wrong. Fix it like this." He can come off as tactless and is quite comfortable so he might say something that sounds rude, depending on if you're more sensitive. He's fun.

I like this man. He knows what his stuff and he explains it in a way that I can understand it. I feel that I have really learned from this class and improved my drawing skills by a lot. He can be harsh with critique, but he does it for a good reason.

Bill... Slow, not to the point, insulting, and somewhat disrespectful. I dont think he understands that every student who walks through his door doesnt have the same experience on their back as he does.. Idk, maybe its just me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Bill is ruthless in critique, but takes the time to tell you exactly how to improve-gives great constructive criticism. He has a respect for style, but an eye for technicality. A quick renderer as well, so he gives great examples. Gives daily homework that you can finish in class with diligence. Personally he is dopey, passionate, and critical.

This was my favorite professor of my first year of college, he is so caring and understanding. I went through a very rough time mentally during his class and missed alot of lectures and he still made sure i understood everything we were doing. Love this guy so much

I consider Michael Burke to be in the top 5 FTVM professors at the University of Michigan. His 290 course is so informative and fun. He really creates a safe space for his students to mess up and learn. Take his sketch comedy class if you can, it's Ann Arbor's SNL. On a Thursday.

Michael Burke was one of the best professors I have had at UMich. He is the coolest guy and taught us so much about the industry through his own experience and by producing ourselves. There are 2 group projects outside of class, but they generally take only a day each and are super fun. Take his class!!!!!

Michael is the best professor! Not to mention I saw him helping the elderly cross the street yesterday and this morning he saved my cat from a burning building! Oh and by the way thank you Mike for punching that guy who tried to jump me! You saved me once again! Can't recommend Mike enough y'all!

In 290 specifically, there is an incredible balance between learning through lecture and learning through doing. If you're planning to take FTVM 290, I can't imagine a better teacher than Michael Burke.

I made a rate my professor account just to write nice things about this guy. If you have an opportunity to take 290 with him TAKE IT!!! He always made himself available for questions, told fun stories about his experience in the industry and he takes time to get to know all of his students.
Mike is super fun and makes the entire experience so enjoyable whether you're a film student or not.
He was an amazing teacher and lecturer. Super fun and caring.

Best professor I have had at school thus far. Always helpful and available whenever you need it. Understanding when things go wrong. Offers great feedback and teaches the content incredibly. I'd give more than 5 stars if I could.

Professor Burke is a fantastic instructor and provides excellent in-class teaching that correlates to real-world experiences in production. I would highly recommend taking this course with Burke if you are looking for impactful criticism, support, and guidance related to all things writing, editing, and production!

Professor Burke is truly one of the best instructors I've had at the University of Michigan! Whether you're an FTVM student coursing through the major curriculum or a CS major with an inkling to experiment with production, Mike is certainly your guy. He's not short on experience, guidance, kindness, or keenness for a good laugh. Highly recommend!
The course and its components are very clearly outlined. If you stay aware of the schedule and take notes during class, it will be an absolute breeze. You're lucky to have this professor!!

Dr. Buvinger is very engaging and accomodating for office hours.The only issue I had was it was difficult to know what to actually study and have written down for the weekly quizzes because the content we had to read and the content we got from lecture was very broad. I recommend taking notes on the readings and participating often in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, and Dr.Buvinger is clearly very passionate about this field. What is expected of you in this course is clearly outlined, and the workload is manageable. The quizzes are also understandable if you follow along with the lectures and textbook readings. Overall, a very engaging class, I would highly recommend taking it!
Sweet lady but amount of pure busy work was ridiculous, however Dr. Buvinger is really caring about extensions, grades and could tell she was passionate about her work.

I really enjoyed Professor Buvinger's lectures! It was frustrating that she didn't get through the slides during class, so you have to take notes outside of class in addition to the textbook reading. Make sure to look at the supplemental lecture videos, as they also appear on the quizzes. No final exam only a final paper and weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is very passionate when it comes to psychology, and I would attend lectures and take notes and still struggle to get above a B on the weekly tests. Also, your GSI will determine how highly you're graded. The workload is fine, but sometimes the grading criteria can be blurry.

Dr. B gave clear & easy to understand lectures. However, we often ran out of time & she would make a Canvas post that took much more time to get through than the equivalent lecture would have. Weekly quizzes that can be very specific. Applied project that's easy but annoying. Lots of small parts adding up to your grade that I wish were condensed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I never rate professors, but Professor Buvinger deserves a high rating. This was my first ever psychology class and I absolutely loved it, and I credit that to the level at which I was taught. Dr. Buvinger came to class prepared and ready to passionately teach. I highly recommend this class and definitely this professor.

Buvinger is the definition of an OK professor. Her teaching is decent but she can move too fast with the lecture and leave many things vague. However, she's very passionate about psychology and is helpful when you email her.

I showed up for every lecture and discussion section, took notes every time, reread the slides in my free time, and went to office hours. But somehow it was never enough to get above an 80% on the weekly tests. No comments either. “This isn't meant to be a weeder class” on the first day of school should've been the first red flag. 🚩
