I found her lectures to be boring. She has a habit of calling people out for talking quite often. Honestly it's your GSI that matters the most. They grade the main paper, which is worth quite a lot. I loved my GSI and thought content is easier to follow with the her rather than Buvinger.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger was a great lecturer! The grades are mostly based on the weekly quizzes that were based on the chapters that were talked about that week. However, your grades are based on your GSI because they grade your quizzes, TRPs, and all that, and my GSI was not all that...He was very strict about discussion participation and not helpful.

She was very knowledgable about the course and its topics, but she had a habit of stopping to ask people to stop talking. If you really want to absorb the content, it's best to go to lectures since she doesn't post lecture recordings and the slides she posts have blanks, forcing you to go to class.

Dr. Buvinger will put you straight to sleep in lecture but her class is an easy A. She doesn't record the lectures and the weekly quizzes do depend on material she goes over in class so you have to be pretty good about showing up. TLDR Easy A but painstakingly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger was a great professor that covered material in breadth and in depth. She did asynchronous, open-note weekly quizzes that tested only a week's worth of content. However, they felt overwhelming since the questions tested oddly specific topics. There was also a paper where you had to apply course concepts to your daily life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: PROFESSOR BUVINGER IS THE BEST!! I genuinely loved this class so much and learned tons. Go to lectures; they are fun and engaging, and you will take away so much more from the class. Her class confirmed my interest in psychology, and I could not be happier. Take good notes + go to lecture = A. Hoping to take another course with her later on!

This class has one of the kindest and most forgiving grading systems I've ever seen here, which allowed a lot of students to never attend lectures and still end with a good grade. Genuinely one of the easiest classes here, so it might not properly prepare you for how unforgiving other classes might be.

Dr. Buvinger is a wonderful person who definitely knows what she's talking about and made psychology very easy to understand through her lectures. The only thing that holds her from a 5 is that the class can be mostly learned through the textbook and the quizzes are online, so you're never really compelled to go to class unless you really need help

open note quiz after every chapter. 4-6 page paper, clear guidelines, lots of support, periodic deadlines. Explains material great and accessible outside of class. GSIs grade quizzes and paper. Few assignments but must read textbook chapter, material on test!! Take notes on everything!! Don't pack up early!! discussion participation required
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned a lot and she is a caring, and attentive professor.When she didn't finish her slides in lecture we'd have to watch the rest at home which was annoying.I liked that there were weekly quizzes instead of cumulative exams,which helped grades.TAKE NOTES IN LECTURE!Majority of the quiz questions are from lecture( they were frustrating@times).

Book requirement, $110. No final or midterm but weekly test on pervious weeks material. Extra credit options. Go to class and you'll do good. Participate in discussion as well. Attendance is not mandatory but go to class to do well. There is a final paper that is about 7 pages long but that was the hardest part of the class. Good Professor.
Good professor, getting an A is very doable and there are no exams! A good GSI will make or break the experience, and there are a few extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great prof! Super understanding and accommodating.

Dr. Buvinger is an amazing human being. The way her course is lined out in comparison to other professors in the same department is quite distinguishable as she specifically said herself that she does not believe in midterms. Class is doable as long as you do the reading and memorize keyterms.

I absolutely loved Prof Buvinger and found her lectures to be pretty interesting considering that this is a pretty basic course. Weekly online, open book tests that are a breeze if you come to class and look through the readings. I am unsure why she has such a low score, I don't think it accurately reflects her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance only mandatory for discussion, lecture slides are blank and only posted right before class starts. Class is super lecture info heavy for tests. Test every week but are relatively easy as long as you do the textbook reading and go to lecture/discussion. There is opportunity for 1.25% extra credit!

An amazing professor who cares so much about her students. I loved the videos she incorporated into lectures and even in a huge lecture I felt like I was in a much smaller space that was not overwhelming at all. Intro to Psych is hard to teach and she did an amazing job!

Buvinger was very organized and I personally loved the class set up. We had an online quiz every Monday that could be completed asynchronously and then usually every other week had to complete a paragraph reflecting on a topic we learned. Lectures felt long and sometimes a little boring, but she is the best person for Psych 111.

I liked Dr. Buvinger's teaching style and I would definitely take her class again. The weekly tests were open note, and as long as you go to lecture you will do well in the class. I think that she is respectful and very fair with how she grades tests and written assignments. Highly recommend!

Dr. Buvinger is a fine teacher. The class is very lecture, and it is hard to stay focused. You can not go to class and get an A if you reference the notes during the weekly tests covering the lecture material. If you want an easy A but are bored and senseless, take this class.

Professor Buvinger is an excellent instructor. She sets up the class in a way that makes sure students are actually learning, rather than just memorizing the basics. It is easy to do well in this class if you show up and pay a moderate amount of attention. The quizzes are open book, so if you have the notes from lecture and textbook you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly tests but they are all super easy, be prepared to put in a lot of time outside of class for Subject Pool

She is very nice and she sets everything up in canvas nicely so you always know what is expected of you. There are weekly quizzes instead of any exams (including NO final exam) so it is relatively easy to keep an A. There is not as much HW as others say, and the HW there is takes no more than an hour per week, and even that is pushing it.

I really liked Prof Buvinger! Not sure why her overall rating is so low- she is very nice and her class isn't too difficult. The textbook readings can be boring and long at times, but nothing about this class makes it hard. It should be an easy A, as the weekly tests are all open-note and the two written assignments are fairly light.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind, no exams (weekly tests which are open book), and is invested in her lectures. She cares about how much her students learn. Would highly recommend and am very confused at why her overall ranking is so low!

I'm not really sure what is up with the awful reviews on Dr. Buvinger. I never attended office hours with her, but during her lectures she was friendly. The class itself is incredibly easy. The downside is that the class is mandatory, but I guess it's what you're paying for. The class has weekly open-book tests and two 5-6 page essays.

I LOVE Dr. Buvinger. No exams, but weekly tests, which are open book, open note, online, and open all day. Go to lectures (not recorded) and do readings, but can always command-F for the tests. only 2 papers and one of them can be a presentation. definitely no-nonsense in class. a good class if you want to go into psych, but not one you can coast.

such a boring class and her lectures are not recorded. nice lady but it all depends on GSI. my GSI was amazing but there are two papers, a ton of extra credit opportunities, and a lot of weekly homework assingments. open note take home quizzes every monday and i have an A and never read the textbook once. take this class if you want an easy A

Idk why she is getting so much hate. I LOVE professor Buvinger. She speaks so clearly and sincerely and is very easy to understand. No tests, midterm or final, and pretty minimal homework considering it is a 4 credit class. If you try, you can easily get an A!

There is no recording for this course. And the ppt the prof send to us is full of blank spaces that you need to fill them up during the lecture. There is quiz every Monday- kind of tough, since not all the content covered were mentioned during lecture. I think the prof covered too many things in one lecture that she often failed to finish it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her lecture is very disorganized and assignment heavy. Yet, the materials are very simple, too superficial. You can learn better from wikipidia than her class. Take it if you REALLY have to.

Psych 111 with Dr. Buvinger is painfully easy. It is a very broad overview of everything and does not go very in-depth. Dr. Buvinger is a good lecturer, however, I often skipped lectures and rewatched sped up just to get through the content. It is very easy to get by in this course without reading or paying much attention.

The only benefit of this course is that it is easy and everyone can get A, no exams!
However, if I can choose again, I will rather wait for another semester than choose this course!
The instructor gives students little respect on the time. It seems we have assignments every day, and deadlines throughout the whole week.

She has very little respect for students time. Gives piles of busy work every week, as well as tests and homework during break. This is what. really got me, she has us doing homework and an online test LITERALLY DURING BREAK! This is so disrespectful to students mental health and the concept of giving students a break from school. Avoid her.

What a horrible course! Glad I didn't take this course in my first year. It is a waste of your life and time. The lecturer seems to lack knowledge and taught very shallow and easy topics from the textbook. And the worst part is the weekly test. It asked you strange questions which made me don't know which kind of answer she wanted!

It was such a boring and easy class. I took AP psychology in high school and this class did not give me more professional information than that the AP class. I would say it's definitely not a good choice for people who want to choose psychology as their major. This course had a super heavy workload every week just for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were a lot but clear and interesting. The grading can be iffy, just depends on which GSI you get. the tests aren't just definition-based, but she makes is so that you can do poorly on some of them but still do good in the class (each chapter test is about 2%). no cumulative midterms, only chapter tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best asynch lectures, clearly puts in effort. They're long but not bad if you space it out. Tests are easy just do the lectures (no exams). The 2 written assignments aren't bad, and the GSIs are helpful. The class is easy/very doable, those that disagree are likely cramming a weeks worth of content in 1 day. Take psych111 w/ Dr Buvinger if you can

Overall, this class has mucho busy work for no reason. The nice thing is you have a test once a week and no big exams but she takes off points on the written Q's just for fun. For the two essays she finds ways to take off points for stuff not in rubric. If you go to office hours she will grade easier for the extra effort. Go for other teacher tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good intro to psych class, lectures pretty hefty but were all online for me. Manageable as long as you have time for tests on monday and do mindtap activities throughout week. Unable to get out of buying txtbook since its cengage & activities are in it. Also she gives a couple... interesting.. examples-you'll see
Dr. Buvinger was very kind. When there was a technical error during my quiz she answered in less than 30 minutes and she gave me another attempt. The class was super understandable and interesting.

along with the textbook, she also types her lectures which just gives students even more reading to do & you need to read all of it to do well on the weekly tests. shes very nice, some of her examples are creepy (if yknow, yknow),  but not a good covid-era prof. changed her office hours the week an essay was due. hope for a good gsi lol

Her Introduction to Psychology course is the most work I've ever had for a class in my life. Yes... an "Introduction" class not even in my major was by far the most stressful course I took all semester (which I feel shouldn't be the case).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Buvinger was great! We transitioned to online teaching partway through the semester, but she made this transition smooth and easy for all students. I did an honors conversion for this class, so I worked more one on one with her and she was always so helpful and interesting to talk to! I would definitely recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger was an excellent lecturer. She is kind, to the point, and cares about students' needs. She shows videos and shares anecdotes during class to help clarify content, and the exams are easy to study for if you memorize her slides. Be sure to do all the MindTap assignments, they don't take long and are a decent part of your grade.

Dr. Buvinger is a great prof. Yes, she reads right off the slides for the most part but that is because she puts everything you need to know on them. She adds small little tidbits of information, but she only does this to make the material more interesting. You have to show up to lecture to fill in the powerpoints. She is great and really cares.

Dr. Buvinger is a very average professor. She reads directly off the slides and doesn't add much of her own insight, which can make lectures boring. She often stops due to side conversations, which is inevitable in a 150+ person lecture hall and feels very high school-esque. She uses lots of interesting videos to aid lectures and grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a good professor and seems to be passionate about her class. This is a pretty easy class, exams are not weighted to heavy, MindTap was okay, rubrics for the two essays are clear and tell you what to write sentence for sentence. Easy class if you review lectures and do your stuff (also don't waste your time reading Hock)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger reads directly, and I mean DIRECTLY, off of her slides. Not sure why I showed up to lecture because attendance is not mandatory. If you make a quizlet for each exam from the slides (posted on canvas) you'll likely get an A. Extra credit available if you're falling behind. Lots of extra unnecessary work like subject pool, mindtap, etc.

I would recommend taking class with Dr. Buvinger, she is a good professor with clear expectations and you know exactly what she wants from your on each assignment. The down side is that she mostly reads off of the powerpoints, but that is what the exams are based off of. The course is meant for you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger was a very nice teacher. Psych 111 was very easy. She gives you the lecture powerpoints and all you have to do is fill in a couple blanks. I just transferred all the powerpoints over to quizlet and studied off of that and got an easy A+. If you don't get a high B you messed up big time in this class. Would reccomend
Class is easy A if you memorize stuff on slides - awful lecturer - lecture didn't even help me at all all you need to succeed is the slides.

Dr. Buvinger is an amazing professor. If you pay attention to lectures, you will not have to read the book. Do the Hock readings though (they will be used in discussion and essays). There are a lot of extra credit opportunities.

I love this class and this professor! She presents lecture material very well, and at least for me if you show up to lecture and do the readings it's not a hard class at all. She does her best to make all the material relate to us, and it's fascinating stuff! Highly recommend her and this class.

would not recommend. she reads off slides without adding much information. there is a lot more work than other 100 level classes. also most of the essays and exams have content from movies which are extremely boring and poor quality and are tedious to learn about. the "essays" feel more like hw from high school. she doesn't post lecture slides.

She is amazing! She brings enthusiasm to class everyday and her class is one of the few that I look forward to. She is great at making lecture a bit more of a conversation rather than a lecture and makes it easy to pay attention to. Love Dr. Buvinger!!!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Buvinger's slides are not well organized. I usually read textbook after class to make sure I can have a clear idea of the teaching content. The exam is difficult based on what she taught. Simply memorizing is not enough. And it's not easy to know what will be on the exam. If you can, choose another instructor instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought prof Buvinger was a fine professor. She was pretty clear during lecture and made concepts easy to understand. She frequently got frustrated when students would talk. I liked how she embedded videos during lectures. This class was sooo easy though. Literally just memorize the slides and you will be fine. I did not do the Hock readings.

TERRIBLE professor. She reads her slides during the whole class and also, there is no logic and transition between slides. So it's hard for me to remember all the details without a clear logic chain. Heavy reading and homework workload. Electronic textbook sucks. Never take her class.

Buvinger is nice and can occasionally have interesting lectures, but basically reads directly from her slides which are available online after class. The textbook is entirely online and includes embedded questions which force you to read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The amount of work for an introductory Psych class is actually ridiculous. There is a ton of reading outside of class with a large portion of your grade based on answering difficult textbook questions from the reading. Attendance is mandatory and tracked online, even though she just reads off her slides. Take Psych 111 with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly tough test maker, barely teaches in class, and only reads off of the slides. You have to do all of the learning yourself and the "optional" materials make up half off the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Buvinger is very caring, and even though she reads right off her slides, the exams are straightforward and directly from her slides. You have to attend lecture to fill out the slides she provides or have a friend that will send them to you if you skip. I only opened the textbook if something presented in lecture didn't make sense (rare).

Loved this professor. She's kinda and really helpful during office hours. Exam questions are the majority of the grade and take direct information from the lecture notes. She does talk directly off the slides, but the content is easy. Overall, exams were very easy and I never even opened the textbook because everything was touched on in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If possible, never take a class with this professor. Her lectures are dense and uninteresting as she reads right off her slides and does not bother to explain in depth. She talks way too fast and does not give enough time to take notes on the slides. Tests are unnecessarily hard and have way too specific details for an intro class. STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor I have ever had. She reads word for word off her slides. Exams have extremely specific information from readings. GSIs are nice, luckily. Just avoid any class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Expects you to memorize multiple chapters of two textbooks and asks extremely specific questions on exams. Discussion was not helpful, and neither were lectures. Too much studying was expected for an intro course, do not take a class with this woman.

Teaches by reading off lecture slides and videos. Tests are hardaverage was a C+ on the first test (and this is coming from someone who did well). Gives you a paper to write, due date in one week, but hasn't taught half the questions asked on the essay prompt. Other psych lecturers seem much more capable of teaching & are more realistic graders.
Only teaches by reading off of her slides and showing videos. Stuffs too much information onto tests and tests are too hard.

I've never had a professor that seemed to have no idea what he was talking about the whole time yet still decided to host hour and a half long lectures in an ART class. He confused himself so often and his directions for projects made no sense. He also never knew how to use the softwares he made us use. Learned nothing from him.

This writing class was disappointing. The instructor rarely gave feedback or graded assignments on time, and when feedback was requested, he dismissed it as unnecessary. His teaching style was unprofessional, often unprepared, and at times awkwardly personal. I expected much higher standards from my university.
While Nathan is super lenient with his grading criteria, he makes you do A LOT for most of these projects. It was super difficult for me to be able to find time to do any of these assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Byon was an okay teacher, slight accent did make her tough to understand. The exams were strangely difficult, and hard to do within the time limit. Didn't finish either midterm or final in time and my grade took a hit. Class was annoying but it was more because I had a heavy course load. Don't underestimate the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures and slides are very unclear & unstructured and the teacher is hard to understand. The class is very exam heavy with almost 70% of the class grade based on it and they are very difficult too. Also there are in class quizzes so attendance is mandatory. Would not take this professor if given the opportunity.

Not too bad of a class ! Her exams are worth a huge chunk of the grade so if you don't study you won't do too well. She has an accent but not too hard to pick up on. Pay attention as the content tends to get math heavy.Labs and HW was very easy though

Eunshin is a nice lady. Her lectures and slides weren't the best, but they were solid enough to learn the material. Her exams were fairly easy, but they composed a heinous percentage of the final grade (final was worth 40% of grade). However, I found her exams to be way too long for the given time, and I didn't finish either of them.

Easy class. Lectures are pretty theoretical, but don't zone out when it gets really math heavy because the exams are a good mix of applied and theoretical material. Eunshin is extremely friendly and I can tell she really cares about her students.
Easy class and solid professor.

Not particularly difficult. My issue is directed more at the IOE department for placing more than 3 midterms for core classes over the same week. I got a lower score on the midterm, and it's going to hurt me a lot since exams are worth 80% of your grade. Other downside is you don't really learn anything practical or hands-on (no projects).

The exams are worth a lot. That is the downside to the class. She teaches very clearly, and repeats material if needed to make sure everyone is on the same page. There are many pop quizzes, but most are moderately easy. I would definitely take another class with her again. She is very clear, and lectures are well organized.
Very sweet professor. Starts every lecture by reviewing past few classes and derivations. Exams and homeworks are straightforward.
Clear lecture notes. You can get good grades without going to class.
Class is extremely easy. Exams are easy and very similar to practice exams.  Homework is completely out of the book

Very nice lady; has an Asian accent so takes a second to follow but not incomprehensible.  Grades fairly easily, material is relatively straightforward, and exams are open-book, open-note.  Also gave us a couple of bonus point opportunities, including class attendance.

She had really detailed lecture slides. Her lectures helped explain everything real well. The best part is that exams were OPEN NOTE AND OPEN BOOK. It doesn't matter how the professor is at that point, its a great class.
She prepared very carefully and orderly. I did not know why so many bad comments on her!! She is originally Korean, I guess. But not easy to get A, we need to write FAST in exam!!

From hearing others' reactions to the class last semester and taking the class this semester, I think the class has changed a lot. I really like the professor and find lectures to be extremely helpful. I know there was a lot of criticism before, but honestly I don't think it applies anymore.
I really don't understand the bad reviews.  She's great at teaching and is nice to her students.

For starters, she is pretty much incomprehensible. Then she does examples that seem to have no relevance to the class. On top of them not being relavent, it takes her ages to go through them. Her powerpoint slides are also terrible. Also, she was given midterm feedback on how to change, and took none of the feedback at all. AVOID!

Absolutely brutal. lectures were useless because she was impossible to understand. her examples were useless, and she made the exam nothing like the homework or examples. Her lecture slides are full of gibberish that she barely explains and when asked to give examples, she literally wouldnt. Half the class dropped after the first exam. Have fun

Way too overhated. Malley is super funny and you can tell he's passionate about his lessons. Quizzes can be pretty difficult but you don't necessarily need to do super well on them to get an A. Outside of quizzes, almost all of the points are free. There are chances for extra credit as well.

First of all, he asks you to pay 100 bucks on the Achieve thing, which is doesn't help you study.
Second, the quizzes are not even related to the lectures. These quizzes are made to fail you. I would review for days, creating long notes noting down EVERYTHING he said in lectures, and still struggle. And my friends agree.
Not nice at all. Doesn't really listen to students and is not accommodating. Doesn't really seem to love to teach, just wants to be the boss of his classroom.

Very nice professor. The workload is very minimal and the homework is easy. The quizzes could be challenging, but they are open-note. I rarely attended the actual lecture tho but the recordings are always uploaded right after class and very clear.

Super chill and funny guy. Great lectures. The quizzes are tough, but I didn't do that well on most of them and still got an A. Just do the homework, which is super easy, go to discussion section, and you'll be fine. Great to take as a NS credit if you're not a big science person.

The reviews for Prof. Malley are too harsh. I am horrible at Natural science, but still earned well above an A with two bad quiz scores (55 and 60). They are hard, but SUCH a small part of the grade. Homework and discussion are extremely easy, and most of the points. Do not let the reviews about the quizzes discourage you from taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Show up to lecture & discussion for miss the extra credit opportunities. The first quiz we recieved was not clear in what it was asking, and the next quizes do not do much better. However, I would urge you to do all the homework and worksheets as that matters a lot. I'd recommend going to office hours very frequently. He assigns work during breaks.

Pretty nice guy but literally says a whole bunch of nothing. Quizzes are VERY specific if you don't say exactly what he would you won't get points. Attendance isn't mandatory you can watch from home. Office hours are at unreasonable times too, so not the most accessible. Extra credit and discussion will be your saving grace in redeeming your grade.

Malley was an awesome professor who really cared about what he was teaching. I will say his quizzes, although open-note, are extremely difficult and criteria is not always clear. Do not be surprised if you fail the first exam, I did, and still ended up with an A. He does gives extra credit, so take advantage of it.

Had weird and inappropriate comments with most of the content, always making things sexual to be funny?? Also, the quizzes were immediate fails if you didn't have the key terms he was looking for. Only good thing about this class is that there is no final exam.

Though quizzes are open note, you are expected to remember every small detail from lecture. The questions can be ambiguous and he refuses to acknowledge that. I don't understand why we are paying over 100 bucks for the textbook when it is rarely even used and he admits that a good portion is irrelevant. Overall, difficult professor to work with.

Dr. Malley is a great professor. His lectures are very captivating, and he is very good at using cool animations and innovative slides. The quizzes can be difficult, but they get easier as the year goes on and you are allowed to use your notes. He is very knowledgeable and answers questions during the lecture.

While his lectures are interesting, the quizzes can be extremely confusing. He requires very specific terminology in a single sentence. Be prepared to rewatch lectures and take DETAILED notes. If you get a bad grade the first time, don't be too stressed; People tend to do better as time goes on. As a whole, really hard for an introductory course.

Tried to talk to Professor Malley about my circumstances and confusion in the class, and straight up insulted me. I attended lectures and discussions frequently and learned nothing of substance from this class. No intro psych class should be structured the way Professor Malley has this class set up. Get these professors off of their high horses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is formatted terribly.

You have several open note quizzes throughout the class, drop the lowest score, they are open note. His grading criteria is a bit strange, but he does offer some extra credit here and there. Have a good relationship with your GSI because a lot of answers come from discussion. Textbook is online. The lectures are boring, but it is important to go

This class had interesting content but lectures would often go off on a tangent. The exams r fr and you will only do well if u pay attention to all parts of the lectures (specific wording, terms, examples, etc.). He is not a great professor & he makes use of inappropriate examples for content. The quizzes r ur grade & criteria is not super clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting and I recommend rewatching before quizzes! Quizzes are difficult but weighted very lightly compared to credit-based homework assignments. Offers a decent amount of extra credit and interesting lectures, did poorly on the first two quizzes but ended with an A.

Don't be afraid if you fail the first quiz, I got a 45% and still ended the class with a 95. As long as you take good notes on the lectures you will do well! Very interesting topic and he seems to care a lot about what he is teaching.
Class is easy if you take notes on everything he says in lecture and go to Q&A sections before quizzes. Get subject pool done early and the extra credit will be very helpful.

He's a nice person and you can tell he cares about the material and students. His quizzes are very frustrating. You can only answer every question with 1 singular sentence, and he's extremely specific in what hes looking for. The questions often feel unclear and open ended despite him wanting a very specific answer. Answering correctly isnt enough.
Quizzes are super difficult to study for as there are no resources to help students succeed. Really not worth taking, take another natural science class instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor's lectures are unclear, confusing, unorganized and cover large swaths of information. He does not help his students succeed in quizzes- no lecture slides, lecture outlines, study guides, practice quizzes, etc.

The quizzes can be tricky, but attending lectures and using resources like unstuckstudy ai really helped me stay on top of the material. The workload is manageable if you're willing to put in the effort.

It doesn't sit right with me that there are no exceptions for makeup work - even if you are genuinely sick and unable to come in to take a quiz, it results in an automatic zero. I hope this is changed for future students.

This class was way more annoying than it needed to be. You need to get decent grades on the quizzes to get an A because there are so few points offered, so I found myself rewatching entire lectures the night before quizzes just to get a consistent 80% each time. There is extra credit offered during lecture, but the questions are extremely specific.

Dr. Malley is very passionate about what he teaches. This class has no exams, but quizzes instead. They are graded particularly hard and if you forget to mention explicit terms points are deducted. Definitely do all discussion and achieve work. 112 is not incredibly difficult but take very good notes in both lecture and discussion.

He is a nice guy but his quizzes are downright annoying. The class is weighted heavily on them and they are worded in the worst way possible and you can only answer in under 2 sentences. On top of that, no explanation as to why they are wrong or what they were looking for. take 111 over this class. It was truly the biggest nuisance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Malley is an incredible professor. I loved his lectures and went to all of them even though he doesn't take attendance. He is funny, likable, and has a very unique teaching style. There are quizzes instead of exams, but they are very difficult. My advice is to take Achieve seriously (HW is not posted on Canvas) and do not memorize the material.

Nice guy, tough grader, class is very manageable if you are willing to do the work, extra credit offered at the end of the year and sporadically throughout lectures, so attendance can help. Go to office hours. Lectures are engaging and cover interesting subject matter.

Dr. Malley was an engaging professor and gave very interesting lectures. He's a nice guy, but he is a ridiculously tough grader. The material in this class is incredibly confusing, and lecture usually doesn't help clear up any confusion, so be prepared to do poorly on a few quizzes with little explanation as to why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his class and the material posted but often felt as though he disregarded the needs of students, such as his policy in which missing a quiz for any reason resulted in an automatic zero. This policy extended to all absences, including that of a friend of mine who was hospitalized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Malley was generally kind, and a little rough around the edges. He sometimes disagreed with science which sat wrong with me but its whatever.10 pt tests every 2-4 weeks, so confusingly written. The book is never talked about in lecture but you HAVE to read. Everything is open note. Extra credit is offered quite often

He's a very conscious person and cares a lot for his students. You can tell by the small things. I'm also shocked at how well he understands the material/ how engaging his lectures are.Your gsi also contributes to how much you'll enjoy the class. Make sure to read the textbook for the quizzes, and don't forget to do the hw on time.
Attending lectures is key! The quiz answers rely solely on lectures, so the bookworm isn't very useful in that sense. Still do it because it's easy points and helps your grade a lot.

Dr. Malley is a very nice man when interacting with him one-on-one - don't be fooled by his tough attitude in lecture! The quizzes he gives are semi-difficult, but they are open note and anyone who puts in a good amount of effort and takes good notes should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very interesting, and he makes the concepts easy to understand. Yes his quizzes are weird, but you can drop the lowest one, and if you study enough you should be fine. He gives out extra credit too. Only real thing against him is he can come across as strict and rude, but not to the point where I would call him strict and rude.

The way he does quizzes is horrible because you can only answer the questions in one sentence. He's also an anthropologist so I picked up a lot of the natural science concepts better than others because I also took an Anthropology class. I would take regular 111 over this class if you can.

Great professor and class! Quizzes are hard but if you take thorough notes you should be good (make sure to listen to specific examples he gives in lecture, not just lecture slides) and lowest grade is dropped. Extra credit is offered and textbook work is super easy. Would def recommend if you're looking for a pretty relaxed NS credit.

Dr. Malley is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are interesting and he is very organized in his teaching. As long as you take good notes during lecture and have a basic understanding of the concepts, you should be fine. There are no tests, just quizzes, and they are all open-note. Malley also offers extra credit. I highly recommend!
He is an amazing professor to me. Very forgiving if you are responsible but beware of his quiz, it is not easy.

Lectures were interesting, but when it came to quizzes they were only like 4 to 6 questions that asked small details. So one wrong answers could kill your grade. But quiz questions didn't reflect what we learned, hat toss on how you did (could be good or bad). On the other hand, some days he gives out extra credit for class attendance.
Do the achieve and take good notes for the quizzes and you can easily get an A. The quizzes are hard but make sure to go into office hours and review what you get wrong.

Dr. Malley is an awesome man who truly loves what he does. His class was always entertaining, and I got a lot out of it. Quizzes can be graded harshly, but I averaged around an A- on them and got an A in the class with no problem. If you go to lecture, there are opportunities for extra credit. Great intro class with a great professor.

Easy A for NS credit. Grade relies mostly off of online hw, which has no relevance to quizzes. Lectures are straightforward so take good notes for the quizzes. No exams, only short open note quizzes throughout the semester. Their structure is frustrating and it's hard to do well on them, but you can still get an A regardless. Lectures are recorded

Professor Malley was fine. His grading of quizzes was specific though. You need to have exact terminology and not just an understanding of the material. As seen on Atlas, he also is not the most respectful of students. Homework assignments often have nothing to do with content covered in assessments. If you are looking for distribution, avoid this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was easy and not a lot of work. Pretty much all test material was from lectures, so you absolutely have to watch them and take thorough notes. Malley is a good lecturer, just make sure that you actually have to write down what he says in lectures and don't just read the slides. I had very detailed notes and thought tests weren't bad.

Dr. Malley was really nice and clearly knowledgeable. All of the HW is reading and answering questions about pretty hard to read texts, but as long as you give it a good effort he'll give you a 100%. Dr. Malley was helpful in office hours and gave me advice about things beyond the class. Would definitely take class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't take if easily offended

Psych 112 with Malley- everything to know:
- 8 points extra credit
- 74 easy hw points 
- 6 quizzes 10 pts each; lowest dropped; OPEN NOTE but graded really hard and specific; my lowest was a 7 and my highest was a 10 but many did worse
- take good notes on everythinggg
- lectures are recorded
- go to lecture after quiz 6, there is extra credit :)

Even if you use his own words from his lecture for his quizzes, you will frequently miss half the points on the question because of the hyperspecific answers he looks for. For example, instead of saying "use this term in your answer," you are just expected to know somehow which term he is looking for.

Mistook black GSI for "little Asian woman"

Good professor. Passionate about psych and will try his best to be clear about course material. His exams are hard but fair. You will do well in his class if you take good class, discussion, and homework notes. Pay close attention to class notes. All exams are open notes and in-person. Questions can be worded weirdly, but you get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You do not get feedback on exams unless you have time to make it to office hours. Pretty much graded on 4 exams, he drops the lowest one. Overall good professor, I struggled to do well on exams but did ok in the class
Super passionate about teaching but the material and exams can difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is so unbelievably hard headed. He is not understanding of students and has a god complex. Should be an easy A even though his quizzes do not match what we learned in class. What should have been a fun, inspiring class was horrible.

This class was completely online when I took it except for discussion section. I relied on discussion since Professor Malley's inclusion in this class was pretty much just posting pre-recorded lectures. My GSI was great so I lucked out, but this could be a slippery class for a non-science major. The quizzes are horrible, so don't slip up.
The quizzes are poorly explained without much explanations to why points were lost. Overall the curse is a lot of random busy work that is not helpful in combination with the quizzes.

I didn't interact much with Professor Malley much! He seemed very kind to those who did ask questions, though. The textbook and work was all on a separate site that was easy to navigate. His lectures were released over time, which I usually sped up a bit to get done with quicker. All in all, I had no complaints!

One of the nicest professors I have met in Michigan. He really wants you to succeed. However I would not take this class again because all readings and lectures were really hard to follow and they get you confused. The class was more wrapped around religion but not psych. Consider this class as your last resort.

Professor Malley would assign chapters to read and supplement the material with one or two video lectures per section. The grade you get in this class, during COVID at least, is very dependent on how dedicated you are to keeping up on the textbook readings and lectures. Self-discipline is key.
For the final paper, he specifically told me that it could "not be graded in any fair manner". Very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Psych 112 with Malley is a pretty easy class and I'd recommend it for natural science credits. Quizzes are graded extremely harshly and are super difficult (even though they're open notes). Ridiculously hard quizzes for a 100 level psych class. That said, lectures are optional (recorded) and assignments otherwise are super easy.

I think Professor Malley is a sound person. He's actually quite nice, and very accessible outside of class if you have a question or concern. Don't panic about the seemingly harsh classwork or quiz grading :) I panicked just about all semester, but ended up okay. If you put in the work that he asks of you, you will be just fine.

Whatever you do, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The grading for this class is absolutely ridiculous. Even if you copy word for word what he says in lecture for his open note tests, you will not do well. The average for each quiz is a 50%.
This class is ridiculous. The quiz grading scheme is so stupid and just the overall structure of how knowledge is being tested is horrible. I literally learned nothing in this class.

The professor is tough to follow even though the material is easy. He has a lot of opinions, can be condescending towards students who don't get his material, and grades his quizzes like someone unjustly wronged by the world. Easy A, but don't expect to take anything away from this class.

The list of things I learned in this psych class is not very extensive. I did not really learn anything, but I did get an easy A by putting in minimum effort. You might not learn psychology in this class, but you will come out with an A on your transcript. Would only recommend to fulfill the NS requirement for lsa.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: the material that he presents in class is explained fairly clearly, the issue is that the test questions are very confusing and not applicable to what is learned in class/on homeworks. discussion sections are VITAL, pray that you get a good GSI. do the hw for free points and the lab assignments. lectures are recorded which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: incredibly confusing and difficult to follow. he constantly contradicts himself and although he acknowledges when he doesn't explain something well, he will not try to explain it in a different way. open-note quizzes which is really nice, but don't expect to do well on them, he does not prepare you to answer the quiz questions.

Basically, you have Joe Rogan as a teacher. More than just a physical resemblance, Prof. Malley also has a history of martial arts, a great speaking voice, and is very intelligent. I encourage you to talk to him in office hours. As long as you attend class and discussion regularly, should be an easy A. No exams, just 6 open note pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Malley is a really funny guy, but I didn't take his intro psych class to hear him crack jokes and share his own "opinions" about psychology. It seemed like he never really knew what he was talking about, because he was always having to ask the GSIs (who sat in the front) for clarification. Also, his pop quizzes are graded way too tough
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and write down the entire textbook that he makes you buy. This guy preaches about how life is not hard and how everything will be okay, yet he grades his answers like a Nazi. If you're answer is not cookie cutter material it wont count. He is a delusional professor who does not follow what he preaches. Do not take this bum.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: get stuff done early and you are golden. e.g. required research participation or papers if you dont wish to participate. so much easier to get done in the beginning of the term. also, go to lecture and you don't really have to read other than for a few discussion assignments
I like how the class is structured, and the material he talks about is inspirational.

Poor lecturer, very little of material discussed in class ends up on quizzes. 75% worth of grade is easy to attain, other 25 is made up of arbitrarily graded quizzes. Good for fulfilling nat science req but If you have a real interest in learning about psychology do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pretty cool guy. If you pay attention and make an effort to print out your notes for the exam its not hard to get a B+/A-. He does not give out A+ unless you go way above and beyond. Super good class for people who are interested in psychology and need a natural science requirement. All in all he's cool.
Takes his intro class way too seriously. Quizzes ask about the most specific word from his lectures that aren't on his slides.
The pop quizzes are boujee and he is a complete jerk off, to be honest. Everyone on here is boosting, and just take psych 111 without this professor lmfao

Only open note pop quizzes that are graded very harshly but not super difficult to get an A. Take detailed notes and always go to lecture or else you won't pass since he doesn't post the powerpoints online. He's a really good lecturer and makes the topic very interesting so I'm glad I took the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: super funny teacher. The pop quizzes were petty hard and are graded very harshly so be ware, but atlas there aren't exams. Take extremely detailed notes, including all of the examples he references, because he does not post the slides and you can use your handwritten notes on the quizzes.

Great guy, and the class was pretty easy. I found his lectures a little difficult to follow at times and its a little inconvenient that lectures aren't posted. As long as you show up and take notes this class should be pretty straightforward, be prepared for those quizzes though as they can be challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Malley is one of the better professors I've had. Great sense of humor and manages to make lectures interesting. That being said, it's crucial you keep up with lectures and readings! The quizzes are unannounced (but he always drops a hint at least a lecture in advance) and the questions are mostly open ended. I wasn't prepared and ended up retaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: All about the pop quizzes so basically you have to come to every single lecture to not miss one. They are open book, and only challenging if you don't pay attention or read beforehand. He is often absent for pain so you get a few days off but when he teaches he throws in a couple jokes, allows questions during lecture, and knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the easiest class I have taken.  Malley is an excellent professor.  He really enjoys teaching and has some pretty funny jokes to complement his lectures.  As long as you do all the work and pay attention, it should be hard not to get at least an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Malley was the definition of fine. Psych 112 was not hard at all.  It was completely dependent on your GSI.  I had an amazing GSI so I lucked out.  Beware of pop quizzes they can be very tough even though they are open note. Rest for he class is cake and you're lucky cuz one quiz gets dropped
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class is mandatory and can't make up pop quizzes or assignments. Didnt learn much because a few classes he gave us tough readings and told us to go home without even teaching. Expected us to be prepared but often times was not himself. Unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class at 830 am unless you know you'll get there. If you miss lectures you will likely miss pop-quizzes which count for a lot. Most assignments are due at the beginning of class. He does not accept ANY late work at all and if you miss a pop quiz or anything, too bad. Not the nicest guy but an okay class (if its not at 830).
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Malley is really nice and pretty funny. His syllabus is intimidating but reality is the class is very relaxed. He tries to make his lectures interesting. Your grade depends on pop quizzes so you have to show up. The discussion section is basically another lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill my natural science requirement and I ended up loving it! not to hard but interesting material
He's a pretty boring lecturer but this class was  basically show up and get an A. Easiest A I have ever gotten.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The pop quizzes were somewhat hard in the beginning but this is a good class to take. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A very interesting class. Dr. Malley made every topic interesting and easy to understand. That being said it's not an easy class, you really have to work hard for your grade and make sure you keep up on work. I recommend this class for those who are interested in a natural science focused introduction to psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Psych 112 is a pretty easy class, 6 pop quizzes, no exams, some pretty easy homework assignments in discussion. Malley was a pretty cool guy! Lectures were almost always interesting and he was easy to talk to. Be prepared for the pop quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: easy class, reasonable prof

This was his first time teaching a first year seminar and he killed it. The class discussions were all based on one book and he always kept it interesting. There are "pop quizzes" but he always hinted at when they would be and you were allowed to use any printed notes. Class got out early much more often than not. Overall, great and fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Honestly, this is a class that is completely dependent on your GSI, and this really should be a rate my class rather than rate my professor type of thing. Put in VERY LITTLE effort and you can get yourself a B. Not hard to obtain an A. 6 pop quizzes graded by your GSI which can go either way. Mine graded pretty easily.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a really funny guy. I was bored because of the content but he managed to make it somewhat interesting. All of the assignments are graded by the GSI's so just get to know them and you'll do fine.  I would take it again if I had to but not for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He was a solid teacher and it was extremely easy to get an A. Your grade is based on 6 open note quizzes and small outside of class assignments which only took about 30 minutes. You will learn a fair amount and lectures are fairly interesting. He sometimes cancels class which was also nice. It is a great natural science credit!

Dr. O'Malley seemed to care about the material and his students, as he would provide help when asked or if you made a dedicated effort to go to his office hours (they were often cancelled or the times were modified). The material discussed in lecture did not usually correlate with the readings, which was a major cause for confusion.

Malley gets a bad reputation sometimes as people think he is arrogant. However, although it's annoying that his quizzes contain very specific, complicated questions from obscure parts of reading/lecture, he is a nice guy who appears to care about his students even if he doesn't know their names. Overall, if you do the work this class isn't hard!

I had his class at 8:30 and actually enjoyed it, even if I'm not interested in psych. He uses relatable and funny anecdotes and explains things in ways I wouldn't consider. Very humble and down-to-earth, willing to admit when he is out of his depth. Some students are bothered by his slight stutter but I didn't mind at all or notice much.
This class was very boring but if you take good notes and have friends in your section an easy A.

Very nice guy and good teacher, but our grade was mostly based on pop quizzes, which everyone did terrible on. No curve. Thought this would be a good way to bring up my GPA from engineering classes, but wow was I ever wrong.

You'll get an easy B if you try AT ALL But for those of us who prefer As, take good notes, the pop quizzes are specific and hard completely based upon the lecture. DONT BUY THE BOOK BUY THE ONLINE CODE

will need to buy mypsychlab code to do quizzes on textbook. But you can take it however many times u want, &it's mult choice. Just google it. Pop quizzes during lec, mostly group ones. Attendance for discussion, and lots of mini papers that are more personal than academic.

I love that there are no exams, it lets you focus on enjoying the material for the sake of it being interesting, not just to get a grade.  Malley tells lots of interesting stories about his own and others' experiences.  I always enjoyed going to lecture.  WOuld definitely recommend Malley for this class

Dr. Malley is an engaging teacher, and he's entertaining. He does not give traditional exams. The pop quizzes he gives are extremely specific, so take down notes on EVERYTHING. The other assignments are easy A's if you follow the instructions. The reading quizzes are extremely specific also, but you can keep taking them over and over.

Easy A as long as you show up to lecture, take notes, and do the assignments. He assigns readings but you don't actually have to do them. Lots of easy homework and assignment points & the other 25% of your grade is pop quizzes. Lowest quiz grade is dropped. Only buy online version of the book, paper is useless. Overall easy/interesting class

Professor Malley knows a lot about psychology and his lectures are interesting. He is an entertaining lecturer. There are no tests just 6 open note pop quizzes so you can't miss class. The quizzes are pretty hard but the other assignments are easy to do well on. Must take notes on lecture and readings to be prepared for quizzes. Readings are long.
The class is super easy. However, he grades on minor material and is not politically correct at all. The rhetoric with which he speaks is so far from clinical that it's uncomfortable.

Lecture is a must as that is where the pop quizzes are.  Also the readings are ungodly long and you have to do them. Pop quizzes are hard but there are so many other gimme points in the class that it doesn't really matter.  Lectures are mostly interesting but Brian is a touch arrogant sometimes which is annoying.  Learned a lot, would take again.
Malley is a very approachable person and his lectures are fun. Everything is not quite clear, but assignments are easy. Give easy grades and helpful office hours. His dirty jokes are the best!

Go to lectures and write down everything he says - he talks fast and his slides are there mainly for him to keep track of what to say (there is not much on the slides). He gives open note pop quizzes which can either be really hard or really easy, but the lowest gets dropped. Make sure you keep track of what's due when.

Malley is a good teacher, keeps lectures interesting. How to do well: write down everything he says in lecture and all the bold definitions from the book chapters, cause he uses open-note pop quizzes. Definitely have to pay attention and go to lecture but often these quizzes are group or take home so you should be fine. Can be harsh grader.

Dr. Malley is seriously so hilarious. You'll love his lectures because he always makes them interesting. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, too. He's also very kind when dealing with sensitive topics and has topics/ assignments dedicated to self-improvement. Expect pop quizzes, but they're not so bad because you can use your notes.

Psych 112 was an easy A for me, but that's because 2 out of 6 "pop quizzes" ended up being take home, and 2 others ended up being group quizzes.  The other 2 were individual pop quizzes, but you drop your lowest quiz score so that left 1 quiz that was actually hard.  Lectures were boring for me, but this class wasn't very difficult at all.

I guess you can say lecture is mandatory because he gives pop quizzes and theres no make up. 50 points of your grade come from quizzes, and he assigns online chapter exams from chapters of the psych book. (fairly easy). Good thing, there was no midterm/ final and only 2 papers but extremely short. A little effort can get you a solid B
Don't take this class, you do not learn anything.
His quizzes were close to impossible.  He was not organized.  Pop quizzes were open note, but lectures/reading did not prepare you.

His quizzes are very difficult, and even though they are open note, they are very poorly written and lectures/reading will not possibly prepare you for the quizzes.  He is unorganized.  He would cancel lecture often.

The pop quizzes are very difficult and don't really have much to do with what you have read or what you do in class.  There is inconsistencies in grading.  The material isn't difficult, it's the grading and the structure of the class that is hard.

Dr. Malley is a great lecture as he makes use of his time by giving lots of information. Beware of pop quizzes, you can use notes but they are still incredibly difficult. Honestly, take PSYCH 112, its basically the same class but 112 looks better. Also, he is very picky about formatting so just be careful with that.
Professor Malley was funny, engaging, and doesn't require much work. I would highly recommend this class for people who need to fulfill a Natural Science requirement.
Great guy, loved his call. Very conversational but be prepared for the pop quizzes. Bright side: no exam!
He's an awesome lecturer, and the 6 quizzes in class are super easy, plus you drop your worst one.

I loved Dr. Malley. His grading criteria is clear and as long as you put in the work, it's easy to do well. He's a cool guy, and very willing to help you out during office hours. His class format (pop quizzes, journal entries) isn't everyone's favorite but I personally found it very enjoyable.

I really liked Malley and Psych 112 is pretty easy. Its almost so easy that you forget about it and some people end up not doing as well as they'd like. Basically you have to go to lecture because theres pop quizzes and you have to keep up with the online work. Its easy to forget about! If you do those two things than its an easy A. No exams!
Great guy, very laid back but also shows he knows hit stuff

PSYCH 112 is confusing due to Dr. Malley's senseless grading techniques. The quiz questions relate to obscure facts from lecture. The class has inconsistent grading and poorly defined extra credit. On homework, I lost points for errors like not indenting paragraphs.  Dr. Malley is a mediocre lecturer and doesn't always come to class.

Dr. Malley is a bit odd, but overall a good lecturer. He's clearly passionate about what he is teaching and wants to make a difference in students' lives. 6 pop quizzes that are fairly difficult, but are always open note, and often take home andor group quizzes. Discussion is optional, but helpful for short writing assignments.

Didn't stay in the class long because he made me feel very uncomfortable. Didn't seem to know what he was talking about, stated things as facts that were easily disproven. Definitely think he needs to go back to school himself.

Dr. Malley is a good lecturer and professor. He was extremely helpful in office hours - I highly recommend going to them, and also sitting in the front in lecture! The class itself was alright; I felt as though I was taking notes on the book a lot, but that's optional. I learned a lot. The quizzes are alright, but be sure to print out your notes!

I loved malley's lectures. very interested in psych and he tells it in a interesting way that makes me want to be there. hes such a nice great guy and very funny at times. hes really laidback and wants to see his students succeed. really loved him and his lectures. i would actually be bummed if I slept through one of his lectures. dont get book

Malley was a really funny guy, I found the lectures to be pretty interesting, though at times can be boring. I think that comes with the breadth of the topic, very briefly touching on many topics. 75% of the class was gimme points, the rest were the pop quizzes that were challenging, but many were either take home or group.

Malley is an interesting lecturer, and this is important considering you need to show up to every lecture. There are six pop quizzes throughout the semester and no exams. Show up, sit with friends, and take some notes, and you will get an A. However, be prepared to learn nothing at all.
Pop quizzes to encourage people to attend lecture, they suck BUT no exams.

Brian is very clear, both in the presentation of the material and his grading expectations. This class is not super interesting, but hands down an easy A. Not much work at all. Just make sure to come to lectures because while there are no exams in this class, there are pop quizzes!
Good professor. Watch out for pop quizzes, they aren't tough but they are spontaneous. He explains the content very clearly.

Dr. Malley is a great teacher, and he has his quirks during lecture when he's going through some tough stuff. Overall, his personality makes you want to go to lecture, and his six pop quizzes throughout the semester make you want to study. FYI, the lowest score gets dropped. Great intro to psych class, and an easy four credits in the NS requirement

Definitely one of the tougher professors I've had at Michigan, but lectures are entertaining. He's an engaging lecturer, and makes you want to go to class. If you ask a question, he'll spend as much time as necessary to make sure you understand before moving on.
I love malley so much. very fun and relatable. gets straight to the point about information and keeps lecture interesting for the most part.

He is a pop quiz master. So don't skip lecture, but he does give you one free one to drop. He really seems like he cares about how well we do through the emails he sends us occasionally. He also is engaging in lecture and throws in a few jokes to keep it enjoyable. I went in already really liking psych, and he made me like it more.
Great

Every student that goes to class is capable of earning an A. The quizzing system is a bit unorthodox, and I found it to be somewhat useless. This class is psychology at its most basic level so don't expect much.

Brian Malley is a great professor. He weeds out nonsense and useless info and delivers only the most interesting and relevant material. It's easy to get an A in this class, but you must go to lecture so you don't miss the Quizzes. He makes lectures humorous and light-hearted. Overall a great, interesting, easy course.

Perhaps the most boring class I have taken so far. Little work, and generally easy to do well, just don't miss the quizzes. Malley though is perhaps the most arrogant professor I have had and he really ruined the class for me.

Class is not a lot of work at all. A few little assignments in discussion and no exams. There are open notes pop quizzes in class that make up your entire grade. they aren't easy but also not impossible. I thought lecture was really boring and really learned nothing, but its an easy A.

The class is kind of interesting, not that great. As far as professor Malley, he is average in my opinion. He has fairly interesting lectures, however, he lost my respect with a lot of very rude comments and he is inconsiderate of students. Seems arrogant. Pop quizzes are easy. Take good notes.

This was one of the hardest classes I have taken at Michigan. Rarely did anyone know what was going on because the readings were so complicated. I felt like everything we learned did not tie together at the end. Malley is a great guy but this was just too much work for what we learned. Would not recommend the class.
The most interesting lecturer I've ever had. He will never try to trick you, even his pop quizzes aren't too horrible. Take good notes, do your readings and you'll have an easy A!

Pop-quizzes during lecture make going to lecture mandatory. Quizzes are very nit-picky but not too hard if you take good notes and print his lecture notes, as you can use these materials on the quiz. Worst quiz score is thrown out. Papers are easy. Long readings are not necessary. Malley makes lectures interesting and funny.
Very funny, very intelligent
He is really funny, knowledgeable, and organized. The assignments make sense and he doesn't believe in exams. Awesome professor.
the class is easy because there are only quizzes and no exams and it's all open note. can be a bit boring but overall good.

Terrible teacher! Rude, lazy, unreliable, ambushed students with unreasonable tricks to take your points off, terrible grading system, quiz questions very ambiguous and grading very subjective. Arrogant and reluctant to discuss questions from quizzes. Posted final grades later than required by LSA rules. Worst ever seen. Avoid! at! all! cost!

Pretty easy class. For the quizzes, just answer the questions in the lecture summaries that he gives you beforehand. I really actually enjoyed going to lecture cause Professor Malley always made it interesting. Warning: Don't forget to do assignments/hw. The little points seem trivial, but they're actually worth a LOT since there aren't many assign

I thought this class was going to be easier than it was. He's very nit picky with the answers on his quizzes. You can get points off for improper formatting on papers, too. However, if you follow the guidelines and pay attention it's a pretty easy class. And Malley knows what he's talking about. He's a good guy overall, too.

Great class! Follow the rules on syllabus & you'll get an A! His quizzes are easy (open note) so go to class and pay attn! Skim the book to take notes. Only downside is each discussion section is different, my GSI had us do a few papers, but all relatively easy and interesting. Tell yourself it's interesting material, and you will enjoy the class!

I honestly have NO idea how he got anything below a 5 for easiness.  If people think this class is hard I honestly dont understand how they survive at this school. EASIEST A OF MY LIFE. lectures aren't THAT bad, I like psych so i enjoyed coming to class. no finals, 5 surprise quizzes so you have to go to class but 3 out of 5 were take home. eaassy
Never had to do a synopsis assignment. Great teacher, hilarious and very interesting. Would definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Malley has some rather unfair policies regarding quizzes and attendance, and has provided no legitimate reason for those policies.  When thinking about good professors, he does not necessarily come to mind.

This was definitely one of my favorite classes I've taken at the University of Michigan.  I am not a Psych major but I still was able to so well in this class and it was not difficult if you paid attention and took good notes!
No exams. 6 quizzes with open notes. Takes top 5 quizzes. Plenty of extra credit in the end. Skim your book once a week and it's an easy A. Highly recommend.

My favorite class so far!! He is really nice& funny and good at explaining and engaging students. First few quizzes are  hard and make u wanna die! But it gets better and he also gives out extra credits at the end of the course.  easy A. Discussion sessions are fun if you are interested in psych. It really depends on YOU!

Dr. Malley is a great professor and he is very engaging in his lectures. However, the material that we were responsible for between lectures, sections, and readings are beyond reason and, therefore, made the open-notebook quizzes very difficult. Lectures were a pleasure but material was dense and the quizzes were very difficult.
Malley is pretty annoying with his quizzes. The questions are so vague but require such specific answers. Overall pretty easy class-take notes and come to lecture and you will get an A

The class was fairly easy, didn't go to class much. No exams, only 6 quizzes in which the top 5 were taken. All quizzes were open note, some were open laptop too. The quizzes were pop quizzes. Discussion section was very boring but a chance to make some easy points.

Brian is hilarious!!!!!!! His lectures were always interesting and the class was pretty easy as long as you payed attention and took notes and read occasionally. However he was a little bit picky about grades and he also had some strange rules but other than that the class was great.

Great class. Great professor. Lots of (sometimes difficult) readings, but Dr. Malley does a good job at pinpointing the important stuff. 6 quizes, a few out of class writing assignments, weekly synopsis assignments (not that hard, but everyone acts like they are). My only critique: Somewhat confusing grading system.

Great class! Malley is an awesome prof! He always keeps lectures interesting and the time flies by really quickly. Material is super interesting and the class isn't that hard. The grading is pretty picky, but it's honestly worth it because you actually learn things worth knowing. Recommend!!
Great guy! Controls himself well. Interesting lectures. Mkay. Very funny! Hilarious sense of humor! LOL!!!!!

EASY class if you're just looking to fulfill your NS requirement. He is really picky about his grading but just pay attention it's not hard. Attendance isn't required but if you want to do well on the quizes go and take notes-can use on quiz. The class was interesting too he made some funny jokes, sometimes.

Boring lecture; way too "synopsis" assignments with REQUIRED reading of 50-150 pages. gave extra credit (a lot of work), but grades hard. He can be cool, but other times, he can be jerk! Take with caution!

Malley is hilarious and is one of the few professors that can keep me awake during lecture. Doing the readings is pointless because the quizzes are either open-book, notes, partner, etc. But he's very specific with how the quizzes and assignments are graded, which makes it VERY easy to get a poor grade. Interesting material, though. I recommend it!

He makes lecture interesting, but he grades SUPER hard. You have to do "synopses" for every reading, summing up at least 50 pages into one sentence that encompasses the entire argument. If you do the slightest thing like not formatting it right, it's -1 point out of 3, which automatically gives you 66%. It feels like I'm being cheated as a student.

Malley keeps lecture interesting and funny with his little jokes and comments. Pretty easy class because there are no exams, just pop quizzes which are open notes. Quizzes are hard as long as you take notes in class and discussion(my gsi put slides online). its an easy class just make sure you follow exact directions.

Dr. Malley is a good professor who makes lectures interesting. Although the quizzes are annoying, it is pretty easy to get an A in the class as long as you go to lectures and discussion and take good notes. I would recommend this class. Definitely more interesting than other intro courses.

Brian Malley is a pretty good professor.  The class was interesting, and it was not difficult to pay attention.  He spiced lectures up with funny comments and videos.  It is not too hard of a class, but it is very possible to do poorly.  The class is based pop quizzes, a paper, and discussion work.  Overall I would suggest intro psych with Malley.

This class is kind of a joke. The grade is calculated based on the best 5 of 6 "pop" quizzes, which are open note, occasionally take-home, occasionally partner. When taking notes during lecture, write down the examples he gives. This helped me very much during the quizzes. This is not a class for someone who is genuinely interested in psych.
He is a straight-forward professor.  His lectures are interesting.  His quizzes are hard! Just take good notes and you'll do fine.  Make sure to go to class.

The worst. I thought I wanted to major in psych before I took this class, but it pretty much killed that idea. He's overly nitpicky and unclear. Overall, I feel like this class was a waste of my time and tuition. Definitely avoid at all costs.
