I don't know which was more awkward: the constant invitations to study "qigong, which is very secret", or the time he described orgasm as, "You're in for a treat if you've never had one. It's like a little seizure down there." (He then proceeded to demonstrate what it feels like through a series of jerking motions).

Class is interesting and Malley keeps class running smoothly. Grading is fair and it is important to take notes in class and attend ALL classes, even discussion. I would recommend this class and this professor!

Dr. Malley made himself very clear at the beginning of the year how he felt about formatting and attending class. Taking this to heart, I listened to what he said and ended up with an A in the class and loving Psych! Plus I had the best GSI, Emily Kean :)

I really enjoyed having Malley as a professor. He made lecture interesting - which is something all of my previous classes have lacked. The grading system is a bit ridiculous, and you seem to be graded on purely formatting at some times. But, if you simply follow directions PRECISELY and attend class, you're golden.

He is honestly one of the worst teachers I've ever encountered in my entire academic career. And that's saying a lot because I am currently a senior. Avoid him at all costs (I believe there's another professor who teaches this class in a 2-hour lecture format)

I thought professor Malley was great!  This class was very interesting to me.  I enjoyed lectures a lot but the readings weren't super interesting and were boring.  As long as you do every assignment and show up for every quiz you should be fine.

I would must definitely not recommend. Ridiculous and strenuous grading scale. Very unwilling to offer any assistance after a dispute with a GSI. I would even go as far to recommending the university to rethink having him as a representative of their educational staff.
Go to discussion & you'll have an A

He's awful. He was completely rude to me, talked down to me, and was so unclear about grading and overly specific about formatting to the point where you'd go from a A on a paper to a C for forgetting to put the page numbers on it. So obnoxious. Avoid him at all costs.

Terrible class.  This course is more like a class on formatting articles you write, to the point where they could be submitted in a peer reviewed journal.  It is supposed to be intro to psych, and I didn't learn any psych.  There are no exams, papers are graded horribly, and the course is very unorganized.  Never take this class!
The worst teacher I have ever encountered. Do not take any of his classes. I didn't learn a single thing except that format is more important than content.

This is the most rediculous class I've ever took. Format is EVERYTHING. The things that get you pass the course have ALMOST NOTHING to do with psychology. Quizzes are easy and fun, and are the only ones that are related. The reason I failed is the margin of the paper. NICE JOB!

Rough class. Not really sure what he wanted us to take from it. A lot of the reading was really weird/difficult. You have to go to class and you have to do the reading, no way around it. There's no papers, no exams only quizzes and writing assignments which was a double edged sword. It's doable but you probably won't enjoy it.
Decent class, but i dont think i really learned anything. I just went to lecture so i didnt fail and then used my notes on most quizzes.

Funny Professor who made class entertaining. They layout of the class was pretty bogus, however. Their are no tests so the whole grade is in-lecture quizzes and a paper. The grading is a bit ridiculous, the phrase nit picky does not do it justice. Despite this, still a great class to take.

Quizzes are REALLY HARD because you have to use specific key words and if you don't you just lose a ton of points. the average is usually like 5/10. don't rely on the quizzes - just make sure your papers are perfect (like you did everything on the syllabus and have perfect format), and do all the extra credit assignments.

Really, people? This class isn't hard if you do the readings and go to lecture. His notes are available online, and you can always go to office hours. Not to mention THERE IS NO EXAM. And as for the quizzes? You can use your books and all of your notes, for crying out loud!
quizzes were hard, he explained material in a non-interesting way. i don't recommened him.

Much harder than I expected an Intro Psych class to be. You have to write a research paper (which took MANY hours). Quizzes are NOT multiple choice and are pretty hard. Having a good GSI made this class manageable, but don't take it if you're just looking for an easy A.

Completely useless professor. He doesn't even have a degree in psychology. All he does is talk about his sexual fetish with monster truck tires and his miserable life. This class taught me nothing about psychology. Don't take it with him.

He's a creep. He has a sexual fetish for monster truck tires, and is always making sex comments that are completely unnecessary and inappropriate. He's also an idiot and doesn't understand real science. Don't take his class.

Not a bad teacher, really wants his students to go well.  He puts outlines of his lectures online before class so if you print those off then you can take notes with those which helps.  The biggest thing that hurt me was how specific some of the quiz questions are.  REALLY NICE to not have a midterm and final.

Always go to lecture and always have your notes printed out if you type them.  Always be ready for a pop quiz.  He was really helpful during the research paper because you could take your drafts to him during office hours and he also really wanted all of us to do well.  Stay away if your looking for an easy A, but overall not bad.

He is horrible. If you actually have an interest in psych, take it with another teacher. There are no exams and no studying, but the class is focused on minute details and whether or not you followed specific format for everything. Easy A, but not worth it. Malley is not intelligent, nor engaging.
Lecture was great. It was a early morning class, yet rarely I fell asleep. Too bad my GSI sucked... really hurt my liking of this class.

All the people that complain about him being hard must not know that this is MICHIGAN and work is obviously required for the classes.  Go to lecture and actually pay attention, do your reading, go to office hours and you will get a good grade.  If you are used to slacking off and not going to class this clearly isn't the class/school for you.
malley was a great teacher. as long as you go to class and take good notes, you'll have all the answers for the quizzes, and you'll be able to do well. office hours help a lot for the papers.

I thought I wanted to major in psych before taking this course.  It's all about whether or not you can understand/identify peer-reviewed research articles and can find random details in the text book for the pop quizzes.  There's no final but the quizzes are impossible and papers are ridiculous.

I found myself in lecture learning about anthropology and common sense more than psychology. To my amazement he doesn't have a single degree in psychology. The quizes aren't based on psychology but rather were you paying attention to all the details. I ended up dropping it because I couldn't stand the absurdity that it was.

The lectures were interesting. However, he graded more on how well you paid attention to minute detail (like 1" margins) versus the subject matter. I didn't find him helpful after class either, he acted kind of like I was stupid for not knowing something he didn't teach. His directions for assignments confused me and everybody I sought for help.

Dr.Malley is a really interesting professor. It is easy to get a good grade in the class but you def. have to do your work. Don't slack off, go to lecture, take good lecture notes and you'll do fine.  Also, schedule office hours meetings with him for papers. It will help you a lot.

I constantly found myself asking my neighbors "what just happened" during this class. Just really strange topics and somehow everything related to sex. Your grade basically depends on how your GSI grades and how well you understand what they say. Content is pretty simple and Malley seems to be a good guy. But it was just a VERY odd semester.

I'm pretty sure his degree is in Anthropology, which would explain how miserable this class was. Bad, bad plan. If you can avoid taking it with him, do so. If not, you can still pull an A. I did. Take advantage of the extra credit.

He is an entertaining professor. The lecture quizzes are difficult; however they do not determine your entire grade. Getting a good GSI is key. There are no exams (at least the semester I took it). Your grade really depends on how your GSI grades.

Malley is entertaining  but he does not give detailed lecture notes during class or post them online. This is difficult because the room is always noisy! Lecture quizzes are really hard, but you can still get an A in the class even if you dont do well on them because discussion section is most of your grade!

This semester was the first that the university decided to have Malley's lecture recorded in one room, while live in the other. This is what we're paying for? Besides that, Malley's quizzes may appear straight-forward, but you'll get docked for one word that he doesn't like. Otherwise, your grade is determined by GSI, so make sure to get a good one!

The quizzes are not that hard. You just have to read. It's one chapter a week. I read, attended lecture, and wrote decent papers. I'm ending up with a high A. Utilize your GSI's office hours, as well as his, and you will be fine. Basically, do what you are supposed to do instead of looking for shortcuts.

Not sour grapes, I probably got an A in this class. But the guy is an absolute joke. I like Psych, the material is pretty interesting overall, and Malley has some interesting things to say, but he goes out of his way to make things unnecessarily difficult. And more often than not I find him annoying to listen to in lecture.

Dr. Malley is an entertaining lecturer. However, the quizzes given in lecture are ridiculously difficult, and unnecessarily so. Simply grasping a concept is not enough.. you pretty much need to read Malley's mind, because the GSI's want only Malley's answers. And lucky for me my GSI sticks to Malley's every word. I will NOT be getting an A.

Not a bad professor. Lectures are usually very funny, but don't let them trick you. There are no tests, just 6 open book quizzes that are VERY difficult. You have to have exact wording that he is looking for. And grade appeals are not easy. Interesting class, but bad for the GPA.

He is an engaging guy. I enjoy his lectures. He tries to ensure that people come to lecture by having pop quizzes and other points given out during lecture. no exams, but the quizzes can be deceptively hard
HORRIBLE!!! DO NOT BY ANY MEANS TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

Dr. Malley is a funny guy, his lectures are usually really entertaining! He is a difficult teacher though. There are no exams in the class, but the lecture quizzes are a little confusing and if you don't write the exact words Dr. Malley wants your GSI will take off points. If you want an A, probably don't take this class.

All of the learning is done outside of class. Not much reading, and he says he doesn't require memomorization. However, in discussion the quizzes (which are created from a bank of questions Dr. Malley himself created) would often require the name of a study or theory. I find the class to be unnecessarily difficult, and Dr. Malley unhelpful.
Honestly, what is taught in lecture has nothing to do with what is on quizes at all. GSI will determine your grade, and luckily I got stuck with a horrible one so we will see how this semester goes.

Well I loved his Psych 111 class, but then 313 (Psychology of Religion) was TERRIBLE. Seriously if there was ever a hot mess of a class, this was it. There were no tests or papers- the grade was from arbitrary pop quizzes and a horrible group project. Avoid 313!

Dr. Malley is a great teacher.  He keeps his class interesting and straightforward. People complain that the quizzes are hard but if you pay attention and do the readings they really aren't. Besides all of the quizzes are open book/note. It's the GSIs that you have to watch out for.

I loved Dr. Malley's intro psych class! He is always trying to make the class laugh.  It was a pretty easy course and really interesting. Plus, no exams and the lecture quizzes were all open book and some were group! Can't beat that
Professor Malley is hilarious, which makes going to lectures fun.  This class isn't that hard if you keep up and study for the quizzes.

Super easy class. No tests or exams. Attendance is mandatory because of random pop quizzes (my grade went down from being sick for 2 weeks and missing 2 quizzes in section & lecture). Pop quizzes are open book. You have to write 2 easy papers for section and have announced quizzes in there that are tougher than lecture quizzes.
Very smart and willing to help. His quizzes aren't that hard, as they are all either open book/notes or group quizzes.

Was extremely interested in course material. However, this class is completely disorganized. He often shows movies, has his gsi's lecture, and when he does lecture lets the class out early. Class itself is on the easy side, but I feel bad that I paid tuition to watch movies...

Dr. Malley seemed like a nice guy, but his lectures were boring sometimes. The pop-quizes were pain because it forces you to come to class for sometimes pointless lectures. It sucks having most of your grade based on 10 point quizzes.

No exams or tests, but pop lecture quizzes instead.  Contrary to previous comments, the quizzes are pretty easy (They are all open book!).  Dr. Malley is a pretty funny and entertaining professor, and he'd better be, since attendance at lecture is pretty much mandatory (pop quizzes are not retake-able).  I'd recommend the class.

While Malley is a super nice guy, and he definitely knows his material, the quizzes are hard. He got rid of finals and tests and tried to make the grading easier for people to obtain an A, but it was still difficult. You definitley have to go to his lectures, he doesn't announce when a quiz will be, if you miss a quiz, it's a zero. No redos.

I heard mixed reviews about him before but now I see why people didn't like him. Makes you come to class for pointless lectures that don't help. I've heard if you go to office hours, he's not very helpful and kind of rude. I wouldn't recommend this class.
Really funny, easy to understand.  Slightly harder than other teachers from what I've heard, but not hard to get an A or B.

I loved 111 with Malley, and then HATED 313. I was extremely disappointed. The whole grade is based on a group project and pop quizzes (no exams or papers.. nothing of substance) and his lectures are lacking in content. GSI is horrific. This class had lots of potential, but it's just a mess.

Brian Malley is interesting, intelligent, and funny. However the tests are way way way too hard. To put it simply, I did much better in Organic Chemistry than I did in Psych 111. I like the class, just not the grade.

I enjoyed Dr.Malley's class. He is enthusiastic about teaching this introductory class and tries to make it interesting through showing short-clips and movies that I found to be very helpful. I recommend you to go to his office hours if you have any doubts in lecture materials or in readings. Make  sure you go to his every lecture too.
Wants to be a comedian (doesn't everybody?) Multiple-choice tests = poor education, go blue?

If you have interest in Psychology he's a good professor - clearly smart.  But I simply wanted an easy A, and he's the one psych 101 section in which that's not possible.  Lectures are clear, but the tests come from the textbook.  Take another professor for an easy a
exams are tricky

I could see why someone would not like Malley, but I actually enjoyed him quite a bit. I thought he was quite humourous, well spoken, and generally an interesting speaker. This was the only class I never missed. You do have to read the text book though, his tests- though he says they're not meant to- are extremely tricky.

I took the class in Fall 2008. The 3 exams, which many people say are hard, are actually only made 30 % of your grade. 20 % are based on quizzes that you can repeat (hence you get 100 % grade for the quizzes), and 50 % from papers. So exam, although hard is not that important. The lecture is also not as important as the TEXTBOOK. Read the TEXTBOOK.

Brian Malley can be very innaproppriate in lecture.  I felt like he tried way too hard to be funny and crossed the line more than once.  He's not a very nice person, and he crafts his tests replete with trick questions just so he can say his class is hard, as though he's a great teacher.  I don't think he is.  I learned nothing in lecture.

I am so surprised by some of the claims here. I loved Dr. Malley!  Lectures were always interesting and he's a funny guy. Just read the book and go to lecture and you will be fine on the tests. I am NOT that smart and I got A's on every single one. It's not a blow off class, but if you study you'll be fine.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! i took this class and everybody talks about how psych 111 is an easy A of a class and it is. Not if you take Malley though as is was not only my hardest class but also the one i did the most work for. Take the class just with another professor. Test are impossible! Stay away!

Very good lecturer, definitely prepared and brings up interesting/debatable points on many if not all topics. Rather funny as well. First third of semester perfect lectures, a little unclear on certain topics in second and third--perhaps he doesn't like these topics as much. Tests are hard, and the class is relatively easy esp if you took AP pysch.

Dr Malley is by far the best freshman psych teacher available.  But his tests are tricky as hell.  You go in feeling very prepared and feel like you aced it when you turn it in, but after you get the grade back its so low you think something happened with the scantron machine.  be prepared to study a lot if you take this class

This class was difficult, but not unmanageable. You definitely need to read the book though. The tests are curved, and I think your grade depends more on the GSI you have. Mine was boring and unhelpful, and it definitely prevented me from enjoying the class.

I went into this class with really low expectations after several friends told me that Dr. Malley was a terrible teacher. They could NOT have been more wrong. Dr. Malley was enjoyable, interesting, and helpful at every turn. He used great visual aids and anecdotes to compliment the material. Just READ THE BOOK and go to lecture and you'll do fine.

Malley keeps lectures interesting with video clips and good examples in his powerpoints. He also posts lecture outlines online which is nice. His tests are tough because you can't just memorize the facts - you have to be able to apply the facts to real situations.

His exams have little to do with what he lectures on, it's all from the book. He is by far the hardest Psych111 prof. Try to schedule another professor for this course if possible. He tries to be funny all the time, it kind of gets old.
Such an amazing man.

This just illustrates how you can't believe what people say on this website. Malley was a terrific professor and I'm amazed that so many people found this class difficult and boring. I thought it was interesting, and not very hard at all. Maybe psych majors are just whiny. This class was great.

Yeah...this class was a HOT MESS. Boring, oh so Boring. It never gets better. The tests are crazy hard and he normally has to curve them because no one does well. Take at your own risk! But he is a nice guy.

He was a great lecturer, he tried to make it interesting with personal anecdotes and film clips.  Half the class depends on discussion section, so I didn't have much interaction with him.  Tests were DEFINITELY harder than in the other intro psych classes, but not impossible.  Read the book very well, take notes in class, and you're fine.

He is very smart and knows what he's talking about. However, I didn't find lectures to be interesting. Also, make sure you always do the readings because he gives quizzes and doesn't always give notice. Even though he is a tough grader, he grades on a curve. Only take if you are very interested in the topic and plan to do the reading
I learned a lot however his exams are difficult.  You have to be willing to reflect on the reading to do well on the exams.  However half your grade is based on section and the other on lecture.

A competent professor, Mr. Malley's lectures are about as interesting as intro psych can be, and the man himself has a decent sense of humor, greatly improving things.  His tests are harder than they seem: READ YOUR BOOK.  Further, it is necessary to serve a test subject in several psych experiments to pass: this is sometimes inconvenient.

I'm graduating soon, and when I took his 111 class I doubted whether Psych was right for me.  Not because it was hard, but because he made the lectures so dull and taught the class as though he truly did not want to be there.  I am glad the rest of the psych department is not like him.  Thank god.  Ps. He has trouble leaving his religious views out

Really interesting lectures. Assignments are pretty easy (no exams! no long papers!) & as long as you spell check them (since I've heard people getting  point deduction for spelling errors), you should be fine. Definitely a good psych elective to take.
WORST CLASS EVER. psych 111 is easy with any other teacher. stupid assignments and class is curved and can hurt your grade not improve it

I really enjoyed Brian's class.  The tests are pretty reasonable; they use a lot of material from lecture AND the book, so it helps to read and attend lecture.  He made lecture interesting and funny, which was refreshing.
i love brian malley
Awesome class, interesting lectures, keeps your interest, recommend

I enjoyed going to lecture, although it was unnecessary for success. Discussions are not useful. The book was fun and easy to understand, and VERY important to read, as most of the 4 tests were based solely on  the textbook material.  Overall a very interesting and fairly easy class with a good professor as long as you know to read the book.

He is an interesting professor, but his tests are fairly difficult. His tests often, cover a lot of textbook material he doesn't cover or review in class. But, if you do the readings - the class itself is not as difficult as it is made out to be.
Hard class, but possible to gat an A.
Easy and fun! Great teacher.
He is a good teacher and the people who say he is hard are probably illiterate or just trying to prevent you from taking a great class.

Definitely not an easy class, but not impossible either. His lectures are usually completely different from the textbook, so you definitely have to read and pay attention in class to do well. Malley is a good teacher, and the class is interesting, you just have to be willing to dedicate some time.

Malley is a really nice guy but for a 111 course, this was more difficult than expected. You need to go to lecture and do a ton of reading, but that will not garauntee you a good grade. His tests are hard even though the material is not challenging. It was more work than expected and compared to other Psych 111 classes, a lot harder too.

Malley is a very good lecturer and a funny guy in general. His tests are NOT that hard if you have half a brain and spend some time studying for them. If you don't want to study for your tests, don't take this class (or just go to State). Great professor.
I didnt like this class at all and did not think that malley was a good teacher.
His tests are very difficult.  He's a very nice guy though, and i thought it was sort of cool that he could use his own personal life as examples.

Very reading intensive class. Very active. Simply going to lecture is not going to cut it, and neither is simply reading the book. You've gotta read and go to lecture. The tests are hard, but you cover a lot of material. A good class, but not one for students who are lazy or have large course loads.

Well, I'm in psych 111 right now. Psychology in my opinion is very interesting. In this class, you are not guaranteed a passing grade just because you study.The exams are REDICULOUSLY HARD! there are only 4and they consist of 40 questions...Don't let that fool you. You just might want to drop him IMMEDIATELY ♥

I loved Malley's class. And it really isn't all that difficult if you're willing to spend some time reading and studying. It's VERY interesting, he's a great lecturer, and I learned more in one semester than the vast majority of other classes I've taken. If you're not going to whine about having to study a little, get Malley because he's great.
I really enjoyed this class. It was very interesting and Mally was a great professor. I only took this class because I needed more credits but afterwards I was very happy that I took the class.
Tests are hard, an he is extremely unclear at times. He's not good.

I thought this class was gonna be an easy A, but Malley's tests are surprisingly hard! For example on the first test he put a picture of the anatomy of the brain and made us label each of the parts. His lectures are absolutely worthless and usually have very little to do with the reading material.

Even as a second semester senior Psychology major, I think its safe to say that "Why do people belive in gods" is by far the worst class I've ever taken at the University of Michigan.  Brian Malley is a useless professor who attempts to teach a topic for which there is no research to support any part of it.  Its so unstructured hard to follow.
The whining is unnecessary.  Professor Malley is a good teacher and teaches the class very well.  The people who complain about his class are bitter that this wasn't a given A+.
He puts up an interesting lecture, but you have to know your stuff. He doesn't curve, but there is a good cushion with small online quizzes.

I don't know why people say he curves the grades, because he doesn't.  And it's definitely not impossible to get an A because I am.  I think people give him a bad grade because the expected psych111 to be extremely easy and then they're bitter when they find out they have to study.  Malley gives interesting lectures and I enjoyed the class.
Why anyone would intentionally take this class is beyond me. Learn from our mistakes. Take another professor for psych 111.  With anyone else, this class is easy... with Malley it is impossible.

Honestly, you do the reading and the class is not hard. I LOVE his lectures, hes extremely interesting, and has definitely got me to like psychology. People who didnt like him probably just didnt read.

Do not take this class.  I thought the class would be interesting but it was not at all.  It could be but Malley has a horrible way of presenting the material.  The assignments were useless (filling in the blanks on his notes, etc...) Lecture made sense, the readings made sense, but put together they made no sense.

I've gotten the impression that he wants his students to fail.  The class average on our first exam was a 62%, which he claimed was exactly where he wanted us to be.  He has turned me away from the subject of psychology.  Avoid taking him at all costs.

If you pay attention in lecture and skim the readings the exams are easy (at least in the summer section). He takes time to make hammer in the important points for the class and always answers questions fully.
He absolutely refuses to let anyone get a good grade in his class with his impossible exams and unfair curves, although he is a nice guy. Basically, avoid him at all costs when taking PSYCH 111.

This guy is an evangelical christian who doesn't beleive in evolution. to top it off, it is next to impossible to pull off better than a B in his class. his grading system is set up to scale the students from A to E with a middle-heavy distribution.  as he says "he uses the whole scale" meaning dont be suprised to get a 1 out of 10 on BS homework
Professor Malley has the ability to teach students a lot about psychology, but the difficulty of his exams immediately turns students off. Easy class to skip though...
He was very awkward and didn't grade very fairly.  Got me turned off of Psych for awhile.

Where to start? Who in their right mind sets the average for an INTRO, psychology, freshman class to a B-? Who, in their right mind, writes these tests with averages in the 60%? Malley needs to understand that this is NOT a science course, especially since he doesn't curve the class in any sort of beneficial way. He had potential, but he blew it.

Horrible teacher. Tests are ridiculous and do not reflect your studying time or knowledge whatsoever. He cares more about his precious normal distribution curve of grades more than you. DO.NOT.TAKE.THIS.CLASS.WITH.MALLEY. take schreyer or siefert instead.
Decent teacher, actually missed a few too many lectures. tests are impossibly hard based on how he teaches. do not take this class with malley

I studied for 20 hours for one of his exams and still didn't do well. The averages for his multiple choice exams are a little more than 50%... so don't expect to do well on the exams. You can do all you want to study but it won't help
Exams are ridiculously stupid. You can study all you want to, but you end up needing to know tiny little tidbits of information.

Professor Malley is a GREAT guy! He gave me a pet bunny at the end of the course. (Seriously, a real animal) But I was no kiss ass. The class was hard basically because you're competing with everyone else more than with yourself. ONLY TEN PERCENT GET A'S! So work hard, read the book, and go to lectures, and you're sure to do well.
His lectures are very well organized and interesting, but the exams are very hard.

The main problem I had with Malley was his exams.  They were far to difficult for the material we were being tested on, asking very particular questions on specific facts when he told us they only tested key concepts.  His class is really good, he's a good lecturer, and the material is interesting, its just those darn tests!
Malley's grading is ambiguous. Is unable to answer questions on the spot during lectures, surprising for someone who stresses on hard tests! Has missed lectures many times.

I think that Malley is extremely intelligent and interesting.  He did a great job teaching this upper level class. He is willing to put in extra effot to ensure that you succeed.  A job well done and not to mention that he's extremely funny.

Not a bad prof.  He is witty and humorous in lecture.  He really makes the hour go by fast.  His tests are on the hard side, so make sure to dtudy thoroughly before taking them.  I have heard great things about Schreier though, so if u can wait to take Psych till the winter, I would recommend her.

Though the class was VERY difficult and I hate the grading system, Malley was extremely interesting and I found lectures quite entertaining.  He is very passionate about psychology and presents material in an interesting way.

By far the worst class and professor I have ever taken in this University. Grading system is asinine, Exams are too hard for the class, and the lectures are a snore. Also: GSIs are terrible teachers and overwhelmed with the number of students.   STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!
Malley is a very nice person who obviously has passion for what he is teaching...however this class was incredibly difficult.

grades on a curve which i thought was gonna hurt my grade but it ended up helping it in a huge way...on the first test i got a 19/25 and it was the 4th highest grade in my section....tests are kinda annoying though cuz they dont really test on the material the right way...but since its compared to everyone else it works out ok

Horrible professor because of his grading system. He insists on having the class on a bell curve by discussion section. 30 ppl in a discussion- 3 A's, 3 A-'s, 15 in the B's, and 10 in the C's. It doesnt allow for equal oppurtunity. My friend in another section does a lot worse than me, but gets a higher grade? come on.

The curve really screws you over. It goes by discussion, which is even more ridiculous. He has a huge ego, and wants the students to know he is smarter than them. He teaches one thing, and tests something completely different.

Just a disaster of a class, the curve would be far more tolerable if it wasn't done by discussion section, far too strict a curve and there are no exceptions, even if he makes you think there are.  On day one if the others in your discussion class aren't stupid, drop it!
He has a huge ego, and wants the students to know he is smarter than them.  He teaches one thing, and tests something completely different.
Ridiculous grading curve for an introduction class.  Only a small percentage will get A's per section.

He teaches well but grades hard... you really have to learn psychology to the specifics to pass this class with a decent grade.  Only two people from each section is allowed to make an A because he bases his grades on a curve.
b-malley is the best teacher at the school. hes excited about the info, the tests are easy, and the info is cool
Horrible exams, only 25 questions on random stuff! Do not take Him!

The class is highly structured so you know exactly what to study, which is a good thing. The bad part is there was a ton of reading, plus the bell curve was very tough. In my class of 33, only 2 people got A's, with the next 4 including me getting A-'s. Discussion was worthless and youdo well in this class by memorizing the readings and lectures.

Excellent lecturer, provides ample detail and examples. Is willing to go on tangents and actually laugh at the funny things in the videos, but never misses a beat in the lecture and goes right back to the subject. Keeps the class fun and interesting. Discussion sections are what wreck the class, and his grading curve is somewhat ridiculous.

His new bell curve idea is horrible.  This an intro course, yet only three people in each discussion (about 30 people) are allowed to get an A.  The videos are interesting, but not worth ruining your GPA.  We had to write 4 papers. Take psych 111 with Schreier if you're looking for an interesting, easy A.

Good guy, great lecturer, somehow gone astray with testing and grading.  Made great material very obscure by trying not to reward memorization.  He's clearly extremely intelligent. If you want a real challenge, go for it - but if you care about your GPA, I'd wait a few iterations, because he can't articulate success and leaves it to the bell curve.
we had to write 5 papers up to 7 pages long, which is more than most english classes. the tests are hard and not lecture based and the bell curve by section is also ridiculous.
this class sucked. his grading system sucked too. it was based on percentages within discussions. top 10% got A's, so that was only 3 people. the exams were ridiculous and tricky. i hated this class.

I honestly don't get where anyone says he "should be handing out bibles"...etc. I'm an athetist and I didn't notice one hint of religious bias in this class anywhere... I guess some people get offended by his little cracks once in a while, but I like his sense of humor. Good class, well taught, but yeah the exams are inconsistent with teachings....

WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN.  There is absolutely no psychology involved.  Be warned, this is a religion class pretending to be a psych class.  Malley makes impossible tests and doesn't help outside of class (even in emails).  I was offended on a weekly basis.  He should be passing out bibles on a street corner, not teaching!!!!

the topic of this class could have been extremely interesting, but he does not really know how to teach what he is thinking. it wasnt hard to get a good grade if you always did the work and went to class. kind of a joke that it's an honors class next semester.
Very good lecturer. Entertaining and helpful. Makes the class interesting. Incorporates material to aspects of our lives that matter. Has a video of a whale being blown up with dynamite.

He is really unclear.  His exams are impossible because he tests you on how good you are at deciphering his tricky multiple choice, not on how well you know the information.  This class had so much potential, but i was really dissapointed.
He seems to be a nice guys but was very unclear in this class.  He tries not to have a religious bias but it does slip out every once and a while. Hard class.
hard. didnt enjoy the class. very difficult.
Dr. Malley is a good lecturer and keeps you awake and interested.  The tests are mostly off the study guide but are not a problem if you read the book.
Awesome professor, seems to relate everything to sex in his lectures.  Usually includes funny videos into his lectures.

Malley is a great teacher, conveys topics easily, altho sometimes the book is helpful for learning. posts notes before lectures. LOTS of extra credit offered (as of Fall 2004), and test require a solid knowledge of terms and how to apply them. Sniffy software is easy to use. One paper, doesn't account for huge % of grade. Very understanding prof.
Good teacher, friendly and funny, and does his best to make sure everyone understands.
very boring lectures

I was very interested in taking this class and thought it would be an easy A...I thought wrong.  The class was still interesting, but the tests are impossible!  They are so short, but cover so much material.  The tests are fair at all...very tricky questions!

This class could have been interesting if it wasn't such a small field and if he wasn't buddies with the 4 other ppl in the field. Readings were repetitive and crazy. But, he tries hard to help you out...plus 48 percent of the class gets an A. Sweeeet!
He's depressed and will always remind you about it.  You will be depressed too after sitting through his pointless lectures.

He is a good teacher and tried hard to keep the students engaged during the 1.5 hr lecture by mixing taking notes in with movies and other things. His notes were posted online so you didn't have to write down everything during class. Also, having an optional final was very very nice :)
No Comments

He emphasize some stuff during the lecture,but they will not be on the freaking test. His test are just random crap from nowhere, don't bother studying. If you get a****ty discussion class you can't get an A

I wasn't that interested in anthropology before, but Dr. Malley made it really fun and interesting. He really seemed to know what he was talking about and some of his jokes were actually enjoyable. He pretty much stuck to the lecture notes. For the exams, just pay attention to terms from the book.

What the hell is this guy doing? This was by far the most unprofessional and sloppy class I've ever taken!  This guy has no idea how to explain anything... only take this class if you enjoy memorizing useless jargon and learning between 0 and nothing in a semester...oh..just don't take it, save 3hrs
No Comments

This class is easy to do well in. Lectures are a waste of time. Malley speaks WAY too fast, its impossible to get any notes down, and he doesn't follow his own lecture notes very well. However, if you go to section, do the BS assignments and just read the textbook before tests, its cake.
This was his first time teaching this class, "why we believe in gods," and the course was awful.  All the paper work and quizzes, as well as what he taugh was very unclear...do not take this class.
Not a bad prof. Tests are harder than you might think based on lecture, but put in some honest study time and you'll do fine

I don't know what the other people here are talking about-- I thought this class was a piece of cake, provided you do the work and attend lectures.  Prof. Malley is interesting and even if you're uninterested in the subject, you will learn something.  If you like psych, take this course.
I did just as good on the exams in his class as I did in organic chemistry.  It was supposed to be a fun class, and an easy A or B, but not what this jackass pulled out of...his ass.
No Comments
The one hour lectures are pretty good. Not as boring as the 2 hour lectures might have been.

Professor Malley's becoming worse at teaching. He suddenly decided to take away power point presentation from the class web page. Can't pay attention to what he is saying, very stupid move. He might've been a good lecturer, but I can't know now, because all I do is write the whole time.
Lots of extra credit.  A lot of busy work and reading.  This class is all about the extra credit though.  If you do it all.. you'll be allright.
Lots of busy work ... dont bother doing the readings they are way to long.  Tests are tough but fair if you study.  Do the extra credits.  Class never lasts the full 2 hours.
I took Malley's first big Psych 111 class and it was obvious he was not used to teaching big classes. He was monotonous and boring. Plus, the amount of reading was outrageous.
A great teacher and a funny guy with a good sense of understanding.

This class was sooo boring I can't describe it. BUT Dr. Malley did a great job as a teacher. He gives a LOT of extra credit-so go to ALL classes and stay for the whole time. His exams are pretty hard so study as much as possible.
hated this class...luckily there was enough extra credit to get an A without trying.  Malley is not as cool as my roommates say.

Malley is a good guy, but this semester he has taken an approach that requires lots of computer homework that is totally pointless. Unless you want to feel like you're back in high school doing busywork and memorizing things for exams, don't take this class with him.Good for freshmen though.Not hard
The paper is a pain in the ass.  Good freshman class, otherwise kind of lame.
He's good

Great, funny guy. His 2 hour lecture ends usually after an hour or hour and a half. Make sure you come to lecture everyday and stay for the entire time. He gives out pop quizes and ex. credit that can really add up.
Malley's 2 hour lecture really only lasts an hour and a half at the most.  It flys by though.  Malley's a great lecturer, very funny, and shows awesome videos.  Don't miss the pop quizzes!
Brian Malley is HOT!!!
Cool dude

I'm a freshman and this has been the best class I have ever taken on campus. Malley makes the class interesting and enjoyable. Don't skip class because he gives pop quizzes, but those are easy. Gives extra credit and curves at the end. Take his class!
Excellent lecturer.  He was very interesting in class, personable, and very prepared.
Brian is great! He made the 500 person lecture so easy to deal with. the 2 hour lecture really only goes for an hour and 15 minutes, give or take... great teacher.

I like psychology to begin with but Professor Malley brought a lot of the material to life. His lectures had plenty of interesting stuff like quizzes and tests that mess with your eyes and both neat and hilarious movies. I enjoyed it thoroughly.
Brian made the 2 hour lecture fly by. class was fun because you could tell how much he loved what he was teaching, and that makes you want to love it too.
I love Brian Malley!
This was a great freshman class.  Big, fun, easy, with easy grading.  Brian teaches with incredible clarity, anyone can understand what he's saying.  I loved the course because Brian loved it.
Brian Malley is amazing
Great professor; very helpful.  Assigns research paper, however - watch out!  Well done lectures, however.  Worth every minute.

Dr. Byers gives really constructive, helpful feedback. Sometimes class can be a little boring but he does his best to keep students engaged. He gives so much creative freedom in the class and he really cares about his students.

Professor Byers teaches one of the most fun classes I've taken at Michigan. He really teaches you to write like a creative writer as he is a writer himself, and through reading great books along the way. It's a really engaging and well-taught class. It's not overly structured - prof. is very human, adjusting class along the way (in helpful ways).

WONDERFUL! I've had so many bad creative writing professors I've really considered dropping it. Prof. Byers is completely different. The class isn't just endless workshops & reading short stories for no reason. He really teaches how to write (by showing how others write) and is encouraging and helpful. Every Creative Writing subcon should have him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Michael was phenomenal. Had a great if incredibly intense reading list, reading quizzes on each book to check that everyone read. Led discussions really well but didn't always focus on the literary aspects, also focused on the larger picture or even sometimes the literary tools. Only 2 papers were fiction based on truth -- fun and different. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Horrible course - the grading is completely subjective and prompts are not clear. Do not take fiction into film, ESPECIALLY if you aren't an english major. Also, no communication between the professors, or between the professors and GSIs, which means you have no idea who your audience is going to be and can't get any reasonable help for the papers.
Really good professor. Cares a lot about his students.
Class was easy, but professor is arrogant and not very helpful.

Byers is funny, intelligent, quirky, and interesting.  He attempts to learn everyones name even though it's a decent sized lecture.  He's adorable in a geeky way, very helpful and has a stellar reading list.  He alludes to Star Wars almost every day.   An A is easily attainable if you do the readings.  Highly recommended course!

What a great professor! He's interesting, funny, and very intelligent. His class is fairly demanding with a heavy reading load, but it is not that difficult to get an A if you do the reading. Highly recommended!
Really nice guy, excellent teacher, superb reading list. He's funny as well.
Very nice guy and a good professor.  Also, it's an easy class and he's very open to meeting with people in office hours, etc.  Take a class with him if you get a chance.
Great prof! Knows what he is talking about, and is very interesting. If you ever get the chance to take a class with him, jump on it!

203 was a bit more challenging for me than coding courses because the math stuff doesn't really come naturally, but Chai made it enjoyable. His lectures are super engaging, and he always comes to class prepared, enthusiastic, and personable. He seems so genuinely excited to talk about math that I can't help but feel interested too.

I took this class FA25; all the EECS203 professors were amazing and very approachable. They clearly care deeply about their students. The course itself is pretty difficult since it isn't like any other math or coding class, but it is very interesting, and there is a lot of support in place.
Very chill guy, makes jokes at lecture. Gives a bunch of practice problems during lecture to help students practice.
Guy is engaging and knows what he is talking about and also super chill
Very engaging lectures; professor genuinely cares about his students. Class is very manageable if practice problems are done without cheating.

Intimidating at first, but building a relationship with her helps a lot. The class is feedback-heavy with detailed critiques on presentations, so you need to be open to improving. Compared to the other 101 professor, Dr. M pushes you to grow, and you'll leave a stronger presenter; you'll have to consistently put in effort to earn an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nice professor but kind of intimidating. The assignments were pretty straightforward, and she gave extra credit (DO ALL EC). However, after the first few assignments, her grading was very strict and left me wondering where I went wrong. I hate making presentations, and she scrutinized every single detail from content to formatting.
Is annoying

I honestly didn't have that much of an issue. She was nice and if u communicated with her she was helpful but she was pretty scary. Shes rly open to feedback and in general reasonable with a lot of EC some people can do. harsh grader on some stuff but def cares abt the students and wants u to like her lmao
Not worth taking this class with this professor. Get a different professor or don't take the class

Dr. M is a tough grader but cares very much about her students' wellbeing and success. The extra credit opportunities she provides are definitely crucial to do well in the class, so do them, especially because one of them is just attending office hours! She's a great mentor and although she is strict, I wouldn't hesitate to take 111 with her again.

She finds the smallest mistakes to mark you down for and will leave you scratching your head with her grading. The extra credit was the one redeeming quality about the class--do it or you'll actually fail. She leaves little room for error and tries to spur unhealthy, toxic competition amongst students. Take ANYONE but her for SM111.
She is a tough grader, and her grading rubric is very strict.
The most terrible professor I have met at Umich. Don't take her class if you have a better choice.
Very harsh grader and not accommodating at all for students. If you have the chance, just take another class or professor - not worth it.
take with whoever the other sm111 professor is. Not her

Professor Taylor is great! He is a really engaging lecturer and cares so much about his students. There are only three essays and participation, so the work load is very manageable. There is one group essay, but he gives you so much time to plan. We also usually get out class early which is really nice.

I loved Professor Taylor! He was super understanding in my opinion, as long as you communicated with him. Participation is super important! I feel bad when no one else participated or just sat on their tablet. He gives good feedback on papers, and I think really wants to help his students succeed.

Professor Taylor is the best lecturer I have ever had. He is so full of wisdom in terms of English, the professional world, and life in general. I would routinely leave his class inspired. Nice part about this class too, is you only have 3 papers the whole year. My knack against him is he is a pretty big grammar stickler when it comes to grading.

Dr. Taylor's class was great! Super easy humanities credit, and it was only graded by 3 papers, a discussion post, and participation points (100 points total for the class). There is one group paper which can be difficult if your group members don't cooperate. Other than that, he was very helpful, and I truly learned so much in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only had 3 papers, and as long as you go to office hours the grading isn't tough at all. There are participation points so attendance matters but there is little preparation for class. Some of the lessons are based on job cover letters and the basics of a grant, etc, so the class is more than only argument essays. Although very monotone voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor is very accessible outside of the class. If you go to his office hours, then your ultimate grade is going to be A because he read your whole paper before the due date, and then gives you reasonable feedback and suggestion to improve. I would highly recommend going to his office hours before any paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor was the best instructor Ive ever had! Hes very accessible outside of class and extremely understanding. I recommend going to office hours because he is super helpful!

Professor Taylor is such a good English teacher. He truly wants to see his students succeed and does everything he can to ensure that you become a better writer. I would definitely recommend taking any English classes with him!

Dr. Taylor is the kindest, funny, and caring person I've met. He has completely changed my perspective on the entire writing process. I highly recommend going to office hours with your essay drafts to get feedback before you submit. He really cares about improving your writing.

Charles Taylor has been by far one of the most understanding and genuine professor I've had. He truly cares about his students and makes sure the class topics are relevant to what is going on in the world. He's very accessible and helpful during office hours... really helps you build and organize your essays.

Dr. Taylor is my favorite professor at umich. He is a very down-to-earth guy and very knowledgable able all thing language arts. He is a paper guru. He made me fall in love with writing after teach me ways and strategies to do it to where it is an enjoyable thing rather than a burden. Highly recommend taking any of his courses, he wont disappoint.
Best English professor at U of M. Super helpful during office hours. He is also easy to find outside of OH. Meet with him frequently if you struggle with writing and you will get an A.
Kind of boring, but always willing to help

Charles is definitely a solid choice for Eng 225. Am not a very confident writer but he breaks down the essays and specifically tells you what he wants to see. Office hours are not super helpful but he is an interesting dude. 4 essays, with increasing weights.
Really enjoy him as both a professor and person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Tough Grader

reviews.comment: Professor Taylor has been the best teacher I have had at UM. Not only is he really nice, but he gives clear outlines, he's always available for help, and he has definitely helped me improve as a writer. He also never judged me for having views in class discussions that were... conservative. Love that guy!
Taylor is a really nice guy. The class is usually interesting and goes by quickly. 4 papers make up your grade as well as participation in class.

I took Dr. Taylor's ENG125 class prior to taking his 225, and it's a shame he doesn't teacher any higher English classes because he is the BEST teacher I've ever had. Beyond helpful, friendly, clear, and the best lecturer. TAKE HIS CLASS! :)
Professor Taylor's argumentation class really improved my writing! This class is not hard if you do the work and attend class, but simultaneously it's very interesting and informative!
Great professor! Interesting class. You won't regret taking it.

He is one of the best and easiest English teachers I have had. I used to HATE english and writing and after his class, he made it so simple.  I don't dread writing anymore and in the end I earned the best english grade I have ever recieved. I enjoyed his "controvesial" discussions he had us do too. They took up almost all class lol:)

Dr. Taylor is really nice, his class was very easy. we only had 3 graded papers throughout the semester and we had ample opportunity to get them drafted and looked over by our peers and by Dr. Taylor. we had discussions all the time and they were on news and recent events too, very controversial lol sometimes took all hour :)
Very easy class, gives you a lot of time to work on essays.  Nice guy and gives good instruction.

I really thought that Dr. Taylor was a helpful teacher. He didnt force you to come to office hours but he definitely encouraged them. Unlike some professors, he WANTED to help. Definitely take advantage of office hours and talking to him regulary even just to say hi

Dr. Taylor is by far the best professor I've had and mostly likely will ever have. He is extremely intelligent, but reaches students on a social and relatable level. Papers DO take a lot of time (if you want an 'A") but it is defintely worth the work. He does an excellent job of helping you to become a better writer, which will be benefical for yea

Taylor is awesome. Smart guy. Very knowledgeable about th subject. Go to him for office hours and he'll help you with you paper. If you do this he'll give you the higher of the two slashed grades on each paper.
He is a nice and easygoing guy. Papers assigned in this class aren't hard, but they are time-consuming. For papers, he is really picky about grammar, so proofread very carefully.

Dr. Taylor is my favorite professor at U of M. I wish I could take more of his classes. He is very clear on what he expects from you in assignments and is always willing to give extra help...go to his office hours. He is soft-spoken and not intimidating at all. He's THE BEST!
Dr. Taylor is one of the best professors I have had at Michigan. He is nice and very helpful-go to his office hours, it helps! I learned a lot from his class.

Dr. Taylor is one of the best professor's I've ever had at Michigan.  He knows a lot about the subject material as well as general knowledge.  The classes can drag on a little but you will leave being a better writer, guarenteed.  Strongly recommended for anyone.
No Comments
She seems to really care about her job and students but it just comes through as extra. It is nurs194...

Really nice lady and she definitely does care about her students. Class was super easy, clear rubric, easy grading.Only issue is that the 3 hour lecture was completely unnecessary. I would do hw or study during it (or sleep). She could've taught it in 1.5 hours or 1 hour 2x a week. Super draining, especially 1-4pm, just a terrible time slot mid day

Overall class content was very meaningful but the class was too long. Most of my time was spent sitting there doing nothing or doing other work. 3 hr lecture could be turned into 1 and a half hour class once a week.

Very tedious but EASY course. It all felt like busy work and lowkey common sense with an overarching theme that could be summed up with "don't be a bad person." I feel like the content is important but could be better taught with more engaging and fun activities. It sucks doing activities on stuff we were supposed to have already learned ourselves.

She was incredibly sweet kind, and always encouraged us to stay positive. Was very accommodating with asking for extensions and excused absences. The class however wasn't as engaging, could be very tedious and boring at times. I didn't really enjoy this class much, but no exams and if you did the work, you should do very well.
Professor Charania is very sweet and caring. She is very good about respect and reaching out to students. Her class is super easy but the content isn't very engaging.

Dr. Charania is one of the most caring and supportive professors you'll ever have. She puts a ton of effort into her lesson plans and powerpoints. She is also incredibly flexible and is super willing to work with you outside of class and provide extensions or accommodations if you need. She's just a lovely human being and a great instructor.

In a few words, Dr. Charania is an amazing, caring, and understanding professor and nursing faculty member. I had her for NURS 194 in an online course due to the pandemic, but even through a semester on screen her passion and care for her nursing students was evident. This class was not only straightforward, but the material taught is so important.

I loved having Dr. Charania; the class was three hours which sort of dragged sometimes, but she always tries to keep it interesting. The material also isn't hard to follow and she isn't a tough grader at all. I loved this class and her passion for the topic made this course one of my favorites.

This class is easy as long as you do all of the assignments. Nadia is so supportive and covers important topics. There were not any exams only 2 papers and weekly assignments that were not graded very harshly.
Her class was very inclusive and educational about diversity, equity, and inclusion. Dr. Charania was extremely welcoming towards her students and always made us smile.
Dr. Charania is super caring and overall great to have as a professor. Her class is pretty easy but covers a lot of super important and interesting topics. She is very understanding and flexible.

He is easily one of the best professors I've had so far. His classes are always engaging, even though they last 1 hour and 30 minutes. He often goes on tangents during lectures, but they are usually very entertaining.

Mr. Christman is the best English professor I have ever had. He is not a tough grader at all, you just need to participate and show that you tried. He will take into consideration your opinions and value them. It is clear that he loves what he does. I would 100% take him again.

Not hard to get a good grade as long as you try. The reading could be a little intense at first but will eventually chill out. He likes to expand on ideas that students bring to discussion, so a lot of what you learn depends on what you (and your class) bring up

He is a really nice professor, and you would get an A in this class if you show up and do the work. He isnt a tough grader. But do participate in the discussion in the class, you can discuss anything, and we will talk about it for 20 minutes. Overall, a really nice professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While Christman is passionate, fun, and dedicated, his courses are clearly very heavy? I'm not sure why many reviews are saying otherwise, but expect to do a lot of work, including reading a 200-page novel in a week (no exaggeration). I spent more time doing homework for this than any of my very difficult STEM courses. Great professor, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tends to ramble during lectures, but overall a fun and enjoyable professor! Content we read about was fairly interesting and assignments felt low pressure. Grade is heavily based on 3 papers and 2 participation grades, but he ensures that you know if you are headed in the wrong direction or not before receiving the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Christman initiates interesting conversation throughout the course. He cares about each student and their writing progress.

Professor Christman is a very nice guy and I really enjoyed his class overall. He does tend to go on long, sometimes confusing tangents during lectures but he's very funny and easy-going. Small weekly assignments and three papers throughout the semester. You will get an A as long as you show up to class and put thought into your papers.

Christman is a really nice guy, and putting in the smallest amount of effort will result in an A. Although they can get political, he often goes on funny tangents. He canceled a bunch of class in solidarity with the striking GSIs, but I don't think that will be repeated in future terms. Great and easy class to take for Creative Expression credits

Christman is a nice guy who genuinely cares.  Curses and is usually funny.  You will not learn a lot in this class; most of the time is spent talking about random topics.  He also brings politics into class and is very heavily biased when talking.  Most of grade is determined by 3 papers. Take for an easy A but not if you actually want to learn.

Christmas is definitely one of the coolest teachers I've had. He assigns a lot of work, but if you really put the time and effort into it, it pays off. He can also go on seemingly random rants in class, but they're usually quite entertaining and fun to be apart of. Would highly recommend the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: incredible prof, has engaging classes and creates fun and interesting discussions

Mr. C is prone to go on hilarious rants about random things. There are only three essays, which is not as many as I expected for an english class. He is accessible and lets you revise your essays to get a better grade after you first turn them in. His comments are clear and helpful. He cares for his students and made a point know each of us.

BEST professor I ever had!! TRULY cares for his students! Loved the discussions in the class and how great of a safe space it was. I truly do not like english and writing classes, but he made me actually enjoy it! I would take one of his classes again any day.
The best.

Christman is great. His lectures are so chill and the class is only graded on attendance and 3 papers. He helps you out so much with the papers so as long as you participate and do the work you'll get an A. He's also down to just talk about whatever and nobody had a bad word to say about him.

Because of the online teaching we meet weekly in small groups and discuss our work. The teaching method was very effective. Mr. Christmas is super helpful and passionate about literature and our creative works.

The best professor for English 125, definitely take his class if you can! The papers were pretty manageable, and he is super helpful to meet with. He went out of his way to talk to each student in our asynch class, and he was super nice about deadlines for Covid.

Definitely not an easy class to blow by. If you're interested on how to produce good papers or what being a writer is like, Mr. C has the answers for you. As a professor, he respects his students and is beyond hilarious! Very enjoyable class, even for a CS student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hands down, the best professor I've had. He gives very specific and helpful feedback, and very quickly too for all papers. His papers are also clear in instructions, and his grading isn't harsh so long as you put in the care and time. Beyond that, he's an amazing, hilarious, and caring person who takes his time to know his students.

Professor Christman is a very funny professor who genuinely cares about his students. Even in an asynchronous class, he put individual attention into each student to give us the best chance to succeed. The class itself is not easy; you have to write three tremendously long and complex essays, but Prof. Christman made this class manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Mr. C is the best professor at UM without a doubt. He gives great feedback on assignments and is incredibly quick to do so. I once submitted an essay and got comments within 5 minutes. The work is sometimes difficult to push through, but if you work with your assigned group and do your best on the essays Mr. C will take care of you and your grades.

Prof. Christman is great! Definitely take a class with him if you can. He genuinely cares about each student and gives helpful feedback on essays. His lectures are also both informative and entertaining. All around a good guy.

If Professor Christman is an option for ENG 125, sign up ASAP. You won't regret. Usual workload for a freshman English class with readings before each class session and 4 or 5 papers, but he is very clear with how he grades and spends time in class going over how to write and develop ideas. Hilarious and friendly professor. 10/10.

Overall a good teacher. Yet, compared with some other sections, he doesn't seem to provide that much about specific writing skills. Someone like this while I prefer more instructions. But in general a good choice.
Christman is amazing. He's funny and super relatable. A super chill professor and if you need an extension on a paper, you just have to ask. I would love to have him as a professor again!
Great prof. Very passionate. Also a socialist - would recommend the class but keep this bias in mind.
Phil Christman is an amazing professor. He's inspirational and consistently passionate about what he's teaching. He makes me want to not only be a better student but be a better person as well.

I had Mr. Christman for my first year writing requirement, and he is truly the greatest teacher. He helps you with class material and makes a point to get to know each student. Not to mention he is also hilarious and will meet you outside of class for just about anything. I highly recommend him for any class!

Mr. Christman is the most genuine and caring professor I have ever had. My class had only 8 students, so we got to know him very well. Unlike most other instructors, he genuinely wants to hear your thoughts and feelings on the readings he assigns, rather than just looking for certain 'correct' responses. DEF take his class if you have the chance.

If you're taking ENG 125, you can't go wrong with Mr. Christman. He is absolutely hilarious, and makes his class enjoyable, even if you aren't a literature person. The class is very straightforward and he clearly outlines his expectations of his students. Class attendance will help you out a lot with understanding the texts and writing papers.

Mr. Christman is one of the best professors I have ever had. He does assign some readings, but I honestly learned so much in his course. GO TO OFFICE HOURS and get to know him. He cares so much about his students and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Bonus, he is hilarious which makes his lectures way less boring than most profs.
A lot of reading (never did one of them). Extremely extremely extremely insightful and will improve your writing if you meet with him. Best teacher I've had at umich so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Christman is the bomb. Not a ton of homework, but you always learn from him and he's got some kick ass stories to tell. He respects his students and talks to you like an equal.

Phil is a great guy! He has a great sense of humor and is very approachable. I talked to him about all of my papers outside of class and he helped me a lot! Fair grader. All of the info is given in class so don't skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hands down my favorite teacher. He's such a great human being. His classes are always engaging, and they are ones that I always look forward too. Mr. Christman cares about a community. His classes aren't difficult at all, but I always learn something and I have grown as a writer in his class.

Mr. Christman was an amazing English teacher! You can tell he really loves his job and cares for all of his students. He is definitely there to help you but sometimes you can't be afraid to seek it out. There are a good amount of readings to do in this class which are all pretty difficult, but they become more clear in class discussion.

He's a great teacher because he loves what he does. If you're stuck on an assignment, do not hesitate to reach out! The readings are long and sometimes difficult, but he definitely helps you clarify the text in class. His roll questions at the beginning of class help you to get to know your classmates better and provides a more comfortable setting.
He is truly the great English professor. I recommend him to my friends. He is funny, accurate, clear and helpful.

Mr. Christman made me feel so much more confident in my writing. He gives awesome feedback on essays, but it isn't necessarily an easy A, you def have to read  (but the readings are really cool). DEFINITELY TAKE A CLASS WITH YOU. He absolutely rocks and your writing will improve immensely if you put the work into it!

Absolutely amazing teacher who keeps everyone in the class engaged. Creates an environment in which you are excited to receive feedback on your essays from him as his comments are top-notch. Although sometimes long, he assigns very eye-opening readings.

Unbelievable professor. Christman is down-to-earth, funny, and very open with his students. He genuinely cares about all his students and wants everyone to succeed in his class. Workload isn't overwhelming, and he is extremely helpful if you come into office hours. Very good teacher, but even more so, just a fantastic guy overall.

Christman is the best teacher I've had at this school so far. Such an awesome guy, you can literally tell him all your problems. Wasn't too interested in the subject but still enjoyed the class because of him. Super hilarious and really cares about his students. Fair grader. If you go to office hours he'll help you out so much.

Mr. Christman is the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are amazingly interesting, and the feedback he gives is extremely helpful. His teaching improved my own writing along with many others in my class so greatly, and I would recommend Paul Christman to anyone.

Mr. C is the best! I took his class to fulfill my first-year writing requirement. He's really funny and most of the class is spent with discussion. A few short papers at the beginning of the semester (easy) and then some longer essays (his grading isn't too hard for these, but you should def review & edit before turning in). Some vague essays.

Christman is the man. If you have a chance to take him for English it will be an enjoyable semester. Just be sure to get started on your papers ahead of time and edit them well. He is a stickler for grammar errors. Very willing to help you with your work and you'll get what you put into this class.
Best teacher I have ever had. Very interactive, hilarious, and friendly. His readings can sometimes be long, but they're really interesting and great reads.
This class was fun, easy to pass, and made me a better person!!

He is one of the funniest teachers. Gives great feedback and overall is a quirky guy with some very insightful opinions. He is great and he made me actually enjoy English again! There is a lot of reading but his papers make you think about yourself in a different way each time.
Hands down best professor I've had! Class is fun and interesting! Highly recommend!

Great professor! His teaching style is funny and engaging. It was also not really necessary to do the readings as long as you can still contribute to class by following the discussion and sharing your opinions (even if they are not directly related to readings). His essay topics are tough, but he is always willing to work with you to understand.

He is the best! Mr. Christman is as charismatic as they come, it is impossible not to like the guy. He keeps class both fun and educational. Workload isn't bad besides a couple long readings, and he isn't a tough grader at all. Definitely recommend!

Best English teacher I could've asked for! I wasn't looking forward to this class at all because I hate reading and writing but he made this class enjoyable. He's such a funny guy and he goes on random tangents and he'll always make you laugh. Class itself isn't that hard as long as you do the reading and put effort into the essays.
Awesome Professor!  He makes class exciting to come to and is a very reasonable grader who works with you on practically anything you want.  Definitely one of the best professors I have had here.

Mr.Christman is an awesome teacher! I was really not looking forward to taking an English class, but he made me enjoy it so much more than I thought I would. The readings are long, but interesting. You definitely need to come to class and put some effort into the essays, but the class is not very difficult. He is also very funny and a nice guy.

As long as you do the readings and participate, you'll do fine. He has been one of the best professors I've had in the two years I have been here. He actually changed my outlook in english literature.

Best English class I have ever taken! His section is on orality and literacy and he makes class very interesting. There isn't too much reading in the beginning, but you do read some longer stories such as the Iliad and Gilgamesh. Class is never boring though! Definitely the best professor I have had here!
Amazing professor! Extremely friendly, helpful, relatable, and interesting. He really encouraged me to do my best writing and essay prompts were fairly clear. Probably the best professor I've had.
A great guy and an interesting class! I definitely recommend.

He's a cool guy and his class is pretty chill. We read a lot of stuff by David Foster Wallace. He spends most of class time with an introduction where everyone contributes and it is usually pretty interesting and relevant to our current topic. He's a relatively easy grader as long as you put in the effort and come to class. Do the readings.

She gives everyone A, only her 'favorites' will get A+. She intentionally changed my marks from 10/10 to 0/10 after 1 month just so I could get an A as I wasn't her favorite student. I emailed her and she said she did it by mistake and that she will revert it but never did that. Everyone else gets A too, had I known that I wouldn't have put efforts

Overall a great class if you are an engineering grad student who needs a course to reach full time status, balance your course load, and boost your GPA. Attendance is graded, so don't plan on skipping class regularly. However, the lectures are interesting and worth attending. Easy A if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are amazing. She has so much experience being out in the corporate world, managing people and projects. Almost every lecture had an anecdote from her past work with a strong message. The group project and class blend really well. You actually apply what you learn from her lecture while working with your client.
A great lecturer! Definitely new to teaching but super knowledgable and ready to help her students.
maybe a great person, but not good at teaching. I also doubt he understands what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's quite famous for structure guy but NEVER for 481. I'm doubtful if he fully understands what he is teaching, as he often leaves the lecture to GSIs from Prof. Martins' lab. Seriously with Prof. Martins were teaching this semester as usual.

Cesnik was a great professor.  He really cared about the students, and that showed through.  Unfortunately I took it at 8:30 AM, so the students weren't terribly energetic which frustrated him, but he's super helpful and really wants you to learn.  Sure, it's challenging material, but work with him, and you can master it.
Very unclear and the lecture slides are unorganized. Prof Powell's notes are much better than his.
cares about students, still a  hard class
Good guy but pretty heinous class. He asks questions on exams that are way harder than we can be expected to complete in the given time. I was lucky to escape with an A-

Prof. Cesnik is one of the better profs I've had so far at Michigan.  He is a very likable guy and he knows the subject very well.  The class is not that difficult if you go to lecture and take good notes...the book is worthless so don't waste your money.
