If you're like myself and most people and can't stand structures, take this guy. He's probably the best possible structures prof. you can get, though it's not a very easy class by any means. Don't get the book, you won't need it. At least I didn't. He has pretty good notes, so unfortunately you can't miss his class.
She's soft-spoken and she is a really nice person.

In her first semester at Penn State, she surprised me with her course. I'm a senior in a 100 level French history elective, and her class was doable. If you come to class prepared, and engage in the class, its an easy A. No textbook required. Shes a soft spoken prof, and willing to help her students, you just have to be willing to put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall her class just bored me to tears. I was really interested to take a class about hipsters because its such an unconventional topic, but everything she talked about was so generic it made me not even want to do the work (which was way too heavy for a freshman seminar anyway).

Celis is a professor who is a little more soft spoken, but is knowledgeable about her subject.  Shes got a good sense of humor if you participate and engage in class.  Her grading is fair, but the work load is heavy, and she cares that you come prepared with the homework.  Overall, she made a subject I'm not crazy about pretty bearable.

Professor Schultz does a great job balancing the totality of Roman Monarchical and Republican History with fun and engaging lectures.  The course is extremely content-dense, but she manages to break it up into nice chunks that are supported by primary source readings. She also does a good job of making the course AI proof, so lectures are 100% req.

Professor Schultz is very knowledgeable and passionate about Roman History. She's witty and funny and takes a lot of time to answer questions when students ask them. As a history major I didn't find this class to be any worse than others for readings or lectures. Attendance is mandatory, but that's common. The only weakness is unclear grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: “They do a good job making it appealing on course guide” very true. A far cry from another Roman class I took at UM. Engr rqment to take a 300 level LAC course, but obviously you need a background on Rome and exemplary writing skills (gained in prior history courses) to do well in this class. 300 level + inadequate preparation don't mix.

Would highly not recommend (Roman history should be an easy, 10/10 fun and memorable class). Lectures were dull and unorganized. The grading is incredibly unclear as it is nearly 3/4 thru the semester without a sense on what is being looked for on essay/weekly responses, as well if you are on track for an A, A-, B+, etc.
Very engaging lectures, she is clearly passionate about the topics being taught which make her classes a treat
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Extremely dry course material which Professor Schultz did not make even slightly interesting. Roman Republic is NOT graded like an intro course. I was often confused by grading criteria and there was MUCH more work then there needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of written assignments, and grading is subjective, so definitely go to your GSI's office hours. Definitely pay attention more to the lecture itself than the slides; she often gets too caught up in lecture and the slides don't correlate to what she's saying. If you're not a strong writer, reconsider taking this class to fulfill any reqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was a massive disappointment (and I love the topic). So many tedious writing assignments and extremely pointless 20-minute timed essays. Discussion is useless. Very picky grading. Lectures are impossible to follow with essentially no slides and a copious amount of rambling. If you want to learn about Rome, take CLCIV 202 or HISTORY 201.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had her for CLCIV 302- Worst class of my academic career. She was the most boring lecturer of all time. Furthermore, she made us buy her expensive book to read from. The check-ins were worth 40% of the class and they were graded like they were the most important thing since Jesus. absolutely terrible. Readings were never ending. Never take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's a nice person, but the class was pretty rough. We had four 20-minute in-class essays. Her slides are AWFUL so if you don't show up, you won't understand anything. The slides have barely any words and she talks a ton. The final is key terms (there are hundreds given to us- impossible), a timeline, two essays, and a huge map all in two hours.
Refuses to investigate a college!!!

Professor Schultz is very passionate about what she teaches and her lectures are absolutely amazing. If you don't like to read or learn about Ancient Rome then you will not do well or enjoy this class at all. There's a lot of writing and reading involved but it's all very enjoyable if you're into this subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took CLCIV 376 (not listed as a course) and Professor Schultz was very wonderful at teaching it. Lectures are pretty much useless for papers and the final exam but attendence is mandatory for a grade. Overall a pretty fun course with a great professor!

Took this as my humanities credit cuz reviews made it seem easy. Lecture is mandatory and boring. She doesn't post slides, and does lots of talking. Vocab is an important part of this course, they look for very specific definitions and you can lose points for leaving one little detail out. Don't take unless you love Roman history and reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took CLCIV 302 for my required humanity for engineering. They do a good job making it sound appealing on course guide, but it's the most dull class I've experienced. Prof. Schultz tries very hard, but she puts kids to sleep in lecture (go to lectures; she does random attendance). Discussion is bleh too. (You dont need to buy the expensive textbook)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you are an engineer looking for a humanities class do not take this class unless you love the early roman republic and love reading. She assigns so much reading that if you want to get an A you need to spend time reading every day. You can pass without doing all the reading but probably will not get an A. So don't take this to boost your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Highlights: -5% of class grade reduced if you miss "spot-check" attendance -Grading based on ability to regurgitate exactly what she says in lecture (word for word) -Expects you to memorize an insane amount of information -Doesn't post slides I'm a student taking 18 academic credits and this 4 credit course was over half of the reading I had to do
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Strong contender for worst prof I've had at Michigan. Lectures were dull (even with the lukewarm humor; sacred chickens quips aren't enough to make the rest of the lectures worth it). The course isn't hard as long as you show up, do the readings, and are interested in Rome - it's just that taking the class is a genuinely disappointing experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Second time with Schultz, and it was even better than the first. Roman Religion is one of her main areas of study, so she was clearly very passionate about the materials in her lectures. Facilitated some fun discussion in the class, too. One of the best classes I've taken at U-M!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Schultz is an amazing professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject matter, and she definitely can hold your attention during lectures, although I would suggest you take this class if you're interested in the material. Otherwise, it might be difficult to follow. Overall, one of my favorite profs at U of M.

Lectures are very long and boring if you aren't specifically interested in the subject matter. There is a ton of reading that you actually need to do for discussion sections and because the midterm and final exam questions are directly about readings. There are 2 quizzes, 2 exams and 2 papers graded fairly easily.

Lectures seem long because she just stands on a podium and talks, hard to be engaged unless she gives funny stories. Class is very easy though (took for HU credit). 2 exams, 2 6 page papers graded very fairly. GSIs were great, read rough drafts provided good feedback. You learn a lot in this class and it is fairly easy, honestly very hard to fail.

History of the Roman Republic was a great course. Prof Schultz had great lectures (especially about the holy chickens) and the GSI Zach Hallock was great as well. There is quite a bit of reading involved, but the grading is very liberal and fair.
Extremely knowledgable about the Latin language and culture, Professor Schultz is an excellent teacher, and has a fun personality that makes translation and in-class work a pleasure.

Only take this class if you are very interested in the course. Don't take it to fill your humanities requirement. She's passionate about the subject but it's extremely boring. She's a pretty tough grader too and expects a lot from you for the class, very picky.
Awesome prof!

Great professor, lectures are interesting and purveyed in a conversational/informal style. Lecture slides only feature pictures, which she elaborates upon in a somewhat comedic fashion. I learned a vast amount from this class. Grade is based on 2 exams and 2 quizzes, which were very fairly graded. Highly recommended.

If you've seen the part of Ferris Bueller where the english teacher is boring the hell out of everyone in class- thats exactly what Celeste sounds like. I fell asleep in every lecture. You have to go to class to do well, but the readings are entirely unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you don't show up to class, it really impacts your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She seemed like an ok professor but she never really lectured. There was almost always a guest lecturer so we never knew what we were going to get during class. Some were interesting, some were boring. The exams aren't hard, as long as you study describing paintings with friends. The exam questions were all brand new, so there was nothing to review
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She has certain things expected from each student. When I went to her office hour to consult with my research paper, she gave many (not that helpful) resources. You have to figure out what she wants to see in your paper. This class was a small-size seminar type class held once a week so if you skip one, she will definitely notice.

Celeste rarely actually lectures in her own class, which seems pretty backwards. Frequent quest speakers and sometimes the quest speakers give no relevant information in their lectures. Nice person, but not an overwhelmingly good teacher. She's also obsessed with Dutch painters, so get ready to hear a lot about those.

463 is a great class. It's all about her specialty, Dutch art, and she really knows her stuff. I wasn't interested going in, but ended up loving it. The class is not offered all that often, take it when you get the chance.
She's a really nice lady but she is a bit of a boring lecturer. There is not much reading in the class, but the finals require a ton of memorization. Interesting subject matter though.
One of those Shaman Drum-only hippies.  Not terribly organized, but overall not bad.
She's an interesting lady - sometimes all over the place, but always has something interesting to say.  The course covered a lot of material though so studying for exams sucks.

Easily the best class I've taken here.  She's super nice and professional and intelligent and all of the course material was engaging.  She's also receptive to student feedback and actually seems to enjoy teaching unlike some of the profs at this university.

Professor Cech is AMAZING. Soc 447 has been the best class I have taken so far. She provided really interesting material in lecture that was different than I have gotten in most soc/women's studies classes. She is really nice and energetic. Reading material and attending class is a must because she doesn't post slides online. But totally worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sociology of Gender was my favorite class of the semester due to the interesting lectures and readings as well as Professor Cech's sunny disposition. Take a class with her if you can.

Professor Cech has opened my mind to so much in the course of Sociology/Women's Studies 447. She is very extremely intelligent, respectful, and professional. Her lectures are always organized and intriguing. I've been recommending this course to everyone. Honestly, this has been my favorite course so far, and I'm not a Soc or Women's Studies major.

First class in my THREE years here at UofM that I didn't get an A in. Obscenely detailed exams that are often almost criminally obscure. Instead of asking about the material of an article, she might instead ask where the author was born to "check if you read the article." Ceballo herself is a very pleasant character and cares for her students.

Really interesting course. She is really nice and makes lectures interesting. Essays are fun to write but she does grade harshly. Exams are very detail specific and tough. Definitely do the readings and go to class and take notes!!! But overall I do recommend the class(:

The readings are actually doable, though some are really long. Most are discussed in class. Memorize everything in the lectures and do the readings not discussed, and you'll get an A on the exams (which were pretty easy). She's a really nice person and is fun to talk to outside of class.

One of the hardest Psych class I've taken simply because Dr. Ceballo writes very detailed exams.  Although we don't have a textbook, she assigns a LOT of supplemental readings and expects you to memorize the details.  The exams questions are very specific regarding the assigned readings.

ridiculously bad teacher.  who teaches clinical psych when they're "not interested'' in the mentally ill (who she calls "severely disturbed").  tests were outrageously detail specific and difficult, but i don't feel like i learned much at the same time.  would NOT recommend this class!!!

I took this last semester and it was AWFUL.  She had no compassion for mentally ill patients and made that very clear.  Also, she is incredibly detail oriented in all the worst ways.  She basicallye xpects you to memorize details so long as they have no thing to do with anything else.  HORRIBLY BORING, also.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ACTUALLY LIKE CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY. She might as well be teaching counseling psych, calls people seeking mental health treatment "seriously disturbed" and puts questions on her exams about the color of M&M's in her story in class. Pointless, offensive, shouldn't be teaching clinical psychology.

This class was very detail specific.  Only really 3 grades count (2 exams and a movie paper) not much to help if you do bad on the first exam.  It's a small lecture class, although there is no attendence if you miss class, you miss a lot.  The book is important and takes a lot straight from the book.

Her exams are ridiculous.  She is really picky in details.  Also, the class has only 3 grades (total 150) which include 2 exams and 1 paper, all equally weighted.  The paper grading was very picky as well.

This class is pretty straightforward. Rosario is a good professor, not particularly exciting but not boring either. She likes to talk about her kids. Grade is two exams and a paper. Doesn't seem to have much clinical experience to draw on for examples, which kind of sucks. Overall a decent class.

Really boring lectures and no one attends, the lecture hall is practically empty. You can look up everything, but she put our last test online because everyone was cheating, she said. Easy class, but so boring, not worth it.

Quizzes are very confusing and often feel like guessing games rather than actually covering readings and material. When I sent emails I was ignored both times. I ended up very frustrated despite having prior knowledge and being passionate about the topic.

If you don't have prior knowledge of this topic, I don't think you will enjoy this class. Prior knowledge is often assumed. Reading quizzes are not fair (questions aren't over assigned reading often). She also doesn't respond to emails sometimes. She seems knowledgeable about the subject, but I am unsure if she really has a passion to teach.

Class was on the harder side but not bad. Lectures were interesting, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. Grades based on online reading quizzes that had nothing to do w/ what we learned, hard exams, easy discussions. However, she dropped 3 lowest quiz grades and curved final exam, so I think she does want whats best for her students!

Class is graded off 2 Exams, weekly quizzes, lab section attendance, and class attendance with exams weighing for only 30% of the grade. That being said the exams cover obscure material, weekly quizzes are often unrelated to the reading, lectures are telling not teaching, and discussion is a joke. Stay away from this class if you able to.

The exams were way too difficult for the class level and what she actually taught in lecture. Being open note helped, but they were still hard. You have to take a lot of notes. Labs were quick and easy. Homework was light and easy as well. Honestly would've been a very solid class had the exams not been too difficult. There was no final, thankfully

The professor was not very engaging and did not adequately teach what was on the test. There were two tests and although they were open book they they were confusing and featured the very specifics of topics that were glossed over in lecture. If you get this professor be prepared to take very thorough notes for the open book quizes.

The test are hard and rely heavily on the lecture notes, but aside from that the quizzes were hit or miss and the labs were easy.

The professor is easy to contact and takes feedback to improve their class.
Tests were difficult and some of the course material was unclear, but she was accessible outside of class. The labs were easy.

Readings were interesting, reflections were annoying. Feedback took a while to get back. Exams/final project had more components than expected & felt intimidating when introduced, but we were given sufficient prep. Participation matters & two group/partner projects (moderation, final project). Overall nice/understanding & communicative.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David is such a fun and clear professor. The class is very straight forward as long as you participate and do decent on the oral exams, you will do fine. I recommend taking spanish280 with David if you get the chance, and he is a very fair grader.

David is honestly one of the nicest guys a person will ever meet. He really cares about his students and make sure they are doing well. he is very young and relatable to his students. He is very accountable and trustworthy. He genuinely helps students when they are confused and class and makes taking this mandatory class for the major fun to take

I love Cathy Barry! I had her for drawing observation (option wasn't available in the drop down menu) and absolutely adored the class. She is very kind and her classes were always engaging and useful. Get ready to do a lot of nature drawing!

I am writing about Cathy as an Art & Design History discussion leader. She is very nice and caring. I managed to receive all 4/4 on my discussion posts, never got a bonus pts tho (might just be me). She will get visibly upset if no one speaks up, but she won't force you to speak if you don't raise your hand. She's probably the best discussion lead
She's a nice person. Her grading is fair. You should be glad if you have her.

Cathy is a wonderful art teacher. This is the first time I learned how to paint with watercolor and I will continue it for a lifetime. She teaches well, gives good feedback. There is hw due every Thurs. Cathy is kind and inspirational and I am thankful for that! You will have to buy art supplies though b/c the course fee does not cover everything.

Cathy is very sweet and very helpful. She is also fairly flexible on syllabus, I reflected my interest in painting outdoors for sceneries and she had adapted the syllabus based on students' suggestions. She gives useful feedback along the way and is very sweet. She encourages students of different levels to paint.

If you don't know something or make a film differently than her specific perspective and preferences, your grade will be affected. Talks disrespectfully to students and her classes are not structured or clear. I would never take a class with her again.

Ling seemed like a nice person, but you definitely don't want to get on her bad side or else your grade will suffer. I ended up doing well in the class, but she's just not super clear on what she expects from you.

Professor Hsu is extremely unclear about grades. There are no graded assignments. Your grade is based peer reviews from sets. It's a LOT of outside work and time commitment, you must show up whenever and wherever. Professor Hsu gives no instructions. She assumes you know everything she wants. If you disagree with her, she will punish your grade.

I love Ling (Carleen). I am 100% honest when I say that she is the best professor that I have EVER had here at the University of Michigan. As someone with an interest in production, she is transforming this department in the best way possible and giving us more opportunities. She will always be my first, best, and favorite mentor.

One of the best film professors Michigan has to offer! Will be a big critic but also an amazing supporter which is perfect for people finding their voice in creating film. Keeps students updated with canvas announcements which helps keep you on track. Take a class with her!

One of my favorite professors! She is incredibly smart and skilled, and has impressive knowledge and experience in film so she gives really meaningful feedback. She is personable and loves motivating students to grow and be their best. I appreciated how she made sure her class was a supportive environment for making mistakes and learning from them.

Carleen Hsu is an amazing professor and I honestly loved taking her class! She is very kind, respectful, and understanding of her students. I found all of her lectures interesting and I never felt overwhelmed by the workload. If you are thinking about taking her class I would highly recommend it!!

Catherine is so kind and really does want her students to succeed. She made learning German fun and was ready to help students inside and outside of class. Also, she is incredibly understanding. One of my favorite professors of all time!!

Nearly a decade later, this remains the only instructor at UMich I cannot recommend. A minor issue became a far larger situation than its substance warranted, escalating to involve multiple people instead of a simple direct conversation. The handling felt disproportionately severe and left me feeling out of place.
Super sweet and understanding. Very reasonable grader.

Fantastic professor. Helpful in every way and made a language class (which historically has been a hit or miss class for me) really really fun. Never felt behind even when I missed class because all you had to do was talk to her and she would happily catch us up.
Easily my favorite class this semester! Catherine was very friendly and easy to communicate with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class was difficult (high workload) but that's just how 232 is-- but Catherine was great! She's very understanding about absences/make-ups/etc. If you communicate with her about struggles you're having about anything class-related, she will do her absolute best to help/work with you. Very clearly cares a lot about the class + material.

Catherine is an AMAZING teacher! I had her for both German 102 & 232 and she made learning German so much fun! There is homework every night and module quizzes but that is normal. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She brings in different activities to make learning about wellness engaging. If you can, take her class!
Catherine is an amazing German professors. She provides great feedback and is very flexible with assignments. If you have the chance to take any German course with her, do it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Catherine is a fantastic professor! She taught my first German class at U of M and I could not have asked for a better professor. I learned a ton, but still had fun in a laidback class where I got to still practice my German almost every day. There are daily assignments and long-term assignments outside of class, but she cares about her students.

Catherine is one of my favorite professors at the university!  She is super nice and wants you to succeed.  You need to show up for class though, attendance is super important.  Most of the grading is completion, but the tests can be kind of tricky sometimes.  If you put effort in you should end up with an A or A-.  I cannot explain how nice she is
Best instructor I've ever had, did spanish in high school and hated and it and Catherine changed how I perceived language education
Catherine is an amazing professor! I encourage you to take German with her
UMich's German department is wonderful. Hartmut, the course coordinator, has a very interesting sense of humor. Catherine is extremely helpful and gives great feedback!

Catherine is an incredible professor. She was very kind and forgiving with grades and homework and she truly has a passion for helping her students. I would take every single semester of German with Catherine if I could.

Catherine is a fantastic teacher, coming from someone who doesn't particularly like foreign languages in the first place. The class is primarily taught in German, however at no point do you feel pressured or stupid. She is super friendly, a VERY generous grader, and an all around great experience! Absolutely take her if you can!

Catherine is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She is always very helpful and speaks slowly during class. She can always identify what you are having trouble with immediately. Highly recommend taking a class with her.

Catherine is the best! She's very flexible and connects with her students. She pays attention to the students' needs and always has a smile on her face. The textbook is very useful, as are the review sheets she provides for the exams. I wish I could have her next semester, too!

Catherine was a fantastic teacher. German 103 is a very fast paced class, but she made it very doable for us all. She's a pretty easy grader as long as you show a commitment to doing well in the class.
Catherine is a very passionate teacher and is willing to do all she can to help you with what you need. She makes class interesting and her homework assignments are not too difficult.

Absolutely fabulous! In HS Language was NOT my thing, but Catherine made the course so rewarding and wonderful.  She was so accessible and whenever I needed extra help or extra time for assignments I did not hesitate to ask.  I absolutely adore her! A real gem.
Easy professor. She's really nice, and flexible to a fault. I couldn't ask for a nicer or more helpful teacher. She grades easy, and not a lot is expected.

A very good language teacher. Helps you along the way, very friendly and always looking to help you move forward. Creates her own form of learning activities sometimes, very helpful and involving. Loved every minute of this class.

Catherine was so excited about German. She has much experience in this field. She is very easy to understand and very clear in her speaking. However, I did NOT like the way this class was run. All verbal teaching, not useful for people who need to write things down to learn! Review sheets for test VERY useful!

Basically teaches straight from the book. She used many activities right out of the book including a lot of interaction between classmates. Tests are basically the study sheet. This class was easier than high school German.

I loved this class.  All the films were interesting.  Catherine was super helpful and knowledgable.  She was always willing to answer questions or to clarify things.  She gives tests that are straight from her amazing study guides.  The film project at the end of the semester is really fun.  Take this class!

Catherine was absolutely great! The class was very clear and the activities were usually pretty fun/interesting. The tests were very easy because she provides a very good study guide for every test. She is also is very willing to help you at any time. Take a class with Catherine if you can!

Catherine is awesome! She is so nice and very accessible. You can email her whenever you want and she's very willing to help. She also lets you rewrite essays as many times as you want. She plans classes very well; there is never dull moment. Nicest, easiest professor ever. Definitely take her classes if you can.

Catherine is the bombbb! She is such a sweetheart. Her classes are really long (2 hrs) but oh well - they were really fun. We worked on dialogue skills a lot, which is really helpful. She is very approachable and she grades very fairly. Her tests are not hard at all; you always get the short answer and essay questions verbatim beforehand. Love her!
really nice, loved her job. grading was more then fair. the class was boring at times but what can you do?
Catherine is very helpful and also has a very kind personality. She's a great teacher.

Very nice woman and grading is straight forward.  Class is very long for the subject matter, we only watch a movie about once every 3 weeks, and the rest of the time we talk about the movie .  overall its a pretty repetitive and boring class, but she's a very nice and helpful woman.

She's a very enthusiastic teacher, and her grading is straight forward and more than fair. Still, her class periods often don't seem to boast your knowledge of test items; they tend to focus more on gaining dialogue skills.

BL510 has been the easiest class of my graduate school career. I have already used the skills learned in this class before graduating, it is useful for many aspects of life outside of BL. You CANNOT miss a single class or make up the in-class assignments. Make sure you can be at every class session or else drop the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ross should consider hiring a more 'in touch' professor. Content was remedial and could be taught by anyone with a J.D.
A true Gem of a course and professor!!!!!!

Professor Schipani was an incredible corporate governance professor.  She was one of the most knowledgable professors on actual subject mater I have ever had.  Would absolutely recommend any course with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Schipani presents herself in a very unprofessional manner. She is rude to her students, unhelpful, and fails to understand the hectic lifestyle of a college student. Highly recommend not taking a course with her.

he's the goat and i can't recommend him enough, he gives out candy every lecture and is super smart, he cares about his students a lot. participation and effort matter but just showing up and doing the reading is enough. LOVES his wife also
Great guy with enjoyable lectures, the workload was very reasonable, and I learned a lot from his class.

He is traditional, doesn't like phones and doesn't give homework because of AI. So grade is just participation (which is very important) and 2 exams. He is a great professor and will help you if you need. Also gives candy in class
The professor was great to be around and always hands out candy as well.

Professor Erdem really cares about his students and will force them to put in effort.  Some may see this as him being harsh, but he is such a funny and happy guy it is clear he does it from a place of passion. He can grade not harshly but accurately, and will deduct your grade for missing more than 1 class, but overall you learn a ton and want more

Erdem knows how to masterfully teach any topic with great enthusiasm and instill that enthusiasm in his students.  For the week on Ottoman farming systems he taught it with such interest and depth that everyone was super invested..  His exams are easy at face value, but he grades them to a high bar. No real homework, and readings are long but good.

He seemed strict at the beginning of the semester, but he cultivated a great classroom environment and brought sweet treats to class! He is an entertaining and funny lecturer and loves student questions. He wants students to succeed and is willing to meet with students before papers and exams! His class made me interested in Ottoman History!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely hated this class. While I expect history courses to be reading heavy he did not tie the material together at all. This would be fine if he was approachable in office hours or outside of class, and while he always says his door is open he is not open to conversation at all. Grades are arbitrarily given and he doesn't give good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor. Manages to find the (impossible for most) balance of being intellectually challenging without being brutally difficult. Coursework is stimulating and engaging, but never excessive. Great lecturer, and acts tough at the start but is a really reasonable, kind guy. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Erdem is great. He starts the semester acting tough, but he's actually super kind and generous. He does demand students' attention and time, but if you do your work, he'll do his. He makes the class enjoyable for both students who know nothing about the subject and students who already know a lot. If you need help in class, he's very accessible.

This is my favorite class I've ever taken. Without a doubt Erdem (as he prefers to be called) is the best professor I have had here at the University. The class is hard and he makes you work for it, but if you participate and pay attention  you can get a good grade. He wants his students to do well! I changed my schedule to take him next semester
One of the best professors in the department.

Here's a class with a ton of reading. Erdem (what he prefers to be called) was a pretty cool guy though with a fun accent to listen to. Unfortunately, I slept through most of his lectures but still did okay. Exams aren't too bad, but the papers you have to really try on.

He is extremely passionate about his subject. He made a dry topic like Turkish politics very interesting, especially for someone like who has had no background in Turkish history and politics. The readings assigned for this class were very challenging but interesting at the same time.
Love Professor Cipa! Great lecturer. Loves questions, even way off topic ones. Super helpful and engaging. He even brings you chocolate sometimes!

Erdem is awesome. I had basically no interest in Ottoman history before this class. Now, I want to learn more! Very easy going guy and will go out of his way to make sure you know what you need to know. Definitely would take another class with him.

Erdem is a great guy who is a master of Ottoman studies.  He often goes on tangents when lecturing, but overall the class is interesting because he throws a lot into each lecture.  He is a very easy grader, and reading isn't really required.  Great class to take if you are generally interested in the subject but want an easier three credit class.

Do not take this class if you are EXTREMELY interested in the subject. I did a mistake just by thinking that it would be fine and interesting. He is all over the place when explaining something, the accent doesn't help either. A funny and ambitious professor, but a very boring class if you 're not interested in the subject.
Great teacher, very willing to help out and is passionate about his class. Not too difficult if you do readings.  Definitively recommend him and his class for those interested in history.
Was a great class. He is extremely knowledgeable and it shows. Very engaging lecturer but sometimes can get off track. Overall a super teacher and a great guy.
Excellent teacher if you like History.
great guy, passionate about what he does. I would definitely take another of his classes

Great professor. He relates history to the present and clearly states his arguments. He provides outlines for historical events that he expects you to remember, and makes it fairly clear what he expects of you. Take if you truly like history.

Okay, but a very tangential and kind of infuriating lecturer.  It makes you really do the reading, but then it's hard to know what to concentrate on for papers and tests.  It's a pity because he's a decent person, but man.  My notes skip backwards and forwards twenty years in time in just two pages.

If you are interested in history and want have a good experience as freshmen at Umich, this class more than worths your attention. It's a discussion which consists of small number of people. Professor has a great understanding of what he is saying and brings it clearly to class. He is very helpful and has excellent sense of humor. Perfect teacher

Lustig is an educator for all the wrong reasons.  For what it's worth, when I expressed concern to my advisors, I was told that they are used to hearing complaints about her.  Do what that information as you will.  Avoid this mess if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This woman should be replaced.  Do not go to her for advice.

Dr. Lustig accused me of leaving class early/skipping because I asked too many questions in the online forum.   I've never been treated with such disrespect from a U of M professor.   I had perfect attendance and took notes diligently.  Take from that what you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Did not give grading rubric for discussion posts. Grades seemed to be randomly assigned for these. Test review sheets did not match what was being tested. Expected full participation from a class of 60 students. If you did not participate, you got no credit. Extra credit was for test prep team assignments that pitted students against each other.

One of my favorite professors I've had at the University of Michigan.  Material isn't particularly interesting, but Dr. Lustig is a really great lecturer.  Able to keep the class engaged and makes sure everyone understands each concept before moving on to the next.  Class consisted of two 300-word blog posts per week and 4 exams (non-cumulative)

I ended up being stuck with a first year seminar of hers: Cognition & the College Student. It was interesting but fairly common sense. We had reading quizzes everyday and easy reading guides that basically laid out the quizzes so they were fine. Lustig didn't really know how to teach freshmen so there were awkward moments but overall, easy class.

Hated the class, but loved the professor. If you go to lecture, pay attention, and do the readings, you can succeed in the class. Professor Lustig is always willing to help answer any questions you have and cares about her students a lot. Exams are all written (no multiple choice).

Professor Lustig is one of the best professors I've had at Michigan.  The class is hard, but if you attend lectures and keep up it's entirely possible to get an A.  Super SUPER helpful and willing to answer questions, provide feedback, etc.
she explains everything very thoroughly. Her exams are straight from her lectures and what she teaches. If you study you can pretty much get an A on every exam. She is very nice and willing to help.

Professor Lustig is excellent. In this graduate course, she put considerable effort into the reading list while also taking into account student preferences. Every aspect of the course is clearly thought out pedagogically, with the goal of helping us to become better scientists. She also gives personal advice and support to students in the course.

she's very helpful and cares how you do in the class. too bad there are pointless things like discussion posts (which are graded insanely hard). it's a 300-level class but you need to study for the tests since they are 75% of your grade. the only thing that upsets me is that i would have had a 4.0 this semester if it wasn't for this class

Most dedicated and devoted professor I have ever had. Wants each and every one of her students to succeed and takes a personal interest in them. Very sweet and helpful- she passed around candy during tests! As far as the material goes, couldn't be more boring.

Dr. Lustig is one of the few professors I've had who care if you do well or not.  She tries to incorporate material about learning into your learning---overall the class is not simple, but definitely doable.
I'm not even going to waste my time writing a description. I'll just say this: BLAH
She is really nice and really wants students to do well. Generally very helpful. It's not her fault that the material is extremely boring.

wouldn't be so bad if she engaged the class during lecture more. the material itself has the potential to be interesting, but the way she presents it completely takes away any interest that i might have otherwise had. the fill-in-the-blank notes have no purpose other than making you come to lecture.  bad readings, unenthusiastic; a waste of time.

she's VERY EASY!  multiple choice tests, straight from the lecture notes, you need to listen in lecture which is very boring.. but once you do! it'll pay off, you memorize the notes then you'll ACE the test! very easy A

the exams are reasonable, but the lecture is bad. She presents a lot of the more abstract concepts in a confusing way and shes not clear. the material is pretty interesting, but her lecures were not helpful to understand it.  she uses powerpoint and is not very interactive with the class.

She tries...she really does...but something's just not working. I agree with all of the comments below. The lectures are horribly mind-numbing, and while she tends to spend a lot of time on less relevent things, she also glosss over rather important concepts. I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

As mentioned, her lectures are painful (very) and she spends much too long on unecessary topics. Her approch to lecturing (reading right off her slides with little elaboration) is not condusive to learning and I would not recomend her to anyone. If you're going to take psych 240 please try to learn from another instructor.
Lectures can be pretty painful, she doesn't explain things very well and spends way too much time on stuff. Overall it's not all that bad I guess but it's definitely not a great class

She's vey boring and takes many long pauses when she lectures.  Sometimes she spends too long on topics that don't need that much explanation.  I like the material, but she makes me dislike the class.
The lectures get pretty boring - she's helpful if you ask her specific questions
Same as last comment.

Aging and Cognition was a great class, and Dr. Lustig always went out of her way to help students with their studying, work, and papers.  There's a lot of feedback throughout the course, which is extremely helpful.  She's a great prof, and is at the cutting edge of her field.

Other ratings are 20 years ago, hopefully newer ratings will not be removed. John's work is based on secondary research and case studies. He is shrewd, often unhelpful, needs external validation and decisions are not always based on work. Don't hold your breath if he promises your first publication as a graduate, protect your research.
Ford School's Finest

John is a genius in about every way possible. He is knowledgeable about everything, and also is very nice, helpful, and approachable. Definitely go to his office hours- sometimes he throws out some great summer internship suggestions.
Excellent credentials but very humble, highly perceptive but will not show it so be careful! Extremely kind.

To be honest, GREAT PROF. Makes the lectures relevant, and is VERY willing to meet with students and discuss real stuff (e.g. careers/internships/goals). Very personable and fair. Assignments are explained very well.

Prof. Ciorciari is a fantastic professor! His lectures are clear, comprehensive and quite entertaining. He's also very approachable and loves talking to students about their careers. He makes the class relevant to your interests. Assignments are not difficult at all - just make sure you attend lecture and take solid notes. Highly reccommend!
He chooses assignments that are relevant to the career field. He is very approachable and interesting, often engages the class in discussion.
Good class

Made class fun and interesting, lenient with deadlines, super caring, and always there to help when you need it. Cares a lot about his students and always open to talk. Best professor and def a good first year writing requirement to take if u have a heavy class load already.
really great overall teacher! super upbeat - not too much homework and genuinely cares about students :)!

Louis is great, he honestly made my semester so much better and is such a good professor when it comes to actually helping out students who need it. He didn't pressure us, due dates were flexible, as long as you put in effort and showed that you cared about/tried at the work he gives, you'll be great.

Super all around great guy. Really strives to hear your voice in your writing and encourages creative thinking in your work. You can tell he is genuinely passionate about his work and wants to see you succeed. I definitely recommend Louis for any student looking for a FYW professor.

The best professor I have had yet at UofM, so understanding and flexible and is very caring towards his students. He had meetings with students to help with their essay writing and always wanted his students to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Louis is incredibly caring, responsive, and understanding. He assigns a good amount of work but is not overbearing. I looked forward to going to his class twice a week because he was teaching it. Made a required class feel as enjoyable as possible.

I LOVE THIS MAN. he slays so hard. take a class with him if you can - he legitimately cares about his students and is passionate for his subject. Every class was a lot of fun, because he cultivated a good energy in the classroom. Don't worry about getting a poor grade because he gives very useful feedback and grades accordingly.

Louis is probably my favorite professor at umich. He was super caring and understanding of our situations and always generous with paper extensions. He is super friendly and easy to talk to as well. If you have the opportunity, take his class!

He is great. Take this class with him to improve your own skills before taking your first year writing. I hope to be in his class again in the future. He encouraged attending class and not skipping. Go and you will not regret it. Louis is there for all his students and supportive.

Louis is undoubtably the best teacher I've had at the University of Michigan. He challenges his students and truly cares about everyone's learning. Perhaps one of the most inspiring people I know. Highly recommend taking a class with him!!
I could write a really long blurb here about how amazing Louis was but I think I'll simply instead: this man changed my life. Take his class if you have the chance, you won't regret it.

Louis is a really involved teacher. He's very helpful, and will set up meeting outside of office hours. He will even push back deadlines. The assignments given are extremely easy, and you have way more than enough time to complete them. If you really need writing 100, I recommend him. However, it was an elementary class, so I'd just go to eng 1245

Take English 325 with Louis Cicciarelli. Louis's relaxed teaching style and funny personality are very conducive to learning. He made sure to take the time to get to know his students and frequently met with me outside of class.

Louis was a fantastic professor, and I really enjoyed this English class although I never really like writing papers. Very engaging and fun! He is very helpful in class and office hours, and really wanted to help all his students. I would definitely recommend Louis to others taking this class.
Louis was a cool professor, he really paid attention to his students. I would definitely take another class from him.

This is one of the few professors at this University I seek out. I am taking another class this coming semester specifically because he teaches it. Louis is incredibly invested in all of his students. I can't emphasize how much I appreciated his enthusiasm for not just the subject but also for the growth of the students in the class.

He is GREAT. Very helpful and he is a VERY funny guy. He really wants to help and will try to do so. He's so great that instead of requiring us to buy a textbook, he uploads the readings on CTools. Awesome professor. It is only my first year but he is certainly my favorite.

Louis has been the best professor I've ever had at this school.  Im on my third year and I haven't had a processor as engaging and helpful as him.  The only reason I had difficulty paying attention in his class was because I also had the biggest crush on him!!!!!!!
Louis is a great professor. He is a very friendly guy and brings a lot of enthusiasm to class. Highly recommended
Louis is awesome! Really cool guy that genuinely wants to see you become a better writer. Leaves great feedback on essays and gives students a lot of freedom when choosing topics.

Awesome teacher.  He does a great job at giving feedback on your papers, makes sure you will become a better writer, and the paper assignments/readings are great compared to similar courses.  Definitely take Louis, you won't regret it.
he gives great feedback on your essays, which is very helpful. he tries to make class fun and is a funny guy--definitely take his class
He's funny.
Coolest. Guy. Ever.

Absolutely great professor. I learned a ton about college writing, and improved so much. I highly recommend him, this class is very enjoyable, but you must do the work to get anything out of this class.

FABULOUS professor! Absolutely LOVED this course. Louis is extremely funny and very dedicated to his students. The last two assignments of the course were creative essays- something I haven't done since middle school and they were extremely fun to write. Not a lot of homework, readings were simple. No tests and only four essays. HIGHLY recommend!

He's a great guy! At first it seemed like he has favorites, but he's very friendly and will give anyone his time who wants it. Quirky and entertaining, laid back, and really easy going about deadlines

So I didn't actually have him as a prof., he just helped me at Sweetland for Eng 325. He's AWESOME though! He's so friendly and super, super helpful. Louis really helped me improve my essay. Next semester, I'm definitely going to try to take a class with him, he's great!

The writing assignments were clear yet broad, so any number of topics worked for them, which really added to the amount of creativity and personalization allowed. Louis is a riot, his grades are very fair, and he's always willing to help during office hours. I would absolutely recommend taking his class!

Louis is a great teacher. He is funny and spazzy and rambly (but it's always amusing). He enjoys discussion in his classes and encourages debates and conversation. He grades very fairly and is always honest, yet encouraging about your writing. I would defintely recommend him.

Louis pushes his students to go beyond their normal writting abilities and think outside the box. Expect to work your hardest, but in the end, it will be worth it! Louis was an excellent teacher and actually gave instruction on how to write rather than criticism.
Best teacher i've ever had. Was funny, smart and always made class fun. Very helpful and smart. Makes himself accesible to you outside of class. Awesome guy, great teacher. A++++++++
The guy is great.  He's fun, helpful and knows what he's doing.  Actually, he and I are friends outside the class.  Take anything with him.
amazing teacher - makes writing fun for those who don't like to write. He forces you to make improvements throughout the semester before he'll give you a better grade, though. So be prepared to work.
best teacher ever sooo funny he swears in class all the time...so helpful and so laid back take any class he teaches...was my favorite teacher ever
best teacher i've ever had. very laid back and lets students write to write - not worried about grades
He's the man, really funny and easygoing
One of the best here!
Fun and interesting teaching style.

It was a joy to be in class with Louis.  Very funny, keeps class fresh, is open to the whims of the class, and always keeps discussion focused.  His grading from the start of the semester implies that your better grades will come at the end of the semester, and sort of forces you to improve (which I don't think is really fair), but is effective.
he is funny and a little disorganized, but a good teacher.  He swears often, but in a funny way not offensive.
Hilarious. Strong Writer.
Louis is one of the best at U of M.  Wow, this class has REALLY improved my writing.  Take it!
Great teacher!  Louis is the man.  Likes the Browns.  His class was really great.

Louis is a fantastic teacher, and just an overall great guy. I hate school but this class was not only entertaining, but extremely beneficial to my writing. Very helpful, funny guy. I definately recommend this class.
Louis has the best sense of humor! Class was always entertaining and he made it a point to meet with students outside of class. He wanted to see improvement over the term from every student.
Great teacher....always willing to meet with you...funny....very engaging
Not a terrible class but definitely a bit disorganized, professor tends to talk a lot and talks down to students

If you're thinking of taking this class, don't. Pick another COMM class. This has been the most difficult and frustrating class I've taken in all of my 4 years at Umich. I'm a COMM major and was excited to learn in this class but the way the course is set up online is such a pain. Professor and GSI are really tough graders too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Dal Sin has been my favorite professor at umich. She genuinely cares that students understand the material and is super approachable. Her lectures can get a little bit monotonous but she tried to keep them interesting. Overall, she is a very kind person who wants students to succeed.

Take this as your capstone! You work with a team of students all semester to create a campaign surrounding a health issue of your choice. Learned marketing techniques and ways to overcome issues that you would encounter in the real world on an actual campaign. Room for creativity, interesting readings. Can finish majority of work during class!

Her exams are awful. She tests on specifics points in the readings (there are like 15 articles and 150 pgs of textbook readings for each exam) rather than overall main points. Worst part is she doesn't thing that anything is wrong. She thought a B- class average for the exam was "fine"... like what? That shouldn't happen for a 200 level class...

Terrible class but is easier than the other comm degree req classes... She's a terrible lecturer, literally reads off the slides. Going to lecture is not necessary because she posts the powerpoints online

This class was supposed to be about Mass Media and the Individual, but it really should be called "here memorize some random facts from a million journal articles". There is SO MUCH READING and exams are only on the journal articles. Fortunately there is a paper that takes a good chunk of your grade and the paper was easy, but the exams are awful

After reading past ratings, I was kind of excited to take this class because I thought it'd be fairly easy. This was not the case - grades were complete wild cards and her exams were written to cover  little details of the theories and not the overall big picture or theories themselves. The paper was fine but the exams were really disheartening
Definitely an above-average professor, is friendly and helpful and able to keep lecture interesting.

Professor Dal Cin finds happy mediums in all aspects of teaching: she is engaging and entertaining without being irritating, understanding without being too much of a pushover, and she made the class easy without being a blow-off. Dal Cin is much more concerned about whether or not you get the big picture than the obnoxious details. Great course.
Sonya was one of the best profs I have ever had.  She is really fun in class, VERY helpful, and really willing to meet and help students out of class.

Great teacher. She really knows what she's talking about and tries hard to make sure every student understands the material. Lots of reading for the class, however. Still, Dal Cin is entertaining and lectures were always interesting.

I really liked Prof. Crawford! The curriculum and grading scale are controlled by Ross so those being really bad aren't her fault, but she really tries to engage her students and make sure that they learn something. Showing up to office hours is definitely super important in this class, and make sure you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: go to office hours. youll get an a

Not a good professor. This class was somewhat useless, but it is in the core curriculum. Basically you have to be a favorite I guess. Even if you go to office hours to get help, she'll still give you median grade. The grading is so subjective it's not even funny. Also don't buy the textbook, we never used it.

The class structure is a disaster since you don't learn anything from lecture. All you do in class is working in a random team on worksheets for every class. The content is unnecessarily hard, take Math 214 if you can. (RIP stats major) Dan is a very nice guy, but as you see, I'm not sure how good he is at lecturing as he did not lecture in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cianci is a great professor in every way. He explains the concepts clearly and is always ready to help out the students during and after class. Taking his class feels so relaxed even though the concepts are challenging.

Prof. Cianci is an excellent professor and really helped me understand concepts of Linear Algebra. He has a very laid-back, relaxed manner of teaching that is conducive to learning in this class which is student inquiry-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 217 is a well-designed class, as discussions and collaboration between students help understanding the materials. Professor Cianci explained the materials clearly and made sure everyone understood. He also gave good hints when we were stuck on worksheet problems. You can never finish the worksheets though, because he will always give you new ones.

As for the course he taught (Math216), a lot was out of his control. Labs were awful and the exams were just an all-round struggle that made me genuinely sad, but that's not on him. Him as a lecturer was as good as we can ask for in a class like this, as in he really did all he could. He explains the material well and has enough office hours.
He was a very engaging professor and was even better outside of class. His office hours were very useful and helped me a lot in the course. I would definitely recommend him for Math 216.

Solid pick for 216 or other classes he teaches. Gives clear explanations and motivation for the use of new topics. Easily accessible both through email and office hours, and is happy to answer questions in class to ensure understanding. Labs suck, but that's out of his control. Definitely take 216 with him, or at least go to his lectures

Prof. Cianci is honestly the best math professor I've had at UofM. Even in a large lecture hall, he still manages to be engaging and informative. He doesn't have much control over the rest of the course structure (the labs are pretty bad) but you can tell he really cares about his students.

Very good at explaining material. Very helpful in office hours for homework and concepts and helps make you understand concepts better. Best professor to go to for office hours. Has a great personality and easy to talk to when asking for help with course material. Math 217 is a hard class, but he makes it much easier to understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took this freshman year in a 17-credit semester, expecting it to be really hard. It was hard, but also the high point amidst the other 13 credits. Lectures were engaging and the material was well-selected. Cindy is kind, knowledgeable, and a great teacher, gives good feedback on papers and willing to talk/help outside of class if you're struggling.

Incredible professor! She is extremely enthusiastic and her lectures are beautifully organized. With some attention and active engagement with readings, papers should be as fun as they are challenging (perhaps more). That said, there will be substantial engagement with religious themes, so if you're not into that you may not enjoy the class.

This class was really brilliant. Lectures were always a presented in an interesting way and generated a lot of good conversation. Cindy assigned three papers spaced fairly evenly throughout the course - never more than 7 pages, but usually 5.

Cindy is the best professor I've ever had. No question. She's a little quirky (typical for the RC) but her interests are vast and she is extremely knowledgable. If you're at all interested in anything she teaches, take the course. It'll change the way you think. I've taken courses I'm not interested in just to take another course with her.

Cindy is amazing. She's extremely knowledgeable and just too dang cute! RCHums (special topic in Freud) is easily one of the most interesting classes I've taken. The readings are not too hard and all of her lectures thoroughly explain any tricky concepts. I would HIGHLY recommend taking a course with her. She's very enthusiastic!
Cindy was a really wonderful professor. I enjoyed this class very much.

I took RCHUMS 318 and 372 with Cindy -- one of the most interesting and intellectual professors I've had at Michigan. If you are at all into literary theory and criticism, this class is for you. I also love the inclusion of art in her lectures. One of the smartest, coolest women I've had the pleasure to meet. I felt smarter after taking her class.

I was surprised to read a lot of the comments below because my experience with Cindy was entirely positive. She gave great feedback on papers (and IMO, graded fairly), was always engaging in class, and taught me about things I never thought I would learn (like castration and fetishism!). You won't regret taking a class with her; she's amazing.
INSPIRATIONAL

My experiences with her were absolutely HORRIBLE.  She was completely apathetic to the psychological difficulties I was experiencing during her class, and only exacerbated matters (she threatened to FAIL me).  The emails she sent to me contained an incredibly disrespectful tone - I cannot believe she is a professor...

Do not bother taking this class if you are not a religious person. You do not have to do the readings, but she is a terribly biased grader. She does has an extremely narrow view of history and philosophy. I was very disappointed.

She is a very helpful and entertaining professor. She is always willing to help with papers and making sure you understand the material. Her voice is very soothing and in this seminar the lights were often off to view paintings. These things combined sometimes made it hard not to be drowsy. However, she is a very engaging and interesting prof!
Prof. Sowers is very enthusiastic about what she teaches.  I had to take this course for my major, so I wasn't really interested in the subject material, but I did learn a lot.
No Comments

Professor Sowers is awesome!  She's very friendly and knows a lot about both Ancient Greek and Ancient Roman history.  She's so passionate about the subjects she teaches!  The reading load is high but the class has less paper-writing (only 3) than other humanities classes!  I strongly recommend it!!
Sally is a very soft spoken and kind professor who gives constructive feedback and is willing to help when needed.

Amazing professor, definitely my favorite from this semester. She is incredibly kind and helpful and will give you very useful feedback. Participation does matter in her grading process but as long as you participate in class, show effort, and generally just show up you are almost guaranteed a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My goat. Super sweet, can be a tough grader for some projects but nothing crazy. Super understanding and gives great critiques.
She was very well organized and helpful. We learned a solid amount of foundation but was still given plenty of creative freedom.

Sally was a fantastic professor. She is very methodical and organized in her teaching. There were only a couple of projects in the class, which made grading difficult, but she gave enough time for students to go back and make revisions if they were unhappy with a grade. Be prepared to work frequently outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sally is incredibly insightful, clear in her instructions, and kind. She has high expectations but also provides a lot of guidance and feedback, so expect to be pushed in her class!
loved
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she's a real one. sally my anchor. my rock. the one teacher i can consistently figure out what's going on in her class and how she's grading things. she serves

She was so kind and caring, it's impossible not to like her. Her instructions and expectations are clear and she's really understanding. Plus, most of her projects were pretty enjoyable. As someone who's not used to working in 3D, I think I learned a lot.

Sally was very well organized as a professor and has a wonderful teaching style. She knows when to push and when to pull back, and all of her assignments have clear goals that help you hone in your focus as an artist. I highly recommend taking SYS with her!

never did practice problems in class just expected you to know how to do them on your own. Just seemed like a research professor who wasn't really there to teach because they wanted to but because they had to.

While Professor Clack is a caring teacher and nice person, he is a bad professor. His lectures are just talking with fill-the-blank slides not suited for the style of thermo. You have to read the book to learn. He never seems prepared for class, even worse for exams. HW is assigned randomly and solutions/grading seem to have no rubric.

Professor Clack is very knowledgeable. The material can be challenging, especially with 8:30 a.m. lectures three times a week, but having lectures available online helped. I relied on the textbook and office hours, and the guided notes made the content easier to understand. The course takes effort, but Professor Clack is supportive throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Prepare to spend a lot of time with the problem sets. He expects students to work through the textbook on their own time. Lots of time needed for this class, but he does a decent job lecturing.

I personally found the course uninteresting but I don't think this was any fault of Dr. Clack. There was variety in the material presented and plenty of guest speakers to share different perspectives. Instructions and expectations were clear, and the workload was appropriately light for a 1-credit course.

He has fill-in-the-blank lecture slides. He doesn't have many examples in class. It is important to look at examples in the book and use textbook questions to practice. The homework sets are assigned at random. If you do badly on one of the quizzes, you can retake one of the quizzes during the final exam (quiz, not cumulative).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is tough. Professor Clack's style of teaching involves sending out lecture templates, then reading through the notes in class. He doesn't elaborate much on the topics beyond the slides or do many practice problems, so it can be difficult to learn at times. My best advice is to stay up to date on textbook readings and do tons of practice.
His lecture style can be hard to learn from because he doesn't give very many examples in class. However, he grades generously and has lots of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor. This was supposed to be a difficult class, but the exams and homework mostly didn't show that. The exams and homework are very textbook-reliant, so if it is like this semester, you could likely do really well off simply reading the book, but the lectures are a great supplement

Previous years the exams were really hard but this year (2016) he made them a lot easier. The average for the first exam was in the 80s and the second was in the 90s which is EXTREMELY high for a thermodynamics class. Not the greatest lecturer but all in all a good professor.

In lecture he mostly reads off the slides. Definitely read the book for this one. Office hours aren't very helpful (he usually confuses me) but he's a nice, smart guy. Sometimes he does flipped lectures, where you work on a single problem in class with your peers and the he'll discuss the solution. It was okay, but lectures could have been better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The guy is really smart, but he is terrible at explaining things.  His lectures are really hard to follow so you really have to read the book to understand anything.  Homework is confusing, and tests are really hard.  He also is very condescending and not easy to ask questions to- makes you feel bad if you don't understand.
You'll have to read the book. He provides fill in the blank lecture notes that are nice to review with once you understand the material, but to really learn you have to read the book.
Very hard to apply what is talked about in lecture to the homeworks and exams.
He's an extremely smart guy but he's not very good at explaining the topic clearly.  He really struggles to simplify anything, and his lectures can be very tough to follow.

He knows his stuff, but lectures are mostly theory with few problems showing how to actually apply the material. Exams are brutal, but usually the class average is so low that if you try, you can get an A or a B. You'll depend on the book a lot.

She is a not a good teacher. We teach ourselves everything, and then even when we know the material, the exams she makes are so abstract that it doesn't even matter. Just take a different semester.
3 weeks in. I should have dropped the class. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL NOT LEARN ANYTHING.

Just take the other semester. This is not worth it.

Clowney was a horrible lecturer and I barely comprehended anything during lecture. Your grade is mostly based off exams which are extremely hard given the amount of content. Clark is better in the second half but they both read off the slides without explaining that much. Be prepared to study a lot and make problem roulette your friend.

This course was the physical manifestation of a headache. The slides are literal essays, and yet Clowney spends about 15 seconds per slide. Nothing is explained clearly enough, and she assumes that students already have a respectable accumulation of biology knowledge, even though this is an introductory biology class :/

She knows her stuff but in incapable by every single measure of teaching a college course this big. She just reads off the slides and doesn't help actually explain tough concepts. My GSI in discussion tough every single topic much more thorough and clearer than she ever did the entire semester. Prof.Clark was a much better lecturer in the 2nd half.

I received below average scores on the first two exams, and above average on the two exams once we switched lecturers. She is a very intelligent and passionate professor, but just difficult to learn from. On a fun tangential note, she is very fashionable and I did love seeing her outfits over the course.

i tried to keep an open mind with prof clowney because she seemed like a nice lady, but i genuinely retained nothing from her lectures. everything i learned was self-taught. the exams were tough as well. do the problem roulette, that's the best i can offer you in terms of advice.

Genuinely one of the worst professors I've ever had. She never explained things clearly and made a 100-level course harder than it should've been.....I've had easier times in 300-level courses, which says a lot. Avoid this course if you can; if not, good luck. You'll need it
Her teaching style leaves me confused about almost every topic, but she's very nice and always willing to answer questions.

Horrible at explaining everything-- she is obviously very knowledgeable, but this makes her explain the topics in a way that is not realistic for a 100 level class. You have to teach yourself everything outside of lecture because the lectures were dense and incomprehensible. Would not recommend taking this in the winter semester when she teaches.

reviews.comment: No just no
If you didn't believe in God well start picking a religion and start praying because this class taught by this woman will make you question your existence as a student

Definitely the worst professor i've had here so far. If I hadn't taken my own notes outside of lectures, this class would have been a nightmare. Felt like a flipped classroom the way I had to teach myself. She knows biology, but she has little care in helping her students understand the content (which is pretty difficult for an intro level class).

If you haven't listened to these other reviews, PLEASE, PLEASE, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. I don't want you to endure what I and many others had to. Her lecture style is very difficult to understand, and she expects a lot out of you despite not thoroughly teaching the content.

She was a terrible professor, sooo much info covered in a terrible way, the exams were very difficult, she didn't know her own material and forgets she's teaching students who are new to bio. She is a bad lecturer and there's only a quiz each week so it's hard to get a lot of practice or get more points outside of exams. TAKE IN FALL W/O HER!

reviews.comment: Dr. Clowney is very nice, but her tests are an absolute nightmare, and you could put in 15 hours of studying and still do average. Attendance is mandatory via iClicker (has to be correct). The discussions are super easy. This is a class where you have to totally focus on the exams for days beforehand if you want to stand a chance of doing well.
Her tests are extremely difficult. I would recommend taking this class in the fall rather than the winter as it seems way easier.

While clearly passionate and intelligent, her teaching method is completely incomprehensible. She lectures as though every viewer is already as adept at she is in the field. In terms of learning/studying, you're on your own. I recommend doing the assigned optional readings and watching Youtube videos.
Doesn't act like she is teaching an intro class. She speeds through material like we already know what she is talking about and expects entirely too much from students especially in tests.

i went into this thinking this class would kill me because of all of the super dramatic reviews. IT IS NOT THAT BAD!!! i think people are going into this with preconceived notions, but she's fine, especially for the size and how much info there is. stop dogging on her and discouraging others!! there's plenty of study material it will be ok :)

Whatever you don't take it with Clowney and Clark, it's set up to tank your GPA. The first exam wasn't awful, but the second was. Doesn't really matter how much you study, you're set up to fail, the questions are almost nothing like previous exams and the short answer questions are hard to read. Take the class in the fall. Way easier.

Bio 172 content is hard, not Clowney's fault. However, Clowney completely fails to synthesize difficult material. Those who enjoy her class are those with significant Bio/chem prior knowledge. She speeds through content without explaining difficult topics. She fails to recognize when she has zoomed through a confusing concept. Awful awful teacher.

Dr. Clowney is clearly overqualified for this position. While I respect her as an academic, she doesn't seem to respect the students of this class for who they are - intro bio undergrads. reviews.comment: If you're thinking abt taking her class... don't. I've never been more consistently lost and confused in my life. Shes very smart but uses her PhD level vocab in an into bio class. I was honestly afraid to take this professor, but I'm glad I signed up for her course. Even though she is lecture heavy, her first exam was fair.
