reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

she is actually so horrific. do not take this class if she is teaching it. this class is like war. it is every man for himself out here.

reviews.comment: Dr. Clowney gets way too much hate, probably because some people can't handle anything beyond a simple Google search. If you were looking for an easy bio class, Washtenaw Community College is right down the street. But hey, you're at Michigan now—welcome to real college, not daycare.

The negative ratings are unfortunately true. Dr. Clowney is clearly passionate and an expert in her field. This makes the material hard to understand, and most students I have talked with find her to be incomprehensible. She has a teaching style that isn't suitable for this level of class, and clearly isn't willing to change. Disappointing.

She is the GOATTTTTTT. I failed the first exam for sure, but she has a great sense of humor. IDK why ppl say she teaches the class like it's upper level bio. She is just super smart. Cut her some slack.

I will admit she is very knowledgeable and I can tell she is passionate about biology, but she teaches us as if we have been learning biology for years. You literally cannot keep up with her in class, and she uses terms as if it's common knowledge. I had high hopes coming into this class and I'm not one to complain, but DO NOT take her class.

These ratings are not lying. She is very passionate about the content but is not fit to lecture an intro-level course. Required lecture attendance just means sitting there for 3hrs a week trying to follow along with Clowney. It sucks because she understands the content very well but has no clue how to teach it.

Run away from Bio172 with this professor as fast as you possibly can. The negative ratings here are not an exaggeration. As someone with a firm background in Biology, I warn you that she makes this class COMPLETELY inaccessible to students studying at an introductory level. "Weeder courses" are one thing, but this has been an absolute nightmare.

I went into this course with an open mind despite her previous reviews but found myself disappointed by her lectures. Josie is an awesome person and professor! She values everyone's input and our class was very collaborative. Clowney is such a good professor! She thought half of MCDB 422 with Collins and even though she is a little bit harder of a grader, her lectures are definitely a little better. She places a lot of emphasis on experimental design rather than just the results, which is unique and cool!

if i could pick one person to represent the human race to an alien population, i'd pick laura clapper. and the aliens would love us.

Laura is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students. W300 is self-graded, so as long as you work hard, you'll get an A. Laura has high expectations, but meeting them has significantly improved my writing.

reviews.comment: Love, love, LOVE Laura. Take any classes you can with her. One of the most genuine people I have ever met in my life. She is kind without being coddling, and both expects and truly wants the best from her students.

Laura is a wonderful professor, who really cares about her students. She will provide excellent feedback to help you improve your reading, writing, and analytical skills. It's important to participate and stay on top of assignments. If I could take her again, I would.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's the best after our 1st half semester professor. He's so caring, makes extra zoom office hours and is so clear in lectures. People aren't afraid to ask questions in a 500+ person lecture becuase of how approachable he is. Highly recommend. Thanks for saving us Dr. Clark!

Dr. Clark only teaches the 2nd half of the semester for this course, but he is WAY BETTER than Clowney! I wish he taught it the whole semester. He tends to go through slides quick, but he explains the concepts well and puts emphasis on the right things. Exams in the second half of the semester after he took over were easier and ran more smoothly.
Great -------

If you're an AP/Transfer starting at UM-AA on the fence about taking this class: know Prof. Clark is patient, passionate, very accessible, and truly an expert; his smaller class size makes iClicker, Study Groups, and Discussions easy points just for showing up—also allows for a personal connection. I honestly dont know anyone who regrets taking it!

Genuinely one of my favorite professors. He explained content really well and was passionate. His exams were usually accurate to the lectures. I also liked the way discussion was structured to not be overwhelming. He also gave a good amount of extra credit. Overall, as long as you understand the content (not just memorize), you'll be all good.

Nice guy overall, but the class itself it tough. He was much better than the first half of the semester's lecturer (Dr. Clowney), and was much more enthusiastic. He also explained some of the concepts clearer, but the exams were still really hard and meant to trick you most of the time. Wish I had him the entire semester for bio172.

This was my first real stem class at UofM, and Clark made it so much easier. He explained things pretty clearly and offered office hours over the weekend which was great. He also is incredibly dedicated to the students' success and not only taught us biology content, but how to succeed in a rigorous class.
prof clark is a very smart man who clearly cares about his students and biology. i liked his half of the semester the most by far.
He's better compared to Clowney. I've never been to his office hours, but he always says he's willing to help students in every way he can.

Clark is 10x better than Clowney who teaches the first half of the semester. Clark actually explains things in a way that is understandable. He does tend to rush through lectures and squeezes a ton of material in. But he recognizes that the material is difficult and actually respects and helps students. The exams are still pretty hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First half of 172 with Clowney is rough, but when Clark takes over it gets a bit more bearable. Recognizes weak areas within exams and addresses them in the following lectures to make sure everyone understands. Rushes a bit through his lectures but thats what you get in almost every intro-level bio class here 🤷.

In Bio 172 we started off with Clowney, who read right off the slides that were inconsistent with exam material- so far Clarks' slides are much more informative yet still straight forward- and he provides helpful insight to go along with the info on the slides; so far much better than Clowney.

I loved going to his lectures they were very interesting. There were times that I didn't understand certain concepts but when I went to office hours, he clarified things in a more comprehendible way. So long as you maintain solid study habits and persistently study, the exams should be relatively fair.

Clark gave great lectures. Put in the work and you will receive a good grade. Readings are not a must to succeed. Multiple extra credit opportunities. Exams are multiple choice but the wording can be difficult at times. Overall, the class was pretty solid and not that hard. Material can build up across lectures and units so make sure to study.

Professor Clark made this tough course manageable. His teaching style is clear, and he provides great study resources like practice exams. Definitely use unstuck ai alongside the textbook for effective prep.

One of the best STEM professors I have had at Umich. Dr. Clark makes himself available to meet with students in office hours, answer questions in + after class, and presents the material in a very digestible way. I wish he taught more upper level courses.

Overall by the end of the course it wasn't a bad but the beginning was definitely difficult, try to memorize the slides early and THEN do problem roulette and the practice exams which was something I eventually got into the groove of doing.

W24 curve for A-B range was 1%, C-D was 4%, nothing crazy but he said we had a lot of As already. Work hard!
I thought he explained the material well and was helpful when questions were asked!

I would avoid this class and professor at all costs. He told us after our third exam that the class would be heavily curved but would never tell us what the curve would be and wouldn't even give an idea of it. He then basically took back the curve after we took our final and only adjusted the grading scale by 1%. Disrespectful and condescending.
Solid class that was pretty interesting. Doesn't take a ton time outside class other than attending discussions, and the tests fair, not too hard.

While better than Clowney's, Clark's lectures were often somewhat difficult to follow. This course needs to be drastically reorganized to be more cohesive. I spoke with him a few times and felt that he had no respect for me as a student and often responded aggressively when I spoke to him about very trivial things.
Hones

Dunno how you'd fail his class cause he serves you everything on a silver platter.

The course itself is pretty dense, but he provides so many resources to practice the concepts and he's always available at office hours to ask questions. If you even try a little, you'll be fine :)

Amazing professor. For a tough course, his exams were pretty easy. He's passionate about what he teaches and is more than happy to help students understand a concept. Tells you exactly what to study and what not to study, no surprises on the exam, which saves us a lot of time during studying.
Prof. Clark held many office hours outside of class which is super helpful. He also records them too and posts them on Canvas. Super helpful and accommodating.

I always enjoy attending Steven Clark's lectures. He is passionate about what he is talking about, always takes questions and is respectful to students, and will go out of his way to help students understand the material. His office hours are very helpful and he often records and posts videos on canvas to clear up anything students are confused on.

Dr. Clark is one of my favorite professors at Umich. He is so passionate, caring, and interactive in his lectures. He does a great job of teaching tough concepts. If you love biology, he is the professor for you. The class can be tough, but if you pay attention, review slides, and attend lecture, he will give you everything you need for exams

He's very passionate about biology and his job, and it shows. Always happy to set up new office hours, all you have to do is ask. Exam questions can be worded weirdly, but as long as you interact with the content enough, you should be fine.
Very doable exams if you know the material. They are very straightforward. Great office hours. Overall very great professor. Do problem roulette and watch the lectures twice and you can pass easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clark was great. He was very clear during lectures about what information to expect and not expect on exams(makes studying a lot easier). The actual exams were wayy better than the Simmons exams and if you study the lectures and concepts, you can finish them in half the allotted exam time. He also had superrr helpful office hours, always available.

Lectures are easy to understand. Exams are majority of the grade, but not too hard to study for.  If you studied the lectures, problem roulette and the practice exams, then the real exams are not very hard. Also had a little bit of extra credit.
He talks so fast during lectures! He was asked to slow down numerous times but continued to talk fast. Not great at explaining things. Hard to keep up in his lectures. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super great lecturer, however his tests are very challenging. Always available for office hours. Don't expect any curve on the final grade.

Fellow transfer students, be ready for the hardest class you will ever take at UM. This is an ACCELERATED class which means the lectures will be going really really fast. Memorizing things will not save you but concept and mechanism will. On the first day, he told us that more than 40% of students get C in his class. SO good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Straightforward biology instructor that bases exams on material covered in lecture and discussion. Dr. Clark is clear and emphasizes important points during lecture. There are countless opportunities to get help and feedback from him. Dr. Clark is an exemplary example of a knowledgable and helpful professor. He is invested in his student's success.

Prof Clark definitely knows his material, it makes his lectures easy to follow (but 192 is acceled, so it's still a lot). Exams are difficult but not impossible. Readings are optional but helpful. Explains concepts very well 95% of the time. Definitely ask questions, he'll be able to answer them. Good prof but makes you work for your grade.

Clark is very knowledgeable on his teaching subjects. His office hours are very helpful and no one shows up so you can ask him whatever you want. His tests are HARD though, do as many practice problems as possible. Lectures can be a drag but barely any homework and gave us so much extra credit. Also, the class is curved at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Clark is great his office hours are very helpful, attend them as often as possible. The lectures themselves, despite being pre-recorded, weren't painful/boring to watch (relative to other lectures obviously this is no Oscar winning movie). I'm sure they'd be even better in person. And he was understanding of the difficulties of online learning

Dr. Clark was great for intro bio for transfers. His lectures have a lot of material, so it can be really beneficial to go through the slides again. He explains topics very clearly and checks to make sure students understand the concepts being taught.

Clark was a great lecturer! He breaks down content really well and his exam questions were straightforward if you studied. Make sure you keep up with lectures because it's easy to fall behind seeing as they're 3 times a week. Also, practice a lot with problem roulette.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: little clarity in what is to be expected from him contentwise. I never knew what my grade was because every week Id get a new email about how to recalculate the grade because the last method wasn't accurate. Was told that we'd get some kind of boost because of corona but I'm not sure if we ever did. Idk what my final % was. Gives confusing answers.
Professor Clark was very enthusiastic. He explained everything but it will be necessary to review afterwards because he goes fast. He is not boring so it is easy to pay attention in class.

Clark is friendly and really knows his stuff. He does talk pretty fast so it helps a lot to rewatch the lectures online after class. He's a pretty approachable guy and encourages students to come to office hours. I think the course content is pretty tough overall regardless of who teaches it.

I got a good grade, so my you can be sure my rating is irrespective of my performance. Clark is a bad lecturer. He moves very fast during lecture and does not do a thorough job of explaining the material. There is a reason why his ratings are lower than other bio 172 professors. Professors don't get low ratings for no reason - think about it.

Prof. Clark cares deeply about students' success. He's VERY helpful during office hours, and he's very accessible outside class. His PowerPoints have all the info you need to know. Exam questions are sometimes a bit confusing, you really need to understand concepts, but very doable. Great professor. Petra, the GSI, extremely helpful. Great class.

Dr. Clark is a pretty decent guy. We went through material pretty quickly but he was very open to helping people outside of class. Some of his exam questions are a bit questionable but hes a nice enough professor and clearly cares about the lecture material.

This class is AWFUL. Clark himself isn't actually awful but he goes fast and you almost never know what is actually going to be on the test. If you can avoid this class, do it. The tests are extremely hard and the discussions are completely useless.

Bio 172 is an awful class to begin with, but if you can, avoid taking it with Clark at all costs. Simmons taught the first half of the course, and while i didn't do great, once clark started teaching my exam grades dropped over 30%. He's lazy, and SO unhelpful when you reach out to tell him you're struggling. 0/5 would NOT recommend

Bio 172 is no doubt one of the hardest classes at this university. Lectures are extremely compacted, however Clark does a good job of explaining through things and even pauses to check if students have questions. Definitely rewatch all the lectures to solidify your knowledge.

Like many  said, he goes way too fast over the material in lec and expects you to comprehend his complex thinking/explanations the first time he says it and then apply it to the very next side. Not only does he speak fast but does not explain well and his only method of explaining, if he does, is giving complex examples that will confuse you more
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although 172 is a hard class no matter who you take it with, Clark does a good job of being accessible in office hours to explain anything you need. He comes off a little intimidating at first, but if you go to his office hours he's willing to help you with even the most basic concepts. Exams were hard but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Clark was a great professor for my BIO192 course. Although exams were difficult at times if you rewatch his lectures online you will do fine on them. Also, attend discussion for this course and study group meetings as they are extremely beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Since it's class meant to weed people out of biology it does just that. The exams are quite hard, especially the multiple choice, and since they are the majority of the grade in the class if you don't figure out how to do well on them you won't get a good grade. Also, he talks really fast during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Clark talked way too fast during lecture... nothing can be understood while he tries to explain in class. Rewatching lectures are helpful, yes, but his tests are way too difficult for an intro bio class. Studied a week in advance and basically memorized the slides but he would still ask questions about one tiny box on one slide.

While I do agree that Professor Clark moved a bit quickly at times, I think this is a very doable class. If you answer all the course concepts at the end of the packets, you'll be fine. I studied for like 3 days before all of the exams. Clark is also super accessible outside of class and always adds extra office hour times if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Clark moves very quickly, and I cried when he talked about putting mice in a blender, but truthfully if you rewatch all the lectures before the exam, you can get 100%. It is a large time commitment, but he explains everything clearly and the exams are specific to material from lecture so do not get carried away with the textbook, it won't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Clark is decent. The class itself is hell and would not recommend it to a single person. Clark goes through lecture extremely fast and sometimes adds extra, non-essential information to slides that adds to my confusion. However, he seems very passionate about his job, but the exams are brutal and cramming is definitely not effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Clark goes extremely fast during lecture. He goes over important, big concepts very quickly and expects you to pick up on it. You have to rewatch the lectures and memorize legit every slide in order to do well, but getting a B is doable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Steven is a really good professor. He's on point about everything. Cut clear in lecture, nice to talk to out of lectures. I think he really cares about being a good teacher.

Clark isn't the best, but how you do in this class isn't dependent on the professors.  Memorize every word of the notes and you are golden.  Do not read the book, it is a waste of time.  Show up to the necessary amount of lectures to get full points, take a few notes (not 100% necessary), then cram in the 48 hours before the exam.

Prof. Clark is very smart, and he really knows his stuff, however, he goes over huge topics too quickly and unless you pay very close attention or re-watch the lectures you will not be prepared for his exam questions. He asks extremely detailed questions and tries to trick you on most of the questions so make sure you know EVERYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Clark's good during lecture! He's much less monotone than people claim. It's outside of lecture where I have a problem. He's very rude to students asking concept questions on piazza. He'll answer with things like "that's a good question" and "rewatch the last three lectures." He's very unapproachable during office hours. And, his exams are harder.
Clark was not a very good professor, very monotone and doesnt explain stuff in a way that is easy to understand. His exams contain information not in the lecture notes so it can be hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I cut Dr. Clark some slack: he has to teach very conceptually challenging concepts.  With that being said, Dr. Clark struggles to provide the basic framework to understand these difficult concepts.  He's obviously very knowledgable but he goes way too quickly through lectures without reinforcing much of the material.

Don't understand the hatred. Not a super easy class but possible to get somewhere in A range, especially with curve. Go to lecture and discussion for easy points. Rewatch the lectures the day of and continually go over lecture notes and eventually you'll get the concepts and won't need to look over older Powerpoints anymore. Join an SLC group.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was not clear about hard topics. Was not approachable and rude to students. Could have explained topics much better. Goes too fast just to get through material. Not a good lecturer and cannot keep students attention. Did not enjoy this class when he taught it.

I don't understand why he has such low ratings. In my opinion, Clark is a great teacher who does a great job of explaining difficult concepts clearly. Yeah the average on exam 3 was a 68 but apparently the high population of freshman and greeks in this class makes students unable to understand what a curve means.
Beware when taking his class. He goes over the notes very quickly and will add a lot of supplementary information while lecturing.

Don't let this class intimidate you, and don't freak when you read the negative reviews. My boy Steve will constantly preach about how you have to focus more on applying concepts rather than memorizing stuff. Just memorize all of the stuffs. Everything is from lecture slides and discussion. Know it all and enjoy your A.

Clark is awful. His lectures are confusing and the average on exam 3 was a 68%! That does not happen in this class. SLC study group leaders for this class say they never have seen an exam score this low in their three years of being a study group leader. AVOID!!!!!

He taught the course for the second half, and I really think 90% of the people in the class have no recollection of what he taught. He runs through huge concepts and honestly makes no sense. The average on his exam was a 68! A 68! Unheard of in an intro class. Just to top it all off, he didn't get an ovation on the last day of class. Avoid. AVOID.

Bio 173 with Clark was okay. This class is tough. The exams are hard and the lectures are sometimes confusing because he gives more information than you really need to know. Keep up with the lecture/learning objective questions and you should do okay. He knows his stuff and is always there to help.

Bio 172 is a hard class and you just have to study for the weeder. Dr. Clark is really smart and sometimes is hard to follow, but he keeps lectures engaging by asking questions. He pulls a lot from the lectures for his exams, so BlueReview and go over his slides. He's a really nice guy if you go to his office hours or meet with him individually.

Professor Clark's lectures are slightly confusing and he tends to over-explain to the point of it being confusing. He gives extra credit questions on exams, however, and he's available for help if needed. If you work hard, it should be fine.

Dr. Clark does move though the material rather quickly but if you pay attention in class and write down what he says it will make sense later. He does a great job of answering difficult questions on piazza too!
Extremely vague and boring lecturer. Goes deep into irrelevant examples, so much so that you cannot learn any of the basic fundamentals from his lectures. Avoid if you can.

Class and exams were manageable if you actually study the lectures and really pay attention to detail. Some questions will be based off of one slide so it was kind of dumb. Clark is pretty rude on Piaaza, on email, and sometimes in person. He expects more out of the students before lecture and goes very fast during lecture. Boo
He's not that bad. Go over all the slides carefully and you'll be fine.

He's a very smart guy who really does care about helping his students learn.  He's very friendly and helpful; however, his lecture slides are very confusing and can seem to complicate a simple concept.  If you can clarify the lecture slides in your own time, you'll d well in the class.  His tests surprisingly weren't too difficult.

Overall, he's a hard professor, but a good teacher. He takes time in every lecture to answer students' questions. He also tries to explain things in a way that everyone will understand. The only problem with this is that sometimes it's hard to follow all the examples and different wording he uses. He seems to truly care about students' though.

He is not a good professor. He rushes over important slides and asks questions during lectures that nobody knows the answer to. I studied a lot for it and still didn't get the grade I deserved because his exams are meant to test your ability to pick up on the trick he makes up instead of the actual knowledge of the material.

Steve literally draws all over the slides; he underlines every single word and circles random things. I hate going to this lecture because his scribbling drives me insane. He is not clear and his exams are hard too.

Reads directly off the lecture slides. Expects you to come to class having already learned the vocabulary. VERY unclear when differentiating between pathways and processes; powerpoints have no structure. Learned everything from the book and my GSI.

Dr. Clark wasn't the worst professor I've ever had, but he was a bit confusing at times. He treated the material on genes as though the class already had a grasp on the subject, which as intro bio students many did not. Other than the exam on genes, exam 3, I didn't think this class was too difficult. Read the book and you'll be fine.

He is an EXTREMELY boring lecturer, to the point where it's almost painful to watch. Also, he is rude at office hours, and responds rudely to emails and Piazza questions. You are obviously on his time. He seems nice when he's in front of the class. Expect tricky exam questions, especially short answer questions, that barely coincide with lecture.

Unlike Amy Chang, you actually have to pay attention in class. He may be a good teacher, but for those days when you are super tired and want to sleep, he is a pain in the ass. SO ACTUALLY for the lazy ppl, which are all of us, he is worse than Amy Chang. Great guy but too good for his own good.

Stephen Clark is an interesting lecturer, he does a good job at varying tone and asking if anyone needs clarification. He does tend to go over complicated ideas very quickly. I found his exams difficult because many/most of the points come from multiple choice so no partial credit is given for those portions.

Dr. Clark is helpful in office hours, but he speaks quickly during his lectures. He teaches very quickly and can be hard to follow. If you can manage to pay attention, you should do fine. However, the class was very boring.

Devastatingly awful. I cannot find anyone worse than him. What he talks about is inconsistance and doesn't make any sense. He tried to put a variety of materials, but he cannot illustrate any one clear. There's no reason we should go to his class since we can only depend on GSI and the textbook. However, he forces student to use iclicker.

Not the most exciting guy. Didn't seem very eager to help. I learned mostly from the book and my GSI. The information is actually interesting... it shouldn't be as painful as he makes it. Possibly the worst professor I've had at Michigan.

His lectures have blanks, which is kind of annoying, because sometimes even if you are present and paying attention you miss one and have to figure it out later. His exams are not nearly as difficult as you might expect, though, as long as you study a ton.
I would recommend not taking this class with Clark. His lectures are super boring, he has an annoying voice, and he gives off an arrogant, hard to ask questions to vibe.
He knows his stuff, but his lectures were super boring. Fell asleep in all of them I think. Exams were pretty difficult for me.
Not crystal clear but his exams were pretty simple and fair. Go to lecture, take notes, and study. Not too bad at all
Attendance is mandatory, nothing spectacular, but is a fine professor. His exams weren't too hard, pretty easy class.

Clark is very boring, especially in the morning. He forces lecture attendance with iClicker, which was super annoying. Also, he does not make concepts very clear and appears not to be very interested in what he teaches.

Dr. Clark was an alright professor. His exams were fair. The course required a lot of studying in order to do well, but that's expected. He tried to make everything clear and was very helpful. Go to lecture because of the notes were fill in the blanks and he uses quizdom.
A ok professor. If you study his slides and read the book, you'll be fine.  I would recommend going to the class because he uses quizdom...otherwise the lectures are pretty boring.

Clark is easy to understand and his lecture slides are easy to follow and include fill ins to keep your attention. Lecture is mandatory because he takes all test Q's directly from the slides. Reading the book is not necessary but worked very well for me (I had no previous Bio experience). Take his class its really not  bad if you attend lecture.

Professor Clark is very well spoken.  His exams are based off of his lectures and quizdom questions during lectures document your attendance - so go!  Expect to do a lot of memorizing, just like any other LSA class.  Biology in general isn't easy unless you have some prior knowledge about the subject so make sure you skim the book before lectures.
Great Lecturer. Very engaging to his students. Answers any questions asked during lecture. Extremely willing to help outside of class.
clark is very precise, and crystal clear.  his lectures are MANDATORY.  his exams are often difficult and require lecture attendance.  pay attention, go to lecture, you will get an A.

the worst class ever. he just reads off the lecture slides which are basically copied from the book. exams are really hard and very specific. class is not curved. plus my GSI's quizzes were really hard.
He drones rather than lectures. I could barely keep awake. Read the book, honestly ..even if you do put yourself throught the boredom of lecture, just read it.
I'm not sure what made him so bad, but he was. just didn't appeal to my learning style. also his in class notes were often very unclear and occasionally incorrect. Very annoying.
Boring lecturer.  The only reason to continue coming to lecture is that his lecture notes are "fill in the blanks".  His exams (the first two) are somewhat easy, though.
Clear lecture notes, straightforward exams, enthusiastic about subject matter.

He made it impossible to acheive anything other than an "average" score. Practice tests were a joke, and review was 2 minutes at the end of lecture, when people were leaving and inturrupting. When people had questions during lecture, he would point to the same bullet over and over on a slide. We know how to read, we want you to explain!!

kind of monotone and boring, but he gets to the point. he reads directly from the notes he posts online, which have blanks. says the info on the exam is only based on lectures, but if you want to do really good on exams you need to read the book. not the best at answering questions in class, sometimes seems he is just rewording the lecture notes

I disagree with most of these ratings.  He wasn't the most helpful or interesting professor I've ever had, but he got the information across.  If you attend lecture and read the book the tests aren't bad at all.  Don't expect him to spoon-feed you all the information, but this is a college course... and not a very difficult one.

I agree with all of the comments before mine. Clark is a terrible lecturer who teaches an intro class as though it was part of a masters program. He contradcits himself and riddles tests with trick questions. If you want to pass i wouldn't suggest taking Intro Bio with Clark until you've already obtained a degree in Biology through other profs.

Clark is the worst professor I've ever had. He shows no excitement at all in regards to the material he teaches which makes the already boring material impossible to digest. He has too many slides per lecture and NEVER gets through them all and tries to rush through the final slides in time for class to end. Get out while you still can!!!

let's just say this is a great "intro to bio" course if you somehow already have an extensive biology background...or a remarkable ability to memorize huge amounts of information.  i went to the lectures to fill in the blanks on the lecture notes, then headed home to spead hours picking through the text.
He refused to answer ANY emails, you could only see him during specific office hours, and he wasn't very easy to understand.

He comes off as pompous and arrogant. He uses overheads instead of powerpoint and can be very confusing. His text book selection is unhelpful for the material he covers, but he seems to expect you to learn a great deal of the information outside of class. He is also not helpful for personal requests and his email responses are often slow at best.

If you know the coursepack problems, you probably can understand 65% of the test questions.  Otherwise , it seems that he chooses obscure items from lectures, which he never explained well in the first place.  Still, he wasn't as condescending as the other prof.

He is a terrible teacher, and his exams don't reflect what he teaches in class, but instead they show his arrogance.  You could be doing very well in the first half of the course, but then cut your grade in half the moment he starts teaching.

Does not seem to want to be in the class.  Does not know what he is talking about a lot (tried to draw the nitrogen bases that comprise DNA and failed miserably).  Misspeaks too often to discount it, has terrible handwriting but insists on using overheads and not powerpoint.  Exams were written to confuse not to test knowledge...there's more...
My only comment is this:  Multiple choice A thru J
This professor made it obvious that he did not want to be in class and did not care to help the students in any way.  Tests do not accurately represent your knowledge of the material.
Clark knows nothing about what he is trying to teach, molecular genetics.  He doesn't even know the difference between a ester and a ether.
definitely do the course pack problems and the exam will be much easier, but don't wait 'til the last minute - - you'll never getthem all done...
he was clear in lecture, and a good teacher, but his exams are very hard.

Professor Clark does a great job teaching - his lectures are clear, accurate and precise.  Study for the exams and learn to enjoy genetics and you'll do fine.  Eat a kilogram of salt if you don't like it!

While Clark is fine at lecturing and giving out notes on his projector, there is simply a gap between him and the students. As the other comments say, the result is unclear tests and unsolved questions which only seek to harm the achievement of students in genetics.

Professor Clark tries to be a good professor but there are a couple of problems related to his inability to communicate. The result? A coursepack of questions that make little sense, test questions worded so that they could be asking two different questions, and lectures that often don't make sense.
He uses a projector with transparencies, instead of power point presentations, which I found helpful, because it was easier to keep up with his notes in class.
Very clear at explaining things, exams aren't to bad as long as you're good at multiple choice.

I thought he was an excellent lecturer, who explained the material very clearly, and was very helpful if you went to his office hours. The class is NOT as hard as people say, I promise - just learn from the notes and you'll do fine!
No Comments
really difficult. really.

I learn the information, but the tests are impossible and are not an accurate representation of showing what you know. Some days he is very helpful, other days deadly boring. A decent class, but again, the exams are very bad and the curve poorly set.
Clark teaches intro to genetics. The exams are structured very poorly, and you HAVE to go to lecture, else you will fail. The readings do not help with the exams.

She is really passionate about what she teaches but struggled to connect with students and get them to participate in the class I had. Even so, she always tried her best. Know that she is a slow grader. Would not necessarily recommend.

- Never graded anything on time. 
- Lectures were boring 
- Accessible outside of class and lenient on deadlines

Professor Creed is so incredibly nice. She really cares about her students. There's a bit of group work with peer edits. Overall the class was pretty easy with only three essays and very little other work.

Claudia was a decent lecturer but struggled to engage the class at times. Her one-on-one conferences often lacked clarity, with repeated points filling time rather than offering useful feedback. Her biggest issue was grading delays—waiting six weeks for feedback made it difficult for students who wanted to do redrafts.

Decent lecturer. Lots of reading, but it's not THAT deep. Lenient on midnight deadlines which was helpful. Fair grader. Lots of writing (bc it's a writing class), but she's super reasonable and understanding. I was a little scared after reading the single rating on this website, but she's super fair, which is all someone could ask for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I literally made an account just because I want other english 125 students to try and get a different professor. Tries to discuss but does a terrible job at engaging with the class, and we all just sit there in silence. Nothing is graded on time so you literally don't know how you are doing in the class until the end. Kinda need to read
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
(EARTH 351) I learned a TON but the class is a train wreck

-Blames the class for being behind but doesn't make assignments on time
-Labs are HARD AF
-Rude to students in class
-Class order is poor
-Homework is convoluted
-Lectures are FAST, must attend to do well
-Thorough compression REQUIRED for exam

Clearly well respeced, but horrible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Marin typifies the very driven/intelligent but also entitled ivy-league-educated academic. When things are not done exactly her way she is RUDE, sometimes boarding on abusive. She tends to be controlling and micromanaging. She lives in an internally generated bubble of constant stress that very few are immune to getting caught up in.
Marin is an excellent professor. She cares about student learning, and is very knowledgeable about her field. Would highly recommend!

Marin writes her lecture notes on the board although she does uses powerpoint slides every now and then, so you have ample opportunity to interrupt her to ask questions.  She has a very practical approach in teaching Geophysics, you will get to learn relevant instruments and softwares used in the field.

She's really nice and is very passionate about her work. It's annoying that this class is only two credits because you have to study a fair amount to get an A on the exam. If you put in the studying hours, you will get an A.
Marin is a good professor. She is very clear and easy to follow. She seems nervous and tense most of the time. Do not get on her bad side though, she can be really tough.
Do not take Geophysics with Marin. Extremely boring and difficult. She is not very helpful when you ask questions either. I did fine in the class, but it was one of the worst I took at Michigan.

Marin is an awesome professor. She presents material in a very organized manner hence her lecture is very easy to follow. Test questions are tricky, makes you think, but that also makes you apply what you learn which is the best way to remember academic stuff.

Interesting class. Only 2 credits, but she doesn't use the textbook anymore (no readings). Your grade is based solely off the 3 test scores and EC for going to class. Class is only an hour long and she is pretty good at explaining things.  Go to class if you aren't a Geosci major. Easy 2 creds if you go to class.
If you have no prior knowledge of the subject don't take her class! She is hard and thinks everyone should know everything that she knows
Marin Clark is a good teacher and is an expert in her field. She can be cold and mean at times but does her job well.

This is a 2 credit class...and it was one of my worst grades. Not clear about what will be on the exam and exams are extremely hard! I received Cs on two of the three exams and an A on the one when she was absent and we were taught by another prof.  Def dont take this class unless you wanna feel dumb for not doing will in a 2 credit course
Terrible class, never take it
Professor Clark is quite the skilled geologist..and she's a cutie pie.

This class is much harder than expected, especially for a 2 credit course.VERY detailed answers are needed on quizzes/exams, and not all of them were well explained in lecture, or in the book. Prof Clark tries though, and you can tell. Perhaps being new she just doesn't know the ropes yet.Overall ok course, but I wouldn't recommend it.

Professor Clark seems very nervous at times, and she has difficulty explaining the material.  The quizzes and exams cover material that is not well explained in lecture and cannot be found in the textbook.  Therefore, it is tough to answer some of the questions on the various assignments.  Overall, I do not recommend taking this class.
She just started, and was a little shaky at first, but you can really tell she wants to make things as interesting as possible for her students. She has a real passion for the subject.

Prof. Crane seems to have a solid amount of experience and knows what she's talking about but as a grader and teacher she's almost impressively unhelpful, she graded harshly based off of having a self-admitted bad night and provided no practical feedback as a result. Don't take her if you want to learn, take her if you want to listen to her talk.

Yes, Colleen Crane is knowledgeable about assessment, and I learned a lot. However, I would have rather stayed home. I hated attending this class, and it should have been my favorite. Collen was rude and condescending, grilling students about clients and judging us for not knowing enough. She would be the least encouraging therapist ever

There aren't too many assignments in this course and some are worth a lot of points. She makes clear her expectations for these assignments so if you try, you will be graded fairly and graciously. Colleen is extremely knowledgable and I think that was what I enjoyed most about her as a professor. I would absolutely take her course again.
Most frustrating thing ever. Lecture heavy and boring. Assignments are graded harshly even when she says she will go "easy". Take another professor honestly, it'll save you a lot of stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most boring class ever. Lectures never ending, all she does is talk the whole time. No break out groups to discuss in smaller groups, no activities, nothing. Just lecture. Would not recommend taking her if you get bored easily. Too much information in each lecture, none retained at end of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great but get ready for tough grading.

Professor Crane is outstanding. Well prepared. Ready to engage students. Never boring. But most of all she is fair and does not push her personal and political beliefs on students, as most professors in the School of Social Work do. I wish I could take every class with her. She works hard to help students learn. Excellent!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The worst decision I've ever made. This class is the worst. Prof is nice though. The assignment rubrics are vague, and the GSIs grade insanely harsh for no reason. I spent more time suffering through this class than all of my upper-level classes combined, and it was never worth it. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr.Lampe is very clearly passionate about his study and his enthusiasm will undoubtedly rub off on you. If you develop good rapport with him, he is eager to help you and guide you. His ability to form relationships with his students and connect with them is impressive for how large his courses are. I highly recommend any class he instructs.

so much work. need to participate on discord and go to lecture and discussion to fulfill weekly engagement points. tests were difficult and it was every other week. lots of readings. big assignments almost every week for like 13 weeks. lecture boring, but interactive. would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SI110 requires far too much work for being an introductory course. Lecture is pointless since exams are exclusively based off reading assignments, however poor attendance can drastically harm your grade. Overall not an awful class and the material is interesting,wouldn't recommend if you're not sure if you want to pursue information science/UX

Professor is nice and funny during lectures but SI 110's class structure is terrible and way too much work for an introductory course. The projects and almost weekly reports are graded rather harshly and very tedious. The exams aren't easy either. This course genuinely made me reconsider if I even wanted to pursue the UX minor. Avoid if you can.

One large project over the course of the semester but some other pretty intensive assignments as well. A lot of reading so the course often feels overwhelming. Lowest test and paper scores are dropped and not all assignments are required though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class simply is too much work for a 4-credit course with the new style. The old reviews reflect the past model of the SI 110 course- the new one created during Fall 2025 has 5 content-heavy exams, 4-6 in-depth written essays, as well as a 5-part in-depth project throughout the year, with mandatory attendance. Professor is also weird egotistical
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. I have never had so many assignments at once. The tests require a full week to study, are every couple of weeks, and even then, the concepts are not always included in the lecture; some are just about readings. Keep in mind that one of 8 readings assigned this week has 200+pages in it and this is on top of everything given.

Prof Lampe is my favorite teacher so far. Genuinely funny guy and is knowledgeable. The class is really not as bad as everyone says. Just be organized, keep track of assignments, and you'll be fine. The class is a point/gamified system. You only need 935 points for an A and you have the chance to earn over 1000 points with the extra credit.

Class has a lot of papers and readings, but the material is very interesting. Go to Cliff's office hours and make sure you read the syllabus and you will be fine. Assignments won't be explained to best so it's up to you to figure it out. Aside from that, the teaching team and Cliff are absolutely amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Lampe is super cool! SI110 is super time-consuming though. A few large projects and lots of writing. The content is super interesting though and Dr. Lampe seemed to genuinely care about what he was teaching, which is always refreshing. Lectures can be a little boring, but Dr. Lampe does his best to integrate cool "nerdy" things and jokes often.

I absolutely loved this class! It was very informative and interesting. Professor Lampe is a great lecturer and very helpful. The workload is definitely doable, it can be slightly overwhelming but it is still a very very great class to take. I highly recommend!

Professor Lampe seems like a nice guy, but the lectures often felt like a waste of time in the context of the class. More essay-heavy than my upper-level writing class, grading was all over the place due to bad rubrics. How well you did on an essay was pretty much based on who was grading your paper. Super frustrating course to try to do well in.

Crazy amount of writing, way more than any actual writing class that I've ever taken. Professor doesn't respond to emails and assigns many readings. Definitely take this class in a semester where you have more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: insane amount of papers and the grading criteria was never clear/seemed subjective. I did good but didn't like that the professor and teaching team made it seem impossible to get higher than a B all semester. lots of readings but you can maybe get away with reading only when you have to write the papers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love Lampe. He's inspirational, knowledgeable, makes huge chunks of information not intimidating but very digestible. It's clear that he cares a lot about his GSIs and PhD students. His class is the only class I would show up to take notes furiously. The workload is A LOT, high expectations, take his class in a semester where you have more time.

I signed up for SI 110 during the 3 week add/drop deadline, and it wasn't too hard to catch up. There is a lot of writing in the class. The readings are only helpful for writing the essays. No quizzes or exams in this class, and your grade is based on the essays and group project final. If you do the minimum for essays you will get an 88% avg.

Dr. Lampe was great. He's very knowledgable in his field, and very funny and interesting. However, the class, SI110, was awful. There's a crazy amount of work for a. 100 level introductory course. 50-75 pages of reading per week, tons of essays, multiple massive projects, combined with the fact that the field of "information" seems kind of made up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not a fun class. Project and paper rubrics are super vague and and GSIs like to give round about answers to questions, making things even more confusing. An 88% is considered "meeting expectations," and to get above this you must "exceed expectations," whatever that means. You will spend a tons of time on papers and not get the grade you deserve.
Cliff has so many years of experience in this field. He's super knowledgeable and the class is super engaging and enjoyable. He provides constructive feedback on assignments which helps you improve!

Dr. Lampe's class was one of my favorite's last semester. SI-110 is not a hard class to get an A in if you follow all the guidelines and details posted in the rubrics. There are a lot of readings but they are necessary to do well on the quizzes so take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of readings for class they do help you understand the concepts well, not 100% necessary but help a lot. Dr. Lampe keeps lectures funny and entertaining as well as engaging outside of class, in dicussons and virtually. Talks a bit fast so keep up but not necessarily all vital information to write down or anything.

Lots of papers, lots of reading, but it's all very very interesting and Professor Lampe has put himself in a position of having a lot of experience in subjects that are just now starting to get noticed. The class is a lot of reading, but fairly straightforward to get an A on. Lampe is incredible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Lampe was really great! He is super understanding and is really passionate about what he teaches. It makes you interested in what he is teaching. The content itself is also very interesting.

Definitely the most interesting class I've taken so far, so if you're passionate about tech and the ethnics behind it this class is for you. Lampe has a great sense of humor and makes class entertaining. GSIs can grade a little tough but overall great class.

Such a good class. Lampe is engaging and clear. GSIs can be tough graders and unclear sometimes though. A lot of reading but the quizzes aren't too bad. Easy A if you don't procrastinate on the projects and talk to your GSIs beforehand.

Definitely recommend taking a class with him. He's funny, fair, and responds to email in a decent amount of time. He gives a lot to read, but it's doable if you manage your time. Projects and class discussions were fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The GSIs are harder to deal with than Professor Lampe himself. Coming in interested in SI, decided to drop it because of this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The GSI's are horrible graders, their feedback is not clear. I don't understand how they grade these assignments. Be prepared for a lot of reading and it will not be helpful for the quizzes. The lectures are very boring. It seems like a lot of the topics are random and do not connect to each other. I wouldn't take this class if not needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Lampe stepped up after our previous professor couldn't teach anymore for personal reasons, and he's been nothing but fair and accommodating. Yes, there were quite a few readings but you really just had to skim them. The tests were also curved so as long as you put in a little effort you'd do well. The final project was also manageable.

AVOID. Too many readings. Too complex of readings. Project w/ absurd amount of work (expected to be 3500-4000 words/person in the group). does not respond to student concerns. tests are so hard (due to vagueness of class). seems like he's purposefully hard to be a cheeky U of M prof. annoyingly arrogant for someone from the west side of michigan.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Absurd amount of work. 100 + pages of reading per week. obscure pop quiz every week. 10 2-4 page essays, 2 projects equivalent to 10 page essay, another 2500 word essay. no assignments relate to actual material you need to know. will ruin your life. required to go to out of class lectures to complete essays. will be biggest regret of your life.

Absolutely terrible class. I was excited to explore the School of Information, and after taking this class I for sure will not pursue that interest. Guidelines for class are incredibly vague, the GSIs are hard graders. Expect to do an insane amount of reading and writing for this class. Lectures are EXTREMELY boring.

The readings each week are so long and the quizzes assess if you memorized word for word one sentence out of the readings. The grading system is extremely confusing and not explained, the projects are ridiculously long and uninteresting. Unless you want to major in information, don't take it. Way too much busy work, but not very hard overall.

There are weekly readings that are extremely boring and dry. Each week, there is a quiz over the boring readings. This class is "gamified" so grading is like a game with a leaderboard and points. The semester is almost over and I am just starting to understand how the grading works. Confusing. Boring. Awful. Pain in the ass. Dr. Lampe is very funny

Ironically, for a class built on gamification, this class is designed really poorly.  Ten 2-4 page writing assignments (which you get little to no helpful feedback for your grade).  2 large projects, 1 semester-long project, weekly pop quizzes (on specific details from the 4 hours worth of reading), final exam.  Don't take this.  HIGHLY SUBJECTIVE

Cliff uses Gradecraft for his class - a program that attempts to turn an academic course at a major university into a video game. The course is structured in a way that is made to let students work at their own pace and instead the teacher drops all of the assignments on you at once. He has planned this class very poorly and I was jk about him hot

The Citizen Interaction Design class was great, it widened my perspective to new design problems in the world. The learning from this course will stay with me throughout my life. Best class of my first semester. I just loved the class and the professor. I want to take this class again.
I liked him well enough, and the class was interesting, but he seemed really arbitrary, and kind of egocentric.

Expectations at times are absurd and unrealistic.  On one hand, he fakes empathizing with students and claims he understands how busy we are, while at the same time gives us grief for not doing the readings for one week.  Our midterm was a MONSTROSITY of a research paper (15 pages and 20-40 sources!!).  Funny, good lecturer, field expert, hard af.

Honestly, did the class take some effort? Yes. Was the grading team evil and did everything to stop you from getting your precious A? No. Cliff was a great professor, always enthusiastic and funny, which made the material a breeze. If you play by the rules of his game and trick yourself into thinking it's "fun," you'll be fine.
I love Cliff. Also informatics. Also the teaching team. Also gamification. Basically perf.

Hardest class ever taken, feels like a 6 credit class instead of a 4 credit class. Impossible to get an A no matter how hard you try. Grading is subjective, tons of reading. Painfully hard, emotions are constantly manipulated. If you end up taking this class, be prepared to pray every night to pass this class or get a B.

Took the class thinking it would be easy and fun, but the curriculum got super revamped. Crazy amount of readings and deadlines every week, which means crazy  slow grading(literally 3 weeks) so you get feedback on what to improve after you hand in the next  big assignment. Class is fun, but it was poorly revamped; it might change next semester.

He dramatically changed his class this year so most people get a B+. Even if you work really hard and do exactly what they ask for, they will give you an 88%. You also have to do immense amounts of readying and are quizzed on it weekly. Don't take this course unless you have to or are interested in the material and willing to get an average grade.
Lampe keeps his lectures interesting and has a great sense of humor. Cool material and truly inspirational professor who cares about his students
Funny optimist who cares.
Hilarious. Extremely well versed in the material. Will keep you interested. Gamification is give or take depending on your interests.
Incredibly easy class, everyone got at least an A-. Readings not required. Lampe swears alot in lecture to keep students interested, but it gets old pretty fast.

Great professor, I always went to lecture it was enjoyable and always hilarious. There are some really big projects and make sure you do Explorer Reports from the beginning so you don't get stuck trying to do a bunch of them at the end.  Doing the readings weren't necessary, overall a fun & semi-easy class.

A great professor and a great class!  "Dungeonmaster" is hilarious, and class was a pleasure every day.  He's just a really good guy.  There are some big projects, but they're interesting and you get to personalize them to fit you.
He's actually soooo funny and really entertaining.  I honestly almost never pay attention in any classes but he's always able to keep my attention.  Not a hard class at all.

Lampe is an awesome professor, you will never laugh harder in another class. Amazing sense of humor, as well as engaging material. This class is a great time and I never mind going to lecture. This professor will be one of your favorites you take at michigan!

eCommunities was a great course - definitely take it instead of 429 if you get a chance. Lots of weekly readings but they can be skimmed. Technical write-up of an online community each week, midterm project and final paper (no exams). Cliff is engaging and the funniest prof I've ever had.
Most hilarious professor I've ever had. Lecture is a lot of fun. The class is easy too, and the assignments are really engaging.

Great Professor who is well known in the school of information but still teachers an introductory course. SI110 is a pretty easy course and he manages to make the slides and lectures really interesting. Sometimes he makes grand claims which aren't exactly true but for the most part he is a great and funny teacher.

By far the best teacher I have had at the University of Michigan. I absolutely loved his breaks halfway through lecture where he would enlighten us to "Geek or Nerd Culture". Incredibly funny, and just a genuinely nice, friendly guy. If you want a great introductory class that is engaging and flat-out funny, take Introduction to Information.

Dr. Lampe is hilarious and his class is extremely interesting. None of the assignments are too difficult (and graded easily), and most are open note. He also posts all the lectures on Ctools as a podcast so you can hear as well. If you're thinking about taking this class at all, TAKE IT! You will not regret it.
Really funny guy. I looked forward to going to his lectures. He tries to tie back the course material to real life and wants his students to learn valuable information not only related to the class

Don't know why people are saying it's difficult. There's no need to do the readings. Just form a study group before the exams and it's an easy A. There's 80 POINTS OF EXTRA CREDIT. GSI's grade both of your papers very easily. Lampe is very tech savvy and the funniest teacher I've ever had. If you take this class, make sure it's with him.Very easy A
Entertaining professor, and explains things pretty well.  However, the exams can be tough and they require a lot of studying.

Unless you're genuinely interested in information studies, I wouldn't take this class. Prof. Lampe, while amusing, goes off topic a lot. His lectures never feel like they have any continuity, much like the course. There are a lot of dense readings which are never really discussed in class or used in any assignments.
Very good lecturer and fun class. Random attendance taken during lectures but offers a lot of extra credit. Definitely possible to get an A.
greeeat professor. genuinely enjoyed going to class and listening to him speak. he does do random attendance in lecture sometimes, but all lectures are online. great class.
bIG FADE!!

Several extra credit opportunities. If you do well on exam 1 and 2 and do the rest of your assignments, you can take a 0/100 on exam 3 and still get an A (what I did). She's super nice and caring. Amazing prof. Would take again.

Colleen is an extremely kind professor, she always makes sure no one is confused and questions are answered. As far as teaching in class, she assumes you know a lot so definitely stay on top of readings if you actually want to understand what she is saying. She offers a lot of extra credit at the end of the semester so your grade will be ok.

(SI 101 used to be called 106) Colleen is the best and cares about her students. shes reasonable, understanding and would always give extensions on our assignments. Readings are helpful since lectures can be fast but many did fine without. 3 exams, 1 makeup date, 1 final project(group or alone), 3 'HWs', weekly quizzes and lecture activities(easy).

Course could be more organized, but overall it's not that bad. You might have to work a bit harder for a few assignments, but if you're a CS major taking it as an elective (like me), the workload should be much lower than what you're used to. Colleen and the GSIs are nice and try their best to help out too.
This class was not bad, but the workload is a bit too much. In addition, lecture was kind of confusing at times but overall, I definitely gained some knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: the most rude professor i've ever had. she puts up a sweet face but is never there to help. she's also straight up mean cause she knows she has the power and the student can't do much. save yourself some trouble and don't take her class.

SI339 shift to CPDs was a disaster. The class was chaotic, unorganized, and confusing for both students and staff. OH were unhelpful, as GSIs and TAs were always confused themselves. I spent more time decoding assignments than learning, focusing solely on meeting deadlines rather than understanding the material. I don't recommend this class AT ALL!

she's a nice person. that's basically the only good thing. everything about this course was a mess and the gsis also didn't know what was going on. this class would have been easy if it was organized properly but instead i fought for my life to get an A. i don't think  colleen knew was going on half the time either. never take this class.
disorganized and does not know how to simplify concepts. be ready to self learn.

This class has amazing grade/work policies to make the class a low-stress enviornment for students to learn Python. She designed the class to be very lenient and forgiving, we get to drop our lowest exam scores. Anyone who says this class is stressful has a skill issue

On the first day of class she proposed an O/U for how many times she would fall off the stage at the front of the lecture hall. Absolutely goated professor. If you know how to code this class is very easy if you don't it should also be pretty easy. She knows her stuff fr.

106 with Colleen was my favorite class this semester. I learned so much about Python, and she structured the course so you can fail over & over & still pass easily. It makes for a super great, learning-focused environment. I found a new love for programming and Colleen is such a great person and instructor. Would recommend taking anything with her.
colleen is a talented instructor, i wish  i can come back and the class again. how she explains different algorithms, is awesome. i will recommend here over and over again

Colleen is one of the best professors I've had here at umich. She is really accommodating and responsive. homeworks are pretty easy but if you have trouble office hours are great. If you have any questions she is very approachable.  If you put in the effort you'll do great.

The course contents are extremely unorganized and everywhere. Not only the students are not sure what is going on, the TAs are also confused by her specs. Her rubric for assignment makes no sense, you have to spend 80% time on figuring out what she wants and only 20% time on ACTUAL learning. NEVER take her course.

Extremely rude and disrespectful as a professor. Non-inclusive and non empathetic towards students. I had a terrible experience with her for auditing her class. She lacks patience and basic decency to talk to students.

grading is point based so you just work up to the grade you want and van lent gave us extra assignments to get more points. GSIs have a ton of office hours to help with homework/projects. programming exams are almost all questions taken from the homework
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class a lot as I learned how to code without any experience before! There are a lot of assignments and exams as the class is structured in a points system. There are many office hours offered and the GSIs are very helpful. The only thing is that it is a little difficult to learn the concepts without a textbook or direct instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I found professor Van Lent extremely caring for her students. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but I went to every lecture because she was very caring towards class. Yes, there are minor inconveniences with issues for the auto-grader, but she accommodates extra points for that reason. She's really funny and tells you what to expect for exams.
Very bad experience, very unclear guidance

I LOVE Colleen. She knows her stuff & is great at teaching it. She's such a caring professor & I learned so much about web development and accessibility from her (especially with her personal stories). When students didn't understand a concept she was never frustrated, & was willing to sit with you for however long it took to get it.

As a non-SI major, I really appreciated how inspiring and caring Dr. Van Lent is. As a professor, she is incredibly kind and one of the best human beings I've met. She shares her passion for teaching with the students, and uses great analogies to connect with students. Exams can be tough tho.
Very casual and lose work style - always updating the homework requirements one day before it's due, which is very disturbing and annoying.

I respectfully disagree with the previous rating; I'm taking the same class (which I think the previous commenter mistyped) and Prof. Van Lent has extremely available, accommodating, and approachable. The autograder issue occurs when code doesn't meet the specificationI haven't had an issue with it. Others who've had get direct help with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is so stupid, the auto grader is so stupid. There are so many ways to write the CSS to get the same effect but the professor and GSIs just choose to use the auto grader which is so rigid and it doesn't make sense at all! Why can't you just grade people's homework by LOOKING INTO THEIR CODE?!

Colleen was probably one of the best instructors I've taken while at U-M. She's always willing to answer any questions, and her teaching style were lecture with in-class activities, which really helps in understand the material. After COVID closed our school, she was still able to maintain the same level of lecture through digital means.

Colleen is an incredibly caring professor and will really help you learn web development in the course. She's really understanding when you have difficulties and plans the course around helping people with the problems they have. Highly recommend

SI 339 was an excellent course. While attendance is not mandatory, her lectures are very clear and sometimes she will even do the homework in front of you. There are a lot of assignments, but none of them are unreasonable and there is a lot of extra credit if you miss something. Very good course for learning web development.

One of the best professors I have ever had. You don't HAVE to go to class but you will want to! I learned so much from the examples and practice we did even though I came in with no web development experience. She really cares about students and the people we design for. If you have the chance, take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Colleen is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She cares about her students and wants the entire class to learn and do well. SI 206 was restructured this semester for the better, but I actually wish we had moved faster and learned even more. Overall, it was a great course and I enjoyed the class a lot!

She's sweet, caring and honest. While fairly decent in large lectures, she's genuinely amazing one-on-one. This semester, SI206 changed a lot from prior ones, so there were still a few kinks in course structure and syllabus. However, I'm sure it'll get better in subsequent terms. Tl;dr: Colleen's great; be sure to actually speak and work with her.
Great all around teacher.  Could have a little more work that pays off, but kills it.  So caring and nice.

You have to work with 10+ students in a complicated (and BORING) group project in a lecture hall that is not designed for group work. Good luck including 10 people in a discussion in rows of desks. 10 minutes of class time everyday was devoted just to moving 200 bodies into groups in this classroom. But it's a requirement, so oh well!
Did not positively contribute to learning at all. Whenever she spoke, it was a tangentially related ramble. Easy class.

She was micro-aggresive from time to time. She normally is just there for an hour talking. She wasn't engaging. Overall, the class itself felt pointless for it to be at 9am. There are a lot of quizzes, some that are open note and some that you should study for. There are online and accessible textbooks for the class.

PCB wasn't that bad a professor. Sometimes she just talks while Dr. Briggs does most of the content lecturing, but she didn't negatively impact the class. The class itself seems pointless, but just stick it out for one semester, and if you participate, you will get an A. PCB will just talk the whole hour, though, so try to stay awake at 9 AM.

She honestly didn't contribute much to the class. Briggs was mostly the one teaching, and all she did was sit there and yell at us every so often. This class is a little silly and very easy since all the tests are open-note. Make sure you actually talk to people in your group, or she will come and yell at you any chance she gets.
PCB is a preacher in her off-time and it shows, very inspirational gal!!

Placed in random groups. Biggest project takes 3 weeks was 35% of grade. Only exam is midterm which is 10%. All the material covered for assignments are mostly done outside of class. Goal of his class is to prepare students for future nursing classes, she was funny, gave personal experiences in her life. Class wasn't helpful, you never use this.

Any new nursing student past 2024, should not take anything before fall 2023 into account for 142...PCB is very knowledgeable on a lot of things healthcare, but the nursing school did make a good choice having this class dually taught.
Class is easy and straightforward, worse thing was mandatory attendance for a friday 9am flipped classroom.
People are being too harsh. She's not that bad she's just not as fun as her co-lecturer. Be ready for group project with up to 10 people. Easy A if you show up and do Pre-readings.

Extremely easy class with little to no substance other than nursing CoE. A flipped classroom with required attendance is insane for a 2 credit class on Friday at 9 am. PCB is extremely nice but often goes on tangents and gets off-topic and attendance was inconsistently taken.
Required attendance, first absence will be penalized, for a flipped classroom on Fridays at 9am is insane.

All other reviews are too extreme. Super nice lady that got handed a really simple intro course that has little to no substance in it besides CoE. Goes on tangents and is a lil too proud for someone with no nurs degree but it helps with the monotony. Just suck it up, there's always more in-depth stuff later. TXTBKS ARE FREE ON MLIBRARY, DO NOT BUY

This class was co taught and PCB and Alec clashed on a lot of the topics discussed. PCB is a good person but does not know how to teach very well. All of her lectures were all over the place and constantly contradicted themselves. It is very evident that she is not well versed in nursing, but she does know a lot about other important topics.

horrible class, towards the end of the semester she realized her syllabus had some mistakes. She is a wonderful person but she was a horrible professor. Grades are heavily based on group assignments. The last group work was made unclear & dropped me from an A to a B+.......good luck to any first yrs taking this, you'll need it

I respect PCB as a person, however, her class was extremely disorganized, and often times we had absolutely no clue what was expected of us. I did not learn much from the class and seemed like a massive waste of time. Would not have taken this class if I didn't have to. I learned more about her personal life than anything related to nursing.

This professor is awful at teaching. The material is very Messy, disorganized, confusing, and boring. There are so many projects and they make it so confusing to understand. Students are better off understanding the material on their own.

Though PCB is a kind soul, I was constantly confused and anxious regarding anything related to her class. She is not qualified to teach in the #3 BSN program, much less a nursing school (no RN degree). She frequently gave us false information and was corrected by students, missed class for other meetings, or zoomed into lectures from her car.
