PCB can not teach to save her life. Her instructions are never clear and are extremely confusing. She forced 4 projects onto us with very little description of what must be done with very tight due dates. Whenever she speaks, she thinks that people can read her mind which makes it very hard to follow what she says during classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: PCB is a beyond horrendous teacher. Don't even bother to understand what comes out of her mouth because it just doesn't make sense. You will not have a good time in her class and you will never know what's going on or what is expected. Any class that involves PCB, you will be confused. Her "lectures" are made up of unrelated tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PCB...where do I begin. If you want to know the personal details of a tenured professor, take this class. If not, too bad you have to. This class is pointless even if it were taught by someone with any nursing experience. Not only does PCB not have a single nursing degree, she requires two TAs to grade and communicate with students. Nice lady.

I'm almost done with this class and I'm still confused about what I should be working on. PCB is a lovable lady but there's no clear instruction or rubrics. She isn't very good with technology. That being said, she is funny.

Her whole class was so confusing and seemed like it didn't have a purpose. I feel like I honestly didn't learn anything. She also says some stuff that's super unrelated and sometimes problematic. There's so many group projects going on at once as well. Not clear on instructions at all.
PCB is a very nice, caring professor, but her class is quite disorganized. It can be confusing and frustrating to know what the expectations of assignments are and when they are due.

PCB is one of the most confusing people I have ever met. No one knew what was going on this entire class. The frustration that I have been caused as a result of this class is insane. Honestly, PCB needs to retire or not be in charge of setting due dates or the main portion of this course. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I am almost done with the semester and I still have no idea what the point of this class is. Not a single person ever has any idea what is going on or what we are supposed to be doing. The coursework is easy, but it is nearly impossible to figure out what the coursework is because PCB has never made a coherent thought. Nice lady though.

There were like 7 textbooks "required" for this class. Now, to be honest, the only one that ended up mattering was the COE Nursing. PCB is horrible at teaching, and the quizzes are pointless. If you are absent, you have to fill out a form on Canvas, and they apparently mistook my grandma passing away for me testing positive for COVID. Waste of time

This class was a nightmare. I don't think PCB managed to convey a single coherent thought the whole semester. She's terrible at explaining things and will just confuse you more if you ask for clarification. It's incredibly frustrating to deal with.

PCB is very quick to respond to emails outside of class, but sometimes clarity is an issue. It can be hard to understand the point of what she is communicating, as well as the wording of her emails. She seems very passionate, and the course was pretty easy, but at times, the course is very disorganized and deadlines can be confusing.
She's such a legend. Make sure to just do the assignments to get a good grade. If you ever need her outside of class, she's really accessible.

PCB seems frustrating at first because the class is not structured in the best way, but she truly is a very caring and dedicated prof. She works with you if grades are not right and really wants everyone to do well. She is very clear that this class is just to get you used to nursing school and is not about accuracy on projects.
PCB is very unclear in what she wants from you and often goes on tangents. She is very sweet about non-class things.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: PCB is very unclear about what she wants her students to do, even though it may seem clear to her. Many of us were confused for every last project assignment. She does not answer emails quickly. The work is mostly busy work, and all that matters is the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I couldn't tell if it was her or the curriculum change, but this class was a mess. It was often unclear what was expected of us each week and we constantly had group projects and either A. didn't know what we were supposed to do or B. had no real time to complete it in class. At the end of the day we didn't have to take a final but it was stressful

The class I took with PCB I believe was new to the school of nursing the year I took it. It's a first year introductory seminar to nursing. Most of the class time was SNB faculty or UM Hospital faculty coming in to meet us and talk to us. Mostly group project based, but easy A and very chill. Go to the TA Kim Byk with any problems, she's awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took NURS 142 (seminar) with her and going to class was pointless besides the 5 minute weekly quiz. The group work was pointless and she never taught, she just talked about random things the entire 2 hours. Most quiz questions were unpredictable and had nothing do with the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tons of ambiguity when it comes to what exactly you're actually supposed to be doing. Weekly quiz questions are unpredictable to the point where reading the chapters before the class is pointless, and you will often be given in-class instructions which are either unclear, or are changed as you are doing the assignment. Do not take a PCB class.

There is no communication in this course. Half of the time when we were assigned a project, she would start changing the directions while we were working on it in class. Not to mention that she only gives about 15 minutes for group work for a 3 hour long class, but that did get better over the semester. She also flat out declined office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Her directions are unclear to a fault; I do other classes' work during the lecture. Other students may also do work, watch Netflix, scroll through IG, etc. They are also repetitive in meaning and the assignments are just tedious; they, to me, are just busywork. Thank God that they're not continuing the class; it's a bit too late for my year though.

She is not an actual nurse and still tried to teach nursing concepts. It was hard to believe her views on nursing because she had no experience. She preached her views during lecture, refused to hold office hours, and talked on and on about anything but what was supposed to be taught. Shes a nice person but not a good professor at all.

While I didn't enjoy this class, I feel like I hated it less than a lot of my peers did. PCB is a nice person, but she is not a good professor. The most irritating thing about her class was when we would take quizzes in class and she would TALK ON THE MIC THE ENTIRE TIME. Lots of pointless group projects and assignments. Very unorganized. Blehhh

The worst professor you could possibly get. This was a 12 week course, with one 3-hour "seminar" a week. PCB lectured ONE TIME the entire semester and it was about ethnicity. We asked her if she could teach on the material and she told us that lecturing was too hard and that it was boring for her. I do not know how she is still employed at U of M.

PCB was a terrible professor. I would recommend avoiding her at all costs. She refused to hold office hours. Completely ridiculous and spent most class going off on random tangents not related to the class at all. She made me seriously consider switch majors.

Refuses to answer emails or hold office hours, does not teach ANY material in class, and severely lacks any sort of communication skills. Only thing she does talk about are her political views which has nothing to do with the class. Do not take this class if she is the professor. It will drive you nuts.

There were no lectures on ANY of the material that was tested. No office hours were offered, and emails are discouraged. All questions were treated as infractions on her personal time. No clear direction on any assignments, and her personal views on politics were discussed in class. 0/10 would not recommend for anyone who wants to stay sane.

Dr. Coleman-Burns is an incredible professor and individual. I think that many of the students do not appreciate her ability to weave her years of experience and pursuit of justice into so many discussions and would prefer instead a set of clear assignments with no personal investment or growth. I think PCB is excellent and I loved the class.
PCB will never give a complete and clear understanding of what is expected and when it is due. That being said, she grades very easily and just expects you to do you're best.

At first the class was a little chaotic, but looking back I really appreciated the easiness of the concepts and the way the rubric was set up. Read the text-book, especially for the final, and get to know the people in your group because you need them for projects and group quizzes. Enjoy it while you can cause it only gets harder.
This class was the most painful thing to sit through! She was a terrible teacher! It is a required course which sucks but it was so boring and the biggest waste of time!!!! HATED IT

PCB was a horrible teacher, she was not clear nor concise. My favorite was when she sent the entire class to the hospital for a "guided tour" which she failed to inform staff of. Wonderful experience. PCB goes off on random tangents about and yelled at us most of the class period. VERY UNORGANIZED.

I loved PCB! most students did not like her blunt personality but if you asked a question about the lectures and the answers were in the textbook she had no problem letting you know where to find it. Her refusal to answer questions in lecture only encouraged students to READ THE MATERIAL!

Not an effective teacher...all I learned from the class was "don't date Bob", meaning don't date the patients--which should be assumed already...?? She is not a nurse, which makes it hard to sit through her class with her telling us what being a nurse is all about...

PCB is a good person, not a good prof. Assignments were weird,  boring, and repetitive. Apparently with our group work if we didn't have relational problems with each other at some point then we had a problem. On exams some of the questions were ridiculous, like why do I need to know this (think nursing architectural history) & the final was brutal
Nice person but cannot teach a nursing class. questions are not really answered just turned into a long lecture about useless info.

She tries very hard to teach and I respect her for that. However, any question you ask her will turn in to a useless rant without ever reaching an answer. Read the book THOROUGHLY because many questions are straight from it, even thought she assures you that the test is on the "main concepts". Not a fun class.

Every lecture feels like a TED Talk - very engaging, but when you ask him to clarify something, he just repeats his TED talk and expects you to understand. This goes for if you ask questions in class or if you go to office hours. 

He is also very accomplished and will make sure you know it, which comes off as full of himself.
hes good and inspirational but lowkey is not a proactive teacher/accessible at all

While his lectures are inspirational and great.  He grades pretty tough and doesn't grieve feedback on what he grades.  Additionally assignments he graded in our class were graded and returned a week later less that 3 hours in some cases before the next assignment was due.  There was also zero feedback so mistakes were repeated commonly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Multiple huge assignments from very beginning to very end that take forever. You must purchase his book as the main reading for the course. Every class uses the same examples and language from his book. He also doesn't share slides and for projects later in the semester, you are required to incorporate and utilize course concepts
Great professor, very professional, and very interesting classes, he does not share slides so take notes in class

Professor Collins has a friendly, engaging style which makes learning easy. Be prepared to laugh out loud and some of the jokes and visual aids. He does a great job keeping the conversation moving and using relevant, timely examples to drive home lessons.
Great speaker, but does not explain things well. Course concepts were unclear because he uses the same description for concepts in every class.

Marcus is the BEST person out there and has shaped by experience at Michigan. I'm not even in Ross and have taken two classes with him just because of how incredible his lectures are. He is so knowledgeable and explains things in such a clear way. He truly gets to know his students and is always willing to help. Definitely take a class with him.

Marcus has a stellar reputation amongst Ross students, and somehow manages to even exceed that reputation. His classes are wildly difficult to get into for a reason. You can tell how much he cares for students to an incredible extent, even going as far as to give his personnel phone number to students. By far the greatest course I have ever taken.

Her graduate level courses are rather boring and are not really engaging. I don't think her teaching style is for me as her class is all over the place. Students who are new to grad school or theory based courses prepare to feel like an imbecile and confused! This comment is based on one of her UT Austin courses
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is super easy as long as you skim the readings and take the weekly quizzes. Readings are very long though so be aware of that (one week we had 90+ pages, which obviously no one is going to do). Overall did not put too much work into this class, 4 fairly easy credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Learned a lot during the first few weeks, but ended up reading the same sort of things over and over again. Prof Cotera has a heavy preference for certain topics, while other (equally important) matters were only swept past pretty quickly. GSIs are really helpful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy to get an A in this class, just skim through the readings for the online quizzes and go to class (but you don't have to take notes because you don't have any tests on lecture material). But I didn't really care for Prof Cotera. She had a pretty heavy bias during lectures and came off as arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: EASY A! But--worst class I've taken at U of M. Opinion based quiz questions, little respect for other epistemological approaches. I'm a liberal, and this was way too far for me. Cherry picking data, little critical thinking, 100 pgs reading/week. Lecture required, no laptops. Belittle opinions. If interested in WOMENSTD, take different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super mediocre course. Lecture was not very exciting and I spent 95% of the ones i actually attended either on my phone or just doodling. Easy grading, just participate in section (25%), skim the readings to do the quizzes (25%), and put in at least some effort on the final project(40%) and you'll get an A even if your midterm essay(10%) is a C.

It's been a year since I took 240 and I still wish I could go back and take it again. I recommend the class often to people who need a HU credit, but I advise them to wait until they can take it with Prof. Cotera! Her lectures are great. I can't imagine how anyone could teach the class better.

She made the lectures interesting and I really liked the class even though I don't agree with everything she taught. My GSI was also very accepting of conflicting viewpoints. There are a lot of readings but you just have to skim them for answers to the online quizzes. The midterm is take home and you work on the final project the whole semester.

very passionate but her lectures only focus on white and black/hispanic feminism (literally a month of reading the same thing) & not very inclusive of other minorities. also a ridiculous amount of reading and grade is mostly determined by reading quizzes which test super specific things from the readings. easy A but u have to put in the effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She only lectures half of the semester and the rest is done by GSIs. The readings are a bit boring but you only need to skim them to get good grades on quiz. It is very important to invest effort to section participation and group project (don't make your project boring if you want good grades). Midterm was takehome exam and there was no final exam

Professor Cotera is amazing and really knows what she's talking about. I learned so much in this class and I'm hoping to take more women's studies classes in the future. Discussion is the most important part of your grade, but also in my opinion the most fun part of class. We talked about current events and issues on campus. Very interesting.

This class is super interesting and Professor Cotera REALLY knows her stuff. She jam packs the lectures with information, but lecture notes are all online. She takes attendance for 2-3 sections after each lecture, so attendance is somewhat mandatory. There are lots of assigned readings and online quizzes, but not hard.

You really don't need the lectures. I attended maybe half and got an A in the class, but she does start taking attendance after spring break. Your entire grade is based off of your GSI so make sure you develop a good relationship with them. The weekly quizzes are brutal if you don't read the material, but you'll do just fine if you skim them
Fell in love with women studies  because of this class, decided to minor in it. Would take again.
The class is easy. I didn't enjoy the class as much as I thought I would have, but I don't regret taking it. Discussions were my favorite part.

Professor Cotera is an amazing lecturer. The topic of the course is already interesting, but her passion makes the course even better! There are weekly readings for the course that you will be quizzed on. Some of the readings are quite long so be ready to buckle down and crank them out!

Maria Cotera was a great lecturer and I learned a lot from the class. The second half of the semester the GSIs taught the class, and that was fine.  The readings were not hard and the weekly reading quizzes were on ctools and not hard.

OK class, a lot of reading and the 2 hour sections weren't fun. She only teaches half the lessons and GSIs do the rest. Before taking her class look up her wikipedia page, it should give you some insight on her personality.

She is an excellent professor! She is fun, lively, and really knows how to engage her students, even on some of the more boring topics. My only complaint is that I wish she had lectured more, instead of bringing in a lot of guest lecturers. Quite a few of them were boring.
Fantastic prof! Definitely go to office hours! She has really interesting things to say and her lectures are fantastic!
Assigns a ton of reading, but it's pretty easy to do well without.
Cotera is a wonderful teacher! I would take anything she teaches. Definitely go to office hours if you can, she's really interesting and interested in talking to her students!

Professor Cotera loves what she does and makes you love what she teaches! The material could be hard to grasp but she made it very entertaining and fun to learn. She is the reason I got so interested in Women's Studies! If you take her, you will love her!
I wish all of my profs were this hot! For an intro class, so much material was covered take more with her to learn more!

This class would have been a lot better and worth the $50,000 tuition if Professor Cotera had actually taught the class the entire way through. Instead, GSI's lectured for the last half of the term, most of them grad students who are only a few years into their field. If you actually want a tenured prof teaching your class, do not take this one.

Professor Cotera did a pretty good job of teaching - her lectures were always well organized but the material was overly simplistic and she basically read off the slides. Attending class was not really necessary in the long run considering the ease of the final exam. Start with another women's studies class - they're a lot more interesting.

Professor Cotera was good and she made the material easy to understand. But I just really didn't enjoy the class itself. Wasn't really interested in the material we were learning in class. But the final exam was a lot easier than expected. And she sends tons of emails about extra credit opportunities which I thought were really useful!
This was an incredibly easy class.  Basically tell her back what she tells you and you'll have no problem.
Professor Cotera was awesome. Interesting lectures, keeps you interested, and very knowledgable. If you get a chance, take one of her classes.
My favorite professor. Glad I took her classes!!

She is really nice looking.  This class is pretty simple.  There is a course pack.  The lectures are straight forward, study them and you will be fine (except unit 3, need to read too).  There is a final project, I did the advocacy project.  Not that time consuming.  Basically go to class and pay attention and you'll get an A, do the extra  credit!

Professor Cotera is a decent teacher, but in the third section of the class, she does not lecture at all. Instead she passes the class off to useless guest professors who read from their own textbooks. The web project is ridiculously time consuming, the exams are pointless, and section is a waste. Easy class but NOT recommended.

I had Cotera for both AmCult 213 and WS240.  The latter took more work to get an A (meaning at least skimming over the readings and making a real effort with written assigments).  213 was a breeze, but in 240, although the assignments/tests were sometimes intimidating, it was interesting; and even though I disagreed often, I still got an A.

Yes, 240 is an intro class but it is not an easy A. Prof Cotera didn't do the grading though because it was a massive class. My GSI was a tough grader but she was very cool. In 240, be prepared to work really hard and get a B. If you are majoring in women's studies then you'll probably love this class.

DO NOT TAKE WS 240 probably one of the worst classes i have taken here. way too much reading, group project is stupid and incredibly unnecessarily time consuming. if you don't agree with their point of view, good luck
Pretty smart, pretty good lecturer, pretty good personal teacher...did I mention pretty?

Fantastic professor! She's very enthusiastic, and the class compose of multiple guest lecturers range from famous authors to **** Monologue actresses. I loved this class, and an easy A. Both the professor and GSI Erik Morales were super helpful and accessible to students.  Highly recommended!
If you don't get an A in this class, quit school. Not only is it incredibly easy, Maria is a fox, too.

The easiest class I've taken at UM. Cotera is great, very friendly and personable.  She is probably the only one in class who really enjoys the boring guest lecturers - lecture attendance is mandatory. Tests are incredibly easy, just study power-points and  coursepack readings.  Minimal work, easy A, interesting topics.

This class is interesting, but can be annoying.  The guest lectures are often boring...and attendence is taken in lecture.  Professor Cotera is a great lecturer though, usually very interesting with great powerpoints (posted on Ctools).  Tests are fairly easy and straigtforward.  Lots of outside activity is required though.

This class could have been way boring but she made it fun and engaging. She is a smarty and one of the more "cool" professors that I have had.  She has a tendency of going off on tangents, but she has a great relationship with students and the class is worth your time.

She's a sweety-pie! She doesn't mind answering any and all questions, and she loves to have fun and crack jokes (when appropriate). This class (theory) could have sucked a whole lot more, but she made it fun!
No Comments

Very interesting class - guest speakers are great, keeps good variety in the class. Constantly available in office hours; always happy to talk to students. (This rating is more for the class than the prof, as there are LOTS of guest lecturers.)

Please listen to the other people. I was one who thought the other people were being dramatic. It is very important you listen to them and me. Corey Powell makes this class way too complicated for no reason and barely tries to explain it so people understand. I took AP Stats and got a 4, but I feel like I have never taken a statistics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class in FA24. Is he good at explaining everything? No, not ALL the contents. However, with some knowledge in AP Stats and all the extra credits he gives for all assignments (it was very doable to have some errors but still get over 100%), it's not very hard to get an A. The exams are also easier than the covered contents.

If you have AP credit and need to take stats 280, take it with a different professor. The lectures often ran far behind in the notes, and the exams were much harder than any homework problems. Homework was also graded really harshly, and professor Powell often cold calls on students during lecture.

It is not worth getting the honors credit for this class, I wish I had taken Stats 250 instead. If you do take this class, take it first semester. Second semester, Powell gets "bored" with asking basic questions and purposely makes the exams harder and does not curve the class to help. Homework is also very difficult and graded on accuracy.

Do not take any class with Corey Powell. Just take 250 even if you took AP stats I promise you it is not worth it. The examples in lectures are SO different from what is on the exam and he is really not great at answering questions clearly. Again, just take 250. I took AP in HS and that wasn't helpful bc of how confusing Corey Powell made things.
Very bad at explanations

Awful. So bad, do not take at all. All the examples he gives in class is different from the exam. When you ask for help, he just repeats the question lol. I've been to almost all office hours and I have just walked out more confused.

Corey covers the page with his hand when he is trying to show us examples of work in class. Second of all, he makes statistics harder than it honestly has to be. He is disruptive during exams, where he actually called someone during our test about accomodations. If the GSIs showed up to class, he could walk out and take the call but why don't they?

I only took this class because I had no other option and would recommend that you do the same. The concepts weren't fully explained and we were expected to memorize R code?? Genuinely did not understand anything going on, I'm flabbergasted that I managed to scrape by in this class.

The class itself wasn't difficult, the format itself just made it difficult to incorporate coding into lectures. Even after going to office hours, Professor Powell was unhelpful, and didn't take feedback for discussions seriously when there were issues going on within the class as a whole.

Powell seems like a nice person, but this class was a bit much. I took AP stats in high school, did every homework assignment, and studied for HOURS on the exams but it wasn't enough. His office hours were required but not very helpful and the labs were required but unnecessary. Take 250 instead unless you're a stats major/want to hate your life

Dr. Powell was an understanding and helpful professor. However, he made concepts seem confusing by over-explaining them. The first midterm was ridiculously harder than the practice exams he gave. Assignments were unrelated to class content and graded on accuracy. He also expected us to memorize R code for exams.

Professor Powell is a kind person, but teaches Stats 280 in an unnecessarily complicated way. I came into the class with no coding or statistics experience and spent hours re-reading the textbook, going to math lab every week, memorizing R code, and attending every office hours (especially GSIs). This class is very unmanageable. Take 250 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Beware!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Is it worth it to lose happiness? :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Powell is very kind and evidently passionate about statistics and education. However, he often teaches in a manner far above the level of the course. Prior experience with AP Stats and coding is paramount to staying on pace. Weekly homework assignments are extensive and graded on accuracy. Little material is published for exam practice.

Professor Powell seems like a kind person outside of class but as for his teaching curriculum, it's terrible. The homework is ridiculously long and is graded insanely specifically. I loved stats before taking this class and my passion for stats has been drained after taking it. If you want at least an A- in this class, prepare to WORK for it.

Don't take this class. It's not taught as an intro course. He writes many of the homework questions, which are much more difficult than lecture content. As someone who went into this class with never taking a stats class before, no coding experience, and no friends in the class, you need all of these! GO TO OFFICE HOURS (esp. gsi), saved my grade.

Lectures were awful in that he barely actually explained much and just talked in front of slides. He didn't really know how to answer questions. When I went to him after exams were released, he was extremely rude and told me I failed, instead of helping and proving guidance as to where I went wrong or even pointing me in the right direction.

This class was much more doable than I expected, but I can't say it was enjoyable. Pretty monotonous lectures and labs, and grading is very specific. I wouldn't take this class if you don't have at least two of these four: 1) coding experience in any language, 2) AP Stats experience, 3) a good GSI, and/or 4) good lab partners/friends.

Corey seems like a cool guy. However, any enjoyment I may have had doing stats had been sucked out of this class. There's an ungodly amount of homework and work you need to do outside of class just to understand the content. I've seen more words than numbers in this class. You also have to learn R coding, which is stupid. I don't recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quite frankly, he doesn't understand how to teach stats. Lectures are not specific, unclear, present material in illogical orders, don't teach statistics in line with other courses, over-emphasize by-hand calculations. Uses few examples and almost exclusively speaks in conceptual terms. Got a 5 on AP STAT exam and was often confused in this class.

Powell is a terrible teacher. Unless you have the ability to teach material to yourself, don't take a class with him. The textbook was way more useful than he ever was. His examples were more confusing than anything because of his terrible explanations. Unless you have perfect understanding of stats and R coding, you won't do well in this course.

Does not break down hard concepts well enough for students to understand as quickly as he expects. Impatient if lectures material is not grasped and makes it clear to students. Homework is long and graded on accuracy. Lots of coding using R studio.

A great guy outside of class, but seriously struggles teaching material. Very unclear and talks as if we're at his level. Do not take this class unless it is absolutely necessary and you've taken AP Stats. Homework is graded on correctness and is very vague. Exams are incredibly hard and include handwriting code. Very helpful at office hours though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have not taken AP Stats, do not take this course. Content is very challenging and advanced, and exams are tough. Homework is graded on accuracy, which creates an added level of difficulty and a stressing environment. Lectures were not very engaging and were often confusing in content. Also, this class requires you to code in R.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expectations on exams were very clear. STATS 280 was the most fair 4 credit college class.
zzz

You get what you put into it. Dr. Powell's lectures weren't the most engaging at times but Dr. Powell himself is very ready to help if you reach out. I failed my second midterm and started going to office hours. He was very helpful and patient with the questions I had, and even offered class wide extra credit towards the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is pretty much just self-studying. Lectures are hard understand, homework and textbooks have typos. Don't take this class if you haven't taken AP Stats.

He is really nice and will always answer your question to the best of his ability. However, he makes simple things seem hard when he explains and talks really fast. Pretty non-engaging with his teaching in general. I think I learn better by reading his lecture slides and listening minimally.

He is not great at teaching but if you work hard, you can get a good grade because his class is basically curved. Homework, lab attendance, and writing assignments are easy ways to get points. If you have taken AP stats before, the class is very similar in content so it will be easier for you. The lab portion depends completely on the GSI.

Lectures are so confusing he makes the simple things too complex. People say he's disrespectful to students but I think he was fine. The lab is the least useful thing I've ever experienced my GSI just read code off the board and couldn't answer any of our questions. Take stats250 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He isn't as bad as the other reviews make him seem, but he did throw a lot of things at you and just kind of expected them to stick. His probability section was probably the worst offender of this, he threw formulas at you and didn't really go over them. The lab was really disconnected from lectures, but that isn't really his fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are all over the place, and the labs are even less sensical. Expectations are unclear little support is given. Respect for students and their questions is low. If I didn't have to take this class, I definitely would've taken the W on my transcript. Tears were shed.
Boring and not a good lecturer
This guy is just kindof a jerk when it comes to how he interacts with students. The class also is pretty all over the place. But yeah he basically is just a dick to students.

This guy is a pretty bad lecturer, and sometimes I come out of lecture way more confused than when I come in. The lab is also horrible since it's very disconnected from class and convers completely different things. Just don't take him.
Nice

Dr. Crowell is seriously amazing!! Her office hours are fantastic, even if you're not in her lecture. She wants students to succeed and truly cares about all students. I don't find EEB all that interesting, but she made it enjoyable to learn. If you're reading this Dr. Crowell, you're an amazing teacher. Cheers to you!

Super nice prof, great lecturer. Don't use the textbook, it's repeat info of what's covered in lecture. Lecture consists of practice problems since you watch lecture videos over the weekend. The problems are the same level as exams but she's very slow giving/explaining them. Attendance is iclicker (participation, not accuracy) so u can do from home

Dr. Crowell is very nice, caring and knowledgeable. Was always available for questions after class or during office hours. 

BIO 171 itself though is difficult and exams are filled with tricky questions that weren't covered as much during class. Lots of time is needed to study for exams to do well.
Dr. Crowell was always so nice and welcoming to all of her students. She is very smart and a great lecturer. You can tell she really cares about the subject matter too.

Dr. Crowell was a great teacher and cared deeply about her students. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about biology! The class isn't necessarily an easy one and you definitely have to put in the extra work for a good grade but Dr. Crowell makes it much more comprehendible! I would definitely recommend her!

Dr. Crowell is the best! I had her for my discussion section and she explains topics in a great way. She makes sure her students understand and was very accessible during office hours for questions. I would definitely recommend taking her and going to her office hours even if it's just to listen.

Dr. Crowell is very kind and is clearly very passionate about what she teaches. Her "real" lectures are all online, and the in-person classes are really just review questions using iClicker (she calls these ALS). I wasn't a huge fan of this format but I don't think it's in her control. She answers to emails very quickly and politely. Love her!
She was great but the asynchronous lectures were not as good as in person ones.

I took Bio 171 with her, and she was amazing! You can tell she really loves the content she is teaching and really cares that her students understand everything. Despite having so many students, she really does take the time to get to know you and give personal advice if given the opportunity. Highly recommend taking Bio with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Dr. Crowell was very sweet, and you could tell that she enjoys teaching the material of BIO 171, which is really important in my opinion. The class is exam-heavy, but attending lecture and doing the iClicker will decrease its weight to 64% overall. 

I would definitely recommend her

Dr. Crowell is the goat of BIO171, her lectures are very clear and she also takes time to go over things requested by students. I was also lucky enough to have her for discussion as well and you can really tell how passionate she is about what she teaches and how much she wants everyone to succeed. Absolutely sweetest person ever, TAKE HER CLASS!

Good lecturer, but the lectures always felt unnecessary. It's unfortunate that attendance is required, because you could easily perform the labs without the lectures. However, he is very kind and clearly loves chemistry, and is great at answering questions and explaining topics clearly.
Cruz was funny and knows how to explain stuff super well. He can be a little awkward at times, but prefered him over Gottfried.

Dr. Cruz is a light-hearted but caring and dedicated professor. He is very passionate about chemistry and will do everything he can to help you. I highly recommend taking this course with him! Additionally, I took the honors section of Chem 211, and I highly recommend that as well; my workload seemed much less than those in the normal 211 sections!

If you want to show up to lab prepared, take Professor Cruz's lecture section. He is gets you up to speed on what you need to know and preps you for labs perfectly so carrying out the procedures is easy as pie! Very approachable, great office hours if you're ever stuck on a pre-lab. Chill guy, would recommend.

Pretty adorable guy lol chem 125/126 isn't hard at all. He explains things pretty well to prepare you for lab. He's a bit awkward but you can tell he really knows his stuff and cares about teaching. Can go pretty fast during lecture sometimes but overall, he's great. Definitely would take him over Amy Gottfried
Really nice and engaging guy. The lectures feel very easy and dull sometimes, especially compared to chem 130, but he always had fun stories and jokes ot keep people engaged. Highly recommend

Dr. Cruz is very caring, funny, and enjoys teaching kids. I will say that I found his lectures to be a little lacking in the ability to teach me, but he always made sure the important stuff was covered and gave loads of examples. He also is very caring about students and takes the time to acknowledge them and their needs.

Highly recommend taking Chem with him, he is an extremely nice guy who really cares about his students. He makes every lecture easy to follow and students always felt prepared for their weekly lab after his lectures. The grading system is also very clear with lots of leeway, often giving points back for any confusing questions.
This guy is so jolly, you can tell he loves his job. He makes lecture participation easy and comprehensive.

Dr. Cruz was an amazing lecturer who explained the chemistry concepts and lab procedures very clearly and thoroughly. He drew very helpful drawings to illustrate how the lab would work. He clearly knows and cares a lot about chemistry. He was always very sweet and understanding in lecture.
pretty chill guy with good lectures - having a good GSI will make this course easy

Dr. Cruz's lectures really helped me understand all of the lab procedures, which can be kind of confusing if you're just reading them on LabFlow. His example set-ups and calculations along with the pictures were helpful as someone who learns by example. Super chill, personable guy who actually cares about how his students do and an easy class.
Very good dude
The class content was pretty repetitive, and the feedback I got on assignments was vague, so it wasn't very helpful for improving. Also didn't get a response to my email.
Professor Rodriguez-Seijas is one of the best I've had during my college career. He has a passion for the field and communicates very well. Thank you

I love the content of the course, but felt as though Dr.R's way of teaching was very reductive to it. He is a very strict behaviorist and belittles other schools of thought. He makes weird remarks during class about certain psychiatric populations. I would still take it, but just wanted to say because it definitely caught me off guard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor! Read before lecture, and go to office hours; he's super helpful. Also, the review on Apr 2nd, 2025, is just straight up lying. He does NOT expect you to memorize every disorder, and even specified that in class. Focus on the disorders we spent the most time on, and just generally understand the others, and you'll be all good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. R-S was a really good lecturer. I enjoyed his class, and would definitely take another with him.

Don't let the bad reviews scare you at all, he is a really great professor. It's a very straight forward class and he is very clear about what needs to be done to succeed. Make sure to read before lecture, review material, ask questions, go to lecture (don't miss the pop quizzes), and you should be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Craig is very knowledgeable about the topic so I learned a lot from this class. There are three exams and two papers about two books you have to read. We have had around seven pop quizzes for 5 points each, but he takes the average score and drops your lowest one. Readings from the textbook are long but very important to do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Abnormal psych has been my favorite psych class I've taken. He does talk really fast, but there is a lot to get through in lecture. Everything that is on the exam is based off what we learn in class, and the textbook we read just helps reiterate what we already talked about. He wants you to succeed so always talk to him if you need too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Rodri-Seijas is truly one of my favorite professor here at UofM, his lectures are pretty direct and exams are all covered by what lecture suggest. My only issue is that whenever you raise your hand to ask a question, he will quickly cut you off before you finish the question which I see as disrespectful but it is not a big problem.

For the love of the lord don't take his class, spare yourself. He doesn't really take feedback, and his test making is really bad. He also talk really fast for no reason. He doesn't give you any direction and expects you to know every disorder talked about in class (there were 70), but only covers a couple on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: if you are currently doing course registration, please for the love of god do NOT take one of his classes. that's all I have to say.
Prof Rodriguez Siejas is a great professor. He genuinely cares for his students and is very engaging.

Dr. Rodriguez-Seijas was a great lecturer and I did like him as both a person and a professor. I did find the pace of the lectures to be a bit fast and it was hard to follow lectures sometimes due to the lectures often having more than one topic, for example, we would finish the slides from the previous lecture and then start a new topic all in one
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a fine professor, kind and funny. The only problem with him is how fast he goes through lecture slides. Literally like 10 seconds per slide and they're FULL of content, and we weren't allowed to have laptops out so I could never really get notes down. But very kind and funny and pretty good overall

Dr. R-S only taught for half of this class, but he was a pretty decent lecturer during it. He has a tendency to speed through lecture slides, which is a little but hard when you have to memorize the requirements for disorders. He is very open to questions though, and seems like he cares about students.

He's super passionate about psychology and overall super nice. Exams are memorization heavy (not hard, but can be specific about disorder symptoms). I never read the textbook and got A's on all the exams from memorizing lecture slides. Pop quizzes at least once a week, and two 5-8 page case study papers on two different books.

Some of the essay prompts were confusing but prof was really open to taking feedback about them and encouraged it. I learned a lot in this class that goes far past just this specific course's content, it's applicable in a lot of different ways. Honestly think anyone who wants to do psych work should take this course.

I took LSWA 125 for my writing requirement freshman year and this was easily my favorite (and easiest) class and professor. Chris gives amazing feedback on essays and projects and wants his students to succeed. He is usually a very light grader and gives very open project and essay guidelines giving you a lot of freedom.

Chris was easily my favorite professor I have had so far. He is so kind and I was always excited to go to class. I took Writing 160 food for thought and he made the class so fun that I considered getting a minor in writing so I could keep taking his classes. 10000% recommend, the class was so easy and a really interesting place to be.

Chris is incredibly caring and super supportive of his students. His class allows you to create projects you are passionate about and receive thoughtful feedback and encouragement. Readings for class can get long but are always interesting. I could not more highly recommend taking a course with Chris, easily my favorite professor I've had so far.
love, love, LOVE Professor Crowder. If you have a chance to take a FYWR with him, take it. You will not regret it. One of the kindest and most fun professors here.

Professor Crowder was one of my favorite professors I took my Freshman year at UMich. The readings before class were optional, but they were honestly interesting and added so much to the lesson the next day if you had the spare time to look at them. Overall, amazing guy and fun teacher. 100% recommend, and would love to take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really sweet guy!! class is super easy, the easiest out of all the lswa classes in my experience. the readings are a lot but they are genuinely interesting and it's pretty easy to bluff your way through it. i didn't have time to read the last half of the semester and was totally fine. very chill grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I would 100% recommend Chris's LSWA class to everyone. He's very chill and cares a lot about his students. The course load isn't bad either since it's mostly just readings.

This class is mostly led by students, we only really see Sara during our first meeting, and when she monitored one of our seminars to see how we're doing. But overall, I highly recommend this class, it was a real blast having those close discussions with other classmates. The homework shouldn't be as bad, if you're fine with reading long passages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: ALA 122 is a great class! There was a lot of reading listed, but I didn't do much of it and still got an A. Sara is an awesome professor who really cares about her students. Highly recommend ALA 122 for getting those social science distribution credits. super easy class, very worthwhile

ALA122 is a student-led dialogue class, but their training came from Sara. It would be practically impossible not to get an A in this class (really, everyone would finish with a 100 if the IGR program wasn't against giving out an A+). Sara assigned the readings for this class, and planned the activities, and nothing was too challenging.

Sara has been probably one of the most inspirational lecturers at UMich. Despite my major not falling under the social sciences, I really enjoyed her class of ALA 220, and I would strongly recommend taking it with her. The skills and knowledge from this course I will carry into my future career.

Sara struggled with many of the things I've seen on other reviews this semester (getting grades back in a timely fashion, having readings and announcements posted in a timely fashion before class). I think the pandemic and online class exacerbated this and it was a struggle at the end. She's a lovely person. But I had way better profs

Overall I like Sara. She is very passionate about what she teaches and she is honestly very nice. If you read her other reviews from Eastern, she is scattered & do not expect to get your grades back. Those that you do receive, she is a tough grader. Participation does matter. Just do the readings and put some effort in & you'll be fine

Super funny in class. Office hours with him can be a little scary. He is quick to correct you on everything, which can be frustrating, but comes from a place of care. Homework can get overwhelming, but it's manageable altogether. He's very passionate, involved in his students, and opinionated. I learned a lot from him, both in Spanish and more!

Cristhian is interesting and I learned a lot about economics from him, but he gets frustrated easily during office hours if you don't understand him right away. He got me interested in something that I had already wanted to explore. Challenging, but informative. Take Indigenous Activism in the Age of Globalization if you can!

I've had two classes w/ Cristhian, and he's one of the professors who genuinely cares. He meets every student where they're at and is great w/ email & office hrs. He works very hard to create good class discussion, so participation & engagement matter a lot. You're held accountable, but he's invested in your success, so just put in the work.

Cristhian is an extremely interesting professor. He facilitated fascinating discussions that challenged me to think analytically in a way I haven't previously. His participation expectations will initially seem high, but as long as you are actively engaged and contributing to discussion you will be fine. I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Great professor - he grades very tough in RCLANG 294 but it definitely prepares you for proficiency. He is very accessible for office hours and I never had difficulty contacting him. If you put in the effort, you will be rewarded. He cares about his students and their progress - go to office hours and get to know him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cristhian is easily one of my favorite professors. He will bend over backwards to make himself available to you if you need help with the class or are struggling with the material. If you don't like him or got a bad grade you probably suck at Spanish and have terrible political opinions and that's your fault not his.

he sucked. worst teacher ever. i have never taken a professor who was so unclear, so rude, not understanding of students' needs, who gave so much work, was so blind about college life, and so poor with tehcnology. i got a good grade and hated him despite that. do yourself a favor and never take a class taught by cristhian.

Cristhian is easily the best professor I had for my first semester at UM - he absolutely wants everyone to succeed and ensures that he is accessible outside of class for any concerns. He emphasized the importance of taking care of ourselves and simply putting in effort to succeed. Great teacher; you have to put in the effort though to earn it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He has strong opinions and grades ruthlessly, but I've never had a professor challenge me and improve my abilities as much as he did. He would read my entire essay drafts in office hours and give supportive feedback. By participating and really getting to know him in OH, I think he gained a mutual respect for my efforts and gave me the A+.

Cristhian was definitely one of the nicest professors I've ever had. I was really intimidated by him at first- he does come off as kind of authoritarian - but he's kind and supportive and very helpful if you go to office hours. He's very intelligent & doesn't get paid enough for all the work he does. He's opinionated, but it makes class interesting

Christian was very opinionated & I frequently found myself feeling like I was getting a worse grade than I deserved because the content of my work went against what he believed. Plus, the criteria for grading was not clear, which heightened that feeling of an unjust grade because he had no real justification for the grades except his own opinion.
He's so opinionated and makes me never want to take Spanish again. Makes you feel like an idiot if you don't fully understand the content or think exactly what he does. Spare yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cristhian is by far the best RC Spanish professor I have had during the intensive program.  He is ridiculously overqualified and makes sure to engage with the students, and he uses videos and presentations in addition to the coursepack to keep class interesting.  I absolutely loved his class, I think it's the best one I've taken at the University.

Christian is a great Professor, he is easily able to teach what is necessary and often does so in an unorthodox but effective manner. He helped me grow not just as a student but also as a person. The only drawback is that he is highly opinionated, but this stimulates interesting discussion

Very partial towards students as well as unfair and opinionated. I took his review class and passed the proficiency exam with very high scores, yet he wrote a very nasty commentary on my transcript simply for not showing up to his (apparently not optional) office hours, and being late to class a couple times.

I dreaded going to this class everyday. I absolutely felt uncomfortable speaking in class. He's clearly opinonated and while we're both on the same side of the political spectrum, I felt that his opinions ruined objective discussions. He only chose weaker students to answer questions leaving the rest of us not to improve. Didn't enjoy

Christhian is a compassionate and enthusiastic professor. Makes himself available to students, very helpful for papers/projects/understanding. Fascinating curriculum, n although he has strong political opinions he's accepting/open. He engages each student during discussion, there is mandatory participation but its helpful. Weekly reading necessary.

Loved the PALMA class and highly recommend it. Readings are interesting and applicable, class is small (we had 7) which makes for good discussion, and tutoring is a valuable experience. You can tell Cristhian enjoys teaching this class, and wants you to take away real life lessons from it. I wish I would have started with PALMA sooner.

Christhian is one of those professors that people love or hate. I don't know if he should be teaching a review course, because I really felt like we weren't reviewing anything and instead just discussing different political issues. Also. Go to his office hours. A lot.

Cristhian is a very difficult professor to get along with for many people. He will give you a good grade if you go to office hours a lot and participate, but he is very authoritarian and difficult to talk to.

Be prepared to read. Didn't like the way he conducted discussion too much- it seemed like he was very opinionated on the issues discussed. Still, the readings are somewhat interesting if you're a Poly Sci/History major. The workload really isn't that bad: 3 4-5pg papers, you get re-writes on 2. Nice + helpful, go to office hours before papers.

Cristhian is a nice enough guy, but pretty unhelpful.  If you're having difficulty in the class, be prepared to have to figure out everything on your own.  Grammar explanations are not the clearest, but office hours help.  Expects you to talk a lot, especially about political and environmental issues.  If you're not interested in those, good luck!

Christhian is a nice guy, but he doesn't always have great explanations for complicated grammatical rules. He is extremely feminist and expects you to be outspoken about women and minority rights. Very political but very cool and overall a very good teacher.
mmm...he is so smart AND so sexy!
No Comments
Great professor, he helped us learn many new words in Spanish and was very helpful overall.

His exams are not bad at all and very straightforward if you put in time outside of class to understand the concepts (reading textbook and slides together helped). He is also nice and funny and his accent is not too bad.
Good prof, the rumors about his accent are not an issue at all, he's very easy to understand and even helpful outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, I have nothing against Javier like I do with the Sleepy Joe of the Econ Department (aka Rabbit aka Chris Proulx). His accent that people complain about isn't an issue at all. He's clear and on point and on topic. The content in 402 isn't the easiest so that may be why ppl complain. He does trip over cables in lecture a lot though

Reviews here are too harsh. Dr. Cravino is a solid professor for ECON 402. His accent isn't too bad, and he is more than happy to repeat himself or speak slower if asked. He has a good sense of humor and organizes his class very well. The only downside was having to turn in the 3 HW assignments in-person and on paper at discussion. Exams were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Came on here just to leave him a good review. I don't understand the hate at all :( He's a good lecturer, accent is not difficult to understand, he cares about his students, and his exams are extremely fair. Exam content is the same format as the lecture slides. As someone who did not enjoy 401 with Proulx, 402 with Cravino was SO much better.

Cravino is over hated. He teaches clearly, except when he skips over the algebra when solving a problem. His exams are for the most part made up of problems that are very similar to the practice psets and exams, so those are your best bet for studying. Graded homeworks are just time killers, but pretty interesting if you're paying attention.

All exams, including the final, took at least 10 days to be graded. Answer keys/practice problems generally skipped many steps of algebra. He cares about his students, but sends students to Piazza, where responses take days.
Even with an A+, I dislike Javier for the course organization rather than his instruction methods (which was also poor).

Totally agree that the reviews are too harsh, he's fine. People saying this class is the worst are the same people saying proulx was the worst because they expect to be spoon fed the material to get a good grade. but in all honesty, this class is not hard. As long as you pay attention and have a remote grasp of macro economics, you'll be just fine

I created a Rate my Professor account just so I could give Professor Cravino a five out of five. He is one of the funniest and most insightful professors I have ever had. He does move math quite quickly, but he is more than willing to slow down and repeat if asked. His office hours are especially helpful, even if you don't have specific questions.

This class is not hard at all lol. legit just pay attention. people crying about it being math and formula heavy maybe shouldn't be studying economics at a prestigious university. go back to 6th grade and practice your y=mx+b

Respectfully, he is easily the worst professor I've ever had. The way umich has him teaching a CORE econ class is insane. Lectures are unclear. Hes disorganized. Seems like a nice and smart dude but that doesn't make you capable of teaching such an important class. Macro shouldn't have to be this hard💀
Going from one math formula to another, never caring about the economy, full of math formulas. I don't really think these formulas help us in any way, except for the exam
if you have to take this class just wait till the next semester and take it with the other professor

Professor doesn't post actually problem set questions like all other econ professors homework is graded on correctness and discussions are confusing because he refuses to post discussion handouts or show the questions. Lectures are also not recorded
Had him for my 402 discussion and he was actually wonderful! I thought the class was so easy when you had him outside of class. Exams were very fair!

I think Professor Cravino is extremely knowledgeable about the topics and seems like a very nice person. With that said, the formulas were often a bit confusing and unclear, and it was sometimes difficult to understand where he was getting certain equations. I cannot emphasize this enough: DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS/HOMEWORK, they are super helpful.
Eventhough I god A+, I still want to say DONT TAKE HIS COURSE! His lecture and material will negatively influence your understading. You shoould and you can only depend on yourself in his course.

Genuinely cannot emphasize this enough, please do not take this course with him. The equations used (which are pretty much the whole exams) are never really made explicitly clear to us and you're expected to know them off the top of your head which simply isn't possible. He also will not return your emails at all, so don't even bother trying.
The class is horribly graded and he is really hard to understand. Take 402 when there is a different professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buddy pulls equations out of thin air. Kids are paying 70k annually in tuition but that's still not enough for Javier to include lecture recordings. Horrible slides that lack info. Messy chicken scratch jumping from equation to equation without explaining steps. Do not take 402 with Javier
The worst econ professor I have met. The only one who can compete with him is Nancy Kimelman (Try to search her name on rmp).
Nice guy who is clear with his formulas. The topics are just hard to understand.

Despite his accent is bad, his slides are pretty clear with important formula highlighted. You just need to look at problem sets and practice exam to pass the exam. The best way to learn is to mark down all the formulas. Exams are very easy and curves are pretty nice. Easy A

Came into this class expecting the worst judging from his reviews here but he actually isn't a bad prof by any means. He explains concepts in a fairly good way and his lectures are better than most econ classes. My main complaint is the lack of assignments leading to the final being cumulative and 45% of the semester grade, which is simply unfair.

Prof Cravino gets terrible reviews on this sight for no good reason in my eyes. He outlines the expectations for his class clearly, weekly problem sets/ practice midterms prepare you for the relatively easy exams and he is a funny, chill dude. If you keep up with what he provides you WILL do well in this class. Don’t listen to the nonsense
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I agree that old reviews do not do Cravino justice today. His accent is not that scary and he explains key concepts repeatedly in lectures and discussion sections. Problem sets prepare you well for the exams. He tries hard to help students to learn economics. He does not elicit the "wow" factor like some other professors, but he is a solid choice.

A lot of people give prof. Cravino undeserved hell on this site. I quite enjoyed this class despite being worried as f that I was going to fail miserably based on what I had heard about him. Does go a bit fast with the math & theory at the beginning of the course, but if you do the practice problems you will do fine on the exams.

All the reviews are from several semesters ago, he's gotten a lot better and his accent really isn't as bad as people make it out to be. Econ classes are just boring and Cravino does his best to make it engaging.

Came here inspired to review my first professor simply because of how enraged his homework made me. Although extremely easy, the monotony and repetitiveness had me almost emailing to ask what the point of all this useless busy work was. Honestly, for the core of a "high ranked econ program", this class is a mess and the professor cant public speak!

He's just awful. That's really all there is to say. I did fine in his class. This class isn't incredibly challenging; in many ways 401 is more difficult. But this professor just sucks. He's the worst teacher I've ever had. This is a person that just shouldn't be teaching. Don't take a class with him.

Cravino had a tough time teaching the lecture but was much better in office hours. The class is honestly straight forward with some sections being much harder than others. Have to take if you're an econ major so just make the most of it.

Honestly, Cravino is the same if not better than other UMich Econ profs. While lectures are boring, all of the necessary info is given to you. Exams are almost exactly like the practice ones he gives you, and going through and doing the recommended HW while exam prepping helps, too. Discussions are great! If you study for the exams, you'll be fine.

Terribly unclear and confusing lecture slides, frequent typos in the answers he provides for homework problems, and he often seems unprepared and unknowledgeable of the concepts he is lecturing on. Frequently stammering and hesitating as he lectures which, coupled with his strong Spanish accent, makes his lectures incomprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Javier was a good professor. A lot of people complained about him but if you pay attention in class and took notes, you wont have a problem with the exams. I enjoyed the class. At times, he also has good anecdotes.

When you first meet him his accent is kinda scary, but either I got used to it or he became more comfortable because it's a non-issue. The class is hard because the material is hard, which you should expect since this and 401 are the basis for everything you learn as a econ major. Easy target to complain if you struggle in the class, but its on you

Good 'ol Javier probably should not be teaching this class. He routinely comes to class unprepared and struggles through reading the information that is on the slides. The exams are difficult due to the lack of example problems in class and they include wildly hard applications of theory. Highly recommend different teacher

I am offensive and I find this Spanish! Yep, this guy is teaching Spanish in his Econ lectures. Buy 1 Get 1 Free you know? You pay for a 3-credit course and you end up learning both Econ402 and Spanish101! Worth!

Professor Cravino gets a bad rap, because his tests are very tough, but honestly he teaches you in a  way that actually allows you to understand the economic THEORY, as opposed to so many professors who just isolate select examples. I rarely do well in economics classes, but I did well in large part because of how Professor Cravino taught.
I walked out of the class, more confused about macroeconomics than ever. He's the most misleading, confusing lecturer I've ever had the misfortune to have at UM. Avoid Avoid Avoid. At all costs! Duh!
#NeverForget
I absolutely would wish this upon my worst enemy.
HE RUINS MY TRANSCRIPT!

Probably the single worst professor I have ever taken. He is an embarrassment to the economics department, and for that matter the University of Michigan. Aside from his thick accent, stuttering, and mumbling. he was totaling a completely disorganized. His lecture slides were incomprehensible and overwhelmingly vague. U of M students deserve better

Just simply avoid. Impossibly confusing slides, his accent makes him exceedingly hard to understand. Furthermore, the exams were very hard, and the class grade was  based solely on exams (2 midterms 25% each; Final exam 50%). Exam material and format was very different than both lecture slides and homework questions.
Nooo!!!

Avoid him at all costs! The worst class I have ever taken. No specific guideline to follow. Lectures have no organization. Cravino has zero confidence as a lecturer. I had no idea what language he was speaking. Can't believe the university hired him to teach 402. No wonder UM's reputation for Econ dept is as bad as it can get. Next!
oof.

Definitely unorganized with his lectures, homeworks, and exams.  Pretty bad lecturer.  Yes the accent is bad, but what's worse is his lack of clarity with everything he explains.  He blazes through slides without explaining anything and when asked about a slide he says "oh, yes, that's a good question" then mumbles and nods.  Avoid at all costs.
Never and ever and ever and ever and ever take this class!

I'm disappointed in the University's lack of discernment when choosing to hire Javier Cravino. Just because someone has a PhD does NOT mean they know how to teach well. I walk out of his lectures understanding absolutely nothing. Slides are useless and contain little info  useful for the exam. Oh, and the final is cumulative and 50% of our grade...
Way over my head, I didn't realize that passing Econ 402 also required a comprehensive background in Spanish and stutter.
He's terrible. Should not be teaching an Economics 400 level course that is part of our major's core curriculum fresh out of graduate school.

The worst professor I have had at Umich. Although I do not want to fault him for his thick accent, when in combination with stuttering, mumbling, and completely disorganized lectures, it has made this class extremely difficult. Avoid taking 402 with this professor at all costs.

Lectures are extremely unclear and hard to follow because of his accent. Slides are unnecessary hard and disorganized to interpret. If you want to succeed in the class make sure you read all the House Notes on ctools and the textbook before even trying to understand the slides. A good understanding of graphs is essential for a good grade.
He really tries his best. He's just young. This class is not fit for someone who wants to get an easy A!

Go to class and READ THE BOOK. He's clearly a very smart guy but not a very engaging lecturerteacher-- that doesn't mean you can't do well. Compared to what I've heard about 402 classes in the past, his exams are much more fair and look a lot like the problem sets (which are optional, but you should really do them).
If I could give him 0, I would.

He is a nice guy, and clearly a very gifted economist.  But when it comes down to it, he just has no idea how to teach.  He is hard to understand, his lecture slides are unhelpful at best, and he explains very little, and assumes we just "know" most of his mathematics.  You NEED to seek out lots of help to do well.  Look elsewhere for a 402 prof.

Avoid taking this class with him. Inexperienced, heavy accent, stutters a lot. He seems smart but teaching is not where he belongs. This is the only Econ class I've had where the final is cumulative, which is absurd. Lectures are boring and he doesn't seem willing to go out of his way to help students outside of class.

Real talk, look up "Salvador Perez interview" on youtube. The first result is how lectures are. Look, I know it's not his fault his English is bad, but I literally can't understand what he is trying to say. You learn nothing from class. I have no reason to think he's anything but a great, intelligent guy, but he's woefully out of place as a prof.
Extremely ridiculous of the University to assign a fresh out of PhD school student  from a foriegn country to a 400 level core class.

I tried to give him a chance, but at this point the consensus is clear. He has a VERY rigid grading scale. He refuses to use a curve based on exam results and instead has a set curve system with rigid % ranges to get a certain letter grade. Despite horrible exam 1 results as a result of his teaching, he says "it's only 25% of your grade!" ONLY. Ha.

By far the worst lecturer I have had. No structure to his lecture slides or the course material for that matter. Course grade is based on 3 tests (25% midterm 1, 25% midterm 2 and 50% final) which makes the course that much harder. If you are not an Econ major, don't take this class, if you are an Econ major, DONT TAKE 402 WITH CRAVINO!

So irresponsible of the university to have this professor for a core upper-level econ class. Expect Incoherent lectures and terribly made lecture slides. For both midterms, there has been 1 practice exam each and big parts of both practice exams (full multi-part problems) weren't to be used until the next exams giving us even less practice...

By far the worst Econ class I have taken at UofM so far. Poor lecturer, zero confidence, disorganized slides, stutters and mumbles a lot (not going to complain about his accent although it makes everything worse). 401 and 402 are extremely important for the remainder of the Econ degree, so how UMich has a prof like Cravino teaching 402 amazes me.

I've taken some really bad Econ classes at the college, but this one tops them all. His lectures are so shockingly bad and misleading that it's really hard to keep up with what's going on in class. I've never hated Econ, but this class makes me despair. Also, he refuses to meet outside the class and is very unaccomodating to students' needs.

A combination of disorganized lecture slides, stuttering and a heavy accent makes following him in lecture extremely difficult. All the math and graphing explanations were very poor and he makes simple concepts seem more confusing. He doesn't have the experience or confidence to teach such an important class in the Econ department.

Very difficult class. He spends time deriving complex growth equations on unorganized and difficult to follow lecture slides while stuttering through the entirety of his explanations. Little use of graphs makes it hard to understand what is actually going on in these growth models. I have barely learned anything while taking this class.

I literally can understand 5 out of every 10 words he says. he says agents as "Asians." Making things worse, his slides have no organization and he flips through extraneous algebra that we learned how to do in the eight grade. Also, looks 12 years old but has a PhD last year. Why is he teaching us? Or anyone for that matter?

I literally couldn't believe what I was hearing in class. His accent is so heavy that if you were not gifted in Spanish back in high school, I highly recommend taking 200-level Spanish in college before taking this Econ class (and 80% of the time he stutters, which doesn't help at all). Also, the lecture slides are confusing and unorganized.

Professor Csaszar is nice, but his lectures were boring. I had another strategy prof at Ross and he was much more interactive and engaging, and he seemed better at encouraging students to expand on their ideas while helping them understand their limitations. Maybe it's unfair that I'm comparing the 2, but prof Csaszar didn't meet my expectations.
Excellent class.  Made difficult and dry concepts simple. would love to take another class with him.

Professor Csaszar was excellent. He's a tough grader, but his lectures are efficient, on point, and thorough. He was able to cut through clutter and direct the course to the essence of the material. I highly recommend taking a course with him.
Best professor at U of M
Best professor at UofM. Really clear lectures, interesting readings.
Well, I love Felipe's instruction during offie hours.  He make me interested in world economy.  A must-take
I found her lectures to be better than Chapman's. I thought both of her exams were fair. Overall, a solid professor. Exams were difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She seems like a very nice person, however, I ended up doing much better Chapman's half of the course.
