The test avg for Chapman was anywhere from 72-75, whereas Exam 3 (w her) the class average was 68%. You can tell she loves teaching what she does, however, she goes WAY too fast and taking notes was a pain.

She only taught the latter half of the course so it was a slight adjustment. I did like that her lectures were more organized & cohesive, and she didn't linger on any topic longer than needed. Take good notes during lecture! Answered questions in class well and clearly stated what to know for exams. Gave extra credit bc class averages were too low.

Dr. C is a kind and caring professor. I never had a problem understanding her or felt she went too fast in lecture, like others have said. Lectures are recorded anyways. She explained concepts well and pointed out important info. Pay attention to the lectures, do the practice exams + problem roulette. We were allowed to have cheat sheets for exams.

Professor C did an amazing job in the second half of 172. Her and Chapman worked really well together and I think made 172 as easy as possible, but no matter what it took a lot of outside of lecture studying for me. Lectures move fast, sometimes they allow you a cheat sheet on exams which was a saving grace.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 417 was the best course I took in the MCDB program. More than chromosome structure and remodeling, Dr. Csankovszki gave valuable instruction and practice in extracting the important details of research papers. Her group work-focused class structure far exceeds the quality of many paper-based upper-level MCDB courses. Great professor.

Dr. Csankovszki was very interested in the material she taught. Reading the textbook was entirely optional. My major complaint is that she moved very fast. If you get lost in a lecture the rest of that lecture made no sense. When you were able to keep up, she was very clear and makes a lot of sense. Lecture recordings are your friend with her.

Prof C was really cool! Although she went through slides fast, she explained everything thoroughly. She used iClicker questions heavily to make sure we were understanding the content throughout the lectures. You can tell she is very passionate about biology. If you put in the work to understand, you'll succeed.
Once you overcome her heavy accent and how fast she talks, professor Csankovszki was actually not too bad. Her exams can sometimes very hard and other times easy.

Dr. C is clearly very knowledgeable about biology, and I enjoyed getting to take BIO 172 from her! Paying attention in lecture is a must (she moves very quickly), but as long as you take the class seriously and put in the work, you will be very successful in this class.
Very clear on explanations

I recommend taking BIO172 with Professor Csankovszki! Even though this class covers challenging content, she was a clear lecturer. I found going to her office hours to be really helpful during the second half of the class especially.
Prof. C is a great lecturer and made the course super engaging! She is very caring and accessible and overall a great professor.
She was such a great teacher. She made my experience in biology here a great one.

Professor C lectured for the second half of Bio 172, which was definitely more complex material. She can be a little monotone when lecturing and I found myself not retaining a lot after watching the lectures, but her problem solving sessions and the post-lecture quizzes really helped alleviate this. Exams were fair based on lecture content.

I had her as an online teacher and thought she was great. She teaches kind of fast so that may suck when in person lectures start again but for online it was fine. She's very clear and concise and the only things on the slides show up on the test. It's a tough course if you don't pay attention but it's definitely doable.

Prof C. is great at explaining concepts in lecture, better than Chapman in my opinion. Her problem solving sessions are also super helpful, and her tests are pretty hard but not impossible to do well on.

Theres nothing on the exam thats not on the lecture slides- this is really how I get through this class with full marks on final. Just attend lecture or watch lecture recordings, multiple times if you can.

She is a very nice and empathetic woman, but these qualities do not transfer into the exams and lectures. She rushes to get all the content in, and the exams are much harder than any of the content taught. Hours of studying yield disappointment.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Csankovski is a rougher take on BIO172. She doesn't review exams and see how the students were doing and goes very fast in lectures. I wish I could watch her in .5 speed

One of my favorite sciences courses I have taken at U of M. Csankovszki is an incredible lecturer, very caring, and grades fairly. I've learned so much in this course and she is so helpful; I highly recommend it.

Really great and clear lecturer. She is extremely intelligent, kind, and wants students to understand. She explained everything that would be on the tests, however it was still a very difficult course. She packed a lot of information into each lecture and the tests were hard.

I'm sure she is a very nice person. However, her teaching style did not correspond with my learning style so I did not do well. I tried my best but she goes through slides very quickly and the tests are extremely hard. you have to make every concept like your own to do well
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gyorgyi is a very by-the-book professor; she is thorough but goes through lectures very fast and doesnt explain difficult concepts that well

Csankovszki is a very nice woman overall, I highly recommend going to her office hours because you can really tell how much she cares about her students. With that being said, the exams are way too difficult for the amount of preparation that is given in lecture. Also, the discussion sections cram way too much important exam info into 1 1/2 hours
She talks very fast about boring topics. It is hard to stay focused. Most classes I ended up shopping on Amazon to stay awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She seems really intimidating at first but opened up as the class went on. She turned out to be pretty funny even though she's better at being serious. Great at answering questions and interacting with students during lecture. Very fast paced lectures, but gets material covered in timely manner

Gyorgi is very nice and a good lecturer. Please don't waste your time doing the reading, she's always saying "your textbook goes too in depth, here's what I want you to know". Anyone could get an A, as it really is just memorization. Make sure you know the lecture slides, and you'll do well. I find her exams to be more straightforward than Chapmans

Gyorgyi is a great professor! She is really nice and explained concepts very well. She was always clear about what we needed to know for the exams and they were very representative of her lectures. Would definitely take a class with her again!
She's a great lecturer and very accessible in office hours. Very clear explanation. If you are not a genius and generally work very hard, go to her lecturers. It will be a good choice.

Took Gyorgyi for the second half of Bio 172. Shes passionate about what she does, and I personally did better on Gyrogyi's half of the class. Her exams were somewhat more straight forward to me in comparison to Chapman's first half of class. Regardless, youre going to have to put in work for Bio 172.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Csankovszki has a passion for biology! She can sometimes be difficult to understand and her lecture slides can be unclear but they're not terrible. She posts 3 practice exams with keys which is very helpful. She also allows unlimited tries to get a 3/3 on the quizzes due before each lecture. Use Piazza, it helps!
Gyorgyi talks VERY fast and just reads right off the slides. I would rewatch every lecture after to retake notes

There's a lot of reading in this class, but if you follow the path that Gyorgyi lays out, you don't have to read that much of it. Just pay attention to the lectures, she does a really good job of organizing them in a way that makes sense. Exams are hard because there's so much information to cover but they're fair. Just make sure to keep up with it

Gyorgyi taught the second half of my course (last 2 exams). She can be funny and presents the material well. very passionate about her work. All powerpoints end up online. Exams are tough because multiple choice are worth 4 pts each.

I took 172 with Chapman for 12 of the semester, and Gyorgyi for the second half. Compared to Chapman, Gyorgyi's lectures are very organized. She covers a lot of material each lecture, so make sure you're paying attention. My one suggestion is to go to office hours. She is extremely helpful, nice, and you can tell she cares about her students.

She's very approachable and her exams are far easier than Dr. Chapman's. Her material is more intensive and requires more effort to learn. However, if you put in the effort you will get a lot out of BIO 172 and do well.
Professor Gyorgyi was a bit more clear than professor Chapman, but the exams were still really really tough. REMEMBER TO STUDY YOUR BUTT OFF!

Dr. Csankovszki was an amazing teacher. She gets straight to the point. Her half of the class is harder material-wise, but the tests were at the same difficulty as Chapman's. The class itself is just not an easy class whatsoever. Don't skip out on discussionlecturehomework points, no reason not to get full points which will really help your grade

Professor Csankovszki was great.  Her lectures were straight forward, and exams were clear and fair.  Make sure you get the "gimme" points where you can, by keeping up with the quizzes and getting full credit for lectures.  I did well on exams, but neglecting those gimme points really hurt me in the end.  There's no such thing as an "Easy A."

This class is hard, but not impossible. I think her exams were much better than Dr. Chapman's, but her teaching style is very confusing. Her slides didn't really include any information so you would have to listen the lecture online over and over again. However, since her exams were much clearer I got much better grades on the second half.

Dr. C is definitely a better lecturer than Chapman hands down. Her PPTs are a lot more organized and pretty clear. For the people that say her exams are harder, it's not true. It's just that the material she covers is harder and a lot more dense than Chapman's.   Put in the time, and you'll do fine. Overall great professor, kind and super helpful

She was a great professor and definitely knew what she was talking about. Her lectures were specific at times yet interesting, and she tried to relate to the students. Kind, funny, and helpful. Her exams were not that bad and the multiple choice questions were more straightforward than Chapman's. Would definitely recommend!
Her lectures are a lot more boring than Chapman's and her tests are much more difficult. I ended up skipping about half of her lectures because they didn't keep me engaged at all.

She is definitely a better lecturer than Chapman, as she explains things much more clearly. However, the exams are much more difficult, which I did not think was possible after Chapman's exams. I've taken 300-level classes with less challenging exams. It's as if they intend to fail you.

Her lectures are not very clear, and she doesn't explain things fully, and leaves out very crucial details. She is pretty helpful, and an overall nice person; however, she doesn't come across as a good teacher.

Gyorgyi writes extremely difficult exams as everybody had pointed out. You will really learn a lot from her though. The material for her part is more dense than for Chapman's part. She is nice and is willing to help you out when you approach her.

Prof. Gyorgyi may be a very hard prof., but you will learn a lot from her. Although she may not look like it from the outside, she is very nice and helpful if you go to office hours. Exams are very difficult, but are fair for the most part.
Class is hard in general. Her exams are MUCH harder than Chapman's. However, you will learn a lot from her.

She's nice and you will learn a lot from her, but like everybody said, her exams are designed to trick you rather than to make sure you understand big ideas. The class makes it very easy to lose points - and you can only lose so many to get an A-. Getting a B is very doable, but to get an A you really need to do a ton.

Yeah she's not an easy professor, but she's not as bad as some people are making her sound. Exams are hard and sometimes ambiguous, but are reflective of lecture material. She does want people to do well.

This class is hard no matter who your professor is. However, she is a professor who actually wants you to do well. She may not look like it from the outside, but if you go to office hours she is very approachable. Exams are hard, but if you put in the expected effort, you will come out alright.

She seems like she really wants her students to do well but this is just a hard class, and a lot of the time there isn't anything you can do to make the material more interesting so lectures can be very boring. Be ready to put in a LOT of time if you want to get an A, but a B is pretty easily attainable.

Gyorgyi may not be the warmest professor I've ever had but she wants you to understand the material and her lectures are straightforward. Exams aren't easy but if you study the lecture slides and pay attention you should be fine. Overall I enjoyed her and the class!
Her exams are very tricky and questions are sometimes ambiguous, but you will learn a lot from her.

Dr. Csankovszki is one of the best professors on campus! Her class is by no means easy... but she makes the material interesting and tries her best to clarify the material. Regardless of the grade received, you will finish her class with a greater understanding of chromatin, and in general, reading scientific papers!

Great teacher. I highly recommend taking this class as your CMB/Biochem/Neuroscience elective. I put in a little effort through the course and pulled out an A. I made sure to go over my proposal topic with her though--this is important. Great class and approachable teacher.
She flew through the material and took little time to explain important concepts.  Exams were very difficult and designed to trick you.  Did not care about student success.

I am determined that she has no soul.  They will never look at you as a student, but as a number because of the size of the class and she is determined to do as little for the student as possible.  Do not take this class ever for any reason.

Although she is very knowledgeable about the topics, her exams were very difficult. They attempted to trick you instead of making sure you knew the information. I would not recommend taking this class with her.
Fantastic professor. She presented the material in an order that built upon itself. Taught us to focus on the important ideas and not get caught up in the minor details.
Very helpful, very clear in lecture.  I think she does a really good job and she's certainly not a professor to avoid.
Her exams were not hard and were always 100% representative of the material covered. I wish she taught the whole term

Awesome class! Shes very dedicated to making her students do well, and she genuinely cares. You can also tell she is clearly passionate about the material. Take it if you get a chance...you learn a lot! If you work hard, there is no reason you shouldn't do well.

yea, shes very strict...and she cant teach some of the things (like Ac/Ds), and her HW/tests/PSAs are REALLY hard (68% average on her exam). EVERYONE hates her. However, after going to her office hours, I changed my mind abt her, because I really felt like she wanted to help me and make sure that I understand what she teaches...shes VERY nice

She is clearly very intelligent, and she uses class time very well, but she sometimes doesn't go into detail. if you can't attend office hours ur screwed.  exams are extremely hard, they are TRYING to trick you, not test your knowledge... If you have to take it, take a light course load with it. she is better than the guy who teaches in the fall

She really wants students to succeed. If you go to her office hours she will clarify any question. Very nice and approachable. I never opened my textbook and still got an A based on only going to lecture.

I would strongly recommend attending lectures, or at least finding someone who does in order to copy the notes on the slides. The tests are very hard, but with good preparation it is possible to do well. She's probably one of the better genetics profs, and she's fair.
csankovszki is VERY nice in person, if you go to her office hours she will go overtime to help you out.  warning: exams are impossible!

She seems to be very nice and thorough when it comes to helping students. Usually, this class does not have any curves beyond the additional 5 pts/exam but she added a curve to the last exam! Thanks to her, my grade is saved...don't take this class unless a)you have to or b)you love studying.
good teacher
Homework is very light. Very helpful office hours. Slides are awesome.

Perhaps Usher was better in the past, but essentially teaching is to load a lot of information in slides and walk you through practice problems. I had trouble staying awake, and tho I did well I don't feel like I have a good understanding of thermo or relativity. To succeed, just cram all practice problems a week before 45% weighted final exam

Class was super interesting but there are problemslike the fact that the final is worth 45% of the grade. The homework aremultiple choice easy questions. His lectures can get boring since he reads off walls of text and it is really hard to stay awake in his lectures. Overall he is pretty good. Only take this class if you are good at test taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class for fun and it paid off. Very funny and smart professor. Lectures flew by with him teaching them, but they were very content-heavy. It's smart to attend class, that's what really helped me out along the way! Make sure to do the practice problems at the end of the slides if you still don't get the material. Overall, highly recommend!

Prof Uher is a legend. He's obviously extremely intelligent and everything is trivially easy to him, but he genuinely tries to bring himself down to our level to help us understand.
Sometimes the lectures are a bit dry but the slides are quite helpful and clearly show what concepts and equations are crucial for the exam. All in all, a good prof!

Lecture style is reading huge paragraphs on slides talking through book explanations/example problems, so some explanations on hard concepts left some understanding to be desired. Doesn't answer questions well, so you're better off looking it up later. Two tests are 70% of your grade which is very unforgiving for small mistakes. Easy class overall.

Lectures dominated by slides. Content that I had been taught prior was taught in a confusing way. It could have been taught better. Still, the information was straightforward and accurate. HW and exams have multiple choice questions, meaning single questions are worth 2% of your final grade, e.g. Exam questions were always HW or example problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: absolutely legendary
This prof is a legend.

Professor Uher is so passionate about physics and is great at explaining the concepts. The exams are challenging if you do not look over ALL the sample exams he gives you. Best physics 140 professors.

Amazing professor. Take him if you have the chance! He definitely makes a difficult course more manageable. Exams are difficult but if you do extra book problems in addition to the assigned ones, you should be fine.

Uher is one of those professors that you can tell is super smart, but you would also like to have a beer with him. If you have him for 140, he'll go through the derivations of basically every formula and concept. Unfortunately, everything seems trivially easy to him, so he doesn't understand when kids are slow to pick up some concepts.

You can get away only coming to class on iClicker days and barely doing the homework for a little bit but I learned the hard way that you get left behind quickly. Most of his lectures are example problems. He makes everything easy to understand and his handwriting is beautiful! Make sure you understand the homework (not graded) and practice tests

I took physics 140 first semester of freshman year with professor Uher and I really enjoyed it. I would highly recommend him. He is a good lecturer and definitely go to office hours. They are very helpful and he is pretty funny.

Really great professor and as far as I know, probably the best or one of the best professors for physics 140. He definitely knows his stuff and does a great job teaching it, it's merely up to you if you choose to attend lectures and attentively listen. He does have a european accent, however,  he's still very clear.

Prof. Uher is helpful both in class and during office hours! He really cares about his students and help them in anyway he can. He explains things mathematically which I found really useful. Also, his reviews are great for test preparations.

This was a deceptively hard class. Professor Uher is an okay professor in my eyes. His lecture style is kind of fast and he writes on the blackboard to solve problems. I wasn't very good at physics so it was sort of hard to keep up with what he was doing and how he got to solutions. My advice: Go to class and do the bookwork. It will be worth it.

Prof. Uher wants his students to succeed.  Not only are classes mandatory through iClicker questions, but he also provides a lot of details in class that aren't on the PowerPoints (which he posts) that help on exams. The test averages are low, but Uher's section is usually 1 point higher. The class is doable as 35% of grading is effort & 65% tests.

Great professor! Every other day is discussion where he gives you one iclicker question based on the problems from the night before that are very easy. His lectures are very organized and expectations are made very clear.

I mean it's Physics, it's going to be really hard.  Uher gave us helpful formula after formula, and did practice problem after practice problem - the majority of which ended up on the actual exams. PAY ATTENTION DURING CLASS he gives hints for exams and he every concept that's on the final at least once.  (Bonus:  only iClickers every other day.)

Citrad is a great teacher, however the class itself is pretty difficult. There are 4 exams, and they're all equally difficult. Citrad's main tool for teaching physics is deriving every formula. The way he teaches it, if you forget a formula, you can usually remember how to derive it from another formula which ends up helping a lot on exams.
He's got a bit of an accent but it's not hard to understand. Easy iclicker questions in class. His section always does a little bit better on the exams than the other sections.

Uher is the best Physics 140 professor out there.  Our section did 5-10% better on every exam than other sections. The day of exams, Uher did example problems exactly like 4-6 exam questions. He gives only 1 clicker question instead of 6, and 97% of the class gets them correct since Uher basically gives the answers out.
Doesn't understand kids questions in class, but otherwise pretty good.

Uher is the man. He's so cute and his lectures are great. The only thing I disliked about his lectures was that he derived every equation. I can see how this would be useful for some, I kinda viewed it as a waste of time. He normally gives hints on what will be on the exam, which is super nice. He actually teaches the material, unlike other profs.

Though I never had him, I went to several of his lectures and he is a FANTASTIC professor. Get him if you can. He explains things very clearly and he makes Physics make a lot of sense. Tests are still hard, but he explains things really well. Another thing I like about him is that he kind of sounds like Dr. Lipschitz from Rugrats XD.
I never took any form of physics in high school, so this class was extremely difficult for me. Prof. Uher was clear in class and helpful in office hours.
Awesome professor.

If you're deciding between taking Yuri Popov's class and Uher's, take Dr. Uher's class! He is VERY clear and thorough, he cares about his students doing well (which is impressive for such large classes) and prepares his classes very well for exams. I was not as impressed with Dr. Popov's lectures. The class is difficult, Dr. Uher makes it less so.
FAV PROF AT UM! A moderately funny guy who is great at making physics easy to understand and clear. Would take any of his classes if I could
Class was hard but Uher is by far the best teacher for Physics 140.  He explains concepts very clearly and he is the one that writes the exams for the class. Must take!
The best.

Excellent prof. The class is very hard in terms that it covers a lot of material. Uher's sections always had better grades on midterms as compared to other sections. Highly recommend to take this guy!
Overrated professor. Difficult to understand accent and isn't very helpful. Take someone like Popov instead.
Great teacher, material was difficult but he managed to explain things slowly and clearly so that everyone understood. And he has an awesome accent!
Prof Uher is willing to take the time to help and teach everyone. Makes physics worthwhile, and has a good sense of humor. wouldn't have done close to as well as I did had I not taken his section.

Abosolutely amazing teacher! He explains questions very clearly, and not too fast. Love his accent! Very gentleman. P.S. I went to some other class when I missed classes, so I can say he is the best phys140 teacher!

I hate physics, and its difficult to me but if you want to get the best grade possible for Physics 140, take Uher!! He's amazing and his class always averages higher than others.  Best Physics Prof by far

Amazing, excellent, superb, magnificent, awesome, extraordinary! Prof. Uher is a great professor with an awesome accent. He clearly knows and loves physics, and the problems he does are relevant to exams. Go to his review sessions!
Uher is the best physics prof out there, read the book tho and attend review sessions

GREAT professor. Walks the class through problems and concepts very clearly. His discussion was extremely valuable for learning the material. He is friendly, but will push you to learn the problems and concepts. Also, he has the coolest accent ever yet you can understand him perfectly.
Great professor, teaches very well and knows a lot of physics.
Uher is a physics god.  His lectures were great, but his exams were a bit hard.  But, if you study a lot and really know the material, you will do well in his class.
Excellent professor, difficult class, be sure to study hard and do practice problems
Very clear explanation of concepts.  Derivations of equations were easy to follow.  Problems from exams came from Mastering Physics, discussion, and in-class examples.  Good physics prof!
Best professor I've had by far. He knows his stuff and can teach it very well. His exams are fair and doable.
Citrad is awesome, he really knows his stuff, and he wants you to succeed. Definitely take his class
Uher is a great lecturer. He presents the theory behind the concepts very well. His exams are very reasonable, and only cover what is presented in lecture.

Lectures are informative and clear, but he doesn't really spend enough time doing problem demonstrations.  He mostly uses lecture to do complex derivations of equations which don't appear on the exams.  Exam averages ranged from 50-75, but the curve is generous.  Pretty cool guy though.
Great prof. Made physics easy to understand. Chill demonstrations
Uher's accent is entertaining.  He's a nice guy and usually fair.  I thought he was boring sometimes but then again I'm not bound to pay attention when I have discussion at 8 am.
One of the coolest profs I've ever had. Helpful, clear, awesome accent, and very low-key funny during lecture.
Great teacher!  I wish he taught the lecture.  He made everything make sense.

Led discussion for physics 135. Very knowledgable man but perhaps bored teaching this intro physics class. He explained everything very well when asked, but otherwise assumes you know the information.

Great professor, probably the best I've had so far.  He's incredibly fair with partial credit on exams and more than willing to help with any questions you have.  Don't worry about his accent, I found it fun to listen to.  If you show up to office hours, he will remember your name and say hi to you around campus.  Very cool prof.

He's awesome. His accent, excitement and good occasional stories alone make the class worth attending. But be sure to keep up with the material, if you get behind you're a goner. Pay special attention once you start rotational. He prepares you for the test really well if you keep up with the material, test scores actually represent your knowledge.

Great discussion leader. He explained problems clearly and went over the solutions step by step. Also lectured on material that wasn't covered in the 140 lecture and explained concepts very clearly. His accent is interesting, but not that hard to understand. I would be lost in physics without him.
Ctirad is a phenominal prof... For some reason his class is actually entertaining to attend, and his enthusiasm for physics will infect you... Take 160 with him if you can.

Prof. Uher is superb. I had trouble in AP last year, but everything makes so much sense now. I got a C on the first exam, and he really helped me out a lot and my grade improved dramatically. He really, really cares about this class and will go out of his way to help you understand the material. There's also a fun group research project at the end.
He's awesome, has lot of experience, knows what he's talking about, loves physics, is interesting, and the best physics teacher ever!!!!!!!

Mr. Uher is extremely helpful and clear. Really really superb. the best. best gsi i have had yet. But you should be warned that although I ended up pulling an A-, the class was ridiculous and the textbook was awful. (Winn--good, but overrated--was my prof)
Ctirad is the man. Great class, especially if you took AP Physics in high school.
extremely fair prof...nice guy, leaves a lot to go to conferences around the world, keeps the whole class on schedule though, learned a lot!
His class is the easiest one I've taken at the university and he writes really large on the board. He just doesn't go into much detail on concepts. Book reading is probably required for most.

Really great prof, teaches clearly with step by step explinations that really help. If you do the work the tests aren't hard, not to mention in this class he hinted a lot to what would be on the tests.
Very helpful discussion leader, explains problems clearly.
Great Professor! excellent knowledge of Physics, knows his stuff!

Prof. Uher is an excellent discussion section professor. He clearly explains and recaps lectures and chooses problems that are relevant to the tests. His reviews for exams are EXTREMELY VALUABLE, he picks examples that you will see on the exam. Prof. Uher is the best.

Very good discussion leader.  Has a thick accent, but enunciates and speakes clearly, so it isn't that bad.  He goes over all of the problems we do in discussion, making sure that people understand it.  Great guy.
He is great, but we never get to do all the questions on the worksheet....I don't really like this fact (he doesn't manage the time well on purpose)
Professor Uher is cool... He's really nice, he's willing to help, and the accent isn't bad, but if you can't make his "office hours", you're at the mercy of the physics help room.
Uher is the man. I feel very fortunate that he was my discussion leader for 140.
Best physics discussion leader ever

Great professor if you can work with her attendance policy! She's tough but clearly communicates her expectations and genuinely encourages people to learn. I didn't know how to sew before coming into this class, and now I can easily operate a home sewing machine! Already signed up for another one of her classes.

This site wouldn't let me enter the course I had with her the past semester (ARTDES 427), but I've taken three of Annica's courses over the years and I really like her. She can be tough grader, especially in ARTDES 206 but she's super knowledgable and helpful when I encounter a problem with a garment/project.

She's TERRIBLE at communicating with students and NEVER replies to emails. I sent her legal doctor's notes, but she thought an AI wrote them and tried to fail me (I had few medical condition). I went to my advisor, and she finally adjusted my grade, but she was rude and ignored me after that. Her lack of professionalism was very disheartening.

wanted to see if garment design/construction was something i was interested in, and annica was the perfect person to help guide me! the attendance criteria is insane though, and i was criticized for missing class even with a doctors note.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class online but this was one of the best online classes I took this semester- Annica did her best to provide as much in depth instruction as possible even over an online format and I really appreciated it. She can grade a bit tough but it is honest and she gives great feedback and will direct you to helpful sources. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mini course is completely different from 3-credit studio. She was super easy on grading in 197. I'm taking 308 now, and I'm not doing the best. I have no idea why I'm doing bad either because she never critiques too hardly during in-process or final crit. Btw attendance policy is miss 1 class only. 2 classes  one letter grade. 3 classes  fail
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class was great and I learned a lot but she grades hard.

On the first day, Annica told us that she understands that we are taking this mini course likely for fun or credits and so she would make it an easy A for us. Just complete the assignments and at the end you turn in a binder full of everything. As long as you do that, your good. She is also very helpful when you ask questions. Learned a lot.

I liked Julie! She is easy to reach and talk to. The class had many good discussions. It was generally quite easy and we covered a lot, but all quite broadly. She encouraged a lot of feedback to improve course. Sometimes her responses to students felt vague tho and I did wish for less general material and more academic readings & focused lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Julie was very inconsistent with her feedback, often praising some answers while heavily critiquing similar answers from other students. She rarely focused on real world solutions. I am disappointed in the quality of her teaching, and I feel as though I learned more from the other students in the class rather than the professor herself.

The class was chaotic and disorganized. It was difficult to identify what we were talking about and why. Guest speakers were scheduled and their schedules changed frequently leading to repeated changes sometimes on the day of which then affected the synchronous and asynchronous times. Leaving me further confused.

Took 505 with Julie. LOTS of readings and busy work. However, Julie herself is nice and the class content is not particularly difficult, likely familiar to those with psych/social science background. She mainly reads off slides when lecturing which can be tedious. Grade based mainly on one big paper/project and group presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She talks a lot, requires tons of readings, and does not grade anything until the very end of the semester. She promised feedback for a month straight only giving it to us days before a group project was due. She gets sidetracked very easily and much of the lecture is not important to the assignments. Little to no discussion in a 3 hour long class.

Took SW 505 and dreaded this class every-week. The material was basic for the field of social work. I was deeply disappointed in the facilitation of class discussion and Julie's inability to highlight marginalized voices. She consistently cut off students of color when speaking and was harmful in her rhetoric in class. I deeply advise against her.
So painful. Avoid if you can.

This is a grant writing class. This was mostly all a group project but only one person was familiar with the agency so the rest of us were really relying on this person (and they did not come through) Tough grader and confusing coursework.

I have never had a professor be so unclear about expectations for assignments. Unless you want to be caught in a constant state of confusion, do not take any of her classes. Her lectures and just general communication are horrible and incredibly unclear.

Nice person, bad professor. She will push to hear feedback but will implement none of it. She's big on participation so be ready to talk. She's never clear about her expectations, can make even the simplest assignment confusing. Super nit picky grader. Lectures are just info dump. Lots of pointless busy work. Avoid her if you can.

Julie's willing to hear feedback, but she won't change the way she does anything. I got a 94.75% in the class and she gave me an A-. I'm going through a months-long process to argue my grade back to an A (still waiting to see if she'll change it). She's slow responding to emails and her grading is super unclear/lazy. I got 100 or 93 on everything.

I would not recommend taking her for SW 560. Even if you work hard on all the assignments and follow directions, she will give you a B. Class content is disorganized, course assignments are not clear as to what she wants, as if we can read her mind. Takes feedback but doesn't USE it. Very nitty picky with projects. Overall did not enjoy her class.

Julie is nice but not a great instructor. She doesn't give clear instructions and doesn't respond to emails for days on end. We had a discussion post due before class on Tuesday and she didn't post the questions until Sunday night. Very annoying for someone who tries to be organized and ahead of schedule like me. Lots of reading but most is NYT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is knowledgeable, but strict grading. The assignment load is a bit heavy, but it is still acceptable. She prepared very well for each class and provided a lot of useful handouts. Some of the lectures were boring, but class activities were helpful to better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor gives many unhelpful assignments with unclear expectations, and her grading standards are arbitrary. Rubrics and slideshows are riddled with spelling and grammatical errors. She offers passive aggressive remarks about lack of student participation most classes, perhaps never considering this as a testament to her ineptitude as a lecturer.
Confusing instructions, too many assignments, uses personal experiences as fact. Would not take again. Incredibly frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was the most difficult class that I have taken at The School of Social Work. She assigns way too much homework to an unnecessary degree, in addition to many group presentations that take up a lot of outside class time. I suggest taking another professor because this class was not a great experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cushman is very knowledgeable and considerate but my gosh is her class hard. She has a million assignments, tons upon tons of readings, and wants class participation. This class was significantly more work than every other class I have had in both under grad and grad school. She has been really great about feedback, but her class is a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This lecturer is rigid to the point that she makes our entire class anxious about our learning. She is very knowledgeable about research. She intentionally over-complicates the lecture content. She does not seem to want you to succeed in her course. I will discourage taking her courses to anyone. Your learning is guaranteed to be frustrating.

Knowledgeable and kind imo... but frustrated a lot of others in class. Students often were passive aggressive in their approach to engaging in conversation with her when they disagreed.. This fostered a negative classroom environment which the professor addressed outright and students coyly shied away from acknowledging their part.

Psychopharm Mini Course, honestly the rudest woman I have ever met and truly limited in her knowledge of psychopharm. Not at all open to student's opinions and blatantly disrespected student's when we tried to disagree. Unable to answer questions on a regular basis.

Prof. Cutler is a nice guy, but the class is very disorganized. On many occasions he forgets to post homeworks, and he would also randomly cancel class. His lectures are not helpful at all, and he goes on long tangents. Use the book to learn. The exams can range from not that bad to literally impossible to finish. Overall the class is just chaotic.
Great Professor, always willing to engage with students after/outside class. Sometimes falls behind on class logistics.

lectures are recorded, but not uploaded in timely manner. hw are good balance of doable and challenging. tests are predictable: review hw and make sure to pay attention in class because sometimes he drops hints about possible exam questions. put everything you can on your cheat sheet; who knows if you'll need it.
Decent lecturer but does not go through challenging applied examples frequently. Recorded lectures are useful but he doesn't upload on time. Hw is mostly doable.

Cutler is a great guy, but not a great teacher. He is a research professor who teaches because he has to. Often unclear and can't always defend derivations. Tests are very different than the homework, and there are no sample tests. Often answers questions with "think about it some" and "look at the text," which is frustrating. Easy homework though.
Extremely smart and helpful. Professor Cutler was one of my favorite professors at Michigan.

He rarely shows respect or care for students in class, and I felt that he often prioritized certain individuals over others. 
Run as fast as you can.
Would like to take this course again!
Really nice Professor!
my friend said he is great.

Copies lectures from textbook and then just copies it down on the board without explaining qualitatively. Seems like he must know a lot about research but can't teach it at all. Homework is completely unrelated to the long derivations in class. My time would have been better spent skipping lecture and reading the textbook (which also sucks).

Lord Cundiff's first semester back at his alma mater, settling in to his new role. friendly, personable and passionate about optics.   Spent the semester BSing lectures, merely copying formulas out of the book, day after day, after day. At this point a better researcher than teacher, but has potential. Not my first choice, nor last

This class is a ton of work but so worth it. I didn't have Prof Cummings for 230 but wish I had -- she's super engaging and I've never seen a professor care more about their students. This class goes by fast and there are lots of deadlines so you have to keep up. Great experience if you're in the right lab.

This was a great class. Dr. Cummings has a really engaging teaching style that keeps you focused and paying attention, including her guided lecture slides. This is especially important since there's a lot of content. I appreciated the extra in-class activities she added in, too. Hope to take another course with her before I'm done.

Dr. Cummings is a fantastic instructor, and I have never felt more engaged in a one-and-a-half hour lecture class. Her slides were helpful for following her lecture and for being interactive through fill-in-the-blank exercises, and I like the variety of activities we got to do both in lecture and in discussion. She's also great with questions.

Professor Cummings was very engaging and very receptive to questions both in the classroom as well as during office hours. All of her teaching methods were very interactive, mixing lecture with questions and hands-on activities to help you understand and further explore the material. Definitely take this course with her if you can.

This class wasn't easy but also the professor didn't help with that. Focused her attention on easier concepts and didn't go over more complex things that actually showed up on the exam. Also a stickler about lecture recordings.

I love Dr. Cummings' teaching style. I took one of her courses before and I loved how she engages with students while also keeping the course challenging. She really makes the material interesting to learn, and made me excited about developmental neuroscience. She is a great instructor and challenges her students in the best way.

Dr. Cummings is by far my favorite professor at UM. She's caring, funny, and explains material really well. This is an incredibly dense class and you will need to study consistently to do well, but her exams are fair, her OH are super accesable, and she always makes class engaging. If you have the chance to take a class with her, absolutely do it!

The ratings are true! I have nothing bad to say about Dr. Cummings and she is probably my favorite professor I've taken at the university. You have to put in effort, but she wants to see you succeed and is clearly passionate about what she teaches and explains everything very clearly. If you have a chance to take a class with her, you should.

Dr. Cummings is amazing at explaining the material, answers questions in a thoughtful and helpful manner, creates very fair exams, and is a very funny and kind lecturer. I love her teaching style and would 100% take another one of her classes. By far my favorite professor I've had at U of M so far.

Developing Brain was my second class with Dr. Cummings and she's great. The content is challenging but she's super accessible outside of class. I ended up meeting with her regularly to keep me on pace and it helped a lot. The class is early but honestly I ended up liking it because it got me up and being productive early. Highly recommend!

I really liked the flip classroom bc I could learn the content and take notes at my own pace. Talking first in small groups in class allowed me to hear my classmates' thoughts and got me thinking about the content in different ways before coming together as a whole class. The group projects were fun and engaging & a nice break from all tests.

Dr. Cummings is an amazing lecturer, but there is a lot of content covered each lecture so be prepared to move quickly. If your looking for a psychology class, I wouldn't recommend this because I felt it was very bio heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cummings is amazing! I love her lecture style and engaging notes that force you to pay attention. When I first had her for 230 I was worried about the short answers on exams but grew to love them as they really make you learn the material. Exams are well written & cover important aspects of every class. I hope I can take another class w/her!

I loved this class despite the heavier workload because it truly advanced my writing and helped me get better talking about my research. By the time the poster session came around I was confident in what I had to say because there's built-in practice. Every assignment had a purpose and Dr. Cummings provided extensive feedback that helped immensely.

Dr. Cummings is an amazing professor who is clearly super knowledgeable in her field and passionate about helping students learn. Her lectures were always interesting and she addressed questions in a way that clarified things and explained them in a different way. I loved all the engaging activities we did to break up lecture too.

I loved this class! I don't have a biology background at all and almost didn't take this class because I thought it would be too hard. I'm so glad I took it! The information is cool and Dr. Cummings is a great professor. I went to see her when I had questions and we had the best conversations. Definitely take this class!
i hate her so much omg

Dr. Cummings is an amazing professor, she explains things clearly and is obviously passionate about the class! I learned a lot and, although the class was more work than others, it is a really interesting topic. She tied the topics we learned about to a lot of real life applications and made the class engaging.

Developing Brain was one of the more challenging classes I had at UM, not to mention the fact that it's at 8:30 in the morning. But Dr. Cummings is a fantastic teacher and made it fun (seriously). (I also had her for 230 and she was equally amazing). I'm studying for the MCAT now and that class was great prep for the development section. Five stars

Dr. Cummings is fantastic at lecturing and is super intelligent. I think her exams are pretty fair and that all the questions are based off the powerpoint slides. The class was very low workload as well. However, I do wish she recorded lectures. Overall, she is a great professor and very approachable if you need to ask questions or for extra help.

Dr. Cummings is hands down one of the best professors I've had at Michigan, and this course was my favorite class I've ever taken here. She is truly so knowledge and passionate about this topic and the structure of this course was created with such intent and passion about having the students truly grasp the material. 100% recommend!
ive taken multiple classes with dr. cummings and she is amazing. So understanding and willing to help
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cummings is great. Truly cares about her students and wants to know how they are doing. She explains material well and is always open to questions. This class is very dense so you need to stay on top of the material and study throughout the semester.

Yes, this class was difficult, but Dr. Cummings made it so interesting and she really cared about her students. She does not post lectures, and you have to download her slides and take notes directly on them to keep up, but I would absolutely take a class with her again. She met with me every week to quiz me on content. Love her!

This is my second class with Dr. Cummings and she's been one of my favorite professors at Michigan. Sex differences is a good mix of outside work and in class discussion, and I've never had a class where we think about how different things like society affect health and disease. Great class.

Hormones & Behavior in the team based learning format with Dr. Cummings was the best class I've taken at U-M. She's so energetic and even though the lectures are pretty full, I liked all the group work we did to break up the material. The workshops are the best! Great way to expand on content. Study everything, and don't wait til the last minute.

I absolutely LOVE professor Cummings. Besides being a great professor, she is also a great person! She explains everything clearly, has very fun assignments, and truly cares for her students. I would 100% take classes with her again. Definitely one of the best professors I have had at umich.

The exams are definetely challenging but Dr Cummings really wants everyone to succeed - exams are only 45% and the rest is based on other, easier stuff (projects, homework, participation, etc). You need to study to do well, but it's a very fair class in my opinion. Would def recommend to fulfill psych breadth requirement!!!!

She was an amazing lecturer, but the class is difficult in itself. It's not her fault, but just the curriculum. If you have an ipad, I suggest taking notes on the lecture slides on the ipad as hand written just wouldn't be possible for you to keep up. SIf you study every day for this class you would do well.

I took 331 after taking 337 with Dr. C and she's still amazing, if not better. You truly learn what it is to write a scientific paper and learn a lot about research, poster-making, and many other skills that will help you later, especially if you're doing a thesis. She's incredibly understanding, just communicate!

I really liked this class! It's definitely not your every day psych class and is much more bio than I'm used to. But Dr. Cummings explains things so well and is super open to helping outside the class. Go see her if you have questions. And leave plenty of time to study.
She was pretty good. Very nice lecturer, but tough grader on exams and presentations. I would say it's pretty difficult to get over a B+, but you learn a fair amount.

Clear she is very passionate about what she teaches! Tests are a mix of short answers and multiple choice and it's highly recommended to study throughout the semester (although I just studied a week before exams and got 80s-90s). Take notes on the slides (ipad) as a majority of material is on them and lectures go too quickly for hand written.

Dr. Cummings is a really great professor and lecturer. She really cares about the info she's teaching and her lectures are not boring. Tests are pretty tricky and she is a pretty harsh grader when it comes to the written portions. Make sure you know EVERYTHING and be specific answering!! I would recommend making flashcards of the lectures.

This course was extremely well instructed by Dr. Cummings. She is one of the most organized professors I have had at UM. Lectures were well paced and filled class time but allowed for questions. Material was presented clearly and thoroughly. Classes were a mix of lectures and activities/workshops that made material exciting.

This class is lecture heavy, but engaging and interesting.  Discussion attendance and assignments were important as well, but they were never difficult. If you take notes in lecture and review them you'll do fine.  The GSI's were helpful outside the classroom, too.  (I would not recommend taking this as distribution requirement).

Dr. Cummings always provided clear, in-depth explanations during every lecture in a way that is easily understandable / digestible to her students. I also appreciated how knowledgable and passionate Dr. Cummings is about behavioral psych and science in general--it made the class much more interesting!

This class has three exams and there is no reviews for any. You have to memorize all the slides in prep for majority short answer exams with a few MC/fill in the blank ?s. The content is great but preparing for the exams was super difficult and unguided. GSIs were also taking off points for ridiculous things. I loved the class, not the curriculum.

Just so everyone knows Dr. Cummings anti-scales. So an A- includes any grade in the 93% range, and a B+ is only a 88-89%. This really impacts grades since the course is very impacted by test grades which the average tended to be a 75-80% with absolutely no scale.

Professor Cummings was prepared and passionate about the subject material. The class isn't super difficult, but definitely not easy studying for the exams due to the open-ended question format and that we were expected to be "responsible for everything on the (dense) slides." Especially since the slides were around 50 slides per lecture.

Dr. Cummings is my fav professor at UMich! I've had her twice and she's been great for both classes (I also had her for 230). Her exams are long and you do have to learn all the info from lectures. But she's super willing to meet outside of class to answer questions which is great. I definitely recommend taking a class with her if you can!

Cummings is great for psych 331! She is super accessible outside of class and gives great feedback. Her lectures are interesting and usually end early which is nice. The class overall is a big time commitment (8-10 hours/week in lab, 2 hour lecture every week, and a 15 page paper) but you learn a lot and it was enjoyable.

Currently taking this class fall 2022, and so far this class is a nightmare. Studied all weekend just to get a 62% on the test. This class is not for people who aren't naturally extremely smart or don't have biology experience. This is NOT a psych class, it is purely biology. The professor packs way too much into lectures and the slides are dense.

I absolutely loved Dr. Cummings. Her class was interesting and engaging and she made an effort to build our understanding of Biopsych in a way in which we could connect it to real experiences and to use in daily life. She may come off as intense, however, she is more than willing to answer questions if you ask.

Exams were tough for me bc it was purely memorising 300 slides per exam && she has a relatively strict grading criteria. As a prof, shes fun and interactive; however at the end of the term, I asked her about grades & curves n stuff & she just walked away from me once she got sick of me lol. the class is fun tho. hard work but rlly interesting

I have had Professor Cummings for two classes now, and she is always amazing and keeps the material interesting. I really appreciate how she is attentive to everyone's needs but also pushes up to learn more and participate.

So happy I had Dr. Cummings for Intro to Behavioral Neuroscience!! Ive had a lot of friends take her upper-level classes so Ive heard great things, and was glad to get her for intro. Great energy and the way she explains the material makes so much sense. Excellent prof!

Dr. Cummings is a gem. She's super accessible outside of class and entertaining in class. Her energy is the best! I'm taking 430 with her in the winter and can't wait -- she's definitely my favorite prof at Michigan. :)

I'm just finishing Sex Differences in Brain & Behavior with Dr. Cummings and it was great. I loved the organization (it's flipped-classroom format) and incorporates social and cultural influences on health and medicine that you don't get from a lot of other classes. It's kept small, so lots of opportunities for great discussion. Great class!
Loved this class and Dr. Cummings. She only did lecture videos, the GSI was more involved.

Dr. Cummings was energetic in class which made material more interesting. Used in-class activities. Talked really fast - made note-taking hard, slides didn't contain a ton of information afterward. Not open to talking about why you lost points on assignments, harsh grader. 2 group projects. 3 exams. Exam qs come from guiding qs on slides
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Cummings is amazing!! I wish I'd taken class with her before senior year so I could have her again. People complain that 430 is more like MCDB and "too hard" for the psych dept. but Dr. Cummings will go above and beyond to help students understand material and succeed in class. Couldn't recommend her or this class more. Work hard; it'll pay off
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had professor Cummings in the Spring for topics in bio-psych, the class itself was extremely easy there were quizzes every week but if you attend lecture regularly you will do fine. She is a great teacher and very down to earth!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She as a professor is great, definitely knows her material and is very smart. However, the way she runs her classroom is a waste of time. I took MGT 4860, and people in class use it as a time to complain about their lives. 75% of the class is people whining about their boring lives and she encourages it. If you like oversharers, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Cummings for Developing Brain and it was such a great class. Its challenging and not an easy A, but definitely doable if you study and worth it. Plus shes funny, and I actually didnt mind going to class (even though its at 8:30 in the morning!).

I enjoyed this class with Dr. Cummings so much I made sure to take another class with her. Although she is a bit of a tough grader she explains material very well and keeps you engaged. She is incredibly easy to approach and is very open-minded. Work load is very do-able, especially if you pay attention in class.

really good class but be ready to put the time in (i.e. make flashcards and start studying week before at least), if you're not passionate about the topic this class isn't an easy A like other 200 psych classes, talks SO FAST in lecture, heard bad things about grading in past but had no issues
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You may find mixed reviews on this prof because the course is not a super easy A compared to some other psych classes. However, do the work and you will do great! I've taken an upper level psych class and psych 230, both featured exams that are short answer. The professor has awesome and interesting lectures, exams ask you to interpret the material

Dr. Cummings is a very knowledgable professor and studies biopsychology. She can answer most questions and tells a lot of funny and all-too-familiar stories. As someone with little college background in biology/chemistry, I was able to follow along well as long as I studied hard at least a week in advance. I'd recommend her for PSYCH220.

Dr. Cummings has sincerely been one of my favorite professors at Michigan, and her teaching of this course is no exception. She came well-prepared every class to teach the lecture, was passionate about the material, and encouraged engagement between students.

I was nervous to take 220 because I dont have a strong biology background. Took it based off recommendations from friends & it was great. Dr Cummings was a very engaging and energetic instructor. She presented the material in a relatable way that made the class interesting even though Im not a Biopsych major. Id take another class w her any time

I loved Hormones and Behavior with Prof Cummings! The material was really cool and her lectures are always good (I had her for 230 too). Im glad there are 3 tests because there was so much material. Didnt love the group projects but oh well. Good class overall.

Dr. Cummings is such a terrific person. However, this class was semi disappointing. Everything is taught at the intro level. She never goes that in depth with topics so I felt like I didn't learn very much from the class. Exams aren't bad but sometimes questions can be vague or are easily misinterpreted.

Psych230 with Dr. Cummings was one of my favorite classes! The material was interesting and challenging, but manageable. And you have to actually understand things for the exams so it takes some studying, but its not tricky. Definitely worth it!

Dr. Cummings was a good instructor, although she explained certain topics better than others and had a tendency to rush through certain topics. She was open to questions and answered them well, and you could tell she wanted us to do well. Exams were long, but they were never tricky and were a fair representation of material covered in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: The course is not hard but the Prof does not explain all the material. Workload heavy. Exam are mostly long answer questions. I understood the material very well but the GSI took points of for almost every question just because I didnt have time to construct the language (im not a native speaker).

Good intro class. Difficult material but it was explained clearly. Went to professor and GSI office hours and both were really helpful. Tests are challenging but fair. Would definitely take a class with Dr. Cummings again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Hilarious that everyone is complaining about how hard it wasdid you even study, bro? Because my friends and I did and we all received As. Dr. Cummings is great and the material was presented and tested fairly. If you think it was too hard, you may want to reconsider Neuroscience as a field. Or suck it up.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: If you thought this class was hard, grow up. It is not nearly as bad as biochem just saying. The material is relevant, interesting, and applicable. Exams are more than fair. It tests key concepts while memorizing specific nomenclature is not necessary. Grading is VERY fair 70/30 Lecture/Discussion. Thank you Professor Cummings (& the amazing GSIs)!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Cummings course was really difficult because there was no guidance for any of the exams!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This is too much work for an introductory course and I completed ALL of my upper level courses with much more ease than this. There is so much material and there is no guidance on what is and is not important. The exams, don't let her lie to you, are almost majority free response. There are no study guides or quality review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was extremely challenging for a gateway BCN course. We received no guidance or study guide for the exams, and the exams were ten pages of free response. When students shared concerns about the level of difficulty, the professor was unwilling to negotiate or curve tests. So much information and such little direction (especially from GSIs)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Loved taking 331 with Dr. Cummings. The Lab I was in was super fun, and even though the writing part was a lot of work it totally wasnt bad for a ULWR. Definitely recommend! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: This class is not bad at all. Study by reviewing lectures and it's an easy A. The concepts taught in this class are all very dumbed down and simple.

I have Intro Biopsych with Dr. Cummings and its awesome. Theres for sure a ton of work but her lectures are great and put together in a really understandable way. Its also clear she actually cares how we do and focuses a lot on studying and study techniques, which is really nice. Challenging, but worth it.

Dr. Cummings is super sweet and also really funny. However, her exams are a bit ridiculous. She doesn't give any guidelines as to what you should be studying (her answer is everything) and its SO much information which makes it nearly impossible to memorize every detail, but if you don't memorize everything then you won't do well on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: the class is definitely more work than you'd expect for a psych 200 level, but overall she's a good lecturer and the exams were fair (but long)

too much material. The professor does not go over everything in the lecture but everything is on the test. There are three test, one writing assignment, a final project, a journal club, and a anatomy practical. Just think it's too much work for a 200 level class. Btw, she's not willing to curve at all and she said she'd only curve down.

Professor Cummings was such a great professor. She was super articulate and explained everything in detail and is clearly and expert in the subject. She was super enthusiastic and personable which was refreshing. Grading was a little harder than expected but not too bad.

Wasn't looking forward to this class because I thought it would be all molecular brain stuff but it was actually good. Prof Cummings is a great teacher and makes things really clear, plus she's pretty funny. Definitely a good class.

Just finished Sex Differences with Dr. Cummings and it was amazing! Cool range of info from biological contributions to social factors for a bunch of stuff I've never even considered before. She actually encourages discussion in class and even though some students can get off topic, it was actually fun. Definitely a good prof!

Professor Cummings really cares about her students. She will meet with you whenever you need to answer all of your questions. Her exams are challenging, but if you study and understand the material, then you will do well! There are no surprises in this class, and the information is actually super cool!

Tests for this class felt a little ridiculous. You are basically expected to memorize EVERYTHING from the class slides. You will be tested on around half of it, but she doesn't provide any study guides. Overall, this was a needlessly stressful class of which I forgot most of what i "learned" because it was just memorization. Honestly, I hated it.

I had Psych 220 with professor Cummings and it was a great class. Overall the instruction is very good, and Dr. Cummings tries to make otherwise boring info interesting. Exams are long and there's a ton material covered but if you study the lectures you'll be fine.

Just had Dr Cummings for Developing Brain and she was awesome. Super funny in class, met with me a number of times out of class for help. I didn't think I was going to like class and I totally did, thanks to her.

I took PSYCH 220, and the class was very easy. Professor Cummings teaches using slides, and everything that's possible to be on an exam is on said slides. With this in mind DO NOT BUY THE BOOK. I got an A- in the class and didn't once open up the textbook which was "required" for the class. Group projects are also interesting and pretty easy.

Dr. Cummings lectures very fast so do not attempt taking notes by hand! Download the slides and add to them on your laptop. You don't need the book at all, exams come completely from the slides. If you study often and do well with memorization, you should have no problem getting an A. Loved her and this class!

Developing Brain was a good class. The material could be a bit dry at times, but Dr. Cummings made it better than most other professors would. Exams are a little difficult - they're long and a little too open-ended for my liking, but they aren't too bad  with some studying. Grade was based off two exams, a presentation, and participation/attendance

Dr. Cummings is great for student's who aren't actually studying psych. She's interesting and fast paced but she knows her stuff. The tests are a little hard because she takes really specific, nit-picky info off lecture slides so you have to study a lot and know all the details if you want to do really well on exams.

As a professor I have no complaints, but come exam time it was very stressful. More than half the test is short answer, and if you didn't know one of the answer you could be down five points right off the bat. Too much information and too difficult of a class to be an intro for non majors in my opinion.

If you're neurodivergent in any way and have to take a psych class she's honestly the best.  She's very receptive to student feedback and really willing to talk about ableism, and she was very respectful about it all.

Professor Cummings is a wonderful woman. She is very passionate about the brain, which makes lectures much more enjoyable. She gets all giddy and excited about certain material and digresses in lecture sometimes which actually helps keep the students engaged. Tests are tough though. They were open ended and the criteria was unclear.
She is literally the best woman ever. I would take 100 more classes with her. So engaging and helpful with students. I learned more in this class than any other.
LOVE Dr. Cummings. Hilarious and insightful, really engages with all her students.

I learned more in this class than most of the other courses in my major - there is A LOT of material but I found it super interesting. As other reviews have said the exams are tough, especially the first one because you don't know exactly what to expect, but I think as a University of Michigan student I appreciated being held to a high standard.

I took Sex Differences in Brain, Behavior and Disease with Prof Cummings over the summer and it was such a fun class! Prof Cummings is a great lecturer, and I loved the mix of in class discussion and guest lecturers too. Definitely my favorite class at UM so far.

This is the first post in my 4 years at Michigan. Do Not take this class with this professor. The other professor gives take home exams and is an easy A, while this professor uses the notes of the other prof. but gives two incredibly hard exams. B+ max grade if you go to her office hours. LOUSY Professor! Most of the class would agree.

Dr. Cummings is an amazing professor. She is incredibly enthusiastic and does a good job of mixing up the pace of the class between lectures, discussions, debates, and group work. Her exams are fairly predictable but you definitely need to know all of the material. She is very approachable and understanding.

This is my last class for my major before I graduate and I could not regret it more. It's a TON of material and she presents it so so fast. She's nice enough, but unless you're ready to be super on top of your sh!t, don't take this class. Also the midterm average was a 74%, and she basically just got mad at our class because of it.

Didn't respond to multiple emails. Lecture slides read like a poorly organized literature review. Example lecture slide heading: "animals are watery." Example fun fact about her life: "Dollar store pregnancy tests work."
gives way worse grade distributions than Jill Becker

I had The Developing Brain with Dr. Cummings during summer session and it was way better than I thought it would be. It was A LOT of info in a short period which was kind of tough, but she made it fun and easier to understand. Very approachable and funny!
This class actually turned out to be one of my favorite this term.  She has realistic expectations and the workload is light
Awesome prof! She presents the material in an interesting way and I feel like I'm learning alot.  The workload is very manageable too. Great class!

I just finished taking this course with Dr. Cummings and it was one of my favorite at UM.  I thought the professor was great and made the information fun -- not dry and boring like a lot of professors.  Some material is difficult but not too hard if you study.

This course has been one of my favorite classes at the University of Michigan.  Not only is the information so interesting, the professor makes the class even more rewarding.  In addition to Dr. Cummings' strong background and overwhelming knowledge of the material, she is always enthusiastic and excited about the topics discussed.  She always make
Very good teacher but you have to study for the exams. It's all memorization so it is extremely possible to do very well. Presentations at the end of the semester which are a lot of work but fun.

I thought this class was great!  I loved the material, and Dr. Cummings made it fun; she always met with me when I wanted to go over material and was quick to answer back via e-mail (even when my e-mails were super long!). I definitely recommend trying to take this class when she teaches it! :)

One of my favorite professors at UM! Prof Cummings is really friendly, extremely helpful and approachable outside of the classroom. The class is challenging but the material is really interesting. If you attend lecture and study for the exams you will succeed in this course. I would definitely recommend this course with Prof Cummings!

Dr. Cummings' lectures were clear & not long at all(no more than 1 hour even though the class is supposed to be 1.5 hours long). Readings are not important. If you don't understand something talk to her after class she'll explain it well! Just go to class and fill the slides in and if you understand the concepts you will do well on both tests!
Dr. Cummings's lectures were very clear but I felt she wasn't that approachable outside of class. :( The midterm turned out  to be easy but the final was ridiculously, surprisingly hard!

Had her for an Honors seminar and she's great! Made Linguistics very interesting and the class discussions we had were very insightful. She is a tough grader though. The "short assignments" were not really short and it was hard to earn a 100% on any assignment because they were reserved for those who went "above & beyond."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Anne is an amazing professor and will keep you engaged despite the early lecture time. I learned so much from her class and she encourages her students to explore language the way they want and change it for the final project. Shes also hilarious and loves learning all the slang.

Anne is amazing! She is not only intelligent but passionate and inspiring. She is very approachable and gives solid feedback. Yes, she is a tough grader, but you REALLY learn a lot from her. If you can take her class, do it. Will it be an easy A? No. But I promise if you put in the work and actively try to be engaged, you won't regret it!

Anne is knowledgeable and passionate but this class was ridiculous. It was 1 credit but homework took 6-8 hrs to finish and her idea of a 'short' essay was 2k words which might be fine for an upper-level course but not a 200-level. Also, it was more a linguists class than a grammar one. Cool information, utterly useless outside the classroom
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Anne is fantastic. From day one she made it clear that Grammar Boot Camp would be exactly as advertised: a boot camp. We worked a lot and I learned so much from her. She's kind, approachable, and always willing to help. I'm going to miss that class. If you're willing to work and open your mind, take this mini course with Anne!

Anne is enthusiastic and inspiring but this is NOT at all what it is advertised to be.
