"Grammar Bootcamp" implies  improving one's understanding and application of grammar; instead you report usage statistics of words which is totally irrelevant outside of this course. It is WAY MORE than 1 credit of work (about 8 hours/week) - should be 2 credits.

Eng292 is a 1 credit 1/2 sem minicourse called "Grammar Boot Camp," and although the lectures can be engaging, the workload is absolutely ridiculous for a 1 credit course. Weekly assignments that take 4 hrs and two 6-8 page essays, along with harsh grading, makes this the class that I regret taking the most. Took all the fun out of grammar for me!

Anne Curzan is a lovely person. However, the courseload is ridiculous for a 300 level English course. It is at least double every other English class I've ever taken as a major. Don't take this class unless you want an overloaded semester. Literally, TIME CONSUMING assignments due EVERY DAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I 3 Anne. Not the most relevant class, sure, but probably my favorite one I've taken at U-M. Is super enthusiastic about teaching and helping her students and about the material she teaches. Very knowledgeable, makes the material very accessible. Very friendly and approachable. Graded rather hard but very helpful during office hours.

Professor Anne is without a doubt the best educator I've ever had. She gives engaging, in-depth lectures using an incomparable teaching style. Her course is well-structured and comprehensive, but the coursework is far from burdensome. Anne learned the name of every student in our large lecture, and is helpful, personable, and simply brilliant.

Anne is an amazing professor. I highly encourage anyone to take her course. She is a fantastic teacher and really cares. In addition, she is very accomplished and you can be sure you will learn a tremendous amount of information from her that is extremely valuable.

Very enthusiastic but easily the most worthless topic you could take. Spent hours discussing worthless topics like if 'K' was 'okay' to text someone. The topics discussed have no application to anything worthwhile outside of class and have no importance. Don't take this if you want any knowledge that will actually help you in life after school.

Thought class was going to be really interesting, pretty boring and useless and lecture is too big for the discussion model.  papers are graded hard. overall, not worth it and not that informative.  she is a fine teacher, but not as good as i thought she would be, after hearing so much about her accomplishments.  i wouldnt recommend this class.

Anne is honestly the best professor I've ever had. She cares about her students. Attendance is mandatory for the most part, but she is so engaging that she really makes you WANT to listen. Her class requires work, but if you pay attention you'll be fine. Take any class from her.

She loves the class and is very knowledgeable. Her class is pointless though. You go over homework in class and talk about useless stuff and the lecture itself doesn't provide any benefit. Each lecture topic was extremely boring and useless in every day life. Overall, this was a horrible class and not interesting at all.

Anne is awesome.  Take this class.  I really felt like I learned the material and still remember it even now, almost a year later.  Her examples are eye-opening and specific and even having her class at 8:30am, it never made me fall asleep.

WONDERFUL. I love Anne. She is brilliant, always has useful examples for incredibly useful lessons about language. Totally interesting to me so I really enjoyed it, but it may be a little tough with no interest.

She's really knowledgeable, nice and makes herself easily available to students. Don't take her class if you want an easy A. Hard exams, fair grader when it comes to papers. There is a ton of homework.

I loved this class.  Anne is super engaging and helpful in office hours.  She is extremely knowledgable in her field, and even if she doesn't know something, she'll help you figure it out.  She understands she gives you a lot of work, but it's worth it - do the homework, it helps raise your grade.  Take anything with Anne that you can!

I am not very interested in English, but I took this class with a friend to fulfill requirements. I was pleasently surprised at how much I enjoyed this class. Ann is a great teacher and was able to keep my attention for an hour and a half lecture.
I'm an engineer, and even I really enjoyed this class!

A hard class, not an easy A. I thought she was a great lecturer, I just wasn't interested in the area. Exams are hard, mostly just short answers, but they aren't worth much. Maybe a worthwhile class for an English major.

Anne is one of the best professors at the university. This class is not an easy A but if you are willing to do the work you will get a good grade. She is so engaging and I loved going to her class. I would recommend taking any of Anne's classes

Professor Curzan is fantastic! She is very intelligent and motivated without being unapproachable. Her lectures are fun and worthwhile, even if the homework gets to be a bit exhausting. I am taking her again at 8:30am because she is worth it!

Wonderful class. Very interesting. Anne is an awesome professor who I really want to take again. The class is a lot of fun. It's cool to see where all the idiosyncrasies in our language come from. Even if you're not interested in language, Anne makes class fun.

Anne Curzan is one of the best professors I've had at the University. She is passionate about what she teaches and transmits this to her students. Her lecture style is humorous in a witty manner and down to earth. She does have high expectations and assigns a lot of homework, but its never busy work, and always has a purpose. I am scheduled to take my third course with her in the upcoming semester and cannot wait.
Prof. Curzan is one of the best English Grammar teachers I have ever had. She impressed me a lot. It seems she has answers to all the questions, and teaching is never a burden to her.

Professor Curzan is one of the best professors I have had thus far in my college experience. She is so passionate about a subject that, before taking the class, I would have had little interest in, and she found a way to make studying language and linguistics relevant to greater life issues. I would recommend Professor Curzan to every U-M student!

Definitely one of my favorite professors at The University of Michigan. She is fun/energetic and an engaging lecturer.  She is personable and learns everyone's name in the lecture hall.  The essay assignments are fun and allow for creativity.  While the homework is tedious, I feel that they all reinforce the material and help come exam time!
This was a great course overall. She loves what she does. A bit too much homework, but what can you do? I'd still recommend the course!

Professor Curzan is one of the BEST professor I have had at U of M. Fantastic. I learned more in 305 than I have in most of my other classes. Yes, it is a lot of "busy" work, but ultimately worth it. I will remember what I learned in this class for a LONG time. Thank you Professor Curzan!

I don't really get into linguistics as a subject. I thought this class would be informative and interesting, but I found the homework to be unhelpful and extremely time consuming. If you have a large load of classes, don't take this one, you will regret it in the wee hours of the morning. Overall I learned a lot, but is all of it useful? No!

Lecture isn't fantastic, but that's more a result of the course's unfortunate tendency to attract morons than it is of Curzan's shortcomings. She does an excellent job of covering all tested material in lecture and keeps material fairly interesting. Incorporates a good deal of participation; class feels more like a big REC than a LEC.

I'm gonna have to agree with the person who said she's a bit focused on herself...I didn't get the vibe she cared about the students as much as the subject. A lot of her assignments could have been cut in half--the repetition of similar exercises is what makes it "busy work". Smart woman, mediocre teacher.
I learned more in Power of Language than I did in the rest of my classes at UofM combined.  THANK YOU PROFESSOR CURZAN!

Anne Curzan is the best professor I had at U of M - her classes were always fun, exciting, and thought provoking. She is an amazing asset to the university. If you can, you should definitely take her classes!

Professor Curzan has an obvious passion for her work but focused on herself just a bit too much by talking about herself too often. Also, at times our class discussions went somewhat off track.  Fun? Sure. Helpful? No. That took too much time away from learning the critical aspects we were expected to know. However, she is very upbeat and helpful.
Easily the best professor here.  I've never had a teacher that even comes close.  She makes such an effort to know her students.  Fun, interesting, just all around enjoyable.

The University of Michigan's best professor.  Professor Curzan is passionate about her work and truly cares about the successes of her students.  She is very helpful, intelligent, and insightful and is a great professor!

She's great.  So interesting, funny, and enthusiastic and makes lectures really fun.  Good readings and assignments.  Team teaches w/ Robin Queen of linguistics who is also great. She seems very accessible and makes everyone feel like a part of the class-she learns everyone's names!
Fantastic lectures.  Without a doubt the best professor I've had yet.

Professor Curzan is absolutely wonderful! Not only are her lectures laid back, interesting and fun, but you actually learn in her class. She is never ever patronizing and she makes an effort (and usually succeeds) to learn everyone's name.  The best Professor I've had at the University so far. Wonderful!

The best testiment to this class is that almost everyone still comes to lecture in early December. Curzan is a great professor and the material is actually made exciting. If you want a great English class, and a good chance at an A, drop in here
Engaging, funny, and an amazingly specific recommender for grad school. You'll be a better person for taking her class. WOW.

WONDERFUL class. She makes an effort to get to know everyone, & the lectures are actually really interesting & fun. Tests aren't very hard if you go to class. The homework assignments could be kind of annoying but they were never too bad.
Really fun lectures, it actually flies by. If you go to class and take notes, you will do well in the class.

Prof. Curzan is an excellent professor. She's extremely fair - go to class, take notes and do the reading - you'll do well.  Her expectations are realistic, she explains things well, and she is a very nice and helpful person.  Best prof in the English dep
very very fun professor

Hes really nice to the class as a whole but shows favoritism. Says he wants us to contribute with any questions/connections no matter how random, but then clearly thinks certain questions are dumb or just gives blank stares at some students' contributions. I still liked the class but it was discouraging and kinda sad as one of his non-favorites tbh
Professor Currie is one of the nicest professors Ive had at UM. He really cares about the material and the course was super interesting as well. I definitely recommend!

Bill is so great! He really cares about the environment and teaches 201 in an easy way. Always open to hear your questions and create a little discussion. This class really primed the way for me in environmental knowledge and overall inspired me to pursue the major.

Even though the material was boring, I like Currie as a teacher. Seems like he wants to get to know his students. Cute in an old man way. Very nice and tries to crack the dad jokes to get a laugh out of the class.

Profesor Currie took time to make a study guide for this semester. I personally love this class and I didn't think he was boring. The average for the first test was like 90% I think, and the second was 86% I think. You will need to have the book, but the homework is super easy.

Professor Currie really knows his stuff but his lectures are very boring. He expects students to know everything that he spits out of his mouth. The exams often had just random information from either the textbook or lecture, so you never truly knew what would be on it. GSI's did not really help either.

By far the worst class.  The lectures are boring because he is boring and if you miss class the lecture slides are super unhelpful because the text does not make sense and it's all pictures. He will complain the midterm grades are bad and then wont give any extra help for the final.  The final is on 24 30-page chapters with no study materials.

Do not recommend this class. Dr. Currie's explanations of things can be really confusing and he's very unclear of what you're supposed to learn for the exams. Speaking of which, the exams were very difficult and entirely based on how good your memory is, not your understanding of the concepts.
It is impossible to describe how boring his lectures are. The GSIs do a better job.
No Comments
really cool and funny. awesome class. hahaha ssss!

He is a very very tough grader. He is looking for very specific things. Participation and attendance doesnt matter. He only gave one A on our first paper and not many on the other two. There were only 3 papers that determined out grade that were all graded harshly. Hes funny and interesting, but a bit harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He literally gives feedback to your essay sentence to sentence (in an extremely timely manner)and writes encouraging notes/suggestions to you. If you want to improve your writing, take him. The class itself is also extremel interesting. Srdjan is an amazing lecturer, hilarious, insightful, and provocative. Lovely classmates too (even through zoom)!

Srdjan is incredible. He's funny, witty, approachable, and leads deeply thought-provoking and intriguing discussions. Be ready to read and come to class with your thoughts and you're set to go. Also, go to his office hours! His feedback is exceptional and you'll walk away feeling smarter than when you got there. A+ lecturer, truly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures, intriguing discussions, and yes, he's totally hot.

Reports of his difficulty are largely overblown. Yeah, you gotta put in the effort to do well, but if you do well if you put that effort it. Expect about 50-100 pages of the novel to read for each class period. There's a lot of writing, but it's also a FYWR so it's expected. Also, his feedback is INCREDIBLE, take advantage; he's really smart!

Really caring, genuine and down-to-earth. He is a tough grader but he's also fair and tells you how to get by. Extremely understanding. Discussions can go off-topic and really philosophical occasionally but they're always interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Srdjan is a great professor. He's so chill and laid-back. He does assign a good amount of work, but if you don't always have time to do the readings, you'll still do fine. He's a tough grader, but you could still pull off an A if you work hard.

I'm in the class he TAs right now. He taught one of the sections, and he was amazing. It was maybe the best class all semester... He's really smart, and if you go to office hours its amazing - he's really helpful. The class is really difficult, but he will really help you figure out the stuff. Oh, and he's totally hot...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's a man who already has a Ph.D. in Philosophy and is pursuing one in Comp Lit. He's verbose, and sometimes the twists of logic he makes can be a little much. But he's a genuinely nice guy who really does want the best for his students. He'll grade you hard, especially at the beginning. But if you listen, and if you read, you'll do great.

Hes awesome. I didnt always know what he was talking about...(he gets lost in his own thoughts sometime, i think) and he goes of topic, but he comes back. Hes super smart and really nice. Be prepared to think. He wont tell you what to do. Youll have to figure it out yourself. Office hours are great. And, on the eyes... omg

Single-handedly made me hate videography with a passion. Assigns a crazy amount of homework and will criticize things you literally have no control over. Insanely petty and passive aggressive. She has no respect for anyone or their time. Literally half of the class doesn't show up to class anymore. People have genuinely given up. RUN!!!

never made assignments or deadlines clear, made classes very stressful and gave a TON of homework and projects. graded critiques very harshly and would never give anyone an A. very rude as well when me and some classmates asked her for tools she was so passive aggressive about it. best to avoid...

She seems intimidating but is actually very sweet! However she doesn't always respond to emails which can be very frustrating. She is BIG into getting you to challenge yourself so the class can be pretty difficult. Love her as a person, would rather not take a class with her again, but you could still really enjoy it if you love film.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everything was very unclear in Cynthia's class. She rarely used canvas, wasn't clear on deadlines, and never issued grades. I had no clue how I was doing in the class until a midterm update and final grade. She was very kind to talk to, but the constant confusion wasn't worth it for me.

Cynthia is awesome, she leaves her assignments very open which some people may interpret as confusing, but she just wants you to push your ideas. She is one of the only stamps professors that I feel give real critiques and doesn't just say "this looks good" and moves on.

The instruction of this course lacked preparedness and explanation to the students. Although Professor Pachikara is a very smart woman and a passionate artist, she lacked attention to the class and could not also stay true to her word. Cynthia offered zero explanation and left students hanging very often. I felt confused all the time in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cynthia is a smart & passionate professor, which I liked. However, the way she taught was disorganized & quite unclear. Assignment descriptions & class usage were complex & often confusing, and steps leading up to projects generally seemed unnecessary. Overall, great thinker but didn't like her teaching style & it made learning difficult.

I had to drop this class because of other things going on. Professor Pachickara was incredibly kind throughout the whole process. She is a hard grader because she aims to push students to strive to do better. Her class is hard but if you are committed to video work, she's a wonderful teacher to learn from. Just be ready for the amount of work.

I can understand why Cynthia may have mixed ratings and reviews, but if you give her something that she has never seen before and get experimental with your final products, you will do well in her class.

THIS PROFESSOR NEVER RESPONDS TO EMAILS. VERY UNHELPFUL. In this class you are basically on your own because she doesn't respond to your emails when you ask for help or have a problem in the class. Very disappointing and stressful. Would not recommend!

She was definitely just okay. If she didn't like students, she made it obvious. It was hard to get substantial feedback from her. I dont really feel like I learned that much from this class. It never seemed like she had anything planned before getting to class. I wouldn't recommend her.

I had some trouble during the semester and found myself with a lot more work than I could handle all of a sudden. Cynthia worked with me after the semester was pretty much over and gave me a second chance. Interesting class with a teacher who cares. :)

She is the best ever. She promotes thinking in projects. She shows very good videos in the class and critiques your projects very well. This is my second class I've taken from her. I learned a lot from her.

She was nice but she wasn't teaching us what she was trained in, so she gave us the wrong information and then expected something that another professor actually told us wasn't possible. We were the guinea pigs of her class.
Great teacher, I took her video class and got a lot out of it.  She made it facinatiang and was tough at points but fair.  I recomend her.
She's easy, but not the best teacher.
She's a really bad teacher.  She's easy, but not the best teacher.
She really cares about her students, and she wants students to learn. Her lectures were great.

Finelli was an amazing professor. I wasn't even in her lecture but she gave me access to her lecture recordings, which was absolutely worth it because she teaches so well. She does the perfect ratio of examples and teaching, and still takes time to explain more of topics the class is confused on. She also provides a free textbook pdf alternative.

I don't think there was a single lecture where she didn't make a mistake. On top of that, the class required purchase of a $90 online textbook, and the lecture notes were not sufficient enough to understand the homework questions. Very poorly taught. If you have the choice, take 215 with a different professor.

EECS 215 is a hard class but Finelli is a solid choice. She really cares about students and actually takes feedback to heart, unlike most professors. For example, she gave us 2 attempts and later deadline on all HW after students complained. She does in class "active learning" where we each work on problems and really engages us to learn.
Great, caring teacher. The book is very helpful, and she goes at an understandable pace. Notes from online, lecture recorded, just overall a good professor

Very nice and approachable and gives excellent lectures with lots of examples. Every other lecture de facto mandatory with quizzes. Homework was apparently less than previous semesters, and I thought it was about the perfect amount. I spent no more than 3 hours on a single assignment. Labs could be time consuming but are uniform between sections.

She's nice and tries to learn everyone's names, and does. Knows her stuff and can teach the material. Gives a ridiculous amount of homework. I took this with 280 and 203 and it was by far the biggest time crunch. Homework at the beginning takes 2-3 hours but then takes 7-12 later (every week-13hw) Lab sucked a lot too(5h per lab--GSI were good tho)
Finelli gives example based lectures which are really helpful when doing your homework. EECS 215 is hard in general, but she does her best to make it easier.

Dr Fenske is amazing. She no longer teaches at U of M, I have her for nursing classes at a different university but regardless, shes very caring and wants you to be an amazing nurse. She is very patient and teachers at a very comprehensible level, no matter the subject. I feel I can go to her for anything and shes always willing to teach.

Dr. Fenske is great, she is so caring and wants you to succeed. She has your best interest at heart, just as long as you put in effort and do your best. She's very thorough on what she teaches, she'll go slow enough for you to take good notes, but not too slow that it's boring. You can get an A in her class if you take notes & study her powerpoints
No Comments

Not a good professor, would not recommend. She's unclear at times and her examples are too easy which leaves you clueless when it gets time to do the hw. Doesn't really prepare you for the exams, and cannot really tell you the key concepts behind a certain topic. Bland overall.
She's alright at explaining things in lecture. But if you ask her questions one on one, she is very helpful.

Cynthia is an OK teacher. She moves pretty quickly in notes; be sure to keep up. My only beef with her is that she doesn't say what she's writing verbatim, and she stands in front of the board, so you have to wait for her to move. Exams are a lot harder since they reorganized the course. I hear that she is still better than other teachers for 216.

Cynthia Vinzant was perhaps the worst math teacher I have ever had. I'll cut her some slack because it was her first year, but her methods of teaching were anything but engaging or helpful. Our class did horrendously on all the tests and all the other sections were prepared.
She is very nice but not very good at teaching.
Awesome professor. I highly recommend taking a class with her.
Blame students for his own failure in teaching. Funny, but gives you bad grade. Avoid if you can.

Very knowledgeable. Has a good sense of humor, though it's different. May seem unapproachable. Very helpful, but he needs to know you need help, he won't seek you. You need to put in an honest effort, he expects one. Fair grader depending on your effort.
No Comments

Cindee was a kind professor and overall very accessible outside of class. However, no matter how much work I put into this class it was never good enough. This class is EXTREMELY time consuming and there's so much content to grasp. The most difficult class I've taken thus far at U of M.

Cindee is a pretty good prof. She has very dry humor which I enjoyed lol The class is very hard and time consuming though. 3 hrs lecture a week, 4 hrs discussion, and 1-2 hrs of online lectures each week will have you going crazy. Grade is dependent on exams which are so freaking hard. Her teaching is meh. Not much to say about her good or bad tbh

Watching the online lecture videos is crucial to your success in the class. Overall, Cindee is super awesome and prepares you for every exam. It's up to you to use what you know for studying and application, though. Exams are a little more difficult, but all questions are multiple-choice, which is helpful.

The most caring and supportive professor I've had at Michigan. I took her course my freshman year (Winter 2023), and now I realize how much of a gem she was. I wish I stayed in touch, because she really changed my trajectory! She stands for everything CSP should be.
Stay on top of your pre-recorded lectures and do the pre-readings and you'll do fine. Cindee is a great prof and made biology really enjoyable! She also has lots of office hours.
Super kind and makes your first biology class at umich great!

Cindee is a great professor. Compared to many other CSP professors, allegedly she has the best methods of teaching. Weekly quizzes, watch pre-recorded lectures, and exit tickets after every discussion. I would highly recommend going to her office hours as well. She explains everything very well and makes jokes to make the class more fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Personally did not enjoy her class.

Bio 171 is a hard course with pre-recorded videos, 4 exams, and weekly quizzes. However, with Cindee it was amazing! She makes sure you understand everything thoroughly and if you have questions she'll answer them to the best of her ability. Compared to other professors, Cindee is a god when helping other students.

Bio 171 can be a hard class to adjust to as a first year, with weekly quizzes and 4 exams, but Cindee honestly was such an amazing professor. She was funny and quirky, made it her goal to get to know her students, and was always willing to help you learn. You have to make an effort to learn the material, but she wants all her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cindee is a fine prof but I was never well enough prepared for exams as they're VERY different from practice exams, problem sets, clicker q's, etc. She often lets class get off topic/distracted and makes uncomfortable jokes. She is really kind though and you can tell she's very passionate. I would opt for a diff prof based on teaching ability.

AMAZING. She is such a kind person and connects with the class. She is very open to meeting up and trying to help you improve and understand the material. She is definitely there to help and she is a funny, caring person in the process.

Absolutely loved Cindee. She knew where students had trouble, and she knows how to fix it. She's been teaching BIO 171 for I think 36 semesters now so she's got it under her belt. 10/10 recommend, probably the best prof I've had yet. Class itself was pretty hard but Cindee made it better.

Super understanding with COVID. She wants her students to succeed and it's beyond encouraging to just go into office hours and talk to her. Some details can be a little unclear after lectures, but she will do everything she can to make that confusion clear if you ask. There's so much material covered but she'll do as much as she can to help.

Prof. Giffen is a passionate and caring professor. She makes the material fun, interesting, and interactive which makes you look forward to showing up to class everyday even though it was early in the morning. She is just awesome and I wish she could teach all the STEM classes at UM.
Although 171 was a boring class, Professor Giffen taught content really well and made sure you were prepared for exams. Overall, great professor.
The absolute best professor I have had at the University of Michigan.
Giffen was very welcoming and understanding to any question we had. I highly disliked that we had exams every 2 weeks that basically made up our grades.

Cindee Giffen is the best professor I've had at the University of Michigan. She truly cares about her students and will do everything she can to make sure we understand the concepts. I'd definitely recommend taking the class with Cindee. Also, make sure to go to office hours if you don't understand something, she'll help through the material.

She is one of the best stem professors Ive had at Michigan. She is kind and caring about any and all situations. I couldnt recommend taking her class more. The exams are okay, but nothing some studying and OH cant help you figure out! She even has personal appointments if you want one on one help:) Best teacher ever!

I really enjoyed having Cindee as my first science instructor at U-M. She is extremely kind and very clearly passionate about the material. There were some technical problems that mislead the class a few times, but those likely won't affect future classes. I wish I could take her Bio 173 class, but she isn't teaching it next semester!

Professor Giffen was decent. She cares a lot about her students. Sometimes, I find myself struggling to keep up with her lectures since she doesnt explain the material that well. Tests were pretty confusing especially with the wording.

Prof Giffen is one of my favorite profs at umich; she's super passionate, extremely down to earth, and very approachable! Class was originally supposed to be held at UMBS, but due to covid it was online. I still felt that the course was super valuable, and assignments were helpful. Expectations were clear & instructors were accessible during OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cindee is an amazing professor. She's so passionate about what she teaches and it shows during lecture. She never passes up an opportunity to make jokes and lighten the mood with such a lecture and exam heavy course. Please go to office hours and use all the resources she tells you to use. The course is still a weeder, no matter the professor.

Cindee is very knowledgable about her subject and can explain things in several different ways. She is very available outside of class, has a great, kind of cheesy, sense of humor, and explains and grades very clearly. iClickers are major. Doing the readings are very important. Not *too* much work for Bio class.
She's a great professor! Office hours are very personal even with other student there. Can explain topics in many different way. Highly recommended.

Cindee is so helpful and approachable. She is so passionate about her job and is a gifted TEACHER. I would definitely recommend taking bio 171 with her she is the best teacher I have ever had and would always meet with me extra to make sure I understood the concepts.

Probably one of the best teachers I've come across so far. The class is difficult, but Cindee makes its bearable. Don't expect an easy A here, even if it is an 'introductory level' course. Office hours are extremely helpful, and really take advantage of them if you need the clarification. Cindee's the only reason I made it through the class.

I am most certainly not a biology major and in fact I find it quite boring, but Professor Giffen is the best professor I've ever had at Michigan thus far. She's so kind and will do anything she can to help you succeed in her class. The lectures are engaging and interesting even for someone like me. I highly recommend taking this class with her!
She is a really nice person and is easy to talk to. Goes out of her way for students.

Cindee was amazing for Bio 171. She made the class entertaining and always tried to keep us interested in the material. She also tried to help us calm down before the exams by telling jokes or giving us candy canes. I'd 100% recommend Cindee as a professor, she made this class more fun than I expected it to be.

A lot of work for a two credit course. Professor is very specific about the answers she wants on short answer exams and papers; hard to read what she will test on and focus on. Is out to deduct points anyway possible. Must always be on your A game in order to do well. You learn a lot from the class, but lets face it, GPAs matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Cindee was very helpful during office hours and answered questions clearly. Had her for bio lab for spring, and tbh the grading was a little tough. There were lots of group projects I wish were more individual. Overall an okay class and teacher.

Test questions are poorly worded expecting answers in a very narrow scope. You may find that you have given a very detailed correct answer, but since the more general answer was the one mysteriously on the key that you have now missed several points.

Cindee was great. The class was very difficult, but I highly recommend taking with Cindee. She made Bio fun and I truly enjoyed having her as a teacher . I saw her in office hours almost everyday and she was so helpful.  She like to push her liberal views a lot towards students, but she is one of the most caring people I have ever met. Great prof

The class is difficult, but taking it with Cindee it became one of my favorite classes. She really cares for her students and makes the lectures worth going to. I would highly recommend taking a class with her because you really do learn a lot especially since she is not judgmental so you can walk into her office hours completely clueless.
Overly passionate about ecology. Says "right" after every sentence. Overall not a bad teacher, just kind of annoying. Good for CSP.

Cindee was fine. I recommend just buying the access to launchpad because you don't really need the book otherwise. Bio is difficult at U of M. If you study it is definitely possible to get a good grade. Iclicker is a MUST.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Easily the BEST class I have taken. It's based on a straight point scale which means that you can only get 36 points off out of 360 to get a 90% in the course. Exam 1 had a 32/50 point average (18 points off there). And the rest of your points  are easily lost despite your understanding of the concepts.  Much Fun. 9/10 would watch again.

Cindee is a phenomenal instructor. She is not only VERY intelligent but is also very relatable to students. She is super down to Earth and makes the time pass by much quicker than you'd expect. I wish all pre-med professors were as easy going as she is. HIGHLY recommend going to office hours-- she really cares about her student's success.

Cindee is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She's willing to work with you for hours on whatever you need and she's not condescending in any way. She's also just hilarious. The class itself was a little bit hard but she tried to make it really fun.

Cindee (as she likes to be called) is really, really passionate about the success of her students. Her office hours were always filled with students and she was always available to help and have extended hours for us. Lectures and discussions could be really long sometimes but her jokes made up for it. Really great professor!
Her lectures are long and boring. Lectures don't prepare you for lab.

I'd recommend EEB 335 with Dr. Green to anyone interested in biodiversity research or biology/environment grad school. You attend weekly seminars from visiting/in-house scholars, speak in a small peer group with the researchers, and develop scientific presentation and comprehension skills. Dr. Green is extremely kind, accommodating, and supportive.
He is a nice caring guy but his teaching skills are lacking. What he presented in class was in no way related to what he tested on exams. Avoid him if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Green is a great guy, he really enjoys genetics and is quite accessible outside of class, however he isn't the greatest public speaker often making small mistakes while talking which makes the lectures a bit more confusing, especially as much of the examples he makes are only made available in the physical lecture. He is not evil or mean.

Although I don't believe that Dr. Green deserves 5/5, I'm hoping to increase his score because I thought he was a good professor. He clearly was passionate and cared about what he was talking about, and in comparison to other professors in hard biology classes that have decent scores, he is very comparable.

Going to lecture is a waste of your time. Simply do the homeworks and the practice exams to prep for exams bc lecture content is ridiculously simple compared to exam content, you can teach yourself the concepts. I truly feel bad for Dr. Green, he has passion but has marginal lecturing and clarification skills.
Horribly spoken and unhelpful. Lectures are pointless

He clearly loves teaching but he is not good at it. He would frequently misspeak and either correct himself after the lecture or go back during lecture, resulting in our class being very behind. He also struggled to teach the course material and answer questions in a clear, concise matter.

I am convinced a stillborn could lecture more effectively than Dr. Green. The "examples" given in lecture don't test  the topic being taught; rather, they are so simple you find the answer with basic number sense and intuition. I've taught myself almost everything I've learned in this class. Also, instructors rarely respond to Piazza questions.

Dr. Green isn't that bad... looking at problem roulette he's actually one of the few professors who have easier questions- sometimes he isn't super clear though! Don't focus too much on memorizing lecture content! Learn the material a little+SPAM PROBLEM ROULETTE if u can do his problem roulette qs then you'll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Lacks confidence while lecturing, leading to a drop in focus across the entire classroom. Constantly forgets what to say and then proceeds to check his notes; I could hear the chatter in the room rise IMMEDIATELY. 

Horribly off topic sometimes and "accepts the null hypothesis". What? Teaches this class like a stats class and gets THAT wrong?

Bad.
This guy is the worst lecturer ever

I marked this “inspirational” because if someone this inept can be paid to teach, there's hope for absolutely anyone. During lecture, he does not sound very knowledgeable or like an authority figure on the subject presented. His lectures are unorganized word salad and very shallow in terms of content taught. Not to mention boring.

Probably the most boring lecturer at umich. His monotonous tone with no engagement during lecture is a snoozefest, especially with such complicated and uninteresting material. No efforts made to simplify concepts or truly explain the concepts going on. Look at the rest of his reviews lol

Had a friend who had already taken genetics with another professor sit in on the class, within 5 minutes turns to me and says he's awful. He has a very slow and monotonous voice. His explanation of basic concepts become so convoluted you don't know what he is talking about. Slides are subpar. Worse than biochem and orgo lecturers. Seems nice tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Read his Pre lecture notes and do the practice exams...You will fall in sleep even if you go to his lectures...Nice Guy but emmm, don't really know how to teach

He is definitely not the best lecturer and often uses roundabout ways to explain concepts that could be simpler. However, people are way too harsh. The exams are very doable and all practice exams and homeworks are indicative of what will be on the exams, he in no way wants you to fail. Office hours are also helpful.

I agree that the class is doable and exams are fair if you do the HW and practice exams. Still, he's an awful lecturer and the lectures are a waste of time, but you have to go for graded clicker questions. The GSIs are effectively teaching the material through problems in discussion. I'm sure he's a nice guy, just can't explain anything.

Everything is doable if you do readings on your own and do all the practice work. However, it's a waste of my time to come to a 1.5 hr lecture just to listen to him spend half the lecture covering simple definitions that he manages to make convoluted.
Ehh. Not the worst, but definitely not the best.

He conveys material...but there is absolutely no joy or self-awareness in his teaching. Never, not once, does he pause for questions; he does not engage students. Very hard to pay attention because of this. Most professors say things like, "This make sense?" or "hello class" or "a way to remember this is..." Dr. Green simply doesn't do that.

He tends to speak on the slower side, which can make it hard to focus in lecture. But at the end of the day, he covers the material, and his past exams are decent reflections of actual exam questions. He's also very willing to help students if you reach out. The course is hard, and you have to put in the work - don't blame it all on the professor.

I've definitely had better profs before, but ultimately his expectations are pretty fair. This is a difficult course for sure (like orgo, biochem, every single other premed weed out class), but the exams are very similar to recent practice exams. I don't think Dr. Green is any worse than profs for other classes, genetics is just a hard subject

First exam attended all lectures; did all pre-lecture notes/readings, discussions, homework, and a few of the practice exams. I did above average -- if you can be a college student you'll do fine in this course. There are iClicker difficulties but all professors have issues with that. On top of that, articulate in lecture. L ratings. Sad asl

This professor talks in simlish and is not very clear when he lectures. IClicker is more or less mandatory and he doesn't know how to use it. Never finishes lecture material and somehow discussion sections are new content (which is a first in my college career). Seems like a nice guy, but a very confusing professor.

OK -- he isn't 5/5 by any means, but you all are dragging this man for no reason. I'm not sure if he's changed up his style, but after finishing the first exam of the course, his exam was exactly representative of the practice exams he provided. Go to class, take notes, do outside work, ask questions -- BE A COLLEGE STUDENT -- and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There's a reason why he's only an assistant professor and should stay an assistant professor, until he learns how to use iClicker.
So bad... His lecture is so unclear, too much readings and homework, leaving students puzzling. Please choose other semester or other lecturers, he's goonna drag down your GPA.
Seemed like his ultimate goal was to leave students as unprepared as possible for the exams
Seemed like he wanted us to do poorly.
Lectures were a mess and the practice exam had 0 correlation in difficulty to the real exams. Avoid him at all costs. Seemed like he wanted his students to do poorly as he hoped for a C+ average.

Probably the worst professor I've had at Michigan. Couldn't explain anything well during lecture. His annotations consisted of him drawing arrows on powerpoints. Graded iclicker Qs seconds after we learned the material. Almost always went over time, so we were always behind in lectures.

Dr. Green is incredibly nice and willing to go through things in office hours or email in depth to try to explain the material to you. However lectures are often all over the place and material is not explained well. The content does not translate to exams very well. Graded i-clicker questions on brand new material you learned seconds before is :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is way overcomplicated & difficult with no altercations to the grading scale/curve to make up for this. He makes points but does not sufficiently explain them & speeds through the material to try to cover every topic regardless if the class understands it or not. Material is taught in a horrible sequence jumping between unrelated topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The iclicker questions are needlessly cruel and count toward the grade. He will show what he majority of the class is answering and watch them gravitate toward an incorrect answer, then tell all of them they were wrong. The exams are difficult and only multiple choice with significant time pressure. There is no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Green is clearly very knowledgeable in the subject. His exams are a bit difficult but he is very accessible outside of class and during office hours he really helps break down topics you find confusing. He cares about his students and wants to see them do well.

Do not choose him! PPTs are fancy but not helpful at all. Online classes are not efficient. You have to do tremendous work on your own to comprehend the material. There was always a question mark in my head when he was explaining things. He could not explain things precisely to address student's common questions.

Intentionally underprepares students to meet projected B-/C+ average. Explicitly told us practice problems reflected exam material, but the first exam was unlike anything we'd seen (D average). Doesn't curve. Concerns expressed by students were entirely ignored. Doesn't seem to care if we succeed or not. Immensely stressful and unenjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have never studied so hard for a class yet performed so terribly, with zero academic or emotional support/understanding from a professor. Dr. Green is obviously extremely intelligent, but avoid taking a class with him if at all possible.

It was his first time teaching this semester, but the lack of sympathy is apparent. Hopefully he learns to care more about his students and consider them more than he did this semester, especially during COVID. It's unbelievable that a professor doesn't find anything wrong with half his class failing and makes no improvement.

Does not provide adequate study materials for exams, had many mistakes in his homework solutions, live lectures were not helpful, homework and practice exam difficulty was no where near the difficulty of the exam. Would not recommend him.

Juan was an okay 232 professor. He was pretty impatient with students. I was 1 minute late to class and he was very upset and ignored me for the entirety of lecture. Other than that, he prepares you semi-well but I suggest you spend time outside of class learning topics.

be sure to pay attention in his class cause he will randomly look at you and call on you but i really enjoyed his class and thought he was great - usually very accessible outside of class with his office hours

his grading criteria is never clear. I got an A on the speaking final, got an 87.64 and the department wouldn't let him round up to a B+. He cold calls every class, and because the department changed the syllabus again, participation isn't worth anything. Overall, okay professor, horrible department. Put time into studying Spanish every day.

honestly he's a really friendly guy and accomdating, really made my last semester in spanish much better cause i had him for span 232, would recommend. def study a lot for his class but he was a great spanish teacher!

Juan was extremely personable, and he will like you if you put forth effort. Homework was easy and exams were reasonable, but it's a good idea to practice writing about topics on your own time to prepare for in-class writing assignments. If there is a reading/video assigned, do not come to class without watching it. Highly recommend.
He's a little boring but his class content was generally accessible and tests were never as hard as they could've been.

Juan was by far one of the worst spanish professors I have ever had. He was unwilling to accomodate and his Podcast quizzes are extremely difficult. Most of the questions asked had multiple correct answers. Also, he always deducts many points from writing and was extremely unfair during the interview project. Do not take him by all means. Rude too.

I don't know what the other reviews are talking about I loved Juan. He was super cool, an easy grader, and the tests were not very hard. He was always helpful if you attended office hours, and was more than willing to help if you asked. He was never mean or rude, but he cold-calls every single question so if you aren't okay with that don't take him

worst Spanish professor I've ever had. he grades extremely tough and he's not that nice. He gets mad if you don't know the answer. I was always scared to go to class and dreaded it everyday. Horrible at teaching and just not nice. tests and quizzes extremely hard. run away
He was such a tough grader and was not the nicest of teachers.
horrible grades way too hard and does not give an opportunity to get grade up

Juan was the best spanish teacher I have ever had. Not getting a solid A was entirely on me, he definitely was not the easiest grader ever but he was far from unfair. I had a wonderful time in his class

Also don't understand why students have rated his teaching low. I personally thought he was a straightforward lecturer and his presenting always matched the slides given. Microbiology is by no means easy, and having short answer questions on exams can be stressful, but he always answered any of my questions after class and held helpful office hours
I don't understand the negative reviews on here. Prof. Denef is great. Microbio is not easy but he made it feel a lot better. Lectures were interesting and easy to follow. Great guy as well.

Despite some of the reviews, I actually really liked Prof. Denef. He has detailed lectures and is direct and clear. He makes class accessible to everyone and you can tell is very intelligent. Microbio itself is just hard so be willing to work outside of class, but Denef provides quality instruction and is always prepared.

I enjoyed this class a lot although that may depend on what section you have. He does present a large amount of information which only a certain unknown amount will appear on the exam. There were a few poorly worded questions for exams. My best advice is going to office hours as the professors for this class kind of spoil parts of the exam.

What I don't get is how this professor consistently writes exams in which the grade average is way below expected but then acts like it was normal. Absolutely no accountability of how bad the professor is by any other staff and the grade breakdown of the class is horrendous. Do not take this professor wait until another one is available!
Stay away from this guy

Is nice but can not teach or make exams for his life. Puts in all grades on deadline date so no disputes can happen over exam questions even though every exam before had questions that were awarded points back.
Do not take this professor.
I want to fight this guy, do not take him.

His lectures are horribly boring and are incredibly in-depth. He expects you to understand everything after only mentioning the content once. Tests are incredibly hard and give you very little guidance on what to know/how in-depth. I would definitely stay away from this professor.

The professor expects a lot without teaching everything specifically. His exams have extra credit and even buffer points and the class average is still a full grade lower than expected and yet the professor is completely unaware. It's as if the professors don't reflect on whether their exams are poorly written. Also grading from sections are diff.

Test are VERY difficult. You get automatic extra credit on exams which is nice. However, entire class receives about 60% grade even with the extra credit is pretty telling... Has lecture concept sheets which are nice. Boring lectures, however, iclicker questions are important for the exam. iclicker not graded.

Lectures were confusing, he did not seem prepared to lecture, and it seemed like he was speaking his train of thought rather than explaining (and he mumbles!) Practice material and slides did not reflect exam material, and concepts on the exam were not well-explained in class. Find another way to learn the material, his lectures will not teach you.

Easy A and class was super interesting, can't ask for anything more than that :) I will say that if you are a science major, the content in this class is relatively surface level. This semester it was 1 credit and a half semester which was even better tbh. Highly recommend.

If you are looking for an easy natural science credit I highly recommend. Initially I thought the class would be much more interesting but it was not all that. However, he is a very nice guy and if you show up to class for the most part and raise your hand you should be good. Take it with a friend because you need notes from lecture for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is really easy. Its not bio heavy at all and Denef does a reasonably good job of teaching. You should go to class because the online slides are kind of hard to follow but assessments are mostly based on the general themes with some specific case studies he goes over in class. He's super available over email too. He wants ppl to do well.

I took this class for an easy natural science class, and had some interest in learning about the ethics of genetics. Readings and class discussions were very interesting but the grading was somewhat unclear on exams. Don't take this if you're just looking for an easy A. I recommend this class if you have a sincere interest in the topic.

EEB 446 was pretty easy, as far as upper-level EEB classes go. If you understand each lecture, study the main concepts before exams, and put effort into your project, you'll do fine. Dr. Denef isn't a tough grader. Also, you really don't need to read the papers. This class was interesting and really helpful if you're interested in ecology.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This is a great class to take if you are looking for an upper level EEB class or are interested in microbial ecology. Prof Denef can be kind of confusing at times, but the class is so small that its easy to ask him to re-explain something. Mostly he just wants you to read the given articles for lecture and put effort into the independent project

This class is much more dependent on your assigned group than the professors themselves. Prof L has good intentions and is very sociable, but I did not learn anything engineering-related in this class (whether that's a reflection of her or IOE itself, I'm not sure). More importantly--pray for a competent group.

My biggest piece of advice is to go to Debra's office hours. Grading criteria weren't always super clear, but I would ask during office hours, which cleared things up. This class is basically one huge group project. I got lucky with my group, but definitely start the deliverables early so you can get feedback and ask questions.

If nothing else Professor Levantrosser is a character. She learns everyone's name, has awesome outfits, is vocal about her vegan food truck, big veteran supporter, and is the type to start up a casual convo with students. Exams were kind of poorly written (and LONG) but you can get points back if you argue that the question was phrased weird.
She is alright, all the previous reviews are true. The class is high workload and grading criteria isn't the most clear. Don't let her catch you on your phone or else you're cooked.

Was worried seeing the ratings that I would not like her as I tend to keep my own in class. Debra finds a way to make the class interactive without callouts or putting people on the spot. If you are looking for a blowoff class she may not be the teacher you looking for, however, if you hope to learn the subject material, she is the best.
Very Fun Professor! She  loves to engage with the  class and tries to learn everyone names. She is very lenient with grading. She talks a lot about her vegan food truck and her personal life often.
I love Debra's classes I take them whenever I can! She is super engaging and so fun to be in a class with, and is always open to negotiating the grading!
Chill frfr. Class was EZ PZ.

Issues about her business promotion and calling out electronics & yawning are definitely true. Lecture material is very easy; most topics could be learned in 10 minutes looking over slides if it weren't for attendance policy (for which some students apparently faced honor code for falsifying). We were required to attend 8-10PM Friday concert.

Do not take a class with Debra. Every semester students try to rationalize her weird grading strategies, narcissistic personality, and unethical promotions of her business by saying that she has corporate experience, but that does not mean she is a good lecturer. She will learn everyone's name, but mainly so she abrasively can call people out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Most of the students I have told about my experience with Debra have a story, whether funny, sad, or weird, of their own that they can tell about the professor. I enjoy the material in the class, but I really do not like the way she teaches it. Take the class if you want to have your own Debra story, otherwise take a different one.

Debra makes a point to learn everyone's name in class, only so she can call out people who haven't participated, have any electronics out around them, or look particularly tired. She is way too personal with some of her students and promotes her external business all the time. The IA's office hours are wildly more helpful than Debra's.

Debra's lectures consist of her calling out students for yawning and checking their phones and unethically promoting her business outside the University. I found her extremely inaccessible and hard to talk to. Students either thought she was crazy in a funny way or crazy in a bad way. Tests have ridiculously hard crossword puzzles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Active engagement helps with the late class time. Definitely one of my favorite professors in the department. Understanding and helpful. Beware, projects are time consuming and there is a very large amount of reading.

Debra's style is learning every student's name and then asking questions throughout the lecture. Most students speak at least once each class, and she picks people who aren't paying attention. Definitely a more personalized lecture style in a large university. Be prepared to shut down your laptop and engage with your professor and classmates.
I loved class with Debra and learning all about her vegan food truck and consulting roles! She was a great lecturer and an even better person. Highly recommend taking a class with her!

I thought 425 was a good class but Debra is very self centered at times.  She talks way too much about herself.  Especially her food truck, veganism, and relationships.  It was very unprofessional.  She also gives students crap for yawning.  Overall a straightforward class but our final exam was ridiculous and dropped my grade a lot.

IOE 425 was great thanks to the professor! she has a very unique style of teaching which makes the class fun and interesting to attend. Expect time consuming group projects that are very helpful and interesting.

Debra is very good at trying to engage her students. It was her first time teaching the class so it was slightly unorganized. Don't bother buying the book. I found the pdf online and didn't use it very much at all. Attendance was "mandatory" more so for a percentage of participation. Material is interesting sometimes. Overall, class was solid.

Debra is not looking to fail any of her students. She teaches with the goal of students practically applying what they've learned in real life. To that end, her exams were  not difficult, as she had students write most of the exam questions themselves. This was very helpful when studying, as we knew exactly what to expect for the most part.

Exams are very easy and the homework is good practice. One project that is not that difficult. Lectures can kind of drag since they are two hours but are not too painful. All around good class and professor.

Do not take classes with this lecturer (she teaches IOE 421 and IOE 425) Irritating personality during lectures with little patience Behaves harshly towards students who are on their phoneslaptops Lectures are disorganized and exams are confusing Promotes her personal business that is borderline unethical Don't buy the textbook
Didn't even look up from his phone when talking to him during office hours

The "practice exam" given is significantly, significantly easier than the actual exam, which had an average grade of 70% (and he did not give us a curve). Professor was uncommunicative, both via slack and email. Insanely difficult class.
It's okay

DW is basically our dad. He meets with us for extra lessons ON WEEKENDS. Of all the professors I have met, he is the most invested in his students by a mile. Incredible teacher of jazz arranging, big band, improvisation, and trombone. I would not change a thing about my time here, but I wish there was an 8th day of the week for even more lessons.

DW cares more about his students than himself. Will give you lessons outside of class on weekends if you ask. Will do literally anything to advocate for his students and provides them all with great opportunities. He can come off as intense sometimes, but it's all in good fun, and he has the best intentions. Take arranging 2.
DW may be disorganized, but he respects the tradition of the music and he programs lots of charts by black musicians.
He is disorganized that half of the class time is lost
Dennis is all over the place and it makes this class exhausting.
not a great time
DW is so disorganized Im not sure how he makes it to class in one piece.
Constantly contradicting himself. I feel exhausted after some of the rehearsals.
Dennis needs to retire. There are students who have been unable to graduate due to this disorganized, sad excuse of a class.
No organizational skills. NONE. He's a great guy though.

While disorganization can sometimes lead to a bit of wasted time, DW knows his stuff. He genuinely cares about his students, checking in on their academic life as well as how things are going in general. He is approachable and incredibly generous with his time outside of his classes.

DW has a lot to offer for jazz musicians at any level; taking Jazz Lab with him should be considered a privilege. While he definitely can be disorganized sometimes, he genuinely cares about his students and will help you grow as a player and a person.
Super hit or miss. Sometimes rehearsal is straight ahead and fun, but sometimes he's all over the place and it's hell. ZERO organization...
Do you hate yourself? If you do then take this class, because he hates you too.

I have been in this class for 2000 years now, it never ends, it never ends, it never ends, it never ends, it never ends.  I am forgetting everything that I have known before this class.  I am this class, I am this teacher, I might be god, I dont know anymore.  realizing I know nothing and that all knowledge is meaningless is all this class gives.
this class gave me cancer. please save us

Dennis is a true master of his art, jazz. You will be very lucky to be in one of his groups because he has a truly unique skillset & decorated jazz background. He will make you work hard and his music choices aren't easy, but you won't regret taking jazz with him. He might come off as full of himself, but really, he just loves jazz and his students

Wilson is often unclear of what he wants. He doesn't seem to have a clear teaching method. He would often forget what tunes my combo was playing and what we had already rehearsed. He is a nice guy and well meaning, but often is intense. He is very good at arranging and gives sparatic tips that very useful. Overall he was not helpful for me.
Great teacher and a great personality to be around and work with.

Fantastic instructor, hard to reach sometimes, but cares a great deal about students. Fun guy with great personality and work experience. Anyone who says anything else simply wasn't making the effort. Kudos DW ;)
No Comments
No Comments

She did have very high expectations, but if they were not met she was willing to explain what problems were. The discussions were very student led, which seemed difficult at first, but later on it was very easy to follow along and take part. She helped me to become a better writer, and although there were a lot of papers, most were not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I went to her office hours all last semester but she's still pretty useless. She just asks a bunch of repetitive questions back at you when you go up to her for questions. The class discussions are student-led and very little teacher input. She has really high expectations for a freshman. Plz be careful! Do not recommend! Also no clear rubric!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Amrita is more of a supervisor than a teacher. Lots of busy work and assignments that you should be able to blow off if you're a good writer. But she leaves everything up to you as a student. When asking about help her common response is "What do you want?"...So if you prefer almost no structure, this class is for you. But I wouldn't recommend it.

Switched into this class because another professor was rated poorly on this site. Worst decision of my life. Amrita is condescending, not helpful, and takes her job as a GSI way too seriously. If you want to come out of an English class with any sanity, find another teacher.

Vague instructions, no real explanation of what she wants. And yet she expected us to know exactly what that was, and graded very harshly afterwards. Doesn't seem to realize this is an undergrad, usually freshman, class. Random coursepack store nobody's heard of, always closed, and she ended up posting them online anyway. Facilis descensus Amrita.

Yeah never take english 125 with amrita.  AWFUL teacher. Ridiculous work load.  Never gives an essay prompt but is extremely critical after we turn them in.  If you can't give on average 3 hours a day to this class, don't take it with her. nobody got time for that

Often times rude and condescending. Directions are sometimes unclear. Coursepack was hardly used and ended up being put up online so I wasted my money. Expects a lot for freshman english, often too much.

(WGS 331) She allows no excused absences. I went to a funeral and gave her a week of notice and she still wouldn't give me an excused. Most of the class felt like a humiliation ritual... she would have us do peer review for our final projects and then pick apart any advice anyone would give. The last half of the semester could've been an email.

331: One of the most disorganized classes I've taken. Deadlines constantly change (midterm said Wednesday, was due Saturday), class randomly switches between Zoom and in-person with no clear notice, and expectations aren't clear. She assigns group work over break with the expectation of you meeting with your group. Easy grade, but not worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff and is passionate about the topic. Lectures are composed of slides with a TON of info on them but they are all made available on canvas so you don't need to rush and take a ton of notes. We have biweekly quizzes but they do not go towards your final grade. 1/2 the semester is lectures, 1/2 is personal interest project.

Probably my least favorite professor at UM. No absences allowed, no laptops for notes allowed unless proof of disability on file, slides are PACKED with information that she SPED through, changed the syllabus multiple times with little to no warning, is unorganized. It is obvious she knows her stuff, she just is not a great teacher and is rude.

Would you take this professor again is a sad question when the favorite professor of so many has resigned. Dr. Dhar's knowledge knows no bounds but for all her brilliance and creativity, she was kind and caring too. There were so many tears when she said goodbye. She said she'd always love us no matter where she is and we can write to her anytime.

Dr. Dhar was fantastic. She was incredibly inspirational and this is one of those classes I will never forget. She was respectful, funny, and one of those professors that clearly cared about students. I will miss Dr. Dhar!!

Dr. Dhar is brilliant, courageous and kind. So many of us took every course she taught, for HER and how amazing she is and not just the course. How she lives her life making bold, unconventional decisions every step of the way is INCREDIBLY inspiring. WE ARE CHEERING FOR YOU TODAY AND EVERYDAY, DR. DHAR!!

The waitlists for Debotri Dhar's classes are VERY long and it can be annoying to wait for 2 years to study with her. This class was totally worth it tho. She basically retells world history/politics though a gender-based violence lens. She is so inspiring and connects theory and real world policies and also shares cool career and life advice.

Dr. Dhar has so much knowledge, politics and economics, law and literature. Seriously talented and versatile. What you will love most is her authenticity. This wasn't just a course, it changed my life.

As a graduating senior, this was my favorite course at U-M, and Debotri Dhar easily the best professor! The course texts she picked out were intellectually stimulating and Prof. Dhar is so interesting and inspiring as a person. She taught us life skills and has become my role model.

Eye opening course! Professor Dhar is very knowledgeable and nuanced in her lectures on world affairs. WGS 345 should be required for every college student of Political Science, International Studies, Law, and Public Policy.

Professor Dhar has designed a delightful course on women and literature, and teaches it in such an engaging way. She is pretty intelligent and warm. Just do the readings and stay on top of the weekly journals.

Prof. Dhar is definitely knowledgeable and caring. If you have not done the work and are failing the course, she gives you the opportunity to withdraw or suggests a different course. Even offers help with time management, speed reading skills!

Dr. Dhar is one of my favorite professors! I also took WGS 313 with Dr. Dhar during COVID and her class made my weeks better. Dr. Dhar is caring and easy to talk to. I recommend scheduling office hours to chat and doing the readings! I think Dr. Dhar facilitates discussion really well and I get to hear from all my classmates.

Assigned LOTS of reading, which would have been fine - if we actually discussed any of it. WGS330 is a very broad and introductory course that requires a more guided approach, which she did not do at all. We pretty much chatted for the entire class. When I voiced my concerns, she accused me of personally attacking her and told me to drop the class.

Dr. Dhar is a brilliant young scholar, and a warm and inspiring professor with a talent for teaching. Like others have said, she is good at simplifying complex theoretical concepts and making them super interesting and relevant. Shes also helpful with career planning and advice if you ask. Be sure to read and participate in class discussions.

This class requires a lot of reading but Dr. Dhar did a great job of synthesizing main parts during class & the frequent student presentations helped provide other interesting perspectives. She was the most inspiring professor I've ever had and these were the most insightful class discussions! Honestly one of my fav classes even tho it was required

I have recommended Dr. Dhar to anyone who is looking at taking a women studies course. She is super passionate about the subject and open to discussing anything the students want to bring up, and she brings in personal and real-world experiences.
Dr. Dhar is the best professor I have encountered so far at UMich. She is kind and truly cares about her students. She is great at explaining concepts and connecting class material to current issues.

Dr. Dhar is an amazing professor and lecturer. She truly cares about her students and their success and understands that the material being covered can be very heavy. I have never had such a candid professor that is open with her students and just wants every to succeed. I highly recommend taking ANY class with her and would definitely take another

Could listen to her talk for hours. Ive never had a class where I felt so empowered or represented. Also shes so good at creating a discussion in the class and carefully listening to all the points made by students. So happy I got to take a class with her!

Sweetest human ever! Truly values the wellbeing of her students and is passionate about her work. Would love to take another class with her. No exams or papers. Very easy to succeed in her class as long as you stay on top of readings. She keeps discussions engaging, relevant, and interesting... love Dr. Dhar and her class!

Professor Dhar is an amazing professor! She is very knowledgeable about the topics she teaches and she is always open to new ideas from students. She is wonderful at fostering communication in class and ensures that students comments and questions were a valuable part of the class. I would HIGHLY recommend taking a class with Professor Dhar.

Dr. Dhar is my favorite professor I have had at the University of Michigan. She is first and foremost an amazing human being. You will learn a great deal not only from the course content but also from her and the conversations she prompts. We developed both a great understanding of various forms of feminist thought and a sense of community.
Dr. Dhar never passed back any grades and you didnt know where you stood in the class until the very end.

Dr. Dhar is a brilliant and inspiring professor and very caring person, who connects warmly with everyone. Even when going through a challenging time herself, she showed up for her students in a way that was so empowering for the whole class. Definitely take a class with her!

Brilliant and inspiring. Caring, but not a pushover (and respects the work rather than false excuses :) Class participation really matters. Take advantage of rolling deadlines to receive grades early. Overall, an excellent learning experience.

WomenStd 330 is an introductory class on feminist thought and theory.  Grades were based on class participation, an autobiographical essay, class presentation, analytical paper, creative project, and the course evaluation.  I received one grade back the entire semester and she would not tell students their presentation grades when they asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I thought I was going to be bored in this class, but instead it was one of the most interesting classes of the semester. Dr Dhar is very understanding, and really gives you a different perspective of women's studies that I greatly enjoyed!

I took WOMENSTD 345: Sexual Violence and the State with Dr. Dhar. Not only is she a brilliant scholar with an amazing resume, but she is also extremely caring and encouraging. I learned so much about sexual violence from this class and was introduced to a wide range of perspectives. Take any class with her that you can! You will not regret it!

The only professor at umich I truly dislike. The class environment was not supportive or encouraging and honestly made me feel uncomfortable and not supported. I have personal experiences that affect my learning and she didn't make me feel like I could share that with her or have her support. She constantly talked down to students unkindly.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've had. She constantly put down students, spoke in a condescending tone, and showed no effort to understand different perspectives. Instead of creating an encouraging learning environment, she made class stressful and unproductive.

A very easy class that counts for the natural science requirement. Homework and class work is only looked at for completion. I thought lectures were interesting, but everyone is different. She has some rules, but they are very easy to follow and conversations can be interesting. Overall, a very easy and good class/teacher.

Unfortunately, I had to take this class in order to graduate. I would completely recommend to stay away if you are not in the same boat. Students, including myself would consistently receive 50-75% on the quizzes/HW assignments despite pulling the information from the literal lecture slides. She also loves to belittle students who ask questions!!!

Overall, this class was a LOT of work. Be prepared to put in a lot of time each week, especially in the beginning of the semester. Quizzes were tough, but not impossible as long as you keep up with content. However, Dr. Spillane was a great prof and really wants students to succeed.
