Best way to fulfill your natural science requirement! Dr. Spillane really cares about her students. Super chill class with weekly homework & classwork that's graded on completion, one final presentation at the end. Literally just show up and you'll be fine

Please run from this class, there are so many wonderful MCDB labs at UofM, and as long as Dr. 
Spillane is teaching MCDB 306, your eyes I hope will be elsewhere on the LSA course guide. The class received 60% averages on both of the large exams, and she claims the grades were "better than expected" and opted for no curve. She's just awesome!

Very good prof, if anything is unclear in lecture come to office hours and she is more than willing to help you understand anything in the content or homework, or work with you if you're struggling with anything going on in life.

Dr. Spillane's exams are touted to be "very clear and understandable" -- but then the exam proceeds to be the most convoluted, unintuitive thing ever written. When the class received a 66% average on the first exam, she said it was our fault. I'm warning you, this lab course was more stressful than the actual Genetics lecture itself. Don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took this class to fulfill my NS requirement and glad I did! There was barely any homework, just weekly worksheets, and no exams, definitely an easy A. She's super knowledgable and sweet, a good lecturer, and wanted to make sure everyone got their questions answered. Although I'm not a science person I enjoyed her course a lot!

100% recommend. Incredibly approachable and helpful. Only lab instructor I've ever had that actually lends a hand in the experiments - helping you sort worms and flies, double checking your plates and vials, and even helping you transfer those incredibly frustrating worms. 306 would be really annoying if taught by anyone else.

I like her. Her slides are organized in a good logic and if you are unclear about something, reviewing slides can help a lot. I really hope other lecturers can be as clear as her. However, 306 does require a lot of extra time and it's really important to have a good partner. Good luck.

MCDB306 is a lot of work. 3-6 hours of extra lab work on some weeks, but the class itself is very rewarding. You'll be doing research like real scientists and actually discovering things. Also Spillane is super nice and easy to talk to. Make sure you go to her office hours. Most of the credit comes from HW and papers and those are graded leniently.

Genetics Lab is not nearly as bad as everyone says it is. Is it a lot of work? Yes. Are the exams hard? Yes. Does it require lab work outside of class time? Yes. Is working with the c. elegans worms annoying? You bet.  Despite these things, Dr. Spillane makes everything extremely clear and is a FANTASTIC resource is you need help. Would recommend.

Wow, the best.  She explains everything very clearly and is also clear about what you need to know/don't need for exams.  No textbook, powerpoint only so that's a plus, and the material combines bio, history and societal studies so it's really interesting.  Highly recommend!  I got an A+ with minimal studying.

Dr. Spillane extremely sweet, articulate, and knowledgable. No papers or homework. I don't find this class that difficult, but I'm also a 3rd year pre-med student....For anyone just trying to fill a science requirement, note that although there's a focus on cultural/society/history, this is still a bio class and biology does indeed appear on exams

No homework, no essays, no reading (basically no outside work ever) and just three multiple choice exams. Seriously the easiest class ever. If you need a few natural science credits like I did, take this class and pass fail it. Interesting material, so you can just sit back and listen without worrying about your grade. Best choice I made.

Tis was favorite class of the semester! Dianne does a good job telling you what you need to know for exams and there's no hw!! Diane breaks up the 90 minute lectures with iClicker questions and video clips. Lectures were boring at times considering this class is for non majors and I'm a bio major but I still loved it.

Spillane is a very clear professor and you can learn a lot from her. Easy class where you can also learn interesting things. Only minus is that class is at 8:30. Other than that, low commitment class. Only need to attend half the lectures and only outside work is studying for exams. Show up to lecture and pay attention and you'll get a high grade.
Very funny and genuine. Extremely helpful-especially if you attend office hours. Explains the material well and knows what is important.

Spillane requires that students attend only 50% of the lectures and she puts all the slides online, so the class is manageable.  She basically reads off the lecture slides, so students don't really pay much attention.  The material can be tricky, but generally it's pretty straightforward.  Just study the week before each exam and you'll be fine.

She's alright as a teacher but nothing special. You have to go to 50% of the lectures which is annoying but doable. She dumbs everything down and it was extremely repetitive for me as a nursing student. The powerpoints give you all of the information that you need for exams. Overall a decent class.

The powerpoints are very clear and the exams are based right on them. If you attend lecture and listen, you'll pretty much get everything. no work other than multiple choice exams. study for a couple days and they're pretty easy. she's helpful and interesting.

Extremely easy, if you attend class (or if not read the lecture notes which are posted online). I never took notes and my studying comprised of rereading the notes she posted. The books are interesting, but not necessary to get an A.

The class is def not a lot of work at all, but it is easy to screw up if you don't know the stuff.  Practice exams bear little resemblance to the actual exams and getting an A is by no means a given.  Spillane comes off as very kind and reasonable, but I challenged her poorly worded exams twice and received discourteous emails in response.

From what I hear this was once an easy class for non-science concentrators. However, word has it that the class average was too high in previous semesters and the course curriculum and exams were changed. I would not recommend taking it if you are not a science major.

Professor Spillane makes 830 in the morning 2 times a week not as awful as it may sound.  I took this class because i heard it was easy but she made it very enjoyable. Definitely take this class for an easy A on an interesting topic and if you aren't a big fan of NS classes!

I don't know what happened, but this semester, this class was very biology heavy and difficult to understand. Hopefully a curve will be in effect. The material is usually on the slides but there are a lot of slides and some are difficult to understand.

Awesome professor.  She will do everything she can to make things clear especially because a lot of people who take the class aren't science majors.  The test questions come straight from the slides and basic questions from the reading.
Incredibly easy class, she put all her slides online and information was interesting.

it suscks bc classes are at 8:30 in the morning but you don't really have to go. All the questions come from the book and the slides. she is good at explaining if you don't understand things. The discussion quizzes are difficult but if you read you are fine, they are trying to fix that.

Lecture is NOT mandatory. All questions come directly from lecture slides or discussion. This semester we started a new policy of having weekly quizzes on the book reading, so reading the book IS mandatory. The quizzes can sometimes be confusing, and are the worst part of class. However, this class is relatively easy.
Really easy, don't even really need to read the books, if you go to discussion they go over any q's that will be on the exams. Exams were easy.

Prof. Spillane is a little spacey during lecture, but if you attend lecture regularly and study a day or so for the exams you will do fine. The material is actually extremely interesting and I ended up altering my major because of this class.
lecture is not boring

Tries really hard to be helpful, but not necessarily a hard class anyways.  Very nice, reads 100% off of powerpoint slides so lecture isn't necessary. Discussion also not necessary.  No textbooks, just 2 novels. Interesting class, though.
Prepare to teach yourself all the content. He's a nice guy and he does try I just don't think he's a very naturally gifted teacher. TA was lowkey hot
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dimou provides all the materials you need to succeed: detailed notes, clear lectures, ample office hours. He's welcoming of questions and doesn't not seem burdened when you need extra help. MATH 3100 was a lot of content and had some confusing concepts, but if you come in ready to work, you'll be fine. Enjoyed this class and this professor!
I really did not enjoy his teaching and I feel like I taught myself the entire class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Dimou was a good teacher. Lectured clearly. Super stingy with partial credit. Luckily the final grade was comprised of a lot of homework and participation
Hes great and pronounced words great
He's pretty great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Take this class if you love math and greek accents. Ratings range from "he's cool I guess" and "he's good about office hours" to "don't take this class it's very hard."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Nice teacher, nice gsis, studied for every exam the day of and still got an A, section attendance is graded tho so make sure to pull up to those and do every extra credit

This class is literally just common sense. It expands a little bit on AP Psych topics but not by much. Every lecture is just the week's textbook reading regurgitated. Exams are extremely easy as well, you lowkey don't even need to study.

I thought Dr. Gohar was a great professor, she was funny and engaging and lectures were always interesting. My only issue with the class were the exams. Sometimes the study guides and exams contained material we haven't learned yet. My advice: please go through all materials given to you, some questions were based on concepts mentioned like once

Word for word reading the slides, majority of the course was covered in the textbook so I still went to class but I didn't need to besides to just know lecture points for the exam. The content was interesting but the slides were also went through quickly, and recordings only available with advance request. Very easy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Gohar makes lectures enjoyable and engaging! She explains concepts well with pop culture examples, I didn't miss a single class! I enjoy how Dr Gohar creates a classroom environment where students are encouraged to ask questions. I appreciated the chance to explain what I got wrong on the midterm for partial credit to encourage a growth mindset
Dina was an amazing lecturer. She always explained things in an easy way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Gohar is kind, approachable, and very knowledgeable on the subject and does a good job making lectures intriguing. As far as the class goes, there is definitely a lot of content, but is manageable if you study. Overall, this was a great course and I hope to take another class with Dr. Gohar in the future!

Dr. Gohar was engaged, but I felt some lectures were all over the place, and there were constant technology issues (obviously, these were not her fault)  that made the class really disorganized. Her GSIs this semester had a hard time explaining concepts during the review sessions and struggled to answer student questions. Very easy overall though.
Dr. Gohar is extremely qualified and an incredible lecturer. Psych 280 is very content heavy, but it's not too bad. Study and you'll do good.

Truly horrible professor. She did two lectures, while students gave the lectures the rest of the semester as she played on her phone. Also incredibly disorganized and made it the students' problem without taking responsibility. Do not take psych of musical theater, no matter how fun it may sound.

Dina made fulfilling the psych methods requirement as painless as possible! She's really kind and provides dynamic lectures for otherwise dry content. Dina is always available to work one-on-one with you to understand class material, research project development, or even just to chat about what's on your mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and Prof. Gohar taught well! However, I would often skip lectures as they were recorded and mostly based on the slides. My favorite part of the class was my discussion because I had a great GSI. Overall, easy class with little extra work and interesting concepts!

After having hit–or–miss psychology classes, I love Dr.Gohar! She was a perfect teacher. Amazing lectures and incredibly organized. I honestly was looking at more psychology classes with her.I really loved learning from her,she was incredible at her job.I love how she often used pop culture examples to deepen our understanding in familiar ways too.

Dr. Gohar did an excellent job of presenting what is usually considered "dry" material in an engaging way. I appreciated the frequent use of examples and opportunities to interpret figures & tables of findings in class. I really enjoyed Dr.Gohar's style of teaching found class to be and educational yet relaxed & welcoming environment for everyone!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Gohar is super knowledgeable about social psych and I feel like I learned a lot in her class! She's a fast lecturer, but I took hand written notes and was fine. Tests cover content in the textbook/lectures- highly recommend making flashcards. Discussion was light and she drops the lower of your 2 test scores.

Dr. Gohar is very kind and knowledgable about psych. The material that she discusses is interesting, but at times can be very broad. She also talks very fast, so it can be difficult to understand her. Otherwise, as long as you engage in lecture, discussion, and the hw assignments, it's a cool & relatively easy class.

Dr. Gohar is really caring, and her class includes many interesting film clips as examples. However, she always just paraphrases the material on the slides without a deeper explanation. The content is too broad but not deep, and you rarely feel the joy of thinking. Her class suits you if you want a basic understanding of social psychology.

Dr. Gohar really cares about her students and puts a lot of time and effort into her lectures. The group project is really fun, and a lot better than writing exams and papers. The grading is straight forward if you follow the rubric. She gives a lot of feedback, and if you follow it you will end up with a good grade. Will recommend to my friends!

This was an awesome class! The topics were so interesting and I learned a lot about happiness that I applied to my own life. Dr. Gohar was a great professor and very passionate about the subjects. The group project was very fun and allowed my group a lot of creative freedom to explore the topic we chose to the extent we wanted to.

Dr.Gohar is very nice and cares about her students, but this class was SO disorganized and difficult to navigate. Grading is confusing and the group project is so painful. It's a class on happiness, but it just stressed me out. Unfortunately most people in the class ended up hating it.

Dr. Gohar has a deep understanding of the material and is very passionate about psychology. She is great at teaching tough concepts in an engaging and easy to understand way, and is always ready to help outside of class. Her exams are exactly based on course content and contain no surprises. She is also super sweet and accomodating!

Dr.Gohar was one of the best psychology teachers I've ever had at UMich! She was very clear in her teachings and I learned a lot throughout the semester.She was always open to answering questions and did all she could to make sure we were getting out of the class what we put into it.She was enthusiastic and made the learning environment comfortable

Dr.Gohar made fulfilling the psych methods requirement as painless as possible! She's really kind and provides dynamic lectures for otherwise dry content. Gives helpful feedback and always available to work one-on-one with you to understand class material,research project development,or even just to chat about what's on your mind.Highly recommend!

Dr. Gohar was one of the kindest professors I've had at the University of Michigan. She was incredibly understanding while also pushing students to be and do their best! She turned one of my most dreaded courses into something that really interested me and made research methods relevant to us. I'm so grateful I got to take a class with Dr. Gohar!
JUST NO, i Liked the class it self but boy the way she grades things is not ok!!!!!!!!

Dr. Gohar shows unmatched care and attentiveness towards her students. As her student, I felt comfortable reaching out for help and could tell how much she wanted us to succeed! Dr. Gohar is exceptional at developing lectures geared towards her students to maximize our learning and retention. Overall, she is an amazing professor!!

I really enjoyed this class.The material's so interesting&I really appreciated Prof.Gohar's teaching
style!She made lectures interactive,fun&educational.Using videos,music,memes,demos&polls made me want to come to class&learn! Prof.Gohar's more than fair w/grading-she's kind&has lots of empathy for her students.I'd take this again&recommend to ALL!

Dr.Gohar is hands down the best Prof I've ever had in my 3yrs at UM!I wasn't super interested initially,but her teaching style helped me enjoy it more&motivated me to learn,even when I watched lectures on LectureCapture.Always present&ready to help all succeed.Reasonable workload.Not super into Psych,but I'd 100% love to take 1 of her classes again

Dr.Gohar's incredibly enthusiastic&clear.I understand all of the material when she explains it&she does so in a very engaging manner.Colorful, well organized slides w/funny images,videos,music&interactive polls.Never a boring lecture!It feels like she genuinely cares about students & we're set up to succeed!Very approachable & gives great resources

Dr. Gohar is knowledgeable and presents info clearly. However, I found her lectures to be a little boring. The discussion section was just a condensed version of the lecture. There are lecture quizzes to make sure you pay attention and Inquizitives due every week. Not too hard if you study a lot for the tests. 2 tests, lowest dropped, and a final.

Dr. Gohar is an amazing professor!Of all the courses I have taken at UofM,this was the most interactive in that the material connected relevantly to her students. We learned about psychology while also practicing resilience exercises ourselves&this experiential seminar was extremely enjoyable. All assignments felt worthwhile,not like busy work&fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What an interesting class! Dr. Gohar made the course interactive and fun. She is full of energy and brings that to her teaching. This class made me learn a lot about myself, and I learned things that I will likely carry with me forever. Would definitely recommend this course, or any course taught by Dr. Gohar!

Dr. Gohar is a clinical psychologist and brings that expertise. Tons of psych interventions implemented into the cirriculum. Way too many peer reviews + self-reflections, and many assignments did not teach anything. Note: the class was not about learning how to *do* therapy; it was more about learning how to *be in* therapy. Mind the difference!

Whilst most classes will teach you how to make money at best, Dina teaches you how to live a worthwhile life, filled with happiness. Dina really cares about her students and goes above and beyond to make sure we have the resources and support we need! Would highly recommend her class to anyone!

Chris is super caring and kind. Lectures were a bit confusing, so be prepared to do some extra learning outside of class. Chris cares so much about his students and was willing to stay after office hours to help.

I'm pretty good at math so 105 wasn't hard for me, but it prob would be hard if you have no basis in precalc. Some people felt like he was confusing. He explains math in terms of concepts and wants you to understand the "why" and not just memorize. He's super nice, responds to emails, will stay later in office hours for you, cares abt students

He is extremely nice, and each review my peers and I have tried to leave has been removed. I think he sees these and requests them to be taken down. Nice, but cannot teach at all. Concepts taught are frequently slightly different than the homework, masteries, and exams. He confuses more than teaches.

Diaz is an amazing lecturer! 203 tends to be very difficult to understand at first, but she does a great job of breaking concepts down and making them easy to understand. I wasn't registered for her section, but went to her lectures as often as I could. I would recommend her the most out of any of the 203 lecturers.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had! The course is hard and can be stressful if you fall behind, especially as I was also taking EECS 280 at the same time. However, Prof. Diaz is very supportive and caring, and wants to help you succeed in the class. She explains lecture material clearly and explains worksheets throughout each class.
difficult content, but a very good lecturer that made me feel prepared

Professor Diaz is an amazing lecturer. She truly cares about the experience of her students and is really clear in how she teaches. The class was not the easiest, but she definitely made it more manageable. The class had a homework and a checkpoint every week, which sometimes took a bit of time.

Prof Diaz is an amazing lecturer and her annotated slides and handouts made difficult topics so much easier to understand! She also makes it worth it to come to lecture in person over the recordings giving time to work with others on problems and build a community! This class is difficult but she made it accessible and enjoyable!
Literally the best 203 lecturer. I stop going to lectures because of how clear her recorded lecture is

Diaz had good lectures that had everything I needed to know. Stopped attending lectures and just watched the recordings a few weeks in because I had some conflicts. My only complaint is with the course design: the 3 exams are worth a lot. I messed up one exam and that screwed me out of an A. Just make sure to stay on top of everything.

Dr. Diaz manages the classroom well and cultivates a great culture of learning. I messed up my grade on the final and though a lower grade, I thought the material was well taught. Dr. Diaz does her best to drive student engagement and would highly recommend going in person.
She is entertaining and provides handouts/notes that provide information very well. I found them to be very useful for studying. Overall I found the class quite easy with the wonderful references.
Amazing and really helpful lectures!

i am thouroughly impressed- math wizard. although she started to use "trickery" she didn't let it get to her. 
wonder what the class would be like without horseplay.

Prof. Diaz was super great and I would 100% recommend her! This class is going to be tough regardless, but she made it more manageable. Definitely be prepared for a lot of weekly homework, most of which is graded on correctness. A lot of time and effort has to go into this class, but I genuinely enjoyed attending Prof. Diaz's lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really love Professor Diaz! She literally saves my life for eecs 203. I origianlly was not in her section and was very lost. Fortunately, I switched to hers. Her lectures were really clear and structured as what slides were. I love her teaching style and her handouts. She always wrote down notes on slides and that helped me a lot. Choose her!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is the best out of the other EECS203 professors, the class is still hard and you will need to study a lot outside of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Diaz is a solid choice if you are considering which section to attend for EECS 203. Very clear lectures and she made sure to address all the questions. She has a calmer and lower-tempo teaching style compared to Emily. I would recommend checking both their sections out to see who suits you better.

Professor Diaz was a great lecturer. EECS 203 goes at a pretty quick pace, but each lecture was very thorough and she stopped to answer any questions before, during, and after lecturing. Throughout the semester she would ask for our feedback and try new strategies to help us like printing out extra exercises and doing more problems on the board.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer and really cares about your learning and understanding of computer programming. Also, she tries her best to still do online lectures and accommodate for students who might be in a stressful time due to the pandemic. 10/10, wish all professors were like her!

EECS 183 is an awesome intro course, and Professor Diaz was a really great professor. You can tell she really cares about everyone engaging with the course and wants us to do well. Lectures don't always cover everything, since you're supposed to read the online book but she was always willing to explain a concept if you need help.
Explains difficult concepts very clearly and often asks if something isn't clear. Questions are always encouraged and always answered well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Diaz knew what she was teaching very well. Her lectures were pretty clear and she answered questions well. She sometimes went a bit of a slow pace so usually i had to look at the parts of the lecture we didn't get to for the hw. Attendance isn't mandatory but watching the lectures at least online is.

Professor Dick is a good lecturer. Every lecture is about a new subject, and you rarely get a boring lecture. For participation, the class uses iClicker, which mine didn't track the location (use this information at your discretion). Weekly quizzes are easy and a quick search. The exam was a compilation of the quiz questions, so studying was easy.

He is fantastic and this is exactly what a half-semester mini-course should be. Lectures were interesting and engaging. Class was structured in a way that makes it impossible to do poorly unless you actively avoid the class material. If you're looking for a light class for one more credit with an amazing professor, this is it.

He's a good professor, but expects a bit too much for a one credit, half-term course. We had to come to early lecture and get correct answers on iClicker and exam is not open-note unlike all of the mini Earth classes I have taken before here.

Gregory was an amazing professor. I looked forward to going to this class, and you can tell he is very passionate about what he is teaching. You have quizzes once a week, but it was questions already asked in lecture. Final exam is incredibly easy as well. If you just show up and pay attention in class you will pass with an A.

Great mini course. Nice intro to the Great Lakes. Greg clearly is passionate and enjoys what he teaches. Expectations are clear from the start. Light workload (as should be expected for a 1 credit course), and enjoyable. Recommend going to lecture or watching the recording.
Really into the subject he teaches. The quizzes and final did not feel overwhelming. If you take notes and pay attention in lecture it's an easy A. I thought it was a very interesting class.
This was a great short and quick class but gave a nice in-depth overall introduction into the Great Lakes. Prof. was very enthusiastic about the topic also.

The perfect one-credit class! The quizzes and one exam were pretty easy, and the lectures were interesting. This class got me to better appreciate the Great Lakes region. One of the best classes I've taken at Michigan!

His half of Earth 313 was really easy to understand and he provided a clear guideline of what we needed to know for exams. His lectures could be a bit boring after a while, but if you're passionate about the topic, he is a good source to get information from. Overall, an excellent professor who listens to students and works well with them.

Greg is very nice and good at explaining things. There are participation points, but it maxs out at a certain point so you don't have to attend every lecture. The exams were really straight forward if you study the lecture slides and in class questions (just be sure to memorize specific things and not just the general idea!)

Dr. Greg is an amazing professor! He does 1.5-hour lectures that are very interesting. He is very knowledgable on the topics related to the class and even outside on things such as jobs. He really cares about his classes. Very easy to do well and to pay attention as he is very pleasant to watch give a lecture.
LOVE HIM
Love Greg. Love the class. Talk to him outside of class as well if you can.

Greg is a great teacher. He can be relatively slow speaking at some times, but you really understand the content afterwards. Super nice guy, really accessible. Absolutely would take another class of his.

Greg's half of 313 was interesting but very stressful. He's interesting, but lectures are VERY dense and fast paced. I had a good 7-10 pages of notes per lecture. He covers so much microbiology content that it can be hard to follow if you are unfamiliar with the topic. It's hard to stay focused. Exams fairly difficult, but there is a good curve.

Good lecturer, but the material covered is pretty dense and sometimes hard to focus on for the entire 1.5 hour lecture.  Weekly quizzes are pretty easy.  Slides are very helpful and contain most of the information needed.  Greg is super nice and helpful.  I would take another class with him in a heartbeat if microbial life didn't drive me bonkers.

Greg's a really good and clear lecturer and answers questions thoroughly and enthusiastically. His lecture material consists of topics that I'm not too familiar with or understanding of, but he gets the information by well. Not an easy class, but doing well is very possible with attention and good notes.

Greg was a good lecturer and his slides usually had good information on them. He was very nice and willing to answer questions. The exam was harder than I expected it to be; it was very detailed rather than sticking to the bigger concepts. Overall though it was a great class!

Greg is a really great professor that loves what he is teaching. He is easy to listen to. Lectures aren't mandatory but he gives many hints and quiz questions out loud that aren't in the slides he posts. Tests are fairly easy, somewhat tricky but not too bad. Weekly quizzes make discussion mandatory, but they are easy.

Awesome teacher. I've had him for 2 classes. He is more passionate about his subject (microbio) than most academics I've met. Sometimes his material is complicated but he wants you to understand and his lectures are organized and clear. Take a class with him if you can!

Gregory Dick is a great professor. He is very easy to listen to and really wants to make sure that everyone understands what he's teaching. Very approachable and the lectures are helpful, though a lot of people skip lecture and do fine (all the lecture slides are on ctools). I would definitely recommend taking a class with this professor.

This course is how all minicourses should be at U of M. Very easy online quizzes (no time limit). You can just skim the slides to find the answers. The final was only 32 questions (26 were repeats from the online quizzes). I read through the slides for the first time an hour before the final. If you don't get an A, you truly do not belong here.
he's a good lecturer.  a few easy online quizes and 1 final

Great prof. Friendly, always willing to answer questions. Weekly quizzes are annoying b/c they make attendance mandatory but lecture slides are posted in full which make it very easy if you DO miss. Exams are easy except for the final exam which is cumulative.  Very interesting class- don't be dismayed by the wordy title!
Wonderful teacher. It can be easily seen that he is extremely smart, however, he is so patient to explain everything so clear. I am so lucky to take his class before he leaves UM.

Djordje is the best math teacher I have ever met. He's incredibly passionate about what he does, which is why he makes it challenging. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to go to class if you intend on doing well.

Dj is the best math teacher i have ever met. I cannot understand why would UM let him go.   If you are good at math, or have interests in math, take Dj's class! He is extremely brilliant and helpful. He sets his pace so well at every lecture.
Very dedicated teacher. Would schedule extra office hours before exams and proof sets were do and stay until late into the night. Difficult class with a lot of emphasis on proofs.

Professor Djorde is extremely enlightening. I am a former math olympiad student so the material is comprehensible. This time he split the class into 2 sections, the regular and the advanced just to make sure that the students without problem solving experience dont feel left behind.  Great Class, Great Teacher. wordofcaution-Attend it if you love m
a
What a great professor.  Class is hard as hell, but you KNOW the material afterwards.

Djordje genuinely cares that you understand number theory. He is very helpful in office hours. He is an excellent lecturer, probably the best I've had in math. He can really help you reach your best. Unfortunately, bringing out the best involves <20 hours of work a week. If you take a class from him, make sure you want it to be your first priority.

Very difficult course if you are not comfortable with proofs.  Djordje's expectations are very high and the content is very difficult, but he explains things very clearly and is entertaining when he lectures.  He is also extremely committed to helping outside of class.  In short, difficult class, but fascinating material and excellent professor.
He grades really really hard.  If you can, go with another professor for linear algebra.
He is a great guy, seems to enjoy teaching alot and also always holds extra office hours.     Especially before exams he would stay past midnight to help us out.
Djordje's really really tough.  No partial credit.

Probably one of the smartest Math Profs at UM. Former Ivy-leaguer, Djorde's quiz score ave. was about 8/20 and exam score ave. was 22/100. Needless to say, they are almost impossible. But the class is curved so as long as you beat the other half you'll be fine. Try to get to know him too, he's nice and really smart and can help during Office hrs

Djordje is a genius and knows what he is talking about.  He is from Princeton and is really smart but is too smart to teach. The board is filled with crazy problems and he grades really hard. He does not give partial credit so its either all or nothing. Hwk due once a week with Quiz once a week. Quizzes have TF and two hard problems which no one ge
Class is hard but the grading system is really helpful

I would avoid him. He is very smart and knowledgeable about economics, no doubt, but his teaching skills are subpar. His lectures are extremely monotonous, boring, unnecessarily math-heavy, and difficult to follow. Exam averages are like 70% and he doesn't curve at all, saying that homework extra credit makes up the difference (it actually doesn't)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: very hard and confusing lecture. He is helpful in office hour, but the materials are really confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'd like to defend this guy a little bit. Some complaints are fair but explains the material well and is helpful during OH. The "complicated" grading system is VERY simple. The homework is hard but is technically optional and only helps your grade and you get to keep your higher midterm. No worse than the average Econ teacher here.

It was his first time teaching the course and he clearly wasn't prepared. He didn't know how to help us study to his tests. We didn't have any practice exams to go off of or review sessions. The homework is lengthy and very difficult. His slides are very disorganized and hard to follow. He is very boring in lecture. I fell asleep. Don't take him.

I'll give him a little leeway since he says it's his first time teaching the course. That being said, he's made the course very difficult. The materials that we're using keep changing, you really need both textbooks to do well, homeworks are REALLY difficult compared to 401, and the grading scale is really strange. Go to office hours, and go often.
Hard exams and hard homework, avoid if you can.

Good luck not falling asleep in his lecture. Good luck understanding the questions he asks in homework and exam.  Good luck with the "interesting" grading system.  Good luck distinguish notation from 3 different resources.   If anyone is up for the experience of failing a major class, do not miss out on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures were confusing and hard to follow in class.  He had ok lecture notes on Ctools but they were from many years ago so they didn't necessarily follow the lecture from this year.  You only count one midterm and homework helps to weight how your midterm and final, so the grading is decent but I only got by because the GSI was awesome.

Prof. Stolayrov is a very traditional teacher. He basically does chalk-talks every class. It can seem difficult to follow them, but if you use outside resources (such as what he posts on ctools and the textbook) you'll be fine and things will flow more smoothly. His exams are fair and he only counts your best midterm. The final is not cumulative.
His lectures are very disorganized, he has no lecture slides and goes on writing math on the board for the duration of the class. He does not take questions well and he does not engage the class.

He is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, quite a bit of calculus in this class but it really explains what we see in the real world, wealth disparity across the globe explained with some math and solid growth theory.
This guy is really good.  Lectures are really interesting.  Exams are not as hard as what he presents in class.  If you stay on top of the material, you should be fine for the exams.
Knows his stuff but presents it in a very disorganized way. Great guy though. Exams are tough but grading system helps you.
Very very nice person and interesting too. Clarify lots of concepts I messed up before.
LOTS of math (including calculus) but he's extremely knowledgeable and fun to have as a prof. Watch out for the exams though - they're rough.
He is really knowlegable and helpful. Learned an awful lot from him. If you take 425, definitely go with him.
Mitya is an amazing professor. I learned a lot from him. He was very helpful at answering questions.
He was very kind and accomodating. He also helped me on outside course work.
Mitya is extremely helpful and inviting. His answers are very informative, and it's clear that he cares a lot about his students.
Professor Mitya is likely the nicest professor you will ever meet.

Mitya's class is extremely hard, and you should be sure that you want to work hard before enrolling. That being said, he is the most helpful and clear Professors in all of the land. His interest and faith in his students is limitless. He will never make you feel inadequate or stupid, and will always be there to help.
Had Mitya for 295 & 296, excellent instructor.  Was genuinely interested in the well being and academic success of his students, a credit to the department.
Mitya is swag // he's so cool i can brag // his classes you should take // a math major you will make // and honors math is so fly // i will hate to say good-bye.
Mityas the best.  His math jokes get me every time.  MITYA!! WOOT WOOT!
Mitya is an amazing teacher. He also has wicked awesome shoes.

Had Mitya for 395-6.  Taught the material in his own order using his own notes to great positive effect.  Learned everything I needed to know for the classes I'm now in (596 especially).  He also has great jokes.

Mitya is really cool.  Considering how hard the course is, he makes it fairly easy to understand.  In addition, if you do the homework and all, you are guarenteed an A, so even if you find it impossible, just stick with it and try your best, and you'll do fine
He goes way too fast
She is super nice and involved. By Fr 232 I was just ready to be done with the language requirement, but she made this class bearable. Great lecturer to have for french.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Enjoyable class. Understanding prof. Very generous with her time outside of class. Create a very good class dynamic.

Professor Van Doren was overall super helpful and nice—I really appreciated her structure and reasonable grading. Not so much on her, but 232 is definitely harder than 231, and her grading was definitely more difficult than I received in the pass (still reasonable though), but otherwise she was a really good French prof!

She is a great professor. She clearly explains material and helps with any and all questions. She grades on participation a little bit more tough than other professors but her dedication to participation only helps you succeed.

Helen was genuinely my favorite professor during my entire time at Umich. She's incredibly good at teaching so you rarely left the classroom confused. If there is a concept you are struggling on, she's incredibly helpful and makes you feel very comfortable asking for help. She's a fair grader and cares about what she teaches. I really recommend.
She's so caring and overall a great prof 10/10 would recommend. Encourages talking and makes all students feel welcome.

232 is a rough class. That being said, HVD is incredible and makes the class better. She is an INCREDIBLE teacher and makes tough content easy to understand. She is incredibly nice and builds a class that is fun to go to. She is truly a special teacher and If you have any chance to take her class do it. Easily one of the best in the department.

Good prof, very nice and super approachable and accessible. Everything is easy and controllable except participation. For the entire semester, nobody got above a 98 on participation, and the average was around 90%. Going to office hours (I only went once) and making a good impression early helped make mine go up.

Mme. VanDoren made my time in French 103 super easy and fun. She explained everything we needed to know very clearly and was a fair grader. Sometimes the VHL homework could get a little boring. If you participate at least twice a day, you'll get an A for participation. There are a lot of assignments graded, so don't slack off!!

Professeure Van Doren gives good feedback and does a good job of helping you when you are having trouble conveying your thoughts in French. The class is pretty easy if you do the homework and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love all my french with Van Doren!!!! Coll lady and makes having the class 4 times a week pretty bearable. Have never needed to meet with her for office hours, just do VHL and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Helen was such an amazing lecturer; the class is a little hard, especially at first, because it's taught completely in French (no speaking English in class) but she makes it clear what she's saying so you can understand. I loved her class and I hope I have her next semester for French 102. I would highly recommend her for anyone taking French 101!!

Awesome and one of my favorite profs in the French department! She explains the material really well and is always ready to help you learn. The activities in class were fun and made class go by really quickly everyday. Grading in the French department seems to be tough, but Helen was very fair and I saw a huge improvement in my French thanks to her

231 can be very demanding but Helen made the course fun and something to look forward to. She can be strict with pronunciation and grading but she genuinely wants you to do well and if you put in the effort she will help you drastically improve your French. Helen has a talent for teaching and explains things in a very easy and comprehensible manner

She assigns a lot of homework, so much that you'll get caught up in trying to finish it and not actually learning the material. She's a super nice person but only take this class if you're willing to put in significant time every night to teach yourself French
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: One of the best instructors that I have had at the university! The French courses can be tough, but Madame Van Doren always explains the material well and is more than willing to help you learn if you put in the effort. The activities she plans in class always help to solidify the material and she gives good feedback to help improve your French.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Definitely more work than I was expecting, expect several hours of homework each night. But Helen is extremely approachable and always wants to help, a great teacher! I found the textbook a bit confusing (extremely overpriced), you will def learn in this class.
The hour goes by quickly because class is highly enjoyable. Helen always seems very well prepared for class and makes the activities run smoothly. Strict, but  very approachable.

Helen was an amazing instructor. She has a talent for teaching. She, or at least 231 itself, is very demanding, but worth it. I learned a ton, and I think I learned it better because I had her as an instructor. I highly recommend her. She is helpful in and out of class.

Best instructor I've ever had! Enthusiastic, explains things well, clearly knows her field, extremely helpful outside of classroom, an understanding and interesting person as well. Take Helen, you won't regret it. P.S. Don't be shocked if you see one of her office hour is at 8am, she has a super healthy lifestyle.
Great teacher. Strict, but also very approachable.
I love Helen! She is so enthusiastic and explains French grammar very well. She is a great teacher, and very willing to help with any questions. I highly recommend her!
Helen was awesome. She's young and hip and smart and extremely helpful, she really cares about her students. She's strict but also very understanding. Take her.

Mandatory attendance sucks! However, she is a solid teacher & it is very hard if not impossible to not learn French in her class. She makes great use of the textbook and makes French fun (however awkward it may be). Helen is strict, but willing to listen. She is also nice to look at :).

Extremely easy class. Lisa Disch is a very easy professor and a very nice woman, but I feel like she was not even trying to challenge us. She usually ended class about half an hour early, which makes everyone happy, but it also gives the impression that she doesn't take teaching seriously. Oh well, political theory is a useless topic anyway.

Very engaging lectures, great sense of humor. Political theory isn't exactly the most fun topic, but she still makes it exciting by incorporating our opinions and writing into the lectures. Easy to get an A, a lot of your grade is automatically 100% for participation/submitting assignments, only two assignments that really get graded on a rubric.

Professor Disch is AMAZING. The class itself is very easy. She doesn't believe in exams so there are none. There's just one group paper and an individual final project. Class gets let out 30 minutes early because part of homework is watching lecture videos that are usually just 20 minutes long. Definitely recommend this class for anyone!
She is so fun and it's such an easy class like actually

Lisa is actually the best. She's so nice, really funny, and a great teacher. It takes a while to get to the political theory part of the class, but the combination of the prerecorded mini lecture and shorter lecture time is actually refreshing.

Prof. Disch was a fantastic professor. She has super engaging lectures, and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. Grading is dependent on your GSI, but its honestly pretty hard to do badly in the class as long as you stay on top of your work. No exams just one group paper and one individual short one. Highly recommend.
Super engaging and energetic. You don't really need to pay attention in lecture or to the readings, but she loves when you participate during the lecture.

Disch has great, engaging lectures and makes boring topics fun and current. Usually let us out early from lecture. No exams, just 2 papers and lots of group work in discussion. Fairly easy course, definitely not just for PoliSci majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed POLSCI 101 with Professor Disch! There are no exams, which makes the class low-stress, and lectures are engaging and enjoyable. Attendance is mandatory, but she makes it worth coming—plus you can watch one 20-minute lecture video outside of class and make a comment for credit. She's also lets students leave 30 minutes early.

Mandatory attendance for lectures where Disch never finishes slide decks and barely discusses content from the readings. Lectures only to ask students for opinions, then shares her own biased opinion, instead of teaching. Recycles lots of outdated materials. Do NOT take POLSCI with Disch if you actually want to learn political theory. GSI saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mandatory attendance for lectures that are nothing but a waste of time. Instead of teaching, Disch only calls on hands from students asking for opinions, meaning that slide decks are never completed in class, are extremely vague and barely related to the reading/reading quizzes. If you wish to ACTUALLY learn anything, do not take Disch's POLSCI101.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is so kind and the lectures are so engaging. My only complaint is about the GSIs and their impossible grading standards. Our GSI had to do a whole lecture on why he does NOT grade harshly and why he never gave anyone a perfect score. It was so bad that Professor Disch curved the class by 5%!

Prof Disch is very nice and engaging, and makes it a point to know all her students names which is impressive in a 250 person class. Her lectures were just based on discussing the readings where she pulled quotes from. Grading on the reading quizzes was tough. Honestly didn't learn too much from her style of lecture but easy A.

Disch is kind and tries to get to know all of her students. Lecture is just a big discussion about the reading you're supposed to do before class. Sometimes the readings can be long. There are no exams, just 2 short papers and a section-wide project. Because it is just based on the readings, I didn't learn a lot, but the class was super easy.

this is the worst class I have ever taken.  For a 101 class, the grading is completely unfair. During lectures, there is no teaching going on. All she does is pull quotes and ask the class what they think. Do not take this class

Whatever the class is, if Lisa is teaching it, I'll take it. By far the best professor in the entire university, she is clear, organized, respectful, and fun. Workload was light, no exams, and she is very willing to work with her students. I've never had a professor with such a loving soul, she always goes above and beyond to brighten our days.

Disch was genuinely a very enthusiastic and passionate lecturer for such a boring class topic. You could easily get an A in this class and never go to lecture, the discussions supplement you with everything you actually need to know. There are no tests, just 12 reading responses and 3 essays graded by a GSI, and the grading is pretty fair.

Dr. Disch is one of the funniest professors I have ever had. The lectures are very engaging and she is a very talented public speaker. The course contains a very manageable amount of work and an A is easily attainable.

Disch was a very good and interesting lecturer. The class was best when she connected ideas to modern events and ideas. Really not much classwork at all. However, the grading in this class made very close to zero sense. I felt like my GSI was just throwing darts at a dartboard. I guess I cannot really complain since I got an A in the class.

Prof. Disch was amazing. This class is reading heavy, and it is easier if you have a genuine interest in political science. However, my GSI made this class difficult, he often didn't show up for discussion and offered little to no instruction or help on assignments and then punished nearly everyone in his section with a low participation grade.
I've never met a professor who can teach a political science class with barely any bias during her lectures. Arguably one of the best in the entire department!

Most of the learning took place in online mini-lectures, with the in-class ones being primarily supplemental. She made an effort to remember names, and frequently engaged the class in participation, but the lectures could get boring. A lot of reading but you DON'T have to do it all, I didn't and got an A+. Has a very fair grading scheme.
The mini lectures make up majority of course content. Professor Disch is very kind and tires to make an engaging lecture. The GSIs are really what affect each students experience in this course.

Disch was great, the content however was painfully boring. (coming from a polsci major). She is really funny, but the lectures are mostly her calling on the same 15 people which I didn't love. Your grade is completely dependent on your GSI. She is super nice tho and lets class out 30 min early every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some cool things I would have wanted to know: class gets out 50 minutes early each day, Dr. Disch is hilarious, and she makes an effort to learn everyone's name despite being a 200+ lecture. I would take this class with her again if I needed to.

Although there's a lot of reading, it's manageable and you can choose which quizzes you take. Lectures are required but she makes them entertaining and clearly cares about her students. There are no exams and the grade is based on 3 papers, 12 quizzes, and participation. For the quizzes, the lowest grade you will can get is a 17/20.
Fun and engaging lectures. No tests/quizzes. Highly recommend!!

Professor Disch is one of my favorite professors! I highly recommend her class. She is funny, wholesome, and tries to get to know every student by name. I felt very welcomed in her class. She did not assign too much work, you need to do a reading before every class, but it isn't hard to catch on. No tests, 3 essays. Lets class out early.

Professor Disch tried to make her lectures funny and engaging, and you can tell she cared a lot about her students. There were only a few things we were graded on, and they were mostly papers, so it depended on your GSI's grading for that. There were also reading quizzes, but you only had to take 12 and you could choose when to take them.

Funniest professor I have ever taken a class with, no one else was laughing at her jokes (at least not out loud) but I was literally dying I could not hold in my laughter! Her lectures are literally TedTalk quality, they are super entertaining and informative. Grading varies by GSI, my GSI's grading was super annoying so fought for an A.
Lectures were easy to follow and notes were helpful on papers. Discussion section attendance is mandatory, but it's worth going to. Overall easy class where I learned a ton.

Overall, Disch was a great professor. While I never really had the chance to form a connection personally, as it was a large lecture, she was one of my better instructors. In-person lectures are mostly discussion-based and provide additional insight into the readings (there is A LOT of reading). The GSIs grade your work, so you need a good one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is a good lecturer given how dull some of the course content can be. The class is structured very well. Partial online lectures were helpful, the quizzes were relatively easy and the three micro themes had clear grading criteria. This class can be an easy A if you want it to be.

Lisa Disch is an amazing professor. This sem she utilized partial online lectures, so she would let us leave after about 50 mins of in-person lecture. Reading quizzes are relatively easy, and paper grading is fair. The content can be quite a drag since you're stuck in the 1800s for most of the class, but she makes up for it with her enthusiasm.

Prof. Disch is an enthusiastic passionate lecturer despite how incredibly boring the class content is. Although it isn't interesting, the class is very easy. Grading is fair and the assignments aren't hard at all. No exams or big papers. There's a lot of reading, but it doesn't need to be closely examined to get by. Disch is a very fair professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lisa was a fun lecturer. She seemed passionate about every thinker which was very refreshing. While lots of reading was involved, this class was easy and highly recommended for anyone interested in politics or getting a social science credit out of the way

Disch uses iclicker so you have to come to lectures, but I have never seen her lecture without a ton of energy and spirit. The course is interesting but it has a ton of readings and reading quizzes, but the grading is fair. If you are looking to take an introductory polsci course, this is the one to take with Disch.

High energy. Answer questions in lecture until she knows your name (sooner than you'll expect) and you'll have a great participation grade. Do the readings and watch the mini-lectures and you'll be fine. SO MUCH READING, and a lot's difficult. Take this class if you are interested in theory, if you aren't then it'll be tough and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content was pretty boring, but it was a really easy class overall. You could get through it with a good grade by doing the minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is boring unless you're passionate about theory. This is the sort of class you multitask in during lectures and honestly, I didn't even take notes. If you have done the readings and annotated those and watched the mini-lectures you don't need to take notes. She is a nice person even though she always lets the same 4 people talk.

I never went to lecture because it was the same 10 students raising their hands and sucking up to Lisa, and unfortunately Lisa let these students drag on. Lectures were a drag so I recommend not going to them. Just do the readings, watch Professor Disch's videos on Canvas, and go to discussion and you'll do well. Also the topics were interesting.

Prof. Disch was passionate about her curriculum and knowledgeable about the subject. Pre-recorded mini-lectures were more helpful to me than in-person lectures, as the in-person lectures don't always connect to the required reading quizzes. If you get a good GSI, you will get a lot out of this class.

Professor Disch is great for what would typically be a boring class. Although many of the readings are from 18th and 19th century political theorists, she does a great job relating it to current day politics and philosophy. Her lectures are interactive and she has so much personality. Take her class if you have even the smallest interest in theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although I ended up with a great grade in this class, the reading quizzes and papers were tough. Most of the time when I was doing a reading quiz, I felt extremely lost. The reading quizzes were hard because 1. language was difficult to understand 2. rubrics were not given out 3. word count. Professor Disch is funny though.
Great professor, makes the material super interesting. She is super caring and respectful or all students. As long as you get a good GSI you should do fine in the class. Material is pretty easy.
i loveeeeeed disch. she is so freaking cool. i loved the way she taught, the way she gave critiques on writing, like just all-around such a wonderful teacher and an even better human.
No midterms or finals only 3 essays

Prof. Disch is a passionate professor. She gives good examples and makes concepts relatable. The grading criteria is pretty clear, but it was not clear how the participation quizzes, some of which were subjective, would factor into our grades. Also, sometimes what she told us was the criteria for essays slightly contrasted with what my GSI said.
Love her. She's hilarious and really smart. She made zoom really fun. You really need a good GSI for this class though...

Professor Disch is amazing! Her lectures are clear, specific, and easy to understand. The assignments and their criteria are super clear as well, making it easy to determine your own grade. A great professor, interesting and relevant subject matter, and not too bad of a workload-- all around great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really great professor overall. Lots of readings, but her lectures are great and reading quizzes are pretty easy. Prof Disch and GSIs are very accessible and I'd highly recommend going to them for feedback/questions on papers prior to the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: College has sucked during COVID, but this class with Prof. Disch has been an absolute pleasure to take. She has been extremely caring, understandable, encouraging, and tried to make the best of this semester virtually. She made students in this class actually feel excited and engaged with the material. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with her.

Each week we had about an hour of lecture along with a large amount of reading (two approximately 30 page writings by old hard to read authors per week). Also, the quizzes we took often had wrong answers or were completely subjective (but still graded). Overall, I feel like not a lot of work was put into the class, and things were often unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Intro to PolSci over zoom with Lisa. She is a very smart, very passionate prof. Super understanding of students needs and loves to make our lives easier (cancelling class during COVID move-out week). Majority of grade is made up by three papers but she basically tells you how to write them to get a good grade. Would have loved to be in perso
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mrs Disch is my favorite professor so far in UM. Her teaching style is unique and I can guarantee you you will never get bored during a class. She learns her students' names in a class of hundreds. The material was so different from an intro to polsci class. It was curated to understand the political talks today. I learned so much. She's the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She's so passionate in class and really challenges you to open up your mind and think about politics and social structures in a way you might never have before. She's also super sweet if you talk to her after class, and while you have to attend class to get iClicker points, her lectures are always interesting. If you don't go, you miss out.

Professor Disch is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. Get to know her and she will write you an incredible recommendation as well. Just be a good student, show up to class, and you will learn a lot.

Professor Disch is super enthusiastic in class. She is driven and very motivated. Her lectures are very interesting and informative but her classes are slightly little work-heavier for an introduction (polisci 101) class.

Shes a real gem at the university, I cant imagine this class being taught by anyone else. Professor Disch really goes out of her way to know her students in a massive lecture hall in a way that many professors cant pull off in small classrooms. Pleasantly surprised
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Highly recommend. Very intelligent and funny person. Lectures were really interesting too, and the reading is frequent but manageable. She's very passionate about her work and it shows. Participation is encouraged, and dissent is welcomed. I came into this class purely on accident, and it ended up being my favorite of the semester.

Overall a funny and engaging lecturer, even if the lecture material is somewhat one-dimensional. No tests/exams, but that means the bulk of your grade is from three small papers, which are graded by your GSI. Overall workload is very small if you're good at quickly finding small details in lengthy readings... otherwise, get ready to read a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Disch makes a lecture feel like an intimate seminar! She's entertaining, helpful, and really knows her stuff. Attendance is required, but you look forward to class--she's that good. There are some tough assignments (essays, mostly) but her grading methods are very reasonable. Put in the effort, you can be successful and learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is an AMAZING professor. She has entertaining lectures, which you receive points for attending, and is really accessible outside of class. I highly recommend going to her office hours as she is really helpful if you don't understand something, but also fun to talk to. She's a great person and is really worth getting to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is by far one of the best professors I've had at Michigan. I wish she taught more classes because she's pretty great. She doesn't have any tests - but for the essays go to her office hours - she's very nice and wants to help you. If you put in the time to do the readings, you'll do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Disch is very into this course! She really enjoys in-lecture participation. I only went to office hours once, but she still learned my name just by participating! The material can be a bit boring. Run your essays/commentary ideas past your GSI to make sure you do well. Overall, not my favorite material, but Professor Disch is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Two 500-word essays, a commentary project, and simple reading checks. No tests! She's passionate about her topic and genuinely enjoys teaching. Subject matter is really interesting if you're into political philosophy.

your average GSI based class. Have an easy GSI, you're going to do well, if not good luck. The lectures are mandatory with Iclicker questions for attendance and the lectures are SO boring. A lot of annoying quizzes and 3 papers. Only good thing about this class was NO TESTS, but still the most mediocre experience. BORING, GSI BASED, NO TESTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof disch was fine, very knowledgeable and kind but I really didn't enjoy the way the lectures worked. It was essentially her calling on students to share their ideas the whole time. This didn't really work for me as I wanted to learn from her, not some random student in my class sharing their often wrong ideas.

Professor Disch has been one of my favorite teachers at the university. Her lectures made political theory interesting and fun. Attendance is mandatory (clickers) but most people are on their laptops. Two mini writings a week, open everything quiz on Fridays, and three papers culminate into a pretty simple class. Highly recommend!

Dr. Disch is extremely intelligent and quick-witted, making her lectures quite engaging and interesting. There were no exams, only 3 major papers, participation, weekly Canvas reading quizzes & re-caps which you have plenty of time to complete. Only downside is that the grades are ultimately determined by your GSI, luckily mine was very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lisa is incredible. You can tell that she really cares about all of her students. Who else takes the time to try and learn the names of 200+ students? The actual content is dry, but she makes it engaging. The class is based mostly on writing assignments that are graded pretty harshly.

her lectures are thought provoking and extremely interesting but they become drier as the course progresses. She really loves what she's doing and is such a kind hearted woman and she tries her best to leave what she believes out of her lectures which I appreciate. However, your grade is determined by 3 essays- and the GSI's are pretty tough
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lisa is a great professor with clear, engaging lectures!! I have yet to find another professor with as much enthusiasm. The only downside to this course is that the grading scale is ultimately determined by your GSI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really great professor, POLSCI 101 has no exams but the grading criteria was still very clear. Professor was informative and enthusiastic about the material, making the whole learning process much easier.

I really enjoyed taking this class! Overall, Dr Disch is very funny and her lectures are very clear. The class is doable and the readings aren't that bad. However, your grade heavily depends on your GSI and mine was pretty tough. No final, two essays and a final commentary. If you are on top of things, it is totally doable!

Good teacher but her lectures can get dry and repetitive. Your grade relies on only a few papers so you have to go to office hours and do well on each to get a good grade. GSIs can be tough graders too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite professor by far. I have never ever been able to sit through an entire lecture without feeling tempted to look at my phone or laptop, until I took this class. I didn't have to distract myself because I enjoyed the way she taught it kept me very engaged.

Best professor I've had in my four semesters so far. She's not only very intelligent, but she knows how to teach material so well. She's incredibly enthusiastic and has the best dad humor in the world. The class itself was graded on three short papers, a project and then attendance and participation (aka iClicker in lecture). Awesome class.

She is really funny and nice. She is really clear during lecture and in her assignments. In order to get an A you have to go to lecture for the attendance points and read the material to answer short question throughout the semester.

Readings are short and you only half to pass 12 out of the 24 reading quizzes, which are basic reading comprehension questions. No exams, 3 short papers. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion. Fairly easy and fair grading, also Professor Disch is very intelligent and makes the lecture interesting

Lisa is hands down the most amazing professor I've had at Michigan. She helped us understand the material and gave us clear guidelines to getting an A in the class. She's funny, so the class was never dull, and genuinely cared about her students. She's one I hope I can take another class with, for sure. If you're in doubt, don't be. Take her class!

Lisa was a GREAT professor.  Her lectures were really engaged and interesting.  She even learns the names of people in lecture.  The difficulty of the essays probably depends on your GSI.  The midterm exam was not too bad as long as you kept up with readings and studied.

I LOVED THIS CLASS.  Lisa was so amazing, I was not interested in Polisci before I took this class and now I'm a Polisci major.  Lisa really holds your attention for an entire lecture, she's funny, and you can tell she cares about her students (she tries to learn as many names as possible, and got pretty far in a 200 person class).  TAKE THIS CLASS
Wow. Lisa was awesome. She came to lecture with passion and enthusiasm. And she had a great sense of humor. Some of the assignments were pretty cool too. Take this class. Lisa is the man :)
LISA DISCH IS A QUEEN. I loved her class. She's so hilarious, and the content was interesting. Her lectures are passionate and enthusiastic. She is a complete boss. Take this class for sure.

Lisa is an amazing professor who actually cares about lecturing to you - you can tell that she's passionate about the material, and it really makes a difference. Awesome professor, really knows what she's talking about. Wish more professors would make the effort and have enthusiasm like she does.

Absolutely fantastic - some of the material is a bit hard/dense to get through, but she explains everything clearly and lecture was never boring. If you don't like lectures that are more discussion based, you probably won't like the style of lecture, but then again it's not for everyone. She's a great person and really nice in general.

This class is easy for those who are good at taking in information and regurgitating it, but for anyone with a more analytic mind, especially if at all conservative, then it can get dry if not at times strait up painful.

AMAZING LADY. TAKE THIS CLASS FOR YOUR INTRO POLISCI REQ. Lisa is a beautiful person, with so much passion, a great sense of humor, and a very strong desire to make her students succeed. and VERY CLEAR. I recommend her highly to ANY type of learner, she will accommodate. GSI's are also amazing for this class. I'm a junior & she is still my fav prof

I LOVE LISA. she has so much personality as well as so much knowledge about her lecture material. she's also pretty funny. i didnt pay attention literally AT ALL the whole year, and got a 97% on the one exam. you dont need to do the readings as long as u take lec notes and study for the exam. there are 3 500-word papers. really reasonable workload

First of all, to the person who said Lisa isn't intelligent, you are clearly not intelligent enough to understand what she says. the women is brilliant and very knowledgeable about her field. great professor and one of the few in the department who actually cares about teaching!

Lisa really loves what she does and it shows. She refers back to the material constantly, so make sure you keep up with the reading. If you take good notes and attend class, you'll learn everything you need to know to succeed in her class. Her GSIs are good too (try to get Keith Veal if you can)

Lisa Disch was a great professor. She went at a great pace and she made things very clear and concise. If you did not understand something she always offered. There is a lot of readings, but that was the only difficult thing about the class.

Her class is super dry. Attendance is a huge factor (seriously, don't not show up to lecture for half of the time) which can either make or break you. The course pack is huge and the readings are all boring and a little hard to read. Most of your grade doesn't even go towards political theory related assignments. Don't take it unless you have to.

I do not understand how people can say anything negative about Lisa. She is awesome! Took 406 with her, had no prior knowledge and really no interest in the class but it ended up being one of my most enjoyable classes. Great lecturer who explains everything extremely well. And she is really nice and enthusiastic.Def take one class before you leave!

Really helpful at office hours. Go to lecture she really explains everything, and she presents the material in a very interesting way. A lot of your grade in the class depends on participation so it's really generous. Only thing that sucks can be the GSIs if you get a bad one but that's a risk at Michigan in general.

Lisa was absolutely incredible. I had never studied political theory but she made it so no prior knowledge was required. There is quite a bit of reading but if you attend class, pay attention, and interact the class is an easy A. Plus she learned everyone's names in our 80 person class within a week. She's a boss.

Professor Disch is amazing. She breaks down her readings with amazing clarity and treats lecture like a in-depth discussion. She takes boring political theory and make you want to learn about it! However, the GSI's have no clue what they're doing. Don't let this ruin the class for you though. Go to her office hours! She is SO helpful!

This was an extremely easy class, and the topics presented (American Political Theory) were interesting. The microthemes are easy as long as you take notes in lecture and go to office hours.
