I would recommend this class to anyone, regardless of their major. Prof Disch gives interesting lectures, she's funny and has spunk. Take this class!

Very interesting and passionate about the material. However, the grading system is awful. There are no tests, but your grade is practically based on 3 essays that are graded VERY brutally.   DON'T TAKE AS YOUR FIRST POLISCI CLASS. It is more of a discussion than a lecture. she walks around and calls on people - the actual discussions are pointless

The professor is great, but the GSI's this year were brutal. There are no tests, but the microthemes are graded very tough. If you don't know anything about polisci and want to check it out - take another polisci like 111 or something - not a political theory class that is unorganized like this one.

If you actually want to learn about political theory, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This class is a glorified American history course, you learn about the Puritans for about three weeks. This is not a joke: We spent more time talking about beastiality than socialism. If you are truly interested in theory, make sure to take the class with another prof.

Class was full of interesting discussion.  Professor Disch really seems like she's having fun teaching the material, and that stimulated class and made it fairly enjoyable.  In a world of frankly, pretty weird professors, Professor Disch was normal, outgoing and intelligent. I'd recommend her to anyone.

Prof. Disch is an absolutely fantastic professor. She is the only professor I know of that can make a lecture period seem like a discussion section. She moves throughout the room while lecturing and makes the material interesting. There's no textbook, only a thick course pack. No exams, but the "microthemes" are a bit challenging.

I don't usually write these, but Prof. T is one of the most brilliant professors I've had at U of M. He's clearly very knowledgeable, and his classes are well organized. If you're not interested in Shakespeare, don't take it—but if you are, you'll learn a lot. He's understanding, professional, and genuinely cares about his students.

Took this Fall 2024. Very interesting class (imo) and I don't usually enjoy writing but assignments were manageable and he's very understanding that this is many students' first time taking an english course at umich. He was very passionate about the material and gave great feedback on assignments/essays.
If I actually liked English courses I would love to take another one with Prof T. He is LeGoated at lectures despite going on random tangents sometimes. Genuine guy
The Best, incredible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: (ignoring his scandal) he's a solid professor. his classes are mildly boring if you don't care for shakespeare, and his assignments definitely weren't difficult, but sometimes you didn't know what he wanted from you. he himself is very nice and understanding (gave me a two week extension when i asked for 2 days), i recommend if you want an easy A

Lectures were long and difficult to parse through at times alongside the essays coming with the criteria to "pick a passage and really dig into it," which I don't think is a very clear requirement. Besides this, he is evidently very passionate about the topic, to the point where I felt a bit bad that I had almost no time to get into the material.

Professor Trevor's lectures were fun but long. It was very easy to get lost and bored in them, and some of the information didn't seem to connect to what we were learning. He was still fun and understanding of absences - I had to miss due to a doctor's appointment, and my grade wasn't touched. Overall, just a decent guy and an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't like this dude. Summarizes. No reason to read. Poor feedback. Look at the Michigan Daily Article about him.

Trevor could not be better. Before you "google him, trust me" google those who advise you to. Did they take his class? Could they gave grudges that don't have to do with his teaching. I have not met anyone who has taken a class with this instructor who did not appreciate his teaching and the respect he showed for every student. 100% great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I am an English major and have had most of the professors in the department. Prof Trevor is the best. In a department not known for it's respectful faculty members, Trevor was respectful, intelligent, challenging, and hilarious.

Doug Trevor is the absolute best!! I learned so much and he was so knowledgeable and helpful. You do have to work though. If you're someone who thinks Google or Sparknotes is a fine substitute for Shakespeare or Milton -- right, you probably won't like him, genius. The rest of us really do.

One of the many delights of the English department at U-M. Google him before taking his class. Unfortunately, taking his class taught me nothing about writing. It was in the early morning, and he offered zero feedback unless it was a weirdly scathing comment directed at someone in class or in oh. If he was nice, it felt like a trap.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Google this professor before taking his class.

Professor Trevor is a solid choice if you enjoy lecture-heavy classes. They aren't my favorite so I was hesitant to give rave review. Trevor has lots of great ideas and chooses solid materials to read and analyze. I took this class because it was part of my required courses but didn't mind it at all.

Prof Trevor may be a little rambley at times in lecture, but he is so insightful and knowledgeable about Shakespeare. He's also so passionate, which is really infectious. Overall a really caring and lovely professor, would recommend!!

Prof. Trevor is by far the greatest professor I've ever had. I took 3 classes with him at UMich and I wish I could take more! His incredible knowledge of Shakespeare translates into all his lectures and I was continually blown away by what I learned from him in such a short time. Definitely take ANY class you can with him - you won't regret it.

I was looking forward to this class because I love Shakespeare but the man pretty much took a gravel to that. Wish I'd never taken his class. We blazed through six plays in six weeks, just so he could say that we now knew 1/3rd of Shakespeare. Honestly? Just go through sparknotes. It details what he says in class, word for word.

Professor Trevor was a phenomenal lecturer. The work of John Milton is at times dense and difficult (especially if you are not well-versed in 17th century literature, as I am not) but Professor Trevor makes the material so accessible. He is also an entertaining guy, striking the perfect balance in lecture between informative and engaging.

Professor Trevor is one of the best professors I have had. He is so passionate about Shakespeare and it is evident in his lectures. There is a lot of reading, but it is worth it. I learned so much from this class and genuinely enjoyed going to class. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Trevor!

Dougie Trev is an amazing professor. His analysis of Shakespeare is incredible and I have yet to meet a more passionate professor at this university. He tends to go on tangents, but they are always interesting. If I was an English major, I would try to take as many classes as I could with him.

Professor Trevor is my favorite literature professor at the university. He helped me to better understand Shakespeare and I learned to love it even more. I regret not being able to take his Milton class, but I speak with him every other week. If you have any ideas, he will listen and help you become a better student.

Brilliant professor, frequently digresses to provide a more accurate impression of the writing. The digressions were probably my favorite part of the class because he explains things with an incredible enthusiasm for the subject matter. Class structure was really basic, and the requirements for an A weren't unreasonable.
I found the subject matter interesting but did not appreciate the way he taught. He was incredibly confusing in lecture, and digressed so often that we quickly fell behind the syllabus.

Trevor is definitely passionate, but it doesn't translate well to the students. For exams, he also expects you to basically repeat his opinion, which I thought was rather strange for an English class. Definitely not a bad prof, but definitely not my favorite either.

His passion and humor for the subject motivates students to engage in his discussions. He comes to class with a great attitude and encourages participation. He is a very fair grader. I am not normally an A student, but still pulled off an A-. Although the reading is heavy, there are only two papers, a midterm, and a final. Great class, great prof.

Doug is wonderful. He is funny, brilliant, and interesting. Always makes the hour and a half go by so quickly. Grades a little on the tough side, but attendance in lecture counts, so go. It's worth it.
He is amazing! One of U of M's best professors. He loves what he teaches too, and it really shows. And it doesn't hurt that he's incredibly gorgeous and has a great personality.
Great teacher, but dont expect an A, even for A quality work. real tough on grading, but he is very knowledgeable on the subject. Definitely take his class

Best professor at UM! I took his class on satirical lit last year, it's still my favorite English class. Difficult grader, but it's totally worth it. He is always willing to meet outside of class, I honestly learned more in his class than in any other. He let our class pick the last novel of our class! Great professor!!

Doug is one of the smartest people I've met. He's very informed and only teaches classes he specializes in. I enjoyed the class but will warn you that he is a tough grader. If you're normally an 'A' student in English, you can expect an A- or B+.  It's a lot of work but well worth it, this professor is a must for Eng majors!

Trevor is a spectacular professor. I wasn't too interested in poetry, but had to take the course as a prerequisite. He has definitely changed my views on poetry. Though I did miss some of the traditional poets (Keats, Wordsworth), Trevor made up for it with contemporary poets that filled the gaps. Overall a great course; grades weren't a problem.

He is one of the best professors I have had at Michigan. I have had him now for 4 courses and if I wasn't graduating I would take a class of his again. He is great and knows a lot about his topics. He is funny and entertaining. I would advise anyone to take his class if you can!

Very brainy and cerebral. Hard grader. Go to office hours to get tips on paper writing, as it will probably boost your grade. At first I was disappointed to get an A-, but I never went to office hours for advice or help, either.

He is awesome!  So interesting to listen to , and is obviously incredibly passionate about what he teaches.  He gives a historical background to what he is teaching and gives us interesting facts, which makes the work more interesting.  So cute too! Hard grader but worth it!

An exceptional professor. Doug's passion is visible, and his charisma and insight make his lectures genuinely interesting. He's human and 'normal' while maintaining an air of unshakable erudition. Be warned: He grades papers according to very high standards, but will also offer really fantastic advice. Do not miss your chance to study with him.
Absolutely adorable. So into Shakespeare -- it's contagious!

Truly exceptional professor.  He is certainly demanding, but contrary to these other comments, I found him (as did my classmates) more than willing to meet outside of class.  He went so far as to invite us out to lunch with him and insist on 'Doug.'  His intelligence can be startling, but never off putting, and he is hardly self-absorbed. Take him.

Great guy, great prof, and he seems to have changed a lot since his days at UIowa.  I had no problem getting help from him outside of class.  His grading can be a little rough, but it's what I expected from a 400-level course.  I'd recommend both the class and the prof.

Sorry, I took him at UIOWA too, but he didn't honor office hours and would not meet with students even when asked. Also grades seemed arbitrary and he did not factor in extra credit for those who did the work. Brilliant man who did not take care of business nor students' concerns in his last semester at Iowa. Maybe he's doing better at Univ.MI.
Great professor. His methods are challenging, not difficult. He's encouraging and confiding. He's effortlessly funny. One of the best professors I had at UIOWA

Excellent professor on nearly all counts.  His character itself carries the class--he's brilliant, yes, but doesn't stifle unorthodox ideas.  I found him more than willing to help with papers given a day or two. When he starts awkwardly insisting that you call him 'Doug' it's hard not to enjoy him.

Grueling class. Yes, he's brilliant, charming, but petty & self-absorbed. I took his course at U.IA. He evaded giving outside help, was dismissive toward students & staff. Disdains undergrads. Refused to return graded final essays at end of course. As an honors student willing to work hard, I hated how he ran this class. Caution, he's new to MI.
Left no impression either way...

I earned an "A" in his taxing winter class, but I would still recommend him.  He loved Shakespeare's material for its verbal prowess and enigmatic characters, and his grading was tough but insightful.  Most of all, I appreciated how he left his personal life at home.  He came in every day with a smile - regardless of how he actually felt.
One of my favorite profs.  Wonderful guy and great class.
I really enjoyed this course, and it broadened my horizons to writing/analyzing films.  I now own every version of Hamlet ever made, except for the Mel Gibson one, which sucks.

He is a great teacher and a really nice guy.  I had him for Shakespeare- i tihnk one of his first years at Iowa. The class was energetic and he brought that energy in with him everyday.  He really turned my on to Shakespeare and made it accessiable.

I would say to the very few people who didn't think Doug was a good professor - you probably got a bad grade in his class.  There's really no dispute - he is crazy smart, and has the personality too.  You don't usually find that in a professor.  Recommend ANY of his classes, but be ready to work!
Stanford + Harvard + Harvard (again) + HOT + excellent professor = Doug Trevor.  Nuff said.
class was okay--he rambled alot. and i really didn't think he was that hot (although im sure he thinks he is.)
Ssssssssteamy!  Oh, and he's a really good professor.  Did I mention he's hot?
Had him years ago and still remember him as one of the best teachers I've ever had. One of the most intelligent people I've known. And yes, the fact that he is beautiful can be slightly distracting.

Professor Trevor is amazing - he's so smart it's sometimes kind of intimidating, but he's extremely engaging and loves his subject.  The fact that he's so hot can be difficult (hard to concentrate) but I'd recommend him very highly.  I learned a lot.
Not for heathens or Philistines. Trevor is easily one of the most charismatic and engaging professors at the UI.
Teaches extremely difficult material really well.  A really nice guy, accessible, and very helpful.  Wonderful sense of humor.  And, yes, he is HOT.

It's not that he's unprepared, but that the subject matter is difficult.  He's very intelligent, kind of a problem in relating to undergrads.  But he'll do anything he can to make it easier.  Recommended, especially for pre-1800s, he makes it fun.
A nice guy.  Not prepared, relies too much on class discussion.  Knows his stuff, but doesn't know how to teach it.  Grading criteria is  ambiguous.
The best teacher ever.  He makes the most difficult material interesting and understandable.  Very loved teacher.
Prepared and easy to approach.  Drawback is that he has trouble relating to apathetic students.  You will get what you put into this course.
unprepared for classes, stream of consciousness lecturing
uses micro-aggressions as an attempt to be funny and get a few laughs.

Really awesome and makes class really. As a Ling Major I do my best to get him as my lecturer because he's very nice and knowledgeable. He's great about answering questions in a very respectful manner and not afraid to say he doesn't know the answer. I will say he's sometimes nitpicky about grading but not to the point were you wont pass.

I was excited to take this class but I was disappointed in the teaching style. I'm sure Dr Merchant is very knowledgable about linguistics however lecture is him reading off of slides and sometimes he gets sidetracked and we don't finish the slides for the day. It's easy to get an A though since the midterm is open note and the "final" is a paper

I absolutely loved this class and the professor! Dr. Merchant and his GSI, Sophie, were both amazing teachers! I had no prior knowledge of linguistics, but they made it so fun to learn and kept things less intimidating than most professors I've had. I highly reccommend if you're a freshman and need to adjust to lectures and assignments.

Lectures were super engaging- he is very passionate about what he is teaching. Super light workload and relatively easy class. We had three homework assignments all semester that were super doable, and then a midterm that was online and a final paper (no final exam!!) Class was engaging and easy.

He is the best. Very chill and relaxed. Also has amazing lectures and class layouts with a couple of homework assignments, 1 midterm exam (open note), 1 essay (which counted as our final). Very open, and outgoing. He also has an amazing GSI named Sophie who is also very kind, knowledgeable, and approachable! Would 100% recommend him to others
Good Class. Great Professor.

I was more stressed out in 3rd grade than I was in Ling106. Only 3 1-2 page assignments that take about 30 minutes and one final paper the entire semester. Those are the only ones though so make sure you proofread. I found a lot of the topics interesting even though I was only taking the class for credit, also Dr. Merchant and Sophie are very nice!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class. Interesting if you have even the slightest interest in linguistics, not interesting if you don't. GPA booster

This was my second class with Prof. Merchant. His passion for and knowledge of syntax is inspiring! Mostly lectures, some ungraded in-class exercises, a few graded homework assignments, and one take-home final exam. Come with an interest in syntax and you'll leave with a lot of interesting knowledge! And don't be afraid to ask questions.

Dr Merchant is the GOAT. He's very passionate about the subject matter, and the lectures are super engaging and surprisingly funny. He's also super caring and gives leniency on due dates. Genuinely one of my favorite professors, this class made me declare a major in linguistics. Show up to class and the exams will be super easy/you'll learn a lot.

Prof. Merchant extended my passion for linguistics. He's very knowledgable and clearly passionate about the topic. His lectures are full of great, interesting material and are often surprisingly funny! He's incredibely likable and clearly very caring. Work is very light with a lot of leniency on due dates. Show up and you'll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Merchant is just about the best, most caring Prof I've had at Michigan.

The class was almost exclusively lecture-based, with a few HW assignments that were easy to complete. The exams were online, open-note, and formatted almost exactly like the HW. The lectures were mostly pretty engaging, you could tell he's passionate about the topic. Highly recommend for an easy-A intro ling class.

Prof Northrop is a passionate professor and cares about his students. I took a 1st-yr seminar with him, and I did find it to be a lot of reading (100-200 pages a week, if not more.) Regardless, I liked the class and the way he set up the seminars was great. He's also very accommodating and understanding, and will help you if you just ask.
He genuinely wants you to do well in the class, and if he sees that you are putting in the work, you will succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He's so nice and so smart. You can tell he really cares about history and teaching. But the workload is insane. Sometimes 200 pages of reading PER CLASS (2 classes/week). Readings are dense and difficult. 2 big projects, both really hard. Doesn't make sense that this is 3 credit class. Still enjoyed him and this class a lot though.

Generally very nice, very smart, and very knowledgable about topics. He was a pretty fair grader, but assigned a LOT of work - dense, difficult reading of around 100 pages + big essays. Felt like it should be a 4 credit class given that I had the most work in this course vs my other 4 credit courses. Really liked him as a teacher though.

The grades for discussion posts and essays depend entirely on the grader or professor's personal opinion about the topic, and the workload is extremely excessive. I wouldn't recommend taking this class.

don't take this class just because it's online. the discussion post and essay grading is entirely based on the grader/professors opinion about the topic and the workload is so ridiculous. don't take this class!!!

He reported me to my advisor after two weeks for not participating on zoom.  
Also get a zero points for discussion, even though the online discussions don't have a topic. And I met double the word count.

There's a lot of reading required, you can get by relatively fine without reading at all (probably won't work for everyone). The lectures are very engaging and the  discussion sections are very small and chill. Would recommend taking this class if you like obscure history classes and as a way to fulfil your race and ethnicity requirement.

There were very few students in the class so participation in group discussions was inevitable, requiring you to read the material beforehand. He assigned 130 pages in 5 days, then another 130 in 2 days immediately after. Overall a very good professor, lots of reading (avg 60-150 pg/week), final group project. Great Russian/Asian History prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very passionate and knowledgeable about subject
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Insanely heavy workload for a three credit class. Would never recommend or take anything with him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Northrop is a nice guy but I wouldn't recommend his class. I took this class during a half-term and the amount of material covered was just too much for 6 weeks. His lectures drone on, have no visual aide, and are overall not helpful. The grading criteria for the papers is also way too vague.

This class was not easy, but I learned a lot. If you know nothing about Central Asia I would recommend taking an intro to Islam or Russian history course before this so that you have some background. Really great lecturer, and willing to help when you go to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a completely fine professor. He drones on and on a bit during lecture and nothing in his class is so interesting. Primary source assignments are graded fairly but harder than most other history courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Northrop is easily the WORST professor I have had at umich. His lectures are incredibly boring, his slides only have pictures and do not help to learn the content, he requires an awful amount of reading, and his exams are ridiculous. He spent most of the time talking about Colonial CA, but his exam questions are primarily about pre-Colonial CA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is specifically for his online classes. Expect to be graded as if you are writing essays as a historian and your document is being professionally peer-reviewed. His essay prompts are extremely vague (worst part of the class IMO). Also, he assumes everyone is cheating during online exams and makes his exams much much harder.

I cannot say enough how much I love Professor Northrop's class! Professor Northrop is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are truly fascinating. Go to all his lectures and you'll get a good grade in the class. Readings are also super interesting. LOVE IT SO MUCH!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I LOVED Professor Northrop's lectures!!! They are super interesting and inspirational. He is truly one of the best history professors I've ever had, and he is super passionate and knowledgable about what he is teaching. Overall class isn't too hard as long as u go to all his lectures. Can't wait to take another class with him next year!

Professor Northrop is a great person. I never saw myself leaving a review on this website, but I can't not after this class. A master lecturer. Taking this class is worth every dollar and cent. I am so pleased with the knowledge I've gained, even with the transition to a remote format. This is coming from someone who sucks at history.

Prof Northrop was awesome. He gives a list of key terms that will help you succeed on exams. Students are able to choose their second essay topic which allows you to explore your own personal interests. He made me very interested in Central Asia which I knew nothing about! Also, very willing to make time to meet you outside of class and office hrs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was SO MUCH reading and the readings were not engaging or all the interesting. Great guy, super nice, and very helpful but the class was boring.

Northrop is an okay lecturer, (although he always goes past the last minute of class, which is annoying if you have a class immediately after). He's very enthusiastic about Central Asia, and he gives you lists of the terms you'll need to know for exams. Exams are reasonable, but require a lot of memorization.

:D He is so nice and fun in class! He has outlines of his notes because he likes students to be able to follow what he is saying without worrying they are missing something and wants the students to know how to spell some of the cities and names of Central Asia, he puts pictures on the slides, has a few guest lecturers, great class and professor!

Very interesting, really knows his stuff. I was astounded at how he could present the material so it was interesting to someone who has next to no interest in history. Really helpful outside of class.

Northrop taught one of the most fun classes ever! The readings are derived from the writings of some of the craziest freaks of history. In addition to being nostalgic for that era in history, I'm also nostalgic for the class.
Prof. Northrop is an excellent instructor. The workload of the class he requires is pretty high, so make sure you have to spend some extra time on his class.

He is great.  Here's the deal, any class with him with him will be tough, make it one of your top 10 priorities for the semester.  But it will all be worth it, he loves teaching, lecturing, and talking with his students, and he is good at all those things.  So please for your benefit and his, take a class with him, you'll never regret it.

One of the best professors I've had at Michigan.  Lectures are always dynamic and interesting.  He's really into helping students see the big picture.  If you want to learn something you never knew before, take Prof. Northrop's classes.

Really knows what he's talking about, very interested in his subject. Sometimes moves a little fast for those of us not as invested in Central Asia.. I probably didn't learn as much as he would have hoped, but still a very informative class overall. Discussion was not helpful, though.

HOLY COW can this guy assign reading. After the class I pitched over 20 pounds of paper from this class! Dozens of online articles, some hundreds of pages long. I now knoe thing about Russians I never wanted to know. (i.e. the Red Yurt Program medical exams!)

He is a great lecturer! He emphasizes important points in his lecture so you know what to make a note of, and he really cares about the success of his students. He seems to work well with the gsi's to make sure they are doing their job, and he even goes to section to keep an eye on things. Awesome class!!

Probably one of the best lecturers I've ever had in my life.  There is a lot of heavy reading in this class, but you can also skip a lot of it without penalty.  Fair amount of out of class mandatory activities.  Filtering through what's actually useful to know for the exams is really the biggest part of the class.  GSI is pretty helpful.

For one, Northrop lectures like he was born to it. He definitely wants his students to do well, and he makes a point of listening to their concerns. A good course with a good professor.  The textbook (Svat Soucek) is absolutely useless, but it's supplemented by the excellent lectures and other readings. Class starts out hard, gets easier as you go.

Great lecturer. Don't use textbook so need to go to most lectures. readings are an assortment of articles and primary sources that supplement the lectures.  some are redundant/boring, but you can limit yourselves to the interesting ones without penalty. had a great gsi too.

Professor Northrop is one of the best lecturers I've ever had at UM. The textbook for this course is basically useless, but it didn't even matter, because his lectures were so engaging and full of information.

Lecturers are pretty good, not the best I've ever had but more than tolerable. There's a lot of reading though, and some of it can be very redundant. Filtering the relevant from the irrelevant is half the battle there, don't expect to be able to complete all of it.

Engaging and interesting class, if you like history and don't mind doing a lot of reading.  I skipped a lot of the reading without penalty, but there was still a great deal that I did.  Learned about a region I would have never covered otherwise, and I am now considering making it my area of concentration.  He's an awesome lecturer.

The professor and the class are chill. The projects do take some time as you are using Snap! to code but overall if you attend the lab days (which is a day where you are not required to attend) it will help you a lot with completing your projects especially if you are struggling.

He's super nice, but when I took the class, it seemed that he wasn't quite sure how to command a room, which made him sometimes hard to follow. One-on-one time with him was extremely helpful, though, and he explained how he did the best with what he was given for class.
Very nice, not a great helper despite his best efforts
10/10 professor
Amzaing professor
Very clear.
We love you Dr. DC!
Dr. DC my goat!
He was great!
Hes perfect

Dr. DC is really nice and I did enjoy this class. But everytime I asked him or the GSI a question, they didn't know the answer and would just tell me to leave my programming how it was. This was really frustrating. Lectures were boring too.
I love dr dc

David Dorris was an amazing professor, super passionate and engaging. I took a Disney class with him and loved how much he cared about the material and his students. He was also very understanding and flexible when I had a conflicting class. Not sure why there are negative reviews, my experience was excellent.

It is extremely difficult to understand him. He talks so low in lecture, plays loud music while he's talking, never likes to turn up the microphone & he just rambles all day. So many long readings. He gives the study guides not even a week before the exams when it's so much info we need to know. Very unorganized, the worst class i've ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are impossible to pay attention to and follow because prof. Doris talks in circles and is always playing music over his voice. much of what we talk about in class is not on the exam and impossible to discern what is important to remember or not. No lecture slides or recordings posted- if you miss class or aren't locked in ur kinda screwed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was horrible. I took it for a fairly easy humanities class to fulfill the LSA humanities requirement and it was far from it. Lectures are terribly disorganized and the prof rambles in circles about different topics and provides no lecture slides, so there is no way to study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor let me hate studying and i was about to drop all classes because of him! A lotttt of readings so according to that much i think you must take it as the only course in one semester.. yeah it's that much. In lectures you'll not hear him even with microphone and he'll not hear you..You,ll not know what to study so it's a blind course.

Contrary to what you might read, Dr. D is an awful professor. He took an interesting class and made it more boring than watching paint dry. He didn't provide lecture recordings or slides either. His lectures were disorganized, and he played music loudly in the background which made it impossible to hear him clearly. Avoid his classes at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! Dr. Doris is extremely knowledgable and has a ton of passion for the subject. His lectures were fun and he clearly cares about his students a lot. There aren't many assignments and it's an easy A if you put at least some effort into the assignments. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. D is there to teach you about more than African Art. When I first began the course, I was intrigued, but not in love. As the course went on, we not only talked about African Art, but about how it related to us as people, how it has shaped our culture, and why learning about African Art is important. This course and Dr. Doris are fantastic.

Incredible, incredible professor, and a very well-read, worldly, and eloquent gentleman.  As someone with little to no previous interest in ancient Yoruban artwork, this man has you hooked the moment he starts talking. His passion is undeniable - keep in mind, AAS 290 was only a two-credit course. One hell of a deal, you ask me.

Dr. Doris is extremely intelligent and passionate about what he teaches. The class was definitely experimental for him and the students so at times it felt like there was no structure. However, he really cares about his students and wants them to learn which is demonstrated in the amazing feedback he gives you on your work and the way he speaks.
Disorganized and just not an overall great teacher....

Dr. Doris's class is one that will change your life if you let it. He is so incredibly passionate about what he teaches that you can't help but share his love for the subject matter by the end of the class. His classes are not for the easy A; they are for expanding your mind.

Dr. Doris is one of the most intelligent professors I've had, and his penmanship is insane (You could tell by the way he introduced RFT at his lecture). I've never met a professor more passionate about their work. His lectures were more like slam poetry and you can tell that he wanted everyone to succeed. If you don't ask, you won't receive!

Dr. Doris talks in circles. Not only that but during lectures he will go on 1.5 hour long tangents. The entire class hated it (we all talked about it). Not only that but there is no structure for the class. We didn't get the syllabus until a month in. He grades hard on participation even though he talks the whole time.
Very caring! Dr. D is willing to discuss course materials and help students who ask for help. If you participate and perform assigned tasks, you will get a good grade.

Innovative course structure. Holds students to high standards, but is very accommodating to those who approach him during office hours. Provides thoughtful, constructive advice and comments on papers. If you participate, you will get the grade you deserve. Heavy on quips and jokes in class.

Doris is a really smart man, but he can ramble/be confusing. 1/4 to 1/2 of lectures are spent talking about things that are not on the exam. If you take this class, remember that the STUDY GALLERY is the most important. Once you start taking notes on the important things he says in class,the class isn't hard at all. Just space the memorizing out.

David Doris is an amazing professor. He truly wants you to be inspired by this subject and see how it has impacted the world as a whole. As long as you take notes in lecture and memorize identifications, it is not difficult to get an A in the class.

Davis is great, but WARNING: IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN EASY A, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. We took it for the easy A but were forced to put in A TON of work: 100+ of hours of studying for the midterm and final, not to mention the two essays. If you like art history, its probably a great class. For all those non-art types of people, think twice

He is extremely smart and his lectures are more like slam poetry. It is important to go to every lecture to get an A, although it isn't mandatory. There is a lot of memorization for the exams. Their are a lot of long, required readings but they are very interesting.

David Doris is ridiculously smart, and is a very entertaining lecturer. He attempts to broaden the perceptions of your mind. Some of what he says is so hard to grasp, but as long as you had a general understanding of what he says, you will do good. There lots of readings, but he explains everything in class.

David Doris leaves a lasting impression. I took an upper level African Art class with 0 background in art history. He transformed my idea of a great teacher and made me wish I'd taken a class of his before my senior year. He's passionate, excited, knowledgeable, and always values students ideas. If you have the opportunity, take any class he offers
This was a great class! Not interested in art at all and really feel like I have learned a lot. Midterm and Finals were easy if you studied for them! I recommend this class!

His outstanding passion makes this class such amazing fun! He puts on a performance and gets you involved. By the end of the course, I loved the subject too. From my experience, he  was also really encouraging and nurturing of each person's academic development.

One of the best professors I've ever had, is it the Cornell background? Friendly, hilarious, witty and interesting. You will sing in this class. You will go places. You will learn a lot about African Art. Study hard for the finals and write decent papers.

Doris is definitely energetic. The papers are easy. Easy A, and fun awesome professor, we listened to music everyday and did some workout one time in lecture. TAKE IT, ONLY IF YOUR AN ART HISTORY MAJOR THOUGH. for outsiders like me, its confusing how every1 knows how to desribe art

Extremely passionate. High level of energy in every class. I really enjoyed this class. There are two exams that are really straightforward and he gives you all of the images you have to know on CTools day one of class. The papers are fun to write because you get to choose what to write about. Overall, great class and great teacher.

While Doris is really uplifting and very passionate about what he teaches, I found him very offensive at times. I'm not an art history major and I took this class for humanities... maybe I don't get it. But I'm also a feminist and some of the things he said were just plain offensive. I have to admit though that he did give good explanations.
Doris is god.
Inspiring teacher.
great teacher, his passion is contageous.  also very funny.

I took this class a while ago, but I only remember good things about Professor Doris and his class.  He was always super passionate about African Art History, and he's a great person to talk to.  The class involves a lot of reading, which he usually discusses on the day it's due.
judgemental
One of the reasons that the History of Art department is the coolest at the school

Prof Doris gets so excited about african art you can't help being exicited too. The material is so interesting, its one of my favorite lectures. However, you're expceted to memorize about 90 images for the midterm and final..name, date, whatever small villiage in Nigeria it was made in, etc- very frustrating. But I still would recommend, good class
the best professor in Art history. he is soo vivacious and really cares about you as a person and a student.  He wants you to do well and will help you do what you need to do.
He is the best professor you will ever have.  No joke.  Passionate, unconventional but still disciplined and knowledgable.
